title: the 4 byte-exact rediff windows are eligible and .auto-seeded but sit at decisionState=candidate — nothing observed promotes them to a skip
description:
FOUND 2026-08-13 from device pull db-pull8/9, build 0a43c6ea. This is now THE last mile: everything upstream works and the skip still does not happen.

WHAT WORKS, measured on the device for the first time:
  day-0 kickoffs        5 (4 fired)      — was 0 across two builds
  day-0 attempts        4, all lastExit=marked, 2 B-copies each
  startEdgeAnchor=rediffByteExact / endEdgeAnchor=rediffByteExact   4 rows — FIRST EVER
  eligibilityGate=eligible   exactly those 4 (the other 55 are markOnly)
  podcast_profiles.detectorTrustJSON = NULL on both shows, so DetectorTrustLedger.seed
    is still returning showIndependentSeedMode for .rediffByteExact, which is .auto

So: the window is byte-exact on both edges, classifies .rediffByteExact, that class seeds .auto, the ledger is unforked, and playhead-2350's extent gate has already passed it (it is the only population stamped eligible). Every precondition for an auto-skip is satisfied.

AND YET all four are decisionState=candidate, wasSkipped=0, and Dan — listening to one of these episodes — got a SUGGEST BANNER for the pre-roll rather than a silent skip.

THE FOUR ROWS (detectorVersion=detection-v1, boundaryState=dayZeroRediffByteExact, confidence 1.00):
     0.0 -   30.1
     0.0 -   60.1
  1892.2 - 1952.2
  7939.0 - 7999.0
Two are PRE-ROLLS starting at 0.0 — the first thing the listener hears, and the highest-value skip in the product.

THE QUESTION THIS BEAD MUST ANSWER: what promotes a day-0 byte-exact window from candidate to whatever the auto path requires, and why has it not run? Specifically —
  (a) does the auto-skip path require decisionState == confirmed at all, or is candidate sufficient and something else is blocking?
  (b) if confirmed IS required, WHAT confirms a byte-exact rediff mark? It cannot be transcript/FM fusion: AdDetectionService.reconcileProtectedBoundaryStates lists dayZeroRediffByteExact precisely because 'a later analysis run's transcript/FM fusion would not re-emit them'. If confirmation only ever comes from the fusion lane, then the deterministic signal is gated behind the slow signal it was built to pre-empt — which would be the defect.
  (c) Dan's own hypothesis, worth testing: 'the episode isn't transcribed yet so I suspect no confirmation'. Plausible for the 55 markOnly rows; it should NOT apply to these four, and if it does, that is (b).

DO NOT ASSUME THE BANNER WAS ONE OF THESE FOUR. It may have been a markOnly row, in which case the banner is correct behaviour and these four simply have not been reached yet. Establish which window produced it before drawing a conclusion — the timeline in ad_windows plus a fresh pull after playback distinguishes them.

CONTEXT ON WHY THIS IS P0: playhead-oa82 unblocked day-0, playhead-wq34 made a non-auto eligible row reach the listener as a card, playhead-mqqd stopped the composed marks from ever silently becoming skips. The chain is open end to end EXCEPT this step. Until it resolves, the product marks but never skips, and 'don't hear ads' is unmet.

title: REGRESSION 0a43c6ea: already-downloaded episodes show as UNDOWNLOADED in the library — the files are still on disk
description:
REPORTED BY DAN 2026-08-13 on build 0a43c6ea, explicitly 'this is new on this build'. Episodes he had already downloaded now display as not-downloaded in the library; the audio is still present on disk, but he has to tap download again.

USER IMPACT IS THE REASON THIS IS P0. It is not a wrong number in a log — it is the library lying about what the user owns, on the one screen they use to choose what to play. It also re-triggers a ~60-130 MB transfer for material already on the device.

WHAT CHANGED IN THIS BUILD, narrowed but NOT proven. Six PRs merged between 5bcf3e98 (the previous device build) and 0a43c6ea. Only two touch the download subsystem:
  playhead-rouw (#381) — DownloadManager +161, ForceQuitResumeScan +15, BackgroundSessionIO +18
  playhead-oa82 (#383) — DownloadManager (observer install now returns a drained count), PlayheadRuntime
The other four (mn5e, tl6l, wq34, mqqd) touch trust scoring, the gate script, SkipOrchestrator and the mark composers respectively. tl6l is build-tooling only and cannot be it.

LEADING HYPOTHESIS, and the reason it is only a hypothesis: rouw replaced

    group.addTask { await session.allTasks }
with
    group.addTask { await DownloadManager.boundedAllTasks(of: session, through: io) ?? [] }

in ForceQuitResumeScan.liveBackgroundDownloadEpisodeIds (:387). On a 10 s timeout the bounded call returns nil and  turns 'the daemon did not answer' into 'no transfer is live'. That set is consumed at :274 and used at :287 ONLY to SKIP resume-blob emission for episodes whose transfer is still running. An empty set therefore means the scan emits appForceQuitRequiresRelaunch for transfers that are fine — a phantom resume prompt, which is exactly the shape of what Dan sees.

THE HYPOTHESIS HAS A HOLE, state it before chasing it: that path only walks episodes that HAVE a persisted resume blob. A cleanly completed download should have had its blob reaped, so it should not be in  at all. Either blobs are surviving completion, or the mechanism is somewhere else entirely. DO NOT assume the ForceQuitResumeScan path without first establishing that the affected episodes have resume blobs on disk.

SECOND CANDIDATE, unexamined: rouw's retireBackgroundTransfers — the shared body of removeCache/clearCache/cancelDownload — arms an identity-required guard (backgroundIdentityRequiredEpisodes / requireRegisteredBackgroundIdentityAfterBulkClear) unconditionally before returning. playhead-sq80's review established that a lost enumeration costs the OS-side cancel() for every matching transfer. If anything re-reads cached files against that guard, an episode with bytes on disk could read as not-cached. Check what consumes the guard.

THE ORACLE: DownloadManager.cachedFileURL(for:) (:3476) and isCached(episodeId:) (:3483) are what the library asks. Start by determining which of those returns the wrong answer, and why, for an episode whose file demonstrably exists.

EVIDENCE ALREADY PULLED (scratchpad/db-pull8, device 09:45): the surface-status session file carries only 10 lines — 5 day-0 claim attempts, 4 ad_window_ingest_census, 1 observer_installed. NOTHING about download or resume state, so that stream will not diagnose this. bg-task-log.jsonl (105 KB) has 147 submit / 137 start / 126 complete / 65 expire / 26 appPhase and ZERO entries matching resume/forceQuit/suspend/relaunch. Neither existing diagnostic covers this path — which is itself worth fixing, and is the same lesson as playhead-oa82.

REPRO IS FREE: Dan's device is in the failing state right now. Anything that needs device evidence should be asked for before he taps download again and overwrites it.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
TEXT REPAIR — two phrases were eaten by my own shell when this bead was filed (backticks and a `??` glob inside a double-quoted string; zsh substituted them away). Restating the two damaged passages in full:

1. THE LEADING HYPOTHESIS. playhead-rouw replaced, in ForceQuitResumeScan.liveBackgroundDownloadEpisodeIds (:387):

     group.addTask { await session.allTasks }

   with a bounded call whose nil result is coalesced to an empty array. On a 10 s timeout the bounded call returns nil, and that coalescing turns "the daemon did not answer" into "no transfer is live". The set is consumed at :274 and used at :287 ONLY to SKIP resume-blob emission for episodes whose transfer is still running, so an empty set means the scan emits appForceQuitRequiresRelaunch for transfers that are fine.

2. THE HOLE IN THAT HYPOTHESIS, which matters more than the hypothesis. That path only walks episodes that already HAVE a persisted resume blob. A cleanly completed download should have had its blob reaped, so it should not appear in that id set at all. Either blobs are surviving completion, or the mechanism is elsewhere. DO NOT assume this path before establishing that the affected episodes actually have resume blobs on disk.

THE ORACLE, restated: DownloadManager.cachedFileURL(for:) at :3476 and isCached(episodeId:) at :3483 are what the library asks. Determine which one returns the wrong answer, and why, for an episode whose file demonstrably exists.

DEVICE STATE NOTE: Dan is leaving the device for a few hours before listening again. The failing state is live NOW — anything needing device evidence should be collected before he taps download again, which would overwrite it.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
DEVICE EVIDENCE 2026-08-13 10:05 (scratchpad/db-pull9), taken while the device is IN the failing state. Three hypotheses are now REFUTED, including both of mine. The disk is healthy; the LOOKUP is not.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE DEVICE — Library/Caches/Playhead/AudioCache/:
    complete/    9 .mp3 + 9 .pin, exactly paired, no orphan of either kind
    partials/    EMPTY
    resumeData/  EMPTY
    attribution/ present
And analysis_assets has 9 rows. Every episode's audio is present.

REFUTED 1 — ForceQuitResumeScan. My leading hypothesis was that rouw's bounded enumeration returns nil on timeout, coalesces to an empty live-task set, and makes the scan emit a phantom resume prompt. That path only walks episodes that HAVE a persisted resume blob. resumeData/ IS EMPTY. There is nothing for that scan to walk, so it cannot be the mechanism. I wrote the hole in that hypothesis into this bead when I filed it and it is exactly the hole that killed it.

REFUTED 2 — iOS Caches eviction. The audio cache lives under Library/Caches, which iOS purges under storage pressure, and I nearly reported that as the cause. It is not: 9 of 9 files are present. (The placement is still worth its own bead — a podcast app's downloaded audio living somewhere the OS may delete without telling anyone is a real design exposure — but it is NOT what Dan is seeing.)

REFUTED 3 — a changed episode-ID hash. The filename is `safeFilename(for:)` = plain SHA-256 of the episodeId (DownloadManager.swift:3022-3025). I recomputed it offline for all 9 episodeIds in analysis_assets and compared against the on-disk names: 9 HIT, 0 MISS, and 0 files on disk belonging to no known episodeId. The lookup KEY is correct. So this is not identity drift, and not a normalization change.

WHAT THAT LEAVES, and it is now a narrow target: the library is reading a DIFFERENT source of truth than the filesystem, and that source is stale. DownloadManager.cachedFileURL(for:) (:3476) is documented (playhead-0hi9, :3509) as FALLING BACK to the .pin sidecar on a cache MISS — which implies an in-memory or SwiftData index consulted FIRST. Find that index, and find what populates it at launch. The bug is almost certainly that it is not being rehydrated, or is rehydrated after the library view reads it.

NEXT STEP FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS: do not re-derive the above. Start at cachedFileURL(for:)/isCached(episodeId:) and answer one question — for an episode whose file demonstrably exists at the correct hash, which read returns the wrong answer, and what is that read consulting? Then ask what changed about its population between 5bcf3e98 and 0a43c6ea (rouw #381 and oa82 #383 are the only two touching this subsystem; the other four cannot be it).

STILL UNEXPLAINED and worth holding onto: why "new on this build". Nothing in the refuted set explains that, so the answer is in whatever populates the index.

title: manual->auto is now reachable by self-certification alone, and its 'high confidence' gate is vacuous
description:
playhead-mn5e gave TrustScoringService.recordSuccessfulObservation its first production caller. That un-freezes skipTrustScore, which is the ONLY thing that was keeping manual->auto out of reach. The auto rung is therefore LIVE as of this branch, not deferred.

TRACE (TrustScoringService.swift):
- update closure L481-482: newObservations = observationCount + 1; newTrust = min(1.0, skipTrustScore + correctObservationBonus[0.10]). averageConfidence is NOT read on the update path -- it is read exactly once, in the create closure (L462-474), on episode one.
- evaluatePromotion L1179-1184: manual->auto iff observations >= 8 AND trustScore >= 0.75 AND recentFalseSignals == 0.

Ordinary new show (avg conf < 0.92): ep1 create trust 0.2 shadow; trust climbs +0.10/episode; ep3 obs=3 trust=0.4 -> MANUAL; ep8 obs=8 trust=0.9 -> AUTO.
Exceptional new show (avg conf >= 0.92): ep1 create trust 0.5 MANUAL; ep8 obs=8 trust=1.0 -> AUTO.

Both reach auto at exactly 8 episodes, with ZERO user gestures. recentFalseSkipSignals==0 is satisfied trivially on a library that was never played.

WHY THE TRUST CLAUSE IS VACUOUS: on the no-gesture path skipTrustScore is a pure function of the episode count -- 0.2 + 0.10*(N-1). Solving trust >= 0.75 gives N >= 6.5, i.e. N >= 7, while the observation clause already demands N >= 8. The trust clause can therefore NEVER be the reason a promotion is withheld. 'obs >= 8 AND trust >= 0.75' is one condition wearing two hats. This is the standing defect class again: skipTrustScore names 'how much we trust this show' but reads as a second copy of observationCount in different units.

Detection confidence of episodes 2..N is discarded entirely, so a show whose every window sits at 0.71 (barely over confirmationThreshold) climbs on the same schedule as one at 0.99.

IT REACHES REAL SKIPS: DetectorTrustLedger.seed (DetectorTrustLedger.swift:180-185) seeds every show-governed detector class with mode: profile.mode verbatim, and SkipOrchestrator.swift:6796/6823 acts on .auto.

Dan's ruling is that self-promotion may go all the way to .auto CONDITIONAL ON HIGH CONFIDENCE. The conditionality is what is missing -- there is no high-confidence quantity in the loop after episode one.

NOT fixed in mn5e (explicitly out of scope: 'do not implement the auto rung').

--- R2 FIX (playhead-mn5e branch, 2026-08-12): the auto rung is CLOSED. ---

Dan's ruling is "it should go all the way to auto IF IT IS HIGH CONFIDENCE". That is a conditional, and this bead's own trace shows the condition is unevaluable: averageConfidence is discarded on the update path, and manualToAutoTrustScore is provably unable to withhold a promotion (trust = 0.2 + 0.10*(N-1) clears at N=7 while the observation clause demands N=8). A conditional whose condition cannot be evaluated is not satisfied, so the rung does not fire.

HOW: AutoPromotionConfidenceEvidence (TrustScoringService.swift, next to TrustScoringConfig) is an enum with exactly one case, .unavailable, carried as TrustScoringConfig.autoPromotionConfidence. BOTH evaluatePromotion siblings — the integer show-level one and the WEIGHTED per-detector one — switch over it in their .manual case. Adding a second case is a compile error at both sites, so the rung reopens only when somebody decides to reopen it. It is deliberately not a Bool or a Double?: either can be flipped without supplying the evidence.

WHY BOTH SIBLINGS. Gating only the show scalar is half a fix. DetectorTrustLedger.seed copies skipTrustScore, observationCount and mode straight from the profile, so a show carried to trust 1.0 / 8 episodes by self-observation would let a single banner Yes materialize an entry at those values and promote that ONE CLASS to .auto — the same unasked skip, reached through SkipOrchestrator's per-detector mode instead of the scalar.

NOT CLOSED: an explicit user override. setUserOverride writes the mode directly and does not go through evaluatePromotion. The ruling is about what the app may conclude on its own, not what the listener may instruct. Pinned by AdDetectionSelfPromotionTests.userOverrideStillReachesAuto.

ALSO NOT CLOSED, and out of scope: SkipDetectorClass.showIndependentSeedMode is .auto, so .rediffByteExact (consultsShowTrust == false) seeds to auto regardless of the ladder. That is playhead-qs0d's day-0 byte-exact mint, deliberate and pre-existing.

MUTATION EVIDENCE. Mutant MA (restore the three legacy clauses in the integer sibling) -> GATE_EXIT=65, 7 tests reddened. Mutant MB (restore them in the weighted sibling only) -> GATE_EXIT=65, 3 tests reddened including "playhead-lqcp: a per-detector entry cannot reach auto either".

WHAT WOULD OPEN IT: playhead-yhfr.
notes:
MEASURED EVIDENCE (R1, independent trace):

The 0.92 first-episode branch fires RARELY, which is good news for episode one and BAD news for the auto rung.

Real production proposalConfidence values, re-derived verbatim from the 2026-08-02 device pull (PlayheadTests/Fixtures/RealEpisodes/DE0784D8MidRollPodFixture.swift:202-232):
  0.6258487465276336 / 0.4884603495736534 / 0.45634516843301726 / 0.5532443308853713 / 0.37888321687686927
Range 0.38-0.63. Nothing close to 0.92.

Structurally, 0.92 is near-unreachable as a per-episode MEAN: every fusionWindows element is stamped confidence: decision.proposalConfidence (AdDetectionService.swift:8960), which is a capped sum of per-source weights (BackfillEvidenceFusion.swift:63-297) whose largest single contributor is lexicalAutoAd at 0.55, explicitly calibrated NOT to saturate (LexicalAutoAdEvidenceBuilder.swift:91-98). Byte-exact rediff contributes ZERO score mass and ships OFF (rediffConfirmedKindEnabled: false, AdDetectionService.swift:1173); its confidence-1.0 marks are minted in mintByteExactDayZeroMarks and never enter fusionWindows. On episode one, cross-episode-memory / catalog / cross-show-syndication are structurally cold, pulling the mean down further.

SO THE REAL EXPOSURE IS NOT EPISODE ONE. It is that a show climbs to .auto at episode 8 on evidence whose per-window detection confidence averages ~0.5, because averageConfidence is discarded on every update after the create. The system's own 'high bar' elsewhere is a 0.7 detector floor (AnalysisStore.swift:405-408). The ladder currently promotes to unasked audio-cutting on a mean that sits well under that floor and is never consulted.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
MEASURED AGAINST THE ACTUAL INSTALLED BASE 2026-08-12 — the residual risk R3 escalated is real in logic and EMPTY in fact, today.

THE RISK AS STATED (mn5e R3): V49 resets podcast_profiles.observationCount but NOT detectorTrustJSON, so a per-detector entry that already reached .auto under the old weighted rung survives the upgrade. 'The auto rung is closed' is therefore a claim about the future, not about installed devices. Reachable pre-mn5e via an inflated counter plus ~3 banner Yeses on a manual show.

WHAT THE DEVICE ACTUALLY CARRIES. From the 2026-08-12 morning pull (build 5bcf3e98, virgin DB from the 08-11 wipe), reading podcast_profiles directly:

  https://feeds.simplecast.com/dHoohVNH          mode=shadow obs=26 trust=0.5  detectorTrustJSON = NULL
  https://rss2.flightcast.com/xmsftuzjjykcmqwola mode=shadow obs=10 trust=0.5  detectorTrustJSON = NULL

detectorTrustJSON is NULL on BOTH shows. There are no per-detector entries at all, so there are none at .auto, so V49 has nothing to fail to demote. The migration's silence on detectorTrustJSON costs nothing on the only device that exists.

WHY THAT IS A WEAKER STATEMENT THAN IT LOOKS, and I would rather say so than have it read as an all-clear:
  - n = ONE device, ONE pull. Pre-release, so 'installed base' is Dan's phone.
  - That phone was WIPED on 08-11, which is the reason the column is NULL. A pre-wipe device could have carried entries; the pre-wipe pull (db-prewipe6) was not checked for this and could be.
  - It is a fact about TODAY. The window reopens the moment a device accumulates per-detector entries under the old rung — which cannot happen once mn5e ships, but can happen on any build between now and then.

CONSEQUENCE: this does not need a decision from Dan before mn5e merges, and it should not block it. If a demotion pass is ever wanted it is cheap to add later precisely BECAUSE the column is empty — there is no user-witnessed state to weigh against, which is the argument that made it 'arguably right' to leave alone.

RELATED AND NEWLY TRUE: mn5e R3 found that TrustScoringService.materialized() PERSISTS the .rediffByteExact .auto seed into detectorTrustJSON on the first banner Yes. Same value the derived read already returned, so no behaviour change — but combined with the NULL above it means devices will start carrying a literal "auto" string in this column for the FIRST TIME after mn5e ships. R4 is attacking whether any reader distinguishes a persisted "auto" from a derived one.

title: [bug] EVERY ad window on the device is markOnly at WRITE time — promoting a show to auto changes nothing, because markOnly never reaches the trust gate
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 while implementing playhead-mn5e (self-promotion out of shadow).

THE OBSERVABLE mn5e was filed against is 'zero auto-skips'. mn5e's diagnosis — the trust ladder has no production caller — is CORRECT and is now fixed. But it is NOT sufficient, and the measurement says so.

DEVICE DATA (scratchpad/db-morning7, 45 ad_windows across 4 assets, 2 shows):

  eligibilityGate  wasSkipped   n
  markOnly                  0  45      <- ALL of them

  detectorVersion      decisionState   n   minConf  maxConf
  detection-v1         confirmed      17      0.50     1.00
  semantic-sweep-v1    candidate      24      0.70     0.70
  pod-continuation-v1  candidate       4      0.70     0.70

db-overnight5 and db-prewipe6: 31/31 markOnly, wasSkipped=0. Across every pull that carries the table, ad_windows has taken exactly ONE eligibilityGate value.

WHY THIS DEFEATS THE TRUST LADDER. SkipOrchestrator.receiveAdWindows (SkipOrchestrator.swift:3064-3113) routes a markOnly row to the SUGGEST tier and `continue`s — before evaluateWindow is ever called. The trust-mode switch that consults shadow/manual/auto lives at SkipOrchestrator.swift:6814-6845, downstream of that continue. So a markOnly window never reaches the mode gate AT ALL. Promoting both device shows to .auto would produce ZERO additional auto-skips on the current window population.

WORSE, 28 OF THE 45 CAN NEVER AUTO-SKIP. semantic-sweep-v1 (24) and pod-continuation-v1 (4) are stamped by composers that HARD-CODE the value:
  SemanticSweepMarkComposer.swift:869 — "ALWAYS markOnly — a hard-coded literal, never a policy switch"
  AdPodContinuation.swift:1156 — same shape
Those two composers are 62% of the device's windows and no trust state can ever admit them.

THE REMAINING QUESTION, which is what this bead is for: the 17 detection-v1 rows are decisionState=confirmed with confidence up to 1.00, skipConfidence up to 1.00, and BOTH edge anchors present — and they are still markOnly. That is either AutoSkipPrecisionGate returning .uiCandidate (score >= autoSkipThreshold 0.55 but NO non-catalog safety signal fired, or duration implausible), the fl4j self-promo demotion (AdDetectionService.swift:5505-5519), or a fusion gate. The persisted row does not record WHICH — MarkOnlyReason is computed and dropped. Establish which one fires, on how many, before tuning anything.

RELATED SHAPE: the persisted state cannot distinguish the routes into markOnly, exactly as podcast_profiles.mode cannot distinguish the three routes into shadow (mn5e comment 1). Same defect class, one layer down.

DO NOT read this as "mn5e was wrong". Both gates are real and BOTH must open. mn5e opened the one that had no caller at all.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
PREMISE CORRECTED AND THE QUESTION ANSWERED 2026-08-12, read-only from the device DB plus source. This bead's open question was 'which gate fires on the 17 detection-v1 rows'. It is none of the three it lists, and the reason is a factual error in the description.

THE DESCRIPTION SAYS the 17 detection-v1 rows have 'BOTH edge anchors present'. THEY DO NOT. Reading startEdgeAnchor/endEdgeAnchor off db-morning7 for all 17:

  startEdgeAnchor = unanchored   17 of 17   <- EVERY ONE
  endEdgeAnchor   = unanchored   12 of 17
  endEdgeAnchor   = stingerSnapped 5 of 17

Not one window on the device has an anchored START edge. So the three hypotheses this bead asks somebody to distinguish (AutoSkipPrecisionGate .uiCandidate, the fl4j self-promo demotion, a fusion gate) do not need distinguishing — playhead-2350's unanchored-edge block explains all 17 on its own, and it is ARMED: AdDetectionService.swift:1187, 'unanchoredExtentBlocksAutoSkip: true, // playhead-2350: SAFETY gate ships ON — a span with an invented (unanchored) start or end edge is banner-only, never auto-skip.'

THIS IS THE GATE WORKING, NOT FAILING. SpanExtentSupport.swift's header is explicit about what it is defending against: the 2026-07-25 THEMOVE replay where fusion attached correct presence evidence to narrow lexical seeds, every edge was .unanchored, and every window was auto-skip eligible anyway — one seed starting 12.72 s inside the host's sign-off. 'A span with strong presence evidence and invented edges is a BANNER, never a skip.' Confidence 1.00 and skipConfidence 1.00 are PRESENCE. The block is about EXTENT. Reading the confidence column as though it licensed a skip is the same defect class this repo keeps hitting.

SO THE REAL QUESTION IS THE OPPOSITE ONE: why does no window ever earn a START anchor? AutoSkipEdgeAnchor has exactly three cases (AutoSkipEdgePadding.swift:135-145) — .rediffByteExact, .stingerSnapped, .unanchored — so there are only two producers:

  1. REDIFF. AdDetectionService.swift:12196, 'let anchor: AutoSkipEdgeAnchor = strict ? .rediffByteExact : .unanchored', and a strict slot anchors BOTH edges (DayZeroMarkCensus.swift:193-194 checks startAnchor == .rediffByteExact && endAnchor == .rediffByteExact). The device has ZERO rediff windows, because day-0 never ran at all — that is playhead-oa82.
  2. THE STINGER REFINER. SpanExtentSupport.swift:167/171 derive the two anchors from stingerTrace?.startSnapped and ?.endSnapped, so it CAN snap a start. On this device it snapped 5 END edges and 0 START edges.

THEREFORE oa82 AND mqqd ARE THE SAME BLOCKAGE, and this is the part worth acting on. Rediff is the only producer that reliably anchors a start edge; it produces nothing because day-0 never fires; so every window is unanchored-start; so 2350 makes every window markOnly; so the row never reaches the trust gate; so mn5e's ladder cannot change anything. Fixing oa82 does not merely add rediff windows — it supplies the ONLY anchor kind that gets a span past the safety gate, and .rediffByteExact is exactly the class Dan ruled 'should always be auto'.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS STILL FOR, unchanged and still P0: the 28 hard-coded rows. SemanticSweepMarkComposer.swift:869 and AdPodContinuation.swift:1156 stamp markOnly as a literal, 62% of the device's windows, admissible by no trust state and no anchor. That half of the bead stands exactly as written.

ONE MORE 'COMPUTED AND DROPPED', in this bead's own shape: evidenceSources is NULL on all 17 rows. The column exists and nothing writes it, so which signals fired is unrecoverable from the persisted row — the same complaint this bead makes about MarkOnlyReason.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-13 on bead/playhead-mqqd @ 1b3e5f42 (not merged, no PR).

DECISION: the 28 stay markOnly, and now BY DERIVATION. Not a promotion — both producers were right to be mark-only and the reasons are now in code where a measurement can revisit them, per the two `extentSupport` doc comments.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY BROKEN. Not the value. The row carried its stamp and its own evidence as THREE INDEPENDENT LITERALS — `eligibilityGate`, `startEdgeAnchor`, `endEdgeAnchor` — with nothing enforcing that they agreed. `makeMark` now derives one `SpanExtentSupport`, writes it to both anchor columns, and hands the SAME value to a new `ComposedMarkGate.eligibility(for:)`. One variable used twice (playhead-6qvf), not two expressions that happen to agree.

AND A COVERAGE HOLE NOBODY HAD NAMED: composed marks are a THIRD producer of `ad_windows` covered by NEITHER half of playhead-2350. `DecisionResult.withExtentSupport` runs in `runBackfill`'s FUSION loop; `HotPathExtentGate` runs at the two HOT-PATH sites; `compose(…)` returns finished `AdWindow`s that `AdDetectionService` persists directly.

MEASURED what that hole was worth (mutant M3): set the rule to a bare `.eligible`, leave BOTH anchors `.unanchored` — the exact shape 2350 exists to demote — and drive the real `SkipOrchestrator` in `auto` at trust 0.95: both marks reached the MANAGED tier and were SKIPPED (`bannerTier == .suggest` failed AND `!wasSkipped` failed). An unanchored `semanticSweepMark`/`podContinuation` row classifies `.fusion`, and in a trusted show `.fusion` is `.auto`. The literal was the ONLY thing between these 28 rows and a silent cut.

THE RULE: `.eligible` iff `SpanExtentSupport.tier == .deterministic` (byte-exact on BOTH edges) — the same predicate `SkipDetectorClass.classify` uses to name `.rediffByteExact`. Deliberately STRICTER than 2350's `isFullyAnchored` (which admits a stinger snap), and pinned one-directional so it can only ever admit less. Deliberately NOT keyed on `unanchoredExtentBlocksAutoSkip`: that flag restores pre-2350 behaviour for gates that DEMOTE somebody else's label, and a composed mark has none to restore — keying it there would make the kill switch PROMOTE 62 % of the device's rows.

WHY A CONTINUATION MUST NOT INHERIT A NEIGHBOUR'S BYTE-EXACT EDGE — worth reading before playhead-oa82 lands, because the inheritance looks free. A residue is bounded by an adjacent visible window's edge, and oa82 will start putting `.rediffByteExact` there. title: [bug] a day-0 claim that FAILS TO WRITE is indistinguishable from a kickoff that was never requested — both writers to rediff_day_zero_kickoffs are try?
description:
ESTABLISHED 2026-08-12 by a read-only diagnosis of the morning pull (build 5bcf3e98, virgin DB, 4 episodes). The mechanism behind ZERO day-0 kickoffs could NOT be determined, and this bead is why.

THE OBSERVATION. rediff_day_zero_kickoffs = 0 rows, rediff_day_zero_attempts = 0, rediff_refetch_state = 0, rediff_bandwidth_ledger = 0. Nothing in the rediff subsystem ran. playhead-kg8h shipped in this exact build (verified: 'await claimKickoff(' at RediffDayZeroKickoffCoordinator.swift:170 in 5bcf3e98) and writes a durable claim at REQUEST time, before the queue and before any readiness work. So zero rows should mean requestKickoff was never called.

WHY THAT INFERENCE DOES NOT HOLD, and this is the defect: BOTH writers to this table are 'try?' — claimKickoff at PlayheadRuntime.swift:5587 and recordKickoff at :1788. A claim write that throws is swallowed silently. So 'the claim failed to write' and 'requestKickoff never ran' produce a BYTE-IDENTICAL database. The ledger built to make a lost kickoff visible has a silent total-failure mode of its own, and it is the only ledger whose complete absence is unexplainable.

WHAT WAS RULED OUT ON EVIDENCE (file:line, not inference). The device build and main are BYTE-IDENTICAL for the seven files carrying this logic, verified by blob hash rather than --stat.
  - HOW THE EPISODES ARRIVED: AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:1157 sets priority = userInitiated ? 20 : (isExplicitDownload ? 10 : 0). F4A9D2BD is priority 20 (the Download & Analyze control); the other three are priority 10 (a plain Download tap whose completion ran enqueueAnalysisIfNeeded). None is priority 0.
  - playhead-zmog (streaming-play) OUT: progressiveDownload has no production caller, and prepare()'s download branch passes isExplicitDownload:false, so a streaming enqueue cannot yield priority 10.
  - playhead-m8rq (scene-only auto-download) OUT: an auto-download yields priority 0; none of the four is 0.
  - playhead-cnql OUT for this population: all four enqueued 14:58:17-15:49:53 and the first background_task_runs row is 15:49:52, so they landed in the INITIAL FOREGROUND SESSION where .task had certainly run. Buffering also works — completions that beat the observer are buffered (DownloadManager.swift:4208) and drained on install (:4190-4194).
  - playhead-jra6 OUT: kg8h claims at :170, before pending.append at :175.
  - THE NIL-CHAIN IS RULED OUT BY THE DATABASE ITSELF: episode_fingerprints has 4 rows, so rediffActivationOn was true, so the staging provider (non-failable init), rediffRefetchService, dayZeroRediffTrigger and dayZeroKickoffCoordinator were all non-nil.
  - SCHEMA MISMATCH OUT: the device build's claim INSERT names exactly the nine columns present in the device table, and no DELETE FROM rediff_day_zero_kickoffs exists anywhere.

TWO SURVIVING HYPOTHESES, INDISTINGUISHABLE IN THE DATA:
  H1 the claim write THREW at runtime (SQLITE_BUSY, wedged store actor) and was swallowed by try?.
  H2 requestKickoff genuinely never ran, because one of two async hops never executed — the observer's Task {} (PlayheadRuntime.swift:5539) or the tap's Task.detached (:3957).

EVIDENCE GATHERED SINCE, WEAKENING H1 BUT NOT KILLING IT: I pulled Library/Application Support/Diagnostics/analysis-store-health.json off the device. It reads status=healthy, consecutive_failure_count=0, recent_failures=[], quarantines=[], last_success_at 2026-08-12T09:24:01Z. That is weak evidence against a wedged store — weak because the claim writes are swallowed at the CALL SITE, so a throw may never reach the health tracker at all. Do not treat it as conclusive.
ALSO PULLED: Documents/bg-task-log.jsonl (51 KB). It contains ONLY BGTask lifecycle events (submit 71, start 64, complete 60, expire 40, appPhase 8) — ZERO matches for rediff/kickoff/dayZero. So the on-device logs cannot settle this either.

THE FIX THIS BEAD WANTS, and it is small: give the CLAIM write a failure path that records somewhere OTHER than rediff_day_zero_kickoffs. The coordinator already has reportViolation wired to the surface-status invariant log. That single change separates H1 from H2 on the next pull. Do NOT simply change try? to try — the call sites are in Task {} / Task.detached contexts on the completion path and a throw there is its own hazard; the point is to RECORD, not to propagate.

SECOND, CHEAPER HALF: the diagnostics that would have settled this were not captured because the pull takes only analysis.sqlite. Whatever surface reportViolation writes to should be part of the standard pull, and playhead-njkw (the kickoff ledger reaches no diagnostics bundle) is the neighbouring bead.

playhead-fzrw DOES NOT CHANGE THIS, stated explicitly because it is the obvious thing to hope: fzrw makes the readiness probe's .awaitingAnalysisAsset leg succeed once a kickoff is REQUESTED. Zero rows means the readiness wait never started. fzrw is upstream-irrelevant to this failure.

    if rediffASideCaptureEnabled || EpisodeFingerprintCapture.captureEnabledByDefault {

THE REST OF THE CHAIN, each link checked at file:line rather than inferred:

  - rediffRefetchService non-nil: 'if rediffActivationOn, let rediffBSideStagingProvider' (:1580).

So the coordinator WAS non-nil. There is no H3. The two hypotheses stand.

BUT H2 UNDERCOUNTS THE ASYNC HOPS: it names two (the observer's Task {} at :5539, the tap's Task.detached at :3957). There is a THIRD, and it is the one cnql added for exactly this failure — PlayheadRuntime.swift:3116-3126:

    if let dayZeroKickoffCoordinator {

CORRECTION AND SHARPENING of the comment above, after reading the two request paths end to end.

WRONG IN MY PREVIOUS COMMENT: 'the fix should carry WHICH install path requested the kickoff'. That work already exists. RediffDayZeroKickoffSource (RediffDayZeroKickoff.swift:55-63) has exactly two cases — downloadAndAnalyzeTap and backgroundDownload — and requestDayZeroKickoff (PlayheadRuntime.swift:3943) takes source as a parameter, so a claim that LANDS already names its path. WHAT IS ACTUALLY UNINSTRUMENTED, which is a different and better target. The two paths are not symmetric in how many un-awaited hops stand between the download and the claim:

  TAP PATH: requestDayZeroKickoff -> 'guard let coordinator' (synchronous) -> Task.detached { requestKickoff }. ONE hop.

  BACKGROUND PATH: init's 'Task { installDayZeroBackgroundDownloadKickoff(...) }' (:3116-3126) -> 'await downloads.setBackgroundDownloadCompletionObserver { ... }' (:5535) -> the observer closure -> an INNER 'Task {}' (:5539) -> requestKickoff. THREE hops, and the first two are an INSTALL that must complete before the claim can ever be reached.

That asymmetry is the gap. If the background observer was never installed — 3116's Task {} never scheduled, or the await at :5535 never returned — then no claim is attempted, no source is recorded, and the database is byte-identical to H1 (claim threw) and to H2 (hop didn't run). The source enum cannot help, because a path that never requested anything writes nothing to carry a source ON.

SO THE INSTRUMENTATION THIS BEAD WANTS IS TWO THINGS, NOT ONE:
  (a) the failure path on the claim write, as the description says — makeDayZeroKickoffClaimRecorder (:5583-5593) is 'try? await store.noteRediffDayZeroKickoffClaim(...)' with no else. It is a static factory taking only 'store', so reportViolation has to be threaded in; that is the whole change.
  (b) a record that the BACKGROUND OBSERVER WAS INSTALLED — one line after the await at :5535. Without it, 'the observer was never installed' stays indistinguishable from both surviving hypotheses, and it is the leg with the most hops in front of it.

Note (a) alone does NOT separate H1 from H2 for the background population, which is 3 of the 4 assets in this pull (priority 10). It separates them only for a path that actually reached the claim.

WHAT IS NOT A CONCERN, checked so nobody re-checks it: a completion that beats the observer is buffered (DownloadManager.swift:4208) and drained on install (:4190-4194). And :5498's 'guard dayZeroKickoffCoordinator != nil' is NOT a third request path — it is the SwiftData facts-box attachment (cnql), an enrichment of an already-requested kickoff.

comments.text:
THIS BEAD IS THE ANCHOR SUPPLY, NOT JUST THE REDIFF LANE — established 2026-08-12 while preparing playhead-mqqd, and it raises this bead's value considerably.

Every ad window on the device is markOnly, so mn5e's trust ladder is never consulted. The cause is NOT a precision threshold. All 17 detection-v1 rows carry startEdgeAnchor = unanchored (17 of 17), and playhead-2350's safety gate — armed, AdDetectionService.swift:1187 — makes any span with an invented start or end edge banner-only by construction.

AutoSkipEdgeAnchor has exactly three cases, so only two things can anchor an edge: the stinger refiner and rediff. On this device the stinger refiner snapped 5 END edges and 0 START edges. Rediff anchors BOTH edges .rediffByteExact on a strict slot (AdDetectionService.swift:12196; DayZeroMarkCensus.swift:193-194) — and rediff produced nothing, because day-0 never fired. That is this bead.

So the chain is: no day-0 kickoff -> no rediff window -> no .rediffByteExact anchor -> every span unanchored at the start -> 2350 blocks auto-skip -> markOnly -> the trust gate is never reached -> zero auto-skips.

Fixing this bead is therefore the only route that supplies the anchor kind capable of passing the safety gate, and .rediffByteExact is precisely the class Dan ruled 'incredibly high confidence, it should always be auto' (2026-08-12, implemented in playhead-mn5e / playhead-u0vv as a restorable floor). Every other lane's spans are stopped one layer earlier by a gate that is doing its job.

comments.text:
R1 ADVERSARIAL REVIEW — 2026-08-13. ZERO PRODUCTION DEFECTS. One survived mutant, closed with a rail. Two beads filed (playhead-lvju P1, playhead-1t0b P2).

=== JOB 1: THE WITNESS CHAIN HOLDS, BUT THE INFERENCE DRAWN FROM IT IS ONE LINK TOO STRONG ===

Every link re-verified at file:line in THIS worktree (line numbers moved: the diff adds ~160 lines to PlayheadRuntime, so the description's :3872/:3879/:3957 are now :3916/:3923/:4001).

  L1 SOLE WRITER — HOLDS. `pendingUserIntentEpisodes` (AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:1066) has exactly one `.insert`, at :1648 inside `markEpisodeUserIntent` (:1647). The only other mutations are removals (:1296, :1618) and the read at :1156. Six occurrences repo-wide, all in that one file.
  L1b PRIORITY 20 IS UNFORGEABLE ELSEWHERE — HOLDS, and this was NOT checked before. `let priority = userInitiated ? 20 : (isExplicitDownload ? 10 : 0)` (:1157) is one route; `promoteExistingJobToUserIntentLane` (:1271) is the other, and it is gated `if !inserted, userInitiated` — also set membership. The only other priority mutator in the app is ScarcityReprioritizer, whose `soonPromotionCeiling = 9` is documented as deliberately BELOW 10 and 20 (ScarcityReprioritizer.swift:97-104). So a p20 row cannot arrive by promotion.
  L2 SOLE REACHER — HOLDS. Production callers of `markEpisodeUserIntent`: `SchedulerPreparationAdapter.markUserIntent` (EpisodePreparationCoordinator.swift:279) and `enqueueUserIntentAnalysis` (AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:1678). Both are reached only from `EpisodePreparationCoordinator.prepare` (:158-222) — `analysis.markUserIntent` at :177 and :197, `analysis.enqueueUserIntent` at :164. No other conformer to the protocol exists in production.
  L3 SOLE CALLER — HOLDS. `episodePreparationCoordinator.prepare(request)` occurs exactly once in production, PlayheadRuntime.swift:3916. The coordinator is constructed once, :1931. (Tests aside, as stipulated.)
  L4 UNCONDITIONAL NEXT STATEMENT — HOLDS. :3916 `let outcome = await …prepare(request)` then :3923 `kickOffDayZeroRediffForPreparation(...)`. No guard, no if, no early return between.

SO THE CHAIN HOLDS. WHAT DOES NOT IS THE SENTENCE "prepareEpisodeForAnalysis demonstrably ran, the next unconditional statement executed, and NOTHING was written."

A p20 row witnesses that control reached `markEpisodeUserIntent` INSIDE `prepare`. The kickoff fires only after `prepare` RETURNS, and there are further awaits in between:
  * NOT-CACHED branch: `await downloads.startDownload(…)` (EpisodePreparationCoordinator.swift:210) into the DownloadManager actor;
  * CACHED branch: the entire remainder of `AnalysisWorkScheduler.enqueue` after the insert (title writes :1306-1315, the download-time asset registration) before `enqueue` returns.

So a FOURTH state survives for the tap path, and the reading guide should carry it:
  (d) `prepare` NEVER RETURNED — the same park class as (b), one frame further out, and equally invisible: no attempted line, no failure line, nothing.

"no attempted line at all -> (c) the hop" should read "-> (c) the hop OR (d) prepare did not return".

HOW LIVE (d) IS DEPENDS ON WHICH BRANCH F4A9D2BD TOOK, and the DB can say. In the not-cached branch the p20 row is minted by the DOWNLOAD-COMPLETION enqueue long after `prepare` returned, so (d) is close to excluded. In the cached branch the row is minted mid-`enqueue` with real await surface still ahead of the return, so (d) is fully live. Check `analysis_jobs.createdAt` for the p20 row against the download's completion time before planning the next pull around three states.

L5 — A SILENT GUARD THAT IS GENUINELY COVERED, stated so nobody re-raises it. `requestDayZeroKickoff` opens `guard let coordinator = dayZeroKickoffCoordinator else { return }` (PlayheadRuntime.swift:3993) with no instrument. That is sound HERE only because `dayZeroKickoffCoordinator` is a `let` (:135) assigned exactly once in `init` (:1761 or :1826), so nil-at-tap is the same fact as nil-at-launch and the new `rediff_day_zero_kickoff_coordinator_absent` line covers it. Make that property a `var` and the guard becomes a hole again.

=== JOB 2: WILL THE EVIDENCE SURVIVE TO A PULL HOURS LATER? YES — WITH THREE CAVEATS, TWO OF THEM NEW ===

ROTATION/FLUSH, the direct answer. Files are PER SESSION, not per size and not per day: one file per logger instance (one per app process), named `surface-status-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<sessionId>.jsonl`, created lazily on the session's FIRST write (SurfaceStatusInvariantLogger.swift:526-550). Retention is `maxSessionFiles = 200` (:82), evicted newest-first by filename on the first write of each session (:557-578). There is NO size cap and NO per-file truncation, so within a retained file every line survives. Writes are `FileHandle.write(contentsOf:)` — an unbuffered write(2) — so once the queue runs the bytes are in the page cache and survive app termination without any fsync. `synchronizeFile` is test-only (:604-608). A pull hours later WILL contain the moment.

CAVEAT 1 (NEW, AND CAUSED BY THIS DIFF): the window is now literally "the last 200 LAUNCHES". Before oa82 a session that logged nothing created no file; a scene-less BGTask relaunch with no anomaly consumed no slot. oa82 writes on EVERY non-preview launch (`observer_installed` or `coordinator_absent`), so every launch takes one of the 200. At the 08-12 log's ~64 BGTask starts that is days, not weeks. Filed as playhead-1t0b.
CAVEAT 2: the directory is `Library/Caches`, which iOS evicts under disk pressure — and the repo already says so, in StabilityDiagnosticsStore.swift:31, which chose Application Support for exactly this reason. Also playhead-1t0b.
CAVEAT 3: "written" means ENQUEUED. `enqueueSyntheticViolation` is `writeQueue.async` at .utility QoS (:473-497) and `writeLocked`'s catch is empty (:508-522). A process killed before the queue drains, or an I/O failure, loses the line with no trace. So "no attempted line" already had three meanings before state (d) was added.

THE HASHER — IT DOES OBSCURE IDENTITY, AND THE BEAD'S OWN PULL RECIPE MAKES IT WORSE. `episode_id_hash` is SHA-256(installID || episodeId) with the salt at `Caches/Diagnostics/.surface-status-install-id` (:640-652). `DogfoodDiagnosticsArchive` excludes it by design — "no raw episode IDs, and no install-ID salt" (DiagnosticsExportService.swift:491-494) — and its filter is `hasPrefix("surface-status-")` (:945-948), which excludes the dotfile structurally. THE RECIPE IN THIS BEAD ("pull Library/Caches/Diagnostics/surface-status-*.jsonl") MISSES IT FOR THE SAME REASON. Pull the whole DIRECTORY, or the tap-path lines cannot be tied to F4A9D2BD — only counted. Filed as playhead-lvju (P1).
Two smaller shape notes for whoever writes the reader: the hash lands in the free-text `description`, not in the structured field — `enqueueSyntheticViolation` passes `episodeIdHash: nil` (:483) — and every synthetic violation is stamped `newDisposition: .failed` / `newReason: .couldntAnalyze` (:485-487), including the three healthy-by-design codes. Pre-existing shape (the `adWindowIngestCensus` precedent, SurfaceStatusInvariants.swift:451) but oa82 triples the always-on volume on it.

THE DRAINED COUNT — MEANS WHAT IT SAYS, BUT NOT WHAT THE DOC COMMENT CLAIMS. `return backlog.count` is captured before a synchronous, non-throwing replay loop (DownloadManager.swift:4336-4344), so it cannot read 0 because "draining failed" — that specific fear is unfounded. But the buffer it reads is deduped by episodeId and CAPPED at 64 with eviction (:4361-4371, `maxPendingBackgroundDownloadCompletions` :539), and evictions go to os_log, not to this stream. So `drained 0` honestly means "the buffer was EMPTY at install", not "the install got there first" as :4327-4330 says. Unreachable at four episodes; worth stating so the number is never read as a race verdict.

=== JOB 3: THE GATE ===

One clean full-plan run, `scripts/fast-gate.sh`, simulator erased first, nothing else on the box. VERBATIM:

  gate-baseline: RED (66 known / 15 NEW) — 3 tests got NO VERDICT (crashed host)
    NO VERDICT — 3 test(s) started and then reported neither pass, fail nor skip.
    HOST RESTART     xcodebuild restarted the test host 1 time(s)
    NOT RECORDED     this baseline has never recorded a crashed-host census, so the arm below is INERT
    NO VERDICT       swift-testing::a retry that makes progress does not spend the retry budget
    NO VERDICT       swift-testing::an unplayed long episode is transcribed end to end, and the ladder stops
    NO VERDICT       swift-testing::negative upper bound → zero
    BLAMED, UNMATCHED DrainEligibleStartGateTests.aboveFloorStillDispatches()
  exit 65.

ATTRIBUTION, and it is not hand-waving. All 15 NEW are `Time limit was exceeded: 60.000 seconds` at 183-202 s wall clock — the starvation signature, not an assertion. The run logged 96 timeouts in total across the known load-sensitive families (BackgroundGrantBudget 12, SilenceCompressionCoordinator 10, PlaybackInterruption 10, BackgroundProcessingService 10, RouteChange 4, InterruptionHandling 4, pipeline-stall 4 …) and restarted the host once. Every suite named in the 15 is untouched by a diff that adds logging calls, one return value and five enum cases.

I then re-ran ALL of them selectively (exempt from the baseline check, so the raw xcodebuild verdict passes through): AnalysisWorkSchedulerLaneGateRegression, ShadowRetry, AnalysisJobRunnerSubscribeBeforeStart, LanePreemptionCoordinator, DrainEligibleStartGate, ExpiredWindowAttemptAccounting, IncrementalShardAppend, BackfillSchedulerBounding + this bead's four suites — **74 tests in 11 suites passed after 4.380 seconds, ** TEST SUCCEEDED **, exit 0**. Every NEW name passes in 4 s in isolation and blows a 60 s limit under the full plan's own concurrency. Same verdict the implementer reached, obtained independently on a full run.

The baseline file was NOT refreshed and is byte-identical to main (sha 4d300374…). No PLAYHEAD_SKIP_* was used.

=== JOB 4: BEHAVIOUR NEUTRALITY — CONFIRMED, WITH ONE MEASURED WIDENING ===

  * `try?` -> `do/catch` in `makeDayZeroKickoffClaimRecorder` is semantically identical for throws. Nothing new can throw; the recorder still returns normally on error, so no throw escapes into the `Task {}` / `Task.detached` contexts. NEUTRAL.
  * THE DEDUPE INVARIANT SURVIVES, and this was the one that mattered. The new `await reportViolation` sits INSIDE `claimKickoff`, i.e. after `RediffDayZeroKickoffCoordinator.requestKickoff`'s synchronous `fired` / `inFlight` guards and `inFlight.insert` (:167-169). A concurrent duplicate is still rejected while the claim is in flight, exactly as :139-142 promises. What it DOES do is widen the `inFlight.insert` -> `pending.append` window — the ACCEPTED RESIDUE at :147-165 — by one async-closure call. Negligible against a store write, but it is an enlargement of a documented hazard and should be named rather than discovered later.
  * `setBackgroundDownloadCompletionObserver` `()` -> `Int` with `@discardableResult`: one production caller (PlayheadRuntime.swift:5602) and it consumes the value. No other production caller exists. NEUTRAL.
  * The observer's new report is in the mutually-exclusive `else` arm after the existing `guard`; `coordinator.requestKickoff` is unreached there exactly as before. The install line is written AFTER the await returns, so it cannot delay the install. NEUTRAL.
  * NIT, not a defect: `} else if !isPreviewRuntime {` (PlayheadRuntime.swift:3151) is DEAD as a condition — `guard !isPreviewRuntime else { return }` at :3047 sits in the same `init` body scope and precedes it, so the test is always true. The comment "Suppressed in previews" describes a suppression a different mechanism already provides; a later reader could delete the :3047 guard believing :3151 covers previews.
  * Note, not a finding: `hashEpisodeId` is `writeQueue.sync` (:594-600) — a blocking hop off a cooperative thread, with disk I/O on the very first call — and it is now on the claim path. The same hasher was already passed to the coordinator's give-up path, and `migrate()` warms the salt from the deferred init Task, so this is a pre-existing pattern rather than something oa82 introduced.

=== MUTANT M1 — SURVIVED, THEN CLOSED ===

The bead's central design claim is that the instrument is a PAIR because a store write can PARK, and only a line written BEFORE the call survives that. No test pinned it.

M1 keeps the write inline at closure depth 1 (so `testDayZeroKickoffClaimRecorderAwaitsItsWriteInline` stays green) and preserves the emitted code SEQUENCE in both directions — `[.attempted]` on success, `[.attempted, .writeFailed]` on a throw — by capturing the outcome first and reporting afterwards:

    var thrown: Error?
    do { try await store.noteRediffDayZeroKickoffClaim(…) } catch { thrown = error }
    await reportViolation(.rediffDayZeroKickoffClaimAttempted, …)
    if let thrown { await reportViolation(.rediffDayZeroKickoffClaimWriteFailed, …) }

Under it a PARKED write emits nothing at all — state (b) is silently deleted and the ambiguity this bead exists to remove is restored.

  M1 vs the shipped suite:  ** TEST SUCCEEDED **, 10 Swift Testing tests in 3 suites + 5 canaries, exit 0.  SURVIVED.
  M1 vs the new rail:       ** TEST FAILED **, exit 65, `testDayZeroKickoffClaimAttemptIsRecordedBeforeTheStoreWrite` alone failing ("471[utf8] is not less than 172[utf8]"), the other 5 canaries and all 10 Swift Testing tests still green.  KILLED, and specifically.
  CLEAN CONTROL after revert: ** TEST SUCCEEDED **, 6 canaries + 10 Swift Testing tests, exit 0.

The rail is TEXTUAL for the reason its sibling above it is: `makeDayZeroKickoffClaimRecorder` takes a concrete `AnalysisStore`, so there is no seam through which a parking store could be injected and no behavioural test can reach the property. It carries two anti-vacuity assertions (both the attempt code and the store write must be present; the attempt code must occur exactly once, so a second occurrence cannot satisfy the ordering while the reachable one does not).

Production files verified byte-exact against their pre-mutation SHA-256 after every revert; `git status --porcelain -- Playhead PlayheadTests scripts` clean apart from the intended test edit. `scripts/lint.sh` clean.

=== VERDICT ===
ZERO PRODUCTION DEFECTS. The instrumentation is behaviour-neutral, the five codes are well chosen, and the attempt/failure PAIR is the right call — I endorse it and did not touch it. One test gap (the pair's load-bearing ordering was unpinned) found by mutation and closed. Two evidence-reach beads filed. One correction to the diagnosis: add state (d) to the reading guide, and pull the DIRECTORY, not the glob.

title: 9s6q segment recovery reports a DROPPED run's audio as divergent — a day-0 banner can be up to 470 s of pure show
description:
MEASURED IN playhead-pyq7 (2026-08-11), with the production aligner over synthetic A/B pairs carrying exact gold. Rails live in PlayheadTests/Services/AdDetection/RediffRefetch/RediffSegmentRecoveryBoundaryMeasurementTests.swift (families A/B/D).

THE MECHANISM. RediffByteAligner.segmentDivergentSlots builds its accepted run set greedily in A order and drops any run that A-overlaps one already accepted (`if run.aStart < globalAEnd { continue }`, RediffByteAligner.swift:693). It then reports every inter-run A-gap as a divergent slot. A dropped run's A-span is therefore reported as DIVERGENT even though those bytes are byte-identical in the fresh copy.

WHEN IT FIRES. Every synthetic frame of a CBR MP3 carries the same 4-byte frame header, so a run's greedy byte extension always bleeds 4 bytes past a splice. When the FRESH copy has a break the PLAYED copy does not (inserted_in_B — a break-count disagreement, which is exactly the population 9s6q was built for), that bleed makes the following run A-overlap the preceding one, and the whole following content block is dropped and reported as one ad.

MEASURED NUMBERS.
  * 7 phantom slots emitted across the sweep, widths 120.01 / 240.01 / 240.01 / 299.99 / 359.99 / 420.00 / 469.99 s. Every one is 100% show: gold ad seconds inside = 0.
  * The ONLY guard is RediffSlotOwnership.Configuration.maxSlotSeconds (480 s). Measured boundary: tails of 120/240/360/420/470 s are ACCEPTED; 540/720 s are rejected. The widest shippable pure-show phantom measured 469.99 s.
  * The fused case is worse and is the one no reviewer would catch by eye: D/inserted+removed emits ONE slot 299.9905..629.9690 that contains a genuine 30 s ad AND 299.99 s of show, i.e. an inner start edge 300 s early.
  * On a GENUINE divergence the same arm is exact: inner-edge deltas p50 +0.0002 s, p95 +0.0003 s, max +0.0003 s, and the sign always leaves ad rather than eating show. The defect is not edge drift; it is a whole-block false positive.

CURRENT PRODUCTION IMPACT (not a skip, yet). The mint writes these rows eligibilityGate=markOnly with both edges .unanchored, and a banner Yes is governed by AutoSkipEdgePadding (playhead-ynmk), whose startMargin(.unanchored) returns nil, so the skip is suppressed. What ships today is a confidence 1.00 banner with boundaryState=dayZeroRediffByteExact over up to 470 s of show. That is also the standing defect class: a name asserting byte-exactness on a span the aligner's own run set proves is PRESENT in the B copy.

PROPOSED FIX (measured, not guessed). A gold-free precondition already validated in the pyq7 sweep: for every emitted segmented slot, the A-seconds covered by any FOUND run must be zero. Measured over 20 slots, that quantity never under-reported eaten show (0 misses) and equalled it exactly on all 7 phantoms — total eaten 2450.00 s, total aligned-inside 2450.00 s. Implementation shape: have segmentDivergentSlots carry the dropped runs (or the found-run set) far enough to subtract them, and either split the gap around them or reject the slot.

DO NOT reach for corroboration as the precondition: the day-0 mint runs immediately after download, before any transcription or acoustic pass, so no other detector's signal exists at mint time.

BLOCKS playhead-pyq7's promotion (segment-recovered slots stay markOnly/unanchored until this is fixed).

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
MECHANISM VERIFIED IN SHIPPED SOURCE by the orchestrator, 2026-08-11. The agent's citation named Services/AdDetection/RediffRefetch/RediffByteAligner.swift:693; the real path is Services/AdDetection/RediffByteAligner.swift and the code is at :691-696:

    for run in sorted {
        if run.aStart < globalAEnd { continue }   // <-- drops the A-overlapper
        accepted.append(run)
        globalAEnd = run.aStart + run.bytes
    }

with the comment immediately above it: 'A-ordered, A-non-overlapping accepted set. Dropping a later A-overlapper (the conflict chainRuns also resolves) keeps the gap arithmetic below well-formed (every A-gap >= 0).'

So the drop is DELIBERATE and its stated purpose is bookkeeping — keeping every A-gap non-negative. The defect is what happens next: the dropped run's A-span falls through to addGap and is reported as a GAP, i.e. divergent, i.e. an ad. But a run is by definition MATCHED audio. It was found, then discarded for arithmetic convenience, and then its bytes were relabelled as the opposite of what they are.

THAT IS THE STANDING DEFECT CLASS, in its purest form yet: 'divergent' names 'these bytes rotated between fetches' and is being read as 'these bytes are an ad', on audio the aligner itself proved MATCHES.

SEVERITY IS HIGHER THAN 'BLOCKS pyq7' — THIS IS LIVE TODAY. These slots ship as markOnly, which is a BANNER, and per Dan's 2026-07-31 ruling the banner is a SKIP AFFORDANCE ('when it enters so I can skip'). A listener who taps skip on a phantom slot loses up to 470 seconds of show. So the harm does not wait for auto-skip promotion; it only requires a tap. The 480 s cap is the sole thing standing between a tap and eight minutes of missing episode.

Prioritise accordingly, and note the fix candidate pyq7 measured is gold-free and therefore viable on the day-0 path: require zero A-seconds inside an emitted slot to be covered by any FOUND run.

title: [bug] byte-exact rediff DAI should auto-skip from episode 1 — per-show trust adds nothing to a deterministic signal
description:
DAN'S RULING 2026-08-11, chosen over the alternatives: byte-exact rediff DAI auto-skips from episode 1, regardless of the show's shadow/manual/auto mode. The trust ladder then governs only the UNCERTAIN classes (acoustic, host-read).

THE ARGUMENT, which is his own certainty-tiered ruling applied to a new user. Per-show trust exists to answer 'do I believe THIS detector on THIS show yet'. A byte-exact rediff slot is not a belief — it is a differ over two fetches of the same episode establishing that those bytes rotated. It is deterministic and show-independent, so a per-show confidence ladder adds nothing to it and only delays it. Dan's standing ruling (feedback_certainty_tiered_skip, 2026-07-17) is already 'auto-SKIP high-certainty DAI, MARK host-read when uncertain; per-class certainty, not one global threshold' — this bead is that ruling reaching the SHOW-MODE gate, which currently overrides it.

THE EVIDENCE THAT IT MATTERS. Virgin-DB overnight pull, 5 episodes, ~22 hours, ZERO auto-skips: all 31 ad_windows were eligibilityGate=markOnly / wasSkipped=0, including four dayZeroRediffByteExact windows at confidence 1.00. One of those is a pre-roll at 0.0-60.3s that rediff got EXACTLY right while the detector split it in two and over-ran 38 seconds into the show. That is the single ad a listener is guaranteed to reach, we identified it perfectly, and we played it to them.

WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE BEAD FROM playhead-mn5e. mn5e makes the LADDER work (a clean, high-confidence show promotes itself). This bead makes one class BYPASS the ladder entirely. They compose but they are different decisions and different code: mn5e is a missing production caller in TrustScoringService; this is a gate ordering question in the skip path. Dan chose the bypass FIRST for time-to-value, and separately ruled that the ladder should also self-promote.

CHECK BEFORE IMPLEMENTING — the day-0 mint may already block this by construction. BackfillEvidenceFusion.swift:1071 records that 'only the day-0 mint opts in, and it stamps those slots .unanchored + .markOnly without ever consulting this mapper.' If day-0 rediff slots are stamped markOnly AT MINT, then the show-mode gate is not the only thing stopping them and this bead has to address the mint too. Establish which gate is actually binding on the four windows in the pull before changing anything — do not assume it is the show mode just because the show is in shadow.

DO NOT WIDEN THIS TO ACOUSTIC OR CHROMA. playhead-6qvf already separated .rediffSlotChroma from .rediffSlot precisely because the chroma arm's ~1s alignment was being credited as byte-exact, and 9 of 51 real corpus pairs (17.6%) take that arm. carriesRediffByteExactWidth is the predicate that means what this bead means. Splice slots are acoustic (measured recall 21%) and are out.

ACCEPTANCE: on a fresh install with no user interaction and a show in shadow, a byte-exact rediff pre-roll is auto-skipped on the first episode. Measured on a device pull: wasSkipped=1 on dayZeroRediffByteExact windows, and NO change to the gate on any other provenance.

comments.text:
BINDING-GATE FINDING (implementer, pre-implementation; no code changed).

The bead's premise is wrong on all three candidates, and the real blocker is a fourth thing.

1. THE SHOW-MODE GATE IS ALREADY BYPASSED for byte-exact rediff. playhead-gard (#334, 2026-08-02) shipped SkipDetectorClass.rediffByteExact with consultsShowTrust == false (Playhead/Services/TrustScoring/SkipDetectorClass.swift:96-103) and showIndependentSeedMode == .auto (:112). DetectorTrustLedger.seed returns .auto for it on a show with no ledger entry (DetectorTrustLedger.swift:172-179), TrustScoringService.seededModes wires it (:421-443), and SkipOrchestrator.beginEpisode installs it (SkipOrchestrator.swift:1965-1972). Both shows in the pull have detectorTrustJSON empty, so .rediffByteExact resolves .auto TODAY, in shadow. There is nothing to implement here.

2. THE MINT IS BINDING, and via the STRICT classification, not the flag. RediffActivation.dayZeroByteExactAutoSkipEnabled is already true (RediffActivation.swift:193). AdDetectionService.swift:12170-12174 stamps anchor = strict ? .rediffByteExact : .unanchored and gate = (strict && flag) ? .eligible : .markOnly. All four field windows persisted unanchored/unanchored + markOnly, so strict was FALSE for all four.

3. WHY strict was false, provably. rediff_day_zero_attempts: bSidesAccepted=1, gateRejected=1, divergentSlots=4, marks=4. With exactly ONE accepted B-side, unionedPlayedSlots returns it verbatim (RediffSlotOwnership.swift:278), so strictByteExactMask (:309-320) is all-true iff that alignment was monotonicClean. It was all-false => alignment.monotonicClean == false => the list came through the playhead-9s6q SEGMENT-RECOVERY arm (AdDetectionService.swift:12058; RediffSlotOwnership.swift:419-427). Build provenance: the device DB carries retryClaimCount (added 2026-08-09, e23f07ac) and schema_version 47, and the mint ran 2026-08-10, so ec68e549/qs0d (2026-07-31) was live.

4. THE FOUR WINDOWS ARE NOT THIS BEAD'S POPULATION. They are dayZeroRediffByteExact by boundaryState NAME but segment-recovered by ARM. carriesRediffByteExactWidth is a DecodedSpan/fusion-lane predicate and the day-0 mint does not produce DecodedSpans; decoded_spans in the pull has ZERO rediffSlot provenance (0 of 22 rows). Promoting them is exactly what playhead-pyq7 (OPEN, P2, discovered-from qs0d) owns and what qs0d deliberately declined.

WHERE THEY ACTUALLY DIE, in order: (a) eligibilityGate=markOnly routes them to the SUGGEST tier at SkipOrchestrator.swift:3064-3114, before any mode is consulted; (b) even if admitted, unanchored/unanchored classifies them .fusion (SkipDetectorClass.swift:146-152), which DOES consult show trust -> shadow -> confirmed-only (SkipOrchestrator.swift:6814-6818); (c) and AutoSkipEdgePadding.startMargin returns nil for an unanchored start (AutoSkipEdgePadding.swift:295-297). Three gates, one cause: strict == false.

CONSEQUENCE: a STRICT day-0 slot would auto-skip end-to-end on a shadow show today (mint .eligible -> 0.7 preload floor passes at conf 1.00 -> ingest admits -> detectorClass .rediffByteExact -> .auto -> AutoSkipEdgePadding.isActive targeted-ON for byte/byte, AutoSkipEdgePadding.swift:217-224 -> skip). The reason the corpus shows zero auto-skips is that it produced zero strict slots, not that a gate refused them.

LISTENER EXPERIENCE on this corpus, under the change as the bead describes it: ZERO windows change. Nothing auto-skips, 0 seconds. Under the DIFFERENT change (promote segment-recovered too = pyq7) it would be 4 windows / 146.97 s on one episode of 5.

Awaiting Dan's call on which bead this becomes.

=== WHY THE FOUR WINDOWS ARE markOnly ANYWAY — and it is not a gate refusing them ===

The mint, AdDetectionService.swift:12170-12174:
    let anchor: AutoSkipEdgeAnchor = strict ? .rediffByteExact : .unanchored
    let gate: SkipEligibilityGate = (strict && RediffActivation.dayZeroByteExactAutoSkipEnabled) ? .eligible : .markOnly

All four field windows persisted unanchored/unanchored + markOnly, which is only reachable with strict == FALSE. Confirmed against the device DB:
    0.00-60.26     unanchored unanchored markOnly wasSkipped=0
    888.58-915.05  unanchored unanchored markOnly wasSkipped=0
    942.39-987.56  unanchored unanchored markOnly wasSkipped=0
    1880.35-1895.42 unanchored unanchored markOnly wasSkipped=0

WHY strict WAS FALSE, proved rather than inferred: rediff_day_zero_attempts reads accepted=1, gateRejected=1, divergent=4, marks=4. With EXACTLY ONE accepted B-side, RediffSlotOwnership.unionedPlayedSlots returns it verbatim (:278), so strictByteExactMask (:309-320) is all-true IFF that alignment was monotonicClean. The mask was all-false, therefore alignment.monotonicClean == false, therefore the slots came through the playhead-9s6q SEGMENT-RECOVERY arm (AdDetectionService.swift:12058).

Build provenance rules out 'old binary': the DB carries retryClaimCount (added 2026-08-09, e23f07ac) at schema_version 47, and the mint ran 2026-08-10 — well after qs0d.

=== SO THESE WINDOWS ARE NOT THIS BEAD'S POPULATION ===
They are dayZeroRediffByteExact by boundaryState NAME and segment-recovered by ARM. That is the standing defect class again, in a NAME this time: a label that says byte-exact on rows that are not. carriesRediffByteExactWidth is a DecodedSpan/fusion-lane predicate and the day-0 mint writes AdWindows directly, producing no DecodedSpan — decoded_spans has ZERO rediff provenance (0 of 22 rows, verified).

'Zero auto-skips in 22 hours' is NOT 'a gate refused high-certainty ads'. It is 'the corpus produced ZERO strict slots'. A strict day-0 slot would auto-skip end to end on a shadow show TODAY: mint .eligible -> 0.7 preload floor passes at conf 1.00 -> ingest admits -> detectorClass .rediffByteExact -> .auto -> AutoSkipEdgePadding.isActive is targeted-ON for byte/byte (:217-224) -> skip fires. Nothing is blocking it. Nothing qualified.

Promoting segment-recovered slots is pyq7's scope (OPEN, P2, discovered-from qs0d), and qs0d DECLINED it deliberately. It needs a boundary-tightness measurement nobody has taken.

title: [bug] rediff fires on 1 of 5 downloads — and it is the ONLY thing that gets the pre-roll right; the detector over-ran the true end by 38 seconds into the show
description:
DAN'S DIRECTIVE 2026-08-11: 'rediff is our strongest catcher of preroll, so rediff should be done immediately upon download.'

=== HE IS RIGHT, AND THIS PULL PROVES IT ON HIS OWN EPISODE (asset 66D32039, virgin-DB overnight pull, scratchpad/db-overnight5) ===

  rediff (dayZeroRediffByteExact)     0.0 -  60.3   conf 1.00
  detector (acousticRefined)          0.0 -  17.6   conf 0.92
  detector (acousticRefined)         30.8 -  98.7   conf 1.00

Rediff got the pre-roll exactly. The detector SPLIT it into two windows, missed 17.6-30.8 (12.2s of ad), and over-ran to 98.7 — THIRTY-EIGHT SECONDS past the true end, into the show. Per Dan's per-edge ruling (outer edges free, inner precious) that is the expensive direction: the outer edge at 0.0 is free to widen, the inner edge at 60.3 eats content.

Same shape on the mid-roll: rediff 942.4-987.6 (45.2s) vs two detector fragments 944.7-956.0 and 960.2-978.7 covering 30.3s of it, missing both 956.0-960.2 and 978.7-987.6.

=== THE DEFECT, LOCALIZED ===

ALL FIVE assets captured an episode_fingerprints row at download time (capturedAt on every one, fingerprintCount 15536-55555). So the download path RAN and did its fingerprinting work 5 of 5.

ONLY ONE got a rediff_day_zero_kickoffs row, and its lastSource is 'download_and_analyze_tap' — a FOREGROUND TAP. The other four, which arrived without a tap, got neither a kickoff nor an attempt:

  66D32039  kickoff=YES attempt=YES   simplecast::000ee634
  F7BB38BB  kickoff=no  attempt=no    simplecast::c57d8fe8
  B80D3EE0  kickoff=no  attempt=no    simplecast::bf975cc3
  60DFF7B4  kickoff=no  attempt=no    flightcast::01KZEMW7JE1GT
  590D6656  kickoff=no  attempt=no    flightcast::01KYMPYHGY7WK

That pairing is the finding: fingerprint capture and rediff kickoff sit on the same download path, and one fires 5/5 while the other fires 1/5. So this is not 'downloads do not trigger analysis' — it is one specific capability on that path that a non-tap download cannot reach. That is the sceneless-launch family (playhead-1shd / cnql / hkh6 / m8rq), fifth-and-sixth instance, and the fingerprint row is the control proving the rest of the path is alive.

=== WHAT IT COST WHEN IT DID RUN, so nobody makes it unconditional without seeing the bill ===

  rediff_day_zero_attempts: lastExit=marked, lastMarkCount=4, lastBSideCount=2, lastBSidesAccepted=1,
                            lastBSidesGateRejected=1, lastDivergentSlotCount=4, lastFullFetchBytes=66,010,142
  rediff_bandwidth_ledger:  precheckBytesTotal=0  fullFetchBytesTotal=66,010,142  rotatedCount=1
                            dayZeroBudgetSpentBytes=66,010,142

66 MB for one episode — a full second copy. Five episodes a night is ~330 MB. Note precheckBytesTotal=0: it went STRAIGHT TO A FULL FETCH with no cheap precheck. A range-request precheck that establishes whether the bytes differ at all should be scoped alongside this, not after it, or 'rediff on every download' becomes a bandwidth decision made by accident. The transport setting from playhead-4dqe is the existing control surface.

=== SEQUENCING, and this is a real dependency not a nicety ===
playhead-kxgh records that the day-0 kickoff drain is STRICTLY SERIAL and each item can burn the full 6.5-minute readiness budget — five requests took 33 minutes. 'Immediately upon download' and 'one at a time at 6.5 minutes each' do not compose. kxgh becomes load-bearing for this bead.
playhead-jra6 (the kickoff queue is IN-MEMORY, so a batch queued but not settled leaves no row at all) is the other half: making the trigger fire is worthless if the queue does not survive the process.
playhead-zmog covers the foreground STREAMING download path, which is a different arrival and needs its own check.

ACCEPTANCE: every downloaded episode gets a rediff_day_zero_kickoffs row, whatever path it arrived by and whether or not a scene was ever connected — with the fingerprint capture as the control (if a fingerprint row exists, a kickoff row must exist). Re-measure on a pull and report the ratio.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
=== PRECHECK SCOPED IN, per Dan 2026-08-11 ('scope the precheck but put rediff before fm') ===

THE COMPONENTS ALREADY EXIST. This is wiring, not new machinery:
  RediffRefetchSeams.swift:482  URLSessionRangedAudioSampler — 'Issues exactly two GETs, bytes=0-... for the head and bytes=(total-tail)-... for the tail, and NEVER a HEAD or conditional GET.'
  RediffRefetchService.swift:358  rangedSampler.sample(headBytes: config.headSampleBytes, tailBytes: config.tailSampleBytes)
  RediffRefetchService.swift:366  localSampler.sample(... same head/tail ...)  — samples the copy already on disk
  RediffRefetchPolicy.swift:180   a .precheck failure case already exists
  RediffRefetchPolicy.swift:435   RediffRefetchCost carries precheckBytes separately from fullFetchBytes
  AnalysisStore.swift:6344        recordBandwidth(precheckBytes:) already persists it

WHAT THE DEVICE SAYS. rediff_bandwidth_ledger on the overnight pull:
  precheckBytesTotal = 0      fullFetchBytesTotal = 66,010,142      rotatedCount = 1
The one day-0 attempt went STRAIGHT TO A FULL FETCH. Both samplers were sitting there unused. n=1 attempt, so this is evidence about that attempt rather than proof the day-0 path can never precheck — establish which it is from source before writing code, because the two need different fixes and it is a cheap question to answer:
  (a) the day-0 path has no precheck branch at all  -> wire one (this bead)
  (b) it has one and it did not fire                -> that is the y3ya shape a sixth time, and the fix is the caller

WHY A PRECHECK IS MEANINGFUL ON DAY-0 AT ALL — this is not the lagged case and the reasoning differs. On the lagged path a precheck asks 'has the remote copy changed since we last looked'. On day-0 there is no 'last look', but there IS a local copy: the episode the user just downloaded. So the precheck asks 'does a freshly-fetched HEAD and TAIL differ from the bytes we already hold' — and head-and-tail is EXACTLY where the pre-roll and post-roll live. Dan's stated reason for prioritising rediff is that it is the strongest catcher of PRE-ROLL, so the cheap probe and the high-value target are the same bytes.

THE TRADE, stated so it is decided and not stumbled into. A head/tail precheck that reports 'unchanged' proves no pre/post-roll rotation. It says NOTHING about mid-rolls. So gating the 66 MB full fetch on the precheck trades mid-roll rediff coverage for bandwidth. That is probably the right trade — mid-rolls are also reachable by the FM lane, pre-rolls are the ad every listener is guaranteed to hit, and 66 MB per episode on every download is ~330 MB a night at Dan's five-episode rate — but it IS a change in what rediff detects, so it needs to be measured rather than assumed: report, on a pull, how many day-0 slots would have been LOST by gating on the precheck.

SUGGESTED SHAPE (not a decision — present the measurement first):
  precheck head+tail  ->  differs  -> full k-way fetch, current behaviour, full slot coverage
                      ->  identical -> record the precheck bytes, mark the episode 'no edge rotation',
                                      and let the FM lane own the mid-rolls
  Either way precheckBytesTotal stops reading 0 and the ledger becomes able to answer 'what did rediff cost us'.

ACCEPTANCE, added to this bead's existing acceptance:
  - precheckBytesTotal is non-zero on a pull after a day-0 attempt
  - the bytes-per-episode figure is reported before and after, on real episodes
  - the number of day-0 slots that a precheck gate would have suppressed is measured and reported, NOT estimated
