comments.text:
=== IMPLEMENTER FINDINGS, 2026-08-11 (branch bead/playhead-kg8h) ===

TWO PARTS OF THIS BEAD'S STATED EVIDENCE DO NOT SURVIVE CHECKING. Recording
them first, because a wrong causal story is worse than an open question.

1. THE BUILD UNDER TEST PREDATES playhead-cnql. db-overnight5 is build
   9e31bf1c; cnql merged as ff338693 at 2026-08-10 16:00:44, three commits
   later. Every asset in the pull was created 09:02-12:50 that same morning. So
   the 4-of-5 population is exactly the one cnql was written for, and the pull
   cannot distinguish "cnql fixed it" from "cnql did not".

2. THE FINGERPRINT ROW IS NOT A CONTROL ON THE DOWNLOAD PATH.
   `episode_fingerprints` has exactly ONE production writer:
   `AnalysisJobRunner.run(...)` (AnalysisJobRunner.swift:497, via
   `EpisodeFingerprintCapture.captureAndPersist`), after a full audio decode.
   It is the ANALYSIS lane, not the download path. The timestamps confirm it —
   the five fingerprints were captured at 09:02:25, 09:08:56, 09:18:32,
   12:49:34 and 12:51:15, i.e. as the serial analysis lane reached each
   episode, NOT when the bytes landed. 5/5 fingerprints prove the analysis lane
   ran; they say nothing about the download-completion hook.

=== WHAT THE PULL ACTUALLY SHOWS, and it is a better story ===

All FIVE `preAnalysis` jobs were created inside a 37-second window —
09:02:21, 09:02:24, 09:02:26, 09:02:33, 09:02:58. One batch of five downloads.

The one kickoff row settled at 09:02:33: `download_and_analyze_tap`,
pollCount=2, waitedSeconds=15.8. That entry point (`requestDayZeroKickoff` <-
`kickOffDayZeroRediffForPreparation`) does NOT go through the DownloadManager
observer at all, so it proves the coordinator was alive and writing while
saying nothing about the observer.

The other four needed the serial drain to reach them. Reading the code with the
measured lags:

  asset      job created   asset row registered   LAG      vs the 400 s budget
  66D32039   09:02:21      09:02:21                    0 s   inside
  F7BB38BB   09:02:24      09:08:46                  382 s   inside
  B80D3EE0   09:02:26      09:18:23                  957 s   OUTSIDE (2.4x)
  60DFF7B4   09:02:33      12:48:53               13,580 s   OUTSIDE (34x)
  590D6656   09:02:58      12:50:56               13,678 s   OUTSIDE (34x)

So even with a perfect observer, that batch settles at roughly 09:02, 09:09,
09:16, 09:22 and 09:29 — the last one 27 minutes after the download. THE ROW IS
WRITTEN AT THE END. `RediffDayZeroKickoffCoordinator.process` is
`wait -> fire -> settle`, and `settle` is the only writer; `fire` is the whole
day-0 re-fetch (66,010,142 bytes on this attempt). A process that does not
survive all of that leaves nothing, indistinguishable from a download that
never happened.

That model is corroborated from the other direction by playhead-kxgh's
2026-08-09 pull, where the process DID survive: five rows at 6m35s spacing,
every one lastPollCount=40, every one `no_analysis_asset`. Same mechanism, two
outcomes, and the only difference is whether anything lived long enough to
write.

=== WHAT SHIPPED (commit 214ca1ed) ===

`requestKickoff` awaits a durable CLAIM before it queues anything
(`AnalysisStore.noteRediffDayZeroKickoffClaim`, `lastOutcome='requested'`), so
the row exists the moment a completion is observed. `kickoffCount` moves to the
claim — which is what its doc comment has said since 4dqe — and
`kickoffCount - (firedCount + gaveUpCount)` becomes the queryable count of
kickoffs owed and never settled. No schema migration: `lastOutcome` is TEXT and
the reader already falls back on an unrecognised raw value.

Claimed at ENQUEUE rather than at the head of `process`, because the pending
queue is itself one of the three losses (kxgh serial drain + jra6 in-memory
array). `claimKickoff` is a required init parameter — a defaulted no-op would
reproduce this defect with the whole suite green.

=== JOB 3: THE PRECHECK. IT IS CASE (a), AND IT SHOULD NOT BE WIRED AS SCOPED ===

`runDayZeroRefetch` has no precheck branch, deliberately, and its own doc says
why: the precheck "false-negatives on client-PINNED DAI (a same-context
re-fetch returns a byte-identical body), the very category day-0's k-way probe
targets".

Established from source, and it is worse than "single-persona":
  PlayheadRuntime.swift:1604   URLSessionRangedAudioSampler(persona: .default)
  RediffRefetchSeams.swift:324 .default   == .appleCoreMediaIPhone
  RediffRefetchSeams.swift:335 .download  == .appleCoreMediaIPhone
The precheck probes under the SAME request context the played A-side was
downloaded under — the one persona `kWayPersonasDistinct` exists to exclude
(playhead-9s6q FIX B, which is also what took Conan and Fresh Air from 0 to
real day-0 width).

MEASURED SUPPRESSION, on the one day-0 attempt in the pull (n=1, stated as
such):
  * day-0 slots minted: 4 — 0.0-60.3, 888.6-915.0, 942.4-987.6, 1880.3-1895.4,
    147.1 s of ad width, including the pre-roll this bead is about.
  * bitrate: 66,010,142 B / 2 B-copies / 1926 s = 17.1 kB/s, so the 64 KiB head
    and tail samples each reach 3.8 SECONDS of audio.
  * the last slot ends 30.6 s before EOF — EIGHT TIMES the tail probe's reach.
    The tail leg is blind on this episode regardless of persona.
  * the head leg overlaps slot 1 but probes under the download persona, which
    on a client-pinned show returns byte-identical bytes by construction.

So for this attempt a precheck gate has only two outcomes and neither is the
one the bead hoped for: it says "unchanged" and suppresses 4 of 4 slots
(147.1 s, including the pre-roll), or it says "changed" and the full 66 MB
fetch runs anyway with 128 KiB added. There is no outcome that saves the bytes
AND keeps the marks.

Not shipped. `precheckBytesTotal` therefore still reads 0 and the
bytes-per-episode figure is unchanged at 66.0 MB — that acceptance criterion is
NOT met, deliberately. What would have to be true first is filed as
playhead-4wzh.

=== FILED, NOT FIXED ===
  playhead-fzrw  the asset-row precondition lags the download by up to 3h46m;
                 3 of 5 could not have reached day-0 by any drain strategy
  playhead-iyru  a completion with no resolvable URL is still a silent return
  playhead-4wzh  what a day-0 precheck would need before it is worth wiring

CONTROL (unmutated, committed 214ca1ed): GATE_EXIT=0, "65 tests in 8 suites
passed" + `Test Suite 'DayZeroBackgroundKickoffWiringCanaryTests' passed`. The

      a claim never RESURRECTS a settled row's evidence

      a settle whose claim write FAILED still records the kickoff
      A KICKOFF FOR AN EPISODE WITH NO ASSET ROW IS RECORDABLE
      a kickoff that FIRED increments only `firedCount`

  M6  take the in-flight guard AFTER the claim suspends             GATE_EXIT=65
      the in-flight guard is taken BEFORE the claim suspends

Restore was byte-exact after every mutant (sha256 checked against the commit).
Worktree residue after the run: none (`git status --porcelain -- Playhead
PlayheadTests scripts` is empty).

=== RESIDUAL RISKS, stated as risks ===

1. The mechanism is NOT uniquely established, and cannot be from this pull. The
   build predates cnql, so a nil observer and the settle-after-the-work hole
   both produce the same signature. What IS established: cnql alone would not
   have produced the four missing rows, because that batch needed ~27 minutes
   of process life to settle through the serial drain.
2. This makes the ROW exist; it does not make day-0 FIRE. "Immediately upon
   download" still needs playhead-fzrw (asset-row lag), playhead-kxgh (serial
   drain) and playhead-jra6 (in-memory pending).
3. Queueing now depends on a store write. `requestKickoff` awaits the claim
   before `pending.append`, so a wedged AnalysisStore blocks the queue where it

   dependency.
4. `kickoffCount` changes meaning across the upgrade. Rows written by earlier
   builds counted SETTLES; rows written from now on count CLAIMS. A pull
   spanning the upgrade has both in one column, and no migration can recover
   the past.
5. `.requested` is a new `lastOutcome` raw value. A DOWNGRADE would read it as
   `.cancelled` through the existing `?? .cancelled` fallback, i.e. report an
   outstanding claim as teardown. Forward-only.
6. The play-while-downloading path still produces no kickoff row at all
   (playhead-zmog) — untouched.

  productive (success + no_ads)   77 rows   1354.6s
  cancelled                        7 rows    613.9s   p50 22.6s, MAX 292.0s
  permissive_decoding_failure      3 rows    296.9s   p50 33.0s, MAX 250.2s
  refusal                          3 rows     27.5s
  WASTED TOTAL                    13 rows    938.4s = 15.6 min = 41% of all FM time

THE SHAPE. A cancelled call that ran 292 SECONDS is a call that was started with nowhere near enough window left to finish it. The longest background window all night was 295.8s. So the runner began a call that could consume the entire remaining grant and then lost it — the work is done, the tokens are spent, the verdict is discarded, and the audio stays unscreened.

WHY IT MATTERS AGAINST DAN'S TARGET. Three episodes a night costs 46.3 min of productive compute. The night spent 38.2 min of FM time and banked only 22.6. Reclaiming the wasted 15.6 min is worth a third of the target on its own, and unlike granting more windows it costs nothing — the compute is already being spent.

SCOPE. Bound the decision to START a call by the window actually remaining and the measured cost of a call of that size (p50 11.7s, p90 42.8s, max 103.7s among successes). Do not start what cannot finish. Prefer banking a smaller window to losing a larger one — playhead-26od made coarsePassA persist incrementally, so a partial pass is now durable and a smaller unit is genuinely cheaper than a lost one.

DO NOT confuse this with playhead-rkfp/ezmv (the per-call FM deadline). That bead bounds how long a call may run; this one is about whether it should have been started.

RELATED, same file of evidence: permissive_decoding_failure at 250.2s is 4 minutes of compute thrown away by a parse. Worth a look while in here, but the cancellations are the larger term.

title: [bug] 17 of 32 granted background windows did ZERO work — including six full-length ones and a 54-minute run
description:
MEASURED on the virgin-DB overnight pull (build 9e31bf1c, scratchpad/db-overnight5/WHY_EXPIRED.txt).

iOS granted 32 DISTINCT background windows overnight (the 44 rows in background_task_runs are 32 slots — the regular and .charged tasks fire at the same instant and must not be double-counted). SEVENTEEN of them produced not one semantic_scan_results row.

Seven of the seventeen had real time:
  08-10 11:40   294.9s   0 rows
  08-10 13:19   233.1s   0 rows   (outcome=admitted_work, so it believed it had admitted something)
  08-10 13:28   289.2s   0 rows
  08-10 20:19  3243.4s   0 rows   <-- FIFTY-FOUR MINUTES
  08-11 01:06   295.1s   0 rows
  08-11 02:37   295.8s   0 rows
  08-11 04:21   268.8s   0 rows
That is roughly 80 minutes of granted compute that did nothing, in a night whose entire productive output was 22.6 minutes.

WHY THIS IS THE HIGHEST-VALUE BEAD IN THE EPIC. Three episodes a night costs 46.3 min of productive FM compute; the night achieved 22.6 across 15 working windows. Making the other 17 work is worth about +25 min on its own and is the single biggest term available.

RULED OUT ALREADY — do not start here. playhead-rbj4 (the fixed 219s minimumWindowBudget) is NOT the explanation, and the data says so: windows of 45.0s, 87.4s, 130.3s, 154.5s, 166.9s, 185.4s and 196.8s all DID work despite being under 219s, while windows of 268.8s, 289.2s, 294.9s, 295.1s and 295.8s did nothing despite being well over it. rbj4 is a real bug and stays open on its own merits; it is not this one.

WHAT TO ESTABLISH FIRST, before proposing any fix: for each of the seven long idle windows, WHICH step returned early. Every one of the five jobs carries a defer reason that could plausibly do it — metadataStall-refused(peers=0) [playhead-a3hf], underCoverage, underCoverageBudgetSpent, cancelled-during-fullEpisodeScan, expiredWithoutProgress. jobsSeen=5 on every single run, so the runner saw all five jobs each time and admitted none. The question is not 'was there work' — there was, four assets were nowhere near covered — it is 'what made the runner decline all five'.

ACCEPTANCE: a granted window of >= 60s either produces a durable semantic_scan_results row or journals a NAMED, queryable reason it could not, and the reason distinguishes 'nothing to do' from 'refused'. Re-measure over a night and report the idle-window count.

title: [epic] Two lanes, both efficient: the analysis must finish before he presses play
description:
DAN'S DECISION 2026-08-11, after the virgin-DB overnight pull: 'we should fix background windows and do work while the app is live. belt and suspenders.' Plus: 'but lets use background windows as efficiently as we can.'

THE PRODUCT TARGET, in his words: if a user listens to an episode and analysis finishes 5 minutes into a 60-minute episode, he would expect to see 4-5 OTHER episodes finished in the background at the same time. And: 'it would be great to wake up each morning and see three new episodes downloaded and analyzed overnight.'

=== THE BUDGET, MEASURED (scratchpad/db-overnight5/BUDGET.txt, build 9e31bf1c) ===

COST OF THE WORK: 1354.6s of productive FM compute screened 5263.3s of audio (merged per asset).
  COST RATIO = 0.257 compute-seconds per audio-second.
  A 60-minute episode costs 15.4 minutes of FM compute. A 90-minute one costs 23.2.
  Redundancy is 1.25x (6950.0s of raw row spans over 5561.3s merged) — playhead-7x1s took this down from the 2.0-2.6x it measured, so that work landed.

THREE EPISODES OVERNIGHT COSTS 46.3 MINUTES OF PRODUCTIVE FM COMPUTE.

WHAT LAST NIGHT ACTUALLY DID:
  productive FM compute achieved     22.6 min   across 15 working windows out of 32
  FM compute WASTED                  15.6 min   41% of all FM time — cancelled / refusal / decoding failure
  if all 32 windows had worked       48.2 min   (assumes the working windows' rate holds)
  ... plus reclaiming the waste      ~64 min

SO THE HEADLINE IS: iOS ALREADY GRANTS ENOUGH BACKGROUND TIME FOR DAN'S THREE-EPISODES-A-NIGHT TARGET. 48.2 >= 46.3 with every window working, and ~64 min with the waste reclaimed — a 38% margin. The overnight budget is being WASTED, not withheld. That is why 'use background windows as efficiently as we can' is the right instruction and not merely a preference: efficiency is the entire gap.

=== THE FOREGROUND TARGET NEEDS RESTATING, and this is a product question not an engineering one ===
'Analysis finished 5 minutes into a 60-minute episode' means 15.4 minutes of FM compute inside 5 minutes of wall clock — 3.1x oversubscribed. It is not reachable by scanning the whole episode, and no amount of efficiency work reaches it.

But the promise the user actually cares about is 'I never hear an ad', which does NOT require the whole episode by minute 5. It requires the scan to stay AHEAD OF THE PLAYHEAD. That needs a 26% duty cycle — 15.4 minutes of FM spread across 60 minutes of listening — which is comfortable. The scan finishes the episode well before the listener does, and no ad is ever reached unanalysed.

RECOMMENDATION (Dan to confirm): make the live-lane acceptance 'no ad boundary is ever reached before it has been analysed', not 'the episode is fully scanned by minute N'. The second is a harder promise that buys the listener nothing extra.

=== LANES ===
LANE A — background efficiency. Every granted window does work, and no FM second is spent on a call that cannot finish.
LANE B — the live app. playhead-hp70 (point FM ahead of the playhead during playback) is the existing bead and is the right shape.

Both lanes feed the same durable rows, so they compose rather than duplicate — which is what makes belt-and-suspenders honest here rather than two half-systems.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
DAN, 2026-08-11, two further rulings on this epic:

1. 'ideally we can not only look ahead at the currently playing episode, but also get some other episodes fully analyzed once the currently playing episode is done.' => the ordering is DEPTH-FIRST: finish the playing episode's look-ahead, then take the NEXT episode all the way to done before starting the one after. Last night was breadth-first — jobsSeen=5 on every window, five jobs each nudged forward, none finished — and the per-episode cost data hints depth-first is also CHEAPER, not merely tidier: the one episode scanned to 100% got 120s of audio per FM call at 10.4s of compute, while the two that barely started got 55s of audio per call at 25.4s. A ~5x yield difference. n=5, so treat as a hypothesis to test, not a settled fact.

2. 'rediff is our strongest catcher of preroll, so rediff should be done immediately upon download.' => filed as its own bead with the witness. Rediff got a pre-roll exactly right (0.0-60.3, conf 1.0) where the detector split it and over-ran 38s into the show.

CAVEAT I OWE THIS EPIC, because I wrote the numbers in it: the 0.257 cost ratio is a weighted average over FIVE episodes and TWO shows whose individual ratios span 0.087 to 0.457 — a 5.3x spread. It has no predictive power for a specific episode. The '46.3 min needed vs 48.2 min available' comparison in the epic body is therefore a 4% gap between two soft numbers and MUST NOT be read as clearing the bar; the honest claim is only that the need and the supply are the same order of magnitude. What is NOT soft, because they are direct counts rather than extrapolations: 17 of 32 windows idle, 41% of FM time producing no verdict, one cancelled call burning 292s of a 296s maximum window.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
SEQUENCING RULING, Dan 2026-08-11: 'scope the precheck but put rediff before fm.'

LANE ORDER IS NOW:
  1. playhead-kg8h  rediff on every download + the ranged precheck   (P0)
  2. playhead-kxgh  the day-0 drain is serial, 5 requests took 33 min — load-bearing for (1), not a nicety
  3. playhead-jra6  the kickoff queue is IN-MEMORY, so a batch that does not settle leaves no row
  4. playhead-8ljj  17 of 32 windows idle          (FM efficiency)
  5. playhead-ejr7  41% of FM compute wasted       (FM efficiency)
  6. playhead-exxc / playhead-se0x / playhead-a3hf / playhead-rbj4
  ... playhead-hp70 (live lane) and playhead-mn5e (shadow ladder) are P0 in their own right and are not gated on the above.

The FM efficiency work is the larger term over a whole library but it is slower to land and its own cost model (the 0.257 ratio) is measured on n=5 with a 5.3x spread. Rediff's value does not depend on that model being right.

title: [bug] a show can NEVER leave shadow mode without a banner tap — 17 observations, clean record, trust 0.5, still shadow; ZERO auto-skips in a 22-hour overnight run
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-11 on the virgin-DB overnight pull (build 9e31bf1c, 5 episodes, ~22h, scratchpad/db-overnight5).

THE OBSERVABLE. 31 ad_windows exist. Every single one is eligibilityGate=markOnly and wasSkipped=0. Not one auto-skip. The listener hears every ad. That includes windows at confidence 1.00 with skipConfidence 1.00.

THE CAUSE, established in source. Both podcast_profiles rows read mode='shadow':
  https://feeds.simplecast.com/dHoohVNH   obs=17  trust=0.50  recentFalseSkipSignals=0
  https://rss2.flightcast.com/xmsftuzj... obs=2   trust=0.50  recentFalseSkipSignals=0
TrustScoringConfig (TrustScoringService.swift:176-177) promotes shadow -> manual at observations >= 3 AND trustScore >= 0.4. The first show satisfies BOTH right now — 17 >= 3, 0.50 >= 0.4 — and has not moved. The promotion condition is met and the state is stale.

WHY IT IS STALE. The path that increments observationCount is AdDetectionService.swift:13141, which writes observationCount: existing.observationCount + 1 while carrying skipTrustScore: existing.skipTrustScore forward (:13140) and touching neither mode nor evaluatePromotion. Its own comment at :12999 says 'TrustScoringService.recordSuccessfulObservation owns subsequent trust adjustments.'

recordSuccessfulObservation has ZERO PRODUCTION CALLERS. This is not my inference — TrustScoringService.swift:870-872 states it outright, in the doc comment playhead-gard added: 'Measured, not reasoned: recordSuccessfulObservation and decayFalseSignals — the only two methods that raise trust or lower the false-signal counter — have ZERO production callers. evaluatePromotion therefore never ran in the shipped app.'

gard supplied the way out: recordCorrectObservation (:897), which does run evaluatePromotion. Its ONLY production caller is SkipOrchestrator.swift:5927 — the banner YES tap.

THE CONSEQUENCE, stated plainly. The only production path that can promote a show out of shadow is the user tapping Yes on a banner. A show can observe any number of episodes with perfect detection and a spotless record and remain in shadow forever. On this pull there are 0 correction_events: nothing was tapped, so nothing was promoted, so nothing auto-skipped in 22 hours.

WHY THIS IS THE TIME-TO-VALUE BUG. gard's fix is right for the show that has been DEMOTED — a user who vetoed twice needs a way back. It does not serve the NEW show, which has never been vetoed and has nothing to undo. A new listener installs the app, adds episodes, and the product does not perform its promise until they first tap Yes on a banner for an ad they were already going to hear. The first tap is the price of admission and nothing in the UI says so.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS NOT. It is not 'lower the bar'. Detection quality is not the blocker here — a show with 17 clean observations already CLEARS the stated bar. The mechanism that evaluates the bar does not run.

SCOPE / OPEN DESIGN QUESTION FOR DAN, do not decide inside a fix: should a clean run of N episodes promote on its own (i.e. give recordSuccessfulObservation a production caller at the point an episode's ad windows are confirmed), or is a user gesture deliberately required before the app ever skips for them? Those are different products. The per-class certainty tiering (playhead-nqey, merged) is a separate axis and is not what is blocking here.

RELATED SHAPE: this is the y3ya / a1r6 pattern for the fourth time — a mechanism that is fully built, fully tested, and has no production consumer. Check the consumer, not the code.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
THIRD ROUTE INTO SHADOW, spotted in the 15d0 merge-gate log 2026-08-11 — establish this before concluding the trust ladder is the whole story:

  [SkipOrchestrator] beginEpisode: skip mode is shadow because trustServiceUnavailable
                     — this is NOT a deliberate shadow

That is a distinct third route, and this bead currently documents only two: (1) never promoted, because the only production caller of the promotion path is the banner Yes tap, and (2) demoted by vetoes. 'trustServiceUnavailable' is neither — it is a show falling into shadow because the trust service could not be READ, which is a failure mode, not a policy.

WHAT MAKES IT WORTH CHECKING RATHER THAN ASSUMING. The log string carries its own disclaimer — somebody wrote 'this is NOT a deliberate shadow' into production logging, which means they hit it, knew it would be misread as policy, and defended against the misreading in prose rather than in the type. TrustScoringService.swift:327 already says the same thing about a sibling: 'Three of this function's four exits return .shadow, and only one of them is the deliberate one' (:320-341: .trustProfileUnreadable, .newShowDefault, .unrecognizedTrustProfileMode). So there is a KNOWN family of failure-shaped shadows and a known concern that they are indistinguishable from the intended one.

HONEST LIMIT ON THIS OBSERVATION: I saw it in a TEST fixture inside a gate log, not on the device. It is not evidence that it fires in production. The device pull cannot settle it either way — podcast_profiles stores only the resulting mode string, so a shadow caused by an unreadable trust service and a shadow caused by never being promoted are the SAME ROW. That indistinguishability is itself the finding worth carrying: the persisted state cannot tell you which of the (now) three routes produced it.

WHAT THIS BEAD SHOULD DO WITH IT: establish whether trustServiceUnavailable is reachable on a real launch (the sceneless-launch family is the obvious suspect — a trust service installed from a scene modifier would be nil on a headless start, which is instance six of that shape). If it is reachable, then part of the zero-auto-skips result may be a nil service rather than an unpromoted ladder, and the two need different fixes. Do NOT fold it into the ladder fix without deciding which one is actually firing on Dan's device.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
=== DAN'S RULING 2026-08-11 ===
'I think a clean show with high confidence should be able to promote itself out of shadow.'

THAT IS THIS BEAD, and it settles the open design question in its body. A show does NOT have to wait for a banner tap. Give the promotion path a production caller at the point an episode's ad windows are confirmed, so evaluatePromotion actually runs on the evidence the app already has.

WHAT THE FIX IS, concretely: recordSuccessfulObservation (TrustScoringService.swift:449) is fully built, runs evaluatePromotion at :484, and has ZERO production callers — the doc comment at :870-872 says so outright. AdDetectionService.swift:13141 increments observationCount while carrying skipTrustScore forward and never touching mode, and its own comment at :12999 says 'recordSuccessfulObservation owns subsequent trust adjustments'. So the two halves exist and are simply not connected. This is the y3ya shape and the fix is the caller, not new machinery.

READ THE RULING CAREFULLY — IT HAS TWO CONDITIONS, NOT ONE. Dan said 'a clean show WITH HIGH CONFIDENCE'. Clean is the observation record; high confidence is a separate bar. The shipped thresholds are observations >= 3 AND skipTrustScore >= 0.4 (TrustScoringConfig, :176-177). 0.4 is not obviously 'high' — it is barely above the 0.2 a new non-exceptional show starts at, and two correctObservationBonus increments (0.10 each) reach it. Before implementing, put the number back to Dan rather than assuming 0.4 satisfies 'high confidence'. Do NOT silently retune it either direction; the thresholds are a product decision and this bead's job is to make the mechanism RUN, not to move the bar.

ALSO IN SCOPE, because it is the same question asked of a different input: is the promotion evidence 'the episode's ad windows were confirmed' or 'the user did not veto them'? Those differ on a show nobody has listened to — which is exactly the state of Dan's device (5 episodes downloaded, ZERO listened, 0 correction_events). If promotion requires a listen, a downloaded-but-unplayed library still never promotes and the bead has not achieved its purpose. Name which one you implement and why.

STILL UNRESOLVED AND NOT PART OF THIS RULING: the trustServiceUnavailable route recorded above. Establish whether it fires on a real launch before concluding the ladder is the whole story.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
=== DAN: YES (2026-08-11) — a clean, high-confidence show self-promotes. Implement it. ===

BUT THE 'HIGH CONFIDENCE' HALF OF THE BAR DOES NO WORK TODAY, and whoever implements this must not read the shipped thresholds as expressing his intent. Measured:

  the bar          shadowToManualObservations = 3   AND   shadowToManualTrustScore = 0.4
  a new show is created at skipTrustScore = 0.5      (AdDetectionService.swift:13008 — the path that actually runs)
  both device shows read exactly                     trust=0.5

0.5 > 0.4 AT CREATION. So the trust clause is satisfied before a single observation is recorded, and the ONLY operative gate is observations >= 3. 'Clean show WITH HIGH CONFIDENCE' is currently just 'clean show'.

(TrustScoringService.swift:431 has a 0.2 constructor and :691 a 0.5 one; production reaches 0.5. The 0.2 path would clear 0.4 after two correctObservationBonus increments of 0.10.)

MY ASSUMPTION, STATED SO DAN CAN OVERRIDE IT: he asked for two conditions and the code offers one, so implementing the promotion caller WITHOUT changing the threshold would ship something weaker than he approved. I am NOT retuning the number inside this bead — that is a product decision and this bead's job is to make the mechanism RUN. Instead:

 1. Implement the production caller for recordSuccessfulObservation so evaluatePromotion actually runs (the mechanism is fully built and has ZERO production callers — TrustScoringService.swift:870-872 says so outright).
 2. Report, from the corpus or a device pull, what skipTrustScore actually DISTRIBUTES like on shows whose detections were correct vs shows whose detections were vetoed. If the two populations do not separate at any threshold, then skipTrustScore is not a confidence measure at all and the 'high confidence' condition needs a different quantity — which is a finding, not a tuning exercise.
 3. Bring the number back to Dan with that distribution attached.

WHY NOT JUST RAISE IT: picking 0.7 because it sounds high is exactly the move this project's standing defect class punishes — a number that names 'confidence' without anyone checking what it measures. The check is: what would skipTrustScore read if detection quality on this show had never been good? Today: 0.5, the same as a show that has never been observed at all.

SECOND CONDITION STILL OPEN from the earlier writeup: is the promotion evidence 'the episode's ad windows were confirmed' or 'the user did not veto them'? On Dan's device — 5 episodes downloaded, ZERO played, 0 correction_events — those give opposite answers. If promotion requires a listen, a downloaded-but-unplayed library never promotes and this bead does not achieve its purpose. Name which one you implement.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
=== IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-12 (commit 279c288b, branch bead/playhead-mn5e) ===

WHAT WAS WIRED. `AdDetectionService.runBackfill` now calls
`recordConfirmedWindowObservation` immediately before `updatePriors`, and that
calls `TrustScoringService.recordSuccessfulObservation`. The trust service
becomes the SOLE incrementer of `observationCount` for that backfill
(`updatePriors` gained a required `countsObservation:` parameter and stands
down when the trust call ran). Two incrementers would have ticked once per
backfill each and silently HALVED `shadowToManualObservations` and
`manualToAutoObservations`. NO THRESHOLD WAS CHANGED.

THE EVIDENCE QUESTION, ANSWERED: "this episode's ad windows were confirmed",
NOT "the user did not veto them". The second names an ABSENCE and cannot
distinguish "no veto because correct" from "no veto because nobody pressed
play" — which is the device's exact state (4 episodes analysed, 0 played,
0 correction_events), so a listen-gated rule promotes nothing at all and the
bead fails its purpose. An episode that confirmed NO windows records no
observation, matching `updatePriors`' own empty-window early return: an empty
window set is the quantity a BROKEN detector also produces.

=== 2. THE TRUST DISTRIBUTION DAN ASKED FOR. THERE ISN'T ONE. ===

Every `db-*` pull in the scratchpad, every row (32 of 35 pulls have a 0-byte
analysis.sqlite; 3 carry data):

  PULL           PODCAST      MODE    OBS  TRUST  FALSESIG
  db-prewipe6    simplecast   shadow   17   0.5      0
  db-prewipe6    flightcast   shadow    2   0.5      0
  db-overnight5  simplecast   shadow   17   0.5      0
  db-overnight5  flightcast   shadow    2   0.5      0
  db-morning7    simplecast   shadow   26   0.5      0
  db-morning7    flightcast   shadow   10   0.5      0

  DISTINCT skipTrustScore over all 6 rows: {0.5}   — ONE value
  DISTINCT mode          over all 6 rows: {shadow} — ONE value
  correction_events / ad_listen_rewinds / implicit_feedback_events: 0 / 0 / 0
    in all three pulls.

THE FINDING, STATED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER: the two populations Dan asked me
to compare — shows whose detections were CORRECT vs shows whose detections were
VETOED — cannot be separated at any threshold, because the vetoed population is
EMPTY and the correct population has a single constant value. `skipTrustScore`
has never taken a second value on any device, ever. It is not a confidence
measure today; it is the creation default (AdDetectionService.swift:13034)
carried forward by every writer that runs.

Applying the standing check — "what would skipTrustScore read if detection
quality on this show had never been good?" — the answer is 0.5, identical to a
show never observed at all, identical to what it reads now. So "high
confidence" as currently spelled discriminates nothing, and I did NOT invent a
number to make it look like it does.

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT A REAL MEASURE: after this bead the column finally MOVES
(+0.10 per confirmed-window backfill, -0.10 per veto), so the distribution
becomes measurable on the next device pull. That is the point at which a
threshold can be chosen from data instead of from taste.

=== 3. SAFETY (verified by test, not by argument) ===

  * 2 vetoes still demote auto -> manual after a self-promotion.
  * A vetoed show CANNOT climb back to auto on self-observation alone:
    manual -> auto requires `recentFalseSkipSignals == 0`, and
    `recordSuccessfulObservation` carries that counter forward untouched. Only
    a banner Yes (`recordCorrectObservation`) decays it. `decayFalseSignals`
    STILL has zero production callers and this bead did not give it one.
  * Byte-exact rediff DAI is untouched — `SkipDetectorClass.consultsShowTrust`
    is false for `.rediffByteExact` and its seed mode is already `.auto`
    (playhead-gard).

=== 4. WHAT THE LISTENER ACTUALLY GETS. READ THIS BEFORE CELEBRATING. ===

WOULD THE DEVICE'S SHOWS PROMOTE? Yes — and fast. Both are shadow/0.5/obs>=10,
so the very next backfill that confirms a window promotes them to MANUAL, and
three backfills later to AUTO:
  bf1: obs 27, trust 0.60 -> MANUAL      bf3: obs 29, trust 0.80 -> AUTO
Three backfills is a fraction of ONE episode's analysis (see playhead-2qz6:
observationCount counts BACKFILLS, ~9 per episode, not episodes).

WOULD ANY AD BE SKIPPED? NO. Not one. All 45 ad_windows on the device are
stamped `eligibilityGate = markOnly` at WRITE time, and
`SkipOrchestrator.receiveAdWindows` (:3064-3113) routes a markOnly row to the
suggest tier and `continue`s — BEFORE `evaluateWindow`, which is where the
shadow/manual/auto gate lives (:6814-6845). A markOnly window never reaches the
trust gate at all. 28 of the 45 (semantic-sweep-v1 x24, pod-continuation-v1 x4)
are markOnly by HARD-CODED literal in their composers and can never auto-skip
whatever the trust state says.

So: this bead removes a blocker that was genuinely total, and the observable
Dan reported does not change tonight. Filed as playhead-mqqd (P0).

=== 5. THE `trustServiceUnavailable` QUESTION FROM COMMENT 1: RESOLVED, NOT REACHABLE ===

`PlayheadRuntime` has exactly one `init` (:758). `trustService` is a
NON-OPTIONAL stored property assigned unconditionally at :851 and passed
straight into `SkipOrchestrator(trustService:)` at :1256-1258. So
`SkipOrchestrator.trustService` is never nil in production and the
`.trustServiceUnavailable` exit (:1977) is unreachable on a real launch — it
fires only for a test that constructs the orchestrator with the default `nil`.
Dan's sighting was in a gate log, and that is consistent. NOT instance six of
the sceneless-launch family.

(`AdDetectionService.trustScoringService` IS a post-init optional installed
from a `Task` at PlayheadRuntime:2191 — but from `init`, not from a scene
modifier, so it runs on every launch including a headless one. The new caller
logs a warning and falls back to the pre-mn5e counter if it is ever nil.)

=== VERIFICATION ===

Gate (5 suites requested, 5 ran): 99 Swift Testing tests in 4 suites + 24
XCTest in AdDetectionServiceUpdatePriorsAtomicityCanaryTests. TEST SUCCEEDED,
GATE_EXIT=0.

Mutation (each clause deleted, gate re-run, byte-exact restore verified by
SHA-256 each time):
  M1  delete the production caller            GATE_EXIT=65
      RED: "A clean shadow show promotes itself to manual when a backfill
            confirms ad windows", "A clean manual show does reach auto..."
  M2  countsObservation: !x -> true (double)  GATE_EXIT=65
      RED: "One backfill counts exactly ONE observation, not two",
           "A clean shadow show promotes itself to manual..."
  M3  drop the empty-window guard             GATE_EXIT=65
      RED: "An episode that confirms no ad windows records no trust observation"

=== THE TWO QUESTIONS FOR DAN ===

Q1 (the threshold, which I did not touch): with the mechanism now running and
observationCount ticking ~9x per episode, both device shows reach AUTO — the
mode that cuts audio without asking — within a single episode of analysis, on
evidence the detector produced about itself. Is that what "a clean show with
high confidence should be able to promote itself out of shadow" meant, or did
it mean out of shadow to MANUAL (the banner), with auto still requiring a user
signal? Those are one clause apart in `evaluatePromotion` and I did not choose
between them.

Q2 (what "high confidence" should measure): skipTrustScore cannot serve as the
confidence half of the bar today — it has one value across every device row
ever pulled. After this bead it starts moving, so one option is to ship as-is,
pull the device in a week, and pick the number from the actual distribution.
The other is to use a quantity that already discriminates (e.g. per-window
extent-anchor tier, which the ledger already carries) instead of a show scalar.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
=== DAN'S RULING, 2026-08-12: SELF-PROMOTION GOES ALL THE WAY TO AUTO — CONDITIONAL ON HIGH CONFIDENCE ===

Asked whether self-promotion should stop at .manual (the button) or continue to .auto (the app cuts audio unasked), Dan: 'yes it should go all the way to auto if it is high confidence.'

So the ladder runs end to end without a human in it. shadow -> manual -> auto, all on the detector's own confirmations.

THE CONDITION IS LOAD-BEARING AND IT DOES NOT EXIST YET. This is the part whoever implements it must not skate past. 'If it is high confidence' is a real precondition, and the quantity that is supposed to carry it — skipTrustScore — provably does not:

  DISTINCT skipTrustScore across every device pull ever taken = {0.5}. One value. Six profile rows, three pulls.
  A new show is CREATED at 0.5 (AdDetectionService.swift:13008, the path that runs).
  The bar is shadowToManualTrustScore 0.4 / manualToAutoTrustScore 0.75.
  correction_events / ad_listen_rewinds / implicit_feedback_events = 0 / 0 / 0 in all three pulls.

So the standing check answers badly: what would skipTrustScore read if detection on this show had never been good? 0.5 — identical to a show observed a hundred times correctly, identical to one never observed at all. It is not a confidence measure today. Shipping auto-promotion gated on it would be gating on a constant, which is not a gate.

WHAT THIS RULING THEREFORE REQUIRES, IN ORDER:
 1. playhead-2qz6 — the counter counts EPISODES, not backfills. In flight. Without it 'manualToAutoObservations: 8' is satisfied inside one episode and the auto rung is reached on ~one episode of evidence.
 2. A quantity that actually discriminates, to carry 'high confidence'. skipTrustScore only starts moving once mn5e's caller lands, so the distribution becomes MEASURABLE on the next pull — but it is not measured yet. Candidates worth weighing rather than assuming: the per-window extent-anchor tier the ledger already carries (which does vary), FM/rediff provenance, or skipTrustScore once it has field spread. DO NOT pick a number before there is a distribution to pick it from. That is the defect class this project keeps paying out on.
 3. Only then wire the manual -> auto rung on self-observation.

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE, and must be preserved: demotion. Two vetoes still take auto -> manual (autoToManualFalseSignals: 2), and a vetoed show must not climb back on self-observation alone — manual -> auto requires recentFalseSkipSignals == 0 and only a banner Yes decays it. Dan's per-edge ruling still bounds what may auto-skip at all: outer edges free, inner edges eat the show; a mark is worth far less than a wrong skip. And byte-exact rediff DAI remains exempt from show trust entirely (playhead-gard, shipped).

STANDING ORDER FOR THE IMPLEMENTER: the ruling authorises the DESTINATION, not a shortcut to it. If the honest answer after 2qz6 is 'no quantity here separates good detection from bad, so high-confidence cannot be evaluated', that is a finding to report — not a reason to promote on observations alone.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
=== DAN'S CLARIFICATION, same conversation: THE QUESTION IS PER-EVIDENCE-CLASS, NOT PER-SHOW ===

'I also think it's not as simple as "should a show promote itself" — Rediff is incredibly high confidence, it should always be auto. But other evidence isn't as strong.'

This reframes the ruling above and it is the more important half. A single per-show mode collapses evidence classes that have wildly different certainty, and asking 'has this SHOW earned auto?' is the wrong question when the answer differs per detector within the same episode.

IT IS ALSO ALREADY HALF-BUILT, which is corroboration rather than coincidence. playhead-gard shipped exactly this axis:
  SkipDetectorClass.swift:96-103   .rediffByteExact -> consultsShowTrust == false
  SkipDetectorClass.swift:112      showIndependentSeedMode: SkipMode = .auto
  DetectorTrustLedger.swift:172-179 seeds .auto with a clean history when no ledger entry exists
  the other three classes — .segmentAggregated, .userAsserted, .fusion — DO consult show trust
So byte-exact rediff already ignores the show ladder and starts at auto. Dan's 'rediff should always be auto' is SHIPPED, not pending. It is not what is blocking a skip today; playhead-mqqd is (every window is markOnly at write time and never reaches the trust gate at all).

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THIS BEAD, restated:
 - The show-level ladder mn5e wires governs ONLY the classes that consult show trust. That is the correct scope and it should be said out loud in the code, because 'a clean show promotes itself' reads as if it governs everything.
 - 'High confidence' therefore does NOT need to be one scalar. It needs to be per class, which is the standing 2026-07-17 ruling ('per-class certainty, not one global threshold') and matches the per-detector ledger gard already persists in detectorTrustJSON.
 - This weakens the case for hunting a single show-level confidence quantity (see the skipTrustScore = {0.5} finding above). The discriminating quantity may already exist per-class in the ledger. Look there BEFORE inventing a show scalar.

THE OPEN QUESTION THIS LEAVES, and it is the real one: for the classes that are NOT byte-exact rediff — fusion, segment-aggregated — should self-observation carry them to auto at all, or is manual their ceiling absent a user signal? Dan's 'other evidence isn't as strong' implies a lower ceiling but does not set it. That is the question to put to him when this resumes, and it is narrower and better-posed than the one I asked.

=== R1 VERDICT: DO NOT MERGE. Two HIGH findings, 13 gate-blocking regressions, and the branch does something I told the reviewer it did not. ===

MY BRIEF WAS WRONG AND THE REVIEWER CAUGHT IT. I wrote that the 13 schema drift pins 'were all bumped 48->49 and none missed'. THE OPPOSITE IS TRUE — all 13 are stale at 48, and the full plan reports EXACTLY 13 NEW failures, every one a pin. I asserted from pattern (fzrw and 3zxd implementers did bump theirs) instead of checking. The implementer's own 133-test scoped control could never have seen them, which is why nobody noticed: it never ran the full plan.

The reviewer deliberately did NOT fix them, and the reasoning is right: these pins are checkpoints whose comment says they are 'pinned to the LITERAL head, so whoever bumps the schema next has to come here and read this rung'. A reviewer silently bumping 13 assertions launders the review the guard exists to force. They must be bumped by whoever owns the schema change, reading each rung.

=== THE FINDING THAT MATTERS: THIS BRANCH ACTIVATES THE AUTO RUNG ===

I briefed that the auto rung was safely out of reach because skipTrustScore reads 0.5 on every profile row in every pull. That premise is exactly what this branch invalidates, and I missed the implication:

  skipTrustScore read 0.5 everywhere BECAUSE NOTHING EVER MOVED IT — recordSuccessfulObservation had no caller.
  Giving it a caller un-freezes it. Trust then climbs +0.10 per episode.
  auto lands at EPISODE 8 with ZERO user gestures, and recentFalseSkipSignals == 0 is trivially satisfied on an unplayed library.
  It reaches real skips: DetectorTrustLedger.seed copies profile.mode verbatim into every show-governed class, and SkipOrchestrator.swift:6796/6823 acts on .auto.

So the branch as it stands ships self-promotion to auto — the thing Dan deferred pending the counter fix AND a high-confidence quantity. Filed playhead-lqcp (P0).

AND 'HIGH CONFIDENCE' IS NOT IMPLEMENTED, TWICE OVER:
  averageConfidence is read ONCE, in the create closure, and discarded on every update. It never gates a promotion.
  manualToAutoTrustScore >= 0.75 is VACUOUS: trust is 0.2 + 0.10(N-1), so it clears at N=7 while the observation clause demands N=8. The threshold can NEVER withhold a promotion. It is decoration.

MEASURED REAL CONFIDENCES, and this is the number Dan needs for the product decision: 0.38-0.63 (verbatim device-pull values, DE0784D8MidRollPodFixture.swift:202-232), against a 0.7 detector floor used elsewhere in the system. A meaningful 'high confidence' bar would rarely fire on real ads.

=== TWO MORE PRODUCTION FINDINGS ===
playhead-fh5v (P1): 'the only writer of observationCount' is FALSE. TrustScoringService.applyCorrectObservation:1055/1097 increments it too, with a LIVE caller at SkipOrchestrator.swift:5927 (banner Yes). Four Yes taps in one episode = four episodes of credit, with no claim row — and it breaks the bead's own two-numbers-must-agree diagnostic by construction.
playhead-89x6 (P1): the claim key is not an episode key. resolveAnalysisAssetId:6823-6831 DELIBERATELY inserts a second permanent row on re-download/feed correction; and the 0hi9 race is still open on one side — AnalysisCoordinator.resolveSession still does check-then-insert with plain insertAsset, never fzrw's atomic guard, and fzrw WIDENED the overlap by moving registration to download-completion. Over-counting is the unsafe direction; magnitude ~2x versus the ~9x being fixed, so the bead is still a large net win.

=== WHAT IS SOUND ===
V49 reset: forward-only, idempotent, inside BEGIN/COMMIT, in both ladder call sites, non-vacuously tested (M1 and M2 both redden it), demoted profiles stay demoted, mode/trust/vetoes/priors verified untouched. M3a proves the PRODUCTION ladder is covered, not just migrateOnlyForTesting.
Claim idempotence for its stated purpose: repeat backfills, re-drives, transcript-version bumps and the 15d0 resume all genuinely no-op.
playhead-kfts (P2) confirmed: podcast_planner_state.observedEpisodeCount has the same bug and computePlannerStableFlag gates on >= 5, so a show reads 'recall-stable' after ~half an episode. Correctly out of scope.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
WHAT THIS BEAD ACTUALLY DELIVERS TO A LISTENER — verified 2026-08-12 against SHIPPED main (not the branch), because R6's commit a7c55403 contradicted a claim this branch was built on and the correction changes how the bead should be read.

SHADOW AND MANUAL ARE BEHAVIOURALLY IDENTICAL. SkipOrchestrator.swift:6814-6822 on main:

    case .shadow:
        let decision = SkipDecisionState.confirmed
        logDecision(... reason: "Shadow mode -- detection logged, no skip fired")
        return decision
    case .manual:
        let decision = SkipDecisionState.confirmed
        logDecision(... reason: "Manual mode -- confirmed, awaiting user tap")
        return decision

Same return value. Only the log REASON STRING differs. So promoting a show out of shadow into manual changes nothing a listener can hear or see through this gate.

THIS BEAD'S TITLE IS 'a show can NEVER leave shadow mode without a banner tap ... ZERO auto-skips in a 22-hour overnight run'. The first clause was a real defect and is fixed. The causal link to the second clause does NOT hold: leaving shadow was never what would have produced an auto-skip, because only .auto skips and manual is not on the way to auto for any class except by the seed.

SO WHAT IS THE BEAD WORTH? Three things, none of them 'the show escapes shadow':
  1. The COUNTER UNIT is now episodes rather than backfills (2qz6), on the show column. That is a ~24x correction and it governs every threshold read against it.
  2. The AUTO RUNG is governed rather than accidental (lqcp + AutoPromotionConfidenceEvidence), so Dan's 'other evidence isn't as strong' is enforced structurally instead of by a threshold nobody could reach.
  3. playhead-u0vv makes byte-exact rediff's .auto a FLOOR a listener can restore rather than a default lost on first veto — which is the only rung that produces a skip at all.

All three are dormant until rediff windows exist. None of them is wasted.

AND THE REASON lqcp GAVE FOR CLOSING THE RUNG WAS WRONG, though the decision was right. Its safety argument was that 'shadow -> manual unlocks a BANNER, and the worst case is a card the user ignores'. It unlocks nothing: evaluateWindow returns .confirmed either way, evaluateAndPush banners only on .applied, and the suggest banner is not mode-gated. The closure is SAFER than it was argued to be. R6 corrected the comment; the behaviour was never at issue.

WHERE THE SKIP IS ACTUALLY BLOCKED, established on playhead-mqqd the same day: every ad_window on the device is eligibilityGate=markOnly at WRITE time because all 17 confirmed rows carry startEdgeAnchor=unanchored, and playhead-2350's extent gate (armed, AdDetectionService.swift:1187) makes an invented edge banner-only. Those rows never reach the mode switch above at all. The only producer of a start anchor is rediff (.rediffByteExact on both edges of a strict slot), and rediff produced nothing because day-0 never fired — playhead-oa82. That, not this bead, is the binding constraint on a first hearable skip.

title: The ad scan has no partial-progress persistence, so it cannot use a short background window at all — transcription can
description:
THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, established 2026-08-10/11 from device pulls and named as the highest-value lever after playhead-4xqf located the width loss.

THE MEASUREMENT, db-db-r2wait -> db-evening2, one 4h20m span on the post-wipe device:

  transcript_chunks     2781 -> 3549   (+768)
  semantic_scan_results   17 ->   17   (+0)

Eight background windows were GRANTED in that span, totalling ~166 s of real background time: 19, 35, 22, 26, 25, 13, 13, 13 seconds. Every one outcome=expired, jobsCompleted=0. Transcription advanced 768 chunks. The ad scan produced NOTHING.

WHY THE ASYMMETRY, and it is the whole bead: transcription is INCREMENTAL and persists partial work — that is what playhead-26od and playhead-fil5 bought (a killed pass no longer discards every screened window; the claim is durable). The ad scan has no equivalent. Its unit of work cannot START inside a 13-35 s grant, let alone finish: FMInferenceDeadline.metadata alone exceeds the whole window. So the scan spends the grant and persists nothing, every time.

REACH IS NOT THE PROBLEM HERE. Windows are being granted. Two of the eight even did real work (16:58 preanalysis_recovery 'recovered_work', 17:19 backfill 'admitted_work'). The scan simply cannot consume a grant of that size.

CORROBORATING COUNTS, db-vtjxverdict (33 assets): ZERO backfill_jobs have EVER reached 'complete' — 15 deferred, 1 failed, 2 queued, 1 running. Post-wipe (5 assets): zero complete, 1 deferred, 2 queued. Across both device states, not one completed backfill job exists. FM has left evidence_events on 2 of 33 assets.

WHAT THIS BLOCKS DOWNSTREAM: playhead-4xqf established that ad WIDTH is lost at candidate generation because FM is the only channel that can anchor a block, and playhead-881t established why FM anchors nothing. But even a perfect FM anchor path fires almost nowhere while FM completes on 2 of 33 assets. Width work is bounded by this bead.

THE REMEDY SHAPE — already proven on this codebase, not yet applied here. 26od/fil5 made the coarse pass persist incrementally and made its claim durable. The same treatment for the scan: a unit of work sized to fit a short grant, and partial progress that survives the window ending. ESTABLISH FIRST what the natural increment is (per-shard? per-window? per-FM-call?) and what the resume key must be so two grants do not redo the same audio — playhead-wxsv already keyed backfill jobs on (assetId, phase, offset), which may be the right seam.

SYMPTOMS THIS WOULD RESOLVE, filed separately and NOT to be duplicated: playhead-k63m (a job that cannot finish inside any granted window retries forever and holds the head of the queue), playhead-78ry (five assets' re-drive budget spent on passes that reached Stage 4 and bailed), playhead-z3jg (a zero-coverage pass re-queues with no circuit-breaker). Those are consequences of the same missing mechanism; this bead is the mechanism.

CAUTION: do NOT reach for a bigger window or a longer deadline. iOS grant duration is not ours to choose — it was 196-295 s earlier the same day and 13-35 s that evening, tracking user activity. The work must fit the grant, not the reverse.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
=== R1 VERDICT (2026-08-11) — one HIGH production defect FIXED, and a CORRECTION to this bead's own flagship number ===

DEFECT F1, fixed at d495287a. The phase scoping I shipped in 25607831 was ONE-DIRECTIONAL, and the missing direction is the one that strands audio. The call site guards 'job.phase != .fullEpisodeScan -> screenedRows = []', so a targeted job is narrowed by nobody. But fetchSemanticScanResults(analysisAssetId:scanPass:) (AnalysisStore.swift:18209-18213) filters on analysisAssetId and scanPass ONLY — there is no jobPhase column in the WHERE clause — so a .fullEpisodeScan job WAS being narrowed by targeted phases' rows.

Those rows over-claim by construction. TargetedWindowNarrower.narrowedResult returns the union of DISJOINT per-anchor intervals (TargetedWindowNarrower.swift:784); FoundationModelClassifier.planPassA packs each window from a contiguous slice OF THAT SPARSE ARRAY and stamps startTime: min(...), endTime: max(...) (FoundationModelClassifier.swift:3029-3046). A window straddling two intervals persists a span covering every segment between them, none of which was ever in a prompt. .scanRandomAuditWindows is the worst case: a sparse sample whose merged span is nearly the whole episode. makeScanResult writes it as passA/.success/current cohort/current version/no sentinel, so it passed every clause of my predicate.

Reachable because jobId = hash(assetId, phase, offset) is not keyed on policy and coveragePlanner.plan(for:) is re-evaluated every runPendingBackfill: recallDegrading / auditMissDetected / sponsorDriftDetected / episodesSinceLastFullRescan all flip a mature show back to fullCoverage WITHOUT changing the transcript version or the cohort.

Fix: jobPhase is a REQUIRED argument on both helpers — deliberately not defaulted, since a default re-opens the hole by omission. Measured cost zero: all 188 passA rows across both pulls carry jobPhase=fullEpisodeScan, so it is latent, arming the first time a show reaches coldStartEpisodeThreshold with stableRecall.

=== CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S 99.8% — the arithmetic HELD, the premise did NOT ===

R1 verified the figure exactly: denominator 1,724.94 = final-transcript max(endTime) 1919.40 (752 pass='final' chunks) minus cursor 194.46; numerator 1,721.28 = the union of examined passA window seconds above the cursor at version 200ebdd5; 1721.28/1724.94 = 99.788%. Every component reproduced.

BUT the clause 'reusable at the CURRENT transcript version' is false on the pull. backfill_jobs.attemptTranscriptVersion is stamped by markBackfillJobRunning (:876-879) from the same inputs.transcriptVersion that isReusable compares against — apples to apples — and on 66D32039 it reads 9e574deb, while the ten passA rows carry only 9afa5627 (4) and 200ebdd5 (6). ZERO rows qualify. The narrowing would have dropped 0 s, not 1,721 s, on the very asset this bead is measured on.

Corpus-wide: 19 of 188 passA rows (10.1%) carry their own job's last-attempt version; 6 of 15 assets have none at all.

WHAT THAT DOES AND DOES NOT MEAN. It does not make the change wrong — it is self-priming: rows written under the version in hand become reusable to the next grant once the transcript settles. It does mean the flagship number is what the fix WOULD have saved had the versions matched, not what it saves today, and it should be stated that way everywhere it appears. I wrote that number and I am correcting it rather than leaving it to be re-derived.

Minor, same family: this bead's prose says 'rows covering 1.0-194.0 and 196.0-1919.0' — two spans. Under the actual non-bridging merge rule ('<=' merges touch and overlap only) the same rows yield SIX, with 0.42 / 0.36 / 1.68 / 0.42 s inter-row gaps. The outcome is identical because no segment straddles those pauses, but the prose overstates contiguity.

=== WHAT R1 PROVED, not just asserted ===
Mutation, against a SHA-256-pinned pristine copy, restored and verified both times, never 'git checkout -- .':
  M2 deleted the new 'row.jobPhase == jobPhase.rawValue' clause -> GATE_EXIT=65, 6 issues, red on all five phases named individually plus the legacy unattributed sentinel.
  M1 deleted 'row.didExamineWindow' -> 11 issues in the target suite (all 10 statuses plus the no-work sentinel) AND 3 integration failures in BackfillRateLimitDeferTests, so the clause is load-bearing end to end. (That mutant wedged xcodebuild; the RED verdict was recorded before the wedge and the pid was killed.)
Control and final: 4 suites, 86 tests, GATE_EXIT=0 both times. lint --changed clean. Never the full plan, never --accept-baseline, never any PLAYHEAD_SKIP_*.

OUT OF SCOPE, FILED NOT FIXED: playhead-7cjo — AnalysisStore.readScannedRegions credits adScanCoveredSec from ANY passA row asset-wide with no cohort, version or phase filter, so coverage now over-reports exactly the sparse targeted spans the scanner refuses to reuse. Same defect class, one layer down, and a measurement error rather than audio loss.

comments.text:
=== DEVICE EVIDENCE FOR THE R2 QUESTION (virgin-DB overnight pull, 2026-08-11, build 9e31bf1c) ===
This is a DIFFERENT database from the one R1 measured, and it answers the reuse question with fresh data.

TRANSCRIPT-VERSION CHURN IS REAL AND LARGE. transcript_chunks holds exactly ONE distinct transcriptVersion per asset. semantic_scan_results holds up to SIX per asset. Matching each scan row's transcriptVersion against its own job's attemptTranscriptVersion:

  asset       rows  MATCH  distinct row-versions
  590D6656      10     10  1     <- scanned AFTER its transcript settled
  B80D3EE0       4      4  1     <- same
  66D32039      18      7  3
  F7BB38BB      34      1  4
  60DFF7B4      29      1  6
  TOTAL         95     23 (24%)

R1 measured 19 of 188 (10.1%) on the older pulls; this one reads 24%. Same phenomenon, and the split is the informative part.

THE PATTERN, and it is exactly the wrong way round for this bead's purpose. The two assets at 100% match are the ones whose transcript had SETTLED before the scan ran. The three that raced their own transcript are 7/18, 1/34, 1/29. So the reuse predicate works precisely when there is least to reuse, and fails precisely on the new-episode case — where transcript and scan run concurrently, which is the case the product's time-to-value depends on.

R1's 'self-priming' explanation is therefore CORRECT BUT NARROW: rows do become reusable once the transcript stops moving. What it does not say is that during the window this bead exists to optimise, most rows are written at a version the next attempt will reject. 66D32039 IS STILL STUCK AT 194.46 AND HAS NOW FAILED. Same asset, same cursor, on a fresh database:
  status=failed  retry=3  deferReason=expiredWithoutProgress-fullEpisodeScan
  cursor={"processedUnitCount":0,"lastProcessedUpperBoundSec":194.46}

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
=== R2 VERDICT (2026-08-11) — one rail gap FIXED, Job 2 answered NO with a byte-exact witness, three prose claims corrected ===

FINDING F-A (MEDIUM, rail gap, FIXED at f98ee3ba). The call-site guard R1's fix leans on had NO RAIL. Mutation M1 deleted 'if job.phase != .fullEpisodeScan { screenedRows = [] }' outright and the whole 82-test scoped gate stayed GREEN (GATE_EXIT=0). The row-side clause R1 added cannot cover it: screenedSpans refuses a job the rows of ANOTHER phase, and the case that loses audio is a targeted phase's RE-DRIVE reading spans it banked ITSELF — row.jobPhase == jobPhase.rawValue matches, every other clause matches, and the phase's whole narrowed subset vanishes. Those spans over-claim across the disjoint per-anchor intervals exactly the way another phase's would. The test the call-site comment named as the catcher ('targeted phases persist distinct passA rows on narrowed subsets') only ever drives a FIRST run, where no rows exist yet; that claim in the comment is now corrected.

New rail: 'playhead-15d0: a targeted phase's re-drive is narrowed by nothing — not even its own rows'. It asserts over the LINE REFS the classifier was handed, because scan-result ids are deterministic and the persisted rows dedupe — row count, job count and the persisted set are identical either way. Under the same mutant: 3 coarse windows -> 0, GATE_EXIT=65.

=== JOB 2 — IS THE FIX INERT IN PRODUCTION? NO, but the 99.8 % is off by two orders of magnitude ===

WHAT RECOMPUTES transcriptVersion, established from source and then WITNESSED. runBackfill canonicalizes -> canonicalTimeOrder -> TranscriptAtomizer.atomize, whose version is versionHash(ofSorted:) (TranscriptAtom.swift:198-206): SHA-256 over, per chunk, a 4-byte big-endian length prefix of normalizedText followed by its UTF-8, truncated to 16 bytes. It is a pure function of the ordered multiset of normalizedText over the canonical chunk set — no windowing, no locality. isReusable requires exact equality, so ONE APPENDED CHUNK INVALIDATES EVERY ROW FOR THE ASSET, including rows over audio the append never touched. A per-EPISODE identity answering a per-WINDOW question — the standing defect class, one layer under this bead.

That is not argued, it is reproduced. I implemented the chain in Python from source alone and it reproduces backfill_jobs.attemptTranscriptVersion BYTE-FOR-BYTE on 4 of the 5 assets in db-overnight5 (a DB I had never seen when the script was written) and 2 of the 3 in db-evening2. Every mismatch is an asset whose transcript was still growing — 60DFF7B4 on both pulls, deferReason cancelled-during-fullEpisodeScan. And 66D32039's dead '9afa5627...' is byte-exact the hash of the 299 fast chunks ending at or below 300 s: that scan ran on a 300 s prefix and the rest of the episode arriving invalidated it wholesale.

(Note for whoever reads transcript_chunks.transcriptVersion and finds one value per asset: that column is a STAMP on the chunk row, not the identity. isReusable compares against the freshly COMPUTED hash. Reading the column as 'the transcript's version' would itself be the defect class.)

WHAT IT IS WORTH, applying the shipped predicate and merge rule to every coverage job:
  db-evening2 + db-vtjxverdict, 22 resumable jobs: 3 fire, 19 drop nothing — 715.7 s of 60,594.2 s of above-cursor audio, 1.18 %.
  db-overnight5, 5 jobs (virgin install, overnight, pulled 2026-08-11): FOUR of five fire — 726.9 s of 6,472.1 s, 11.2 %; over jobs that can still resume (two are terminally failed), 343.4 s of 4,747.2 s, 7.2 %.
  Per asset on the fresh pull: 590D6656 103.7 s (25.5 %), 66D32039 383.6 s (22.2 %, but the job is failed so it will never cash it), B80D3EE0 198.4 s (5.3 %), 60DFF7B4 41.3 s (6.9 %), F7BB38BB 0.

On 66D32039 at db-evening2 — the asset the 99.8 % headline is measured on — the answer is 0.0 s, 0.0 %: current version 9e574deb, rows at 9afa5627 (4) and 200ebdd5 (6).

SELF-PRIMING IS CONFIRMED, and the qualifier is the finding. 66D32039 went from ZERO qualifying rows on db-evening2 to SEVEN on db-overnight5. The priming completed. It bought nothing only because the job reached failed/expiredWithoutProgress first. Priming completes when TRANSCRIPTION does and cannot complete before — which is why the yield is 'whatever the last attempt banked after the transcript stopped moving' and nothing else, and why the two db-overnight5 assets whose transcripts had settled match at 10/10 and 4/4 while the three that raced match at 7/18, 1/34 and 1/29.

Not widened. The fix for the underlying issue is a per-WINDOW content hash so an append invalidates only the windows it touches; that is a design change, not a clause, and it needs a decision rather than a review round.

=== JOB 3 — PROSE CORRECTED (three claims, all in this bead's diff) ===

1. The 99.8 % is now stated as what the narrowing WOULD have saved had the versions matched, with the measured yield beside it, in BackfillJobRunner.swift and in the test suite's own doc.
2. 'rows covering 1.0-194.0 and 196.0-1919.0 — the whole transcribed extent' is SIX merged spans — 0.78-115.26, 115.68-194.46, 195.66-276.18, 276.54-941.64, 943.32-1902.78, 1903.2-1919.4 — covering 1,914.54 of the transcript's 1,918.62 s; the '<=' rule bridges none of the five gaps (0.42, 1.20, 0.36, 1.68, 0.42 s). The extent is 0.78-1919.4, not 1.0-1919.0. The field-case fixture now uses the six REAL rows and pins spans.count == 6, so a future bridging 'simplification' cannot make the old prose true by changing the code.
3. NEW, and R1 did not flag it: 'coarseCheckpointWalk stops at a 1.2 s pause in speech' is false — the walk never examines time adjacency at all (BackfillJobRunner.swift:2728-2771). It advances over an unbroken run of FULLY COVERED plans and caps at the earliest uncovered plan's start. The 194.46 cursor is two windows into the four the first attempt banked, not a property of the transcript.
4. Also corrected, and load-bearing because it is the justification for the whole predicate: 'fetchCoverageSummariesByAssetIds already reads those same spans, under this same predicate' and 'the same three conditions the coverage reader and the suppression guard already apply'. readScannedRegions applies ONE of the three (didExamineWindow) plus scanPass and a positive width — no cohort, no transcript version, no phase. That is why it credits all ten of 66D32039's rows and reports the episode ad-scanned while this function qualifies zero. Same defect class, opposite direction; already filed by R1 as playhead-7cjo.

=== JOB 4 — NO NEW PRODUCTION DEFECT, and what I cleared ===

Cleared by reading and, where it mattered, by data: scanCohortJSON at the call site is the runner's own (what rows are stamped with — confirmed equal on every device row); .fullEpisodeScan is never handed narrowedInputs (narrowedInputs returns rootInputs for it unconditionally, :5361); the empty-segments short-circuit returns a CoverageOutcome with nil cursor halves so an emptied job cannot advance the cursor; the sentinel is excluded twice over (isNoWorkSentinel AND the 0-width clause — every sentinel on the pulls is 0.0/0.0); the '<=' merge is order-insensitive under ties; the doc's 'all 188 passA rows carry jobPhase=fullEpisodeScan' is confirmed (14 + 174). releaseInFlightReservationIfUnclaimed is DownloadManager's and is not reachable from this diff.

RESIDUAL RISK, stated as a risk and NOTED ON playhead-a1x0 rather than fixed here. 15d0 punches INTERIOR holes in the segment array, which is a second source of exactly what a1x0 is about. planPassA packs windows from contiguous ARRAY slices and stamps min/max over the slice, and coarseCheckpointWalk sets walkedUpperBound = plan.endTime with no adjacency check, so a window straddling a 15d0 hole advances the cursor across it. It is LESS severe than a1x0's transcript-hole case — the audio in a 15d0 hole IS covered by a durable row at the moment the cursor is written, so the claim is true when made — but the ROW is version-gated and the CURSOR is not, so after the next append the rows stop counting and the cursor keeps deleting. Net: 15d0 lets audio screened at an older version be laundered into a version-blind cursor one generation further back than before. Capping the cursor at the first interior hole is the threshold decision a1x0 exists to make, and 15d0's holes would want a different answer from transcript holes. One thing carried to a1x0: its own argument for not capping cites that those re-attempts 'cost ZERO FM inference', and 15d0 is now a second reason that short-circuit fires.

=== JOB 5 — VERDICT BY MUTATION ===
All runs scoped to 3 suites (BackfillScreenedWindowResumeTests, BackfillJobRunnerTests, BackfillRateLimitDeferTests), REQUESTED_SUITES=3 confirmed against 3 reported in every log, selective so the raw xcodebuild code stands.
  baseline (pristine)                       GATE_EXIT=0, 82 tests
  M1  call-site phase guard DELETED         GATE_EXIT=0, 82 tests — SURVIVED. The finding.
  R2 fixes + new rail                       GATE_EXIT=0, 83 tests
  M1b same mutant, against the new rail     GATE_EXIT=65 — 'the targeted re-drive submitted 0 coarse windows where run 1 submitted 3', both expectations red
  final clean                               GATE_EXIT=0, 83 tests
Mutations applied and restored from a SHA-256-pinned copy, 'shasum -a 256 -c' OK both times, git status --porcelain -- Playhead PlayheadTests scripts clean after each. Never 'git checkout -- .', never 'git add -A', never --accept-baseline, never any PLAYHEAD_SKIP_*. lint --changed clean.

I did NOT re-run R1's M2 and I did not attack the clauses R1 already reddened. Not proven by me and left as a limit: the row-side jobPhase clause carries R1's verdict, not mine.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
=== CORRECTION: the '1.2-second pause in speech' story is WRONG (R2, 2026-08-11) ===

I framed this bead — and reported to Dan twice — that asset 66D32039's cursor stops at 194.46 because of a 1.2-second pause in speech. That is not what the code does. R2 read coarseCheckpointWalk (BackfillJobRunner.swift:2728-2771) and it never examines TIME ADJACENCY at all. The walk stops at the first plan that is not FULLY COVERED. The pause was a coincidence of the data I happened to look at, and I built a causal story on it.

The distinction matters for whoever fixes this: 'the walk is confused by a gap in speech' suggests a tolerance or a bridging rule. 'The walk stops at the first incompletely-covered plan' says the cursor is a contiguous-prefix scalar and the remedy is about coverage bookkeeping, not about audio geometry. Two different fixes.

R2 also corrected a second claim of mine: readScannedRegions applies ONE of the three conditions, not three, which invalidates the 'the predicate is borrowed from the coverage reader' justification I used to argue the predicate was already vetted.

=== R2 VERDICT: one MEDIUM rail gap, FIXED at f98ee3ba ===

F-A. The call-site guard 'if job.phase != .fullEpisodeScan { screenedRows = [] }' that 25607831 added had NO RAIL. Mutation M1 deleted it outright and the 82-test scoped gate stayed GATE_EXIT=0. R1's row-side clause cannot cover it: screenedSpans refuses a job ANOTHER phase's rows, but the audio-losing case is a targeted phase's RE-DRIVE reading spans it banked itself, which over-claim across its own disjoint per-anchor intervals identically. The test the guard's own comment named as its catcher only ever drives a first run. New rail asserts over submitted line refs (scan-result ids dedupe); under the same mutant it goes 3 coarse windows -> 0, GATE_EXIT=65.

=== JOB 2 ANSWERED: the fix is NOT inert, but the 99.8% is off by TWO ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE ===

R2 reproduced transcriptVersion from source in Python and matched backfill_jobs.attemptTranscriptVersion BYTE-FOR-BYTE on 4 of 5 assets in db-overnight5 (a database it had not seen when the script was written) and 2 of 3 in db-evening2. Every mismatch is an asset still transcribing. So this is confirmed, not argued:

  transcriptVersion = SHA-256 over the length-prefixed normalizedText of EVERY canonical chunk.

ONE APPENDED CHUNK INVALIDATES EVERY ROW FOR THE ASSET. It is a PER-EPISODE identity answering a PER-WINDOW question — the standing defect class, sitting underneath this bead's own reuse key. 66D32039's dead 9afa5627 is byte-exactly the hash of the 299 fast chunks ending <= 300s.

MEASURED YIELD, the honest replacement for 99.8%:
  older pulls      3 of 22 jobs fire   715.7s of 60,594.2s = 1.18%
  fresh overnight  4 of 5 jobs fire    726.9s of  6,472.1s = 11.2% (7.2% over jobs that can still resume)
  66D32039 at db-evening2, where the headline was measured:  0.0s

R1's self-priming claim is CONFIRMED — that asset went 0 -> 7 qualifying rows between the two pulls — and its limit is now named: priming completes when TRANSCRIPTION does, never before. So the reuse cannot help the concurrent transcribe-and-scan case, which is the new-episode case the product's time-to-value depends on.

RESIDUAL RISK, filed on playhead-a1x0 not fixed here: 15d0 punches interior holes in the segment array, a second source of a1x0's problem. Less severe (the audio IS row-covered when the cursor is written) but the row is version-gated and the cursor is not, so 15d0 launders older-version screening into a version-blind cursor one generation further back.

STREAK: zero. R1 found a defect, R2 found a rail gap. Two consecutive clean rounds still required; R3 dispatched.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
=== R3 VERDICT (2026-08-11) — ZERO production defects. One surviving mutant, LOW, safe-direction, REPORTED NOT FIXED. Nothing in the tree changed. ===

All five gate runs scoped to SIX suites (BackfillScreenedWindowResumeTests, BackfillJobRunnerTests, BackfillRateLimitDeferTests, BackfillCoarseCheckpointTests, BackfillCoverageTerminalTests, BackfillStallBoundTests) — REQUESTED_SUITES=6 printed as line 1 of every log and matched against '6 suites' reported by xcodebuild every time. Selective, so the raw xcodebuild code stands. Mutations applied and restored from a SHA-256-pinned pristine copy; 'shasum -a 256 -c' OK after every restore; 'git status --porcelain -- Playhead PlayheadTests scripts' clean after every one. Never 'git checkout -- .', never 'git add -A', never --accept-baseline, never any PLAYHEAD_SKIP_*. lint --changed clean. HEAD still f98ee3ba.

  baseline (pristine)                        GATE_EXIT=0, 125 tests
  M-A  guard reads coveragePolicy != .fullCoverage instead of phase != .fullEpisodeScan
                                             GATE_EXIT=0, 125 tests — SURVIVED
  M-B  composition: screened narrowing applied to rootInputs (resume narrowing dropped)
                                             GATE_EXIT=65, 59 issues
  M-C  composition ORDER SWAPPED             GATE_EXIT=0, 125 tests — equivalent mutant, see below
  final clean + R3 probe                     GATE_EXIT=0, 126 tests

=== JOB 1 — R2's RAIL IS CORRECTLY SHAPED. No mutation of the guard can keep the line refs. ===

R2's rail asserts more than the count: 'shape(resubmitted) == shape(refsAfterFirst)' compares the exact sorted ref sets. The guard is boolean, so a mutation either leaves screenedRows empty (correct behaviour) or fetches them — and when it fetches, a targeted phase's own rows cover its own submitted segments exactly (that is how they were written), so the narrowing removes the whole subset and 3 windows become 0. The only middle ground is a guard that discriminates AMONG the three targeted phases, which changes the count. There is no single-edit mutation of the guard that breaks it and preserves the refs. Keeping the line refs while breaking the guard needs a SECOND edit neutering 'jobPhase: job.phase' as well, and R1's row-side clause is what makes that second edit necessary.

M-A is the honest exception and it does NOT break the targeted protection. Under 'job.coveragePolicy != .fullCoverage' every targeted job still gets screenedRows = [], so the rail is untouched — and it is untouched CORRECTLY. What M-A changes is the .periodicFullRescan case: CoveragePlanner.plan emits 'policy: .periodicFullRescan, phases: [.fullEpisodeScan]' (CoveragePlanner.swift:371-377), so under the mutant a periodic full rescan has phase == .fullEpisodeScan but policy != .fullCoverage and the whole 15d0 narrowing goes INERT for it. Non-equivalent, reachable (shouldUsePeriodicFullRescan fires on sponsorDriftDetected or every N episodes, on a mature show past coldStartEpisodeThreshold — the same reachability class as R1's own fix), and no test sees it.

WHY I DID NOT FIX IT, stated so the next round does not have to re-derive it. The mutant's ONLY effect is that a periodicFullRescan job loses the saving. It cannot strand audio, cannot advance a cursor, cannot corrupt a population. It is strictly the direction this whole function is allowed to move. R2's F-A was a rail gap on a direction that LOSES AUDIO, which is why it was worth a round; this one is not, and adding a rail costs another review cycle for a saving that is already latent. Reported for Dan's call rather than absorbed.

=== JOB 2 — THE COMPOSITION IS RAILED, and the order is not a rail question ===

M-B (apply the screened narrowing to rootInputs, i.e. drop narrowedForResume from the composition): GATE_EXIT=65. Two distinct tests redden — 'playhead-wxsv: a transcript that grows resumes the scan instead of restarting it' (BackfillJobRunnerTests:2201, 'resubmitted.isEmpty') and 'playhead-hvk0: 30 no-progress runner cycles never promote and never run away' (:967 'scans.count <= cap', :975 'coarseCallCount == firstCalls'). So the fear that 15d0 subsumed pmp9's only end-to-end witness is WRONG, though it is right about the fixture R2 edited: BackfillRateLimitDeferTests cannot tell the two apart, because with rows covering windows 0 and 2 the answer is coarseCallCount == 1 under 'both narrowings' AND under 'screened only'. The witnesses are elsewhere and they hold.

M-C (order swapped: narrowedForResume(narrowedForScreenedWindows(rootInputs, …), cursor:)): GREEN, and that is the correct outcome rather than a gap. The two are pure filters over the same array — narrowedForResume keeps 'endTime > cursor', narrowedForScreenedWindows keeps 'not fully inside a merged span' — and screenedSpans depends only on inputs.transcriptVersion, which neither narrowing touches. Filters commute, the early-return identity guards return equal values, and AssetInputs is a value type, so the two orders are byte-equal by construction. An equivalent mutant returning GREEN is not evidence of a missing rail, and no rail on the ordering is possible or wanted. The call-site comment's stated reason for the order ('on a first run it leaves the list untouched so screenedRows is empty') is a non-sequitur — screenedRows is empty on a first run because no rows exist, and the store read happens before either narrowing regardless — but the ORDER it justifies is harmless either way.
