=== JOB 3 — the cursor. NEW: 15d0's hole can land at the HEAD, and there the guarded and unguarded writers do opposite things. ===

R2's a1x0 filing is ACCURATE and I confirmed every link of it (planPassA min/max over an array slice, coarseCoverageWalk's walkedUpperBound = plan.endTime with no adjacency test, the version gate on rows and its absence on the cursor). What it does not say is that 15d0's holes are not confined to the interior. narrowedForResume drops at-or-below the cursor and narrowedForScreenedWindows then drops the segments IMMEDIATELY ABOVE it whenever a reusable row covers them — 66D32039's own shape (cursor 194.46, merged span 195.66-276.18, first plan then at 276.54, 82 s above).

DEMONSTRATED with a temporary probe (added, run, PASSED, deleted; suite hash restored byte-exact): screened row 10-30 over segments [10-20, 20-30, 30-100] leaves [30-100], and EpisodeSeconds.promoting(PlanListSeconds(100), priorEpisodeCursor: 10, firstPlannedStart: 30, bridge: adScanBridgeableGapSec) returns NIL, where the pre-15d0 firstPlannedStart of 10 promotes. BridgeToleranceSec.bridges is 'gapSec <= 5.0'.

So 41mu's head guard — the ONE cursor writer that has one — now reads 15d0's screened hole as unscanned audio and pins the cursor at prior, on exactly the shape this bead exists to exploit. Traced end to end: runJob:3431 -> CoverageOutcome:4163 -> underCoverageCursor:2467 -> promoting:1036-1044.

IT IS NOT A DEFECT, and the reasons are worth recording so nobody re-raises it. (a) No audio is lost — under-claiming throughout. (b) No FM cost — the screened narrowing drops the same audio the cursor would have, so the planner input is identical either way. (c) No retry regression — recordUnderCoverageTerminal charges a flat budget with no reset-on-progress clause, and the BG-expiry path goes through cursorAdvanced/salvagedCursor, which uses unsoundPlanListPromotion and has no head guard at all. (d) The only behavioural delta appears after a transcript append kills the rows, when a frozen cursor re-plans what an advanced one would have dropped — and re-planning audio whose screening died with its version is the SOUNDER answer, not the worse one.

What IS worth carrying: 15d0 concentrates cursor-writing on the three UNGUARDED sites, because the one guarded site now declines. Filed as a comment on playhead-a1x0, which is where the 'enforce the rule everywhere at 60 s' decision lives and which must now decide what a 15d0 hole IS — screened audio, not unread audio, and not distinguishable from the segment array alone.

Nothing in this diff makes a1x0 strictly worse than R2 described; the head position is an addition to the description, and Dan's ratified a1x0 decision already scopes 'interior and tail holes, not just the head'.

Also cleared this round, by reading rather than assertion: AssetInputs has exactly seven stored properties and both narrowers copy all seven explicitly (acousticBreaks is defaulted in the initialiser but passed by both), so no field is silently reset; the empty-segments sentinel takes 0/0 bounds from attemptedRange over an empty list and is excluded twice over; the .segmentListCompletion and .specialistScanCompletion cursors read jobInputs / the root list, not the narrowed one, so 15d0 does not move them.

=== JOB 4 — the corrected prose is TRUE, with one naming imprecision ===

Read BackfillJobRunner.swift:2726-2779 with the Read tool. The walk sorts plans by startTime, breaks at the first plan not in fullyCoveredPlanIndices, sets walkedUpperBound = plan.endTime, then caps at min(walked, earliest uncovered plan's startTime). It never compares one plan's endTime to the next plan's startTime, i.e. it never examines a GAP. R2's correction is correct.

Imprecision, not error: that code is coarseCoverageWalk (:2588). coarseCheckpointWalk (:2791) is a four-line wrapper that delegates to it, so the claim holds of the name R2 used, transitively — but the line citation 2728-2771 points at the callee.

99.8 % appears in exactly three places in the source (BackfillJobRunner.swift:3136, :3144, :3189) and once in the suite doc (BackfillScreenedWindowResumeTests.swift:15-16), and every one states it as what the narrowing WOULD have saved had the versions matched, with 'Do not quote 99.8 % as this function's yield' at :3189. No test NAME states it. The bead DESCRIPTION does not contain it at all — every occurrence in this bead is inside R1's and R2's own correction comments.

=== RESIDUAL, stated as risks ===

- The M-A gap above (LOW, safe direction, unfixed).
- Two doc comments are now stale in a way 15d0 introduced and did not update: CoverageOutcome.firstPlannedSegmentStartSec (:2113-2118) and its construction site (:4160-4162) both describe 'inputs' as the POST-narrowedForResume list. Post-15d0 it is post-BOTH. The CONCLUSION each draws ('this is literally where this run's plans begin') is still true — it is still the list handed to coarsePassA — so this is naming, not arithmetic, and it is why the head-guard interaction above went unnoticed.
- Not proven by me and left as a limit: R1's row-side jobPhase clause and didExamineWindow carry R1's verdicts, and R2's M1/M1b carry R2's. I did not re-run them.

title: CorrectionScope round-trip DESTROYS every show-scoped identity: podcastId is a feed URL, deserialize splits on its scheme colon
description:
Found in playhead-shjn R1 review. VERIFIED from source AND from device data.

`CorrectionScope.serialized` writes `"sponsorOnShow:\(podcastId):\(sponsor)"`
(UserCorrectionStore.swift:83). `deserialize` parses it by splitting the
remainder on its FIRST colon (UserCorrectionStore.swift:135-140), with the
comment "split on first colon only so sponsor may contain colons" — written
assuming the podcastId has none.

THE PODCAST ID IS A FEED URL. Verified against the device DB
(db-corrected2, analysis_jobs.podcastId, 4 distinct values, ALL of this shape):
  https://rss2.flightcast.com/xmsftuzjjykcmqwolaqn6mdn
  https://feeds.simplecast.com/dHoohVNH
  https://rss.libsyn.com/shows/101338/destinations/535577.xml
  https://anchor.fm/s/10412e4e0/podcast/rss
Every one contains "://". The chain is Episode.resolvedShowIdentity ->
Podcast.feedURL.absoluteString, canonical-spelling-gated by
RecurrenceMaterialIdentity.canonicalIdentifier.

So the round trip is:
  in   sponsorOnShow(podcastId: "https://feeds.simplecast.com/dHoohVNH", sponsor: "acme")
  wire "sponsorOnShow:https://feeds.simplecast.com/dHoohVNH:acme"
  out  sponsorOnShow(podcastId: "https", sponsor: "//feeds.simplecast.com/dHoohVNH:acme")

CONSEQUENCES

1. playhead-shjn IS INERT ON REAL DATA. shjn wires the READ side to query
   `activeEntriesWithNegativeMemory(forPodcast:)` with the CORRECT feed URL
   (AdDetectionService.swift:4431 -> RegionShadowPhase.swift -> AnalysisStore
   `WHERE podcastId = ?`). The WRITE side
   (LearningArtifactIngestor.swift:212-238 -> :378 recordCandidate) persists the
   row keyed "https". Exact string equality: NEVER MATCHES. shjn's own tests all
   pass because every fixture id ("pod-shjn-active", "show1") is colon-free.

2. EVERY SHOW COLLAPSES INTO ONE BUCKET. All https feeds key to "https", so
   "Always skip X on this show" would, once the key bug is fixed in isolation,
   leak across every show on the device. Per-show scoping is the product promise.

3. THE SPONSOR VALUE IS ALSO DESTROYED. normalizedValue becomes
   "//feeds.simplecast.com/dhoohvnh:acme", so SponsorKnowledgeMatcher's
   \b-anchored regex could never fire even if the key matched.

4. NEGATIVE MEMORY SILENTLY NEVER SUPPRESSES.
   SponsorKnowledgeStore.activeEntriesWithNegativeMemory (:419-434) RE-serializes
   the scope from the READ-side podcastId and compares strings against stored
   scopes. Correct-vs-corrupt: no match. A sponsor the user later revoked would
   keep firing. This is why a partial fix is worse than none.

5. FOUR OTHER CASES SHARE THE PARSE: phraseOnShow, campaignOnShow,
   domainOwnershipOnShow, jingleOnShow (UserCorrectionStore.swift:141-158).

BLAST RADIUS TODAY IS ZERO, WHICH IS WHY THIS SHOULD BE FIXED NOW.
Measured across the device pulls: correction_events holds ONLY exactTimeSpan
scopes (30 rows in db-corrected2, 27 in db-marked) — that case parses correctly
(last-two-parts). sponsor_knowledge_entries = 0 rows, sponsorOnShow scopes = 0,
in all five pulls. So there is nothing to migrate. The moment one listener
presses "Always skip <sponsor> on this show", corrupt rows start accruing.

WHY THIS IS FILED AND NOT FIXED IN shjn
The format is genuinely ambiguous — `type:podcastId:value` where BOTH sides can
contain colons — so choosing the rule is a persistence decision, and it has to
be made once for all five cases plus the negative-memory string comparison.
Fixing only the podcastId (e.g. having LearningArtifactIngestor prefer
`correction.podcastId` and `correction.targetRefs.sponsorEntity`, both of which
are already carried CORRECTLY on the event) would leave clause 4 broken in the
OPPOSITE direction — revocation stops working while confirmation starts — which
is worse than uniform inertness. Options for Dan:
  (a) length-prefix or percent-escape the podcastId in `serialized` (changes the
      wire format; no migration burden today, per the zero-row measurement);
  (b) parse from the RIGHT for the *OnShow cases, accepting that a sponsor
      containing a colon breaks instead of a podcastId always breaking;
  (c) stop round-tripping identity through the scope string at all — read
      `correction.podcastId` / `targetRefs.sponsorEntity` and make the scope
      string a dedupe key only, with the negative-memory comparison moved off it.

BLOCKS: playhead-shjn cannot deliver its stated outcome until this lands.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED (branch bead/playhead-fzpj). Scoped gate GREEN: 45 Swift Testing tests / 6 suites + 99 XCTest, 0 failures, GATE_EXIT=0; 9 of 9 requested suites reported.

THE READ TOPOLOGY — established first, and it materially changes the fix.

15 production callers of CorrectionScope.deserialize. Only TWO read a *OnShow
payload: LearningArtifactIngestor:139 and :299, both feeding
applySponsorSideEffect. Everything else either matches on the CASE only
(TrainingExampleMaterializer:399, AtomEvidence.splitScopes, UserCorrectionStore
:1096/:1166/:1194, activeFalse*Scopes -> AdDetectionService:9318), requires
.exactTimeSpan (AnalysisStore :12360 :12436 :12923 :19517, AdDetectionService
:11826 :11836), or only nil-checks it (CorpusExporter:498).

CLAUSE 4 OF THIS BEAD IS REFUTED. activeEntriesWithNegativeMemory does NOT
deserialize. It SERIALIZES both sides — CorrectionScope.sponsorOnShow(...).serialized
compared against the raw correction_events.scope column via
AnalysisStore.suppressingCorrectionScopesPresent (SQL 'scope IN (...)'). Both
sides are wire strings, so the comparison is unaffected by the split bug, and
fixing the write side does NOT break revocation. There was no
'enables-confirmation-while-breaking-revocation' trap; the fix is materially
smaller than the bead assumed.

NOTHING PERSISTS A CORRUPTED SCOPE. normalizedScopeKey IS persisted from
deserialize(scope)?.normalizedIdentityKey (AnalysisStore:19861, :4613, :12974,
UserCorrectionStore:292) — but for *OnShow, normalizedIdentityKey == serialized,
and splitting on a colon then rejoining with a colon is LOSSLESS. The string is
a FIXPOINT under either split direction. That is why nothing downstream ever
noticed, and it is why changing the split rule would move nothing on disk.

The one durable corruption is sponsor_knowledge_entries: recordCandidate/
recordRollback key rows on (podcastId, entityType, normalizedValue) with the
UNIQUE index on exactly that tuple. Clause 2 needs one correction: the shows do
NOT actually collide, because the rest of the URL migrates into normalizedValue —
podcastId collapses to 'https' but the natural key stays distinct.

WHAT CHANGED (no wire-format change, not one byte):
  * CorrectionEvent.authoritativeShowScopePayload(for:) — resolution by
    RECONSTRUCTION. The value column anchors the split from the right, the
    podcastId column from the left, and the result must reconstruct the stored
    scope string or it is refused. Both present must agree. Neither present
    falls back to the parse only when the string admits one split.
  * CorrectionScope.showScopeSplitIsDetermined(bySerialized:) — a STATIC over
    the wire string, not a property of a parsed scope.
  * LearningArtifactIngestor routes both sites through it and counts refusals
    in a new sponsorSideEffectsSkippedUnresolvableShow counter.
  * The five duplicated firstIndex(of:) blocks collapse to one named
    ambiguousShowScopeSplit — the name is the warning, and it is why
    sponsorOnShow read as 'the broken one' while four siblings read as fine.

Rung 1 is strictly stronger than what the bead's option list contemplated: given
the value, a colon-bearing sponsor under a colon-bearing podcastId resolves, and
no split rule over the string alone can do that.

WORTH RECORDING: the FIRST implementation committed this bead's own defect one
layer up. It asked 'does MY podcastId contain a colon?' of an ALREADY-PARSED
scope — whose podcastId is 'https', colon-free — so it reported the corrupt
scope as clean, and 9 of 9 resolver tests failed on the gate. A quantity
computed over the pre-serialization population, read on the post-parse one.
A rail now pins it (testTheQuestionIsAboutTheWireStringNotTheParsedScope).

RESIDUALS: playhead-uv7o (the wire-format decision, PRESENTED not implemented —
phrase/campaign/jingle have no value column, so they can only reach the
show-column rung), playhead-ma23 (recordVeto scopes a sponsor to an EPISODE).

title: Day-zero rediff fires only for TAPPED downloads — the one lane that beats the pipeline (12s vs 4.5h) never starts for most episodes
description:
DAN'S DECISION 2026-08-10, Option C from playhead-pa6a's establish round. Split out so pa6a stays open for the structural cold-start finding (84% of window time is decode; A and B deferred).

THE EVIDENCE, measured on the fresh-install device (virgin DB, build 9e31bf1c):
- Asset 66D32039 downloaded 13:02:21. Day-zero rediff RESOLVED AT 13:02:33 — TWELVE SECONDS LATER — fetching 66MB and producing four dayZeroRediffByteExact windows at confidence 1.0.
- The other two episodes on the same device have NO rediff_day_zero_attempts row at all, and zero ad_windows 3.5 hours later.
- The difference: 66D32039's kickoff source was 'download_and_analyze_tap'. The others were downloaded without that tap.

Meanwhile the transcript pipeline needs ~4h30m (measured end-to-end on the warm control, asset 52EBDD96: download to 90% transcript, 03:58->08:28) and 1-2 days on a cold daytime install. So the deterministic lane beats the pipeline by roughly three orders of magnitude, produces conf-1.0 byte-exact marks, and is the ONE detector Dan has never vetoed when he has judged it — and it simply is not started for most downloads.

SCOPE — establish before changing:
1. Enumerate EVERY path that can produce a downloaded episode and determine which reach the day-zero kickoff. The witness is that 'download_and_analyze_tap' fired and the others did not; name the real sources (background URLSession completion, subscription auto-download, queue drain, force-quit resume, etc.) rather than assuming there is one.
2. READ playhead-4dqe FIRST (closed: 'day-0 at DOWNLOAD time, accountable kickoffs, transport setting'). Its stated intent looks like exactly this, so this may be a GAP in what it shipped rather than new work — establish what 4dqe actually wired and where the tap-only path came from.
3. DO NOT weaken the p70f protections. Day-zero once cost 108MB per replay; that is why DayZeroRediffAttemptPolicy has a 24h backoff, and why playhead-3oyz's same-session retry is restricted to zero-byte fetch_failed exits. This bead changes WHO STARTS a day-zero attempt, not when it may retry.
4. QUANTIFY THE BANDWIDTH. Firing on every download multiplies fetch volume by the number of untapped downloads. Compute bytes-per-attempt x expected downloads/day from the pulls and state it plainly. Dan pays for this in the user's data plan. If it needs a cap, a wifi-only transport gate, or a per-day budget, propose it — the transport setting 4dqe shipped may already be the hook.
5. MEASURE THE EXPECTED BENEFIT HONESTLY: how many assets across the pulls would have received a day-zero attempt under the new rule, and what fraction plausibly would have produced byte-exact marks (not every episode has rotating DAI — see project_cross_network_dai_survey_2026-07-21: baked and shared-stitch behaviours are invisible to rediff by construction). Do not claim a benefit the corpus cannot support.

Related: pa6a (parent finding, still open for the decode/stage-order root cause), 4dqe, p70f, 3oyz, evc1 (a day-0 mark may seed a pod walk), xygy.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED on bead/playhead-cnql (758a3c2d + 94560f3d). This is a GAP IN WHAT
4dqe SHIPPED, and the gap is the INSTALL SITE, not a missing call site.

=== ESTABLISH: every path that lands a downloaded episode ===

Two production paths land a complete pinned artifact AND register an
analysis_assets row:

  A. `DownloadManager.handleBackgroundDownloadComplete` (:3629) — reached by
     every `backgroundDownload` caller: the "Download & Analyze" tap
     (EpisodePreparationCoordinator:268), the plain Download button and
     Download-Next-N (EpisodeListView:256), subscription auto-download
     (BackgroundFeedRefreshService:1017), and force-quit resume
     (ForceQuitResumeScan, which finalizes through this same path). It calls
     `notifyBackgroundDownloadCompleted` (:3986) at the LAST statement of the
     success path — 4dqe's seam, correctly placed.
  B. `DownloadManager.finalizeStreamingTransfer` (:1652) — pressing PLAY on a
     not-yet-downloaded episode. Never notifies. Covered incidentally by the
     play-time `kickOffDayZeroRediff`; FILED as playhead-zmog.
  (`progressiveDownload` has no production caller; the tap on an ALREADY-cached
  episode fires `kickOffDayZeroRediffForPreparation` directly.)

So path A — the whole background/auto funnel — DID reach the kickoff by
construction. What it did not reach was an OBSERVER.

=== ROOT CAUSE ===

`PlayheadRuntime.attachDayZeroBackgroundDownloadKickoff` was invoked from
`attachRediffEnclosureResolver`, which is invoked from `PlayheadApp.swift:170`
— inside a SwiftUI `.task`, i.e. a SCENE modifier.

iOS relaunches this app with NO SCENE to deliver
`handleEventsForBackgroundURLSession`, and wakes it the same way for a BGTask.
`DownloadManager.attributionDirectory` (:362) already documents the
consequence: the analysis enqueue "routinely runs in a DIFFERENT PROCESS from
the `backgroundDownload` that started the transfer". `PlayheadApp.swift:150`
documents the other half in its own words — "Background-launch BGTask wakes
(where `.task` may run minimally or not at all…)".

In such a process `backgroundDownloadCompletionObserver` is nil, and
`notifyBackgroundDownloadCompleted` was:

    guard let observer = backgroundDownloadCompletionObserver else { return }

A bare, unrecorded return — the same silence 4dqe was built to kill, displaced
one layer up, above the coordinator that 4dqe made accountable. No attempt, no
give-up, no `rediff_day_zero_kickoffs` row: indistinguishable from a download
that never happened. 4dqe's own tests start at `requestKickoff`, one step AFTER
the drop, which is why it shipped green.

MEASURED (db-vtjxverdict, the 2026-08-10 control pull). Cutoff = the first
kickoff row, 2026-08-01 15:14:04, i.e. when the 4dqe build went live.
  * 27 analysis_assets created 2026-08-01 15:12:01 -> 2026-08-10 10:31:18
    (8.81 days). 16 of them (59%) have NO kickoff row of any kind.
  * 12 kickoff rows exist: 9 `download_and_analyze_tap`, 3
    `background_download`. The background hook DOES fire — when the app happens
    to be running with a scene. That is what makes this a race, not a
    never-wired feature.
  * Caveat on the denominator, stated because it matters: an asset row is
    created at job ACQUISITION, not at download, so "assets" is a proxy for
    "downloads". An episode downloaded before the build whose asset registered
    after it would inflate the 16.

=== WHAT CHANGED (three parts, all about WHO STARTS an attempt) ===

1. `PlayheadRuntime.init` installs the observer on the LAUNCH path, beside the
   BGTask handler registrations, via a new
   `nonisolated static installDayZeroBackgroundDownloadKickoff`. It captures
   only Sendable values (never `self`), so a URLSession completion callback
   never hops to the MainActor.
2. `DownloadManager` BUFFERS a completion that arrives before an observer
   (bounded at 64, keyed by episode, evictions logged) and drains it on
   install. The hand-off is now order-independent instead of lucky.
3. The SwiftData half — current enclosure URL + publish date — becomes an
   UPGRADE delivered through `dayZeroKickoffEpisodeFactsBox`.
   `attachRediffEnclosureResolver` still installs it. Without it the kickoff
   falls back to the URL the download itself recorded (`publishedAt` nil, which
   the ordering already documents as sorting LAST).

p70f PROTECTIONS UNTOUCHED, verified: no change to
`DayZeroRediffAttemptPolicy`, the 24 h backoff, 3oyz's same-session retry
restriction, suppression recording, or attempt accounting. The 4dqe transport
gate (WiFi-only default, Low Data Mode wins on both transports) and the rolling
24 h byte budget are read exactly as before, downstream of the kickoff.

=== BANDWIDTH — numerator and denominator both named ===

Bytes per attempt, db-vtjxverdict `rediff_day_zero_attempts`: 11 attempts,
sum(totalFullFetchBytes) = 1,125,288,584 B. Two exited `fetch_failed` having
spent ZERO bytes, so the honest per-fetching-attempt figure is
1,125,288,584 / 9 = 125.0 MB (over all 11 it is 102.3 MB). db-postwipe2's
single attempt at K=2 cost 66.0 MB — the low end. 4dqe's field figure was
120.3-131.8 MB. Use 125.0 MB.

Downloads/day: 27 assets / 8.81 d = 3.06/day. A second, looser denominator —
distinct episodes with an analysis_job in the same window — gives 34 / 6.87 d =
4.95/day, which over-counts (re-mints and backfills share the table).

Projected steady state: 3.06 x 125.0 = 383 MB/day (upper denominator: 619
MB/day). The same device actually spent 1,125.3 MB / 8.81 d = 128 MB/day. So
this is roughly a 3x increase.

NO NEW CAP ADDED, deliberately: 4dqe already built the ceiling this needs —
`RediffDayZeroDailyBudget.dailyCapBytes` = 1 GB per rolling 24 h, across the
whole library, on BOTH transports, admitted on the FULL k-way estimate. 383
MB/day is 38% of it (619 is 62%). The cap bites at ~8 episodes/day, which is
the intended behaviour for a subscription batch. The transport default is still
WiFi-only, so a metered user pays nothing until they opt in.

=== EXPECTED BENEFIT — stated so the corpus can support it ===

16 of 27 assets (59%) newly get an attempt. Their feeds, and each feed's
OBSERVED day-0 record on this device:
  * flightcast   8 assets — 8 attempts ran: 6 marked, 1 all_slots_already_covered, 1 fetch_failed
  * simplecast   2 assets — 1 attempt ran: 1 marked
  * libsyn       1 asset  — 2 attempts ran: 1 marked, 1 fetch_failed
  * anchor.fm    5 assets — ZERO attempts ever ran. No evidence either way.

Applying each feed's own rate: 8x(6/8) + 2x(1/1) + 1x(1/2) = 8.5 of the 11
non-anchor assets. The 5 anchor.fm assets are UNMEASURED — per
project_cross_network_dai_survey_2026-07-21, baked and shared-stitch
behaviours are invisible to rediff by construction, so they may return
`unchanged` at zero mark yield while still costing the bytes.

HONEST HEADLINE: ~8-9 of the 16 plausibly yield conf-1.0 byte-exact marks; 5
are a coin-flip nobody has measured. NOT 16.

And the marks are markOnly — all five windows on the virgin device were — so
this produces banners, not skips, until the eligibility work lands. That was
already in this bead's parent (pa6a option C risks) and has not changed.

=== FILED, NOT FIXED ===
  * playhead-jra6 — the kickoff queue is IN-MEMORY; a batch queued but not
    settled when the process ends leaves no row at all.
  * playhead-kxgh — the drain is strictly serial and each item can burn the
    full 40-poll / ~6.5 min readiness budget. Witness: five rows on 2026-08-09
    at 16:48:54 / 16:55:29 / 17:02:06 / 17:08:41 / 17:15:17, all
    lastPollCount=40, all `no_analysis_asset`. 33 minutes, zero fires.
  * playhead-zmog — `finalizeStreamingTransfer` leaves no kickoff record, and
    the play-time trigger fires with `result.fileURL` BEFORE
    `result.downloadComplete()` — a partial A-side.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
R1 REVIEW (fresh reviewer). ONE finding, HIGH, FIXED here (9a4ab1f6). One
follow-up FILED (playhead-fqlk). The three claimed mechanisms hold; the
bandwidth and benefit numbers reproduce from the control pull.

=== CHECK 1 — SCENELESS LAUNCH: the observer arrives, the EVENT did not ===

`PlayheadRuntime.init` genuinely runs on every launch path. Witness, not
inference: `PlayheadApp.swift:8` is `@State private var runtime =
PlayheadRuntime()`, evaluated in the App struct's init, and init registers
BGTask handlers (`backgroundProcessingService.registerBackgroundTasks()`,
`BackgroundFeedRefreshService.registerTaskHandler()`,
`rediffRefetchService.registerBackgroundTaskHandler()`). BGTaskScheduler
requires registration before launch ends and TRAPS on a duplicate — so the
shipped app proves both that init runs at launch and that it runs exactly
once per process.

But the completion could not reach it. `PlayheadAppDelegate` is the only
production code that re-instantiates a background `URLSession` in a
relaunched process (`handleEventsForBackgroundURLSession` ->
`DownloadManager.shared` -> `resumeSession(identifier:)`), and sessions are
lazily created by `backgroundSession(for:)`. `DownloadManager.registerShared`
and `registerAppDelegate` had exactly ONE call site each —
`PlayheadApp.swift:127-128`, inside `.task`, the same scene modifier this
bead moved the observer OFF. In the headless relaunch cnql is about,
`shared` was nil, no session object was ever created, the delegate never
fired, `handleBackgroundDownloadComplete` never ran, and there was no
completion to buffer or deliver. The drop was one step EARLIER than the
`guard let observer` this bead closed — the same shape, one layer down.

Two further consequences of the same nil slot on that launch:
`didFinishLaunchingWithOptions` logged "scanForSuspendedTransfers skipped —
no DownloadManager registered" (playhead-hyht never ran), and
`urlSessionDidFinishEvents` could not reach the stored OS completion handler,
which is how an app loses its background scheduling budget.

FIXED: init publishes the manager below the `isPreviewRuntime` guard; the
delegate self-registers in `didFinishLaunchingWithOptions`; both `.task`
calls stay (idempotent). A second source canary pins both sites.

=== CHECK 2 — BUFFER: clean ===
Actor-isolated on `DownloadManager`, so concurrent completions serialise.
`notify` either delivers OR buffers, never both — verified by the suite's own
control (a second install finds an empty backlog). The drain copies, clears,
then delivers with no `await` in the loop, so it cannot re-enter or replay.
At capacity the OLDEST goes, which is the right end given the drain is
newest-first, and it is logged. Orphans are bounded at 64 and only reachable
in a process that never installs an observer (day-0 off), where they would
never be consumed anyway. Double kickoff (tap + background on the same
episode) cannot double-fetch: `RediffDayZeroKickoffCoordinator.requestKickoff`
dedups on `fired` and `inFlight` before enqueueing.

=== CHECK 3 — FALLBACK URL: safe, and safer than the primary ===
The fallback is `originalURL ?? loadPin(...)?.sourceURL`, and `originalURL`
is `downloadTask.originalRequest?.url` (DownloadManager:4324) — the URL the
transfer was STARTED with, before any redirect. That is by construction the
URL that produced the A-side bytes on disk, so a day-0 diff against it
compares like with like. It is the FEED's current URL (`facts?.enclosureURL`,
preferred when known) that carries the stale/wrong-audio risk, and that
preference is 4dqe's, unchanged here. Cannot mint marks against wrong audio
via the new arm.

=== CHECK 4 — p70f UNTOUCHED, read directly ===
`DayZeroRediffAttemptPolicy` lives in `RediffDayZeroOutcome.swift` and the
gates in `DayZeroRediffTrigger.swift`; neither file is in the diff (5 files:
PlayheadRuntime, DownloadManager, RediffDayZeroKickoff,
RediffRefetchProduction, pbxproj + the new test). Read in place and intact:
`.decide` backoff at :260 before any fetch, 3oyz's `grantsSameSessionRetry`
loop at :311 with the claim-before-delay at :322, `suppressionRecorder` on
every denial, and the budget re-read across the retry delay at :347.

=== CHECKS 5 & 6 — NUMBERS RE-DERIVED from db-vtjxverdict ===
All three headline counts reproduce EXACTLY: 27 assets created 2026-08-01
15:12:01 -> 2026-08-10 10:31:18 (8.805 d); 16 with no kickoff row; 12 kickoff
rows (9 tap / 3 background); 11 attempts, sum(totalFullFetchBytes) =
1,125,288,584 B, two `fetch_failed` at zero bytes.
  125.0 MB = 1,125,288,584 / 9   (denominator = fetching attempts)
  3.07/day = 27 / 8.805
  383 MB/day = 38% of RediffDayZeroDailyBudget.dailyCapBytes (1e9, verified,
  transport-agnostic, admitted on the FULL k-way estimate at K=2).
CAP CONFIRMED to bite at the 8th episode: 7 x 130 MB = 910, 8 x 130 = 1,040.

TWO HONEST ADJUSTMENTS, neither changing the decision:
  * 125.0 MB averages a 49.1 MB `all_slots_already_covered` in with eight
    `marked` attempts whose own mean is 134.5 MB (1,076,150,061 / 8). Using
    that instead gives 413 MB/day, 41% of the cap. Still comfortably under.
  * The admission ESTIMATE (65 MB/B-copy, 130 MB/attempt) is below the
    observed mean and 37% below the worst observation (206.6 MB), so a full
    day of admitted attempts could overshoot the 1 GB cap by ~45%. Not a cnql
    regression — cnql is what makes it reachable. FILED as playhead-fqlk with
    three options; the remedy is a policy constant, so it is Dan's call.

BENEFIT: the arithmetic checks (8x6/8 + 2x1/1 + 1x1/2 = 8.5). My independent
attribution via `analysis_jobs.podcastId` splits the 16 as flightcast 7 /
anchor.fm 5 / simplecast 1 / 3 unattributed, and the 11 attempts as
flightcast 6 (5 marked, 1 fetch_failed) / 5 unattributed — consistent with
the implementer's table once the unattributed rows are assigned, and the
load-bearing part reproduces EXACTLY: the 5 anchor.fm assets have zero day-0
history in either derivation. ~8-9 of 16 stands, with kxgh's serial drain
bounding what is actually realised.

VERIFICATION: scoped gate GREEN — 15 requested = 13 Swift Testing suites (79
tests) + 2 XCTest classes (13 tests), 0 failures in BOTH formats,
GATE_EXIT=0, baseline check correctly skipped as a selective run. Mutation
rail: reverting `notifyBackgroundDownloadCompleted` to the bare `guard let
observer else { return }` KILLS
`completionBeforeObserverIsDeliveredOnInstall` with 3 issues (rc=65);
restored byte-clean, `shasum -a 256 -c` OK, residue = the three intended
files only.

NOT RE-LITIGATED: jra6, kxgh, zmog, pa6a options A/B.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
VIRGIN-DB FIELD CONFIRMATION, and a cleaner witness than the one this bead was opened on. Pull db-db-r2wait, 2026-08-10 17:33 UTC, device build 9e31bf1c (which does NOT contain this fix).

Five episodes have been downloaded since the 13:02 wipe. ONE has a rediff_day_zero_kickoffs row.

  66D32039  13:02:21  kickoff FIRED  lastSource=download_and_analyze_tap  -> marked, 4 marks, 66.0 MB, 12s
  F7BB38BB  13:08:46  NO KICKOFF ROW
  B80D3EE0  13:18:23  NO KICKOFF ROW
  60DFF7B4  16:48:53  NO KICKOFF ROW
  590D6656  16:50:56  NO KICKOFF ROW

  numerator   4 assets created since the wipe with no kickoff row
  denominator 5 assets created since the wipe
  miss rate   80%
  background_download kickoffs since the wipe: ZERO

This is the same defect the bead was filed on (16 of 27 = 59% on the pre-wipe device, 9 tap / 3 background) but it is a STRONGER witness, for three reasons. The DB is virgin, so every download since 13:02 is accounted for and there is no pre-4dqe history to explain a missing row away. Every miss is a modern build. And the single kickoff that DID fire came from a tap while the app was open, which is exactly the population the scene-installed observer can serve.

A mechanism that fits the split, and is testable rather than assumed: 66D32039 is a 32-minute episode whose kickoff fired 12 SECONDS after creation, comfortably inside one foreground session. The four misses are 32, 70, 114 and 114 minutes of audio — larger files, longer transfers, far likelier to COMPLETE after the app is backgrounded or suspended, which is precisely when the completion arrives on a sceneless relaunch and finds no observer (and, per R1, no registered DownloadManager either). A tap download is not immune; it only looks that way when it finishes fast enough.

WORTH OF THE ONE THAT WORKED, since it is the argument for the fix: 4 marks at confidence 1.0, twelve seconds after download, on the detector Dan has never vetoed. The other four episodes got none of that.

I am NOT revising the bead's benefit estimate from this. n=5 is small, I have not established which of the four completed in the background versus merely lacking a row for another reason, and R1's ~8-9 of 16 already carries kxgh's serial-drain bound. Recorded as independent confirmation of the PREMISE — that the miss is real, current, and large — not as a new number.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
CORRECTION to my own earlier comment on this bead — the 80% figure I recorded from pull db-db-r2wait is WRONG, and wrong in the way this project keeps getting caught by: I named a denominator that does not measure the population in question.

WHAT I SAID: '4 of 5 assets since the wipe have no kickoff row = 80% miss; zero background_download kickoffs.'

WHY IT IS WRONG (found by R3): today's pull contains ZERO auto-downloads. All five post-wipe jobs carry priority 10 or 20 — isExplicitDownload / user-intent tap. None carries priority 0. And a TAP gets its kickoff from kickOffDayZeroRediffForPreparation BEFORE the download completes, so the observer's own .backgroundDownload request is then dropped by 'guard !inFlight.contains' (RediffDayZeroKickoffCoordinator.swift:110-111). So 'zero background_download kickoffs' is the EXPECTED reading of a window containing zero background downloads. The denominator is 0, not 5. The number said nothing about the defect this bead fixes.

Nor were the 4 missing rows evidence of a nil observer: the kickoff row is written only in settle (:181), pending/inFlight are in-memory, and the serial drain does not survive the app being backgrounded. That is playhead-hbia's territory.

THE HONEST NUMBER, from R3, on the population that can only be served by the observer — episodes with a priority-0 job (auto-downloads), db-vtjxverdict, since 2026-08-01:

  numerator    3 episodes with a background_download kickoff row
  denominator  24 distinct episodes with a priority-0 job
  miss         21 of 24 = 87.5% left no background_download kickoff at all
  (9 of the 24 have a kickoff row of ANY source)

Two causes are live and NOT separable from the DB: a nil observer in a sceneless process, which this bead fixes, and the serial drain not surviving suspension, which it does not (hbia). Distinguishing them needs a device run on the fixed build with a genuine plain/auto download — not another pull of the current one.

The bead's premise survives and the number is close to what R1 estimated; my supporting evidence for it did not. Recording the correction because the wrong denominator is on this bead in my own hand, and leaving it would make the next reader over-credit the fix.

title: COLD START: on a virgin DB, background windows complete ZERO jobs and add ZERO transcript chunks in 3.5h — all progress came from the foreground burst
description:
MEASURED on the fresh-install device (wipe + install from 9e31bf1c = vtjx + ar60 + q6y3), 2026-08-10. This is the NEW-USER path Dan said he cares most about right now.

TIMELINE (asset 66D32039 downloaded 13:02:21 UTC):
  13:02:21  download
  13:11:17  first semantic_scan_results row  (+8m56s)  <- FOREGROUND, app open
  13:12:01  last scan row
  13:12 -> 16:37 (3h25m): transcript_chunks stays at 1530. ZERO added.

BACKGROUND WINDOWS SINCE THE WIPE — 4 runs, ALL outcome=expired, ALL jobsCompleted=0:
  13:08:44  backfill              expired  seen 4  done 0  197s
  13:18:21  preanalysis_recovery  expired  (no counters)   23s
  13:18:21  backfill              expired  seen 4  done 0   23s
  15:40:36  backfill              expired  seen 5  done 0  295s
Note the 2h22m GAP between 13:18 and 15:40 with no window granted at all.

STATE NOW: 66D32039 fastWM 990/1926 (51%), F7BB38BB 150/1931 (8%), B80D3EE0 0/4224 (0%). Both backfill_jobs deferred on 'cancelled-during-fullEpisodeScan'. analysis_jobs: one running (B80D3EE0, lastErr backgroundWindowExpired), rest queued with backgroundWindowExpired / transcription:cancelled.

WHY THIS IS NOT lmrx/13kf ALREADY-FIXED: lmrx made a killed window's outcome DURABLE and countable (that is why we can see 'seen 4, done 0' at all — the counters are working). 26od/fil5 made partial scan work persist and the claim durable (hence 'deferred', not lost). 13kf reordered so the FM/coarse phase runs BEFORE the transcription drain. All three are on this build and all three are behaving. The problem they do NOT solve is COLD START: a virgin DB has NO transcript, so the coarse-first phase has nothing to scan and falls through to the drain, and the drain cannot transcribe a 32-70 minute episode inside a 200-300s grant. Every window therefore spends its whole budget without crossing any completion line.

ESTABLISH FIRST (do not assume the cause):
1. Did the 295s window at 15:40 do ANY work? jobsCompleted=0 does not prove zero progress — check whether chunks/watermarks moved inside that window (they did not at the asset level, but confirm at the chunk level with createdAt) and whether the coarse phase ran, refused, or found nothing to scan.
2. Is the thermal/capability depth gate refusing? See playhead-ewag (CLOSED): the thermal depth gate misclassified every 15min+ download, and LaneAdmission.allows(lane:) was dead code. Verify it is not misclassifying here.
3. Where did the window's time actually GO? 197s and 295s are substantial. If it is ASR, measure chunks-per-second and compute how many windows a 32-minute episode needs at that rate — that number IS the new-user time-to-value, and if it is 'dozens of windows over days' the design needs a different answer, not a faster loop.
4. The 2h22m grant gap is a SEPARATE question from what a window does with its time. Do not conflate them. See project_backfill_stall_bgtask_2026-07-22: iOS granted ~0 discretionary windows overnight when the device was never idle.
5. Compare against the pre-wipe device, which DID make progress (db-vtjxverdict: outcomes included running/recovered_work, and reach moved 143->210). The difference is that it had transcripts already. That contrast is the evidence.

WHAT GOOD LOOKS LIKE (Dan's standard, feedback_timely_and_magic): the work is finished BEFORE he presses play. A first listen that arrives before the pipeline does is the product failing, however durable the bookkeeping is.

Related: lmrx, 13kf, 26od, fil5 (all merged, all working as designed); ewag (thermal gate, closed); playhead-4dqe (day-0 at download time); project_backfill_stall_bgtask_2026-07-22 (BGTask starvation); gayl (both BGTask identifiers firing at identical instants).

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
ESTABLISH — root cause named, rate measured, three options. No production changes. Derivations committed at 14df6b06 (.pa6a-notes.md on bead/playhead-pa6a).

FIELD SEMANTICS FIRST (source, not guessed). AnalysisJobRunner.swift:1919-1990: slice_duration_ms is wall time inside STAGE 3 (transcription) ONLY — the clock starts at line 608, immediately before startTranscription. Stage order in run() is 1 decode (:392) -> 2 features (:521) -> 3 transcription (:600) -> 4 ad detection (:877). So **Stage-3 start = journal timestamp minus slice_duration_ms**, and that subtraction is what this whole answer rests on. transcript_coverage_end_time is fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime read at journal time — the audio-seconds meter. chunk_rate_per_sec = chunks_persisted / (slice_duration_ms/1000); verified exactly (299/370.139 = 0.8078).

=== Q1. DID THE 15:40 WINDOW DO WORK? YES — 278 of its 295 seconds, and none of it was transcript. ===

Window AA7ECEC7 ran 15:40:36-15:45:31 (294.9 s), acquired B80D3EE0 (the 70-min episode) at 15:40:38. Its journal row at 15:45:31 reads slice_duration_ms=14713. So Stage 3 began at 15:45:16.3 and **278.0 s elapsed inside Stages 1-2 before ASR started at all**. ASR then got 14.7 s and persisted 0 chunks.

What those 278 s bought, with a witness: feature_windows holds 1,920 rows for B80D3EE0 spanning 0.0-3,840.0 s, and analysis_assets.featureCoverageEndTime = 3840. B80D3EE0's asset was created 13:18:23; its only acquisitions are 13:18:23 (preempted 21 s later), 15:40:38, and 16:13:57. db-postwipe1 — pulled after 15:45:31 and before 16:13:57, since it carries the 15:40 run and lacks the 16:13:57 acquired row — ALREADY shows all 1,920 rows. 21 seconds cannot decode 4,224 s of audio and extract 3,840 s of features. **The 15:40 window decoded a 70-minute episode and extracted 3,840 audio-seconds of features. It produced zero transcript chunks.**

At chunk granularity: transcript_chunks has no createdAt, so the witness is the population itself. postwipe1 and postwipe2 are byte-identical here — 1,530 rows, max rowid 1530, same per-asset/per-pass split (66D32039 1,051 fast + 285 final; F7BB38BB 52 fast + 142 final) — and B80D3EE0 has ZERO rows in both with a NULL fast watermark. Its own journal row agrees: chunks_persisted 0, transcript_coverage_end_time 0.000.

The coarse/FM phase in that window: zero semantic_scan_results rows created (all 11 rows in the DB carry runCorrelationId fm-df8fc59780340b4b and createdAt 13:11-13:12), and backfill_jobs.fm-df8fc59780340b4b still has cursor lastProcessedUpperBoundSec=194.46 — unmoved since 13:12 — merely re-deferred at 15:45:32. It neither refused nor found nothing; it never got the CPU.

=== Q2. WHERE THE TIME GOES, AND HOW LONG A NEW USER WAITS ===

All three backfill windows since the wipe, Stage-3 start back-computed:

  #  window (UTC)       granted  asset run       pre-ASR        ASR wall  fastWM gain  chunks
  1  13:08:44-13:12:01  196.8 s  F7BB38BB 32 m   155.6 s (79%)   40.4 s   0 -> 120 s    142
  2  13:18:21-13:18:44   22.9 s  66D32039 32 m     0.4 s          22.3 s   300 -> 330    41
  3  15:40:36-15:45:31  294.9 s  B80D3EE0 70 m   278.2 s (94%)   14.7 s   0 -> 0          0
     TOTAL              514.6 s                  434.2 s (84%)   78.7 s   150 audio-s   183

**84 % of granted background time was spent before the transcription stage began. 15 % reached ASR.**

YIELD: numerator = 150 audio-seconds of fast transcript (sum of the three watermark deltas, each read from its own journal row); denominator = 514.6 granted background seconds (sum of finishedAt-startedAt over the three backfill runs; the co-timed preanalysis_recovery run is excluded so its 22.8 s is not double-counted). **0.29 audio-seconds of transcript per granted background second.** If nothing had been transcribed this reads 0.00, so it is real — and it is tiny.

WINDOWS NEEDED, extrapolated (3-window sample, stated as a range): 66D32039 needs 1,925.7 s. At 0.29 that is ~6,600 granted seconds. Mean window here is 171.5 s => **~39 windows**. At the observed cadence (3 windows in 151.9 min; 5.5 % duty cycle) that is **34-50 hours — one and a half to two days — for ONE 32-minute episode**, with the device otherwise to itself. B80D3EE0 (4,223.6 s) needs ~85 windows, ~3-4 days, and has yet to persist its first chunk.

MEASURED END-TO-END, not extrapolated — the CONTROL is better evidence. Asset 52EBDD96 (1,901.7 s, 31.7 min), created 03:58:16, walked by eight transcriptionTimeout rows:

  03:58:48  slice 18.5 s  wm    90     06:28:49  102.0 s   210     07:00:58   74.6 s   450
  07:31:37  slice 95.9 s  wm   720     07:37:25  145.2 s   840     07:57:43   40.3 s  1050
  08:15:38  slice 40.5 s  wm  1530     08:28:18   38.5 s  1710

Aggregate 1,710 audio-s / 555.5 s of Stage-3 wall = **3.08x realtime** (a lower bound on ASR itself — slice_duration also carries stopTranscription). Wall clock: **4 h 30 m from download to 90 % transcript**, spanning 21 background runs and 3,998 granted seconds, of which only 8 reached ASR at all.

So the honest statement of the product situation, and it is a DESIGN finding: **on this machine's best day — warm cache, idle overnight, phone charging — a 32-minute episode is ready four and a half hours after download. On a fresh install during daytime use it is one to two days.** ASR speed is not the constraint: at 3.1x realtime a full 300 s of ASR would carry ~930 audio-seconds, so a 32-minute episode is a THREE-window job in the perfect case. It takes 8 warm and ~39 cold because the window's budget is consumed before ASR starts and because grants are 20-300 s apart.

=== Q3. REFUSAL OR STARVATION? STARVATION. Nothing refused. ===

- All four runs reached at least Stage 3 — proven by the existence of a transcriptionTimeout journal row, which is emitted from inside Stage 3.
- checkStopConditions (AnalysisJobRunner.swift:1304-1316) trips on exactly two things: Task.isCancelled and thermalState == .critical. Neither fired; a thermal stop returns .pausedForThermal and no run carries it.
- Depth gate is NOT clamping. desiredCoverageSec is 1,721 / 1,604 / 3,832 against durations 1,925.7 / 1,931.3 / 4,223.6 — 83-91 %, i.e. escalated well past t2DepthSeconds (900 s). The ewag failure mode (every 15min+ download misclassified) is not present.
- Capability/lane admission is NOT deferring: zero deferred_capability outcomes on the virgin device. The control has 10, so the outcome is reachable and simply did not occur here.
- FM availability is fine: 10 passA scans returned status=success on-device in background.
- Job selection is working AS DESIGNED and that is part of the problem. analysis_jobs.priority is 20 for B80D3EE0 (the 'Now' band — user intent) and 10 for the two 32-minute episodes (explicit download). AnalysisStore.swift:14510 claims ORDER BY priority DESC, createdAt ASC. So the 15:40 window correctly handed its 295 seconds to the 70-minute, zero-progress, un-decoded episode instead of the 32-minute one sitting at 51 %. Right answer by intent, worst possible answer for throughput.

=== Q4. THE GRANT GAP — kept separate, and the DB cannot settle it ===

background_task_runs records only runs that STARTED. There is no row for a submit that was never granted, so this data CANNOT distinguish 'iOS declined for 2 h 22 m' from 'the app never re-submitted'. Do not let anyone read the gap off this table as an iOS verdict.

The instrument that CAN settle it exists and is not in any pull: BGTaskTelemetryLogger.swift:18 writes Documents/bg-task-log.jsonl with submit / start / expire / appPhase events and its own header documents the submitted-vs-fired jq recipe. **Pulling that file is the single highest-value next artifact** and it is a device-free ask once the file is off the phone.

What the data CAN say is that the gap is unremarkable. Control backfill inter-arrivals on 2026-08-10: 30.4, 20.2, 10.4, 19.8, 10.3, 32.2, 30.7, 7.3, 22.8, 18.1, 12.5, 30.4, 18.8, 0.9, 10.5, 30.1, **125.3**, 25.5, 6.9 min. The 125.3-minute gap is 09:58 -> 12:03 — daytime, device in use. The virgin device's 142.3-minute gap (13:18 -> 15:40) is the same regime and the same magnitude, consistent with project_backfill_stall_bgtask_2026-07-22. It is NOT a new defect and it is NOT what makes the windows unproductive: windows 1 and 3 were 197 s and 295 s and still delivered 120 s and 0 s of transcript.

=== Q5. THE PRE-WIPE CONTROL — confirms cold-start, and corrects the hypothesis ===

CONFIRMED, but the mechanism is decode/feature WARMTH, not bookkeeping. Look at window 2 on the virgin device: 66D32039 had been decoded at 13:02 and its features were already at 1,740 s, so Stage 3 began 0.4 s after acquisition and 22.3 of the 22.9 granted seconds went to ASR. Same device, same build, same day — the only difference is that Stages 1-2 had nothing left to do. That is the cold-start effect isolated in one row.

CORRECTED #1: jobsCompleted is the wrong meter and 'jobsCompleted=0' is NOT the anomaly. On the warm control: expired = 344 runs, 1,641 jobs seen, **8** completions across 69,456 granted seconds. Backfill windows essentially never cross the completion line even on a device making good progress. What moves on the control is the WATERMARK. All 138 of the control's completions come from preanalysis_recovery runs averaging **17.9 s** — jobs that were already finished and only needed finalizing. A virgin DB has nothing in that state, which is exactly why the virgin device's one preanalysis_recovery run (13:18:21) expired with no counters.

CORRECTED #2: the bead's hypothesis said the coarse-first phase 'has nothing to scan and falls through to the drain'. That is not what happened. In window 1 the coarse phase had plenty to scan — day-zero rediff plus the final-pass runner had already laid down transcript out to 1,919 s — and it ran 10 passA scans totalling **98.2 s of FM latency**, plus a passB scan of **36.8 s** that was cancelled at expiry. **135.0 s of FM inference inside a 196.8 s window (68.6 %)**, overlapping Stage 3 rather than preceding it. So on a cold DB the coarse phase is a COMPETITOR for the window, not a no-op. (Three of those windows — 0.78-115.26, 115.68-194.46, 195.66-276.18 — are scanned TWICE, 21 s apart, in the same window: ~24 s of the 135 s is duplicate work. That shape is already owned by y8a3 / 5q8l / 7iy5; not re-filed.)

=== ROOT CAUSE ===

**The analysis job's per-window budget is spent in stage order, and transcription is stage 3 of 4. On a cold asset, stages 1-2 cost O(episode length) — 278 s for a 70-minute episode, 155.6 s for a 32-minute one — and there is no checkpoint that lets a granted window BEGIN at stage 3. Every window on a not-yet-decoded asset therefore pays the whole decode+feature bill first and reaches ASR with whatever seconds remain. Measured: 84 % of granted background time never reached the only stage that produces the artifact everything downstream needs.**

file:line —
- AnalysisJobRunner.swift:392 (Stage 1 decode, whole file, unconditional), :521 (Stage 2 features), :600 (Stage 3 transcription). No entry point resumes at Stage 3.
- AnalysisAudio.swift:251 — 'an episode's cache directory is only created at decode COMPLETION (saveShards, step 9)', and :461 a truncated decode is deliberately NOT cached. So a window that dies mid-decode leaves nothing durable and the next window re-pays in full. (B80D3EE0's decode DID complete at 15:45, so its NEXT window will be cheap — but the 21-second window at 13:18 bought nothing at all.)
- AnalysisJobRunner.swift:665-668 — Stage 3 is a race against Task.sleep(300). Irrelevant in background: iOS granted 196.8 / 22.9 / 294.9 s, so the GRANT expires first and the 300 s cap only ever binds in foreground (the 13:02 run's 370 s slice).
- AnalysisStore.swift:14510 ORDER BY priority DESC, createdAt ASC + priority 20 on B80D3EE0 — the scarcest window is handed the most expensive asset.

DB witnesses — background_task_runs (4 rows, all expired, all jobsCompleted 0); work_journal (19 rows, the five transcriptionTimeout rows carry the whole time accounting); feature_windows (1,920 rows for B80D3EE0, 0-3,840 s); transcript_chunks (1,530 rows, zero for B80D3EE0, identical across both post-wipe pulls); semantic_scan_results (11 rows, 135.0 s of FM, all inside window 1).

=== THE FACT THAT SHAPES THE OPTIONS ===

The only ad detection that arrived before the pipeline came from day-zero rediff, and it was not close. rediff_refetch_state.updatedAt = 1786366953 = **13:02:33 — twelve seconds after the 13:02:21 download** — resolved=1, lastExit=marked, lastMarkCount=4, 66,010,142 bytes fetched. Those are the four dayZeroRediffByteExact ad_windows at confidence 1.0. It fired for 66D32039 only, because rediff_day_zero_kickoffs.lastSource = 'download_and_analyze_tap'. F7BB38BB and B80D3EE0 have NO rediff attempt and ZERO ad windows three and a half hours later. The transcript pipeline's entire additional contribution in that time is one semanticSweepMark at confidence 0.70. All five windows are markOnly.

=== OPTIONS (not implemented — Dan's call) ===

**A. Move decode + feature extraction out of the analysis window, to download completion.**
Buys: every later window starts at Stage 3 warm. On the observed data that converts 84 % of grant from setup to ASR — the same 514.6 granted seconds would have carried ~430 s of ASR instead of 78.7 s, roughly 5.5x the transcript per window, and it makes the cost a one-time O(episode) charge when the bytes land rather than a recurring per-window toll. It is also the only option that helps EVERY downstream stage.
Risks: download completion is itself a background event with its own budget, and a 278 s decode does not fit a BGAppRefresh grant either — this needs the BGProcessingTask lane and would still get truncated, and a truncated decode is deliberately not cached (AnalysisAudio.swift:461), so it needs a resumable/checkpointed decode to avoid re-paying. Storage: ~230 MB of non-purgeable Application Support per decoded hour; three episodes is ~700 MB.
Cost: MEDIUM-LARGE. DownloadManager + AnalysisAudioService.performDecode (the checkpointed partial cache is the real work) + job minting. Adjacent to playhead-4dqe.

**B. Bound the first promise to what one window can actually deliver: a first-listen slice.**
Buys: cap the first job at ~300 audio-seconds of depth from the playhead. At 3.1x realtime that costs ~100 s of ASR and fits inside a 197 s window even paying a cold 32-minute decode. The user gets a clean first five minutes — where pre-roll lives — within ONE grant of the download instead of 4.5 hours. This is the only option that changes the number Dan feels on day one.
Risks: explicitly not full coverage; mid-roll and post-roll stay unknown for a long time, which is precisely the coverage program's complaint. It also cuts against the current escalation ladder, which pushes desiredCoverageSec to 83-91 % of duration so the episode is fully scanned.
Cost: SMALL-MEDIUM. The tiering exists (defaultT0DepthSeconds / t1 / t2); this is a policy change to how fast the ladder escalates, plus a 'finish one T0 slice before starting anyone else's' rule in the drain.

**C. Fire day-zero rediff for every completed download, not only tapped ones.**
Buys: the fast path that already works. Twelve seconds, no transcript, no ASR, no FM, four DAI ad boundaries at confidence 1.0. All three episodes would have had day-zero boundaries instead of one. It is the only thing on this device that met Dan's 'finished before he presses play' bar.
Risks: bandwidth — 66 MB per episode (the ledger already tracks a day-zero byte budget: dayZeroBudgetSpentBytes 66,010,142); it finds DAI-stitched ads only, so host-read still needs the transcript; and all four landed markOnly, so without the eligibility work it produces banners rather than skips.
Cost: SMALL for the kickoff change. The byte-budget policy is the real conversation. Overlaps playhead-4dqe.

My read, offered not decided: B is the only one that moves the day-one experience this week, C is the cheapest real win and is already proven on this device, A is the correct long-term fix and the largest. B+C together would give a new user pre-roll boundaries in seconds and a good first five minutes in one window.

=== FILED / RESIDUAL ===

FILED playhead-xygy (P1): engine_silent_timeout is reported for a stage that ran 14.7 s. AnalysisJobRunner.swift:665-668's timeout arm returns a hardcoded (0, nil, false), and a BGTask expiry produces the SAME tuple via the observer, so classify() cannot tell 'nobody spoke for five minutes' from 'the OS took the window back'. They have opposite remedies, and this one cost real time in this investigation.

NOT FILED, noted: (i) analysis_jobs.featureCoverageSec is 0.0 for job 5D8284BD while its asset holds 3,840 s of durable features — arguably correct-until-outcome, but AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:1977 reads job.featureCoverageSec in an eligibility predicate, so it is worth a look if anyone touches that path. (ii) the duplicate FM windows in window 1 belong to the y8a3 / 5q8l / 7iy5 family.

RESIDUAL, honestly: the 278 s is decode PLUS features and this data cannot split them — PreAnalysisInstrumentation stage signposts are os_signpost only and are not persisted. If the split matters to choosing between options A and B, one instrumented device run settles it. And Q4 stays open until Documents/bg-task-log.jsonl is pulled.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
DAN'S DECISION 2026-08-10: OPTION C FIRST — fire day-zero rediff on EVERY download, not only tapped ones.

WHY C AND NOT A OR B: the establish round's strongest single fact is that day-zero rediff resolved at 13:02:33, TWELVE SECONDS after download, producing four dayZeroRediffByteExact windows at confidence 1.0 for a 66MB fetch. It fired for exactly one of three episodes because the kickoff source was 'download_and_analyze_tap'; the other two have NO attempt row at all and zero ad windows 3.5 hours later. So the lane that already beats the pipeline by three orders of magnitude simply is not being started for most downloads. That is the best ratio available: smallest change, largest and most immediate user-visible effect, and it is the deterministic lane whose marks Dan has left alone every time he has judged them.

A and B are NOT rejected — deferred pending C's measurement. A (decode+features at download completion, ~5.5x more transcript per window) is the structural fix for the 84%-decode finding and remains the right long-term answer; B (a bounded ~300 audio-second first-listen slice one window can finish) is the middle option. Re-decide after C is on device and measured.

SCOPE FOR THE IMPLEMENTING ROUND — establish before changing:
1. Find every path that can produce a downloaded episode and enumerate which ones currently reach the day-zero kickoff. The witness is that 'download_and_analyze_tap' fired and the others did not; name the actual sources (background download completion, subscription auto-download, queue drain, etc.) rather than assuming.
2. Do NOT weaken the p70f protections. Day-zero once cost 108MB per replay; playhead-3oyz added a same-session retry ONLY for zero-byte fetch_failed exits precisely because bandwidth is the constraint. Firing on every download multiplies fetch volume by the number of untapped downloads — QUANTIFY that (bytes per attempt x expected downloads/day) and state it. If it needs a cap, a transport gate (wifi-only), or a per-day budget, say so; Dan pays for this in the user's data plan.
3. Respect the existing attempt/backoff machinery (DayZeroRediffAttemptPolicy) — this is about WHO STARTS it, not about relaxing when it may retry.
4. Measure the expected effect honestly: how many of the pull's assets would have gotten a day-zero attempt under the new rule, and what fraction of them would plausibly have produced byte-exact marks. Do not claim a benefit the corpus cannot support.

Related: playhead-4dqe (day-0 at DOWNLOAD time — read it first, this may be a gap in what it shipped), p70f (the replay bleed that justifies the backoff), 3oyz (same-session retry, merged), evc1 (a day-0 mark may seed a pod walk), xygy (filed by this round: engine_silent_timeout is indistinguishable from a BGTask expiry).

STILL OPEN from the establish round, not blocked by C: the 84%-decode root cause itself (AnalysisJobRunner stage order; AnalysisAudio.swift:251 caches only at decode COMPLETION and :461 deliberately does not cache a truncated decode), and Q4 — whether iOS is granting fewer windows than we think — which needs Documents/bg-task-log.jsonl pulled from the device (BGTaskTelemetryLogger.swift:18). Neither is settled.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
CANDIDATE CAUSE FOR THE 2h22m GRANT GAP — found in the playhead-cnql R1 review, 2026-08-10. UNPROVEN; recorded so it is not lost.

MECHANISM. cnql R1 found that DownloadManager.registerShared/registerAppDelegate had exactly one production call site each — PlayheadApp.swift:127-128, inside a SwiftUI .task. On a sceneless handleEventsForBackgroundURLSession relaunch that never runs, so DownloadManager.shared is nil. Two consequences on that launch, both observed in the log:

  1. didFinishLaunchingWithOptions logged 'scanForSuspendedTransfers skipped — no DownloadManager registered' (playhead-hyht's force-quit scan never ran).
  2. urlSessionDidFinishEvents(forBackgroundURLSession:) could not reach the stored OS completion handler, so it was NEVER INVOKED.

(2) is the one that bears on this bead. iOS hands the app that completion handler expressly to be called back when the app has finished processing background-session events, and an app that does not call it is documented as being treated less generously by the background scheduler thereafter. That is the correct SHAPE for 'no window granted at all for 2h22m' — a scheduling penalty, not a budget exhaustion. It is a different failure from the 'expired, jobsCompleted 0' windows this bead is about: those are windows GRANTED and wasted; this would be windows NOT GRANTED.

WHY IT IS ONLY A CANDIDATE. I have not shown the handler actually went uncalled on this device, only that the code path could not reach it. The gap is a single observation (n=1) and iOS withholds discretionary windows for many reasons — thermals, charge state, and 'device never idle' is the documented cause of the 2026-07-22 backfill stall (project_backfill_stall_bgtask). Do not treat this as diagnosed.

THE TEST, which is free. cnql fixes exactly this: registration moves to PlayheadRuntime.init on the launch path and the delegate self-registers in didFinishLaunchingWithOptions, so the handler becomes reachable on a headless relaunch. PREDICTION: after cnql installs, background-window GRANT FREQUENCY rises — i.e. gaps like 13:18 -> 15:40 get shorter — INDEPENDENTLY of whether any window completes more jobs. That separates it cleanly from this bead's own cause, which predicts the opposite (grants unchanged, completions still zero). Measure grant timestamps from background_window_runs on the next pull after the cnql build and compare gap distribution against the db-postwipe2 control.

If the prediction holds, part of what looks like a cold-start problem is a scheduling penalty we inflicted on ourselves, and options A/B should be re-costed before either is built.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
SELF-CORRECTION on the cnql grant-gap hypothesis I recorded earlier today. The pull db-db-r2wait (17:33 UTC) WEAKENS it, and I would rather say so now than let it stand as the leading theory.

GRANT TIMELINE since the wipe, all 10 windows in background_task_runs:

  13:08:44                     13:18:21  (+9m37s)   13:18:21  (same instant, 2nd entry point)
  15:40:36  (+2h22m)  <- the gap this bead recorded
  16:48:50  (+1h08m)
  16:58:25  (+9m35s)  recovered_work
  17:19:30  (+21m)    admitted_work
  17:28:35  (+9m)

The gaps are 9m, 2h22m, 1h08m, 9m, 21m, 9m. Grants become DENSE from 16:48 onward — five windows in 40 minutes against one in the preceding 2h22m.

WHAT CHANGED AT 16:48: Dan downloaded two new episodes, 60DFF7B4 at 16:48:53 and 590D6656 at 16:50:56. The dense grants begin at 16:48:50, three seconds BEFORE the first of them is recorded.

So grant density tracks USER ACTIVITY, which is the documented iOS behaviour and the recorded cause of the 2026-07-22 backfill stall ('iOS granted ~0 discretionary windows overnight; device never idle'). This device is on 9e31bf1c and does NOT contain cnql, so the improvement cannot be attributed to the fix — an unfixed build produced dense grants as soon as the user touched it.

STATUS OF THE HYPOTHESIS: weakened, not refuted. An uncalled urlSessionDidFinishEvents completion handler remains a real mechanism with a real penalty, and it would predict a LOWER floor on grant frequency during idle. But it is no longer needed to explain the 2h22m gap, because ordinary idleness explains it, and ordinary idleness is already documented on this project. Prefer the boring explanation until the measurement says otherwise.

THE TEST IS UNCHANGED BUT NOW NEEDS A CONTROL. Comparing grant gaps before and after the cnql install is not enough, because Dan's usage differs between the two windows. The comparison has to be gaps during COMPARABLE IDLE — e.g. overnight, no downloads, screen off — on each build. Without that control the measurement will show whatever his listening schedule showed.

The bead's own finding is untouched by this and is where the value still is: ten windows since the wipe, TWO of which did real work (recovered_work, admitted_work), and jobsCompleted = 0 in every single one.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
FULL-DAY BACKGROUND WINDOW PROFILE, device build 9e31bf1c, pulls db-db-r2wait / db-evening2 / db-night1. This is the complete grant record since the 13:02 wipe and it shows a THREE-PHASE degradation.

  PHASE 1  13:08 - 16:58   windows 196, 197, 233, 239, 288, 289, 294, 295 s
  PHASE 2  20:12 - 21:53   windows 19, 35, 22, 26, 25, 13, 13, 13 s
  PHASE 3  21:53 - 23:40   NO WINDOW GRANTED AT ALL (1h47m)

Across every phase, in every window, jobsCompleted = 0.

STATE AT 23:40, unchanged from 21:53 (1h47m apart, byte-identical counters):
  transcript_chunks        3549 -> 3549
  semantic_scan_results      17 ->   17

THIS SUPPORTS THE BORING EXPLANATION, and I am recording that against my own earlier hypothesis. I proposed that cnql's uncalled urlSessionDidFinishEvents completion handler was costing background scheduling budget. Phase 3 is total quiescence on an idle evening device with no user activity — exactly what project_backfill_stall_bgtask_2026-07-22 documents ('iOS granted ~0 discretionary windows overnight; device never idle' was that day's inverse). Phase 2's dense-but-short grants also began three seconds before Dan's 16:48 download. Activity explains the shape without needing a penalty. The cnql hypothesis is not refuted, but it is not needed, and it should not be the leading theory.

WHAT IS NOT EXPLAINED BY IDLENESS, and is this bead's own finding: PHASE 2. Eight windows were granted totalling ~166 s of real background time, and they produced ZERO scan rows while transcription advanced 768 chunks over the same span. Transcription made progress because 26od/fil5 made it incremental and persistent. The ad scan produced nothing because its unit of work cannot start, let alone finish, inside a 13-35 s grant — the FM metadata deadline alone exceeds the whole window.

SO THE LEVER THIS BEAD IS ABOUT IS WORK-UNIT GRANULARITY, not window count. Options A and B as filed both assume the window is long enough to be worth entering. Phase 2 says that assumption fails on a real device in a real state, and that the remedy that already worked once — make the work incremental and persist partial progress — has not been applied to the scan. Worth re-costing A and B against a third option shaped like 26od.

CAVEAT, stated plainly: no thermal state, battery level or Low Power Mode reading is recorded in this DB, and all three produce the Phase 2 shape. I am naming the CONSEQUENCE as established and the CAUSE as unestablished.

title: "Always skip this sponsor" persists .falsePositive — the button may teach the OPPOSITE of its label
description:
Found while reviewing playhead-ar60 (R1 noticed it; orchestrator confirmed the call site). NOT fixed there — it predates ar60 and is a product-semantics question for Dan.

WITNESS: Playhead/Views/NowPlaying/NowPlayingView.swift:431-458, the onAlwaysSkipSponsorAsync handler behind AdBannerView.alwaysSkipSponsorAction (the button on an AUTO-SKIPPED banner, playhead-3bv.4). It writes:
  scope = CorrectionScope.sponsorOnShow(podcastId:sponsor:)   // 'Sponsor veto across all episodes of a podcast' (UserCorrectionStore.swift:43-44)
  source = .manualVeto
  correctionType = .falsePositive

In this codebase .falsePositive means 'the detector said ad, and it was not' — it SUPPRESSES future detection. The user's gesture means 'yes, this is an ad, always skip it', which should REINFORCE. If the persisted direction is what the pipeline acts on, one tap teaches the system that this sponsor is not an ad, across every episode of that show — and detection suppression removes the skip, not just the banner.

Downstream evidence (from ar60 R1, measured): a fresh suppressor's decay weight is near 1, so passthrough goes to ~0, so every span in the asset lands under the 0.40 gate (BackfillEvidenceFusion.swift:989) and comes back blockedByUserCorrection. ar60's R1 fix (e32d6600) stops that from muting the banners, but the suppression of the DETECTION direction is untouched and is the thing in question here.

A second writer of the same scope+type: PersistentUserCorrectionStore.recordVeto(span:ledgerEntries:) (UserCorrectionStore.swift:831) emits a sponsorOnShow falsePositive for every brandSpan evidence entry on a vetoed span — that one is a genuine veto and is probably correct; it is the BUTTON whose direction is suspect.

QUESTIONS FOR DAN (do not implement without his call):
1. What should the button mean? 'Always skip' (reinforce: this IS an ad — arguably .falseNegative or a new confirmation type), or 'stop showing me this banner' (a UI-suppression concept that must NOT touch detection)?
2. If it is reinforcement, the fix is a correctionType change plus a migration decision for any already-recorded events (Dan is the only user; the pull currently shows ZERO sponsorOnShow rows, so there may be nothing to migrate — verify before assuming).
3. If it is banner-suppression, that is a new concept: detection stays, actuation stays, only the affordance goes quiet — and it needs a name that cannot be read as a detection verdict (the standing defect class).

Related: ar60 (the fix that made this reachable-looking), atr3, 3bv.4 (the button's origin), feedback: 'the banner is a skip affordance' — it fires on playhead ENTRY so Dan can skip.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
DAN'S RULING 2026-08-09: the button SHOULD always skip the sponsor — i.e. the gesture is REINFORCEMENT ('yes, this is an ad'), not a veto. So the shipped correctionType .falsePositive is INVERTED and this is a real bug, not just ambiguous naming: today the button teaches the detector that this sponsor is NOT an ad (show-wide), which suppresses detection and therefore removes the skip. Press 'always skip' -> get 'never skip'.

SCOPE now has two parts:
1. FIX THE DIRECTION. The persisted event must mean 'this IS an ad, keep skipping it across this show'. Do NOT just flip .falsePositive -> .falseNegative without checking what each type does downstream (falseNegative may mean 'you MISSED an ad here', which is a different claim from 'this detection was right'); the right shape may be a confirmation/reinforcement type that does not exist yet. Establish before implementing. Also decide what a reinforcing sponsorOnShow should do to the correction factor — it is the boost direction, and ar60 measured that boosts crossing SkipOrchestrator's 0.7 preload floor is a real effect, so a reinforcement must not become an unbounded inflator.
2. CLEARER CTA (Dan: 'maybe lets make the cta clearer?'). The copy should say plainly what the tap does and over what population — it is show-wide, permanent-ish, and about a SPONSOR, not this one span. External-copy rules apply (no 'ad detection'/'AI'; peace-of-mind framing, not metrics).

Migration: the pull shows ZERO sponsorOnShow rows today, so there is likely nothing to migrate — VERIFY against the device DB before assuming, since Dan may press it before this ships.

Prereq/interaction: ar60's R1 fix (e32d6600) means a show-wide veto keeps .confirmed so banners still fire; and atr3 (the 0.7 preload floor reading detection) interacts with the boost direction. Read both before designing.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
PROMOTED by Dan 2026-08-09: moved ahead of jzj0/absa/nsjn — runs immediately after ar60 merges.

WHY IT GOT MORE URGENT TODAY: Dan's atr3 decision (SkipOrchestrator's 0.7 cross-launch preload floor now reads ACTUATION, not raw detection, landing in ar60 as 803013bd). Before that change an inverted .falsePositive merely lowered a score. Now it can push a span BELOW the preload floor entirely, so on relaunch that span is neither skipped NOR bannered — it goes silent. Strictly larger blast radius than when this bead was filed hours earlier. (Recorded by ar60 R3; not speculation.)

Also note ar60's R1 fix (e32d6600) already shrank one part of the radius: a show-wide veto now keeps .confirmed, so it no longer withholds every fusion banner in the episode. What remains is the DIRECTION being wrong.

READ BEFORE DESIGNING: this bead's earlier comment (Dan's ruling + the two-part scope: fix the direction, clearer CTA), playhead-atr3 (the decision and its reasoning), ar60's diff (the V47 detection/actuation split and CorrectionFactorSnapshot per-span scoping — the reinforcement direction has to compose with that), and the memory principle 'the highest quality signal we have is a user correction' (feedback_user_correction_is_the_best_signal_2026-08-09) — an inverted correction is far more damaging under a system that trusts corrections, which is what we just built.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
ESTABLISH (implementer, R0) — traced every consumer before touching code.

FINDING 1 — THE DIRECTION DISCRIMINATOR IS `source`, NOT `correctionType`. Every live read-side consumer keys on `event.source?.kind` (CorrectionSource.kind -> CorrectionKind), not on the persisted `correctionType`:
  * PersistentUserCorrectionStore.correctionPassthroughFactor (source?.kind == .falsePositive || source == nil)
  * .correctionBoostFactor(for:) and (for:overlapping:)
  * .correctionFactorSnapshot(for:)  <- the ONLY path to actuationConfidence
  * .activeFalsePositiveScopes / .activeFalseNegativeScopes
  * TrainingExampleMaterializer (userReverted / userReportedFalseNegative)
  * LearningArtifactIngestor.applySponsorSideEffect (source?.kind ?? kindFor(effectiveCorrectionType))
`correctionType` is read only by AnalysisStore's dedupe identity (effectiveCorrectionType is a column of the UNIQUE INDEX), CorpusExporter (diagnostics), and as the legacy FALLBACK when source is nil. So flipping ONLY correctionType would have changed nothing on the live path: `source: .manualVeto` -> kind .falsePositive -> suppress. BOTH must move.

FINDING 2 — A REINFORCEMENT SHAPE ALREADY EXISTS; no new CorrectionType is warranted. Direction is a 2-valued vocabulary (CorrectionKind); the SCOPE carries the population. `sponsorOnShow` + FN already has a defined production meaning, in LearningArtifactIngestor.applySponsorSideEffect: 'FN on a sponsor scope means every episode of this show really did sponsor X, please remember that' -> knowledgeStore.recordCandidate. FP on the same scope -> recordRollback. So the reinforcing shape is (scope: .sponsorOnShow, source: .falseNegative, correctionType: .falseNegative). CorrectionSource.fidelityRank already documents `.falseNegative` as 'manualVeto's opposite-signed twin' at the same rank 3 — the inversion the ladder anticipated. A third CorrectionType case would fork every CorrectionKind switch and the persisted-identity path for zero new expressive power.

FINDING 3 — TWO PLACES WOULD STILL READ IT BACKWARDS after a naive flip:
  (a) CorrectionFactorSnapshot: a show-wide scope is stored range: nil = applies to EVERY span, so a fresh booster multiplies every span in the asset by up to 2.0. That is the unbounded inflator ar60 measured (five spans crossed the 0.7 preload floor on inflation alone). It also FALSIFIES the safety claim SkipOrchestrator.preloadAdmissibleWindows already asserts in its own doc: 'CorrectionFactorSnapshot now evaluates per span, so a reinforcement can only lift a span it actually overlaps.' True for span scopes; false for show-wide ones.
  (b) SponsorKnowledgeStore.activeEntriesWithNegativeMemory is DIRECTION-BLIND — it calls AnalysisStore.correctionScopesPresent(from:), a bare 'SELECT DISTINCT scope ... WHERE scope IN (...)'. ANY row with that scope string removes the sponsor from the active lexicon. So pressing 'always skip Squarespace' would delete Squarespace from the show's sponsor lexicon. Same inversion, one layer down.

FINDING 4 — SECOND WRITER: PersistentUserCorrectionStore.recordVeto(span:ledgerEntries:) keeps .manualVeto/.falsePositive (a genuine veto). Verified callers: ZERO in production. `recordVeto(span:)` and the ledger variant are referenced only from PlayheadTests (UserCorrectionReadSideTests, SpliceSlotOwnershipCorrectionTests, CorrectionAttributionTests, two test doubles) and from one AdDetectionService COMMENT. This extends ar60 R2's finding to the ledger variant. Unchanged.

FINDING 5 — MIGRATION: VERIFIED, nothing to migrate. Device DB (scratchpad/db-corrected2/analysis.sqlite, copied before reading) has 30 correction_events rows, ALL `exactTimeSpan`: manualVeto/falsePositive 13, falseNegative/falseNegative 11, bannerAutoSkipConfirmed/falseNegative 3, bannerSuggestionConfirmed/falseNegative 3. ZERO sponsorOnShow rows (query: scope LIKE 'sponsorOnShow%' -> empty). No migration, no data decision for Dan.

ALSO NOTED, NOT TOUCHED: BroadCorrectionEvaluator (shouldPromote/shouldActAloneSuppress) has ZERO production callers — test-only today. AtomEvidence.splitScopes drops show-wide scopes entirely, so sponsorOnShow contributes nothing to the veto/confirm atom masks either direction.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED + VERIFIED (R0 implementer). Branch bead/playhead-q6y3, three commits on base 0ad56882.

THE DECISION. The button persists scope: .sponsorOnShow (unchanged — the right population), source: .falseNegative, correctionType: .falseNegative. BOTH fields move, and that is not belt-and-braces: every live read-side consumer keys on event.source?.kind and reads correctionType only as the legacy fallback for source == nil rows, so flipping correctionType alone would have changed nothing that runs. No new CorrectionType case — the SCOPE carries the population and the SOURCE carries the direction, and (scope: .sponsorOnShow, direction: FN) already had a defined production meaning in LearningArtifactIngestor.applySponsorSideEffect ('every episode of this show really did sponsor X, please remember that' -> recordCandidate). CorrectionSource.fidelityRank already documented .falseNegative as .manualVeto's opposite-signed twin at the same rank 3.

THE BOUND, in two places, both required:
(A) PersistentUserCorrectionStore.correctionFactorSnapshot no longer records a SHOW-WIDE scope as a BOOSTER (show-wide SUPPRESSORS unchanged, still range: nil).
