This is ar60's own rule — 'a correction that cannot say WHERE acts in the direction that cannot cost the user a skip they did not ask for' — extended from .unplaceable to .everywhere, and it MAKES TRUE the invariant SkipOrchestrator.preloadAdmissibleWindows already asserts in its own doc ('a reinforcement can only lift a span it actually overlaps'), which was true for span scopes and false for show-wide ones. No second numeric bound on the boost; the fix is scope, which is what atr3 asked for.
(B) AnalysisStore.correctionScopesPresent was direction-BLIND (bare SELECT DISTINCT scope WHERE scope IN (...)), so SponsorKnowledgeStore.activeEntriesWithNegativeMemory would have read 'yes, this is an ad' as grounds to delete the sponsor from the show's active lexicon — the same inversion one layer down. Replaced by suppressingCorrectionScopesPresent, SQL predicate mirroring the Swift one exactly (including unknown/corrupt source == suppressor), boost-source list DERIVED from CorrectionSource.kind.

The reinforcement's POSITIVE effect is the knowledge-store confirmation, which is corroboration-gated by construction: recordCandidate at minCandidateConfidence 0.5, minConfirmationsForActive 2, and the ingestor fires side effects only on a NEW insert whose identity includes analysisAssetId — so promotion needs presses on TWO DISTINCT EPISODES, which is exactly BroadCorrectionScope.sponsorOnShow.requiredDistinctEpisodes. It raises the sponsor where the sponsor is named; it never multiplies a span.

MIGRATION: none. Verified twice against scratchpad/db-corrected2/analysis.sqlite (read from a copy; md5 98ee77aace766ae221210dfb82ae2d0b both times): 30 correction_events, ALL exactTimeSpan, ZERO sponsorOnShow, ZERO source IS NULL. NOTE FOR DAN if he presses the button before this ships: a pre-fix row would COEXIST with a post-fix one (effectiveCorrectionType is part of the durable dedupe identity), and the old row is a show-wide suppressor that still applies everywhere — so the inversion would remain in force. That is a data decision, deliberately not migrated silently.

CTA: 'Always skip <Sponsor> on this show' (was 'Always skip this sponsor', which named neither the sponsor nor the population). Hint: 'Remembers <Sponsor> as one to skip on this show — every episode, from now on'. It says REMEMBERS, not 'will skip', because after the bound no single tap can guarantee the outcome — an adversarial-review finding, and the honest framing. Receipt mirrors the CTA. Copy is three static helpers so it is unit-testable.

VERIFICATION.
* Scoped gate, 15 requested suites, requested == reported (11 Swift Testing suites + 4 XCTest classes): 62 Swift Testing tests + 113 XCTest cases, 0 failures, GATE_EXIT=0.
* ANTI-VACUITY BY MUTATION, not by inspection. Reverted all three production changes at once and re-ran: GATE_EXIT=65, and exactly the intended rails went red — showWideBoosterIsAppliedNowhere (5 issues, INCLUDING 'actuation < preloadFloor', the 0.7 rail), placedBoosterSurvivesAlongsideAShowWideOne (3), reinforcementDoesNotNegate (1), testWiringPersistsTheReinforcementDirection (4 assertions). Every neighbouring pre-existing test still PASSED under the mutation (show-wide SUPPRESSORS apply everywhere; DE0784D8; activeEntriesWithNegativeMemory filters corrected sponsors; non-sponsor types unaffected), so the rails are specific rather than blanket. Sources restored with an explicit-path git checkout; git status --porcelain -- Playhead PlayheadTests scripts is clean.
* Worth recording for the next person: a SOURCE CANARY is evaluated against the working tree at TEST time, not against the compiled binary, so a mutation run must not restore sources until the tests have finished — restoring after the build phase would have silently green-lit the canary.

FILED, NOT FIXED (bead is the ceiling): playhead-hpyt (TrainingExampleMaterializer stamps EVERY scan region of an asset from a show-wide scope; the boost direction is newly reachable — offline training labels only, nothing touching the preload floor or the auto-skip gates) and playhead-k511 (recordVeto(span:), recordVeto(span:ledgerEntries:) and ALL of BroadCorrectionEvaluator have zero production callers, and prose in AdDetectionService cites the second one as a live writer).

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
R1 REVIEW (fresh reviewer). Verdict: the direction fix and both bounds are CORRECT. One copy defect fixed here (1b02f96b); two beads filed. The headline is not a defect in the diff — it is what the diff reveals about the button.

WHAT ONE PRESS ACHIEVES, AND WHAT TWO ACHIEVE — traced end to end, and Dan needs to hear it in these words.

ONE PRESS: nothing observable, anywhere. It writes a correction_events row (sponsorOnShow / falseNegative / falseNegative), a KnowledgeCandidateEvent, and a sponsor entry at confirmationCount 1 -> state `.quarantined`. Every live consumer of the correction is now correctly indifferent to it: the booster is placed nowhere (bound A), AtomEvidence.splitScopes drops show-wide scopes so the masks are `[:]`, correctionBoostFactor(for:overlapping:) already excluded show-wide scopes, and correctionReplayCandidates requires `.exactTimeSpan`. Nothing reads a `.quarantined` knowledge entry. No skip moves, no banner changes, no confidence changes.

TWO PRESSES, ON TWO DISTINCT EPISODES: the entry reaches confirmationCount 2 -> `.active`. It must be two distinct analysisAssetIds — the ingestor fires side effects only on a NEW insert and the durable identity includes analysisAssetId, so two presses on the same episode dedupe to one. (Corollary: if `runtime.currentAnalysisAssetId` is nil the site falls back to `"podcast:<id>"`, which is the SAME string for every episode of the show, so two such presses can never promote.)

AND THEN? MEASURED: the only production reader of an `.active` SponsorKnowledgeEntry is `ASRVocabularyProvider` — the sponsor name joins the speech recognizer's contextual strings for that podcast, affecting episodes transcribed after that point. That is the whole delivered effect. `SponsorKnowledgeMatcher.match(atoms:podcastId:knowledgeStore:)` has ZERO production callers (RegionShadowPhase.swift:188 calls the legacy stub returning `[]`, and RegionShadowPhase.Input has no knowledgeStore field), and `CompiledSponsorLexicon` is never constructed in production (all 9 production `LexicalScanner(...)` sites take the default `compiledLexicon: nil`). Device pull corroborates: `sponsor_knowledge_entries` = 0 rows and `knowledge_candidate_events` = 0 rows — `LearningArtifactIngestor.applySponsorSideEffect` is the store's ONLY production writer, and until this bead the only sponsorOnShow writer wrote FP, which routes to `recordRollback`, a no-op with no entry. THIS BEAD IS WHAT MAKES THE TABLE NON-EMPTY FOR THE FIRST TIME. Filed as playhead-shjn (P1) with the three fix shapes.

FINDING FIXED HERE (copy, in scope by Dan's request): the receipt said "Always skipping <sponsor> on this show" — a standing-behaviour claim, sitting one control away from a hint the implementer had already softened to "Remembers …" for exactly this reason. It is the second over-promise. Now "Remembering <sponsor> as one to skip on this show": the HINT's words in the present continuous rather than the BUTTON's. The label stays imperative — that is the instruction Dan ruled the button should express; the receipt reports what the app did with it.

VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY, the source-not-correctionType claim: true of eight readers, FALSE of one. `AdDetectionService.correctionReplayCandidates` (11789, 11799) keys on the RAW `event.correctionType` column — neither `source?.kind` nor `effectiveCorrectionType`. It does not affect this bead (it also requires `.exactTimeSpan`, which sponsorOnShow never satisfies) and has zero live instances (0 of 30 device rows have a NULL correctionType), but the establish note's "every live read-side consumer" is one reader too strong. Filed as playhead-q9ks (P3).

BOUND (A) — I argued it both ways and it is RIGHT, for a reason the diff does not state. The decisive point is not the inflation risk: it is that `weightedCorrections(for:)` loads by analysisAssetId, so a show-wide booster could only ever have lifted spans in the ONE episode the user was listening to. It was never the mechanism that made the button show-wide; it was an accident that over-fired locally on evidence about no span. Dropping it discards nothing that was reaching future episodes. On the suppress-everywhere / boost-nowhere asymmetry: real in the code, VACUOUS in production — after this change there is no production writer of a show-wide SUPPRESSOR either (recordVeto(span:ledgerEntries:), the only one, has zero production callers — playhead-k511). The show-wide arm of CorrectionFactorSnapshot is now unreachable in both directions. The principled home for the reinforcement is a span-local boost where the sponsor is NAMED, which is exactly playhead-shjn.

BOUND (B) — SQL/Swift mirror AGREES today and the drift is compiler-enforced along the axis that matters: `CorrectionSource.kind` is an exhaustive switch with no default, so a new source case cannot compile without being classified, and `boostSources` is derived from it rather than spelled out. Unknown/undecodable source is a suppressor on both sides (Swift: `source == nil`; SQL: the explicit `source IS NULL OR` disjunct, which is required because `NULL NOT IN (...)` is NULL, not true). One residual axis is NOT enforced: a third `CorrectionKind` case would be a suppressor in SQL (`NOT IN boost`) and a non-suppressor in Swift (`== .falsePositive`). Two-case enum; noted, not filed. NOTE HONESTLY: bound (B)'s only caller chain terminates in a matcher with no production callers, so it is correct and currently unreachable — it becomes load-bearing the day playhead-shjn is wired.

ANTI-VACUITY, delete-the-call-site (2 rails, one combined mutation, disjoint reads):
  * Restored the direction-blind SQL (dropped the directionClause) -> `reinforcementDoesNotNegate` FAILED on `surviving.contains("keepsponsor")`: the reinforced sponsor was deleted from the lexicon, the exact pre-fix inversion. Active Filtering, Matcher Integration and Per-span correction factor scoping all stayed GREEN — the rail is specific, not blanket.
  * Restored "Always skipping …" -> only `testReceiptReportsTheMemoryNotAStandingSkip` failed (3 assertions); the other 13 XCTest cases stayed green.
  Sources restored by copying pre-mutation snapshots back and verified byte-clean with `shasum -a 256 -c` against the WORKING TREE (not against the copies); `git status --porcelain -- Playhead PlayheadTests scripts` shows only the intentional fix.

SCOPED GATE, verdict run (before the mutation, with the fix in place): REQUESTED_SUITES=14, reported 12 Swift Testing suites + 2 XCTest classes = 14. 76 Swift Testing tests in 12 suites passed; 19 XCTest cases, 0 failures. GATE_EXIT=0.

title: Coarse-first scan claim refuses 4 backlog assets: absent podcastId rendered as empty string (scan_claim:podcast_id_missing)
description: First hours of build 2a027a48 on-device (pull db-overnight, 2026-08-08 ~11:00-11:56 UTC): the 13kf coarse-first phase runs and reaches the scan-claim step, but fullEpisodeScan for DE0784D8, AD5F3A0A, 53FC53E3, 83592353 defers with scan_claim:podcast_id_missing (timestamps 11:03-11:31). These are exactly the backlog assets the reach program needs scanned; semantic_scan_results held at 143 rows. The refusal itself is CORRECT and self-documenting: SemanticScanClaim.swift:124-127 — the caller (final-pass hook) passes request.podcastId ?? "", an absent podcast id rendered as a podcast whose id is the empty string — the standing defect class, caught at the claim boundary instead of poisoning the claim key. Fix is UPSTREAM: find why these assets' claim requests carry no podcastId (predate a podcast-identity column? 0hi9/b8hj family) and populate or backfill it; do NOT weaken the claim refusal. Contrast: earlier defer on the same assets was scan_claim:no_coverage_lane_row (old build) — the reorder moved the frontier from ordering to identity. Fresh asset F2F2FC4C completed preAnalysis 11:56 and queued adScanRedrive — watch whether the fresh path banks scan rows.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE ESTABLISHED (witnesses below). NOT a plumbing defect at the claim boundary — a BACKFILL problem with an INHERITANCE chain that guarantees it never self-heals.

1. The single site that renders the absence: AnalysisCoordinator.coarseScanOneAsset (Playhead/Services/AnalysisCoordinator/AnalysisCoordinator.swift:820-838) resolves podcastId from ONE source, analysis_jobs.podcastId on the episode's latest row, and hands "" through when it is NULL. AdDetectionService.runBackfill:4303-4312 then correctly refuses with the fil5 podcastIdMissing claim.

2. Why the row is NULL. analysis_jobs.podcastId is SQL NULL on 53 of 72 rows in db-evening (12 of 19 assets, including all four named). The set/NULL split is temporal at the boundary of playhead-kkzu (7da9a7fa, 2026-08-03), which made the show identity a compulsory spelled-out field of DownloadContext: every one of the 19 non-NULL rows was created at or after 2026-08-03 17:48:58; every row before it is NULL.

3. Why it never heals. Every re-mint path copies job.podcastId verbatim — AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:5225 (tier successor), :6435 (ad-scan re-drive), :6721 (canonical-audio replacement). WITNESS: 53FC53E3's newest row, created 2026-08-08 07:55:05, workKey b60427dd...:1:preAnalysis:adScanRedrive:1, is a re-drive minted on the CURRENT build and carries NULL because its pre-kkzu parent did. F2F2FC4C's identical re-drive at 2026-08-08 11:56:12 carries https://rss2.flightcast.com/xmsftuzjjykcmqwolaqn6mdn because ITS parent was post-kkzu. Same code, same day, opposite outcome — the difference is entirely inherited.

4. The identity is NOT absent from the device; it is in the OTHER store, and the bridge already exists. podcastId IS the feed URL (podcast_profiles.podcastId and podcast_planner_state.podcastId hold exactly the 3 feed URLs; every non-NULL analysis_jobs.podcastId equals the prefix of its own episodeId before '::'). analysis_assets.episodeId IS Episode.canonicalEpisodeKey = feedURL + '::' + feedItemGUID (Playhead/Models/Podcast.swift:222-224), and Episode.resolvedShowIdentity (Podcast.swift:250-274) resolves the show from the relationship with the key-derived inverse as fallback. PlayheadRuntime.setEpisodePodcastIdResolver / episodePodcastIdResolverBox (PlayheadRuntime.swift:318, 3683) is an ALREADY-SHIPPED cross-store seam, installed by PlayheadApp.swift:197, built for the final-pass launch sweep to populate FinalPassJob.podcastId — the exactly analogous problem. The coarse-scan path simply never consulted it.

FIX SHAPE: consult that existing seam, admit the value only in canonical spelling, and REPAIR analysis_jobs.podcastId for the episode so (a) every other NULL reader is fixed too (AnalysisJobReconciler.swift:1551 claim mint, AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:4759, RediffRefetchProduction.swift:521) and (b) the inheritance chain propagates a real id from then on. No schema change, no new persistence strategy, no new Gate case: absence remains expressible and stays TRUE when neither store knows.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED + VERIFIED (scoped, three warm runs, all green).

CHANGE
- AnalysisCoordinator.CoarseScanShowIdentity + static pure resolveCoarseScanShowIdentity(jobPodcastId:episodeStoreIdentity:): one admission gate (RecurrenceMaterialIdentity.canonicalIdentifier) applied to BOTH sources, returning a CASE not a String so the caller can tell 'found' from 'recovered' and repair the lane. Lane wins over episode store — a second observation may fill a hole, never re-point an episode.
- The lane read is now AnalysisStore.fetchRecordedPodcastId(forEpisodeId:) (podcastId IS NOT NULL, ORDER BY createdAt), NOT fetchLatestJobForEpisode(_:)?.podcastId. The latter has no NULL filter and orders by updatedAt, so one newer NULL shadows every attributed row — and NULL rows are still minted daily by AnalysisJobReconciler.discoverUnEnqueuedDownloads (filed as playhead-7ba4). Without this switch the repair would work once and then stop.
- AnalysisStore.backfillJobPodcastId(episodeId:podcastId:) -> Int: UPDATE ... WHERE episodeId = ? AND podcastId IS NULL. Idempotent and non-destructive by construction; deliberately does NOT touch updatedAt (that column is the clock fetchLatestJobForEpisode orders by and the stranded-lease reaper keys on, and this write changes no state).
- PlayheadRuntime wires the coordinator's resolver from the ALREADY-SHIPPED episodePodcastIdResolverBox, reading the box AT CALL TIME so PlayheadApp's later install is race-free without a poll.
- PlayheadApp's two resolvers now answer Episode.resolvedShowIdentity rather than podcast?.feedURL.absoluteString — canonical spelling only (the value is now PERSISTED as a key) plus usn1's key-derived fallback when the relationship is unmaterialised.

NOT WEAKENED: SemanticScanClaim.Gate.podcastIdMissing and AdDetectionService's gate are untouched. When both stores are silent the argument is still '' and the claim still fires — now a statement about the device rather than about one table. No new Gate case was needed because the identity CAN be present.

NO SCHEMA CHANGE, NO MIGRATION: the diff adds one UPDATE on an existing nullable column. Grepped the diff for schemaVersion / user_version / CREATE TABLE / ALTER TABLE / migrat — zero hits.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:

VERIFIED BY THE REVIEW (independent of me), worth recording because it is the bead's acceptance criterion:
- All four assets qualify for fetchAssetIdsWithResumableBackfillJobs at positions 1,3,4,5 of 7, inside coarseScanSweepLimit=8 — so coarseScanOneAsset genuinely runs for them. Each owns exactly one backfill_jobs row (its own deferred claim, retryCount 0), 2,949-6,812 transcript chunks, 3-6 analysis_jobs rows, and every podcastId is true SQL NULL (53 NULL / 19 VALUE / 0 EMPTY of 72) — so backfillJobPodcastId's WHERE podcastId IS NULL will match.

- No consumer of the PlayheadApp resolver change branches on nil (FinalPassRetranscriptionRunner 462/652/850, FinalPassJob.podcastId, FinalPassRevalidationRequest); no test asserted the old value.
- No retain cycle (the wiring closure captures resolverBox + coordinator, never self); no new actor hazard (coarseScanOneAsset already suspends on store and adDetectionService).
- not bumping updatedAt is correct against THREE readers, one of which I had not named: fetchLatestJobForEpisode (14240), the stranded reaper's 600s freshness floor (1759), and DELETE FROM analysis_jobs WHERE updatedAt < ? (14975).

THE ONE THAT MATTERED (P1, now filed as playhead-1shd, NOT fixed here): PlayheadApp's WindowGroup .task is the ONLY writer of episodePodcastIdResolverBox, so on a sceneless background launch — which BackgroundProcessingService:1551 explicitly supports — the resolver is nil and the episode is refused as before. Not fixed because the remedy is moving an install out of a SwiftUI .task, which is an app-bootstrap change. It is a DELAY not a hole: the recovery is needed at most once per episode (the identity is written back, so every later launch reads it from fetchRecordedPodcastId), the shipped final-pass sweep has the same dependency, and the remaining refusal logs resolverInstalled=false. title: a growing transcript should CONTINUE the scan: key the backfill job on (assetId, phase, offset) and carry transcriptVersion as a column
description:
## Supersedes the playhead-7x1s approach. Dan's decision, 2026-08-07.

`playhead-7x1s` is abandoned UNMERGED (branch `bead/playhead-7x1s` kept for reference, 18 commits, 4 review rounds). Its yield was never the code — it was the mechanism and the four rounds of findings, which are this bead's SPECIFICATION.

## The mechanism (verified independently three times)

`backfill_jobs.jobId` is `SHA256(assetId | transcriptVersion | phase | offset)` truncated to 16 hex. The row carries **no transcript version**, and `runJob` re-derives every input from the CURRENT transcript. So `transcriptVersion` names the **transcript's** identity while being read as the **job's**.

`transcriptVersion` is a CONTENT HASH. Transcription runs across sessions, so a longer transcript is a different version, so **every session that extends a transcript mints a new job id with `progressCursor = nil` and orphans the previous row.**

**This is a shipping defect that hits NEW users hardest, not a legacy-install problem.** Measured on `db-new-t2h`, the correlation is exact — one stale row per transcript version:

| asset | stale rows | transcript versions in scan results |
|---|---|---|
| F4CE7F47 | 3 | **3** |
| AD5F3A0A | 2 | **2** |
| DE0784D8 | 1 | **1** |

`transcript_chunks` holds only ONE version per asset today; the extra rows are fossils. `CDD611C4` (6,114 s of audio) holds **4 stale rows and ZERO scan rows** — four full-episode scans minted and orphaned, none ever producing a result. N scales with how many sessions transcription took, so **the longest episodes are punished worst**.

## Why the hash is the defect, not the embedding

R4-Fix6 embedded `transcriptVersion` deliberately and for a GOOD reason, stated at `BackfillJobRunner.swift:615`: so a regenerated transcript produces a fresh row instead of colliding with the prior `.complete` job under the same id, which the M-5 idempotency check would skip — defeating reprocessing. **That reason is legitimate and must be preserved.**

The error is the instrument. Answering "same version?" by hashing makes "same WORK?" unanswerable, and `BackfillJobRunner`'s own comment admits the consequence: the fallback exists "to address the work by what it is instead of by the id one invocation happens to derive." All of 7x1s's bugs lived in that reconstruction.

## What to build

- `jobId = f(assetId, phase, offset)` — **stable across transcript growth**.
- `transcriptVersion` becomes a **column** on `backfill_jobs`.
- Idempotency becomes a real query: *is there a `complete` job for this asset+phase AT THE CURRENT VERSION?* Different version → reprocess. Same version → skip. Exactly R4-Fix6's intent, now expressible.
- **The prize, which neither main nor 7x1s can express: when the transcript GROWS, UPDATE the row and KEEP ITS CURSOR.** Main restarts from zero; 7x1s orphans and later adopts. Neither continues. A longer transcript is more text over the same audio — the scan should carry on, not start again.
- **Legacy rows are DROPPED, not migrated.** Dan: *"I am ok with breaking a schema, I am still the only user."* This also removes the trap: back-filling `transcriptVersion` from the CURRENT transcript would be the standing defect class committed inside the fix for it.

## Deletions this enables

The unfinished-row fallback, the adoption claim row, `replaceAdoptionClaim`, `coveragePolicyPeers`, and rails SX01–SX10 / SY01–SY05. Do NOT port them.

## The SPEC — four rounds of 7x1s findings, each a real production defect. The new design must satisfy all four.

1. **A row nothing can START must not BLOCK.** (7x1s R1) A `failed` row under the retry budget cannot be restarted by `markBackfillJobRunning`, and treating it as live permanently suppressed the asset. **Live in the field: all 5 `failed` rows carry `retryCount = 1` against `maxRetries = 3`, across 4 assets** (causes: `Request has been rate limited`, `FMInferenceTimeoutError`).
2. **A completed row must not be resurrected**, and reprocessing after a version change must still happen (R4-Fix6's original intent).
3. **The playhead-onn6 re-drive window must not be evicted.** `countResumableBackfillJobs` filters to a 0.5 s newest-batch window off an unfiltered `MAX(createdAt)`; a row whose timestamp moves can zero the count and shut the re-drive gate. (7x1s R3/R2, `playhead-9ocm`.)
4. **No value may carry a premise that can EXPIRE.** (7x1s R3) A claim asserting "a carrier is handling this" became permanent suppression once the carrier went terminal, with no version rotation left to escape via.

## Also settle while here

`SemanticScanClaim.jobId` uses the SAME derivation (`playhead-5q8l`, `playhead-r8fl`) — it must move with this change or it re-creates the duplicate on the claim path.

## Relationship to playhead-mfeq

This IS mfeq Tier 3 (opaque composite identity), scoped to its first instance. mfeq Tiers 1 (singleton-for-a-set lint) and 2 (Provenance generalisation) remain separate.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: Correction to the bead body and briefs, caught by the implementer's re-derivation: the 5 `failed`-under-budget rows span **3** assets (DE0784D8, 0C2FC22E x2, 52CD8F5B x2), not 4. The '4' was my miscount of my own table. Every row still carries retryCount=1 vs maxRetries=3; the spec-1 consequence is unchanged.

title: make the standing defect class UNTYPEABLE: three shapes that manufacture mis-readable values, and the mechanism for each
description:
## Why this bead exists

The standing defect class — *a value that names one thing, read as though it named another* — has ~19 shipped instances, and `playhead-lmrx` alone produced **nine inside its own fixes**, four of them in the TEST AND RAIL INSTRUMENTS rather than the code. `playhead-7x1s` has produced one per review round for four rounds, each introduced by the fix for the previous one.

**Vigilance has the failure record. Types have the success record.** The two defenses that have actually held are `playhead-x0lb`'s `CoverageQuantities` (11 single-field frozen structs, making unit confusion untypeable, verified by UNTYPEABLE rails that require the mutant to FAIL TO COMPILE) and `RegionFillDoor` (one identifier every spelling must write, so a fabrication is `missing argument for parameter 'door'`). Dan, 2026-08-06: **"Compiler guarding is best."**

So stop treating this as a reading problem. It is a **manufacturing** problem: the codebase keeps creating values that CAN be misread. There are three recurring shapes. Ban the shapes.

---

## SHAPE 2 — a singleton standing for a set  (TIER 1: cheapest, catches a LIVE class today)

An optional `var` holding "the current X" on a type where more than one X can exist concurrently.

**Confirmed live in `AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift` right now** (2026-08-07, `nowCap` is 2):

| line | field |
|---|---|
| 769 | `private var currentJobId: String?` |
| 770 | `private var currentEpisodeId: String?` |
| 889 | `private var pendingCancelCause: InternalMissCause?` |

`playhead-lmrx` R3 replaced two siblings (`currentRunningTask`, `leaseRenewalTask`) with a `[String: RunningJob]` registry keyed by job id; these three survived. `pendingCancelCause` is precisely what produced lmrx's F9 — a destructive read of a global slot let a second job fall back to `.pipelineError`, take the attempt-spending arm, and **supersede an episode permanently**.

Retroactive catch list for this rule: `playhead-mk6z` (`currentJobId` = last DISPATCHED read as still RUNNING), lmrx F4 (single-slot task), lmrx F9 (global cause), R3's `leaseRenewalTask`. **Four instances, one rule.**

**Mechanism.** Mechanically detectable, no type surgery: a preflight or custom SwiftLint rule flagging an optional stored property matching `^(current|pending|last)[A-Z]` on a type whose concurrency cap exceeds one. Allowlist with a written justification per site, the way `.swiftlint.yml` already tiers its measured rules. **Measure the violation count BEFORE adding it** — the repo's own rule is that a candidate is admitted at a count of exactly zero, or listed with its measured count as a follow-up tier. Do not add a red rule.

---

## SHAPE 3 — a derived number without its derivation  (TIER 2)

Instances: `jobsCompleted` as `baselinePending − residualPending` (queue shrinkage — the queue shrinks on FAILURE too); `jobsAdmitted` as a copy of `jobsSeen`; the battery printing `errors: 72` where 72 is OCCURRENCES ACROSS BATCHES and the distinct rail count is 34 (I misreported that number myself before checking); sum-of-spans read as coverage; `fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime` (a watermark) read as coverage.

**Mechanism.** `playhead-lmrx` already invented the cure and proved it kills mutants: `BackgroundGrantBudget.Provenance`, carrying `.measured(grantObservations:teardownObservations:checkpointObservations:)` vs `.assumed`, with per-field denominators — rail LX18 flips `grantObservations: 132 → 203` and dies. Generalise it: a persisted count or ratio carries the NAMES of its numerator and denominator, so "queue shrinkage" cannot type-check as "completions", and a `.measured` claim is checkable against the ledger.

---

## SHAPE 1 — opaque composite identity  (TIER 3: needs Dan's approval, dissolves 7x1s's whole fallback)

`backfill_jobs.jobId` is a SHA-256 hash over `(assetId, transcriptVersion, phase, offset)`, truncated to 16 hex chars. The row carries **no transcript version**, and `runJob` re-derives every input from the CURRENT transcript. So `transcriptVersion` names the TRANSCRIPT's identity while being read as the JOB's.

**The hash is the defect.** It destroys the ability to ask "is this the same work under a different transcript?", and `BackfillJobRunner.swift`'s own comment says so out loud:

> *"…the unfinished-row fallback below, which addresses the work by what it is instead of by the id one invocation happens to derive."*

Every `playhead-7x1s` bug lives in that reconstruction, and each was introduced by the fix for the previous one:
- **R1** — the fallback adopted a `failed` row under the retry budget, which nothing can START, making it a permanent SUPPRESSOR of the asset's every future coverage-lane pass. Live in the field: all 5 `failed` rows in `db-new-t2h` carry `retryCount = 1` against `maxRetries = 3`, across 4 assets.
- **R2** — the adopt path `continue`d past the mint, so no row existed at the current version's id and the next same-version pass minted a cursor-less FULL episode scan. A redundancy bead ADDING redundancy.
- **R3** — the claim fixing R2 could expire, recreating R1's shape one layer up: no pass, ever, with no version rotation to escape via (`transcriptVersion` is a content hash).

**Mechanism.** Make the key a struct with named fields and put `transcriptVersion` on the row as a column. Then "the same work under a new transcript" is a QUERY, not machinery — and the adopt path, the claim row, `replaceAdoptionClaim`, `coveragePolicyPeers` and their four rounds of repair all stop being necessary.

**This is a persistence-schema change and is Dan's call.** Note the migration is the interesting part: existing rows have no `transcriptVersion`, and back-filling one from the current transcript would be the standing defect class committed during the fix for it.

---

## The specific trigger

Asked while `playhead-7x1s` R4 was reviewing R3's repair, which introduces a claim ROW NAMING ITS CARRIER (`adopted_by:<jobId>`) — a new value, of a kind that is not a job, living in the jobs table, in a codebase whose defining failure is values naming one thing and being read as another. Tier 3 removes the need for it entirely; absent Tier 3, that row wants a type the compiler can see rather than a string convention.

## Sequencing

Tier 1 is independent and can land in any quiet window. Tier 2 wants a real consumer to shape the API. Tier 3 should NOT land mid-loop on `7x1s` — decide it after that bead merges, since it would delete much of what `7x1s` built.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
**Dan approved the schema change, 2026-08-07:** *"I am ok with breaking a schema, I am still the only user."*

So Tier 3 is authorised. The migration concern in the bead body is largely dissolved by that — with one user and a wipeable device DB, back-filling `transcriptVersion` onto existing rows is unnecessary: the rows can be dropped rather than migrated, which also removes the trap named above (back-filling from the CURRENT transcript would have been the standing defect class committed during the fix for it).

**Sequencing question this raises, recorded so it is decided rather than drifted into.** Tier 3 makes the following `playhead-7x1s` machinery unnecessary: the unfinished-row fallback, the adoption claim row, `replaceAdoptionClaim`, and `coveragePolicyPeers`. Four review rounds have found one production defect each, ALL of them inside that machinery. So merging 7x1s and then deleting most of it is churn — but abandoning a working fix for an unproven rewrite is its own risk.

**Decision rule, stated in advance so it is not post-hoc:** let 7x1s R4 finish, then
- **R4 clean →** merge 7x1s (a working reduction available now) and do Tier 3 next as a clean deletion diff.
- **R4 finds a fifth defect in the fallback →** that is the evidence to abandon the fallback approach, close 7x1s unmerged, and go straight to Tier 3.

Either way 7x1s's real yield survives: the MECHANISM (jobId hashing `transcriptVersion`, with per-asset duplication predicted exactly by transcript-version count — F4CE7F47 3 versions / 2.62x, AD5F3A0A 2 / 2.00x, DE0784D8 1 / 1.00x) and the four rounds of findings, which are the SPECIFICATION Tier 3 must satisfy: a row nothing can START must not BLOCK; a completed row must not be resurrected; the onn6 re-drive window must not be evicted; a claim's premise must not be able to expire.

title: a granted window runs the FM scan FIRST, so a complete-transcript episode banks coarse windows instead of starving behind a transcription drain that cannot finish
description:
## Dan's decision, 2026-08-06

Presented three ways to make a ~219 s background grant produce durable work. Dan chose **reorder within the grant** over slicing transcription or admission-by-cost. Rationale recorded: smallest blast radius, no new persistence machinery, and it raises ad-scan coverage directly — which is the actual goal — while leaving the transcription pipeline alone.

## What to do

In `handleBackfillTask`, run `runPendingBackfill()` (the FM / coarse ad-scan phase) BEFORE `drainEligible()` (the transcription drain), both under the `BackgroundGrantBudget` that `playhead-lmrx` introduces.

Today the order is reversed. `drainEligible` awaits an entire `AnalysisJobRunner` job, so on the measured ledger it consumes the whole grant and `runPendingBackfill` is never reached: **108 of 203 expired windows contain exactly one `acquired` event and nothing else**, 33 contain none.

## Why this banks something (re-derive before trusting)

Measured on `scratchpad/db-fg1/analysis.sqlite`, `semantic_scan_results.latencyMs` by pass:

| pass | n | p50 | p90 | max | sum |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| passA | 113 | **6.2 s** | 51.3 s | **1955.6 s** | 4213.8 s |
| passB | 29 | 5.4 s | 19.4 s | 21.8 s | 236.2 s |

At the p50 a 219 s work budget buys ~35 coarse windows; at the p90 it buys ~4. Both are strictly better than the zero it banks today. `playhead-26od` (#345) already makes coarsePassA persist incrementally, so each completed window is durable the moment it lands — no new persistence is needed. **Numerator = FM wall-clock per window; denominator = windows completed. Re-derive both; do not carry these numbers forward on faith.**

## HARD DEPENDENCY on playhead-rkfp — do not land this first

The max above is not decoration. **One passA call took 1955.6 s and ended in `permissive_decoding_failure`/abstain — 44 % of all FM time on the device, spent to produce nothing.** Reordering FM to the front of the grant WITHOUT a per-call deadline makes a bad day worse: that single call eats the entire window, transcription is skipped because FM was first, and the window banks nothing exactly as it does today, only now with the transcription drain starved too.

So `playhead-rkfp` (bound the per-call FM budget) is a prerequisite, not a sibling. Land it first or fold it in.

## Scope note

This does nothing for an episode with no transcript yet — there are no windows to scan. That population is `playhead-lmrx`'s residual and, if it turns out to matter more than the numbers suggest, the transcription-slicing option Dan declined here.

## Watch the standing defect class

"The transcript is complete" must be read from the both-pass union (`fetchTranscribedRegion`), NOT from `fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime` — a watermark reads complete over interior holes. That confusion is playhead-346z and playhead-6r4z, and it is the exact predicate this reorder keys on.

title: transcription re-runs on an already-complete transcript: 96 of 115 attempts persist ZERO chunks, 74 on one episode
description:
## Measured 2026-08-06 from scratchpad/db-fg1/analysis.sqlite (my own re-derivation)

Denominator = the 115 `work_journal` rows that carry a `chunks_persisted` value.

| chunks_persisted | n | share |
|---|---|---|
| **0** | **96** | **83.5 %** |
| >0 | 19 | 16.5 % |

Cause on the 96 zero rows: `pipeline_error` 93, `asr_failed` 3. **Not one of them is an expiry** — these are attempts that ran and produced nothing, not windows that were cut short.

Concentration matters more than the rate: **74 of the 96 are the same episode** (`xmsftuzjjykcmqwolaqn6mdn::flightca…`), which also has the only 13 productive attempts in the set. Four `dHoohVNH::` episodes account for 22 more.

## Why this is separate from lmrx and from 7x1s

`playhead-lmrx` is about a granted window being *cut short*. This is the opposite failure: the attempt runs to a terminal `pipeline_error` and banks nothing. Fixing the grant budget does not help an attempt that would produce zero chunks in any budget.

`playhead-7x1s` is about the same audio being scanned more than once by FM. This is about the same audio being TRANSCRIBED more than once — and 83 % of those re-transcriptions keeping nothing at all.

## The shape to check first

The lmrx implementer observed `chunks_persisted: 0` alongside `transcript_coverage_end_time == episode_duration` — i.e. the episode's transcript is already complete and the pipeline is re-transcribing it anyway. If that holds, the defect is upstream of the failure: work is being *scheduled* that has no reason to run, and the `pipeline_error` is what happens when it does. Confirm the coincidence before assuming the direction.

## Watch the standing defect class

`transcript_coverage_end_time` is a WATERMARK, not coverage — the exact confusion in playhead-346z and playhead-6r4z. Before concluding "the transcript is complete", check the both-pass union (`fetchTranscribedRegion`), not the watermark. A watermark at episode_duration with interior holes would make re-transcription *correct* and move the defect somewhere else entirely.

## Journal context worth carrying

Across the whole ledger: 294 `acquired`, 118 `failed`, 46 `finalized`, and **3 `checkpointed`**. Three checkpoints, total.

title: a ~210 s background window cannot finish a backfill scan, and almost nothing durable survives the expiry
description:
## Measured 2026-08-06 from `scratchpad/db-fg1/analysis.sqlite`

Denominator = all 254 `background_task_runs` rows for `com.playhead.app.analysis.backfill`:

| outcome | n | share | avg duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| **expired** | **203** | **80.0 %** | 209.8 s |
| no_eligible_work | 23 | 9.1 % | 4.7 s |
| admitted_work | 12 | 4.7 % | 168.6 s |
| failed | 9 | 3.5 % | 1581.3 s |
| deferred_capability | 7 | 2.8 % | 3.0 s |

**203 of 254 backfill wakes expired**, each burning ~210 s of OS-granted background
time — roughly 11.8 hours of granted windows in this ledger.

Recovery, by contrast, is healthy: 86 of 97 `recovered_work` at 5.1 s average. The
problem is specific to backfill.

## The work does not finish, and it does not resume

* Across the 12 `admitted_work` runs: **26 jobs admitted, 0 completed**
  (`sum(jobsAdmitted) = 26`, `sum(jobsCompleted) = 0`).
* Only **4 of the 203** expired runs wrote a single `semantic_scan_results` row
  inside their own start/finish window. **199 of 203 produced nothing durable.**
* `backfill_jobs` (denominator 30 rows): 16 queued (14 with `progressCursor IS NULL`),
  7 deferred (6 NULL), 5 failed (5 NULL, 5 retries), 2 complete. **25 of 30 carry no
  `progressCursor` at all** — no job-level resume point, so the next window restarts
  from nothing.

`playhead-26od` (#345) made `coarsePassA` persist incrementally, and that is a
different layer from the `backfill_jobs.progressCursor` measured here. Establish
whether the device binary (`build/device-6r4z`, built 2026-08-06 04:55, later than
26od's 2026-08-04) includes it before concluding anything about coarsePassA.

## Why this is P0 and why it is NOT a lease bead

Filed out of `playhead-mk6z` deliberately. That bead made the live scheduler loop
reclaim a lease whose deadline has passed, which returns a stranded row to the
queue. **It does not make the row completable.** If a granted window cannot finish
a job, faster reclaim only recycles the same job through the same window — it mints
orphans rather than progress. The two fixes compose only if this one lands.

This is a chunking / checkpointing question — how much work is attempted per grant,
and what is written durably when the grant ends — not a lease question, and it should
not be grown into the lease bead.

## Watch the standing defect class

`outcome = 'expired'` names "the OS reclaimed the task", NOT "no work happened", and
`jobsSeen`/`jobsAdmitted`/`jobsCompleted` are all NULL on every expired row because
`finishRun` on the expiration path writes only the outcome. So the ledger cannot
currently answer "how much did this window actually achieve" for 80 % of runs — the
4-of-203 figure above had to be reconstructed by joining scan-row timestamps against
the run window. Instrumenting the expiration path to persist the counters it already
has would make the next measurement direct instead of inferred.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
## Root cause, re-derived 2026-08-06 (db-new-t2h)

The bead's "~210 s window" is the MEAN of a bimodal distribution and understates
the grant. Over the 203 expired backfill runs: p10 36.4 / p25 73.2 / **p50 294.0**
/ p90 295.9 / p95 296.0 / max 321.4. 57 % land at >=290 s (the OS running the task
to its own limit); 24 % end under 60 s (early reclaim). The nine `failed` rows
averaging 1581 s are all `orphan_at_launch` — reaped by a LATER launch, so their
`finishedAt` is not a grant end — and are excluded.

**`handleBackfillTask` gave both of its work drivers `now + 25 * 60` = 1500 s,
5.07x the p90 grant.** `work_journal` shows the consequence exactly: of the 203
expired windows, 108 contain exactly one `acquired` event and nothing else, 33
contain none, and the first `acquired` lands at a median of t+1.0 s. One analysis
job is picked up ~1 s in and the window goes silent to expiry.

Mechanism: `drainEligible` awaits each dispatch pass to completion, and a pass is
a whole `AnalysisJobRunner` job. So the grant is spent inside the first pass;
`runPendingBackfill` is never reached, and neither is the handler's own terminal
`finishRun` — which is why `jobsSeen`/`jobsAdmitted`/`jobsCompleted` are NULL on
every expired row.

**26od IS in the shipped binary and is working.** All 4 of the 203 expired runs
that wrote a `semantic_scan_results` row inside their own window are on 2026-08-06
(0 of 183 before). Job `fm-36377e9d0ae29697` banked 26 rows across three grants.
The coarse checkpoint is not the gap.

**`progressCursor` is honest, not broken.** `fm-36377e...` reads 96.84 with 91 %
of the episode banked because the attempt order is SEEDED (playhead-lxkq) and the
contiguous prefix genuinely stops at the first failed window (97.5-130.9). It is
lossy, not wrong. Making resume consult the durable scan set is `playhead-7x1s`
territory (case (b) in that bead), so it was left alone. Cross-night re-scans of
the same audio are also 7x1s: the three jobs on asset F4CE7F47 carry three
DIFFERENT `transcriptVersion`s, so the reuse key legitimately misses.

## What landed

1. Both drivers bounded by a measured `BackgroundGrantBudget` (255 s design grant
   - 36 s teardown reserve = 219 s of work), derived from the percentiles above.
2. The backfill expiry now tells `AnalysisWorkScheduler` the grant ended
   (`cancelCurrentJob(.taskExpired)`) and WAITS for the requeue to commit. The
   healthy sibling (recovery, 86/97 `recovered_work`) has done this since
   playhead-1nl6; backfill never did, so the dispatched job ran on unaware into
   suspension, leaving a leased `running` row for mk6z's reaper.
3. The expiration path persists `jobsSeen` and `jobsCompleted`.

## The fix that fix made necessary

Wiring the expiry to `cancelCurrentJob` routes ~80 % of grants through the
cancel-catch arm, which charges an attempt and SUPERSEDES at `maxAttemptCount`
(5) with `nextEligibleAt: nil`. A superseded row never comes back (`workKey`
UNIQUE + `INSERT OR IGNORE`). Uncorrected, that would abandon every long episode
permanently on its fifth window. `.taskExpired` is now exempt from the attempt
charge and requeues at the flat `interruptedRequeueDelaySeconds` floor — the
accounting playhead-ngev already established for playback displacement. The
terminal is real: the pull holds two episodes at
`maxAttemptsReached:cancelMidRun` (both `original_cancel_cause = pipeline_error`,
so expiry did not cause those two — but it would have caused many).

`jobsCompleted` was ALSO the standing defect class in this bead's own first
draft: computed as `baselinePending - residualPending` it measures how much the
GLOBAL QUEUE SHRANK. The queue shortens on failure too (112 `failed` vs 45
`finalized` in the pull), and the drain MINTS work while running (tier-advance
`insertNextJob`). It is now the intersection of the baseline job-id SET with
terminal `complete`. `jobsAdmitted` is deliberately left NULL: the pre-fix code
wrote the denominator into it, and this handler has no honest admission count.

## HONEST LIMIT — this does not move 199/203 on its own

The change makes the failure legible and survivable; it does not make it stop.
`drainEligible` still hands a whole analysis job to `runSingleDispatchPass` and
awaits it, and the deadline is only consulted BETWEEN passes — so in the 108
one-dispatch windows the drain is still parked at t+219 s and the handler still
does not reach its normal return. What changes for those windows: the row now
records what was pending and what completed, the in-flight job is cancelled,
requeued and journaled instead of stranded, and it no longer burns an attempt.

Making a granted window productive needs the unit itself to be smaller — slicing
the analysis job so a 219 s budget buys a whole one. That is an architectural
change to the transcription pipeline and is NOT in this bead. Filing it is the
recommended next step, ahead of 7x1s.

title: an expired lease on a running job is never reclaimed, so one wedged episode stops ALL analysis indefinitely
description:
## Measured live, 2026-08-06, `scratchpad/db-charged-early/analysis.sqlite`

    asset           F4CE7F47
    state           running
    leaseOwner      preAnalysis
    leaseExpiresAt  2026-08-06 10:03:50
    updatedAt       2026-08-06 09:58:50
    expired         132 minutes before the pull

The lease was acquired at 09:58:50 and set to expire at 10:03:50 — a **five-minute** lease. It
expired 132 minutes before the pull and **nothing reclaimed it**. Meanwhile 10 jobs sat `queued`.

Lease population at that pull (denominator = 60 `analysis_jobs` rows):

| state | n | leaseExpiresAt NULL | expired |
|---|---|---|---|
| complete | 45 | 45 | 0 |
| queued | 10 | 10 | 0 |
| superseded | 3 | 3 | 0 |
| failed | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| **running** | **1** | **0** | **1** |

So the lease is written correctly at acquisition — one row, non-NULL, on exactly the running job.
**The write path works. The reclaim path did not run.**

## What the device did while blocked

`transcript_chunks` and `semantic_scan_results` were **byte-identical across four pulls spanning
2 h 18 m** (61,315 chunks / 142 scan rows at 09:46, 11:16, 11:55). Last write of any kind:
09:37:46. Last job touch: 09:58:50.

**Charging does not help.** The device was plugged in and idle for ~33 minutes (11:22–11:55) and
produced **zero** rows. That refutes the iOS-background-starvation explanation for this window —
the queue is not starved, it is BLOCKED.

## Why this is P0 and outranks the rest of the board

The scheduler runs **one job at a time** (`currentRunningTask`). A single job holding an expired
lease stops every other episode indefinitely. No reach fix, no detection fix, no amount of idle
time or power can do anything while the slot is held. Every other open bead is downstream of this.

## The mechanism EXISTS — find out why it did not fire

* `AnalysisStore.swift:~14407` writes `leaseOwner`, `leaseExpiresAt`, `state = 'running'`.
* `AnalysisJobReconciler.swift:419` — `let recoverable = expired.filter { $0.state == "running" || $0.state == "queued" || $0.state == "paused" }` — the filter already names `running`.
* `AnalysisJobReconcilerOutcome` carries `expiredLeasesRecovered` and `recoveredStrandedSessionJobs`, and the header says the latter exists precisely because `recoverExpiredLeases` **cannot see** some jobs.

So this is not a missing feature. Establish which of these is true before writing anything:

1. **The reconciler never ran** in that window (nothing invokes it while backgrounded / after the
   app is suspended and resumed).
2. **It ran and `expired` did not include this row** — check how `expired` is computed; if it
   keys on a different clock, column, or a `leaseExpiresAt IS NOT NULL AND < now` predicate that
   is subtly wrong, that is the defect.
3. **It ran, selected the row, and the reclaim write failed or was rolled back.**
4. The row is reachable only by `recoveredStrandedSessionJobs`, and THAT path did not run.

`expiredLeasesRecovered` vs `recoveredStrandedSessionJobs` being counted separately is a strong
hint that (4) is live. Do not guess — instrument or trace.

## Dan's framing, which is the design principle here

> "even if its suspension we shouldnt hold everything if a foreground job gets suspended"

**Correct, and it makes the stuck-vs-suspended question irrelevant to the fix.** A lease exists so
that the cause does not have to be known: it expires, the slot frees, work resumes. A 5-minute
lease that is 132 minutes stale must be reclaimed whether the holder hung, was suspended, or
died. Any fix that requires diagnosing WHY the holder stopped has missed the point of a lease.

## Watch the standing defect class

`leaseExpiresAt` is a DEADLINE, not a heartbeat — a job that is alive and working past its lease
looks identical to one that is dead. If the fix reclaims on expiry alone it may kill live work; if
it requires proof of death it reproduces this bug. **Name which one you are building and why.**
Related: [[playhead-z3jg]] (a pass producing zero coverage re-queues with no brake) and
[[playhead-zv0i]] (priority inversion) were both filed against this same silence and may be
symptoms of THIS defect rather than defects of their own — re-derive before implementing either.

LABELS: reach, scheduler

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
## SHARPENED 2026-08-06 12:54 — the reclaim EXISTS and WORKS, but appears FOREGROUND-ONLY

The original description said the reclaim path "did not run". That is right about the outcome and
wrong about the mechanism, and the difference changes the fix. **Corrected by observation:**

Dan plugged in and foregrounded the Library view at ~12:50. Pull at 12:54:07
(`scratchpad/db-fg1/analysis.sqlite`):

    F4CE7F47   state=complete   leaseOwner=(empty)   leaseExpiresAt=(null)   updated 12:52:16
    F2F2FC4C   state=running    leaseExpiresAt=12:57:16  (172 s in the FUTURE — valid)

The job that had held `running` with a lease expired **132 minutes** cleared at 12:52:16 — the
moment the app came to foreground — and the scheduler immediately claimed the next job with a
fresh valid lease. A second cluster of job updates at **12:01:16** sits between the 11:55 pull
(which showed nothing since 09:58:50) and this one; most plausibly another foreground moment,
but that is inference, not evidence — **establish it, do not assume it.**

### So the defect is narrower and more actionable than first written

Not "expired leases are never reclaimed". Rather: **reclaim appears to run only on foreground /
launch, so a lease that expires while backgrounded stays expired until a human opens the app.**
The mechanism that exists to make the stuck-vs-suspended question irrelevant only fires in the
one state where it is not needed.

### What this does NOT change

The impact is identical and still P0: one job holding the single scheduler slot blocks all
analysis, and **charging does not help** — 33 minutes plugged in and idle (11:22–11:55) produced
zero rows, with `transcript_chunks` and `semantic_scan_results` byte-identical across four pulls
spanning 2 h 18 m (61,315 / 142, last write 09:37:46).

### Re-scoped investigation

Supersedes causes 1–4 in the description. Establish, with evidence:

1. **What invokes the reconciler**, and under which scene phases / BGTask paths. If it is only
   wired to foreground or launch, that is the defect and the rest is detail.
2. **Does a background BGTask path invoke it at all?** `semantic_scan_results.scenePhase` shows
   24 rows written with `background` earlier that morning, so background execution DOES happen —
   the question is whether reclaim is on that path.
3. **Which reclaim actually cleared it** — `recoverExpiredLeases` or `recoveredStrandedSessionJobs`?
   They are counted separately in `AnalysisJobReconcilerOutcome` precisely because the former
   "cannot see" some jobs. The answer decides where the fix goes.
4. Confirm or refute the 12:01:16 cluster as a foreground moment. If work resumed at 12:01
   WITHOUT foreground, the foreground-only hypothesis is wrong and this whole comment is.

### The trap in the fix, restated because it is now closer

`leaseExpiresAt` is a **DEADLINE, not a heartbeat**. A job alive and working past its lease looks
identical to a dead one. Reclaiming on expiry alone can kill live work; requiring proof of death
rebuilds this bug. **Name which you are building and why.** A live example is in this very pull:
`F2F2FC4C` is `running` with a lease 172 s in the future — a correct, healthy claim that must not
be disturbed by whatever reclaim you add.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
## IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-06 — but the sharpened comment's central inference is REFUTED

Branch `bead/playhead-mk6z`, commits `1da496fc` (fix + tests) and `9fbcc546` (MK mutation rails).
Not merged, no PR.

### The four investigation points, with evidence

**1. What invokes the reconciler.** `AnalysisJobReconciler.reconcile()` has exactly TWO production
call sites: `PlayheadRuntime.swift:2668` (the launch bootstrap Task) and
`BackgroundProcessingService.handlePreAnalysisRecovery` (the `preAnalysisRecovery` BGProcessingTask,
`BackgroundProcessingService.swift:1769`). `AnalysisCoordinator.recoverOrphans` has exactly ONE:
`PlayheadRuntime.swift:2642`, bootstrap only. **Nothing is wired to a scene phase at all** — there is
no foreground hook on any reclaim path. The "foreground-only" hypothesis is refuted at the source.

**2. Does a background path invoke it? YES, and it demonstrably ran.** `background_task_runs` in
`db-fg1` records 97 `preanalysis_recovery` runs, every one `scenePhase='background'`, firing every
~30 min through the night: 06:14:56, 06:45:08, 07:15:09, 07:45:29, 08:15:44, **08:45:43 — and then
nothing at all through the 12:54 pull.** (Corrected figure: `semantic_scan_results` for 2026-08-06
UTC is 44 `background` / 9 `active`, denominator 53 rows created that day, table total 142 — not the
24 quoted in the comment.)

**3. Which reclaim cleared it — NEITHER of the two the comment names.** It was
`AnalysisCoordinator.recoverOrphans`. `_meta.scheduler_epoch` went 66 -> 67, and
`incrementSchedulerEpoch()` has exactly one production caller: `recoverOrphans`'s resume branch
(`AnalysisCoordinator.swift:953`). `recoverExpiredLeases` and `recoverStrandedSessionJobs` never
touch the epoch. All ten queued rows also carry `updatedAt = 12:01:16`, the signature of
`restampQueuedJobEpochs` — a `reconcile()` step. So a full bootstrap ran at 12:01:16.

**4. The 12:01:16 cluster — CONFIRMED as a bootstrap, REFUTED as Dan's foreground.** `work_journal`:

    09:58:50  acquired   gen C57ADCD2  epoch 66      <- the stuck claim
    (nothing for 2h 2m)
    12:01:19  acquired   gen 65A7F78E  epoch 67      <- reclaimed and re-dispatched
    12:51:10  checkpointed  slice_duration_ms 2990966  stage ...transcriptionAlreadyComplete
    12:52:16  finalized  /  12:52:16 acquired  gen 8F7DBD6E

`analysis_jobs.jobId 9767C9D8...` -> `analysisAssetId F4CE7F47-47A2-4525-8017-E14CFEEF8193`. It is
the bead's row. **It was reclaimed at 12:01:16 and re-dispatched at 12:01:19 — fifty minutes BEFORE
Dan foregrounded at ~12:50.** The `state=complete / updated 12:52:16` in `db-fg1` is the job
FINISHING, not being reclaimed. And 12:01 was not a BGTask either: no `background_task_runs` row
exists between 08:45:43 and the pull. `slice_duration_ms = 2,990,966` = 49 m 51 s = exactly
12:01:19 -> 12:51:10, so ONE process spanned that window.

### So the bead's headline premise is refuted too

The two-hour silence is not explained by the lease. **The process was dead.** The lease-renewal
task (`AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:3923`, every 120 s against a 300 s TTL) writes `updatedAt` on
every renewal, and `updatedAt` on the running row never moved off 09:58:50 — not one renewal ever
fired. Zero writes of any kind for 2 h 2 m. When a process finally existed, the reclaim ran and
dispatched in **three seconds**. A `running` row also does not block anything else:
`fetchNextEligibleJob` selects `queued`/`paused`/`failed`, so the other ten rows were never gated on
it. "One wedged episode stops ALL analysis" is not what happened here.

### What IS broken, and what I built

Every reclaimer is reachable only from a **process bootstrap** or an **OS-granted BGTask**. The
long-lived `AnalysisWorkScheduler.runLoop` — the one component that runs for the rest of the
process's life, polling every 5 s — never swept. So an orphan minted AFTER bootstrap pins its
episode out of the queue for the whole remaining process lifetime, because `fetchNextEligibleJob`
cannot see a `running` row.

Fix: `AnalysisStore.reclaimExpiredLeases(now:excludingJobId:)` + a 60 s-throttled
`sweepExpiredLeasesIfDue()` at the top of `runLoop`, above the admission gate (a thermal pause is a
reason not to start work, never a reason to keep a dead claim).

**EXPIRY-based, not liveness-based.** Safe because `leaseExpiresAt` is ALREADY a heartbeat, not a
bare deadline — the bead's "that is a bigger change" note is superseded: `leaseRenewalTask` re-stamps
it every 120 s against a 300 s TTL, so an expired lease means two renewal ticks failed to land. Two
guards on top: the expiry predicate lives INSIDE the UPDATE (the existing `recoverExpiredLease` has
`WHERE jobId = ?` alone and relies on a preceding SELECT — a TOCTOU the loop cadence would
exercise), and `excludingJobId` protects the caller's own row by identity, which is exact knowledge
rather than an inference from a clock.

Verdicts: lint clean; scoped gate 198 tests / 17 suites / 0 failures in BOTH formats; mutation
battery MK01/MK02/MK03 all KILLED, 0 survivors, 0 errors.

### Filed separately — see the report

* `requiresExternalPower = true` on `preAnalysisRecovery` (`BackgroundProcessingService.swift:1893`):
  the ONLY OS-driven reclaim cannot run off-charger. That is why the runs stop dead at 08:45:43.
* `(try? await store.renewLease(...)) ?? false` (`AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:3925`): a THROWN error
  is read as "someone else owns it", so a transient SQLite failure mints exactly the orphan this
  bead is about. Standing defect class.
* The 50-minute `engine_silent_timeout` slice: a wall-clock watchdog counting suspended time as
  silence.
* Uncovered edge: no test proves the SCHEDULER passes `currentJobId` rather than `nil` (the store
  guard itself is covered by MK02). Needs an injected clock to reach a second sweep.

comments.text:
## ROUND 2 — two folded fixes, one refuted recommendation, one bead filed

Commits `e574bdf8` (guard + tests) and `4f873ac4` (MK04-MK06 rails), on top of round 1's
`1da496fc` / `9fbcc546`. Branch clean, no PR.

### Point 3 — `requiresExternalPower` on recovery: **REFUTED. NOT IMPLEMENTED.**

The recommendation was to add a battery-eligible recovery sibling mirroring `playhead-i6oi`.
Re-derived from `db-fg1`, it buys nothing, and the ledger says so directly.

`handleBackfillTask` records `taskIdentifier: BackgroundTaskID.backfillProcessing`
(`BackgroundProcessingService.swift:1140`) for BOTH siblings, so the plain
(`requiresExternalPower = false`) and charged (`= true`) variants land under one identifier
and are separated only by `taskInstanceID`. Grouping the 254 backfill rows by wall second:
**75 seconds carry 2 rows, 104 carry 1** (denominator 179 distinct seconds; 150 of 254 rows
are paired). Every one of the last twelve wake-seconds is a pair with two distinct
`taskInstanceID`s — 08:45:43, 08:15:44, 07:45:29, 07:15:09, 06:45:08, 06:14:56, and back.

**So the battery-eligible sibling already exists for backfill, it fired every single time
right up to 08:45:43 UTC, and then `SELECT count(*) FROM background_task_runs WHERE
startedAt > 08:45:44` returns 0** — for all three identifiers at once. A per-task power flag
cannot explain a simultaneous stop of a power-gated and a non-power-gated class. The device
was then plugged in and idle 11:22–11:55 and still produced zero rows.

The remaining explanation consistent with every observation is iOS withholding discretionary
windows from an in-use device. A plain-power recovery sibling would have produced exactly
zero extra windows in this dataset, so it is not shipped. The `i6oi` comment's finding
("the battery-budgeted class's idle suppressors starved the plain identifier all night")
is about a DIFFERENT night and does not survive contact with this one.

### Point 2 — the anti-bulldozing guard: **HOLDS, implemented.**

`schedulePreAnalysisRecovery()` had no `pendingTaskRequestIdentifiers()` check and no
reentrancy flag; `scheduleBackfillIfNeeded()` has had both since `playhead-txq3`, whose
comment gives the reason — `submit(_:)` de-dups on identifier but every submit AGE-RESETS
the pending request.

New `schedulePreAnalysisRecoveryIfNeeded()`, wired at `start()` (`:804`) only. The handler's
self-rearm (`:1735`) stays unguarded **by design**, documented at the method so it is not
"fixed" later:

* it cannot bulldoze — it runs at the instant iOS has just CONSUMED that identifier's
  request, so nothing is pending to age-reset; and
* `playhead-c25o` established that nothing in a BGTask handler may `await` before
  `task.expirationHandler` is installed. That self-rearm is synchronous today; awaiting the
  pending query there would buy nothing and cost the invariant.

Fails OPEN, including on c25o's bounded-continuation timeout — a launch that arms nothing is
the `playhead-fuo6` blackout, the strictly worse defect.

**Honest limit: this does not explain the outage.** Backfill is guarded and went silent at
the same instant. The guard closes a real asymmetry with a documented rationale; it is not
the cause.

### Point 1 — the 203 expired backfill runs: **filed as `playhead-lmrx` (P0), not folded.**

203 of 254 backfill wakes expired (80.0 %) at ~210 s each. Across the 12 `admitted_work`
runs: 26 admitted, **0 completed**. Only **4 of 203** expired runs wrote a
`semantic_scan_results` row inside their own window. `backfill_jobs`: **25 of 30 rows have
`progressCursor IS NULL`** — no job-level resume point.

This is chunking/checkpointing, not leases, and it bears directly on round 1's sweep: if a
granted window cannot finish a job, faster reclaim recycles the same job through the same
window rather than making progress. The two compose only if `lmrx` lands.

### Verdicts

* `scripts/lint.sh --changed` → `6 changed Swift file(s) vs ba738618` / `lint: clean`
* Final scoped gate, rc=0: **234 tests in 25 suites passed**, `** TEST SUCCEEDED **`.
  25 requested suites → 25 display lines. Swift Testing `failed after`: **0**.
  XCTest `Test Case … failed`: **0**.
* Mutation battery, all six MK rails KILLED, 0 survivors, 0 errors:
  MK01/MK02/MK03 (batches 530-532) and MK04/MK05/MK06 (533-535).
  MK06 is killed by exactly one test, which is the point — a stuck reentrancy latch and a
  working guard are indistinguishable across one call AND across two consecutive calls
  (the second is legitimately skipped as already-pending). `StubTaskScheduler.clearPending`
  models iOS consuming the request between them, which is what separates them.

### Still uncovered, deliberately

* Nothing proves the SCHEDULER passes `currentJobId` rather than `nil` to
  `reclaimExpiredLeases` (the store-side guard is covered by MK02). Reaching a second sweep
  needs an injected clock.
* `handlePreAnalysisRecovery` awaits `awaitPreAnalysisServicesInjected()` BEFORE installing
  `task.expirationHandler` (`:1852`) — the exact `playhead-c25o` exposure that backfill
  fixed and recovery did not. Pre-existing, untouched here, worth its own bead.

comments.text:
## REVIEW ROUND 2026-08-06 — 2 real defects found and fixed, both mutation-proven

Commits `8780b540`, `a5801665`, `1721aa64` on top of round 2. Tree clean, no PR.

### F1 (HIGH) — the sweep excluded the LAST job dispatched, not the one still running

`sweepExpiredLeasesIfDue` passed `currentJobId`. That property names the job dispatched MOST
RECENTLY: `processJob` overwrites it on entry and nils it in its `defer`. Two dispatch drivers
can be in `processJob` at once — `runLoop` and `drainEligible`, whose own header says it is
'safe to run alongside the long-lived runLoop()'. `nowCap` is 2 and a `playback` job bypasses
the cap entirely, so the overlap is admitted:

    drain dispatches A   -> currentJobId = A
    loop  dispatches B   -> currentJobId = B      (A's identity lost)
    B completes          -> currentJobId = nil    (A still running)
    loop reaches its top -> sweeps with nil, and A's lease, if renewal was starved past the
                            deadline, is reclaimed out from under a runner still working.

The bead's design note claims `excludingJobId` 'protects the caller's own in-flight job by
identity'. That was false for the second of two overlapping dispatches. Fix: `inFlightJobIds:
Set<String>`, added in the prologue and removed in the SAME defer that nils `currentJobId`, so a
sibling's completion removes only its own entry. Standing defect class exactly.

### F2 (MEDIUM) — the NEW sweep made the OTHER reclaimer double-charge attemptCount

`AnalysisJobReconciler.recoverExpiredLeases` is `fetchJobsWithExpiredLeases` then
`recoverExpiredLease(jobId:)` per row, keyed on `jobId` alone. One reclaimer per bootstrap made
that gap free; a 60 s sweep can land inside it, so one orphan is billed twice. `attemptCount` is
what `maxAttemptCount` reads to supersede an episode permanently, and 3 of 61 rows in db-fg1
already sit at exactly 5 (two `maxAttemptsReached:cancelMidRun`). Fix: `AND leaseOwner IS NOT
NULL`, which cannot change any existing caller (the only production caller selects through
`fetchJobsWithExpiredLeases`, whose predicate already requires a non-NULL owner).

### F3 (the test I wrote was wrong first) — `state == 'running'` is not a witness

MK07 SURVIVED my first version. A reclaimed row returns to `queued` with `nextEligibleAt` still
nil, so the same loop re-dispatches it on the next pass and re-acquires — the row reads
`running`/`preAnalysis` under BOTH answers. The bead's own defect class committed inside its
test. Replaced with the witnesses a reclaim-then-reacquire must move: `attemptCount` (4->5) and
`leaseExpiresAt`. MK07 then KILLED.

### currentJobId gap: CLOSED

MK08 (call site excludes nothing) KILLED, MK07 (excludes `currentJobId`) KILLED, MK09 (blanket
`removeAll()` in the defer) KILLED. No injected clock was needed for the store; a MutableClock
plus a parked decode reaches the second sweep.

### Verified self-reported claims

* **requiresExternalPower refutation HOLDS.** 179 distinct backfill wake-seconds, 104 carry 1 row
  and 75 carry 2 (150 of 254 paired); last twelve wake-seconds all pairs with 2 distinct
  `taskInstanceID`s. `count(*) WHERE startedAt > 08:45:44` = **0 for all three identifiers**, and
  max `startedAt` overall is 08:45:43. Source side confirmed: both siblings register to
  `handleBackfillTask` (:659, :716) which records `taskIdentifier: backfillProcessing` (:1154), so
  all 254 rows carry one identifier. CAVEAT: 97 of the 104 singleton seconds fall AFTER the first
  paired second (2026-08-01 03:31:25), so 'fired every single time' is true for the tail, not the
  whole window. The load-bearing half — a simultaneous stop of a power-gated and a
  non-power-gated class — is unaffected.
* **MK06 discriminates.** Mutation drops the `defer`; call 1 latches and submits, `clearPending`
  models iOS consuming, call 2 hits the stuck latch and returns, count stays 1, `#expect(count ==
  2)` fails. Without `clearPending` both answers give 1.
* **MUTABLE_FILES assertion covers `$BGPS`.** The check iterates ALL `${MUTATIONS[@]}` (not the
  selected subset) on every invocation before selection; 17 battery invocations this round, none
  aborted.

### Round-1 figures re-derived, all confirmed

97 `preanalysis_recovery` runs all `scenePhase=background`, last six 08:45:43 / 08:15:44 /
07:45:29 / 07:15:09 / 06:45:08 / 06:14:56. `semantic_scan_results` 2026-08-06 UTC = 44
background / 9 active of 53, table total 142. work_journal for the stuck episode: 09:58:50
acquired gen C57ADCD2 epoch 66 -> 2h02m silence -> 12:01:19 acquired gen 65A7F78E epoch 67 ->
12:51:10 checkpointed -> 12:52:16 finalized; `_meta.scheduler_epoch`=67. Reclaim at 12:01,
~50 min BEFORE the ~12:50 foreground. db-fg1 running row: lease 12:57:16 vs updated 12:52:16 =
172 s in the future at the 12:54:07 pull. ONE correction: 9 of 10 queued rows carry
updatedAt=12:01:16, not all ten (the tenth is 12:52:16). Immaterial.

### lmrx composition: the sweep does NOT make it worse

Re-derived: 203/254 expired = **79.9%** (not 80.0), avg 209.8 s; 12 admitted_work runs, 26
admitted, **0 completed**; 25/30 `backfill_jobs` `progressCursor IS NULL`; **4 of 203** expired
runs wrote a scan row inside their own window. Judgement: reclaim does not create BGTask windows,
so it cannot recycle a job through more of them. An orphan requires a DEAD owner, which means a
dead process, which already got one bootstrap reclaim — the sweep takes the same charge SOONER,
not an extra one. What it actually converts is 'wedged until relaunch' into 'retried', and inside
a live foreground process the loop is not window-bounded, so that retry is real progress. The one
thing to watch is attemptCount pressure, which is why F2 mattered and is now closed.

### Verdicts (rail logs collected by mtime against run start 11:35:42; mb530-535 are the
### implementer's stale 09:39-11:06 logs and were NOT used)

`scripts/lint.sh --changed` -> `6 changed Swift file(s) vs ba738618` / `lint: clean`

Mutation rails, 0 survivors 0 errors: MK01 KILLED, MK02 KILLED, MK07 KILLED, MK08 KILLED (twice),
MK09 KILLED, MK10 KILLED. **MK03/MK04/MK05/MK06 were NOT independently re-run** — they target
`recoverExpiredLeases`'s state filter and `$BGPS`, neither touched by this round.

Final scoped gate rc=0: **109 tests in 9 suites passed**, `** TEST SUCCEEDED **`. Swift Testing
`failed after`: **0**. XCTest `Test Case … failed`: **0**. 9 requested suites -> 9 display lines.

### Not evaluated

Full plan (playhead-q1go). MK03-MK06. Any device run. The prepare-vs-step half of the SQLite
TOCTOU is closed by construction, not by test — no single-threaded test can observe it.

### Also

`playhead-jaa2` already covers the `handlePreAnalysisRecovery` c25o exposure; commented there
with current line numbers (:1710 / await :1756 / expirationHandler :1866).

**Merge judgement: MERGE.**

title: one 51.5s window cost 1955.6s of FM (38x realtime) and ended in permissive_decoding_failure
description:
## The single worst FM call observed, measured 2026-08-06

From `scratchpad/db-new-t30/analysis.sqlite`, `semantic_scan_results`:

    asset      F4CE7F47
    window     51.5 s   (windowEndTime - windowStartTime)
    latencyMs  1955575.3  =  1955.6 s  =  32.6 MINUTES
    status     permissive_decoding_failure
    scanPass   passA

**38x realtime for one window, and it produced nothing usable.** FM already runs ~2.4x slower
than realtime; this is 16x worse than that, on the scarcest resource in the pipeline.

It is not a lone outlier of the *failure* kind — the second slowest is 421.2 s for a 31.5 s
window (`DE0784D8`, status `success`), and 2 of 141 calls exceed even the 300 s `standard`
inference budget. But it IS the extreme, and the pairing of extreme latency with
`permissive_decoding_failure` is what makes it worth its own bead rather than a footnote in the
contention one.

## What must be established first

**Is 1955.6 s wall-clock, or does it include queueing?** `latencyMs` is measured around the call;
if the daemon was busy with other work (see the sibling bead on self-contention), part of that
32.6 minutes may be *waiting*, not *inferring*. **That distinction decides everything** — a slow
inference is a model problem, a long queue is a scheduling problem, and this bead should not
assume which.

Then:

* **Why did it not hit a deadline?** `FMInferenceDeadline.standard` is 300 s. A 1955.6 s call is
  6.5x that. Either this path is not deadline-guarded, or the deadline is measured over something
  other than the whole call. Find out which — an unguarded inference path is a bigger finding
  than the latency itself.
* **What does `permissive_decoding_failure` mean here**, and is a 32-minute run more or less
  likely to end in one? If long runs correlate with decode failure, the retry policy may be
  feeding the problem.
* Correlate with `inputTokenCount` / `outputTokenCount` (both columns exist) and with
  `transcriptQuality`. A 51.5 s window should not be a large prompt; if it is, the window/prompt
  relationship is the defect rather than the daemon.

## Do NOT fix by lowering a timeout before the above is answered

Cutting the call shorter converts a slow success into a fast failure unless the cause is queueing.
Two of 141 calls already exceed 300 s; capping them harder without knowing why would trade
throughput for reach, which is the wrong direction for this queue.

## Sibling findings from the same device-day

* self-contention: `tokenCount` and `respond` share one daemon, 21 % of inference calls exceed the
  30 s metadata budget (filed separately, P0)
* [[playhead-7x1s]] — 2.60x redundant scanning on this same asset
* [[playhead-3gzp]] — the ground-truth markup for this same episode: 0 of 2 real ads found

`latencyMs` is wall-clock for ONE call, not daemon busy-time. Name numerator and denominator for
anything you derive; re-derive from the pull rather than copying this bead.

LABELS: detection, performance, reach

The row's batch write is 08:49:48 inside the 08:45:43-08:50:39 grant; 1,955.6 s earlier is 08:17:12, inside the 08:15:44-08:20:39 grant; the 1,504 s between grants (numerator: 08:20:39->08:45:43; denominator: 1,955.6 s) is the app frozen. The remaining ~452 s of awake time spans TWO deadline-guarded permissive attempts (row attemptCount=2; ~207 s + ~245 s, each under the 300 s budget). The deadline WAS live on the device build (metadataStall-refused defer rows on 08-06 prove e75l #351 >= 8d5r #308) and never fired because a frozen process runs no timer, and at thaw the buffered XPC reply raced the elapsed timer through AbandonableRace and won — which is also why the status is permissive_decoding_failure (a decode failure REQUIRES a returned reply). latencyMs names 'continuous wall-clock of the whole window attempt' and was read as 'one call's inference time' — the standing defect class.
