title: tokenCount and respond share one daemon: 21% of inference calls exceed the 30s metadata budget, so a pass stalls on its own work
description:
## Measured on the live device, 2026-08-06, from `scratchpad/db-new-t30/analysis.sqlite`

`FoundationModelClassifier.swift:~6951` says it outright, and it is `playhead-qk44`'s own comment:

> every `tokenCount` below is an XPC round trip to the **same on-device model daemon** that
> `respond` goes to, and every one of them was UNBOUNDED — `planPassA` makes one per candidate
> window, so a hang here stalls the coarse pass before it ever reaches a
> `FMInferenceDeadline`-guarded call.

`qk44` bounded it at 30 s (`FMInferenceDeadline.metadata`) and `playhead-e75l` made the timeout a
DEFER rather than a job failure. **Neither addressed why the daemon is busy.** It is busy with our
own inference.

### `respond()` latency, n=141 (`semantic_scan_results.latencyMs`, > 0)

    min     2.0 s      p50     6.1 s      p90    49.1 s
    p95    57.6 s      p99   421.2 s      max  1955.6 s

**30 of 141 calls (21 %) exceed the 30 s metadata budget.** Numerator = calls with
`latencyMs > 30000`; denominator = calls with `latencyMs > 0`. So roughly one inference in five,
if in flight when `planPassA` issues a `tokenCount`, is on its own enough to blow that budget.

### The stalls line up with concurrent inference

Every `metadataStall-refused` / `FMInferenceTimeoutError` row in `backfill_jobs`, against scans
in flight in its window:

| asset | stall | self scans | other scans | max latency in window |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F4CE7F47 | 364 s | **10** | 0 | 43.6 s |
| F2F2FC4C | (long) | 0 | **35** | 1955.6 s |
| F4CE7F47 | (long) | **26** | 0 | 1955.6 s |
| F2F2FC4C | 29 s | 0 | 0 | — |
| 0C2FC22E / 52CD8F5B (08-03/04) | 52 / 366 / 172 s | 0 | 0 | — |

The zero-scan rows are all from **before `26od`** made scan rows persist mid-pass, so absence of
rows there is absence of *evidence*, not evidence of absence. **Do not read them as counterexamples.**

The 29 s stall is the cleanest single fact: the budget is 30 s and the call was cut at 29 —
it did not error, it **never returned**.

## What is NOT established, and must be before any fix

**Which calls actually contend.** `planPassA` issues one `tokenCount` per candidate window
*before* any inference in that pass. Whether those interleave with (a) the app's own `respond`
calls in the SAME pass, (b) a PREVIOUS pass's inference still draining, or (c) another process
entirely, is not visible in the DB — it needs the code path traced. **The three have different
fixes** (batch the metadata calls / serialise metadata against inference / raise or drop the
budget), so picking one before establishing which is the failure this repo keeps punishing.

Also worth establishing: `contextSize` and `coarseSchemaTokenCount` are on the same seam and the
schema token count is a CONSTANT per build — if it is being recomputed per window, that is free
to cache and needs no policy decision at all.

## Why P0

FM is the scarcest resource in the system (~2.4x slower than realtime) and it is now carrying
three separate taxes, all measured on the same device-day:

1. **2.60x redundant scanning** — [[playhead-7x1s]]
2. **self-inflicted metadata stalls** — this bead; 4 deferred passes in 8 h, each one an ad-scan
   that reached the prologue and turned around
3. **a single 51.5 s window costing 1955.6 s** — [[playhead-fkkn]]

Reach work (QUEUE 3) stopped work being DISCARDED. These three are work being WASTED, and they
sit directly between Dan and "finished before I press play".

## Watch the standing defect class

`latencyMs` is wall-clock for one call, NOT daemon busy-time, and window span is NOT coverage.
An earlier reading of this same pull called a watermark "coverage" ([[playhead-346z]]). Name
numerator and denominator for every figure you quote, and re-derive from the pull rather than
copying this table.

LABELS: detection, performance, reach

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: **Link correction:** the third tax is filed as **playhead-rkfp** (one 51.5 s window cost 1955.6 s and ended in `permissive_decoding_failure`). The `[[playhead-fkkn]]` reference in the description was written before that bead was created and does not resolve — use `rkfp`.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: ESTABLISHED (branch bead/playhead-rkfp, shared diff): the contention question is now MEASURABLE per stall. FMDaemonCallCensus counts in-process FM calls at the FMInferenceDeadline.run chokepoint, INCLUDING abandoned-but-unreturned calls (exit runs in the operation task, after Apple's call actually returns — an abandoned tokenCount/respond is still daemon load). Every metadataStall-refused defer now appends (peers=N) with N read at the instant the stalled call was ISSUED and carried on FMInferenceTimeoutError, so the next pull answers confirm/refute per row: peers>=1 confirms self-contention, peers=0 refutes it for that stall (frozen wait or external load). Every passA scan row also records daemonPeersAtStart + suspendingLatencyMs. The 29-s-cut stall reproduced as freeze-straddle: F2F2FC4C deferred 01:38:45->01:39:15, exactly the 30 s budget, spanning a no-grant window. NOT counted (lower bound, documented): prewarm and chapter-path FM calls (playhead-4meb). Also found: backfill + backfill.charged BGTask instances fire simultaneously every wake, 71 identical-instant pairs — possible second contention source, filed playhead-gayl (scheduling decision, not implemented). Cannot see daemon-internal queue-vs-compute from the app; the census is the visible half.

title: semantic scan does 2.60x redundant FM work: 43 windows, 3093.6s of scanning for 1188.4s of audio
description:
## Measured on the live device, 2026-08-06

Asset `F4CE7F47` (1316.7 s episode), from `scratchpad/db-marked/analysis.sqlite`,
table `semantic_scan_results` (`windowStartTime` / `windowEndTime`):

    windows                 43
    sum of window lengths   3093.6 s   <- FM work actually performed
    union of coverage       1188.4 s   <- distinct audio covered
    REDUNDANCY              2.60x      (1905.2 s duplicated)
    union as % of episode   90.3 %

**16 distinct start-times are used by more than one window.** Concrete overlap Dan noticed by
ear at 17:00–17:56:

    1010.6 -> 1028.7
    1029.9 -> 1068.5   (38.6 s)
    1029.9 -> 1133.3   (103.4 s)  <- same start; CONTAINS the row above entirely
    1069.3 -> 1145.0   (75.7 s)   <- overlaps the row above by 64 s

## Why this is P1 and not cosmetic

FM runs **~2.4x slower than realtime** and is the scarcest resource in the pipeline — it is the
reason an episode is not finished before Dan presses play. **62 % of the FM work on this episode
bought nothing.** At 2.60x, a scan that takes four hours of device time is doing about ninety
minutes of actual work.

Everything QUEUE 3 fixed was about work being DISCARDED (26od persistence, iu0t, e75l retries).
This is the opposite failure — work being DUPLICATED — and it is invisible to every existing
measure because each window individually succeeds.

**And the redundancy did not buy accuracy.** The 1020–1078.9 s region covered by the overlapping
windows above produced a **false positive** that Dan vetoed (see the ground-truth bead for
`F4CE7F47`). More scanning of the same audio produced a wrong answer, not a better one.

## Establish before fixing

* **Re-derive the numbers**, naming numerator and denominator. Then check the other 13 assets in
  the pull — is 2.60x typical, an outlier, or the low end?
* **Where do the windows come from?** Distinguish (a) the planner proposing overlapping windows
  in one pass, (b) successive passes re-proposing audio an earlier pass already covered, and
  (c) `scanPass` genuinely differing (a coarse pass and a refine pass over the same span may be
  legitimate). `semantic_scan_results` carries `scanPass`, `runMode`, `jobPhase`,
  `runCorrelationId` and `reuseKeyHash` — **use them**; the answer changes the fix completely.
* **`reuseKeyHash` exists.** Establish whether a reuse/dedup path is present and simply not
  firing, versus absent. If it exists and is not firing, that is a much smaller fix than a new
  planner rule.
* A window that legitimately re-scans (a refine over a coarse) is NOT redundancy. Say which
  windows are which before quoting a ratio as waste.

## Watch the standing defect class

`windowStartTime`/`windowEndTime` are a SPAN, not coverage. Summing spans and calling it coverage
is exactly the watermark-vs-coverage error committed against this same pull on 2026-08-06 (see
[[playhead-346z]]). The 2.60x above is deliberately reported as *sum of spans over union of
spans* — both named — and any fix must keep that distinction.

LABELS: detection, performance, reach
notes:
## MECHANISM ESTABLISHED (2026-08-07), then fixed

Re-derived on `scratchpad/db-new-t2h/analysis.sqlite`, 142 rows / 4 assets.
Numerator SUM = sum over rows of `windowEndTime - windowStartTime` (FM work
performed). Denominator UNION = length of the union of those intervals
(distinct audio scanned). Both are SPANS; neither is episode coverage.

    asset      n gens     SUM s   UNION s   total    legit   DUPLICATE
    F4CE7F47  53    3    3838.4    1188.4   3.23x    1.23x       2.62x
    AD5F3A0A  45    2    3085.6     888.5   3.47x    1.74x       2.00x
    DE0784D8  42    1    2646.6    2646.6   1.00x    1.00x       1.00x
    53FC53E3   2    1      71.6      35.8   2.00x    2.00x       1.00x
    TOTAL    142         9642.2    4759.3   2.03x    1.27x       1.59x

`legit` = SUM / (sum of each GENERATION's own union) — a passB window re-reading
a passA span is a refine over a coarse and is legitimate. `DUPLICATE` = (sum of
generation unions) / UNION — the same audio read by N separate passes. They
multiply exactly to `total`.

**The bead's 2.60x was the right order and the wrong denominator to blame.** The
waste is the DUPLICATE column, 1.59x overall and 2.62x on F4CE7F47. `53FC53E3`'s
2.00x is entirely coarse->refine over one 35.8 s window and is NOT waste.

### Where the windows come from — (b), not (a) or (c)

* (a) the planner proposing overlaps within one pass: NO. Within a single
  `(transcriptVersion, passA)` generation redundancy is exactly **1.00x** on
  every scanned asset.
* (c) `scanPass` genuinely differing: YES and legitimate, and it is the whole of
  the `legit` column.
* (b) successive passes re-proposing covered audio: **this is it.**

### The value that names one thing and is read as another

`backfill_jobs.jobId = hash(analysisAssetId | transcriptVersion | phase |
offset)` (`BackfillJobRunner.makeJobIdForTesting`). But the ROW carries no
transcript version — `backfill_jobs` has no such column — and `runJob`
re-derives every input from the CURRENT transcript, using the actor-level
`self.scanCohortJSON` rather than the row's. So `transcriptVersion` names the
TRANSCRIPT's identity while being read as the JOB's, and every re-transcription
rotates the id of work that is otherwise unchanged.

The M-5 idempotency branch directly below the id derivation is the dedup, and it
is CORRECT — `complete` skips, anything else re-drives without inserting. It
simply never matches, because it looks up the rotated id. **Present, not firing,
keyed too tightly** — the smaller of the two fixes the bead contemplated.

Corroboration, three independent ways:
* 30 `backfill_jobs` rows / 15 assets, all `fullEpisodeScan`/`fullCoverage`;
  **14 are duplicates of a still-unfinished row** for the same
  (asset, phase, coveragePolicy). CDD611C4 holds 4, three assets hold 3.
* On F4CE7F47 the 3 rows are 1:1 with the 3 `runCorrelationId`s and the 3
  `transcriptVersion`s in `semantic_scan_results` (26/17/10 rows).
* **`DE0784D8`, the 1.00x asset, has exactly ONE transcript version and ONE
  generation.** The asset with zero redundancy is the asset that was never
  re-minted.

Windows repeat with IDENTICAL atom ordinals across versions (0..82, 154..244,
245..341 on F4CE7F47), i.e. the same text re-asked, because the final pass on
that asset starts at 180.0 s and nothing below it had changed.

The code documented the defect as harmless: "this transcriptVersion embedding is
defensive for a Phase 4 re-trigger path that does not yet exist... it costs
nothing" (BackfillJobRunner, HIGH-R5-1). And `countResumableBackfillJobs`' own
doc already lists `transcriptVersion` as orphan producer #1 — playhead-onn6
worked AROUND it with newest-batch scoping rather than fixing it, which is also
a ratchet: an orphan keeps `resumableCount > 0`, which is the gate
`AnalysisJobReconciler.adScanRedriveCandidate` mints fresh passes on.

## FIXED

`AnalysisStore.fetchUnfinishedBackfillJob(analysisAssetId:phase:coveragePolicy:)`
plus a fallback in `runPendingBackfill` when the by-id lookup misses. `complete`
is excluded, which preserves R4-Fix6 exactly; retry-exhausted is excluded so an
asset is never stranded; `running` is INCLUDED (unlike
`countResumableBackfillJobs`) because minting beside a live pass is the worst case.

Measured after, in the 30-cycle runner harness `noProgressRunnerCyclesStayBounded`:
30 re-transcriptions wrote **41 scan rows against a 60-row ceiling**. That test's
row-count arm previously asserted EXACT linear growth and its own comment called
it "pre-existing M-5 behaviour"; linear is now the ceiling with a strict floor.

8 mutation rails SX01-SX08, all KILLED, 0 survivors / 0 errors.

## RESIDUALS FILED

* **playhead-pfye** (P1) — the resume cursor is a contiguous PREFIX, so one early
  hole re-scans the rest of the episode. F4CE7F47's cursor stalled at 96.84 s of
  1185.5 s scanned. **This is why the harness sits at 41 rows and not ~2.**
* **playhead-ig0g** (P1) — `semanticScanReuseKeyHash` includes the WHOLE-transcript
  hash, and `fetchReusableSemanticScanResult` has zero production callers.
* **playhead-7enr** (P2) — the specialist-phase enqueue has the identical defect
  (flag-gated off, zero rows on the pull).
* **playhead-kk1f** (P2) — the battery's baseline gate refused 3 of 4 times on
  playhead-lmrx's load-sensitive grant suites.
## CORRECTION to the note above (same session, before the report)

I wrote that the orphan rows are 'also a ratchet: an orphan keeps
`resumableCount > 0`, which is the gate `adScanRedriveCandidate` mints fresh
passes on.' **That is overstated and I am withdrawing it.**
`countResumableBackfillJobs(assetId:)` is scoped to the asset's NEWEST enqueue
batch (playhead-onn6, `backfillEnqueueBatchWindowSec`), so an orphan from an
earlier batch does NOT feed the mint gate; only the newest row's
non-completion does. The orphans reach `fetchAssetIdsWithResumableBackfillJobs`
(the deliberately broader CANDIDATE sweep) but the per-asset count is the
authority and rejects them.

**The narrower claim, which is the one the evidence supports:** each session
minted a NEW job with `progressCursor = nil` instead of resuming the previous
session's row, so every session restarted the episode from zero. On F4CE7F47
three sessions each scanned ~1185 s of the same 1188 s. The fix makes session N
resume session N-1's row, and the saving is exactly what that cursor carries —
32 % over 30 cycles in the harness where the cursor advances normally, but only
~8 % on F4CE7F47 where it stalled at 96.84 s. That stall is playhead-pfye and is
why this fix alone does not take the DUPLICATE factor to 1.00x.
## Generation-to-job is 1:1, MEASURED not assumed

Joining on `semantic_scan_results.runCorrelationId = backfill_jobs.jobId`:

    fm-ef073bd6a914c55b  F4CE7F47  17 rows  1 transcriptVersion
    fm-36377e9d0ae29697  F4CE7F47  26 rows  1 transcriptVersion
    fm-86c4a6202d582386  F4CE7F47  10 rows  1 transcriptVersion

17+26+10 = 53 = every scan row on the asset. So 'a generation' in the
decomposition above is not a proxy: one `backfill_jobs` row is exactly one
transcriptVersion's worth of scanning, and the DUPLICATE column counts rows the
duplicate-job defect minted.
## R1 ADVERSARIAL REVIEW — one correctness bug found and fixed, four claims corrected

**The bug (found, fixed, railed).** The first cut scoped the new selector by

## R2 (2nd round) CORRECTION TO ITS OWN VERDICT — the round is ONE production defect, not zero

The adversarial pass, run last as the process requires, overturned the
zero-finding verdict in the note above. I re-traced it myself before accepting
it. **The round is ONE production defect. It is FILED, not fixed — see below for
why, and treat that as the honest partial rather than a completed round.**

### THE DEFECT — playhead-y8a3 (P1)

**An ADOPTED row leaves no row at the current transcriptVersion's id, so the
NEXT SAME-VERSION pass mints a duplicate full-episode FM scan.** The bead that
removes duplicate full-episode FM passes introduces one, on a different axis.

    Pass 1 @ version V: by-id(V) MISSES; the fallback adopts R_old and
      `continue`s at :779, so the mint at :782 is SKIPPED and no row is ever
      inserted at id(V). The drain runs R_old and marks it `complete`.
    Pass 2 @ the SAME version V: by-id(V) misses again; the fallback returns
      nil (R_old is `complete`, excluded by R4-Fix6 design); control falls
      through and MINTS a fresh row with progressCursor = nil — a full-episode
      FM pass from zero over audio pass 1 just read.

Pre-7x1s, pass 1 minted id(V) and completed it, so pass 2's by-id HIT the
`complete` row, `continue`d, left `enqueuedJobs` empty and did **zero FM work**.
Post-7x1s the pair costs one RESUMED pass plus one FULL pass. The saving on
pass 1 is smaller than the pass added on pass 2 for every cursor value.

**It breaks `runPendingBackfill`'s own documented contract, verbatim, on exactly
the condition the contract names** (BackfillJobRunner.swift:552-556):
*"Idempotent: callers can re-invoke for the same asset without producing
duplicate work as long as the scan cohort and **transcript version are
unchanged**."*

**Reachable on shipped defaults, and one value drives both halves.** The adopted
row must reach `complete`, which `coverageTerminalDecision` gives three ordinary
ways: `.notMeasurable` (nil `adScanFraction`), measured >= the sufficiency floor
(i.e. SUCCESS), and unconditionally for every phase that is not
`.fullEpisodeScan` (so all three targeted-lane phases duplicate). The same nil
`adScanFraction` that completes the row also guarantees pass 2 runs:
`AnalysisJobRunner.shouldSkipSemanticBackfill` (:1221) opens `guard let
adScanFraction = adScanFraction.finiteValue else { return false }` — nil means
DO NOT SKIP.

**Root cause in the standing defect class.** `backfill_jobs` carries no
transcript version, so `jobId` was naming two things at once: the WORK, and the
VERSION THE WORK WAS LAST DONE UNDER. This bead correctly split off the first
and did not rehome the second, so the record the by-id branch used to carry is
simply gone.

### Why it is FILED and not fixed here

Every repair is an architectural choice, and the project rule is to present
those rather than implement them: (1) re-key the adopted row to `id(V)` —
smallest behavioural restoration, but `jobId` is the row's identity and the
`runCorrelationId` generation join this bead was MEASURED with breaks; (2) write
a `complete` marker row at `id(V)` when an adopted row completes — no identity
change, no FM cost, one extra row per (asset, version), which is the row count
R4-Fix6 already produces; (3) add a `transcriptVersion` column and make the
record explicit — the honest fix, and a migration. Option 2 is the smallest;
option 3 is the one that stops the class recurring.

### The test that would have caught it, and does not exist

`newTranscriptVersionResumesRatherThanDuplicating` rotates the version between
runs, so it cannot see this. The missing rail is: adopt, complete, then
**re-invoke with the version unchanged** and assert zero new rows and zero new
scan rows. Write that first; it fails today.

**ABANDONED UNMERGED, 2026-08-07, superseded by playhead-wxsv.**

Four review rounds, 18 commits, three production defects found and fixed — every one of them INSIDE the unfinished-row fallback this bead added, and each introduced by the fix for the previous one:
- R1: adopting a `failed`-under-budget row made it a permanent suppressor (nothing can START it).
- R2: the adopt path minted no row at the current version's id, so the next same-version pass ran a duplicate FULL episode scan — a redundancy bead ADDING redundancy.
- R3: the claim fixing R2 could expire, recreating R1's shape one layer up.

R4 was clean and found nothing new. But it could not establish a net FM saving, and my own measurement of the field pull agrees: the branch costs N-1 extra full passes at an unchanged transcript version where main does zero, and N is *the number of sessions transcription took* — so it punishes the longest episodes worst. Against that, the recurring saving is resume-instead-of-restart per rotation, ~8 % on F4CE7F47 (cursor stalled at 96.84 s of 1,185.5 s, capped by `playhead-pfye`), which stops paying once transcription settles.

**Not a failed bead — a bead that found the right answer and proved the wrong fix.** Everything of value carries to `playhead-wxsv`: the mechanism, the exact per-asset correlation, and the four rounds' findings as that bead's specification.

The branch `bead/playhead-7x1s` is kept unmerged for reference.

title: F4CE7F47 ground truth: 0 of 2 real ads found, 4 of 4 marks wrong, and the two misses are the OUTER edges
description:
## Dan marked up a whole episode by ear on 2026-08-06. This is the first complete ground truth we have.

Asset `F4CE7F47`, "Most Replayed Moment: Are You Really Gluten Intolerant? It Could Be This
Instead!", Diary of a CEO, 1316.7 s (21:57). Corrections are in `correction_events`, pulled to
`scratchpad/db-marked/analysis.sqlite`. **Re-derive from that table; do not trust this summary.**

| span | length | Dan's verdict | confidence | detector | boundaryState |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **0:00–0:59** | 59.8 s | **REAL AD, MISSED** | — | — | — |
| 1:04–1:59 | 55.6 s | false positive | 0.4024 | detection-v1 | segmentAggregated |
| 9:50–11:19 | 89.4 s | false positive | 0.7000 | semantic-sweep-v1 | semanticSweepMark |
| 14:31–15:59 | 88.7 s | false positive | 0.4191 | detection-v1 | segmentAggregated |
| 17:00–17:58 | 58.9 s | false positive | 0.4674 | detection-v1 | segmentAggregated |
| **20:56–21:56** | 59.7 s | **REAL AD, MISSED** | — | — | — |

**Precision 0/4. Recall 0/2.** 120 s of real ad missed; 293 s of SHOW proposed for removal.

## The pattern is inverted, and that is the finding

**Both real ads are OUTER (pre-roll, post-roll). All four false positives are INNER.**

That is the exact inverse of the standing rule ([[feedback_outer_edges_free_inner_precious_2026-07-29]]):
outer edges are free to widen because there is no show to lose beyond them; inner edges eat the
show. The system currently leaves the free edges untouched and carves 293 s out of the middle.

## Every false positive shares one signature

All four: `eligibilityGate = markOnly`, `decisionState = candidate`, `startEdgeAnchor` **and**
`endEdgeAnchor` = `unanchored`, confidence **0.40–0.70**. None would have auto-skipped — the
safety gate held, which is worth saying plainly. But all four were SHOWN to Dan, and all four
were wrong.

**The cheapest available lever:** in this episode, unanchored + confidence 0.40–0.70 was
**4 for 4 wrong**, and raising that band costs ZERO recall because neither real ad was detected
at all. Measure it across the corpus before moving it — one episode is one episode — but this is
a threshold with a measured, non-speculative failure rate behind it.

## Two causes are already known and filed

1. **The post-roll miss is caused by the transcription stall.** The ad runs 1256.6–1316.3 s. The
   transcript STOPS at 1199.8 s (fast reaches 179.8, final reaches 1199.8, union 90.3 %). It was
   never transcribed, so it could never be found. Dan listened: **that tail is speech, not
   music.** See [[playhead-z3jg]] — this promotes it from "a loop with no brake" to "a loop that
   demonstrably cost a real detection".
2. **The 17:00 false positive sits inside the duplicated-scan region.** Measured on the same
   asset: 43 windows, sum of window lengths **3093.6 s** against a union of **1188.4 s** =
   **2.60x redundancy**, 1905 s of duplicated FM work. Sixteen start-times are used by more than
   one window; e.g. 1029.9→1068.5 and 1029.9→1133.3 (the second contains the first entirely),
   then 1069.3→1145.0 overlapping by 64 s. FM runs ~2.4x slower than realtime and is the scarcest
   resource in the system; 62 % of its work here was redundant AND the region produced a wrong
   answer. **File the redundancy separately if it is not already** — it is a throughput defect,
   not a detection defect, and it should not be fixed inside this bead.

## What this bead should actually do

Nothing yet. **Establish first, then decide:**

* Re-derive every number above from `db-marked`, naming numerator and denominator.
* Does the outer/inner inversion hold on the other 13 assets in the pull, or is it one episode?
  That decides whether this is a policy fix or an anecdote.
* Why was the PRE-roll missed? Unlike the post-roll it IS transcribed (fast reaches 179.8 s,
  final covers it). So the transcript existed and the detector still did not find it — a
  different failure from the post-roll, and probably the more interesting one.
* The 9:50 false positive came from `semantic-sweep-v1` at a flat 0.70, not from `detection-v1`.
  A constant is not a confidence. Check whether that 0.70 is ever anything else.

**Do not "fix" precision by raising a threshold until the recall question is answered.** Recall
is 0/2 here; a tighter threshold that leaves it at 0/2 has bought nothing a user can feel.

LABELS: detection, ground-truth, reach

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
ESTABLISH findings (read-only; DB = device pull db-marked/analysis.sqlite via .backup copy; asset A = F4CE7F47-47A2-4525-8017-E14CFEEF8193, duration 1316.728s).

## Q1 — Re-derived table. The bead's summary has one materially wrong row and one missing row.

SQL: `SELECT scope, effectiveCorrectionType, targetRefsJSON FROM correction_events WHERE analysisAssetId='F4CE7F47-...'` joined to `SELECT * FROM ad_windows WHERE analysisAssetId='F4CE7F47-...'`.

ad_windows holds SEVEN rows: 5 detector windows + 2 userCorrection rows minted by Dan's marks. The bead's "1:04-1:59" FP row is Dan's VETO span (exactFeedbackSpan 64.2-119.82), not the detection. The detection (B4C8165F) is **0.0-120.0**, and the same veto co-targeted a SECOND window the bead's table omits entirely: **sweep-9cbb969bf816ef90, 0.0-96.84 @ 0.70 semantic-sweep-v1** (`adWindowIds` in targetRefsJSON). Both windows CONTAIN the whole real pre-roll.

| window | span | conf | detector | boundary | gate | anchors | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sweep-9cbb96... | 0.00-96.84 | 0.7000 | semantic-sweep-v1 | semanticSweepMark | markOnly | unanch/unanch | co-vetoed |
| B4C8165F | 0.00-120.00 | 0.4024 | detection-v1 | segmentAggregated | markOnly | unanch/unanch | vetoed 64.20-119.82 |
| sweep-8028f2... | 590.04-679.44 | 0.7000 | semantic-sweep-v1 | semanticSweepMark | markOnly | unanch/unanch | vetoed exactly |
| 2A974FBC | 870.00-960.00 | 0.4191 | detection-v1 | segmentAggregated | markOnly | unanch/unanch | vetoed 871.14-959.88 |
| E729658C | 1020.00-1080.00 | 0.4674 | detection-v1 | segmentAggregated | markOnly | unanch/unanch | vetoed 1020.00-1078.86 |

Real ads (falseNegative events): 0.000-59.820 and 1256.640-1316.340.

Numerator/denominator discipline:
- Show vetoed = 292.62s (sum of the 4 veto spans) / 1316.73s = 22.2% of the episode. The bead's "293s" holds.
- Detector-marked audio (union of 5 windows) = 359.40s = 27.3% of episode; real ad inside it = 59.82s (16.6%); show inside it = 299.58s.
- Ad seconds not acted on = 119.52 / 119.52 (100%); wasSkipped=0 on all 5 detector windows.
- Recall: ACTION level 0/2. WINDOW-OVERLAP level **1/2** - the pre-roll is 100% covered by two candidates (IoU 0.62 sweep, 0.50 detection-v1). "0 of 2 found" is only true when "found" means correctly-bounded-or-actioned. The headline conflated the two - the standing defect class applied to the bead's own summary.
- Precision: 0/5 windows correctly bounded; 2/5 overlap a real ad; 3/5 zero overlap.
- "All four false positives are INNER" is FALSE at the window level: FP1's two windows touch 0:00 and are OUTER.

## Q2 — Corpus: the inversion holds directionally, and it decomposes into something sharper.

Ground truth exists on FIVE assets, not one: 0C2FC22E, CDD611C4, D9B513CD, DE0784D8, F4CE7F47 (27 correction rows). Exclusions applied before counting (each is itself an instance of the defect class - a correction row read as a verdict it does not carry):
- DE0784D8's FN spans 210-240 / 2670-2700 / 4800-4950 were each re-vetoed ~20min later at identical spans (2026-07-31 feedback-UI session) - mark-then-retract churn, excluded from BOTH sides.
- 0C2FC22E's FP 64.08-67.74 targets Dan's OWN userMarked window (a trim), not a detector.
- CDD611C4's lone FN (0-27.623) exactly equals an already-existing dayZeroRediffByteExact window (7A107F72, conf 1.0, applied, wasSkipped=1) - a confirmation flow artifact, not a miss. correctionType=falseNegative does not always mean "the system missed this".

Un-retracted real-ad FN spans by zone (OUTER = within 90s of 0 or episode end), n=11:
- OUTER 9/11: 0C2FC22E 0-6.78, 7.5-67.5, 2028-2071, 2072.04-2085.72 (dur 2086.02); CDD611C4 0-27.62; D9B513CD 4.02-44.7, 47.58-94.32; F4CE7F47 0-59.82, 1256.64-1316.34. (+1 implicit OUTER: DE0784D8's byte-exact pre-roll 0-60.13, which Dan trimmed by 2s rather than denied.)
- INNER 2/11: DE0784D8 2838.18-2897.94, 2898.66-2953.68 = the already-filed playhead-j4wi mid-roll hole.

Vetoed DETECTOR windows by zone (excl. churn trio + self-mark trim), n=8:
- OUTER 4: F4CE7F47 0-120 and 0-96.84 (both CONTAIN the real pre-roll), DE0784D8 0-60.13 (IS the real pre-roll; 2s tail trim), 0C2FC22E 2014.44-2027.95 (ends 0.05s before the real 2028-2071 ad). **All four outer "false positives" are width/offset errors around REAL ads. Zero outer hallucinations in the pull.**
- INNER 4: F4CE7F47 590-679, 870-960, 1020-1080 (zero overlap with any real ad = pure misclassification) + DE0784D8 2828.4-2836.44 (ends 1.74s before a real ad = offset error, j4wi's neighbor). Net: 3 pure hallucinations, all on F4CE7F47, all unanchored conf 0.40-0.70 markOnly.

Proxy, corpus-wide (no verdicts; where detections SIT): 93 detector windows (detectorVersion != 'userCorrection') across 13 of 19 assets: 29 OUTER / 64 INNER.

Actioned skips on real ads in the audited set: exactly ONE - CDD611C4's pre-roll, dayZeroRediffByteExact conf 1.0 applied+wasSkipped. The only correct ACTION in the entire audited corpus came from the deterministic rediff lane.

REFINED VERDICT: real ads live at the outer edges (9-10 of 11-12); when detectors err at OUTER edges it is always a width error around a real ad; the only pure hallucinations are INNER, all three on this one episode, all in the unanchored 0.40-0.70 markOnly band. So "outer/inner inversion" is really two separable defects: outer = boundary width, inner = classification.

## Q3 — The pre-roll was never dropped by the FM pipeline. It was detected twice at the wrong width, and the lane that nails pre-rolls exactly died on ONE network timeout whose backoff outlives a same-day listen.

Stage walk, witnesses named:
1. Scanned? YES: semantic_scan_results scan-a264eded689a6cf8 and scan-cb5b1b03fb39f925, window 0-96.84, passA, quality good, disposition **containsAd**, certainty strong, status success.
2. FM said no-ad? NO - it said ad, twice, strong.
3. Screened below threshold / clipped by isp5-b6r2? NO: both composed windows persisted unclipped (sweep 0-96.84 @0.70; detection-v1 0-120 @0.4024, 60s-grid quantized), decisionState was candidate until the veto.
4. So no stage "dropped" it. What failed: (a) WIDTH - both candidates overshoot the true end 59.82 by +37.0s and +60.2s (4xqf boundary family), and (b) unanchored => markOnly => no action; Dan met a mark that was half show, marked 0-59.82 real (09:32:47) and vetoed 64.2-119.82 (09:33:30).
5. The deterministic lane: rediff_day_zero_attempts[F4CE7F47] = attemptCount 1, lastExit **fetch_failed** (NSURLErrorDomain -1001 "The request timed out."), lastMarkCount 0, lastFullFetchBytes 0, suppressedCount 2, rescueAttemptCount 0, policyGeneration 2. Timeline: download 01:01, kickoff fired 01:02 (+120s poll), fetch timed out; Dan listened ~09:26-09:39; both re-drives were suppressed by DayZeroRediffAttemptPolicy's 24h baseBackoff (lastSuppressedAt 09:38:35, mid-listen). fetchFailed IS classified retryable in RediffDayZeroOutcome.swift, but baseBackoff=24h guarantees the retry lands after any day-0 listen; the ug9m rescue is scoped to assets that already HAVE day-0 marks, so a zero-mark fetch_failed asset is structurally outside it; the lagged sweep's 3-day gate makes the backstop just as unavailable. On the sibling assets this same lane produced 0-27.62 (CDD611C4, applied+skipped - the corpus's only correct action), 0-45.11 (D9B513CD), 0-60.13 (DE0784D8). One -1001 at download+2min is the entire difference between this episode's pre-roll and CDD611C4's. Filed as playhead-3oyz (checked open AND closed lists first; p70f built the backoff, ug9m built the rescue, neither covers a zero-mark fetch_failed asset on a day-0 listen).

## Q4 — The 0.70 is a constant, by declared design, and it is not alone.

`SELECT DISTINCT confidence FROM ad_windows WHERE detectorVersion='semantic-sweep-v1'` => exactly one value, 0.7 (5 windows, 2 assets: F4CE7F47 x2, AD5F3A0A x3). Minting site: Playhead/Services/AdDetection/SemanticSweepMarkComposer.swift:143 `static let markConfidence = 0.70`, pinned to SkipOrchestrator.preloadConfidenceThreshold (SkipOrchestrator.swift:265) so marks clear the cross-launch preload floor; its own doc-comment says it is NOT a calibrated probability (the coarse lane emits a categorical verdict). Same pattern: SpecialistMarkComposer.swift:66 and AdPodContinuation.swift:209 - THREE detectors mint flat 0.70. Measured consequence: the uncalibrated 0.70 outranks detection-v1's derived 0.40-0.47 in any confidence-ordered consumer - the least informative detectors claim the most confidence. What it could derive from WITHOUT inventing a probability: the scan rows already carry certainty (strong/weak) x pass agreement (passA/passB) x transcriptQuality (good/degraded). The 590-679 FP was composed from DEGRADED-quality rows; 0-96.84 had two independent strong votes. A categorical tier from existing columns is derivable; any change must handle the preloadConfidenceThreshold coupling. Decision is Dan's.

## Q5 — Width vs classification: 1 of 4 is width, 3 of 4 are classification, and the split maps exactly onto outer/inner.

- FP "1:04-1:59" (windows 0-120 + 0-96.84): **mis-WIDTH.** Contains 100% of the real pre-roll plus 37-60s of show. Remedy family: boundary machinery (4xqf) + the rediff lane, NOT thresholds.
- FP 9:50-11:19 (sweep 590.04-679.44 @flat 0.70): **mis-CLASSIFICATION.** Nearest real ad 530s away; transcript is ordinary show (gluten/glyphosate). Composed from transcriptQuality=degraded scan rows.
- FP 14:31-15:59 (870-960 @0.4191): **mis-CLASSIFICATION.** 297s from the nearest real ad; FM passB also said containsAd at 851.7-933.96 on good-quality text (fructan study) - the misread is upstream of aggregation.
- FP 17:00-17:58 (1020-1080 @0.4674): **mis-CLASSIFICATION with a co-located transcript-integrity defect:** the final-pass transcript in 1020-1080 is DOUBLED - 48 of 104 chunks are verbatim duplicates at identical startTimes with distinct ids/segmentFingerprints ("Now, these Now, these inflammatory inflammatory..."). The detector aggregated stuttered text. Likely i2am-family residue; not re-filed.

## Decision options (establish only; no fixes made)

**A. Give the deterministic outer lane a same-session second chance (rediff fetch_failed).** Buys: the only lane with a correct action in the audited corpus; 9-10 of 11-12 audited real ads are OUTER, where rediff is byte-exact at conf 1.0; this single -1001 cost both a pre-roll skip and, downstream, made the FM lane's wrong-width marks the only voice. Risks: bandwidth (the existing kickoff/budget/ledger machinery bounds it; a fetch that timed out spent ~0 bytes); does nothing for inner FPs or host-read ads. Filed as playhead-3oyz.

**B. Unanchored-INNER band policy, stated with its true cost.** Measured: unanchored + 0.40-0.70 + markOnly is 0-for-5 correct on this episode; corpus-wide every pure hallucination (3/3) is in this band AND touches neither edge. Suppressing (or demoting below the banner surface) unanchored marks that touch NEITHER edge would have removed all 3 pure FPs at zero ACTION-level recall cost (nothing in the band ever auto-skips). The bead's claim "costs ZERO recall because neither real ad was detected" rests on a false premise - the band also contains the two wrong-width marks that fully cover the real pre-roll; an edge-conditional band keeps those. This is Dan's outer-free/inner-precious rule made into eligibility policy.

**C. Outer-edge snap: treat an unanchored mark that touches an edge as having ONE uncertain edge, not two.** The four outer wrong marks are all width errors around real ads. Pinning the outer edge to 0:00/end and treating only the inner edge as uncertain turns "0-120, half wrong" into "starts at 0:00, ends ~1:00-2:00" - per-edge eligibility (ye0n/lc4c family) applied to presentation/clipping. Risks: the inner edge still needs real width evidence (rediff/stinger/anchor) - this narrows 4xqf, it does not solve it.

A+B are independent and cheap; C is the 4xqf program. Not proposing an order - the numbers above are the frame.

## Residuals
- What the player UI literally rendered for each mark is unrecoverable from this DB (decision_events has zero rows for this asset; only backfill_fusion detectOnly rows exist corpus-wide). The veto projections prove the windows surfaced in the correction UI at their stored extents; the 4.4s gap between the real ad end (59.82) and Dan's veto start (64.2) is presumed slider placement.
- The bead's cause-2 note says fast reached only 179.8s; in THIS pull fast covers 0-1316.34 (fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime 1316.728) - fast completed after the bead was written. Final still stops at 1199.82. Post-roll numbers posted to z3jg.
- DE0784D8's 2s tail-trim veto (60.06-62.10) left the whole correct 60.13s byte-exact pre-roll window decisionState=reverted - a partial veto reverting an entire correct window. Adjacent to dsq5 (MIXED revert weakening); flagged here rather than filed because the UI gesture semantics are not recoverable from the DB. If Dan confirms he meant "trim", this is its own bead.
- Near-zero-confidence acoustic windows (0.0013 / 0.0012) were user-visible marks on 0C2FC22E/DE0784D8 - that is playhead-8x59's territory, not re-filed.
- 0C2FC22E has ZERO semantic_scan_results rows and rediff exit all_slots_already_covered with lastMarkCount 0 - both its real breaks (outer start AND outer end) had no detection at all except an abutting conf-0.001 acoustic fragment. Not fully walked (budget); if the corpus question graduates to a program, this asset is the next establish target.

comments.text: Dan's decision 2026-08-08: Option A approved — 3oyz (same-session rediff retry for zero-byte fetch failures) starts now. Options B (demote inner unanchored band) and C (outer-edge snap) DEFERRED until after the 7:04am device pull adds field data. B, if taken, should be scoped to detection-v1's calibrated confidences until the flat 0.70 constant becomes a derived value (it is semantic-sweep/FM's lane — the host-read mid-roll mechanism).

title: Make the recurring defect STRUCTURALLY impossible: same-unit quantities that mean different things must not be interchangeable
description:
## The defect class, and why a checklist will not close it

Eighteen instances across six beads in one queue (2026-08-03/04). Every one is the same shape: **two quantities share a unit — seconds, a ratio, a count — and one is read as though it were the other.** The compiler cannot object, because both are `Double` or `Int`. Review catches them one at a time, and **three of the last five were introduced BY the fix for a previous one.** That is the signature of a class that cannot be fixed by care.

## The evidence

**Cursors vs coverage (the most expensive family)**
1. `26od` — the resume cursor claimed coverage no persisted row supported. **Seven distinct variants** at different granularities.
2. `41mu` field witness — 53FC53E3's cursor recorded `2525.82`: the **end of the last segment it was handed**, read as **how far through the episode it had got**. It completed 23 s after creation at 1.42 % coverage and locked its own re-drive out forever.
3. `5pyq` (open) — `contiguousUpperBoundSec` is a **plan-list** prefix, published as an **episode** cursor at three call sites.
4. `41mu` R2 — `recordUnderCoverageTerminal` fed the cursor rule the **pre-narrowing** segment list where its contract is the **narrowed** one. Identical on attempt 1, divergent on every resume.

**Transcript reach vs transcript watermark vs transcript density**
5. `fil5` R3 (P0) — the sweep divided the **raw interval union** by duration. That is speech DENSITY, not reach. **0 of 12 field assets cleared the gate**; the feature was dead and every test passed, because every fixture was single-chunk — the one shape where the two coincide.
6. `9y9e` R1 — `transcribedIntervals = fast + final` dropped the watermark fallback, so the measure could DECREASE (1,000 s → 300 s) while its own comment asserted it could only rise.
7. `9y9e` R2/R3 — a divergence table measured `analysis_assets.fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime` (a **fast** column) for a paragraph about `chunks.map(\.endTime).max()` over **both** passes, hiding the largest divergence on the pull.
8. `41mu` R3 — an interior-gap count was **ten** under the fast-union definition and **nine** under the canonical one; the sentence used one number and the other definition.
9. `0sro`/`pz32` — the readiness checkmark keyed on the DSP watermark and `max(endTime)` of detected ads, so **worse detection read as more complete**.

**Decisions computed twice instead of consumed once**
10. `41mu` UC04 — `recordUnderCoverageTerminal` re-derived `attempts >= maxRetries` instead of reading the arm the pure decision had already chosen; `.failUnderCoverage` was computed and discarded, end-to-end green while the pure rail reddened.
11. `fil5` R2 — the sweep's candidate query correctly named "assets with no coverage-lane row"; the sweep consumed it as "assets nobody will call runBackfill for again".

**Absence vs zero vs contradiction**
12. `fil5` R4 — `podcastId` read as `""` when it is **SQL NULL** on 43 of 44 rows.
13. `41mu` R1 — a **non-finite** `.measured` fraction returned `.complete`; the terminal was the only consumer reading that absence as "read".
14. `41mu` R1 — `.notMeasurable` justified against 1 of the 4 ways the fraction returns nil; the other three are a **contradicted** denominator, not a missing one (`w4rd`).

**Counts of the wrong population**
15. `9y9e` R1 — "four of twelve had a ceiling below the floor": four is the number **lifted**, nine were **capped**.
16. `fil5` R4 — the zero-row population is **four**, not three, restated wrongly in five places.
17. `41mu` R1 — a test argument list of **five** values labelled "the three field assets", two matching nothing in the pull.

**And the one that hid a P0 for months**
18. `hc7e` wrote at `AdDetectionService.swift:4147`: *"Every consumer now reads `canonicalChunks`."* Line 9697 does not. A **completeness claim that was not complete** — two reviewers had to rediscover `iu0t` from device data.

## What to build

**1. Distinct types for the quantities that keep being substituted.** They are all `Double` today. At minimum, in the coverage/reach path:

- `EpisodeSeconds` (a position in the episode) vs `PlanListSeconds` (a position in a handed-over segment list) — instances 1–4
- `ReachRatio` (covered ÷ duration) vs `DensityRatio` (spoken ÷ duration) vs `WatermarkSeconds` (a high-water mark, not an area) — instances 5–9
- `BridgeToleranceSec` (a hole small enough to bridge WHEN MEASURING, 5 s) vs `RescanThresholdSec` (a hole big enough to be worth RE-SCANNING, 60 s per `a1x0`) — these are about to collide; see the scope note on that bead

A `RawRepresentable` struct over `Double` costs nothing at runtime and makes instances 1–9 **compile errors**.

**2. A doc rule with teeth: every ratio names its numerator AND denominator at the declaration.** `adScanFraction` says neither. Instances 5, 8, 15, 16, 17 are all readers guessing the denominator.

**3. A mutation-battery convention for this class.** The existing battery proves a test fails when behaviour is reverted. This class needs the inverse: a mutant that **substitutes one quantity for its lookalike** must fail to COMPILE. Record those as a distinct verdict (`UNTYPEABLE`) — a compile failure is the strongest kill available and the battery currently cannot express it.

**4. An audit, and it is the deliverable that pays first.** Enumerate every `Double`/`Int` crossing a module boundary in the coverage/reach path; for each, write its numerator, denominator and unit. Anything that cannot be stated in one line is a latent instance. `playhead-5pyq` and `playhead-w4rd` are already-known entries.

## Scope discipline

Do NOT convert the whole codebase. Start with the eight or so quantities named above, all in `AnalysisStore` / `BackfillJobRunner` / `AnalysisCoverageMath` / `AnalysisJobReconciler`. The value is concentrated: every one of the eighteen instances is in that path.

## How to know it worked

The next reach bead's review rounds should find **zero** instances of this class. Today the rate is roughly one per round, and it has not fallen across four beads.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
## PRIORITISED (Dan, 2026-08-04): runs NEXT, immediately after playhead-iu0t — not after the device build

Order is now: **iu0t (in flight) -> x0lb -> e75l -> dl9k -> device install -> pu7e.**

The reason to front-load it rather than treat it as cleanup: **every bead after this one inherits compile-time protection instead of shipping another instance.** The class rate has been roughly one per review round and has not fallen across four beads — 26od, fil5, 9y9e, 41mu — so the expected cost of doing e75l and dl9k first is two more instances found by hand, plus however many are not found.

**The immediate collision this prevents.** `playhead-a1x0` introduces a 60 s re-scan threshold that will sit directly beside the existing 5 s `adScanBridgeableGapSec`. title: retryShadowFMPhaseForSession replays a candidate-local final-only transcript, not the canonical one — a second transcriptVersion id space
description:
## The defect

`AdDetectionService.retryShadowFMPhaseForSession` (AdDetectionService.swift:9696-9697) builds the chunk set it replays as:

    let finalChunks = chunks.filter { $0.pass == TranscriptPassType.final_.rawValue }
    let chunksForReplay = finalChunks.isEmpty ? chunks : finalChunks

That is RAW persisted chunks, or FINAL-ONLY chunks. It is never canonicalized.

`runBackfill` (AdDetectionService.swift:4169-4171) does the opposite and says why in a long comment: `TranscriptChunkCanonicalizer.canonicalize(chunks).chunks.sorted(by: canonicalTimeOrder)`. That comment is explicit that the pre-hc7e `filter { pass == \"final\" }` was the bug — 'collapsed the whole timeline to the candidate-local final chunks the moment a single final chunk existed (a candidate-local atom timeline instead of full-episode coverage)' — and that 'Every consumer now reads canonicalChunks'.

`retryShadowFMPhaseForSession` was never converted. It is the surviving instance of the exact shape hc7e removed.

## Two consequences, both on the reach path

1. **A second transcriptVersion id space.** `runShadowFMPhase` atomizes whatever chunks it is handed, so the retry drain derives V_final while every other path derives V_canonical. `BackfillJobRunner`'s deterministic jobId embeds transcriptVersion, so the retry path's rows can never dedupe against the primary path's: a drain re-mints and re-scans audio the primary pass already scanned, and its `complete` rows are invisible to the next `runBackfill`.
2. **A truncated FM input.** Once any final-pass chunk exists, the replay sees ONLY the final chunks — narrow re-transcribed ad windows — so the shadow retry reads a candidate-local timeline instead of the episode.

## Why it is filed rather than fixed

Found in the playhead-fil5 R2 review. fil5 only PROPAGATES it: the durable scan claim minted on a closed gate derives its id from the same chunk set its caller would have atomized, so the claim correctly names the job THAT path would mint — internally consistent, and changing it there would be wrong. The defect is the chunk set itself, and repairing it changes FM replay input and runner dedupe, which is a different bead's behaviour.

## Fix shape

Route `chunksForReplay` through `TranscriptChunkCanonicalizer.canonicalize(...).chunks` the way `runBackfill` does, keeping the non-empty guard. Check first whether any existing test pins the final-only preference (the fallback comment cites lines 1395 and 2607 of the same file as the pattern source — those may need the same treatment).

LABELS: ad-detection, reach

**53FC53E3 on the 2026-08-03 device pull: 99.3 % transcript, 1.4 % ad-scan.** Proven by hash, not inference: its persisted `transcriptVersion 55afd3e8bb41833c004ee7d4b1be7589` is byte-exact `transcriptVersionHash` over the **32 final chunks alone**. Canonical fast+final would be `61872a4d…`; fast-only `766ea8ba…`.

    let chunksForReplay = finalChunks.isEmpty ? chunks : finalChunks

**2,917 fast chunks covering [0, 2490] were on disk and were discarded.** The job scanned one window over [2490, 2525.8], completed 23 s after creation, published cursor `2525.82` — the end of the last segment it was HANDED, read as how far through the episode it had got — and `countResumableBackfillJobs` then read 0, locking the re-drive out permanently. `playhead-3ort` is this bead. Closing it as a duplicate; its evidence is above. Promoting to **P0**: it is live on `main` at `adab7bc6`, it is in the reach path this queue exists to fix, and it has field proof of destroying 2,490 s of transcribed audio on a real episode.

The fix is not just swapping in `canonicalChunks` — the replay path's `transcriptVersion` identity changes with it, so a resumed job's id derivation moves. Check against `BackfillJobRunner`'s jobId derivation and `countResumableBackfillJobs`' batch window before landing.

## R2 — the `backfill_jobs` bucketing, settled by re-derivation

Two earlier readings disagreed. The implementer reported **14 rows across 12 assets**,
bucketed 1 final-only / 5 canonical / 8 neither. R1 reported **14 rows across 8 assets**,
1 / 5 canonical / 1 fast-only (`fm-be3e58602b483130`, DE0784D8) / 7 neither, and argued the
remainder could not be called "a pre-existing orphan class" because transcript GROWTH after
mint explains a NEITHER bucket just as well.

**R1 is right on the counts, and the interpretation goes further R1's way than R1 claimed.**

Counts: `COUNT(*) FROM backfill_jobs` = 14; `COUNT(DISTINCT analysisAssetId)` = **8**. No
filter narrows it — all 14 rows are `fm-`-prefixed, `phase='fullEpisodeScan'`,
`coveragePolicy='fullCoverage'`. **12 is `COUNT(*) FROM analysis_assets`**, not the assets
`backfill_jobs` references; the four with zero rows are 48E903D7, FCDDB309, 4FF3A238,
2C5C3699 — exactly the four `SemanticScanClaim`'s doc comment already names. 8 + 4 = 12.
The tally is R1's: **1 final-only / 5 canonical / 1 fast-only / 7 neither.**

One methodological note worth keeping: **`backfill_jobs` has no `transcriptVersion` column.**
Bucketing by "the row's persisted version" is not available on the row; job-id re-derivation
is the only direct method. Cross-checked against the two places a version IS persisted
(`transcript_chunks.transcriptVersion` on final rows, `semantic_scan_results.transcriptVersion`)
and the two methods never disagreed.

### The 7 "neither" rows are transcript growth. All seven. Proven, not inferred.

Searching 11 prefix families per row, **every one of the 7 is an exact hash preimage over a
CANONICALIZED strict prefix of that asset's current chunk set** — i.e. `canonicalize` applied
to the first N chunks, N < today's count. An exact SHA-256 hit is ~2^-64 per trial over a
~4x10^5-trial search, so these are not coincidences.

Four corroborating lines:

1. **Every mint set is a contiguous PREFIX**, one of ~n candidates out of 2^n subsets. Nothing
   was replaced or removed; chunks were only added.
2. **Chronology is monotone on all four multi-row assets, and the newest row on every one of
   them lands on today's FULL canonical set**: 58882C47 N=1605 -> 2029 -> 2183; AD5F3A0A
   N=1136 -> 1192 -> 5167; 0C2FC22E N=2139 -> 2212; DE0784D8 fast-only -> full canonical.
   An orphan class has no reason to be ordered.
3. **Two of the reconstructed versions are independently persisted in `semantic_scan_results`**
   — AD5F3A0A's `bc0cac8e…` (23 rows) and `ce9c3e48…` (22 rows), plus DE0784D8's `62771a45…`
   (42 rows). Real scans ran under those versions and wrote results keyed to them, so each was
   live and self-consistent AT MINT TIME. It stopped reproducing only because more chunks
   arrived.
4. Final rows interleave with fast rows on 8 of 12 assets, i.e. the transcript was still
   accumulating across both passes while jobs were minted.

Stated caveat: `transcript_chunks` has no `createdAt`, so rowid is the only insertion-order
proxy and on 53FC53E3 it is demonstrably not literal insertion order. That does not weaken
the result — the load-bearing fact is the exact preimage over a nested subset family, and
rowid ordering is corroboration, not premise.

**Ruling.** The NEITHER bucket contains **zero** orphans, so it may not be cited as evidence
for a pre-existing orphan class — it now positively refutes one. The orphan class is real and
has exactly **one** member, `fm-041dedcf8293523e` on 53FC53E3, and that member was never in
the NEITHER bucket: it matches final-only exactly, its 32 chunks span the tail [2490.0,
2525.82] rather than a prefix, and it is precisely the defect this bead fixes. The migration
conclusion (no migration needed) is unaffected, as both prior agents said.

R1 added rules 1–2. R2 added declaration scoping and rule 3 — a genuinely new SINK, not a refinement.
R3 and R4 have both been closing the *same two* defects (spelling-bound needles, missing vacuity
anchor) across three rules one at a time, because the fixes were applied per-rule instead of
per-property. That sweep is now complete: all three rules carry a pattern rather than literals, all
three carry a vacuity floor, and the walk itself has a rail. There is no fourth rule to sweep.

The machinery IS the expensive part and is the source of findings 4 and of R2's scoping finding.
Recommendation: **freeze the parser's capability here.** Rule 1's resolver is at two hops with a
300-character window; the next request of it (three hops, `var` bindings, a receiver whose name lacks
"chunk") should be refused, and the answer should be to canonicalize at the site or allow-list it with
a reason — not to make the parser smarter.

### The production fix is complete — re-verified, not re-read

All four converted sites reach a terminal reader that orders its own input (`atomize` and
`transcriptVersionHash` both sort with `canonicalTimeOrder`), so the omitted `.sorted(…)` at the
retry drain is genuinely unobservable. Nothing downstream compares the catalog's version
(`setEvidenceCatalog` matches on assetId, `catalogEntries` slices by time,
`CommercialEvidenceResolver` keys on `category|normalizedText`). `guard !atoms.isEmpty` protects the
`atoms[0]` read in `runPhase5ProjectorPhase`.

**Migration, re-derived rather than inherited.** Of the 14 `backfill_jobs` rows, exactly **1** is
final-only (`fm-041dedcf8293523e` — the defect's own output), **5** land on today's canonical id, and
**8** are earlier canonicalized prefixes. The fix strands nothing resumable. Exact agreement with R2.

**New corroboration for the R2 fix.** On the pull, 2 of 4 `episode_summaries` rows carry a **NULL**
transcriptVersion despite their assets now holding 329 and 21 final chunks; 1 is a stale earlier value
of the column; exactly 1 matches the column verbatim. None matches any canonical version. The old code
copied a snapshot of a column rather than deriving anything — visible directly in the data.

**Reach the fix recovers:** canonical minus final-only coverage over the 11 mixed-pass assets is
**22,521.6 s (6.26 h)**, and it cross-checks against the diff's own denominators
(7,295.59 + 22,521.60 = 29,817.19).

### Re-derived independently (clean-room canonicalizer + hasher, controlled first)

`55afd3e8…` / `61872a4d…` / `766ea8ba…` byte-exact; `fm-041dedcf8293523e`,
`fm-46ea5fad09da03b2` (un-minted, confirmed absent), `fm-af6aeeb497745eca`; 29,247 fast NULL /
8,251 final stamped, 1 distinct value per asset; 7295.5914 / 29817.1914 = 24.4677 %, worst 1.5432 %;
14 rows / 8 assets; `droppedFast > 0` on exactly 7 of the 11 mixed-pass assets with residual overlap 0
on all twelve; 9 of 12 assets at 0.00 % ad-scan. Every number in the diff reproduces.

### No sixth instance

Not by redoing R3's narrowing census — I could not name a shape it misses — but by the complementary
SINK-rooted enumeration: `atomize` and `transcriptVersionHash` (8 call sites, all audited), the
persisted `transcript_chunks` columns (0 reads outside the two exempt files), other tables'
`transcriptVersion` columns (only carried forward from the row that owns them), and literals. Those
are the only routes to a version.

### Observation, filed not fixed

`FoundationModelClassifierShadowDispatcher.buildPrompt`, `SpecialistShadowDispatcher.buildPrompt` and
`LiveShadowWindowSource` window-filter the RAW persisted chunks, so on a mixed-pass asset the audio
the final pass re-transcribed appears in the prompt TWICE — hc7e's duplicate-evidence half, surviving
outside iu0t's rule because it reaches no identity sink. Measured: **1,544 chunks / 1,393.9 s across
7 of 12 assets.** Pre-existing on `main`, untouched by this diff, and changing it changes FM prompt
content — its own bead.

## R5 — 4 findings, all in the ENFORCEMENT, all demonstrated by planting; the production fix is confirmed complete

**This is not the closing round.** Findings went 4 -> 10 -> 4 -> 5 -> **4**. R4's declaration on the
production change holds and I verified it computationally rather than by re-reading. Its declaration
that the enforcement had *converged* does not: the sweep R3 and R4 ran ("patterns not literals,
a vacuity floor per detector") had never been applied to rule 1's own two mechanisms, and both were
still in the pre-sweep state.

### What I planted, and what happened

Four shapes nobody had planted. The canary passed on three of them.

| plant | canary before R5 | after |
|---|---|---|
| uncanonicalized `atomize(chunks: chunks, …)` written `TranscriptAtomizer` NEWLINE `.atomize(` | **PASSED** | rule 1 names it |
| the SAME defect written inline (the control) | FAILED, named the site | FAILED |
| `filter { $0.pass != "fast" }` + `.isEmpty ? chunks :` | **PASSED** | rule 2 names it |
| `atomize(chunks: canonicalize(chunks).chunks.filter { $0.pass == "final" })` | **PASSED** | rule 1 names it |

The first two rows differ by one line break. That was the difference between a red test and silence,
and in the silent case the site was not even COUNTED — the `audited` floor never moved.

### Findings

1. **P2, enforcement — the site finder was a SPELLING.** `guardedCalls` held the literal substrings
   `"TranscriptAtomizer.atomize("` / `"…transcriptVersionHash("`, searched with
   `String.range(of:)`. A member call split across lines was not a call site at all: unaudited,
   uncounted, unreported, indistinguishable from a clean tree. This is the fail-OPEN direction in
   the walk's FOUNDATION — R4 closed exactly this drop one level down (a call with no `chunks:` of
   its own) and the same drop remained above it for a call the finder never found. Now
   `\bTranscriptAtomizer\s*\.\s*atomize\s*\(`. Rail:
   `testTheSiteFinderSeesACallSplitAcrossLines`, on synthetic source, asserting the split and
   inline spellings parse IDENTICALLY — finding the site but reading a different argument out of it
   would only move the hole. Stated limit, which the old form did not have: a call through a
   typealias or a stored function reference is still invisible and closing that needs type
   information this test does not have.

2. **P3, enforcement — rule 1's vacuity floor was SUMMED over two detectors.** Measured by reading
   the counts back, R3's method: `atomize` 6, `transcriptVersionHash` 2, floor 6. So the
   `transcriptVersionHash` detector could match nothing whatever — renamed, or a pattern that stops
   compiling — and the guard stays green off `atomize`'s hits. That is R3's finding 3 and R4's
   finding 3 verbatim, one rule over from where R4 fixed it per (file, FIELD) in rule 3. Two
   floors now (4 and 1); the sum is not one of them.

3. **P3, enforcement — `isCanonicalized` tested for a TOKEN, not a value.** It answered "is this
   argument canonicalized" with "does the string `canonicalize(` appear", so a site that
   canonicalizes and then throws the result away passed. The bead's own defect class, inside the
   check named for it, failing OPEN. Rule 2 cannot cover it: its conjunction needs the
   `X.isEmpty ? chunks : X` fallback and a bare `.filter` has none.

   **And fixing `isCanonicalized` alone did not kill it.** The measurement caught what reading
   would not have: a duplicated bare `argument.contains("canonicalize(")` one line below still let
   the same argument through. That second check is gone — one predicate now serves the scoped and
   file-scope cases. This bead's fixes have reintroduced its own defect in R2, R3 and R4; this is
   R5's, caught before it landed only because the plant was re-run rather than the diff re-read.

4. **P3, enforcement — rule 2's half one still required `==` against a final literal.** So the
   collapse spelled as a NEGATION was invisible. Not hypothetical: instance #5 of the five IS the
   negation (`backfillLegacyTranscriptChunksPhase1IfNeeded`, `WHERE pass != 'fast'`), and the
   canary's own header already called it "the collapse spelled as a negation". Added the `!= fast`
   arm and RE-MEASURED over `Playhead/` minus the exempt files: half one 1 -> 2 files
   (`FinalPassRetranscriptionRunner`, and `AnalysisStore` — the negation's own permanent home, which
   makes the anchor better), half two 1, CONJUNCTION still 0. No false positive bought.

P4, documentation: the file header said "THREE tests" and there were four. A stale census in the
census-checker's own header. Rewritten as THREE RULES plus rails.

### Verdict on R4's two declarations

**Production fix — complete. Confirmed, not re-read.**
- `canonicalize` is idempotent: verified on all 12 device assets (chunk ORDER and version hash both
  stable under a second application) and across 20,000 randomised adversarial mixed-pass sets with
  zero-length spans, duplicate `chunkIndex`, empty text and coincident boundaries. 0 violations.
- It never empties a non-empty set: 0 violations over the same 20,012 cases. So the preserved
  `!chunksForReplay.isEmpty` guard cannot newly bail.
- Both terminal readers order their own input — `TranscriptAtom.swift:103` and `:186` each
  `sorted(by: TranscriptChunkCanonicalizer.canonicalTimeOrder)` — so the omitted `.sorted(…)` at
  the drain is genuinely unobservable, as the comment claims.

**Enforcement — was NOT converged; is closer now.** R4's "all three rules carry a pattern rather
than literals, all three carry a vacuity floor" is true in letter and incomplete in substance,
because rule 1 is a TWO-stage rule — find the site, then judge the argument — and only the judging
half was ever swept. Both of its other mechanisms (findings 1 and 2) were in the pre-sweep state.

**On "freeze the parser's capability" — the recommendation is right, and R5 is not a request of it.**
Every fix here removes a fail-open, none adds resolving power: no third hop, no `var`, no
receiver-name inference. Finding 1 is not the parser getting smarter at arguments, it is the walk
being able to SEE a call it could not see. The capability is also now honestly documented for the
first time — as of R4 `argumentListEnd` stated its string-literal limit, `pattern(for:)` stated the
chunk-shaped-receiver limit, `isCanonicalized` listed three measured escapes, and `guardedCalls`
stated NOTHING. A limit that is not written down is the same defect class as a completeness claim
that is not complete, which is why finding 1 was findable at all.

### Every numeric claim in the diff, re-derived independently

Clean-room canonicalizer + hasher, written from the Swift source, CONTROLLED first against all three
of 53FC53E3's hashes (`55afd3e8bb41833c004ee7d4b1be7589` / `61872a4d3e718e8bb4b8156dc2099444` /
`766ea8ba068ffce5e3f48be66c9fa13f`, all byte-exact) before computing anything downstream.

- 53FC53E3: 2,917 fast over [0.00, 2490.00], 32 final over [2490.00, 2525.82].
- Persisted column: 29,247 `fast` rows ALL NULL, 8,251 `final` rows all stamped, exactly 1 distinct
  value per asset, 11 distinct values overall.
- `backfill_jobs`: 14 rows / 8 distinct assets, all `fm-`, all `fullEpisodeScan` / `fullCoverage`.
  Bucketed by job-id re-derivation: **1 final-only** (`fm-041dedcf8293523e`, 53FC53E3 — the defect's
  own output), **5 today's canonical**, **8 earlier canonicalized prefixes** (7 mixed-pass prefixes
  plus DE0784D8's fast-only `fm-be3e58602b483130`). **0 unmatched.** Nothing resumable is stranded.
- Reach recovered: final-only 7,295.5914 s vs canonical 29,817.1914 s over the 11 mixed-pass assets
  => **22,521.6000 s = 6.2560 h**; 24.4677 %, worst **1.5432 %** (33.9600 / 2200.5600 on 53FC53E3).
  4FF3A238 is the twelfth and has no final chunks, exactly as the `pushEvidenceCatalog` comment says.
- `droppedFast > 0` on **7 of 11** mixed-pass assets; `residualFastFinalOverlapCount` **0 on all 12**.
- **9 of 12 assets at exactly 0.00 % ad-scan** (0 `semantic_scan_results` rows). The three that are
  not: 53FC53E3 1.63 %, AD5F3A0A 23.60 %, DE0784D8 51.11 % (union of `windowStartTime`/`windowEndTime`
  over canonical coverage).

Every figure reproduces. Nothing in the diff overstates.

### playhead-3fak — measurement exact, one named site over-included

1,544 chunks / 1,393.9314 s across 7 of 12 reproduces to the decimal, and filing rather than fixing
is right (it changes prompt content and therefore model verdicts). But `LiveShadowWindowSource` does
not belong on the list: its only chunk read is `chunks.map(\.endTime).max()`, which canonicalization
provably cannot move (delta 0.0000000000 on all 12 assets). Corrected on that bead — two builders,
not three.

### Mutation

**CN01-CN12: 12 of 12 KILLED, 0 survivors, 0 errors, tree restored byte-exact.** CN01-CN09 re-run
because their victim file changed. Three added, one per newly-asserted property, each on
`pushEvidenceCatalog` so it is directly comparable to CN06/CN09:

- **CN10** — an uncanonicalized `atomize` call SPLIT ACROSS LINES. Victim: rule 1 only. Rule 2 is
  deliberately NOT named — the mutant carries no final-pass filter, so rule 2 is correct to stay
  green and naming it would be an expectation the mutant cannot meet.
- **CN11** — the collapse spelled `!= "fast"`. Victims: rules 1 and 2. Rule 2 is the discriminating
  one; under R4's pattern it stayed green.
- **CN12** — canonicalize-then-collapse. Victim: rule 1. The `canonicalize(` call is KEPT on purpose;
  removing it would be CN03's shape and would prove nothing about laundering.

### Gate — SCOPED, and labelled as such

Findings are non-zero, so no full plan and **no `playhead-s08j` observation from this round**. The
baseline was not accepted and could not be: selective runs are exempt.

    Test Suite 'Selected tests' passed at 2026-08-05 00:32:49.828.
    	 Executed 6 tests, with 0 failures (0 unexpected) in 2.339 (2.343) seconds
    ✔ Test run with 55 tests in 6 suites passed after 0.411 seconds.
    ** TEST SUCCEEDED **
    fast-gate: baseline check SKIPPED — selective run, a different population

Both formats triaged: 6 XCTest cases (the canary, which is invisible to the Swift Testing count) and
55 Swift Testing tests in 6 suites. Suites: the canary, ShadowRetryCanonicalReplay, ShadowRetry,
TranscriptChunkCanonicalizer, BackfillCoverageTerminal, SemanticScanClaim, SemanticScanClaimWireIn,
EpisodeSummaryBackfillCoordinator, EpisodeSummaryAdExclusion. `scripts/lint.sh --changed`: clean.

### What R6 should do

The production fix has now been declared complete by two independent rounds and verified
computationally by this one; I would not spend R6 on it again. R5's four findings were all in rule
1, which is the only rule that had never been swept — there is no fifth mechanism of that kind left
in the file. So R6 is the round that should either find nothing or find something outside the
canary entirely, and if it finds nothing, the bead closes on R5+R6 as the two consecutive clean
rounds Dan's rule asks for.

## R6 — 0 findings in the scoped area. The production fix verified independently, not inherited.

Findings: 4 -> 10 -> 4 -> 5 -> 4 -> **0**. Scope was deliberately narrow (production diff,
behavioural tests, the CN series' production cut). The canary was out of scope and I did not
audit, harden or plant against it; two observations for `playhead-x0lb` are at the bottom.

### The production change is 4 lines. I re-derived every number behind them from the device DB.

Clean-room canonicalizer + hasher written from `TranscriptChunkCanonicalizer.swift` and
`TranscriptAtom.swift`, **controlled against all three of 53FC53E3's hashes before computing
anything downstream** — `55afd3e8bb41833c004ee7d4b1be7589` / `61872a4d3e718e8bb4b8156dc2099444` /
`766ea8ba068ffce5e3f48be66c9fa13f`, all three byte-exact on the first run.

Everything reproduces, to the decimal:

- 53FC53E3: 2,917 fast over [0.00, 2490.00], 32 final over [2490.00, 2525.82].
- Persisted column: **29,247 fast rows ALL NULL, 8,251 final rows all stamped, exactly 1 distinct

- Reach: final-only 7295.5914 s vs canonical 29817.1914 s over the 11 mixed-pass assets =>

  not: 53FC53E3 1.63 %, AD5F3A0A 23.60 %, DE0784D8 51.11 %.

  of the 14 job ids: **1 final-only, 5 today's canonical, 1 fast-only, 7 canonicalized strict

**Nothing in the diff overstates, and nothing is stale.**

### No sixth instance, by three methods that do not share a failure mode

today** (checked by count), so none can drift-apply. `T_IU0T_FIXTURE` is deliberately not named as

2. **`AnalysisStore.swift:19517`'s `WHERE pass = 'fast'`** feeds the episode-summary coverage gate,

title: Reach: onn6 re-drives die in the transcription stage on fully-transcribed episodes and the 2-mint budget is spent — 9 queued fullEpisodeScan rows stranded
description:
## The defect (STILL BROKEN at d3dfa1ca)

An onn6 ad-scan re-drive dispatches a FULL preAnalysis pipeline, and on a fully-transcribed episode that pipeline cannot reach Stage 4 (ad detection). The transcription stage re-runs ASR on covered shards — mptr (#335, 440e8783) only REORDERS unread-first, it does not skip: FastTranscriptCoverageIndex.swift:169-171 ("still transcribes covered shards"), and the commit itself says "the dedup saves a row insert, not the transcription". With zero unread audio the flat 300s stage cap (AnalysisJobRunner.swift:662-665) always expires before `.completed`, the run exits `transcription:zeroCoverage` (AnalysisJobRunner.swift:736-783), and Stage 4 — the ONLY thing the re-drive exists for, the M-5 resume of queued backfill rows (BackfillJobRunner.swift:541-559) — never executes.

Each such doomed pass spends one of `maxAdScanRedrives = 2` (AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:6159). Once ordinal 2 terminates, `nextAdScanRedriveWorkKey` returns nil forever for this (fingerprint, analysisVersion) — the queued backfill rows have NO future pass until the 7-day analysis_jobs GC lets `discoverUnEnqueuedDownloads` re-mint a full re-analysis (and only if the audio is still cached).

## Measured on the 2026-08-03 device pull

- AD5F3A0A (100% transcript): `adScanRedrive:1` superseded `maxAttemptsReached:transcription:zeroCoverage`; `adScanRedrive:2` running with lastErrorCode `transcription:zeroCoverage`. Query: `SELECT workKey, state, lastErrorCode FROM analysis_jobs WHERE workKey LIKE '%adScanRedrive%'`.
- Both re-drive ordinals already spent: D9B513CD, 58882C47, DE0784D8, 44F076BB, 83592353 (all at :2, complete — several with `coverageInsufficient:noProgress`).
- 9 backfill_jobs rows sit `queued` across 6 assets (58882C47 x3, AD5F3A0A x2, 0C2FC22E, 44F076BB, 83592353, D9B513CD), retryCount 0 — never dispatched to completion, and now unreachable.
- Secondary stranding: jobIds embed transcriptVersion (BackfillJobRunner.swift:527-532), and every final-pass append rotates the version, so old-version queued rows (e.g. 58882C47's three) can NEVER be matched by M-5 again — yet they still count as "resumable" for onn6's mint guard (backfill_jobs has no transcriptVersion column, so `countResumableBackfillJobs` cannot tell), wasting re-drive ordinals on rows no pass can resume.

onn6 did not regress — it fired exactly as designed; its premise ("one pass drains the rows") is what fails in the field.

## The fix

1. A re-drive whose asset already has full transcript coverage must not require new transcription progress: either short-circuit the transcription stage to success when persisted coverage >= desired (letting Stage 4 run), or mint a scan-only job type that goes straight to the coverage lane.
2. Retire (supersede) old-transcriptVersion backfill rows when a new version's job is minted, so "resumable" counts only rows a pass can actually resume.
3. A one-time rescue for the already-stranded population (budget spent, rows queued) — e.g. re-drive ordinals reset when the failure was `transcription:zeroCoverage`, or an explicit reconcile step for queued rows older than N days with adScanFraction < floor.
notes:
## QUEUE 3 — REACH, Dan 2026-08-03. Six beads from the device-pull investigation.

    26od -> fil5 -> 9y9e -> 41mu -> e75l -> dl9k

**Why this queue exists.** A fresh device pull (2026-08-03, scratchpad/db-aug3/analysis.sqlite,
the first usable field data in two weeks) measured: **12 episodes, 9 transcribed to ~100%, only 3
with ANY semantic ad-scan, ZERO at >=98%.** An episode at 0% scan cannot produce a skip no matter
how correct the downstream logic is. The sixteen beads merged 2026-08-02/03 (#327-#344) all
improved downstream CORRECTNESS; none moved REACH. Reach is the dominant term.

**Order is by multiplier, not severity.**
  * 26od FIRST because it is the multiplier: coarsePassA persists nothing until it returns,
    passes need 12-45min, lifecycle windows are ~30min, so ~4.6 HOURS of FM compute this weekend
    produced ZERO durable scan rows. Until this lands every other fix in this queue evaporates
    the same way.
  * fil5 second: 3 of 12 episodes have NO path to a scan at all, and every shadow-phase bail is
    silent (FCDDB309 ran runBackfill TWICE and minted nothing; which of four gates fired is
    recorded nowhere). Also makes the NEXT device pull attributable.
  * 9y9e third: onn6 re-drives structurally cannot drain (full preAnalysis pass re-transcribes
    covered audio; mptr only REORDERS, does not skip; 300s cap wins; zeroCoverage). maxAdScanRedrives=2
    is SPENT on five assets.
  * 41mu / e75l are correctness-of-accounting on the same path. dl9k is a rescue nudge, last.

CLASSIFIED AGAINST THE SHIPPED BUILD (d3dfa1ca): rate-limit terminal is FIXED (kvs8 #320); the
mptr covered-prefix MECHANISM is fixed (#335) but no vehicle re-mints a pass for already-stuck
assets. Everything else in this queue is STILL BROKEN on the phone.

Method: iterative-implementation-with-review-loops. One bead at a time, full gate + mutation
battery each, cap 20 review rounds, stop on two consecutive clean.

title: Reach: transcript completion never durably requests a semantic scan — 3 of 12 field assets (95-100% transcript) have zero backfill_jobs and no recovery path
description:
## The defect (STILL BROKEN at d3dfa1ca)

Nothing durably requests a semantic ad-scan when a transcript completes. The only three paths that mint a `fullEpisodeScan` backfill_jobs row are:

1. `AnalysisCoordinator.finalizeBackfill` (AnalysisCoordinator.swift:2244; call sites 1529, 2075) — requires a live SESSION, i.e. the user-playback pipeline. Only 3 sessions exist in the whole weekend pull.
2. `AnalysisJobRunner` Stage 4 (AnalysisJobRunner.swift:908) — requires a preAnalysis pass to survive stages 1-3 first.
3. The final-pass hook (PlayheadRuntime.swift:1905-1917 -> revalidateFromFeatures, AdDetectionService.swift:6903 -> runBackfill) — requires >=1 AdWindow above the 0.5 confidence floor to have been re-transcribed.

All three then funnel through `runShadowFMPhase` (AdDetectionService.swift:9208), which SILENTLY drops the work at four gates with no durable trace: mode `.off` via cohort (9218), missing factory (9220), `canUseFoundationModels` false (9260 — and on the sessionless paths 2 and 3 the bd-3bz retry marker is skipped at 9264-9266, so the drop is permanent), and empty podcastId (4253-4254; the fp hook passes `request.podcastId ?? ""` at PlayheadRuntime.swift:1910). A transient FM-probe false is cached 15 min (`FoundationModelsUsabilityProbe.falseCacheTTL`, cited in FMDaemonThrottle.swift:91-93), so one throttle can silently swallow every completion that lands in that window.

## Measured on the 2026-08-03 device pull

- FCDDB309 (100% transcript), 4FF3A238 (100%), 48E903D7 (95%): ZERO backfill_jobs rows. Query: `SELECT id FROM analysis_assets WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT analysisAssetId FROM backfill_jobs)`.
- FCDDB309 proves runBackfill RAN twice and minted nothing: decision_events at 2026-08-02 12:44:01 (= its :1911 tier completion) and 2026-08-03 06:47:42 (= its final-pass completion) — fusion ran, the FM phase (step 6) was gated, and no row records why.
- onn6's re-drive cannot reach these assets by design: `mintAdScanRedrives` starts from `fetchAssetIdsWithResumableBackfillJobs` (AnalysisJobReconciler.swift:1166) — zero rows means zero mints, forever. No merge in #327-#344 touches runShadowFMPhase or adds a trigger (verified: `git log a6c9987b..HEAD -- .../AdDetectionService.swift .../AnalysisJobReconciler.swift`).

These three episodes (25% of the field library) have NO path to a scan on the build now on Dan's phone.

## The fix (two halves, both needed)

1. A durable "scan wanted" trigger: when measured transcript coverage crosses the finalize floor and measured adScanFraction is below `semanticBackfillSufficientAdScanFraction`, the asset must own a persisted claim to a scan that survives process death and gate-closures — not an in-flight call that evaporates at the first closed gate. (Shape suggestion: mint the backfill_jobs row FIRST, gate only its dispatch — the row is exactly this claim; the current code gates its creation.)
2. kvs8 discipline for every runShadowFMPhase bail: each of the four silent gates must write a durable named row so the next device pull can attribute a missing scan in one query.
notes:
