the first usable field data in two weeks) measured: **12 episodes, 9 transcribed to ~100%, only 3
with ANY semantic ad-scan, ZERO at >=98%.** An episode at 0% scan cannot produce a skip no matter
how correct the downstream logic is. The sixteen beads merged 2026-08-02/03 (#327-#344) all
improved downstream CORRECTNESS; none moved REACH. Reach is the dominant term.

**Order is by multiplier, not severity.**
  * 26od FIRST because it is the multiplier: coarsePassA persists nothing until it returns,
    passes need 12-45min, lifecycle windows are ~30min, so ~4.6 HOURS of FM compute this weekend
    produced ZERO durable scan rows. Until this lands every other fix in this queue evaporates
    the same way.
  * fil5 second: 3 of 12 episodes have NO path to a scan at all, and every shadow-phase bail is
    silent (FCDDB309 ran runBackfill TWICE and minted nothing; which of four gates fired is
    recorded nowhere). Also makes the NEXT device pull attributable.
  * 9y9e third: onn6 re-drives structurally cannot drain (full preAnalysis pass re-transcribes
    covered audio; mptr only REORDERS, does not skip; 300s cap wins; zeroCoverage). maxAdScanRedrives=2
    is SPENT on five assets.

title: Reach: coarsePassA persists nothing until it returns — every mid-pass death loses the whole scan (~4.6h FM lost this weekend, 0 rows)
description:
## The defect (STILL BROKEN at d3dfa1ca)

`coarsePassA` persists NOTHING until it returns. HEAD's own doc states it: FMInferenceDeadline.swift:353-355 — "coarsePassA persists NOTHING until it returns. Every scan row is written by BackfillJobRunner.runJob from the returned windows, so a pass in flight is invisible in the database by construction." A healthy coarse pass takes 12-45 min of FM wall-clock per episode (AdDetectionService.swift:922), which does not fit inside an app-lifecycle window or a ~30-min BG grant. So every mid-pass death (jetsam, suspend, BG expiry that is not a clean CancellationError) loses ALL banked windows; the reaper (AnalysisJobReconciler.swift:1029) flips the row back to `queued` and the next run starts the FM work from zero. playhead-t1kq's honest-cursor salvage fires only on a graceful CancellationError (BackfillJobRunner.swift:940-958) and salvages the CURSOR, not the scanned windows' results.

## Measured on the 2026-08-03 device pull (scratchpad/db-aug3/analysis.sqlite, pre-#327 build)

- AD5F3A0A (4280s episode, 100% transcript): two fullEpisodeScan runs of 37.4 min (08:48:12->09:25:37) and 29.8 min (09:49:06->10:18:52) ended with rows reset to `queued` by the reaper and ZERO semantic_scan_results past windowEndTime 900s. Query: `SELECT max(windowEndTime) FROM semantic_scan_results WHERE analysisAssetId LIKE 'AD5F3A0A%'` -> 900.0. All 45 of its rows came from the one run that RETURNED (08:20:33->08:23:05, against a then-900s partial transcript).
- 58882C47: three runs, 30.1 + 28.0 + 29.7 min (backfill_jobs createdAt->updatedAt), zero scan rows total.
- Summing created->updated across all 9 queued + 1 deferred rows: up to ~4.6 hours of running time produced zero durable scan rows this weekend. (updatedAt advanced per qk44's per-window lease touch, so windows were being banked in memory — and still nothing survived.)

None of #327-#344 touches this: lxkq (53da9f96) reorders the sweep by ad-likelihood but persistence still happens only at pass return.

## The fix

Persist each banked window's scan result (or checkpoint batches of N windows) while the pass is running, so every granted minute becomes durable coverage. The reuseKeyHash UNIQUE constraint already makes re-runs idempotent. This is the multiplier for every other reach fix: without it, triggered scans on episodes longer than ~15 min structurally treadmill on this device.
notes:
## QUEUE 3 — REACH. Canonical order, read this rather than a hardcoded list.

    26od -> fil5 -> 9y9e -> 41mu -> e75l -> dl9k

Status is whatever `bd show playhead-<id>` says (OPEN/CLOSED). The NEXT bead is the first
still-OPEN id in that order whose worktree/branch does not already exist. Derive it at check
time; do not trust a list written into a monitoring prompt, which goes stale the moment a
bead lands.

title: the test scratch root is never reclaimed DURING a run, so a full gate needs ~2x the disk this box has
description:
BLOCKS THE ENTIRE BEAD QUEUE. Five gate attempts on playhead-lxkq died with NSPOSIXErrorDomain Code=28 'No space left on device', always near the end of the suite (~99%). This is not a machine-size problem.

MECHANISM (PlayheadTests/Helpers/TestHelpers.swift:26-47):
makeTempDir() hands every test a fresh subdirectory under a process-wide scratch root at tmp/PlayheadTestScratch. There are exactly two cleanup paths and BOTH fire only at process boundaries:
  - line 29: removeItem(root) inside the lazy global initialiser (wipe on FIRST USE)
  - line 31: an atexit hook that removes the root on NORMAL exit
Nothing reclaims anything WHILE the suite runs. So across ~2,848 Swift Testing tests plus ~1,050 XCTest cases the scratch grows monotonically, and peak disk is the SUM of every test's scratch rather than the max of any one.

That is why failure always lands near the end: consumption only ever rises. Measured 2026-08-02: a run starting with 10.9 GiB free consumed all of it and died at ~4,141 ST + 900 XC passes; 1,856 leftover dirs / 1.2 GiB remained afterwards because the abnormal exit skipped the atexit hook.

The file's own header comment records the prior incident ('140k+ dirs / 70 GiB accumulated before cleanup existed'). The fix made at that time addressed ACROSS-run accumulation and left WITHIN-run growth untouched.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE GATE: with no verdict possible, every bead after lxkq merges on partial evidence. The voez baseline mechanism (RED N known / M NEW) is also disabled — the failed run reported 'RED (0 known / 82 NEW)' where all 82 were ENOSPC casualties and 35 of 41 baseline tests were never reached.

FIX DIRECTION (not prescriptive): give makeTempDir a per-test teardown so a test's scratch is released when it finishes, rather than at process exit. Swift Testing has no XCTest-style tearDown, so this likely needs the store/dir factories to return a handle that removes on deinit, or a confirmation-scoped helper. Care needed: some tests hold open SQLite handles, so removal must happen after the store is released.

ALSO WORTH MEASURING: 1,856 dirs = 1.2 GiB is ~650 KiB each, which extrapolates to only ~1.9 GiB for the full suite, but the run consumed ~10 GiB. So makeTempDir is one contributor and something else (audio fixtures?) is larger. Quantify before fixing.

WORKAROUND IN USE MEANWHILE: xcrun simctl erase <udid> on the idle sim reclaims ~4.6 GiB and is the documented remedy; combined with deleting leftover PlayheadTestScratch it took free space 8.9 -> 12.8 GiB.
notes:
MEASUREMENT (2026-08-02, scripts/scratch-sampler.sh). The bead's 'quantify before fixing' was right, and the answer is that makeTempDir is NOT the dominant term.

A full-plan run, sampled and guard-killed at 151 MiB free (9,675 Swift Testing + 900 XCTest cases in), consumed 7,995 MiB of free space:
  swap files      ~5,630 MiB (70%)  vm.swapusage total went 12,800M -> 7,168M the instant the test host died
  simulator dir    2,923 MiB        of which PlayheadTestScratch 2,026 MiB
  derivedData        100 MiB

So the ENOSPC is roughly three quarters MEMORY PRESSURE landing on the disk as swap, and one quarter test scratch. The swap half is a 16 GB box compiling and running a simulator, not something a test-only change can reach; it is reported, not fixed.

The scratch half is exactly the described mechanism and now has a shape: 2,847 leftover directories, 2,591 of them 732.6 KiB each, each holding one migrated analysis.sqlite (696 KiB) + -shm (32 KiB). The unit of cost is a STORE, not a temp directory, so makeTestStore* is the choke point and bare makeTempDir is not.

Two operational facts worth keeping:
- 'chmod -R u+w' does NOT make an abandoned scratch root removable. The mode the suite leaves behind is 0o300 (-wx------): write is already granted, READ is what rm needs to enumerate it. It is u+rwx or nothing.
- Free space fell 1.72 GiB -> 0.15 GiB inside a single 10s sample period, so any disk guard has to poll per second.

title: cappedByFMSuppression says 'capped to mark-only' and produces no banner — the orchestrator drops it
description:
Found while implementing [[playhead-y3ya]]. Same defect SHAPE as y3ya, different gate.

`SkipEligibilityGate.cappedByFMSuppression` documents itself as "FM noAds consensus
suppression: no strong proposal survived, **capped to mark-only**" and carries
`severity == 1`, the SAME severity as `.markOnly`. `AdDetectionService.runBackfill`
genuinely produces it (AdDetectionService.swift:5193) and `buildFusionAdWindow`
persists it into `ad_windows.eligibilityGate`.

`SkipOrchestrator.receiveAdWindows` then:
  * routes `decodedGate == .markOnly` to the suggest tier (SkipOrchestrator.swift:2895)
  * and DROPS everything else that decodes to a non-`.eligible` case at
    playhead-bq70's guard (SkipOrchestrator.swift:2993), stamping
    `ingest_dropped_blocked_gate` with `detail = "cappedByFMSuppression"`.

So a span the pipeline deliberately demoted to "banner only" produces NO banner. The
name, the doc comment and the severity all say mark-only; the surface says nothing.

This is the y3ya finding one gate over: a lane that computes a suggest-tier verdict
and then has it silently discarded at the door.

WHAT TO CHECK FIRST, because it may be intentional: `.cappedByFMSuppression` means an
FM `noAds` consensus fired over the span, i.e. the model actively said there is no ad
here. Banners for spans the model voted DOWN may be the wrong trade. But then the
gate is misnamed and the severity is wrong, and the honest fix is to rename it
(`suppressedByFMConsensus`) and give it severity 2 alongside the other blocked cases
— NOT to leave a gate whose name promises a surface it does not have.

Measure before deciding: playhead-isp5's census makes the population countable —
`ingest_dropped_blocked_gate:cappedByFMSuppression` in the
`ad_window_ingest_census` rows of a device pull.

ALSO NOTE the y3ya interaction: `BackfillJobRunner.swift:3645` persists an empty
pass-B refinement as `disposition = .noAds` with `transcriptQuality` HARDCODED to
`.good` (line 3644). `FMSuppressionGuard`'s guard 5 fires on 2+ overlapping `.noAds`
windows at `.moderate`+ certainty, and the band is derived as
`transcriptQuality == .good ? .moderate : .weak`. So a coarse `containsAd` whose
refinement merely failed to LOCALIZE the ad manufactures the negative consensus that
caps the region — the pipeline turning a failure to find edges into a vote that there
is no ad. Worth its own measurement.

## QUEUE — revised 2026-08-01, position 5 of 11

    isp5(done) -> b6r2(done) -> y3ya(done) -> lxkq -> avbn -> sik9 -> nqey -> 9v09 -> gard -> mptr -> hx6n

**The OTHER half of the same population, and it does active harm: an empty pass-B is relabelled .noAds with transcriptQuality hardcoded .good, FMSuppressionGuard fires on 2+ overlapping .noAds, and the surviving lexical/acoustic evidence is downweighted 0.3x. FM failing to LOCALIZE manufactures evidence of ABSENCE and suppresses the detectors that did find something.**

One at a time. No device build until the queue completes.

title: The inventory sanity filter rejects every pre-roll: rule (b) tooEarly kills any span starting inside the first 3 s
description:
Found by [[playhead-isp5]]'s instrumentation, and MEASURED rather than argued —
`theFieldPreRollIsDroppedByTheInventoryFilterAsTooEarly` reproduces it in 0.2 s.

## The rule

`InventorySanityFilter.evaluate` rule (b), head edge:

    if startTime < edgeMarginSeconds { return .rejected(reason: .tooEarly) }

`edgeMarginSeconds` is 3.0. **A pre-roll starts at 0.0.** So every pre-roll is
rejected at the `AdDetection -> SkipOrchestrator` boundary, before tier routing:
no auto-skip, no suggest banner, no mark. The tail edge is the same rule
mirrored (`endTime > duration - 3`), so post-rolls go the same way whenever
`activeEpisodeDuration` is known.

This is not one detector's problem. The filter runs at BOTH admission doors
(`receiveAdWindows` :2593 and `receiveAdDecisionResults`) plus the retroactive
`reapplyInventoryFilterToManagedWindows`, so it applies to day-0 rediff, the
hot path, the final-pass backfill and the cross-launch preload alike.

## Why it survived eleven weeks and two investigations

`SkipOrchestrator.init` defaults `inventoryFilter` to
`InventorySanityFilter(isEnabled: false)`. Production passes
`.production()`, which is ON (`LightweightInventoryChecksSettings.defaultEnabled
= true`, and Dan's 2026-07-31 wipe+reinstall left the key absent, so ON).

The init default's own comment states the hazard outright:

    // playhead-xr3t (review): default to a disabled no-op filter so
    // pre-existing test surface ... doesn't silently lose pre-roll/post-roll
    // spans to the head-/tail-edge rules.

The xr3t review KNEW the edge rules lose pre-rolls and post-rolls. The remedy
turned the filter off in the OBSERVATION surface and left it on in the field.
Consequence: [[playhead-djl0]]'s own reproduction of the 2026-08-01 D9B513CD
case — same asset, same four windows, same `start: 0, end: 45.1` — asserts
`banners.map(\.windowId) == ["d0-1"]` and PASSES, because its orchestrator has
the filter off. Every SkipOrchestrator suite inherits that default.

## Why xr3t's acceptance did not catch it

The bead's bar was "rejects >= 98% of SYNTHETICALLY INVALID spans", with
"spans in the first/last 3s of the episode" listed as one of the three
known-bad classes. Synthetic negatives only — the corpus never contained a real
pre-roll, so the premise was never tested against the population it excludes.
Note also the wording drift: the spec says spans IN the first 3 s (a sliver
pinned at the edge); the implementation rejects any span that STARTS there
(a 45-second pre-roll).

## The decision Dan owns

isp5 deliberately did NOT flip this. It changes AUTO-SKIP admission for every
detector, not only the banner, and it rewrites ~15 xr3t contract tests.
Options, cheapest first:

1. **Containment reading.** `tooEarly` iff `endTime <= edgeMargin`; `tooLate`
   iff `startTime >= duration - edgeMargin`. A [0, 45.1] pre-roll passes; a
   [0, 3.0] sliver still rejects, so the rule keeps a real job. Matches the
   spec's wording and Dan's standing ruling that OUTER edges are free
   (feedback_outer_edges_free_inner_precious, 2026-07-29).
2. **Drop the head/tail rules entirely.** Rule (a) (duration floor) already
   catches slivers; the tail rule's only genuinely-defective case is
   `endTime > episodeDuration`, which could be kept on its own.
3. **Leave the rule, flip the init default to match production** so at least
   the tests observe what the field does. Honest, and would have caught this in
   April, but it does not restore any pre-roll.

Whatever lands, the init default should stop diverging from production — that
divergence is the reason the loss was invisible.

## Verifying the fix

`AdWindowIngestOutcomeCountTests.theProductionFilterMovesExactlyThePreRoll`
measures the reach today: with the filter ON, exactly 1 of the 4 field windows
moves from `armedSuggest` to `droppedInventorySanity`. After a fix that number
is 0. On device, the isp5 census row names it directly:
`ingest_dropped_inventory_sanity:tooEarly=N`.
## QUEUE — inserted at position 2, 2026-08-01

    isp5(done) -> **b6r2** -> y3ya -> lxkq -> gard -> mptr -> hx6n

Promoted ahead of the FM work because it is cheap, it is on the magic path, and **it must land
before the next device build** — otherwise the dogfood pass shows no pre-roll banner again and
Dan's subjective read is taken on a build that structurally cannot surface the one detection that
already works (byte-exact rediff, measured 2 of 2 correct with a 2 s overshoot on a 60 s ad).

Note the interaction with what just shipped: [[playhead-isp5]] (#324) now names and durably records
this exact drop as `ingest_dropped_inventory_sanity:tooEarly=N` in the session file the device pull
reads. So after this lands, the fix is verifiable from a pull rather than from absence — and if
some OTHER guard is also eating pre-rolls, the census will say so instead of leaving a third
investigation.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED on bead/playhead-b6r2 (worktree .worktrees/b6r2). Option 1, applied
symmetrically, plus option 3 (the init default).

RULE (b) now reads the span's INNER edge:
    tooEarly iff endTime   <= edgeMargin
    tooLate  iff startTime >= duration - edgeMargin

MEASUREMENT THE BEAD DID NOT HAVE. The bead says post-rolls die "whenever
activeEpisodeDuration is known", but isp5's fixture builds its asset row WITHOUT
a duration, so the tail rule was dormant in the only harness that reproduced the
field session. Giving the row a duration puts both halves in one log line:

    AdWindow d0-1 rejected by inventory sanity filter: tooEarly
    AdWindow d0-4 rejected by inventory sanity filter: tooLate

So the reach is 2 of 4 windows per episode, not 1. Production reaches this state
on every episode (AnalysisCoordinator calls setEpisodeDuration immediately
before receiveAdWindows on both the hot path and the final pass).

OPTIONS 2 AND 3 REJECTED / FOLDED IN:
* Option 2 (drop the head/tail rules): rule (a) does NOT subsume them — it
  passes exactly 2.0 s, so [0, 2.0] and [598, 600] would become admissible
  auto-skip material. Its proposed keeper, `endTime > episodeDuration`, is the
  part to avoid: declared durations are approximate and day-0's measured
  overshoot on this show is ~2 s, so it reintroduces this bug by another door.
* Option 3 is INCLUDED, not discarded. The init default is now
  `InventorySanityFilter.productionDefaultConfiguration`, one static let bound
  to `LightweightInventoryChecksSettings.defaultEnabled`.

THE TAIL, HONESTLY. The old tail rule's protection against a show-eating span
was incidental, not a width guard: it keyed on the OUTER edge, so it rejected
[3928, 3930] and [0, 3930] alike while admitting [500, 3920] — 57 minutes of
show — because that span stops ten seconds early. The delta the fix admits is
exactly "spans longer than 3 s anchored to the episode end", which contains
every genuine post-roll. Only a WIDTH test separates a 30 s post-roll from a
57-minute one, and this filter has no ceiling by design. ADDING ONE IS A POLICY
DECISION FOR DAN (what is the widest legitimate ad break?) — filed here rather
than taken. The loss is pinned by a named test so it cannot resurface as a
surprise.

MUTATION BATTERY: B01-B07, batches 85-90, plus a re-run of batch 81 whose W02
expectation this bead re-pointed. 9 KILLED / 0 SURVIVED / 0 ERROR.

B01's issue list says something new: restoring the old head rule reddens FOUR
tests belonging to OTHER beads, including playhead-d3g0's "Pre-roll banners when
the playhead is AT 0:00". Those passed on main for eleven weeks while the
behaviour they describe was broken in the field — because the init default had
the filter off. They are reachable only now. That is option 3 measured: flipping
the default alone would have gone red in April.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
TAIL SAFETY — the right lever already exists and is NOT this filter.

While checking what protects show at the tail after the containment change, the
gate log surfaced playhead-wraj's POST-ROLL GUARD
(`FusionWeightConfig.postRollGuardSeconds`, default 90.0): an `.eligible` span
ending within 90 s of a KNOWN episode duration is demoted to `.markOnly` —
banner, never auto-skip — regardless of rediff anchoring or skipConfidence, with
NO rediff exemption. Its own doc gives Dan's reasoning verbatim: "post-roll ads
are the least important to auto-skip (the user just jumps to the next episode)
and a wrong skip near the end clips the host's closing content".

IT SHIPS OFF. `certaintyTieredSkipEnabled: false` in the production
`FusionWeightConfig` — "enablement is Dan's Gate-2 decision (2026-07-19
gate-delta measurement 32/32 at T=0.9 + 90s post-roll)".

So: the tail auto-skip risk this bead's change widens is exactly the risk wraj
was built for, it has already been measured, and it is one flag away. That is a
far better instrument than a width ceiling bolted onto the inventory sanity
filter, and it is already Dan's pending decision rather than a new one. Nothing
was changed here; recording it so the tail question is answered by the guard
designed for it.

Note the two are independent and both are needed: the inventory filter decides
ADMISSION (does the window exist at all — pre-b6r2 the answer was "no", so the
listener got no banner either), while the wraj guard decides the TIER of an
admitted tail window. Flipping wraj without b6r2 would still have shown Dan
nothing, because the post-roll never survived ingest.

title: FM budget must land likely-slot-first before play: it swept 0-2676s linearly and never reached the pod at 2838
description:
The other half of the mid-roll program. Sibling to [[playhead-y3ya]] (surfacing), which must land
first or this changes nothing Dan can hear.

## The measurement that motivates it

Episode DE0784D8, the one Dan corrected on 2026-08-01. FM's 42 `semantic_scan_results` rows cover
**0 - 2676 s, LINEARLY, front to back**, ending `2581-2676 | abstain | cancelled`.

**His missed pod is at 2838 - 2954 s. FM never reached it.**

It had roughly FIFTEEN HOURS between download and his listen, and spent the entire budget sweeping
the first 48% of the episode in episode order. Those 42 rows are also the **only**
`semantic_scan_results` rows in the whole device database — FM has partially scanned exactly one
episode, ever, on this phone.

So the mid-roll failure is, in measured order: **scheduling first, surfacing second
([[playhead-y3ya]]), FM capability a distant third.** "FM is 2.4x slower than realtime" is
currently a footnote to "FM essentially does not run".

## The arithmetic that makes this tractable

At 2.4x slower than realtime, FM covers ten 3-minute neighbourhoods in ~72 minutes of wall clock.
**That fits an overnight gap easily.** The 3.7-hour full-episode linear sweep does not. The budget
was never the problem; the ORDER was.

## The work

When a day-0/backfill scan plan is built for an episode with download-to-play headroom, order FM
windows by **ad-likelihood**, not episode order. The linear sweep becomes filler after the seeds
are exhausted.

Seeds, in rough priority:
  * **acoustic / stinger seam fragments** — the machinery already fires. On this very episode,
    fragments at 2667-2702 and **2828-2836** sat immediately at the missed pod's edge. DOAC has a
    known page-turn stinger at both ad edges. **The seam channel found the seams and the pipeline
    emitted them as junk verdicts instead of using them as pointers.** That is
    [[feedback_lexical_as_attention]] exactly: brittle signals say WHERE to look, never the
    verdict. A 6.7e-6-confidence fragment is a terrible answer and an excellent pointer.
  * position priors (mid-episode break structure), chapter cues
  * neighbourhoods of rediff-found slots (pod continuation already does the adjacent case; this is
    the wider sweep)

Machinery that already exists — reuse, do not rebuild: the `scanLikelyAdSlots` phase,
`CoveragePlanner.swift:386`, `TargetedWindowNarrower.swift:254`, `SpecialistScanPlanner.swift:119`.
The field episode nonetheless ran a linear `fullEpisodeScan`. Establish WHY the targeted phase did
not own that plan before writing new planning code.

## Dependencies and sequencing

1. **[[playhead-y3ya]] first.** Without surfacing, better targeting is invisible.
2. **Ride [[playhead-hx6n]] along with it** (V42 timestamp + scene phase on `semantic_scan_results`).
   Without it this change is UNMEASURABLE — scan rows carry no timestamp at all, and two separate
   investigations have already ended in "cannot be determined from device data".
3. Pull [[playhead-5lkz]] forward into this work: an unbounded usability probe can hang the
   serialized FM lane for 27 minutes, which is a direct timeliness hazard in the lane we are about
   to lean on.

## Acceptance

On the DE0784D8 fixture, the 2667/2828 seam fragments cause the **2800-2960 neighbourhood to be
scanned within the first N minutes of FM budget**, rather than at 3.7 hours. Measured on corpus as
**ad-seconds heard at first listen**, attributable by phase via hx6n's timestamps.

This absorbs [[playhead-j4wi]] work-item 3 and the download-time half of [[playhead-hp70]].
hp70's live-playback ordering is the FALLBACK lane — the before-play lane comes first, because
magic means the work is finished before he presses play
([[feedback_timely_and_magic_2026-08-01]]).
## QUEUE — Dan 2026-08-01, the mid-roll program

Position **3 of 6**:

    isp5 -> y3ya -> lxkq -> gard -> mptr -> hx6n

**The scheduling half. FM had 15 hours and swept 0-2676s linearly, never reaching the pod at 2838. Ten 3-minute neighbourhoods fit in ~72 min of budget; the order was the problem, not the budget.**

One at a time (16 GB box, one build slot). No device build until the queue completes, then ONE
build and one dogfood pass.
## QUEUE — revised 2026-08-01, position 4 of 9

    isp5(done) -> b6r2(done) -> y3ya -> lxkq -> sik9 -> nqey -> gard -> mptr -> hx6n

**The scheduling half. Also what gives the host-read confidence floor a real population, without which nqey's calibration is validated against nothing.**

One at a time. No device build until the queue completes, then ONE build and one dogfood pass.
## QUEUE — revised 2026-08-01, position 4 of 11

    isp5(done) -> b6r2(done) -> y3ya(done) -> lxkq -> avbn -> sik9 -> nqey -> 9v09 -> gard -> mptr -> hx6n

**The scheduling half of the mid-roll program. FM had 15 hours and swept 0-2676s linearly, never reaching the pod at 2838.**

title: A semantic containsAd verdict must surface as a suggest-tier candidate — FM found two ads on Dan's episode and both were discarded
description:
Dan, 2026-08-01: **"we already know that rediff isnt enough, it only catches half the ads."**
Correct — and the other half is not primarily an FM CAPABILITY problem. Measured today: FM already
found ads on his episode and they never reached him.

## The evidence (device DB, 2026-08-01)

Episode DE0784D8. `semantic_scan_results` says FM returned `containsAd` for:

    508 -  599 s   -> NO ad_window exists anywhere near it
   1604 - 1731 s   -> NO ad_window exists anywhere near it

A sweep-lane `containsAd` verdict dies unless fusion can attach it to a narrow seed. **Presence
without extent is discarded.** So on the one episode FM has ever partially scanned on this device,
it fired twice and produced zero user-visible output.

That is the detection portfolio's stated policy violated in the semantic lane: **any signal fires
-> banner** ([[feedback_detection_portfolio_belt_suspenders]]). Every other lane honours it. This
one silently drops.

## Why this bead comes BEFORE any targeting or prompt work

Pointing FM at better places (the sibling bead) changes nothing Dan can hear until a reached
verdict can surface. And no prompt/model/specialist work is measurable until there is a
scanned-and-surfaced path to measure through. **This is the gate on all FM investment.**

## The work

A semantic `containsAd` verdict must become a user-visible **suggest-tier / markOnly candidate**,
with a derived extent.

Decide the extent policy explicitly — this is the substance:
  * refine the coarse window with pass-B before emitting, where budget allows;
  * clip to seam/stinger/rediff edges **when available**, but **never REQUIRE them**. Hard
    boundaries CLIP FM edges, they must never GATE eligibility
    ([[feedback_fm_hostread_irreplaceable]]) — that inversion is what produced this bug;
  * where no anchor exists, emit the coarse window UNANCHORED. playhead-2350 then holds it at
    markOnly and playhead-ynmk makes a confirmation MARK rather than cut, so the downside is a
    banner, never lost show. That safety net already exists and is proven.

Route the result through the same markOnly/suggest path day-0 marks use — do not invent a second
surfacing path.

## Acceptance

On the DE0784D8 fixture, the 508-599 and 1604-1731 verdicts produce user-visible candidates.
And the negative: a verdict FM declined must still produce nothing.

Do NOT fix this by lowering a fusion threshold globally — that re-floods the surface with the
near-zero-confidence acoustic junk Dan vetoed five times on this same episode
(confidences 1.6e-3 down to 6.7e-6). The fix is that a SEMANTIC verdict has standing on its own,
not that everything does.
## QUEUE — Dan 2026-08-01, the mid-roll program

Position **2 of 6**:

    isp5 -> y3ya -> lxkq -> gard -> mptr -> hx6n

**Gates all FM investment. FM already found two ads on Dan's episode and both were discarded — better targeting is invisible until a reached verdict can surface.**

One at a time (16 GB box, one build slot). No device build until the queue completes, then ONE
build and one dogfood pass.
## QUEUE — revised 2026-08-01, position 3 of 9

    isp5(done) -> b6r2(done) -> y3ya -> lxkq -> sik9 -> nqey -> gard -> mptr -> hx6n

**Gates all FM investment — a containsAd verdict that cannot surface makes every later FM change unmeasurable.**

One at a time. No device build until the queue completes, then ONE build and one dogfood pass.
notes:
2026-08-01 IMPLEMENTATION (branch bead/playhead-y3ya): new pure `SemanticSweepMarkComposer`
(mirrors `SpecialistMarkComposer`) turns persisted `containsAd` rows into MARK-ONLY
`AdWindow`s routed through the existing markOnly/suggest path. EXTENT POLICY: (1) presence =
containsAd AND the status says the window was examined AND not a pz32 no-work sentinel;
(2) REFINE with an already-persisted passB row (the model's own narrowing, in seconds, zero
extra FM budget) — a DECLINED passB does NOT retract the coarse verdict, which matters because
BackfillJobRunner.swift:3645 persists an empty passB as `.noAds`; (3) MERGE within 2 s;
(4) CLIP to a PROVEN edge (non-`unanchored` AutoSkipEdgeAnchor — the same definition
SpanExtentSupport uses) within 20 s, NEVER required, and a clip never becomes an anchor CLAIM;
(5) DEDUPE — never emit over ANY existing window in ANY decisionState incl. `.reverted`, so the
producer is strictly additive to regions the pipeline left empty and cannot resurface a veto;
(6) EMIT markOnly/candidate/unanchored/content-addressed. Wired at TWO sites reading ONE flag:
runBackfill Step 18c (last among additive producers) and BackfillJobRunner.runJob's tail (the
TIMELY half — the field sweep spent 15 h writing rows with nothing re-fusing, and it ended
`cancelled`, so the tail runs on every path that reaches the return). Both additionally gated on
`canProposeNewRegions`, because ApprovedCohortRegistry collapses an unapproved cohort to
`.shadow` and surfacing shadow verdicts would defeat that protection. Registered in
`isLocalOnlyBoundaryState` (ALL-or-nothing gate — an omission aborts cross-user snapshots
silently, and unlike the two producers already listed there this one ships ON).
ADJACENT FINDING FILED: playhead-avbn — `.cappedByFMSuppression` is the same defect one gate
over (named "capped to mark-only", severity 1 == markOnly, dropped by bq70's guard so it
banners nothing); it also records the passB `.noAds` relabel + hardcoded `.good` quality that
turns "failed to localize" into an FMSuppressionGuard negative consensus.

title: Measured mid-roll hole: 116s of back-to-back ads undetected, with an 8s acoustic false positive right beside them
description:
The best-documented mid-roll miss we have: exact boundaries from Dan's own marks, an adjacent
failed acoustic fragment, and proof rediff had no purchase.

Dan, 2026-08-01: **"pre and post roll were excellent, mid roll was bad"**

## The episode: DE0784D8, 92 min (5522.65 s)

What the pipeline produced, and what he corrected at 11:23-11:26:

    POSITION    SPAN                 WIDTH   MECHANISM                RESULT
    pre-roll      0.0 -   60.1 s     60.1s   dayZeroRediffByteExact   EXCELLENT
                 (he vetoed 60.06-62.10, a 2.0 s overshoot = 3% on a 60 s ad)
    mid-roll   2828.4 - 2836.4 s      8.0s   acousticRefined conf 0.00  FALSE POSITIVE (vetoed)
    mid-roll   2838.2 - 2897.9 s     59.8s   *** NOTHING ***          MISSED (he marked it)
    mid-roll   2898.7 - 2953.7 s     55.0s   *** NOTHING ***          MISSED (he marked it)
    post-roll  5462.6 - 5522.7 s     60.1s   dayZeroRediffByteExact   EXCELLENT

**116 seconds of back-to-back ads at ~47 minutes, entirely undetected.** The only thing offered
anywhere near them was an 8 s acoustic fragment at confidence 0.00, immediately BEFORE the pod,
and it was wrong.

## Why this is NOT fixed by anything merged 2026-08-01

[[playhead-eks2]] (pod continuation ON) and [[playhead-evc1]] (a day-0 rediff mark may seed a pod
walk) recover the NEIGHBOURS of a found ad. **Here nothing was found in the pod at all.** Rediff's
two slots are the pre-roll and post-roll, ~2,700 s away; there is no byte-exact seed anywhere near
2838. Pod continuation with no seed recovers nothing, correctly.

This is the OTHER failure mode, and it is the dominant one:
  * eks2/evc1 fix: rediff finds ad 1 of a pod, ads 2-3 are missed  -> now recovered
  * THIS bead:     rediff finds NOTHING in the pod                 -> still 100% missed

Rediff is structurally blind here because it detects what CHANGED between two fetches. A mid-roll
that did not rotate between the A and B fetches is byte-identical and therefore invisible, no
matter how good rediff gets. See [[project_cross_network_dai_survey_2026-07-21]] — baked and
shared-stitch behaviours are exactly this.

## What this says about where detection actually stands

The position split is now measured, not inferred:

    OUTER edges (pre/post-roll, DAI, rotating)  -> byte-exact, ~2 s accuracy, EXCELLENT
    INNER (mid-roll, non-rotating or host-read) -> 0 detected of 116 s, plus a false positive

This is the FM-shaped hole. FM is the only mechanism that can find a non-rotating or host-read
mid-roll ([[feedback_fm_hostread_irreplaceable]]) — and it is measured at **2.4x slower than
realtime**, so it cannot serve a first listen ([[feedback_timely_and_magic_2026-08-01]]).

## Work

Not a fix — a CASE. Use it as a fixture and a target:
1. Freeze this episode's pod (2838.2-2953.7, two creatives, plus the 8 s acoustic false positive at
   2828.4) as a regression fixture. It has ground-truth boundaries from the owner.
2. Establish WHY the acoustic path fired 8 s at conf 0.00 right before a real 116 s pod but the pod
   itself produced nothing. An acoustic break detector that finds the seam and not the content is
   a clue about the seam-vs-span split, not just noise. Relevant: [[playhead-4xqf]]
   (boundary-undersizing), [[playhead-pggn]] (aggregator dilutes over a wider region than reported).
3. Decide whether an acoustic fragment adjacent to an unscanned region should TRIGGER a targeted FM
   scan of the neighbourhood, rather than being emitted as a candidate span on its own. That would
   convert a useless 8 s false positive into a pointer at 116 s of real ad — a much better use of
   the same signal ([[feedback_lexical_as_attention]]: brittle signals say WHERE to look, never the
   final determination).

Item 3 is the interesting one and may be cheap: the fragment was in the right PLACE and wrong about
everything else.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
ITEM 2 ESTABLISHED — why the acoustic path emitted 8s at conf 0.00 at the seam while the pod produced nothing. Walked the real code against the real device pull (2026-08-02 analysis.sqlite). Four mechanisms, each witnessed.

== 0. The span was never acoustic ==
buildFusionAdWindow HARDCODES boundaryState 'acousticRefined' for every fusion window (AdDetectionService.swift:8780). The real trigger was LEXICAL: EvidenceCatalogBuilder's disclosure regex \bin partnership with\b (EvidenceCatalogBuilder.swift:802) matched SHOW CONTENT — the fast-pass chunk 2828.40-2836.44 'work in partnership with the artificial intelligence, ...' (Ray Dalio talking about AI). Witnesses: correction_events DF39FEBF (causalSource='lexical', atomIds=[2551]); decoded_spans 49d909cc (atoms 2551-2551, anchorProvenance evidenceCatalog/disclosurePhrase/'in partnership with', firstTime 2828.77). The 8.04s geometry is EXACTLY that one ASR chunk's width — no acoustic snap ever moved the edges (feature_windows 2820-2960: musicBedLevelRaw 'background' throughout, bedChange 0.0-0.49 noise). 'An acoustic break detector that found the seam' is the wrong read: a chunk-width lexical span wearing an acoustic label.

== 1. What 0.00 means, and who reads it as a candidate ==
ad_windows.confidence for fusion windows stores DecisionResult.skipConfidence (AdDetectionService.swift:8779 'confidence: decision.skipConfidence'), NOT the detection confidence. Detection (proposal) was 0.456: decision_events 2026-08-01 00:42:34 shows proposalConfidence=0.45634516843301726, skipConfidence=0.0011507587713741739 for fusion-f8d4c169288e9a37. skipConfidence = calibrate(proposal) x correctionFactor, and correctionFactor is ASSET-SCOPED — 'Queried once per backfill run (not per span)' (AdDetectionService.swift:4592-4600): Dan's three 07-31 falsePositive vetoes at 210/2670/4800 (the mark-then-retract churn pairs) collapsed the blanket passthrough, nuking skipConfidence for EVERY span in the episode including this one 2600s away; <0.40 also forces gate=blockedByUserCorrection (BackfillEvidenceFusion.swift ~986-996). Then the emission: there is NO confidence floor on the fusion path, and policyAction detectOnly persists the window with decisionState CONFIRMED unconditionally (buildFusionAdWindow: 'logOnly and detectOnly: always confirmed'). So the row every reader sees is decisionState='confirmed' + confidence=0.00115 — the UI showed Dan a confirmed span labelled conf 0.00 and he had to veto it (his veto event embeds exactly that projection). ANSWER: 0.00 means 'the asset-wide correction blanket left ~zero permission to auto-skip', read by everyone downstream as 'detection confidence of a confirmed span'. What would it read if the thing it measures never happened? calibrate(0.456) — and indeed the same windows' skipConfidence churned 3.7e-07 -> 1.1e-05 -> 0.0043 -> 0.0044 across five decision_events runs with ZERO new evidence at 2828, purely as the blanket recomputed. All five fusion windows on this episode share the shape (6.7e-06 .. 0.0039) and ALL FIVE were false positives.

== 2. Why the pod (2838.18-2953.68) produced nothing ==
(a) FM: semantic pass A (shadow, fullEpisodeScan) covered 0-2676.06 in 42 windows and was CANCELLED (last row 2581.08-2676.06 status='cancelled'); the pod was never inside ANY semantic_scan_results window. 51.5% of the episode was never scanned.
(b) Rediff: structurally blind mid-roll (per the bead); its two byte-exact slots are 0-60.13 and 5462.57-EOF.
(c) Lexical — the decisive one: the pod's copy contains exactly ONE catalog-matchable string, 'go to ketone.com slash' (chunk 2940.84-2944.44). It MATCHES (\bgo to \w+\.com and \b\w+\.com\b) and anchors its atom — but the atom is 3.60s wide with unanchored neighbours, and MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder DROPS spans under minDurationSeconds=5 (DecodedSpan.swift:137, decoder step 5). The pod's only TRUE lexical anchor dies as a micro-fragment; the seam's FALSE anchor survives only because its host chunk happens to be 8.04s long. Same defect class again: span width measures 'how long the ASR chunk was', read as 'how much ad is here'. Creative 1 (WhisperFlow) matches NOTHING AT ALL: 'whisperflow.ai' — the URL patterns cover .com/.co/.org/.io, no .ai (EvidenceCatalogBuilder.swift:748-760); CTA is 'head to' but only 'head over to' is a pattern; disclosure is 'because of our sponsor called Whisper Flow' — not in the disclosure list.
(d) Hot-path classifier: zero candidate rows anywhere in this episode's ad_windows from the 0.40-threshold path (absence witness).
CONFIRMATION BY HASH: the wide decoded span 2551-2675 (2828.40-2958.96 — covering the ENTIRE pod) is a POST-MARK artifact, not a missed pre-mark detection: its content-addressed window id SHA256('asset=DE0784D8-...|version=detection-v1|start=2551|end=2675') = fusion-75c9b932f335720f, which first appears in decision_events at 15:26:51 — 47s AFTER Dan's second mark — because his falseNegative marks correction-anchored the atoms between seam and pod end. Pre-mark, the only span near the pod was the single-atom seam FP.

== Neighbors ==
4xqf (undersizing): different — nothing was emitted here to undersize. pggn (aggregator dilution): related in spirit; the asset-blanket correctionFactor is a distinct, per-ASSET mechanism — filed separately. 8x59 (acoustic promotion bar): would not have touched this FP — it was not acoustic and detectOnly persists regardless of any bar.

Fixture: DE0784D8MidRollPodRegressionTests reproduces mechanism (c) LIVE through the production catalog->projector->decoder path over the frozen transcript — exactly one 8.04s seam span decodes, the ketone.com anchor provably fires and dies at the 5s floor, and the pod yields nothing (known-hole assertions).

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
ITEM 3 RECOMMENDATION (decision is Dan's) — should an acoustic/lexical fragment adjacent to an UNSCANNED region trigger a targeted FM scan of the neighbourhood, instead of being emitted as a candidate span?

== What it would have done on THIS episode ==
The fragment was in the right place: it ends 1.74s before creative 1. The pod region was NEVER inside any semantic_scan_results window — pass A (shadow) covered 0-2676.06 and was cancelled; the pod starts 162s past the last window. So the trigger's firing condition ('fragment borders audio FM never scanned') is exactly the state this episode was in. A +/-150s neighbourhood window centred on the fragment covers 116 of the pod's 116 seconds.
Would FM have found it? The transcript there is complete and usable: fast-pass, avgConfidence 0.848 over 125 chunks in 2826-2954, and the copy is as explicit as host-read gets ('because of our sponsor called Whisper Flow' at 2841.7, 'whisperflow.ai slash Stephen' at 2894-2897, 'go to ketone.com slash Stephen ... 30% off your 1st subscription' at 2940-2948). On this same episode, with this same transcript quality, pass A returned containsAd certainty='strong' on 2 windows and 'moderate' on 1. Host-read is FM's irreplaceable job. High likelihood of a hit; not a certainty (FM recall on unseen shows plateaus 64-79%, but DOAC is not unseen).

== Cost, measured on THIS device from semantic_scan_results ==
1178.8 FM-seconds for 2097.2 audio-seconds scanned = 0.562 FM-s per audio-s (n=32 successful pass-A windows, 0 prewarm hits, avg window 63 audio-s, avg latency 36.8s, median ~10.9s, max 421s).
- +/-150s neighbourhood = ~300 audio-s = ~4-5 windows = ~169 FM-seconds (~2.8 min) at the measured rate.
- Tail risk: one 421s cold-window outlier exists in the sample; worst-case bound ~8 min.
- Timing vs magic: Dan hit the pod ~47 min into a first listen. A ~3-min targeted job triggered at day-0 (or even at listen start) finishes LONG before playhead 2838s. This is the rare FM job small enough to serve a first listen.

== Risk ==
1. FP-seeded pointing: on this episode, ALL FIVE fusion fragments were false positives (skipConfidence 6.7e-06..0.0039, every one vetoed or blocked). A trigger keyed on them buys FM time pointed at WRONG places on clean episodes. Bound it: fire only when the neighbourhood is UNSCANNED (the condition here), cap at N=2 neighbourhood scans/episode (~6 min FM ceiling), and count it against the episode's scan budget.
2. Consumption: pass A on this pull ran runMode='shadow'. A targeted scan only converts the 8s-junk signal into 116s of caught ad if its verdict can reach the mark/banner tier (or seed the eks2/evc1 pod walk — one containsAd inside creative 1 walks to creative 2). Without that, the trigger produces evidence nobody consumes.
3. Overlap with playhead-hp70 ('point FM at likely ad slots AHEAD of the playhead'): same family — hp70 is playhead-driven prioritization, this is evidence-driven prioritization of a coverage hole. If both land they should share the targeting machinery, not duplicate it.

== Recommendation ==
YES, worth building, bounded: fragment (any sub-emission-quality lexical/acoustic hit) + unscanned neighbourhood -> queue ONE targeted pass-A window set (+/-150s), budgeted, verdict feeding the banner/mark tier only (never auto-skip). It converts the exact signal that today costs a veto into a pointer at the dominant miss class, at ~3 min FM per firing on measured device numbers. The trigger population, neighbourhood width, per-episode cap, and consumption tier are the four knobs — all Dan's call. NOT implemented in this bead (item 3 is a write-up by design).

title: episode.podcast is nil, so a new show has no identity: no trust profile, no auto-skip, and no way to turn it on
description:
Dan, 2026-08-01, on the post-batch build: **"i now dont appear to have anyway to turn autoskip on
for a new show? it just says show unknown"**

He has lost the per-show auto-skip control entirely. That is a P0 on its own, but the pill is the
messenger, not the cause.

## The chain

`PlayheadRuntime.performPlayEpisode` (:3838):

    let podcastId = episode.podcast?.feedURL.absoluteString
    ...
    currentPodcastId  = podcastId          (:3875)
    currentPodcastTitle = episode.podcast?.title   (:3877)
    currentArtworkURL   = episode.podcast?.artworkURL (:3878)

**`episode.podcast` is nil** — a broken SwiftData relationship. One nil cascades into everything:

  * `currentPodcastId` nil -> `SkipOrchestrator.beginEpisode` cannot look up a trust profile ->
    `activeSkipMode = .shadow` -> **no auto-skip fires, ever, for this episode**
  * `setShowSkipMode` (:5037-5042) is `if let podcastId = currentPodcastId { ... }` — it SILENTLY
    SKIPS the persist when nil, so a menu would accept a choice and forget it
  * playhead-djl0 therefore correctly sets `isModeSelectable = false` and renders "Show Unknown"
    rather than offering a control that lies

## djl0 did NOT cause this — it EXPOSED it

Before djl0 the pill rendered only when `podcastTitle` was non-empty. The title comes from the SAME
nil relationship, so the one session that had something to say said nothing at all: the user saw a
missing pill and assumed normality. djl0 widened visibility precisely so this case is visible, and
on its first day in the field it surfaced a real, pre-existing defect. **Do not "fix" this by
reverting the pill.** The control being hidden is a symptom; restoring a menu that silently forgets
would be strictly worse and is the exact defect djl0 exists to close.

## What to find out first

**Why is `episode.podcast` nil?** For a NEWLY ADDED show this should be the trivial case. Candidates:
  a. the relationship is never set on insert for episodes arriving via one particular path (feed
     refresh vs. subscribe vs. background download) — note `DownloadManager.backgroundDownload`
     (:2169) has no context parameter at all, which is the same shape as the NULL `podcastId`
     column documented in [[playhead-isp5]] and [[playhead-kkzu]]
  b. the relationship exists but is not faulted in on the actor/context the runtime reads from
  c. the episode predates the podcast row (ordering on first subscribe)

Establish which with evidence before changing anything. (a) and (b) need very different fixes.

## The fix has two halves

1. **Make the identity resolve.** Fix the relationship at its source. If it cannot always be
   guaranteed, RECOVER it — playhead-djl0 already recovers a missing identity in
   `SkipOrchestrator.beginEpisode` from the durable `analysis_jobs` row; the same recovery belongs
   on `currentPodcastId` so the runtime, the menu and the trust lookup all see it.
2. **`setShowSkipMode` must never silently skip.** `if let ... { }` with no else is the arc's
   recurring defect in miniature. If the write cannot happen it must be a named, surfaced refusal —
   never a no-op that returns as if it worked.

## Acceptance

On a newly subscribed show, playing an episode shows the real skip-mode pill with a working menu,
and a chosen mode persists across relaunch. Verify on device — and verify the NEGATIVE too: an
episode that genuinely has no show still shows "Show Unknown" and still refuses the write loudly.

Related: [[playhead-isp5]] (banner still unexplained), [[playhead-gard]] (trust is per-show and
global across detectors), [[playhead-djl0]] (#317, the surfacing that revealed this).
## TWO CORRECTIONS FROM DAN, 2026-08-01 — both change this bead

### 1. It is NOT a new show

> "its not a brand new show it was a show i had downloaded several eipsodes if"

**Candidate (c) — "the episode predates the podcast row (ordering on first subscribe)" — is
effectively OUT.** The show already existed and already had several episodes downloaded. So the
relationship is breaking for episodes of an ESTABLISHED show, which points hard at the path that
created THOSE episode rows, not at subscribe ordering.

Re-weighted candidates:
  a. **(now primary)** the relationship is not set for episodes arriving via one specific path.
     `DownloadManager.backgroundDownload` (:2169) has no context parameter at all — the same shape
     as the NULL `podcastId` column in [[playhead-isp5]] / [[playhead-kkzu]]. Feed refresh
     (`BackgroundFeedRefreshService:993`) is the other suspect.
  b. the relationship exists but is not faulted in on the actor/context the runtime reads from —
     would present identically and needs a completely different fix. **Distinguish (a) from (b)
     before writing code**: (a) is a missing write, (b) is a read on the wrong context.

Useful discriminator: does the SAME show render correctly for an episode added by a DIFFERENT path
(e.g. an explicit tap-download vs. an auto/background download)? If yes it is (a) and the path is
named.

### 2. Hiding the control is NOT acceptable right now — Dan

> "thats only ok when detection gets good enough"

This overrides the framing above. I argued the hidden menu was correct because the write would
silently fail. Dan's point is sharper and it wins: **the per-show auto-skip toggle is his lever
precisely BECAUSE detection is unreliable.** Removing it while detection is weak takes away the
only manual control he has over the feature's core behaviour. "Correctly hidden" is not an
acceptable end state at the current detection quality — see
[[feedback_timely_and_magic_2026-08-01]] ("right now its no where near good enough").

So the ordering is:
  1. **Make the identity resolve so the menu works.** This is the whole bead. Not "hide it well."
  2. If an identity genuinely cannot be resolved for some episode, THEN the refusal must be loud
     (never a silent no-op in `setShowSkipMode`) — but that is the rare tail, not the state Dan is
     in with an established show.

Do NOT close this bead with the pill improved and the control still absent.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND — and it is NOT `episode.podcast == nil`. Correcting the bead.

## The hypothesis is ruled out by three independent facts

1. **One creation path, and it always sets the relationship.** The only production
   `Episode(...)` construction in the app is `PodcastDiscoveryService.persist`
   (:320-330) and it passes `podcast: podcast`. There is no other write to
   `episode.podcast` anywhere in `Playhead/` (only `Podcast.swift:203`, the init).
   Nothing ever assigns nil. So candidate (a) has no ORIGINATION mechanism.
2. **A showless episode cannot be tapped.** `EpisodeListView`'s `@Query` filters on
   `episode.podcast?.persistentModelID == podcastID` (:90-96). An episode with a
   NULL relationship is not rendered in the library at all.
3. **The NULL `analysis_jobs.podcastId` is a different producer.** That column is
   written by `AnalysisWorkScheduler.enqueue` from `context?.podcastId`, and
   `DownloadContext` is constructed at exactly ONE site in the tree. It is
   [[playhead-kkzu]], already filed. On the fresh post-wipe device pull
   (2026-08-01 11:07) it is NULL for **13 of 13** job rows — while
   `podcast_profiles` in the SAME database carries real feed URLs for both shows
   (`feeds.simplecast.com/dHoohVNH` mode=auto, `rss2.flightcast.com/...`
   mode=manual). The app knows the show identity perfectly well.

Candidate (b) has no mechanism either: single container, single `mainContext`,
`@MainActor` runtime, no `@ModelActor` in the app target.

## What it actually is: a one-shot read of a value that is not ready yet

`EpisodeListView.playEpisode` (:369-375):

    selectedEpisode = episode
    Task { await runtime.playEpisode(episode) }   // async
    navigateToNowPlaying = true                   // presents Now Playing NOW

Now Playing appears in the SAME turn. Its `onAppear` called
`viewModel.loadSkipMode(...)` exactly once. Meanwhile `performPlayEpisode` calls
`clearPriorEpisodePlaybackStateBeforeReplacement` -> `skipOrchestrator.endEpisode()`
EARLY, which installs `.shadow` / `.noActiveEpisode`, and only reaches
`beginEpisode` — the one thing that resolves the show — after `playbackService.load`,
`play()`, and `analysisCoordinator.handlePlaybackEvent`.

So the single read reliably observed the CLEARED pair.
`SkipModeResolution.noActiveEpisode.hasResolvedShowIdentity == false`, which is
exactly what djl0's pill renders as "Show Unknown" with `isModeSelectable = false`.
For a show whose identity resolves perfectly.

The podcast TITLE never showed this because `syncMetadata()` re-reads it on every
playback state event. Two facts about the same show on two cadences: one correct,
one frozen before the answer existed. Pre-djl0 the same staleness rendered a
plausible-looking "Shadow" pill, which is why nobody noticed for months.

## Corroboration from the device DB

`podcast_profiles` for `feeds.simplecast.com/dHoohVNH` reads
`mode=auto, observationCount=0, skipTrustScore=0.30000000000000004,
recentFalseSkipSignals=0`. Promotion to `auto` requires >=8 observations, so this
can only be `setUserOverride` — whose ONLY caller is
`PlayheadRuntime.setShowSkipMode`, i.e. the Now Playing menu. And 0.5 -> 0.4 ->
0.30000000000000004 is exactly two `falseSignalPenalty` decrements from
`setUserOverride`'s create default. So the menu HAS worked since the wipe — when
Now Playing is opened LATER (from the mini player, after `beginEpisode` landed),
the one-shot read gets the right answer. It only fails when the screen is opened
BY starting playback, which is the common flow. That asymmetry is the discriminator.

## Fix

- `SkipOrchestrator` publishes a `SkipModeSnapshot` (mode + cause) at every
  transition and replays the current pair on attach; the view model subscribes for
  as long as the screen is mounted.
- `Episode.resolvedShowIdentity` recovers the show from the ROW: `canonicalEpisodeKey`
  is `feedURL + "::" + feedItemGUID` and the row carries its own guid, so stripping
  that exact suffix returns the exact feed URL — byte-identical to the
  relationship's value, and immune to a `::` inside either half.
- The identity djl0 recovers inside `beginEpisode` is carried BACK to
  `currentPodcastId`. One direction of recovery is not a recovery: djl0 left the
  orchestrator holding a show (so the pill offered the menu) while the runtime's
  write target was nil.
- `setShowSkipMode` returns a named outcome, counts the refusal, and writes
  `skip_mode_write_refused_no_show_identity` to the diagnostics session file. The
  surface withdraws its optimistic `.sessionOverride` when the write is refused.

NOTE for [[playhead-kkzu]]: `analysis_jobs.podcastId` being NULL 13/13 in the field
means djl0's `recoverShowIdentity` (which reads that column) is a dead letter in
practice. The episode-key derivation added here is the recovery that actually fires.

comments.text:

- Full gate (`scripts/fast-gate.sh`, PlayheadFastTests): exit 65,

  (33-72 flakes >= 110 s, 0 XCTest). Five of the 43 were mine on the first run —

  machine but runs ~3 minutes under the gate's 10,000-test concurrency, blowing

  writes dropped, limits raised to 5 minutes of headroom.

## Known transient, NOT fixed (a deliberate scope call)

Between `endEpisode()` and `beginEpisode` — roughly the transport-load window —
the pill now reads "Show Unknown" for a second or two before flipping to the
real mode, because the podcast TITLE is published early and `.noActiveEpisode`
is the honest state until the show is resolved. Previously that state was

The obvious suppression (hide the pill entirely while `.noActiveEpisode`) is NOT

without the other would leave them inconsistent. Out of scope here.

title: A day-0 byte-exact rediff mark cannot seed a pod-continuation chain — it is .candidate, and seedDecisionStates is {confirmed, applied}
description:
Found while implementing [[playhead-eks2]] (the pod-continuation flip), and it is the reason
that flip does NOT address the field case that motivated it.

## The mechanism

`AdDetectionService.mintByteExactDayZeroMarks` persists every day-0 byte-exact rediff slot with
`decisionState: AdDecisionState.candidate` (AdDetectionService.swift:11469) — confidence 1.00,
`boundaryState = dayZeroRediffByteExact`, both edge anchors `.rediffByteExact` on a strict slot.

`AdPodContinuation.seedDecisionStates` is `{confirmed, applied}` (AdPodContinuation.swift:272).
So `isSeed` refuses a day-0 rediff row, and a pod whose only detected ad came from day-0 rediff
produces ZERO continuation marks.

## Why this matters exactly here

Dan's field pod, episode D9B513CD (2026-08-01), is that population verbatim:

    day-0 rediff FOUND    0.0 -  45.1 s   (ad 1)   conf 1.00
    day-0 rediff MISSED  47.6 -  94.3 s   (ad 2)   he marked it by hand

With `podContinuationEnabled` ON, composing over that exact state recovers 0.0 s. Changing ONLY
the seed row's `decisionState` to `.confirmed` — same geometry, same confidence, same provenance,
same links, same barriers — recovers essentially all of ad 2 and stops at the show boundary.
Both arms are pinned in
`AdPodContinuationFlipTests.dayZeroRediffMarkCannotSeedAContinuationChain`.

## Why the exclusion looks accidental rather than intended

`seedDecisionStates`' own doc justifies excluding `.candidate` as "the segment aggregator tiles
fixed 30 s regions as candidates, and chaining off an unconfirmed tile would build a pod claim on
a guess". That rationale is about a coarse proposal. A day-0 byte-exact rediff slot is the
opposite: byte-derived (the origin served DIFFERENT BYTES over that range), confidence 1.00,
`.rediffByteExact` on both edges.

And `AdPodContinuation.userOwnedBoundaryStates` already carries a note saying the FIRST
implementation reused `reconcileProtectedBoundaryStates`, which contains `dayZeroRediffByteExact`,
and that doing so "silently refused to seed from exactly the best seed" — calling a day-0 rediff
row "the most obviously correct thing to chain a pod walk off". The author fixed that filter and
the decisionState filter still blocks the same row through a different door.

## Candidate fix (NOT applied — this is a detection-policy change, Dan's call)

Widen `isSeed` to admit a row that is byte-derived rather than merely `.candidate`, e.g.

    boundaryState == AdDetectionService.dayZeroRediffByteExactBoundaryState
      && startEdgeAnchor == AutoSkipEdgeAnchor.rediffByteExact.rawValue
      && endEdgeAnchor   == AutoSkipEdgeAnchor.rediffByteExact.rawValue

restricted to the STRICT (anchored) arm so 9s6q segment-recovered slots — which keep
`.unanchored` precisely because their boundaries are not yet validated — stay out.

## What must be measured before flipping it

- The corpus dump (`playhead-dogfood-diagnostics-pipeline-dump-new9.json`) carries ONLY
  `confirmed`/`eligible` windows (132 of 132), so `AdPodContinuationCorpusEvalTests` says nothing
  about this population and would report an IDENTICAL number before and after. The measurement
  must come from a lane that has day-0 rows — the device lane
  (`AdPodContinuationDeviceLaneTests`, `PLAYHEAD_POD_DEVICE_LANE`) or a fresh device pull.
- The output stays mark-only/candidate/unanchored, so the downside is still a wrong BANNER
  (playhead-2350 and ynmk both hold) — but a day-0 slot sits at a pod EDGE, so the walk direction
  matters: an outer edge is free, an inner edge eats show.
## PROMOTED 2026-08-01 — P1 -> P0, and it moves AHEAD of playhead-kvs8

playhead-eks2 (#319) merged and the flip is live, but **it does not recover Dan's ad 2** — this
bead is why. The eks2 agent isolated it two-armed through the production link/barrier
derivation: same window, same 1.00 confidence, same provenance, same links and barriers, only
`decisionState` differing.

    .candidate  ->  0.0 s recovered
    .confirmed  ->  [45.1, 94.3) — ALL of ad 2 plus the 2.5 s stitch gap,
                    terminating exactly at the show boundary

**The mechanism is correct and precise. It simply cannot see the one row type that found the
ad.** `mintByteExactDayZeroMarks` writes `.candidate` (AdDetectionService.swift:11469);
`AdPodContinuation.seedDecisionStates` is `{confirmed, applied}` (AdPodContinuation.swift:272-275).

Why this outranks [[playhead-kvs8]]: Dan's standard is **"the app must feel almost like magic",
and magic means the work is done before he presses play**
([[feedback_timely_and_magic_2026-08-01]]). Day-0 rediff + pod continuation is the ONLY path that
marks a whole break in the first seconds of a first listen. kvs8 is background FM deepening —
real, but it cannot serve a timely first listen at 2.4x slower than realtime. This bead is the
one that turns "we found ad 1 and you heard ad 2" into "the break is covered."

## Field case it must satisfy

Episode D9B513CD, ground truth = Dan's own marks:
    day-0 rediff found  0.0 -  45.1 s  (ad 1, .candidate, markOnly, unanchored)
    Dan marked         47.6 -  94.3 s  (ad 2 — nothing detected it)
With the carve-out, ad 2 must be MARKED. Output stays mark-only/candidate/unanchored, so 2350
and ynmk still forbid it from cutting anything.

## What must be measured before it ships (the eks2 agent's own caution — honour it)

The corpus A/B could NOT have caught this: the existing dump is 132 of 132 `confirmed`/`eligible`
windows with **zero day-0 rows**. So the current lane cannot evaluate the change either.
**Build/obtain a lane containing day-0 rediff rows**, or state plainly that the evidence is the
field case plus the bounded downside and let Dan decide — do not fabricate a measurement.

Note the exclusion looks ACCIDENTAL, which is evidence for the carve-out: the doc justifies
excluding `.candidate` because "the aggregator tiles fixed 30 s regions as candidates" — a
statement about the AGGREGATOR, not about byte-exact rediff. And `userOwnedBoundaryStates`
already carries a note calling a day-0 rediff row "the most obviously correct thing to chain a
pod walk off". The same row was fixed through one door and still blocked through this one.

Carve the exception on PROVENANCE (byte-exact day-0 rediff), not by admitting `.candidate`
wholesale — the aggregator's 30 s candidate tiles are exactly what the original filter was right
to exclude, and Dan's aggregator went 0-for-3 in the field.

title: Still unexplained: no suggest banner for four markOnly day-0 windows with the playhead inside one (shadow ELIMINATED)
description:
Carries forward the ONE unresolved question from [[playhead-djl0]] (closed #317). djl0's shipped
work — naming/counting/surfacing the five facts `.shadow` was conflating — was correct and
complete on its own merits. **Its leading hypothesis, which I wrote, was REFUTED.** This bead is
the symptom, with the eliminations banked so nobody re-walks them.

## The symptom (Dan's device, 2026-08-01 03:20, post-batch build)

Played D9B513CD (Conan, 65.5 min). Day-0 rediff fired 14 s in and WORKED: 4 divergent slots,
4 marks, 120.3 MB, all persisted at confidence 1.00, `eligibilityGate = markOnly`. The first
window is the pre-roll, 0.0 - 45.1 s, and the playhead was INSIDE it when the mint landed.

**No skip, no banner. He heard the ad.**

The absent SKIP is fully explained (slots were non-strict so qs0d correctly left them markOnly;
markOnly never auto-skips). **The absent BANNER is not.**

## ELIMINATED — do not re-investigate

1. **Shadow mode.** `.shadow` does NOT gate the suggest tier. `activeSkipMode` is read at exactly
   five sites, ALL on the managed auto-skip tier (:5703 audit gate, :5750/:5755 accessors, :6061
   `.auto` promotion, :6071 skip-decision switch). The suggest path — `receiveAdWindows`'
   markOnly branch (:2464), `registerSuggestedWindow` (:1237),
   `emitSuggestBannersOnPlayheadEntry` (:1292), `updatePlayheadTime` (:2949) — never consults it.
   Independently re-verified: zero `activeSkipMode` references in either function body. Pinned by
   a parameterized test across all three modes (djl0).
2. **The podcastId NULL as evidence.** Different producer from the runtime local: runtime reads
   `episode.podcast?.feedURL` (`PlayheadRuntime:3730`); the column is written by
   `AnalysisWorkScheduler.enqueue(podcastId:)` from `context?.podcastId`, and
   `DownloadManager.backgroundDownload` (:2169) has no context parameter at all. A NULL there is
   fully explained by the download path, not by a nil relationship. See [[playhead-kkzu]].
3. **markOnly routing.** markOnly DOES route to the suggest tier (:2464).
4. **d3g0's entry gate.** Emission is CONTAINMENT (`time >= start && time < end`), not a
   transition — a window armed while the playhead is already inside fires on the next 0.25 s
   tick. Not the bug.
5. **`applyManualSkip` and mode.** It never consults `activeSkipMode`, so Dan's `.applied` user
   mark neither confirms nor refutes anything.

## THE REMAINING CANDIDATE

**Did `ingestPersistedAdWindows` actually run for this mint, with the played asset active?**
playhead-96ot gates on `activeAssetId` read inside the actor and logs its own drop path
(SkipOrchestrator.swift:1936, "ingestPersistedAdWindows: dropping mismatched asset ..."). If the
ingest never fired or dropped, the windows were never handed to the orchestrator, never armed,
and no banner is the correct downstream consequence of an upstream miss.

Everything downstream of the ingest is now PROVEN mode-independent, which is what makes this the
only live candidate.

## How to get the witness — it is a LOG LINE, not a table

The DB cannot show whether an in-actor call happened. Options:
- `log show --predicate 'subsystem == "com.playhead"' --start '<t>' --style compact` on device,
  or a sysdiagnose pull.
- **Cheaper: repeat the test on the NEXT build.** djl0 (#317) added coded entries
  (`skip_mode_show_identity_unresolved` / `skip_mode_trust_lookup_failed`) to the
  `SurfaceStatusInvariantLogger` session file that the device pull ALREADY reads — so the next
  dogfood pass yields file-based evidence for the mode half without a log pull, and 96ot's drop
  line is the one thing still needing os_log.

Do NOT theorise further ahead of the witness. Every wrong root cause in this arc — including
mine on djl0 — came from reasoning past the available evidence.
## QUEUE — Dan 2026-08-01, the mid-roll program

Position **1 of 6**:

    isp5 -> y3ya -> lxkq -> gard -> mptr -> hx6n

**Cheapest item, and the fresh build makes NOW the one moment to catch it. If ingest drops windows, all 15 merges are invisible in the field and every later measurement is garbage.**

One at a time (16 GB box, one build slot). No device build until the queue completes, then ONE
build and one dogfood pass.
notes:
## RESOLVED 2026-08-01 — cause FOUND and instrumented, both halves shipped

**The banner was absent because the pre-roll never reached either tier.**
playhead-xr3t's `InventorySanityFilter` rejected it as `.tooEarly` — rule (b)
rejects any span starting inside the first 3 s of the episode, and the field
pre-roll is 0.0-45.1 s. The filter runs at :2593 in `receiveAdWindows`, BEFORE
the markOnly branch that routes to the suggest tier, so the window was retired
rather than armed. Measured, not inferred:
`theFieldPreRollIsDroppedByTheInventoryFilterAsTooEarly` reproduces it.

The policy fix is [[playhead-b6r2]] (P0) — deliberately NOT flipped here,
because it changes auto-skip admission for every detector and rewrites ~15 xr3t
contract tests.

### The four remaining candidates, all now answered

1. **Did the ingest run?** YES, and this is no longer inferable-only: the
   not-playing drop writes a durable `ad_window_ingest_census` row.
2. **Now Playing host attach / `replayPendingSuggestBanners`.** Not reached —
   the window was dropped upstream of arming, so replay had nothing to withhold.
3. **`banneredWindowIds`.** Not it; the ids were fresh UUIDs from the mint.
   Now named as `ingest_dropped_already_bannered` if it ever is.
4. What the instrumentation revealed: (1).

### Why two investigations missed it

`SkipOrchestrator.init` defaults `inventoryFilter` to
`InventorySanityFilter(isEnabled: false)` while production wires
`.production()` (ON). djl0's own reproduction of THIS field case — same asset,
same `start: 0, end: 45.1` — asserts the banner IS emitted, and passes, because
its orchestrator has the filter off. The init default's comment says the
head-/tail-edge rules "silently lose pre-roll/post-roll spans" in as many words.

### What shipped

`AdWindowIngestOutcome` — 20 named dispositions, process-lifetime counts, one
`ad_window_ingest_census` row per delivery in the `SurfaceStatusInvariantLogger`
session file the device pull already reads (djl0's channel, v7q6's rule that the
durable row IS the audit trail). Retrievable as e.g.
`door=mid_session_ingest asset=<id> forwarded=4 delivered=3 ingest_armed_suggest=3
ingest_dropped_inventory_sanity=1 ingest_dropped_inventory_sanity:tooEarly=1`.

One deliberate silence: an empty-store preload counts but writes no row
(`beginEpisode` runs per episode start; an episode with no windows cannot have
lost one). Pinned by `aPreloadThatReadNothingWritesNoRow` + rail W07.

19 tests / 5 suites; mutation rails W01-W07 in batches 81-84, all KILLED.
