comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
PR #335. ROOT CAUSE: not a 45-minute bound — none exists (searched 2700, 45*60, .minutes(45), all N*60 constants). 2700.000 is the asset's STORED watermark re-read five times (emitTranscriptionTimeoutJournal reads fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime), and it is round because defaultShardDuration = 30 and the watermark tracks shard ends: 2700 = 90 x 30.

The bug: AnalysisJobRunner caps the transcription stage at a flat 300s (unconditional Task.sleep, not an inactivity watchdog), and runTranscriptionLoop re-transcribed the covered prefix first because transcribeShard dedups AFTER running ASR. 90 shards of already-bought audio before reaching shard 91 => zero chunks, frozen watermark, engine_silent_timeout. Self-reinforcing: every second of coverage earned makes the next run more expensive, so past a crossing point the episode is stranded forever.

FIX: order, do not filter — unread audio first, covered audio still runs after. The first shape SKIPPED covered shards; the gate proved that deletes the speakerId/avgConfidence upgrade path (2 NEW failures + host crash), so it was reworked. A wrong answer from the artifact test now costs latency, never coverage.

WATCH ITEMS: (1) y8f3 capRetry mints CORRECTLY by construction (cap terminal, ordinal 1, 1h cooldown, ladder next rung 3929.9) — NO GAP — but was futile: it re-ran into the same wall. Scheduling remedy vs compute-budget defect. (2) Same offset five times = one frozen watermark, answered. (3) se2h journal expected EMPTY, and that rules out the model-load path: any non-ready outcome emits speech_engine_not_ready, which classifies engine_reported, not engine_silent_timeout.

VERIFY: lint clean; full gate RED (24 known / 14 NEW), all 14 at 174-207s in known load-sensitive families, 0 XCTest failures, none in changed area, did NOT accept-baseline (that is o89d). Mutation battery K2 series 10/10 KILLED, 0 survived.

EVIDENCE CAVEAT: the 2026-08-01 03:37 pull is NOT on this box (newest is 2026-07-22, zero engine_silent_timeout rows, no D9B513CD). Field row read only as quoted in the bead; no field numbers invented.

title: Day-0 rediff at download time: verify the existing trigger post-ewag, and decide the auto-download bandwidth policy
description:
From Dan 2026-08-01: "why cant rediff happen quickly in background or after first download".

## What exists (and why he has never seen it work)

Download-time day-0 ALREADY SHIPPED: `kickOffDayZeroRediffForPreparation`
(PlayheadRuntime.swift:3653, xsdz.36.4) fires on the "Download & Analyze" tap, WiFi-gated, no
charging needed. Its detached task WAITS (bounded) for the pinned file AND the registered
analysis asset, then gives up silently ("the lagged sweep is the backstop").

**On the pre-ewag build the analysis-asset row was exactly what never materialized** — dispatch
was frozen, so the wait expired and the trigger died silently for every download. Field
evidence 2026-07-31: 5 downloads, 5 completed files, ONE asset row (the played episode), zero
day-0 attempts for the other four. Post-ewag (#310) the asset registers in seconds, so the
existing trigger should now actually fire.

## Work

1. VERIFY on device that a fresh Download & Analyze now produces a
   `rediff_day_zero_attempts` row within ~a minute of download completion, no playback needed.
   (Candidate: whichever new episode is downloaded next; 48E903D7 if it arrived via the tap.)
2. DECIDE (Dan, bandwidth policy): extend day-0 to PLAIN/AUTO background downloads, not just
   the explicit tap. Cost: ~120-250 MB re-fetch per episode (measured 120.3-131.8 MB per
   attempt), for episodes that may never be played. The rediff_bandwidth_ledger already exists;
   proposal = WiFi-only + daily byte budget + newest-episode-first, and the day-0 k-way floor
   (>=2 distinct-persona B-copies) unchanged.
3. Whatever is decided, the give-up path must stop being silent — a day-0 trigger that expires
   waiting for its preconditions should count and surface, same bound as everything in this arc.

Payoff: marks exist BEFORE first listen, so the first-listen experience stops depending on the
19-second in-play race entirely. Combined with [[playhead-eks2]] the whole pod is marked before
the user presses play.
## DECIDED — Dan 2026-08-01

> "yes rediff on background. wifi vs 5g should be a user setting, most people have unlimited
> bandwidth."

1. **Day-0 rediff runs on plain/auto background downloads**, not just the explicit
   "Download & Analyze" tap. Marks exist BEFORE first listen; the 19-second in-play race stops
   being the thing the experience depends on.
2. **Cellular vs WiFi becomes a USER SETTING**, not a hardcoded WiFi-only policy. Dan's
   reasoning: most people have unlimited data. The current gate ("WiFi only, or the deep-scan
   opt-in", RediffActivation.swift:95) is replaced by the preference.

### Sub-decisions NOT covered by the above — my recommendations, overrule freely

- **Default value**: ship default = **WiFi only**, with the setting surfaced plainly (Settings,
  and worth a line at first download). Rationale: Dan is right about the population, but the
  cost of a wrong default is asymmetric — a metered user silently loses ~200 MB per episode
  before they ever find the toggle, and that is the kind of thing that earns a one-star review
  and an App Store data-usage complaint. A user with unlimited data flips it once, costlessly.
- **Always respect iOS Low Data Mode**, on both transports, regardless of the setting. That is
  the user's OS-level instruction and overriding it is never defensible.
- **Keep the daily byte budget** in the rediff_bandwidth_ledger under BOTH transports — the
  setting governs *which network*, the ledger governs *how much*. They are different questions
  and one must not silently become the other.
- Newest-episode-first ordering when the budget is contended.
## PROMOTED 2026-08-01 — P1 -> P0, queue position 2

Dan: **"detection and analysis also beeds to be timely. the app must feel almost like magic"**

This bead is the single biggest lever on that. Everything else in flight fixes why detection did
not SURFACE; this is what makes it EARLY. Magic means the marks exist before he presses play —
not a 19-second race during the first listen while the pre-roll is already playing.

New order: `djl0` -> **`4dqe`** -> `eks2` -> `kvs8`. djl0 stays first because without it nothing
surfaces no matter how early it is computed.

See [[feedback_timely_and_magic_2026-08-01]].
## INVESTIGATION FINDINGS 2026-08-01 — several CONTRADICT the scope as written

Established by reading the code, independent of who implements. Where these disagree with the
scope above, **these win**.

1. **"Keep the daily byte budget in `rediff_bandwidth_ledger`" — THERE IS NO BUDGET TO KEEP.**
   Pre-4dqe that table is a pure cumulative ACCUMULATOR (7 counters + `lastUpdatedAt`,
   `AnalysisStore.swift:5280`), written after the fact and read by nothing that decides
   anything. The only bound on day-0 bytes is `DayZeroRediffAttemptPolicy.maxAttempts = 3`
   **per asset**, which bounds replays of ONE episode and says nothing about a library-wide
   daily total. **The budget must be BUILT, not kept.** My scope wording was wrong.

2. **`RediffActivation.swift:95` is only a DOC COMMENT.** The real gate is
   `DayZeroRediffGate.allows` at `DayZeroRediffTrigger.swift:36-55`.

3. **A gate-only change cannot work — there is a SECOND, HARDCODED WiFi gate at the socket.**
   `RediffFetchRequest.makeBaseRequest` sets `request.allowsCellularAccess = false`
   (`RediffRefetchSeams.swift:458`), and `makeWiFiOnlySession()` sets
   `config.allowsCellularAccess = false` plus `allowsExpensiveNetworkAccess = false` (~:506).
   **Session config is a CEILING a request cannot lift.** Flipping only the policy would let the
   decision pass and the socket refuse — recorded as `.fetchFailed`, burning one of the three
   per-asset attempts and MISREPORTING THE CAUSE. Classic instance of the arc's defect.

4. **Day-0 needs its own fetcher, or the LAGGED SWEEP goes cellular too.**
   `RediffRefetchService` holds ONE `fullFetcher` shared by the lagged BGTask sweep and
   `runDayZeroRefetch`, and the lagged sweep's WiFi-only-ness is enforced SOLELY by that session
   flag (stated at `RediffRefetchSeams.swift:474`). Making it cellular-capable silently puts the
   library-wide lagged sweep on cellular — far beyond what this bead authorises.

5. **The TRANSPORT refusal is silent too, not just the readiness give-up.**
   `triggerIfEligible` (`DayZeroRediffTrigger.swift:183-190`) does
   `guard DayZeroRediffGate.allows(...) else { return SweepSummary() }` — no record, no counter,
   no log. Scope item 4 named only the readiness wait; this has the identical defect and needs
   the same treatment.

6. **The give-up record CANNOT live in `rediff_day_zero_attempts`.** That table is keyed
   `analysisAssetId REFERENCES analysis_assets(id)` under `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON`, and the
   pre-ewag give-up is PRECISELY the case where no asset row exists. It needs an EPISODE-keyed
   table. (`RediffDayZeroExit.assetRowMissing` already documents this tautology for the mint
   path.)

7. **`prepareEpisodeForAnalysis` fires the kickoff UNCONDITIONALLY** (`PlayheadRuntime.swift:3613`),
   including on the `.waitingForWifi` outcome where no download was even started — leaving a
   detached task polling ~6.5 min for a file that will never arrive. Once give-ups are recorded
   that becomes recurring false `.noPinnedFile` noise. Gate it on the coordinator outcome.

8. **The background-download funnel is small and well-defined.** `scheduler.enqueue` is reached
   from exactly two sites, both in `DownloadManager`: :1360 (direct finalize) and :2105
   (`enqueueAnalysisIfNeeded`, called from :1576 and :3637). Callers of
   `backgroundDownload(episodeId:from:)` are `EpisodePreparationCoordinator` (the tap),
   `ForceQuitResumeScan:498`, and `BackgroundFeedRefreshService:993`.

9. **iOS Low Data Mode was INVISIBLE to the app.** `LiveTransportStatusProvider.reachability(from:)`
   read `isExpensive` and `usesInterfaceType(.cellular)` but never `NWPath.isConstrained`. So the
   "Low Data Mode always wins" requirement could not have been honoured — the signal was not
   being read at all.

10. Schema is at **V40**; the next migration is **V41**.

title: During live playback, point FM at likely ad slots AHEAD of the playhead instead of scanning linearly
description:
From Dan's question 2026-08-01: "why cant that happen anyway, do the best in first listen and
also still do fm".

Measured FM throughput is ~2.4x slower than realtime ([[playhead-qk44]]'s measurement; may
improve after [[playhead-kvs8]]'s non-streaming fix — re-measure first). During a 65-minute
listen FM covers ~27 minutes of audio. Scanned linearly from 0:00, most of that lands BEHIND
the playhead — useless for skipping this listen.

## The change

During ACTIVE PLAYBACK of an episode, the FM scan lane prioritizes windows AHEAD of the
playhead, ordered by ad-likelihood (position priors, candidate windows, chapter/acoustic cues)
rather than by episode order. The machinery mostly exists: the backfill lane already has a
scanLikelyAdSlots phase and the CoveragePlanner computes candidates; what changes is the
ORDERING POLICY while the episode is live: likely-slot-first, ahead-of-playhead-first,
full-episode sweep resumes when playback stops.

## Bounds and cautions

- Do not starve the background sweep permanently: when playback ends, the plan reverts to the
  coverage ladder. The ladder's tier accounting (8bp2) must see ahead-of-playhead work as real
  coverage, not as a detour that resets tiers.
- Seek interaction: a seek re-orders "ahead". Debounce; do not thrash the plan on scrubbing.
- Do NOT gate any user-facing state on this — it is an optimization of where FM's limited
  budget lands, not a new dependency ([[feedback_fm_hostread_irreplaceable]]: FM finds
  host-reads no deterministic signal can; this points it where they can still be skipped).
- Measure before/after on the corpus lane: ad-seconds heard in first listen, with rediff+pod
  continuation active, FM linear vs FM playhead-ahead.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: REPRIORITIZED P1 -> P2 in the 2026-08-11 triage. Not a downgrade of the finding — the queue-6 evidence establishes COMPLETION as the binding constraint (zero backfill_jobs have ever reached complete across 33 assets; FM evidence on 2 of 33). P1 is reserved for that path until it moves.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
PROMOTED P2 -> P0 on 2026-08-11 by Dan's decision, and I am correcting my own call: I demoted this to P2 in this morning's backlog triage on the grounds that it was off the critical path while COMPLETION was the binding constraint. Dan's ruling makes it half the critical path.

His words: 'we should fix background windows and do work while the app is live. belt and suspenders. if a user listens to an app and that app finishes analysis 5 minutes into a 60 minute episode, i would hope to see 4-5 other episodes finished in the background at the same time.'

This bead — point FM at likely ad slots AHEAD of the playhead during live playback — is LANE B of that decision and is already the right shape.

THE BUDGET SAYS THIS LANE IS COMFORTABLE, which is worth knowing before scoping it. Measured on the overnight pull: 0.257 productive compute-seconds per audio-second, so a 60-minute episode costs 15.4 minutes of FM compute. Staying ahead of the playhead therefore needs a 26% DUTY CYCLE — 15.4 minutes of FM spread over 60 minutes of listening. There is ample headroom.

WHAT IS NOT REACHABLE, so nobody scopes it by accident: 'the whole episode analysed by minute 5' is 15.4 minutes of compute inside 5 minutes of wall clock, 3.1x oversubscribed. No efficiency work gets there. The acceptance criterion should be NO AD BOUNDARY IS EVER REACHED BEFORE IT HAS BEEN ANALYSED — which is what the listener actually experiences — not a whole-episode deadline.

title: Flip pod continuation ON: rediff is structurally blind to ad #2 in a pod (field-proven tonight)
description:
Successor to [[playhead-xsdz.65]] (CLOSED — shipped flag-off in #301, "flip after corpus A/B").
This bead is the FLIP, with the field evidence the gate asked for.

## Tonight's field case (2026-08-01, Dan's device, ground truth = his own marks)

Episode D9B513CD (Conan, 65.5 min). Day-0 rediff, 14 s after play started:

    rediff found:   0.0 -  45.1 s   (ad 1)   conf 1.00, end edge 0.4 s from Dan's mark
    rediff MISSED: 47.6 -  94.3 s   (ad 2)   Dan marked it manually

Two ads back-to-back in one pre-roll pod, 2.5 s apart. Rediff caught #1 with sample accuracy
and is STRUCTURALLY blind to #2 — it detects what CHANGED between two fetches, and ad 2 was
identical in both copies (baked, or same creative served twice). No amount of rediff
improvement finds it. This is exactly Dan's founding complaint ("one banner, whole break, ads
#2/#3 still play") reproduced with byte-exact evidence on either side.

Pod continuation exists precisely for this: recover the pod NEIGHBOURS of a found ad.

## The flag

AdDetectionService.swift:1075 — `podContinuationEnabled: false` ("ships OFF and fully inert;
zero ad_windows writes, byte-identical backfill; flip after corpus A/B").

## What the flip needs

1. The corpus A/B the close reason gated on — run it on the corpus lane (l2f.8 baseline exists)
   OR make the explicit decision that tonight's field case + mark-only output is evidence
   enough to flip on dogfood. The mechanism emits mark-only/candidate/unanchored rows ONLY
   (playhead-2350 and ynmk hold: continuation spans cannot auto-skip and a confirmation cannot
   cut them), so the downside on dogfood is a wrong BANNER, not lost show.
2. Verify interaction with playhead-d3g0: continuation windows arrive AFTER the pod's first ad
   is found mid-listen; they must arm and fire on entry like any suggest window (96ot's
   in-session ingest is the delivery path).
3. Keep [[playhead-djl0]] in view: if the orchestrator is silently in shadow, continuation
   banners are invisible too — flip verification needs djl0 fixed first or a show with a
   resolving podcastId.

Dan has twice leaned yes ("whats the argument to turn it on"; queue approval pending). The flip
itself is one line; the work is the verification around it.
## CORRECTION 2026-08-01 — point 3 above is FALSE, and it was load-bearing

I wrote: "if the orchestrator is silently in shadow, continuation banners are invisible too —
flip verification needs djl0 fixed first or a show with a resolving podcastId."

**Wrong.** Continuation windows are mark-only/candidate/unanchored, so they route to the SUGGEST
tier (`SkipOrchestrator.swift:2464`), and the suggest path never consults `activeSkipMode` — the
five reads are all on the managed auto-skip tier (:5703, :5750, :5755, :6061, :6071). Continuation
banners are therefore visible in EVERY mode, including shadow.

Consequences: **eks2 does not depend on djl0**, and its verification does not need a show in any
particular trust mode. Strike that dependency. (Found by the djl0 agent while refuting the same
mistaken model on that bead.)
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-01 (from [[playhead-djl0]]'s implementation) — point 3 of "What the flip
needs" is FALSE as written, and it is load-bearing for your verification plan.

eks2 says: "if the orchestrator is silently in shadow, continuation banners are invisible
too — flip verification needs djl0 fixed first or a show with a [known trust mode]".

Shadow does NOT suppress the suggest tier. `activeSkipMode` is read at exactly five sites
in SkipOrchestrator.swift, ALL of them on the MANAGED (auto-skip) tier:

    :5703  the auto_skip_fired audit-event gate on a manual skip
    :5750  currentSkipMode() / :5755 setActiveSkipMode()
    :6061  the candidate -> confirmed promotion, `.auto` only
    :6071  the trust-mode switch inside the skip decision

The suggest path never consults it: `receiveAdWindows`' `decodedGate == .markOnly ->
registerSuggestedWindow` (:2464-2482), `registerSuggestedWindow` (:1237),
`emitSuggestBannersOnPlayheadEntry` (:1292) and its ONLY caller `updatePlayheadTime`
(:2949) are all mode-free. A mark-only window banners identically in shadow, manual and
auto.

This is pinned by a test so it cannot be re-adopted silently:
`PlayheadTests/Services/SkipOrchestrator/UnresolvedShowIdentityTests.swift`,
suite "The suggest tier is not gated by trust mode (playhead-djl0 refutation)" — a
parameterized test over all three modes asserting the same single banner.

CONSEQUENCE FOR YOUR FLIP: pod-continuation windows are mark-only/candidate/unanchored by
construction, so they route to the SUGGEST tier and are visible regardless of trust mode.
You do NOT need djl0 landed to verify the flip, and you do not need a show with a
particular trust mode. djl0 IS landed (#317) either way, but not for this reason.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-01. Flag flipped, verified, corpus A/B RUN (not fabricated). Branch
bead/playhead-eks2.

## The flip

`AdDetectionConfig.default.podContinuationEnabled` false -> true, and the init default with it
(every other flipped flag in that config tracks its `.default` value; 71 test files construct a
config without the argument, so a disagreement would have them measuring a configuration
production does not run). `PlayheadRuntime:952` builds the live service from `.default`, so this
IS the production setting.

## The corpus A/B the close reason gated on — it RAN

`AdPodContinuationCorpusEvalTests` is already in the FastTests plan and its three artifacts are
staged in the main checkout, so it executes on every gate. Measured, 13 episodes / 44 rediff
slots / 17-slot detected cohort, SHIPPING arm (lexical + rhetorical, single-strong-kind, gap 30):

    slots with a >30 s uncovered run    13 -> 12
    uncovered seconds in those slots    1324 -> 1195
    newly claimed seconds               129
      OUTSIDE every rediff slot         0.0      (asserted, frozen budget)
    slots that got WORSE                0

The sweep also shows what is being left on the table: gap 60 + single-strong-kind takes 13 -> 7
and 1324 -> 768 s, still at 0.0 s out-of-slot on this corpus. It is NOT taken because the
held-out device lane caught gap 45+ claiming a sponsored show SEGMENT (see maxLinkGapSeconds).
Gap 90 is the first arm to leak (2.7 s, conan-2026-07-09).

## Safety, proven rather than argued

Both gates asserted against rows `runBackfill` ACTUALLY persisted at the shipped flag value, in
an auto-mode orchestrator with a vacuity control that fires a real cue:

  * playhead-2350 — walking the playhead across the whole recovered span pushes no cue that
    overlaps it.
  * playhead-ynmk — `acceptSuggestedSkip` on a continuation banner records a `.confirmed` /
    `wasSkipped == false` promoted row at the detector's own confidence, and pushes no cue.

Neither is vacuous. Re-applying the two literals as mutations BY HAND and reading the issue list:
gate `markOnly -> eligible` makes a real skip cue land on the continuation span; anchors
`unanchored -> rediffByteExact` makes the tap actually cut (`wasSkipped` true, `.applied`).

## playhead-d3g0 / playhead-96ot interaction — verified

A continuation window persisted mid-listen while the playhead is ALREADY inside it: ingest ARMS
and emits nothing; the next tick inside emits (containment, not a transition); twelve further
ticks inside emit nothing. Also pinned: the mark confidence ceiling 0.70 IS
`preloadConfidenceThreshold`, so dropping it to 0.60 makes 96ot's ingest filter every
continuation row out and the banner never arrives (mutation L09).

## THE FINDING — the flip does NOT recover Dan's ad 2 [[playhead-evc1]]

`mintByteExactDayZeroMarks` persists a day-0 byte-exact rediff mark as `decisionState ==
.candidate` (AdDetectionService.swift:11469). `AdPodContinuation.seedDecisionStates` is
`{confirmed, applied}`. So on episode D9B513CD, where the ONLY row that found ad 1 was that mark,
continuation seeds nothing and recovers 0.0 s even with the flag ON.

Isolated two-armed over the field pod, composed through the production link/barrier derivation —
same window, same confidence, same provenance, same links, same barriers, only `decisionState`
differs: `.candidate` -> 0.0 s; `.confirmed` -> essentially all of ad 2, stopping exactly at the
show boundary. The corpus dump cannot see this population at all (132 of 132 windows are
`confirmed`/`eligible`), which is why the A/B never surfaced it.

The exclusion looks accidental: its own doc justifies excluding `.candidate` as "the aggregator
tiles fixed 30 s regions as candidates", which is about a coarse proposal, and
`userOwnedBoundaryStates` already carries a note calling a day-0 rediff row "the most obviously
correct thing to chain a pod walk off". Carve-out NOT applied — it is a detection-policy change
that needs a lane with day-0 rows to measure. Filed as [[playhead-evc1]] with the candidate fix.

## Also corrected

The bead's point 3 (djl0 dependency) was already struck by the djl0 agent and is confirmed
independently here: continuation rows banner in every trust mode.

## Tests / mutations

New suite `AdPodContinuationFlipTests` (8 tests). 7 FAILED against 95bd2f63 and were committed
before the flag change; the 8th (the day-0 blocker) passed on unflipped main, which is the
finding. Mutation battery L01-L09 added, batches 53-61: 9 KILLED / 0 SURVIVED / 0 ERROR.

## Gate

`scripts/fast-gate.sh`, exit 65. XCTest: 925 executed, 30 skipped, 0 FAILURES. Swift Testing: 37
failures, every one at >= 140.688 s — all timeouts in the documented voez load-flake families
(SpeechRecognitionRequestGate, BGTask/backfill handlers, PlaybackInterruption/RouteChange,
AnalysisPipelineStallInvariantHarness, Phase3ShadowReplayHarness benchmark, LongFormPlayback
dealloc, CorrectionAttributionCapture race). None in AdDetection or SkipOrchestrator; the eks2,
wire-in and pure continuation suites all passed. Flipping the init default caused ZERO collateral
failures across the 71 test files that build a config without the argument.

title: The FM daemon rate-limits STREAMING background requests — the named cause behind overnight FM starvation
description:
Filed from the 2026-08-01 03:37 device pull. The FM ad-scan lane produced ZERO new
semantic_scan_results in the 2.7 h since the new build was installed (42 rows / 44.1 min,
frozen since 00:55) — but for the first time the failures have NAMES instead of silence
(playhead-qk44's surfacing paying off).

## The named cause — the OS is rate-limiting background FM

backfill_jobs, DE0784D8 fullEpisodeScan, status=failed, retryCount=1, upd 2026-07-31 20:42:34.
deferReason contains, verbatim, the FoundationModels daemon's message:

    "Request has been rate limited. Please try again later.
     If you are using streaming responses in a background request, consider using
     non-streaming requests in background activities to reduce the likelihood of
     rate limiting."

**Apple's daemon throttles STREAMING responses from background requests, and says so.** This is
the missing explanation for overnight FM starvation that we have been attributing to BGTask
windows and thermal alone ([[project_backfill_stall_bgtask_2026-07-22]]): even when a window is
granted, a streaming respond() from the background can be rejected at the daemon.

Also in the same pull: DE0784D8 fullEpisodeScan status=deferred,
deferReason=cancelled-during-fullEpisodeScan, cursor {"lastProcessedUpperBoundSec":683.58} —
bkhc's banking working as designed (kept 683 s). D9B513CD scan running, updatedAt 03:29:58
(fresh — qk44's lease-as-work-clock in effect).

## Work

1. Inventory which FM call sites use STREAMING responses, and under what scene phase they run.
   If the background lanes (backfill/final-pass/shadow) stream, switch them to non-streaming per
   the OS's own guidance. Foreground/interactive paths can keep streaming. NOTE: this is
   response delivery, not decoding — greedy/reproducibility (two-lane measurement) is untouched.
   Present the change before implementing if it alters any measured-latency contract (8d5r's
   FMInferenceDeadline assumed streaming timing?).
2. Rate-limit handling: the failure consumed a retry with no backoff class of its own. A
   rate-limit is not a model failure — it needs its own named cause, a real backoff, and must
   NOT count toward consecutiveInferenceTimeoutAbortThreshold or trust/coverage penalties.
3. Re-measure the 2.4x-slower-than-realtime figure ([[playhead-qk44]]) split by
   foreground/background once (1) lands — the rate limiter may be a large share of it.

Watch alongside: D9B513CD's running scan should now either advance its cursor or be reaped by
the FMNoProgressWatchdog with a named terminal — either outcome is the new machinery working;
silence again means qk44 missed a path.

title: An unresolved podcastId silently forces SHADOW mode: detection runs, persists, and never surfaces
description:
Measured on Dan's device 2026-08-01 03:20, first field test after playhead-d3g0 (#314) and
playhead-96ot (#315). NOT root-caused — this bead records the observation and the elimination
done so far.

## The observation

Episode D9B513CD, 65.5 min. Playback started 03:20:03. Day-0 rediff minted at 03:20:17 —
so ~14 s in, with the playhead INSIDE the first window. Four windows persisted:

    0.0 -   45.1 s   conf 1.00  dayZeroRediffByteExact  markOnly  unanchored/unanchored  candidate
 1436.4 - 1508.1 s   conf 1.00  dayZeroRediffByteExact  markOnly  unanchored/unanchored  candidate
 3194.5 - 3371.2 s   conf 1.00  dayZeroRediffByteExact  markOnly  unanchored/unanchored  candidate
 3899.8 - 3929.9 s   conf 1.00  dayZeroRediffByteExact  markOnly  unanchored/unanchored  candidate

Dan: "no skip, no banner, heard an ad." The ad he heard is the 0 - 45.1 s pre-roll.

The absent SKIP is explained (three independent reasons: the slots are non-strict so qs0d
correctly left them markOnly; the show is in `manual` mode per [[playhead-gard]]; and markOnly
never auto-skips by design). **The absent BANNER is not explained.**

## Why a banner was expected

- `eligibilityGate == markOnly` routes to the SUGGEST tier — `SkipOrchestrator.swift:2464`,
  `if decodedGate == .markOnly { ... registerSuggestedWindow(adWindow) }`.
- playhead-d3g0's emit is CONTAINMENT, not a transition:
  `emitSuggestBannersOnPlayheadEntry` filters `time >= startTime && time < endTime`
  (`SkipOrchestrator.swift:1292`). A window armed while the playhead is ALREADY inside its span
  therefore fires on the very next observation — the 0.25 s tick. This was checked
  specifically; "armed while already inside never fires" is NOT the bug.
- playhead-96ot delivers a day-0 mint to the live orchestrator in-session via
  `ingestPersistedAdWindows`, and its own tests assert an armed suggestion results.

So on paper the banner should have appeared at roughly playhead 14.25 s.

## Not yet eliminated — investigate in this order

1. **Did `ingestPersistedAdWindows` actually run for this mint?** 96ot gates on
   `activeAssetId` read inside the actor. Confirm the asset was active at 03:20:17 and that the
   call happened. The DB cannot show this — it needs the unified log (subsystem `com.playhead`).
2. **Does `manual` mode suppress the suggest tier?** `activeSkipMode` gates the MANAGED path
   (:5957) but the suggest path is not obviously mode-gated. If it is gated somewhere, that is
   the answer and it interacts with [[playhead-gard]].
3. **Was a Now Playing host attached?** `replayPendingSuggestBanners` handles late attach, and
   d3g0 made replay a second consumer of the entry gate. An armed-but-unreached suggestion is
   deliberately withheld from a late host — confirm that logic is not withholding a REACHED one.
4. **`banneredWindowIds`** — the register call is skipped when the id is already present
   (:2479). Fresh UUIDs make this unlikely, but confirm.

## How to get the evidence

`log show --predicate 'subsystem == "com.playhead"' --start '2026-08-01 03:20:00' --style compact`
on the device, or a sysdiagnose. The relevant lines exist: the mint logs
`[xsdz.36.4] day-0 byte-exact minted N banner(s)` (`AdDetectionService.swift:11507`), the
markOnly routing logs at debug (`:2475`), and 96ot logs its own drop path
(`SkipOrchestrator.swift:1936`).

Do NOT guess at this one. Every wrong root cause this week came from theorising ahead of the
witness, and the witness here is a log line, not a table.
## LEADING HYPOTHESIS 2026-08-01 — an unresolved podcastId silently forces SHADOW mode

Dan confirmed the episode he played was **Conan** (simplecast, `mode: auto`, trust 0.5), NOT the
demoted flightcast show. So [[playhead-gard]] does not explain it — see the correction there.

What the DB actually shows for the played asset **D9B513CD**:

    analysis_jobs.podcastId      NULL
    backfill_jobs                NO ROW
    final_pass_jobs              NO ROW
    correction_events            NO ROW
    => podcastId is recorded NOWHERE for this asset

And `SkipOrchestrator.beginEpisode` (SkipOrchestrator.swift:1765-1774):

    if let podcastId = normalizedPodcastId, let trustService {
        activeSkipMode = await trustService.effectiveMode(podcastId: podcastId)
    } else {
        activeSkipMode = .shadow          // <-- unresolved id => SHADOW
    }

Shadow mode's own decision text is **"Shadow mode -- detection logged, no skip fired"** (:5960).

That fits every observation exactly: rediff ran, minted 4 windows, persisted them — and nothing
user-facing happened. Detection is perfect and completely invisible. **No error, no terminal, no
explanation anywhere in the UI.** The failure mode is silence, which is the defect class this
whole 07-29 -> 08-01 arc has been about.

Note the asymmetry: for OTHER assets the podcastId IS recorded (58882C47 -> simplecast,
DE0784D8 -> flightcast), and those rows come from `backfill_jobs` / `final_pass_jobs`. D9B513CD
has neither, so nothing ever wrote one. Whether `normalizedPodcastId` was also nil at RUNTIME
(it may come from a different source than the persisted rows) is the one link still unproven.

### Verify in this order

1. **Was `normalizedPodcastId` nil at `beginEpisode` for D9B513CD?** If yes, this is the root
   cause and the banner question is answered with it. The witness is the unified log or a
   `beginEpisode` trace — the DB cannot show a runtime local.
2. **Why does this asset have no podcastId anywhere** when its siblings do? A day-0 mint creating
   an asset without one, versus the backfill path which always records it, is the likely split.
3. Only if 1 is false, continue with the four candidates already listed above.

### The fix has two halves, and the second is the important one

- Resolve the podcastId (or carry it onto the asset row so it cannot be missing).
- **`.shadow` must never be a silent fallback for "I could not look something up."** Shadow is a
  deliberate diagnostic state; reaching it because an identifier was nil is a different fact and
  must be surfaced and counted, not merged into the same silent branch. Right now a single nil
  turns a fully working detection pipeline into a no-op with zero user-visible trace, and there
  is no way to tell that from "no ads in this episode".
## REVIEW ADDENDUM 2026-08-01 (bead review pass)

**A piece of evidence that may cut AGAINST the shadow hypothesis — resolve it first.** Dan's
second manual mark on this episode (47.6-94.3 s) persisted with `decisionState = applied`,
`wasSkipped` behavior observed. If a user-marked skip cannot apply in `.shadow`, that row
REFUTES shadow and sends this back to the four original candidates. If user-initiated skips
bypass the mode gate (plausible — the :5957 trust-mode gate sits on the DETECTION path, and
:5589 suggests shadow only suppresses the AUDIT EVENT for skips, not the skip), the row is
consistent with shadow and proves nothing either way. **Determine which, in code, before
spending on the log pull** — it is a five-minute read that can invalidate the whole hypothesis.

Cross-reference: the same ewag freeze that starved this asset's podcastId chain also silently
killed the download-time day-0 trigger for four episodes ([[playhead-4dqe]]) — both are "a
bounded wait for a row that dispatch never produced, expiring into silence." Fix djl0's
surfacing half with both call sites in mind.
notes:
CLOSING NOTES 2026-08-01 (#317). The leading hypothesis is REFUTED as the explanation for
the missing banner. Both halves of the fix shipped anyway, because the surfacing half is a
real defect independent of the field symptom.

## The hypothesis is dead, on two independent grounds

1. THE CAUSAL LINK IS BROKEN — decisive, and it does not depend on whether the podcastId
   was nil. `.shadow` does not gate the suggest tier at all. `activeSkipMode` is read at
   exactly five sites in SkipOrchestrator, ALL on the MANAGED auto-skip tier (:5703 the
   audit-event gate, :5750/:5755 the accessors, :6061 the `.auto` candidate promotion,
   :6071 the skip-decision switch). `receiveAdWindows`' markOnly -> `registerSuggestedWindow`
   routing (:2464), `registerSuggestedWindow` (:1237), `emitSuggestBannersOnPlayheadEntry`
   (:1292) and its only caller `updatePlayheadTime` (:2949) never consult it. Even if
   `normalizedPodcastId` HAD been nil and the session HAD been in shadow, all four mark-only
   day-0 windows would still have armed and banner"ed on the next 0.25 s tick.
   Pinned by `SuggestTierIsNotGatedByTrustModeTests` (parameterized over all three modes).

2. THE EVIDENTIARY LINK IS BROKEN. `analysis_jobs.podcastId IS NULL` does NOT witness a nil
   runtime value, because the two come from different producers.
   RUNTIME: `PlayheadRuntime.performPlayEpisode:3730` reads
   `episode.podcast?.feedURL.absoluteString` on the MainActor and passes it to
   `beginEpisode`. That is a SwiftData relationship.
   THE COLUMN: written only by `AnalysisWorkScheduler.enqueue(podcastId:)`, whose two
   production callers both pass `context?.podcastId` — and `DownloadContext` is constructed
   at ONE site in the tree (PlayheadRuntime:3888, the streaming-play branch).
   `DownloadManager.backgroundDownload` (:2169), the auto-download / prefetch /
   force-quit-resume entry, has no context parameter at all, so it enqueues
   `podcastId: nil` even when the show is perfectly well known. A NULL in that column is
   fully explained by "this episode was downloaded through a context-free path". Filed as
   [[playhead-kkzu]].
   Corollary worth noting: the absent `backfill_jobs` / `final_pass_jobs` rows are equally
   unremarkable for an episode being played for the first time — backfill had not run.

3. A CONFIRMING DETAIL, not proof: `currentPodcastTitle`, `currentArtworkURL` and
   `keepFullMusic` all read `episode.podcast?` on the same three lines
   (PlayheadRuntime:3742, :3769, :3770). A nil relationship would have blanked the show
   title and artwork in Now Playing — a much louder failure than Dan described.

WHAT STILL EXPLAINS THE MISSING BANNER: unknown. The bead's four original candidates stand,
and candidate 1 (did `ingestPersistedAdWindows` run for this mint, and was `activeAssetId`
the played asset at 03:20:17?) is now the strongest, because everything downstream of it is
proven mode-independent. That still needs the unified log; the DB cannot show it.

## What shipped (#317), and why the second half was still worth it

`.shadow` was reached by FIVE distinct facts and named all of them: a deliberate
observing posture, a new show with no profile, an unresolved show identity, an unwired
trust service, a profile read that threw, and a stored `mode` that did not decode. Every
one produced a byte-identical SkipMode, decision-log line and pill, and logged nothing.

  * `SkipModeResolution` names each cause. `isLookupFailure` / `hasResolvedShowIdentity`
    are single definitions shared by the counter, the diagnostics record and the pill.
    `newShowDefault` is deliberately NOT a failure — shadow for a new show is the design.
  * `TrustScoringService.resolveMode` returns the cause with the mode. `effectiveMode`
    is kept as the mode-only front door.
  * Per-cause counters on the orchestrator, plus a coded entry in the
    SurfaceStatusInvariantLogger session file the device pull already reads:
    `skip_mode_show_identity_unresolved` / `skip_mode_trust_lookup_failed`.
  * The Now Playing pill reads "Show Unknown", withholds the per-show menu (because
    `setShowSkipMode` cannot persist a choice with no show id), and is now rendered even
    with an empty podcast title — the title comes from the same relationship, so the one
    session with something to say used to say nothing at all.
  * Half one: `beginEpisode` recovers a missing identity from `analysis_jobs` via
    `AnalysisStore.fetchRecordedPodcastId` before falling through, applying the same
    canonicalization the caller path applies. The caller's value always wins.

No skip behaviour changed: SkipMode remains the only policy input and every failure still
lands on the non-actioning default.

## Verification

51 tests across 8 new suites. Mutation battery extended with J01-J18 (batches 41-47):
FINAL 18 KILLED / 0 SURVIVED. One genuine survivor found and fixed (J02: the "a new show is
not a failure" test asserted a DIFFERENT cause's counter, so reclassifying `newShowDefault`
as a failure left it green — every first listen would have written a diagnostics incident).
Full PlayheadFastTests: 10,126 Swift Testing + 895 XCTest passed; 0 XCTest failures;
20 Swift Testing failures, all >= 120 s and all in the documented voez baseline-RED families.

title: Trust is per-show and global across detectors: a 0.40-confidence detector's vetoes suppress byte-exact rediff
description:
Measured on Dan's device 2026-08-01 03:20, first test of the six-bead batch.

## What happened

Dan played D9B513CD (65.5 min). Day-0 rediff fired 14 s in and worked: 4 divergent slots,
4 marks, 120.3 MB. He saw NO skip, NO banner, and heard the pre-roll (0 - 45.1 s).

One reason is this bead. `podcast_profiles` for that show:

    skipTrustScore              0.20
    recentFalseSkipSignals      3
    implicitFalsePositiveCount  3
    mode                        manual        <- demoted out of auto

Promotion back requires (TrustScoringService `evaluatePromotion`):
    observations >= 8  AND  trustScore >= 0.75  AND  recentFalseSignals == 0
Actual: 1, 0.20, 3.

**Those 3 false-skip signals are Dan's own vetoes from 2026-07-31**, on the three
`segmentAggregated` windows (confidence 0.40-0.42, both edges unanchored) that
[[playhead-ynmk]] has since stopped from ever skipping. The aggregator went 0-for-3, cost him
210 s of show, and in doing so poisoned the trust score for the WHOLE SHOW.

## The defect: trust is per-show and GLOBAL ACROSS DETECTORS

A low-certainty detector's mistakes now suppress a high-certainty deterministic one. Byte-exact
rediff divergence had nothing to do with those three bad skips — it is a different signal with
a different error profile (2-of-2 correct on the same corpus where the aggregator went 0-for-3)
— and it is being gated by them.

That directly contradicts the certainty-tiered policy: auto-skip high-certainty DAI, mark
host-read when uncertain, PER CLASS, not on one global threshold. See
[[feedback_certainty_tiered_skip_2026-07-17]] and [[playhead-wraj]].

## The trap that makes it worse: manual mode may be SELF-SUSTAINING

Leaving `manual` needs `recentFalseSkipSignals == 0`. That counter is reset (TrustScoringService
:171) on a CORRECT OBSERVATION. If a correct observation requires a skip to fire and not be
reverted, and skips do not fire in manual mode, the show can never earn its way back out.
**Verify whether a confirmed banner counts as a correct observation.** If it does not, this is a
one-way door and every show a user ever vetoes three times is permanently manual.

## What to decide (Dan's call, it is a policy question)

1. Should trust be PER-DETECTOR-CLASS rather than per-show? Byte-exact rediff arguably should
   not consult show trust at all — it is deterministic, and its certainty does not depend on
   the show's history.
2. Should a veto of an UNANCHORED low-confidence window carry the same penalty as a veto of an
   anchored high-confidence one? Right now they are the same `falseSignalPenalty` (0.10).
   Weighting the penalty by the certainty of what was skipped would have left this show in auto.
3. Independently: confirm manual mode is escapable, and if not, fix that regardless.

## NOTE ON THE FIELD TEST

Because of this, the batch's acceptance test could not have passed on this show no matter what
the six beads did. Any future device test must either use a show still in `auto`, or reset the
trust profile first. The other subscribed show (`feeds.simplecast.com/dHoohVNH`) reads
`mode: auto`, trust 0.5.
## CORRECTION 2026-08-01 — this bead did NOT cause the failed field test

Dan: "the episode i listened to was conan."

Conan is the SIMPLECAST feed (`feeds.simplecast.com/dHoohVNH`), which reads **`mode: auto`,
trust 0.5**. The demoted show is FLIGHTCAST (`rss2.flightcast.com/...`, Diary of a CEO) — the
one carrying his three vetoes. I resolved the played episode to flightcast by INFERENCE ("that
is where the corrections are") rather than measurement; `analysis_jobs.podcastId` was NULL and I
filled the gap with an assumption. Same error shape as everything else this week.

**So: strike the note claiming the acceptance test could not have passed on this show.** It
could have. The trust demotion is real and the design defect below still stands on its own
merits, but it is NOT what Dan observed on 2026-08-01.

The likely actual cause is in [[playhead-djl0]]: the played asset has **no `podcastId` recorded
anywhere**, and `beginEpisode` falls to `activeSkipMode = .shadow` when the id does not resolve.

## What still stands, unchanged

Trust is per-show and GLOBAL ACROSS DETECTORS, so a 0.40-confidence aggregator's mistakes
suppress byte-exact rediff on the same show. That contradicts the certainty-tiered policy and is
worth fixing regardless of which show Dan happened to play. The possible one-way door out of
`manual` (needs `recentFalseSkipSignals == 0`, reset only on a correct observation, which may
require a skip that manual mode prevents) is also unverified and still worth checking.

Priority dropped P0 -> P1: real design defect, but not the live blocker it was filed as.
## DECIDED — Dan 2026-08-01: trust becomes PER DETECTOR

> "per detector is good"

Trust/mode is no longer a single per-show scalar governing every detector. A detector class's
own error history governs its own eligibility.

Consequences to implement:
- **Byte-exact rediff does not consult show trust at all.** It is deterministic; its certainty
  does not depend on the show's history. Measured 2-of-2 on the same corpus where the
  aggregator went 0-for-3.
- A veto attributes its penalty to **the detector that produced the window**, not to the show
  globally. Dan's three vetoes were of `segmentAggregated` spans; nothing about them is
  evidence against `dayZeroRediffByteExact`.
- Reconsider whether the veto penalty should also be **weighted by the certainty of what was
  skipped** (a 0.40-confidence unanchored span vetoed should not cost what a 1.00-confidence
  anchored span vetoed costs). Not explicitly decided — raise it with the implementation.
- Still verify the possible one-way door: escaping `manual` needs `recentFalseSkipSignals == 0`,
  reset only on a correct observation, which may require a skip that manual mode prevents. Fix
  regardless of the per-detector split.

This is [[feedback_certainty_tiered_skip_2026-07-17]] applied to the trust layer, which is where
it was missing.
## QUEUE — Dan 2026-08-01, the mid-roll program

Position **4 of 6**:

    isp5 -> y3ya -> lxkq -> gard -> mptr -> hx6n

**Every junk-card veto during dogfooding degrades the detector that works: 5 near-zero-confidence vetoes dropped DOAC to trust 0.20/manual, which now suppresses byte-exact rediff that went 2-for-2.**

One at a time (16 GB box, one build slot). No device build until the queue completes, then ONE
build and one dogfood pass.
## QUEUE — revised 2026-08-01, position 7 of 9

    isp5(done) -> b6r2(done) -> y3ya -> lxkq -> sik9 -> nqey -> gard -> mptr -> hx6n

**Every junk-card veto during dogfooding degrades the detector that works.**

One at a time. No device build until the queue completes, then ONE build and one dogfood pass.
## QUEUE — revised 2026-08-01, position 9 of 11

    isp5(done) -> b6r2(done) -> y3ya(done) -> lxkq -> avbn -> sik9 -> nqey -> 9v09 -> gard -> mptr -> hx6n

**Every junk-card veto during dogfooding degrades the detector that works.**

One at a time. No device build until the queue completes.
notes:
## QUEUE — revised 2026-08-02

    isp5(done) -> b6r2(done) -> y3ya(done) -> lxkq(done) -> avbn(done) -> sik9(done)
      -> nqey(in flight) -> 6qvf -> 9v09 -> gard -> mptr -> hx6n

**6qvf inserted directly after nqey (Dan, 2026-08-02).** It is the safety half of the flip that
just shipped: `certaintyTieredSkipEnabled` ON makes the certainty tiers load-bearing, and 6qvf is
the reason one of those tiers is not what it says. `carriesRediffByteExactWidth` is true for the
~1s chroma fallback as well as the byte differ, so a chroma edge is admitted to auto-skip at
`deterministic` tier and padded with margins derived from MEASURED byte-exact edge error
(0.50s start / 0.75s end). Live today, independent of any flag.

MEASURE FIRST: how often the chroma fallback is actually taken decides whether the persisted
AnchorRef change is worth it. Rare => theoretical. Common => a real wrong-skip hazard.

One at a time. No device build until the queue completes.

title: Day-0 rediff marks are persisted but never pushed to SkipOrchestrator in-session
description:
Found while implementing playhead-qs0d (2026-07-31).

AdDetectionService.mintByteExactDayZeroMarks persists its AdWindows via store.upsertHotPathAdWindows and then NOTHING delivers them to SkipOrchestrator during the session that minted them:

  * Both DayZeroRediffTrigger call sites in PlayheadRuntime (the play-time trigger and the Download-and-Analyze tap) are fire-and-forget Task.detached and ignore the outcome.
  * RediffRefetchProduction's .dayZeroMarked arm only writes rediff state + the day-0 attempt ledger row.
  * SkipOrchestrator.receiveAdWindows is therefore only reached later, via the cross-launch beginEpisode preload or a push from some other producer for the same asset.

CONSEQUENCE. Day-0 fires ~19 s into a first listen — exactly when the ads it found are still ahead of the playhead. Under playhead-qs0d those windows are now eligibilityGate=.eligible with rediffByteExact anchors, i.e. genuinely auto-skippable, but they cannot fire in the session that minted them. The user has to re-open the episode. The same latency applied to the mark-only banners before qs0d, so this is pre-existing, not a regression — but it is now the difference between 'rediff is on' and 'rediff visibly skipped an ad'.

FIX SHAPE (not decided): after a .dayZeroMarked outcome, fetch the asset's AdWindows and hand them to the active SkipOrchestrator when the minted asset is the one currently playing. Needs care around the ordering rules receiveAdWindows already documents (edge-anchor stamping precedence, suggest-tier routing, producer-revision identity).

Verify on device by minting day-0 on a first listen and checking whether a skip fires WITHOUT relaunching.
## QUEUE — Dan 2026-07-31: added as BATCH 6 of 6

    ewag(done) -> qk44(done) -> qs0d(done) -> ynmk -> d3g0 -> **96ot**

Promoted P1 -> P0 and pulled into the batch because it is what decides whether the single
dogfood pass at the end of this batch READS as success or failure.

playhead-qs0d (#312) has now made day-0 byte-exact spans genuinely auto-skippable —
`eligibilityGate = .eligible`, `rediffByteExact` on both edges, late-safe padding active. But
without this bead those windows cannot fire in the session that minted them. Dan would download
an episode, play it, and watch rediff skip NOTHING — then reasonably conclude the whole batch
failed. The mechanism would be correct and invisible.

There is NO intermediate device build. This is the last bead before the build.

Verify on device by minting day-0 on a FIRST listen and confirming a skip fires WITHOUT
relaunching. That is the acceptance test and it is the one Dan will run himself.

title: A running fullEpisodeScan makes no progress and never times out — 23 min, empty cursor, no error, app foregrounded
description:
Observed on Dan's clean install 2026-07-31, main @ a4d5ad32. NOT yet proven causal — the
discriminating test is stated at the bottom and should be run before implementing anything.

## The observation

Episode DE0784D8 (92 min), transcript 100%, features 100%.

    backfill_jobs:          fullEpisodeScan, status=RUNNING since 15:05:47,
                            progressCursor EMPTY, retryCount 0, untouched for 14 min
    semantic_scan_results:  0 ROWS          <- the PRODUCTION ad scan
    shadow_fm_responses:    17 ROWS         <- the SHADOW capture lane
    confirmedAdCoverageEndTime: 0.0

The shadow lane kept receiving FM calls AFTER the production scan started:
15:06:00, 15:08:37, 15:09:14, 15:09:15, 15:09:48, 15:09:53, 15:10:25, 15:10:30, 15:11:04.
In that same window the production scan produced nothing and never advanced its cursor.

Shadow capture is ON deliberately — ShadowCaptureConfig.swift:90 says "Production/Dan-build
default: dual-run capture ON, conservative budget", wired at PlayheadRuntime.swift:1892.
So this is a dual-run by design; the question is whether the budget is actually conservative
in the presence of a live production scan.

## Why this matters more than it looks

FM is the scarce resource on device (see the mlhostd core-pinning note in
[[project_two_lane_measurement_2026-07-17]]). If a DIAGNOSTIC subsystem is winning FM
scheduling against the lane that produces user-visible ad detection, then the product's core
promise is being starved by its own instrumentation — on the build Dan actually uses.

Note also the shadow lane's own throughput, which is worth recording either way:
    17 windows, 0.0 - 505.8 s covered of a 5522 s episode = 8.1%
    first 14:51:39, last 15:11:04 -> ~20 min wall clock for ~8.4 min of audio
That is ~2.4x SLOWER THAN REALTIME. Extrapolated, a 92-min episode needs ~3.7 hours of FM.
Whatever the contention verdict, that rate is the quantified form of Dan's standing complaint
that analysis does not reach where it needs to in time.

## THE DISCRIMINATING TEST — run this before writing code

Turn shadow capture OFF (ShadowCaptureConfig `.default`, or nil the coordinator at
PlayheadRuntime.swift:1892-1902), rebuild, install on a clean container, download + play one
episode, and measure whether `semantic_scan_results` starts filling.

  * If the production scan starts producing rows -> contention CONFIRMED, and the fix is a
    priority/budget rule: production ad scan must outrank shadow capture for FM, always.
    Shadow is an evaluation aid; it can wait.
  * If it still produces nothing -> the production scan is wedged for an unrelated reason and
    this bead is a red herring. Look instead at why a `running` fullEpisodeScan with an empty
    progressCursor makes no progress for 14 minutes, and note 8d5r's FMInferenceDeadline
    (300 s standard, abort after 2 CONSECUTIVE timeouts) should have surfaced SOMETHING by
    then — a silent 14-minute "running" with no journal row is itself suspect
    (`work_journal` is empty).

Do NOT disable shadow capture permanently as "the fix" without the test — it is deliberate
instrumentation that the corpus/eval lane depends on, and removing it to fix a symptom would
cost the measurement program.

## Related

[[playhead-ewag]] — the preAnalysis lane is separately frozen by a thermal depth gate. These
are DIFFERENT stalls in different lanes: ewag is jobs never dispatched; this is a dispatched
job producing nothing. Do not conflate them.
## RESCOPED 2026-07-31 15:29 — the contention premise is REFUTED

Pulled again 18 minutes later. **Nothing moved, in either lane:**

    semantic_scan_results    0 rows                                   (unchanged)
    backfill fullEpisodeScan running, progressCursor EMPTY,
                             updatedAt 15:05:47                       -> 23 min stale
    shadow_fm_responses      still 17, newest capture 15:11:04        -> 18 min stale, STOPPED
    confirmedAdCoverageEndTime  0.0
    analysis_jobs            5 queued, attemptCount 0, last touched 14:51:13
    ad_windows               11                                       (unchanged)

The shadow lane did NOT keep running while production starved. **Both stopped, together.** So
"instrumentation is starving detection" is refuted — there is no winner, only a halt.

### And the app was AWAKE the whole time

From Documents/bg-task-log.jsonl (converted to ET):

    15:06:03  active -> inactive -> background
    15:07:26  -> ACTIVE
    15:07:26 .. 15:29:29   ACTIVE, foregrounded, 22 MINUTES
    15:29:29  -> inactive -> background   (user set the phone down)

**Twenty-two minutes foregrounded and active, with zero analysis progress in any lane.** Not a
suspension, not a BGTask-budget problem, not thermal `.critical` at last reading
(capabilitySnapshot showed thermalState 2, foundationModelsUsable true, 157 GB free). The app is
demonstrably alive — bg-task-log was written at 15:29 — it simply is not analysing.

Container mtimes corroborate: analysis.sqlite-wal last written 15:15, nothing since.

### What this bead now is

**A `fullEpisodeScan` marked `running` makes no progress and never times out.** Empty
progressCursor, retryCount 0, `work_journal` empty, no rows, no error, no terminal. 23 minutes
and counting. Note 8d5r's `FMInferenceDeadline` (300 s standard, abort after 2 CONSECUTIVE
timeouts) should have surfaced *something* by ~10 minutes. Either it is not on this path, or the
work never reached the deadline-guarded call at all.

Investigate in this order:
  1. Does the fullEpisodeScan runner ever start work after the row flips to `running`, or does
     it claim the row and then block/return silently? The empty progressCursor suggests it never
     completed a first unit.
  2. Is the FM/session resource held by something that never releases (the shadow lane's last
     call at 15:11 is a candidate — did it leave a session open)?
  3. Is 8d5r's deadline actually wrapping this path?

### The bound this needs (as every bead in this arc has)

A job in `running` with no cursor advance for N minutes must become a SURFACED, COUNTED,
recoverable state — requeue with a consecutive-failure count, or a terminal with a named cause.
"Running forever, silently" is exactly the shape [[playhead-gqx4]] and [[playhead-y8f3]] fixed
elsewhere; the backfill lane still has it.

Priority raised: this, not shadow contention, is why the one played episode will never finish.
## QUEUE REVISED — Dan 2026-07-31 15:35

qk44 inserted SECOND. Batch is now **5** beads, position **2**:

    ewag -> qk44 -> qs0d -> ynmk -> d3g0

Rationale: ewag makes work START, qk44 makes it FINISH. Without qk44 the other three have
nothing to act on — a build after ewag+qs0d+ynmk+d3g0 alone would still detect ZERO ads,
because the lane that actually scans hangs silently. qs0d in particular cannot be validated
with no scans running.

Still NO intermediate device build. All five land, then one build, then dogfood.
## ROOT CAUSE HANDED OVER BY THE ewag INVESTIGATION (2026-07-31, not yet fixed)

Two independent liveness gaps explain the 23-minute silent `running`:

**1. No foreground sweep exists at all.** `resetStrandedBackfillJobs`
(`AnalysisStore.swift:14990`) is the ONLY timeout for a stuck backfill row, and it fires only
from `AnalysisJobReconciler.reconcile()` — called at launch (`PlayheadRuntime.swift:2528`) and
from `BackgroundProcessingService.swift:1772`. **No foreground timer sweeps it.** During a
foregrounded session nothing checks a `running` row, ever. That alone accounts for the observed
23 minutes with the app awake and in front of the user.

**2. The reaper's own liveness signal is self-refreshing — the deeper bug.** Its freshness floor
is `updatedAt < now - 600`. But `BackfillJobRunner` calls `markBackfillJobRunning` as a pure
**heartbeat** (`:1609, :1654, :1877, :1908`), which bumps `updatedAt` WITHOUT touching
`progressCursor`. So a job wedged inside FM keeps refreshing its own liveness clock and becomes
**permanently exempt from the reaper** — it can never age past the floor.

The check asks *"is the process alive?"* when the question is *"is the work advancing?"* An empty
`progressCursor` beside a fresh `updatedAt` is precisely the state that combination cannot
detect. Field evidence matches exactly: `status=running`, `progressCursor` EMPTY, `retryCount 0`,
`updatedAt` 15:05:47 and 0 scan rows.

This is the same defect class as everything else in this arc — a quantity read as something it
does not measure. See [[feedback_ask_what_the_quantity_measures_2026-07-29]].

### What the fix therefore needs

- A liveness signal that advances only when WORK advances (`progressCursor`, a scan-row count, a
  journal entry) — not a heartbeat. Or keep the heartbeat for crash detection but add a SEPARATE
  no-progress deadline that a heartbeat cannot reset.
- A foreground sweep, so a wedged job is reaped during the session that wedged it rather than at
  the next launch.
- The usual bound: consecutive no-progress intervals counted, a named terminal cause, and the
  state surfaced rather than silent.

Do NOT simply shorten the 600 s floor — the heartbeat makes the row permanently exempt, so no
floor value fixes it.

### Still open, and worth checking first

Why the FM call itself never returned. 8d5r's `FMInferenceDeadline` (300 s standard, abort after
2 CONSECUTIVE timeouts) should have surfaced something by ~10 minutes. Either it does not wrap
this path, or the work never reached the deadline-guarded call. Establish that before designing
the reaper, because if the FM call is simply hanging unbounded, the reaper is a mitigation and
not the cure.
## CLOSED #311 — and the root cause I recorded above was HALF WRONG. Read this.

**Claim 2 ("the heartbeat self-refreshes `updatedAt`, so the row is permanently reaper-exempt")
is REFUTED — by this bead's own field evidence.** `updatedAt` was **23 minutes STALE**. It could
not have been refreshing. All four `markBackfillJobRunning` sites
(`BackfillJobRunner.swift:1609/1654/1877/1908`) are **downstream of `coarsePassA` returning**, so
a job wedged inside it never reaches one. The row cleared the 600 s floor at minute 10 and simply
nothing asked. **Claim 1 (no foreground sweep) was the whole story.**

I recorded claim 2 as established after it came from the ewag investigation. I should have
checked it against the stale `updatedAt` sitting in the same bead — the two are directly
contradictory. Flagged here so nobody builds on it.

**And the corollary inverts the fix.** `updatedAt` also freezes during *healthy* work (a coarse
pass runs 12-45 min), so **adding a foreground sweep on the old lease would have reaped LIVE jobs
mid-pass**, destroying the very FM work the reaper exists to protect. Making the lease a WORK
CLOCK is what makes the sweep safe — not optional polish.

## The actual cure: a reaper would only ever have been mitigation

`FMInferenceDeadline` (8d5r) bounds `respond` **and nothing else**. Three families of unbounded
`await` into the model daemon sat on the coarse pass's critical path *before* the first bounded
call:

  * `SystemLanguageModel.tokenCount(for:)` x4 (`FoundationModelClassifier.swift`
    6640/6652/6664/6676) — one XPC round trip PER CANDIDATE WINDOW inside `planPassA`
  * `FoundationModelsUsabilityProbe.probeIfNeeded`'s bare `respond`
    (`FoundationModelsUsabilityProbe.swift:170`) — awaited by `liveRuntime.availabilityStatus`,
    i.e. `coarsePassA`'s **first line**

A hang in any of these never reaches a deadline-guarded call and produces exactly the observed
row. Now bounded (`.metadata` 30 s; `.standard` for the probe). The watchdog is the backstop for
whatever remains, not the fix.

**Why it was undiagnosable:** `coarsePassA` persists nothing until it returns, so a healthy
45-minute pass and a permanent wedge are BYTE-IDENTICAL in the database. No *duration* threshold
can separate them; only a *silence* bound can.

## Shipped

`FMNoProgressWatchdog` (3 x 180 s consecutive silence -> named `FMNoProgressError`; 540 s
deliberately below `strandedJobFreshnessSeconds` 600 s so the in-process bound always beats the
DB reaper) - per-unit progress out of `coarsePassA` - the lease touched per resolved window -
`sweepStrandedBackfillJobsInSession()` on scene activation.

7 mutations run, 7 killed. **Two initially SURVIVED and both were test defects**, now fixed in
1039cda8: one test recorded progress on a contiguous opening run so no strike ever accumulated
(making "reset to zero" and "never increment" indistinguishable), and one fixture fit in a single
window making `max(1, plans.count)` vacuously 1. A latent flake found in the same run (two tests
racing the watchdog for first-writer, passing on scheduler luck) was fixed too.

Gate exit 65: XCTest 922 executed / 0 failures; Swift Testing 24 distinct failures, ALL >= 118.4 s,
30 of the issues literally `Time limit was exceeded: 60.000 seconds`. Documented voez families
only, zero ~2 s failures. This run was also the first validation of the y8f3 x ewag combination —
the scheduler/reconciler failures are 60 s time-limit exceedances at ~151 s wall, load-shaped, not
interaction-shaped.

## FILED, NOT SMUGGLED — follow-up needed

`refinePassB` is **not** wrapped by the watchdog. It runs only after a coarse pass returned
windows, so a wedge there leaves durable evidence that the silent-`running` state does not. Worth
its own bead.

**Caveat that no simulator test can close:** the `liveRuntime` bounds are device-only code the
simulator gate physically cannot execute — which is precisely why they were the calls left
unbounded in the first place. The source canary (`FMUnboundedCallCanaryTests`) is the guard, not
a runtime test. Verify on device.

title: A banner confirmation bypasses the 2350 unanchored-edge gate and skipped 210s of show (0 of 3 correct)
description:
Found 2026-07-31 on Dan's clean install while investigating [[playhead-d3g0]]. Separable from
that bead: d3g0 is about WHEN the banner fires, this is about what a CONFIRMATION is permitted
to do once it fires.

## What happened

Episode DE0784D8 (92 min). Three `segmentAggregated` windows were offered as suggestions and
confirmed. Every one carried, AT CONFIRMATION TIME:

    confidence         0.40 - 0.42
    startEdgeAnchor    unanchored
    endEdgeAnchor      unanchored
    eligibilityGate    markOnly
    decisionState      candidate / suppressed
    wasSkipped         false

After one tap each, all three became:

    boundaryState      userConfirmedSuggested
    confidence         1.00
    decisionState      applied
    wasSkipped         TRUE
    eligibilityGate    (cleared)

**ALL THREE WERE FALSE POSITIVES.** Dan vetoed 210-240 s, then 4800-4950 s, then the third.
Precision of the aggregator on this episode's mid-rolls: **0 of 3**. Total show content
skipped: 30 + 150 + 30 = 210 seconds.

## The defect

[[playhead-2350]] exists to block auto-skip on unanchored edges — presence of an ad is not
extent of an ad, and an unanchored edge has no evidence for where the span actually ends. That
gate held: it correctly marked all three `markOnly`.

**A single banner tap cleared the gate.** Confirmation overwrites confidence to 1.00 and
promotes straight to applied+skipped, with no re-evaluation of edge anchoring. The safety gate
is enforced against the DETECTOR and not against the promotion path that supersedes it.

This is the [[feedback_outer_edges_free_inner_precious_2026-07-29]] failure in its exact
predicted form: these are INNER edges, both unanchored, and widening/skipping them ate show.

## Why "the user asked for it" is not a defence

1. Under d3g0 the user had not heard the audio when asked — a tap is a guess, not consent to
   cut 150 s of show. Even after d3g0 is fixed, a tap at span ENTRY (Dan's chosen trigger,
   recorded in d3g0) still means ~0 s heard.
2. Confidence 1.00 is *manufactured* by the confirmation. Nothing measured it. Apply the
   standing check: what would that 1.00 read if the span were pure show content? Still 1.00 —
   it records that a tap happened, not that an ad exists.
3. The user is answering "is this an ad?", not "is it safe to cut from here to there?". Extent
   was never asked about, yet extent is what gets applied.

## Proposed fix (needs Dan's call on the policy half)

- A confirmation must NOT clear the unanchored-edge gate. Options: keep the skip but clamp it
  to the anchored portion; or apply the skip while holding the unanchored edges to a
  conservative inset; or honour the skip once and require an anchor before repeating it for
  the same show.
- Do not synthesise `confidence = 1.0` from a tap. Record user assertion in its own field so
  it cannot be read as measured certainty. This is the same class as pz32's checkmark.
- Whatever the choice: an unanchored inner edge must never silently define a skip boundary.

## Related, and the contrast worth acting on

On the SAME episode, day-0 rediff produced two byte-exact windows at confidence 1.00 (0-60.1 s
pre-roll and 5462.6-5522.7 s post-roll), both OUTER edges, both correctly `markOnly` and never
skipped. So the pipeline auto-skipped 3 low-confidence unanchored INNER windows (0/3 correct)
while declining to skip 2 byte-exact OUTER ones (2/2 correct). That inversion is the argument
for [[playhead-qs0d]].
## QUEUE — Dan 2026-07-31

Batch position **3** of 4: ewag -> qs0d -> ynmk -> d3g0.

Dan: "agree on order. I won't dogfood until all are done though" — so there is **NO intermediate
device build**. All four land, then ONE build, then one dogfood pass. Do not stop to install
between beads.
## QUEUE REVISED — Dan 2026-07-31 15:35

qk44 inserted SECOND. Batch is now **5** beads, position **4**:

    ewag -> qk44 -> qs0d -> ynmk -> d3g0

Rationale: ewag makes work START, qk44 makes it FINISH. Without qk44 the other three have
nothing to act on — a build after ewag+qs0d+ynmk+d3g0 alone would still detect ZERO ads,
because the lane that actually scans hangs silently. qs0d in particular cannot be validated
with no scans running.

Still NO intermediate device build. All five land, then one build, then dogfood.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
Implemented on bead/playhead-ynmk, PR #313. 4 commits (tests-first, fix, mutation-driven fix, fixture fixes).

POLICY CHOICE (the half you flagged as needing your call). Options (a) clamp to
the anchored portion and (b) apply with a conservative inset are the SAME
behaviour under the derived margins, because the padding derivation
(docs/autoskip-edge-padding-derivation-2026-07-20.md §5) explicitly refuses to
certify ANY unanchored-start margin: "spans without a hard start anchor stay
markOnly". Picking (b) with a nonzero number would mean inventing a constant the
data does not support — the exact defect class this bead is about. So: a
confirmation is now governed by the same per-edge policy as an auto-skip, and a
both-edges-unanchored confirmation becomes a MARK.

Option (c) (honour once per show) was rejected: it still burns one span per show,
and it still never asks about extent.

PRODUCT CONSEQUENCE WORTH YOUR EYES: on a both-edges-unanchored span the user taps
"Skip" and playback does NOT move. The tap is still recorded — the correction
receipt, the recurrence learning and the MISS calibration all fire, and the row is
marked userConfirmedSuggested — but no audio is cut. Given 0-of-3 precision and 210 s
of show lost, refusing is the right default; but it is a real UX change and it is
yours to overrule. The alternative (skip end-minus-10.25s) would still have cut
~180 of the 210 s.

CONFIDENCE FIELD: no new column. `boundaryState = "userConfirmedSuggested"` is
already a dedicated, exclusive record of the tap, and the .bannerSuggestionConfirmed
CorrectionEvent already stores the full detection projection (measured confidence,
gate and anchors at tap time). A second boolean would be a second source of truth
that can disagree. It is now typed (UserSpanAssertion) instead of a magic string.

TWO THINGS FOUND THAT WERE NOT IN THE BEAD:
1. Your three existing bad rows would re-skip 210 s on EVERY relaunch after upgrade
   — beginEpisode's preload forwards .applied rows straight back to the cue path.
   Now re-checked. Pinned by a test.
2. The preload's 0.7 confidence floor was only ever cleared by the fake 1.0. With
   the measured value restored, an ANCHORED confirmation would have silently lost
   cross-launch continuity — the one population qs0d wants skipping. Fixed.

title: Queued preAnalysis jobs are never dispatched: 5 downloads, 5 queued jobs, 0 progress on a clean foregrounded install
description:

(8bp2 + bkhc + 8d5r + onn6 + wvdz + csbq + r5um + hvk0 + se2h all present).

Dan deleted the app and its container, reinstalled, subscribed, hit Download on 5 episodes
and played exactly 1. Device foregrounded and on the charger. Five minutes later:

## The measurement
