  Library/Caches/Playhead/AudioCache/complete/  -> 5 .mp3 + 5 .pin
  60 MB, 63.2 MB, 30.2 MB, 26.1 MB, 23.9 MB, all written 14:50-14:51.

analysis_jobs:
  jobType      state    n   want    got
  preAnalysis  queued   5   5417.0  0.0

FIVE jobs queued. ZERO running. ZERO progress. Nothing dispatched them.

analysis_assets: exactly ONE row -- DE0784D8, the episode that was PLAYED. The other four
downloads have a queued job but no asset row, because the asset row is materialised by the
job when it runs, and the job never runs.

## This is the starvation, reproduced clean

This is the same shape as the standing "27 episodes needing work, 1 dispatchable job"
condition, but it is now proven NOT to be an artifact of accumulated bad state: a virgin
database reaches it in five minutes. Everything merged in the 07-29/07-30 honesty arc is in
this build, so none of it addresses THIS.

Note what it is NOT:
- Not "download fails to enqueue" -- DownloadManager DOES enqueue.
  performDownload:~1360 (via progressiveDownload:1207) and enqueueAnalysisIfNeeded, called
  at :1576 and :3637, both reach scheduler.enqueue. The jobs exist. That is the proof.
- Not BGTask starvation in the overnight sense -- the app was FOREGROUNDED and charging.
- Not the 90-second tier ceiling (8bp2) -- want is 5417 s, the whole episode. The ladder is
  asking for the right amount. It simply never gets to run.

## What to investigate, in order

1. What SELECTS a queued preAnalysis job for dispatch, and what gates it? Suspect a
   playback-context gate: the one episode making progress is the one being played, and
   AnalysisWorkScheduler carries schedulerPlaybackContext (observed values "playing" /
   "paused" in the asset-lifecycle log). If dispatch requires an active playback context,
   then by construction only the played episode ever advances -- which is exactly the
   observed behaviour and exactly Dan's complaint.
2. Concurrency limit of 1: is the played episode's in-flight work occupying the only slot,
   with no preemption and no round-robin? If so, four queued jobs behind one long episode
   is indistinguishable from a deadlock to the user.
3. backfill_jobs is EMPTY while analysis_assets.analysisState = 'backfill' for the played
   asset. A state named for a queue that has no row in it is worth explaining -- it may be
   benign, or it may be the same "a value that names one thing read as another" defect.

## Acceptance

A completed download must reach meaningful analysis coverage WITHOUT the episode ever being
played, on a foregrounded charging device, within a bounded and stated time. Verify by
re-running exactly this experiment: clean container, download N, play zero, measure
analysis_jobs.state and per-asset coverage after a stated interval.

Whatever the fix, it needs the same bound every bead in this arc has needed: dispatch must
make PROGRESS, and "queued forever" must become a surfaced, counted, terminal condition
rather than silence.

Supersedes the framing in [[playhead-kq25]], which guessed "analysis requires playback"
from a correlation on the old DB. The correlation was real; this is the mechanism, and it
is sharper -- the work is created, it is simply never dispatched.
## ESCALATION 2026-07-31 ~15:15 — it is not just the UNPLAYED episodes

Re-pulled the device DB ~25 min after the clean install. The PLAYED episode (DE0784D8,
92 min) has now finished transcription:

    fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime  5522 / 5522 s  (100%)
    featureCoverageEndTime         5522 / 5522 s  (100%)
    confirmedAdCoverageEndTime     0.0 s
    semantic_scan_results          0 ROWS
    backfill_jobs                  0 ROWS  (the queue that drives ad scanning is EMPTY)
    ad_windows                     11      (deterministic detectors only)
    analysis_jobs                  still 5 preAnalysis / queued / gotT=0

So a fully transcribed, fully feature-extracted episode sitting on the device has had
**ZERO semantic ad scan**. Not a partial scan, not a failed scan — no scan row was ever
created. And `backfill_jobs` is empty, so nothing is even QUEUED to scan it.

**On this clean install, no episode in the library has been ad-scanned at all.** Ad
detection is, end to end, not running.

This widens the bead. The original filing said queued preAnalysis jobs are never
dispatched. That is still true and still needs fixing, but it is now clearly ONE of at
least two independent stalls:

  A. preAnalysis jobs enqueue and never dispatch (5 queued, 0 progress).
  B. Transcription CAN complete without anything ever enqueueing the ad scan that consumes
     it. Nothing writes a backfill_jobs row for a transcribed asset.

(B) is the one that matters most for the release gate, because the gate is detection
quality and (B) means detection never runs. Investigate what is supposed to create the
backfill_jobs row once transcript coverage is sufficient, and why it did not fire for an
asset at 100% transcript. Note playhead-i7qe covered assets stalling in backfill with a
100% transcript — but that assumed a backfill row EXISTS. Here there is none.

Also re-examine: analysis_assets.analysisState = 'backfill' for this asset while
backfill_jobs is empty. A state named for a queue with no row in it is exactly this repo's
recurring defect shape, and it may be the direct cause — if some selector reads the STATE
as proof of enqueue rather than checking the queue, the asset is parked forever.
## RETRACTION 2026-07-31 15:08 — the escalation above is WRONG on point (B)

Dan: "its possible the transcript had JUST finished when you checked. Try pulling again."
He was right. Re-pulled at 15:08:06:

    backfill_jobs: 1 row
        jobId fm-be3e5, asset DE0784D8, phase=fullEpisodeScan, status=RUNNING,
        coveragePolicy=fullCoverage, priority=5, retryCount=0, deferReason=none,
        created 15:05:47

**Point (B) is RETRACTED. The ad-scan hand-off works.** Transcript completed ~15:05 and a
fullEpisodeScan backfill job was created and started at 15:05:47. My "backfill_jobs is EMPTY,
nothing is even queued to scan it" was a snapshot taken at 14:53, BEFORE the precondition
(transcript complete) was met. I read an absence caused by "not yet" as an absence caused by
"never". Do not act on point (B).

Capability snapshot at the same moment confirms the engine is healthy, so nothing is being
silently skipped: foundationModelsAvailable true, foundationModelsUsable true,
appleIntelligenceEnabled true, contextSize 4096, thermalState 2, isLowPowerMode false,
157 GB free.

## What SURVIVES, and it is still the bead

Point (A) stands, unchanged and now sharper:

    analysis_jobs: 5 preAnalysis / queued / transcriptCoverageSec 0 / attemptCount 0
    last updatedAt across ALL FIVE: 14:51:13  -- untouched for 17 minutes

Five queued jobs, zero attempts, not one row touched since a minute after they were created.
Meanwhile the PLAYED episode went all the way through transcription and into an FM scan.

## The observed timeline is itself the discriminating evidence

    14:50:42  5 preAnalysis jobs created (5 downloads)
    14:51:13  jobs last touched -- nothing since
    14:51:25  asset row created for the PLAYED episode
    ~15:05    played episode transcript reaches 100% (~14 min for 92 min of audio)
    15:05:47  fullEpisodeScan enqueued AND started for the played episode

The played episode monopolised the pipeline for its entire ~14-minute transcription and then
immediately took the next stage too. That is consistent with BOTH surviving hypotheses:

  1. playback-context gate (only the playing episode is eligible), and
  2. concurrency limit of 1 with no round-robin (the played episode held the only slot).

**The discriminating experiment is now available and cheap**: the played episode has finished
transcription and moved to the FM scan phase. If a queued preAnalysis job starts while the FM
scan runs, the limit is per-stage/concurrency (2). If all five stay queued with attemptCount 0
until playback happens again, it is a playback gate (1). Re-pull and check
analysis_jobs.state/attemptCount. Prefer this over reading code first — it settles it in one
observation.
## ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-07-31 (investigation agent, evidence below)

**The run loop's post-selection DEPTH filter misclassifies every user-initiated download as
Background-lane work, and the Background lane only opens at QualityProfile `.nominal`. The
device has been at `.serious`/`.fair` throughout, so all five jobs are selected, silently
skipped, and re-selected every 30 s, forever.**

The gate — AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:2598-2606 (run loop), duplicated at :2396-2402
(runSingleDispatchPass, which also serves the BGTask overnight drain):

    if job.jobType != "playback",
       !admission.allowsDeferredJob(desiredCoverageSec: job.desiredCoverageSec,
                                    t2Threshold: config.t2DepthSeconds) {
        logger.info("Skipping job ... under QualityProfile ...")
        await sleepOrWake(seconds: Self.rejectionBackoffSeconds)   // 30 s, re-select SAME job
        continue
    }

The classifier — AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:261-269:

    let isBackgroundLane = desiredCoverageSec >= t2Threshold      // t2 = 900 s
    if isBackgroundLane { return policy.allowBackgroundLane } else { return policy.allowSoonLane }

QualityProfile.swift:155-186: `allowBackgroundLane` is TRUE ONLY for `.nominal`. `.fair`
closes it; `.serious` closes Soon as well (the foreground-aggressive relaxation at :3179-3191
reopens ONLY Soon, deliberately).

### The two-commit pincer — and it is this repo's recurring defect shape

- **r835 era**: the depth test was written when every enqueue carried desiredCoverageSec = 90
  and the ladder escalated later. Depth ~= cost of the NEXT dispatch. Harmless.
- **playhead-3xtw (#262, "Download & Analyze")**: the tap path now stamps priority = 20 and
  desiredCoverage = FULL EPISODE DURATION at enqueue (EpisodePreparationCoordinator.swift
  :159/:170/:190 -> markEpisodeUserIntent :1090-1098 -> enqueue :772-776). From that commit on,
  **every user download >= 15 min is depth-classified as deep Background work on its very first
  dispatch, before one second of audio has been processed.**

`desiredCoverageSec` names the eventual coverage TARGET; `allowsDeferredJob` reads it as the
COST of the next dispatch. It reads 5417 whether the job has done 0 s or 5416 s of work.
Textbook instance of [[feedback_ask_what_the_quantity_measures_2026-07-29]].

**The bitter twist**: `LaneAdmission.allows(lane:)` at :285-292 — whose own doc comment says
Now-lane jobs are "user-initiated (Play / explicit Download) and must drain promptly even in
serious thermal states" — is **DEAD CODE with zero callers**. Priority 20 maps to `.now`
(:5673). The r835 design intended exactly these five jobs to dispatch; the shipped run loop
uses the depth dual instead and ignores priority entirely.

### Evidence, and all three of my hypotheses refuted

- **NOT a concurrency slot**: lane counters only count jobs that `didStart`; none ever started
  (no lease, `work_journal` empty). The FM scan runs via a DIFFERENT path —
  AdmissionController.swift:150 gates only on `pauseAllWork` (i.e. `.critical`) — which is why
  the FM scan runs happily at serious while this lane is frozen. Sharpest form: between 14:51
  and 15:05 the hot path transcribed 70+ min while the scheduler loop sat completely free and
  still dispatched nothing.
- **NOT a playback-episode gate**: no dispatch predicate compares the job's episode to the
  playing one. The correlation is indirect — the played episode's whole pipeline ran through
  the playback hot path and backfill lanes, NEVER touching its own analysis_jobs row (that row
  still reads transcriptCoverageSec=0). The played episode is not the one job that dispatches;
  it is the one episode that does not need this queue.
- **NOT a missing selector**: fetchNextEligibleJob (AnalysisStore.swift:13034-13051) DOES
  select these rows. They are selected, then skipped.
- **Elimination chain in the DB**: rows exist (enqueue worked) -> never leased (attemptCount=0
  and updatedAt untouched; lease acquisition writes both) -> never reached the multi-resource
  gate (since gy2s RC-2 a hard reject durably writes lastRejectReason at :3088-3099; all five
  are NULL). The ONLY silent, DB-invisible skip between selection and the gate is the depth
  filter at :2598.
- **Profile evidence**: asset-lifecycle-log stamps schedulerQualityProfile "serious" at 14:51:25
  and 14:52:34; capabilitySnapshot shows thermalState 2, isCharging false. And the starvation is
  SELF-SUSTAINING: the transcription/FM work that IS admitted keeps the SoC at serious, which
  keeps this lane shut.

**Honest gap**: the depth filter deliberately writes nothing, so its firing cannot be proven
from the DB. The clinching witness is in the unified log — "Skipping job ... (depth=...s) under
QualityProfile serious", subsystem com.playhead, category WorkScheduler, repeating every ~30 s.
One `log show --predicate 'subsystem == "com.playhead"'` settles it.

### Fix options — the lane matrix is ratified thermal policy, so the choice is DAN'S

- **A. Honour the lane** (restores r835's written intent, minimal diff): use the dead
  `admission.allows(lane: job.schedulerLane)` at both gate sites. User Now-lane jobs dispatch
  under fair/serious; auto (priority 0) stays nominal-only. Caveat 1: one dispatch currently
  runs the full [0, desiredCoverageSec] (runner request :3495-3507), so this admits a
  multi-minute burn at serious — though the hot path and FM lane ALREADY run full episodes at
  serious; preAnalysis is the only lane observing this gate. Caveat 2: the SQL's
  `deferredWorkAllowed` bind (:2520) must also learn about Now-lane rows.
- **B. Classify by INCREMENT, not target**: gate on the next dispatch's actual work
  (min(desired - transcriptCoverageSec, tierStep)). Preserves the thermal intent literally;
  larger change to the runner contract.
- **C. The bound (REQUIRED regardless)**: record the skip durably
  (recordJobAdmissionReject(reason: "depthGate:<profile>")) counting CONSECUTIVE skips; surface
  it in Activity ("waiting for device to cool"); and enforce a progress floor so a job queued
  beyond X minutes with attemptCount==0 gets one Soon-depth slice at fair/serious (never
  critical).

Recommendation: A (or B) plus C. A without C leaves the next misclassification silent again.

### Blast radius

Two call sites only (:2598 run loop, :2396 BGTask drain) — so **the overnight recovery path is
equally frozen** except when an idle device reads nominal, which is why overnight-on-charger
eventually drains while a foregrounded working device never does. Do NOT touch the
QualityProfile matrix (4 documented consumers, QualityProfile.swift:137-145) — it is
bead-ratified thermal policy from playhead-5ih; only the scheduler's classifier is at fault.
## DECIDED — Dan, 2026-07-31: OPTION A

> "let's do a"

Wire up the existing, currently-dead `LaneAdmission.allows(lane:)` (AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift
:285-292) at both depth-filter sites (:2598-2606 run loop, :2396-2402 runSingleDispatchPass) in
place of the `allowsDeferredJob(desiredCoverageSec:t2Threshold:)` depth test. User Now-lane jobs
(priority 20, mapped at :5673) dispatch under fair/serious; auto priority-0 work stays
nominal-only. This restores the r835 design that the dead method's own doc comment describes.

Option B (classify by increment) is NOT chosen. Do not implement it.

### Rationale recorded, because this admits compute at `.serious`

The hot path and the FM/backfill lane ALREADY run full episodes at serious — AdmissionController
.swift:150 gates only on `pauseAllWork` (i.e. `.critical`). preAnalysis is the ONLY lane
observing this thermal gate. That asymmetry is what makes this an oversight rather than a policy
being overturned. The QualityProfile matrix itself (QualityProfile.swift:137-186, 4 documented
consumers, ratified in playhead-5ih) is NOT to be modified — only the scheduler's classifier.

### MANDATORY, ships with A (this is option C, not optional)

1. **Record the skip.** The depth filter currently writes nothing, which is why attemptCount=0
   and lastRejectReason=NULL made this invisible for weeks. Call
   `recordJobAdmissionReject(reason: "depthGate:<profile>")` at both sites.
2. **Count CONSECUTIVE skips, not lifetime.** Every bead in this arc has needed this bound.
3. **Surface it.** A job held for thermal reasons must be visible ("waiting for device to cool"),
   not silent. Silence is what made this bug survive.
4. **Progress floor.** A job queued beyond a stated interval with attemptCount == 0 gets one
   Soon-depth (<= t1DepthSeconds) slice admitted at fair/serious — never at critical. "Queued
   forever" must become a surfaced, counted, bounded state.

### Do not forget

`fetchNextEligibleJob`'s `deferredWorkAllowed` bind (AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:2520) must also
learn about Now-lane rows, or under unrelaxed `.serious` the SQL still hides them and the fix is
inert. The investigation flagged this explicitly as Caveat 2.

### Verification

Unit-testable via the profile matrix. Field-verifiable on Dan's device by the same experiment
that found it: downloads present, `analysis_jobs` state/attemptCount, device warm at serious.
## QUEUE — Dan 2026-07-31

Batch position **1** of 4: ewag -> qs0d -> ynmk -> d3g0.

Dan: "agree on order. I won't dogfood until all are done though" — so there is **NO intermediate
device build**. All four land, then ONE build, then one dogfood pass. Do not stop to install
between beads.
## QUEUE REVISED — Dan 2026-07-31 15:35

qk44 inserted SECOND. Batch is now **5** beads, position **1**:

    ewag -> qk44 -> qs0d -> ynmk -> d3g0

Rationale: ewag makes work START, qk44 makes it FINISH. Without qk44 the other three have
nothing to act on — a build after ewag+qs0d+ynmk+d3g0 alone would still detect ZERO ads,
because the lane that actually scans hangs silently. qs0d in particular cannot be validated
with no scans running.

Still NO intermediate device build. All five land, then one build, then dogfood.

comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED — Option A + the full bound. PR #310, branch bead/playhead-ewag.

Fix: gate on LaneAdmission.allows(lane:) at BOTH sites (run loop + runSingleDispatchPass,
which serves drainEligible and therefore the BGTask overnight drain). QualityProfile matrix
untouched. allowsDeferredJob deleted; its four matrix tests restated onto allows(lane:).

Caveat 2 handled: fetchNextEligibleJob gained a Now-lane carve-out (plus its Swift mirror in
isEligibleForDispatch) sharing one nowLanePriorityFloor constant with AnalysisJob.schedulerLane.
Without it the SELECT hides every non-playback row at unrelaxed .serious and the fix is inert.

Bound shipped: durable laneGate:<profile> advisory on every hold; LaneHoldRecord with
CONSECUTIVE skip count cleared on dispatch; live cause fed to the Activity provider (its
cause: input was a hardcoded nil, so a held episode was indistinguishable from an idle queue)
with the cause derived honestly as lowPowerMode / batteryLowUnplugged / thermal rather than
assuming thermal from the severity; progress floor admitting ONE Soon-depth slice to a job
queued >10 min with attemptCount == 0, never at .critical, capped at min(desired, t1Depth),
never persisted.

Verification: RED first (3 assertions committed separately at 98ca941c, all failed pre-fix).
Mutation battery of 4 — all killed with clean attribution. Full gate exit 65, 30 failures, ALL
>=112s (load-flake band); the two dispatch-adjacent suites pass in isolation in 8.2s/10.1s.

ROOT-CAUSE ANALYSIS CONFIRMED, with one correction: the analysis said allowsDeferredJob has a
priority-derived DUAL that is dead code. Correct. But it also implied the depth gate alone
starved the jobs — in the FOREGROUND state the field device was in, the foreground-aggressive
relaxation reopens Soon, so the rows WERE selected and the depth filter was indeed the only
skip. In the BACKGROUND/unrelaxed .serious state the SQL hides them one step EARLIER, so there
are two independent stalls on the two paths, not one. Both are fixed; only fixing the depth
gate would have left the overnight BGTask drain frozen.

title: Uncertain-ad banner fires on DETECTION delivery, not when the playhead reaches the span
description:
Found by Dan on device 2026-07-31, on a CLEAN install (fresh container, main @ a4d5ad32).

> "the banner is showing up whenever an uncertain ad is detected, NOT when the playback
> head is playing over that span. That's a real issue"

Confirmed in source. The uncertain/suggest banner has NO playhead gate at all.

## The path

  SkipOrchestrator.receiveAdWindows(_:)          line 1964  <- DETECTION delivery
      -> registerSuggestedWindow(adWindow)       line 2246  (inside receiveAdWindows, which
                                                             ends at retireAdWindows:2389)
          -> emitSuggestBanner(for: adWindow)    lines 1156 and 1169
              -> AdSkipBannerItem(...)           line 1008

  SkipOrchestrator.updatePlayheadTime(_:)        line 2706  <- contains NO banner emission
                                                                whatsoever

## Why this is wrong, and why it is not merely cosmetic

The suggest banner asks the listener a question -- "was that an ad?" -- about a span. The
question is only answerable if the listener has just HEARD the span. Firing on detection
delivery means:

- The banner can ask about audio minutes AHEAD of the playhead, which the listener has not
  heard and cannot judge.
- It can ask about audio already passed, long after the moment.
- Detection delivery is BATCHED, so several banners can arrive at once, none of them
  corresponding to what is currently playing.
- Worst: the answer is recorded as user feedback. A "yes" given about the wrong span
  teaches the system the wrong thing, and per the fidelity ladder a marking outranks
  banner response and inferred revert -- so bad banner input is PERSISTED at high rank.

## Contrast: the auto-skip banner is already correct

emitBannerItem(for: ManagedWindow) at line 999 is documented as emitting "after an
automatic skip is actually applied" -- i.e. it is driven by the playhead reaching and
crossing the span. That is the correct shape. The suggest path simply never got the same
treatment.

## What the fix must preserve (do not regress these)

- The existing "fires at most once per window per episode" guarantee.
- The pending-suggestion replay when a Now Playing host attaches late (there is explicit
  handling for suggestions produced while Now Playing is absent -- these must still be
  delivered once, but gated on position, not dropped).
- The evidence-catalog snapshot semantics: a banner carries the evidence snapshot taken at
  EMIT time, and late catalogs do not retroactively update already-emitted banners. Moving
  the emit point later actually IMPROVES this -- the snapshot will be richer.
- discardAllOnPlaybackContextChange / discardAllOnHostDisappear behaviour.

## Suggested shape

Register the suggested window on receiveAdWindows (keep that -- the orchestrator needs to
know about it), but ARM it rather than emit. Emit from updatePlayheadTime when the playhead
enters the span (or, better, when it EXITS / has heard enough of it -- an ad the listener
is 2 s into is not yet judgeable). Decide the trigger point deliberately and write the
choice down: "entered", "heard N seconds of", and "finished" are three different products.

Seeking must not re-fire an already-answered window; recordUserSeek(to:) at line 2739 is
the natural place to reason about that.

## Open question for Dan (product, not engineering)

Should the banner fire on ENTERING the span, or after the listener has heard it? Firing on
entry interrupts the ad they are about to hear; firing after means the question arrives
once they have the information to answer it. My recommendation is after -- the banner is a
CORRECTION affordance, and you cannot correct something you have not heard.

Related: [[playhead-2350]] auto-skip safety gate, [[playhead-1mq1.1]] banner copy.
## QUEUE POSITION

Dan 2026-07-31: this runs immediately AFTER playhead-y8f3 (bounded cap-out retry), which is
in flight. Do not start it before y8f3 merges.

Note it is deliberately ordered BEFORE playhead-ewag despite both being P0. ewag is under
investigation and its fix is not yet scoped; this one is fully diagnosed and its blast
radius is understood, so it is the one that can actually be picked up and finished.
## DECIDED — Dan, 2026-07-31: fire on ENTRY

> "when it enters so I can skip."

Trigger: the playhead ENTERING the span. Not after the listener has heard it. This closes the
open question above; the "fire after hearing" recommendation is RETRACTED, do not revive it.

### What this decision changes beyond the trigger time

The banner is a **prospective skip affordance**, not a retrospective correction. It exists so
Dan can act on an ad he is about to hear. That reorders everything downstream:

- **The primary action is SKIP, not "was that an ad?"** Copy and button order must lead with
  the skip. Feedback capture is a secondary effect of the same tap. Coordinate with
  [[playhead-1mq1.1]] (banner copy pass) — that bead's copy was written for a different
  interaction model and should be re-read against this.
- **A tap at entry is a PREDICTION, not an observation.** The listener has heard ~0 s of the
  span when they answer. This is the mechanical reason banner response sits BELOW transcript
  marking on the fidelity ladder, and it means an entry-fired "yes" is weaker evidence than a
  post-hearing one would have been. Do not let this feedback outrank a user marking. See the
  fidelity ladder: transcript marking > banner response > inferred listenRevert.
- **Latency is now correctness, not polish.** A banner that appears 3 s into the ad has missed
  the point of the decision — the listener is already hearing what they wanted to skip. The
  position observer's tick granularity and the emit path's main-actor hop are now on the
  critical path and need a stated budget.
- **The pre-roll case is real**: an ad starting at 0:00 means the banner fires the instant
  playback starts. Decide deliberately whether that is wanted or whether pre-roll gets
  different treatment — do not let it fall out of the implementation by accident.
- **Re-entry on seek.** Scrubbing backwards into an already-answered span must not re-fire.
  `recordUserSeek(to:)` (SkipOrchestrator.swift:2739) is the place to reason about this. The
  existing once-per-window-per-episode guarantee must be preserved.

### Still true from the original filing

The defect is unchanged: emission happens on DETECTION delivery
(`registerSuggestedWindow` at :2246, inside `receiveAdWindows` 1964-2389) and
`updatePlayheadTime` (:2706) emits nothing. Keep registering the window on receive — the
orchestrator needs to know about it — but ARM rather than emit, and emit from the position
path on entry.
## FIELD PROOF 2026-07-31 — the harm is measured, not hypothetical

Dan: "i'm worried then, because i just corrected two mid-roll false positive ads."

correction_events from the device, episode DE0784D8 (92 min):

    14:53:05   bannerSuggestionConfirmed   210- 240 s   (3.5 min into the episode)
    14:53:23   bannerSuggestionConfirmed  2670-2700 s   (44.5 min in)   +17.9 s
    14:53:25   bannerSuggestionConfirmed  4800-4950 s   (80 min in)     +20.1 s
    15:11:35   manualVeto  falsePositive   210- 240 s   +18.5 min
    15:13:01   manualVeto  falsePositive  4800-4950 s   +20.0 min

**Three spans located 3.5, 44.5 and 80 minutes into the episode were confirmed within 20.1
SECONDS of each other.** It is physically impossible to have heard them. The banners arrived
as a detection batch; the user answered what he was asked; each answer authorised a skip of
audio he had never heard. ~18 minutes later, when playback actually REACHED those spans, two
were show content and were vetoed. One of them is 150 SECONDS of show.

Outcome: 2 of 3 banner confirmations were false positives, and all 3 were skipped
(wasSkipped=1) before the listener could evaluate any of them. That is the failure mode this
bead predicted, observed in the field within an hour of filing.

This also poisons the learning signal: three `falseNegative` corrections were written at
explicit-feedback fidelity, two of which are now contradicted by `falsePositive` vetoes on the
identical span. See [[feedback_manual_marks_override_2026-07-29]] — the ladder resolved it
correctly, but it should never have been asked to.

## A SECOND, SEPARABLE DEFECT FOUND HERE — filed separately

All three confirmed windows carried:
    confidence 0.40 - 0.42
    startEdgeAnchor = unanchored,  endEdgeAnchor = unanchored
    eligibilityGate = markOnly
Confirming promoted them to decisionState=applied, wasSkipped=1, eligibilityGate cleared.

**A banner tap bypassed the playhead-2350 unanchored-edge auto-skip safety gate.** That gate
exists to stop low-confidence unanchored windows from eating show content; one tap walked
around it. Fixing d3g0's TIMING alone would not have prevented the 150 s loss if the user had
tapped yes at the right moment on a 0.40-confidence unanchored window. Both need fixing.
## QUEUE — Dan 2026-07-31

Batch position **4** of 4: ewag -> qs0d -> ynmk -> d3g0.

Dan: "agree on order. I won't dogfood until all are done though" — so there is **NO intermediate
device build**. All four land, then ONE build, then one dogfood pass. Do not stop to install
between beads.
## QUEUE REVISED — Dan 2026-07-31 15:35

qk44 inserted SECOND. Batch is now **5** beads, position **5**:

    ewag -> qk44 -> qs0d -> ynmk -> d3g0

Rationale: ewag makes work START, qk44 makes it FINISH. Without qk44 the other three have
nothing to act on — a build after ewag+qs0d+ynmk+d3g0 alone would still detect ZERO ads,
because the lane that actually scans hangs silently. qs0d in particular cannot be validated
with no scans running.

Still NO intermediate device build. All five land, then one build, then dogfood.

title: Background work never checkpoints: progressCursor is written only on completion, so every expired window discards its work
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-31 on the device pull. This is why background analysis never completes, and it is upstream of throughput, the planner, and the transcription ladder.

BACKFILL JOBS BY STATUS, AND WHO CARRIES A CHECKPOINT:

    status     n    progressCursor
    complete   37   PRESENT (26 distinct values)
    queued     35   EMPTY
    running     1   EMPTY
    failed      8   EMPTY
    deferred    3   EMPTY

`progressCursor` is a JSON checkpoint of the form
`{"lastProcessedUpperBoundSec":1140,"processedUnitCount":1}`. **It is only written when a job COMPLETES.** A job that is mid-flight, expires, fails or is deferred records nothing.

THE ARITHMETIC THAT FOLLOWS. From playhead-8bp2's measurement of the same device: iOS granted 14-38 BGTask windows per day (so this is NOT starvation — the 2026-07-22 incident was, this is not), yet every `backfill` window on 2026-07-29 ended `expired` after 26-295 SECONDS, and four ended `orphan_at_launch` after 1,825-3,036 s. From playhead-hvk0: a full-episode scan costs 12-45 MINUTES of FM wall-clock.

    work needed per episode   12-45 min
    work window granted       26-295 s
    progress retained on window expiry   NONE

**So the job restarts from zero every window, performs 30 s to 5 min of work, and discards it.** No number of granted windows can ever finish it. This is not a throughput shortage; it is a treadmill.

WHY THE OTHER FIXES DO NOT REACH IT:
  * playhead-8bp2 (merged) made the coverage ladder reach the whole episode instead of stopping at 15 min. Its own report flags that it proves the LADDER, not the DRAIN — this is the drain.
  * playhead-onn6 (merged) mints re-drive jobs. A re-drive that also cannot checkpoint just re-enters the treadmill.
  * playhead-8d5r (open, P0) compounds it viciously: a single failing FM call averages 174-582 s, so ONE failing call can consume an entire window AND lose all progress made in it. The two together are much worse than either alone.

ESTABLISH BEFORE BUILDING, do not assume:
  * **WHY is the cursor only written at completion?** Is it deliberate (a completed job's cursor is the resume point for the NEXT job) or is the mid-flight write simply missing? Read what `lastProcessedUpperBoundSec` is consumed by before adding a second meaning to it.
  * **Is the work unit resumable at all?** `processedUnitCount: 1` suggests coarse units. If a "unit" is a whole episode pass, a checkpoint mid-unit may be meaningless and the real fix is to make units smaller. Check the shard/window granularity the runner already has — `lastProcessedUpperBoundSec` implies a time cursor exists conceptually.
  * **Does the expiry handler get a chance to persist?** iOS gives an expiration callback with a short grace period. If the handler currently only marks state and does not flush a cursor, that is the cheapest possible fix and it is a few lines. playhead-wvdz and playhead-se2h both found expiry/failure paths that recorded nothing.
  * **Is a partial cursor SAFE to resume from?** If a pass writes rows as it goes, resuming mid-pass must not duplicate them — playhead-6av0 dealt with duplicated child rows, and playhead-0hi9 with split asset state. Check idempotency before enabling resume.

ACCEPTANCE:
  * Work performed in a background window SURVIVES the window ending. Prove it with a test that runs a partial pass, expires it, restarts, and asserts the second pass begins where the first stopped — asserting on SECONDS OF AUDIO PROCESSED, not on a row state.
  * Resume is idempotent: no duplicated chunks, spans or windows across a resumed pass.
  * Bounded — a job that makes no progress across N resumptions must terminate with a named cause rather than resuming forever. Seven beads in a row have landed on this rule.
  * Measured before/after on how much audio a fixed number of background windows can process.

DO NOT repair existing rows (the product owner has declined four times). Fix the path.

RELATED: playhead-8bp2 (ladder, merged — explicitly did not prove the drain), playhead-8d5r (failing FM calls burn the window, open P0), playhead-hvk0 (measured the per-episode cost), playhead-onn6 (mints the jobs that then treadmill), playhead-bbut (a drainEligible busy-spin under write-lock — check it is not related).

title: 48 failing FM calls consume 79% of all model wall-clock — a failure costs 35x a success and nothing bounds it
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-30 on the device pull. This is why analysis never finishes, and it is a bigger term than transcription reach, the CoveragePlanner, or scheduling.

WHERE THE MODEL TIME GOES — all `semantic_scan_results`, by outcome:

    status                        calls   minutes    avg     % of FM wall-clock
    success                        200      56.1    16.8 s        20.8%
    permissive_decoding_failure     13      67.7   312.3 s        25.1%
    refusal                         20      58.2   174.5 s        21.6%
    failedTransient                  6      58.2   582.3 s        21.6%
    guardrailViolation               6      29.3   293.2 s        10.9%
    cancelled                        3       0.4     8.1 s         0.1%

**48 FAILING CALLS CONSUME 79% OF ALL MODEL WALL-CLOCK.** 200 successful calls consume 21%.

A SUCCESSFUL scan takes 16.8 s. A `failedTransient` takes 582 s — **35x longer, and it produces nothing.** `permissive_decoding_failure` averages 312 s; `guardrailViolation` 293 s; `refusal` 174 s. Every failure class is an order of magnitude more expensive than success.

THE CONSEQUENCE. Reclaiming even most of those 213 minutes would roughly QUADRUPLE productive scan throughput without touching the model, the prompt, the scheduler or the planner. playhead-hvk0 measured a full-episode scan at 12-45 min of FM wall-clock per episode and noted 92% of it goes to calls that fail — this is that finding, generalised across every scan on the device.

THE SHAPE, and it is familiar. playhead-se2h found the MODEL LOAD had no timeout anywhere in its chain, down through an unbounded `downloadAndInstall()`, so a stall became a permanent silent hang. This is the same defect one layer up: the INFERENCE calls appear to have no effective deadline either, so a call that will never succeed still blocks for minutes. Six beads in a row have landed on the rule that unbounded work is worse than the bug it was meant to avoid.

ESTABLISH BEFORE FIXING, do not assume:
  * IS THERE A TIMEOUT AT ALL on an FM inference call, and if so what is it? 582 s suggests either none or one far above any useful value.
  * ARE THE SLOW FAILURES SLOW BECAUSE THEY TIME OUT, or slow because the model genuinely grinds before refusing? Those need different fixes — a deadline versus a pre-flight admission check. `refusal` at 174 s is suspicious: a refusal is a MODEL DECISION, so the model produced a verdict and it still took three minutes.
  * IS `permissive_decoding_failure` RETRYING INTERNALLY? 312 s average over 13 calls is the largest single bucket; if it is retrying a decode that cannot succeed, that is a bounded-retry bug, not a latency one.
  * WHAT IS THE WINDOW SIZE RELATIONSHIP? Check whether slow calls correlate with larger windows — if so, the fix may be to cap window size rather than to add a deadline.
  * DO FAILURES BLOCK THE LANE? If these calls are serialised, 213 minutes of failure is also 213 minutes the successful work could not run. Establish whether this is throughput loss or merely wasted battery — the fix priority differs sharply.

ACCEPTANCE:
  * A bounded deadline per inference call, with the timeout NAMED as its own outcome rather than folded into an existing class. playhead-gqx4's `AdScanLimit` cause vocabulary is the established precedent.
  * Measured before/after on FM minutes-per-successful-scan, not on call counts.
  * MUST NOT convert a slow success into a failure. The distribution has successes at 16.8 s average, so headroom exists — but establish the success TAIL before choosing a deadline, or a legitimate slow scan gets killed and coverage silently drops. That would be a worse bug than the one being fixed.
  * Bounded retry with a no-progress guard if any retry is added.

DO NOT change the prompt, the model, the scorer or thresholds. This is about not spending ten minutes on a call that returns nothing.

RELATED: playhead-se2h (merged, the model-load half of the same defect class), playhead-hvk0 (merged, measured the per-episode cost), playhead-8bp2 (the transcription gap — necessary but NOT sufficient; transcribing more audio only feeds more work into a pipeline whose model time is 79% wasted), playhead-qbib (FM refusal must degrade locally, merged).

title: 66% of long-episode audio is never TRANSCRIBED — 19 assets in 'queued' hold 82% of the gap, across four distinct causes
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-30 on the device pull, after playhead-hvk0 refuted the planner as the reach bottleneck. This is the largest single term in reach by a wide margin.

WHERE THE AUDIO GOES. Of all long-episode (>15 min) audio on the device:
    66.4%  NEVER TRANSCRIBED
    28.2%  transcribed but never scanned
     5.4%  scanned

So the ad scanner is starved upstream. Every prompt, scorer, threshold and boundary change optimises a stage that never receives two-thirds of the audio.

THE GAP IS CONCENTRATED IN ONE STATE. Long episodes by `analysisState`:

    state                       n   avg transcript %   at >=95%   untranscribed
    queued                     19        33.4%             1         909 min
    backfill                    5        86.3%             4          98 min
    completeTranscriptPartial   3        60.2%             1          65 min
    failedFeature               1        37.8%             0          30 min
    completeFull                6       100.0%             6           0 min

**19 assets in `queued` hold 909 of the 1,102 untranscribed minutes — 82% of the entire gap.** They are not failing. They are not progressing.

AND IT IS FOUR DISTINCT SUB-PROBLEMS, not one. Joining those 19 against `analysis_jobs`:

    9 assets — job row state `queued`     -> dispatch/throughput: the work exists and is not being run
    4 assets — job row state `complete`   -> STATE INCONSISTENCY: the job says done while the asset
                                             sits at `queued` with ~33% transcript. One of these two
                                             records is lying.
    3 assets — NO JOB ROW AT ALL          -> nothing will ever pick them up
    2 assets — `superseded`               -> the playhead-y8f3 trap: UNIQUE workKey + INSERT OR IGNORE
                                             makes them permanently un-requestable
    1 asset  — `failed`

All 19 have a `sourceURL`, so this is NOT a download problem. 4 of the 19 have ZERO transcript.

DO NOT ASSUME THIS IS playhead-8ysk. That bead (147 acquired / 9 finalized) is MERGED, and playhead-i7qe/onn6 fixed the scan-side skip and re-drive. These four shapes are what remains, and at least two of them (the `complete`-job-but-`queued`-asset inconsistency, and the assets with no job row) are distinct defects that no merged bead addresses.

ESTABLISH BEFORE FIXING, and take the four separately:
  * The 9 `queued` jobs: is this scheduler throughput, an admission predicate, or BGTask starvation? RULE OUT STARVATION FIRST — an earlier "analysis stalled" report was NOT a code bug (iOS granted ~0 discretionary windows). The distinguishing evidence is whether foreground playback sessions occurred on those assets.
  * The 4 `complete`-job-but-`queued`-asset rows: which record is authoritative, and how did they diverge? This is the highest-value one to understand because it is a correctness bug, not a throughput one.
  * The 3 with no job row: is this the 7-day GC (which playhead-onn6 found deletes the workKey ledger), and does `discoverUnEnqueuedDownloads` own them?
  * The 2 superseded: playhead-y8f3 already owns the forward-looking half. Do not duplicate it.

SEQUENCING, per Dan 2026-07-30: transcription first, then playhead-b8hj, then flip playhead-hvk0's promotion gate ON once transcription is fixed. His reasoning for deferring the flip: paying hvk0's measured 3-10x FM wall-clock to scan transcripts that do not exist buys nothing.

MEASUREMENT NOTE: the ruler is trustworthy as of today — playhead-csbq fixed three scan-window producers reporting up to 294% of an episode scanned, and playhead-r5um fixed the atom ordering underneath it (`chunkIndex` is a shard-emission counter that resets to 0, leaving `transcriptVersion` undefined for 21 of 30 assets). Use `AnalysisCoverageSummary.adScanFraction`; do not introduce a second measure.

title: CoveragePlanner switches stranded episodes to targetedWithAudit, which by design never re-reads the episode — the largest remaining reach lever
description:
SURFACED 2026-07-30 by playhead-onn6's final report, which named it as "the next lever on reach, and it is a bigger one than this bead was". It was never filed. Filing it so the largest remaining term in coverage is not carried only in a merged agent's prose.

THE MECHANISM. onn6 measured that some stranded episodes have a FULLY DRAINED coverage lane — no resumable backfill_jobs row at all — because CoveragePlanner had switched them to the "targetedWithAudit" policy. That policy by design narrows scanning to anchor windows and never re-reads the whole episode. So onn6 correctly DECLINES to re-drive them: a pass would read no audio and achieve nothing. The decline is right; the underlying policy is what caps their coverage.

WHY IT IS THE BIGGEST REMAINING LEVER. What has landed, and what each bought:
  * playhead-pz32 — made the readiness checkmark honest. It had keyed on the DSP watermark and max(endTime) of detected ads, so an episode where detection did WORSE could read as MORE complete.
  * playhead-gqx4 — made the terminal state honest. The clean terminal now requires measured ad-scan coverage, and a short scan lands in a degraded terminal with a machine-readable cause.
  * playhead-i7qe — stopped a DISPATCHED run from skipping the scan. The skip predicate read "no candidate windows" as "nothing to do", but candidate windows are PRODUCED BY the scan, so their absence in unscanned audio meant nothing was ever proposed there.
  * playhead-onn6 — gave under-scanned episodes a bounded re-drive; 6 of Dan's 34 long episodes got a brand-new pass that would never have existed.

Between them the product now TELLS THE TRUTH about coverage and raises it wherever a lane is resumable. What it does NOT do is change how much audio the planner ever INTENDS to read. Measured on the 2026-07-29 device pull with pz32's definition: ZERO of 34 episodes over 15 minutes reach 95% ad-scan coverage; 29 are under 25%.

AND IT IS UPSTREAM OF ALL DETECTION-QUALITY WORK. Re-measured 2026-07-30 at N=44 rediff-confirmed slots: 27 of 44 (61%) have ZERO overlap with any pipeline window; 51% of all ad audio is lost to TOTAL MISSES versus 34% to narrow windows; and of the missed slots, ZERO were "candidate generated then rejected" while 17 had NO CANDIDATE AT ALL. Every prompt, scorer, fusion and threshold change optimises a stage that never sees the audio.

ESTABLISH BEFORE CHANGING ANYTHING — this is a policy decision with a real cost on the other side, not a bug with an obvious fix:
  * WHY does the planner switch to that mode? Find the trigger. It presumably exists to bound cost — battery, thermal, FM budget, wall-clock. Read that rationale before overriding it; the mode is probably correct for its intended case and wrong only as a TERMINAL state an episode can never leave.
  * Is the right change (a) a different trigger, (b) an escape so an episode in that mode can be promoted back to a full scan when cheap conditions hold (charging, wifi, idle, cool), or (c) a bounded widening of the audit itself? Prefer the smallest change that moves the measured number.
  * MEASURE THE COST, do not assume it. The policy exists for a reason. Quantify what full-scanning those episodes would cost before proposing to do it.
  * MUST stay bounded with a no-progress guard. Four beads in a row — gqx4, onn6, wvdz, se2h — hit the same rule: an unbounded retry or widen is a worse bug than the one being fixed.

A TRAP THAT IS AVAILABLE HERE. playhead-4xqf's original N=12 conclusion — "the pipeline detects most mid-rolls but collapses onto a tiny sub-span" — was a SELECTION ARTIFACT: it measured only PAIRS, which conditions on an overlap already existing, so a slot missed entirely could not appear in the sample. Conditioning on detection and then concluding detection works is circular. Any measurement here must include the episodes the planner never scanned, or it will report that the planner is fine.

Related: playhead-onn6 (merged; declines these episodes correctly), playhead-gqx4, playhead-i7qe, playhead-pz32, and playhead-4xqf (the width residual, which is the SMALLER half and sits downstream of this).

title: 0hi9's reconciliation duplicated 8,648 transcript_chunks rows: confirmed from the device database
description:
CONFIRMED FROM THE DEVICE DATABASE 2026-07-29 (52 MB pull, analysis.sqlite + WAL). playhead-0hi9's reconciliation IS the cause. Two competing hypotheses raised during investigation are refuted below.

=== THE MEASUREMENTS ===
transcript_chunks: 64,749 rows, 56,101 distinct by (analysisAssetId, segmentFingerprint) => 8,648 EXCESS ROWS.
Same-(asset,startTime,endTime) twin groups: 10,469. Of those, 10,452 have IDENTICAL text, 4,197 are mixed-pass (fast+final residue, a separate and partly legitimate phenomenon), 6,596 have IDENTICAL segmentFingerprint — i.e. genuine byte-identical duplicates.
Copies per twin group: 2 copies x 8,897 groups, 3 copies x 1,064, 4 copies x 494.
_meta: did_duplicate_asset_reconcile_v1 = 1, and ZERO episodes remain with more than one analysis_assets row — the sweep ran and consumed every pair.
Worst assets by twin groups: 144C8A80 (3,205), 8FECFDDE (2,196), B10C7BC8 (1,127), 4E4730D8 (843), 1A9616D1 (533).

=== THE DECISIVE DISCRIMINATOR ===
Of 10,455 twin groups keyed on (asset, startTime, endTime, text), **10,320 have DIFFERENT chunkIndex** and only 135 share one.

That is the signature of SEPARATE TRANSCRIPTION RUNS, each numbering its chunks from 0 independently, subsequently merged onto one asset. Identical text and identical times because both runs transcribed the same audio; different indexes because each counted its own chunks from zero. And critically: the pre-insert dedupe probe hasTranscriptChunk is ASSET-SCOPED (AnalysisStore.swift:9006-9008), so it could never have seen across the asset boundary — which is exactly the condition repointChildRows creates by moving rows wholesale.

Corroborating: colliding chunk indexes run CONTIGUOUSLY FROM 0 on every affected asset (lowIdx = 0 universally), consistent with complete 0-based sequences interleaved rather than scattered collisions. The 2/3/4-copy distribution matches episodes whose merged assets carried one, two or three prior runs between them.

=== REFUTED HYPOTHESES — recorded so they are not re-raised ===
1. playhead-kcz.1 (94809607, Jul 25) unmasking pre-existing rows. REFUTED. Its removed collapse grouped by chunkIndex and kept one row per index; these twins have DIFFERENT indexes, so that collapse would never have hidden them. kcz.1's second change (selection identity moving to (startTime,endTime)) IS what makes the pair co-select, so it shapes the SYMPTOM, but it did not create or reveal the rows.
2. The correction/scoring path. REFUTED at the call graph. No production path writes transcript_chunks in response to a user gesture; recordFalseNegative (the only synthetic-span minter) has zero production callers; the veto writes correction_events and updates ad_windows only. Separately confirmed: correction_events has a UNIQUE identity index, so the owner's repeated taps this morning collapsed to ONE row with submissionCount bumped, not one row per attempt.
3. playhead-u45d's read pair. REFUTED. fetchDecodedSpansIncludingUserVetoed is never called on the peek path; LiveTranscriptPeekDataSource.fetchSnapshot calls each read exactly once and combines nothing.

=== WHY THE OWNER COULD NOT TELL IT WAS A MERGED EPISODE ===
The sweep calls deleteAssetRow(id: victim.id) (AnalysisStore.swift:15539), destroying its own evidence. After it runs there is no way from the app to know an episode was ever a pair. His report that the affected episode was "not one of the split pairs" is therefore not observable and should not have been treated as evidence against the merge — 14 of his 25 episodes were pairs.

=== A SECOND, PRE-EXISTING DEFECT SURFACED BY THE SAME DATA — file separately, do not fix here ===
chunkIndex is not unique and is never seeded from the store's max. TranscriptEngineService.chunkCounter resets to 0 at four sites (:648, :746, :801, :866); grep finds no MAX(chunkIndex) anywhere; there is no unique index on (analysisAssetId, chunkIndex). Any episode transcribed across more than one engine session accumulates index collisions independently of any merge. That is a writer-side data-shape problem and it is why ORDER BY chunkIndex gives SQLite an unordered tie-break, so display order among colliding rows is not stable across refreshes.

=== SCOPE, UNCHANGED FROM THE ORIGINAL BRIEF ===
Prevention AND cleanup — 8,648 excess rows are on disk now and did_duplicate_asset_reconcile_v1 is set, so nothing revisits them. Cleanup key for transcript_chunks is (analysisAssetId, pass, segmentFingerprint) — pass must stay in the key because computeFinalPassFingerprint deliberately prefixes fp-final- so a final row never dedupes against its fast twin. Keep the lowest rowid per group. Deletions MUST go through SQL so the FTS triggers fire (AnalysisStore.swift:7590-7617) or transcript_chunks_ad leaves ghosts in the FTS index. Leave chunkIndex alone or reassign wholesale, since nextFinalChunkIndex reads max(chunkIndex)+1. Add the UNIQUE INDEX afterwards — repointChildRows' UPDATE OR IGNORE is ALREADY WRITTEN to do the right thing the moment such a constraint exists; it is inert today only because the constraint is missing.
Assess decoded_spans and ad_windows for the same treatment; decoded_spans duplication is invisible on this screen but corrupts loadSyntheticOrdinalTimeMap and the corpus/egress path.
DO NOT dedupe in the view. DO NOT restore any display-level collapse.
acceptance_criteria: Cause confirmed by evidence — either the affected episode is a reconciled pair and duplicate rows exist in decoded_spans, or it is the read path. The reconciliation cannot create duplicate spans for the same audio. Dan's device is CLEANED UP, not just protected going forward, since the duplicates are already there. Established whether any downstream consumer double-counted duplicated spans as evidence. NOT fixed by deduping in the view. A regression covers merging two assets whose spans cover the same audio.

title: Ad-window boundaries are shifted inward: too narrow at the free episode edges, too wide where they eat the show
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-29 against the 52 MB device pull. Dan's observation is CONFIRMED IN DIRECTION, the policy is justified, and the mechanism it needs ALREADY EXISTS with the wrong constant.

=== PROVENANCE FIRST — most "corrections" are not ground truth ===
83 correction events across 9 episodes; most had to be discarded before any number meant anything:
 - All four banner* sources record THE DETECTOR ROW'S OWN EXTENT verbatim (SkipOrchestrator.swift:4116, 4232, 5154). Circular. Discarded (9).
 - The player's "Hearing an ad" button records NO user extent. It seeds BoundaryExpander, whose top branch returns the union of existing detector windows if the seed is within +/-5s, and whose fallback is SEED +/- 30s. That is the origin of every exactly-60.000s "correction".
 - Only TranscriptPeekView.submitMarkedChunks yields a real user extent, and it is identifiable because BOTH endpoints land exactly on a transcript_chunks boundary.
Of 54 falseNegative marks: 37 chunk-exact (real), 14 expander-derived (prove an ad was audible; edges are artifacts — used only to extend a pod, never to set an edge), 3 detector echoes. Of 18 manualVeto: 10 user chunk-selections, 8 popover vetoes carrying the detector's extent. Episode 1A9616D1 dropped entirely (only correctionReplay echoes of itself).
RESULT: 8 episodes, 20 truth pods — 8 pre-roll, 6 mid-roll, 6 post-roll. Position derived per the AdDetectionService.swift:1446-1448 precedent (pre: starts <=120s; post: ends >= duration-180s; else mid).

=== PER-EDGE SIGNED ERROR (detected - truth; + = later in the episode) ===
  edge               class          n   median   mean    range
  pre-roll START     OUTER/free     6   +13.4    +24.0   -4.0 .. +74.6
  pre-roll END       INNER/costly   6    +1.4     +0.1   -49.0 .. +29.7
  mid-roll START     inner          5   +63.4   +100.4    0.0 .. +295.0
  mid-roll END       inner          5   -49.7    -47.9  -124.0 .. +11.9
  post-roll START    INNER/costly   3   -97.9    -69.8  -116.4 .. +5.0
  post-roll END      OUTER/free     3   -35.9    -25.2   -40.2 .. +0.4

=== VERDICT: confirmed in DIRECTION, not universal in FORM ===
The strict "both edges moved the same way" form holds in only 3/6 pre-roll and 2/4 post-roll — weak at this n. But the two OPERATIVE halves hold much better:
 - OUTER EDGE UNDER-REACHES THE FREE BOUNDARY: 7 of 10 outer edges with any detection. Pre-roll misses t=0 by >1s in 4/6 (by 11.8, 15.0, 46.4, 74.6s). Post-roll misses EOF by >1s in 3/4 (by 35.9, 40.2, 157.3s).
 - INNER EDGE OVER-REACHES INTO THE SHOW, corroborated by FOUR VETOES — Dan explicitly said "not an ad" on the over-run, so this is not arithmetic: 752926FF vetoed 86.8-100.8 just past a pre-roll ending 79.6; 8FECFDDE vetoed 90.3-119.9 just past a pre-roll ending 90.3; 70EC53D7 vetoed 1197.7-1252.4, the front 55s of a window running 97.9s back into the show; 8FECFDDE vetoed 3492.4-3498.5 inside a window ending 0.5s before the true post-roll BEGAN.
MID-ROLL IS A DIFFERENT FAILURE, NOT A SHIFTED ONE. Both edges move inward (start +63.4, end -49.7): 3/5 strictly narrower, 0/5 shifted. That is boundary COLLAPSE — playhead-4xqf's finding, unchanged.

=== THE FREE EDGES — the strongest single result ===
Pre-roll truth starts <=5s in 8/8 pods; 5/8 have a chunk-exact mark starting at <=4.02s (0.00, 0.18, 0.42, 0.72, 4.02).
Post-roll truth ends within 2.23s of EOF in 6/6 pods, ALL SIX chunk-exact (0.00, 0.15, 0.20, 0.39, 2.04, 2.23).
FREE AD-SECONDS LEFT AUDIBLE: 147.8s at the top + 233.4s at the tail = 381.2s across 8 episodes, ~48s/episode.
Note 2/8 pre-roll and 2/6 post-roll pods had NO detector window in the region at all — a snap has nothing to snap. Those are detection misses, not edge errors.

=== RESIDUAL AFTER A POSITIONAL SNAP (outer snapped, inner untouched) ===
  position  pods(w/detection)  ad-secs  covered now  after snap  residual share
  pre       8 (6)               601.8    43.6%        68.2%       16.0%
  mid       6 (5)              1008.3    11.4%        11.4%       74.6%
  post      6 (4)               321.8    20.4%        64.8%        9.5%
  TOTAL     20 (15)            1931.8    22.9%        38.0%
The snap closes ~15 points, about 34% of the current gap, and AFTER IT 75% OF WHAT REMAINS IS MID-ROLL where neither edge is free.

=== COST ACCOUNTING — the decisive number ===
  pre-roll snap:                    147.8s ad recovered,  0.2s non-ad claimed
  post-roll snap, naive:            142.9s recovered,    94.8s non-ad
  post-roll snap, GUARDED (only if detected end already within 60s of EOF): 76.1s recovered, 2.2s non-ad
  BOTH, GUARDED:                    223.9s recovered,     2.4s non-ad  =  94 : 1
The naive post-roll cost is 92.6s from ONE episode whose last window was disjoint from the ad. The guard fixes it, but that 60s threshold is FITTED ON n=4 — a starting point to measure, not a constant.

=== THE MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS ===
PreRollStartClamp SHIPS ON TODAY (Playhead/Services/AdDetection/PreRollStartClamp.swift, playhead-xsdz.66, landed 2026-07-22, wired at AdDetectionService.swift:5859). It does exactly the right thing — first visible window only, .unanchored start only, demoted to mark-only — but its ceiling is maxPreRollStartSeconds = 20.0 (AdDetectionService.swift:995). Of the 6 observed pre-roll starts it covers 11.8 and 15.0; it does NOT cover 46.4 and 74.6. RIGHT MECHANISM, WRONG NUMBER.
There is NO post-roll analogue. postRollGuardSeconds = 90.0 (playhead-wraj) is a DEMOTION guard and is inert behind certaintyTieredSkipEnabled: false.

=== RECOMMENDATION — two edits, not a new subsystem ===
1. RAISE maxPreRollStartSeconds. Measure 45 / 90 / 120. The existing safety structure (first-visible-window-only, unanchored-only, mark-only demotion) is what makes a wider ceiling safe and it is already there.

1. A MARK IS NOT A CONSOLATION PRIZE. I wrote the demotion up as a preserved outcome.
