title: asr_failed still names an absence: the runner's zero-coverage branch journals it with no failure class when the engine reported nothing
description:
TRACED 2026-07-29. The one-line answer: transcriptFailure is nil on the most common route into the zero-coverage branch, which is the 300-SECOND TIMEOUT ARM — a literal `return (0, nil)` at AnalysisJobRunner.swift:656-659.

    group.addTask {
        try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(300))
        return (0, nil)
    }

AND `cause: .asrFailed` IS HARDCODED at :1413 and :1428 with NO reference to `failure` at all. So every path below is stamped asr_failed — including paths where ASR was provably never invoked, and paths where a CONTRADICTING failure_class sits in the same row's metadata. A row can read failure_class = no_shards while its cause column says ASR failed.

=== THE LIKELY DOMINANT CAUSE, AND IT IS NOT A FAILURE AT ALL ===
PlayheadRuntime.swift:804 builds ONE TranscriptEngineService and hands it to BOTH AnalysisCoordinator (:1466) and AnalysisJobRunner (:1619). Any of startTranscription (TranscriptEngineService.swift:473, which calls activeTask?.cancel()), handleScrub (:520) or handleSpeedChange (:537) cancels the RUNNER's loop. The loop returns silently, the runner waits out the full 300s, and journals asr_failed.

So: **the listener scrubbing, changing playback speed, or starting a different episode cancels analysis and it is recorded as an ASR failure.** Same for AnalysisCoordinator.cancelPipeline() -> transcriptEngine.stop() (AnalysisCoordinator.swift:1953). If this is what has been driving the 147-acquired / 9-finalized ratio, then a large share of "analysis failures" are ordinary app usage, and the completion problem is substantially a SHARED-RESOURCE problem rather than a transcription-quality problem. That would also explain why the failures are deterministic per episode (the user does the same things) and why retries never helped.

DO NOT treat that as established — it is the strongest hypothesis the enumeration supports, and fix 1 below is what will confirm or refute it on the next device pull.

=== ENUMERATION: paths reaching the zero-coverage branch with transcriptFailure == nil ===
Pre-stage-3 exits (decode threw :404, no shards :410, thermal :516, features :541, preempt :549-556) return directly and CANNOT reach the branch — the ~14 pipeline_error emitters are innocent here.
Three mechanics make transcriptFailure nil (observeTranscriptEvents :1327-1350): N1 the timeout child wins (:658); N2 .completed arrives and persistedCoverage() reads 0; N3 the stream ends with no terminal event — in production only after N1, because NOTHING in TranscriptEngineService ever calls continuation.finish().

 P1 shared engine re-tasked by playback (scrub / speed / new episode)   -> N1  asr_failed is WRONG
 P2 engine torn down by cancelPipeline()                                -> N1  WRONG
 P3 stop gate: TranscriptEngineStopped                                  -> N1  names the runner's own bookkeeping
 P4 .failed emitted then DESTROYED by emitEvent's stoppedAssetIds drop (:1533-1543); the runner inserts the asset at :701 BEFORE journaling at :729 -> the class existed and was thrown away 30 lines before the journal was written. WORST ONE.
 P5 classified shardFailures discarded by an early return               -> engine knew, was interrupted before it could say so
 P6 loop never scheduled (guard let self, :503)                         -> nothing ran
 P7 .completed with zero coverage read; persistedCoverage binds store off a WEAK self (:665) so a deallocated runner returns 0 unconditionally
 P8 genuinely silent episode — a SUCCESS reported as an ASR failure
 P9/P10 .failed(.noShards) :801 and .failed(.speechEngineNotReady) :814 — classes DO exist, yet cause is still hardcoded asr_failed, and ASR was never invoked

Preemption does NOT leak in: PreemptionSignal is sticky (LanePreemptionCoordinator.swift:86-88) so the runner intercepts at :711 and returns .preempted. That is why Dan's session shows three honest preempted/pipeline_error rows against one asr_failed.

=== THE RESIDUAL GATE (the round-5 variant rounds 3 and 4 each found once) ===
Not in the gate's condition — in the THIRTEEN silent returns that never reach it: :832 :847 :850 :858 :888 :894 :897 :900 :916 :923 :930 :952 :964 :967 :970. ELEVEN can execute with shardFailures NON-EMPTY. Concrete shape: shards 0..k fail with model_not_loaded (all classified), the user scrubs, startTranscription cancels the task, :832 returns, and k named diagnoses go out of scope. Same defect as rounds 3 and 4 one level further out: THE CODE COMPUTED THE RIGHT ANSWER AND LOST IT ON THE WAY TO THE EMITTER.
Secondary: chunksInsertedThisRun (:377) and shardsCompletedThisRun (:412) are ACTOR-scoped, not run-scoped, and their doc comments wrongly assert per-pass. startTranscription cancels and immediately spawns the successor (:473, :502-509) without awaiting the predecessor; cancellation is cooperative so two loop bodies overlap. The silent-shard path (TranscriptEngineService.swift:1174-1186) has NO cancellation check between the recognizer returning and the increment, so a cancelled predecessor credits the successor's tally and suppresses a genuine .failed.

=== FIX, RANKED BY DIAGNOSTIC POWER PER UNIT OF RISK — scope is 1-3 ===
1. EMIT .failed BEFORE EVERY SILENT RETURN in runTranscriptionLoop. Where shardFailures is non-empty emit dominantFailure(shardFailures) — already computed, already tested. Where empty, the return reason IS the diagnosis (cancelled / stopped / preempted). Pure addition; no existing arm changes behaviour; preempt arms stay silent since the runner intercepts at :711. Converts most of P1/P2/P3/P5 from a 300s stall into an instant named row AND KILLS THE MULTI-MINUTE HANGS as a side effect.
2. ADD A `failure_observation` KEY (three literals: engine_reported | engine_completed_zero | engine_silent_timeout) always present on a zero-coverage row, describing how the run ended from the runner's own vantage — something it always knows with certainty, unlike the class. Absence is currently overloaded across four distinct diagnoses. AND CONDITION `cause`: no_shards, speech_engine_not_ready and every engine_silent_timeout row belong under .pipelineError; reserve .asrFailed for rows whose class implies the recognizer actually ran. Safe by the same construction argument TranscriptFailureClass already won — compile-time literals, nothing derived from audio, a feed, a URL or user text.
3. STOP DESTROYING .failed at the emit gate for the asset the runner is about to journal — either capture the failure before stopTranscription at :701, or exempt .failed from the stoppedAssetIds drop. Recovers a FULLY CLASSIFIED failure that is currently deleted on purpose. Defensible because .completed is gated for triggering downstream work and .failed does not.
4. (same pass if cheap) Scope the two tallies to the run — loop-locals or keyed by (assetId, runToken).
5. (FOLLOW-UP, not this bead) The scheduler already stashes "runner_reason": "transcription:<class>" into extras (AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:4079, ~:4126) and extractFailure does not read that key. Dan's 11:54:04 preempted/pipeline_error row is the SIBLING of the 11:54:04 failed/asr_failed row — SAME FAILURE, TWO ROWS, and the one carrying the name is the one the projection cannot read. THE BUNDLE IS THEREFORE DOUBLE-COUNTING FAILURES, which distorts any aggregate built from it — including the pipeline_error 25 / asr_failed 17 counts quoted in playhead-8ysk.

CAVEAT TO STATE IN THE PR: fixes 1 and 3 change what the next bundle looks like relative to this one, so the two are not directly comparable in aggregate. A RISE in named rows is the fix working, not a regression.

DO NOT default the class to .unknown when nil — that relocates the defect one level up, a name carrying no information, which is what asr_failed already is.
=== SCHEDULER-ACCOUNTING DECISION, 2026-07-29 (Dan approved) ===
REVIEW ROUND 1 FOUND A REGRESSION THIS BEAD INTRODUCES. An interrupted run now returns .failed INSTANTLY. AnalysisWorkScheduler:4045 increments attemptCount on every .failed, and at maxAttemptCount = 5 the job goes `superseded` with nextEligibleAt: nil — PERMANENTLY ABANDONED.

So scrubbing the timeline five times across an episode's analysis lifetime silently and permanently kills analysis for that episode. Ordinary listening behaviour, irreversible outcome, no signal to the user.

WHY IT IS A REGRESSION AND NOT A PRE-EXISTING POLICY QUESTION: pre-bead the runner waited out 300s and then burned the attempt, BUT there was a genuine rescue — the successor's .completed inside that window produced non-zero coverage and no attempt was burned. This bead removes the rescue AND makes the burn instant. It converts an occasional loss into a reliable one.

DECISION: route interruption-caused terminations to PREEMPTION-STYLE ACCOUNTING — requeue, no attempt increment. The honest REPORTING is unchanged: the row still says cancelled/stopped, which is true and is the whole point of the bead. Only the scheduler's accounting changes.

RATIONALE: a user moving the playhead is not an analysis failure. The codebase already has the precedent — .preempted (AnalysisWorkScheduler:4205) requeues WITHOUT incrementing attemptCount, because the work was displaced by something with a better claim and nothing about the analysis went wrong. An interruption is the same shape with a different displacer.

THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT, considered and rejected: the five-attempt budget exists to stop infinite retries on a genuinely broken episode, and if interruptions never count, an episode the user always scrubs could requeue forever. Rejected because requeues are now CHEAP — an interrupted run fails instantly rather than holding a 300s slot, which was the expensive part — the loop is bounded by user behaviour, and it terminates the moment they stop scrubbing. The alternative failure mode (five scrubs = never analyzed, permanently, silently) does not self-correct. One of these recovers on its own and the other does not.

CONSTRAINTS ON THE IMPLEMENTATION:
 - Do NOT widen .preempted itself to swallow interruptions. That path carries lane semantics that should not be disturbed, and conflating them would make the journal LESS honest, not more. Use an explicit accounting decision keyed on termination kind.
 - PIN BOTH DIRECTIONS by mutation: an interruption must not burn an attempt, AND a genuine transcript failure must still burn one — otherwise a permanently broken episode retries forever.

TO WATCH RATHER THAN PRE-BUILD: if a future device pull shows an episode requeuing many times, that is the unbounded case appearing, and the answer is a SEPARATE interruption budget rather than folding it back into the failure budget. Prefer seeing it in data over adding a knob now.

FLAG THIS IN THE PR as a scheduler-accounting change so it is visible rather than buried inside a diagnostics bead.
acceptance_criteria: Every silent return in runTranscriptionLoop emits .failed first — carrying dominantFailure(shardFailures) when classified failures exist, and the return reason when they do not. A zero-coverage journal row always carries a failure_observation from a closed three-case vocabulary, so absence is never overloaded. cause is no longer hardcoded asr_failed: rows whose class implies ASR never ran are not labelled as ASR failures. A .failed for the asset the runner is about to journal is not destroyed by the stop gate. Verified on a real device pull: every failure row answers 'why' with either a class or a named reason there is no class. The PR states explicitly that a rise in named rows is the fix working, since the next bundle is not aggregate-comparable to this one. Do NOT default the class to .unknown.

title: Marking a span not-an-ad is a silent no-op: the veto searches live orchestrator state while the transcript renders persisted spans
description:
REPORTED BY DAN, 2026-07-29, on the dogfood build at main ea40ded8 (p70f + 0hi9 + 8ysk).

HIS REPRO, recorded verbatim so it is not distorted by my paraphrase:
"marking a detected span as not an ad doesnt work — you mark it, click done, the modal pops up, you click dismiss ad and the ad remains highlighted but not dismissed and the modal disappears"

So: the user selects a detected span, marks it as not-an-ad, taps Done, a confirmation modal appears, they tap "dismiss ad", the modal closes — AND NOTHING CHANGES. The span stays highlighted as a detected ad.

WHY THIS IS P0 RATHER THAN A UI PAPERCUT:
 - It is the listener's ONLY recourse when detection is wrong, and detection being wrong is Dan's stated number-one problem. Wrong detection that cannot be corrected is materially worse than wrong detection that can.
 - It breaks the LEARNING loop, not just the display. Corrections feed the ad catalog and the per-show threshold controller. On Dan's device 54 of 166 ad windows — a third of the total — are his own corrections replayed back, so this path carries a large fraction of everything the system knows.
 - It fails SILENTLY after four deliberate user actions. The modal confirming and then dismissing reads as success.
 - It contradicts the product intent recorded in playhead-1mq1.2, "Fixing Playhead's mistake takes one tap".

THE FIRST QUESTION TO ANSWER, because it splits the causes cleanly: DOES THE CORRECTION SURVIVE AN APP RESTART? Ask Dan, or check a diagnostics bundle.
 - If the span is dismissed after a relaunch, the correction WAS recorded and this is a view-refresh failure — the store changed and the UI did not observe it.
 - If it is still highlighted after a relaunch, the correction was never persisted, or was persisted against something other than the window being displayed.

CANDIDATE CAUSES — establish, do not assume:
 - Attribution to the wrong asset row. playhead-0hi9 just fixed one episode producing two analysis_assets rows with state split between them; a correction written against one row while the view reads the other would present exactly like this. That bead's reconciliation ships in this same build, so check whether the reported episode was one of the merged pairs.
 - The view-layer podcastId/assetId read after an await (the family of playhead-254m, already fixed once) resolving to a stale identifier.
 - The correction persisting but not transitioning the window's decisionState, so the highlight predicate still matches.
 - The modal's confirm action wired to dismiss-the-sheet rather than to commit-the-correction — i.e. the button does what it says (dismiss) and nothing else.
 - A silent dedupe. playhead-q0tj records that a repeat 'hearing an ad' on an already-corrected span is silently swallowed; the inverse direction may have a sibling.

RELEVANT DEVICE EVIDENCE ALREADY IN HAND: the eligibilityGate distribution on Dan's pull included 17 windows at blockedByUserCorrection, so corrections DO reach the store on some path. That argues against a wholesale persistence failure and toward attribution or refresh.

DO NOT fix the highlight by filtering the view. If the correction is not being persisted, hiding the span makes the app lie in a new way and destroys the learning signal at the same time.
=== TRACED 2026-07-29 — the write commits; it lands where nothing looks ===

THE VETO'S ONLY DURABLE MUTATION (AnalysisStore.swift:10235-10241, inside a real BEGIN/COMMIT):
    UPDATE ad_windows SET decisionState = ? WHERE id = ? AND analysisAssetId = ?
setting decisionState = 'reverted'. Nothing else. Not boundaryState, not eligibilityGate, and no row in decoded_spans.

THE HIGHLIGHT PREDICATE (TranscriptPeekViewModel.swift:214-216):
    (spansByChunkIndex[chunkIndex] != nil) || userMarkedChunkIndices.contains(chunkIndex)
Source A is decoded_spans, matched by pure geometric overlap (:429-451). That table's schema (AnalysisStore.swift:7624-7632) has NO decision, gate, revert or tombstone column — there is nothing to filter on even in principle, and the only writers that delete a row are interior to a detection re-run's supersession bookkeeping. Source B filters ad_windows on boundaryState == "userMarked" (:433) — a DIFFERENT FIELD from the one the veto writes.

So the correction succeeds and the highlight cannot see it. Structural, not a race.

RULED OUT with evidence, do not re-investigate:
 - "The button only dismisses the sheet" — it calls submitNotAdChunks() -> revertCallback -> runtime.revertAdWindows -> skipOrchestrator.revertByTimeRange -> persistRevertedAdWindowsIfCurrent -> real SQL, all awaited, errors rethrown and logged, no try? swallowing.
 - Task cancellation on sheet teardown — the Task is UNSTRUCTURED (not a .task modifier, no parent), and TranscriptPeekView is not torn down when the alert dismisses; only showNotAdConfirmation flips.
 - playhead-254m shape — assetId is read BEFORE the Task (TranscriptPeekView.swift:765 vs :787) and is an immutable let on the view model.
 - playhead-0hi9 shape — read and write use the same id, guarded at NowPlayingView.swift:619, PlayheadRuntime.swift:4711-4712 and SkipOrchestrator.swift:3712. A split would make the write return false, not misdirect it.
 - Stale view — TranscriptPeekViewModel polls every 2s and re-reads from SQLite (:112-121, :456-482).
 - The 17 blockedByUserCorrection windows are a DIFFERENT field written by a DIFFERENT actor: BackfillEvidenceFusion.swift:977-982 sets it at DETECTION time from a correction factor derived from the persisted store. They prove corrections shape FUTURE passes; they say nothing about retroactive display.

SECOND LIVE CANDIDATE, not mutually exclusive with the above: exactTargets empty -> early return false before any write (SkipOrchestrator.swift:3782-3784). Targets are drawn from the orchestrator's IN-MEMORY windows/suggestWindows dictionaries (:3742-3763) while the highlight is drawn from PERSISTED decoded_spans. A span rendered in the transcript with no live orchestrator entry — stale process, span never promoted to a managed/suggest window, or already .reverted from a prior attempt (:3745) — yields no targets and a silent false.

THE DISCRIMINATOR, and it must be observed BEFORE any relaunch (@State resets either way, which is why the post-restart observation did NOT settle this):
Immediately after tapping "Dismiss ad", does the header button snap back to "Not ad" with the selection cleared, or stay on "Done" with the checkmarks intact?
    TranscriptPeekView.swift:792-794
        guard await revertCallback(syntheticSpan) else { return }
        notAdMarkedChunkSelections = []
        isNotAdMarkingMode = false
 - Snaps to "Not ad", selection cleared  => callback returned TRUE  => the write committed; the highlight simply cannot see it.
 - Stays "Done" with checkmarks         => callback returned FALSE => nothing was written; chase exactTargets.
Also pullable from the device: ad_windows rows with decisionState='reverted' and correction_events with source manualVeto at exactTimeSpan scope. Prefer a raw DB pull over the corpus export — CorpusExporter.swift:421-422 NULLs decisionState when redacting.

FIX CONSTRAINT, restated because the tempting remedy is unusually tempting here: decoded_spans has no state column, so the path of least resistance is to filter decodedSpans in LiveTranscriptPeekDataSource.fetchSnapshot or rebuildSpansByChunkIndex(), or to hold vetoed ranges in the view model. ANY variant that makes the span disappear WITHOUT the correction becoming legible to the detection pipeline's own read path destroys the learning signal — the UI would agree with the user while BackfillEvidenceFusion's correctionFactor and the recurrence-revocation machinery keep seeing what they see now, and it would permanently mask whether the second candidate is also firing. The correction must remain the thing that changes the answer, not a veneer over it.

NOTE candidate 1 is a latent defect regardless of whether candidate 2 fired on Dan's device, so fixing 2 alone would leave the highlight stuck.

=== DISCRIMINATOR ANSWERED, 2026-07-29 — BOTH DEFECTS ARE LIVE ===

Dan, after tapping "Dismiss ad" and observing BEFORE any relaunch: "Stays on done."

The header stayed on "Done" with the checkmarks intact. Per TranscriptPeekView.swift:792-794 the selection is cleared ONLY on a true return, so **revertCallback returned FALSE and nothing was written.** Candidate 2 confirmed.

So this bead now covers TWO defects, and both must be fixed:

**DEFECT A (fires on Dan's device): the veto cannot find its targets.**
SkipOrchestrator.swift:3782-3784 returns false when exactTargets is empty. Targets are collected from the orchestrator's IN-MEMORY `windows` and `suggestWindows` dictionaries (:3742-3763). The transcript highlight is rendered from PERSISTED `decoded_spans` (AnalysisStore.swift:16128-16134, no state filter). **These two sources have fundamentally different lifetimes** — one is live playback state for the episode the orchestrator is currently tracking, the other is a durable analysis artifact that outlives any session.

CONSEQUENCE, and this is the shape of the bug: a listener can only dismiss an ad the orchestrator happens to be tracking right now. Every span shown from stored analysis — a previous session, an episode not actively playing, a span never promoted to a managed or suggest window, or one already marked .reverted by an earlier attempt (:3745) — is UN-DISMISSABLE, and fails silently with a modal that confirms and closes.

**DEFECT B (latent, proven from source, would survive a fix to A): the write lands where nothing looks.**
When the veto DOES find targets it sets ad_windows.decisionState = 'reverted' and nothing else. The highlight reads decoded_spans geometry (a table with NO state column) and ad_windows.boundaryState. So fixing A alone yields a veto that commits and still leaves the span highlighted — the same user-visible symptom, one layer along.

FIX ORDER MATTERS: fixing A first without B would take a silent no-op and turn it into a silent partial success, which is harder to diagnose, not easier. Address B's read/write mismatch as part of the same change.

THE DESIGN QUESTION AT THE HEART OF IT — resolve deliberately, do not paper over: what is the veto's source of truth? The user is looking at persisted analysis; the veto operates on live orchestrator state. Either the veto must be able to target what the user can actually see (persisted spans), or the transcript must only offer the affordance on spans the veto can act upon. The first is almost certainly right — the affordance should work on what is displayed — but it means the correction path must reach persisted state directly rather than only through the live session.

CONSTRAINT RESTATED: do not solve the display half by filtering decodedSpans in the view. That would make the UI agree with the user while BackfillEvidenceFusion's correctionFactor and the recurrence-revocation machinery keep seeing what they see today, destroying the learning signal and masking defect A permanently.
=== ROUND 1 FOUND THE BUG STILL REACHABLE, AND DAN DECIDED THE RULE (2026-07-29) ===

REVIEW ROUND 1 FINDING (reported, not fixed — it needed a decision): a manual veto can STILL be silently swallowed after this bead's fix. correction_events dedupes on (assetId, effectiveCorrectionType, normalizedScopeKey, correctionIdentityKey) — SOURCE IS NOT IN THE KEY — and ON CONFLICT ... source = COALESCE(correction_events.source, excluded.source) keeps whatever wrote FIRST. A rewind-through writes a listenRevert correction through the SAME path (makeManualCorrectionVetoEvent), and .exactTimeSpan bounds quantize to 100ms buckets. So a manual veto over a previously-rewound range only bumps submissionCount, never becomes a veto, userVetoedTimeRanges (manualVeto-only) does not suppress, the span stays highlighted, revertByTimeRange still returns true, and the modal closes. THAT IS THIS BEAD'S EXACT REPORTED SYMPTOM, REPRODUCED AFTER THE FIX. The reviewer hit it accidentally when its own positive control failed.

DAN'S DECISION, verbatim: "A manually marked span should override anything else." And immediately after: "the banner is lower fidelity than the marking this is not an ad."

So this is a FIDELITY LADDER, not a manual/automatic binary:
  1. Transcript span marking  (HIGHEST) — the listener selected specific sentences; the time bounds are THEIRS.
  2. Banner response          (middle)  — a tap about a whole detected window, often mid-listen; the range came from the DETECTOR.
  3. Inferred listenRevert    (lowest)  — a rewind-through, which may mean anything.

IMPLEMENT AS PRECEDENCE, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS:
 - A higher-fidelity correction arriving over a lower one WINS and takes effect.
 - A lower-fidelity one arriving over a higher one MUST NOT downgrade it.
COALESCE in either direction is wrong. Sources need a RANK, and the rank is the ladder above.

NOT DECIDED — ask before assuming: whether the FACT of the lower-fidelity event should still be retained alongside the winning one for learning purposes. Dan's rule settles precedence, not whether the inferred event survives as a second record. Both remedies round 1 identified are still on the table for HOW to express the rank (a source-aware dedupe identity that keeps both rows, versus one row whose source is promoted) — the constraint is the ladder's semantics, not the storage shape. If keeping both rows, note the reviewer's caution that changing the dedupe identity touches semantics LearningArtifactIngestor and the egress privacy baseline depend on.

WHY THIS BELONGS IN THIS BEAD RATHER THAN A FOLLOW-UP: without it, Dan's next dogfood can reproduce the original symptom on any span he had previously rewound through, and the fix will read as having failed.

ROUND 1 ALSO CONFIRMED, do not re-investigate: the forbidden view-filter fix was AVOIDED — suppression resolves in AnalysisStore.fetchDecodedSpans keyed on the persisted CorrectionEvent, the same row BackfillEvidenceFusion reads (traced AdDetectionService:4299 -> correctionPassthroughFactor -> BackfillEvidenceFusion:976-982), so the span disappears BECAUSE the correction exists and does so identically for every reader. All 9 production call sites of the filtered/unfiltered read pair were audited and correctly classified. 8 claims, 8 mutations, 8 killed; no vacuous tests. Two coverage gaps (trust-penalty withholding, .manualVeto narrowing) were asserted by NOTHING and are now pinned by mutation-proven tests in 405087de.
=== ROUND 2 CLOSED IT (2026-07-29). The round-1 note above saying "reported, not fixed / undecided" is STALE — the ladder is implemented and proven. ===

STORAGE SHAPE CHOSEN: rank-promote `source` on the single deduped row (CorrectionSource.fidelityRank — marking 3 > banner 2 > listenRevert 1). NOT a source-aware dedupe identity. The deciding trace: LearningArtifactIngestor gates applySponsorSideEffect — a NON-IDEMPOTENT SponsorKnowledgeStore counter — on appendCorrectionEvent's wasNewlyInserted, which comes from the pre-upsert identity probe. Widening the identity would make a veto-over-rewind report a FRESH INSERT and re-fire that side effect for material already accounted for. Keeping the identity untouched also leaves the v32/v34 egress keys alone and needs no migration.

DAN'S UNDECIDED QUESTION IS NOT FORCED BY THIS AND STAYS OPEN. Retention is exactly as before: one row, the losing gesture still counted in submissionCount/lastSeenAt. Adding `source` to the identity later is a migration ON TOP OF the ladder, not a rewrite of it.

BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE PROVEN INDEPENDENT — different mutations, different tests, no overlap:
  PROMOTE  M1 (promotion arm -> correction_events.source) killed ONLY the promote test + the end-to-end repro; defend and pin stayed green.
  DEFEND   M2 (demote arm -> excluded.source) killed ONLY the defend test; promote stayed green.

AND THE MOST IMPORTANT THING ROUND 2 FOUND: **COALESCE got the defend direction right BY ACCIDENT.** First-writer-wins happens to preserve a manualVeto against a later listenRevert — so a test would have PASSED against the broken code. It was correct for a reason that would evaporate the moment anyone touched arrival order. A test alone could never have found that; only asking WHY it was correct did. It is now correct on purpose and M2 proves a test notices.

ROUND 2 FINDING 2 (Major, new): the defend direction was ACTUALLY LIVE-BROKEN in the half round 1 did not examine. causalSource and targetRefsJSON used COALESCE(excluded, stored) — LAST-writer-wins — so a later rewind-through silently repointed a manual marking's exactFeedbackSpan and window ids at THE DETECTOR'S window. The row would keep saying manualVeto while carrying the detector's geometry. That is the listener's own time bounds, i.e. precisely what Dan's rule protects. Both columns now refuse a lower-ranked overwrite.

ROUND 2 FINDING 3 (Low, defensive): a stored banner source with an empty identity key was promotable to manualVeto, flipping isPrivateExplicitFeedbackReceipt false and moving a PRIVATE receipt into CorpusExporter's export path. Unreachable in production (v32 backfills every legacy banner row) but one loadCorrectionEvents round-trip from expressible, so the pin is explicit rather than inherited from a migration two versions back.

LEDGER: round 1's 8 claims/8 mutations/8 killed carried forward; round 2 added 8 more (R2-1..R2-8) including live re-verification of both round-1 fixes. NO MUTATION SURVIVED across either round. Every precedence test keeps the losing row PRESENT and proves the collision (appendCorrectionEvent returning false, one row, submissionCount == 2), so "still suppressed" cannot pass vacuously — M8 tripped those precondition guards exactly as designed.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause established by tracing, and the restart question answered first since it splits persistence failures from refresh failures. Dan's exact repro — mark not-an-ad, Done, modal, dismiss ad — results in the span no longer being highlighted AND the correction durably recorded, verified by a diagnostics bundle rather than by the UI alone. The learning path is intact: the correction reaches the catalog and the per-show threshold controller, not just the display. A regression covers the full interaction, not just the store write. The fix must NOT be a view-layer filter that hides the span without persisting the correction.

title: Analysis jobs almost never finish: 147 acquired to 9 finalized over 6 days on real hardware (6%)
description:
ROOT CAUSE TRACED 2026-07-29. Two separate defects compound: the failure is caused by an unvalidated shard cache, and it is undiagnosable because the error is discarded three times over.

=== PART A: WHY IT FAILS — the poisoned shard cache ===

AnalysisAudio.swift:432-435 short-circuits every decode:
    // Return persisted shards if available.
    if let cached = ShardCache.loadShards(episodeID: episodeID) { return cached }

ShardCache.loadShards (AnalysisAudio.swift:123-147) is keyed on episodeID ALONE. Manifest entries carry only id, startTime, duration — no source fingerprint, no byte length, no SHA. So decoded shards are IMMORTAL AND UNVALIDATED. Every retry, every scheduler epoch, every job generation receives byte-identical input. That is the answer to "why does retry never help": the failure is deterministic by construction.

IT ALSO RENDERS THE COMPLETENESS GATE INERT. The gate is real and correct at admission — AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:3221 calls downloadManager.cachedFileURL(for:), which is byte-exact (DownloadManager.swift:2898, servingURLIfComplete at :2790-2824 compares fileSize against pin.expectedBytes with SHA verification). But the gate guards the URL, and THE URL IS DISCARDED ON A CACHE HIT at AnalysisAudio.swift:433.

The only production eviction is PlayheadRuntime.swift:3902-3904, whose own comment names the hazard ("the truncated 2MB file had different shard count/content"). It sits AFTER try await result.downloadComplete() (:3891) AND after guard !Task.isCancelled, self.isCurrentPlayRequest(...) else { return } (:3892-3896). So if the user switches episodes, backgrounds the app, or the download throws (catch at :3905), that return fires and the poisoned cache SURVIVES PERMANENTLY. Nothing else clears it.

WHY THE FAILURE TAKES MILLISECONDS: a millisecond failure does not need ASR to be fast, it needs ASR never to run. A partial decode's tail shards are silent, and TranscriptEngine.swift:1048-1052 throws "shard is entirely silent (all zeros)" on a pure CPU scan — sub-millisecond. Siblings at :1026 (empty samples) and :1043 (NaN/Inf) do the same.

HYPOTHESIS TO VERIFY, NOT ASSUME — why the existing truncation guard does not stop the caching. AnalysisAudio.swift:948-967 computes isTruncated and already refuses to cache when true. But isTruncated compares decodedDuration against assetDuration, and assetDuration is read from the PARTIAL FILE ITSELF via AVURLAsset. A partial file reports a partial duration, so the decode matches its own file's declared length and isTruncated is FALSE. The file looks complete to itself. This is corroborated by playhead-0hi9: placeholder asset rows carry durations of 528-561s, which is exactly 8 MiB of audio at ~123 kbps — i.e. the partial file really does measure ~530s. CHECK THIS DIRECTLY before building on it.

=== PART B: WHY IT IS UNDIAGNOSABLE — three independent drops ===

1. THE ERROR IS DESTROYED. TranscriptEngineService.swift:555-565 catches a fully-formed TranscriptEngineError/AppleSpeechBoundaryError carrying the Speech domain, code and reason, writes it to logger.error, and continues. Not accumulated, not counted, not returned, not stored. Duplicate drop in the drain loop at :596-602.

2. THERE IS NO CHANNEL FOR IT. TranscriptEngineService.swift:82-85 defines TranscriptEngineEvent with exactly two cases — chunksPersisted and completed. NO .failed CASE. Even if the catch wanted to forward the error, the event type cannot express it. Worse: after every shard has failed, the loop falls through to :680 and emits .completed — A TOTAL FAILURE IS REPORTED TO THE RUNNER AS SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION, distinguishable only by the coverage number being zero.

3. WHAT SURVIVES IS NOT EXPORTED. runner_reason ("transcription:zeroCoverage") IS persisted (AnalysisStore.swift:13259 binds entry.metadata), but DiagnosticsBundle.swift:492-495 deliberately omits metadata on PII grounds, and WorkJournalRecord (:496-503) and SchedulerEvent (:478-482) both drop it. That is precisely why the journal row carries only cause.

CONSEQUENTLY asr_failed IS NOT AN ASR ERROR REPORT. Its sole emitter is AnalysisJobRunner.emitTranscriptionTimeoutJournal (:1324-1334), triggered by "if transcriptCoverage == 0" at :697. NO Error VALUE IS IN SCOPE ANYWHERE IN THAT BLOCK. The cause is hardcoded at :1309/:1331. It is a label applied to an ABSENCE, not to a failure — the doc comment at :1256-1258 says so honestly ("zero coverage").

Nine distinct paths (silent shard, empty shard, NaN/Inf, converter creation, buffer allocation, format mismatch, modelNotLoaded, locale assets, analyzer format) are COMPLETELY INDISTINGUISHABLE in the journal today.

=== pipeline_error RESOLVED ===
The millisecond pairing is mechanical, not a second failure: emitTranscriptionTimeoutJournal (:722) -> stopReason .failed("transcription:zeroCoverage") (:729-735) -> scheduler case .failed (AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:4045) -> attempts<5 emits preempted/.pipelineError (:4129), attempts>=5 emits failed/.pipelineError (:4084). Two awaits and one SQLite commit apart. That IS the 5-186ms gap.
BUT pipeline_error is ALSO independently produced at ~14 other sites (AnalysisJobRunner.swift:404 decode, :410 "no shards within desired coverage", :541, :777, :811, :851; AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:3388/:3448/:3468/:3654/:4283/:4324; plus DownloadManager and ForceQuitResumeScan emitters). Note :410 also fails in milliseconds and never reaches the transcript stage — which is why some episodes show pipeline_error with NO asr_failed. It is a catch-all and is not diagnostic on its own; runner_reason is the only discriminator and it lives in the dropped metadata.

=== CORRECTIONS TO THIS BEAD'S ORIGINAL NUMBERS ===
The 6% completion figure is partly a WINDOWING ARTIFACT. DiagnosticsBundleBuilder.swift:95 sets schedulerEventsCap = 200 and :163 takes the last 200. The observed counts sum to exactly 200 (147+9+20+24), so the window is saturated and terminal rows for older acquisitions fell off the front. The 147-acquired-to-53-terminal ratio within one contiguous window is still damning, but do not quote 6% as a clean rate.
Also: preempted-with-pipeline_error is a DELIBERATE MISLABEL, not a fault in itself. AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:4106-4113 documents choosing .preempted over .failed so orphan recovery does not treat a retryable job as terminal. Genuine lane preemption uses .userPreempted (:4205-4237). The semantics are defensible; the taxonomy is not — event_type is overloaded to encode retryability.

=== SECONDARY HYPOTHESIS, keep alive ===
modelNotLoaded after a swallowed launch-time failure. loadFastModel() is invoked exactly once (PlayheadRuntime.swift:2775) and its failure is swallowed by an empty catch at :2776-2779 whose comment claims "the transcript engine will surface failures when first used" — IT DOES NOT; they land in the drop at TranscriptEngineService.swift:555. Nothing ever retries the load. Compounding: loadFinalModel (TranscriptEngine.swift:649-660) calls unloadModel() at :652 BEFORE loadModel() at :656, so a throw leaves the device with NO model loaded and activeModelRole stale. Weakened by Dan's healthy eligibility_snapshot — but note that snapshot reads Apple Intelligence availability, NOT SpeechService.activeModelRole, so a device can be fully eligible while the actor holds prepared == false. His 9 finalized rows argue against a global outage.

=== THE FIX, two independent parts ===
A. BREAK THE DETERMINISM. Key ShardCache on {episodeID, sourceFingerprint, expectedBytes} — the scheduler already holds job.sourceFingerprint and uses it at AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:3342 — or evict unconditionally on the .failed requeue arm. Either makes a retry meaningfully different from the attempt before it.
B. NAME THE FAILURE. Add .failed(analysisAssetId:reason:) to TranscriptEngineEvent, populate it from the catch at TranscriptEngineService.swift:555, and add a REDACTED error-class field that survives the DiagnosticsBundle projection. Respect the PII reason metadata was dropped: export an error class/domain/code, never free text.
Part B is what makes the next capture name the cause outright. Causes 1-3 cannot be separated from the existing six days of data no matter how long they are analysed.

RELATIONSHIP TO playhead-0hi9: same disease, different propagation path. A partial decode at the 8 MiB playable threshold poisons BOTH the duration (0hi9) and the shard cache (this bead). 0hi9 part 1 gates the duration write on isTruncated; if the hypothesis above holds, isTruncated is FALSE for these files and that gate will not help here. Verify the interaction before assuming either bead fixes the other.
acceptance_criteria: asr_failed and pipeline_error carry the underlying error (domain, code, message) so the cause is determinable from a diagnostics bundle without a device attached — mirroring how playhead-p70f named day-0's exits. The completion rate is re-derived from an uncapped source and reported as a baseline. Root cause of the dominant failure mode is established with evidence and fixed. After landing, re-measure playhead-gqx4 and playhead-i7qe against a fresh device pull to determine whether they were symptoms of this rather than independent defects. A regression covers the deterministic-retry loop: the same episode failing on consecutive scheduler epochs must not silently repeat forever.

title: Absolute container paths are persisted in analysis_assets.sourceURL — they break on reinstall/restore
description:
Found 2026-07-28 while tracing playhead-0hi9. A latent bug, independent of that bead's root cause, and the likely explanation for its one anomalous pair.

analysis_assets.sourceURL stores an ABSOLUTE local path. Both live insert sites write one — AnalysisCoordinator.swift:1687 (audioURL.url.absoluteString) and AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:4823 (localAudioURL.absoluteString) — and the column is WRITE-ONCE: there is no 'UPDATE ... SET sourceURL' anywhere in the codebase.

Those paths derive from cacheDirectory, which is rooted at .cachesDirectory (DownloadManager.swift:955), i.e.
    /var/mobile/Containers/Data/Application/<CONTAINER-UUID>/Library/Caches/...
The container UUID CHANGES on reinstall, on device restore, and on some TestFlight upgrades. Every persisted sourceURL then points at a path that no longer exists, permanently, with no update path.

CONSEQUENCES, all of which look like unrelated bugs:
 - The anchored-A-side guard in day-0 rediff (AdDetectionService.swift:11003) fails => the mint exits silently. See playhead-p70f.
 - The lagged rediff sweep's candidate enumerator (RediffRefetchProduction.swift:91) skips the asset => 'no_eligible_work'.
 - Duration re-probing via cachedFileURL cannot find the file.
This is a strong candidate for BOTH observed rediff symptoms at once, and it would survive every fix in p70f and 0hi9 because neither touches path storage.

SECOND, SMALLER MECHANISM in the same area: completeFileURL (DownloadManager.swift:2482) appends resolveExtension(for:) (:2875), which reads an in-memory extensionCache, else scans the directory, else FALLS BACK to 'mp3'. A cold launch with the file absent yields '.mp3'; a later run with an .m4a present yields '.m4a'. Same episode, two different paths.

DISCRIMINATOR for which one produced 0hi9's 14th pair (two rows, different sourceURLs): if the two URLs share the same trailing <64-hex>.<ext> but differ in the Application/<UUID>/ segment, it is container drift. If they share directory and basename and differ only in extension, it is the extension fallback. If neither, it is a third mode needing its own trace.

FIX SHAPE: store a container-RELATIVE path (or just the basename plus a directory key) and resolve it against the CURRENT container at read time. Do not migrate by rewriting stored absolutes — the old container is gone, so recompute from the relative form. Note DownloadManager.swift:1694-1701 already warns that a normalized .mp3 suffix is not evidence of MP3 bytes, so extension handling in this area is known-fragile.

Related: playhead-0hi9 (found during its trace), playhead-p70f (day-0 rediff exits silently on a missing A-side).
acceptance_criteria: sourceURL (or its replacement) survives a container UUID change — proven by a test that stores a path, simulates a container move, and still resolves the file. The extension-fallback path cannot produce two different stored paths for one episode. Dan's existing rows are migrated or recomputed rather than left pointing at a dead container. Determine which mechanism produced playhead-0hi9's 14th pair using the stated discriminator and record the answer there.

title: One episode, two analysis_assets rows: duration measured mid-download splits all state across both, and neither is complete
description:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED IN SOURCE 2026-07-28. One episode gets two analysis_assets rows because row identity is (episodeId, assetFingerprint), and Pipeline A mints its row BEFORE any content hash exists, writing the row's own UUID into assetFingerprint as a deliberate placeholder.

THE PLACEHOLDER — AnalysisCoordinator.resolveSession, AnalysisCoordinator.swift:1683-1695:
    assetFingerprint: assetId, // Placeholder until content hashing
    weakFingerprint: nil,
Reached from handlePlayStarted (:1075) via PlayheadRuntime.performPlayEpisode (:3819 streaming, :3923 cached). This is the OLDER row: UUID fingerprint, NULL weak, non-empty local file:// sourceURL — matching the device data exactly.

THE SECOND ROW — AnalysisWorkScheduler.resolveAnalysisAssetId, AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:4818-4834, with assetFingerprint = job.sourceFingerprint = FileHasher.sha256 of the COMPLETED file (64-hex).

WHY RECONCILIATION NEVER FIRES — and this is the elegant part. A reconciliation path was BUILT for exactly this case: canUpgradeWeakAssetToCanonicalSHA (AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:5009-5029). Its final gate is
    return asset.assetFingerprint == currentWeakFingerprint || asset.weakFingerprint == currentWeakFingerprint
The placeholder's assetFingerprint is a UUID and its weakFingerprint is NULL, so neither disjunct can EVER be true. And weakFingerprint is always NULL because its only writer, updateAssetFingerprint (AnalysisStore.swift:7396), has exactly two callers — both INSIDE the upgrade path that requires it to already be written. A closed loop: the column that would enable reconciliation is only written by the code path that requires it to already be populated.

SECOND, INDEPENDENT BLOCKER: currentAudioFingerprint comes from downloadManager.fingerprint(for:) (DownloadManager.swift:2930), a pure in-memory dictionary read. fingerprintCache (:349) is never persisted and is cleared on removeAll(). After ANY relaunch it is empty, so the upgrade is unreachable regardless of column contents. The strong SHA IS durable — in the .pin sidecar (pin.sha256, DownloadManager.swift:3527-3536) — but nothing rehydrates the cache from it.

The schema permits the duplicate: analysis_assets has PRIMARY KEY(id) only; idx_assets_episode on (episodeId) is NON-unique (AnalysisStore.swift:6531-6547).

THE 528-561s NUMBER IS 8 MiB OF AUDIO. DownloadManager.swift:1365-1367 sets defaultPlayableThreshold = 8 * 1024 * 1024 (its doc comment claims ~2MB and is stale by 4x). streamingDownload resumes the instant that threshold is crossed (:2005-2015), PlayheadRuntime fires .playStarted, resolveSession mints the placeholder, and runFromSpooling decodes whatever is on disk. 8,388,608 bytes / 16,000 B/s (128 kbps) = 524.3s. Observed 528-561, mean 543 => ~123 kbps, i.e. ordinary podcast bitrate. A fixed BYTE prefix across a fixed BITRATE cohort is exactly why episodes of 2933s, 1746s and 4379s all report ~540s.

THE ORTHOGONAL DURATION DEFECT that makes the split harmful: AnalysisAudio.performDecode COMPUTES isTruncated (AnalysisAudio.swift:948-967), uses it to suppress the shard cache — with a comment explaining that caching a partial result would poison it permanently — and then DISCARDS it. runFromSpooling (AnalysisCoordinator.swift:1244-1260) therefore persists the shard-sum of a partial decode as episodeDurationSec. This is the confirmed source of playhead-csbq's >100% coverage ratios: transcription ran against the real audio while the row records an 8 MiB prefix.

HOW STATE SPLITS: AnalysisCoordinator.activeAssetId is set once in handlePlayStarted (:1088) and every terminal-state write for the session goes to it — the OLD row. Meanwhile analysis_jobs.analysisAssetId durably pins jobs to whichever row they resolved (AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:4692), and fingerprint-keyed resolvers see the NEW row. Newest-wins resolvers (fetchAssetByEpisodeId, AnalysisStore.swift:7340; fetchLatestAssetByEpisodeIdMap, :7452) also see the NEW row — which is why Activity and the Library show 'queued' for 14 episodes while the terminal states sit on rows nobody displays.

NO RECONCILIATION EXISTS. No merge, no duplicate-aware query, no unique index anywhere. Both launch sweeps that touch this table are one-shot and _meta-gated and are ALREADY MARKED DONE on Dan's device (did_duration_backfill_v1, did_terminal_state_reconcile_v1), and both are per-row duplicate-blind. Dan's 13 pairs are STRANDED — a prevention-only fix leaves his library broken.

DEAD CODE FOUND: AnalysisCoordinator.resolveAssetId (:1540-1566) inserts with sourceURL: '' and has ZERO callers repo-wide. Not the bug; delete it while here.

THE 14th PAIR (different sourceURLs) is almost certainly the same root cause plus a path-instability confound — filed separately.

THE FIX — four parts, and note the dependencies:
1. NEVER write a duration from an unverified decode. Surface isTruncated out of AnalysisAudioService.decode (already computed) and gate runFromSpooling's updateEpisodeDuration on it, matching the guard that already protects ShardCache. Smallest possible change; kills the bogus 528s.
2. POPULATE weakFingerprint at both insert sites. AudioFingerprint.makeWeak(url:metadata:) is available before the download completes — that is the column's entire purpose. THEN rehydrate fingerprintCache from the existing .pin sidecar so fingerprint(for:) survives relaunch. Together these make the EXISTING upgrade path reachable. This is the fix, not new machinery.
3. RECONCILE EXISTING PAIRS. A new one-shot _meta-gated sweep: group by episodeId; where >1 row and the older row's assetFingerprint equals its own id, re-point child rows (analysis_sessions, semantic_scan_results, ad_windows, transcript_chunks, analysis_jobs.analysisAssetId) at the canonical-SHA row, take max of each coverage watermark, re-probe duration via cachedFileURL, delete the placeholder.
4. ADD UNIQUE INDEX on analysis_assets(episodeId, assetFingerprint) — AFTER 3, or it will fail on existing duplicates.

(1) and (2) are INDEPENDENT and BOTH required: (1) alone still leaves two rows; (2) alone still lets a partial duration land on the surviving row.
acceptance_criteria: All four parts land, in the stated order. (1) A truncated decode can no longer set episodeDurationSec — isTruncated is surfaced rather than discarded, with a regression covering an 8 MiB partial file. (2) weakFingerprint is populated at both insert sites AND fingerprintCache is rehydrated from the .pin sidecar, proven by a test that survives a simulated relaunch — verify the existing canUpgradeWeakAssetToCanonicalSHA path now actually fires rather than adding parallel machinery. (3) A one-shot reconciliation merges existing pairs, re-pointing every child table; run it against a copy of Dan's real database and prove all 13 pairs converge with no orphaned child rows and watermarks taken as max. (4) The unique index is added last and its migration is proven to succeed on the reconciled data. Delete the dead resolveAssetId. AFTER landing, re-measure playhead-gqx4 and playhead-i7qe against a fresh device pull, and update playhead-csbq to record that the >100% ratios are explained by the truncated-decode duration.

title: Day-0 rediff fetches ~300MB of B-copies and produces NOTHING: zero windows, zero recorded outcomes
description:
CORRECTION 2026-07-28: this bead's original headline claim was WRONG and is retracted. I claimed 'every episode has exactly ONE fingerprint capture, so there is nothing to diff'. That proof carries zero information: episode_fingerprints has PRIMARY KEY(analysisAssetId) (AnalysisStore.swift:4627-4635) and holds ONLY the A-side by design — the B-copies are deliberately never persisted ('NEVER-PERSIST-B', RediffRefetchService.swift:15-16, :573-575, AdDetectionService.swift:10979-10981). '24 rows across 24 assets, one each' is exactly what a PERFECTLY WORKING rediff produces. Recording the error because the same mistake is easy to repeat: I inferred absence-of-work from a table that structurally cannot show it.

ALSO RULED OUT: the 'xsdz.36 provider wiring remainder' is CLOSED. Every leg is wired on main — master switch on (RediffActivation.swift:38), day-0 on (:99), BGTask registered (PlayheadRuntime.swift:2738-2741) AND submitted (RediffRefetchService.swift:167-182), identifier in Info.plist:12, play-time day-0 fired (PlayheadRuntime.swift:3867/:3964/:4012), enclosure resolver attached (PlayheadApp.swift:170). Closed by 0f521ba3 / 47ca4e7c / 66e6326d.

WHAT THE DEVICE DATA ACTUALLY SHOWS (rediff_bandwidth_ledger, rediff_refetch_state, background_task_runs — none of which are in the diagnostics bundle, which is why this looked invisible):

  rediff_bandwidth_ledger: fullFetchBytesTotal = 299.6 MB, lastUpdatedAt = 2026-07-28 18:44:19
                           unchangedCount 0 | rotatedCount 0 | failedCount 0 | parkedCount 0
  rediff_refetch_state:    0 rows
  background_task_runs:    rediff_refetch ran EXACTLY ONCE, 2026-07-21 19:08:01,
                           outcome 'no_eligible_work', precheckBytes=0 fullFetchBytes=0

Read that carefully. The ONE lagged BGTask run fetched ZERO bytes. So the 299.6 MB was NOT spent by the lagged sweep — it was spent by the DAY-0 path, which fires at playback start. Day-0 costs ~108 MB per play (K=2 B-copies, RediffActivation.swift:113-117), so ~300 MB is roughly THREE day-0 attempts. The ledger's last write is 2026-07-28 18:44:19 — during Dan's most recent listening session, minutes after the diagnostics snapshot.

SO: day-0 rediff IS FIRING. It downloads B-copies. It spends real bandwidth on a metered device. And it produces zero ad windows, zero state rows, and does not even increment its own failure counter. Every outcome bucket is 0 while 299.6 MB went out the door. That is the bug.

THE REAL QUESTION: where between 'B-copies fetched' and 'slot minted' does it die, and why silently? Candidates to establish, NOT assume:
 - K-way floor: AdDetectionService.swift:10987 guards bSideURLs.count >= dayZeroMinKWayBCopies. If one of the two fetches fails, nothing mints — and if that early-return skips the ledger increment, it would look exactly like this.
 - Persona distinctness: day-0 stages personas guaranteed distinct from the download UA (kWayPersonasDistinct, RediffActivation.swift:108-119) because a B-fetch reusing the download persona returns byte-identical bytes. If persona staging silently falls back to the download persona, every B-copy is identical, rotation is 0, and nothing mints.
 - The byte-diff / segment-recovery (9s6q) stage producing no intervals.
 - An error thrown after the fetch but before any recorder call.
The zero-ness of failedCount is the strongest clue: a path that FAILED should have incremented it. Something is returning early on a non-error path, or throwing past the recorder.

SECONDARY (lower priority, different fix): the lagged sweep got ONE window in 7 days while preanalysis_recovery got 283 and backfill got 93 over the same period. iOS is granting background time generously — just not to this task. Its BGProcessingTaskRequest sets requiresExternalPower = true (RediffRefetchService.swift:172-175). Consider dropping it, since the WiFi-only URLSession already pins the expensive constraint. Its single run returned 'no_eligible_work', so the 3-day gate (RediffRefetchPolicy.swift:107-109, production preset = 3 days not 24h), the played-file-still-on-disk guard (RediffRefetchProduction.swift:91, and DownloadManager LRU-evicts), and the >3h-episode exclusion (RediffActivation.swift:45-56) all need checking as eligibility blockers.

STRATEGIC FINDING THAT CHANGES PLANNING — day-0 has NO TIME GATE (DayZeroRediffTrigger.swift:147-149 states this explicitly). The '24h' figure applies ONLY to the lagged sweep. The xsdz16 spike's '0/10 at 10 seconds apart' varied the WRONG AXIS: it re-fetched the same URL from the same client context, varying only elapsed time. The dominant variable for DAI re-stitching on the two biggest client-PINNED stacks is REQUEST CONTEXT, not time — varied personas turned those stacks from 0 to real day-0 width (Conan 211s, Fresh Air 203s, corroborated across Mac+Overcast at matching A-times; RediffActivation.swift:89-98). So a listener who downloads today's episode and plays it the same day CAN be served by rediff, minutes later. Rediff is NOT structurally incompatible with same-day listening. That was my error and it materially changes the auto-skip outlook.

THIRD ITEM, cheap and high-leverage: DiagnosticsBundle.swift contains ZERO rediff references. Three tables of decisive telemetry are written and never exported. Add them — this entire investigation required pulling the raw database.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause of the silent day-0 failure is established by tracing the path from 'B-copies fetched' to 'slot minted', not inferred. Whatever the cause, the ledger can no longer record ~300MB of fetches with every outcome counter at zero — a fetch that mints nothing MUST increment a counter and write a state row, so the next occurrence is visible without pulling a database. Day-0 produces at least one rediff-sourced ad_window with a byte-exact anchor on Dan's device, verified from the pulled DB. rediff_bandwidth_ledger, rediff_refetch_state and background_task_runs are added to DiagnosticsBundle. The lagged sweep's requiresExternalPower is re-decided with the 283-vs-1 grant disparity as evidence. Report the measured day-0 rotation yield, since the xsdz16 spike named the days-gap number as its single biggest open question and day-0 sidesteps it entirely.

title: The library checkmark says 'analysis ready' on an episode 47% scanned — it keys on feature extraction and last-ad-end, never on ad-scan coverage
description:
Dan, 2026-07-28, on the dogfood audit: 'One thing is that the ui showed the check mark for analysis complete on the episode.' The episode was asset 820134BF: transcript 100%, semantic ad scan 47%, analysisState='backfill'. This is the user-facing face of playhead-gqx4/playhead-i7qe and it is the reason Dan trusted a half-analysed episode.

THE LIVE PREDICATE (traced 2026-07-28). The checkmark that fired is EpisodePreparationControl's .ready state (playhead-3xtw), Playhead/Views/Library/EpisodePreparationControl.swift:44-55, accessibility label 'Analysis ready'. It resolves to:

    max(featureCoverageEndTime, confirmedAdCoverageEndTime) / episodeDurationSec >= 0.98
      OR projected persisted status == .done

  - EpisodePreparationReadiness.swift:154-159 (.ready wins, supersedes even the cellular gate)
  - EpisodePreparationReadiness.swift:274-285 (threshold 0.98 at :249)
  - EpisodePreparationStatusModel.swift:181-193 (the max() of the two watermarks)

BOTH ARMS OF THAT max() ARE THE WRONG QUANTITY:
  - featureCoverageEndTime is the ACOUSTIC/DSP feature-extraction watermark (FeatureExtraction.swift:1257 -> store.updateFeatureCoverage). Feature extraction sweeps the whole episode INDEPENDENT of the semantic scan. On Dan's episode this arm is what reached 0.98 — the DSP finished, so the UI said analysis was ready while 53% of the audio had never been read for ads.
  - confirmedAdCoverageEndTime is not coverage at all. AdDetectionService.swift:6208-6211 writes it as max(endTime) OF DETECTED AD WINDOWS. So a single late-placed ad detection pushes this watermark near the end of the episode and lights the checkmark with almost nothing scanned. A worse-detecting episode can look MORE complete.

NOTHING ANYWHERE CONSULTS SEMANTIC SCAN COVERAGE. Confirmed exhaustively: semantic_scan_results is referenced only inside AnalysisStore; SemanticScanCoverage (SemanticScanResult.swift:199-270), the type that computes real scan extent, has exactly ONE call site in the entire app (BackfillJobRunner.swift:3287) and is pipeline-internal telemetry never persisted anywhere the UI can read. The honest read model added by playhead-sd71 (AnalysisStore.swift:8779-8785) also uses the same feature/confirmed-ad pair.

SECOND DEFECT — DEGRADED TERMINALS RENDER AS CALM SUCCESS. EpisodeSurfaceStatusObserver.swift:272-278 folds FOUR distinct terminals into .done: .complete, .completeFull, .completeFeatureOnly, .completeTranscriptPartial. The latter two are explicitly degraded per AnalysisCoordinator.swift:55-66 — feature-only means the transcript never advanced past preview — yet all four render the identical checkmark with zero visual distinction. The code comment concedes the split was deferred.

THIRD DEFECT — THE TWO SURFACES HAVE ALREADY DRIFTED. EpisodePreparationStatusModel.swift:177-180 documents itself as mirroring the Activity screen 'so the two surfaces cannot drift'. That mirror is STALE: playhead-sd71 moved Activity to the gap-aware analyzed AREA (ActivitySnapshotProvider.swift:309-317) and off the raw frontier watermark, which the Library checkmark still uses. Activity would report a lower AN% for the same episode the Library row shows a checkmark for.

DORMANT SIBLING — the second checkmark (playhead-8ssx) at EpisodeListView.swift:478-483 keys on Episode.coverageSummary, which has NO writer anywhere in the app (only the memberwise-init default, Podcast.swift:180/:201). It always renders false, so there is no double-render today. Episode.analysisSummary is dormant the same way, so the first-checkmark tooltip and the ad-count numeral never render either. Fixing this bead may be the moment to decide whether coverageSummary becomes the real source rather than patching the watermark arithmetic — coordinate with playhead-8ssx rather than duplicating it.

WHY P0: this is not cosmetic. The checkmark is the contract that tells Dan an episode is safe to listen to. Today it can be satisfied by DSP finishing plus one late ad detection, with the semantic scan barely started. Every downstream detection-quality improvement is invisible to a user who was already told the work was done.
acceptance_criteria: The readiness checkmark cannot be satisfied by feature-extraction coverage or by a late confirmedAdCoverageEndTime alone — semantic ad-scan extent participates in the predicate, or the indicator is honestly re-scoped to say what it actually means. Dan's asset 820134BF (feature complete, scan 47%, state backfill) is the fixture and must NOT show a ready checkmark. Degraded terminals (completeFeatureOnly, completeTranscriptPartial) are visually distinguishable from a genuine full analysis, or are excluded from the ready state. The stale mirror comment at EpisodePreparationStatusModel.swift:177-180 is corrected or the drift with the sd71 Activity derivation is closed. A regression asserts the specific shape 'feature coverage 100% + semantic scan well short' does not read as ready — this is the exact case no existing test covers. Coordinate with playhead-8ssx on whether coverageSummary becomes the source of truth instead of extending the watermark max().

title: Coverage ratios far above 1.0 pass the full-coverage check unvalidated (observed 5.277)
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-28 in Dan's dogfood analysis.sqlite. A data-integrity hole that makes every coverage number untrustworthy, including the ones the completeFull check consumes.

THE EVIDENCE — the code wrote these terminalReason strings itself:
  F3EDBC24  episodeDurationSec 608s   transcriptEnd 3210s   'full coverage: transcript 5.277, feature 5.277'
  B994F346  episodeDurationSec 528s   transcriptEnd 1110s   'full coverage: transcript 2.158, feature 5.110'
  27C7C4B4  episodeDurationSec 549s   transcriptEnd 3466s   'full coverage: transcript 0.999, feature 0.999'

A coverage ratio of 5.277 means the watermark claims 527.7% of the episode was covered. The check treats it as full coverage because it only tests a lower bound. Nothing anywhere asserts coverage <= 1.0, so a wildly corrupt watermark is indistinguishable from a healthy one.

Note B994F346's two ratios DISAGREE (transcript 2.158 vs feature 5.110), which rules out a single shared scaling error and means at least one watermark is independently wrong.

TWO HYPOTHESES, BOTH UNPROVEN — establish which before fixing:
 (a) episodeDurationSec is wrong for these assets. All the affected rows have suspiciously clustered short durations (528-846s) while their watermarks are large, consistent with a duration read from a partial or still-downloading file.
 (b) Cross-asset watermark contamination. Some values match other assets' real durations exactly — 27C7C4B4's transcriptEnd of 3466.0 is exactly asset B10C7BC8's transcriptEnd, and 40F73A2B's 1746.0 is exactly asset 752926FF's episodeDurationSec. That pattern would indicate a watermark write landing on the wrong asset row, which is the same defect family as playhead-0sro's blind UPDATE.

Hypothesis (b) is the more serious one and is cheap to test: check whether the watermark UPDATE is scoped by asset id on every path. If it is contamination, it can also corrupt HEALTHY assets and would explain unrelated coverage weirdness elsewhere.

Regardless of cause, the missing guard is its own defect: a ratio above 1.0 should be loud, not silently accepted as success.
=== MEASURED 2026-07-30 ON THE DEVICE PULL — THIS BEAD IS NOW LOAD-BEARING, AND THERE IS A SECOND DEFECT ===

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN WHEN FILED. When this was filed, a coverage ratio above 1.0 was a diagnostic curiosity. As of 2026-07-30 it is not: playhead-pz32 made the readiness checkmark key on measured ad-scan coverage, and playhead-gqx4 made `completeFull` REQUIRE it. A bogus ratio can now promote an episode to a clean terminal state, which is terminal — nothing returns to it. The unvalidated number became a decision input.

DEFECT 1, CONFIRMED AT SCALE. A naive SUM over `semantic_scan_results` windows reports one asset as **294% of its episode scanned**, average 67.5% across 16 assets. Overlapping windows are double-counted. (playhead-pz32's `adScanFraction` does this correctly — interval UNION, intersected with the transcribed region, sub-ad-width gaps bridged — so the UI and terminal path are sound. The raw rows are not, and anything else reading them directly inherits the bug.)

DEFECT 2, NEW AND SEPARATE — IMPOSSIBLE GEOMETRY PERSISTED AS SUCCESS:

    rows with windowEndTime < windowStartTime :  6   (of 248 total, 2.4%)
    worst inversion                           : -635.2 s
    assets affected                           :  3
    by status: refusal 2, success 1, guardrailViolation 1, failedTransient 1

**One row has `status = 'success'` on a window that ends 635 seconds BEFORE it begins.** A successful scan of a negative-length region is not a coverage measurement, it is a corrupted row that every consumer will silently fold into a total. `windowStartTime < 0` does not occur (0 rows), so the corruption is in the END time or in the pairing, not a global offset error.

WHAT TO ESTABLISH, do not assume:
  * WHERE the inverted rows are written. An ordinal/atom-offset mix-up and a truncated-duration write are both plausible; note playhead-cmjo already records a second shard-sum duration write that can persist a truncated duration, and playhead-6av0 dealt with duplicated child rows. Check whether these share a cause before writing a third fix.
  * WHETHER a `success` verdict on an inverted window means the scan actually ran on SOMETHING (and only the bounds are wrong) or ran on nothing. Those need different fixes: the first is a bounds bug, the second means a verdict was invented for a region never examined — which is the "quantity that names an absence" shape this project keeps hitting.
  * WHETHER `adScanFraction` is genuinely immune. It clips and unions, so an inverted window most likely contributes zero — but that is an inference, not a test. Pin it.

ACCEPTANCE:
  * Impossible geometry is rejected at the WRITE, not tolerated at every read. A row that cannot exist should not be persisted.
  * Any ratio consumed as a decision input is bounded and validated at its source, with the out-of-range case named rather than clamped silently. gqx4's `unmeasurableDuration` is the established precedent for naming rather than guessing.
  * A regression test using these real shapes: the 294% asset and an inverted-window row.
  * State explicitly whether existing bad rows are repaired or left. Dan has twice declined historical repair ("i dont really care abkjt the existing library as long as the forward looking oicture is fixed"), so the default is LEAVE THEM and fix the write path — but the read path must then tolerate them without producing a wrong answer.

WHY THIS SHOULD PROBABLY PRECEDE playhead-hvk0: hvk0 is the biggest remaining reach lever and will be judged by exactly these coverage numbers. Fixing the ruler before taking the measurement is the same argument that redirected playhead-4xqf on 2026-07-30, where an N=12 conclusion inverted at N=44 because the measurement conditioned on detection having already succeeded.
acceptance_criteria: Which of the two hypotheses holds is established by evidence, and if contamination is found, every watermark write path is verified to be asset-scoped. A coverage ratio materially above 1.0 can no longer be reported as full coverage — it fails loudly or is clamped with a recorded anomaly. Regression covers the observed 5.277 case. If episodeDurationSec is the corrupt term, the fix addresses where it is populated, not just the consumer.
notes:
=== RESOLVED 2026-07-30 on branch bead/playhead-csbq ===

BOTH MEASUREMENTS REPRODUCED FIRST.
  * Defect 1: naive SUM over examined rows = 4871.64s on asset CD1AD629 against a
    1655.82s episode => 294.2%; 16 assets, average 68.1%. (Bead said 294% / 67.5%.)
    Two stacked causes: every window is DUPLICATED (the 6av0 child-row family) and
    passB extent attempts sit INSIDE the passA windows they refine.
  * Defect 2: 6 of 248 rows inverted, worst -635.22s, 3 assets. CORRECTION to the
    bead: TWO rows carry status='success', not one (scan-1227b814c9828f40 passA and
    scan-2a8101dca1638d10 passB). windowStartTime<0 occurs 0 times, confirmed.

WHAT A 'success' ON AN INVERTED WINDOW MEANS — ANSWERED: a BOUNDS bug, not an
invented verdict. Both success rows carry real model output (real spans, 12.6s and
6.1s latencies, certainty 'strong'). The scan ran on real text; only the projection
to two numbers was wrong.

ROOT CAUSE — three producers took first/last of an array never sorted by time:
  * makeRefinementScanResult read spans.first.startTime / spans.last.endTime.
    `spans` is unsorted: `sanitize` appends in model emission order and `mergeSpans`
    APPENDS any expansion span that overlaps nothing, so an outward expansion
    widening LEFTWARD lands at the tail. scan-2a8101dca1638d10's spans are ordered
    [107..108] then [105..105] — that is the whole bug.
  * attemptedRange and planPassA order segments by segmentIndex, which equals time
    order only while the atom sequence is monotone. It is not (see playhead-r5um).
All three now take min/max — byte-identical for ordered input, pinned by a test.

NOT the same cause as cmjo (shard-sum duration write) or 6av0 (duplicated child
rows), though 6av0's duplication is one of the two contributors to the 294%.

adScanFraction WAS ALREADY CORRECT — now pinned by test, not inference. It is
immune at THREE independent layers: the SQL read drops end<=start before the union,
AnalysisCoverageMath.normalize drops it again, and the intersection sweep's
`if end > start` contributes zero. Mutation testing confirmed: removing any ONE
layer does not change the answer; only the tempting "swap the bounds" coercion does,
