        XCTAssertLessThan: 0.406983083 !< 0.25
        "PlayheadRuntime.init wall-clock median = 407.0 ms; budget = 250 ms.
         Samples (post-warmup): [407.0ms, 519.5ms, 70.0ms, 491.9ms, 60.5ms]"
        run 2: failed again (7.541 s)

    PlayheadRuntimeMainActorFreedomTests.testMainActorIsNotHeldDuringRuntimeInit  FAILED 2/2
        XCTAssertGreaterThan: ("2") is not greater than ("3")
        "Main-actor freedom probe collected only 2 samples during the init window …
         the probe didn't actually measure anything."
        run 1 then took the HOST DOWN: `Swift/ContiguousArrayBuffer.swift:695:
        Fatal error: Index out of range`, after which xcodebuild restarted and printed
        `Test Suite 'PlayheadRuntimeMainActorFreedomTests' passed … Executed 0 tests`.

Both are PerfGate'd, so both have been unrun since playhead-zx0l — these are newly VISIBLE,
not newly broken. The pass exits `** TEST FAILED **` both times.

WHY IT WAS MISSED, and it is the standing defect class: `✔ Test run with 13 tests in 12
suites passed after N seconds` is the SWIFT TESTING summary. The XCTest half reports in the
`Test Case '-[…]' failed` / `Executed N tests` format and contributes nothing to that line.
A reader who stops at it sees a green pass with `** TEST FAILED **` underneath.

The two samples of 407 ms / 519 ms against a 250 ms budget on an idle box suggest a real
init regression rather than noise (the 60–70 ms samples show the budget IS achievable), so
the launch-perf one should be triaged before it is widened. The MainActorFreedom crash is
its own defect: an index-out-of-range during runtime init that destroys the evidence of
itself by killing the host.

DO NOT widen either assertion to make the pass green. See playhead-0vju for the separate,
genuinely marginal AdmissionController case (617 µs), which PASSED 2/2 at this review.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
R2 REVIEW: the `Index out of range` is a TEST-CODE defect, not a production one, and the
mechanism is exact. Whoever takes this should not go hunting in PlayheadRuntime for it.

PlayheadTests/Services/Diagnostics/MainActorFreedomTests.swift

    private static let warmupSamples = 2
    ...
    XCTAssertGreaterThan(                                   // line 183 — NON-FATAL
        allSamples.count, Self.warmupSamples + 1,
        "…the probe didn't actually measure anything.")

    let postWarmup = Array(allSamples.dropFirst(Self.warmupSamples))   // 2 - 2 = EMPTY
    let sortedSamples = postWarmup.sorted()                           // []
    let medianLatency = sortedSamples[sortedSamples.count / 2]        // [][0] -> TRAP
    let maxLatency = sortedSamples.last ?? 0                          // guarded!

`XCTAssertGreaterThan` records a failure and CONTINUES — the class does not set
`continueAfterFailure = false` — so with `allSamples.count == 2` (the count actually
reported) `postWarmup` is empty and the very next line subscripts it. That is
`Swift/ContiguousArrayBuffer.swift:695: Fatal error: Index out of range`, and it is the
line AFTER the assertion whose message says the probe measured nothing.

Note line 196 guards the same array with `?? 0` and line 195 does not. One of the two was
written defensively and the neighbour was not.

WHAT THIS CHANGES ABOUT THE TRIAGE

* The host death is NOT evidence of a crash in `PlayheadRuntime.init`. It is the test
  stepping off the end of its own empty array after correctly detecting that it had no
  data. Severity of the CRASH drops accordingly.
* The REAL defect the assertion is reporting is still open and is the interesting one:
  why does a racer spinning `MainActor.run` in a tight loop land only 2 hops across a
  ~400 ms init? Two readings, and they want opposite fixes — either the racer is being
  starved (the probe is broken) or the main actor really is held for essentially the whole
  init (the product is broken, which is exactly what this test exists to catch). The
  second reading is consistent with the OTHER failure in this bead — init median 407 ms
  against a 250 ms budget.
* So do NOT "fix the crash" by turning line 195 into `sortedSamples.first ?? 0` and moving
  on. Converting the trap into a clean failure is right and is two lines (an early
  `return` after the guard, or `try XCTUnwrap`), but it is the smaller half. The
  sample-starvation question is what determines whether 407 ms is a regression or the
  probe is lying, and both halves of this bead point at the same init.

NOT FIXED HERE: outside playhead-o89d's scope, and verifying either half needs a run of
the serial perf pass, which this review round is not spending. playhead-3f79 is now
BLOCKED on this bead — a third PerfGate'd test should not be moved into a pass whose
verdict cannot be read.

title: gate: absorb a TIMEOUT-kind failure in a deadline-carrying test by CLASS, not by name (Dan's call, o89d option C)

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
DAN'S DECISION, 2026-08-13: option C, class-based tolerance. Chosen over PerfGate-ing the
measured 136 (option A) and over PerfGate-ing the whole property (option B).

WHY C WON. The measurement in [[playhead-o89d]] is that the population needing to move is
>=377 tests (Chao1 on the baseline's own spectrum, f1=51 f2=5), not the 136 anyone has ever
observed, and that the failing set ROTATES -- two measurements fifteen days apart on unchanged
code shared not one name. So any NAME LIST is ~35% complete the day it lands and decays from
there. C keys on the PROPERTY instead, so it never needs re-measuring, and it moves ZERO tests
out of the default gate.

THE RULE:
    a TIMEOUT-kind failure in a test that carries a wall-clock deadline  -> absorb
    any other failure KIND, or a test with no deadline                   -> report NEW

This is the same identity discipline the baseline already uses: identity includes the failure
KIND, so a deadline-carrying test that fails an EXPECTATION still bites. That is what keeps the
tolerance from being a hole.

## THE BLIND SPOT, NAMED -- and it must be closed, not just noted

C's cost is that a REAL hang in a deadline-carrying test now looks exactly like starvation and
is absorbed silently. That is the standing defect class pointed at our own gate: "absorbed
because the box was busy" read as "absorbed because the box was busy OR the code hangs forever".

THE MITIGATION, and the reason it is now actually available: a wall-clock deadline is a valid
measurement on a QUIET box. `scripts/perf-tests.sh` is that box -- parallelism off, serial. So
a test whose timeout the default gate absorbs should be RE-CHECKED there, where the quantity
means what it says.

That is only worth anything because o89d fixed the destination bug: the serial pass named
`iPhone 17 Pro,OS=27.0`, which does not exist on this machine, so it exited before a single test
and had run ZERO tests since 2026-07-04. Before that fix, "relocate the check to the perf pass"
would have been relocating it to nowhere -- gated and deleted were the same thing.

SO THE BEAD IS TWO HALVES, and shipping only the first is how this becomes a hole:
  1. the absorb rule in gate_baseline.py, keyed on kind + the deadline property
  2. every ABSORBED test lands in the serial perf pass's population, so the deadline is still
     asserted somewhere it is meaningful. Absorbed-and-never-rechecked is not acceptable.

DO NOT implement half 1 without half 2.

ANTI-VACUITY, required before this can merge: mutate a deadline-carrying test into a genuine
infinite hang and prove the pipeline still reports it (via half 2). A tolerance that cannot be
shown to still catch a real hang has not been tested, it has been asserted.

PREREQUISITE TO CHECK FIRST: [[playhead-wwbr]] (P1) -- PlayheadFastTests.skippedTests is 20/32
a no-op, so 163 integration/benchmark tests run in every fast gate that the plan claims to skip.
That inflates the very saturation this tolerance is calibrated against, so wwbr may change the
numbers here. Sequence wwbr first or measure around it deliberately.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
RESCOPED 2026-08-13 by Dan's revised call: "do both, A then C."

This bead is NO LONGER the whole gate fix. [[playhead-06t7]] PerfGates the measured union first;
this bead now absorbs ONLY THE RESIDUAL that survives it.

WHY THE RESCOPE. The two arguments that made C the sole answer were both measured false (the
>=377 population was withdrawn at R1; the "a name list decays" claim was refuted at R2 -- the
07-29 cluster is still the top of the ranking today, and my two "near-disjoint" lists were two
top-6 truncations of one stable ranking). A name list DOES bound the population over the
measured window, so it goes first.

WHAT THIS BUYS THIS BEAD. The blind spot is the whole risk of class-based tolerance: a REAL hang
in a deadline-carrying test reads exactly like starvation and is absorbed. Applying the
tolerance to a residual rather than to the whole population shrinks that blind spot by roughly
the size of the union -- the tolerance covers what a measured list could not, instead of
covering everything.

UNCHANGED AND STILL REQUIRED:
  - the rule keys on failure KIND plus the deadline property, so an EXPECTATION failure in a
    deadline-carrying test still reports NEW. Identity includes kind; that is what keeps the
    tolerance from being a hole.
  - TWO HALVES. (a) the absorb rule; (b) every ABSORBED test still asserts its deadline in the
    serial perf pass, on a quiet box where the quantity means what it says. Do not ship (a)
    without (b).
  - anti-vacuity before merge: mutate a deadline-carrying test into a genuine infinite hang and
    prove the pipeline still reports it. A tolerance not shown to catch a real hang has been
    asserted, not tested.

NOW BLOCKED BY: [[playhead-wwbr]] -> [[playhead-1och]] -> [[playhead-06t7]] -> this.

title: PlayheadFastTests skippedTests is 20/32 a no-op — 163 integration and benchmark tests run in every fast gate
description:
Found while measuring playhead-o89d step 2, 2026-08-13. Not fixed there — fixing it needs a
mechanism the repo does not have yet, and a decision about whether a four-month-old intent
still holds.

## The number

`TestPlans/PlayheadFastTests.xctestplan` lists 32 entries in `skippedTests`. **12 are honoured.
20 are silently ignored, and the 163 tests behind them ran in the 2026-08-13 merge gate — all
163 confirmed present in the log.**

The cause is already documented in CLAUDE.md ("Xcode's xctestplan filter honors XCTest class
names but silently ignores Swift Testing identifiers"). What was not known is the SIZE: every
one of those 20 entries names a Swift Testing @Suite, so the plan's declared contract is
two-thirds fiction.

    silently ignored (tests)          honoured (tests)
      FoundationModelClassifierTests 107   BackgroundingCycleTests 1
      PreAnalysisIntegrationTests      9   FoundationModelShadowBenchmarkTests 5
      CombinedTuningReplayTests        6   ForceQuitCycleTests 1
      RealEpisodeBenchmarkTests        5   InterruptionHarnessInjectTests 5
      CorpusPhase1TranscriptPipelineTests 4  InterruptionHarnessTests 2
      CorpusEvidenceCatalogTests       4   LowPowerTransitionCycleTests 1
      Phase5IntegrationTests           4   MetricsCorpusIntegrationTests 3
      ReplaySimulatorE2ETests          4   NetworkLossCycleTests 1
      CorpusFullPipelineTests          3   RelaunchCycleTests 1
      CorpusAcousticBreakTests         3   StoragePressureCycleTests 1
      Phase3ShadowReplayHarnessTests   3   ThermalDowngradeCycleTests 1
      Phase4ShadowBenchmarkTests       2   UserPreemptionCycleTests 1
      + 8 more at 1 each

## Why it matters beyond tidiness

1. **CLAUDE.md's description of the plan is wrong.** It says FastTests "skips XCTest
   interruption-cycle integration suites" and runs in ~3 minutes. It also runs 163 integration
   and benchmark tests nobody thinks it runs — including `FoundationModelClassifierTests`, all
   107 of them.

2. **It hid a benchmark for four months.** `Phase3ShadowReplayHarnessTests` was added to
   `skippedTests` on 2026-04-10 (d55b0c1c). Its `benchmarkGate` has run in every fast gate
   since, failed every one, and been triaged as one more starvation flake — while its own
   comment says a trip "usually means a per-episode N^2 walk crept into the runner". Measured
   2026-08-13: 1.9 s alone, 25.2 s at a 443-test scope, 105–162 s in the full plan, against a
   5,000 ms budget. playhead-o89d PerfGate'd it, which is a fix for that one test, not for the
   plan.

3. **It is part of the load that starves the plan.** Those 163 tests run in 35–37 s scoped
   (measured, N=2), and every one of them is competing with the ~11.9k others.

## The fix is not a one-liner, which is why it is filed rather than done

`skippedTests` cannot express it, so honouring the declaration means gating in SOURCE — a
sibling of `PerfGate` keyed off an env var the IntegrationTests plan sets, applied to 20 suites.
That is a real mechanism plus a real coverage move, and it needs someone to confirm the
2026-04-10 intent is still the intent after four months of those tests actually running.

Cheap partial that needs no decision: a source canary asserting that every name in a plan's
`skippedTests` resolves to an XCTest class, so a new entry that will be ignored fails at test
time instead of silently doing nothing.

title: downloaded episode audio lives in Library/Caches — iOS may delete a user's downloads without telling anyone
description:
FOUND 2026-08-13 while diagnosing playhead-1216. Not the cause of that regression (all 9 files were present), but a real product exposure surfaced by looking.

WHERE THE AUDIO LIVES:
    Library/Caches/Playhead/AudioCache/complete/<sha256(episodeId)>.mp3   (+ .pin sidecar)
    Library/Caches/Playhead/AudioCache/{partials,resumeData,attribution}/

Library/Caches is the directory iOS PURGES UNDER STORAGE PRESSURE, without notifying the app and without asking the user. Measured on Dan's device: 9 complete files, 20-92 MB each, ~290 MB total.

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THIS PRODUCT SPECIFICALLY. A downloaded episode is not a cache entry — it is the thing the user asked for, often the thing they downloaded ON WIFI precisely so they could listen without a network. The failure mode is: user boards a plane, opens the app, and the episodes they deliberately downloaded are gone, with no explanation and no network to re-fetch them. That is the exact opposite of the felt experience this app is selling.

It also silently costs bandwidth: a purged episode re-downloads at 20-92 MB, and the day-0 rediff lane spends a further ~130 MB re-fetching B-copies for an asset whose bytes it already had.

THE REPO ALREADY KNOWS THIS PATTERN. StabilityDiagnosticsStore.swift:31 chose Application Support over Caches FOR EXACTLY THIS REASON, and playhead-1t0b was filed 2026-08-13 against the surface-status instruments for the same defect on a smaller quantity. Audio is the largest and most user-visible instance.

WHAT MAKES IT A DECISION RATHER THAN A ONE-LINE MOVE, and why this is filed rather than fixed:
  - Application Support and Documents are BACKED UP to iCloud/iTunes by default. Moving ~300 MB of re-downloadable podcast audio there without setting isExcludedFromBackup would bloat every user's backup and is the kind of thing App Review notices.
  - The correct shape is probably Application Support WITH the do-not-backup flag set, plus an explicit eviction policy the APP owns (LRU by last-played, a user-visible storage screen) rather than one iOS applies silently.
  - There may be a deliberate reason for the current placement that predates me; check the file's history before moving it.
  - A migration has to move existing files, not orphan them: the .pin sidecar and the sha256 naming both have to come along, and DownloadManager.cachedFileURL's pin fallback (:3509) has to keep working across the move.

SUGGESTED FIRST STEP: do not move anything yet. Instrument it — record when a cachedFileURL lookup finds a .pin but no .mp3, which is the signature of an OS purge, and see whether it ever fires in the field. If iOS is in fact never purging this app's cache, the exposure is theoretical and the migration can wait behind work that is measurably hurting. If it IS firing, that is a silent data-loss bug and it jumps the queue.

title: the surface-status episode_id_hash cannot be resolved to an episode from any supported pull — the salt is excluded from the archive by design
description:
ESTABLISHED 2026-08-13 in playhead-oa82 R1 review, while checking whether oa82's five new instruments can be read against a SPECIFIC asset on the next device pull. They cannot, and the reason is a deliberate privacy decision nobody has reconciled with the diagnostic use.

THE MECHANISM, at file:line.
  * Every producer on the surface-status JSON Lines stream stamps a HASHED episode id: SHA-256(installID || episodeId), hex (SurfaceStatusInvariantLogger.swift:594-600, SurfaceStatusEpisodeIdHasher).
  * The installID salt is a per-install random UUID persisted at Caches/Diagnostics/.surface-status-install-id (SurfaceStatusInvariantLogger.swift:640-652).
  * DogfoodDiagnosticsArchive — what Settings -> Send Diagnostics produces — states its exclusion outright: "no audio cache, no transcripts, no raw episode IDs, and no install-ID salt" (DiagnosticsExportService.swift:491-494). The filter is `filename.hasPrefix("surface-status-")` (:945-948), so the dotfile is structurally excluded too.

CONSEQUENCE. From a diagnostics archive you can count lines and read their codes, but you cannot say WHICH episode any line is about. For oa82 that is the difference between "some claim was attempted" and "the claim for F4A9D2BD — the one asset whose priority=20 row proves prepareEpisodeForAnalysis ran — was attempted". The whole tap-path narrowing is per-asset.

THE PULL-RECIPE TRAP, which is the part that will actually burn the next pull: oa82's recipe says pull `Library/Caches/Diagnostics/surface-status-*.jsonl`. That glob ALSO misses the salt, because the salt is a dotfile with a different prefix. A raw container pull of the whole `Library/Caches/Diagnostics/` DIRECTORY does carry it, and then the hash is recomputable offline. So the immediate remedy is a recipe change, not code.

WHY IT IS STILL A BEAD. The supported, in-app, no-cable path (Send Diagnostics) is attribution-blind by construction, and that is the path a non-developer dogfooder uses. Options, none chosen here:
  * pull the directory rather than the glob, and say so in every recipe (zero code, fixes only the cable path);
  * emit a SHORT per-session correlation token alongside the hash that maps to the episode within the archive's own contents (keeps the raw id out, restores intra-archive joins);
  * include the salt only in a developer-mode export.

NOT A DUPLICATE OF playhead-njkw, which is the SQL kickoff ledger's reach gap. This is about the JSONL stream's identity being unrecoverable once it does reach a reader.

title: background URLSession CONSTRUCTION is unbounded — DECIDED: bound it and fail the call (6 sites, one crossing per process)
description:
FOUND while fixing playhead-rouw, 2026-08-13. Filed rather than fixed because closing it needs a decision the bead did not own.

`backgroundSession(for:)` in DownloadManager.swift does

    URLSession(configuration: .background(withIdentifier: ...), delegate:, delegateQueue: nil)

on the actor, i.e. on the fixed-width Swift Concurrency cooperative pool, with NO bound. Creating a background session attaches to `nsurlsessiond`, which is the same daemon playhead-nsjn showed can park a caller in `mach_msg2_trap` indefinitely — and the same daemon that, MEASURED in this bead's after-run, failed to answer `downloadTask(with:)` seventeen times in one full plan (`the background transfer daemon did not answer within 10.000000s`).

So the two calls playhead-nsjn and playhead-rouw bounded are both reached THROUGH an unbounded one. `retireBackgroundTransfers` instantiates all three roles before it enumerates anything.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED HERE. `backgroundSession(for:)` returns a non-optional `URLSession` that ~a dozen call sites use directly. Bounding it means it can fail, which means every one of those call sites has to grow a "the daemon would not give me a session" path. That is an API change to the download subsystem, not a containment patch, and CLAUDE.md reserves that class of change for Dan.

EVIDENCE THIS IS NOT THEORETICAL: it is the only remaining unbounded crossing in the download path, and playhead-rouw's after-run still shows three tests with no verdict (unrelated names, merely in flight). If the census ever comes back naming download tests again with `allTasks` already bounded, this is where to look first.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
DAN'S DECISION 2026-08-13: BOUND IT AND FAIL THE CALL.

`backgroundSession(for:)` becomes failable with a timeout, on the same `BackgroundSessionIO` pattern playhead-nsjn and playhead-rouw already established. When the daemon will not hand back a session, the download subsystem REPORTS that it cannot download rather than parking forever on the cooperative pool.

Dan was given three options — bound-and-fail, leave-it-and-watch, and bound-with-a-foreground-fallback — and chose bound-and-fail. The fallback option was explicitly rejected as the shape this project keeps re-discovering: a session that still calls itself `background` while silently having stopped being one would take the overnight "wake up to analyzed episodes" behaviour away with nothing saying so.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS BEAD'S OWN SIZING, both measured before the decision:

1. THE COST IS SIX CALL SITES, NOT "~A DOZEN". `grep` returns 10 hits, but four are comments (`PlayheadRuntime.swift:3060`, `DownloadManager.swift:693`, `:1381`) and one is the internal no-arg forward (`:1316`). The real sites are:
     ForceQuitResumeScan.swift:543   (.interactive)
     DownloadManager.swift:1324      (`_ =`, a warmup — may not need a failure path at all)
     DownloadManager.swift:1342
     DownloadManager.swift:2512/2513 (.maintenance / .legacy, one ternary)
     DownloadManager.swift:2780      (inside retireBackgroundTransfers)

2. THE EXPOSURE IS ONE CROSSING PER PROCESS, NOT PER DOWNLOAD. `:1267` is `if let existing = _sessionsByRole[resolvedRole] { return existing }` — it is MEMOIZED — and `useDualBackgroundSessions` defaults false, so in practice exactly one role (.legacy) is ever constructed. That lowers the frequency a great deal and does NOT lower the consequence: the one crossing happens at first download, and if it parks, the download subsystem is dead for that entire process launch with no error anywhere.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS DESPITE NEVER BEING OBSERVED: it is the only remaining unbounded crossing in the download path, and both calls bounded tonight are reached THROUGH it — `retireBackgroundTransfers` instantiates all three roles before it enumerates anything. The worst moment for it to park is a background relaunch, which is precisely the moment nobody is looking.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES for whoever takes this:
  - A failed construction leaves `_sessionsByRole` empty, so the NEXT call retries naturally. Do not cache the failure.
  - The warmup site (`:1324`, `_ = backgroundSession(for: role)`) may legitimately swallow the failure — it is a warmup, and the real call retries. Decide that deliberately rather than by default.
  - Record the refusal where playhead-oa82's instruments write, so a device pull can tell "the daemon refused a session" from "no download was requested". That distinction is the whole lesson of oa82.
  - playhead-rouw's `boundedAllTasks` is the shape to copy: callback form, own serial queue, two independent bounds.

title: mutation-battery-gate-baseline.py --only prints 'control not run' and 'the vacuity control survived' in adjacent lines, and exits 0
description:
FOUND 2026-08-13 in playhead-tl6l R3 review, driving the committed R-series battery.

    $ python3 scripts/mutation-battery-gate-baseline.py --only RA1
    RA1   KILLED         NO VERDICT leaves the exit code again...

    1 mutation(s): 1 killed, 0 survived, 0 error, control not run
    All mutations killed, and the vacuity control survived.
    $ echo $?
    0

Two adjacent lines, one saying the control was NOT RUN and the next asserting it SURVIVED. Exit 0. This is the module's own standing defect class — a value that names one thing read as though it named another — inside the script whose entire job is to notice that.

WHY IT MATTERS. R99 is the vacuity control: a cosmetic edit that MUST survive, and if it is killed the battery is reddening on any edit at all and every KILLED above it is worthless. A partial run therefore has no evidence its verdicts mean anything, and it says the opposite in plain English. Anyone driving a focused rail — which is the normal way to iterate on one — reads a line asserting the control held.

MECHANISM, scripts/mutation-battery-gate-baseline.py:

  613  selected = [m for m in MUTATIONS if args.only in (None, m[0])]
  702  bad = [r for r in results if r[1] in ("SURVIVED", "ERROR", "CONTROL-KILLED")]
  708  next((r[1] for r in results if r[0] in EXPECT_SURVIVE), "not run")
  718  print("All mutations killed, and the vacuity control survived.")

`bad` cannot contain a control that never ran, so the run is clean; line 718 is unconditional. The summary at 708 computes the truth and line 718 contradicts it.

THE REPO HAS ALREADY RULED ON THIS EXACT HOLE, for the other battery. CLAUDE.md, on scripts/mutation-battery-untypeable.py: '--only cannot drop the control (a selection that omits TY99 has it appended, because a partial run printing `control not run` and exiting 0 is exactly the hole this battery replaces)'. The R series never got the same treatment.

THE FIX, and it is small — adopt the TY battery's rule rather than inventing a second one: append the control when --only omits it. If that is judged too slow, the alternative is that line 718 must be conditional and the exit code must be non-zero when the control did not run. Do NOT just soften the wording: a partial run that exits 0 with no control is the thing being fixed, not the sentence.

VERIFIED NOT A REGRESSION FROM playhead-tl6l: lines 702-718 are untouched by bead/playhead-tl6l (git diff main...HEAD over that file shows no hit for either string). The branch added rails and repaired three anchors; this hole predates it. Filed rather than fixed for that reason.

RELATED: [[playhead-wuic]] is the neighbouring bead — verification artefacts that report success without running — and this is the same class one layer in: not a battery that vanished, a battery that ran partially and claimed a control it never executed.

title: tests die without a verdict on MAIN — 33 started and reported neither pass, fail nor skip; the SUITE SCOPE is now a hypothesis
description:
FOUND 2026-08-12 by a control full-plan run on main @ 76b0a09a, executed to answer whether playhead-mn5e caused a crash block. It did not — main has the same one.

WHAT HAPPENS. xcodebuild's summary block on main lists 18 failing tests. NONE of them emits a per-test result line anywhere in the 7.5 MB log: no 'failed after', no 'Test Case ... failed', no 'error: -[', no 'recorded an issue'. A test that produces no per-test line did not fail an assertion — the test HOST DIED before it could report. Four names appear TWICE, which is the retry signature.

THE POPULATION, and it is coherent rather than scattered — every one is download/transfer:
    DownloadShowAttributionTests            8 entries
    ResumeSuspendedTransferTests            4 (two names, each listed twice)
    StreamingDownloadCachedTests            2
    DelegateWorkJournalTests                1
    DownloadManagerDaemonUnavailableTests   1
    SkipOrchestratorRevertTests             1
  and on the mn5e branch's run, additionally ExpiredWindowAttemptAccountingTests and
  EpisodeDownloadDelegateResumeHarvestTests.

HOW LONG THIS HAS BEEN TRUE. scripts/gate-baseline.PlayheadFastTests.json records 117 tests over 9 observed runs and contains ZERO entries from any of these suites. They have never once been captured — not as passing, not as failing. Nine full-plan runs produced no verdict about this family and nobody could tell, because [[playhead-tl6l]] is the tool's inability to see exactly this.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE GATE. These are the suites that cover download attribution surviving a process restart, resume-blob consumption, force-quit resume recovery, and abandoning a transfer the daemon could not resume. That is the machinery the whole background-download story rests on — and playhead-oa82's open question is whether a background download's kickoff observer ever ran. We are debugging the download path with a test family that has not reported a result in nine runs.

A LIKELY LEAD, NOT A DIAGNOSIS. CLAUDE.md records that DownloadManagerTests deliberately chmods a 'complete/' directory to 0o300 to prove a permission failure is handled, and restores it in a defer that an abnormal exit skips — the same mechanism that stranded 15 GiB of CoreSimulator trash (playhead-cgka). A suite that can leave the filesystem in a state its own teardown cannot undo is a plausible host-killer, and it is in the same family. Verify before acting: the crash may equally be a background-URLSession/daemon interaction, which is what most of these suites exercise.

FIRST STEP IS CHEAP: run just this family in isolation
    scripts/fast-gate.sh -only-testing:PlayheadTests/DownloadShowAttributionTests ...
and read the crash log out of the .xcresult. Isolated, the host has nothing else to take down with it and the diagnostic should be legible. Note the selective-run exemption in the gate baseline means this will not fight the baseline check.

DEPENDENCY: fix [[playhead-tl6l]] first or in parallel, otherwise there is no way to tell whether a fix here worked — the mechanism that would report success is the one that cannot see this population.
notes:
R1 REVIEW OF tl6l (2026-08-12): the population is 30 on main @ 76b0a09a and 14 on bead/mn5e, not 33 and 15. Four of the tests in the original count had truncated-but-present `passed after` lines and had actually PASSED; tl6l R1 widened the outcome patterns and re-measured. Two independent routes (global set-difference, and an order-sensitive launch-partitioned walk with retries subtracted) agree on 30/14.

TWO THINGS THAT WILL SAVE THIS BEAD A ROUND:

* THE LOG CONTAINS TWO TEST-HOST LAUNCHES, not one. `Restarting after unexpected exit, crash, or test timeout` is followed by a fresh `◇ Test run started.` and xcodebuild RE-RUNS part of the plan (524 tests on main, 573 on mn5e; each log's only `Test run with N tests` summary line is launch 2's and does NOT cover launch 1). Measured per launch: main launch 0 leaves 34 tests open at the crash, launch 1 rescues 4 and leaves 0 open; mn5e leaves 16, rescues 2, leaves 0. So the retries are real and must be subtracted — the casualty is a test that started before the crash and was never re-run.
* ZERO XCTest casualties in both logs (966 started = 936 passed + 30 skipped, exactly, in each). The dead population is entirely Swift Testing. main's casualty list is dominated by download/cache/streaming names (clearCache*, removeCache*, didCompleteWithError*, cache deletion*, delegate staging*), which is also where the `Failing tests:` block's retried entries cluster — DownloadShowAttributionTests, ResumeSuspendedTransferTests, StreamingDownloadCachedTests. That is a lead for the suite scope, not a verdict.

The two 7.2 MB logs the numbers come from live in a session scratchpad that will not outlive the session (see playhead-<new>); pull fresh ones rather than trusting those paths.
(The scratchpad-fragility bead referenced above is playhead-fer3.)

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
MEASUREMENT CORRECTION from playhead-tl6l's implementation, 2026-08-12. The population named in this bead is largely WRONG, and the method that produced it is the reason — the same method that produced tl6l's own wrong number.

The 'Failing tests:' summary spells a test `SuiteType.function()`. Swift Testing's console prints the test's DISPLAY NAME, e.g. @Test("A completion delivered to a NEW manager instance still carries the show"). The two spellings share nothing, so grepping a summary entry against the console returns zero for a test that reported perfectly well. That is where 'NONE of them emits a per-test result line anywhere' comes from.

RE-MEASURED by mapping every summary entry through its @Test attribute in PlayheadTests/ source:

  main @ 76b0a09a : 14 distinct summary names, 13 DID report a real failure and were already counted. ONE emitted nothing at all: SkipOrchestratorRevertTests.failedSuggestNoRestoresLatestBufferedRevision().
  bead/mn5e       : 15 distinct summary names, ALL 15 reported.

So the summary block is NOT the crash cohort. It is mostly ordinary failures that happen to live in the same launch.

THE REAL COHORT is the tests that STARTED and then reported neither pass, fail nor skip — exact, console-only, no name mapping needed:

  main : 33 Swift Testing tests
  mn5e : 15

after subtracting deliberate skips (30 XCTest PerfGate skips per run; before subtracting them the naive number reads 45 and 63). Neither run's cohort is confined to download/transfer — main's includes 'A record claiming a different schema rejects', 'Catches gap at start of timeline', 'apportionment is robust to extreme word-length variation' and 25 others across the tree. What they have in common is being IN FLIGHT when the host died, which under Swift Testing's in-process concurrency is a wide and largely arbitrary slice.

The crash itself is confirmed by xcodebuild's own words, present in both logs and needing no interpretation:

    Restarting after unexpected exit, crash, or test timeout; summary will include totals from previous launches.

WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR THIS BEAD. 'Which suites crash' is not answerable from the summary block, and the 7-suite list in the description should not be used to scope the fix. Start from the restart marker and the no-verdict census — `scripts/gate_baseline.py check` now prints both, so a single re-run names the cohort for you. The suspicion that it is download/transfer may still be right (that family is heavily represented and DownloadManagerTests is already known to chmod a directory to 0o300), but it is now a hypothesis rather than a measurement.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
R2 REVIEW OF tl6l (2026-08-13): THE POPULATION IS 11, AND IT IS THE SAME 11 ON BOTH BRANCHES. Not 33/15, not 30/14. This narrows the bead considerably and the narrowing is the useful part.

    main @ 76b0a09a : 11
    bead/mn5e       : 11
    identical sets, Jaccard 1.00

R1's 30/14 was the same defect class as the two corrections before it, one token further out. The app-log intrusion carries ITS OWN NEWLINE, so a spliced verdict becomes TWO physical lines and no line-oriented pattern can read either half. R1's widening only covers cuts that land after ` after`. The cuts also land inside the NAME, inside the verb, and once inside the word `Test`:

    ✔ Test "a b<TS> …                 + `yte-exact span outside the 90s window…" passed after 96.666 seconds.`
    ✔ Test "fast transcript chunks override stale transcript watermark" pa<TS> …   + `ssed after 107.082 seconds.`
    ✔ Tes<TS> …                       + `t "watermark within one shard past the duration is tolerated…" passed after 117.944 seconds.`

18 such lines on main, 3 on mn5e, EVERY ONE a passing test. gate_baseline.py now rejoins the halves before parsing; the census is exact and was cross-checked by three independent routes.

THE ELEVEN, verbatim, and they are ONE FAMILY — this is the scope hypothesis the bead asks for, now much tighter than "download/transfer":

    Cross-extension replacement purges stale siblings and removal cannot resurrect them
    background placement canonicalizes a routing URL suffix
    cache deletion during journal finalization revokes the stale finalized tail
    cleanup keeps the incomplete pin when artifact enumeration fails
    clearCache removes all cached files
    clearCache retires every staged background completion
    clearCache revokes an active streaming writer before deletion
    explicit cancellation invalidates the matching streaming transfer
    identity-qualified staging isolates a retired task from its replacement
    removeCache deletes both partial and complete files
    removeCache retires a staged background completion and its resume state

Every one is cache deletion / streaming-writer revocation / staged-background-completion retirement. That is a much sharper lead than the `Failing tests:` block's suite list, and it points at the SAME machinery from the other side: a writer or a staged completion being torn down while something still holds it.

Three things that follow:

1. THE 0.46-JACCARD ARGUMENT DOES NOT APPLY HERE. Two runs on different trees lost exactly the same eleven. This is a DETERMINISTIC crash, not a starvation flake, so it should reproduce in isolation — the bead's cheap first step is likely to work on the first try. Run the cache/streaming suites, not the whole download family.

2. THE THREE NAMES R1's LAUNCH-PARTITIONED WALK ADDED ON MAIN AND NOT ON mn5e are gone: `fast transcript chunks override stale transcript watermark` and `journal fetch result is threaded into the default bundle's work_journal_tail` both PASSED (spliced pass lines), as did mn5e's `watermark within one shard past the duration is tolerated`. So there is no main-vs-branch difference to explain — do not spend a round on one.

3. R1's other two measurements HOLD and are worth keeping: zero XCTest casualties in both logs (966 started = 936 passed + 30 skipped exactly), and the two-launch structure with retries that must be subtracted.

STATUS OF THE DEPENDENCY: playhead-tl6l is done and playhead-buvn is closed with it. The gate now records the crashed-host census per plan and FAILS on a name that is not in the record, so this bead has what it needed — a mechanism that can tell whether a fix worked. Note the record is currently UNRECORDED (the committed baseline is byte-identical to main's), so the arm is inert until the first `--accept-baseline`; when this bead succeeds, the accept should shrink that record and the accept output will name each of the eleven as `~- reports again`.

comments.text:
R3 GIFT FROM THE .xcresult (playhead-tl6l R3, 2026-08-13). The SUITE SCOPE this bead calls a hypothesis is now MEASURED, from a source with no display-name problem at all.

The .xcresult ACTION LOG carries a `Run test case` section per test titled `Suite/function()` — structured, exact, and completely independent of the console's @Test display names. Mapping the eleven casualties through it gives the suites directly:

    DownloadManagerCacheTests                5   (clearCache, removeCache, clearCacheCancelsActiveStreamingOwnership,
                                                  clearCachePreventsBackgroundResurrection, removeCachePreventsBackgroundResurrection)
    DownloadManagerImmutableArtifactTests    3   (backgroundPlacementCanonicalizesRoutingSuffix,
                                                  cleanupEnumerationFailureRetainsPin,
                                                  crossExtensionReplacementAndRemovalAreSiblingAtomic)
    BackgroundDownloadCompletionTests        2   (cacheDeletionRacingFinalizationDoesNotJournalSuccess,
                                                  identityQualifiedStagingIsIsolated)
    StreamingDownloadOwnershipTests          1   (explicitCancellationInvalidatesStreamingTransfer)

IDENTICAL on both runs, suite for suite and name for name. All four suites live in PlayheadTests/Services/Downloads/ — DownloadManagerTests.swift (8), BackgroundDownloadCompletionTests.swift (2), StreamingDownloadTests.swift (1). So the family claim holds, and it is now names rather than a lead.

THAT REVISES THIS BEAD'S SUITE LIST. The population here (DownloadShowAttributionTests 8, ResumeSuspendedTransferTests 4, StreamingDownloadCachedTests 2, DelegateWorkJournalTests 1, DownloadManagerDaemonUnavailableTests 1, SkipOrchestratorRevertTests 1) came from the `Failing tests:` block, and the .xcresult says those are ORDINARY FAILURES with real messages, not casualties. Four examples straight out of the bundle's testFailures:

    DownloadShowAttributionTests/attributionSurvivesProcessRestart()
        Expectation failed: await relaunched.loadDownloadAttribution(...)?.podcastId == Self.showId
    ResumeSuspendedTransferTests/resumeConsumesBlob()
        Expectation failed: outcome == .resumed / outcome -> .daemonUnavailable
    DownloadManagerDaemonUnavailableTests/backgroundDownloadAbandonsATransferItCouldNotResume()
        Expectation failed: await manager._backgroundDownloadAdmissionCountForTesting() == 1
    SkipOrchestratorRevertTests/failedSuggestNoRestoresLatestBufferedRevision()
        Test exceeded execution time allowance of 1 minute

The last one is the test the implementer called main's one genuine casualty because it printed no console line. It is in the bundle with a verdict and a reason: a ONE-MINUTE TIME LIMIT, not a dead host. So the `Failing tests:` block was never this bead's cohort, in either direction.

WHAT THE CRASH ITSELF LOOKS LIKE, and it is thin. main's log, line 53679-53684: the last thing launch 0 emits is `> Test "the coverage-guard sweep costs the merge its adopted terminal — in BOTH orders" started.`, then two blank lines, then `*** If you believe this error represents a bug, please attach the result bundle at ...` with NO MESSAGE ABOVE IT, then the relaunch (pid 93019 -> 93903). The banner's own text is empty in the console AND in the .xcresult action log — I searched every `messages` array in both bundles and there is no error/crash record at all. So the bundle does NOT carry a crash reason. Do not spend a round looking for one in it.

ONE MORE THING WORTH KNOWING BEFORE THE ISOLATION RUN. The .xcresult is a LESS complete record of a crashed run than the console, by a wide margin: 1,048 tests on main (1,121 on mn5e) have an action-log section but NO node in the structured results tree and `duration: 0` — their results were never committed to the database — and 1,035 of those 1,048 demonstrably RAN AND PASSED (e.g. `high confidence FM result shows brand name`, `passed after 195.586 seconds` in the console). stdout was already flushed; the result stream was not. So an isolation run's verdict should be read off the console, and the .xcresult used only for the structured Suite/function identity it uniquely provides.

THE ELEVEN, identical on main @ 76b0a09a and on bead/playhead-mn5e, derived from the .xcresult action log rather than the console text:

  DownloadManagerCacheTests             5
  DownloadManagerImmutableArtifactTests 3
  BackgroundDownloadCompletionTests     2

By name:
  Cross-extension replacement purges stale siblings...
  background placement canonicalizes a routing URL suffix
  cache deletion during journal finalization revokes the stale finalized tail
  cleanup keeps the incomplete pin when artifact enumeration fails
  clearCache removes all cached files
  clearCache retires every staged background completion
  clearCache revokes an active streaming writer before deletion
  explicit cancellation invalidates the matching streaming transfer
  identity-qualified staging isolates a retired task from its replacement
  removeCache deletes both partial and complete files
  removeCache retires a staged background completion and its resume state

THE SAME ELEVEN ON TWO DIFFERENT TREES — Jaccard 1.00, against 0.46 for this repo's ordinary load flakes. That is a DETERMINISTIC crash, not a starvation flake, so it should reproduce in isolation on the first try. Every one is cache-deletion / streaming-writer / staged-background-completion.

MY ORIGINAL SUITE LIST WAS WRONG AND IS SUPERSEDED. This bead was filed naming DownloadShowAttributionTests, StreamingDownloadCachedTests, ResumeSuspendedTransferTests, EpisodeDownloadDelegateResumeHarvestTests, DownloadManagerDaemonUnavailableTests, DelegateWorkJournalTests and ExpiredWindowAttemptAccountingTests. That list came from xcodebuild's  summary block, and the bundle shows those are ORDINARY FAILURES carrying real messages — not casualties. Including the one I singled out to Dan as 'main's one genuine casualty', SkipOrchestratorRevertTests/failedSuggestNoRestoresLatestBufferedRevision(), which the bundle records as 'Test exceeded execution time allowance of 1 minute'. A plain timeout.

The  block is a LEAD, never a census — the same lesson tl6l learned four times over.

DO NOT GO HUNTING FOR A CRASH MESSAGE. The crash banner carries NO message in the console OR the bundle. R3 checked both. A round that spends itself looking for one will find nothing.

METHOD NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS, because it is counter-intuitive: the .xcresult is a sound independent ROSTER and a BAD outcome source. Its test tree gives every node it has a verdict — there is no present-but-unjudged state — so casualties are ABSENT-FROM-BUNDLE and must be found against the action log's 'Run test case' sections (11,893 on main vs 10,845 tree nodes). Of the 1,048 sections with no tree node, 1,035 ran and PASSED and simply were not written to the result stream. Taking the bundle's own apparent casualty count would overstate the truth by ~95x.

TYPO FIX to the comment above: two phrases were eaten by my own shell. I wrote the comment with backticks inside a double-quoted string, so zsh executed the backticked text as a command and substituted its (empty) output. Both gaps are the same missing phrase, "the Failing tests: summary block":

The second sentence is the load-bearing one and was left nearly meaningless. Restated in full:

  THE FAILING TESTS: BLOCK IS A LEAD, NEVER A CENSUS. It names tests xcodebuild
  blamed; it does not tell you whether they reported a verdict, and its spelling
  (SuiteType.function()) shares nothing with the Swift Testing console's @Test

Noted for the mechanism as much as the content: a tracker comment is the durable artifact a later round reads, and a shell that silently deletes part of it is the same shape as everything else this pair of beads is about — evidence destroyed by the thing that was supposed to record it.

comments.text:
R1 REVIEW, 2026-08-13 (worktree rouw, tip 7f27f995). VERDICT: the fix is PROVEN, but NOT by the census delta the bead reported — by a different measurement in the same logs that is far stronger, and the determinism claim I gave Dan was wrong.

THE DETERMINISM CLAIM WAS WRONG AND I MADE IT. I told Dan the eleven were deterministic: four gate runs at 11/11/15/11, the same eleven every time, Jaccard 1.00, 'nothing has ever recovered'. The implementer's own control run on the branch base lost only THREE of the eleven, which is not what that predicts. Re-reading all four of this bead's full-plan logs through scripts/gate_baseline.py:

    full1  (control, no fix)          8 NO VERDICT   3 of the eleven
    after1 (fix, sampler-contaminated) 391 NO VERDICT 0 of the eleven
    after2 (fix, SHARED queue)         217 NO VERDICT 0 of the eleven
    after3 (fix, own queue — ships)      3 NO VERDICT 0 of the eleven

So the census count is load-dependent and 8 -> 3 IS run-to-run noise. It counts whatever was in flight when the host died, and after1/after2 show that number moving by two orders of magnitude on the same code.

WHAT ACTUALLY PROVES IT is per-test, not aggregate. Take the eleven plus the two download-attribution names the control also lost, and ask each log whether the test STARTED and then REPORTED:

    full1  (control): 5 of 13 started and never reported
    after1 (fix):     13 of 13 reported  — in a run that lost 391 others
    after2 (fix):     13 of 13 reported  — in a run that lost 217 others
    after3 (fix):     13 of 13 reported  — in a run that lost 3

That is the measurement that separates 'the fix works' from 'the daemon happened to answer', and it separates them in the right direction: the two post-fix runs where the box was in FAR worse shape than the control still lost none of this family. Under the load-noise hypothesis those thirteen should have been swept up with the other 391. They were not, in any of three runs.

The bound's own log line is corroboration but is weaker than the bead claims, on two counts. It fires 17 times in after2, 9 in after1, 4 in after3 — not a stable count, and the 17 is from the SHARED-queue build, not the shipped one. And on a serial queue a submission that never reaches the front logs 'did not answer' for a daemon it never spoke to, so the count is an upper bound on genuine daemon silence, not a census of it. Every firing in all three runs names com.playhead.episode-downloads, i.e. one session, which is consistent with useDualBackgroundSessions being off.

TWO DOWNLOAD TESTS FAIL ON THE FIX BRANCH AND ARE NOT THE FIX'S DOING. DownloadShowAttributionTests.cancelReapsAttribution and clearCacheReapsAttribution fail in after2 and after3 on the POSITIVE WITNESS (loadDownloadAttribution != nil at :353/:381), i.e. backgroundDownload never wrote the record — the downloadTask bound firing, which is playhead-nsjn/gpdb territory. Both are already recorded in the gate baseline as load-sensitive, both PASS under a scoped run, and both had NO VERDICT in the control so the control cannot be used to argue they regressed.

ZERO PRODUCTION DEFECTS FOUND. Three test-side defects were found and fixed in 7f27f995 (an evadable source canary — three probes got the exact hazard past it, verified rc=0; a positive clause that let boundedAllTasks keep its name and lose its body; and nothing checking that onItsOwnQueue carries the .neverAnswers seam, whose loss makes both recovery rails pass while covering nothing). Three follow-ups filed: playhead-sq80, playhead-f1wb, playhead-3erm.

THE SAFETY ARGUMENT SURVIVES ITS ATTACK, with one qualification. All three of removeCache, clearCache and cancelDownload arm an identity-required guard (backgroundIdentityRequiredEpisodes / requireRegisteredBackgroundIdentityAfterBulkClear) unconditionally, before returning, needing no daemon — so a late completion for a deleted episode is discarded whether or not the enumeration answered, and the bytes cannot be resurrected. That is the property that makes failing open acceptable and it is genuinely there. What 'never a lost deletion' does not cover: the OS-side cancel() for a task this process never admitted (force-quit, reattached on relaunch — activeBackgroundTransfers is not repopulated for it until its COMPLETION callback), and cancelDownload's attribution reap, which reads retireBackgroundTransfers' return value. See playhead-sq80.

NO DEADLOCK in the DispatchSemaphore latch: all three background sessions are constructed with delegateQueue: nil (DownloadManager.swift:1282), so URLSession makes its own serial OperationQueue and getAllTasks' completion can never be delivered on the dispatch queue perform runs on. The one real coupling is that the delegate queue does a synchronous file copy in didFinishDownloadingTo, so an enumeration issued during a completion waits behind it — bounded at 10 s, and a plausible contributor to the observed firings.

title: gate_baseline.py was BLIND to tests that get NO VERDICT — 11 deterministic + load-sensitive churn, now recorded as a union with counts
description:
FOUND 2026-08-12 verifying playhead-mn5e's merge gate. The gate's whole purpose is that its verdict is about the DIFF rather than the count; this is a population it cannot see at all, and it is silent about that.

THE OBSERVATION. mn5e R6's full-plan run reported:

    gate-baseline: RED (71 known / 16 NEW)

and R6 reconciled every Swift Testing failure against the baseline — 83 distinct, 0 unaccounted. That reconciliation was correct AND the verdict was still incomplete, because xcodebuild's own summary block carried NINETEEN MORE:

    Failing tests:
        ExpiredWindowAttemptAccountingTests.expiryDoesNotSpendAnAttempt()
        DelegateWorkJournalTests.stagingFailureReleasesOwnership()
        DownloadShowAttributionTests.attributionSurvivesProcessRestart()      <- listed TWICE
        ... 7 suites, 19 entries, 4 of the names duplicated

VERIFIED SIGNATURE, not inferred. Each of those names appears ONLY in the Failing tests: block and NOWHERE else in the 7.5 MB log. Greps over the whole log: 'failed after' -> 0 for these names; 'Test Case .* failed' -> 0 in the entire run; 'error: -[' -> 0; 'recorded an issue' -> 110, none of them these. A test that produces no per-test line at all did not fail an assertion — the HOST DIED before it could report. The duplicate entries are the retry signature.

WHY THE TOOL CANNOT SEE IT. scripts/gate_baseline.py parses per-test result lines. A crashed host emits none, so these tests are absent from the run's observed set entirely — they are neither matched against the baseline (not 'known') nor reported as regressions (not 'NEW'). They fall out of the arithmetic in BOTH directions. Confirmed against the baseline file: all 7 suites have ZERO entries in scripts/gate-baseline.PlayheadFastTests.json (117 tests, 9 runs), i.e. nine recorded runs and this population has never once been captured.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A MISSING NUMBER. CLAUDE.md's rule for reading a red gate is 'RED (N known / 0 new) -> exit 0'. A run whose entire test host crashed in seven suites can therefore print a reassuring known/new split and exit 0, because the crash removed the evidence of itself. That is the same failure shape the disk preflight was built for — 'a gate that runs out of room WEDGES... indistinguishable from a slow test run' — one layer up.

THE FIX, and it is small: parse the 'Failing tests:' block, diff its entries against the tests that DID emit a per-test line, and report the difference as its own category — something like 'K tests failed with NO per-test result (crashed host)'. It must be a distinct verdict line, not folded into NEW, because the remedy differs: a NEW failure is triaged against the diff, whereas a crashed host means the run did not produce a verdict about those suites AT ALL and must be re-run.

SECOND, CHEAPER HALF: the same block is where a renamed or deleted baseline member would show up, so the parser already has a reason to read it.

SCOPE NOTE. Whether THIS crash is a regression is a separate question and is being answered by a control run on main @ 76b0a09a. All 7 suites are download/transfer code (DownloadShowAttribution, StreamingDownloadCached, ResumeSuspendedTransfer, EpisodeDownloadDelegateResumeHarvest, DownloadManagerDaemonUnavailable, DelegateWorkJournal, ExpiredWindowAttemptAccounting) and mn5e touches TrustScoring/AdDetection/AnalysisStore only — but that is an argument, not a measurement, which is why the control is running. This bead is about the BLINDNESS, which is a defect whatever that control says.

RELATED: [[playhead-o89d]] carries voez steps 2+3 (the PerfGate question and the pass-direction check) and is the neighbouring gate-honesty bead.

They have been failing to report for at least nine full-plan runs and the gate said nothing, in either direction, on either branch. The verdict line 'RED (85 known / 14 NEW)' is not merely incomplete; it is stated with the same confidence it would have if those suites had passed.

That is the exact hazard: main today would print 'RED (N known / 0 new) -> exit 0' on a run where an entire test family never executed to a verdict.

The crash ITSELF is now filed separately — the two are different defects and must not be fixed as one. This bead is the TOOL being unable to see a crashed host; the neighbouring bead is the download suites crashing.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-12 on bead/playhead-tl6l. The defect is real and is closed. The POPULATION named in this bead was not, and the correction matters more than the fix.

THE BEAD'S OWN EVIDENCE WAS MEASURED THE WRONG WAY. 'Each of those names appears ONLY in the Failing tests: block and NOWHERE else in the 7.5 MB log' is true and means nothing: the block spells a test `SuiteType.function()` while Swift Testing's console prints its @Test DISPLAY NAME. Grepping one against the other returns zero by construction, for a test that reported perfectly well. Re-measured through the source-level @Test mapping:

  mn5e : 15 distinct block names, ALL 15 had reported and were already counted
  main : 14 distinct block names, 13 had. ONE was genuinely invisible.

So '19 failures counted toward neither known nor NEW' was 0 and 1, not 19 and 18.

THE BLINDNESS IS REAL AND BIGGER, JUST ELSEWHERE. Tests that STARTED and then reported neither pass, fail nor skip — exact, console-only, no mapping needed:

  main @ 76b0a09a : 33      mn5e : 15

(45 and 63 before subtracting the 30 XCTest PerfGate skips per run — which is why parsing SKIP as a third outcome had to land with this.) Zero of them appear in the baseline file's 117 tests over 9 runs. And both logs carry xcodebuild's own unambiguous `Restarting after unexpected exit, crash, or test timeout`, about which the verdict said nothing.

WHAT SHIPPED

  gate-baseline: RED (85 known / 0 new) — 33 tests got NO VERDICT (crashed host)

The all-clear string can no longer stand alone. GREEN is unreachable while the count is non-zero. NO VERDICT is its own category, never folded into NEW, because the remedies differ. An ABSENT baseline member now names the crash as its cause instead of 'renamed, deleted or newly skipped', which used to send the reader hunting a rename that never happened. And `--accept-baseline` CARRIES FORWARD a recorded entry that got no verdict rather than pruning it — merge treats unreached as renamed, so a crash would have shrunk the file from inside the one command meant to maintain it, and the shrinking diff would have read as good news.

EXIT CODE: reportable, NOT fatal, deliberately. It fires on main today on a pre-existing crash owned by [[playhead-rouw]], and CLAUDE.md is explicit that a gate red for a reason its reader cannot fix is one they learn to route around — 'strictly worse than having no linter'. The repo's own answer to 'red for a pre-existing reason' is to record it and diff, and this bead was not permitted to refresh the baseline. A baseline member with no verdict is still fatal, via ABSENT, unchanged. Arming it is filed as [[playhead-6h3f]].

THE BLOCK IS A LEAD, NOT A CENSUS — and this is a limit, written down rather than glossed. `Suite.cancelReapsAttribution()` (reported under a display name) and `Suite.failedSuggestNoRestoresLatestBufferedRevision()` (main's one genuine casualty, which never printed a line at all) are INDISTINGUISHABLE from the log. Resolving them means parsing PlayheadTests/**.swift for @Test attributes — trading a sound log-only tool for a source-coupled heuristic whose every miss is a false crash alarm. Not taken. The block is parsed, reported with an exact entries-vs-distinct count (19 entries / 15 distinct on mn5e; a repeat is a retry, not a second test), and labelled a lead. It earns its place by naming a casualty that never started, which the started-set cannot see.

VERIFICATION. 117 unit tests (36 new), ~1.9s, no build. comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
R2 REVIEW 2026-08-13. One PRODUCTION DEFECT found and fixed; the census was wrong for a FOURTH time and the correction is again the same defect class. playhead-buvn's arming shipped with it, and playhead-fer3 is fixed rather than filed. Both closed.

THE CENSUS IS 11 AND 11, AND IT IS THE SAME ELEVEN TESTS. R1's 30/14 was contaminated by 18 spliced lines on main and 3 on mn5e, every one of them a test that PASSED.

R1 correctly identified that xcodebuild splices app output into a verdict line and correctly widened the patterns so a cut inside the trailing ` seconds` still reads as a verdict. What it missed is that the intrusion carries ITS OWN NEWLINE: one logical verdict becomes TWO PHYSICAL LINES, cut at an arbitrary byte, and no line-oriented pattern can read either half. The cuts land inside the NAME, inside the verb, and once inside the word `Test` itself:

    ✔ Test "flag OFF is byte-identical<TS> …    +  ` for both the exempt and the guarded shape" passed after 96.203 seconds.`
    ✔ Test "…watermark" pa<TS> …               +  `ssed after 107.082 seconds.`
    ✔ Tes<TS> …                                +  `t "watermark within one shard…" passed after 117.944 seconds.`

R1's own two routes agreed with each other and were both wrong the same way, which is the reminder worth keeping: two routes that share an ASSUMPTION are one route.

FIX: `rejoin_spliced_lines`, run over the lines before anything parses them, so start / pass / fail / issue / skip / XCTest are all repaired at once rather than one pattern at a time. Three guards make it unable to invent a verdict — the head must carry a marker and must NOT already parse, the following line must NOT parse on its own, and the join must parse; together the second and third force the match to SPAN the join. The `following` guard was added because a rail caught the repair without it FABRICATING a test named `victim" recorded an iss✘ Test "victim`. Measured: the repair added 18 and 3 outcomes and LOST NOTHING (started/passed/failures/skipped compared set-wise, before and after, on both 7.2 MB logs), and costs 30 ms of a 129 ms parse.

WHY IT IS A PRODUCTION DEFECT AND NOT TRIVIA: playhead-buvn arms the gate on this number. 19 of main's 30 were an artefact of how chatty the app happened to be on that run, so arming on the unrepaired census would have armed the gate on log interleaving. And the direction never yet hit is the dangerous one — 88 fail lines against 10,910 pass lines is the only reason it was passes that got severed; a severed FAIL is a LOST FAILURE that reads as a not-fatal crash casualty.

INDEPENDENT CENSUS, THREE ROUTES, none sharing code with the parser: (a) a per-identity state machine keyed on the LAST event; (b) prefix resolution of severed lines against the naive casualty set; (c) exact reconstruction by undoing the splice. (a) gave 29/14 and exposed the first extra case; (c) is exact and gives 11/11. Every one of the 21 repairs is corroborated by the test's own start line. Route (a) also disagreed with the module on 28 names — that turned out to be MY parser truncating names that contain a double quote, not the module's; two parsers with different bugs converging on the same eleven is the strongest evidence available here.

M23 — R1's claimed equivalent mutant — CHECKED, NOT ACCEPTED, AND IT IS TRUE FOR A STRONGER REASON THAN R1 GAVE. R1 argued from two logs rendering identically. It holds for EVERY input: `run.passed` has already had `failures` removed one line above, so the set subtracted is exactly `ran`, and both of the only two readers of `run.skipped` (`no_verdict`, which subtracts `ran` first; `identities`, which unions `ran` in) are indifferent to the overlap. The line stays as an invariant with the reasoning written at it, not as behaviour.

THE COMMITTED BATTERY HAD NOT RUN FOR TWO ROUNDS. scripts/mutation-battery-gate-baseline.py refuses to start on a drifted anchor, and three (R06, R14, R27) had been dead since 40ac7dcc — this bead's own implementation commit. So the "17 rails, all killed" and "37 rails, 36 killed" both rounds report came from ad-hoc scratchpad scripts that no longer exist and never protected anything. Anchors repaired; R1's four safety properties added as committed rails RB1-RB5; filed playhead-wuic for the process question.

comments.text:
R3 REVIEW 2026-08-13. ZERO PRODUCTION DEFECTS. The census was re-derived by a method nobody here had used — the structured .xcresult rather than the console text — and it CONFIRMS 11 and 11, the same eleven, on both runs.

WHY THAT IS WORTH SOMETHING. All five earlier numbers (19/18, 33/15, 30/14, and R2's 11/11) parsed the SAME text log. R2's own verdict on R1 was 'two routes sharing an assumption are one route', and the assumption none of the five ever tested was that the console is the roster. This route takes the roster from the bundle instead.

WHICH POPULATION I COUNTED, because the task's warning was right in an unexpected direction:

  PRESENT-BUT-UNJUDGED IS EMPTY. The bundle's test tree gives every node it has a verdict — Passed/Failed/Skipped, no third state. So a casualty is ABSENT-FROM-BUNDLE, and absence needs a roster.
  THE ROSTER is the bundle's ACTION LOG: one `Run test case Suite/function()` section per test. 11,893 on main, and a strict SUPERSET of the tree's 10,845 — 0 tree nodes lack a section.
  1,048 sections carry `duration: 0` and no tree node: results never committed to the database. 1,035 of them RAN AND PASSED — `high confidence FM result shows brand name` is in the console at `passed after 195.586 seconds`. stdout was flushed, the result stream was not. mn5e: 1,121 lost, 1,108 with a console verdict.
  13 of the 1,048 have no console verdict. Two are my own mapper failing on a @Test whose display name is a Swift multi-line literal, and both passed in both runs. The remaining ELEVEN are the census.

SO THE .xcresult IS A SOUND INDEPENDENT ROSTER AND A BAD OUTCOME SOURCE — its casualty population is ~95x the truth. Recorded in the module docstring so a seventh attempt does not 'fix' the census by switching to it.

TWO CORROBORATIONS, both new. The bundle records 41 skips on main and 42 on mn5e and this module counts 41 and 42 — the third-outcome parsing the whole census rests on is exact, from an independent source. And the display-name collision limit is now measured end to end: 64 colliding names over 141 ids, 0.59 % of 10,833, with NONE of the eleven sharing a name with a test that reported.

THE ARMING WAS ATTACKED. 14 probes over the two real logs against throwaway baselines, plus 10 mutants of gate_baseline.py to prove they bite — unrecorded-read-as-zero, new-casualties-off-the-exit-code, recovery-made-fatal, census-unioned, carry-forward-deleted, the >50 % refusal disabled, no_verdict-off-crashed_host, diff-direction-inverted, ABSENT-off-the-exit-code, absent_crashed-never-populated. 10 killed, 0 survived, control green, restore byte-exact by SHA-256. INERT-when-absent holds and is the only reason main is not red. Substitution exits 65, a recovery exits 0, accept holds the census across a 2nd and 3rd accept on alternating trees, and a >50 % baseline loss still refuses.

ONE OF MY OWN PROBES WAS VACUOUS AND A MUTANT CAUGHT IT. Judged against the committed baseline both real logs are already RED for 14 NEW FAILURES, which masks what ABSENT contributes — so 'ABSENT dropped from the exit code' SURVIVED until the probe was rebuilt on a baseline merged from the run itself. Same conflation R1 and R2 each shipped once; worth the sentence.

playhead-wuic IS CLOSED IN PRACTICE. I ran the committed battery myself: 51/51 anchors match exactly once (no drift refusal), 51 rails, 50 killed, R99 OK-SURVIVED, exit 0, and all three files byte-identical afterwards. No rail is vacuous in the way R1's and R2's were: the free unmutated pass verifies all 61 named tests exist and pass before anything is mutated, and it earned its keep here — my own docstring edit put a `"""` inside the module docstring and the battery refused with 'the rails are RED before any mutation' rather than crediting 51 kills. BUT THE BATTERY HAS A HOLE, FILED AS [[playhead-bgs1]] (P1, pre-existing, outside this diff). `--only RA1` prints 'control not run' and then, on the next line, 'All mutations killed, and the vacuity control survived.' — and exits 0. CLAUDE.md records the TY battery closing exactly this hole ('--only cannot drop the control'); the R series never got it. Not fixed here: lines 702-718 are untouched by this branch.

INDEPENDENT HUNT over git diff main...HEAD found nothing to change. Five adversarial probes on the splice repair behave as documented, including the direction the wild has never produced — a severed FAIL is recovered, a double splice stays a REPORTED casualty rather than an invented verdict, glyph-bearing app output is not repaired into one, a whole-verdict tail is not swallowed, the restart banner is not absorbed. On the real logs 19 of 19 severed TEST lines are repaired on main and 3 of 3 on mn5e; the one apparent residue is a `Suite` line, which the census does not read. fast-gate.sh's diff is comments only and it always passes --plan, so the one unguarded cross-plan census comparison in verdict() is unreachable through the driver.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
THIRD OBSERVATION, from a REAL GATE RUN on the armed code (bead/playhead-tl6l @ 4dfffc4c, cold build, full plan, 2026-08-12 23:10). This is evidence no amount of re-analysing the two preserved logs could have produced, and it contradicts the arming's central assumption.

VERDICT RENDERED CORRECTLY, end to end:
  gate-baseline: RED (68 known / 6 NEW) — 15 tests got NO VERDICT (crashed host)
  HOST RESTART   xcodebuild restarted the test host 1 time(s)
  NOT RECORDED   this baseline has never recorded a crashed-host census, so the arm below is INERT
  exit 0
0 XCTest failures; 0 Swift Testing failures under 97 s, so all 6 NEW are load flakes. The INERT-when-unrecorded design works exactly as specified — this is why the gate is not red today.

THE SET IS NOT STABLE, and two runs could not show it. Parsed with the shipped parse_run over all three logs:

  run1 main control    11
  run2 mn5e            11
  run3 tl6l (tonight)  15

  run1 vs run2   Jaccard 1.00   (the basis for choosing a SET)
  run1 vs run3   Jaccard 0.73
  core present in ALL THREE: 11
  recovered in any run: ZERO

So the eleven are a DETERMINISTIC CORE — three runs, three different trees, never once absent. That is a much stronger claim for playhead-rouw than two runs gave. But run 3 adds FOUR names on top:

  Bank wired => orchestrator holds it (write trigger live)
  a retry that makes progress does not spend the retry budget
  an unplayed long episode is transcribed end to end, and the ladder stops
  extractAndPersist rolls back seam batch when persistence fails after coverage update

Those are not download/cache tests; they read as the load-sensitive families this repo already knows about.

WHY THIS IS A DESIGN DEFECT IN THE ARM, not a curiosity. R2 chose a SET, REPLACED not unioned, arguing from Jaccard 1.00 that churn was not a risk and substitution was. With a third observation the set only ever GROWS. Under replaced-set semantics an armed gate on a night like tonight reports four NEW casualties and exits 65 — red for a reason its reader cannot fix, which is precisely the hazard R2's own exit-code argument was constructed to avoid. The gate would then be routed around, which CLAUDE.md calls strictly worse than having no linter.

THE REPO ALREADY SOLVED THIS ONE LAYER UP. The failure baseline is explicitly a UNION over observations carrying seen/failed counts, because Jaccard there is 0.46 and 'fewer than half the failures recur'. Its own prose says to expect the file to grow for a run or two and not to read that as regressions. The crashed-host census needs the same treatment: union with observation counts, so a name seen in 1 of 3 runs is load-sensitive and a name seen in 3 of 3 is deterministic — which is exactly the distinction between the eleven and the four.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE: the census parsing (11/11 confirmed independently from the .xcresult), the INERT-when-unrecorded semantics, the substitution argument (a count still cannot see 11 die and 11 different recover), or the decision to keep it non-fatal for now. Only the record's SHAPE is wrong.

The real-gate log and its .xcresult are preserved OUTSIDE the worktree at scratchpad/tl6l-realgate/.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
R4 REVIEW 2026-08-13. ONE DESIGN DEFECT FIXED — the record's SHAPE — and ZERO PRODUCTION DEFECTS beyond it. Committed at 76ae6264.

THE RECORD IS NOW A UNION WITH OBSERVATION COUNTS, shaped exactly like `tests`:

  "no_verdict": {"runs_observed": 3,
                 "tests": {"<key>": {"seen_runs": 3, "lost_runs": 3}}}

Accepting the three real runs in order leaves ELEVEN at 3/3 DETERMINISTIC and FOUR at 1/1 LOAD-SENSITIVE, with nobody labelling either. It is still a set of NAMES, never a count — the half of R2's argument the third run does not touch is that a count cannot see eleven tests dying while eleven different ones recover.

READ 1/1 AS "ONE OBSERVATION", NOT "ONE OF THREE". A name accrues observations only from the accept that first records it; the two earlier runs reached those four and watched them pass, but there was no entry to credit. `tests` behaves identically. My own first draft of the prose said "1/3" and the end-to-end CLI run caught it — the same defect class as everything else on this bead, so it is pinned by a rail asserting the four are exactly {seen 1, lost 1}.

WHAT ARMS FATALLY, decided and argued rather than inherited:

  * A NEW CASUALTY is NAMED from the first observation and FATAL only once the census has MIN_RUNS_FOR_DETERMINISTIC. The grace the failure baseline does not get is about the REMEDY, not the evidence: a NEW FAILURE names a test that failed and can be triaged against your diff, while a test with no verdict was never judged at all and the only honest response is to re-run a 20-minute plan. Naming it from run 1 is non-negotiable — a newly-observed casualty is indistinguishable from a regression, and absorbing it silently is the hole this module exists to close.
  * A DETERMINISTIC entry that REPORTED AGAIN is FATAL. This is the PRICE OF THE UNION, not a bonus: R2's one real objection was that "a union can only grow, so a crash that is genuinely fixed stays recorded forever and the gate never speaks about those names again". The pass-direction arm makes a fixed crash loud on the first run that fixes it, so the record can shrink. It cannot fire before three observations by construction, and it fires only on POSITIVE evidence — the test started and reported.
  * A LOAD-SENSITIVE entry reporting again is good news and exits 0, unchanged.
  * A recorded name that NEVER STARTED is never fatal in either direction. A rename, a deletion and a host that died before the start line are indistinguishable from a log.

THE ANSWER TO "WHAT WOULD TONIGHT HAVE EXITED": 0. Probed with the `tests` half taken from run 3 ITSELF so NEW FAILURES cannot mask what the census contributes — the vacuity trap R3 named and fell into once. Against the record runs 1 and 2 would actually have built (11 names, 2 observations): new_failures=0, absent=0, fiction=False, new_casualties=4, EXIT 0, all four NAMED under a PROVISIONAL banner. Force the same probe to three observations and it is EXIT 65. A substitution probe on the real logs — the eleven recover, eleven healthy tests go silent, total unchanged at 15 — fires BOTH arms (11 new casualties AND 11 now-reports).

THREE STATES, THREE CLAIMS, never spelled the same way. No `no_verdict` key = INERT (nobody looked). 1-2 observations = PROVISIONAL (a real measurement, too few observations to bound a population this load-sensitive; casualties named, not fatal). 3+ = ARMED, including a recorded EMPTY census. `empty_baseline` no longer writes an empty census at all — {"runs_observed": 0, "tests": {}} spells "nobody has looked" as a measurement of zero, which is the conflation the ladder exists to prevent.

WHAT AN ACCEPT DOES: lost again -> seen+1/lost+1; started and REPORTED -> seen+1 alone (the only thing that demotes); never started -> PRUNED on a healthy run, CARRIED FORWARD untouched on a crashed one. That last clause is the census analogue of `protected`, and without it a crash would shrink the census from inside the one command meant to maintain it — rail RA11.

THIRD FIXTURE COMMITTED: scripts/tests/fixtures/crashed-run-tl6l-realgate.log, distilled from the 9.4 MB real-gate log. It is the only fixture carrying a 15-name census with churn, so it is the only one that can pin this behaviour, and RealCrashedRunTests now runs the three-run measurement end to end through `merge` itself.

THE FIXTURE GENERATOR HAD A REAL GAP AND ITS OWN REFUSAL CAUGHT IT. The splice can land in a test's STARTED line — which the distiller keeps byte-exact by design — while its PASS line is dropped as uninteresting, so the distillation grew two crashed-host casualties out of two tests that PASSED. The fixture reproducing the defect it exists to measure. Fixed by resolving what a spliced line refers to in its REPAIRED form (`head + following`, not `raw[n] + raw[n+1]`, which still has the app log wedged in the middle and parses as nothing — getting that wrong left the refusal firing with no explanation and cost a round-trip). The two existing fixtures are regenerated: ADDITIONS ONLY, 11/11 census unchanged, same failures, same blamed counts.

ONE TEST-SIDE DEFECT, FOUND AND FIXED, NOT A PRODUCTION ONE. CommittedBaselineTests carried four per-entry invariants on the file the gate actually reads — failed_runs >= 1, seen_runs <= runs_observed, kinds non-empty, kinds valid — and R2 indented them inside `if NO_VERDICT_KEY in data:` when the census block was added. No committed baseline has ever carried that key, so all four ran on nothing, against `entry`/`key` leaked from an earlier loop. They hold on the committed file; nothing was checking that. Same shape as a rail that skips itself.

BATTERY: 58 rails, 57 killed, 0 survived, 0 error, R99 OK-SURVIVED, exit 0. Every R1/R2/R3 rail still green (R01-R31, RA4-RA7, RB1-RB5, RC1-RC5, RF1). RA3 is INVERTED rather than deleted — it used to assert the census is replaced, and now asserts an accept records an observation instead of overwriting with a snapshot. Ten new: RA8 (census tier read off the wrong numerator), RA9 (deterministic recovery de-armed), RA10 (arm fires without a start line), RA11 (a crash prunes the census), RA12 (a reported name credited a loss, so nothing can demote), RA13 (census borrows the FILE's observation count), RA14 (a census promotion goes unannounced), plus CensusMergeTests. RB2's anchor re-cut, RA1/RA2's re-anchored on the new lines.

VERIFICATION: 171 tests, ZERO SKIPS, 2.3 s, no build. scripts/lint.sh clean. scripts/gate-baseline.PlayheadFastTests.json byte-identical to main's (4d300374...). Restore verified byte-exact by SHA-256 after both battery runs; `git status --porcelain -- Playhead PlayheadTests scripts` clean.

NOT MINE, STILL OPEN: [[playhead-bgs1]] (`--only RA1` prints "control not run" then "All mutations killed", exit 0) is untouched — every verdict above is from a FULL battery run, never a selective one.

title: the eligibility ladder is inverted at the listener: a .eligible span for a non-auto class produces NO skip and NO banner, while .markOnly produces a card
description:
FOUND 2026-08-12 by the R6 verify round on playhead-mn5e while enumerating what the playhead-lqcp closure stranded. PRE-EXISTING — not introduced by that branch — but lqcp makes it the ONLY remaining self-reachable auto-skip channel for a show-governed class, so it stops being a small asymmetry.

THE SHAPE. The eligibility ladder is inverted at the listener: a STRONGER stamp reaches them with LESS.

  * `eligibilityGate == .markOnly` -> `SkipOrchestrator.receiveAdWindows` routes to the SUGGEST tier (:3067 -> `registerSuggestedWindow` :1388). `emitSuggestBannersOnPlayheadEntry` (:1443) fires on playhead entry and consults the playhead, never the skip mode. The listener gets a card with Yes/No.
