  * `eligibilityGate == .eligible` / `"autoSkip"` / nil -> the MANAGED tier. `evaluateWindow` (:6748) returns `.confirmed` for both `.shadow` and `.manual` (:6838-6845 — the two arms differ only in a log string), and `evaluateAndPush` emits a banner only when `decision == .applied` (:6554). So for any class that is not `.auto`: no skip AND no card. Only a passive timeline block (`broadcastAppliedSegments` includes `.confirmed`, :1825-1833).

Post-lqcp, `.segmentAggregated`, `.fusion` and `.userAsserted` can never be `.auto` without an explicit user override — `DetectorTrustLedger.seed` copies `profile.mode` into all three and `evaluatePromotion`'s `.manual` case is now a no-op. So for those three classes, today, on the shipped default: the pipeline's HIGHEST-confidence output is the one the listener never sees.

TWO CONSEQUENCES WORTH NAMING SEPARATELY.

1. `HotPathAdmission` (`HotPathExtentGate.swift:63-77`) is an ordinal declared to be "about the LISTENER rather than about the string", with `case autoSkip = 2 /// The managed tier. Audio is removed without asking.` `HotPathExtentGateMonotonicityTests` proves exhaustively that admission never rises. Both are now false in fact: `gatedLabel`'s only transition, `autoSkip -> markOnly`, INCREASES what the listener experiences. The extent gates (playhead-2350 / bllt / 98co) now help the listener when they fire and hide the span when they do not.

2. playhead-527u's product-owner AC is dead. `AdDetectionService.recordUserMarkedAd` (:3141-3170) stamps a user's own transcript mark `eligibilityGate: .eligible` precisely because "a user's manual ad mark is the highest-certainty 'this IS an ad' signal we have". `SkipDetectorClass.classify` tests `UserSpanAssertion` FIRST (:149-151), so the row is `.userAsserted` — show-governed, `modeAuthority == nil`, never `.auto`. A user-marked ad region therefore auto-skips on no show, and being `.eligible` it does not banner either. `UserAddedMarkSurvivesBackfillTests`' MR1 claim that a pre-existing dogfood mark "ALSO auto-skips on reload" is conditioned on a mode no show can reach.

CANDIDATE FIX, for Dan. Route a managed-tier row to the suggest tier when its detector class's mode is not `.auto`, instead of dropping it to a silent `.confirmed`. That restores the ordinal's meaning (`markOnly` <= `autoSkip` at the listener), revives 527u's marks as cards, and is the general form of the byte-exact reachability gap filed alongside this. It is a real UX change — more cards — so it is Dan's call, not an improvisation.

title: playhead-u0vv's restoration is unreachable on the mainstream byte-exact path: the debt is incurred in the managed tier and can only be paid in the suggest tier
description:
FOUND 2026-08-12 by the R6 verify round on playhead-mn5e, behaviourally (probe P3b) plus an exhaustive read of every production `AdWindow.eligibilityGate` stamp site.

THE CLAIM u0vv MAKES IS TRUE. Once `.rediffByteExact`'s `falseSkipWeight` decays to 0, `DetectorTrustLedger.restoredMode` hands it back `SkipDetectorClass.showIndependentSeedMode`. Its unit tests and its `SeedRestorationReachesTheGateTests` probe both hold, and four of six R6 mutants were killed.

THE GESTURE THAT DISCHARGES THE DEBT IS NOT REACHABLE ON THE PATH THAT INCURS IT. The only production writer that lowers a weight through `restoredMode` is `TrustScoringService.recordCorrectObservation`, whose only production caller is `SkipOrchestrator.acceptSuggestedSkip` (:5949) — a banner Yes. `acceptSuggestedSkip` requires `suggestWindows[windowId]`, i.e. the SUGGEST tier, which `receiveAdWindows` enters only for `eligibilityGate == .markOnly` (:3067) or `catalogProvenanceMustFailClosed` (:3067/:3522). Everything else goes to the managed tier, and there `evaluateAndPush` emits a banner only on `.applied` (:6554) — which needs `.auto`. So:

  * DEMOTION population: byte-exact spans stamped `.eligible`. The day-0 mint stamps exactly that (`AdDetectionService.swift:12206-12211`, gated by `RediffActivation.dayZeroByteExactAutoSkipEnabled = true`, RediffActivation.swift:193). They auto-skip, they banner on `.applied`, the listener says "not an ad", two vetoes demote the class.
  * RESTORATION population: byte-exact spans stamped `.markOnly`. Enumerated, there are two producers, both narrow — the music-only demotion in `BackfillEvidenceFusion.swift:1113-1115` (the ONE eligibility demoter with no `!span.carriesRediffByteExactWidth` carve-out, so it needs `anchorProvenance == [.sustainedMusicOffset, .rediffSlot]` with no other corroborating presence), and a stale/mismatched catalog claim on a byte-exact row.

The two sets are disjoint in the ordinary case. On a show whose day-0 mint works, a listener who vetoes byte-exact rediff twice will never again be offered a byte-exact banner to say Yes to, so the debt never discharges and the class stays `manual` — which is exactly the state playhead-u0vv was opened to end.

PROVED, not reasoned. R6 probe P3b drives the real `SkipOrchestrator`: shadow-mode show, two attributed deterministic vetoes (class demoted to `manual`, `#require`d), then a byte-exact window stamped `.eligible` and a playhead entry into its span. Result: `activeSuggestWindowIDs()` empty, `emittedAutoSkipBannersSnapshot()` empty, zero correct observations recorded. The companion P3a shows the same window stamped `.markOnly` DOES reach suggest and DOES credit `.rediffByteExact`, so the difference is the stamp and nothing else.

WHY THIS IS NOT A u0vv BUG. u0vv's acceptance was Dan's ruling — restore-to-seed on decay — and it implements it. Nothing in the commit claims the discharge is common. What is missing is a decision about what SHOULD discharge a byte-exact debt when the class is mark-only-invisible, and that is a policy question:
  (a) a time/episode-based decay for the exempt class only (a clean episode that produced byte-exact spans discharges a unit) — but "clean" is the value-that-names-an-absence problem, and self-observation restoring is exactly what u0vv's MU5 mutant proves the suite forbids today;
  (b) surface a demoted byte-exact class as MARK-ONLY rather than silent — i.e. route `.eligible` byte-exact rows to the suggest tier when their class is not `.auto`, so the listener keeps being asked and can pay the debt off. This is the more honest fix and it is the general form of the inversion filed alongside this bead;
  (c) accept it, on the grounds that the Settings/pill override is the intended escape hatch.

(b) is the one to weigh first because it also fixes the general case, not just rediff.
notes: 2026-08-13, playhead-wq34: CLOSED BY THAT FIX, option (b) as this bead recommended. A row the managed tier cannot act on now takes the suggest tier, so a demoted `.rediffByteExact` class keeps being OFFERED and every banner Yes pays a unit of its debt off through `recordCorrectObservation` -> `restoredMode`. Proved behaviourally, not reasoned: `EligibilityLadderMonotonicityTests.demotedByteExactClassStillReachesTheListener` is P3b inverted — same setup (shadow show, two ATTRIBUTED deterministic vetoes, class `#require`d at .manual, a byte-exact window stamped .eligible, playhead entry into its span) and it now asserts the suggest card IS emitted and that the Yes credits .rediffByteExact. It reddens under both wq34 self-mutants.

title: ShowTraitProfile.episodesObserved counts BACKFILLS, not episodes — the trait prior tier matures inside ONE episode
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 (playhead-mn5e R5, reading the same device pull that motivated playhead-2qz6).

THE QUANTITY. `ShowTraitProfile.episodesObserved` (ShowTraitProfile.swift:117) is documented, verbatim: "Number of episodes that have contributed to this profile."

WHAT ACTUALLY WRITES IT. `AdDetectionService.updatePriors`' update closure calls `Self.mergedTraitProfileJSON(...)` (AdDetectionService.swift:13309), which calls `existing.traitProfile.updated(from: snapshot)` UNCONDITIONALLY (:13413). `ShowTraitProfile.updated(from:)` does `episodesObserved + 1` on every call. `updatePriors` runs once per `runBackfill`, and an episode is backfilled ~9 times — hot path, final pass, re-drives, transcript-version bumps, playhead-15d0's resume. That is the SAME 9x that playhead-2qz6 measured on `podcast_profiles.observationCount` (36 observations across 4 assets, 2026-08-12 device pull).

WHO READS IT AS EPISODES, AND WHAT IT COSTS.
  * `ShowTraitProfile.isReliable` -> `episodesObserved >= 3`. The trait tier turns on after roughly ONE THIRD of one episode.
  * `PriorHierarchy` level 2 (PriorHierarchy.swift:230) -> `traitBlendWeight(episodesObserved:)` (:333), which ramps 0.4 at 3 episodes to 0.6 at 7+ and clamps. Full weight is reached INSIDE the first episode.
  * The profile itself is an EMA at alpha=0.3 over those ~9 snapshots, and they are ~9 near-identical snapshots of the SAME episode. Its own comment says the EMA "converges after ~5-7 episodes"; in fact it converges within one, onto one episode. A one-episode show is blended into the prior hierarchy at the weight of a mature seven-episode show.

WHY THIS IS NOT ALREADY COVERED. playhead-2qz6's V49 migration enumerates FOUR readers of `podcast_profiles.observationCount` and resets that column to 0. This is a FIFTH quantity with the identical unit defect in a DIFFERENT column (`podcast_profiles.traitProfileJSON`), so V49 does not touch it and every field device carries the inflated value forward across the upgrade. Same shape as playhead-2qz6 (the show column), playhead-kfts (`podcast_planner_state.observedEpisodeCount`) and playhead-scc6 (the per-class mirror): the standing defect class, a value that names one thing read as though it named another.

DIRECTION (not a decision taken here). Either gate the trait EMA on the `trust_episode_observations` claim playhead-2qz6 added — the claim already exists and is the fact, rather than a proxy — or reset `episodesObserved` in a migration and move the increment behind the same claim. Note that unlike `observationCount`, resetting is not obviously conservative here: at 0 the trait tier deactivates and the resolver falls back to the network/global blend, which IS the honest reading of "this show has no maturity of its own yet", so the direction matches V49's.

title: V49 resets observationCount on the show row but NOT its per-class mirror in detectorTrustJSON — and the mirror is what the skip gate reads
description:
FOUND IN playhead-mn5e R4, by reading the V49 migration against the value the SKIP GATE reads.

V49 corrects `observationCount` from a per-backfill unit (~9x inflated) to a per-episode one, and it does so with one statement:

    UPDATE podcast_profiles SET observationCount = 0

That statement reaches ONE of the two places the quantity lives. The other is `podcast_profiles.detectorTrustJSON`, where `DetectorTrustLedger` stores a per-class `observationCount` for every materialized entry — and that column is not touched by the migration.

WHY IT MATTERS. `TrustScoringService.resolveDetectorModes` returns the STORED entry in preference to the seed, and `SkipOrchestrator.skipMode(for:)` (SkipOrchestrator.swift:6714) reads the per-class verdict, not `profile.mode`. So on a device that has a forked ledger, the numbers the gate consults are still in the old unit while the show scalar has been reset — the ~24x correction the bead is about does not apply to the values that decide anything.

HOW A LEDGER GETS FORKED. `TrustScoringService.applyFalseSkipSignal` calls `materialized(...)` on any veto that names a detector (TrustScoringService.swift:1131), and EVERY production veto site names one (SkipOrchestrator.swift:4558, 4992, 5229, 5374; AdDetectionService.recordListenRewind:10238). `applyCorrectObservation` materializes unconditionally. So one gesture of any kind, since playhead-gard shipped, and the entries exist — seeded by `DetectorTrustLedger.seed` from the then-current, inflated show scalar.

FIELD STATE. `detectorTrustJSON` is NULL on both shows in the 2026-08-12 device pull, so no device we have measured is affected today. The path is open for the next veto.

BOUND ON THE HARM. With the auto rung closed (playhead-lqcp) the worst an inflated per-class count can buy is `shadow -> manual` on a class that has not earned three real episodes — a banner, not an unasked cut. That is why this is filed rather than hot-fixed.

WHY IT WAS NOT CAUGHT. `TrustEpisodeObservationV49MigrationTests.v49ResetsObservationCountOnly` builds its three fixtures with `makeProfile(...)`, which never sets `detectorTrustJSON`. The migration's blind spot and the test's blind spot are the same one.

REMEDY — A DECISION, NOT A MECHANICAL FIX, which is the other reason this is filed. Two candidates and they disagree about a user's gestures:
  (a) zero every entry's `observationCount` alongside the scalar. Simple, matches the migration's stated intent ("every observationCount goes to 0"), but an entry's counter is ALSO advanced one-per-gesture by `applyCorrectObservation`, so this discards banner Yeses the listener actually gave.
  (b) leave entries whose count came from gestures and reset only the seeded copies. There is nothing in the persisted row that distinguishes the two, so this is not implementable without a new column.
Doing (a) needs a Swift-side migration pass (decode, zero, re-encode, upsert) — `AnalysisStore` already depends on `DetectorTrustLedger` via `PodcastProfile.detectorTrustLedger`, so the dependency is not new.

RELATED SHAPE: the same "the scalar moved and its per-class mirror did not" mistake was a live defect in the same branch — `recordSuccessfulObservation` moved `profile.mode` without touching the ledger, so a promoted show still gated at `shadow`. That one was fixed in R4. This is the migration-side instance of it.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
MEASURED AGAINST THE DEVICE 2026-08-12, AND THE TRIGGER IS NOW NAMED — this is empty today, and R4's own Finding 1 says exactly when it stops being empty.

WHAT THE DEVICE CARRIES. From the 2026-08-12 morning pull (build 5bcf3e98, virgin DB from the 08-11 wipe), reading podcast_profiles directly:

  https://feeds.simplecast.com/dHoohVNH          mode=shadow obs=26 trust=0.5  detectorTrustJSON = NULL
  https://rss2.flightcast.com/xmsftuzjjykcmqwola mode=shadow obs=10 trust=0.5  detectorTrustJSON = NULL

detectorTrustJSON is NULL on BOTH shows. There is no per-class mirror, so V49 has no mirror to fail to reset, so this defect has ZERO instances on the only device that exists.

WHY IT IS NULL, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MATTERS. Not luck, and not the wipe alone. R4's Finding 1 establishes the mechanism: every production veto site passes an attribution, and an attributed veto makes applyFalseSkipSignal MATERIALIZE THE WHOLE LEDGER — 'the first gesture a listener makes pins every class'. Dan's device reads NULL because no gesture has been made on it since the wipe. The column is one banner veto away from being populated for every class at once.

CONSEQUENCE, and it cuts both ways:
  - This bead is not urgent for the current device and should not block mn5e's merge. There is no user-witnessed per-class state to weigh against, which is precisely the argument that made the remedy 'a decision' — today there is nothing on either side of the scale.
  - It becomes live the FIRST TIME Dan vetoes a banner, and the population it creates is every class at once rather than the one he vetoed. So 'zero instances' has a short shelf life and is not a reason to defer indefinitely.
  - The cheap window is NOW: a demotion/reset pass added while the column is empty is untestable-against-real-state but also costs nothing, whereas the same pass added after gestures accumulate has to distinguish seeded copies from gesture-earned ones — which R4 correctly says the row does not support.

SAME MEASUREMENT, SAME CAVEAT AS playhead-lqcp: n = ONE device, ONE pull, pre-release. The pre-wipe pull (db-prewipe6) was not checked for this column and could be, and would be the only available evidence of what a gestured device actually looks like.

title: the manual->auto rung has no high-confidence quantity to open it
description:
playhead-lqcp closed the manual->auto rung rather than leaving it to fall through a vacuous threshold. AutoPromotionConfidenceEvidence (TrustScoringService.swift) has exactly one case, .unavailable, and both evaluatePromotion siblings switch over it — so adding a second case is a compile error at both sites and the rung cannot reopen by accident.

WHAT THIS BEAD OWES: a named, PERSISTED, show-level detection-confidence quantity, plus Dan's floor for it.

WHY IT COULD NOT BE DONE IN mn5e:
- averageConfidence is computed per backfill in AdDetectionService.recordConfirmedWindowObservation and handed to recordSuccessfulObservation, which reads it ONCE in the create closure (exceptionalFirstEpisodeConfidence, 0.92) and discards it on every update. Nothing accumulates it.
- Persisting it means a new podcast_profiles column (a V50 migration) and a decision about the estimator: running mean, EMA, min-over-episodes, or a quantile. Those are not equivalent — a mean hides a show with one 0.99 and four 0.45s, which is exactly the population auto must not fire on.
- The floor is Dan's call and needs field data that only exists once mn5e ships. Measured real ad-window confidences on the current corpus are 0.38-0.63 (DE0784D8MidRollPodFixture.swift:202-232) against a 0.7 floor used elsewhere, so a naive 0.7-0.75 floor would close the rung permanently rather than conditionally.

DO NOT reopen by deleting the switch or by lowering manualToAutoTrustScore. The 0.75 threshold is provably unable to withhold a promotion on the self-observation path (trust = 0.2 + 0.10*(N-1) clears at N=7 while the observation clause demands N=8), which is why it was not used as the gate.

title: one episode can claim twice: (podcastId, analysisAssetId) is not an episode key
description:
playhead-2qz6 dedupes trust observations on (podcastId, analysisAssetId) via trust_episode_observations, documented as 'ONE ROW PER EPISODE THAT HAS CONTRIBUTED A TRUST OBSERVATION'. The key is sound against repeated backfills of the SAME asset (its stated purpose, and the 15d0 resume / re-drive / transcript-version-bump cases genuinely no-op). It is NOT sound as an episode key, because one episode can hold two analysisAssetIds.

analysis_assets.id is always UUID().uuidString (AnalysisCoordinator.swift:2305, AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:6708 and :6875) -- never derived from episodeId. The only uniqueness rail is V39's CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_assets_episode_fingerprint ON analysis_assets(episodeId, assetFingerprint) (AnalysisStore.swift:7441-7443), whose own doc disclaims episode-level uniqueness: 'WHY NOT UNIQUE ON episodeId ALONE. Two rows for one episode under DIFFERENT fingerprints is legitimate' (AnalysisStore.swift:7377-7381).

TWO REACHABLE PATHS:

1. DESIGNED, not a race. AnalysisWorkScheduler.resolveAnalysisAssetId (:6823-6831): 'Same episode id can legitimately point at changed bytes after a feed correction or re-download. Keep the old analysis anchored to its SHA and create a new asset for this file below.' Both rows persist, both are backfillable, both claim under different keys. Same episode, two observations. The placeholder-merge sweep does NOT cover this -- it folds only rows where victim.isPlaceholder (assetFingerprint == id, guarded at AnalysisStore.swift:19332), and here neither row is a placeholder.

2. THE 0hi9 RACE IS STILL OPEN ON ONE SIDE. playhead-fzrw added the atomic insertAssetIfEpisodeHasNone (AnalysisStore.swift:9781-9813) for registerDownloadedAssetRowIfAbsent, citing the competitor by name. But AnalysisCoordinator.resolveSession still does check-then-insert: fetchAssetByEpisodeId (:2211), then await-suspending work (capability snapshot, downloadManager.fingerprint), then an unconditional store.insertAsset (:2351) -- never the guarded variant. fzrw moved registration to download completion, which is exactly when a user is most likely to press play, so the overlap window is now WIDER, not narrower.

AND THE MERGE HIDES IT. repointChildRows uses UPDATE OR IGNORE then DELETE (AnalysisStore.swift:19612-19637). trust_episode_observations is picked up dynamically by assetReferencingChildColumns() on the column name, so on a placeholder merge the duplicate claim row is silently discarded -- while podcast_profiles.observationCount keeps BOTH increments. The two numbers the bead says must agree end up permanently unequal, in the unsafe direction.

Direction is UNSAFE (over-count -> faster promotion). Magnitude is ~2x on affected episodes, far smaller than the ~9x this bead fixed, so mn5e is still a large net improvement -- this is residual, not a regression.

--- R2 REVIEW DECISION (playhead-mn5e, 2026-08-12): DEFER. Not fixed in mn5e. ---

WHAT CHANGED SINCE THIS WAS FILED, and it is decisive: playhead-lqcp CLOSED the manual->auto rung. AutoPromotionConfidenceEvidence has one case (.unavailable) and both evaluatePromotion siblings switch over it, so an over-counted observationCount now reaches at most shadow->manual. That unlocks a BANNER and cuts no audio. The unsafe direction this bead names — 'over-count -> faster promotion' — no longer terminates in an unasked skip. 89x6 is now an ACCURACY defect, not a safety one.

THREE MORE REASONS IT IS SAFE TO DEFER:
1. Magnitude, restated against what shipped. mn5e takes the counter from ~9x per episode to 1x on every episode. 89x6 leaves at most 2x, and only on episodes that hit one of two uncommon paths. Holding mn5e for it would keep the 9x defect in the field to avoid a 2x one.
2. The honest fix is an IDENTITY change, not a patch. Making the claim an episode key means re-keying trust_episode_observations (a V50 migration) AND carrying an episodeId into two trust call sites that do not have one. That is a persistence-strategy change and needs approval; it is not a line to slip into a counter bead.
3. The 0hi9 half is somebody else's one-line swap. AnalysisCoordinator.resolveSession (:2211 fetchAssetByEpisodeId -> :2351 insertAsset) should use fzrw's insertAssetIfEpisodeHasNone. Verified still true at 2658fd8b. That edit changes asset creation in the pipeline hot path and belongs with fzrw's work, not here.

WHAT WAS DONE INSTEAD, so the deferral is not silent: the branch's own over-claiming prose is corrected. The table comment in AnalysisStore.createTables now reads 'ONE ROW PER ANALYSIS ASSET', names both paths by which one episode holds two assets, and says explicitly that 'episode' in the table name states the intent rather than a guarantee, with 89x6 named as the bead that would make it true. claimEpisodeTrustObservation's doc says the same. A reader can no longer take the guarantee at face value.

CONFIRMED WHILE REVIEWING: assetReferencingChildColumns() (AnalysisStore.swift:19452-19479) discovers child tables by the column name analysisAssetId, so trust_episode_observations IS swept by the placeholder merge — this bead's claim that repointChildRows silently drops the duplicate claim row while observationCount keeps both increments is correct.

title: a banner Yes counts as an EPISODE: recordCorrectObservation is a second writer of observationCount
description:
playhead-mn5e/2qz6 states, in two production doc comments, that recordConfirmedWindowObservation is the ONLY writer of observationCount:
- AdDetectionService.swift ~L12886: 'It is the ONLY writer of observationCount, and it counts EPISODES'
- AdDetectionService.swift updatePriors doc: 'nothing does any more except recordConfirmedWindowObservation'

Both are FALSE. TrustScoringService.applyCorrectObservation (L1049-1102) does:
  L1055  let newObservations = profile.observationCount + 1
  L1097  observationCount: newObservations
and it has a live production caller: SkipOrchestrator.swift:5927 (await trustService.recordCorrectObservation(...)), i.e. the banner Yes tap.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is the same defect class the bead exists to fix: a banner tap is a per-GESTURE event being counted into a column whose every consumer reads it as episodes (ShowLocalPriorsBuilder 'number of episodes processed', NetworkPriors.decayedWeight(episodesObserved:), TrustScoringConfig.shadowToManualObservations). A user who taps Yes on four banners inside ONE episode hands the show four episodes of credit plus 4 x 0.10 trust, with no trust_episode_observations claim row behind any of it.

It also breaks the bead's own stated diagnostic. AnalysisStore.episodeTrustObservationCount is documented as 'the independent count it must agree with -- two numbers that are supposed to be equal, so a drift is observable rather than inferred'. After any banner Yes they are unequal by construction, and nothing checks.

Direction is UNSAFE: it over-counts, accelerating the ladder toward .auto.

Fix shape (not decided): either route recordCorrectObservation through the same claim table, or stop it moving observationCount and let it move only trust / the veto counter, or split the trust-bonus counter from the episode counter.

--- R2 FIX (playhead-mn5e branch, 2026-08-12): both writers now share ONE claim. ---

CHOSEN SEMANTICS: the banner Yes CLAIMS THE SAME EPISODE, idempotent with the backfill's claim. It does not count on a separate axis.

WHY, over the two alternatives:
- Over "carry observationCount forward and let only the backfill write it": a user's Yes is a better witness than the detector's own output, and it should be able to be the FIRST claimant. The backfill claims only when it confirms a non-empty window set AND a trust service is installed; an episode that fails either test would otherwise get no credit at all even though the user confirmed an ad on it.
- Over "a separate counter": the column's own definition settles it. ShowLocalPriorsBuilder reads it as "number of episodes processed" and NetworkPriors.decayedWeight names its parameter episodesObserved. A banner tap is not a new episode. A second axis would also need a V50 column and would make this bead's "the two numbers must agree" diagnostic permanently unusable, since one side would have no rows to count.

IMPLEMENTATION: recordCorrectObservation gains analysisAssetId (SkipOrchestrator passes the already-captured `assetId`, i.e. suggested.analysisAssetId), claims via the shared AnalysisStore.claimEpisodeTrustObservation, and threads the result into applyCorrectObservation as `countsAsEpisode`, which gates ONLY `profile.observationCount`. Trust bonus, false-signal decay and the whole per-detector entry are per-GESTURE and still move on every tap.

ONE ORDERING SUBTLETY, and it is the mirror of recordConfirmedWindowObservation's: the mutation is `updateProfileIfExistsCapturing`, which no-ops for a show with no profile row. Claiming first would burn that episode's claim on a mutation that never happened, costing it credit permanently. So the profile is read first and the claim is skipped when it is absent. The gap is benign in one direction only — profiles are created but never deleted, so a stale read can only under-count by one episode.

DELIBERATELY NOT GATED: DetectorTrustEntry.observationCount. Gating it on the same claim FREEZES it (the backfill claims nearly every episode without touching the ledger), which would remove the per-class escape from shadow that playhead-gard exists to provide. Filed as playhead-jh4y; bounded today because playhead-lqcp closed the auto rung, so an over-counted entry reaches at most a banner.

MUTATION EVIDENCE. Mutant MC (ignore countsAsEpisode, always +1) -> GATE_EXIT=65, both fh5v tests reddened. Mutant MD (drop the profile-exists guard so the claim is spent regardless) -> GATE_EXIT=65, "A correct observation on a show with no profile creates nothing" reddened.

The two false "ONLY writer of observationCount" doc claims this bead named in AdDetectionService are corrected to say there are two writers behind one claim.

title: [bug] observationCount counts BACKFILLS (~9 per episode), not episodes — so 'shadowToManualObservations: 3' is a fraction of one episode
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 on scratchpad/db-morning7 while implementing playhead-mn5e.

  4 distinct analysisAssetId in ad_windows (4 episodes)
  observationCount = 26 (simplecast) + 10 (flightcast) = 36

36 observations for 4 episodes is ~9 per episode. `observationCount` is incremented in exactly one production place — AdDetectionService.updatePriors, once per completed runBackfill — and runBackfill runs many times per asset (hot path, final pass, re-runs). So the column counts BACKFILL INVOCATIONS, not episodes.

WHY THIS MATTERS NOW, and did not before. Until playhead-mn5e the column fed nothing that acted: evaluatePromotion never ran. mn5e gives it a production consumer, so `TrustScoringConfig.shadowToManualObservations = 3` and `manualToAutoObservations = 8` become live against a counter that ticks ~9x per episode.

CONSEQUENCE, computed against the device's actual state (both shows mode=shadow, trust=0.50, falseSignals=0):
  backfill 1:  obs 27, trust 0.60  -> shadow  -> MANUAL  (27>=3, 0.60>=0.4)
  backfill 2:  obs 28, trust 0.70  -> manual  -> manual  (0.70 < 0.75)
  backfill 3:  obs 29, trust 0.80  -> manual  -> AUTO    (>=8, >=0.75, falseSignals==0)

Three backfills is a FRACTION OF ONE EPISODE's analysis. So with the thresholds unchanged, a show reaches the mode that cuts audio without asking inside a single episode, on evidence it produced itself, with zero user input. Nobody chose that; it is what "3 observations" means when an observation is a backfill.

THE STANDING CHECK applied: what would `observationCount` read if this show had been analysed ONCE? Between 1 and ~9, depending on how many times the pipeline re-ran — i.e. the quantity does not name the thing its threshold is named for.

TWO WAYS OUT, both product decisions, neither taken inside mn5e:
  (a) make an observation PER EPISODE (idempotent on analysisAssetId), leaving the numbers 3 and 8 meaning what they say; or
  (b) keep the counter and re-derive 3 and 8 against measured backfills-per-episode.
(a) is the honest one but needs a durable per-asset marker — a persistence change, so Dan's call.

Related: playhead-mn5e's own report, and the ad_windows markOnly bead filed alongside this one (which is why the practical blast radius TODAY is nil — no window on the device can reach the trust gate at all).

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: PROMOTED IN IMPORTANCE by Dan's 2026-08-12 auto-rung ruling: self-promotion now goes all the way to .auto, conditional on high confidence. That makes this counter safety-critical rather than cosmetic — with it counting backfills (~9/episode), manualToAutoObservations: 8 is satisfied INSIDE ONE EPISODE, so the app would begin cutting audio after roughly one episode of self-generated evidence. Fix this before the auto rung is wired.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
=== FIXED on bead/playhead-mn5e, commit 2658fd8b (Dan: "fix the counter first, then decide") ===

UNIT EVENT: "a backfill of THIS analysis asset confirmed at least one ad window,
and this asset has not contributed an observation for this show before." The
asset IS the episode — `runBackfill` is always scoped to exactly one — and the
fact is recorded as itself rather than inferred.

NOT DERIVED FROM A PROXY, and that is the whole point. Every candidate already
in the store is a proxy for the fact, which is how this bug happened:
  * `analysis_assets.confirmedAdCoverageEndTime` — how far confirmation
    reached, not that an observation was counted.
  * `analysis_assets.analysisState` — a lifecycle, not a ledger.
  * `analysis_assets.episodeId` — embeds the show as a `::` prefix; counting by
    it means parsing an identifier for a fact it never promised to carry.
  * `podcast_planner_state.observedEpisodeCount` — HAS THE SAME BUG (21 and 6
    on the 2026-08-12 pull, for the same ~4 episodes). Untouched here; it is
    the planner's own quantity and a separate consumer.

DEDUPE KEY: `(podcastId, analysisAssetId)`, persisted as the PRIMARY KEY of a
new table `trust_episode_observations`. Claimed with ONE statement —
`INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` + `sqlite3_changes` — so the claim and the
test cannot interleave the way a SELECT-then-INSERT pair can. Keyed on the show
as well as the asset, so a re-subscribed feed under a new URL is a distinct
claim rather than a suppressed one. The claim is taken only immediately before
the observation is actually recorded: a backfill with no trust service claims
nothing and the episode stays claimable, because a claim standing for an
observation nobody made would cost that show an episode of credit permanently.

`updatePriors` no longer writes `observationCount` AT ALL — unconditional, no
fallback flag. A path that cannot record an episode observation must not write
a per-backfill number into a column whose consumers all read it as episodes.
Its create path now seeds 0 rather than 1.

EXISTING ROWS: **RESET TO 0. This is a data migration (V49) and it is stated
explicitly.** No faithful reconstruction exists — the fact was never recorded,
which is the defect — and every available reconstruction is another proxy.
Zero says "we do not know", which is true, and it is the conservative direction
for a counter that decides whether the app may cut audio unasked.

WHAT A FIELD DEVICE DOES ON UPGRADE: every profile's `observationCount` goes to
0. `mode`, `skipTrustScore`, `recentFalseSkipSignals` and the learned priors are
NOT touched — no show changes mode as a result, and a user's vetoes survive.
Asserted by test, including on a deliberately-demoted profile.

The two other misreaders are corrected by the same reset:
`ShowLocalPriorsBuilder` (its `episodeCount`, doc-commented "number of episodes
processed") and `NetworkPriors.decayedWeight(episodesObserved:)` — a parameter
literally named for the quantity it was not being given. Both under-credit
maturity at 0, which falls back to the broader prior tier: conservative.
(Immaterial on Dan's device either way — `networkId` is NULL on both profiles,
so the network tier is inactive.)

NO THRESHOLD CHANGED.

VERIFICATION. Gate: 6 suites requested, 6 ran — 109 Swift Testing in 5 suites +
24 XCTest. TEST SUCCEEDED, GATE_EXIT=0.
Mutation, each restored byte-exact from a SHA-256 pin:
  N1 ignore the claim result                    65  one-episode / ledger-agreement
  N2 INSERT OR REPLACE (claim never dedupes)    65  + idempotence
  N3 updatePriors increments again              65  7 tests incl. Bug-4a carry-forward
  N4 drop the V49 reset                         65  V49-resets-counts
  N5 key the claim on the show only             65  two-distinct-episodes / ledger-agreement

title: Activity Up Next accrues permanent ghosts: a download-time asset row outlives the download that justified it
description:
playhead-fzrw R5 finding F-A (verified, filed not fixed — outside fzrw's scope).

THE PREMISE THE BEAD BROKE. ActivitySnapshotProvider's population is exactly 'episodes that have an analysis_assets row' (Playhead/Services/Activity/ActivitySnapshotProvider.swift:182 fetchLatestAssetByEpisodeIdMap, :187 eligibleEpisodeIds, :307 'guard let asset = allAssets[episodeId] else { continue }'). Its own comment at :300-306 states the assumption in words: 'Episode rows that have never been queued for analysis are not interesting to the Activity screen.' Row EXISTENCE was the proxy for QUEUED-FOR-ANALYSIS. playhead-fzrw makes the row exist at download time instead of at first dispatch, so the proxy no longer holds.

THE CHAIN, VERIFIED.
1. AnalysisWorkScheduler.registerDownloadedAssetRowIfAbsent (:6593) writes the row when the bytes land.
2. EpisodeSurfaceStatusReducer Rule 5 (:205-218): no live cause + fully eligible => disposition .queued, reason .waitingForTime.
3. ActivityViewModel.swift:478-505: .queued && !isRunning => Up Next.
4. isTerminal (ActivitySnapshotProvider.swift:653-662) only rescues .queued when playbackReadiness == .complete, which a coverage-less row never is. So the row never leaves Up Next.
5. NOTHING DELETES IT. AnalysisWorkScheduler.retireDownloadAnalysis (:1505-1541) deletes analysis_jobs only. AnalysisStore.deleteAsset(id:) (AnalysisStore.swift:10216) has ZERO production callers; the only deleteAssetRow uses (:7451, :19193) are the duplicate folds, which need two rows for one episode. DownloadManager.evictIfNeeded does not call retireDownloadAnalysis at all.

SCENARIO. Overnight batch downloads five episodes (fzrw's own 2026-08-10 measurement: the lane was 3h46m behind by episode four). In the morning the user deletes three without playing them, or LRU eviction reclaims them. Their jobs are gone (or will run and land blocked:missingFile), but each keeps a 'new' analysis_assets row, so Activity shows three Up Next rows promising analysis that has no job behind it — permanently, with no state they can reach that evicts them.

BEFORE fzrw these episodes had no row at all (the row was minted inside processJob, which never ran), so Activity showed nothing. The pre-existing analogue — a 'queued' row stranded after processJob began — is the seconds-wide window already filed as playhead-qom2. This one is hours wide by construction.

NOT A DEFECT, FOR THE RECORD: a downloaded episode that is still WAITING for the lane now appearing in Up Next is arguably correct and is within fzrw's spirit. The defect is confined to the ORPHAN case, where the audio is gone and no job survives.

CANDIDATE REMEDIES (pick one, do not do both blindly):
(a) retireDownloadAnalysis deletes the asset row when it carries the registration token and has no artifacts — narrow, but needs the FK cascade audit at AnalysisStore.swift:19275-19277.
(b) The Activity provider stops using row-existence as its population and requires a live job or a non-'new' state — the premise fix, and it also covers the LRU path that never calls retireDownloadAnalysis.

title: [bug] the scheduler lane writes 'queued' onto analysis_assets and NEVER writes it back down — a background analysis that finishes under the 0.98 floor, or whose runner dies, leaves a permanent working bar with the tap DISABLED
description:
FILED BY playhead-fzrw R4 review. PRE-EXISTING and NOT widened by fzrw (verified:
the asset carried the same `queued` before the bead, written by
`AnalysisWorkScheduler.resolveAnalysisAssetId`'s fall-through insert at
AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:6887; fzrw R3 only moved WHEN it is written). Outside
fzrw's ceiling, which is "the analysis_assets row is registered when the bytes
land".

THE COMPLETE WRITER SET for `analysis_assets.analysisState`, established by
reading every call site (grep for `updateAssetState`, `insertAsset`,
`insertAssetIfEpisodeHasNone`, `markRegisteredAssetQueued` across Playhead/):

  * `AnalysisStore.insertAsset`            <- AnalysisWorkScheduler:6887 ("queued")
                                              AnalysisCoordinator:2351   ("queued")
  * `AnalysisStore.insertAssetIfEpisodeHasNone` <- AnalysisWorkScheduler:6681 ("new", fzrw)
  * `AnalysisStore.markRegisteredAssetQueued`   <- AnalysisWorkScheduler:4911 ("new"->"queued", fzrw R3)
  * `AnalysisStore.updateAssetState`      <- AnalysisCoordinator ONLY (2105, 2128,
                                             2134, 2248, 2285, 3894, 4212, 4790)
                                             + the one-shot duplicate-asset fold
                                             (AnalysisStore:19566)

`AnalysisJobRunner` is not in that set, and
`AnalysisStore.ProcessJobOutcomeArmCommit` (AnalysisStore.swift:15865-15902) has
NO asset-state field — its `StateUpdate` writes `analysis_jobs.state` only. So
the scheduler lane can move a row INTO `queued` and can never move it out.
Only `AnalysisCoordinator.transition` writes spooling/featuresReady/backfill and
the terminals, and it runs exclusively on the PLAY path
(`handlePlayStarted` -> `resolveSession` -> `runPipeline`).

TWO USER-VISIBLE CONSEQUENCES, both on the library control:

1. BACKGROUND ANALYSIS THAT FINISHES SHORT. The lane completes the job, no
   terminal is written, the row stays `queued`.
   `episodePreparationAnalysisActive` (EpisodePreparationReadiness.swift:415)
   reads `.queued` as ACTIVE, so `deriveEpisodePreparationReadiness` returns
   `.analyzing` -- a working bar promising progress that will never arrive --
   and `EpisodePreparationStatusModel.isActionable` (:106) returns FALSE for
   `.analyzing`, so the playhead-kanf promote-to-now tap is disabled. This is
   F1's exact shape, one dispatch later. It resolves only if measured ad-scan
   coverage reaches 0.98, because `analysisComplete` is coverage-driven and has
   highest precedence (:212). Per the coverage program's own numbers (ZERO of 34
   episodes at 95% scan, 29 under 25%), that is the common case, not the corner.

2. RUNNER DIES MID-ANALYSIS. The cancel-catch and failure arms revert
   `analysis_jobs` to `queued`/`failed` and release the lease; the asset row is
   untouched and stays `queued`. Until the serial lane returns to that episode
   -- measured at up to 13,678 s on the 2026-08-10 pull -- the row shows the
   same frozen bar with the same disabled tap.

WHAT A FIX LOOKS LIKE (a design decision, hence a bead not a patch). Either
(a) give the scheduler lane a symmetric demote — write the row back off `queued`
in the cancel-race arm, the cancel-catch arm and the failure/requeue arms, with
the same `AND analysisState = ?` conditional discipline
`markRegisteredAssetQueued` uses so a coordinator write is never clobbered; or
(b) let the lane write its own terminal on `.reachedTarget` /
`coverageInsufficient` outcomes (this is Pipeline B's missing half and overlaps
playhead-gqx4 / playhead-i7qe's re-drive work); or (c) stop reading `queued` as
"active" and derive the working bar from a LIVE signal (an in-flight lease)
rather than from a persisted token nothing retracts.

Note that (a) and (b) are not equivalent: (a) restores the actionable tap, (b)
gives the honest ◐. The bar-vs-tap tradeoff is the decision this bead owes.

title: [BUG] the gate baseline records ZERO XCTest/method-format entries, so a recurring 14-test download-family cluster is invisible to the NEW/known verdict

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
FILED BY playhead-fzrw (found while attributing that bead's full-plan gate result; outside its ceiling).

scripts/gate-baseline.PlayheadFastTests.json has 117 entries and EVERY ONE is prefixed `swift-testing::` — there are zero XCTest/method-name-format entries. That is not a coincidence of which tests are broken: those names emit NO `✘ Test "..."\' display-name line at all. They appear only in xcodebuild's trailing `Failing tests:` summary, in method form with parens, often listed TWICE. That is the signature of a test whose HOST WAS KILLED mid-test and re-run, not of an assertion failure — and gate_baseline.py parses the Swift Testing display-name stream, so it cannot see them.

MEASURED, three full PlayheadFastTests runs on 2026-08-11/12 plus one from an earlier bead:

  gate-jzj0-closer.log (a DIFFERENT bead, earlier tree)   15 such names
  playhead-fzrw full run 1                                14 such names
  playhead-fzrw full run 2                                16 such names
  playhead-fzrw control run (base production code)         2 such names

The recurring cluster is essentially identical across jzj0 and both fzrw runs:
  DownloadShowAttributionTests x7, StreamingDownloadCachedTests x2,
  ResumeSuspendedTransferTests x2, DelegateWorkJournalTests,
  EpisodeDownloadDelegateResumeHarvestTests,
  DownloadManagerDaemonUnavailableTests.

The gate reported `RED (73 known / 5 NEW)` for the run that contained 14 of them — none of the 14 counted toward either number. A genuine regression in that family would merge silently. This is the 2026-07-31 / PR #313 shape ('gate triage misses XCTest') recurring one layer down: the triage was fixed, the BASELINE was not.

Two corollaries worth recording:

1. The 7 DownloadShowAttributionTests names DO exist in the baseline under their swift-testing DISPLAY names, so the same test is trackable one way and invisible the other, depending on whether it failed an expectation or died with the host. Identity is not stable across those two failure kinds.

2. The NEW count on this box is far noisier than the file's own churn note suggests. Three full runs whose trees differ by ONE production file gave 5 NEW, 25 NEW and 10 NEW, with the CONTROL (unmodified base production) the noisiest of the three. Attribution of a full-run NEW set to a diff is currently not possible without a reachability argument.

REMEDY (not attempted here): teach gate_baseline.py to also parse the `Failing tests:` summary block, record those names under a distinct kind (e.g. `xcodebuild::`), and treat 'listed with no display-name line' as its own failure KIND so a host-kill is never confused with an expectation failure.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
=== FINDING CONFIRMED, BUT THE STATED CAUSE IS WRONG — corrected by the orchestrator, 2026-08-12 ===

THE FRAMING IN THIS BEAD IS 'the baseline holds 117 entries, ALL swift-testing::, zero XCTest, so gate_baseline.py cannot see XCTest failures.' The first clause is true and the inference is FALSE. scripts/gate_baseline.py parses BOTH formats and says so in its own docstring at :101-103:

  'Swift Testing prints ✘ Test "name" failed after 123.4 seconds; XCTest prints
   Test Case '-[Suite testFoo]' failed (0.025 seconds). Triage that greps only
   the first is how playhead-ynmk merged unnoticed, so both are parsed here.'

Four regexes cover it: _ST_FAIL_NAMED (:196), _ST_FAIL_FUNC (:197) for the bare-function display form, and _XC_RESULT (:208) for XCTest. The baseline has zero XCTest entries because zero XCTest tests have FAILED, not because they cannot be seen. That is the same wrong inference I made earlier in this session and corrected then; it has now been made twice, which is worth noticing.

=== THE REAL DEFECT, WHICH IS NARROWER AND STILL SERIOUS, VERIFIED ON THREE LOGS ===

A test whose HOST IS KILLED emits NO per-test line at all — neither the Swift Testing form nor the XCTest form. It appears exactly ONCE in the whole log, inside xcodebuild's trailing 'Failing tests:' summary block, in method form (Suite.method()). The parser has literally nothing to match, so such a failure counts toward NEITHER 'known' NOR 'NEW'. It is invisible.

MEASURED, by extracting the summary block and searching each name for any per-test line:
  gate-15d0-merge.log   15 names in the summary block, of which 15 have NO per-test line
  gate-kg8h-merge.log    5 names
  gate-3zxd-merge.log    1 name (this one DID also emit a display-name line and WAS counted)

Spot-checked four by hand — cancelReapsAttribution, clearCacheReapsAttribution, stagingFailureReleasesOwnership, resumeConsumesBlob: each occurs exactly once in a 7.3 MB log, in the summary block. func-form failures in that entire log: 1. XCTest-form failures: 0.

CONSEQUENCE, stated plainly: on the playhead-15d0 merge gate, FIFTEEN test failures were invisible to the mechanism whose entire job is to tell a regression from a known flake, and my scoped confirmation for that bead did not cover them (I re-ran the four suites the baseline NAMED, which is exactly the trap — the named set is the visible set). They are almost certainly starvation casualties of a killed host, and the same suites passed scoped during the kg8h triage hours later — but THE MECHANISM CANNOT TELL ME THAT, which is the defect.

=== WHAT THE FIX IS ===
Parse the 'Failing tests:' summary block as a THIRD source, and reconcile it against the per-test lines. A name there with no per-test line is not a pass and not a known flake — it is an UNRESOLVED failure and should be reported as its own category, because its cause (killed host) is precisely the one that also truncates the run. Note the block prints method form while the baseline is keyed on display names, so reconciliation needs the suite/method identity, not the display string.

RELATED AND ALREADY KNOWN: CLAUDE.md documents that a killed host makes the summary line cover only the relaunch, so real totals must come from per-test lines. This is the same hazard from the other end — when the host dies, SOME tests have no per-test line to come from.

Keeping this bead at P1 with the corrected diagnosis. It belongs with playhead-o89d (PerfGate the load-sensitive families) since starvation is what kills the host in the first place — fix that and this becomes rare, but do not let that be a reason to leave the hole.

title: [bug] the entire beads database is untracked — bd auto-exports to a path .gitignore blocks, and warns on every single write until nobody reads the warning
description:
FOUND 2026-08-11 while checking why 'Warning: auto-export: git add failed: exit status 1' printed after every bd write all day.

THE STATE, verified:
  .beads/issues.jsonl   4,541,137 bytes   IGNORED by .gitignore:11    tracked? NO
  .beads/dolt           436K              IGNORED by .gitignore:7     tracked? 0 files
  .beads/beads.db       248K              IGNORED by .beads/.gitignore:63 (*.db)
  git ls-files .beads/  ->  .gitignore, README.md, config.yaml, and five hooks. NOTHING ELSE.

So every issue in this tracker exists ONLY on this machine, in files git is instructed to ignore. There is no copy in the repo, no copy on the remote, and no copy in any bead worktree. CLAUDE.md says 'Canonical data lives in .beads/dolt/' — which is exactly one of the ignored paths.

WHY IT IS NOT MERELY UNTIDY. bd is TRYING to do the right thing: it auto-exports to .beads/issues.jsonl and then runs git add, which fails because line 11 of .gitignore blocks that very path. Two mechanisms disagree, the export loses, and the failure is reported as a warning on EVERY write. Today that warning printed on dozens of operations, and I stopped reading it — which is the actual defect. A durability failure that announces itself constantly is indistinguishable from noise.

WHAT IS AT RISK RIGHT NOW, one day's worth: 34 issues killed with recorded evidence, 13 merged, 25 reprioritized, ~11 created (z1px, kg8h, 5o7p, mn5e, fzrw, njkw, bz44, 0hqr, 4wzh, iyru, 7cjo), and the long analytical writeups attached to 15d0, 4xqf, a3hf and mn5e — several of which are the only record of measurements that took hours to produce (the 0.257 compute ratio, the transcriptVersion SHA-256 finding, the precheck suppression arithmetic).

DO NOT JUST DELETE THE IGNORE LINE. The reason it is plausibly deliberate is that issues.jsonl is 4.5 MB and rewrites on every bead write, so tracking it as-is would put a multi-megabyte churning diff in front of every commit and every review. That is a real cost and somebody may have chosen it knowingly.

OPTIONS, for Dan:
 (a) Track issues.jsonl and accept the diff noise. Simplest; makes every bead write a repo change.
 (b) Track it but commit on a cadence (a periodic 'chore(beads): snapshot' rather than per-write), and silence the per-write auto-export so the warning stops being noise.
 (c) Leave it untracked and back it up out-of-band (the export already runs; only the git add fails), e.g. a copy into a synced directory. Keeps the repo clean, keeps the data.
 (d) Decide the data is genuinely disposable and REMOVE the auto-export so the warning stops lying about intent.

MY RECOMMENDATION IS (b) OR (c). What is not acceptable is the current state, where the system attempts durability, fails, says so every time, and everyone has learned to route around the message.

Whichever is chosen, silence or fix the warning. A warning that fires on every operation trains its own audience to ignore it, and that is how I read past it all day.

title: [bug] an implementer and a reviewer can share one worktree and mutate the same file — the battery lock does not cover hand-rolled mutation scripts
description:
MY ORCHESTRATION ERROR, 2026-08-11, caught by the playhead-kg8h implementer rather than by any mechanism.

WHAT HAPPENED. I dispatched the kg8h R1 reviewer into /Users/dabrams/playhead/.worktrees/kg8h while the implementer's agent was still nominally alive. Both ran mutation campaigns against the same file, RediffDayZeroKickoffCoordinator.swift. They did not overlap — the implementer's battery finished ~11:15, the reviewer's started 11:34 — BY LUCK, NOT BY MECHANISM. Nothing would have stopped them interleaving.

WHY THE EXISTING LOCK DOES NOT HELP. playhead-pu7e added a per-worktree lock and CLAUDE.md documents it as 'ONE BATTERY PER WORKTREE, ENFORCED', with the correct reasoning that a concurrent battery is UNDETECTABLE FROM INSIDE EITHER RUN: between run A's restore and its next apply the tree is genuinely clean, so B's dirty-tree guard admits it, and from then on each run's restore reverts the other's mutant while both byte-exactness checks keep passing, because each verifies only its OWN restore.

That lock is held by scripts/mutation-battery.sh. It does not cover anything else. The kg8h implementer used a hand-rolled mutate.py and the reviewer a hand-rolled run-gate.sh; NEITHER takes the lock, so the documented enforcement was absent exactly where two agents were pointed at one file. The guarantee people believe they have is narrower than the guarantee that exists.

WHY IT IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN JUST REMEMBERING. The failure is silent and it destroys VERDICTS, not code — playhead-9y9e R1 lost four verdict attempts to this shape and three rails still carry the implementer's own verdicts because no reviewer could obtain an independent one. A review round whose mutant was reverted by a neighbour reports GREEN and is read as 'no defect found'.

OPTIONS, not a decision:
 (a) Make the lock a small standalone helper any script can source, and require review-round scripts to take it. Cheapest, still opt-in, still forgettable.
 (b) Enforce at the ORCHESTRATION layer instead: one agent per worktree, full stop. A reviewer gets its own worktree off the same commit. Costs ~2 GB of derivedData per extra worktree and a cold build; buys a guarantee that does not depend on any script remembering.
 (c) A pre-commit / pre-gate guard that refuses when the worktree is dirty with someone else's mutation, keyed on a recorded owner pid like pu7e's info file.

MY RECOMMENDATION IS (b) FOR REVIEW ROUNDS SPECIFICALLY. The lock family keeps needing extension because it is defending a shared resource that has no reason to be shared: an implementer and its reviewer have no need to occupy one checkout, and separate worktrees also give the reviewer a genuinely independent build. (a) is worth doing anyway as defence in depth.

NO DAMAGE THIS TIME, verified: git show 214ca1ed of the coordinator carries 'await claimKickoff(' at line 150; only the working tree held the reviewer's fire-and-forget mutant mid-probe. The branch was never at risk because nothing was committed on top of a mutant — which is the actual hazard to guard, and it is one commit away.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
DAN ASKED WHAT HE IS NEEDED FOR HERE (2026-08-11). ANSWER: NOTHING. This is an orchestration rule, mine to follow, and I have adopted it as of now — a reviewer gets its own worktree off the same commit, never the implementer's.

The only thing that touches him is COST, so it is stated rather than absorbed silently: an extra worktree is ~2 GB of derivedData and one cold build (~3 min). On today's volume — kg8h ran four review rounds — that is up to four extra checkouts if they overlapped. They do not overlap in practice, since I run one build at a time on this box, so the steady-state cost is one extra worktree alive at a time, not four.

If disk gets tight the mitigation is already in hand: scripts/disk-cleanup.sh, plus erasing the simulator between rounds (it grew 3.8 GB across kg8h's four rounds and erases back to 35 MB).

WHAT I AM NOT DOING, and why it is worth writing down: extending the pu7e lock to cover hand-rolled scripts (option (a) in this bead). It is cheap and it is defence in depth, but it keeps guarding a shared resource that has no reason to be shared. Separate worktrees REMOVE the sharing. If someone later wants (a) as well, nothing here precludes it — but it should not be the primary fix.

This bead stays OPEN as the record of the rule and of the incident that produced it; it does not need code. Close it if you would rather the rule live in CLAUDE.md instead — that is the one call I would take from Dan on it, since CLAUDE.md is where the other agent-ops rules live and this one is the same species.

title: a day-0 head/tail precheck must probe under a DISTINCT persona — the existing sampler uses the DOWNLOAD persona, so its verdict is blind to exactly the shows day-0 exists for
description:
FILED BY playhead-kg8h (Job 3: the precheck was scoped into kg8h, investigated,
and NOT shipped — this bead carries what would have to be true first).

`runDayZeroRefetch` bypasses the rotation precheck deliberately, and its own doc
says why: "the pre-check is a single-persona head/tail probe that
false-negatives on client-PINNED DAI (a same-context re-fetch returns a
byte-identical body), the very category day-0's k-way probe targets."

Established from source, and it is worse than "single-persona":
  * `PlayheadRuntime.swift:1604` builds the production sampler as
    `URLSessionRangedAudioSampler(persona: .default)`
  * `RediffFetchPersona.default == .appleCoreMediaIPhone` (Seams:324)
  * `RediffFetchPersona.download == .appleCoreMediaIPhone` (Seams:335)
So the precheck probes under the SAME request context the played A-side was
downloaded under — the one persona `kWayPersonasDistinct` exists to exclude
(playhead-9s6q FIX B). On a client-pinned show it returns byte-identical bytes
by construction, the gate says "unchanged", and the full fetch is suppressed.

A SECOND, INDEPENDENT LIMIT, measured on the one day-0 attempt in
scratchpad/db-overnight5: 66,010,142 B over 2 B-copies / 1926 s = 17.1 kB/s, so
the 64 KiB head and tail samples (`RediffRefetchPolicy` defaults) each reach
3.8 SECONDS of audio. That episode's four day-0 slots are 0.0-60.3, 888.6-915.0,
942.4-987.6 and 1880.3-1895.4 — the last one ends 30.6 s before EOF, EIGHT TIMES
the tail probe's reach. So "head and tail are exactly where pre-roll and
post-roll live" is only true of the first and last ~4 seconds at this bitrate.

WHAT WOULD HAVE TO BE TRUE before a day-0 precheck is worth wiring:
  1. the probe runs under the personas the k-way fetch will actually use
     (`kWayPersonasDistinct(from: .download, count: 1)` -> Mac), so "unchanged"
     is evidence about the fetch that would follow;
  2. the sample window is sized from a measured bitrate rather than a fixed
     64 KiB, or the claim about post-rolls is dropped;
  3. the mid-roll coverage traded away is measured on a corpus, not one episode.

title: the day-0 kickoff's asset-row precondition lags the download by minutes to HOURS — 3 of 5 downloads on the overnight pull could never have reached day-0
description:
FILED BY playhead-kg8h (established while establishing that bead's mechanism;
outside its ceiling, which is "a row exists for every download").

`RediffDayZeroKickoffCoordinator`'s readiness probe needs TWO things: the pinned
file (present the moment the download completes) and an `analysis_assets` row
(`PlayheadRuntime.swift`, the coordinator's `probe` closure —
`kickoffStore.fetchAssetByEpisodeId`). The budget for both is
`dayZeroPreparationReadinessMaxAttempts (40) x dayZeroPreparationReadinessPollNanos (10 s)`
= 400 s.

MEASURED, scratchpad/db-overnight5/analysis.sqlite. All FIVE `preAnalysis` jobs
were created inside a 37-second window — 09:02:21, 09:02:24, 09:02:26, 09:02:33,
09:02:58 — i.e. five downloads landed as one batch. The `analysis_assets` rows
they need arrived at:

  asset      job created   asset row registered   LAG
  66D32039   09:02:21      09:02:21                    0 s   inside the budget
  F7BB38BB   09:02:24      09:08:46                  382 s   inside the budget
  B80D3EE0   09:02:26      09:18:23                  957 s   OUTSIDE (2.4x)
  60DFF7B4   09:02:33      12:48:53               13,580 s   OUTSIDE (34x)
  590D6656   09:02:58      12:50:56               13,678 s   OUTSIDE (34x)

So THREE OF FIVE downloads could not have reached the trigger no matter how the
queue is drained, how fast the network is, or whether the process survived. They
would give up `no_analysis_asset` — which is exactly what the 2026-08-09
db-vtjxverdict pull recorded FIVE times (playhead-kxgh: five rows, every one
`lastPollCount=40`, every one `no_analysis_asset`).

That makes the asset-registration lag, not the kickoff plumbing, the binding
constraint on Dan's "rediff should be done immediately upon download". The lag
is set by the serial analysis lane: the asset row appears when the job runner
first picks the job up, and on this pull the runner was 3h46m behind by episode
four.

TWO CANDIDATE DIRECTIONS, not a decision:
  (a) register the `analysis_assets` row at ENQUEUE rather than at first RUN, so
      the day-0 precondition is satisfied when the bytes land. Cheap, but it
      changes what an asset row means.
  (b) drop the asset-row precondition from the day-0 probe and key the kickoff on
      the episode id + pinned file, resolving the asset later. The kickoff ledger
      is already episode-keyed for exactly this reason.
Both are architecture calls, not fixes to make in passing.

RELATED: playhead-kxgh (serial drain), playhead-jra6 (in-memory queue),
playhead-kg8h (the durable claim, which makes this lag VISIBLE rather than
fixing it).

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
MECHANISM (established, file:line).

`analysis_assets` rows have exactly two writers:
  * AnalysisWorkScheduler.resolveAnalysisAssetId — insert at AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:6649, and its ONLY caller is processJob (:4669). So the row appears when the SERIAL analysis lane reaches the episode. enqueue already says so in a comment at :1306 ('created lazily by resolveAnalysisAssetId at job execution time').
  * AnalysisCoordinator.resolveSession — insert at AnalysisCoordinator.swift:2351, reachable only from handlePlayStarted.

Neither runs at download time, which is why the lag on db-prewipe6 was 0 / 382 / 957 / 13,580 / 13,678 s against a 400 s budget. Dispatch was not stalled; it was BUSY. The prose in RediffDayZeroKickoff.swift claiming 'post-ewag the asset registers within seconds' was wrong and is corrected.

WHAT THE DAY-0 PATH READS OFF THE ROW — the question that decides whether an early mint moves the failure. Exactly two things:
  * asset.id — the mint key, and the key of rediff_day_zero_attempts / suppressions / AdWindow.analysisAssetId.
  * asset.sourceURL — the read-only pinned A-side. AdDetectionService.resolveDayZeroASide (:12288-12312) fetches the row, maps sourceURL through byteDifferASideURL, mmaps it. That resolver is shared by mintByteExactDayZeroMarks (:12001) and its free pre-fetch blocker (:12274), so the two can never disagree.

No duration, no fingerprint, no transcript — nothing the analysis lane produces. So an early mint is the right answer, not a placeholder that relocates the give-up.

FIX: AnalysisWorkScheduler.registerDownloadedAssetRowIfAbsent, called from enqueue. Three preconditions, each with a mutation rail: a cached file exists; its bytes HASH to the job's canonical fingerprint; and the episode has NO asset row at all (so every reuse arm of resolveAnalysisAssetId is vacuous by construction and playhead-0hi9 stays closed). Everything excluded falls through to the lazy path unchanged.

title: [bug] the retry budget kills a CONVERGING job: F7BB38BB was terminated at 84% scanned for being 'under coverage'
description:
MEASURED on the virgin-DB overnight pull.

  asset=F7BB38BB  status=FAILED  retry=3  deferReason=underCoverageBudgetSpent-fullEpisodeScan
  cursor={"processedUnitCount":0,"lastProcessedUpperBoundSec":1620}   episode duration 1931s

It had scanned to 1620 of 1931 seconds — 84% of the episode — and was terminated for being under the coverage floor. The remaining 311 seconds will never be scanned by this job.

THE MECHANISM, and it is deliberate in the source. BackfillJobRunner.swift:1890-1896: 'The retry count advances on every under-coverage attempt. Unlike playhead-bkhc's expiry budget there is no reset on progress clause, and the difference is deliberate: an expiring background window is a fragment of one attempt, so charging it would starve a converging job, whereas this branch is reached only after a FULL pass over everything the job was handed. Each attempt is a whole attempt, so a flat budget of maxRetries is both finite and never unfair.'

WHY THE REASONING DOES NOT HOLD ON THIS EVIDENCE. The premise is that reaching this branch means a full pass completed over everything the job was handed. But playhead-15d0 established that what the job is handed is itself narrowed by a resume cursor, and R2 established that the reuse predicate fires on only 1.18-11.2% of jobs because transcriptVersion is a per-episode hash invalidated by every appended chunk. So a 'full pass over what it was handed' can be a full pass over a small and arbitrarily-chosen fraction, three times, while real coverage climbs steadily. That is exactly what 1620 of 1931 looks like.

The second failure in the same pull is the same shape from the other direction: 66D32039, retry=3, expiredWithoutProgress, cursor pinned at 194.46 across three attempts.

SCOPE. The budget should be spent by ATTEMPTS THAT DID NOT ADVANCE COVERAGE, not by attempts. A job whose covered seconds grew since its last attempt has demonstrated it is converging and should not be charged. Note the counter-argument the existing comment is defending against — a job that can never converge must still terminate — so the fix is a reset-on-progress clause with a floor, not an unbounded budget.

DO NOT reuse the 'is it under the floor' test as the progress test: that is the quantity that is already wrong. Progress means covered seconds INCREASED, and the numerator and denominator both need naming.

title: [bug] every FM call pays a cold start — prewarmHit is 0 on all 95 calls, and pre-call latency runs to 74 seconds
description:
MEASURED on the virgin-DB overnight pull (scratchpad/db-overnight5/WHY_EXPIRED.txt).

  prewarmHit: {0: 95}          ZERO hits out of ninety-five calls
  suspendingLatencyMs          n=50, p50 11.3s, MAX 74.1s

Every single Foundation Models call overnight was a cold start. The column exists, is persisted (AnalysisStore.swift:18063), and reads false every time.

WHY IT COSTS DAN'S TARGET DIRECTLY. The longest window all night was 295.8s. A 74-second prologue is a QUARTER of the best window gone before the first scan begins; at the p50 of 11.3s it is still 4% off every window, and windows are the scarce resource. Across 95 calls the suspending latency alone accounts for a large share of the gap between the 38.2 min of FM time spent and the 22.6 min banked.

WHAT TO ESTABLISH FIRST. Whether a prewarm path exists and never fires (the y3ya shape — a mechanism with no production consumer, which this queue has now hit four times), or whether it fires and cannot hit because each background window is a fresh process. Those need different fixes and the difference is cheap to determine: find every writer of prewarmHit and every caller of whatever sets it.

If it is the second — a fresh process per window cannot inherit a warm model — then the honest conclusion is that the cold start is a FIXED COST PER WINDOW, which argues for fewer, longer windows rather than more, and that is a scheduling change to weigh against playhead-rbj4 rather than a bug to fix here.

ACCEPTANCE: state which of the two it is, with the source trace. Fix only if it is the first.

title: [bug] adScanCoveredSec credits ANY passA row asset-wide — no cohort, no transcriptVersion, no jobPhase filter, so coverage over-reports exactly the sparse targeted spans the scanner now refuses to reuse
description:
FOUND 2026-08-11 by the playhead-15d0 R1 reviewer, out of that bead's scope, filed not fixed.

AnalysisStore.readScannedRegions (AnalysisStore.swift:11074-11118) credits adScanCoveredSec from any passA semantic_scan_results row for the asset. Its WHERE clause has NO cohort filter, NO transcriptVersion filter, and NO jobPhase filter — the guard is only 'endTime > startTime' plus the no-work sentinel exclusion (:11109).

WHY THIS IS THE SAME DEFECT ONE LAYER DOWN. playhead-15d0 R1 established that a TARGETED phase's passA rows over-claim by construction: TargetedWindowNarrower.narrowedResult returns the union of DISJOINT per-anchor intervals (TargetedWindowNarrower.swift:784), and FoundationModelClassifier.planPassA stamps each window's span as min(startTime)...max(endTime) over a contiguous slice OF THAT SPARSE ARRAY (FoundationModelClassifier.swift:3029-3046). A window straddling two intervals therefore persists a span covering every segment between them, none of which was ever in a prompt. .scanRandomAuditWindows is the worst case: a sparse sample whose merged span is nearly the whole episode.

15d0 closed that hole for the SCANNER — a full scan will no longer let those rows delete its own audio. It did NOT close it for the COVERAGE READER, which still counts them. Nor does the reader filter transcriptVersion, so a row written against a superseded transcript still counts.

CONSEQUENCE, stated precisely. This is a MEASUREMENT over-report, not audio loss: no seconds are dropped, the number is wrong. adScanCoveredSec is the pz32 numerator — the thing that decides whether the readiness checkmark is shown and what the Activity screen claims. So after 15d0 the coverage percentage is MORE optimistic than the scanner actually is, and the gap widens the moment a show reaches coldStartEpisodeThreshold with stableRecall and starts producing targeted rows.

THE STANDING DEFECT-CLASS CHECK, applied: what would adScanCoveredSec read if the audio it claims had never been screened? Today: the same number, provided some targeted window's span happened to bracket it. Numerator = seconds a passA row's [startTime,endTime] covers, ANY phase / ANY cohort / ANY transcript version. Denominator = episode duration. Those are not the same population.

SCOPE. Bring the reader's predicate into agreement with SemanticScanResult.isReusable(cohort:version:) and add the jobPhase filter, OR — if targeted phases should legitimately contribute coverage — make them persist their true examined segments rather than a bracketing span. That is a real design choice and should not be decided inside a fix.

DO NOT reuse 15d0's helper wholesale without deciding that question first: 15d0's answer ('a full scan is narrowed only by full-scan rows') is right for the scanner because a full scan must not skip audio, and may be wrong for the reader, which is trying to report everything genuinely examined.

VERIFY THE COST BEFORE ASSUMING IT IS FREE. 15d0 R1 measured the phase filter at zero cost — all 188 passA rows across db-evening2 and db-vtjxverdict carry jobPhase=fullEpisodeScan. The transcriptVersion filter is NOT free by the same measurement: only 19 of 188 rows (10.1%) carry their own job's last-attempt version, and 6 of 15 assets have none. Adding it will visibly LOWER reported coverage. That is the honest direction, and it is the same arc as playhead-pz32 / the 2026-07-30 coverage-honesty work, but it should land with the number named rather than as a silent drop.

title: The coarse scan's 'is there time for another asset' gate measures a FIXED 219 s constant, not the grant actually in hand
description:
Established while implementing playhead-15d0 (source trace).

`AnalysisCoordinator.runCoarseScanLoop` gates each asset on remaining time (AnalysisCoordinator.swift:841-845):

    let remaining = now().duration(to: deadline)
    guard remaining > .zero, remaining >= minimumWindowBudget

`deadline` comes from `BackgroundProcessingService.swift:1532`:

    let workDeadline = budget.workDeadline(from: grantStart)

and `workBudget = designGrant - teardownReserve = 255 s - 36 s = 219 s` (BackgroundGrantBudget.swift:269-278, :413-424) — **measured averages over 132 full-length grants, baked in as constants.** They are not the current window.

So on the 13 s grants measured in playhead-15d0, `remaining` still computes ~219 s, clears the 60 s `minimumCheckpointBudget` floor, and the loop starts an asset whose p95 coarse WINDOW alone is 57.5 s (BackgroundGrantBudget.swift:383-388).

NAME THE QUANTITY. `remaining` reads "seconds left in this grant". It measures "seconds left in an average grant, counted from when this one started". Those are the same number only when the grant is average. The standing defect class.

WHAT MAKES THIS HARD, and why it is filed rather than fixed: **nothing in the process knows the real answer.** `grep -rn "backgroundTimeRemaining|remainingTime"` over Playhead returns only `ForegroundAssistHandoff.swift` (an unrelated download ETA). Nothing reads `UIApplication.backgroundTimeRemaining` and nothing reads a `BGTask` expiration time. iOS gives the app an `expirationHandler` callback and no advance notice, and the observed grants ranged 196-295 s in the afternoon and 13-35 s the same evening, tracking user activity.

So the honest options are (a) read `UIApplication.backgroundTimeRemaining` where it is meaningful and stop pretending otherwise, (b) drop the start gate's pretence and rely purely on incremental persistence, or (c) keep the constant but stop calling it `remaining`. This needs a decision, not an implementation.

RELATED, deliberately separate: playhead-15d0 removed the largest consumer of a short grant (re-planning already-screened audio). This bead is about the gate that was supposed to prevent starting work that cannot finish.

title: A hard-killed backfill job is invisible to the NEXT background grant — status='running' is excluded and no backfill grant runs the reaper
description:
Established while implementing playhead-15d0 (source trace, not yet reproduced on a device pull).

THE SHAPE. When a background window ends by a hard kill (jetsam/suspend) rather than a graceful `expirationHandler` cancellation, the `backfill_jobs` row stays `status='running'`. Both candidate queries the FM-first background phase uses then EXCLUDE it:

  * `AnalysisStore.fetchAssetIdsWithResumableBackfillJobs` binds `status <> 'running'` (AnalysisStore.swift:16857-16873, bind at :16872)
  * `fetchAssetIdsMissingCoverageLaneJobs` requires `NOT EXISTS` any row (:16931-16944)

The only thing that flips a stale `running` back to `queued` is `AnalysisJobReconciler.resetStrandedBackfillJobs` (AnalysisStore.swift:17011-17024, floor `strandedJobFreshnessSeconds = 600` at :1830). Its production callers are:

  * `PlayheadRuntime.swift:2729` (launch)
  * `BackgroundProcessingService.swift:2387` — the **preAnalysisRecovery** handler
  * `AnalysisJobReconciler.sweepStrandedBackfillJobsInSession` from scene activation (`PlayheadApp.swift:654`)

`handleBackfillTask` does NOT call `reconcile()`.

CONSEQUENCE. Two backfill grants in a row, with no launch, no scene activation and no preAnalysisRecovery wake in between, and the second grant sees the asset as having NO WORK and skips it entirely. It does not re-scan the audio, but it does not resume either — the asset is simply absent from the sweep until something unrelated happens to run the reaper. On the evening measured in playhead-15d0 the grants were 13-35 s, so a hard kill is the expected termination, not the exception.

NOT ESTABLISHED, and it is what decides the priority: whether two `handleBackfillTask` grants can in fact be separated by none of those three events in the field. The 2026-08-10 pull's rows were all `queued`/`deferred`, so this shape is not witnessed there.

CANDIDATE REMEDY (not designed): have the backfill handler run the same stranded sweep the recovery handler already runs, or scope the reaper to the asset the sweep is about to consider. Both are one call; the question is whether the 600 s freshness floor is the right one for a lane whose own grants are 13-35 s.

title: FM regions are built wide and then discarded by an unreachable consensus floor — give them a mark-tier anchor path that survives the next run
description:
ESTABLISHED in playhead-881t. Dan chose to investigate before building, and the answer is that the machinery already exists and is switched off by a floor that cannot be reached.

WHAT IS ALREADY TRUE. FM refinement regions ARE built, reach RegionProposalBuilder through a live ungated path (BackfillJobRunner.RunResult.fmRefinementWindows -> AdDetectionService.swift:4348 -> RegionShadowPhase.Input.fmWindows:286 -> RegionProposalBuilder.build:237), and are exactly the width the pipeline lacks: 11 device spans of 10, 70, 81, 85, 88, 93, 101 and 329 atoms.

WHY THEY NEVER ANCHOR. consensusStrength (RegionProposalBuilder.swift:566-587) is the sole writer of fmConsensusStrength and returns .low unless ALL of three hold. Each fails structurally on the layout production actually uses:
  - uniqueWindows > 1 — planAdaptiveZoom emits exactly ONE plan per coarse window, and device coarse windows PARTITION the episode with zero overlap. uniqueWindows == 1 always.
  - hasAnchors — 9 of 11 device passB spans carry anchors:[] with ownershipInferenceWasSuppressed:true.
  - minimumIoU >= 0.4 — the only second-window source is outward expansion, whose merged span is a UNION and therefore much wider. Measured 0.213 and 0.258. canCluster fails; they never even join a cluster.
Path 1 demands >= .medium (0.7). .low is 0.35. Path 3 cannot substitute: fmAcousticCorroborated needs an acoustic break within +/-2 atoms, so over a 70-329 atom region it anchors ~5 atoms — an atom-level path like lexical, not a block proposer.

THE FIX, two halves, both required:

(A) A MARK-TIER anchor path for .low FM regions — a distinct AnchorRef case that BackfillEvidenceFusion.computeGate treats like sustainedMusicOffset. Cost: one filter in AtomEvidenceProjector, one enum case, one gate clause, one carriesOnlyMusicPresenceHint-style predicate update.

  DO NOT SIMPLY LOWER PATH 1's FLOOR TO .low. computeGate (BackfillEvidenceFusion.swift:1275-1302) routes any .fmConsensus ref into quorumGateForFMConsensus, which can return .eligible — so a floor change silently makes 70-329 atom FM regions AUTO-SKIP eligible. That is what feedback_certainty_tiered_skip forbids without its own argument. The whole point of a separate case is that it cannot reach the skip tier by accident.

(B) DURABILITY, or (A) does not survive. The FM->region handoff is IN-MEMORY and per-invocation: BackfillJobRunner.swift:728-732 states RegionProposalBuilder is deliberately not given persisted semantic_scan_results. So fmWindows is non-empty only in the run that itself performed the refinement. Any later run — FM off, podcastId empty (AdDetectionService.swift:4326), FM unavailable, job deferred, work already done — rebuilds regions with fmWindows == [] and re-upserts decoded_spans with NO FM provenance. evidence_events.atomOrdinals carries the exact range, so the persisted rows CAN rebuild a RefinedAdSpan.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO CARRY, both measured in 881t and both load-bearing:
  - FM coarse windows are ~70 s on device, NOT ~1,000 s. n=171 non-sentinel passA rows, mean 70.1 s, max 121.0 s. Earlier beads (i40t, 881t as filed) cite ~1,000 s and overstate the inner-edge risk by an order of magnitude. Do not reuse that figure without re-deriving it.
  - FM width ALREADY reaches ad_windows by another door: SemanticSweepMarkComposer reads persisted scan rows and mints markOnly candidates at 80.0 / 89.4 / 160.0 / 215.3 s on this device. The shortfall is specific to the ANCHOR path. Any proposal must say what it adds over that.
