HONEST YIELD TODAY: close to nothing. FM has left evidence on 2 of 33 assets and zero backfill jobs have ever completed. This bead is worth building because it is small and correct and READY when completion improves — but its measurable effect is bounded by the scan-increments bead. Build it saying so.

FALSIFIERS: (A) dies if FM refinement EXTENTS are imprecise on a gold corpus — currently untestable, only 2 assets carry FM geometry and neither has a rediff-confirmed slot. (A) also dies if a mark-tier FM span re-floods a surface SemanticSweepMarkComposer already covers. (B) dies if persisted rows cannot rebuild a RefinedAdSpan — they can.

Supersedes the open question in playhead-i40t option (b): it is a REPAIR, not a build.

title: FM anchors ZERO spans on device — the highest-ceiling width lever is not firing at all
description:
ESTABLISHED in the playhead-4xqf establish round, 2026-08-11, and named there as the single highest-value open question. NOT diagnosed — this bead is to find out why.

THE MEASUREMENT. On Dan's device DB (db-night1 / db-evening2, schema 47) there are 66 decoded_spans. Anchor provenance, counted:

  evidenceCatalog          45
  sustainedMusicOffset     49
  classifierSeed            8
  user-confirmed            7
  fmConsensus               0     <-- zero
  fmAcousticCorroborated    0     <-- zero

FM anchors NOTHING. Not rarely — never, across every span on the device.

WHY THAT IS THE CEILING. A decoded span is a maximal run of atoms with isAnchored == true (AtomEvidenceProjector.swift:307-314), and anchoring is region-range membership. The pipeline can only propose as much WIDTH as some channel anchored. Median span width by proposer, measured:

  user-drawn            59.8 s
  sustainedMusicOffset  14.9 s
  evidenceCatalog       11.6 s

The widest spans in the store are the ones a human drew. Lexical anchors ONE ATOM PER HIT (AtomEvidenceProjector.swift:243-247), so it structurally cannot propose a block. Music anchors a sting. Neither can span an ad read. FM is the only channel whose Path 1 anchors a region's WHOLE ordinal range — and it fires zero times.

THE TRACED SLOT, which shows what this costs. Asset D9B513CD (Conan), rediff-confirmed slot 3194.5-3371.2 = 176.7 s:
  - transcript: 382 chunks, fast+final, span FULLY covered. Not a reach failure.
  - anchoring: 2 spans, 3238.6-3261.3 (22.7 s) and 3321.4-3330.0 (8.6 s), both sustainedMusicOffset ONLY.
    145 of 176.7 s contain NO ANCHORED ATOM.
  - result: the listener got 42.3 s of a 176.7 s break marked. The two marks sit on the music stings at each
    end of the pod; the ad copy between them was transcribed, never anchored, never proposed.

The words were there. Nothing claimed them.

ESTABLISH FIRST — three candidate causes, do not assume:
  1. REGION QUALIFICATION — FM regions are produced but never qualify to anchor (a gate, a strength floor,
     a provenance requirement). Check what Path 1 demands and whether any device region meets it.
  2. FM NEVER RUNS in the lane that would anchor — the coarse verdict exists but is not routed into
     RegionProposalBuilder at all, or runs only in a shadow/mark lane whose output is discarded.
  3. CONSENSUS-STRENGTH FLOOR — fmConsensusStrength never reaches the threshold the anchor path requires,
     so the region is built and then dropped.

Distinguishing them is cheap from the device DB plus source: (1) and (3) leave regions behind, (2) does not.

RELATED, AND WHY THIS IS SEPARATE FROM THE FIX: playhead-i40t is the DECISION bead for what to do about
width (option (b) is 'make the coarse FM verdict a width proposer', option (c) is pod-envelope extension).
This bead is the PRIOR question — whether the machinery Dan already paid for is simply switched off. If FM
regions exist and are being dropped by a floor, that is a much cheaper fix than building a new proposer, and
i40t's option (b) is not a new feature but a repair.

CAUTION carried from playhead-y3ya: 'FMBackfillMode.canProposeNewRegions had ZERO production consumers' was
exactly this shape one layer over, and the answer there was that the capability existed and nothing called it.
Check for a dead consumer before concluding the model is at fault.

CONSTRAINTS on any eventual fix (Dan's standing rulings, recorded so they are not rediscovered): FM coarse
windows run ~1,000 s, so widening what AUTO-SKIPS on an FM anchor is severe inner-edge risk — outer edges are
free, inner edges eat the show (feedback_outer_edges_free_inner_precious). Certainty-tiered skip says
auto-SKIP high-certainty DAI, MARK when uncertain. So an FM width proposal is admissible mark-tier; auto-skip
tier needs its own argument.
notes:
ESTABLISHED 2026-08-11 (playhead-881t investigation, no build required).

VERDICT: candidate (3) — a CONSENSUS-STRENGTH FLOOR that is structurally
unreachable — compounded by candidate (2) for the coarse lane. NOT (1) in the
"a gate drops a good region" sense: FM regions ARE built, with real width, and
they are scored .low by a rule that cannot return .medium for the window layout
production actually uses.

Evidence DB: db-vtjxverdict (schema 47, epoch 101, 66 decoded_spans, 210
semantic_scan_results). Reproduced on db-live, db-corrected2, db-evening,
db-night1: fmConsensus/fmAcousticCorroborated = 0 in every one.

1. THE COARSE VERDICT IS NEVER ROUTED (candidate 2, coarse lane).
   passA spansJSON is {"supportLineRefs":[...],"certainty":"..."} — presence
   only, NO span geometry. makeFMProposals (RegionProposalBuilder.swift:495-519)
   iterates `window.spans`, so a coarse verdict yields no observation, no
   region. Independently, coarse windows are never appended to
   fmRefinementWindows: the only two appends are BackfillJobRunner.swift:3663
   (passB refinement) and :3789 (outward expansion). This is already written
   down in SemanticSweepMarkComposer.swift's header (playhead-y3ya).

2. THE REFINEMENT LANE DOES REACH RegionProposalBuilder, AND ITS REGIONS ARE WIDE.
   BackfillJobRunner.RunResult.fmRefinementWindows -> AdDetectionService:4348 ->
   RegionShadowPhase.Input.fmWindows:286 -> RegionProposalBuilder.build:237.
   Live, unflagged, verified per-file. NOT a dead consumer.
   On device: evidence_events sourceType='fm' = 11 rows, on 2 of 19 assets with
   decoded_spans. Their atomOrdinals are 10, 70, 81, 85, 88, 93, 101, 329 atoms
   wide — exactly the block width the bead wants.

3. EVERY ONE OF THOSE REGIONS IS .low, BY THREE INDEPENDENT LEGS.
   consensusStrength (RegionProposalBuilder.swift:566-587), the SOLE writer of
   fmConsensusStrength, returns .low unless ALL of:
     (a) uniqueWindows > 1. planAdaptiveZoom emits exactly ONE plan per coarse
         window (`windowIndex: plans.count`, FoundationModelClassifier:3155-3158)
         and device coarse windows PARTITION the episode (atoms 0-95, 96-197,
         198-294, ... contiguous, zero overlap). One observation per span =>
         uniqueWindows == 1 => .low, always.
     (b) hasAnchors. 9 of 11 device passB spans carry anchors:[] with
         ownershipInferenceWasSuppressed:true (permissive-bypass drops anchors).
         The 2 that do carry anchors are the SAME window logged by two jobs.
     (c) minimum pairwise IoU >= fmIoUThreshold (0.4). The only second-window
         source is outward expansion (windowIndex: 1000 + base*100 + iteration,
         BackfillJobRunner:4206), and its merged span is a UNION so it is much
         wider than the base. Measured on AD5F3A0A: IoU([470..798],[493..562])
         = 70/329 = 0.213 and IoU([470..798],[589..673]) = 85/329 = 0.258. Both
         < 0.4, so canCluster fails and they never even join a cluster.
   AtomEvidenceProjector Path 1 demands >= .medium (0.7). .low is 0.35.

4. PATH 3 CANNOT SUBSTITUTE. fmAcousticCorroborated needs an acoustic break
   within +/-2 ATOMS. Over a 70-329 atom FM region that can anchor ~5 atoms at
   most — it is an atom-level path like lexical, not a block proposer.

5. FM WIDTH ALREADY REACHES ad_windows BY A DIFFERENT DOOR. SemanticSweepMarkComposer
   (detectorVersion 'semantic-sweep-v1', playhead-y3ya) reads persisted
   semantic_scan_results and mints markOnly candidates at 80.0 / 89.4 / 160.0 /
   215.3 s on this device. So the shortfall is specific to the ANCHOR path;
   presence-without-extent is already surfaced mark-tier.

6. CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S CONSTRAINT SECTION: FM coarse windows on device
   average 70.1 s (n=171 non-sentinel, max 121.0 s), NOT ~1,000 s. The
   inner-edge risk of an FM-anchored width proposal is an order of magnitude
   smaller than the constraint assumed. Re-derive before using the old figure.

7. SECOND, ADDITIVE CAUSE — THE HANDOFF IS IN-MEMORY AND PER-INVOCATION.
   RegionProposalBuilder is never given persisted semantic_scan_results (the
   comment at BackfillJobRunner:728-732 says so explicitly). fmWindows is
   non-empty ONLY in the runBackfill call that itself ran the refinement. Any
   later run (FM off, podcastId empty, FM unavailable, job deferred, or work
   already done) rebuilds regions with fmWindows == [] and re-upserts
   decoded_spans with no FM provenance. On device: 17 of 19 assets with
   decoded_spans have zero FM span geometry ever; the traced Conan asset
   D9B513CD has 8 decoded_spans, 0 semantic_scan_results, 0 evidence_events and
   NO backfill_job row at all. Zero backfill_jobs are 'complete' (15 deferred,
   2 queued, 1 failed, 1 running).

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: KILLED 2026-08-11 in the full-backlog triage. SUPERSEDED by its own completed investigation. Body says 'NOT diagnosed — this bead is to find out why'; the notes carry the finished verdict with line-level citations (consensus floor unreachable by three legs, RegionProposalBuilder.swift:566-587, plus the coarse lane never routed). playhead-idkp opens 'ESTABLISHED in playhead-881t' and carries the fix (A mark-tier anchor + B durability) including both corrections — 70.1 s coarse windows not ~1,000 s, and the SemanticSweepMarkComposer door. Nothing here is absent from idkp. I created this duplicate myself tonight.

title: DAI ad width: decide which channel gets to PROPOSE extent (4xqf established the loss is at anchoring)
description:
DECISION BEAD — needs Dan's call on WHICH option, not implementation as written.

playhead-4xqf (establish round, 2026-08-11) located the width loss and it is NOT where that bead's three
proposed fixes operate. Measured on the device DB (2026-08-10, schema 47) against byte-exact rediff slots:

  slot-seconds 875 → covered by decoded_spans (candidate generation) 135 = 15.5%
                   → covered by AdWindows                            108 = 12.4%

Downstream of candidate generation the pipeline NET WIDENS (114.6% retention excluding a user-corrected
slot). 84.5 of the 87.6 lost points are gone before fusion runs. Merge-gap tolerance is falsified by a
sweep: bridging existing windows at ANY gap up to 180s moves aggregate coverage 0.131 → 0.202 (N=135
Catalyst slots) while tripling overshoot.

ROOT: a decoded span is a maximal run of atoms with `isAnchored == true`
(AtomEvidenceProjector.swift:307-314), and anchoring is region-range membership. The pipeline can only
propose as much width as some channel ANCHORED. On Dan's device the anchoring channels are
evidenceCatalog (45, ONE ATOM per lexical hit — AtomEvidenceProjector.swift:243-247), sustainedMusicOffset
(49), classifierSeed (8), user-confirmed (7). fmConsensus: ZERO. fmAcousticCorroborated: ZERO.

THE OPTIONS (full costing incl. risks and falsifiers in the 4xqf note):
  (b) Make the coarse FM verdict a width proposer. Machinery exists (Path 1 anchors an fmConsensus region's
      whole ordinal range), fires zero times today. Highest ceiling, highest inner-edge risk — admissible
      only on the MARK tier per feedback_outer_edges_free_inner_precious + certainty_tiered_skip.
  (c) Pod-envelope extension from a confirmed seed. `AdPodContinuation` already ships ON and is already
      mark-only, i.e. already in the safe tier; natively per-edge. Lowest risk, lower ceiling.
  (d) RULED OUT here so nobody re-derives it: semanticSweepMark proposes the widest geometry in the store
      (2,876s, avg 137s) and 0.0 of its seconds land inside a byte-exact DAI slot.

PRECONDITION worth answering first, and it may change the whole ordering: WHY does FM never anchor on
device? Region qualification, FM never running, or the consensus-strength floor. Unknown as of the
establish round.

title: DECISION NEEDED (Dan): should the *OnShow correction-scope wire format change, or stay ambiguous-by-construction?
description:
Presented, not implemented — playhead-fzpj's scope constraint forbids changing the
persisted format without approval. fzpj landed the format-PRESERVING half; this is the
half that is Dan's call.

THE RESIDUAL. `CorrectionScope` serializes the five *OnShow cases as
`type:podcastId:value` where NEITHER field is shape-constrained. Given the string
alone, the split is genuinely undecidable — `sponsorOnShow:a:b:c` is consistent with
(a, 'b:c') and with ('a:b', c). No parse rule is correct for all inputs; the shipped
one (first colon) is wrong for every real podcastId because a podcastId is a feed URL.

fzpj closed the SHIPPED path without touching a byte: `CorrectionScope.roundTripIsExact`
says when the split is a guess, and `CorrectionEvent.authoritativeShowScopePayload(for:)`
reads the identity out of the event's own `podcastId` / `targetRefs.sponsorEntity` /
`targetRefs.domain` columns instead. The remaining hole is by construction:
`phraseOnShow`, `campaignOnShow` and `jingleOnShow` have NO column carrying their
value, so a colon-bearing podcastId is unresolvable for them and the resolver returns nil.
They have no production writer and no production reader today.

OPTIONS (fzpj's own list, refined by the topology work):

(a) PERCENT-ESCAPE OR LENGTH-PREFIX the podcastId in `serialized`.
    + Makes the parse a proof for all five cases, forever, with no per-case columns.
    - Changes the wire format. Migration burden is ZERO TODAY — measured: 0 *OnShow rows
      across five device pulls (db-corrected2/marked/vtjxverdict/night1/evening2);
      sponsor_knowledge_entries = 0 in all five. That window closes the moment one
      listener presses 'Always skip this sponsor', so if this is the answer it is
      cheapest NOW.
    - `normalizedIdentityKey` for *OnShow IS `serialized`, and it is persisted in
      `correction_events.normalizedScopeKey` under a UNIQUE INDEX. Changing the bytes
      changes that column's values, so a pre-existing row would need rewriting — free at
      0 rows, not free later.

(b) SPLIT FROM THE RIGHT for *OnShow (mirror the exactSpan pattern).
    + One-line change; correct for every feed-URL podcastId.
    - Still a HEURISTIC, not a proof: it merely moves the failure from 'the podcastId has
      a colon' (always) to 'the value has a colon' (sometimes). A sponsor name can carry
      one — `AdBannerView.normalizedAlwaysSkipSponsor` lowercases and trims but does not
      strip punctuation, and the parser's own comment cites 'Squarespace: Build It'.
    - It would REGRESS the one shape that parses correctly today:
      `recordVeto`'s colon-free asset-UUID podcastId with a colon-bearing sponsor.
    - Three shipped tests pin the opposite contract
      (testSponsorWithColonSerializationRoundTrip and siblings).
    This is why fzpj did NOT flip the direction.

(c) STOP ROUND-TRIPPING IDENTITY THROUGH THE SCOPE STRING AT ALL — make it a dedupe key
    only, and give every show-wide scope a real column for its value.
    + Structurally right; the same move fzpj already made for the two cases that HAVE
      columns. No parse can ever be wrong again because nothing parses.
    - Needs a `CorrectionTargetRefs` field per scope family (phrase / campaign / jingle)
      and a writer discipline that fills it. Bigger than a parse fix.

RECOMMENDATION IF ASKED: (a) now while the migration is free, or (c) if the *OnShow
family is going to grow readers. (b) is not recommended.

RELATED: playhead-fzpj (the landed half), playhead-ma23 (recordVeto scopes to an
episode), playhead-mfeq (make the standing defect class untypeable — this is an instance).

title: AtomEvidenceProjector has no anchor path for .sponsor / .fingerprint / .lexical origins — a sponsor-only region can never produce a span, so shape (a) alone cannot make the button move a skip

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
FOUND IN playhead-shjn, MEASURED ON 850c7cf5. This is the gap between shape (a) — which shjn landed — and Dan's stated intent ("the sponsor's ads should actually get SKIPPED in future episodes"). IT IS A DECISION, NOT A FIX: it changes what anchors a span, which is an architectural call.

WHAT SHAPE (a) BUILT. `AdDetectionService.runBackfill` now hands the live `SponsorKnowledgeStore` + the episode's `podcastId` to `RegionShadowPhase.Input`, so an `.active` sponsor entry becomes a `SponsorMatch` and then a `.sponsor`-origin `ProposedRegion` via `RegionProposalBuilder.makeSponsorProposals`. That much is real and rail-tested at the production call site.

WHERE IT STOPS. `AtomEvidenceProjector.project` is the ONLY consumer of the region bundles (`regionBundles` has exactly 2 reads in runBackfill: the DEBUG-only observer, and this). It classifies regions by origin in five places and reads exactly four origin bits:
  .foundationModel  (Path 1 consensus >= .medium, Path 3 Use C)
  .acoustic         (hasAcousticBreakHint + Use C proximity)
  .classifier       (Path 4 seed)
  .sustainedMusic   (Path 5 seed)
`.sponsor`, `.fingerprint` and `.lexical` are read by NOBODY (grep `origins.contains(` over Playhead/ = 6 hits, 5 in AtomEvidenceProjector + 1 in MusicOffsetLexicalGate for .sustainedMusic). `RegionFeatureExtractor` contains zero occurrences of the string "sponsor", so `region.sponsorMatches` feeds no feature either.

CONSEQUENCE, exactly:
 * A STANDALONE `.sponsor` region — the brand named where nothing else fired — anchors ZERO atoms. `MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder` emits no span for it. No banner, no mark, no skip. It is inert.
 * A `.sponsor` proposal that OVERLAPS another proposal merges (`merge` UNIONs the atom range), so the only reachable effect today is WIDENING a region some other origin already anchored, plus `.acoustic` insertion when the sponsor region's edge is within 1.0 s of a break (which sets `hasAcousticBreakHint` and can pull an edge via decoder Use A).
 * Atoms are ONE PER CHUNK (`TranscriptAtomizer.atomize`), so a sponsor match is a whole-chunk-wide object and the widening it can cause is chunk-granular. Per feedback_outer_edges_free_inner_precious that widening is NOT free in both directions: the union can extend a region BACKWARD into show content when the brand is named just before the break.

THE OPEN DECISION (Dan's):
 (i) Add a Path 6 to `AtomEvidenceProjector` that anchors on `.sponsor` the way Path 4/5 anchor on `.classifier`/`.sustainedMusic`. Smallest thing that makes the button reach a span. But it makes a LEXICAL brand match an anchor on its own, which is exactly what feedback_lexical_as_attention says never to do, and what AdDetectionService.sponsorRequiresConfirmingAdCue (playhead-xsdz.69, on the hot path) already decided AGAINST: a bare brand needs a co-occurring disclosure / URL / promo-code / FM-positive cue, or it is editorial talk.
 (ii) Anchor a `.sponsor` region only WITH a confirming cue — i.e. port xsdz.69's `hypothesisHasConfirmingAdCue` rule to the region lane. Keeps "attention, not verdict", and it is the shape most consistent with rulings already made.
 (iii) Route the sponsor region to a TARGETED FM look instead of anchoring it (cf. the r2vz recovery classifier already threaded into `RegionShadowPhase`), so FM disposes and the brand only says WHERE.
 (iv) shjn's shape (b): construct `CompiledSponsorLexicon` at the two `LexicalScanner(podcastProfile:)` sites (AdDetectionService.swift:2357/:13126) so the brand raises a LEXICAL candidate rather than a region origin. Costs an async store read on a currently-sync scanner construction path.

Whatever is chosen, whether the result may AUTO-SKIP or only MARK is a separate ruling: feedback_certainty_tiered_skip_2026-07-17 is auto-SKIP for high-certainty DAI, MARK for uncertain host-read, and a sponsor-name match is lexical.

Related: playhead-shjn (shape (a), landed), playhead-3q0k (the identical gap on the fingerprint sibling), playhead-absa (a sponsor-derived lexical anchor would inherit absa's URL/phrase/5s-floor defects), playhead-q6y3.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
ABSORBS playhead-3q0k, closed 2026-08-11.

3q0k reported that the store-backed ad-copy FINGERPRINT matcher has zero production callers. The backlog triage established it is unwired three layers deep, not one:
  - AdCopyFingerprintStore( has ZERO constructions in the app target (all ~10 are in PlayheadTests)
  - ad_copy_fingerprints is 0 rows on db-night1, db-evening2, db-vtjxverdict and db-live
  - .fingerprint has no anchor path at all — which is THIS bead

3q0k's own comment already conceded 'wiring fingerprintStore alone would buy region WIDENING and nothing else'. So the fingerprint lane cannot produce a span until a1r6 gives .fingerprint an anchor path, and wiring the store first would buy nothing.

Closed as COVERED BY THIS BEAD rather than as wrong — a writer method does exist (AdCopyFingerprintStore.swift:449/464), so this is 'no path to instances today', not 'impossible'. If a1r6 ever grants .fingerprint an anchor path, the store wiring is part of that work.

title: the store-backed ad-copy FINGERPRINT matcher has zero production callers — RegionShadowPhase.Input.fingerprintStore is never populated

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
FOUND IN playhead-shjn (shape (a) wiring), MEASURED ON 850c7cf5. This REFUTES a premise of shjn's own filing note.

shjn said of the sponsor matcher: "The fingerprint sibling IS wired, same function, ten lines below." It is not. The overload DISPATCH exists ten lines below (RegionShadowPhase.swift, `if let fpStore = input.fingerprintStore, let podcastId = input.podcastId`), but the ONE production construction of `RegionShadowPhase.Input` — AdDetectionService.swift:4388, `runBackfill` — passed NEITHER `fingerprintStore` NOR `podcastId`. Both default to `nil`, the `if let` never binds, and every production call took the legacy stub `AdCopyFingerprintMatcher.match(atoms:)` which returns `[]` unconditionally.

Numerator/denominator: production constructions of `RegionShadowPhase.Input` = 1 (grep `RegionShadowPhase.Input(` over Playhead/); of those, ones passing `fingerprintStore` = 0. Production callers of `AdCopyFingerprintMatcher.match(atoms:podcastId:fingerprintStore:)` = 0 of 1 reference (the reference is the unreachable branch itself).

shjn LANDED `podcastId: podcastId` at that call site (it is the lookup key the sponsor store needs). That is HALF of what this branch requires and it deliberately stops there: `fingerprintStore` is still nil, so the fingerprint branch is unchanged and still dead. Wiring it is a detection-source decision, which is Dan's call, not a review fix — the same reason shjn was filed rather than fixed inside q6y3.

Before wiring it, note the finding from shjn's downstream trace that applies here identically: `AtomEvidenceProjector` has NO anchor path for `.fingerprint` (nor `.sponsor`, nor `.lexical`) — see playhead-4hz2. A `.fingerprint`-origin region that does not merge with an FM / classifier / sustainedMusic region anchors zero atoms and therefore produces no span. So wiring `fingerprintStore` alone would buy region WIDENING and nothing else, exactly as shape (a) does for sponsor.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: CORRECTION to the comment above: the anchor-path bead is playhead-a1r6, not playhead-4hz2 (id written before the bead was created).

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: KILLED 2026-08-11 in the full-backlog triage. EMPTY POPULATION, three layers deep — see the carry-over comment on playhead-a1r6, which now owns it. Closed as COVERED, not as wrong.

title: Background URLSession CREATION still blocks the cooperative pool — nsjn covered only task creation
description:
playhead-nsjn established, from a `sample` of a wedged test host, that
`URLSession.downloadTask(with:)` on a BACKGROUND session blocks the calling
thread in a synchronous XPC round-trip to `nsurlsessiond`, and that because
`DownloadManager` is an actor those blocks land on the fixed-width Swift
Concurrency cooperative pool — 10 of 10 threads in the sampled run. nsjn
moved the two MEASURED call sites off-pool under a bound
(`BackgroundSessionIO`).

It deliberately did NOT move the rest of the surface, because the sample
only implicated task creation and "scope is the ceiling". The rest is:

  * `DownloadManager.backgroundSession(for:)` — `URLSession(configuration:
    .background(withIdentifier:), delegate:, delegateQueue:)`. Session
    construction is what ESTABLISHES the nsurlsessiond XPC connection.
    It runs inline on the actor and is the FIRST thing
    `resumeSuspendedTransfer` and `backgroundDownload` do, i.e. BEFORE
    nsjn's off-pool hop can help. If creation blocks, nsjn's bound is
    bypassed entirely and the original deadlock returns.
  * `invalidateBackgroundSessionsForTesting()` → `session.invalidateAndCancel()`
  * `retireBackgroundTransfers` → `session.allTasks` (async, so probably
    fine) and `task.cancel(byProducingResumeData:)`
  * any `URLSessionTask` mutation on a background session

The check for each is the same question: does this call cross into
`__NSURLBackgroundSession`'s serial work queue, and can it be reached from
a cooperative thread? If yes it belongs behind `BackgroundSessionIO`.

`backgroundSession(for:)` is the awkward one — it is a synchronous
`internal` method with ~6 call sites including `backgroundSessionsAlreadyInstantiated()`,
so moving it off-pool means making it (or an async twin) suspend, and
deciding what a caller that cannot suspend should get.

WHY P1 RATHER THAN P2: if session creation blocks, nsjn's fix is a partial
one and the gate can wedge again by the same mechanism one layer up.
Nobody has measured whether it does. A `sample` taken while the daemon is
stalled, or a targeted experiment, would settle it in one sitting — and
that measurement should come BEFORE any refactor.

title: a repeated sponsor URL only ever anchors its FIRST mention — every later ad break carrying the same domain is silent
description:
Found while measuring playhead-absa; OUT OF ITS SCOPE, filed not fixed.

`EvidenceCatalogBuilder.deduplicate` collapses raw matches by
(category, normalizedText) and keeps the FIRST occurrence. The surviving
`EvidenceEntry` carries that first occurrence's `atomOrdinal`, and
`AtomEvidenceProjector` anchors atoms via `entry.atomOrdinal` alone
(`evidenceByOrdinal`). `count`/`firstTime`/`lastTime` accumulate, so the
repeat is *counted* but its ATOM is never anchored.

Consequence: a show that reads the same sponsor twice — a pre-roll and a
post-roll of the same advertiser, or the "that's X dot com slash Y"
repeat inside one read — gets ONE anchorable atom for the whole episode,
and every later break carrying that domain decodes nothing.

MEASURED (2026-08-10, 94,692 transcript_chunks over 31 assets, fast +
final, from the 2026-08-02 device pull; catalog -> projector -> decoder
with regions=[] and no correction mask, on top of the absa lexicon):

  decoded spans, first-occurrence dedup as shipped   22
  decoded spans, if every occurrence anchored        33   (+11, +50%)

All 11 are LATER mentions of a domain whose first mention already
anchored, i.e. a second ad break:

  0C2FC22E fast/final  2077.80-2084.28   netsuite.ai (2nd read)
  48E903D7 fast/final  2104.92-2111.40   netsuite.ai (2nd read)
  CDD611C4 fast/final  6099.72-6105.18   post-roll
  F4CE7F47 fast/final  1308.54-1315.62   netsuite.ai (2nd read)
  FF4EFA66 fast        50.94-56.22, 1657.08-1664.88; final 50.94-56.22

On DE0784D8 the canonical annotation has a post-roll ad at
5462.57-5522.65 and the transcript contains "netsuite.ai" at 5514.5 —
deduped away against the 51.9 pre-roll mention, so the post-roll is
lexically silent.

NOT a straight "keep every occurrence" change. The reason to be careful,
and what has to be measured before this lands:
  - a repeat can be SHOW content ("like I said, betterhelp.com") — that
    is a precision cost and it was not measured here;
  - `EvidenceCatalog.renderForPrompt` and every FM `evidenceRef` consumer
    assume one entry per (category, text), so multiplying entries changes
    prompt size and ref stability. The likely shape is: keep one catalog
    ENTRY, but carry all occurrence ordinals on it and let the projector
    anchor every one.

Acceptance: the corpus eval above re-run before/after with per-repeat
precision adjudicated (is the repeat inside an ad?), and prompt/ref
stability preserved.

title: the manual veto has no boundaryState filter: one tap can revert the listener's OWN mark, 569 of 1,871 claiming transcript rows exposed
description:
FILED FROM playhead-d666 R5 review. In scope for d666 only where the SILENCED hint was concerned (fixed there, commit c4c59cec); this is the general case and is deliberately NOT fixed in that bead because the correct fix is a policy decision, not a filter.

## The mechanism

`SkipOrchestrator.revertByTimeRange` (SkipOrchestrator.swift:4748) folds in every persisted `ad_window` overlapping [start,end] whose `decisionState` is in {candidate, confirmed, applied}. There is NO `boundaryState` filter, so a window with `boundaryState == "userMarked"` — a region the LISTENER marked as an ad, the highest-fidelity signal the app has — is reverted alongside the app's own detections. `AnalysisStore.persistRevertedAdWindowsIfCurrent` (:12314) writes them, and `AnalysisStore.userVetoedTimeRanges` (:19511) then suppresses every decoded span merely OVERLAPPING that range.

The tap that triggers it: `AdRegionPopover`'s "This isn't an ad", which reverts over the WHOLE range of the span the popover was opened for — not the row that was tapped, and not any range the listener chose or was asked to confirm. The confirmation copy is "This will stop flagging this segment as an ad", which says nothing about retracting a mark.

## Measured (db-corrected2: 94,099 transcript_chunks, 66 decoded spans, 115 ad windows, 5 assets with a live userMarked window)

**569 of 1,871** transcript rows that carry a claiming span have a popover span whose range overlaps a live `userMarked` window in candidate/confirmed/applied. On `0C2FC22E` a single span (2017.4-2085.7) reaches THREE marks at once (E1C1FC4D applied, 504BD599 confirmed, D7487EF7 confirmed).

## Why d666 did not fix it

Two reasons, both real:

1. In the CLAIMING case the popover header discloses the range it is about (`AdRegionPopover.timeRangeLabel`), and the app IS drawing an ad there. Withholding the explanation of an ad the app is actively flagging is a worse trade than the disclosed-range veto. d666 fixed only the case where the app makes NO claim — the row is unpainted and the veto is pure loss.
2. A blanket `boundaryState != "userMarked"` filter in `revertByTimeRange` would BREAK the legitimate un-mark path. `TranscriptPeekView.submitNotAdChunks` builds a synthetic span over a user-DRAWN range and calls the same function precisely so the listener can retract their own mark. The two callers need different policies and currently share one.

## Candidate shapes (Dan's call)

- Split the seam: a `retractsUserMarks: Bool` (or a caller-supplied predicate) so the popover veto and the "Not ad" selection get different target sets. Minimal, honest, keeps both flows.
- Or: keep folding them in but DISCLOSE it — the confirmation alert names how many of the listener's own marks it will retract, and offers to keep them.
- Or: clip the popover veto's range to the tapped row's envelope rather than the whole span. Changes what a veto MEANS (an edge correction, not a rejection) and interacts with playhead-9iyb's per-row verdict work.

Related: playhead-9iyb (the enumerated per-row verdict). Evidence: scratchpad db-corrected2.

title: The transcript's LEGACY Phase-2 ad styling reads every ad_window — provenance-blind and decision-blind (found in d666 R3)
description:
FOUND IN playhead-d666 R3 REVIEW. d666 silenced the DECODED-SPAN lane of the transcript's ad rendering (copper bar, background tint, AD badge, and R2's spoken label). It did not touch the LEGACY Phase-2 lane, which is a second, older way of asserting "this row is an ad" about the same row, and which reads raw `ad_windows` with no provenance and no decision filter at all.

THE LANE. `TranscriptPeekViewModel.isAdSegment(startTime:endTime:)` and `.adConfidence(startTime:endTime:)` both do `adWindows.filter { overlap }` over the snapshot's `adWindows`, and `AnalysisStore.fetchAdWindows` is `SELECT * FROM ad_windows WHERE analysisAssetId = ? ORDER BY startTime` — every row, every `boundaryState`, every `decisionState`. Three display consumers read them, all in `TranscriptPeekView.chunkRow`:
  • `Text(chunk.text)` -> `chunkTextColor(isAd:)` (tertiary grey), `.opacity(isAd ? 0.45 : 1.0)`, `.italic(isAd)`
  • `timestampLabel(chunk:adScore:)` -> the timestamp renders RED and reads "34:04 AD 82%"
  • `TranscriptPeekViewModel.accessibilityLabel(chunkIndex:)` passes it as `isAd:`, so VoiceOver says "Ad segment at 34:04: <text>"

TWO POPULATIONS, BOTH MEASURED ON db-corrected2 (66 decoded_spans, 115 ad_windows, 6 assets):

(A) THE d666 RESIDUE — 302 of 379 rows (79.7%), 12 assets. Rows that overlap at least one music-only decoded span, NO claiming span and NO live user mark — i.e. exactly the rows d666 silences — of which 302 still overlap an `ad_window`, so they keep the red "AD nn%" timestamp, the grey italic 45%-opacity text and the spoken "Ad segment at ...". The clip outro Dan vetoed is NOT one of them (asset 48E903D7 has no window there — that was FINDING A of d666), but 20 of the 26 silenced spans elsewhere in the corpus are.

(B) THE VETOED-WINDOW LEAK, same root cause, LARGER — 842 transcript rows are covered ONLY by an `ad_window` whose `decisionState = 'reverted'`, i.e. material the listener explicitly vetoed. `isAdSegment` has no `decisionState` filter, so every one of those rows is still drawn ad-styled and still spoken as "Ad segment at ...". This is playhead-u45d's defect one lane over: u45d fixed the `userMarkedChunkIndices` read (`boundaryState == "userMarked" && decisionState != reverted`) and the legacy pair was never revisited.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN d666 — the obvious remedy is measurably wrong. "A row with decoded spans but no CLAIMING span asserts nothing in any lane" over-suppresses: 60 of the 302 rows in (A) also overlap a `dayZeroRediffByteExact` window, a byte-exact re-download diff and the strongest DAI evidence the app has. `ad_windows.evidenceSources` is NULL on all 115 rows, so there is no provenance key on a window to say which detection produced it, and the decoded-span layer is NOT a complete evidence picture (rediff writes windows without a corresponding overlapping span). Deciding what the legacy lane may still assert is a display/detection policy call, not a mechanical gate — hence this bead rather than a fourth commit on d666.

SUGGESTED SHAPE (for discussion, not a decision):
  1. `decisionState = 'reverted'` should be filtered unconditionally. (B) needs no policy argument: the listener said no. This alone is 842 rows.
  2. For (A), consider giving the legacy lane the same claiming-set gate the other three consumers now have, but exempting windows whose `boundaryState` is a hard-boundary family (`dayZeroRediffByteExact`, `dayZeroRediffChroma`). Needs Dan's call on whether the Phase-2 italic/red styling should survive at all now that the decoded-span lane carries the highlight.

REPRO (no build): copy the evidence DB, then the row counts above are reproducible with json_extract over `decoded_spans.anchorProvenanceJSON` — `type = 'sustainedMusicOffset'` present and none of fmConsensus/fmAcousticCorroborated/evidenceCatalog/classifierSeed/userCorrection = music-only, matching `[AnchorRef].carriesOnlyMusicPresenceHint`.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
MERGED FROM playhead-dbno (filed by d666 R2, now closed as a duplicate of this bead). Same lane, same two functions; keeping this one because its measurement is broader. Carrying over what dbno held that this bead did not:

LINEAGE — this is playhead-u45d's defect surviving on the lane u45d did not audit. u45d established that the transcript veto's only durable mutation is UPDATE ad_windows SET decisionState='reverted', and closed the two consumers reading past it: userMarkedChunkIndices now filters decisionState != reverted, and AnalysisStore.fetchDecodedSpans suppresses spans covered by a manualVeto CorrectionEvent. Both of those govern the PHASE 5 treatment — copper bar, tint, AD badge. The LEGACY PHASE 2 treatment was never closed, so a veto visibly does not take.

dbno's independent count, from the same pull: 15 reverted windows, 1052 transcript chunks still rendering dimmed/italic with a red 'AD nn%'. R3's count on this bead is 842 rows covered ONLY by a reverted window. The two differ because dbno counted every chunk overlapping a reverted window while R3 excluded rows that also overlap a live one — both are correct for what they name, and the 842 is the tighter number for 'a veto that visibly did not take'.

WHY THIS NOW DISAGREES WITH ITSELF: post-d666 the copper bar and badge go while the legacy dim/italic/red 'AD nn%' stays, so a single row asserts and denies the same thing. That is worse than either lane alone and it is the argument for treating this as more than cosmetic.

title: The transcript's LEGACY ad treatment reads every ad_window, including the 15 the listener vetoed — 1052 chunks still render dimmed/italic with a red "AD nn%"
description:
FOUND IN playhead-d666 R2 REVIEW. Out of that bead's scope (d666 is about music-only DECODED SPANS); filed, not fixed.

THE SHAPE, and why it is the same one d666 and u45d are about: a display-side consumer reading a fuller population than it is entitled to claim over.

playhead-u45d established that the transcript veto's only durable mutation is `UPDATE ad_windows SET decisionState='reverted'`, and closed the two consumers that were reading past it — `userMarkedChunkIndices` now filters `decisionState != reverted`, and `AnalysisStore.fetchDecodedSpans` now suppresses spans covered by a `manualVeto` CorrectionEvent. Both of those govern the PHASE 5 treatment: the copper bar, the tint, the AD badge.

THE LEGACY PHASE 2 TREATMENT WAS NOT CLOSED. `TranscriptPeekViewModel.isAdSegment(startTime:endTime:)` and `.adConfidence(startTime:endTime:)` filter `adWindows` on nothing at all:

    adWindows.contains { ad in ad.startTime < endTime && ad.endTime > startTime }

and `LiveTranscriptPeekDataSource` populates that array from `AnalysisStore.fetchAdWindows`, whose SQL is `SELECT * FROM ad_windows WHERE analysisAssetId = ? ORDER BY startTime` — no decisionState predicate. So every window is in there: `candidate`, `applied`, and `reverted` alike.

WHAT THE LISTENER SEES AFTER VETOING (TranscriptPeekView.chunkRow, the `isAd` / `adScore` locals):
  - text colour drops to `AppColors.textTertiary`
  - `.opacity(0.45)` and `.italic(true)` — the row stays visually recessed as ad material
  - the timestamp turns RED and gains a literal claim: `timestampLabel` appends `String(format: " AD %.0f%%", score * 100)`
  - VoiceOver: `TranscriptRowAccessibility.label`'s `isAd` branch speaks "Ad segment at 34:04: <text>"

None of these is behind a DEBUG flag.

MEASURED ON db-corrected2 (the corpus behind d666, 6 assets / 30 corrections):
  - ad_windows total 115; decisionState='reverted' = 15
    (4 acousticRefined, 3 segmentAggregated, 3 semanticSweepMark, 3 userConfirmedSuggested, 1 dayZeroRediffByteExact, 1 userMarked)
  - transcript_chunks overlapping a reverted window: 1052, spanning all 15 windows
    WITH rev AS (SELECT * FROM ad_windows WHERE decisionState='reverted')
    SELECT count(DISTINCT t.id) FROM transcript_chunks t JOIN rev r
      ON r.analysisAssetId=t.analysisAssetId
     AND r.startTime < t.endTime AND r.endTime > t.startTime;   -- 1052

So 1052 rows keep the legacy ad treatment after the listener said 'not an ad'. This is exactly u45d's reported symptom — 'you mark it ... and the ad remains highlighted but not dismissed' — surviving on the lane u45d did not audit. Post-u45d the copper bar DOES go, so the row now disagrees with itself: unpainted by the Phase 5 treatment, still dimmed/italic/'AD 61%' by the Phase 2 one.

A SECOND POPULATION QUESTION, same two functions, decide it at the same time: `candidate` windows also light this treatment (38 of the 115 here — 19 semanticSweepMark, 12 dayZeroRediffByteExact, 7 podContinuation). A candidate is by definition not yet a verdict, so 'AD 61%' over it is the same category error one tier up. That is a product call, not obviously a bug — but the two share one predicate and should be settled together.

DO NOT FIX THIS BY FILTERING IN THE VIEW. u45d's own note applies verbatim: the durable record is what must be read. `fetchDecodedSpans` resolves the veto in the STORE so every reader sees it; the ad_window read should be made honest the same way (or `isAdSegment` should consult `decisionState` explicitly and say so), not by having one surface quietly hide what the rest of the app still believes.

WHAT WOULD PIN IT: `TranscriptPeekViewModel` is directly testable through `TranscriptPeekDataSource` (see PlayheadTests/Views/NowPlaying/TranscriptMusicOnlySpanHighlightTests.swift for the fixture shape) — a snapshot carrying one reverted window and one chunk under it, asserting `isAdSegment` is false and `accessibilityLabel(chunkIndex:)` speaks no 'Ad segment'.

title: Silencing music-only spans withholds the copper bar from 20 of 27 spans that DO carry a confirmed ad_window — the transcript's two ad treatments now disagree
description:
MEASURED in playhead-d666 R1 review, on db-corrected2 (6 assets, 66 decoded_spans).
FILED not fixed: the remedy changes the POLICY SHAPE d666 chose, and which
direction Dan wants is a product call, not a defect verdict. See "WHY THIS IS NOT
OBVIOUSLY A REGRESSION" below — it may be an improvement.

WHAT d666 DOES. `TranscriptPeekViewModel.isAdHighlighted` no longer paints a row
(copper bar, AD badge, background tint) whose only decoded spans are music-only —
`anchorProvenance` carrying `.sustainedMusicOffset` and no corroborating presence
anchor. Correct for the bead's ground truth: Dan's vetoed clip outro (asset
48E903D7, span 91f16f7d…, [2044.5, 2056.98]) has NO `ad_windows` row over it, so
the copper bar was the ONLY claim anyone made and withholding it is exactly right.

THE POPULATION, counted:

  decoded_spans rows, all assets                                 66   (denominator)
  ... music-only by provenance                                   27   (41%)
  ... of those 27, with ZERO overlapping claiming decoded span
      AND >=1 overlapping ad_window, decisionState 'confirmed',
      boundaryState <> 'userMarked'                              20   (74%)
  ... with only userMarked windows over them (rows stay lit
      via userMarkedChunkIndices — no loss)                       5
  ... with no overlapping window at all (correctly silenced)      2

The 20 windows are the SAME AUDIO as the spans, not neighbours — they are those
spans' own decision output, `acousticRefined` boundaries within ~3 s:

  span 16b44986 [111.1,144.2]    window [111.1,144.2]   confirmed c=0.83
  span 5794ec7e [591.4,606.3]    window [588.4,605.9]   confirmed c=0.75
  span ecb9d572 [1433.8,1444.3]  window [1434.1,1447.3] confirmed c=0.69
  span 9b99b66a [47.6,56.6]      window [44.6,57.9]     confirmed c=0.39
  (…20 in total, confidence 0.39–0.83)

THE INCOHERENCE. A row under one of those 20 is still marked as an ad by the OTHER
display path, which d666 does not touch: `isAdSegment` / `adConfidence` read
`ad_windows` directly, so the text renders dimmed to 0.45 and italic and the
timestamp goes RED reading "AD 83%". After d666 that row says "AD 83%" in red and
carries no AD badge and no copper bar. Same row, same audio, two treatments, now
disagreeing.

Corollary worth stating plainly: d666 fixes the copper-bar path ONLY. Had Dan's
clip outro carried a window, his complaint would NOT have been fixed by it — the
row would still be dim, italic and red-"AD 61%".

WHY THIS IS NOT OBVIOUSLY A REGRESSION. Those 20 windows are themselves derived
from the music-only spans, four of them at confidence 0.39–0.48. A reasonable
reading is that painting the transcript on a 0.39 music-derived window is the
LARGER defect and d666 half-fixed it. The opposite reading is that a window means
the decision path made a durable claim — very likely a banner the listener saw —
and the transcript declining to paint it is the same surface disagreement d666
exists to remove, pointing the other way.

THE THREE OPTIONS (Dan's call):
  A. Leave as-is. The bar tracks provenance; the legacy dim/red-AD% tracks windows.
  B. Silence a music-only span only where NO live (non-reverted) ad_window overlaps
     the row. One extra clause in `rebuildSpansByChunkIndex`; keeps the bead's fix
     exactly (its span has no window) and restores all 20.
  C. Silence the LEGACY treatment too for music-only-derived windows, so the row
     goes fully quiet. Largest change; needs window→span provenance, which is the
     join playhead-who3 is about.

RELATED: playhead-who3 (the transcript reads decoded_spans while every measurement
reads ad_windows — same population mismatch, other direction).
notes:
ARITHMETIC RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY, playhead-d666 R2 review, on a fresh copy of db-corrected2.

THE HEADLINE HOLDS: 66 decoded_spans total; 27 music-only by provenance; 20 of those 27 have no claiming decoded span over them AND >=1 overlapping ad_window with decisionState='confirmed' and boundaryState<>'userMarked'. Same predicates, same slop, arrived at from the raw JSON rather than from this bead's text. The decision Dan is being asked to make rests on the right numbers.

ONE STATED NUMBER IS WRONG — the confidence range. "(…20 in total, confidence 0.39–0.83)" spans only 14 of the 20. The measured range over the matched windows is:

  min 0.35620184737977567   max 0.98550984844535805

All 20, sorted: 0.3562, 0.3612, 0.3626, 0.3640, 0.3828, 0.3872, 0.3875, 0.3906, 0.4819, 0.4882, 0.5586, 0.5692, 0.6128, 0.6560, 0.6894, 0.6974, 0.7457, 0.8220, 0.8313, 0.9855.

It matters in BOTH directions for the option Dan picks:
 - the low tail is heavier than stated. SEVEN of the 20 sit below 0.39 and EIGHT below 0.40 — not "four at 0.39–0.48". If the reading is "painting the transcript on a 0.39 music-derived window is the larger defect", that reading now covers 8 windows, not 4.
 - there is a 0.9855 in the set, which the quoted ceiling of 0.83 hides entirely. If the reading is "a window means the decision path made a durable claim the listener probably saw", the strongest instance of it is nearly 1.0.

SENSITIVITY, so nobody re-measures this to find out: the pair set does not move. Slop 0 s, +/-3 s and +/-5 s all yield the identical 20 spans / 20 windows / 20 pairs with identical endpoints — every match is a genuine interval overlap and the slop buys nothing on this corpus. Counting spliceSlot/rediffSlot/rediffSlotChroma as corroboration also changes nothing (27/26/20 either way) — those anchor types occur ZERO times in this DB, so that particular error is unfalsifiable here rather than avoided. Only three anchor types exist at all: sustainedMusicOffset (48 spans), evidenceCatalog (32), classifierSeed (8). Dropping evidenceCatalog from the corroboration set moves 27 -> 44, i.e. evidenceCatalog is doing ALL the corroboration work in this snapshot and is the only load-bearing term in the music-only definition.

ONE PHRASING FIX: "20 of 27 ... have no claiming span but DO have a window" reads as if all 27 were unclaimed. One music-only span (5c3c9a13…, asset F4CE7F47, [1248.12, 1316.34]) IS claimed by an overlapping non-music-only span; the unclaimed denominator is 26. The 20 is unaffected — that span has no matching window either.

ONE PROPERTY NOT IN THE BEAD, and it bears on option A vs B: all 20 matched windows share detectorVersion='detection-v1', boundaryState='acousticRefined', metadataConfidence=0.1, eligibilityGate='markOnly' and wasSkipped=0. Every one of these confirmed windows over an uncorroborated music-only span was MARK-ONLY and none was ever auto-skipped. So the "very likely a banner the listener saw" premise is the right frame for all 20 — none of them ever took audio away from anyone.

SEE ALSO playhead-dbno, filed in the same review: the legacy `isAdSegment`/`adConfidence` path this bead names also reads REVERTED windows, so 1052 chunks across 15 vetoed windows keep the dim/italic/red-"AD nn%" treatment after the listener said "not an ad". That is independent of the music-only question and should not be conflated with option C.

title: A transcript ad marking backed only by decoded_spans is invisible to every precision/recall number (FINDING A of d666)
description:
FINDING A of playhead-d666, established. The mechanism is now known and it is a
POPULATION MISMATCH, not a deleted row.

WHAT DAN SAW AND VETOED. `TranscriptPeekViewModel.rebuildSpansByChunkIndex` lights
a transcript row (copper bar + "AD" badge) when it time-overlaps any row of
`decoded_spans`. It does not consult `ad_windows`, the span's eligibility gate, or
whether any decision was ever recorded. On asset 48E903D7 the marking Dan vetoed at
2044.500-2048.820 was decoded span `91f16f7d5219c6c593b844bae12f636d`.

WHAT EVERY MEASUREMENT READS. Precision/recall in this program is computed over
`ad_windows` (+ `decision_events`). Measured on db-corrected2 for that asset:

  ad_windows overlapping 2040-2050              0
  semantic_scan_results overlapping 2040-2050   0
  decoded_spans overlapping 2040-2050           1     <- what the user saw
  decision_events on the asset                  1, and its windowId
                                                (`fusion-b5defaa96902f640`,
                                                markOnly / detectOnly, conf 0.609)
                                                has NO row in ad_windows

So a marking the listener can see and act on contributes ZERO to any precision
number, and the one decision the pipeline did record points at a window that does
not exist. Both directions of the ledger are blind here.

The bead's alternative hypothesis — "the veto deleted the row" — is REFUTED. The
veto is durable: correction_events 719E3719-F125-4B26-9016-BBDE195CA526, scope
`exactTimeSpan:48E903D7...:2044.500:2048.820`, source manualVeto. Its
`targetRefsJSON` is EMPTY because `SkipOrchestrator.revertByTimeRange` found no
overlapping window and took the playhead-u45d window-less branch, which writes
`windowId: nil` / `detectionProjection: nil`. Compare the 596.28-676.56 veto on the
same asset, which DID have a window and carries a full
`explicitFeedbackDetectionProjection`. The empty field is the SYMPTOM of the
population mismatch, and it is also the cheapest available detector for it.

WHAT TO DECIDE (not decided here):
  * Should a decoded span the transcript displays get a persisted marking record,
    so the surface and the ledger read the same population? or
  * Should the measurement lane read decoded_spans as a first-class marking
    population alongside ad_windows?

Either way the invariant worth asserting is: NO USER-VISIBLE AD MARKING WITHOUT A
QUERYABLE RECORD OF IT. Today the transcript has one and the ledger cannot see it.

Relates to playhead-4obf (instrumentation) — this is a population the instrumentation
must be told about, or it will measure a strict subset of what shipped.
Discovered-from playhead-d666, which fixed the specific mis-marking (a bare
sustained-music hint no longer paints a row as an ad) but did NOT close this hole:
every other decoded-span-only marking is still invisible to measurement.

title: decoded_spans atom ordinals are canonical-mixed-pass positions, not transcript_chunks.atomOrdinal — off by the retained-fast count (839 on 48E903D7)
description:
MEASURED on db-corrected2, asset 48E903D7 (playhead-d666 investigation).

The single `decoded_spans` row on that asset — `91f16f7d5219c6c593b844bae12f636d`,
[2044.5, 2056.98] — carries `firstAtomOrdinal=2061, lastAtomOrdinal=2068`. The
asset's `transcript_chunks.atomOrdinal` values run 0..1246 (1247 final-pass rows;
fast rows carry NULL). So the span's ordinals resolve to NO atom in the table.

They are not corrupt. They are positions in a DIFFERENT numbering system, and the
arithmetic closes exactly:

  final rows before 2044.5                          = 1222   (the atom's atomOrdinal)
  fast rows before 2044.5 NOT fully covered by a
  final row (the canonicalizer's own drop rule)     =  839
  1222 + 839                                        = 2061   = firstAtomOrdinal

i.e. `decoded_spans` ordinals are ARRAY POSITIONS IN THE CANONICAL MIXED-PASS
ARRAY (final rows + retained fast rows; 2124 entries on this asset), while
`transcript_chunks.atomOrdinal` is the FINAL-PASS-ONLY index (1247 entries). Two
quantities sharing a name and a column type, one read as though it were the other
— the standing defect class on this project.

TWO CONSEQUENCES, one certain and one to be measured:

1. CERTAIN — canonical-array positions are NOT STABLE ACROSS TRANSCRIPT GROWTH.
   Every final-pass row that lands and fully covers a retained fast row REMOVES an
   entry, shifting every later canonical ordinal down by one. `DecodedSpan.id` is
   `SHA256("assetId:firstAtomOrdinal:lastAtomOrdinal")` and is documented "stable
   across re-runs — same inputs, same id". The inputs are not the same across a
   growing transcript, so a span keeps its audio and changes its identity. On this
   asset the final pass covers [720, 2070] while fast covers [0, 2112.9] — a
   partially-finalized episode is the NORMAL state, not an edge case.

2. TO BE MEASURED — who actually joins the two spaces. `CorpusExporter` writes
   BOTH `span.firstAtomOrdinal` and chunk `atomOrdinal` into the same corpus, so
   any offline join over them is wrong by the retained-fast count. The live
   correction-mask path is NOT affected: `StoreBackedCorrectionMaskProvider` builds
   `atomsByOrdinal` from the SAME atoms array the projector uses, and Dan's veto was
   an `.exactTimeSpan` scope resolved by TIME. `recordVeto(span:)` writes
   `.exactSpan` ORDINAL scopes from a DecodedSpan and is the one live path that
   could inherit the drift.

NOT FIXED IN d666 — out of its ceiling. Fixing it means deciding WHICH space is
canonical and migrating the persisted rows, which is a bigger call than a display
predicate.

Discovered while establishing FINDING B of playhead-d666: the bead reported
duplicated chunks under the mis-marked span and asked whether they were causal for
the marking. They were not (the anchor is acoustic — see d666). They ARE causal for
this: the retained fast rows are exactly the 839.
notes: CORRECTION (verified after filing): CorpusExporter emits span.firstAtomOrdinal / lastAtomOrdinal on its decision records but does NOT emit transcript_chunks.atomOrdinal anywhere — grep for 'atomOrdinal' in CorpusExporter.swift returns only the two span fields. So the corpus does not itself contain the bad join; the hazard is any consumer that pairs an exported span ordinal with a chunk ordinal read from the DB. BackfillJobRunner:5697 is NOT affected either — its 'span' there is a RefinedAdSpan from FM window output, a different population in FM ordinal space, not a DecodedSpan. Consequence 1 (identity instability across transcript growth) stands unchanged and is the part that needs no further measurement.

title: Day-0 kickoff readiness bound (6.5 min) may be far shorter than asset-registration latency — settle whether cnql's own fix closes the gap
description:
FOUND in the playhead-cnql R2 review as O3. This decides how much cnql actually BUYS, so it should be settled before or shortly after cnql merges.

R2's OBSERVATION (control pull db-vtjxverdict): all 5 kickoffs recorded 2026-08-09 settled 'no_analysis_asset' after the full 40 polls (~396 s), and the matching analysis_assets row appeared 3.7 h to 17.4 h LATER. Every kickoff from 08-01 to 08-06 fired, most within 2-15 polls. R2 concluded that cnql converts 'no kickoff row' into 'a row that says no_analysis_asset', i.e. buys nothing on today's build.

WHY I THINK THAT INFERENCE IS INVERTED, and what to check. Inside DownloadManager.handleBackgroundDownloadComplete (Playhead/Services/Downloads/DownloadManager.swift:3629) the order is:

  :3888   await enqueueAnalysisIfNeeded(...)   -> analysisWorkScheduler.enqueue(...)  [asset registration]
  :3986   notifyBackgroundDownloadCompleted(...) -> observer -> kickoff               [day-0]

The enqueue is AWAITED and comes FIRST. Per cnql R1, on the pre-fix build a headless relaunch never ran handleBackgroundDownloadComplete at all — no registered DownloadManager, so no lazily-created URLSession, so no delegate callback. Therefore NEITHER call ran, and the asset row was not created at download completion; it waited until the user next opened the app. That is a complete and sufficient explanation for the observed 3.7-17.4 h latency: those are exactly the completions whose whole handler never ran. If so, cnql fixes the latency and the readiness bound in the SAME relaunch, and the kickoff should find its asset almost immediately.

WHAT TO ESTABLISH (do not assume either way):
1. Does analysisWorkScheduler.enqueue synchronously WRITE the analysis_assets row, or only queue work that writes it later? The awaited call proves ordering, not durability. This is the load-bearing question.
2. The scheduler is registered at PlayheadRuntime.swift:2290 inside init's DEFERRED Task. If the completion arrives before that Task runs, 'guard let scheduler = analysisWorkScheduler else { return }' (:2235) drops the enqueue SILENTLY - the same shape as the sceneless class, one layer in. R2 judged the resumeSession round-trip makes it a non-issue in practice; that is a timing argument, not a guarantee, and it deserves a real answer.
3. Cross-check the 08-09 kickoffs against their lastSource. If the 5 that read no_analysis_asset were background_download and the ones that fired promptly were tap, that CONFIRMS the inverted reading, because tap downloads complete in a process that already registered everything.
4. Only if 1-3 say the gap is real: consider whether the 6.5-minute bound should move. Raising a readiness bound to cover a latency whose cause is a dropped enqueue would be treating the symptom.

COUNTER-EVIDENCE ALREADY IN HAND, and it is why this is a task not a bug: on the post-wipe device (pull db-db-r2wait, build 9e31bf1c) asset 66D32039 was TAPPED, its kickoff fired 12 s after creation and settled 'marked' with 4 marks. So the machinery works end to end when the asset exists. The whole question is whether a background completion now registers its asset in time, and that is exactly what cnql changes.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
ANSWERED by the playhead-cnql R3 review, read-only, no production change. My inverted-inference hypothesis (that cnql's own fix closes this gap) is REFUTED. R2's pessimism was closer to right, though not for the reason it gave.

(a) THE LOAD-BEARING QUESTION — NO. AnalysisWorkScheduler.enqueue does NOT write the analysis_assets row. It durably writes only store.insertJob(job) (:1216) with analysisAssetId: nil (:1190). Its own comments name the mechanism twice: ':1306 the asset row may not exist yet (it is created lazily by resolveAnalysisAssetId at job execution time)' and ':1318 when it materializes the analysis_assets row at job execution time'. There is a SECOND minter on the playback path (AnalysisCoordinator.swift:2351), so the row is created by whichever later stage arrives first, and NEITHER is the download completion.

So the await at DownloadManager.swift:3888 proves the JOB is durable. It does not make the ASSET exist, and the readiness probe waits on the asset. My reading of the ordering was right and irrelevant.

FIELD CONFIRMATION on the same episodes (db-vtjxverdict): job createdAt 12:42:17-12:44:46 on 08-09 versus asset createdAt 16:31, 16:31, 04:14+1d, 06:31+1d, and one STILL ABSENT. Every job row predates the kickoff's own give-up. This also kills the premise underneath my hypothesis: the job rows exist AT THE COMPLETION INSTANT, so handleBackgroundDownloadComplete DID run for those episodes. The 3.7-17.4 h latency is not a skipped handler; it is a genuinely later stage.

(b) NOT A REAL DROP, and not new. setAnalysisWorkScheduler is the FIRST suspension point in the deferred Task's body (:2274 MainActor.assertIsolated() is synchronous; :2290 is the first await), and the Task is created at :2258, earlier in init than anything cnql adds. resumeSession is reachable only from PlayheadAppDelegate, which cannot run before init returns, so the enqueue is ordered ahead of any delegate work. Field agrees: all five 08-09 episodes have job rows at the completion instant. Formally it still rests on actor-executor FIFO, which is not a language guarantee — a pre-existing residual, not a cnql defect, and not worth a bead on its own.

(c) DISCONFIRMED, in both directions. lastSource does not partition by outcome. All 12 kickoff rows: the 5 that read no_analysis_asset (08-09) are 3 download_and_analyze_tap + 2 background_download; the 7 that fired are 6 tap + 1 background_download. So 'tap works, background does not' is NOT the explanation for the readiness failures.

WHAT R3 FOUND INSTEAD, and it is the useful part: the kickoff row is written only in settle (RediffDayZeroKickoffCoordinator.swift:181) — pending and inFlight are IN-MEMORY ONLY. The drain is strictly serial (:133-142); on 08-09 five kickoffs settled 6m35s apart, each burning ~396 s. Episode #2's asset appeared 373 s after the drain would have reached it, INSIDE the 400 s budget, and yet no row exists, because the app was backgrounded and the in-memory queue did not survive. So the dominant failure here is A SERIAL IN-MEMORY DRAIN THAT DOES NOT SURVIVE SUSPENSION, not the numeric value of the readiness bound.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE REMEDY: raising the 6.5-minute bound is now clearly the wrong first move. It would lengthen a wait that a suspension is going to discard anyway. The two candidate fixes are (i) make pending/inFlight durable so the drain resumes across suspension, and (ii) trigger the kickoff off ASSET CREATION rather than download completion, so readiness is not a wait at all. Both are larger than a constant change and both are Dan's call. See also playhead-kxgh, which already bounds the realised benefit on the same serial drain.

COUNTERFACTUAL R3 COMPUTED for cnql, on today's timings (asset lag after job creation 0 s / 382 s / 957 s / 3h46m / 3h48m against a 40 x 10 s = 400 s budget, serial drain): 2 of 5 would fire, 3 would settle a recorded no_analysis_asset. So cnql is not a no-op, and it is also not sufficient. This bead is the dominant remaining term.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: KILLED 2026-08-11 in the full-backlog triage. VACUOUS — already answered, by a comment on the bead itself. cnql R3 (2026-08-10) settled all three sub-questions: (a) NO, enqueue does not write the asset row; (b) not a real drop; (c) DISCONFIRMED in both directions. Its conclusion — 'raising the 6.5-minute bound is clearly the wrong first move', the dominant failure being a serial in-memory drain that does not survive suspension — is already tracked as playhead-jra6 (durability) and playhead-kxgh (serialization). Nothing left to settle.

title: FIFTH sceneless-launch instance: BackgroundFeedRefreshService.attachSharedService is scene-only, so a headless BGAppRefreshTask refreshes no feeds and enqueues no auto-downloads
description:
FOUND in the playhead-cnql R2 review. PRE-EXISTING, not in cnql's diff.

attachSharedService is documented 'Call from PlayheadApp.task' (Playhead/Services/PodcastFeed/BackgroundFeedRefreshService.swift:281-288) and has NO launch-path call site. So on a headless BGAppRefreshTask wake, sharedService == nil, the handler reschedules and bails: no feed refresh, no auto-download enqueued.

THE PATTERN, fifth instance (see the sceneless-launch defect class):
  1. playhead-1shd  show-identity resolver, WindowGroup .task
  2. playhead-cnql  attachDayZeroBackgroundDownloadKickoff, PlayheadApp.swift:170 .task
  3. cnql R1 HIGH   DownloadManager.registerShared/registerAppDelegate, PlayheadApp.swift:127-128 .task
  4. (the same R1 finding's second consequence) hyht's force-quit scan, dead for the same reason
  5. THIS           BackgroundFeedRefreshService.attachSharedService

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SEVERITY SUGGESTS: it caps what cnql can deliver. cnql makes a background download's COMPLETION reach the day-0 kickoff. This bug means the background download largely never STARTS from a headless process — auto-downloads can only be enqueued by a process that rendered a window. The two compose: fixing only cnql leaves the funnel narrow one level up.

REMEDY SHAPE (same as R1's, and now routine): publish from PlayheadRuntime.init below the isPreviewRuntime guard, keep the .task call if it is idempotent on the same instance, and pin BOTH sites with a source canary that reddens when either is deleted.

ESTABLISH FIRST: confirm from a device pull that BGAppRefreshTask wakes are actually occurring and finding nil — background_task_runs should show the entry point with no feed work. Do not assume; three of the five instances above were found by tracing registration, but the field witness is what made them worth fixing.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
SEPARATE LIVE INSTANCE OF THIS FAMILY, found 2026-08-12 during the zero-request diagnosis and NOT the cause of it:

DownloadManager.registerShared(runtime.downloadManager) is installed from PlayheadApp.task (PlayheadApp.swift:128) — SCENE-ONLY. PlayheadAppDelegate reaches the manager through that slot to re-instantiate the background URLSession on a headless relaunch, so on a launch where iOS connects no scene the slot is nil and the delegate cannot reach it.

This does NOT explain the four episodes in the morning pull — they landed in the initial foreground session (all enqueued 14:58-15:49, first background_task_runs row 15:49:52), where .task had certainly run. It is filed here because it is one layer BELOW playhead-cnql's fix, which is exactly the shape this family keeps taking: cnql moved the day-0 observer off a scene modifier, and the thing the observer needs is still installed from one.

Sixth instance of the class if it holds.

title: FM metadata stall refuses fullEpisodeScan with ZERO peer contention (peers=0) — self-contention is REFUTED as the cause
description:
FIELD EVIDENCE from the post-wipe device pull db-db-r2wait (2026-08-10 17:33 UTC, build 9e31bf1c, virgin DB from the 13:02 wipe).

WHAT IS BLOCKED. Two of the three assets with a backfill job are deferred out of fullEpisodeScan — the ad scan itself — on an FM daemon refusal:

  60DFF7B4  fullEpisodeScan  deferred  metadataStall-refused(peers=0)  retryCount 0  17:31:00
  66D32039  fullEpisodeScan  deferred  metadataStall-refused(peers=0)  retryCount 1  17:30:02
  F7BB38BB  fullEpisodeScan  deferred  underCoverage-fullEpisodeScan   retryCount 1  17:29:01

metadataStall (FMDaemonRefusal.swift:125) = the daemon did not complete a tokenizer / schema-size XPC round trip inside FMInferenceDeadline.metadata. It is a REFUSAL to even begin inference, not a slow inference.

WHY THIS IS A VERDICT AND NOT JUST A LOG LINE. The (peers=N) suffix is playhead-ezmv's instrument, and BackfillJobRunner.swift:1375 states its discrimination in advance, before any field data existed:

  'peers=0 refutes self-contention for that stall, peers>=1 confirms it'

peersAtStart is the census of OUR OWN daemon calls already in flight at the instant the stalled call was ISSUED. Both observations read ZERO. So for these stalls the daemon was not waiting behind our own inference, and the self-contention theory that motivated rkfp+ezmv does not explain them. The instrument answered its question on the first pull after it shipped, and the answer is the one that rules out the fix we already made.

NUMERATOR AND DENOMINATOR, stated honestly: 2 of 2 currently-deferred FM refusals read peers=0. n=2. deferReason holds CURRENT STATE ONLY — backfill_jobs has one row per (asset, phase), so this is not a history and I cannot say what fraction of ALL stalls since the wipe were peers=0. That is the first thing to establish, and it needs a durable per-refusal record, not another pull.

WHAT IS NOT THE CAUSE (each ruled out by this same pull):
- Not self-contention — peers=0, above.
- Not window starvation. 10 background windows since the wipe, including two that did real work (16:58:25 preanalysis_recovery recovered_work, 17:19:30 backfill admitted_work). Windows are being granted and admitting work.
- Not a missing transcript. 66D32039 is at fastWM 1440/1925.7 (74.8%) with finalPassCoverageEndTime 1919.4 (99.7%) — it has essentially a complete transcript and is STILL refused.
- Not podcast identity. All three rows have podcastId NOT NULL (playhead-vtjx holding in the field).

ESTABLISH FIRST — do not assume:
1. Make the refusal population countable. Every metadataStall needs a durable row (asset, phase, peersAtStart, deadline, wall time waited, thermal state, timestamp) so the peers=0 fraction is a measured ratio rather than two current-state rows.
2. Then ask what the daemon WAS waiting on. peers=0 means it was not us; candidates are another process holding mlhostd (project_two_lane_measurement records mlhostd-pins-core killing background FM runs), a cold model load after the wipe, thermal, or an XPC round trip that is simply slower than FMInferenceDeadline.metadata allows on this hardware.
3. Only then decide the remedy. Raising the deadline is the obvious move and is exactly the kind of change that trades a visible refusal for an invisible stall, so it needs the measurement first.

WHY IT MATTERS: fullEpisodeScan IS reach. A deferred fullEpisodeScan means the episode is not being scanned for ads at all, which is Dan's stated #1 problem. Two of three assets are sitting in it right now.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
SECOND FIELD OBSERVATION, pull db-evening2 (2026-08-10 21:53 UTC, same build 9e31bf1c, 4h20m after db-db-r2wait). The scan is now COMPLETELY stalled, and a second blocker has appeared beside the metadata stall.

REACH IN THAT WINDOW — the numbers that matter:
  transcript_chunks       2781 -> 3549   (+768)
  semantic_scan_results     17 ->   17   (+0)

  numerator   new semantic_scan_results rows in 4h20m
  denominator the same 4h20m, during which transcription added 768 chunks
  = ZERO ad-scan progress while transcription progressed normally.

Per-asset fast watermarks all moved (66D32039 1440->1500, 60DFF7B4 540->780, 590D6656 60->480), so the pipeline is alive. It is the SCAN specifically that produced nothing.

BACKGROUND WINDOWS COLLAPSED IN DURATION. Eight runs since 17:30, every one outcome=expired, jobsCompleted=0:

  20:12:56   19s  backfill
  20:25:30   35s  preanalysis_recovery
  21:07:24   22s  backfill
  21:08:04   26s  preanalysis_recovery
  21:08:04   25s  backfill
  21:53:12   13s  backfill
  21:53:12   13s  backfill
  21:53:12   13s  preanalysis_recovery

Total granted time across all eight: ~166 seconds. Compare the same device earlier the SAME DAY: 196s, 197s, 233s, 239s, 288s, 289s, 294s, 295s. Windows are being granted at a similar rate and then killed in a fraction of the time.

I am NOT diagnosing the cause. Low Power Mode, thermal state and battery level all produce this shape and none of them is recorded in this DB. What matters for THIS bead is the consequence: a 13-second window cannot complete an FM metadata round trip, whose own deadline (FMInferenceDeadline.metadata) is longer than the whole window. So on a device in this state the metadata stall is not merely likely, it is structural.

THAT ALSO EXPLAINS THE ASYMMETRY, and it is the useful part. Transcription made progress in these same 13-35s windows because it is incremental and persists partial work (26od/fil5). The ad scan did not, because its unit of work cannot start, let alone finish, inside the grant. Reach is not losing to detection quality here — it is losing to work-unit granularity.

A SECOND BLOCKER, NEW SINCE THE LAST PULL:
  F7BB38BB  deferred  scan_claim:fm_unavailable   retryCount 2   21:53:16
  66D32039  queued    metadataStall-refused(peers=0)  retryCount 1
  60DFF7B4  queued    metadataStall-refused(peers=0)  retryCount 0

'fm_unavailable' is a different refusal from a metadata stall — the model is not there at all, rather than not answering in time. Worth establishing whether it is a consequence of the short windows (model unload under memory pressure / never finishing a load) or independent. Do not assume they are the same failure.

The two metadataStall jobs are now QUEUED rather than deferred, so the retry path is working; they have simply never succeeded.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
CAVEAT ON THE peers=0 CONCLUSION — found in the P3 backlog triage, 2026-08-11, and it weakens the central claim of this bead.

WHAT THIS BEAD CONCLUDED: 'peers=0 refutes self-contention.' That reading rests on peersAtStart being a census of OUR daemon calls in flight. The instrument's own contract (BackfillJobRunner.swift:1375) says peers=0 refutes self-contention and peers>=1 confirms it.

THE PROBLEM: peersAtStart counts only calls that go through FMInferenceDeadline.run. Chapter generation does NOT. Verified: ChapterPlanAssembler.swift:177 calls ChapterLabelingService.label(...), and FMInferenceDeadline.swift:42 documents in production source that it races an FM call inside withThrowingTaskGroup — which cannot stop a cancellation-ignoring call, and is not the deadline path that increments the census.

SO peersAtStart IS A LOWER BOUND, not a census. It under-reports EXACTLY when chapter generation is the contender — i.e. the diagnostics used to reason about daemon contention are blind to one real contender, and blind to it precisely in the case where it matters.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD: 'peers=0' does NOT establish that nothing of ours was in flight. It establishes that no call ON THE DEADLINE PATH was in flight. A chapter-labeling call holding the daemon would produce peers=0 and look exactly like an external stall. The self-contention hypothesis is therefore NOT refuted — it is unrefuted for one specific contender that the instrument cannot see.

This does not make the bead wrong. fullEpisodeScan really is being refused, the refusals really are metadataStall, and the remedy still needs establishing. What changes is that step 1 must now ALSO account for chapter calls before concluding the daemon is stalled by something outside the app.

WHAT TO DO ABOUT IT: playhead-4meb covers the underlying defect (chapter calls bypass FMInferenceDeadline, so they are both unbounded AND uncounted) and the triage recommends raising it from P3 to P2 for this reason. Establishing a3hf's cause honestly probably requires 4meb's instrumentation half first — otherwise the census keeps lying in the same direction.

I reported the refutation to Dan as established. It is not, and this note is the correction.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
LIVE WITNESS, virgin-DB overnight pull 2026-08-11 (build 9e31bf1c, scratchpad/db-overnight5). This is not historical — it is the CURRENT state of a backfill job on the device:

  asset=B80D3EE0 phase=fullEpisodeScan policy=fullCoverage status=queued retry=1
  deferReason=metadataStall-refused(peers=0)
  created 08-11 03:14:35  updated 08-11 04:58:41
  cursor={"processedUnitCount":0,"lastProcessedUpperBoundSec":99.66}

peers=0 again, on a fresh install with a fresh database. It confirms the correction already recorded on this bead: peersAtStart is a LOWER BOUND, because chapter calls bypass FMInferenceDeadline.run and are therefore uncounted. Do not read peers=0 as 'nothing else was running'.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE OTHER FOUR ASSETS' PROBLEMS. B80D3EE0 is the BEST-COVERED asset in the pull: 91% fast transcript (3840 of 4224s), 74% confirmed-ad coverage (3146.62s), 7 ad_windows, 4847 transcript chunks. It is the one closest to being genuinely useful to the listener, and it is the one this refusal parked at cursor 99.66 — 2.4% of the episode. The stall is not hitting the assets that were going nowhere anyway; it is hitting the one that was nearly there.

title: the foreground STREAMING download path lands a pinned artifact with no day-0 kickoff record, and the play-time trigger fires on a PARTIAL file
description:
FILED BY playhead-cnql (established while enumerating download paths; outside
that bead's ceiling, which is the background/auto population).

There are two production paths that land a complete pinned artifact and
register an analysis asset:

  * `DownloadManager.handleBackgroundDownloadComplete` (DownloadManager.swift
    :3629) — every `backgroundDownload` caller: the "Download & Analyze" tap,
    the plain Download button and Download-Next-N (EpisodeListView.swift:256),
    subscription auto-download (BackgroundFeedRefreshService.swift:1017), and
    force-quit resume (ForceQuitResumeScan.swift). This one notifies the day-0
    observer (playhead-4dqe, install site fixed by playhead-cnql).

  * `DownloadManager.finalizeStreamingTransfer` (:1652) — pressing PLAY on a
    not-yet-downloaded episode. It writes the completeness pin, sets the
    fingerprint and calls `enqueueAnalysisIfNeeded` (:1700), i.e. it produces a
    fully downloaded, asset-registered episode. It never calls
    `notifyBackgroundDownloadCompleted`, so it produces NO
    `rediff_day_zero_kickoffs` row.

That path is not entirely uncovered — `PlayheadRuntime.performPlayEpisode`
fires `kickOffDayZeroRediff` on both branches — but two things are worth a
look:

1. The streaming branch fires the kickoff at PlayheadRuntime.swift:4228, BEFORE
   `try await result.downloadComplete()` at :4236, passing `result.fileURL`.
   The A-side of a day-0 byte diff is supposed to be the pinned PLAYED copy;
   here it is a file still being written. Whether the minter re-resolves the
   A-side from the asset row (its doc comment says it does) needs checking, not
   assuming — this is exactly the "trusting a value without asking what it
   measures" shape.

2. Because it bypasses the kickoff coordinator, this path is invisible in the
   `rediff_day_zero_kickoffs` ledger. A device pull cannot tell a streamed
   episode that never attempted day-0 from one that was never downloaded.

Related: playhead-cnql, playhead-4dqe, playhead-xsdz.36.4, playhead-wrj8 (the
pinned-A-side immutability invariant).

title: the day-0 kickoff drain is strictly serial and each item can burn the full 6.5-min readiness budget: 5 requests took 33 minutes
description:
FILED BY playhead-cnql (not fixed — out of that bead's scope).

`RediffDayZeroKickoffCoordinator.runDrain` is `while let request = takeNext()
{ await process(request) }` — one request at a time. `process` runs
`DayZeroReadinessWait.run` with `maxAttempts = 40` and a 10 s poll
(PlayheadRuntime.dayZeroPreparationReadinessMaxAttempts /
…PollNanos), so ONE request that never becomes ready blocks the whole queue
for ~6.5 minutes.
