MEASURED (db-vtjxverdict, 2026-08-09): five `rediff_day_zero_kickoffs` rows at
16:48:54, 16:55:29, 17:02:06, 17:08:41, 17:15:17 — spaced 6m35s apart, every
one `lastPollCount=40`, `lastWaitedSeconds` 395.3-397.3, every one
`no_analysis_asset`. Five requests, 33 minutes, zero fires.

TWO SEPARATE QUESTIONS, and they should not be conflated:

1. SERIALIZATION. Head-of-line blocking is what makes the in-memory queue
   (sibling filing) lose its tail. But parallel drains mean parallel ~125 MB
   day-0 fetches, so any concurrency here is a bandwidth decision. A cheaper
   answer may be to keep the drain serial but stop letting a NOT-READY request
   hold the head — e.g. re-queue it behind the ready ones rather than sleeping
   on it.

2. THE 6.5-MINUTE BUDGET IS SHORT FOR THE THING IT WAITS ON. All five of those
   give-ups were `no_analysis_asset`, and the assets did eventually appear —
   PEFM4NEHJPGZG9 at 20:31:32 (3h36m after its kickoff gave up) and
   HB44TJM37PBHZ3 at 08:14:58 the next day (15h06m). On a loaded device the
   analysis asset is registered when the job is ACQUIRED, not when the download
   completes, so on a cold/starved device the wait is measuring the analysis
   backlog rather than the download. That is playhead-pa6a's territory; the
   coupling is worth naming before anyone lengthens the poll budget, which
   would only hold the queue open longer.

Related: playhead-cnql, playhead-4dqe, playhead-pa6a (why asset registration
lags on a starved device), and the sibling filing on the in-memory queue.

title: the day-0 kickoff queue is IN-MEMORY: a batch queued but not settled when the process ends leaves no row at all
description:
FILED BY playhead-cnql (not fixed — cnql's ceiling is WHO STARTS an attempt).

`RediffDayZeroKickoffCoordinator` holds `pending` and `inFlight` as plain actor
state (RediffDayZeroKickoffCoordinator.swift:15-17). A durable row is written
only in `settle(...)`, at the END of the bounded readiness wait. So every
kickoff that is queued but has not yet settled when iOS suspends or terminates
the process disappears with NO record — the same unrecorded silence
playhead-4dqe was created to kill, displaced from the give-up to the queue.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE AFTER cnql: cnql makes every completed background download
request a kickoff, so the queue is now routinely non-empty, and a subscription
batch is exactly the shape that exceeds one foreground session.

WITNESS (db-vtjxverdict, 2026-08-09): five kickoff rows at 16:48:54, 16:55:29,
17:02:06, 17:08:41 and 17:15:17 — spaced 6m35s apart, each `lastPollCount=40`
and `lastWaitedSeconds` 395.3-397.3. That is the drain running SERIALLY, one
request at a time, each burning the full 40-poll / ~6.5-minute readiness budget
(see the sibling filing on serialization). Five requests took 33 minutes to
settle. A sixth would have needed the app alive for 40.

Two things to decide together, because a fix for one alone makes the other
worse:
1. Should the REQUEST be durable (a row written at enqueue, settled later)
   rather than only the outcome? The `rediff_day_zero_kickoffs` table is
   episode-keyed and already free of the analysis_assets FK, so it can hold a
   pending state; playhead-fil5 set the precedent ("a dropped ad-scan request
   now leaves a durable, queryable claim").
2. Should a durable pending request be re-driven at next launch? That is a
   bandwidth decision, not a bookkeeping one — see cnql's measurement
   (125.0 MB per fetching attempt, 1 GB rolling 24h cap).

Related: playhead-cnql (the install-site fix), playhead-4dqe (the ledger),
playhead-fil5 (the durable-claim precedent), playhead-p70f (why the bytes are
bounded at all).

title: [bug] engine_silent_timeout is reported for a transcription stage that ran 14.7s — a BGTask expiry is indistinguishable from a real 300s silence
description:
MEASURED on the virgin-install pull (2026-08-10), while establishing playhead-pa6a.

work_journal row at 15:45:31 for asset B80D3EE0:
  stage                = analysisJobRunner.run.transcriptionTimeout
  failure_observation  = engine_silent_timeout
  slice_duration_ms    = 14713
  chunks_persisted     = 0

The name says 'nobody said anything for five minutes'. The row says the stage
ran fourteen point seven seconds. Both are emitted by the same path.

WHY. AnalysisJobRunner.swift:660-668 races the event-stream observer against
'try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(300))'; the timeout arm returns a
hardcoded (0, nil, false). TranscriptRunObservation.classify maps
sawCompleted == false && failure == nil to .engineSilentTimeout. When the
BGTask expiration handler cancels the run, the observer's stream terminates
with no .completed and no failure — the SAME (0, nil, false) tuple — so an
expiry is classified as a five-minute engine silence.

The two have opposite remedies. A real silence is an engine/model fault worth
chasing. An expiry is a budget fact and the correct reading is 'the window ran
out 14.7s into ASR'. playhead-ngev introduced this class precisely to separate
'nobody said anything' from 'the engine reported success over an empty
transcript' — the third case, 'the OS took the window back', was not given a
name and fell into the first.

The 15:45:31 row has a sibling 'preempted / task_expired' at the same second
(stage analysisWorkScheduler.taskExpiredRequeue), so the information exists;
it just is not joined into the failure class, and the class is what the
diagnostics aggregate groups on.

FIX SHAPE (not implemented): the timeout arm should distinguish 'my 300s sleep
completed' from 'the group was cancelled', and the observer should distinguish
'stream ended cleanly' from 'stream ended under cancellation'. A fourth
observation value (e.g. backgroundWindowExpired) then carries it.

WITNESS: also 13:18:23 (slice 1284 ms, class 'cancelled' — that one IS routed
correctly via failure_class, so the gap is only on the arm where no failure
object exists at all).

Found while investigating playhead-pa6a; filed rather than fixed, per scope.

title: unionSpan decouples a span's CertaintyBand from ownershipInferenceWasSuppressed — the permissive gate's escape hatch
description:
LATENT, not live: `BackfillJobRunner.mergeSpans` has NO production caller today (grep: only `BoundarySpanExpansionTests`). Filing it because playhead-92im just made `ownershipInferenceWasSuppressed` load-bearing for a shipped confidence, and this is the one construction in the tree that can produce a span carrying a FABRICATED band with the flag CLEARED.

`BackfillJobRunner.unionSpan` (~:4501) picks metadata from whichever input ranks higher on `certaintyRank`:

    let preferred = certaintyRank(rhs.certainty) >= certaintyRank(lhs.certainty) ? rhs : lhs
    ...
    certainty: preferred.certainty,
    ownershipInferenceWasSuppressed: lhs.ownershipInferenceWasSuppressed
        && rhs.ownershipInferenceWasSuppressed

Union a PERMISSIVE span (`PermissiveAdClassifier.makeAnchorlessSpan`: hardcoded `certainty: .strong`, `ownershipInferenceWasSuppressed: true`) with any genuine FM span graded `.moderate`/`.weak` and the result is `certainty: .strong` (the hardcode wins the rank) with `ownershipInferenceWasSuppressed: false` (the AND clears it). Persisted through `encodeRefinedSpansForTesting`, that row is byte-indistinguishable from a model-graded `strong`.

The AND is CORRECT for what its comment claims — ownership/commercialIntent, where "either side carried a real inference" is the right reading. It is wrong for `certainty`, which is not a union of the two inputs but a copy of ONE of them, and the flag must follow whichever one was copied.

FIX (one line, no schema change): take the flag from `preferred`, not from the conjunction — or, if the ownership reading must be kept for the other fields, track the two independently.

CONSUMER THIS WOULD DEFEAT: `SemanticSweepMarkComposer.certaintyFactor(of:)` reads `ownershipInferenceWasSuppressed` to decide whether a band is the model's. A laundered span returns the CEILING factor for a verdict nothing graded — exactly the defect playhead-92im's review round caught one layer up.

Do NOT close this by deleting `mergeSpans`: check first whether boundary-span expansion is meant to be re-wired.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: REPRIORITIZED P3 -> P1 in the 2026-08-11 triage. Its own premise is wrong, in the flattering direction. The bead opens 'LATENT, not live: BackfillJobRunner.mergeSpans has NO production caller today.' It does: runJob -> :3779 -> runOutwardExpansion :4086 -> Self.mergeSpans :4259 -> unionSpan :4489, no feature flag. And the fuel is on the device: 9 rows carrying ownershipInferenceWasSuppressed:true coexist with 2 carrying false, which is the exact input the merge reads. This is live width damage, not a latent hazard.

title: [bug] buildFMLedgerEntries FABRICATES a CertaintyBand from transcriptQuality while the model's real band sits unread in the same row
description:
Found while establishing playhead-92im. NOT fixed there — 92im's ceiling is the sweep composer's persisted confidence; this is detection-v1's fusion weight, a different lane and a different blast radius.

AdDetectionService.buildFMLedgerEntries (~line 8425) weights every FM ledger entry like this:

    // Map scan result to a certainty band. The coarse scan
    // carries transcript quality; use it as a band proxy.
    // Strong quality -> .moderate, degraded -> .weak.
    let band: CertaintyBand = result.transcriptQuality == .good ? .moderate : .weak

The comment states the premise plainly and the premise is FALSE. The coarse scan carries the model's OWN CertaintyBand, persisted in the same row it is reading:

  semantic_scan_results.spansJSON, passA shape:
      {"supportLineRefs":[17,18,20],"certainty":"strong"}
  passB shape: an ARRAY of refined spans, each with its own "certainty".

Measured on the 2026-08-10 device pull (db-vtjxverdict): 55 of 55 passA containsAd rows and 11 of 11 passB containsAd rows carry a band. Split: 40 strong / 15 moderate. ZERO carry an empty support payload.

Consequences, all in the same direction:
  * `.strong` is UNREACHABLE. The proxy can only ever produce .moderate or .weak, so the fmCap branch of the weight ladder (case .strong: weight = fusionConfig.fmCap) is DEAD CODE at this call site. 40 of 55 rows -- the ones the model graded strong -- are weighted at 0.75x fmCap.
  * A `moderate` verdict on a `good` transcript and a `strong` verdict on a `good` transcript are weighted IDENTICALLY. The band the model emitted is discarded and replaced by a property of the input text.
  * The two quantities are not even about the same thing: transcriptQuality is a deterministic on-device estimate of ASR cleanliness (TranscriptQualityEstimator), the band is the model's confidence in ITS OWN verdict. FoundationModelClassifier's own header says quality is deliberately NOT part of the @Generable schema precisely because they are separate.

The fix is a one-line read of what is already persisted; the decode helper now exists next door as SemanticSweepMarkComposer.certaintyBand(of:) and handles both payload shapes.

WHY IT NEEDS ITS OWN BEAD: this moves detection-v1's proposalConfidence, which feeds DecisionMapper and the auto-skip gates. 40 rows getting MORE weight is a reach/precision change, not a cleanup, and it needs its own measurement over the corpus before it ships. Do not fold it into a confidence-plumbing bead.

Standing diagnostic (feedback_ask_what_the_quantity_measures): what would this band read if the model had expressed no certainty at all? Exactly what it reads when the model said `strong` -- .moderate, as long as the transcript was clean.

title: already-persisted always-skip vetoes survive the q6y3 fix, and the button can no longer undo them
description:
Found in playhead-q6y3 R2 review. FILED, not fixed — repairing shipped rows is a persistence migration, which is a decision for Dan (CLAUDE.md: never change persistence strategy without approval), and it is outside q6y3's acceptance criteria.

WHAT. playhead-q6y3 fixed "Always skip <sponsor> on this show" going forward: the write site now records `source: .falseNegative` / `correctionType: .falseNegative` instead of `.manualVeto` / `.falsePositive`. It does not touch rows already written by the shipped inversion, and there is no migration in the diff. Anyone who pressed that button on a previous build — Dan has been dogfooding it — still carries a durable SUPPRESS-direction `sponsorOnShow` row.

WHY PRESSING IT AGAIN DOES NOT HELP. The dedupe identity for a correction is `(analysisAssetId, effectiveCorrectionType, normalizedScopeKey, correctionIdentityKey)` — see `AnalysisStore.appendCorrectionEvent`, probe at lines 19890-19902, and the v23 unique index at 4544. `effectiveCorrectionType` is part of that tuple, so the new `.falseNegative` row does NOT collide with, replace or supersede the old `.falsePositive` one. The two coexist. And q6y3's own bound (A) then makes the new row inert against the old one: a show-wide BOOSTER is applied to no span, while the show-wide SUPPRESSOR is still applied asset-wide. So the user has no in-app way to undo the veto they never meant to cast.

WHAT THE STALE ROW STILL DOES. Two live effects, both still reachable:
  1. `AnalysisStore.suppressingCorrectionScopesPresent` queries by SCOPE STRING across all rows, not by asset, and the old row's source (`.manualVeto`) is not in the boost-source list. So `SponsorKnowledgeStore.activeEntriesWithNegativeMemory` keeps filtering that sponsor out of the show's active lexicon, on every episode, permanently. That is exactly the state bound (B) was added to prevent for new taps.
  2. On the episode where the tap happened, `correctionFactorSnapshot` still classifies it `.everywhere` + suppressor, so `range = nil` and it suppresses EVERY span in that episode by `max(0, 1 - weight)`. This is the shipped "press always-skip, get never-skip" bug, still live for old rows, decaying only with `correctionDecayWeight`.

SO THE BEAD'S OWN HEADLINE IS ONLY HALF TRUE IN THE FIELD: new presses reinforce, old presses still veto and cannot be revoked.

SCOPE NOTE. Impact of (1) is bounded by playhead-shjn — the only production reader of an active sponsor entry is `ASRVocabularyProvider` — so the practical cost is that the sponsor stays out of the ASR contextual vocabulary. Impact of (2) is real skip suppression but confined to the single episode the tap landed on, and decays.

OPTIONS. (a) A one-shot migration rewriting `sponsorOnShow` rows whose `source == 'manualVeto'` AND that came from this button — but the button's rows are not distinguishable from a genuine sponsor veto written by any other path, which is the hard part and worth stating plainly before anyone starts. (b) Leave old rows and let decay handle (2), accepting that (1) never decays because `suppressingCorrectionScopesPresent` is presence-based, not weighted. (c) Give the user an explicit "stop always-skipping this sponsor" affordance that writes whatever revocation the store needs.

WITNESS. `Playhead/Persistence/AnalysisStore/AnalysisStore.swift` lines 4497/4544 (identity tuple), 19855-19914 (`appendCorrectionEvent` probe), 20191-20226 (`suppressingCorrectionScopesPresent`); `Playhead/Services/AdDetection/UserCorrectionStore.swift` lines 1275-1293 (bound A's direction split).

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: KILLED 2026-08-11 in the full-backlog triage. EMPTY POPULATION. Six device pulls queried directly: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM correction_events WHERE scope LIKE '%OnShow%' returns 0 in every DB that has rows (db-live 27, db-evening 27, db-vtjxverdict 30, db-corrected2 30 — all exactTimeSpan). sponsor_knowledge_entries = 0 in all six. The premise — 'Dan has been dogfooding it and still carries a durable SUPPRESS-direction sponsorOnShow row' — is false. The migration has nothing to migrate, and option (a)'s hard part is unreachable. Corroborated independently by playhead-uv7o's own measurement across five pulls.

title: a show-wide reinforcement labels EVERY region of the episode 'reportedAd' in the training corpus
description:
Found in playhead-q6y3 R2 review. FILED, not fixed — outside that bead's acceptance criteria, which stop at the two bounds it added.

WHAT. `TrainingExampleMaterializer.correctionOverlaps` returns TRUE for a show-wide scope (`sponsorOnShow` and friends) against EVERY scan region of the asset, by construction and by its own doc:

    case .sponsorOnShow, .phraseOnShow, .campaignOnShow,
         .domainOwnershipOnShow, .jingleOnShow:
        // Wider, non-span-bound scopes. They apply to every region of
        // the asset by construction.
        return true

Since playhead-q6y3 the "Always skip <sponsor> on this show" button writes a `sponsorOnShow` scope with `source: .falseNegative`. So one tap sets `userReportedFalseNegative = true` for every region of that episode, which gives every region `userAction = "reportedAd"` and — via `TrainingExampleBucketer.bucket`, first rule, `!fmPositive && userReportedFalseNegative` — the `.disagreement` bucket. That is the whole show body, since most regions are FM-negative. The corpus ends up asserting the listener reported a missed ad in regions the listener said nothing about.

IT IS THE TAP THAT DOES IT, IMMEDIATELY. `LearningArtifactIngestor.ingest` calls `materializer.materialize(forAsset: correction.analysisAssetId)` on every new correction, so the press re-materializes the very episode it was pressed on.

WHY IT IS THE SAME DEFECT q6y3 ALREADY BOUNDED TWICE. q6y3's rule is "a show-wide scope names WHAT is an ad, never WHERE the ads are". Bound (A) applied it in `correctionFactorSnapshot` (a show-wide booster now lifts no span); bound (B) applied it in `AnalysisStore.suppressingCorrectionScopesPresent` (a reinforcement no longer deletes the sponsor from the lexicon). The materializer is the third live consumer keyed on `source?.kind` — the diff's own comment on `onAlwaysSkipSponsorAsync` enumerates it — and it is the one that did not get the rule.

NOT A REGRESSION IN KIND, BUT WORSE IN VOLUME AND MEANING. Before q6y3 the same tap wrote `.manualVeto`, so the blanket contamination was `userReverted` on every region: `.disagreement` only where FM was positive (few regions), `.negative` elsewhere. After q6y3 it is `.disagreement` on every FM-NEGATIVE region — nearly the whole episode — and `.disagreement` is the highest-priority, most training-valuable bucket.

SEVERITY IS BOUNDED BY THERE BEING NO READER. `training_examples` is written but never read in production: `AnalysisStore.loadTrainingExamples(forAsset:)` has zero production callers (tests only), and `TrainingExampleMaterializerTests.trainingExamplesRemainInsideLocalLearningBoundary` exists precisely to keep it that way. So nothing a listener experiences changes today. What is damaged is the durable local corpus that the measurement/cert program will read when it does.

SUGGESTED FIX, mirroring bound (A) exactly. Give `correctionOverlaps` the event's direction and return false for a show-wide scope in the BOOST direction, leaving the show-wide SUPPRESSOR asset-wide (the safe direction, same asymmetry as bound A). The filter is at TrainingExampleMaterializer.swift:159.

WITNESS. `Playhead/Services/AdDetection/TrainingExampleMaterializer.swift` lines 159-167 (the filter), 240-274 (the signals and userAction), 392-425 (`correctionOverlaps`); `Playhead/Services/AdDetection/TrainingExampleBucketer.swift` lines 87-96; `Playhead/Services/AdDetection/LearningArtifactIngestor.swift` lines 244-255.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: ABSORBS playhead-hpyt (closed 2026-08-11). Same defect, same file, same line, same day — both out of the q6y3 R2 review: TrainingExampleMaterializer.correctionOverlaps returns true for all five *OnShow scopes (both quote the identical 5-line case block; both cite :392 and the :159 filter). This bead survives because it additionally establishes the BUCKETER consequence (.disagreement, the highest-priority bucket), the volume/meaning change versus pre-q6y3, and the severity bound (loadTrainingExamples has zero production callers). Carrying hpyt's option list (a)/(b)/(c) across — this bead's suggested fix IS hpyt's option (b).

title: [bug] the sponsor knowledge store reaches ASR vocabulary and nothing else — "Always skip <sponsor> on this show" cannot move a skip

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
FOUND IN playhead-q6y3 REVIEW (R1), NOT FIXED THERE — wiring a detection source is an architectural decision, not a review fix.

q6y3 correctly inverted the button's direction and then bounded it: a show-wide REINFORCEMENT is recorded as a booster nowhere (CorrectionFactorSnapshot), because a scope that names a SPONSOR cannot say WHERE the ads are. The bead's account of where the positive effect goes instead is `LearningArtifactIngestor.applySponsorSideEffect` -> `SponsorKnowledgeStore.recordCandidate` -> "it raises the sponsor where the sponsor is named". MEASURED ON 4cf8ca93, that last hop does not exist in production.

WHAT READS AN `.active` SponsorKnowledgeEntry, exhaustively:
  * ASRVocabularyProvider.loadActiveSponsorEntries (ASRVocabularyProvider.swift:248) -> contextualStrings -> SpeechAnalyzer AnalysisContext. WIRED (PlayheadRuntime.swift:833). This is the ONLY one.
  * SponsorKnowledgeMatcher.match(atoms:podcastId:knowledgeStore:) (SponsorKnowledgeMatcher.swift:49) -> SponsorMatch -> RegionProposalBuilder.makeSponsorProposals. ZERO PRODUCTION CALLERS. The single production call site, RegionShadowPhase.swift:188, calls the LEGACY STUB `SponsorKnowledgeMatcher.match(atoms:)` which returns `[]` unconditionally — and `RegionShadowPhase.Input` has a `fingerprintStore` field but no `knowledgeStore` field at all, so the store-backed overload is unreachable from there by construction. (The fingerprint sibling IS wired, same function, ten lines below: `AdCopyFingerprintMatcher.match(atoms:podcastId:fingerprintStore:)`.)
  * CompiledSponsorLexicon (LexicalScanner.compiledLexicon) — ZERO PRODUCTION CONSTRUCTIONS. Every production `LexicalScanner(...)` (9 sites) uses the default `compiledLexicon: nil`; the only `CompiledSponsorLexicon(entries:)` in Playhead/ is its own `static let empty`.

AND THE STORE HAS NEVER HELD AN ENTRY. `LearningArtifactIngestor.applySponsorSideEffect` is the ONLY production writer of SponsorKnowledgeStore (only caller of `recordCandidate`/`recordRollback`; `upsertKnowledgeEntry` has no other path). Before q6y3 the only production writer of a `sponsorOnShow` scope wrote the FP direction, which routes to `recordRollback`, which no-ops when no entry exists. Device pull (scratchpad/db-corrected2/analysis.sqlite, read from a copy): `sponsor_knowledge_entries` = 0 rows, `knowledge_candidate_events` = 0 rows, of 30 correction_events rows (all `exactTimeSpan`, 0 `sponsorOnShow`). So q6y3 is what makes this table non-empty for the first time.

CONSEQUENCE, in the words the CTA has to answer to:
  * ONE press: a correction_events row, a KnowledgeCandidateEvent, and a sponsor entry at confirmationCount 1 -> state `.quarantined`. Nothing reads `.quarantined`. NO observable behaviour change anywhere.
  * TWO presses ON TWO DISTINCT EPISODES (the ingestor's side effect fires only on a NEW insert, and the durable identity includes analysisAssetId, so two presses on the SAME episode dedupe to one): confirmationCount 2 -> `.active`. The sponsor name enters the ASR contextual-strings vocabulary for that podcast, which can only affect episodes transcribed AFTER that point. It never touches actuationConfidence, the 0.7 preload floor, the auto-skip gates, or any banner.

So the strongest, most deliberate signal the product collects — a named advertiser, a named show, permanent — buys a transcription hint. That is not wrong as a bound (see q6y3's reasoning; a blanket span multiplier is worse), but the reinforcement has nowhere PRINCIPLED to land until a sponsor lexicon is consulted at detection time.

THE FIX SHAPE (Dan's call, which is why this is filed):
  (a) Wire the store-backed matcher: add `knowledgeStore` + reuse the existing `podcastId` on `RegionShadowPhase.Input`, and swap line 188 to the store-backed overload — exactly the shape `fingerprintStore` already has ten lines below. Smallest change; makes `SponsorMatch` a real proposal source again.
  (b) Wire `CompiledSponsorLexicon` into `LexicalScanner` where the scanner is built with a podcastProfile (AdDetectionService.swift:2357, :13126).
  (c) Neither, and accept that the button's effect is transcription-quality only — in which case the CTA copy has to keep saying "remembers", which is what q6y3 R1 left it saying.

Whichever way it goes, note that (a) and (b) both make the `activeEntriesWithNegativeMemory` direction-blindness that q6y3 fixed (bound B, `AnalysisStore.suppressingCorrectionScopesPresent`) load-bearing for the first time. Today that fix is correct and unreachable.

SECOND, SMALLER DEFECT IN THE SAME PATH, newly reachable: `applySponsorSideEffect` passes the scope-parsed sponsor as `entityValue` to `recordCandidate`, and the scope carries the NORMALIZED (lowercased) key. `ASRVocabularyProvider.compiledEntries` appends `entry.entityValue` verbatim, so the vocabulary receives "squarespace", not "Squarespace". Contextual strings for a proper noun are exactly where casing might matter. Before q6y3 no entry was ever created this way, so this is new.

Related: playhead-q6y3 (the direction fix and its two bounds), playhead-hpyt, playhead-k511 (the same "cited but uncalled" pattern one layer over), playhead-ar60.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
DAN'S INTENT, confirmed 2026-08-10: YES — 'Always skip this sponsor' should mean the sponsor's ads actually get SKIPPED in future episodes of that show. Today the only production reader of an .active SponsorKnowledgeEntry is ASRVocabularyProvider, so two presses teach the transcriber to spell the brand and nothing else. This bead is what closes that gap.

DESIGN CONSTRAINT that falls out of q6y3 and ar60 — read before choosing a shape:

1. IT MUST BE SPAN-LOCAL, NOT SHOW-WIDE-BLANKET. q6y3 established that weightedCorrections(for:) loads BY analysisAssetId, so a show-wide booster could only ever lift spans in the ONE episode being listened to — it was never the show-wide mechanism, just an accident that over-fired locally on evidence about no span. And ar60 MEASURED the danger of unbounded boosts: five spans crossed SkipOrchestrator's 0.7 preload floor on inflation alone under the old asset-wide blanket. So the reinforcement must lift a span BECAUSE THE BRAND IS NAMED IN IT, not because the episode belongs to a show where the brand was once vetoed.

2. THE RIGHT SHAPE IS PROBABLY 'ATTENTION, NOT VERDICT'. See feedback_lexical_as_attention: brittle signals say WHERE to look, never the final determination. Sponsor knowledge is exactly that — it tells the pipeline that a span mentioning this brand on this show deserves a closer look (or a targeted FM scan, cf. j4wi item 3), rather than asserting the span IS an ad. That keeps the user's signal load-bearing without making one tap an auto-skip authority.

3. THE CORROBORATION GATE ALREADY EXISTS and should be kept: recordCandidate at 0.5, minConfirmationsForActive == 2, identity includes analysisAssetId, so promotion needs presses on TWO DISTINCT EPISODES (BroadCorrectionScope.sponsorOnShow.requiredDistinctEpisodes agrees). One press stays inert by design — the CTA now says 'Remembers…' precisely because of this.

4. LIKELY PREREQUISITE: playhead-absa. If the wiring makes sponsor knowledge a LEXICAL ANCHOR, it inherits absa's defects — the URL catalog has no .ai TLD, 'head to' / 'our sponsor called' are missing, and the 5s decoder floor drops sub-5s single-atom anchors (that floor is what killed 'go to ketone.com', 3.6s, the only true anchor in the j4wi mid-roll pod). A sponsor-derived anchor would die the same way. Sequence absa first, or co-design.

5. DEAD MACHINERY TO EITHER WIRE OR DELETE, established by q6y3 R1: SponsorKnowledgeMatcher.match(atoms:podcastId:knowledgeStore:) has ZERO production callers (RegionShadowPhase.swift:188 calls the stub returning []; RegionShadowPhase.Input has no knowledgeStore field), and CompiledSponsorLexicon is never constructed in production (all 9 LexicalScanner sites pass compiledLexicon: nil). Decide deliberately — this is the y3ya shape (FMBackfillMode.canProposeNewRegions had zero consumers), and shipping more unwired machinery is how it recurs.

6. FIELD BASELINE for the eventual measurement: sponsor_knowledge_entries = 0 rows and knowledge_candidate_events = 0 rows on the device pull (db-corrected2). q6y3 is what makes them non-empty for the first time, so any before/after here starts from a true zero.

QUEUE PLACEMENT (orchestrator's proposal, Dan to overrule if wrong): after absa, before the 4xqf width program.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
SHAPE (a) IMPLEMENTED on branch bead/playhead-shjn (3 commits off 850c7cf5). Shape (b) deliberately NOT implemented — presented below and in playhead-a1r6 for Dan.

CLAIMS VERIFIED (all on 850c7cf5, whole-file reads, not summarized greps):
 * `SponsorKnowledgeMatcher.match(atoms:podcastId:knowledgeStore:)` production callers = 0. CONFIRMED. The whole `Playhead/` tree references the type in 6 places; 5 are comments/decl and the 6th was `RegionShadowPhase.swift:188` calling the stub.
 * The legacy stub `match(atoms:)` is `{ return [] }`, 4 lines, no branches. CONFIRMED.
 * `RegionShadowPhase.Input` had no `knowledgeStore` field. CONFIRMED.
 * `CompiledSponsorLexicon` production constructions = 0 (only its own `static let empty`); all 9 `LexicalScanner(...)` sites use the default `compiledLexicon: nil`. CONFIRMED.
 * `ASRVocabularyProvider` is the wired reader (PlayheadRuntime.swift:841, drifted from :833). CONFIRMED.
 * Field baseline: `sponsor_knowledge_entries` = 0 rows, `knowledge_candidate_events` = 0 rows on db-corrected2 AND on db-vtjxverdict, db-marked, db-night1, db-evening2. `sponsorOnShow` scopes = 0 of 30 correction_events (corrected2/vtjxverdict), 0 of 27 (marked). CONFIRMED, five pulls not one.

ONE CLAIM REFUTED, and it changes what "shape (a)" costs:
 * "The fingerprint sibling IS wired, same function, ten lines below" is WRONG. The overload DISPATCH is there; the ARGUMENT never was. The one production construction of `RegionShadowPhase.Input` (AdDetectionService.swift:4388) passed neither `fingerprintStore` nor `podcastId`, so `AdCopyFingerprintMatcher.match(atoms:podcastId:fingerprintStore:)` also has zero production callers. (a) was therefore not "restore symmetry with a wired sibling" — both siblings were dead, and the missing piece was the CALL SITE, not the field. Filed playhead-3q0k. This bead threaded `podcastId` (the sponsor store needs it as the lookup key) but left `fingerprintStore` nil, so the fingerprint branch is unchanged and still dead.

WHAT (a) ACTUALLY BUYS — say this out loud before anyone reads a corpus delta into it:
 * It changes NO detection on today's corpus. Every device pull has zero sponsor entries, so `activeEntriesWithNegativeMemory` returns [] and `match` exits on its `guard !entries.isEmpty`. q6y3 is what makes the table non-empty for the first time; the first observable effect is on the FIRST episode of a show BACKFILLED AFTER a second press on a second episode of that show. Population: episodes of shows with >=1 `.active` sponsor entry, backfilled after promotion. That population is currently EMPTY.
 * Even on that population, a sponsor match cannot create a span. `AtomEvidenceProjector` reads four origin bits (.foundationModel, .acoustic, .classifier, .sustainedMusic); `.sponsor` is not one of them and `RegionFeatureExtractor` contains zero occurrences of "sponsor". A standalone `.sponsor` region anchors zero atoms => no span => no banner, no mark, no skip. The only reachable effects are (i) UNION-widening a region another origin already anchored, and (ii) `.acoustic` insertion when the sponsor region's edge is within 1.0 s of a break, which sets `hasAcousticBreakHint` and can pull a decoder Use A edge. Atoms are ONE PER CHUNK, so both effects are chunk-granular.
 * So (a) makes the button's second press capable of PROPOSING a region. It does not yet make it capable of moving a skip. Dan's intent is not fully served; the remaining decision is playhead-a1r6.

LEXICAL-AS-ATTENTION: (a) respects it, arguably to a fault. A sponsor name is lexical, and after (a) it can only ever WIDEN or ANNOTATE something another source already found — it never asserts an ad. The certainty-tiered ruling is not even reached, because nothing sponsor-only can decode to a decision at all.

BLAST RADIUS the wiring introduced and closed: `runBackfill`'s catch around `RegionShadowPhase.run` sets `regionBundles = []`, so a throw inside `run` discards the FM/classifier/music/acoustic proposals too. Before this bead `run` could only throw from the unreachable fingerprint branch. The store-backed sponsor read is now caught locally and degrades to `[]` sponsor matches instead of nuking the episode's detection.

TESTS: 5 new, in `SponsorKnowledgeRegionWiringTests` (RegionShadowPhaseIntegrationTests.swift). They drive `AdDetectionService.runBackfill`, not `RegionShadowPhase.run`, because a field existing was never the defect — nothing populating it was. Brand is `Zorbium`, in no shipped lexicon, so a `.sponsor` origin can only come from the store. Covers: active entry proposes (and covers the right atom); ONE press stays `.quarantined` and proposes nothing; an active entry on a DIFFERENT podcast proposes nothing; store not installed proposes nothing; empty podcastId proposes nothing.

GATE: scoped, 3 runs, final on the final tree — 30 requested / 30 reported, 7 suites, 0 failures, 0 XCTest cases (all Swift Testing), `** TEST SUCCEEDED **`, GATE_EXIT=0. Full plan not run (closer's).

Also updated: the `alwaysSkipSponsorReceipt` doc comment in AdBannerView, which asserted ASRVocabularyProvider is the only reader. COPY UNCHANGED — "Remembering …" is still exactly true and is now true for a documented reason.

title: [bug] a show-wide correction labels EVERY scan region of the asset in TrainingExampleMaterializer — and the boost direction is now reachable
description:
NOTICED WHILE FIXING playhead-q6y3, NOT FIXED THERE (out of that bead's scope: it is an offline artifact, not the live decision path).

WITNESS: TrainingExampleMaterializer.correctionOverlaps (Playhead/Services/AdDetection/TrainingExampleMaterializer.swift:392) returns TRUE unconditionally for the five show-wide scopes:

    case .sponsorOnShow, .phraseOnShow, .campaignOnShow,
         .domainOwnershipOnShow, .jingleOnShow:
        // Wider, non-span-bound scopes. They apply to every region of
        // the asset by construction.
        return true

That result feeds the per-scan `corrections` filter at line 159, which then sets BOTH training labels for every scan region of the episode:

    let userReverted = corrections.contains { $0.source?.kind == .falsePositive }
    let userReportedFalseNegative = corrections.contains { $0.source?.kind == .falseNegative }

-> TrainingExampleBucketerSignals -> TrainingExampleBucketer.bucket(...). So ONE show-wide correction stamps a whole episode's training examples with a claim the user made about a sponsor, not about those regions.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE NOW. Until playhead-q6y3 no production writer produced a show-wide FALSE-NEGATIVE, so only the `userReverted` half was reachable and it was at least documented as intended. q6y3 makes the 'Always skip <sponsor> on this show' button write a show-wide .falseNegative, so `userReportedFalseNegative` is now reachable the same way: one tap can label every scan region of the episode 'the user told us we missed an ad here', which is poisonous for exactly the population a future on-device classifier would train on.

Same defect class as playhead-ar60's: a claim about a SPONSOR read as a claim about a POSITION. ar60 fixed it in the live confidence path (CorrectionFactorSnapshot) and q6y3 extended that to the boost direction; this is the third copy of the same read, in the offline artifact path.

NOT URGENT: nothing here touches actuationConfidence, the 0.7 preload floor, or the auto-skip gates. It costs training-label quality, not a skip.

DECISION NEEDED, which is why this is filed rather than fixed: dropping show-wide scopes here changes the SUPPRESS direction's behaviour too, which is long-standing and documented. Options: (a) drop show-wide scopes from both directions (simple, changes shipped FP behaviour), (b) drop them only in the boost direction (mirrors q6y3's asymmetry exactly, leaves the older behaviour alone), (c) keep them but carry the scope kind into the bucketer so the label can say 'asserted show-wide' rather than 'asserted here'.

Related: playhead-q6y3 (the direction fix), playhead-ar60 (the per-span snapshot), playhead-4obf.

title: The clip-outro ("what you just listened to was a most replayed moment") is marked as an ad — recurring, formulaic, self-promo, and it has NO persisted window
description:
GROUND TRUTH, Dan 2026-08-10 on asset 48E903D7: he vetoed 2044.500-2048.820 (4.3s) as a falsePositive and explained it — 'marked as ad in transcript and preceded the postroll but it was actually the host reading his normal end of episode script for this kind of shorter episode (that this episode is a clip of a larger episode that you can listen to)'.

THE ACTUAL TRANSCRIPT at that span (transcript_chunks, 48E903D7):
  2039.3  What you just
  2039.8  listened.
  2040.5  was
  2040.8  a most replayed moment from a previous episode.
  2044.0  If  / you / want  ...

So it is the CLIP OUTRO: the host says this episode is an excerpt and points at the full episode. Three properties, and the pipeline has machinery for each — none of which caught it:
  1. SELF-PROMOTIONAL (the show promoting its own content) -> SelfPromoSuppression exists (SelfPromoSuppressionWireInTests).
  2. RECURRING/FORMULAIC — Dan: 'his NORMAL end of episode script for THIS KIND of shorter episode'. Same words on every clip episode of this show -> the repeated-ad / recurrence catalog and per-show learning exist.
  3. Immediately PRECEDES the post-roll, so it reads as pod-adjacent to anything doing continuation.

FINDING A — the marking has NO PERSISTED WINDOW. Measured on db-corrected2: zero ad_windows rows overlapping 2040-2050 on this asset; zero semantic_scan_results windows overlapping 2040-2050; and ZERO decision_events for ANY window on this asset. Dan could see and veto a marking that the decision path never recorded. Either the transcript view derives markings from something other than ad_windows (a decoded span / candidate that never becomes a window), or the veto deleted the row. EITHER WAY it is a hole in measurement: a marking a user can act on but that leaves no trace is invisible to every precision/recall number this program computes, including the instrumentation playhead-4obf was just re-scoped to build. ESTABLISH THIS FIRST — it may be the more important half.

FINDING B — the doubled-transcript defect is on this asset too. 'was', 'a most replayed moment from a previous episode.', 'If', 'you', 'want' each appear TWICE at identical startTimes. Same shape j4wi measured on DE0784D8 (48 of 104 final-pass chunks verbatim duplicates at identical startTimes). It sits directly under the mis-marked span, and duplicated text plausibly inflates any lexical/recurrence/density signal computed over the window. Related: playhead-h7pr (transcript_chunks.pass mis-tagged). Do not assume causation — measure whether the duplicate chunks are what pushed this span over whatever fired.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE SPAN: this is the ad-gradient case Dan has flagged from the start (project_ad_gradient — ads exist on a skip-worthiness gradient). A show's own outro is the LEAST skip-worthy thing that looks lexically like a promo. It is also cheap recall to protect: it is the same script every time, so a per-show learned exemption should be high-precision.

Corpus context (db-corrected2, 30 corrections / 6 assets): on this episode the deterministic lane auto-skipped the pre-roll CORRECTLY, a semantic-sweep mark at the flat 0.70 constant cost 80s of show (see playhead-92im), the post-roll was MISSED entirely (Dan marked it himself), and this clip-outro was mis-marked. One episode, four distinct behaviours.

title: The user-suppression promotion at SkipOrchestrator:5754 forwards skipConfidence with ZERO test coverage — deleting the argument is invisible and FAILS OPEN
description:
Found by playhead-ar60's R5 closer (F7), filed rather than fixed because the merge-candidate full plan was already in flight. ar60 is now MERGED (#363, 0ad56882), so this is a live gap on shipped code.

THE LINE: SkipOrchestrator.swift:5754, 'skipConfidence: suggested.skipConfidence' in the banner-confirmation promotion. It is a NEW line introduced by ar60's V47 detection/actuation split.

WHY IT MATTERS — its own comment spells out the failure mode: 'nil here would silently PROMOTE a user-suppressed span, because actuationConfidence would then fall back to the (higher) detection score.' That is a FAIL-OPEN on the auto-skip path: a span the user suppressed becomes eligible again, i.e. Playhead skips audio the user said not to skip. Worst-case user harm in this codebase.

THE GAP, measured by R5: 'rg' for promoted.skipConfidence / promoted.actuationConfidence over the ENTIRE test tree returns NOTHING. Three suites (BannerConfirmationExtentGateTests:231/:376, AdPodContinuationFlipTests:682, SkipOrchestratorCharacterizationTests:1453) assert the promotion preserves 'confidence' — the DETECTION half — and none asserts it preserves ACTUATION. Delete the argument today and the whole suite stays green.

This is precisely the failure this repo keeps repeating: a rail proves the mechanism works, not that anyone uses it (see feedback_ask_what_the_quantity_measures, the delete-the-call-site rule). It is also the exact shape of ar60's own F1/F3 findings, one layer up: those were rails reading the column V47 emptied; this is a NEW column with no rail at all.

THE FIX is small and R5 scoped it: one assertion on an existing fixture. Requirements:
1. Assert the promoted window's ACTUATION is preserved (not just confidence).
2. Anti-vacuity control, per R5's own pattern: actuationConfidence FALLS BACK to confidence, so an assertion on it can silently be the old assertion wearing a new name. Lead with '#expect(promoted.skipConfidence != nil)' to prove the fixture produces a two-number row.
3. Prove it load-bearing: delete the 'skipConfidence:' argument at :5754, confirm the new assertion goes RED and the detection-half assertions stay GREEN (so it discriminates direction, not just sensitivity), then restore byte-clean from a pre-mutation copy verified with 'shasum -a 256 -c'. Never 'git checkout -- .'.

Related and worth reading first: playhead-ar60 (merged; the split, the per-span scoping, and R1's show-wide-veto fix), playhead-atr3 (closed; Dan's decision that the 0.7 preload floor reads actuation — which is what makes a fail-open here reach cross-launch continuity), playhead-q6y3 (P0, the inverted 'Always skip this sponsor' direction — an inverted correction plus a fail-open promotion is the bad pair).

comments.text:

my previous comment. Fixed in commit 3aa3ec8d (comments + one failure-message
string only; no expectation expression changed, so the mutation verdict
measured at 27336e13 still holds).

title: semantic-sweep-v1 mints a CONSTANT 0.70 for every mark — 22/22 rows, and it is 2-for-2 wrong on judged episodes
description:
A constant is not a confidence. Measured on the device pull db-corrected2 (2026-08-10):

  detectorVersion       n    min conf              max conf
  detection-v1          74   6.7274513060489565e-06  1.0     <- a real distribution
  semantic-sweep-v1     22   0.7                     0.7     <- ONE value, every row
  userCorrection        12   1.0                     1.0     <- correct, an assertion
  pod-continuation-v1    7   0.4644130636211205      0.7

Every semantic-sweep mark carries exactly 0.70. Minted at SemanticSweepMarkComposer.swift:143 (static let markConfidence = 0.70), deliberately pinned to SkipOrchestrator.preloadConfidenceThreshold — i.e. the value is chosen to CLEAR THE GATE, not to describe the evidence. Same pattern in SpecialistMarkComposer.swift:66 and AdPodContinuation.swift:209 (three detectors mint a flat 0.70, outranking detection-v1's calibrated 0.40-0.47).

GROUND TRUTH, now 2 for 2 AGAINST on the episodes Dan has judged:
- F4CE7F47 9:50-11:19 (89.4s), sweep @ 0.70 -> Dan vetoed it (playhead-3gzp).
- 48E903D7 596.3-676.6 (80.3s), sweep @ 0.70, semanticSweepMark -> Dan vetoed it 2026-08-10 10:32:40.
That is ~170 seconds of SHOW proposed for removal by this detector across two episodes, with zero confirmed hits. N=2 decides nothing on its own, but the flat constant means the number can never separate the good marks from the bad ones — there is no signal in it to threshold on.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE AFTER ar60/atr3: the 0.70 is pinned to the preload floor, and Dan's atr3 decision made that floor read ACTUATION. A sweep mark therefore still exactly clears the floor unless a user correction deflates it — so the constant is load-bearing for cross-launch continuity, not just for banners.

WHAT TO ESTABLISH FIRST (do not just pick a formula):
1. What evidence does the sweep actually have per mark? The 3gzp establish found candidates: certainty x pass agreement x transcriptQuality — and noted the 590s F4CE7F47 FP came from DEGRADED-quality rows, which a real confidence would have reflected.
2. Does any consumer depend on the value being exactly 0.70? Grep before changing it — the pin to preloadConfidenceThreshold is deliberate and documented, so a derived value may drop marks out of preload, which is a REACH change and Dan's call.
3. Report the would-be distribution over the existing 22 rows before shipping, so the change is measured rather than argued.

Related: playhead-3gzp (where the constant was first established), playhead-4obf (emission floor — re-scoped by Dan to 'instrument first'; this bead is the same shape: make the number mean something before thresholding on it), feedback_ask_what_the_quantity_measures (what would this read if the thing it claims to measure never happened? 0.70, always).

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED on bead/playhead-92im (base a9a09f01). Seven commits; scoped gate GREEN.

ESTABLISH — the evidence WAS there, unread. Every `containsAd` scan row carries the model's own `CertaintyBand` inside `semantic_scan_results.spansJSON` (`{"supportLineRefs":[17,18,20],"certainty":"strong"}` for passA; an array of refined spans each with a band for passB). 55/55 coarse + 11/11 refined rows on db-vtjxverdict, split 40 strong / 15 moderate. The composer never read it. So the old comment's premise -- "the coarse lane produces a categorical verdict, not a score" -- was false of the persisted rows.

Two more per-mark signals, also unread: `transcriptQuality` (36 good / 19 degraded over coarse containsAd rows) and REPLICATE AGREEMENT -- 36 of 125 coarse windows carry >1 passA row, each a separate FM call in a separate run (distinct runCorrelationId, distinct latency), and on 4 windows `containsAd` is the MINORITY verdict.

THE 3gzp CLAIM HOLDS. F4CE7F47 590-679 is `degraded` on all four passA replicates AND its passB refinement; 48E903D7 596-677 likewise. Both are the marks Dan vetoed (correction_events confirms sweep-8028f2402a7801ba and sweep-7b7ad2e5538c382b as manualVeto/falsePositive).

WHAT SHIPPED. confidence = 0.70 (unchanged CEILING) x certaintyFactor x transcriptQualityFactor x corroborationFactor. The band and quality ladders are BORROWED from `buildFMLedgerEntries`' existing fmCap x {1, .75, .5} over the same enum, not invented. Corroboration is Laplace-smoothed (1+affirming)/(1+affirming+dissenting) over presence-pass replicates -- it can only DEDUCT, so unanimity is never a bonus and absence of dissent never reads as corroboration. Merged extents take the duration-weighted mean by INTERPOLATION. Nothing can exceed the old constant: the change is monotone non-increasing.

DISTRIBUTION over all 22 pull rows (numerator = sweep marks graded from the presence rows overlapping each one; denominator = the 22 persisted `semantic-sweep-v1` rows): min 0.047, p25 0.467, median 0.616, max 0.700, 12 distinct values. >=0.70: 6/22. >=0.525: 13/22. >=0.50: 16/22. >=0.40: 20/22. The composer independently REPRODUCES 19 of the 22 by geometry; the other 3 are stale marks whose backing rows changed after they were written.

CONSEQUENCE FOR YOU, NOT DECIDED HERE. 16 of 22 fall below `preloadConfidenceThreshold`, so they would no longer hydrate on the next launch; 6 of 22 fall below `FinalPassRetranscriptionRunner.defaultConfidenceFloor` (0.50) and would no longer earn a final-pass re-transcription. The transcript overlay's "AD n%" label stops reading a constant 70%. atr3's threshold is untouched. Both vetoed marks grade 0.467 with 16 of 22 above them -- which is NOT evidence the grade separates good from bad at N=2. The claim is only that there is now something in the number to separate on.

REVIEW ROUND CAUGHT A REBUILT BUG. `PermissiveAdClassifier` HARDCODES `certainty: .strong` on the permissive bypass, and 9 of the 11 refined containsAd spans in the pull are permissive. Reading those as the model's grade returned the CEILING factor for a verdict nothing graded -- this bead's own bug, on the population where it bites hardest. Now gated on `ownershipInferenceWasSuppressed`, the same flag the sponsor-memory writers already have to respect. The COARSE half of that fabrication is undetectable at rest (`usedPermissiveFallback` has no column) and is filed separately.

SCOPE CALLS. SpecialistMarkComposer and AdPodContinuation do NOT share the defect and the bead's premise there is wrong: the specialist's 0.70 is a decision THRESHOLD (tau) and its confidence is `probabilityOfAd`; pod-continuation's is a CAP on an inherited seed confidence, and its 7 pull rows span 0.464-0.70. Filed as playhead-4f3h (they are CENSORED at the gate value from opposite sides, which is milder and blocked on the same tiering decision).

ALSO FILED: playhead-yx0f -- `buildFMLedgerEntries` fabricates a CertaintyBand out of transcriptQuality ("use it as a band proxy") while the model's real band sits unread in the same row, making the `.strong`/fmCap branch dead code for 40 of 55 rows.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
DAN'S TIERING DECISION 2026-08-10: SHIP AS-IS. The honest grade drops 16 of 22 sweep marks below the 0.70 cross-launch preload floor and 6 of 22 below the 0.50 final-pass floor, and that consequence is ACCEPTED. Rationale: the 0.70 was chosen to CLEAR the gate, not to describe evidence, so marks that only ever cleared it by fiat should stop clearing it. preloadConfidenceThreshold itself is untouched (atr3's settled territory). The grade is monotone non-increasing — nothing can exceed the old constant — which is the right direction for a detector that is 2-for-2 wrong on judged episodes (~170s of SHOW proposed for removal, zero confirmed hits).

HONEST LIMIT, recorded so nobody over-claims later: both vetoed marks grade 0.467 with 16 of 22 ABOVE them. At N=2 that is NOT evidence the grade separates good marks from bad. The claim this bead supports is only that there is now something IN the number to separate on — a constant could never separate anything. Whether the grade actually predicts correctness is 4obf's question (re-scoped by Dan to instrument-first) and needs more judged episodes.

title: AnalysisJobReconciler.discoverUnEnqueuedDownloads mints analysis_jobs with podcastId: nil, and every re-mint inherits it
description:
Found while fixing playhead-vtjx; OUT OF SCOPE for that bead (vtjx repairs the column at the coarse-scan read, which is enough for its four assets).

AnalysisJobReconciler.discoverUnEnqueuedDownloads (Playhead/Services/PreAnalysis/AnalysisJobReconciler.swift:746, struct at :767, hardcoded 'podcastId: nil' at :771) is Step 7 of the reconciler and runs on every reconcile pass, including every half-hourly BG sweep. It enumerates downloadManager.allCachedEpisodeIds() minus store.fetchActiveJobEpisodeIds() — pure on-disk/SQLite state with no SwiftData in scope — so it structurally cannot name a show and mints an UNATTRIBUTED row every time.

That matters because it is not merely a NULL: every re-mint path copies job.podcastId verbatim (AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:5225 tier successor, :6435 ad-scan re-drive, :6721 canonical-audio replacement; AnalysisJobReconciler.swift:655 enqueueReplacement, :1103 capOutRetry, :1667 adScanRedriveCandidate), so one nil at mint time propagates through the entire tier ladder, cap-out retries, re-drives and stale-fingerprint replacements for that episode.

WITNESSES (db-evening, 2026-08-08): NULL rows are still being minted well after playhead-kkzu closed the download path on 2026-08-03 — five on 2026-08-06 in two same-second batches (00:56:26 x3, 01:14:17 x2, the batch signature of a sweep rather than a download), plus singles through 2026-08-08 10:00:17. Of 72 analysis_jobs rows, 53 carry SQL NULL.

WHY IT IS NOT ALREADY FATAL AFTER vtjx: vtjx switched the coarse-scan read to AnalysisStore.fetchRecordedPodcastId(forEpisodeId:) (AnalysisStore.swift:9397), which filters 'podcastId IS NOT NULL' and orders by createdAt, so a fresh sweep NULL can no longer shadow an attributed row. Anything still reading fetchLatestJobForEpisode(_:)?.podcastId CAN be shadowed — that query has no NULL filter and orders by updatedAt. Live instances: AnalysisJobReconciler.swift:1551 (the noCoverageLaneRow claim mint), RediffRefetchProduction.swift:521, and AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:4759 via job.podcastId ?? "".

LIKELY FIX (cheap, same store, no cross-store hop): have discoverUnEnqueuedDownloads mint with 'try store.fetchRecordedPodcastId(forEpisodeId: episodeId)' rather than nil — for an episode that already has any attributed row that is a real identity recovered from the lane's own record, and nil stays honestly nil otherwise. Consider auditing the three fetchLatestJobForEpisode podcastId readers above at the same time.

title: ForceQuitResume scan can hang the entire Swift Testing phase indefinitely — no time limit fires
description:
Two consecutive PlayheadFastTests full-plan runs on 2026-08-08 (worktree j4wi, tip 1a7f263c) hung the same way: the XCTest phase completed in ~4 min, then the Swift Testing phase sat for 90+ minutes accruing ~2.5% CPU with zero test output. A 2s `sample` of the test host (saved at scratchpad/j4wi-simhost-sample.txt in session bee44b12) shows every busy thread inside:

  DownloadManager.backgroundDownload(episodeId:from:context:) — DownloadManager.swift:2424
  via DownloadManager.resumeSuspendedTransfer(episodeId:) — ForceQuitResumeScan.swift:512 and :524

No Swift Testing time limit ever fired (the load-flake families cap at 60s; this ran >90min). The hang recurred on a SECOND fresh run of the same plan, then did not recur after `simctl erase` of the shared device — consistent with the force-quit-resume scan reacting to suspended-download residue that earlier interrupted runs left in the simulator, and then blocking in a way structured cancellation/time limits cannot interrupt.

Two questions for the fix:
1. Why does a poisoned/suspended transfer make resumeSuspendedTransfer block forever rather than fail? (Production concern too: a real force-quit with a half-suspended URLSession transfer may hit the same loop on device.)
2. Why does no test-level time limit bound it? If the block is a non-cooperative wait (semaphore/runloop spin) the 60s limit cannot cancel it, and one such test starves the whole in-process parallel phase — the gate then wedges with the exact signature of the disk-wedge (alive, zero output, no exit), which scripts/disk_preflight.py exists to prevent for the disk case.

Repro state is destroyed by sim erase (that is the workaround: DEVELOPER_DIR=Xcode-beta xcrun simctl shutdown all && simctl erase <udid>). Related: the ForceQuitResume load-flake family (gate-baseline), be3s/2x8z test-health cleanup.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
ESCALATION — the hang now blocks the closer gate reliably, and erasing the simulator only downgrades it. Evidence from the playhead-absa closer, 2026-08-10, two consecutive full-plan runs on the same tree.

RUN 1 — the classic indefinite hang.
  - log byte-static for 918 s starting immediately after '[ForceQuitResume] resumeSuspendedTransfer:'
  - sim host flat at ~5% CPU (1.6 s per 30 s, sampled 19 times)
  - 10,022 Swift Testing tests STARTED and ZERO completed — not one 'passed after' line in the whole log
  - 'sample' of the sim host: main thread parked in -[XCTWaiter waitForExpectations:timeout:enforceOrder:] inside XCTAsyncEnumerateWithWaiter, i.e. the XCTest driver waiting on a Swift Testing phase that never reports
  - killed (own pid verified via lsof cwd), wrapper self-diagnosed correctly: '** BUILD INTERRUPTED **', 'gate-baseline: CANNOT EVALUATE — the log is incomplete', GATE_EXIT=143

RUN 2, after 'simctl shutdown all' + 'simctl erase 19B59D40-...' — SAME underlying failure, one notch less severe. Last Swift Testing event 20:46:33; for the next 62 s the app logged only a 2-second-cadence Capabilities poll on a single thread; then XCTest's watchdog relaunched the host ('Restarting after unexpected exit, crash, or test timeout').

SO THE DOCUMENTED RECOVERY DOES NOT RECOVER. It converts an indefinite hang into a watchdog restart. That is better — the run terminates — but it is not a fix, and the run it produces is not a verdict.

WHAT THAT COSTS, measured: the surviving run reported 'RED (6 known / 22 NEW)' while '76 of 83 recorded tests were never reached'. So the headline verdict covers about 8% of the recorded population. The closer confirmed the shortfall is real rather than a restart-parsing artifact by finding tests with a start line and no completion anywhere ('Backfill completes successfully', 'Backfill handler invokes real work method, not startCapabilityObserver'). A gate that cannot reach 92% of its own baseline cannot answer the question it exists to answer.

FREQUENCY: this fired on the cnql closer (run 2 of 3), the d666 closer (run 1 of 2), and both absa closer runs. Four occurrences in one day across three unrelated branches, none of which touches ForceQuitResume. It is not branch-correlated.

WHY THIS IS NOW WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN WORKING AROUND: the documented workaround costs a full-plan run (5-15 min) plus a simulator erase every time, and as of today it no longer produces a usable verdict even when it 'works'. Three closers in a row have had to reason around an inconclusive gate, and each time the merge decision rested on scoped runs plus review rounds instead. That is the mechanism playhead-voez built the baseline check to remove.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
DIAGNOSIS ESTABLISHED, both questions answered from the sample the bead already carried (scratchpad/j4wi-simhost-sample.txt). Fix on bead/playhead-nsjn (f64067c2, 40b57ccb).

Q1 — the blocking primitive. `URLSession.downloadTask(with:)` / `downloadTask(withResumeData:)` on a BACKGROUND session is `-[__NSURLBackgroundSession _downloadTaskWithTaskForClass:]` -> `performBlockOnQueueAndRethrowExceptions:` -> a dispatch BARRIER on the session's serial work queue -> `xpc_connection_send_message_with_reply_sync` to `nsurlsessiond` -> `mach_msg2_trap`. Synchronous XPC; no suspension point, no cancellation point. `DownloadManager` is an actor, so it runs on the cooperative pool — width == activeProcessorCount == 10 on this box, and it never grows. The sample shows exactly 10 of 10 cooperative threads in that chain: one holding the barrier inside the XPC wait (labelled `com.apple.NSURLSession-work` because dispatch_sync ran the block inline on the caller's thread), nine in `_dispatch_event_loop_wait_for_ownership` behind it. Zero runnable concurrency in the process. Not a ForceQuitResume bug — five different suites appear in that sample (ResumeSuspendedTransfer, DownloadShowAttribution x3, StreamingDownloadCached), which is why it was never branch-correlated.

Q2 — why nothing bounded it. Two independent reasons. (a) The tests that actually blocked have NO `.timeLimit` at all: `ResumeSuspendedTransferTests` and `DownloadShowAttributionTests` declare none. (b) The limits that DO exist could not fire: `.timeLimit` is a task-group race against `Task.sleep`, and the sleep's continuation needs a cooperative thread to run on. With all 10 blocked, the timer is enqueued and never dequeued. Even had it fired, cancellation only sets a flag that a suspension point must observe, and there is none inside the blocked region. So the limit is not merely ineffective — it never runs. This also explains the escalation's run 2: after a `simctl erase` only ONE call stalls rather than ten, the pool survives, and XCTest's own watchdog (which is not a Swift Concurrency mechanism) is the thing that eventually terminates the host.

FIX. `BackgroundSessionIO` runs each such call on a dedicated non-cooperative serial queue under a wall-clock bound (10 s), so a stalled daemon strands one ordinary thread instead of the pool, the caller suspends cooperatively, and an unanswered call becomes a named outcome. A late answer goes to a discard hook (`cancel()`) rather than being dropped — otherwise it leaves an untracked live transfer, which is the residue class that poisons the next run. `backgroundDownload` is now `async` (every caller already awaited this actor method) and reserves its in-flight slot before the new suspension point; `resumeSuspendedTransfer` gained `.daemonUnavailable`, which RETAINS the blob because it is the only copy of the bytes already fetched.

VERIFICATION. scripts/lint.sh clean (whole repo). Scoped gate over all 45 download + feed-refresh suites: 226 tests, 45 of 45 requested suites reported, TEST SUCCEEDED, GATE_EXIT=0.

NOT DONE, filed. playhead-ola7 (P1) — background session CREATION (`URLSession(configuration: .background(...))`) still runs inline on the actor and is the FIRST thing both fixed paths do, so if it blocks the new bound is bypassed entirely; nobody has measured whether it does, and that measurement should precede any refactor. playhead-ornc (P2) — the suite registers real transfers with the simulator's `nsurlsessiond` on three process-global identifiers, which is the residue `simctl erase` was working around.

title: pod lexical anchors die before fusion: URL catalog has no .ai TLD, 'head to'/'our sponsor called' missing, and the 5s decoder floor drops sub-5s single-atom anchors
description:
Established in playhead-j4wi item 2 on episode DE0784D8 (116s host-read pod, 0 detected). The pod's ad copy produced exactly ONE catalog-matchable string and zero surviving anchors:

- creative 1 (WhisperFlow, 59.76s): NOTHING matches. 'whisperflow.ai' — EvidenceCatalogBuilder URL patterns cover .com/.co/.org/.io only (EvidenceCatalogBuilder.swift:748-760), no .ai and no spoken 'dot ai'. CTA 'head to whisperflow.ai' — only 'head over to' is a pattern. Disclosure 'because of our sponsor called Whisper Flow' — not in the disclosure list.
- creative 2 (Ketone-IQ, 55.02s): 'go to ketone.com slash' DOES match and anchors its atom — but the atom is 3.60s wide (chunk 2940.84-2944.44) with unanchored neighbours, and MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder drops spans under minDurationSeconds=5 (DecodedSpan.swift:137, step 5 DROP). The only true anchor in 116s of ad dies as a micro-fragment, while a FALSE disclosure hit 2s before the pod survived because its host chunk happened to be 8.04s.

The floor is doing its precision job (single 3.6s URL fragments alone SHOULD NOT become 5s spans) — the miss is that a dropped anchor leaves no trace for anything else to consume; see j4wi item 3 (fragment->targeted FM scan) and playhead-hp70 for the consumption side. Lexicon side is cheap and measurable: add .ai/.co/.fm/.tv TLDs + spoken forms, 'head to', 'our sponsor called'; re-run the corpus eval before/after (lexical = attention, never verdict). Live regression pin already exists: DE0784D8MidRollPodRegressionTests.ketoneURLAnchorIsDroppedByMinimumDuration fails loudly when any of this is fixed.
notes:
playhead-absa measurement limitation, recorded 2026-08-10 for whoever measures the next lexicon term. The corpus used is the 2026-08-02 device pull (94,692 transcript_chunks, 31 assets, fast + final) and it is NOT show-diverse: 23 of the 31 assets are Diary of a CEO via the same flightcast feed, 5 are one anchor.fm show, 3 libsyn. So a per-term false-positive count of 0 means 'zero on THIS show mix', not 'zero on podcasts'. Concretely: 40 of the 44 .ai hits are one advertiser (NetSuite) read on eight DoaC episodes, and all 12 .co hits are one advertiser (MarketReach) on one show. That is why 'support for' was rejected on 0/6 rather than on a principle — the public-radio disclosure form 'support for X comes from' would have had NO true positives to find in this corpus either, so its rejection here is evidence about bare 'support for', not about the public-radio family.
IMPLEMENTED on branch bead/playhead-absa, commit de0e716c (not yet pushed / no PR).

Shipped: URL patterns .ai (path + bare + spoken 'dot ai'), .co (bare + spoken), .fm and .tv (path + bare + spoken); ctaPhrase 'head to'; disclosurePhrase 'our sponsor called'; brandStem separator list extended in step so a .ai/.fm/.tv URL seeds a brand stem.

Measured REJECT: 'support for' (0 of 6 corpus matches in an ad). Out of scope, filed: playhead-04rx (first-occurrence dedup silences repeat mentions, +11 spans / +50% at stake) and playhead-onnk (.org/.io have no bare-domain pattern; 1 measured ad invisible).

The pod itself still decodes NOTHING and that is the intended outcome. Creative 1's three new anchors form runs of 2.22 s and 4.14 s, creative 2's ketone.com 3.60 s — all under DecoderConstants.minDurationSeconds. The floor was left alone. Consuming a dropped fragment remains j4wi item 3 / playhead-hp70.

Regression pin ketoneURLAnchorIsDroppedByMinimumDuration was INVERTED consciously: its 'creative 1 produces zero anchoring evidence' expectation is now false, so it names the three anchors individually and asserts each still dies at the floor. livePipelineReproducesSeamFPAndPodHole (one span, nothing in the pod) is unchanged and now a stronger statement.

title: fusion emission chain manufactures a mis-readable confirmed row: asset-WIDE correction blanket + ad_windows.confidence=skipConfidence + detectOnly->confirmed
description:
Established in playhead-j4wi item 2 on episode DE0784D8; splitting the FIX out since j4wi is establish-only. Three stacked mechanisms, each individually defensible, jointly producing a row Dan had to veto:

1. correctionFactor is ASSET-SCOPED ('Queried once per backfill run (not per span)', AdDetectionService.swift:4592-4600): three falsePositive vetoes at 210/2670/4800 collapsed skipConfidence for EVERY span in the episode, including spans 2600s away with independent evidence. Witness: decision_events for all 5 fusion windows drop to 3.1e-07..5.1e-07 at 2026-08-01 15:24:40 (7s after ONE veto), then churn back to ~0.004 by 08-02 with zero new evidence.
2. buildFusionAdWindow writes decision.skipConfidence into ad_windows.confidence (AdDetectionService.swift:8779) while proposalConfidence (0.456 here) goes to metadataConfidence and is later overwritten by the metadata fallback (0.1). Every reader of ad_windows.confidence sees the actuation number as the detection number: the UI showed 'conf 0.00' on a span it also called confirmed.
3. detectOnly persists as decisionState='confirmed' unconditionally (buildFusionAdWindow: 'logOnly and detectOnly: always confirmed') and the fusion path has NO emission floor, so a 0.00115-actuation span still ships as a confirmed row.

Candidate fixes to weigh (not decided): per-span or per-neighbourhood correction scoping; a separate persisted proposalConfidence column so confidence stops being two quantities; an emission floor or a decisionState that is not 'confirmed' for detectOnly. Related: playhead-pggn (dilution, per-region), playhead-mfeq (the UNTYPEABLE program — this is a live instance of shape 'two quantities share a column'). Fixture coverage already exists: DE0784D8MidRollPodRegressionTests.frozenFalsePositiveShape pins the shipped shape.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED (branch bead/playhead-ar60, 6e5923e7..8ad726c4). All three mechanisms FIXED; the general emission floor DEFERRED and filed as playhead-4obf with measured evidence.

== ESTABLISH, re-derived from the pulls (not from the bead summary) ==
* 40 of 104 ad_windows rows on the 2026-08-02 pull (38.5%) carried an ACTUATION number in a column that means DETECTION for the other six producers. 48/107 on the evening pull. Every one is a fusion row.
* 40/40 lost proposalConfidence completely: metadataConfidence was overwritten by the metadata extractor on ALL of them (28 at the 0.1 fallback, 12 at 0.3). The detection number was NOT recoverable from ad_windows.
* It IS recoverable from decision_events: 40/40 and 48/48 rows have an event whose skipConfidence is BIT-IDENTICAL to the row's confidence, and NO non-fusion row matches that join.
* The blanket, witnessed: within each run the ratio skipConfidence/proposalConfidence is bit-identical across all five DE0784D8 windows (0.00252168501165 -> 8.16025237649e-07 -> 1.77560023944e-05 -> 0.00683 -> 0.00708) while each window's own proposalConfidence never moved a bit. A per-span quantity cannot have a per-asset ratio.
* CORRECTION TO THE BEAD'S SUMMARY: the 15:24:40 collapse followed FIVE falsePositive vetoes, not three. The three at 210/2670/4800 produced the 00:42:34 factor (0.0025); the 60.06 and 2828.40 vetoes (15:23:34 and 15:24:33) produced the 8.16e-07 one. And the 385x recovery to ~0.0068 by 08-02 06:11 came from DECAY plus two falseNegative marks, with zero new evidence at any of the five spans.
* THE BIGGER HALF WAS THE BOOST DIRECTION, which the bead does not mention: on another asset two marks nearly DOUBLED seven spans they did not overlap (proposal 0.35-0.66 -> persisted 0.69-1.00), and FIVE of them crossed SkipOrchestrator's 0.7 preload floor on inflation alone. That floor's own comment calls itself "a DETECTOR-confidence filter".
* 8/40 rows sit on a corrected asset and overlap NO correction (the ar60 population). 13/40 carry a persisted number different from their own detection number.

== DECISIONS ==
1. Correction blanket -> PER-SPAN, via a new CorrectionFactorSnapshot. ONE store query per backfill (the property the old "not per span, for performance" comment protected) + a pure per-span evaluation. Span-scoped corrections apply where they overlap; SHOW-WIDE scopes (sponsorOnShow, phraseOnShow, ...) still apply everywhere, the same split correctionBoostFactor(for:overlapping:) already draws. An UNPLACEABLE correction acts in the direction that cannot cost a skip the user did not ask for: a suppressor everywhere (its exact pre-ar60 reach), a booster nowhere.
2. Two quantities -> TWO COLUMNS, schema V47. `confidence` becomes the DETECTION number for ALL SEVEN producers (six already wrote it); new nullable `skipConfidence` carries actuation; `actuationConfidence == skipConfidence ?? confidence` keeps every one-number producer and every pre-V47 row byte-identical. buildFusionAdWindow also stops squatting on metadataConfidence (that column gates AdBannerView's advertiser name at 0.60 and the extractor overwrote it anyway).
   Migration V47 is a pure MOVE joined against decision_events — no value is invented, an unmatched row is untouched. Verified against the real corpus: 40 repaired, 64 untouched and bit-identical, 0 non-fusion touched, second pass 0 changes.
3. detectOnly -> `.suppressed` when the gate is blockedByUserCorrection, `.confirmed` otherwise. Deliberately narrow: every OTHER blocked gate still banners, because those are the system's uncertainty and the banner is a skip affordance. The general EMISSION FLOOR is NOT taken here -- 13/40 fusion rows have detection < 0.40 and suppressing a third of the emitted population is a REACH decision. Filed as playhead-4obf with the distribution.

== READERS, all grepped ==
Rerouted to actuationConfidence: evaluateWindow (the auto-skip policy), the AdWindow->AdDecisionResult projection, BOTH producer-revision envelope equalities, AdDetectionService's post-clamp rebind, and the decision LOG (which was recording a number ~400x from the one the decision used). Left on confidence, now honest, each with a comment saying why: the 0.7 preload floor, both cue-window gates, FinalPassRetranscriptionRunner's floor, catalog + repeated-ad learning, TranscriptPeek's "AD n%", both exporters (which now emit BOTH). producerRevisionToken, the runtime ingest door, validWindow, every copy-with, and the cross-user wire (bumped 4 -> 5, because without the bump `nil` means both "one-number producer" and "a pre-ar60 peer put actuation here").

== VERIFICATION ==
Scoped gate, 25 requested / 25 reported (24 Swift Testing suites + 1 XCTest class): 406 + 13 tests, 0 failures in EITHER format, ** TEST SUCCEEDED **, exit 0. Repo-wide constant: currentSchemaVersion 46 -> 47, all 11 literal pins across 10 files updated (grepped scripts/, docs/, .py, .json too — none). lint --changed clean on 31 files.

Adversarial review found 13 items; the one blocker-class was MINE: the snapshot dropped FP corrections it could not place (real-ordinal .exactSpan, undecodable scopes), which correctionPassthroughFactor never did -- a fail-OPEN on the veto path. Closed. Also closed: the idempotence test tested the version guard rather than the WHERE clause; the entire SkipOrchestrator half was mutation-survivable (no test built an AdWindow whose two confidences DIFFER); the migration's ORDER BY lacked a rowid tiebreaker and its predicate was in only one of two halves.

RESIDUAL, not fixed: no coverage for the cross-user skipConfidence round-trip, the CorpusExporter key, or producerRevisionToken's new component. A show-wide veto can now suppress a whole episode's banners (unreachable today: zero show-wide scopes in either pull) -- recorded in the code at the mechanism-3 site.

title: Day-0 rediff: ONE -1001 fetch timeout at download darkens the deterministic pre-roll lane for the whole first-day listen (24h backoff; ug9m rescue excludes zero-mark assets; lagged sweep 3-day gated)
description:
Witness (device pull db-marked, 2026-08-06, asset F4CE7F47 = the playhead-3gzp ground-truth episode):

rediff_day_zero_attempts[F4CE7F47]: attemptCount=1, lastExit=fetch_failed, lastDetail=NSURLErrorDomain -1001 "The request timed out.", lastMarkCount=0, lastFullFetchBytes=0, suppressedCount=2, lastSuppressedAt=2026-08-06 09:38:35 (MID-LISTEN), rescueAttemptCount=0, policyGeneration=2. rediff_refetch_state: no row.

Timeline: download 01:01, kickoff fired 01:02 (kickoffCount=1 fired=1, waited 120.4s), fetch timed out; Dan listened 09:26-09:39 the same morning; both re-drive requests during the listen were suppressed by DayZeroRediffAttemptPolicy backoff.

Why no mechanism catches this today (all three are BY DESIGN, and their intersection is the hole):
1. RediffDayZeroOutcome.swift classifies fetchFailed RETRYABLE, but DayZeroRediffAttemptPolicy.baseBackoff = 24h (maxAttempts=3/generation) - so the retry structurally lands AFTER any day-0 listen. A timeout costs ~0 bytes, yet pays the same backoff as a full failed diff.
2. The ug9m rescue (rescueAttemptCount, DayZeroMarkCensus) is scoped to assets that ALREADY have day-0 marks ("an asset with ZERO day-0 rows is not a rescue case") - a zero-mark fetch_failed asset is outside it by construction.
3. The lagged sweep backstop is >=3-day gated (RediffRefetchPolicy), useless for first-day listens.

What it cost, measured (playhead-3gzp): the audited corpus's ONLY correct actioned skip is a day-0 byte-exact pre-roll (CDD611C4 0-27.62, conf 1.0, applied+skipped); the same lane produced 0-45.11 (D9B513CD) and 0-60.13 (DE0784D8). On F4CE7F47 the lane went dark on this one timeout, leaving the FM lane's two wrong-width pre-roll candidates (0-96.84 @0.70, 0-120 @0.4024, both markOnly/unanchored) as the only voice - Dan experienced the pre-roll as MISSED and both marks as false positives. 9-10 of the 11-12 audited real ad spans are OUTER; this lane is the only conf-1.0 detector for exactly that population.

Decision, not implementation (Dan's call on shape): a cheap same-session retry ONLY for exits that spent ~zero bytes (fetch_failed before any B-copy landed), vs. a shorter backoff tier for zero-cost failures, vs. retry-at-play-start when lastExit=fetch_failed and the listen is day-0. Any shape must not reopen the p70f replay bleed - the 24h backoff exists because day-0 once cost 108MB per replay; a timed-out fetch spent 0 bytes, which is the distinction the policy currently cannot see (an exit that names "failure" being read as if it named "bandwidth spent" - the standing defect class again).

Related: playhead-p70f (closed; created the attempt/backoff machinery), playhead-ug9m (rescue, different population), playhead-4dqe (closed; day-0 at download time), playhead-j4wi (the INNER miss counterpart).

Shape (i) as approved: DayZeroRediffAttemptPolicy.grantsSameSessionRetry — pure, granted ONLY on exit==.fetchFailed AND measured landed bytes==0 (sum of completed B-copy byteCounts; reads 0 if the fetch never started), bounded to 1 retry @30s (bound derived from maxAttempts=3: attempt+retry leaves one budgeted attempt for a later >=24h session; 30s sits inside the observed 20.7-507s session envelope from the device pull). Durable claim per fil5: V46 adds retryClaimCount/lastRetryClaimAt to rediff_day_zero_attempts, written BEFORE the delay; lastRetryClaimAt > lastAttemptAt is the queryable dropped-retry signature. Witness re-derived from db-marked: F4CE7F47 attemptCount=1 fetch_failed lastFullFetchBytes=0 suppressedCount=2 lastSuppressedAt=09:38:35 policyGeneration=2; kickoff waited 120.4s. Re-derived the zero-byte predicate (measuredFullFetchBytes = sum of COMPLETED B-copy byteCounts; never-started and mid-transfer-death both read 0, any landed copy reads >=54MB and declines — p70f bleed stays closed, double-gated because a post-fetch diff failure carries a non-fetchFailed exit AND non-zero bytes).
