title: [blocker] the mutation battery cannot reach a verdict: its FOCUSED_SUITES baseline is RED from starvation, 41 tests, none diff-related
description:
Found driving playhead-y8a3 R3, 2026-08-07. Blocks every mutation verdict in this repo, not just this bead.

scripts/mutation-battery.sh refuses to run any batch unless the ENTIRE FOCUSED_SUITES set (~150 suites in one xcodebuild invocation) is green first — correctly, because a red baseline would credit every mutation KILLED for a reason unrelated to the mutation. That baseline is currently unattainable on this box.

MEASURED, two runs on the same commit:
  run 1 (13:25, DTServiceHub wedged at 97% CPU for 2h44m): 16 failures
  run 2 (13:44, after xcrun simctl shutdown all, box quiet):  41 failures
Overlap is partial — the churn signature CLAUDE.md documents at Jaccard 0.46. Note run 2 was QUIETER and had MORE failures, so the driver is the baseline run's own in-process concurrency, not external load.

PROOF THEY ARE STARVATION, NOT REGRESSIONS: the seven suites owning run 1's red tests — BackfillExpiryDurabilityTests, BackfillSchedulerBoundingTests, DrainEligibleStartGateTests, ExpiredWindowAttemptAccountingTests, ShadowRetryTests, SkipOrchestratorRevertLifecycleRaceTests, SkipOrchestratorRevertTests — pass 125/125 with exit 0 when run scoped on the same commit.

The families are the ones CLAUDE.md already names as PerfGate candidates: grant/window expiry accounting, revert calibration, capability observer, ledger writes, scheduler timeouts. Only 3 of the 16 in run 1 are recorded in scripts/gate-baseline.PlayheadFastTests.json.

CONSEQUENCE: rails can be anchor-verified (--dry-run proves they apply exactly once) but cannot be proven KILLED. playhead-y8a3 shipped 5 new SY rails with dry-run verification only, for this reason.

FIX DIRECTIONS (a decision for Dan, since it is a coverage tradeoff):
  a) PerfGate the load-sensitive families out of FOCUSED_SUITES — the deferred step CLAUDE.md already describes.
  b) Give the battery a baseline TOLERANCE, reusing scripts/gate_baseline.py's known-broken machinery, so it refuses only on failures inside the rail's own expectation set.
  c) Shrink FOCUSED_SUITES so the baseline is a set that actually holds green.
notes:
FOURTH INDEPENDENT MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-07 16:32, playhead-wxsv, commit 5275c8c4, `--batch 575`: baseline RED with 6 failures.

  ✘ Test F: observer waits 60s of stable FM=true before draining; cancels on flip  (ShadowRetryTests)
  ✘ H2: wake() drains immediately when capability is already stable-true            (ShadowRetryTests)
  ✘ five expired windows in a row still leave the job alive                         (BackgroundGrantBudgetTests)
  ✘ awaitJobsSettled waits for a running job and times out rather than lying        (BackgroundGrantBudgetTests)
  ✘ stale Auto-Yes cannot commit after durable material changes mid-suspension      (SkipOrchestratorRevertTests)
  ✘ stale suggest completion cannot clear replacement provisional ownership         (SkipOrchestratorRevertTests)

Three suites, all three already named in this bead's families (capability observer, grant/window expiry accounting + awaitJobsSettled, revert calibration). Run counts across five observations on four different commits: 16, 41, 13, 6, and the sets differ every time. Nothing in the wxsv diff touches any of the three suites.

wxsv proceeded under `PLAYHEAD_MB_SKIP_BASELINE=1` after (a) running its own four suites scoped and green (BackfillJobStoreTests, BackfillJobRunnerTests, ResumableBackfillJobSelectorTests, BackfillJobIdentityV44MigrationTests — 184 tests in 13 suites and 119 in 8 suites, both exit 0), and (b) confirming its rails' expectation set is DISJOINT from the red set: every WX expectation string begins "playhead-wxsv: ", none of which appears above. 11/11 WX rails KILLED.

That disjointness argument is the manual form of fix direction (b) in this bead — evaluate a rail against the failures inside its OWN expectation set — and having now been done by hand twice, it is worth automating.

title: [bug] SemanticScanClaim.record reads a y8a3 adoption claim as .alreadySatisfied, losing playhead-fil5's gate attribution
description:
playhead-y8a3 R3 adversarial pass, finding F3.

SemanticScanClaim.jobId(analysisAssetId:transcriptVersion:) delegates to BackfillJobRunner.makeJobIdForTesting(..., phase: .fullEpisodeScan, offset: 0) — BYTE-IDENTICAL to the id a y8a3 adoption claim occupies on the fullCoverage lane.

SemanticScanClaim.record (SemanticScanClaim.swift:499-502) branches on existing.status == .complete -> .alreadySatisfied, whose doc reads 'the scan this claim would request has already run'. For an adoption claim that is FALSE by construction: the row read zero audio.

REACHABLE: asset holds a stale unfinished row; the runner adopts and writes the claim; later runShadowFMPhase hits a gate (canUseFoundationModels false — the probe caches false for 15 minutes and fil5's own doc calls it 'frequently TRANSIENT') -> record() sees the claim, returns .alreadySatisfied, records nothing. playhead-fil5's entire deliverable — SELECT analysisAssetId, deferReason FROM backfill_jobs WHERE deferReason LIKE 'scan_claim:%' answering 'which gate refused this episode a scan?' — silently loses that episode.

FIX: check BackfillJob.isAdoptionClaim at SemanticScanClaim.swift:501. The predicate already exists (added by y8a3); it just is not consulted here.

Note this contradicts the comment in BackfillJobRunner claiming 'nothing in a shipped build parses it back — the consumer is the pull'. SemanticScanClaim.record IS a shipped-build consumer that needs the distinction.
notes:
## R4 REVIEW — independently re-derived, and the harm is larger than 'attribution'

Two independent R4 passes (mine and my adversarial subagent's) reached this by
different routes without knowing it was filed. That is worth recording on its
own: it is the most findable thing on the branch.

**One escalation to the description.** This bead scopes the loss to fil5's gate
attribution — the `WHERE deferReason LIKE 'scan_claim:%'` pull. There is a REACH
consequence too, in one conjunction:

  * the adoption claim's carrier has reached
    `retryCount >= AdmissionController.maxRetries`, so it is excluded by BOTH
    `countResumableBackfillJobs` (AnalysisStore.swift:16379) and
    `fetchAssetIdsWithResumableBackfillJobs` (:16443); and
  * an FM gate closes for that asset at the SAME transcript version.

Then `countResumableBackfillJobs` reads 0 (the claim is `complete`, so uncounted;
the carrier is exhausted, so uncounted), `shouldMintAdScanRedrive`'s
`guard resumableCoverageJobCount > 0` shuts onn6's re-drive, and
`fetchAssetIdsMissingCoverageLaneJobs` (:16509) skips the asset because it DOES
own rows. Pre-y8a3 the same state left the id empty, so `record` minted a
`deferred` / `retryCount 0` row — resumable, and the newest — which reopened the
gate. The write that does not happen is not only a label.

The remaining escape is the runner's own revival path
(BackfillJobRunner.swift:840-848), and note what it requires: an ordinary
`runPendingBackfill` at that version. A closed FM gate is precisely what
suppresses one. So the fix this bead already names — consult
`BackfillJob.isAdoptionClaim` at SemanticScanClaim.swift:501 — is load-bearing
for reach, not only for the device pull. Worth keeping at P1.

Interaction to respect when fixing: do NOT let the `.queued/.deferred` arm's
`markBackfillJobDeferred` run on a claim. It would overwrite `deferReason` with
`scan_claim:<gate>` and destroy the `adopted_by:<carrier>` pointer the revival
path reads — turning a claim into a row that `replaceAdoptionClaim`'s WHERE can
no longer match, which is a fresh permanent suppressor. A new `Outcome` case is
the safe shape; a refresh is not.

Linked: playhead-9ocm and playhead-upm1 own the other half (what the count should
have read). Duplicate playhead-yhzm, filed by me before I found this bead, is
closed against it.

title: [bug] the adopt path still runs one full FM pass per invocation when an asset holds >1 stale unfinished row
description:
playhead-y8a3 R3 adversarial pass, finding F2.

fetchUnfinishedBackfillJob returns ONE row (ORDER BY createdAt ASC, LIMIT 1). The y8a3 adoption claim stops the SECOND invocation at an unchanged transcript version from minting — but only while there is exactly one stale row.

With N stale rows for the same (asset, phase, policy-class):
  inv 1: claim written at id(V), A1 adopted, A1 completes
  inv 2: by-id finds the claim (.complete) -> falls through the hoist -> fallback returns A2 -> A2 is driven: a progressCursor = nil full-episode FM pass over audio inv 1 just read
  inv 3: A3.  inv 4: A4.

So at an UNCHANGED transcript version the runner still runs one full pass per invocation for N-1 more invocations.

THIS IS THE FIELD MAJORITY, not a corner: AnalysisStore.swift:15855-15860 records 30 rows across 15 assets, of which 2 assets hold 2 rows, 5 hold 3, and CDD611C4 holds 4 — 8 of 15 hold >=2, mostly with NULL cursors.

Not a regression introduced by y8a3 (the parent commit behaves the same); y8a3 simply does not reach it. The new test adoptingARowClaimsTheCurrentVersionsMintSlot seeds exactly ONE stale row, so it cannot see this.

Fix direction: the claim should record that the id is claimed regardless of how many carriers remain, or the fallback should drain the stale set rather than adopt one per invocation.
notes:
## R4 REVIEW AMENDMENT — the framing 'not a regression' is right about the PARENT COMMIT and wrong about MAIN

This bead says: *'Not a regression introduced by y8a3 (the parent commit behaves
the same); y8a3 simply does not reach it.'* Both halves are true. The comparison
they make is within-branch, and it is not the comparison a merge decision needs.
Against **main (5c05233f)** the direction reverses, and re-deriving it is what
answers 'does 7x1s still deliver its purpose'.

MAIN, at an UNCHANGED transcript version V:

    inv 1: by-id(V) misses -> mint R@id(V), cursor nil, ONE full-episode pass, completes
    inv 2: by-id(V) hits R, status .complete -> `continue`.  ZERO FM work.
    inv 3..N: ZERO FM work.

The asset's stale rows A2..A4 are never touched again — no selector on main
re-derives their ids, which is precisely why 7x1s calls them orphans.

BRANCH (e51ab4d2), same asset, same unchanged V, N stale unfinished rows:

    inv 1: fallback adopts A1, claim written at id(V), A1 driven, completes
    inv 2: by-id(V) hits the CLAIM (.complete) -> falls through -> fallback returns
           A2 -> A2 driven. A2's progressCursor is NULL, so this is a FULL pass.
    inv 3: A3.  inv 4: A4.
    inv N+1: fallback nil, standing claim's carrier A1 is .complete -> `continue`.

So the branch spends **N-1 extra full-episode FM passes** where main spends none.
On CDD611C4 (4 rows) that is 3; on the 5 assets holding 3 rows it is 2 each.
Fleet-wide on the 2026-08-06 pull that is bounded by the 14 rows R1 counted as
duplicates of a still-unfinished row — a ONE-TIME cost, because the pool drains
as each adopted row terminates.

Set against the recurring saving, which is real but small and is what the bead
actually buys: on a transcript-version ROTATION over an unfinished row, the
branch resumes where main restarts. R1 measured that at 32 % of a pass in the
30-cycle harness and ~8 % on F4CE7F47, where the cursor had stalled at 96.84 s of
1,185.5 s (playhead-pfye caps it — the cursor is a contiguous prefix).

Two consequences worth carrying into whoever fixes this:

* The saving requires ongoing version rotation and the cost does not. Once
  transcription settles, main does zero work on repeat sessions and the branch
  keeps draining the pool.
* `runPendingBackfill`'s own doc contract (BackfillJobRunner.swift:552-555) —
  'callers can re-invoke for the same asset without producing duplicate work as
  long as the scan cohort and transcript version are unchanged' — is the sentence
  the y8a3 commit cites as the thing it restored. With N>1 stale rows it is still
  false, and 8 of 15 field assets have N>1. Fixing this bead is what makes that
  sentence true; until then the comment overstates.

title: REGRESSION (playhead-7x1s): an ADOPTED row leaves no row at the current transcriptVersion's id, so the NEXT same-version pass mints a duplicate full-episode FM scan
description:
## The bead that removes duplicate full-episode FM passes introduces one

Found in R2 review of playhead-7x1s, by an adversarial pass, and re-traced
independently before filing. **This is a regression against pre-7x1s behaviour,
denominated in exactly the currency 7x1s is about: full-episode FM seconds.**

### The broken contract, verbatim

`BackfillJobRunner.runPendingBackfill` (BackfillJobRunner.swift:552-556):

> Walks the FM backfill pipeline for one asset. **Idempotent: callers can
> re-invoke for the same asset without producing duplicate work as long as the
> scan cohort and transcript version are unchanged.**

That is the condition the fallback breaks — an UNCHANGED transcript version.

### The path

Asset holds an unfinished row `R_old`, minted under transcript version `U`.
Current version is `V`, and stays `V`.

1. **Pass 1.** `fetchBackfillJob(byId: id(V))` (:654) MISSES — no row was ever
   minted at `id(V)`. The playhead-7x1s fallback (:768-780) finds `R_old` and
   ADOPTS it, then `continue`s at :779 — **so the mint at :782-796 is skipped and
   no row is ever inserted at `id(V)`.** The drain runs `R_old` and
   `markBackfillJobComplete` (:1195) marks it `complete`.
2. **Pass 2, same version `V`.** `fetchBackfillJob(byId: id(V))` misses again.
   `fetchUnfinishedBackfillJob` returns nil — `R_old` is `complete`, excluded by
   design (R4-Fix6). Control falls through to :782 and mints a fresh row with
   **`progressCursor: nil`** → a full-episode FM pass from zero over audio that
   pass 1 just read.
3. Pass 3 at `V` is a no-op again (the pass-2 row now sits at `id(V)`, complete).

**Pre-7x1s the same two passes cost strictly less.** Pass 1 minted `id(V)` and
completed it; pass 2's by-id HIT a `complete` row, `continue`d, left
`enqueuedJobs` empty and did ZERO FM work. So:

    pre-7x1s   pass1 = one full pass      pass2 = nothing
    post-7x1s  pass1 = one RESUMED pass   pass2 = one FULL pass

The saving 7x1s buys on pass 1 is smaller than the full pass it adds on pass 2,
for every cursor value. The cost is one extra full-episode FM pass per
`(asset, transcriptVersion)` in which an adopted row COMPLETED.

### Reachable on shipped defaults — and one condition drives both halves

The adopted row must reach `complete`. `coverageTerminalDecision` (:1887-1894,
:2333-2357) returns `.complete` in three ways, and all three are ordinary:

* **`.notMeasurable`** — `AnalysisCoverageSummary.adScanFraction` is nil →
  `underCovered = false` → `.complete`.
* **measured >= the sufficiency floor** — i.e. the SUCCESS case.
* **any phase that is not `.fullEpisodeScan`** — `guard job.phase ==
  .fullEpisodeScan else { return .complete }`, so on the targeted lane all three
  phases complete unconditionally and all three duplicate.

And the SAME nil that completes the row also guarantees pass 2 happens:
`AnalysisJobRunner.shouldSkipSemanticBackfill` (:1208-1223) opens
`guard let adScanFraction = adScanFraction.finiteValue else { return false }` —
a nil fraction means DO NOT SKIP, so `runBackfill` is called again. One value,
both halves.

### Root cause, stated in the standing defect class

`backfill_jobs` carries **no transcript version**, so nothing can express "this
row's work was completed under version V". The by-id branch used the id as that
record; 7x1s deliberately stopped minting the id, and nothing replaced the record
it carried. `jobId` was naming two things at once — the WORK and the VERSION THE
WORK WAS LAST DONE UNDER — and 7x1s split off the first without rehoming the
second.

### Candidate fixes — NOT chosen here, this is an architectural call

1. **Re-key the adopted row to `id(V)`** when the fallback adopts it. Restores
   same-version idempotency exactly (pass 2's by-id hits the completed row) and
   still lets a later version `W` mint fresh (id rotates, the row is `complete`,
   the fallback excludes it). Also closes half of playhead-5q8l, since
   `SemanticScanClaim` derives the same id. Risks: `jobId` is the row's identity
   — check for a FK from `semantic_scan_results`, and old scan rows keep the old
   `runCorrelationId`, which breaks the generation join used to MEASURE this bead.
2. **Write a `complete` marker row at `id(V)`** when a phase was satisfied by an
   adopted row that completed. Restores pre-7x1s idempotency with no identity
   change and no FM cost, at one extra tiny row per (asset, version) — which is
   the same row count R4-Fix6 already produces. Must fire only on `complete`, or
   a deferred adoption would be blocked from being re-adopted.
3. **Add `transcriptVersion` to `backfill_jobs`** and make the record explicit.
   The honest fix and a schema migration.

Option 2 is the smallest and the only one with no identity semantics; option 3
is the one that stops this class recurring.

### Not to be confused with

* **playhead-9ocm** — a different consequence of the same "adoption mints
  nothing": the adopted row's old `createdAt` can fall outside
  `countResumableBackfillJobs`' newest-batch window.
* **playhead-5q8l** — `SemanticScanClaim.jobId` shares the derivation. Its
  "not a regression" note covers gate-closure-before-any-mint, NOT this sequence:
  here the unminted `id(V)` makes `SemanticScanClaim.record` (:499-535) take its
  MINT branch where pre-7x1s it found the runner's own row and only refreshed it,
  adding a cursor-less claim row that the by-id branch then prefers over the
  cursored adopted row.

### Evidence

Code-traced, not measured — the 2026-08-06 device pull is not on this box. No
test currently exercises a second same-version invocation after an adoption that
completed; `newTranscriptVersionResumesRatherThanDuplicating` rotates the version
between runs, so it cannot see this. That missing test is the first thing to
write.

title: the scan-claim row re-creates the duplicate full-episode pass 7x1s removed — its id embeds transcriptVersion too, so the by-id branch hits it and the unfinished-row fallback never runs
description:
## The hole, in one line

`SemanticScanClaim.jobId` is `BackfillJobRunner.makeJobIdForTesting(assetId,
transcriptVersion, .fullEpisodeScan, offset: 0)` — the SAME derivation the
runner's M-5 by-id branch uses for a full-episode plan. So a claim row minted
under transcript vN is found BY ID, the `continue` fires, and playhead-7x1s's
unfinished-row fallback (which sits below that branch and only runs when the
by-id lookup MISSES) is never reached.

## Why that re-creates the duplicate 7x1s removed

    session 1, transcript v1, gate closed  -> claim C1(v1) minted, cursor NULL
    session 2, transcript v1, gate open    -> by-id hits C1, re-drives it;
                                              C1 earns a cursor, defers
    session 3, transcript v2, gate closed  -> claim C2(v2) minted, cursor NULL
    session 4, transcript v2, gate open    -> by-id hits C2  <-- FALLBACK SKIPPED
                                              full-episode pass RESTARTS at 0,
                                              C1's cursor abandoned

Every (re-transcription x gate closure) pair therefore still costs one
cursor-less full-episode FM pass — exactly the cost playhead-7x1s measured at
14 of 30 rows on the 2026-08-06 pull.

## Reachability is not marginal

`SemanticScanClaim.Gate.foundationModelsUnavailable` is documented in its own
enum as "Frequently TRANSIENT — Apple Intelligence still downloading, a thermal
probe, a locale flip — and `FoundationModelsUsabilityProbe` caches a false for
15 minutes, so one throttle can swallow every completion landing in that
window." `fmModeOff` and `podcastIdMissing` are also live, and the reconciler
sweep mints `noCoverageLaneRow`. The `isOwed` guard only stops claims once the
asset clears `semanticBackfillSufficientAdScanFraction` — and per the 2026-07-30
measurement ZERO of 34 episodes were at 95% scan, so the guard is open on
essentially the whole library.

## NOT a regression

Pre-7x1s the same sequence produced the same full rescan. This bead did not
make it worse; it just cannot see it. Filing so the win is not over-claimed:
7x1s closes the runner's own mint, not the claim path's.

## What a fix has to decide (why this is not a one-liner)

`fetchUnfinishedBackfillJob` orders `createdAt ASC`, which is a DETERMINISM rule
and explicitly NOT a progress rule (its own doc says so — `CDD611C4` holds four
rows with NULL cursors). So "when the by-id row has a NULL cursor, prefer an
older row that has one" needs a real precedence answer, not just a second
lookup. Options worth weighing:

  * consult the fallback when the by-id row's `progressCursor` is nil, and
    order the fallback by cursor rather than `createdAt`;
  * have `SemanticScanClaim.record` itself adopt an existing unfinished row for
    the asset instead of minting a version-keyed one (it already has
    `refreshed` / `leftInPlace` outcomes for the same-version case);
  * drop `transcriptVersion` from the claim id and rely on `complete` exclusion
    the way 7x1s does.

Interacts with playhead-pfye (the cursor is a contiguous prefix) — decide that
one first if they are worked together.
notes:
## THE 14-OF-30 NUMBER MAY ALREADY BE CONTAMINATED — someone with the DB should check

`SemanticScanClaim` landed 2026-08-04 (commit 8ce94915, playhead-fil5). The
device pull playhead-7x1s measured is 2026-08-06. So claim rows could already be
in the 30 rows the bead counted, and a claim row is INDISTINGUISHABLE from a
runner-minted row on the columns 7x1s used: both are
`fullEpisodeScan`/`fullCoverage`, both non-terminal, both keyed on the same id
derivation. The one discriminator is persisted:

    SELECT COUNT(*) FROM backfill_jobs WHERE deferReason LIKE 'scan_claim:%';

Why it matters: a duplicate row that a CLAIM minted is a row the by-id branch
hits first, so the 7x1s fallback never gets the chance to block it. Every such
row inside the 14 is a row 7x1s does NOT actually remove. Until that count is
run, "14 of 30 rows never minted" is an upper bound on the win, not the win.

Run it against `scratchpad/db-new-t2h/analysis.sqlite` (the pull was not
present on the review box, so R2 could not).

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
Field evidence from db-new-t2h (my own query, 2026-08-07):

**There is no `semantic_scan_claims` table in the pull**, and no `CREATE TABLE` for a claim table anywhere in `AnalysisStore.swift` — only `specialist_scan_results` and `semantic_scan_results`. So before assuming the 14 duplicate rows may be claim rows, establish WHERE `SemanticScanClaim` persists. If it does not own rows in `backfill_jobs`, this bead's premise changes shape.

Separately, and relevant to R1's F1 fix: `backfill_jobs` in this pull is 16 queued / 7 deferred / 5 failed / 2 complete = 30 rows. **All 5 failed rows carry `retryCount = 1` against `AdmissionController.maxRetries = 3`** — i.e. every one is 'failed but under budget', the exact population nothing can start. They span 4 assets (DE0784D8, 0C2FC22E x2, 52CD8F5B x2), causes `Request has been rate limited` and `FMInferenceTimeoutError(deadline...)`. Note DE0784D8 is the 1.00x asset — the one with no redundancy at all — so the un-fixed fallback would have suppressed even the well-behaved case.

Those causes are FM budget failures, which ties this population to playhead-rkfp and playhead-ezmv.

title: the coverage-lane resume cursor is a contiguous PREFIX, so one early hole re-scans the rest of the episode forever
description:
## Measured on the 2026-08-06 pull, while fixing playhead-7x1s

`BackfillJobRunner.narrowedForResume` is the ONLY intra-episode skip in
production. It drops every segment with `endTime <= cursor`, where the cursor is
the **contiguous scanned PREFIX** (`BackfillProgressCursor.lastProcessedUpperBoundSec`,
an `EpisodeSeconds`). A prefix cannot express "windows 0, 2, 3 done, window 1
failed", so **one early hole pins the cursor near zero for the rest of the
episode's life.**

Asset `F4CE7F47`, `backfill_jobs.progressCursor` on two of its three rows:

    lastProcessedUpperBoundSec = 96.84

while that same job's generation had already scanned a UNION of **1185.5 s** of
the 1316.7 s episode (17 rows, 0.0 -> 1199.8). The cursor stalled at window 1
because window 2 (97.5 -> 130.9) came back `permissive_decoding_failure` — 9 of
that asset's 53 rows did.

## Why it matters now

playhead-7x1s made a re-transcription RESUME the existing coverage-lane job
instead of minting a duplicate. That removed the duplicate full-episode passes,
but what the resumed job then SKIPS is bounded by this cursor: 96.84 s of
1185.5 s, about 8 %. Measured in the 30-cycle runner harness
(`noProgressRunnerCyclesStayBounded`), 30 re-transcriptions still wrote **41
scan rows against a 60-row ceiling** — the 19 rows saved are the cursor's
contribution, and the remaining 41 are re-scans of audio the store already holds
a successful row for.

## The shape of the fix (NOT decided — options only)

The store already holds the exact answer: `semantic_scan_results` rows with
`status = 'success'` name precisely which windows were read. A resume narrowed by
*the set of successfully scanned windows* rather than by a prefix bound would be
exact.

**Do not do this naively.** Dropping segments because a row OVERLAPS them in time
is the watermark-vs-coverage error (playhead-346z, playhead-9y9e): the persisted
row's `transcriptVersion` differs from the current one, so "a row covers this
time range" does NOT establish "the text at this time range is unchanged". The
narrowing needs a content identity, which is what playhead-<reuse-key bead>
is about — the two are coupled and should probably be sequenced together.

## Acceptance

* State which quantity is the narrowing denominator and prove it names windows
  actually READ, not audio a watermark claims.
* Re-measure the 30-cycle harness: 41 rows is the current number to beat.

title: lostOwnership is a global single slot: one job's lease reclaim suppresses a sibling's cleanup writes
description:
playhead-lmrx R3 named this and R4 confirmed it is out of scope for a review round.

nowCap is 2 and both dispatch drivers can be inside processJob, so two jobs hold independent leases at once. `lostOwnership` is one Bool for both:

* A's lease-renewal CAS fails -> `lostOwnership = true` -> B, which still fully owns its lease, skips EVERY cleanup write (state revert, progress, backoff, releaseLease, journal). B's resume point is never committed; it sits at 'running' until its own lease expires and orphan recovery requeues it.
* The converse: B's processJob entry sets `lostOwnership = false` (AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift ~4482), un-suppressing A after A genuinely lost its lease, so A's cleanup writes clobber the new owner's bookkeeping. This is the direction R3 did not name.
* `retireDownloadAnalysis` sets it under `currentEpisodeId == episodeId` -- a single-slot AIM, so a retire for the OTHER episode raises it globally and a retire for a non-most-recent episode does not raise it at all.

WHY R4 DID NOT DO IT. `lostOwnership` is read at ~23 sites across 8 helper methods (writeIfStillOwned, commitOutcomeArm, emitJournalFinalized/Failed/FailedForJobSnapshot/Preempted, recordGrantWindowObservationIfEnabled, resolveAnalysisAssetId), none of which has a job id in scope. Moving it into the RunningJob registry means threading an id through all of them, or introducing a task-local -- an architectural change, in the scheduler's hot path, inside a review round. That is the change most likely to introduce the next defect.

Severity is bounded and self-healing (lease expiry + orphan recovery requeue), which is why it is P1 rather than P0.

title: 34 mutation rails cannot apply their anchor and are silently unevaluable — the safety net has holes in exactly the files it guards most
description:
## Measured 2026-08-06 by my own full `--dry-run` sweep

13m22s, 0 builds, run against `bead/playhead-lmrx` AFTER R3 repaired the three drifts its own diff caused. So these 34 are pre-existing and independent of that bead.

**34 distinct rails FAIL TO APPLY** — `anchor matched 0 times … (need exactly 1)`:

```
C06 C07 E01 E04 J01 J08 L09 M11 M12 M15 M16 Q01 Q02 Q03
RT02 RT03 RT06 RT12 RT13 RT14 RT15 RT16 RT17
SC01 SC04 SC21 SC25 SC30 SC31 SC33 UC05 UC06 UC09 Z01
```

By file:

| file | rails |
|---|---|
| `SkipOrchestrator.swift` | 8 |
| `AnalysisJobReconciler.swift` | 5 |
| `BackfillJobRunner.swift` | 5 |
| `AnalysisStore.swift` | 5 |
| `SemanticScanClaim.swift` | 4 |
| `AnalysisJobRunner.swift` | 2 |
| `SpanExtentSupport` / `DecodedSpan` / `AdPodContinuation` | 1 each |

## Read the counter correctly — this is the standing defect class in the tooling

The run's summary line says **`errors: 72`**. That is **occurrences across batches**, not rails: a rail appearing in two batches errors twice. Distinct rails is 34, and the distinct-name ERROR set is 40 (34 drifted + 6 erroring for other reasons). I misreported 72 as a rail count once already. A value that names occurrences read as though it named rails — the summary line should say which.

## Why it matters

A drifted anchor means the mutation is never applied, so **the rail proves nothing and says so only in a line nobody reads.** These are not obscure rails: SkipOrchestrator is the auto-skip decision surface, AnalysisJobReconciler and SemanticScanClaim are the job-lifecycle invariants that `playhead-mk6z`, `fil5` and `lmrx` have each found real defects in. The files with the most drift are the files under the most active change — which is exactly the correlation that makes drift silent: every bead that edits `SkipOrchestrator.swift` moves an anchor and nothing tells it.

## What to do

1. Re-anchor all 34 onto **contiguous code**, never comments or prose. `playhead-lmrx` retired one rail (LX17) that was anchored where a comment edit could kill it, and R3 re-anchored LX12 off two comment lines for the same reason. **A rail anchored on prose is not a rail.**
2. For each, confirm it still KILLS after re-anchoring. A rail that applies but no longer reddens its named test is a coverage hole that drift was hiding.
3. **Make drift loud.** The mechanism that let 34 accumulate is that `--dry-run` is the only thing that reports it, it takes 13 minutes, and nothing runs it. Options: a cheap anchor-only preflight (no apply/restore cycle) run at the head of every battery invocation, or a CI/cron sweep. `scripts/mutation-battery-untypeable.py` already has `--check-inventory` as a buildless preflight — the same idea applied to anchors.

## Sequencing

Do NOT land during a live review loop — `mutation-battery.sh` is the instrument every open bead's round is using. Pairs naturally with `playhead-4t4j` (batching to cut the ~5 min/rail cost), since both are surgery on the same script and both want one quiet window.

## Also worth fixing while in here

`--only` takes exactly ONE rail name (exact match). R3 spent ~2 hours on 11 sequential single-rail invocations because of it. Accepting a list would have made that one pass.

title: the mutation battery costs ~5 min per rail because every rail pays a full xcodebuild; batch the re-confirmations and keep individual verdicts only where they carry trust
description:
## The problem, measured 2026-08-06

`playhead-lmrx` review round R1 ran **4.5 hours in one round**. The cost model is `fix rounds x rails x ~5 min`, and the rail count only grows: the implementer left 17 LX rails, R1 added 5 (22 total), and one full pass is **~110 minutes**. R1 ran `--only LX01…LX22` **one at a time** — 22 builds where ~3 would do.

## Where the time is NOT

**Test execution.** Measured: 75 tests / 14 suites in **7.1 s** (implementer); 93 tests / 19 suites (R1). Even all 151 entries in `FOCUSED_SUITES` is well under a minute. **Scoping the suites per rail — the intuitive fix — buys almost nothing.** Do not spend the round on it.

## Where the time IS (inferred by elimination — MEASURE THIS FIRST)

`run_focused()` calls `scripts/fast-gate.sh`, which per invocation does disk preflight -> lint -> **xcodebuild test (build + sim + test)** -> baseline check. Every rail mutates a file (forcing a rebuild) and then restores it (forcing another). The mutable files are large and heavily depended upon:

| file | lines |
|---|---|
| `AnalysisStore.swift` | 21,243 |
| `AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift` | 6,760 |
| `BackgroundProcessingService.swift` | 1,959 |

Swift type-checking is superlinear in file size, so a one-line edit to `AnalysisStore.swift` is a multi-minute recompile plus relink.

**Step 0 of this bead is a measurement, not a change:** time one rail whose FILE_KEY is a small leaf file against one that mutates `AnalysisStore.swift`. If they differ by 3x or more, batching BY FILE is worth as much as batching at all. Do not skip this — the whole design below rests on "the build dominates", which is currently an inference.

## The safety property that makes batching sound

**A batch can only lie in ONE direction.** `playhead-7n7u` recorded the failure: DR01 masked DR02 — a **false KILL**, crediting a rail that would have survived alone. The converse cannot happen: if a batched run leaves an expected test **GREEN**, that is a genuine survivor and no masking can fabricate it.

So batching is unsafe for establishing a kill and perfectly safe for detecting a survivor. The design follows from that.

## Design

1. **Split the round's rails by what the verdict is FOR.**
   - **NEW rails** (a round typically adds ~5) need a trustworthy KILLED verdict. Run these **individually**. Never batch a rail whose kill has never been established.
   - **RE-CONFIRMATION of existing rails** (~17) only needs to answer "did my change break a rail that already held?". **Batch these.** Any expected test still green is a real regression; a masked false-kill among rails that were already killed against older code is a far smaller risk than the 90 minutes it costs to rule out.
   - Expected saving: 5 individual (25 min) + 17 batched in ~2 builds (10 min) = **~35 min, down from ~110**.

2. **Batch by `FILE_KEY`.** Group so consecutive mutations hit the same file and do not re-invalidate a 21k-line file's dependents. No risk.

3. **Hoist the per-rail overhead.** Disk preflight, lint and the baseline check run once per rail today and none of them need to. Run them once at battery start.

## Explicitly rejected, with reasons — do not re-litigate

- **Per-rail test-suite scoping.** Measured above: tests are seconds. Buys nothing.
- **Raising `PLAYHEAD_BUILD_JOBS` above 4.** The cap exists because a COLD build OOM-kills xcodebuild on this 16 GB box (`Killed: 9`). Trading a reliable 5 min for an occasional OOM is a bad trade. If pursued at all it must be conditional on a warm `.derivedData/Build`, and that condition was already tried and rejected once for the disk threshold — see the cold/warm split in CLAUDE.md that the data refused.
- **`playhead-b5b6`'s fast lane for pure-logic rails.** Its own measurement says ~3% whole-battery saving because the expensive rails need the simulator. Not the fix for this.

## Do not land this during a review loop

`scripts/mutation-battery.sh` is the instrument every open bead's review round is using. Land it in a quiet window, and re-run one already-closed bead's rails both ways to prove the batched path reaches the same verdicts.

## Watch the standing defect class

`BATCH` in the rail record names *which group a mutation belongs to*, not *whether its verdict was independently established*. If the batched path starts writing KILLED for rails it screened rather than proved, that is a value naming one thing read as though it named another — the exact class this repo keeps shipping. The verdict record should say WHICH way each rail was run.

## Two more footguns in the same script, found 2026-08-06/07

**`--batch` does not accumulate.** `--batch 570 --batch 571` in one invocation silently runs only the LAST — it prints `1 mutation(s) in 1 batch(es)` and the first batch's verdict is a phantom. Found by R5 on playhead-lmrx. Either accumulate them or refuse a repeated flag; silently honouring the last is the worst of the three options.

**`--only` takes exactly ONE exact-match name.** R3 spent ~2 h on 11 sequential single-rail invocations, each paying its own build, because of this. Accepting a list would have made it one pass.

Both belong in the same quiet-window pass as the batching work above.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
CARRIED FROM playhead-b5b6, which is being closed as cost-exceeds-value (its own measurement: 12 of 119 rails movable, ~3% whole-battery saving; 4t4j already records 'Not the fix for this').

b5b6's investigation surfaced FOUR LATENT BATTERY DEFECTS that must not die with it. Two were re-confirmed live in the 2026-08-11 backlog triage:

1. DUPLICATE RAIL ID 'L09|61' — scripts/mutation-battery.sh:3334 AND :3378. Two different rails share one identifier, so one silently overwrites the other's verdict in any per-rail accounting.
2. V/Q BATCH-ID COLLISION — V01-V06 occupy batches 62-67 (:3347-3377) and Q01-Q06 ALSO occupy batches 62-67 (:3390-3417). Same batch numbers, two series.

Both are the standing defect class in the battery's own bookkeeping: an identifier that names one rail read as though it named another. A collided id means a verdict is attributed to the wrong rail, which is exactly the failure mode a mutation battery exists to prevent.

The other two b5b6 findings are in its body if wanted; these two are the ones verified against source today.

title: an analysis job that cannot finish inside any granted window now retries forever and holds the head of the queue
description:
## What playhead-lmrx traded away, and why it is worth its own bead

`playhead-lmrx` exempted `.taskExpired` from the attempt charge in
`AnalysisWorkScheduler`'s cancel-catch arm. That is correct for the population it
targets: without it, wiring the backfill expiry to `cancelCurrentJob` would charge
one attempt per background window, and at `maxAttemptCount` (5) the arm supersedes
with `nextEligibleAt: nil`. A superseded row never returns — `workKey` is UNIQUE and
`insertJob` is `INSERT OR IGNORE` over a key stable across launches — so every long
episode would have been abandoned permanently on its fifth window, by the OS doing
exactly what the OS does.

**It also removed the only bound on a third population.** Three shapes reach a
background window, and only two are still bounded:

| shape | what bounds it |
|---|---|
| the job FAILS | the `.failed` arm charges an attempt and supersedes at 5 |
| the job hangs WITHOUT observing cancellation | `processJob` never returns, the process is suspended holding the lease, and `reclaimExpiredLeases` requeues with `attemptCount + 1` |
| the job DOES observe cancellation but never advances | **nothing** |

The third is a job whose first durable checkpoint costs more than a whole grant. It
requeues with `attemptCount` frozen, and `fetchNextEligibleJob` orders by
`priority DESC, createdAt ASC` — so it is picked first again in the next window, and
every window after. It cannot die, and it can hold the head of the queue
indefinitely while the episodes behind it never run.

## Why this is not hypothetical

From the 2026-08-06 pull (`background_task_runs`, `work_journal`), the same
measurements that motivated lmrx:

* 203 of 254 backfill wakes (80.0 %) ended `expired`.
* **108 of those 203 windows contain exactly one `acquired` event and nothing
  else**, with the first `acquired` at a median of t+1.0 s. One job picked up, then
  silence to expiry — which is exactly the third shape.
* Only 4 of the 203 wrote a `semantic_scan_results` row inside their own window.

Pre-lmrx those jobs rotated: the reaper charged an attempt each window and the
episode superseded after five, freeing the lane (at the cost of never analysing it).
Post-lmrx they do not rotate at all.

## What a fix needs, and what it is not

Bounding the third shape needs a durable per-window PROGRESS witness — "did this
grant bank anything for THIS job?" The cancel-catch arm has none: no
`AnalysisOutcome` arrives (the runner threw `CancellationError`), so there is no
`progress` to commit, and `analysis_jobs`'s `featureCoverageSec` /
`transcriptCoverageSec` / `cueCoverageSec` are written only by the outcome arms.
The witness would have to come from the incrementally-persisted artifacts
(`semantic_scan_results`, transcript rows), sampled at dispatch and at cancel.

The alternative — and the better one — is to make the unit small enough that a
219 s grant can finish one, which is the architectural change lmrx explicitly
declined to make and presented three options for. That decision is Dan's. This bead
exists so the residual is not carried silently in the meantime.

Do NOT fix this by re-charging the attempt: that restores the permanent-abandonment
defect lmrx removed. The two must be solved together or the escape valve is a
death sentence.

**Rails/tests that pin the current behaviour** (any change must move them
deliberately): `ExpiredWindowAttemptAccountingTests.repeatedExpiryNeverSupersedes`
(five windows, `attemptCount` frozen), `.genuineCancelStillEscalates` (the vacuity
control), and mutation rails LX11 / LX12 / LX13.

title: an asset whose ONLY coverage-lane row is a stale `complete` has no rescue path — 53FC53E3 stays locked out after iu0t
description:
## The gap

playhead-iu0t stops `retryShadowFMPhaseForSession` discarding the transcript, and playhead-41mu stops a new under-covered job calling itself `complete`. Neither touches the row ALREADY on disk. Measured on the 2026-08-03 device pull: asset 53FC53E3 has exactly one `backfill_jobs` row, `fm-041dedcf8293523e`, status `complete`, minted from the final-only transcriptVersion. After iu0t no dispatcher re-derives that id, so it orphans — which is good (its false verdict is unreachable) and insufficient (nothing mints a replacement).

## Every candidate rescue path, checked against the pull

* `AnalysisWorkScheduler.shouldMintAdScanRedrive` — `guard resumableCoverageJobCount > 0 else { return false }`. `countResumableBackfillJobs` excludes `complete` and scopes to the newest enqueue batch; the stale row IS the newest batch. Reads 0. **Declines.**
* `fetchAssetIdsWithResumableBackfillJobs` (the reconciler sweep) — `status <> complete`. **Not selected.**
* `fetchAssetIdsMissingCoverageLane` (playhead-fil5) — `NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM backfill_jobs …)`. The asset has one row. **Not selected.**
* `AnalysisJobReconciler.capOutRetry` (playhead-y8f3/9y9e) — `guard AnalysisWorkScheduler.isAttemptCapTerminal(tail)`. Both of 53FC53E3's `analysis_jobs` rows are `complete` at `attemptCount 0`. **Declines.**
* the shadow-retry drain itself — needs `session.needsShadowRetry`. The pull has three `analysis_sessions` rows total, NONE flagged, and none for this asset. **Never fires.**

Five paths, five declines. 53FC53E3 is at 99.3 % transcript / 1.4 % ad-scan and there is no way back for it short of a re-transcription changing the version hash.

## Shape of the class, not one row

The predicate that is missing is "a coverage lane whose newest batch is COMPLETE but whose MEASURED `adScanFraction` is below the floor". Every existing selector reads the STATUS; none reads the measurement against the status. That is the same defect family as the rest of this queue — a value that names one thing (`complete` = 'the runner finished what it was handed') read as though it named another ('the episode was scanned').

## Why it is P1 and not P0

It is a rescue for historical rows, not a live leak: with iu0t + 41mu landed, no NEW row can enter this state. One asset on one device pull is the known population, and the honest count could be larger on devices nobody has pulled.

## Do NOT

Do not fix it by making `countResumableBackfillJobs` count `complete` rows — that reopens finished work for every healthy asset and is what SC19/SC16 in the mutation battery exist to prevent. The new predicate has to carry the MEASUREMENT, and it must be bounded (the `adScanRedrive` ordinal budget or an equivalent) so an episode whose transcript cannot support the floor does not re-drive forever.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
## playhead-iu0t R2 — the "no way back" sentence is wrong, and the bead is CHEAPER than it says

Re-derived against the 2026-08-03 device pull, with the canonicalize/atomize/jobId
derivation reimplemented in Python and controlled against 53FC53E3's three known
hashes byte-exact before any downstream number was computed:

    V(final-only) 55afd3e8bb41833c004ee7d4b1be7589 -> fm-041dedcf8293523e   <- the row on disk
    V(canonical)  61872a4d3e718e8bb4b8156dc2099444 -> fm-46ea5fad09da03b2
    V(fast-only)  766ea8ba068ffce5e3f48be66c9fa13f -> fm-af6aeeb497745eca

**`fm-46ea5fad09da03b2` does not exist in `backfill_jobs`.** `SELECT COUNT(*) … WHERE
jobId='fm-46ea5fad09da03b2'` returns 0. The canonical id is un-minted for **7 of the 12
assets** on the pull (2C5C3699, 48E903D7, 4FF3A238, 53FC53E3, 83592353, D9B513CD,
FCDDB309); it exists for the other five.

So this bead's sentence — *"no way back short of a re-transcription changing the version
hash"* — is inaccurate as written. playhead-iu0t already moved the id space: the drain now
canonicalizes, so the id any dispatcher derives for 53FC53E3 today is the canonical one,
and the stale `complete` verdict sitting under the final-only id is **unreachable**. No
re-transcription and no migration is needed to make a re-drive scan the full episode.

**What that changes, and what it does not.** It does not make the bead unnecessary, because
nothing SELECTS the asset. Every selector is asset-scoped or status-scoped, not id-scoped:

  * `fetchAssetIdsMissingCoverageLane` uses `NOT EXISTS (… WHERE analysisAssetId = …)`.
    53FC53E3 has one row, so it is not missing a lane and is never selected.
  * `countResumableBackfillJobs` / `fetchAssetIdsWithResumableBackfillJobs` exclude
    `complete`. The one row is `complete`, so both read 0.

That is exactly this bead's own conclusion — *the missing predicate is a coverage lane whose
newest batch is COMPLETE but whose MEASURED `adScanFraction` is below the floor*. The
diagnosis was right; only the cost sentence was wrong.

**Revised cost: one selector, no migration, no re-transcription, no data repair.** Measured
ground truth for the acceptance test: 53FC53E3's two `semantic_scan_results` rows both span
[2490.0, 2525.82], union 35.820000 s over `episodeDurationSec` 2528.448 = **1.416679 %** —
the bead's "1.4 %", confirmed to six places.

title: the under-coverage cursor strides over INTERIOR transcript holes — the head rule is necessary, not sufficient
description:
## The residual playhead-41mu (R2 review) left on the table

`BackfillJobRunner.underCoverageCursor` refuses to advance the coverage-lane cursor
when there is a hole at the HEAD — between the prior cursor and the first segment
this run planned over. That closes the 53FC53E3 shape. It does NOT close a hole
sitting INSIDE the run's own segments, and the reason is structural:
`CoarseCoverageWalk.contiguousUpperBoundSec` is contiguity over the PLAN LIST, and
`planPassA` partitions whatever segments it is handed. Two plans either side of a
400 s untranscribed stretch are adjacent by index, so the walk strides over the
stretch and the terminal publishes a cursor above it. `narrowedForResume` then
drops every segment at or below that cursor on the next attempt — including
segments that did not exist yet when the cursor was written.

## Both halves are MEASURED on the 2026-08-03 device pull, not argued

**The residual is real, and it is recoverable audio.** Nine of twelve assets carry
at least one interior fast-transcript gap wider than
`AnalysisCoverageMath.adScanBridgeableGapSec` (5 s). The four widest gaps are also
the four the FINAL pass later fills:

| asset | interior fast gaps > 5 s | filled by the final pass |
|---|---|---|
| AD5F3A0A | 2,395.5 s | 2,356.3 s |
| D9B513CD | 1,196.2 s | 1,161.8 s |
| 48E903D7 | 660.0 s | 659.5 s |
| 83592353 | 150.2 s | 149.4 s |

4,327 s of 4,401 s. On AD5F3A0A that is 55 % of a 4,281 s episode that a cursor
published on the fast-only tier would delete from every subsequent attempt.

**The obvious fix is mis-calibrated at this tolerance.** Capping the cursor at the
first gap wider than 5 s would force attempts 2 and 3 to re-scan:

| asset | first fast gap at | gap width | episode re-scanned per attempt | audio recovered |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4FF3A238 | 38.0 s | 5.3 s | 96.9 % | 20.9 s |
| FCDDB309 | 64.4 s | 5.3 s | 95.4 % | 21.7 s |
| 58882C47 | 88.9 s | 10.1 s | 92.4 % | 41.0 s |
| 83592353 | 570.0 s | 150.2 s | 88.9 % | 150.2 s |

Today those attempts cost ZERO FM inference — `narrowedForResume` empties them and
`runJob`'s empty-segments short-circuit writes a `noWork:` sentinel — and that is
the load-bearing half of 41mu's accepted cost. Spending 12–45 min of FM wall-clock
twice to recover 21 s is worse than the defect.

## What the decision actually is

The threshold, not the mechanism. `adScanBridgeableGapSec` answers "is this hole
too small to have hidden an ad from a scan that ran?", which is the right question
for the coverage NUMERATOR and the wrong one for "is this hole worth a re-scan?".
The second question wants a gap wide enough to hold an ad — a new constant, on the
order of an ad slot rather than an inter-utterance breath. On the pull that one
constant separates the two tables cleanly: every gap in the first is >= 150 s,
every gap that drives the second is <= 10.1 s except 83592353's, which appears in
both.

Picking it is a policy call with a measured FM-wall-clock price, so it is Dan's
under CLAUDE.md Decision Authority rather than a reviewer's.

## Related

## R3 review of playhead-41mu — one number in this bead is wrong, re-derived from the pull

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
## DAN'S DECISION (2026-08-04): raise the threshold, then enforce the rule EVERYWHERE — not head-only.

Rejected: leaving it head-only at 5 s, and enforcing at 5 s regardless. The first skips real holes forever; the second forces 92-97 % episode re-scans on 4FF3A238/FCDDB309/58882C47 to recover 21-41 s, destroying the zero-FM-cost property attempts 2-3 currently have.

## The number is 60 s, and it is MEASURED, not chosen

Full fast-pass gap census over all 12 assets of the 2026-08-03 pull (n=668 gaps >1 s):

    p50 1.4s   p75 1.9s   p90 3.3s   p95 4.5s   p99 15.7s   max 2370.4s

**The distribution is bimodal with an EMPTY BAND.** Per asset, widest gap and what the final pass later fills:

    0C2FC22E    4s -> fills    0s      48E903D7   660s -> fills  596s
    2C5C3699    4s -> fills    0s      83592353   150s -> fills  129s
    44F076BB    7s -> fills    0s      AD5F3A0A  2370s -> fills 2120s
    4FF3A238   16s -> fills    0s      D9B513CD  1170s -> fills 1058s
    53FC53E3   15s -> fills    0s
    58882C47   10s -> fills    0s      <- eight assets: widest gap 24s, final pass fills NOTHING
    DE0784D8   24s -> fills    0s      <- four assets: narrowest hole 150s, final pass fills 129-2120s
    FCDDB309   16s -> fills    0s

**Nothing on this library has a gap between 24 s and 150 s.** Thresholds of 30/60/120 s are therefore IDENTICAL in effect (4 gaps, 4,351 s of audio); only >5 s (24 gaps) and >300 s (3 gaps) differ. And the separation is not arbitrary: the four assets with structural holes are exactly the four where the final pass supplies the missing audio.

**60 s = the geometric mean of the empty band, sqrt(24 x 150) = 60.0** — 2.5x above the widest breath gap, 2.5x below the narrowest real hole. Symmetric margin in log space, on a band the data actually leaves empty.

## What this buys

Recovers the four structural holes — AD5F3A0A alone is 2,370 s of which the final pass fills 2,356 s, **55 % of a 4,281 s episode** that `narrowedForResume` would otherwise drop — while triggering ZERO re-scans on the eight breath-gap assets, so attempts 2-3 stay free there.

## Scope when implemented

- The constant is NOT `adScanBridgeableGapSec` (5 s, the coverage reader's bridge). This is a distinct quantity — 'a hole big enough to be worth re-scanning' vs 'a hole small enough to bridge when measuring'. **Two names, or the next reviewer finds the seventeenth instance of the family here.**
- Apply the rule to interior and tail holes, not just the head. R2 verified the head case and the 5.0 boundary complementarity; the other positions are unexamined (playhead-41mu R3 is probing them).
- Re-measure the band on the next device pull before trusting 60 s again — it is derived from 12 episodes, and an empty band is exactly the kind of fact a bigger library can fill in.

comments.text: ABSORBS playhead-5pyq (closed 2026-08-11).
