comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
playhead-15d0 R2 (2026-08-11): 15d0 ADDS A SECOND SOURCE OF INTERIOR HOLES, and it is not a transcript hole.

This bead's residual is stated over UNTRANSCRIBED interior stretches — 'two plans either side of a 400 s untranscribed stretch are adjacent by index, so the walk strides over the stretch'. playhead-15d0's narrowedForScreenedWindows now punches interior holes into the SAME segment array for a different reason: a segment fully inside a merged screened span is deleted before planPassA ever sees it. planPassA packs windows from contiguous ARRAY slices and stamps startTime=min/endTime=max over the slice (FoundationModelClassifier.swift:3029-3046), so a window straddling a 15d0 hole reports a span across it, and coarseCheckpointWalk sets walkedUpperBound = plan.endTime with no time-adjacency check at all.

WHY IT IS LESS SEVERE THAN THE TRANSCRIPT-HOLE CASE, stated so nobody re-raises it as new: at the moment the cursor is written, the audio in a 15d0 hole IS covered by a durable row — that is why the segments were dropped. The claim is TRUE when made.

WHERE IT STILL BITES: the ROW is transcript-version-gated and the CURSOR is not. transcriptVersion is TranscriptAtomizer.transcriptVersionHash — a SHA-256 over the length-prefixed normalizedText of every canonical chunk — so one appended chunk invalidates every row for the asset (R2 reproduced this byte-for-byte against backfill_jobs.attemptTranscriptVersion on 4 of 5 assets in db-overnight5). After the next append the rows stop counting and the cursor keeps deleting. So 15d0 lets audio screened at version V-old be laundered into a version-blind cursor one generation further back than before.

NOT FIXED in 15d0 and deliberately not: capping the cursor at the first interior hole is exactly the threshold decision this bead exists to make, and 15d0's holes would want a different answer from transcript holes (they are screened audio, not unread audio). One thing to carry into that decision: this bead's argument for NOT capping cites that today those re-attempts 'cost ZERO FM inference (narrowedForResume empties them and the empty-segments short-circuit fires)'. 15d0 is now a second reason that short-circuit fires, so the cost side of that trade has moved.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
playhead-15d0 R3 (2026-08-11): the 15d0 hole can land at the HEAD too, and there the guarded and unguarded writers do OPPOSITE things. R2's note above describes 15d0's holes as INTERIOR. They are not confined to the interior: narrowedForResume drops segments at or below the cursor and narrowedForScreenedWindows then drops the segments IMMEDIATELY ABOVE it whenever a reusable row covers them — which is precisely 66D32039's measured shape (cursor 194.46, merged screened span 195.66-276.18). The run's first plan then starts at 276.54, 82 s above the prior cursor.

DEMONSTRATED, not argued. R3 added a temporary probe (run, passed, then deleted; tree restored byte-exact): narrowedForScreenedWindows over [10-20, 20-30, 30-100] with one reusable row 10-30 leaves [30-100], and EpisodeSeconds.promoting(PlanListSeconds(100), priorEpisodeCursor: 10, firstPlannedStart: 30, bridge: adScanBridgeableGapSec) returns NIL. With firstPlannedStart 10 (the pre-15d0 value) the same bound IS promoted. BridgeToleranceSec.bridges is 'gapSec <= 5.0'.

WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THE RULE THIS BEAD WILL WRITE:

1. underCoverageCursor (the ONE writer with the head guard) now refuses to promote on exactly the shape 15d0 exists to exploit, and keeps prior forever. That is the SAFE direction and costs no FM inference — the screened narrowing drops the same audio the cursor would have — but it means the guarded writer stops advancing while the three UNGUARDED sites (UnsoundCursorPromotionSite.coarseCheckpoint / .rateLimitDefer / .cancellationSalvage) stride straight across the same hole with no check at all. On a BG-window expiry, which is the dominant field path for this lane, the terminal never runs and .cancellationSalvage is what writes the cursor.

2. So when a1x0 enforces the rule EVERYWHERE at the 60 s threshold, it must decide what a 15d0 hole IS. It is SCREENED audio, not unread audio — the premise behind 'a hole at the head is unscanned audio, the cursor must not speak for it' (BackfillCoverageTerminalTests:310) does not hold for it. Treating a 15d0 hole as a hole freezes the cursor permanently on every asset where 15d0 fires; treating it as covered launders version-gated evidence into a version-blind cursor, which is the risk R2 recorded above. The two cases want different answers and they are not distinguishable from the segment array alone — only screenedSpans knows which holes it punched.

3. Corollary for the cost side of this bead's own argument: R2 noted 15d0 is a second reason the empty-segments short-circuit fires. Add that 15d0 is also a reason the head guard fires, so the 'attempts 2-3 cost ZERO FM inference' property now has two sources rather than one.

NOT A DEFECT IN 15d0 and not fixed there: no audio is lost, no retry budget is charged differently (recordUnderCoverageTerminal has a flat budget with no reset-on-progress clause), and the direction is under-claiming throughout.

title: the shadow-retry replay hands the coverage lane FINAL chunks only — the pre-hc7e collapse, still live
description:
## The defect

`AdDetectionService.retryShadowFMPhaseForSession` (AdDetectionService.swift:9696-9697)
builds the chunk array it hands the coverage lane as

    let finalChunks = chunks.filter { $0.pass == TranscriptPassType.final_.rawValue }
    let chunksForReplay = finalChunks.isEmpty ? chunks : finalChunks

The final pass is INCREMENTAL — `FinalPassRetranscriptionRunner` re-transcribes a
candidate-local slice, not the episode — so "prefer final" means "scan only the
re-transcribed tail and DISCARD every fast chunk", including all the audio the
final pass never touched.

This is the pre-playhead-hc7e defect, verbatim. hc7e removed exactly this
`filter { pass == "final" }` from `runBackfill` and left a comment saying why
(AdDetectionService.swift:4140-4150): it "collapsed the whole timeline to the
candidate-local final chunks the moment a single final chunk existed (a
candidate-local atom timeline instead of full-episode coverage)". `runBackfill`
now passes `TranscriptChunkCanonicalizer.canonicalize(chunks)`, where a final
chunk REPLACES only the fast coverage it fully contains. The replay path never
got the fix.

## Measured, 2026-08-03 device pull (scratchpad/db-aug3/analysis.sqlite)

Asset 53FC53E3, a 2,528 s episode:

  * `transcript_chunks` holds 2,917 FAST chunks over [0, 2490] and 32 FINAL
    chunks over [2490, 2525.8]. The transcript was ~98 % complete.
  * Its one `fullEpisodeScan` job examined ONE 36 s window, [2490, 2525.82],
    and reached `complete` 23 s after creation. Measured `adScanFraction`
    **0.0142**.
  * DECISIVE: the persisted `semantic_scan_results.transcriptVersion` for that
    asset is `55afd3e8bb41833c004ee7d4b1be7589`, which is byte-exact
    `TranscriptAtomizer.transcriptVersionHash` over the 32 FINAL chunks ALONE.
    The canonical fast+final set hashes to `61872a4d3e718e8bb4b8156dc2099444`
    and fast-only to `766ea8ba068ffce5e3f48be66c9fa13f`. So the dispatcher was
    this replay path, and it discarded 2,917 of 2,949 chunks.

Reproduce: `scratchpad/r1_txversion.py` in the playhead-41mu R1 review scratch,
or re-derive the hash (SHA-256 over chunks in `canonicalTimeOrder`, each
length-prefixed `normalizedText`, first 16 bytes hex).

## Why it is worth a bead of its own

playhead-41mu's terminal now catches the CONSEQUENCE — the job defers instead of
falsely completing — but the wasted pass still happens, and every such pass is
handed the same sliver, so the row burns its whole `maxRetries` budget without
ever being able to clear the floor.

It is also a DIFFERENT bug from playhead-9new (the early-transcript dispatch).
9new's witness is AD5F3A0A, whose transcript really was the 900 s tier. 53FC53E3
was misattributed to 9new; the transcript was complete and the dispatcher threw
it away.

## The fix

Route the replay set through `TranscriptChunkCanonicalizer.canonicalize` exactly
as `runBackfill` does. The stated reason for preferring final chunks — "they
carry the higher-accuracy transcriptVersion" — is satisfied by the canonical
merge, which is where every other consumer already gets it.

Found in the playhead-41mu R1 review.
close_reason: Duplicate of playhead-iu0t (filed earlier, during playhead-fil5 R2). The field proof from this round — 53FC53E3's transcriptVersion hashing byte-exact over the 32 final chunks alone, 2,917 fast chunks discarded — is recorded on iu0t, which is now P0.

title: the coarse walk's contiguous bound is a PLAN-list prefix, written as an EPISODE prefix cursor
description:
## The defect

`BackfillJobRunner.CoarseCoverageWalk.contiguousUpperBoundSec` is documented as
"End time of the last plan in the unbroken run of fully-covered plans **from the
start of the episode**". It is not. It is the unbroken run from the start of the
PLAN LIST, and the plan list is `narrowedForResume(rootInputs, cursor)`'s output
— which need not begin at 0, because `rootInputs.segments` is whatever transcript
the dispatcher handed over.

Three writers publish that value as `backfill_jobs.progressCursor`, i.e. as an
assertion that `[0, x]` of the EPISODE is covered, which is exactly how
`narrowedForResume` consumes it (`segments.filter { endTime > cursor }`):

  * playhead-26od's incremental checkpoint (`checkpointCoarseProgress`),
  * playhead-t1kq's cancellation branch,
  * and the completion cursor at the `markBackfillJobComplete` call.

## Measured, 2026-08-03 device pull

Asset 53FC53E3 (2,528 s episode): `transcript_chunks` holds 2,917 FAST chunks
over [0, 2490] and 32 FINAL chunks over [2490, 2526]. Its `fullEpisodeScan` was
dispatched with only the final-pass tail as segments, scanned its one window, and
the row carries

    {"processedUnitCount":1,"lastProcessedUpperBoundSec":2525.82}

on a 2,528 s episode — a cursor asserting the episode is read while 98.6 % of it
was never in the job. Measured `adScanFraction` for that asset is **0.0142**.

## What playhead-41mu did and did NOT do

41mu added `underCoverageCursor`, which refuses to advance the cursor past a hole
at the head — but ONLY on its own under-coverage defer path. The other three
writers are untouched, so a rate-limit defer or a BG-window expiry on a job
dispatched against a mid-episode transcript still publishes a cursor over audio
nobody scanned, and the next resume narrows to nothing.

## The fix

Either give the walk the episode-relative bound it claims (cap the contiguous run
at the first plan's start when that start is above the prior cursor), or rename
the field and make every writer apply the head-hole rule. One rule, one place —
41mu's `underCoverageCursor` is the rule, it just is not wired to the other three
sites, and 26od's own comments already warn about exactly this drift.

Found while implementing playhead-41mu; deliberately not widened there because
the walk is 26od's code and three call sites is a different blast radius.
notes:
## playhead-41mu R1 review — the writer list above is WRONG, corrected here

The count of three is right; the membership is not. Verified against adab7bc6:

The three writers of `walk.contiguousUpperBoundSec` as `backfill_jobs.progressCursor` are
  * playhead-26od's incremental checkpoint — `checkpointCoarseProgress`, BackfillJobRunner.swift:2618  [listed above, correct]
  * playhead-pmp9's RATE-LIMIT defer — BackfillJobRunner.swift:976, via `coverage.lastCoveredUpperBoundSec` (which IS `coverageContiguousUpperBound`, set at :3011)  [OMITTED above]
  * playhead-t1kq's cancellation branch — BackfillJobRunner.swift:1128 / :1151, via `honestCursorBox.lastCoveredUpperBoundSec` (set at :3020)  [listed above, correct]

The completion cursor named above is NOT a `contiguousUpperBoundSec` writer. It is
`BackfillProgressCursor(processedPhaseCount: 1, lastProcessedUpperBoundSec: jobInputs.segments.last?.endTime)`
at BackfillJobRunner.swift:1051-1057 — a different expression, a SEGMENT-list bound rather
than a PLAN-list one. It is nonetheless the same defect shape, and it is the one that actually
wrote the 53FC53E3 row this bead quotes: the persisted JSON is `{"processedUnitCount":1,...}`,
and `processedPhaseCount: 1` is written by the completion path alone (every walk-bound writer
writes 0).

So the general defect — a list-relative bound published as an EPISODE cursor — is live at FOUR
sites: three on the walk's bound, one on the segment-list bound. playhead-41mu guards a fifth
(`underCoverageCursor`) and, for `.fullEpisodeScan`, incidentally defuses the completion one,
because after 41mu a job only completes at adScanFraction >= 0.98, where an episode-end cursor
is honest.

Separately: 53FC53E3's job was dispatched by `AdDetectionService.retryShadowFMPhaseForSession`,
which discards the fast pass entirely — see playhead-3ort. That is WHY its plan list began at
2,490 s on a transcript that was already complete.

title: mutation-battery has no worktree lock: two concurrent runs corrupt each other's verdicts and report it as a broken baseline
description:
## What actually happens

Observed 2026-08-04 during playhead-9y9e R1: four verdict attempts destroyed, each reporting

    mutation-battery: the baseline did not run tests (rc=65)

The baseline was fine. A **second** `mutation-battery.sh` was running in the same worktree, and the collision surfaced as `database is locked`.

## What is already correct — do not "fix" these

The script is well guarded and the guards work:

- `restore_sources()` (:10159) is **scoped**: `git checkout -- "${MUTABLE_FILES[@]}"`, not `.`. It cannot touch a file it does not mutate.
- `require_clean_tree()` (:10137) **refuses to start** (exit 2) when a mutable file is dirty, and its message distinguishes "your work" from "an interrupted run's mutant".
- `restore_and_verify()` (:10177) SHA-256s every mutable file **after every batch** and goes FATAL on mismatch — specifically so a failed restore cannot silently produce false KILLs in later batches.

Earlier prose in this repo (including my own summary to Dan) said the battery restores with `git checkout -- .` and destroys uncommitted work. **That is wrong** and the CLAUDE.md/battery-header wording should be corrected with it.

## The two real defects

**1. No lock. The clean-tree guard has an interleaving window.**
A holds a mutant → B starts → B sees a dirty mutable file → B correctly refuses. But between A's `restore_and_verify` and A's next `apply`, the tree is **clean**, so B passes the guard and begins. Both now mutate, and each one's restore reverts the other's mutant. Verdicts on both sides become untrustworthy, and nothing detects it: A's hash check passes because A's own restore succeeded.

Fix: a worktree-scoped `flock` held for the whole run (not per batch). On contention, name the holder — pid, start time, and its `--only` argument if any — and exit non-zero with a message that says *another battery is running here*, not *your baseline is broken*.

**2. The failure diagnoses itself as the wrong thing.**
:10415 tests `grep -q "Test run with"`; when absent it prints `the baseline did not run tests (rc=$BASE_RC)` and greps `error:|BUILD FAILED|Killed: 9`. `database is locked` matches none of those, so the operator is told the tree is broken when the cause is contention. Same shape as the defects this queue keeps finding: a message that names one thing while the cause is another.

Fix: widen the diagnostic grep to contention signatures (`database is locked`, `unable to attach`, `Mach error`, `index.lock`) and print the matched line. Absent any known signature, say plainly that the cause is undiagnosed rather than asserting the baseline failed.

## Cost of leaving it

RT11, SC25, SC30 and SC33 in the `playhead-9y9e` series still carry the IMPLEMENTER's KILLED verdicts because R1 could not obtain an independent one across four attempts. That is a real hole in the coverage ledger, created entirely by this bug.

## Verification

`scripts/mutation-battery-gate-baseline.py` (R series) and `python3 -m unittest scripts.tests.test_gate_baseline`. A rail for the lock itself: start a long batch, start a second, assert the second exits non-zero naming the first, and assert the first's verdicts are unaffected.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
## Deferred to the END of the queue (Dan, 2026-08-04): after the device install, not before.

Order is now: 41mu -> e75l -> dl9k -> DEVICE BUILD + INSTALL -> pu7e.

**A 585-line draft already exists** and is preserved at `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-dabrams-playhead/pu7e-draft/mutation-battery-lock.sh`. It was written by a duplicate loop running in a second process before that process was shut down; it was never committed and its worktree is removed. Start from it rather than from scratch, but review it — it has had no review round.

## Add this to the scope — a THIRD misattribution, found by 9y9e R3

`rc=65` currently reads to an operator as "a concurrent battery", but R3 measured a run where competing batteries were **zero** and the tree was clean, and the real cause in `baseline.log` was:

    blessSimulatorHub failed. Simulator service hub IS NOT still alive
    Test crashed with signal kill before establishing connection

**The simulator was wedged.** Worse, the battery surfaces `xcrun: error: unable to find utility "simctl"` in that path, which is a *secondary* symptom from xcodebuild's diagnostic-collection shelling out through the global `xcode-select` — it actively misdirects toward the 2026-07-16 gotcha. R3 recovered with `simctl shutdown all` + boot (DEVELOPER_DIR-qualified) and the very next run reached `baseline green`.

So the diagnostic needs to separate at least three causes that currently all print as one line:
1. a concurrent battery (`database is locked`, `index.lock`)
2. a wedged simulator (`blessSimulatorHub`, `Simulator service hub IS NOT still alive`, `signal kill before establishing connection`) — and it should suggest the recovery
3. genuinely undiagnosed — say so, rather than asserting the baseline failed

R3 also notes the sim wedge is a shared root cause with the full-plan gate producing no terminal verdict at 40 GiB free, which is evidence for `playhead-s08j` that the shortfall there is NOT purely capacity.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
## Implementation landed on bead/playhead-pu7e (commit 6180b952) — premises verified first

**All three premises CONFIRMED against c36770bb** (line numbers moved by 6r4z/#353):

1. **No lock.** `command -v flock` is EMPTY on this box — flock(1) is util-linux and macOS does not ship it, and bash has no flock builtin. So the lock is an atomic `mkdir` in the worktree's own git dir (`.git/worktrees/<slug>/mutation-battery.lock`), carrying a payload flock could not have held anyway: pid, pid start time, argv, and every mutable file's pristine + mutant hash. `require_clean_tree` is :12534 (called once at :12787) and `restore_and_verify` :12574 — the window between them is exactly as described.
2. **rc=65 misdiagnosis.** `grep -q "Test run with"` is at :12854 (baseline) and :12948 (batch); the diagnostic grep was `error:|BUILD FAILED|Killed: 9` in both.
3. **Stale `dr-*.log`.** REFUTED as a defect *of this script* — `WORK` is a fresh `mktemp -d` per run, so the battery's own logs cannot be stale. The hole is in the ad-hoc operator collection procedure. Took the cheap in-file half (the run is now stamped with start time + pid + argv at the HEAD **and** the FOOT, so a stale file is self-identifying from its own contents); filed the rest as **playhead-wj8u** (P2).

**A defect in the draft, found and fixed:** it read a lock directory with no `info` yet as STALE and reclaimed it — which would steal the lock from a holder in the microseconds between its `mkdir` and its first write, i.e. hand the worktree to a second battery at the exact moment the first starts. Now: wait for `info` (5 s), then refuse; a directory still empty after 5 minutes is reclaimed as ABANDONED, which is safe because no `info` means no recorded state means no mutation was ever applied under it. Both directions have rails.

**Order matters and is now enforced:** the lock is acquired BEFORE `require_clean_tree`. A live holder mid-batch has a mutant on disk, so checking the tree first tells the second run "commit your work first" — the same misattribution one layer over.

**Rails:** `scripts/tests/test_mutation_battery_lock.py`, 26 tests, 22.6 s, no build. Four drive the real battery two-process. Every absence assertion carries a positive control on its own observer.

**Measured live, against a genuinely running battery (pid 5463, `--only M05`):**
```
mutation-battery: REFUSING — another mutation battery is already running in this worktree.
mutation-battery:   holder pid : 5463
mutation-battery:   started    : 2026-08-06 05:20:15 EDT (21s ago)
mutation-battery:   invoked as : --only M05
EXIT=75
```
The holder was unaffected and ran on to its verdict.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
## DONE on bead/playhead-pu7e — 4 commits, tree clean, no PR opened

Final verification on the committed state: `scripts/mutation-battery.sh --only M07` -> **baseline green, M07 KILLED, 0 survivors / 0 errors, 2 builds, 4m26s, exit 0**, tree clean, lock released. Earlier on the same branch `--only M05` -> same shape, 8m48s (cold).

### Four more defects found by DRIVING the battery, not reading it — all the same shape as the bead's own

1. **SIGPIPE left the lock AND the mutant on disk.** Bash's default SIGPIPE disposition kills the shell WITHOUT running the EXIT trap, so `mutation-battery.sh … | head` died mid-report with its mutation applied and its lock held. Operators pipe this constantly. `trap … PIPE` now.
2. **Trapping PIPE was not enough**, and this one is worth remembering. At EPIPE bash holds an unflushed stdout buffer from the failed write; a command substitution forks a subshell that INHERITS it and flushes it into the substitution's own pipe. `mb_lock_release` read its owner as `74929\n=== batch 1: 1 mutation(s) ===`, compared that to `$$`, and declined to release its own lock — a message accurate about what it read and wrong about the world. Fixed twice: the trap does `exec >/dev/null` first, and the owner is read with a fork-free bash loop.
3. **Recovery could half-restore and then say it had not.** It restored as it walked, so an objection on the fourth file left the first three already checked out, under "Nothing has been changed." Two passes now — classify, then act — and a pass-2 failure says so instead of borrowing pass 1's guarantee.
4. **An untouched file was accused of carrying a mutant.** A batch mutates 1-2 files but the lock records `post` for all 57, so an untouched one has post == pre; editing it after a crash was refused (correct) with a printed "mutant" hash byte-identical to the pristine one.

### Verbatim rails
- `python3 -m unittest scripts.tests.test_mutation_battery_lock` -> **Ran 31 tests in 27.7s, OK**
- `python3 -m unittest scripts.tests.test_gate_baseline scripts.tests.test_disk_preflight` -> **Ran 128 tests, OK (skipped=1)**
- `scripts/mutation-battery-gate-baseline.py` -> **33 mutation(s): 32 killed, 0 survived, 0 error, control OK-SURVIVED**
- `scripts/lint.sh --changed` -> `no lintable Swift files changed` (no Swift touched — NOT coverage)

### Not evaluated, stated plainly
- The **diagnosis** is verified against synthetic logs carrying R1's and R3's measured signatures. No real contention or wedge occurred during this work, so it has not been seen firing on a live one. Note also that the lock now PREVENTS the same-worktree contention case from ever reaching the diagnosis — its CONTENTION branch remains live for cross-worktree collisions, which the lock does not scope.
- Only M05 and M07 of 417 entries were run to a verdict; the full plan was not attempted (playhead-q1go).

### Filed
- **playhead-wj8u** (P2) — verdict collection: a stale `dr-*.log` still reads KILLED to a `grep -c`. pu7e's run stamp makes it detectable by reading one line; a collector would make it undetectable-by-omission.
- **playhead-zsqh** (P2) — a killed battery leaves its `xcodebuild` child running. Observed here (pid 41050 outlived its SIGKILLed parent). pu7e's prompt lock release makes the next run start straight into a shared sim an orphan is still using.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
## Review round (single) — 3 defects found by PLANTING, all fixed; commit 0abedbc1. Merge recommended.

Probed the three harm modes the lock could introduce. **False refusal: one defect, fixed. False grant: two defects, fixed. Lost work: no defect — every rail holds.**

### F1 — FALSE GRANT (High). A holder that could not record its identity kept the tree and lost the lock.

**Probe.** `mkdir` shadowed to chmod 500 the lock directory it creates, i.e. the state a full volume leaves: directory present, identity unwritable. Shipped code: `EXIT=0  OWNED=1`, `info size: ABSENT`. Then backdate the directory 5 minutes and a second battery: `reclaiming an ABANDONED lock … Nothing was recorded, therefore nothing was mutated under it` → `EXIT=0  OWNED=1`. **Two batteries, one worktree** — the bead's own defect.

`mb__write_info`'s redirection was unchecked and `mb_lock_acquire` set `MB_LOCK_OWNED=1` regardless. Reachable on this box: ENOSPC (100 % capacity four times on 2026-08-01), EDQUOT, EACCES. The ABANDONED rule reads *no owner recorded* as *no owner ever existed*, and that inference was assumed, not enforced.

**Fix.** `mb__take` makes mkdir + record one step that either happens or does not, and REMOVES the directory it created rather than leaving it ownerless — leaving it is what arms ABANDONED. **Re-plant:** `EXIT=2  OWNED=0`, "could NOT record who holds it", directory gone; the second run finds nothing to abandon.

### F2 — FALSE REFUSAL, misdiagnosed (Medium). `mkdir` failing was reported as contention.

**Probe.** `chmod 500 .git`, nobody holding: `REFUSING — lost the race … Another run took it while this one was waiting.  EXIT=75`. 75 is EX_TEMPFAIL — wait for a process that does not exist. ENOSPC, EROFS and a missing parent all land here too.

**Fix.** The directory's own existence is the discriminator and it is free. **Re-plant:** `EXIT=2`, "could NOT create the run lock and NOBODY holds it … this is NOT contention and waiting will not help", quoting mkdir's own `Permission denied`. A regular file at the lock path is now named as such.

### F3 — FALSE GRANT on a malformed record (Medium).

**Probe.** Plant `pid=<live>\npid_start=Thu Aug` (truncated). Shipped: `reclaiming a STALE lock — pid 72127 is gone` → `EXIT=0  OWNED=1`, **while the named pid was running**. A fragment mismatches exactly like a recycled pid does. `info` was written non-atomically while `state` was already temp-and-renamed *for this reason*.

**Fix.** `info` is renamed into place, so this code can no longer author a partial one; plus a second wall — a recorded pid is not believed dead while that pid is running a mutation battery. **Re-plant:** `EXIT=75  OWNED=0`, "pid … IS RUNNING A MUTATION BATTERY right now", holder's lock intact, holder still running. The recycled-pid reclaim is unaffected and keeps its existing rail as the positive control.

### Also fixed
- `mb_lock_record_pre` reports a failed state write instead of discarding it (same unchecked-write class, one call later, and the last free moment before the first mutation); `|| exit 2` at the call site.
- **playhead-zsqh, in scope to assess:** RUNNER-NEVER-LAUNCHED now names a live xcodebuild BEFORE offering `simctl shutdown all`. Reproduced here — orphan pid 50621 outlived its SIGKILLed parent 44904 — and the shutdown loses to an orphan that boots the device again underneath it. **Judgement: releasing the lock promptly is NOT worse than holding it.** The orphan is named on the way in by `mb_warn_if_xcodebuild_running` (observed firing) and diagnosed on the way out; before this bead the next run started silently and reported rc=65 as a broken baseline. Refusing on any live xcodebuild would be wrong — the lock's scope is source corruption in THIS worktree.

### The four self-found defects — all four verified
SIGPIPE (`--dry-run --only M05 | head -4`): lock released, tree clean. Both belt and braces present — `exec >/dev/null` in the PIPE trap AND the fork-free owner read in `mb_lock_release`. Recovery is two-pass (probe: refusal left `MY PRECIOUS UNCOMMITTED WORK` on disk and said "nothing was restored"). `post == pre` is refused as somebody's edit, not called a mutant.

### Lost work — no defect
`restore_sources` is scoped to `MUTABLE_FILES`; `require_clean_tree` exits 2; `restore_and_verify` SHA-256s after every batch and only then drops the `post` hashes; 6r4z's assertion fires before the lock (:12819 vs :12876). Recovery refuses on a foreign edit (both the mutated-file and the untouched-file cases) and keeps the bytes.

### Premise 3 refutation CONFIRMED
`WORK` has exactly one assignment — `WORK="$(mktemp -d …)"` at :1765 — with no env default and no reuse. The battery's own logs cannot be stale. `playhead-wj8u` is the right home for the operator-collection half.

### Residuals, stated
- A pid recycled onto an *unrelated* process whose recorded start time matches to the second still refuses (probe PD). Safe direction; needs a manual `rm`.
- A partial `info` whose pid is recycled onto a non-battery still reclaims (probe PE3). No longer producible by this code.
- If `rm -rf` also fails after a failed identity write, the directory stays — same as before, but the operator is now told.

### Verbatim
- `python3 -m unittest scripts.tests.test_mutation_battery_lock` → **Ran 39 tests in 27.779s, OK** (was 31; 8 new)
- all three modules → **Ran 167 tests in 29.053s, OK (skipped=1)**
- `scripts/mutation-battery-gate-baseline.py` → **33 mutation(s): 32 killed, 0 survived, 0 error, control OK-SURVIVED**
- `scripts/mutation-battery.sh --only M07` → **baseline green, M07 KILLED, 0 survivors / 0 errors, 2 builds, 4m25s, exit 0**, tree clean, lock released
- live contention vs pid 28694 → **EXIT=75**, holder named (pid/start/argv), holder ran on to its verdict; `--list` still needs no lock
- SIGKILL mid-batch → mutant + lock left; next run reclaimed, restored verbatim with a rescue copy, named the orphan, tree clean
- `scripts/lint.sh --changed` → `no lintable Swift files changed`. **Not coverage** — this bead is bash and Python; the rails above are the coverage.

### Not evaluated
Full plan not attempted (playhead-q1go). Only M05/M07 of 417 entries run to a verdict. The diagnosis branches are still verified against synthetic logs carrying R1's and R3's measured signatures — no real contention or wedge occurred; the new orphan branch was driven with a live fake `xcodebuild` and has a negative control. Cross-worktree collision (which the lock does not scope) unexercised.

**Merge judgement: MERGE.** The lock is a net reduction in failure modes even before this round; with F1–F3 closed I could not construct a state where it grants twice, refuses without cause, or destroys work. No PR opened, worktree clean.

title: Reach: five assets' ad-scan re-drive budget is spent on passes that reached Stage 4 and bailed at a fil5 gate — no rescue reaches them
description:
## The population

On the 2026-08-03 device pull, five assets have both `adScanRedrive` ordinals
spent and coverage-lane rows still outstanding:

    DE0784D8  :1 complete (no error)   :2 complete (no error)
    D9B513CD  :1 complete (no error)   :2 complete (no error)
    83592353  :1 complete (no error)   :2 complete (no error)
    58882C47  :1 complete (no error)   :2 complete (no error)
    44F076BB  :1 coverageInsufficient:noProgress   :2 same

`AnalysisWorkScheduler.nextAdScanRedriveWorkKey` returns nil at ordinal 3
(`maxAdScanRedrives = 2`), so neither the scheduler's terminal arms nor
`AnalysisJobReconciler.mintAdScanRedrives` can mint for them again.

## Why the two existing rescues do not reach them

* **playhead-y8f3's cap-out retry** requires `isAttemptCapTerminal` — state
  `superseded` AND a `maxAttemptsReached:` prefix. All ten of these rows are
  `complete`. (playhead-9y9e widened y8f3's OTHER refusal, the transcript-only
  `noOutstandingWork` decline, which is what unblocks AD5F3A0A — a genuine
  attempt-cap terminal. It does nothing for these five.)
* **playhead-fil5's claim sweep** selects assets with ZERO coverage-lane rows.
  These have rows.

## Why the budget was spent

Not on playhead-9y9e's defect. These re-drives terminated `complete` with an
empty `lastErrorCode`, i.e. they reached Stage 4. 58882C47 has 8 ad_windows with
2 candidates, so `shouldSkipSemanticBackfill` cannot have fired
(`semanticBackfillHasNoOtherWork` is false whenever candidates remain) — meaning
`runBackfill` ran and the shadow phase bailed at one of the four gates
playhead-fil5 has since made recordable. Those bails were silent on the shipped
build, which is precisely why the budget looks spent for no reason.

So the budget was fairly charged under the old accounting, and what has changed
is that the gate is now recorded and (for the transient ones) survivable. That is
a real argument for a rescue, and it is also why the rescue must not be a bare
`maxAdScanRedrives += 1`: the next silent-gate era would consume the extra
ordinal the same way.

## Options, none taken here

1. **Charge the ordinal only for a pass that reached the SCAN.** The ledger is
   meant to bound FM passes; a pass that never called the model bought nothing.
   Costs a query over the chain's rows and a judgement about which
   `lastErrorCode`s mean "pre-scan".
2. **Budget per transcript version rather than per (fingerprint,
   analysisVersion).** Principled — a new transcript is a new scan question —
   but the workKey carries no version and adding one changes the key shape.
3. **Tombstone the chain** the way `retiredStaleCanonicalWorkKey` already
   tombstones a stale-fingerprint row, letting a fresh chain start from `:1`.
   Needs its own bound or it is an unbounded retry.

Dan's call which, if any. The measured cost of doing nothing is five episodes
with outstanding coverage-lane work and no path to a pass until the 7-day
`analysis_jobs` GC lets `discoverUnEnqueuedDownloads` re-mint — and only if the
audio is still cached.
notes:
## CORRECTION — playhead-9y9e R1 review, 2026-08-04.

Two things in the prose, both re-derived from the 2026-08-03 pull.

1. **"These re-drives terminated `complete` with an empty `lastErrorCode`" is not
   true of all five.** The table above is right and the sentence generalises past
   it: 44F076BB's two ordinals are `complete` with
   `lastErrorCode = 'coverageInsufficient:noProgress'` (`typeof()` = 'text', not
   NULL and not ''). Four assets carry NULL; the fifth carries a named terminal.
   That matters for option 1 — "charge the ordinal only for a pass that reached
   the SCAN" needs a judgement about which `lastErrorCode`s mean "pre-scan", and
   44F076BB is the one row in this population that already has one to read.

2. **A sixth asset has a re-drive, and its budget is NOT spent.** 0C2FC22E's
   `…:adScanRedrive:1` is `queued` with `transcription:cancelled` and no `:2`
   exists. Correctly excluded from the budget-spent population; worth naming so
   the next reader does not rediscover it as a seventh case.

Neither changes the bead's argument or its three options.

## CORRECTION — playhead-9y9e R1 review, 2026-08-04.

The prose says "These re-drives terminated `complete` with an empty
`lastErrorCode`, i.e. they reached Stage 4." The TABLE above is right and the
sentence over-generalises: 44F076BB's two ordinals both terminated `complete`
with `lastErrorCode = 'coverageInsufficient:noProgress'` (typeof `text`, not
empty and not NULL). Four of the five carry NULL; the fifth does not.

That distinction matters to option 1 ("charge the ordinal only for a pass that
reached the SCAN"), because 44F076BB is the one row in this population whose
error code already says something about WHY, and it says the pass read
1,620 s of a 1,977 s episode — a transcript-lane shortfall, not a silent
shadow-phase gate. It is the weakest member of the "budget spent for no reason"
argument, not a representative one.

Also for the record: 0C2FC22E is a SIXTH asset with an `adScanRedrive` row —
ordinal 1 only, `queued`, `transcription:cancelled`. Its budget is NOT spent, so
excluding it from this population is correct; noted so a later reader does not
re-derive it as a discrepancy.

title: gate_baseline gives a CONFIDENT verdict on an INTERRUPTED log if the run got far enough
description:
## Observed 2026-08-04, playhead-fil5 R7

A SIGTERM'd full-plan run produced:

```
gate-baseline: RED (51 known / 1 NEW)
```

with **30 baseline members reported as "passed this run, removal candidate"** — purely because the run was killed before reaching them. A second, shorter interruption correctly printed `CANNOT EVALUATE — the log is incomplete`.

So the incomplete-log guard catches the silent wedge, but **not an interrupted run that got far enough to look plausible**. The failure mode is the dangerous direction: it invites removing baseline entries that were never executed, which would then be reported as NEW on the next run — or worse, promotes entries toward `deterministic` on evidence that does not exist.

## Why it matters more now

playhead-<the disk bead> means full-plan runs on this box are routinely killed part-way. Under the old assumption (runs either complete or wedge silently) this gap was rare; it is now the common case.

## Suggested fix

Require positive evidence of completion before emitting a membership verdict — e.g. the terminal `Test Session Results` / `** TEST (SUCCEEDED|FAILED) **` marker, or a count of finished-vs-started that closes. Absent that, print `CANNOT EVALUATE` regardless of how far the log got. A pass-direction claim in particular must never be made from a truncated log.

Not this diff's defect — pre-existing, found while verifying playhead-fil5. Rails: `scripts/gate_baseline.py`, `python3 -m unittest scripts.tests.test_gate_baseline`, `scripts/mutation-battery-gate-baseline.py` (R series).

title: Reach: a fully-covered coarse pass with NO ad windows pays for its whole rescan to protect refinement that does not exist
description:
Found by playhead-26od R5 while investigating (and rejecting) a proposed change to the same site.

playhead-t1kq's rule: when a `CancellationError` arrives with the coarse pass FULLY COVERED, `runJob` does not fill `honestCursorBox`, so the drain loop's not-advanced arm writes `job.progressCursor` — the admission-time value — over whatever the run had reached. Since playhead-26od the mid-flight checkpoint has usually put a real partial cursor there, so the write NULLS it and the next granted window re-does the entire coarse pass (12-45 min of FM on device).

That is CORRECT as a default and must not be naively "fixed". `planAdaptiveZoom` plans refinement from the IN-MEMORY `FMCoarseScanOutput` of the run that is executing, never from persisted rows, so any coarse window a resume does not re-scan is a window that never gets refined — by any later run. Carrying the checkpointed cursor forward therefore trades "pay the coarse pass again" for "every ad window below the cursor stays at COARSE extent forever", and an unrefined mark is a suggest banner whose inner edges eat show. t1kq chose the re-scan; that is the right way round.

THE NARROW CASE THAT IS NOT COVERED BY THAT ARGUMENT: a fully-covered coarse pass in which NO window returned `containsAd`. `planAdaptiveZoom` then returns no zoom plans, there is no refinement to strand, and the rewind costs a whole coarse pass and buys nothing at all. On a clean episode — which is most of a long tail — that is pure treadmill.

WHY IT IS NOT A 26od CHANGE: knowing there is no refinement pending requires `planAdaptiveZoom`, which runs AFTER the `Task.checkCancellation()` that produces the cancellation. Answering it means either moving that check or deciding "no containsAd window" from `coarse.windows` before planning (cheap and probably sufficient — `planAdaptiveZoom` keys off the same dispositions). Either way it re-specifies t1kq's rule, so it wants measuring on a device pull first: how many fully-covered-then-cancelled jobs had zero `containsAd` coarse rows?

VERIFICATION NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS: the guard rail is `a task cancellation after FULL coarse coverage does NOT checkpoint an episode-end cursor (would strand refinement)` in BackfillRateLimitDeferTests.swift. It goes red the moment the cursor is carried forward, which is how R5's proposed fix was caught.

title: Resume cursor is an episode-time scalar applied to a RE-DERIVED anchor population — scattered-anchor phases can strand audio no row covers
description:
## The defect

`BackfillProgressCursor.lastProcessedUpperBoundSec` is an EPISODE-TIME SCALAR, and
`BackfillJobRunner.narrowedForResume` consumes it by dropping every segment whose
`endTime <= cursor`. That is only sound when the population the cursor was computed over
is the same population the resume is narrowing — which is true for `.fullEpisodeScan` and
FALSE for every phase whose inputs are phase-narrowed to scattered anchors
(`.scanHarvesterProposals`, `.scanLikelyAdSlots`, `.scanRandomAuditWindows`).

`runJob` applies `narrowedForResume` to the ALREADY phase-narrowed `jobInputs`
(`BackfillJobRunner.swift`, top of `runJob`). The anchor set is RE-DERIVED on every run
from current DB state, and for `.scanRandomAuditWindows` it is re-derived *deliberately
differently*: `TargetedWindowNarrower.Inputs.episodesSinceLastFullRescan` is mixed into
`auditSeed` "so consecutive observations of the same (podcastId, transcriptVersion) rotate
across distinct audit windows".

So:

- run 1 of an audit job covers its anchor at 200-240 s and checkpoints cursor 240;
- the job does not finish (rate limit -> pmp9 defer, BG expiry -> t1kq salvage, or — since
  playhead-26od — a jetsam mid-pass);
- run 2 re-narrows and this time selects an audit block at 90-200 s;
- `narrowedForResume(240)` DROPS it. No row covers 90-200, the job then marks complete, and
  the M-5 idempotency gate skips the row forever.

The cursor was honest about run 1's population. The unsound step is the consumer applying an
episode-time scalar to a re-derived population — so this is a `narrowedForResume` /
cursor-contract defect, not a defect in any one writer.

## Provenance and why it is filed rather than fixed in playhead-26od

PRE-EXISTING. playhead-pmp9's rate-limit defer branch and playhead-t1kq's CancellationError
salvage already persist this cursor for these phases; 26od only adds a third writer (the
mid-flight checkpoint) on the jetsam path. Gating 26od's cursor write to `.fullEpisodeScan`
would NOT close the hole — pmp9 and t1kq would still reach it — so there is no 26od-local
change that fixes this, and 26od's reviewers deliberately did not narrow a shipped contract
on the way past. Raised by 26od's R2 adversarial review.

Note what IS fixed in 26od and is a different bug: within a SINGLE population, a covered plan
could end after an uncovered plan began (plan time ranges overlap because `planPassA` slices
by `segmentIndex` and playhead-csbq measured the atom sequence is not time-monotone on 27 of
30 device assets). `coarseCoverageWalk` now caps the cursor at the earliest uncovered plan's
`startTime`. That fix is population-internal and does nothing for this bead.

## Candidate directions (settle by measurement, not assumption)

1. Do not narrow at all for scattered-anchor phases — `narrowedForResume` returns `inputs`
   unless `job.phase == .fullEpisodeScan`. Cheapest and obviously sound; costs those phases
   their resume, so it re-pays FM for anchors that already have rows. Measure that cost
   before choosing it.
2. Make the cursor population-aware: persist WHICH plans/segments were scanned (the scan rows
   already carry `windowFirstAtomOrdinal`/`windowLastAtomOrdinal`), and narrow by "has a
   durable row" rather than by a time scalar. Strictly better and strictly more work; it also
   subsumes direction 1 and would make the whole class of cursor-vs-population bugs
   unrepresentable.
3. Freeze the anchor set per job: derive the narrowing once at enqueue and persist it, so a
   resume faces the population its cursor describes. Interacts with why the audit block
   rotates in the first place (Cycle 2 Rev3-M3).

## Verification a fix needs

A test that runs a targeted phase twice with a DIFFERENT anchor set on the second run and
asserts no segment lacking a durable row is dropped from the resume. Today no such test
exists — every resume test in `BackfillRateLimitDeferTests` / `BackfillCoarseCheckpointTests`
uses `.fullEpisodeScan`, where the population is stable by construction.
notes:
## Exposure rate — correction from playhead-26od's R3/R4 review (2026-08-04)

The description above says 26od 'only adds a third writer ... on the jetsam path'. That word
'only' understates it and must not be carried into 26od's PR unqualified. The mid-flight
checkpoint is installed in `runJob` UNCONDITIONALLY — it is not gated on `job.phase` — so after
26od every phase writes a resume cursor on the jetsam path, which 26od's own field evidence says
is the DOMINANT one (10 of 10 jobs in the 2026-08-03 device pull died mid-pass).

Before 26od the scattered-anchor phases (.scanHarvesterProposals / .scanLikelyAdSlots /
.scanRandomAuditWindows) acquired a cursor only via pmp9's rate-limit defer or t1kq's graceful
cancellation — both comparatively rare. After it they acquire one on the common death.

So: the DEFECT is unchanged, no 26od-local fix exists (see the three points above, all confirmed
by R3 and R4), and no fix belongs in 26od. But its EXPOSURE RATE rises, and that is the reason
this bead is P1 rather than a curiosity.

title: a checkpointed coarse row is never re-scanned, so it is never refined — coarse extent becomes permanent
description:
DECIDED BY DAN 2026-08-03, arising from playhead-26od's review. He chose 'make them refinable' over narrowing y3ya or accepting permanent coarse extent.

## The harm 26od introduces

Before 26od, a coarse pass killed mid-flight left NOTHING. The audio was eventually re-scanned — and on that re-scan it was also REFINED, so its extent got tightened before it ever reached the listener.

After 26od, the screened prefix is durable and the resume cursor means that audio is never re-scanned. `SemanticSweepMarkComposer.presenceExtents` stage 2 emits the COARSE extent verbatim when no passB overlaps (ships ON), so those verdicts surface at coarse width and STAY THERE FOREVER. Durability bought reach and, as a side effect, froze precision.

This is not an argument against 26od — the reach win is the dominant term and Dan took it deliberately. It is the follow-through that keeps the widened marks from being permanently imprecise.

## Why it is NOT a surfacing fix (measured, playhead-26od R1)

Requiring a refinement before a coarse verdict may surface is a GLOBAL narrowing of playhead-y3ya, not a 26od rail:
  * there is no row-level witness separating 26od's rows from y3ya's — y3ya's own field case (DE0784D8) is a pass that RETURNED with a non-.success status, which skips refinement, producing the same rows with the same absent passB;
  * the change measured 38 failing assertions across SIX merged y3ya suites, including y3ya's own acceptance test, plus every later composer stage losing its input.

So the fix belongs on the REFINEMENT side, not the surfacing side.

## The work

Make refinement able to run over already-checkpointed coarse rows. The resume cursor must keep its promise for the COARSE pass (do not re-run FM presence over screened audio — that is 26od's entire value) while still allowing passB refinement to visit those spans and tighten their extents.

Open questions to settle with measurement, not assumption:
  * what currently drives passB, and does it key off the same cursor that 26od advances?
  * can refinement be scheduled independently of the coarse sweep, or does it require a pass that the cursor now suppresses?
  * cost: refinement is cheaper than a coarse pass, but not free — bound it the way 26od bounded checkpoint writes.

## Acceptance

  * A coarse row persisted mid-flight is later refined, and its surfaced extent narrows accordingly.
  * The negative: the coarse FM presence pass is still NOT re-run over that audio — 26od's reach win is not traded back.
  * A row that has already been refined is not refined again (idempotency).
  * Use playhead-le02's idiom: a negative assertion needs a positive witness.

Related: [[playhead-26od]] (creates the condition), [[playhead-y3ya]] (owns the surfacing behaviour, deliberately unchanged), [[playhead-41mu]] (`complete` claimed rather than measured — same accounting family).

title: Prologue FMInferenceTimeoutError (30s metadata bound) still spends lifetime retry budget — same daemon-condition class kvs8 fixed for the throttle
description:
## The defect (STILL BROKEN at d3dfa1ca)

A wedged-daemon timeout in the pass PROLOGUE still lands in the generic catch-all and is recorded as a job failure: `FMInferenceTimeoutError` from the `metadata` 30s bound (FMInferenceDeadline.swift:169, guarding `tokenCount` XPC round trips in promptBudget/planPassA per qk44) escapes runJob and hits BackfillJobRunner.swift:1160-1178 -> `markBackfillJobFailed(reason: String(describing:), retryCount+1)`.

playhead-kvs8 (#320, 0dc34200) fixed EXACTLY this disposition for the throttle sibling — named catch above the catch-all (BackfillJobRunner.swift:1100-1148), DEFER not fail, retryCount preserved, groupable token — and its own doc argues the principle: a daemon condition "says nothing about the job". A tokenCount timeout is the same class of daemon condition (the daemon wedged/slow), not evidence about this job or this model window (8d5r's consecutive-timeout counter deliberately counts only in-window inference timeouts). Three wedged-daemon moments currently disqualify an episode forever: retryCount cap is `AdmissionController.maxRetries = 3` (AdmissionController.swift:99), enforced at BackfillJobRunner.swift:552-554.

## Measured on the 2026-08-03 device pull

0C2FC22E: backfill_jobs row `failed`, deferReason `FMInferenceTimeoutError(deadline: 30.0 seconds)`, retryCount 1, created 08-03 15:21:38, failed 15:22:31 — 53s into the pass, i.e. the prologue, while the device was concurrently running AD5F3A0A's pass (daemon under load). One of its 3 lifetime attempts is spent on a daemon condition.

Note the deadline itself is CORRECT and should stay 30s: it bounds tokenizer metadata calls, not inference (scan-window inference is bounded by `standard` = 300s, FMInferenceDeadline.swift:142). The defect is the DISPOSITION, not the number.

## The fix

Extend the kvs8 named-catch to prologue `FMInferenceTimeoutError`: defer with a named resumable cause (e.g. `inferenceTimeout-prologue`), preserve retryCount, count toward the kvs8 consecutive-daemon-refusal drain abort.
notes:
## QUEUE 3 — REACH, Dan 2026-08-03. Six beads from the device-pull investigation.

    26od -> fil5 -> 9y9e -> 41mu -> e75l -> dl9k

**Why this queue exists.** A fresh device pull (2026-08-03, scratchpad/db-aug3/analysis.sqlite,
the first usable field data in two weeks) measured: **12 episodes, 9 transcribed to ~100%, only 3

PREMISE CONFIRMED at c2835be9, then FIXED (commit 8230c4ae, branch bead/playhead-e75l, NOT merged).

VERIFICATION OF THE PREMISE. Line numbers moved (kvs8's arm 1100-1148 -> 1296-1355; catch-all 1160-1178 -> 1356-1393) but the escape path holds exactly. FMInferenceTimeoutError is not CancellationError, not AnalysisStoreError, and SemanticScanStatus.from(error:) maps it to .inferenceTimeout not .rateLimited so FMDaemonThrottle.isThrottle is false -> generic catch-all -> markBackfillJobFailed(retryCount+1). Proven empirically by the pre-fix RED run, which logged 'FM backfill job ... failed: case=untyped detail=FMInferenceTimeoutError(deadline: 30.0 seconds)' — the field row verbatim.

FIELD NUMBERS RE-DERIVED from db-aug3-work/analysis.sqlite. 0C2FC22E: failed / retryCount 1 / deferReason 'FMInferenceTimeoutError(deadline: 30.0 seconds)' / created 15:21:38 / updated 15:22:31 = 52.2 s (bead said 53 s). Zero semantic_scan_results rows for the asset, so it was the prologue. Denominator: 14 backfill_jobs rows, 2 of them 'failed', and 2 of 2 are daemon conditions (one rate-limit prose = kvs8's row, one metadata timeout = this one); 0 of 2 are the job's own merits.

ONE BEAD CLAIM NOT SUPPORTED. 'while the device was concurrently running AD5F3A0A's pass' does not reproduce: AD5F3A0A's last backfill_jobs row updated 08-03 10:18:52, and there are ZERO semantic_scan_results rows anywhere in the 15:00-16:00 hour. The load context is unverified. Nothing else in the bead depends on it.

THE FIX. New Playhead/Services/AdDetection/FMDaemonRefusal.swift names the class kvs8's doc already argued for ('a daemon condition says nothing about the job'), with .throttle and .metadataStall. kvs8's catch arm is GENERALIZED to it rather than copied, so the drain keeps one counter that cannot disagree with itself. Defer, retryCount preserved, named cause, counts toward the same consecutive-stop threshold (delegated to FMDaemonThrottle, not duplicated).

DISCRIMINATOR IS THE BUDGET, NOT THE TYPE: error.deadline == FMInferenceDeadline.metadata. A standard (300 s) timeout stays a failure — it is evidence about the MODEL, consecutiveInferenceTimeoutAbortThreshold already escalates it in-window, it cannot reach the drain loop today (.inferenceTimeout has failureScope == .window so both passes RETURN rather than throw), and the cost bound is what licenses kvs8's 'no terminal cause': 30 s per drain is cheap to retry forever, 300 s per window is not.

NAMING (the standing defect class). The counter's meaning genuinely broadened, so throttledThisJob -> daemonRefusalThisJob (carrying the KIND, not a flag) and consecutiveThrottledJobs -> consecutiveDaemonRefusals. Swept siblings now get inferenceTimeout-batchSibling when a stall stopped the drain; rateLimited-batchSibling there would record a rate limit that never happened. kvs8's four tokens are byte-identical and the new ones share no prefix, so grepping rateLimited- still counts rate limits. No production code reads or filters on deferReason (verified) — it is a pure audit artifact.

TESTS. New PlayheadTests/Services/AdDetection/FMDaemonMetadataStallTests.swift: 6 definition tests + 10 runner tests, including threeStallsDoNotDisqualifyTheEpisode which drives maxRetries stalls then a healthy run and asserts the episode still completes (the reach cost end-to-end, not inferred from retryCount). TestFMRuntimeFailure gains .metadataTimeout, deriving its Duration from the production constant.

GATE. lint --changed clean. Scoped: 144 Swift Testing tests in 12 suites PASSED + FMDaemonThrottleCanaryTests 'Executed 2 tests, with 0 failures' — 0 failures in BOTH formats. Suites covered: the two new ones, all four kvs8 suites, BackfillJobRunnerTests, BackfillRateLimitDeferTests, BackfillStallBoundTests, BackfillCoverageTerminalTests, BackfillCoarseCheckpointTests, BackfillJobRunnerJobCompletePersistenceInvariantTests. Two mutations applied and both KILLED by the predicted rails. NOT EVALUATED: the full plan (unobtainable on this box, playhead-q1go) and the mutation battery beyond the two hand-run mutations.

SEPARATE-BEAD CANDIDATES, not widened into this diff:
1. A drain in which every job was refused by the daemon still bumps the coverage planner's observedEpisodeCount / episodesSinceLastFullRescan, because the jobs WERE admitted. The comment at BackfillJobRunner.swift ~1478 says a wholesale-deferred run 'never touched the transcript and must not bump the counter' — a daemon-refused run touched it just as little. Pre-existing, applies to kvs8's throttle identically.
2. kvs8's DeferCause.passPrologue ('rateLimited-prologue') is written for ANY throttle escaping runJob, including from planAdaptiveZoom / planExpansionWindow / refinePassB planning — its doc claims 'before a single window was planned', which is not true on those paths. The same latitude exists for the new metadata token, which is why it is named for the BOUND that elapsed rather than for a position in the pass.

comments.text:
R1 REVIEW (review-and-fix) — 4 findings, all FIXED in-branch. Commits 6e404f3b and 76d738b8 on bead/playhead-e75l. NOT merged, no PR.

WHAT I PROBED AND WHAT IT SAID.

F1 (MEDIUM). The drain-stop LOG EVENT was not split per kind. FMDaemonRefusal split the durable defer TOKENS (inferenceTimeout-* vs rateLimited-*) and the per-job logEvent, and argued the rule explicitly — an operator counting rateLimited- is counting rate limits — but BackfillJobRunner still emitted the hard-coded fm.backfill.drain_stopped_by_throttle when a drain was stopped by two metadata stalls. The cause= field the implementer added on that line does not repair a NAME, which is the unit a support-bundle grep counts. FIX: FMDaemonRefusal.drainStoppedEvent, kvs8's spelling byte-identical, fm.backfill.drain_stopped_by_daemon_metadata_stall for the stall. RE-PLANT: mutation DR06 restores the literal — KILLED by a new SOURCE canary (FMDaemonRefusalEventWiringCanaryTests), which exists because no test on this harness can read a log line, so the enum test alone could pass forever while the runner emitted the wrong name.

F2 (MEDIUM) — found by a probe, not by reading. stalledBatchStrandsNothing's sibling-token assertion was VACUOUS: allSatisfy on an empty array. I added #expect(!siblingReasons.isEmpty) and it FAILED on the first run. Root cause: the batch fixture (inherited from kvs8) passes an EMPTY EvidenceCatalog, and TargetedWindowNarrower narrows .scanHarvesterProposals on evidenceLineRefs — so that phase planned zero windows, never reached the daemon, and COMPLETED, which RESETS consecutiveDaemonRefusals. The drain could therefore only cross the stop threshold on its LAST job, where no sibling is left to sweep. Consequence: batchSiblingCause — added by this bead — had NO test at all, and neither did kvs8's batchSibling path. FIX: the fixture builds a real catalog from sponsor-bearing lines, which puts a third refusable job ahead of the threshold. RE-PLANT: DR04 (sibling token back to kvs8's literal) — KILLED.

F3 (LOW). TestFMRuntimeFailure.inferenceTimeout built its error from a literal .seconds(300) while the test consuming it is named standardDeadlineTimeoutThroughTheSameSeamStillFails. The standing defect class in a fixture: what would this read if FMInferenceDeadline.standard were not 300? It would keep passing while no longer exercising standard. FIX: derived from the constant, as the new .metadataTimeout case already was. RE-PLANT: DR03 (predicate reads the OTHER budget) — KILLED.

F4 (LOW). The where-clause catch arm re-derived its classification in a body where the compiler no longer knew it was non-nil, defaulting ?? .throttle. Unreachable (classify is pure — SemanticScanStatus.from(error:) is a total function of the error value), but the direction is doubly wrong if ever reached: it would DEFER a genuine failure, which kvs8 deliberately gives no terminal cause, and stamp rateLimited-prologue on a rate limit that never happened. FIX: merged into one catch that binds once; the split is now if/else with byte-identical semantics.

REVIEWER'S FOUR NAMED PROBES, ANSWERED.

1. deadline == FMInferenceDeadline.metadata — the comparison is on a Duration and BOTH sides are durations. Two rails hold it: theTwoBudgetsDiffer pins metadata != standard AND metadata == .seconds(30), so making a second budget numerically equal goes red. What is NOT covered by construction: a THIRD budget set to 30 s, or an injected inferenceDeadline of 30 s (FoundationModelClassifier.Config.inferenceDeadline and PermissiveAdClassifier both take one, default standard; no production caller overrides). Today the only two FMInferenceDeadline.run budgets in production are standard and metadata. Mutations DR02 (predicate keys on the TYPE) and DR03 (reads the OTHER budget) both KILLED.

2. throttledThisJob -> daemonRefusalThisJob READERS: exactly one write site and one read site, both in the drain loop, structurally 1:1 with kvs8's. Grep confirms zero remaining throttledThisJob / consecutiveThrottledJobs anywhere. No reporting, logging or decision path outside the loop reads either.

3. consecutiveDaemonRefusals MIXING TWO POPULATIONS — probed, not argued. There was no runner-level test for it, so I added TestFMRuntime.coarseSchemaTokenCountFailures (a per-call prologue queue; a single-valued failure cannot express two kinds in one drain) and aThrottleAndAStallShareOneConsecutiveCounter: job 1 throttles, job 2 stalls, threshold 2 is crossed, job 3 is swept as inferenceTimeout-batchSibling. With two per-kind counters the sweep could never happen. RE-PLANT: DR07 (only throttles advance the counter) — KILLED.

4. retryCount PRESERVED — nothing downstream reads a deferred row as a spent attempt. threeStallsDoNotDisqualifyTheEpisode asserts it end to end (drive maxRetries stalls, then a healthy run, and the episode still completes with a full cursor) rather than inferring from the column. DR01 — the pre-e75l production line VERBATIM — KILLED it.

OTHER VERIFICATIONS.
* kvs8 UNCHANGED: all four kvs8 suites green; the four frozen tokens byte-identical; fm.backfill.job_throttled byte-identical; fm.backfill.drain_stopped_by_throttle byte-identical for the throttle. Two logger.warning PROSE strings were reworded by the implementer ("throttle-deferred" -> "daemon-deferred"); neither is an fm.-prefixed event token and nothing greps them. Accepted.
* deferReason HAS NO PRODUCTION READER — verified by grep, not accepted. The only Swift parser of a deferReason is DiagnosticsBundleBuilder.rediffAnnotationValue, which reads background_runs.deferReason filtered to entryPoint == .rediffRefetch — a different table. SemanticScanClaim states in-source that there is deliberately no Swift parser for a persisted backfill_jobs.deferReason.
* THE FOUR CONTROLS PASS PRE-FIX: DR01 restores the pre-e75l disposition and the three runner controls (standardDeadlineTimeoutThroughTheSameSeamStillFails, nonTimeoutPrologueStillFails, cleanPrologueStillCompletes) stayed GREEN under it while the four stall tests went red. That is what makes them controls.
* THE 300 s BOUNDARY HOLDS: DR02 (make every FMInferenceTimeoutError a refusal) is KILLED by the standard-deadline control.

FIELD NUMBERS RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY from db-aug3-work/analysis.sqlite. 14 backfill_jobs rows total (2 complete / 1 deferred / 2 failed / 9 queued). Both failed rows are daemon conditions: DE0784D8 carries the rate-limit prose (kvs8's), 0C2FC22E carries FMInferenceTimeoutError(deadline: 30.0 seconds), both retryCount=1. 0C2FC22E created 1785770498.776 -> updated 1785770551.0 = 52.24 s, and ZERO semantic_scan_results rows for the asset. The implementer's 52.2 s is right and the bead's 53 s is rounded. Denominator confirmed: 2 of 2 failures are daemon conditions, 0 of 2 the job's own merits.

THE UNSUPPORTED BEAD CLAIM: confirmed unsupported and confirmed load-bearing on NOTHING. AD5F3A0A's three backfill_jobs rows last update at 2026-08-03 06:18:52 local, and there are zero semantic_scan_results rows anywhere in the hour containing 0C2FC22E's failure. Nothing in the fix, the tests or the mutation series takes device load as an input — the discriminator is deadline == metadata, a pure function of the error value.

VERDICTS.
* lint: scripts/lint.sh (whole repo, strict) -> "lint: clean".
* Mutation battery: NEW DR series, 7 mutations in 5 batches, FMDaemonRefusal.swift added to MUTABLE_FILES and the three suites to FOCUSED_SUITES. DR01 DR02 DR03 DR04 DR05 DR06 DR07 = 7 KILLED, 0 SURVIVED, 0 ERROR. Baseline green on batch 502's unmutated run. One harness defect found and fixed on the way: a ';' in a @Test display name is the MUTATIONS record separator, so DR02/DR03 first printed "expected test never ran" while having killed the test perfectly — the test was renamed with an em dash (commit 76d738b8), the same remedy the script's header records for a K2 test.
* Scoped gate, 20 suites: "Test run with 188 tests in 16 suites passed after 16.025 seconds", "** TEST SUCCEEDED **". ZERO failures in BOTH formats — 0 Swift Testing "failed after", 0 XCTest "Test Case ... failed"; the XCTest half reports "Executed 6 tests, with 0 failures" (kvs8's canary 2 + FMUnboundedCall 3 + the new wiring canary 1). Every requested suite confirmed present in the log by name.

NOT EVALUATED. The full PlayheadFastTests plan — per Dan's gate economics (a round that FIXED things runs scoped only) and playhead-q1go (~50% of full runs never reach a verdict on this box). The battery ran only the DR series; the rest of the battery was not re-run, and the DR baseline was skipped on batches 500/501/503/504 after batch 502 established it green (every expectation name was verified present in the gate log first, which is the check the baseline performs).

FOLLOW-UPS FILED, both confirmed before filing, neither widened into this diff:
* playhead-ws6m (P2) — a drain in which EVERY job was refused still bumps observedEpisodeCount / episodesSinceLastFullRescan. Confirmed: admitted.append(job.jobId) is at line ~856, BEFORE runJob, so the "if !admitted.isEmpty" gate fires. Pre-existing; applies to kvs8's throttle identically.
* playhead-x8ck (P3) — rateLimited-prologue's doc claims "before a single window was planned", which is false for a throttle out of planAdaptiveZoom (called with a bare try await in runJob AFTER coarsePassA has checkpointed windows) and planExpansionWindow. Confirmed at both call sites. R1 corrected the NEW file's doc comments; kvs8's token and doc were left alone deliberately.

READY TO MERGE: yes, on the evidence above. The disposition is right, the discriminator is the budget and is mutation-proven, kvs8 is byte-identical where it matters, and the three code paths this bead added that had no rail now have one each.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
R2 REVIEW (review-and-fix) — 6 findings, all FIXED in-branch. Commits d7f24564, 3c3bf00b, c3ae1278 on bead/playhead-e75l. NOT merged, no PR. Tree clean.

THE HEADLINE. R1's four fixes hold — all seven of its mutations still KILL — but the layer below F3 was live and had been since the implement commit: the two DURABLE TOKENS this bead added, 'inferenceTimeout-metadata' and 'inferenceTimeout-batchSibling', joined playhead-8d5r's existing 'inferenceTimeout-noProgress' family. That token is what BackfillJobRunner writes when the coarse pass aborts on a run of 300 s inference timeouts, and the runner's own comment gives its operator reading: 'a run of inference timeouts means the model is not answering on this device'. FMDaemonRefusal's doc states the prefix rule explicitly for 'rateLimited-' — and the fix broke it one family over. grep -c 'inferenceTimeout-' on a device pull would have counted wedged TOKENIZER round trips as evidence about the MODEL, which is the single distinction this whole type exists to hold, and the same distinction that licenses a standard-deadline timeout staying a failure. The standing defect class, introduced by the fix for a previous instance, exactly as F3 was.

R2-F1 (MEDIUM). Found by grep, not by argument: 'rg rateLimited-|inferenceTimeout-' over Playhead/ turned up BackfillJobRunner.swift:3719 setting coarseIncompleteDeferReason = "inferenceTimeout-noProgress", and BackfillRateLimitDeferTests pins it with 'the cause is named, not folded into the rate-limit reason'. FIX: renamed to 'metadataStall-refused' / 'metadataStall-batchSibling'. Prefix is the CONDITION, suffix is the ROLE — and '-refused' deliberately does NOT repeat kvs8's '-prologue' position claim, which is what playhead-x8ck is filed against. RE-PLANT: DR09 restores the pre-review spelling verbatim — KILLED, by a new SOURCE canary (testDaemonRefusalCausesDoNotJoinAForeignTokenFamily) that anchors the foreign literals in the runner so an 8d5r rename re-opens the question instead of silently emptying the check, plus two collateral victims.

R2-F2 (LOW) — found by a PROBE, and the probe is the lesson. R1's wiring canary forbade 'fm.backfill.job_throttled' and 'fm.backfill.drain_stopped_by' BY NAME: the two kvs8-era spellings it had just watched go wrong. Mutation DR08 plants a literal of the event THIS BEAD ADDED, one line up from DR06's anchor — the per-job line emitting 'fm.backfill.job_daemon_metadata_stalled' verbatim, so every THROTTLE logs the stall's name and a support bundle's rate-limit count reads zero. It SURVIVED on first plant (batch 505, baseline green, 'still green: …testDaemonRefusalLogEventsAreNotHardCodedInTheRunner'). A blacklist covers the mistakes already made and is blind by construction to the next one. FIX: the forbidden set is derived from FMDaemonRefusal.allCases, and both logEvent AND drainStoppedEvent must be READ, not merely not-hard-coded. RE-PLANT: DR08 — KILLED.

R2-F3 (LOW). The drain-stop line's 'cause=' field, added by this bead, holds batchSiblingCause — the token written to the SWEPT jobs — on a line whose event NAME already carries the condition, and it prints unchanged when nothing was swept. What would it read if no sibling existed? The same. Renamed 'siblingCause='. R1's F1 is what made the field redundant as a disambiguator; it was the implementer's workaround for the event name being hard-coded.

R2-F4 (LOW). FMInferenceDeadline.metadata's doc — the paragraph LICENSING the 30 s value — still said 'Where it does propagate (planPassA), the outcome is a named inference_timeout row and a TERMINAL job'. Both halves are false after this bead: the throw escapes before a window is planned so there is no scan row at all (verified: 0C2FC22E has zero semantic_scan_results rows), and it is now a defer. Corrected in place with the correction stated, since the licence survives it and is in fact stronger.

R2-F5 (LOW) — R1's named open gap, CLOSED BY ENUMERATION rather than repeated. R1 wrote that the discriminator is uncovered by construction against a third 30 s budget. That is only true if the set of budgets is open, and it is not: 9 FMInferenceDeadline.run call sites across 3 production files, all passing FMInferenceDeadline.metadata (4), FMInferenceDeadline.standard (1, the readiness probe), or an injected inferenceDeadline (4) whose default is standard. New canary testEveryProductionInferenceBudgetIsEnumerated judges every call site against that set and pins Config.default.inferenceDeadline == standard — the one budget a caller can move without touching a call site. If it moved to 30 s today, every genuine inference timeout would start deferring with an unbounded retry and nothing else in the suite would notice. Now something does.

R2-F6 (LOW), the vacuity sweep result. 195 assertions swept, COUNTED not estimated: 109 in FMDaemonMetadataStallTests.swift and 86 in kvs8's FMDaemonThrottleTests.swift. TWO still passed with their subject forced empty, and they are the same assertion: '#expect(scans.allSatisfy { $0.status != .success && $0.status != .noAds })' in metadataStallDoesNotPenaliseCoverage and in kvs8's throttledPrologueLeavesCoverageUntouched. Both paths produce ZERO scan rows — which the same tests assert with coarseCallCount == 0 — so allSatisfy could not fail. R1's F2 shape, two tests over, one of them kvs8's. Replaced with #expect(scans.isEmpty), which is the actual state, is strictly stronger (it also rejects a fabricated FAILURE row for a window nobody called — the shape 8d5r had to fix once already), and was VERIFIED green rather than assumed. Every other collection assertion is guarded by an explicit count, is an exact array equality that cannot hold on [], or is a positive contains that proves non-emptiness before its negative siblings run.

FIELD NUMBERS RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY from db-aug3-work/analysis.sqlite, and they agree with R1: 14 backfill_jobs rows (2 complete / 1 deferred / 2 failed / 9 queued); 0C2FC22E failed / retryCount 1 / deferReason 'FMInferenceTimeoutError(deadline: 30.0 seconds)' / 1785770551.0 - 1785770498.7755 = 52.2245 s / ZERO semantic_scan_results rows; both failed rows are daemon conditions (DE0784D8 the rate-limit prose, 0C2FC22E the metadata timeout), 0 of 2 the job's own merits. New this round: the only NAMED durable cause present in the whole pull is 'cancelled-during-fullEpisodeScan', which is the second family the new canary anchors against — so the family rule is anchored on something the field actually writes.

VERDICTS, VERBATIM.
* lint: scripts/lint.sh (whole repo, strict) -> 'lint: clean'.
* Mutation battery: DR01-DR09, batches 500-505. Batch 505 with a green baseline, 500-504 re-run behind it on the same commit with PLAYHEAD_MB_SKIP_BASELINE=1. 9 KILLED / 0 SURVIVED / 0 ERROR, 7 builds, ~19m. DR08 SURVIVED pre-fix and KILLED post-fix — that pair is the probe. No survivor remains.
* Scoped gate, 16 suites, flags passed LITERALLY: 'Test run with 157 tests in 13 suites passed after 4.948 seconds' + '** TEST SUCCEEDED **'. ZERO failures in BOTH formats: 0 Swift Testing 'failed after', and 16 XCTest 'Test Case' lines of which 0 contain 'failed' ('Executed 8 tests, with 0 failures' — FMDaemonThrottleCanaryTests 2 + FMUnboundedCallCanaryTests 3 + FMDaemonRefusalSourceCanaryTests 3). Every requested suite confirmed present by name. One log artifact worth recording so the next round does not chase it: FMDaemonThrottleClassificationTests prints its 'Suite … started' line but NO 'passed after' line, while all four of its tests print theirs and the summary counts it in the 13. Verified test-by-test rather than trusted.

NOT EVALUATED. The full PlayheadFastTests plan — per Dan's gate economics and playhead-q1go (~50% of full runs never reach a verdict on this box); two runs wedged identically today. Also not evaluated: the rest of the battery outside the DR series, which carries its earlier verdicts.

ONE PROCESS NOTE, because it cost twenty minutes. I ran 'git checkout -- Playhead PlayheadTests' after a battery invocation as a reflexive restore and it DISCARDED the round's uncommitted fixes. The battery refuses to start on a dirty tree for a file it mutates and says so — 'Otherwise commit your work first' is not advice, it is the workflow. Commit before every battery invocation.

FILED, NOT WIDENED: playhead-6q7p (P3) — the drain-stop line reports 'deferredSiblings=\(deferred.count)', but 'deferred' is the run-wide accumulator appended at FIVE sites, so a three-job drain with two refusals and one sweep reports deferredSiblings=3 for one sibling. What would it read if no sibling were swept? The same non-zero number. kvs8-era, on a line this bead only renamed.

READY TO MERGE: not yet — this round FOUND and FIXED six, so the two-consecutive-clean rule needs one more round. The open items I would hand it are precise rather than manufactured: (1) the bead's 'no scan row is fabricated' claim now has a sharper assertion but still no mutant, because there is no pre-review code that fabricated one — a synthetic rail would have to be invented rather than reverted; (2) the family canary anchors 8d5r's token as a bare literal, which is the honest limit of a rule about a string nobody parses; (3) playhead-6q7p is filed but unfixed. The disposition itself I consider settled: the discriminator is the budget, it is mutation-proven from both directions, the budget set is now enumerated rather than assumed, kvs8's four tokens and two event names are byte-identical, and retryCount preservation is asserted end to end by threeStallsDoNotDisqualifyTheEpisode.
