comments.text:
R3 REVIEW (review-and-fix) — 3 findings, all LOW, all FIXED in-branch. Commits 81121e0d and 7b17acb4 on bead/playhead-e75l. NOT merged, no PR.

THE PATTERN HELD, AND IT WAS THE ONE R2 NAMED. R2's DR08 lesson was "a rail written as a list of known-bad spellings is not a rail; it is a memory of the last bug", and it fixed ONE of the two list-shaped rails in that file. The other was three lines below it.

F1 (LOW, the rail-shape sweep). testDaemonRefusalCausesDoNotJoinAForeignTokenFamily checked this bead's four durable tokens against a hand-written foreignTokens list of TWO families. PROBE, not argument: enumerate every hyphen-family string literal BackfillJobRunner writes. It writes SIX — cancelled- (1199/1220), expiredWithoutProgress- (2044), underCoverage- and underCoverageBudgetSpent- (2378/2385, playhead-41mu), inferenceTimeout- (3726), noWork- (3857). Four were outside the rule by construction, so a third FMDaemonRefusal kind named into any of them passed a canary whose stated rule is "an operator counting a family must be counting one thing". FIX: the forbidden set is DERIVED from the runner's own source — quoted literals beginning with a word and a hyphen, containing no whitespace and no colon, which is exactly what separates a cause token from the log-format prose in the same file ("bd-m8k: planner-state observation failed …" is also word-hyphen and is a sentence). Measured six; R2's two are kept as ANCHORS (a rename of either must still surface) and as a floor. Also pins the one family family(of:) structurally cannot see: playhead-fil5's scan_claim: prefix, same column, documented device-pull query. RE-PLANT: mutation DR10 names the token into underCoverage-. Under R2's list it survives by arithmetic; against the derived set it is KILLED.

F2 (LOW, the vacuity sweep continued). R2's own fix — replacing a vacuous allSatisfy with #expect(scans.isEmpty) — is an ABSENCE with no positive control. Ask the diagnostic: what would it read if fetchSemanticScanResults could never observe a row for this asset in this fixture (wrong id, shadow mode persisting nothing)? TRUE, the passing value. R2 said a rail here "would have to be invented rather than reverted". It does not: the missing instrument is not a mutant on the WRITER but a control on the OBSERVER. FIX: both clean-prologue tests (e75l's and kvs8's) now assert the same query returns rows on the healthy path. It PASSED on first run, so the query is live and the two empty results now mean "the prologue examined nothing" rather than "nobody was looking". The claim is not idle — the runner has makeNoWorkSentinelScanResult with three call sites, a live mechanism that mints a .noAds row for work it did not do. After this, all three absence assertions in metadataStallDoesNotPenaliseCoverage have positive controls in cleanPrologueStillCompletes (nil cursor vs 30, empty scans vs non-empty, 0 coarse calls vs 3).

F3 (LOW, the battery). Two defects in the rails rather than the code. (a) T_DR_STANDARD was DEFINED at R1 and referenced by NO mutation — the runner-level control "a 300 s inference timeout still fails and still spends a retry" had a test and no mutant. (b) Two fixtures still spelled .seconds(300) where they meant FMInferenceDeadline.standard (FMDaemonThrottleTests 89 and 721) — R1-Fix2's correction, missed in kvs8's file, and this bead is what made WHICH BUDGET load-bearing. FIX: DR02 now names T_DR_STANDARD, both literals derive from the constant, and the isThrottle case also asserts the metadata budget because classify asks that question FIRST — a true answer there would stamp rateLimited-prologue on a wedged tokenizer. DR02 had to MOVE OUT of batch 500 to do it: DR01 reduces classify to the throttle-only ternary, under which the control stays green, so the batch would have reported SURVIVED for a mutation DR02 kills alone. Growing an expectation set can invalidate a sound batch.

THE FOUR ASSIGNMENTS.

1a. THE FABRICATION CLAIM. Judged: a mutant is NOT the right instrument and a rail IS constructible — see F2. A mutant would have to invent a write path; the actual exposure is that an absence is only as good as the observer reading it, and that is closable with a control on the same query. Reported as fixed rather than accepted.

1b. NOBODY PARSES THE FAMILY — VERIFIED BY GREP, NOT ASSUMED. The only Swift parser of any deferReason is DiagnosticsBundleBuilder.rediffAnnotationValue, and it reads background_runs.deferReason filtered to entryPoint == .rediffRefetch — a DIFFERENT TABLE. Nothing routes on backfill_jobs.deferReason. The rule is not vacuous, though: playhead-fil5 gives that column a documented device-pull query (WHERE deferReason LIKE 'scan_claim:%') and SemanticScanClaimTests already carries the same family rule for it, so "a durable token's family is read by SQL, not by Swift" is now true of two independent families. The canary keeps the bare-literal anchor and now also pins scan_claim:. FIELD EVIDENCE the anchor is live: the only NAMED token in the whole 2026-08-03 pull is cancelled-during-fullEpisodeScan.

1c. playhead-6q7p CONFIRMED OUT OF SCOPE. deferredSiblings= is a CONTEXT line in this diff — kvs8's, unchanged. Five deferred.append sites (804 admission, 1018/1061 cancellation, 1371 the refused job itself, 1483 the sweep). Sharper form for whoever takes 6q7p: the refused job is itself in `deferred`, and the drain only stops at threshold 2, so deferredSiblings reads AT LEAST 2 when the sweep swept NOTHING — the answer to "what would this read if the thing never happened" is 2, not 0. The same line's siblingCause= has the identical shape (R2 documented it rather than fixing it); both are one edit and belong together in 6q7p.

2. RAIL-SHAPE SWEEP — 9 canary tests checked across 4 classes, 1 fixed, 2 recorded. DERIVED FROM A TYPE: testDaemonRefusalLogEventsAreNotHardCodedInTheRunner (allCases, R2). NOW DERIVED FROM SOURCE: the family canary (F1). DENY-BY-DEFAULT RULES, correct shape: testEveryProductionInferenceBudgetIsEnumerated (allow-list + >=9 floor; 9 non-comment call sites re-counted, the 10th match is a doc comment); FMDaemonThrottleCanaryTests.testProbeFailureCacheIsGuardedByTheThrottlePredicate (single anchor + exact count 1); FMUnboundedCallCanaryTests x3 (one needle + measured floor each). RECORDED, NOT FIXED: (i) FMDaemonThrottleCanaryTests.testNoFoundationModelsStreamingCallSiteExistsInProduction forbids ["streamResponse(", "ResponseStream", "PartiallyGenerated"] — genuinely list-shaped, and NOT derivable, because the set is an external framework's API surface with no type in this repo to enumerate; a fourth streaming spelling in a future SDK is invisible to it. That is kvs8's and an honest limit, not a fix. (ii) the log-event canary's second half requires ["logEvent","drainStoppedEvent"] to APPEAR by name — property names are not enumerable in Swift, so this half stays a list. Residual on all the source canaries: the site finders are literal substrings, so a call respelled across lines is invisible (the CN10 lesson); each carries a count floor, so a site DISAPPEARING is red, but adding one while respelling another is not.

3. VACUITY SWEEP, CONTINUED PAST R2's 195. Named and checked what was outside: PlayheadTests/Helpers/TestFMRuntime.swift (no assertions — it is the fixture; its queue semantics are pinned by aThrottleAndAStallShareOneConsecutiveCounter's exact outcomes); the battery's own $T_DR_* expectations (checked BY RUNNING — a wrong name reports ERROR, and one was unreferenced, F3a); and the four other test files that touch the metadata deadline — FMInferenceDeadlineTests, FMNoProgressWatchdogTests, Cycle4FixesTests, FoundationModelClassifierTests. FMNoProgressWatchdogTests already pins metadata > .zero and metadata < standard, an independent rail under theTwoBudgetsDiffer. Three of the four carry .seconds(300) literals; the two inside a file this diff already edits are fixed (F3b), the two outside it are NOT widened into this diff and are described below. Assertions added by R1/R2 and examined here for the first time: the two clean-prologue absence assertions (F2), tokens.count == 4, foreignFamilies.count == 2 (which HARD-CODED the list's own size and is now a derived floor), !siblingReasons.isEmpty (already a guard), and stopRuleIsShared's loop (0...threshold+2, non-empty, and a genuine duplication detector rather than a tautology — it fails the moment anyone re-implements the rule instead of delegating). Assertion count in the two files is now 113 + 89 = 202.

4. THE MISSING SUITE LINE — RESOLVED, AND IT IS A READER BUG, NOT A SKIP. The log carries TWO suite formats and only one ends with the words "passed after". Swift Testing writes: Suite "<display name>" started. … Suite "<display name>" passed after N seconds. XCTest writes: Test Suite '<TypeName>' started at <ts>. … Test Suite '<TypeName>' passed AT <ts>. So a grep for "started" finds 21 lines in this run and a grep for "passed after" finds 16 — every XCTest class looks like a suite that started and never finished. Parsed on the quoted form, started == passed == 16 exactly. And FMDaemonThrottleClassificationTests appears in the log EXACTLY ONCE, in the echoed xcodebuild -only-testing: argv: its @Suite display name replaces the type name in every result line, so there is no line under that name to be missing. Both halves are artifacts of matching a name the reporter does not use. Nothing was skipped — the suite's own display name has a matching "passed after", and the XCTest half reports Executed 8 tests, with 0 failures (3 + 2 + 3 across the three canary classes). This is the same class as the "Gate Triage Misses XCTest" note: "passed after" is a Swift-Testing-only terminator; XCTest says "passed at".

FIELD NUMBERS RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY from db-aug3-work/analysis.sqlite, not copied. 14 backfill_jobs rows: 9 queued / 2 complete / 2 failed / 1 deferred. Both failed rows are daemon conditions — DE0784D8 carries the rate-limit prose (kvs8's) and 0C2FC22E carries FMInferenceTimeoutError(deadline: 30.0 seconds), both retryCount 1. 0C2FC22E: 1785770551.0 - 1785770498.775505 = 52.2245 s, so 52.22 (R1's 52.24 is a rounding slip; the implementer's 52.2 and the bead's 53 are both consistent). ZERO semantic_scan_results rows for that asset out of 89 in the pull — the prologue, confirmed. 0 of 2 failures are the job's own merits. Only three deferReason values exist in the whole table and 11 of 14 rows are NULL; the two daemon rows carry RAW framework/Swift descriptions, which is exactly what this bead replaces with named tokens.

retryCount CLEARED BY ENUMERATION, not by argument. markBackfillJobDeferred's SQL sets status and deferReason and updatedAt — it does not name the column. The ONLY readers of retryCount as a budget are the two re-enqueue gates (BackfillJobRunner 661 and 710), both comparing the persisted value against AdmissionController.maxRetries. Nothing anywhere reads status == .deferred as a spent attempt.

TWO SITES CLEARED THE SAME WAY — by naming what else is in scope, not by reading carefully. (1) The USABILITY PROBE. kvs8's doc says a daemon condition must never be cached as a usability verdict, and shouldCacheFailure is still !isThrottle, so a metadata stall WOULD be cached for 15 minutes. It cannot arise: probeIfNeeded's only bounded call is FMInferenceDeadline.run(FMInferenceDeadline.standard) around a session.respond with no tokenizer round trip inside, so the errors in scope at that catch are the framework's respond errors, FMInferenceTimeoutError(standard), and CancellationError. There is no second budget in scope. (2) recordFailedOperationalMetricsEvent is called from the refusal arm, so a deferred job goes through a function with "Failed" in its name — but the row it writes has NO outcome field at all: 16 counters, wall time, audio duration, jobId, phase, cohort. Nothing downstream can read a daemon-refused job's telemetry as a failure. The name is internal-only.

VERDICTS.
* lint: scripts/lint.sh (whole repo, strict) -> "lint: clean", twice (after the code fixes and after the battery-header commit).
* Mutation battery: batch 506 with a GREEN baseline (DR02 moved + DR10 new), then 500-505 re-run behind it with PLAYHEAD_MB_SKIP_BASELINE=1 on the same commit. DR01 DR02 DR03 DR04 DR05 DR06 DR07 DR08 DR09 DR10 = 10 KILLED / 0 SURVIVED / 0 ERROR, 8 builds, ~17m. Tree verified clean after every batch by the loop itself; no blanket git checkout was ever run.
* Scoped gate, 19 -only-testing: suites, EVERY ONE confirmed present in the log by name (16 Swift Testing display names + 3 XCTest classes). "lint: clean", "Test run with 190 tests in 16 suites passed after 4.418 seconds.", "Executed 8 tests, with 0 failures (0 unexpected)", "** TEST SUCCEEDED **". ZERO failures in BOTH formats: 0 Swift Testing "failed after", 0 XCTest "Test Case '...' failed". "fast-gate: baseline check SKIPPED — selective run, a different population" — correct, and no --accept-baseline was run.
* NOT EVALUATED: the full plan. Per playhead-q1go it is unobtainable on this box today (two runs wedged identically), and the round's instruction was to spend the time on probes instead.

OUT OF SCOPE, FILED OR NOTED RATHER THAN WIDENED.
* playhead-6q7p (P3) — confirmed out of scope, sharpened above.
* playhead-ws6m (P2), playhead-x8ck (P3) — untouched. x8ck's territory was re-confirmed: planAdaptiveZoom (runner 3502) and planExpansionWindow (runner 4306) both make metadata-bounded tokenCount calls and throw past runJob, so the "prologue" token names a position the throw does not always have. Nothing new to add.
* Two .seconds(300) fixtures OUTSIDE this diff's files carry R1-Fix2's defect: FMInferenceDeadlineTests:214 and Cycle4FixesTests:403. The second is the more interesting one — it is the only test of PermissiveAdClassifier's FMInferenceTimeoutError rethrow, and post-e75l that seam feeds a discriminator, so it exercises only the budget that is NOT a daemon refusal. The rethrow arm itself is CLEAR (catch let error as FMInferenceTimeoutError { throw error } — deadline-agnostic, nothing to get wrong), so this is a fixture-hygiene item, not a defect.

WHAT REMAINS UNPROVEN, stated plainly. The discriminator compares two Durations and NOTHING IN THE TYPE SYSTEM distinguishes them. DR03 (read the other budget) is killed by a test, not by the compiler. This repo has a mechanism for exactly that class — the TY series, scripts/mutation-battery-untypeable.py, whose verdict is "the mutated source must FAIL TO COMPILE" — and it was not applied here, because making it applicable means giving inference budgets a distinct type, which is an architectural change and Dan's call. The enumeration canary (testEveryProductionInferenceBudgetIsEnumerated) is the substitute and it is a source walk, not a capability.

MERGE JUDGEMENT. Three LOW findings, all fixed and all re-planted. None of them is a defect in the SHIPPING BEHAVIOUR — the production diff is unchanged by this round; every fix is in a rail, a fixture or the battery. That is itself the signal I would weigh: R1 and R2 each found production-side defects, R3 found none and the layer below turned out to be the instruments rather than the code. The two-consecutive-zero rule is not satisfied — this round found three — so one more round is owed regardless, and the highest-yield thing for it is NOT another sweep of these two files but the residual named above: every source canary here finds its sites by literal substring, and no probe has yet tried respelling one.

## DAN'S DECISION 2026-08-05: "Compiler guarding is best"

The discriminator `error.deadline == FMInferenceDeadline.metadata` decides "is this a daemon
condition, or evidence about the model?" by comparing two `Duration` values. Nothing in the
type system separates a 30 s TOKENIZER budget from a 300 s INFERENCE budget -- they are the
same type. Today it is killed by a test (DR03), not by the compiler.

**Dan has approved making it compiler-enforced.** This is the architecture approval that was
required; do not treat it as still open. The mechanism is the repo's existing TY series
(`scripts/mutation-battery-untypeable.py`, verdict `UNTYPEABLE`: the mutant must FAIL TO
COMPILE, with the expected diagnostic KIND, so a syntax break reports `WRONG-ERROR` rather than
being credited as a kill), same as playhead-x0lb shipped in #350.

**What is NOT yet decided is the SCOPE:** whether the budget type lands inside this bead or as
a follow-up. That waits on R4's cost/benefit write-up -- what the type is, what it costs, what
it buys -- because deciding scope without it would be the exact "argue instead of measure"
failure this bead's own rounds keep punishing. R4 was told not to implement, and that stands
for R4.

Standing context for whoever implements it:

* The 30 s `metadata` deadline is CORRECT and must stay 30 s. It bounds tokenizer metadata
  calls, not inference; scan-window inference is bounded by `standard` = 300 s
  (`FMInferenceDeadline.swift:142`). **The defect was always the DISPOSITION, not the number** --
  do not "improve" this by touching a timeout.
* The 300 s `standard` timeout must STILL FAIL. It is evidence about the model, and the cost
  bound is what licenses the asymmetry: 30 s per drain is cheap to retry forever, 300 s per
  window is not.
* R3 closed the current gap by ENUMERATION: 9 `FMInferenceDeadline.run` call sites across 3
  files, all passing `metadata`, `standard`, or an injected `inferenceDeadline` defaulted to
  `standard`, pinned by a canary that also asserts `Config.default.inferenceDeadline ==
  standard`. **An enumeration is a census and a census goes stale the moment someone adds a
  call site** -- that is precisely what the type replaces.

R4 REVIEW (review-and-fix) — 8 findings, all FIXED in-branch. Commits 75635fa5, 97dc6c02, ff067599 on bead/playhead-e75l. NOT merged, no PR. Tree clean.

THE HEADLINE. R3 reported that the production diff was unchanged and only the instruments were moving. That was true and it was the tell: EVERY source canary in this bead found its sites by literal substring over ONE LINE. I planted EIGHT respellings. SEVEN walked past. The single evasion that failed was killed by SwiftLint's `no_space_in_method_call`, not by any rail here.

THE EVASION TABLE, including the failure. Pre-fix verdicts, each planted and RUN, not argued.

  CN-A1  SURVIVED  the two log-event properties SWAPPED. No literal anywhere.
  CN-A2  SURVIVED  drain-stop event hard-coded, split by a `\` continuation
                   inside the multiline string these log lines already use,
                   with a decoy `logger.debug` supplying the property read.
  CN-A3  SURVIVED  per-job event hard-coded as `"fm.backfill.job_" + "..."`.
  CN-B1  SURVIVED  41mu's token rewritten `"\(Self.underCoverageFamily)-…"`,
                   then DR10's exact token planted into that family.
  CN-C1  SURVIVED  `FMInferenceDeadline.run(FMInferenceDeadline.standard / 10)`.
  CN-C2  SURVIVED  an ADDED call site split over two lines, `.seconds(30)`.
  CN-C3  KILLED    `run (` — a space before the paren. By SWIFTLINT.
  CN-C3b SURVIVED  `FMInferenceDeadline . run(` — spaces around the dot.
  CN-C4  SURVIVED  budget in a local; the allowed name only in a TRAILING COMMENT.

R4-F1 (MEDIUM), and the sharpest because it uses no literal at all. CN-A1 swapped `logEvent` and `drainStoppedEvent` between the per-job line and the drain-stop line. R2's rail asked whether both properties are READ, which says nothing about which SITE reads which — both are read, so it passed, and on a device every daemon-refused JOB would be counted as a drain stop by a support-bundle grep and every drain stop as a job. This bead's own defect class, committed inside the check written for it. FIX: exactly one read of each, and `logEvent` must precede `drainStoppedEvent` — which is a consequence of the control flow (the per-job event is emitted inside the drain loop, the drain-stop event after it breaks), not a pinned accident. RE-PLANT: mutation DR11 — KILLED.

R4-F2 (MEDIUM). CN-A2 / CN-A3: a forbidden event name split across a `\` continuation or a `+` join is invisible to a per-line finder, and the decoy read that satisfies R2's half is one `logger.debug`. FIX: the forbidden set is also matched against a COLLAPSED read of the file (lines trimmed, trailing `\` dropped, joined, `"a" + "b"` folded), and the decoy is dead because the read must be exactly once. RE-PLANT: DR12 — KILLED.

R4-F3 (MEDIUM). Four ways to get a third 30 s budget past the enumeration canary, each turning every genuine 300 s inference timeout into a deferrable daemon refusal with an unbounded retry — the exact hazard R2-F5 built it for. CN-C1 is the instructive one: `standard / 10` IS thirty seconds and the line MENTIONS an allowed budget, which is all `contains` asked. CN-C2 is the other: the site count is a FLOOR, so a site that DISAPPEARS is red and a site nobody can see is not — adding an unreadable one is free. FIX: the finder runs over a whitespace-free read and the first argument is extracted by balanced-paren scan and matched EXACTLY. This also makes CN-C3 independent of SwiftLint. RE-PLANT: DR13, DR14 — both KILLED.

R4-F4 (LOW). R3's derived foreign-family set is defeated by refactoring the WRITER rather than the rail: `isDurableTokenShaped` requires a letter first, so an interpolated family prefix drops the family, six fell to five, the `>= 5` floor still cleared, and DR10's exact token passed. FIX: a leading interpolation resolves one level through a string constant in the same file. Two levels, a computed property or another file remain invisible and that is stated in the source. RE-PLANT: CN-B1 by hand — RED, with the assertion naming `underCoverage-refused` and the family. NOT encodable as a battery record: it needs edits in two files and a record names one. Stated in the battery header rather than hidden.

R4-F5 (LOW). The doc paragraph LICENSING the whole fix said three daemon moments disqualify an episode "for the life of the install". The budget is spent per JOB ROW and a row's identity is `hash(asset | transcriptVersion | phase | offset)`, so the field pull quoted three lines above is the counterexample: 0C2FC22E's failed row `fm-443333542600941c` is followed 7,351 s (2 h 02 m, failure to next creation) by `fm-673a3b2b167fc4c7` — queued, retryCount 0, same asset, same phase. Corrected in place: it is true against a FINAL transcript, which is when the scan matters and is nearly all of an episode's life. The disposition is wrong at any scope; the magnitude claim was not.

R4-F6 (LOW-MEDIUM). R2-F5 closed the "third 30 s budget" hole by ENUMERATING the nine call sites — derived, measured — then pinned ONE default by hand, calling it "the one budget a caller can move without touching a call site". There are THREE: `PermissiveAdClassifier.init`, `FoundationModelClassifier.Config.init` (which the runtime pin does reach transitively, since `Config.default` omits the argument), and the classifier's inner FM-call type. Four of the nine sites pass `inferenceDeadline` and are allowed precisely because that name resolves to `standard`. R3-Fix1's shape one axis over. FIX: the defaults are derived from source too, floor measured at three, each required to BE `FMInferenceDeadline.standard`. RE-PLANT: DR15 (PermissiveAdClassifier's default → metadata) — KILLED.

R4-F7 (LOW). The threshold this bead now feeds two populations into still described one. `FMDaemonThrottle.consecutiveDeferStopThreshold`'s doc argued the number from what the daemon SAID ("try again later") and half of what reaches it is a wedged tokenizer, which said nothing. Doc corrected to say which half of the argument survives. And `shouldStopDraining(consecutiveThrottles:)` received `consecutiveDaemonRefusals` at every call site — R1 renamed the runner's counters for exactly this reason and the shared rule they delegate to kept the narrow name. A label is not a durable token and nothing greps it, so unlike the four `DeferCause` strings it is safe to correct; renamed at 6 sites.

R4-F8 (LOW). `stalledBatchStrandsNothing` asserted the swept sibling token avoids `rateLimited-` and `inferenceTimeout-` — a hand-written list of the two wrong answers already known, which passes for a third. Its sibling test already asserted exact equality. Now Set-equality against `FMDaemonRefusal.metadataStall.batchSiblingCause`.

Also: every offender this canary class has ever printed named the WRONG LINE — `runnerSource()` filtered comments out and reported the index into the survivors, and BackfillJobRunner is two-thirds comment. Line numbers are carried now.

FIELD NUMBERS RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY and the R1/R3 disagreement SETTLED. 14 `backfill_jobs` rows (9 queued / 2 complete / 2 failed / 1 deferred). 0C2FC22E: 1785770551.0 - 1785770498.7755051 = 52.224495 s, so 52.22 — R3 is right and R1's 52.24 is a transcription slip. ZERO of 89 `semantic_scan_results` rows for that asset (89 = 45 AD5F3A0A + 42 DE0784D8 + 2 53FC53E3). Both failed rows are daemon conditions, both retryCount 1, 0 of 2 the job's own merits. 11 of 14 deferReason NULL; the only NAMED token in the pull is `cancelled-during-fullEpisodeScan`.

NEW FROM THE PULL, and it is what produced F5: 0C2FC22E has TWO job rows under different jobIds, and DE0784D8 has two as well. jobId is a hash over asset|transcriptVersion|phase|offset, so a moving transcript mints a fresh row at retryCount 0.

THE BUDGET-TYPE WRITE-UP FOR DAN. Recommendation: do NOT take the phantom-typed budget.
* A phantom type (`FMBudget<MetadataRole>` / `FMInferenceTimeoutError<Role>`) DOES NOT reach the site that matters. Discrimination happens in `FMDaemonRefusal.classify(_ error: Error)`, called from a generic `catch` that must handle every error, so the discriminator down-casts: `error as? FMInferenceTimeoutError<MetadataRole>` — and the mutant `…<InferenceRole>` compiles. TY's criterion (the mutant must FAIL TO COMPILE) is not achievable. Second obstruction: 2 role-agnostic rethrows in `PermissiveAdClassifier` and 4 `is FMInferenceTimeoutError` checks would need a non-generic protocol, whose existential erases the role at exactly the seam the discriminator reads through.
* The design that WOULD remove the class is different in kind: two ERROR TYPES chosen at the THROW site. `FMInferenceDeadline.run(_ budget: FMInferenceBudget, …)` already knows which budget it holds and today discards that, carrying only the elapsed Duration and forcing every reader to re-derive identity by comparing numbers. Then `classify` is `error is FMMetadataStallError` — a type test, no quantity comparison.
* COST, measured: 9 production sites across 5 files (1 declaration, 1 construction, 2 typed catches, 4 `is` checks, 1 `as?`), 9 `run` call sites changing from a Duration to a budget case, 23 test references across 6 files. One genuine semantic decision falls out: `SemanticScanStatus.from(error:)` maps `FMInferenceTimeoutError` to `.inferenceTimeout`, and the split forces an answer to what a metadata stall reaching a window should persist as — a question nobody has had to ask because both wear one type.
* BUY: it removes the comparison rather than typing around it, and a NEW budget must declare its population where it is introduced — the RegionFillDoor-style naming obligation the repo has already found is what actually holds.
* IS THE TEST-LEVEL RAIL ADEQUATE MEANWHILE? Yes, and the probe rather than the argument: TY's premise — "the two are equal on every fixture a test author would write" — is NOT met here. 30 s and 300 s are not equal and reading the wrong one produces a visibly different disposition, which is exactly why DR03 is killable and IS killed, by two independent expectations. DR02 (key on the TYPE) is killed by the standard-deadline control. The residual the type could not close either — a third 30 s budget — is closed by enumeration, which R4 made read the ARGUMENT (DR13/DR14) and cover all three defaults (DR15). Three directions, all measured.

VERDICTS.
* lint: `scripts/lint.sh` (whole repo, strict) -> "lint: clean", after each of the three commits.
* Mutation battery: batch 507 with a GREEN baseline, then 508-510 and 500-506 behind it with PLAYHEAD_MB_SKIP_BASELINE=1 on the same commit; then batch 511 with its own green baseline after the F6/F7/F8 commit. DR01-DR15 = 15 KILLED / 0 SURVIVED / 0 ERROR, 14 builds, ~30m. No blanket `git checkout` was ever run; the tree was verified clean by `[ -z "$(git status --porcelain)" ]` after every batch.
* Scoped gate, 17 `-only-testing:` suites, flags passed LITERALLY: "lint: clean", "Test run with 168 tests in 14 suites passed after 4.128 seconds.", "Executed 8 tests, with 0 failures (0 unexpected)", "** TEST SUCCEEDED **". ZERO failures in BOTH formats: 0 Swift Testing "failed after", 0 XCTest "Test Case '...' failed". Swift Testing suites started == passed == 14, parsed on the quoted form. "fast-gate: baseline check SKIPPED — selective run, a different population"; no --accept-baseline.
* THE FIRST FINAL GATE HAD A MISSPELLED SUITE AND IT READ AS A PASS. I asked for `FMDaemonThrottleDeferTests`, which does not exist — the real suite is `FMThrottledPrologueRunnerTests`. rc=0, "** TEST SUCCEEDED **", and kvs8's runner-level defer suite never ran. Caught by mapping every requested name to a suite display line in the log rather than trusting the count; re-run with the three real kvs8 runner suites added.

NOT EVALUATED. The full PlayheadFastTests plan, per playhead-q1go and Dan's gate economics. Also not evaluated: the rest of the battery outside the DR series, which carries its earlier verdicts.

WHAT REMAINS UNPROVEN, precisely.
1. The ordering rule would be defeated by a mutation that ALSO moves the two emission sites (emitting the drain-stop event from inside the loop). That changes control flow and runner tests would see it, but it was not probed.
2. `collapsedCode` joins all lines with no separator, so it could in principle synthesize a false positive across two unrelated lines. Measured clean today; the names are 20+ characters.
3. The constant resolution follows ONE level of naming. Two levels, a computed property, or a constant in another file are still invisible.
4. CN-B1's rail is verified by hand, not by a battery record.
5. playhead-ws6m (P2), playhead-x8ck (P3), playhead-6q7p (P3) remain filed and unfixed. Nothing new filed this round.

READY TO MERGE: not yet — this round FOUND and FIXED eight, so the two-consecutive-clean rule needs one more. The disposition itself I consider settled and I would not spend another round on it: the discriminator is the budget, mutation-proven from both directions, the budget set is now enumerated on BOTH axes, kvs8's four tokens and two event names are byte-identical, and retryCount preservation is asserted end to end. What R5 should push on is the layer this round opened rather than closed — every one of these eight was in an INSTRUMENT, and the instruments are now more code than the fix.

## R5 REVIEW — 3 PRODUCTION / 0 INSTRUMENT

The split is the headline. R3 and R4 found 11 findings and ZERO production defects;
R5's mandate was to stop reviewing the review and answer one question with evidence.
Every finding this round is shipped behaviour, and none is a respelling of a canary.

### Method

Three probes planted against production VERBATIM in ONE build. All three predicted
to survive, so a green run attributes unambiguously. **All three SURVIVED**, with
every one of the eight suites in this bead's scope green (36 Swift Testing tests in
6 suites, 5 XCTest, 0 failures in both formats).

### PRODUCTION (3)

**R5-Fix1 — `deferredSiblings=` on the drain-stop line held the drain's total.**
Established by reading, and the mutant IS the shipped code. `deferred` is the
drain-WIDE accumulator, appended at FIVE sites (admission-defer sweep 804,
rate-limited coverage hole 1018, 41mu under-coverage terminal 1061, the refused
job's OWN defer 1371, the sibling sweep 1483) — the field named for the sweep
reported every job the sweep did not touch. Measured on the mixed-refusal fixture:
**3 for one swept sibling**. The sharpest form is that it could never read ZERO —
reaching that line requires `consecutiveDaemonRefusals >= 2` and each of those
appended — so "the stop landed on the last job and cost the batch nothing" was
unrepresentable. This is the FOURTH field on the line whose event name R1 corrected
and whose `siblingCause=` R2 corrected, and the same defect class all three times.
FIX: `sweptSiblingCount`, incremented only on a SUCCESSFUL defer so a sibling
skipped by the terminal-row guard is correctly not counted.
RE-PLANT: DR16 — **KILLED**.

**R5-Fix2 (probe PB1) — kvs8's per-job event name was pinned by nothing.**
`FMDaemonRefusal.throttle.logEvent` is `fm.backfill.job_throttled`, which THIS bead
moved out of a hard-coded literal in the runner's log line into the enum.
`drainStoppedEvent` was pinned for BOTH kinds; `logEvent` had only
`metadataStall.logEvent != throttle.logEvent`, which a rename satisfies. Renaming it
to `fm.backfill.job_daemon_throttled` left every rail green — the wiring canary
derives its forbidden set from `allCases`, so it dutifully forbids whatever the NEW
spelling is. On a device, the support-bundle grep an operator already runs to count
throttles reads zero. Both literals are pinned now.
RE-PLANT: DR17 — **KILLED**.

**R5-Fix3 (probe PB5) — the swept-sibling token was proven in one direction only.**
DR04 proves "not always the THROTTLE's". Nothing proved "not always the STALL's":
both e75l batch tests are stall-terminated, and kvs8's own `throttledBatchStrandsNothing`
passes an EMPTY `EvidenceCatalog`, so `.scanHarvesterProposals` narrows to zero
windows and COMPLETES, which resets the counter — the drain never reaches the stop
threshold and no sibling is ever swept there. So hard-coding
`FMDaemonRefusal.metadataStall.batchSiblingCause` at the sweep survived: a
RATE-LIMITED drain would record a wedged tokenizer that never happened, in the
durable column an operator greps. FIX: the mirror test, reusing the `makeBatchInputs`
fixture R1 built for exactly this and had only ever pointed at a stall.
RE-PLANT: DR18 — **KILLED**.

### INSTRUMENT (0)

None found and none looked for beyond what production required. Three rails were
added and every one guards production that was otherwise unguarded (rule 3): two
assertions on an existing test, one runner test, one source canary. R4's
balanced-paren scanner was LIFTED into `firstArguments(after:in:)` rather than
copied, so the instrument gained a canary and lost a duplicate.

The new canary is a rule, not a blacklist: it judges the ARGUMENT by balanced-paren
scan over the dense read, rejects any `.count` (every collection in scope there is
drain-wide), and requires the identifier it names to occur EXACTLY 3 times in the
runner — declared, incremented, read. `deferred` occurs nine times, so the defect is
caught by the rule rather than by naming it.

### FILED, not fixed

* **playhead-zize** (P3) — probe PB3: deleting `consecutiveDaemonRefusals = 0` turns
  the consecutive counter into a lifetime one and SURVIVES. Not fixed, and the third
  reason is binding: the line is kvs8's and unchanged in substance; the cost is a
  delayed drain and not lost reach (swept siblings are deferred, re-drivable,
  `retryCount` preserved); and it is **unobservable in any fixture the planner can
  build** — the difference needs a 4-job drain and `CoveragePlanner.plan` returns at
  most THREE phases. A fourth job means the specialist phase (flag + runtime), which
  drags an unrelated subsystem in to observe a log difference.
* **playhead-bsw6** (P3) — R4 open item 4. A `MUTATIONS` record names ONE file and
  CN-B1 needs edits in two, so it is verified by hand and re-verified by nobody. The
  general shape matters more than the probe: any canary that DERIVES its rule from
  production source can be evaded in two files and recorded in none.
* **playhead-fua7** (P3) — R4 open items 1 and 3. The ordering rule vs a mutant that
  also MOVES the emission sites (filed under rule 2: relocating a `logger.error`
  across a `break` is a control-flow change the runner tests observe, and no
  plausible author writes it), and one-level constant resolution. Both would be
  closed by a compile-enforced naming obligation — the `RegionFillDoor` shape from
  x0lb — not by another enumeration.

### CLOSED, not filed

R4 open item 2, `collapsedCode` joining lines with no separator. Joining without a
separator can only ADD substrings, never remove one, so its failure direction is a
LOUD false positive and never a silent miss — and it is exactly what Swift does to a
`\` continuation whose indentation matches its closing delimiter, which is the shape
being modelled.

### Also verified by reading, and all held

* `markBackfillJobDeferred` is `SET status, deferReason, updatedAt` — it does not
  touch `retryCount`, and `runPendingBackfill`'s C-B gate re-enqueues any row under
  `maxRetries`. Nothing downstream reads a deferred row as a spent attempt:
  `coverageTerminalDecision`'s budget reads the same preserved `retryCount`, and it
  is only reachable from a pass that COMPLETED.
* The fix improves a real downstream consumer that no test names.
  `AdDetectionService` maps `result.deferredJobIds.isEmpty` to `.ranSucceeded` and
  non-empty to `.ranNeedsRetry` — so **pre-fix, a wedged daemon reported
  `.ranSucceeded` to the scheduler** while the row said `failed`.
* All FOUR `FMInferenceDeadline.metadata` call sites are `model.tokenCount(...)`, so
  the discriminator's claim holds against today's code.
* `classify`'s throttle-first order is provably irrelevant: `isThrottle` is
  `SemanticScanStatus.from(error:) == .rateLimited`, and the two enum expectations
  on `FMInferenceTimeoutError` cover both budgets.
* The doc's claim that a `planAdaptiveZoom` refusal defers with a real cursor holds
  — `planAdaptiveZoom` runs only after `coarse.status == .success`, by which point
  the mid-flight `checkpointBackfillJobProgress` has persisted one, and the defer
  SQL preserves it.

### VERDICTS

* **lint**: `scripts/lint.sh` whole repo, strict -> `lint: clean`, after each commit.
* **Mutation battery, DR01-DR15 re-run at HEAD `ff067599` BEFORE any change**:
  **15 KILLED / 0 SURVIVED / 0 ERROR**, 13 builds, ~29 min, `baseline green`. Batch
  500 carried the baseline; 501-511 behind it with `PLAYHEAD_MB_SKIP_BASELINE=1`.
* **DR16-DR18 re-plants** on the fix commit, batch 512 with its own green baseline:
  **3 KILLED / 0 SURVIVED / 0 ERROR**. `--dry-run` first on all three: "every anchor
  applied exactly once and the tree was restored."
* **Final scoped gate**, 8 `-only-testing:` flags passed LITERALLY:
  `lint: clean`; `Test run with 37 tests in 6 suites passed after 0.905 seconds.`;
  `Executed 4 tests, with 0 failures (0 unexpected)` +
  `Executed 2 tests, with 0 failures (0 unexpected)`; `** TEST SUCCEEDED **`.
  **0 failures in BOTH formats** (0 Swift Testing `failed after`, 0 XCTest
  `Test Case '...' failed`). `fast-gate: baseline check SKIPPED — selective run, a
  different population`. No `--accept-baseline`.
* **Suite-name mapping, all 8 requested names found as display lines** (R4's
  misspelled-suite trap): FMDaemonRefusalDefinitionTests -> "playhead-e75l:
  FMDaemonRefusal is the one definition of a daemon condition";
  FMDaemonMetadataStallRunnerTests -> "playhead-e75l: a metadata-deadline timeout in
  the prologue DEFERS with a named cause"; FMDaemonThrottleClassificationTests ->
  "playhead-kvs8: FMDaemonThrottle is the one definition of a daemon throttle";
  FMThrottledPrologueRunnerTests -> "playhead-kvs8: a throttled coarse-pass prologue
  DEFERS with a named cause"; FMThrottlePermissiveLaneTests -> "playhead-kvs8: the
  permissive lane records a throttle as a throttle"; FMThrottleUsabilityProbeTests ->
  "playhead-kvs8: a throttled readiness probe must not be cached as an unusable
  model"; FMDaemonRefusalSourceCanaryTests and FMDaemonThrottleCanaryTests as XCTest
  `Suite '...' started/passed`. Swift Testing suites started == passed == 6.
* No blanket `git checkout` was run. The tree was verified with
  `[ -z "$(git status --porcelain)" ]` after the battery, after the probe restore
  (explicit paths only) and after each commit.

### NOT EVALUATED

The full `PlayheadFastTests` plan, per playhead-q1go (~50% of full runs never reach
a verdict on this box) and Dan's gate economics. The rest of the battery outside the
DR series carries its earlier verdicts. `playhead-zize`'s counter reset remains
unrailed by construction, which is the bead's content.

### MERGE JUDGEMENT: YES

**The shipped behaviour is correct and adequately railed.** The disposition is
mutation-proven from both directions (DR01/DR02/DR03), the budget set is enumerated
on both axes (DR13/DR14/DR15), `retryCount` preservation is asserted end to end
including the three-stall reach test, and after this round every durable token AND
every log event name is pinned per kind and exercised on BOTH paths rather than only
the one this bead added. Eighteen mutations, zero survivors.

The residual is stated rather than implied: one unrailed reset (zize, cost = a
delayed drain), two canary limits that want a capability rather than an enumeration
(fua7), and one battery-tooling gap (bsw6). None of the three touches the
disposition.

## R6 REVIEW — 0 PRODUCTION / 2 INSTRUMENT

R5's method, repeated: probes planted against production VERBATIM in ONE build,
each predicted to survive so a green run attributes — plus, new this round, a
positive control on the OBSERVER, because a green run with five plants is also
what "the suites did not run" looks like.

Result: the control was KILLED BY NAME and every probe SURVIVED. Nothing this
round changes shipped behaviour. The runner is correct today; what was missing
is that it could stop being correct silently.

### THE PROBE BUILD

One build, six plants. `Test run with 37 tests in 6 suites failed after 1.091
seconds with 1 issue` — exactly one, `causesAreNamedAndDistinct`, the control.
0 XCTest failures.

  CTRL  KILLED    `metadataStall-refused` -> `...-refusedZZ`  (observer control)
  PB1   SURVIVED  per-job line `cause=` reads `batchSiblingCause`
  PB2   SURVIVED  drain-stop `siblingCause=` reads `passPrologueCause`
  PB3   SURVIVED  `sweptSiblingCount += 1` moved ABOVE the defer it counts
  PB4   SURVIVED  `consecutiveDaemonRefusals += 1` only on a SUCCESSFUL defer
  PB5   SURVIVED  `deferred.append(job.jobId)` regardless of defer success

### INSTRUMENT (2), both folded into canaries that already exist

**R6-Fix1 — the two log lines' CAUSE pair was pinned by nothing.** R4-Fix1
established that "both properties are READ" says nothing about which SITE reads
which, and pinned the EVENT pair on the per-job line and the drain-stop line
after probe CN-A1 swapped them with no literal anywhere. The SAME two lines
carry a second pair of exactly that shape and nobody had looked at it:
`cause=` (`passPrologueCause`, the token written to THIS job's row) and
`siblingCause=` (`batchSiblingCause`, the token written to the jobs the sweep
touched). PB1 and PB2 ran it in both directions and both survived, because the
durable columns are asserted by the runner tests and the log fields by no one.
On a device PB1 is a job the daemon refused on its own run reporting the cause
reserved for jobs that were never asked.

DERIVED, not pinned, and the distinction is the R2/R3/R4 lesson: the test names
NEITHER property. It extracts the `reason:` argument of every
`markBackfillJobDeferred` in the runner that writes an `FMDaemonRefusal` cause
(exactly two, asserted) and requires each log field to be TEXTUALLY the argument
of the write it describes. A rename moves the rule with the code.
RE-PLANT: DR19, DR20 — both KILLED, one per batch (515/516) because either
alone kills the same test and one batch would let each be credited for the other
(the R3 lesson that moved DR02 out of batch 500).

**R6-Fix2 — three sites in the right places is not three sites.** R5's canary
requires `sweptSiblingCount` to occur exactly three times: declared,
incremented, read. That is position-blind, and the claim R5 wrote into the
runner — "incremented only on a SUCCESSFUL defer, so a sibling skipped by the
terminal-row guard is correctly not counted" — lives entirely in WHERE the
increment sits. PB3 moved it above the `do` and every rail stayed green; no
fixture can make the sweep's store write throw, so nothing runtime sees it
either. It is reachable in the field: M-5 re-enqueues `.failed` rows under the
retry budget and the sweep's `invalidStateTransition` guard exists precisely
because that happens, so `deferredSiblings=` would count siblings that were
never deferred — the defect R5 removed from this field returning by a different
door. The increment must now come after the sweep's own defer write, located by
the two things true only of it (a `reason:` label and the sibling token).
RE-PLANT: DR21 — KILLED.

### PROBED, UNRAILED, DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED

PB4 and PB5 both concern the accounting when `markBackfillJobDeferred` itself
throws in the refusal arm. Both survive and neither is fixed, and not for the
same reason:

* PB4 (count only a successful defer) inverts the SAFE direction — the daemon
  refused the job whether or not the row write landed, so the drain-stop counter
  must advance. Shipped code is right; no plausible author moves it.
* PB5 (append regardless) is also the safe direction, and the current code's
  direction only bites when `markBackfillJobDeferred` raises
  `invalidStateTransition`, which means the row is ALREADY terminal and there is
  nothing to retry for it.

Filing either would be manufacturing. They are recorded here instead.

### VERIFIED BY READING, AND ALL HELD

* **THE DISCRIMINATOR'S POPULATION IS COMPLETE, enumerated rather than argued.**
  Four `FMInferenceDeadline.metadata` call sites, all `model.tokenCount(...)` in
  `liveRuntime`. Eight consumers propagate rather than `try?`: `planPassA` (x2),
  `planAdaptiveZoom` (x2), `planExpansionWindow`, `planBoundaryExtractionWindows`
  (NO production caller), `preambleTokenCount`, `promptBudget` — and there is no
  intervening `do`/`catch` on any of their paths to the drain (checked: runner
  3400-3620 for `planAdaptiveZoom`, 3900-4270 for the expansion chain). So a
  metadata stall CANNOT be folded into `failedWindowStatuses` as
  `.inferenceTimeout` and advance `consecutiveInferenceTimeoutAbortThreshold` —
  which would have been this bead's own defect class one layer down, a wedged
  tokenizer counted as evidence about the MODEL and written into 8d5r's
  `inferenceTimeout-noProgress`. The six `try?` sites swallow.
* **R3's usability-probe clearance re-verified as a fact, not an expression.**
  `shouldCacheFailure(for:)` is `!FMDaemonThrottle.isThrottle(error)`, so a
  metadata stall WOULD be cached as an unusable model for fifteen minutes.
  `probeIfNeeded`'s bounded call is `FMInferenceDeadline.run(FMInferenceDeadline
  .standard)` around a `session.respond` whose closure calls nothing in our
  runtime — there is no second budget in scope at that catch. The narrow
  predicate is safe today for a structural reason, not a careful one.
* **THE DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCE IS SHARPER THAN R5 STATED.** R5 recorded that
  `AdDetectionService` maps empty `deferredJobIds` to `.ranSucceeded`. What that
  costs is one line further on: `shouldClearRetryFlag` is `self == .ranSucceeded`,
  and `retryShadowFMPhaseForSession` calls `clearSessionShadowRetry` on it. So
  PRE-FIX a wedged daemon did not merely report success — it CLEARED the durable
  `needsShadowRetry` flag, retiring the episode's rescue lane, while the row said
  `failed` with a retry spent. Post-fix `.ranNeedsRetry` leaves the flag set. The
  runner-side half of the seam is railed (`result.deferredJobIds.contains(jobId)`);
  the mapping is pre-existing and not widened into this diff.
* **REACH END TO END, by enumeration.** The C-B re-enqueue gate reads only
  `status != .complete` and `retryCount < AdmissionController.maxRetries` — it
  does NOT filter on `deferReason`, so the new tokens cannot fall outside a
  resumable set. `countResumableBackfillJobs` is `status <> complete AND status
  <> running AND retryCount < maxRetries`, so a preserved `retryCount = 0` keeps
  the asset eligible where three failures used to retire it at 3.
* **AND THE OBVIOUS OBJECTION TO THAT IS BOUNDED, checked rather than assumed.**
  "Retry forever is cheap" is licensed on DAEMON time, not on the onn6 sweep's
  slots, and that sweep is ordered oldest-stranded-first — so a chronically
  refused asset sorting first forever would be a new scarcity the cost argument
  never addressed. It cannot: `nextAdScanRedriveWorkKey` caps the chain at
  `maxAdScanRedrives = 2` per asset. Post-fix strictly dominates pre-fix here
  (pre-fix the asset retired at `retryCount = 3` and no re-drive was ever minted).
* `markBackfillJobComplete` PRESERVES `deferReason`, so a job that stalled and
  later completed keeps `metadataStall-refused` on a `complete` row. Deliberate
  and documented ("audit trail"), kvs8-era for `rateLimited-prologue`, and the
  counterfactual is right: 11 of 14 rows in the pull are NULL, so the token still
  means "a stall happened", which is what it is for. Not a defect.
* The rest of the functional production diff is smaller than it looks:
  `FMInferenceDeadline.swift` is DOC-ONLY, and `FMDaemonThrottle.swift`'s only
  non-comment change is the `shouldStopDraining` parameter label — semantically
  inert and enforced at every call site by the compiler.

### NOT WIDENED

`siblingCause=` printing unchanged when nothing was swept is **playhead-6q7p**,
filed, and is a DIFFERENT defect from R6-Fix1 on the same field (uninformative
vs. naming the wrong property). Fixed the second, left the first.
`playhead-ws6m`, `x8ck`, `zize`, `bsw6`, `fua7` untouched. Nothing new filed —
every candidate this round either resolved to shipped-and-correct or was already
somebody's bead.

### NAMED RESIDUAL, examined and deliberately NOT railed

"The MOST RECENT refusal wins" is exercised throttle-then-stall (test 716) and
throttle-then-throttle (test 768); stall-then-throttle has no test. It was
checked rather than assumed and adds nothing: a counter that advanced only for
stalls and a counter that advanced only for throttles BOTH fail 716, because
either asymmetry stops the drain reaching threshold 2 on a mixed run and no
sibling is swept. A third test would be instrument bloat, so it is named here
instead.

### VERDICTS, VERBATIM

* **lint**: `scripts/lint.sh` whole repo, strict -> `lint: clean`, before the
  commit, after the commit, and again before the final gate.
* **Mutation battery, the new group**: `--dry-run` first on all three — "every
  anchor applied exactly once and the tree was restored". Then DR19 (batch 515),
  DR20 (516), DR21 (517), EACH WITH ITS OWN GREEN BASELINE: 3 KILLED / 0
  SURVIVED / 0 ERROR, 2 builds and ~4m10s apiece.
* **Mutation battery, the DR01-DR18 regression** re-run behind them at the fix
  commit with `PLAYHEAD_MB_SKIP_BASELINE=1`, batches 500-514: **18 KILLED / 0
  SURVIVED / 0 ERROR**, 15 batches, all rc=0. **Twenty-one mutations, zero
  survivors.** Tree verified with `[ -z "$(git status --porcelain)" ]` after
  every batch; the loop breaks on a dirty tree and never did.
* **Final scoped gate**, 8 `-only-testing:` flags passed LITERALLY:
  `lint: clean`; `Test run with 37 tests in 6 suites passed after 1.276 seconds.`;
  `Executed 5 tests, with 0 failures (0 unexpected)` +
  `Executed 2 tests, with 0 failures (0 unexpected)`; `** TEST SUCCEEDED **`;
  `fast-gate: baseline check SKIPPED — selective run, a different population`.
  No `--accept-baseline`.
* **ZERO failures in BOTH formats**: 0 Swift Testing `failed after`, and 14
  XCTest `Test Case` lines of which 0 contain `failed`.
* **Suite-name mapping, all 8 requested names found** (R4's misspelled-suite
  trap). Swift Testing `Suite "…" passed after`: FMDaemonRefusalDefinitionTests ->
  "playhead-e75l: FMDaemonRefusal is the one definition of a daemon condition";
  FMDaemonMetadataStallRunnerTests -> "playhead-e75l: a metadata-deadline timeout
  in the prologue DEFERS with a named cause"; FMDaemonThrottleClassificationTests
  -> "playhead-kvs8: FMDaemonThrottle is the one definition of a daemon
  throttle"; FMThrottledPrologueRunnerTests -> "playhead-kvs8: a throttled
  coarse-pass prologue DEFERS with a named cause"; FMThrottlePermissiveLaneTests
  -> "playhead-kvs8: the permissive lane records a throttle as a throttle";
  FMThrottleUsabilityProbeTests -> "playhead-kvs8: a throttled readiness probe
  must not be cached as an unusable model". XCTest `Test Suite '…' passed at`:
  FMDaemonRefusalSourceCanaryTests, FMDaemonThrottleCanaryTests. Swift Testing
  suites started == passed == 6, parsed on the quoted form.
* No blanket `git checkout` was ever run. The probe restore named its two files
  explicitly, and the tree was verified clean immediately afterwards.

### NOT EVALUATED

The full `PlayheadFastTests` plan, per playhead-q1go (~50% of full runs never
reach a verdict on this box) and Dan's gate economics. The rest of the battery
outside the DR series carries its earlier verdicts. `playhead-zize`'s counter
reset remains unrailed by construction, which is that bead's content.

### MERGE JUDGEMENT: YES

**The shipped behaviour is correct and adequately railed.** This round planted
five probes against production verbatim and found NO defect — the production
diff is byte-identical to what R5 left. That is the second consecutive round in
which the disposition itself was not moved, and this time the probes were aimed
at production rather than at the canaries.

What the round adds is that the last two unheld claims on the two log lines are
now held: every DURABLE TOKEN and every EVENT NAME on both lines is now tied to
the write it describes, and the sweep counter is tied to the write it counts.
Twenty-one mutations, zero survivors. The residual is unchanged from R5 — zize
(one unrailed reset, cost = a delayed drain), fua7 (two canary limits wanting a
capability rather than an enumeration), bsw6 (a battery-tooling gap), 6q7p
(`siblingCause=` is uninformative when nothing was swept), ws6m and x8ck. None
touches the disposition.

## R7 REVIEW — 0 PRODUCTION / 3 INSTRUMENT

R6's design repeated and extended: probes planted against production VERBATIM in ONE
build, each predicted to survive so a green run attributes, plus an observer control
killed by name. New this round, a SECOND build carrying two mutants predicted to be
KILLED — because two of this bead's load-bearing claims had been cleared by READING in
every round so far and never by planting.

**Nothing this round changes shipped behaviour.** The production diff is byte-identical
to what R6 left. All three findings are places where the runner is correct today and
could stop being correct silently.

### THE PROBE BUILD — one build, five plants, nine suites

`Test run with 43 tests in 7 suites failed after 1.038 seconds with 1 issue` — exactly
one, and it was the control. 0 XCTest failures ("Executed 5 tests, with 0 failures" +
"Executed 2 tests, with 0 failures").

  CTRL  KILLED    `"metadataStall-batchSibling"` -> `...QQ`   (observer control,
                  `causesAreNamedAndDistinct`, "Expectation failed:
                  FMDaemonRefusal.metadataStall.batchSiblingCause == ...")
  PC1   SURVIVED  drain-stop `consecutive=` reads `deferred.count`
  PC2   SURVIVED  per-job `consecutive=` reads `job.retryCount`
  PC3   SURVIVED  drain-stop event reads `FMDaemonRefusal.throttle.drainStoppedEvent`
  PC4   SURVIVED  `AdDetectionService`'s `deferredJobIds.isEmpty` branches INVERTED

The scope deliberately included `AdDetectionServiceShadowModeTests` so PC4 had an
observer that could plausibly have seen it. It did not.

### THE VERIFICATION BUILD — two claims re-planted rather than re-read

`Test run with 37 tests in 6 suites failed after 1.135 seconds with 6 issues`, 0 XCTest
failures. Both predicted KILLED, both killed, by name.

* **PB-A**, `deferred.append(job.jobId)` deleted from the refusal arm — the seam
  `AdDetectionService` maps to `.ranNeedsRetry`. Killed by "a metadata-deadline timeout
  in the PROLOGUE defers the job" AND kvs8's "a daemon throttle in the coarse-pass
  PROLOGUE defers the job". R6 asserted this half was railed; now it is measured.
* **PB-B**, `retryCount = retryCount + 1` added to `markBackfillJobDeferred`'s UPDATE —
  retryCount preservation at the STORE, which R1, R3 and R5 each cleared by reading the
  SQL. Killed by "a metadata stall does not spend a lifetime retry", kvs8's throttle
  mirror, and "THE COST, DIRECTLY: three metadata stalls must not disqualify an episode
  forever".

### INSTRUMENT (3), both fixes folded into canaries that already exist

**R7-Fix1 (PC3) — R1's PRODUCTION defect is re-emittable with no literal.** R1 found the
drain-stop event hard-coded to `fm.backfill.drain_stopped_by_throttle` for a drain
stopped by metadata stalls. The rails that bought forbid the LITERAL (derived from
`allCases`, R2-Fix2) and pin the read ORDER (R4-Fix1). Binding the read to a fixed KIND
instead puts the byte-identical name on the wire while `drainStoppedEvent` is still read
exactly once and still after `logEvent`. Fixing a value by forbidding its SPELLING is
the shape R2-Fix2, R3-Fix1 and R4-Fix8 each had to replace — one round after R4's CN-A1
showed the same thing for the property PAIR. FIX: each line's event must be read off the
SAME VALUE as the cause the defer beside it wrote, derived from the receivers R6-Fix1
already extracts (`\(` anchored, because `refusalThatStoppedUs` has `refusal` as a
prefix and only the anchor separates them). RE-PLANT: DR22 — KILLED.

**R7-Fix2 (PC1, PC2) — `consecutive=` is the fifth field on that line and the first
with no rule at all.** R1 corrected its event NAME, R2 its `cause=` -> `siblingCause=`,
R5 its `deferredSiblings=`, R6 the cause pair's binding; `consecutive=` rode through all
four untouched, on BOTH lines. PC1 gave the drain-stop field `deferred.count` — the
drain-wide accumulator R5 had just removed from `deferredSiblings=` one field to its
right. PC2 is the sharper one: `job.retryCount` is the quantity THIS BEAD EXISTS TO HOLD
CONSTANT, so the field would read the same number whether the daemon refused this job
once or four times running. What would it read if the run of refusals had never
happened? The same value, and normally zero. FIX: the expected identifier is read out of
the `shouldStopDraining(consecutiveRefusals:)` call — report the number you decided on.
Measured in production: exactly one such call, exactly two `consecutive=` fields.
RE-PLANT: DR23, DR24 — both KILLED, separate batches for the R3 reason.

### FILED, not fixed

* **playhead-6d6v (P2)** — probe PC4. `AdDetectionService` maps `deferredJobIds.isEmpty`
  to `.ranSucceeded`, `shouldClearRetryFlag` is `self == .ranSucceeded`, and
  `retryShadowFMPhaseForSession` calls `clearSessionShadowRetry` on it — so PRE-FIX a
  wedged daemon CLEARED the episode's durable rescue flag. Inverting those two branches
  restores exactly that and SURVIVED, with `AdDetectionServiceShadowModeTests` in scope.

  `ranNeedsRetry`, `ranSucceeded` or `clearSessionShadowRetry` from a runner result. Not

  asserted.** `coarsePassA` writes the durable cursor incrementally
  (`checkpointBackfillJobProgress`, BackfillJobRunner:2945, playhead-26od), so a refusal

* **`FMInferenceTimeoutError` carries the BUDGET, not the elapsed time**

title: fullEpisodeScan marks complete having examined 2-21% — the job terminal is claimed, not measured (53FC53E3: one 36s window in 23s)
description:
## The defect (STILL BROKEN at d3dfa1ca)

A `fullEpisodeScan` job's terminal is NOT gated on measured coverage: `markBackfillJobComplete` fires whenever runJob returns without a rate-limit hole (BackfillJobRunner.swift:907-913), where "done" means "swept the segments I was handed" — and the segments are atomized from whatever transcript exists at invocation time (AdDetectionService.swift:9273-9279). The final-pass hook fires runBackfill the moment final chunks land (PlayheadRuntime.swift:1905), which is typically EARLY in the transcript's life, so the job for that transcriptVersion completes having read a sliver, and M-5 skips it forever (BackfillJobRunner.swift:542-544).

pz32/gqx4 made the ASSET-level verdict and the library checkmark honest (measured, not claimed). The JOB-level terminal is the one place still claiming completion without measurement — and it feeds `shouldMintAdScanRedrive`'s no-progress guard via countResumableBackfillJobs (a complete row is not resumable), so a 2%-examined "complete" job actively blocks the re-drive that would have fixed it.

## Measured on the 2026-08-03 device pull

- 53FC53E3 (2528s episode, 98% transcript at pull time): fullEpisodeScan created 2026-08-02 04:38:43, complete 04:39:06 — 23 seconds — having durably examined ONE 36s window (2490-2526, exactly its lexical-candidate span). Query: `SELECT windowStartTime, windowEndTime FROM semantic_scan_results WHERE analysisAssetId LIKE '53FC53E3%'`.
- AD5F3A0A (4280s): fullEpisodeScan complete 08-03 08:23:05 with scan windows spanning only 3-900s — the transcript at that moment was the 900s tier; the fp hook ran against it.
- Same shape hvk0 measured on the 07-29 pull and documented at AdDetectionService.swift:895-898: "every fullEpisodeScan on feeds.simplecast.com/dHoohVNH examined 82-167s of episodes 1,503-4,379s long (2-5%)".

None of #327-#344 touches the job-complete condition.

## The fix

Complete a fullEpisodeScan only when measured adScanFraction (pz32's number, same numerator/denominator as the checkmark) clears `semanticBackfillSufficientAdScanFraction`; otherwise defer with the honest cursor (the pmp9 shape at BackfillJobRunner.swift:865-905 already exists for the rate-limit case — extend it to under-coverage generally). Alternatively/complementarily: the fp hook should not dispatch the coverage lane against a transcript that has not reached the finalize floor.
notes:
## QUEUE 3 — REACH, Dan 2026-08-03. Six beads from the device-pull investigation.

    26od -> fil5 -> 9y9e -> 41mu -> e75l -> dl9k

**Why this queue exists.** A fresh device pull (2026-08-03, scratchpad/db-aug3/analysis.sqlite,
the first usable field data in two weeks) measured: **12 episodes, 9 transcribed to ~100%, only 3
with ANY semantic ad-scan, ZERO at >=98%.** An episode at 0% scan cannot produce a skip no matter
how correct the downstream logic is. The sixteen beads merged 2026-08-02/03 (#327-#344) all
improved downstream CORRECTNESS; none moved REACH. Reach is the dominant term.

**Order is by multiplier, not severity.**
  * 26od FIRST because it is the multiplier: coarsePassA persists nothing until it returns,
    passes need 12-45min, lifecycle windows are ~30min, so ~4.6 HOURS of FM compute this weekend
    produced ZERO durable scan rows. Until this lands every other fix in this queue evaporates
    the same way.
  * fil5 second: 3 of 12 episodes have NO path to a scan at all, and every shadow-phase bail is
    silent (FCDDB309 ran runBackfill TWICE and minted nothing; which of four gates fired is
    recorded nowhere). Also makes the NEXT device pull attributable.
  * 9y9e third: onn6 re-drives structurally cannot drain (full preAnalysis pass re-transcribes
    covered audio; mptr only REORDERS, does not skip; 300s cap wins; zeroCoverage). maxAdScanRedrives=2
    is SPENT on five assets.
  * 41mu / e75l are correctness-of-accounting on the same path. dl9k is a rescue nudge, last.

CLASSIFIED AGAINST THE SHIPPED BUILD (d3dfa1ca): rate-limit terminal is FIXED (kvs8 #320); the
mptr covered-prefix MECHANISM is fixed (#335) but no vehicle re-mints a pass for already-stuck
assets. Everything else in this queue is STILL BROKEN on the phone.

Method: iterative-implementation-with-review-loops. One bead at a time, full gate + mutation
battery each, cap 20 review rounds, stop on two consecutive clean.
## R2 review (fresh reviewer) — 2 findings, both fixed, 3 mutants run

**1. MEDIUM, the bead's own family, inside the fix.** `recordUnderCoverageTerminal`
fed `underCoverageCursor` the CALLER's `jobInputs` — the segment list BEFORE
`narrowedForResume` trims the covered prefix — while the rule's contract is the
list `coarsePassA` was handed. The two are the same value on a first attempt (why
the implementer, R1 and eight mutants all passed over it) and differ on every
RESUME by exactly the hole the rule detects: the pre-narrowing list starts at the
asset's first transcript segment (~0 s) while the run's first plan starts at the
cursor, so `first - priorUpper` went negative and the head test could never fire.
Field: AD5F3A0A's persisted cursor is 900 and its fast transcript does not resume
until 3,270 s — a 2,370 s hole of which the final pass later fills 2,356 s, 55 %
of a 4,281 s episode, which `narrowedForResume` would drop on the next attempt.

match its contract.

**2. LOW, documentation.** `underCoverageCursor`'s doc stated "only honest when
the run's own plans began at the head" — a necessary condition presented as

property this bead's accepted cost rests on. The decision is the THRESHOLD, not

intersect-then-bridge algorithm); all five sub-floor ceilings (.1300 .8109 .8833

really is unreachable at this terminal; `narrowedInputs` short-circuits
`.fullEpisodeScan` so the H13 `markBackfillJobComplete` is not an ungated writer.

transcriptVersion hash argument (playhead-iu0t's evidence), and the UC02-UC06 /

title: carriesRediffByteExactWidth is TRUE for chroma-derived rediff width — the name promises byte-exactness the predicate does not check
description:
Found while scoping playhead-sik9's post-roll exemption. Recorded because FIVE
shipped carve-outs now key on this one predicate and none of them can tell the
two differs apart.

## The finding

`DecodedSpan.carriesRediffByteExactWidth` is defined as
`anchorProvenance.contains(.rediffSlot)`, and its doc block calls that "the
byte-exact REDIFF width-oracle". But `.rediffSlot` is stamped by
`AdDetectionService.applyRediffSlotOwnershipPass` for BOTH differ paths:

  * BYTE PRIMARY — `computeByteAlignedPlayedSlots` -> `RediffByteAligner` +
    `RediffSlotOwnership.gateAndDiffBytes`. Genuinely byte-exact.
  * CHROMA FALLBACK — taken whenever the byte path yields nothing (no B-side
    URL, no anchored A-side file, unreadable bytes, or EVERY B gate-rejects) ->
    `RediffSlotOwnership.gateAndDiff`, which is ~1 s chroma-fingerprint
    alignment. NOT byte-exact.

Both produce `playedSlots`, both go through the same `SpliceSlotRewriter.apply(
provenance: .rediffSlot)`, and `SpanExtentSupport.derive` then stamps
`.rediffByteExact` on BOTH edges from the same single test. So a chroma-derived
width currently reads as `deterministic` tier everywhere.

The chroma path is REACHABLE in production. `computeByteAlignedPlayedSlots`
warns explicitly that every device `sourceURL` ends in `.mp3` but that the
suffix "is not evidence that the bytes are MP3" — if the container is AAC/M4A
the aligner finds no frames and every diff gate-rejects, which is precisely the
"fall back to chroma" branch.

## Who reads it

  * `FusionWeightConfig.hostReadConfidenceFloor` exemption (playhead-wraj)
  * the FM-suppression cap exemption (playhead-qs0d)
  * the creator-chapter suppression exemption (playhead-pzy2)
  * the self-promo suppression exemption (playhead-fl4j / pzy2)
  * the post-roll guard exemption (playhead-sik9)
  * `SpanExtentSupport.derive` -> `AutoSkipEdgeAnchor.rediffByteExact` ->
    `ExtentAnchorTier.deterministic` -> the playhead-2350 auto-skip admission
    and `AutoSkipEdgePadding`'s per-tier margins

That last one is the sharpest edge: `AutoSkipEdgePadding` derives its late-safe
margins (0.50 s start / 0.75 s end) from MEASURED byte-exact edge error. A
chroma edge does not have that error distribution, so it is being padded with a
budget derived from a different instrument.

## Why sik9 did not fix it

Splitting the two needs a distinct `AnchorRef` case (or an associated value),
which is a persisted-provenance change: `decoded_spans.anchorProvenance` is
JSON-encoded by `AnchorRef: Codable` and `LossyAnchorRef` exists precisely
because older binaries must tolerate unknown `type` strings. That is a schema +
migration decision, and sik9 was scoped to the guard. Forking the predicate for
ONE of five consumers would also have been strictly worse than the status quo:
the five would then disagree about what "byte-exact" means.

## Suggested shape (not a decision)

Add `.rediffSlotChroma` (or `.rediffSlot(byteExact: Bool)`) at the rewrite site,
keep `carriesRediffByteExactWidth` meaning BYTE-exact only, and give the chroma
case its own `ExtentAnchorTier` — `.corroborated` is the honest home for a ~1 s
independent acoustic re-observation, which is exactly what `.stingerSnapped`
already occupies. Then re-derive whether each of the five carve-outs wants
byte-only or byte-or-chroma; they may not all answer the same way.

## First measurement to take before deciding

How often is the chroma fallback actually taken on the live corpus? The
`[xsdz.57] byte differ ... falling back to chroma` log line already exists and
already names the reason. If the answer is "never on real devices" this is a
naming fix; if it is common, it is a precision bug in the auto-skip admission.
notes:
## QUEUE — revised 2026-08-02

    isp5(done) -> b6r2(done) -> y3ya(done) -> lxkq(done) -> avbn(done) -> sik9(done)
      -> nqey(in flight) -> 6qvf -> 9v09 -> gard -> mptr -> hx6n

**6qvf inserted directly after nqey (Dan, 2026-08-02).** It is the safety half of the flip that
just shipped: `certaintyTieredSkipEnabled` ON makes the certainty tiers load-bearing, and 6qvf is
the reason one of those tiers is not what it says. `carriesRediffByteExactWidth` is true for the
~1s chroma fallback as well as the byte differ, so a chroma edge is admitted to auto-skip at
`deterministic` tier and padded with margins derived from MEASURED byte-exact edge error
(0.50s start / 0.75s end). Live today, independent of any flag.

MEASURE FIRST: how often the chroma fallback is actually taken decides whether the persisted
AnchorRef change is worth it. Rare => theoretical. Common => a real wrong-skip hazard.

One at a time. No device build until the queue completes.

title: a test that asserts only 'no banner was emitted' no longer proves 'no banner will fire' — d3g0 made banner emission deferred
description:
Found via the A11 mutation survivor while verifying playhead-avbn (#329). Not specific to that bead — it is a suite-wide test-validity question.

THE SHAPE:
playhead-d3g0 (#314) changed banner delivery so a suggest-tier banner is ARMED when the window is registered and EMITTED later, when the playhead ENTERS the span. Before d3g0, registering a suggest window and observing no banner within the test's window was reasonable evidence that no banner would appear. After d3g0 it proves only that the playhead had not yet entered the span — which, in a test that never advances the playhead, is true by construction and independent of the code under test.

HOW IT SURFACED (worth reading, because the test suite looked green):
avbn's A11 mutation routed the blocked gate to the suggest tier — i.e. it made a span that must be dropped instead produce a banner in the field. The blocked-gate suite stayed GREEN. All five of its assertions are negative ('no banner emitted'), and the mutant only ARMED a banner, so nothing fired inside the test. A real regression was invisible to a suite written specifically to catch it.

The avbn fix added a positive witness (the isp5 census row plus armedSuggest == 0) and the rail now kills A11. That repair is landed. What is NOT done is checking whether other suites have the same blind spot.

THE WORK:
1. Enumerate tests whose ONLY evidence of 'this span does not surface' is the absence of a banner emission. Grep for the emission observer/spy assertions and look for suites with no positive witness and no playhead advance.
2. For each, decide the right witness: assert the ARMED state (armedSuggest count), or the isp5 census row (ad_window_ingest_census disposition), or advance the playhead past the span so emission actually has its chance.
3. Mutation-test the repaired suites — the criterion is that routing a must-drop span to the suggest tier FAILS them. A suite that still passes under that mutation has not been fixed.

WHY P1: this is the vacuous-assertion class, which this repo has hit before (playhead-auz3, playhead-2x8z). Its cost is not a wrong answer but a false sense of coverage: every affected suite reports green while proving nothing about the contract it names. Combined with the fact that most of these guard AUTO-SKIP admission, a silent hole here is one that lets a wrong skip reach Dan.

RELATED: [[playhead-d3g0]] (the deferral that created the shape), [[playhead-avbn]] (where it was found), [[playhead-isp5]] (the census that provides the positive witness), [[playhead-auz3]] / [[playhead-2x8z]] (prior vacuous-test cleanups).
notes:

title: The ingest census has a silent retraction path: a retroactively retired window still reads as armed
description:
Found by playhead-y3ya while using the instrument playhead-isp5 (#324) shipped hours earlier.

## The hole

`SkipOrchestrator.reapplyInventoryFilterToManagedWindows` (`SkipOrchestrator.swift:2511`) retires
managed windows AND suggestions **without stamping an ingest outcome**.

So a span that was armed by the cross-launch preload, and is then retroactively dropped when
`setDeclaredChapters` / `setEpisodeDuration` arrives, leaves the census reading
`ingest_armed_suggest = 1` **with no counter-evidence anywhere**. The audit trail says the window
was armed. The listener sees nothing. Both are true, and the census cannot tell you that.

## Why it matters more than its size

isp5's census is now the instrument the whole mid-roll program is being verified through — every
bead since asserts on `ad_window_ingest_census` counts rather than on absence, precisely because
reasoning from absence is what cost three investigations on the banner question.

**An instrument with a silent retraction path can certify a fix that did not hold.** A future bead
will assert `ingest_armed_suggest == 2`, pass, and ship — while the window is retired moments later
by a duration arriving from the analysis coordinator. That is the same shape as the defect isp5 was
built to catch, one layer up, in the catcher itself.

Note the timing is exactly the risky one: `AnalysisCoordinator` calls `setEpisodeDuration`
immediately before `receiveAdWindows` on the hot path — but the PRELOAD door runs earlier, so the
retroactive sweep is a real ordering, not a hypothetical.

## Work

Give the retroactive path its own named outcome (`ingest_retired_reapplied_inventory_filter` or
similar, with the filter's rejection reason), counted, and written to the same
`SurfaceStatusInvariantLogger` session row the device pull reads. Follow isp5's existing naming —
do not invent a second vocabulary.

The census should be readable as a balance: what was armed, minus what was retired, equals what the
listener could actually have seen.

## Acceptance

Arm a span through the preload door, then deliver a duration that makes the inventory filter reject
it. The census must show BOTH the arm and the retirement, with the reason. And the negative: a span
that is armed and stays armed records no retirement — an outcome that fires on every delivery is as
useless as one that never fires.

Related: [[playhead-isp5]] (the instrument), [[playhead-b6r2]] (why a duration arriving late changes
the filter's verdict at all).
## QUEUE — revised 2026-08-01, position 8 of 11

    isp5(done) -> b6r2(done) -> y3ya(done) -> lxkq -> avbn -> sik9 -> nqey -> 9v09 -> gard -> mptr -> hx6n

**The census is now the instrument the whole program is verified through — a silent retraction path can certify a fix that did not hold.**
