just shipped: `certaintyTieredSkipEnabled` ON makes the certainty tiers load-bearing, and 6qvf is
the reason one of those tiers is not what it says. `carriesRediffByteExactWidth` is true for the
~1s chroma fallback as well as the byte differ, so a chroma edge is admitted to auto-skip at
`deterministic` tier and padded with margins derived from MEASURED byte-exact edge error
(0.50s start / 0.75s end). Live today, independent of any flag.

MEASURE FIRST: how often the chroma fallback is actually taken decides whether the persisted
AnchorRef change is worth it. Rare => theoretical. Common => a real wrong-skip hazard.

One at a time. No device build until the queue completes.

title: Flip certaintyTieredSkipEnabled ON — after sik9 gives the post-roll guard its byte-anchored exemption
description:
The flip itself. [[playhead-wraj]] has been IN_PROGRESS since 2026-07-18 with the mechanism built,
measured and shipping OFF behind `certaintyTieredSkipEnabled`; this bead is the enablement, which
the flag's own doc block reserves as "Dan's Gate-2 decision".

**Dan approved the direction 2026-08-01, conditional on [[playhead-sik9]] landing first.**

## What the flag does — both effects are DEMOTIONS

`certaintyTieredSkipEnabled` only ever moves `.eligible` -> `.markOnly`, never the reverse, and
never touches a score. It cannot create a wrong skip. Two effects:

1. **`hostReadConfidenceFloor` (T = 0.9)** — a NON-rediff (host-read) span below the floor demotes
   to markOnly. Rediff-anchored spans are exempt. Calibrated on the themove host-read fixture
   (2026-07-17: T=0.9 skips the confident reads, banners the uncertain ones and the low-confidence
   fragments).
2. **`postRollGuardSeconds` (90 s)** — a span ending within 90 s of a KNOWN duration demotes to
   markOnly. **Today: regardless of rediff anchoring or score.** That is what sik9 fixes.

Verified by the 2026-07-19 gate-delta measurement: 32/32 windows predicted-vs-observed agree at
T=0.9 + 90 s post-roll.

## Why it was NOT flipped when Dan first asked (2026-08-01)

Its two halves currently point opposite ways:

  * **The host-read floor is INERT in practice.** FM barely runs, and when it does its `containsAd`
    verdicts do not surface at all ([[playhead-y3ya]]). There is no host-read population reaching
    `.eligible` for the floor to protect against. It buys nothing yet.
  * **The post-roll guard is a PURE LOSS.** Dan's post-roll on DE0784D8 is 5462.6-5522.7 on a
    5522.65 s episode — byte-exact, confidence 1.00, measured 2 of 2 correct. Flipping today
    demotes one of only TWO things measured working on his phone.

So: costs a working skip, buys protection against a population that does not exist yet.

## Preconditions — all three, in order

1. **[[playhead-sik9]]** — the post-roll guard exempts a byte-ANCHORED inner edge. Without it the
   flip actively removes a correct skip.
2. **[[playhead-y3ya]]** — semantic `containsAd` verdicts surface as suggest-tier candidates.
   Without it the host-read floor has nothing to act on and its calibration is untested in the
   field.
3. **[[playhead-lxkq]]** — FM budget lands likely-slot-first, so host-read spans actually EXIST in
   the population the floor is calibrated for. Without it the floor is calibrated on a fixture and
   validated against nothing.

sik9 is the hard blocker. y3ya and lxkq are what make the flip MEAN anything rather than merely be
safe.

## What to verify at flip time — measure, do not assume

- On the DE0784D8 fixture: the byte-exact post-roll STAYS `.eligible` and produces a cue (proves
  sik9 held); a tail span with an UNANCHORED start still demotes (proves the guard still guards).
- A host-read span at skipConfidence < 0.9 demotes to markOnly; one at >= 0.9 stays eligible.
- Rediff-anchored spans are unaffected by the floor.
- **Count what changed.** The flip should demote a NAMED, SMALL set. If it demotes a large
  fraction of currently-eligible windows, the calibration has drifted since 2026-07-19 and the
  right answer is to re-measure, not to ship.
- Use the [[playhead-isp5]] census (`ad_window_ingest_census`) for the evidence — assert on counts,
  not on absence.

## The standing principle this serves

[[feedback_certainty_tiered_skip_2026-07-17]]: auto-skip high-certainty DAI, mark host-read when
uncertain, PER CLASS rather than on one global threshold. With sik9 in place both halves finally
express that: the floor demotes uncertain host-reads (rediff exempt), and the guard demotes
uncertain tails (byte-anchored exempt). Without sik9 the second half is certainty-BLIND, which is
the inversion Dan objected to.
## QUEUE — revised 2026-08-01, position 6 of 9

    isp5(done) -> b6r2(done) -> y3ya -> lxkq -> sik9 -> nqey -> gard -> mptr -> hx6n

**The flip. Safe by construction (demotions only) but meaningless until y3ya+lxkq give the floor something to act on, and harmful until sik9 lands.**

One at a time. No device build until the queue completes, then ONE build and one dogfood pass.
## QUEUE — revised 2026-08-01, position 7 of 11

    isp5(done) -> b6r2(done) -> y3ya(done) -> lxkq -> avbn -> sik9 -> nqey -> 9v09 -> gard -> mptr -> hx6n

**The wraj flip. Safe by construction; meaningful only once y3ya/lxkq give the host-read floor a real population.**

One at a time. No device build until the queue completes.

title: The post-roll guard must exempt a byte-anchored inner edge — it currently demotes the most certain signal like the least
description:
**DAN DECIDED 2026-08-01: "we do need a rediff exemption."**

## The rule as written

`FusionWeightConfig.postRollGuardSeconds` (90 s, playhead-wraj) demotes any `.eligible` span
ending within 90 s of a KNOWN episode duration to `.markOnly` — **regardless of rediff anchoring
or skipConfidence.** The doc block states the no-exemption choice explicitly, unlike
`hostReadConfidenceFloor`, which DOES exempt rediff-anchored spans.

Dan's recorded reasoning, 2026-07-19: *"Post-roll ads are the least important to auto-skip (the
user just jumps to the next episode) and a wrong skip near the end clips the host's closing
content."*

## Why that reasoning does not survive contact with the byte-exact case

It is sound for an **uncertain** detector. A byte-exact rediff post-roll is not uncertain:

  * the origin literally served DIFFERENT BYTES over that range — divergence IS the ad
  * measured 2 of 2 correct on Dan's device, confidence 1.00
  * boundary accuracy measured at **0.4 s** against his own manual mark on the pre-roll
  * the OUTER edge is the episode end, so it is bounded and cannot overrun into anything

Applying a blanket demotion there is the **certainty-tiered principle inverted** — treating the
most certain signal in the system exactly like the least. That contradicts
[[feedback_certainty_tiered_skip_2026-07-17]] (auto-skip high-certainty DAI, mark host-read when
uncertain, PER CLASS) and [[feedback_outer_edges_free_inner_precious_2026-07-29]] (the outer edge
is free; only the inner edge can cost show).

Field evidence: Dan's post-roll on DE0784D8 is `5462.6 - 5522.7` on a 5522.65 s episode. Under the
rule as written, flipping wraj ON would demote one of only TWO things measured working on his
phone.

## The work

Give the post-roll guard a rediff exemption, mirroring `hostReadConfidenceFloor`'s.

**Scope it to what the evidence actually covers** — this is the part to get right:
  * exempt spans whose width is BYTE-DERIVED (`.rediffByteExact` on both edges / `.rediffSlot`
    width ownership), NOT merely "rediff touched this episode"
  * the INNER edge is the one that can cost show. A post-roll's inner edge is its START. If that
    edge is anchored byte-exact, the span cannot creep backwards into the show. If it is NOT
    anchored, the guard should still apply — an unanchored start near the episode end is exactly
    the case Dan's original reasoning describes.
  * segment-recovered / non-monotonic (9s6q) slots are NOT byte-exact and must NOT be exempt
  * playhead-2350 still holds independently: an unanchored edge cannot auto-skip at all

So the exemption is narrower than "rediff": it is **"the inner edge is byte-anchored."**

## Interaction — do not lose this

playhead-b6r2 (#325) just fixed ADMISSION (the inventory filter was rejecting every pre-roll AND
every post-roll before either tier saw them). This bead is about the TIER of an admitted tail
window. Both are needed and they are independent — flipping wraj without b6r2 would have shown
Dan nothing at all.

## Then reconsider shipping wraj ON

With this exemption in place, wraj's two halves both point the right way:
  * host-read floor (T=0.9) — demotes uncertain host-reads, rediff exempt
  * post-roll guard (90 s) — demotes uncertain tails, byte-anchored tails exempt

At that point the gate is genuinely certainty-tiered rather than certainty-blind in one half.
**Recommend flipping wraj after this lands AND after [[playhead-y3ya]]/[[playhead-lxkq]] give the
host-read floor a real population to act on** — today FM verdicts do not surface, so that half is
inert and the tail half is a pure loss.

## Acceptance

On the DE0784D8 fixture with wraj ON: the byte-exact post-roll stays `.eligible` and produces a
skip cue; a synthetic tail span with an UNANCHORED start still demotes to `.markOnly`; a
segment-recovered tail slot still demotes. Assert the negative cases, not just the positive one —
an exemption that exempts everything is the failure mode.
## QUEUE — revised 2026-08-01, position 5 of 9

    isp5(done) -> b6r2(done) -> y3ya -> lxkq -> sik9 -> nqey -> gard -> mptr -> hx6n

**HARD BLOCKER on nqey. Without the byte-anchored exemption, flipping wraj actively removes a correct skip — Dan's post-roll, 2 of 2, confidence 1.00.**

One at a time. No device build until the queue completes, then ONE build and one dogfood pass.
## QUEUE — revised 2026-08-01, position 6 of 11

    isp5(done) -> b6r2(done) -> y3ya(done) -> lxkq -> avbn -> sik9 -> nqey -> 9v09 -> gard -> mptr -> hx6n

**HARD BLOCKER on nqey — without the byte-anchored exemption the flip removes a correct skip.**

One at a time. No device build until the queue completes.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-02 — PR #330 (bead/playhead-sik9).

The exemption: the post-roll guard skips a span with
`DecodedSpan.carriesRediffByteExactWidth` — the SAME key
`hostReadConfidenceFloor` uses, so this is the 5th member of the pzy2
exemption family, not a new mechanism. certaintyTieredSkipEnabled STAYS OFF
(playhead-nqey owns the flip).

Why a WIDTH key is the INNER-EDGE key: the rediff differ is a width oracle and
`SpanExtentSupport.derive` stamps `.rediffByteExact` on BOTH edges from the
one `contains(.rediffSlot)` test, so at the mapper 'the start is byte-anchored'
and 'the width is rediff-owned' are the same predicate.

STILL GUARDED (the reviewable table, `PostRollGuardTailShapes.stillGuarded`):
unanchored `.classifierSeed`; ACOUSTIC `.spliceSlot` (the discriminating
negative — it is a width oracle that also sets both edges); `.evidenceCatalog`;
`.userCorrection`; bare span; playhead-9s6q segment-recovered (structurally
unreachable — the lagged path passes the `false` default to
`gateAndDiffBytes`, and day-0 stamps recovered slots `.unanchored` +
`.markOnly` without consulting the mapper); and a geometry-REWRITTEN rediff
span (playhead-2350 demotes it downstream, untouched).

Gate: RED (31 known / 17 NEW), all 17 triaged as the known load-sensitive
family — 0 XCTest-format failures, fastest failure in the whole run 129 s, and
all four containing suites run 22 tests green in 4.8 s isolated. The FIRST full
run also surfaced one genuine expectation-kind failure,
`UnanchoredExtentAutoSkipGateTests.signOffOverlappingLeadingEdgeNeverAutoSkips`,
whose 'reason 2' pinned the old contract; rewritten with the sign change stated
in the test plus a new arm using the provenance the replay ACTUALLY recorded.

Mutation: C series, batches 140-144, 10 KILLED / 0 SURVIVED / 0 ERROR.

DISCOVERED: playhead-6qvf — `carriesRediffByteExactWidth` is TRUE for
CHROMA-derived rediff width too (the fallback stamps the same `.rediffSlot`),
so the predicate is wider than its name. Inherited, not introduced; it already
governs four shipped carve-outs and feeds `AutoSkipEdgePadding`'s measured
byte-exact margins. Splitting needs a new `AnchorRef` case (persistence).

title: Fast mutation lane for pure-logic rails: measured 227s->3s on 12/119 rails; whole-battery saving only ~3% (investigation)
description:
# Fast mutation lane for pure-logic rails — measured feasibility, honest scope

INVESTIGATION ONLY (no code changed). Prompted by playhead-voez: the R-series battery
(`scripts/mutation-battery-gate-baseline.py`) runs 29 mutations in ~1s because it never
builds the app, while `scripts/mutation-battery.sh` spends one xcodebuild per batch.

## VERDICT IN ONE PARAGRAPH

The hypothesis "much of what we mutate is pure decision logic" is TRUE at the FILE level
and mostly FALSE at the RAIL level. The mutated files are often Foundation-only, but the
battery deliberately judges most rails through behavioral app suites (orchestrator, store,
runner) — and per this repo's own doctrine (the L04/L05 hand-re-runs; "a KILL only proves
SOME expectation failed") that is a feature, not an accident. Empirically, 12 of 119 rails
(10%) are judged ENTIRELY by suites that compile and pass outside the app, byte-identical
sources and tests; +5 more (14% total) with two small file splits. For those rails the
per-batch cost drops from a MEASURED 227s to a MEASURED 3-5s (~50-70x). But because
batches amortize builds and the movable rails share batches with app-bound anchors, a
whole-battery run saves only ~2 of 68 builds (~3%). The dramatic win is real but narrow:
it lands on AUTHORING loops of policy-heavy beads (4dqe-class) and on the marginal cost of
ADDING pure rails, not on the certification battery's wall clock. Recommendation: the
smallest viable fast lane (generated SwiftPM package + manifest, sibling runner mirroring
the R-series precedent) — worth doing, but sized as a ~1-bead tool, not a program. A full
module split of the app is NOT justified by these numbers and is rejected below.

## MEASURED NUMBERS (all measured today, 2026-08-01, on this box)

Today's cost per battery batch (xcodebuild, current 35-suite FOCUSED_SUITES):
- 227.4s — the one "Testing project Playhead" activity in the main checkout's
  `.derivedData/Logs/Build/LogStoreManifest.plist` (started 14:43, warm derived data).
- Corroborating provenance in the script header: eks2 = 10 builds ~23m (~2.3 min avg);
  07-28 whole battery = 21 builds / 13m24s (~38s avg — but that was a 6-suite focused
  set; the set has since grown ~6x, which is why per-batch cost has drifted to minutes).
- A whole-battery run today = 68 distinct batches + baseline ≈ 69 builds ≈ 3.5-4.5 hours.
  Nobody has paid that price since 07-28 (35 entries); the array has since tripled.

Standalone SwiftPM probe (macOS, no app build, no simulator) — built at
`<scratchpad>/fastprobe`, copies of production files, verbatim test-suite extracts:
- Cold `swift test` from empty .build: 13.7s. Disk: .build = 108 MB (vs ~8 GB gate).
- Warm no-change `swift test`: 2.3-2.6s.
- FULL MUTATION CYCLE — applied the battery's OWN K01 and Q08 edits (byte-identical
  anchors from `apply_mutation`) to the kernel copies, `swift test`, read verdicts:
  3.1s, and the exact expected display names went red:
    K01 → "LOW DATA MODE WINS ON CELLULAR too …" + "Low Data Mode outranks …" FAILED
    Q08 → "the drain stops CONSECUTIVELY, not on a lifetime tally" FAILED
  Restore + green re-verify: 2.3s. These are genuine KILLs in the battery's sense.
- Final probe scope: 59 tests / 8 suites pass in 5.1s wall including recompile
  (DayZeroTransportPolicy, RediffDayZeroDailyBudget, RediffDayZeroKickoffOutcome,
  RediffDayZeroKickoffOrdering, RediffDayZeroKickoffCoordinator, AutoSkipEdgePaddingPolicy,
  FMDaemonThrottleClassification, FMThrottleUsabilityProbe).
- Swift Testing output format is IDENTICAL to xcodebuild's (`◇ Test "…" started`,
  `✘ Test "…" failed`), so `extract_failures`/`extract_ran` in mutation-battery.sh work
  on swift-test logs UNCHANGED. Vacuity discipline ports for free.

Per-rail: ~227s → ~3-5s = 45-75x for rails that fit. Per whole battery: ~2 builds saved
(batches 68, 69 are the only all-movable batches) ≈ 3%.

## INVENTORY — which of the 119 rails could move (list, not vibes)

Method: parsed `--list` (120 records, 119 unique — see defects below), mapped every
expected display name to its defining @Suite, classified each suite by what it
instantiates, then applied the JOINT criterion: a rail moves only if (a) the MUTATED file
compiles standalone AND (b) EVERY expected test's suite compiles standalone.

PROVEN MOVABLE, 12/119 (compiled + ran in the probe; K01/Q08 additionally kill-verified):
- K01 K04 K05 K06 (RediffDayZeroBandwidthPolicy.swift → transport-policy/budget suites)
- K09 K10 K11     (RediffDayZeroKickoff.swift → outcome/ordering/coordinator suites)
- K12 K13 K14     (RediffDayZeroKickoffCoordinator.swift → coordinator suite)
- Q07             (FoundationModelsUsabilityProbe.swift → usability-probe suite;
                   FoundationModels imports cleanly on the macOS 27 SDK)
- Q08             (FMDaemonThrottle.swift → classification suite)

MOVABLE WITH SMALL SPLITS, +5 → 17/119:
- K20 K21 K22: judging suite (DayZeroFetchTransportTests) is pure, but
  RediffRefetchSeams.swift also references RediffRefetchService/AdDetectionService/
  AVFoundation → the URLSession sampler/fetcher types need their own file (same module,
  no semantic change; xcodegen globs pick it up automatically).
- K02 K03: SPLIT rails — one expectation pure (policy suite), one app-bound
  (DayZeroTriggerTransportBudgetTests uses RediffRefetchService; TransportSettingTests
  uses UserPreferencesSnapshot, which lives in DownloadManager.swift ~3.9k lines). Moving
  them means splitting each into a fast entry + an app entry. Legitimate, but bookkeeping.

NOT MOVABLE, 102/119 (86%) — and RIGHTLY so:
- All M/N/S/O/P (17+6+7+5+2): mutate SkipOrchestrator/AnalysisStore; judged by
  orchestrator race/learning suites that instantiate SkipOrchestrator + AnalysisStore.
- All D + E (13+7): mutate SkipOrchestrator/AdBannerView/DayZeroRediffTrigger/
  RediffRefetchService; entry-gate + delivery suites are app-bound. (Suites like
  SuggestBannerEntryGateSecondPassTests grep "pure" but the mutated file is the 6,426-line
  orchestrator — joint criterion fails.)
- All J (18): the classifier statics ARE pure, but every SkipModeResolution* suite drives
  them through makeOrchestrator()/PlayheadRuntime/NowPlayingViewModel. Moving the rails
  would mean re-judging them by unit restatements — exactly the "restatement of the
  emitted literal" the battery header warns against.
- All L/V (10+6): AdPodContinuation.swift is pure-ish (CryptoKit+Foundation) but the
  suites go through AdDetectionService/runBackfill/AnalysisStore — deliberately (evc1's
  admission sweep, the wire-in tests).
- Q01-Q06: BackfillJobRunner/FoundationModelClassifier rails; runner + permissive-lane
  suites build BackfillJobRunner + AnalysisStore.
- K07 K08 (readiness-wait suite reads PlayheadRuntime constants), K15-K19 (trigger/store
  suites use RediffRefetchService/AnalysisStore).

## DEPENDENCY CREEP, MEASURED (the honest cost of "just compile the files")

The kernel converged at 12 production files + 3 type shims + 2 test shims. Total probe
content: ~4,100 lines. Creep chain actually hit, in order:
1. RediffDayZeroBandwidthPolicy → TransportSnapshot (lives in AdmissionGate.swift).
2. FMDaemonThrottle → SemanticScanStatus.swift → FMInferenceTimeoutError
   (FMInferenceDeadline.swift, 477 lines — came along cleanly).
3. AutoSkipEdgePaddingPolicyTests → AdWindow — which is defined INSIDE the 20,100-line
   AnalysisStore.swift. Extractable (lines 337-502, stringly-typed, Sendable) EXCEPT its
   `hasCompatibleCatalogMatchProvenance` helper, which reaches AdCatalogStore/
   CatalogLearningSource/CatalogLearningLifecycle/RecurrenceMaterialIdentity. The struct
   is clean; one method drags in the catalog subsystem.
4. RediffDayZeroKickoff/Coordinator → InvariantViolation — defined inside
   SurfaceStatusInvariants.swift, whose OTHER contents drag EpisodeSurfaceStatus/
   CoverageSummary/PlaybackReadiness. The one struct extracts cleanly (lines 343-481).
5. Test side: FMDaemonThrottleClassificationTests needs TestFMRuntimeFailure, which lives
   in PlayheadTests/Helpers/TestFMRuntime.swift NEXT TO app-coupled fixtures
   (FoundationModelClassifier, BackfillJobRunner) — the enum itself is clean (lines
   231-282); DayZeroProbeCounter sits between suites inside DayZeroDownloadTimeTests.swift.
Pattern: the pure LOGIC is pure, but pure TYPES are physically trapped inside monolith
files. Every shim is a copy that can silently diverge — the worst drift class (a stale
AdWindow shim = testing a phantom, failing in the direction that reads as success).

## RECOMMENDED MECHANISM (if Dan wants it)

Smallest viable, mirroring the R-series precedent the script header already blesses
("same discipline, same vocabulary" sibling runner per judging toolchain):

1. FILE MOVES, not module moves, to kill the shim risk: move AdWindow, TransportSnapshot,
   InvariantViolation (and the seams URLSession types if K20-22 are wanted) into their own
   files IN THE SAME TARGET. No access-level changes, no behavior change, no project.yml
   edit (sources are directory-globbed). Likewise split the 3 mixed test files so pure
   suites/helpers live in their own files (TestFMRuntimeFailure, DayZeroProbeCounter,
   already-pure suites). These files remain in PlayheadTests and keep running on the gate.
2. `scripts/mutation-battery-kernel.sh` (or a `LANE=kernel` column): owns the 12-17 fast
   rails. At run time it: applies the mutation to the REAL production file (same patcher,
   same anchors), copies the MANIFEST files verbatim into a generated SwiftPM package
   under /private/tmp/playhead-* (auto-swept by disk-cleanup), runs `swift test`, judges
   with the SAME extract_failures/extract_ran (glyphs identical), restores. Copies are
   byte-identical by construction on every run — no checked-in duplicate of any source.
3. Compile failure of the kernel = ERROR, loud. A file that grows an app-bound dependency
   breaks the fast lane toward red, not toward false-green. That is the right failure
   direction and the manifest's built-in drift alarm.
4. The moved rails' suites STAY in PlayheadTests and STAY in FOCUSED_SUITES — the gate
   loses zero coverage; periodic whole-battery certification can still run everything
   through xcodebuild if wanted.

## REJECTED MECHANISMS

- New SPM package / framework target holding the pure types, app depends on it: forces
  public/access-level churn on every moved symbol, changes what `@testable import
  Playhead` reaches, touches project.yml + pbxproj (documented cross-worktree conflict
  pain), and is an architecture change requiring explicit approval — all to serve 12-17
  rails. Cost/benefit fails today. Revisit only if the pure-rail population grows severalfold.
- Second Xcode unit-test target linking a file subset: still xcodebuild + simulator;
  saves maybe half the 227s, not 98% of it. Adds a target-membership drift list with weak
  payoff.
- Bare `swiftc` harness without SwiftPM: same speed as `swift test`, worse ergonomics
  (hand-rolled Testing plugin flags), no gain.
- Speeding up the 86%: no honest lever found. Batching is already near the false-KILL
  boundary; each batch is inherently one distinct binary. (Catalyst-host execution might
  shave simulator overhead but not build time — not pursued.)

## RISKS — including the ones that argue against doing it

- TWO PLACES TO LOOK. A second runner + manifest is a new drift surface in the repo's
  recurring defect class. Mitigations are real (loud compile failure; no checked-in
  copies; same verdict vocabulary) but the surface exists. If nobody authors pure-policy
  beads for a quarter, the lane rots.
- PLATFORM DELTA: kernel judges on macOS, product ships iOS. For Foundation-only decision
  logic the delta is ~nil, and the same tests still run on the sim in every gate run; but
  a rail whose semantics ever grow an #if os branch must move back. State it in the
  runner header.
- THE 86% IS UNTOUCHED. Dan's felt pain ("10-30 builds per bead") mostly comes from
  orchestrator/store beads (djl0: 0 of 18 rails movable; eks2: 0 of 9). This tool does
  NOT fix those beads. It fixes 4dqe-class beads (10-13 of 22 rails) and makes future
  pure-rail additions ~free.
- TEMPTATION RISK: the fast lane makes it cheap to author unit-restatement rails instead
  of behavioral ones. The convention must stay: if the defect's OBSERVABLE harm is in app
  behavior, the rail belongs in the gate lane even when the mutated file is pure. The
  policy-suite/wiring-suite file convention (AutoSkipEdgePaddingTests) is the template.
- If the verdict on the above is "not worth a second lane", a strictly smaller fallback
  still captures most authoring value: keep the probe harness as a dev-only tool (not a
  certifying lane), used to pre-screen new pure rails before spending builds.

## LATENT BATTERY DEFECTS FOUND WHILE COUNTING (fix regardless; ~30 min)

1. DUPLICATE L09: `"L09|61|PODC|$T_EKS2_ENTRY_ONCE"` appears a second time (stray line
   after V06). A `--batch 61` re-run will apply L09, then fail its second anchor
   application and ERROR the whole batch. 120 records, 119 unique.
2. BATCH-ID COLLISION V vs Q: evc1 used batches 62-67 (V01-V06); kvs8 then also used
   62-69 (Q01-Q08). Batches 62-67 each now hold one V and one Q entry, silently violating
   BOTH series' written "one mutation per batch, deliberately" notes. Victims are disjoint
   (different suites) so past verdicts stand, but one rotten anchor now takes down the
   other series' entry, and any per-batch rerun runs more than its author intended.
3. kvs8 added 8 entries with NO provenance recount in the header (last recount: 111;
   actual live: 119 unique) — the exact "figure already wrong when written" failure the
   header warns about in its own first provenance paragraph.
4. describe_mutation returns "(no description)" for J01-J18 in `--list` (cosmetic).

## ARTIFACTS

- Probe package (temporary, scratchpad):
  /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-dabrams-playhead/bee44b12-4e4b-4bbd-ada7-8d211ef3d4e6/scratchpad/fastprobe
- Measured against: scripts/mutation-battery.sh @ a6c9987b (120 records, 68 batches);
  .derivedData/Logs/Build/LogStoreManifest.plist (227.4s focused run, 08-01 14:43).
- Classification method: display-name → @Suite → instantiation scan; joint criterion
  (mutated file AND all judging suites standalone-compilable).

COST EXCEEDS VALUE, by its own measurement: 12 of 119 rails movable, ~3% whole-battery saving, and playhead-4t4j explicitly rejects it ('Not the fix for this'). Its four latent battery defects are preserved on 4t4j — two re-verified live today: duplicate rail id L09|61 at mutation-battery.sh:3334 AND :3378, and the V/Q batch-id collision (V01-V06 and Q01-Q06 both on batches 62-67).

title: fast-gate must refuse to start below the disk headroom it needs, and stop the silent wedge
description:
Filed 2026-08-01 after FOUR disk rescues in one day, every one caught by luck rather than by the
tooling: 117 MB, 1.3 GB, 2.4 GB, and one near-miss. Each was found only because Dan happened to
ask for status at the right moment. The next one will not be.

## The measurement (playhead-voez, #322, measured across three runs)

A full-plan gate is a **transient** disk event, not a steady one: the destination simulator grows
from **~3.7 GB to ~9 GB** during the Swift Testing bulk and shrinks back afterwards. On top of the
~2.7 GB `.derivedData` per worktree that CLAUDE.md already accounts for.

  * starting with ~13 GB free -> finished
  * starting with ~10 GB free -> hit 100% capacity and **WEDGED**

**The wedge is the dangerous part: xcodebuild stayed alive with zero output for four minutes,
having failed to write its result bundle. It presents as a HANG, not as an error.** No POSIX 28,
no non-zero exit, nothing in the log. Exactly the silent-failure class this whole arc has been
about — a resource failure wearing the costume of a slow test.

Also measured: `.derivedData/Logs/Test/*.xcresult` accumulates **~100 MB per run** and nothing
prunes it.

## Why hand-catching does not work

Two agents each hold ~2.7 GB of derivedData and neither reclaims until its bead CLOSES. A
mutation battery is one build per batch, so a bead can run 10-30 builds over hours while its
worktree grows monotonically. Free space therefore goes from comfortable to critical inside an
hour with no event to trigger on. Today I reclaimed by deleting an idle worktree's derivedData
mid-run each time — that works, but only because someone was watching.

## Work

**1. Preflight in `scripts/fast-gate.sh`: REFUSE to start below a threshold.**
Roughly 8 GB, derived from the measurement above rather than guessed — state the derivation in a
comment so the number can be re-derived when the suite grows. The refusal must be LOUD and must
name what to do about it. A gate that declines to start is strictly better than one that wedges
silently for four minutes and then lies.

Include `PLAYHEAD_SKIP_DISK_PREFLIGHT=1` for the rare deliberate override, but do NOT make it easy
or advertise it in the failure message — the same reasoning as `PLAYHEAD_SKIP_BASELINE=1`.

**2. Prune `.xcresult` bundles.** ~100 MB per run, unbounded. Keep the most recent (it is what
gets inspected after a failure) and delete older ones at gate start. Cheap, safe, entirely
mechanical.

**3. Detect the wedge and say so.** If the run produces no output for N minutes AND free space is
near zero, kill it and report `WEDGED — out of disk`, not a timeout. Distinguishing "the box ran
out of room" from "the test is slow" is the whole point; today they are indistinguishable and one
of them wasted four minutes plus the diagnosis.

**4. Reclaim DURING a long run, not only at bead close.** The current sequence only frees
derivedData when a worktree is removed. Options to weigh:
   * a sweep at gate start that removes `.derivedData` from worktrees with NO live build (check
     `lsof`/`pgrep` before touching anything — never delete under a running gate)
   * prune xcresults from all worktrees, not just this one
   * document a `scripts/disk-cleanup.sh --aggressive` mode and call it from the preflight when
     below the threshold but above a hard floor, so the gate self-heals once rather than refusing

Prefer self-healing once, then refusing. A tool that fixes it silently every time hides a real
capacity problem.

## Constraints — these are the ways to get this wrong

- **NEVER `rm` a booted simulator's directory.** Reclaim via `simctl shutdown` then `simctl erase`
  (needs `DEVELOPER_DIR`). The 11 GB device on this box IS the one the gate boots.
- **Never delete a `.derivedData` under a live build.** Resolve the running build's cwd (`lsof -a
  -p <pid> -d cwd`) and skip it. Today's rescues did this by hand; the script must do it.
- The existing `rm -rf` safety rails in CLAUDE.md apply: path must be under `.worktrees/` or
  `/private/tmp/playhead-`, must not appear in `git worktree list --porcelain`, and every removal
  must be echoed so the transcript audits it.
- `scripts/disk-cleanup.sh` already exists and runs weekly via cron — extend it rather than
  writing a second cleaner, or the two will drift.

## Acceptance

Start a gate with ~5 GB free: it refuses, loudly, naming the number and the remedy. Start with
~13 GB: it runs. Run three gates in a row without a bead closing: xcresults do not accumulate.
And the wedge case, if it can be provoked safely, reports as a disk failure rather than a hang.
notes:
## QUEUE 2 — Dan 2026-08-02, picked by a fable prioritization agent

    3nfa -> le02 -> bllt -> ug9m -> pggn -> kkzu

**The bet: skip-admission CORRECTNESS over width work.** nqey (#331) shipped
certaintyTieredSkipEnabled ON, so every eligibility defect is now live on the next build Dan
installs — and avbn's A11 mutant proved the suite currently CANNOT see a must-drop span routed to
the suggest tier. A wrong skip eats show, which is the one audible event worse than an ad.
Width work (4xqf/z5ly/uorw) is deferred: 4xqf's own 07-30 re-measurement inverted its premise
(61% of slots are TOTAL MISSES, not narrow) and sequences width behind field-verified candidate
coverage, which needs a device.

ORDERING CONSTRAINTS (not arbitrary):
  * 3nfa STRICTLY FIRST — every other bead ends in a full gate on a box that hit 100% capacity
    four times in one day and presented it as a silent hang. Insurance before the trip.
  * le02 BEFORE bllt/ug9m — d3g0 made banner emission deferred, so a suite written to catch
    "must-drop span surfaced" is green by construction. Fix the instrument before operating on
    what it measures, or beads 3-5 inherit the blind spot.
  * bllt BEFORE ug9m — bllt NARROWS (unanchored hot-path rows demote), ug9m WIDENS (rescues
    trapped day-0 marks). Narrow first so anything the rescue gets wrong is still demoted at the
    last mile rather than skipping show.
  * pggn is the width/quality slot and unblocks 8x59 (Dan's decided calibration).
  * kkzu is least coupled — the drop if the budget dies at five.

CONSTRAINT: Dan is away ~13h and cannot install a build or produce a device pull. No bead here
may need field data. The newest DB is 2026-07-21 with zero .rediffSlot spans and an
episodeDurationSec that contradicts its own rows.

One at a time. Full gate + mutation battery each.

title: voez steps 2+3: decide the PerfGate question per family with isolated pass rates, and arm the pass-direction check
description:
Carries forward steps 2 and 3 of [[playhead-voez]], which CLOSED with only step 1 shipped (#322).
Step 1 was deliberately the thing that makes this cheap and safe; without this follow-up the gate
stays permanently RED-with-41-known and the underlying coverage question is never answered.

## What step 1 already bought

`scripts/gate-baseline.PlayheadFastTests.json` now records, per test, `seen_runs` / `failed_runs`
and the failure KIND. So the question "is this family a coverage asset or a harness artifact?" is
now answerable from data instead of judgement.

And PerfGate-ing a family is now SAFE to attempt: a baseline member that stops running surfaces as
`DID NOT RUN` and fails the gate, demanding an explicit `--accept-baseline` with a justification
in the commit message — rather than silently shrinking coverage, which is what made this decision
scary enough to defer in the first place.

## Step 2 — decide per family, with data

The failures cluster in a small number of files (measured 2026-07-29):

    10  SilenceCompressionCoordinatorTests
    10  BackgroundProcessingServiceTests
    10  AnalysisPipelineStallInvariantHarnessIntegrationTests
     6  BackgroundProcessingServiceTelemetryTests
     4  BackgroundProcessingServiceLedgerTests
     3  InterruptionHandlingTests
     3  BackgroundFeedRefreshServiceTests
     1  SettingsViewTests

For each, get an ISOLATED pass rate (run the file alone, N times, quiet box) and compare with its
in-gate rate from the baseline file.

  * passes ~N/N isolated, fails ~N/N in the full gate  -> **harness artifact.** PerfGate-ing it
    loses nothing real: it is not testing a behaviour, it is testing whether the box was busy.
  * fails in isolation too                             -> a REAL defect hiding in the noise. Fix it.
  * mixed                                              -> a genuine race worth understanding before
    either.

**That reframes Dan's deferred call as eight small evidenced decisions rather than one big blind
one**, which is exactly why he deferred it.

## Step 3 — only then, fix or gate individual tests

Do not start here.

## DO NOT

- Do not add sleeps or retries to make these pass. The bead voez inherited says so explicitly and
  it remains true: a masked flake is worse than a named one.
- Do not delete tests. They test real behaviours (thermal/BGTask/interruption paths that have
  produced genuine field bugs — see playhead-ewag, playhead-qk44).
- Do not PerfGate a family without the isolated measurement. The whole point is that this stops
  being a guess.

## Immediate, unrelated to the above: ARM THE PASS-DIRECTION CHECK

Dan decided the baseline is EXACT, not a ceiling — a known-failing test that starts PASSING must
fail the gate. That arm is implemented and rail-tested (R03) but **inert**: promotion to
"deterministic" needs 3 observations and the shipped file has 2 (a measured Jaccard of 0.46
between runs made 2 unsafe). **One more `scripts/fast-gate.sh --accept-baseline` on a QUIET box
arms it.** Do that when nothing else is running — it is a single gate run, not a project.

Expect the file to GROW on that accept: capture-recapture estimates ~47 true members against 41
recorded, so a handful of names will be reported NEW and then absorbed. That is the mechanism
working, and CLAUDE.md documents it so it is not misread as regressions.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
PROMOTED P2 -> P1 on 2026-08-11 after THREE merge gates in one day came back RED for reasons unrelated to their diffs. This is no longer a tidiness bead; the default plan's verdict on a merge candidate now carries almost no information, and I merged three times on the scoped re-run instead.

THE EVIDENCE, three independent runs on a deliberately quiet box (sim erased, 26-37 GiB free, nothing else building):

  bead   verdict                        failures  under 97s  XCTest  scoped re-run
  15d0   RED (69 known / 11 NEW)        97        0          0       52 tests / 6 suites in 3.4 s, all pass
  kg8h   RED (69 known / 7 NEW + 2 DNR) 95        0          0       52 tests / 6 suites in 3.4 s, all pass
  3zxd   RED (58 known / 8 NEW + 4 DNR) 83        0          0       46 tests / 6 suites in 1.951 s, all pass

ZERO failures under 97 seconds across all three runs — not one expectation failure in 275 failures total. Every single one is a blown time limit. Individually those tests take 1.2-1.8 s scoped and 130-147 s under full-plan load: two orders of magnitude.

THE FAILING SET ROTATES, which is the 0.46 Jaccard the CLAUDE.md baseline section already documents. 15d0 hit AnalysisWorkSchedulerLaneGate / BoundedContinuation / TranscriptEngineCoverageOrdering; 3zxd hit SkipOrchestratorRevertLifecycleRace / ShadowRetry / BackfillExpiryDurability. Little overlap. So the baseline cannot converge by accumulation — each run surfaces a different sample of the same starved population.

THE DANGEROUS HALF IS 'DID NOT RUN', NOT 'NEW FAILURE'. kg8h had 2, 3zxd had 4. A recorded test that is never reached is indistinguishable from one that was deleted or renamed, and the baseline treats it as unforgivable — correctly, since a name nobody can reach is not evidence. Tonight they were starvation casualties, but the MECHANISM CANNOT TELL, and that is the failure mode this bead prevents.

A SECOND HAZARD THAT MAKES TRIAGE COSTLIER THAN IT LOOKS: on 3zxd, four of the twelve failing tests live in structs whose names differ from their FILE names (teardown cancelled mid-settle is in BackfillExpiryDurabilityTests, not BackgroundGrantBudgetTests; the download ones are in DelegateWorkJournalTests and EpisodeDownloadDelegateResumeHarvestTests). A -only-testing: target that names a file is SILENTLY SKIPPED and the run still reports TEST SUCCEEDED. Resolving them requires parsing the test files for the enclosing @Suite struct. That is per-incident work that a PerfGate would make unnecessary.

WHAT THIS BEAD SHOULD NOW DO, per its own step 2: PerfGate the load-sensitive families out of PlayheadFastTests and into the serial PlayheadPerfTests pass, so the default plan's RED means something again. The families are identifiable from these three logs plus the committed baseline. CLAUDE.md already records this as 'a coverage tradeoff for Dan's call' — three data points in one day is the argument for making that call.

CAUTION FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: moving a test out of the default plan SHRINKS COVERAGE, and the baseline check will report every moved test as DID NOT RUN until the baseline is refreshed. That is the mechanism working, not a regression — but it means this bead's own gate run needs --accept-baseline WITH the diff justified in the commit message, which is the one sanctioned use.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
STEP 2's DATA, MEASURED 2026-08-13 ACROSS 61 PRESERVED FULL-PLAN LOGS — and Dan has approved acting on it ("ok, do that plan" / "Begin doing it that way immediately", 2026-08-13).

THE HEADLINE NUMBER: 649 NEW failures reported across those 61 runs. Essentially NONE were real.

Only 8 of the 61 logs contain a single Swift Testing failure under 97 s OR any XCTest failure — and most of those 8 are deliberate mutant runs, controls, or probes, where the failure IS the intended result (fzrw's gate-full-CONTROL, run4-mutACB, probe-run1, 3zxd's g1-prefix). Every other one of the 649 was a `Time limit was exceeded: 60.000 seconds` reported at 150-200 s wall clock.

THE RECURRING NAMES, which is what step 2 asked for:

    19  recovery's work-deadline return does not strand the job it leaves running
    16  the default floor is zero, so non-grant callers are unchanged
    15  recovery's teardown cancelled mid-settle leaves the ending to the expiration handler
    15  a pass IS started when the remaining grant clears the checkpoint floor
    14  engine does not emit .completed until finishAppending is called
    14  control: a genuine mid-run cancel still spends an attempt and still supersedes
    14  an expired background window leaves the job queued and spends no attempt
    13  The reschedule latch is released on the timeout path
    13  Test F: observer waits 60s of stable FM=true before draining; cancels on flip
    13  H2: wake() drains immediately when capability is already stable-true
    10  the work-deadline return does not strand the job it leaves running
     9  an expired run's completion count is measured, not a literal zero

SUITES: BackfillSchedulerBounding, BackgroundGrantBudget, TranscriptEngine, ShadowRetry, DrainEligibleStartGate, SpeechModelLoad. NOTE these are DIFFERENT from the 2026-07-29 cluster this bead recorded (SilenceCompressionCoordinator, BackgroundProcessingService*, AnalysisPipelineStallInvariantHarness, InterruptionHandling). The population has MOVED. Re-measure before PerfGate-ing rather than trusting either list — that drift is itself evidence these tests track the box rather than the code.

THE ARGUMENT FOR PERFGATE-ING THEM, stated as the defect class this repo already names: each asserts an ABSOLUTE wall-clock budget (a 60 s time limit) while running inside a plan that saturates a 16 GB box with ~8,000 concurrent tests. So the quantity they measure is machine load; the quantity they are read as measuring is code correctness. A value that names one thing read as though it named another — the standing defect class, in the harness rather than the product.

WHAT THIS IS NOT: it is not an argument that the behaviours are unimportant. Selectively re-run, these same tests pass in 2-9 s (measured repeatedly today: 117 tests/10 suites in 8.6 s, 188/10 in 7.2 s, 74/11 in 4.4 s). They test real things. They cannot test them under a load that makes every timing assertion meaningless. Moving them to the serial PlayheadPerfTests pass makes them MEANINGFUL for the first time, and makes the gate's NEW column trustworthy for the first time.

COST OF THE STATUS QUO, since this bead has been open since 08-01: every red gate needs a human or agent to triage both failure formats, check every duration against 97 s, and read the `Failing tests:` summary block. That is a decision point on every review round of every bead, and today it produced 649 judgements with no defects behind them.

Step 1's safety net (a PerfGate'd baseline member surfaces as DID NOT RUN and hard-fails, demanding an explicit --accept-baseline with justification) is exactly what makes this safe to do now.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
THE DRIFT IS THE PROOF — pulling this out of the paragraph above because it is the single strongest argument in this bead, and because it changes HOW step 2 should be done.

TWO MEASUREMENTS, FIFTEEN DAYS APART, ON CODE THAT DID NOT CHANGE IN THESE SUITES:

  2026-07-29 (recorded in this bead's own description)
      SilenceCompressionCoordinatorTests                        10
      BackgroundProcessingServiceTests                          10
      AnalysisPipelineStallInvariantHarnessIntegrationTests      10
      BackgroundProcessingServiceTelemetryTests                   6
      BackgroundProcessingServiceLedgerTests                      4
      InterruptionHandlingTests                                   3

  2026-08-13 (61 preserved full-plan logs)
      BackfillSchedulerBoundingTests
      BackgroundGrantBudgetTests
      TranscriptEngineTests
      ShadowRetryTests
      DrainEligibleStartGateTests
      SpeechModelLoadBoundTests

NEAR-DISJOINT. Not one name in common. Nobody rewrote these suites between those dates; what changed is what else was running beside them and how loaded the box was.

WHY THAT SETTLES THE QUESTION. A test whose failing set changes while its code does not is not reporting on its code. Every one of these asserts an ABSOLUTE wall-clock budget (a 60 s time limit) inside a run that saturates a 16 GB box with ~8,000 concurrent tests, so what it actually measures is contention. Run selectively the same tests pass in 2-9 s. This is the repo's standing defect class — a value that names one thing read as though it named another — sitting in the harness rather than the product, which is exactly why it went unexamined for so long.

THE CONSEQUENCE FOR HOW TO DO THIS BEAD, and it is the actionable part:

**Do NOT PerfGate from a list of suite names.** Both lists above were accurate when measured and both are now misleading. A name-based selection is stale the moment the box's load profile shifts, and it leaves the next generation of offenders unhandled while carrying dead entries for suites that no longer fire.

**Select by the PROPERTY instead.** The population is "a test that asserts an absolute wall-clock budget while the plan runs it concurrently" — which is mechanically identifiable: a `.timeLimit(...)` trait, or an assertion on elapsed time, in a test that is not already `PerfGate`d. That predicate is durable across load changes in a way a name list can never be, and it can be enforced by a source canary so a NEW timing-sensitive test cannot be added to the concurrent plan without someone deciding to.

If a name list is used anyway for the first pass, re-measure it on the day rather than trusting either list here — and say in the commit which measurement it came from, because the next reader will otherwise inherit a third stale list.

A SECOND-ORDER POINT WORTH KEEPING: this drift also means the baseline's own churn figure (Jaccard 0.46, recorded in CLAUDE.md) understates the problem. That number compares two runs days apart; across fifteen days the overlap in the FAILING SUITE SET is approximately zero. The baseline is not converging on a stable known-broken set because there is no stable set to converge on.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
STEP 2 IS DONE, MEASURED 2026-08-13. The headline: 135 of 136 are harness artifacts, 1 is a
benchmark that has never been readable, and the population is roughly 3x larger than anything
that has ever been observed — which is what settles what step 3 can and cannot be.

## How the population was built (not from either stale name list)

Union of the committed baseline (117 names / 9 runs) and the two preserved full-plan logs of
2026-08-13 = **136 tests in 52 suites**. Every name was resolved to its enclosing @Suite struct
by parsing the tree with brace-depth tracking: **41 of the 52 struct names differ from their
file name**, and a -only-testing: target that names a file is silently skipped while still
reporting TEST SUCCEEDED. All 52 targets were verified to actually run (0 DID NOT RUN).

## The measurement

    443 tests / 52 suites, scoped, quiet box, N=5:  27.9 s per run
    135 of 136 pass 5/5.   1 of 136 fails 5/5.

Against in-gate rates from the baseline of 12 % to 100 %. Full per-suite table is in the bead
branch's commit messages; the short version is that every family the two stale lists named —
SilenceCompressionCoordinator (10/10), BackgroundProcessingService*, AnalysisPipelineStall*,
InterruptionHandling, RouteChange, BackfillSchedulerBounding, BackgroundGrantBudget,
TranscriptEngine, ShadowRetry, DrainEligibleStartGate, SpeechModelLoad — passes 5/5 isolated.

## Three things the measurement changed my mind about

**1. "Asserts a wall-clock budget" over-selects by 5x and mis-names the mechanism.**
Mechanically there are 774 tests subject to some absolute wall-clock deadline (499 with a
.timeLimit trait, 220 with a timeout-bearing waiter, 176 measuring elapsed time). But
CPU-BOUND budget assertions PASS under the full plan — AnalysisEligibilityPerformanceTests
asserts <200 ms and passes; ChapterBoundaryDetectorPerfTests asserts 200 ms and passes;
PerformanceSmokeTests asserts <5 s and passes. What fails is **scheduler-dependent waiting**
measured on an absolute clock: a poll loop, an AsyncStream consumer, a cross-actor callback.
That is the property, and it is sharper than the one in the bead.

**2. "passed after N seconds" is not test cost, and the 97 s triage rule reads it as if it
were.** 82–89 % of PASSING tests in a full-plan run report over 60 s; the median is ~150 s;
291 tests that carry a .timeLimit(.minutes(1)) PASSED while reporting 151–198 s. The number is
enqueue-to-completion. Proof from a single test that reports its own internal measurement:
benchmarkGate reported 220.1 s while its own ContinuousClock read 105.5 s. So a failure's
reported duration selects tests that failed EARLY in the run, not tests that failed for
behavioural reasons.

**3. The baseline union will NOT saturate, and the ~47 estimate in CLAUDE.md is ~8x low.**
New names per accepted run: 32, 41, 69, 73, 73, 81, 81, 83, 117, then +10 and +9 from the two
gpdb logs. Still climbing ~9–10 per run after eleven runs. Chao1 on the baseline's own failure-
frequency spectrum (f1=51 names failed in exactly 1 run, f2=5 in exactly 2) gives a lower bound
of **377**, against 136 ever observed. 390 tests carry a 60 s time limit, which is where 377
lands. So the recorded set is a ~35 % sample of a population that a name list cannot bound.

## What this means for step 3 — and the part that is Dan's

Moving the 136 measured names would remove ~58 of a typical run's ~68 failures and leave the
next run to surface ~10 fresh ones, forever. It does not make the gate green; it makes it less
red while costing 136 tests of default coverage and needing re-measurement every few weeks.

Landed in this bead (needs no coverage call, licensed by the measurement):
  * PerfGate for the two tests whose wall-clock quantity IS the assertion — the one
    sub-property that does not rotate, because a benchmark is a benchmark on any box.
    Enumerated mechanically: 16 such tests, 11 measured CPU-bound and passing, 3 already
    gated, exactly 2 in the load-sensitive population. Both registered in MEASUREMENT_TESTS.

Still open, and genuinely a call rather than a measurement:
  A. PerfGate the measured 136. Costs 136 tests of default coverage; leaves ~10 failures/run.
  B. PerfGate the whole property (~390–774). Makes the gate green; moves 3–7 % of the suite
     into a serial pass that no gate currently runs.
  C. Class-based tolerance in gate_baseline.py: a timeout-kind failure in a test that carries
     a wall-clock deadline is absorbed as a KNOWN CLASS rather than reported NEW. Costs zero
     coverage and kills the 649 judgements outright, but widens voez's tolerance from "names
     already recorded" to "the property", which is a change to the contract Dan set.

title: semantic_scan_results has no timestamp or scene phase — FM throughput cannot be split foreground vs background
description:
Filed from playhead-kvs8's report, 2026-08-01. Blocks a measurement we keep needing and cannot make.

## The gap

`semantic_scan_results` persists 22 columns and **not one of them is a timestamp**. No `createdAt`,
no scene phase, no run id. `background_task_runs` has `scenePhase` + `startedAt`/`finishedAt` but
there is no join key to scan rows.

## What that makes impossible

- **Splitting FM throughput foreground vs background.** kvs8 was asked to re-measure the 2.4x
  slower-than-realtime figure split by phase and could not: the data to attribute a scan row to a
  phase does not exist. That split matters because it decides whether background FM is viable at
  all, or whether FM work should only ever be scheduled in the foreground.
- **Measuring the effect of any scheduling change.** Every future bead that alters WHEN FM runs is
  unmeasurable against history for the same reason.
- **Reconstructing a stall timeline.** During the 2026-07-31/08-01 investigation the only reason
  the 23-minute silent `running` window could be dated at all was `backfill_jobs.updatedAt`; the
  scan rows themselves were undateable.

## Work

Add to `semantic_scan_results`: a creation timestamp, the scene phase at completion, and a run/job
correlation id joinable to `backfill_jobs` / `background_task_runs`. Schema is at V41 after
playhead-4dqe, so this is V42.

Additive only — no backfill of historical rows (they are genuinely unattributable, and inventing a
value for them would be exactly the defect this repo keeps hitting). Rows written before the
migration should read as NULL/unknown and every consumer must treat unknown as unknown rather than
defaulting it to a phase.

## Why it is worth its own bead

This is measurement infrastructure, not a fix. It has no user-visible effect and will feel like it
can always wait — but it is the reason two separate investigations produced "cannot be determined
from device data". See [[feedback_ask_what_the_quantity_measures_2026-07-29]]: the recurring failure
here is a number nobody can attribute, and the remedy is to record the attribution at write time.
## QUEUE — Dan 2026-08-01, the mid-roll program

Position **6 of 6**:

    isp5 -> y3ya -> lxkq -> gard -> mptr -> hx6n

**Rides with lxkq — without a timestamp on scan rows the targeting change is unmeasurable, and two investigations have already ended in 'cannot be determined from device data'.**

title: The download path drops podcastId, so analysis_jobs.podcastId is NULL for every background/auto download
description:
Found while root-causing [[playhead-djl0]] on 2026-08-01. This is the asymmetry djl0's
bead noted ("for OTHER assets the podcastId IS recorded... D9B513CD has neither"), with
the cause identified.

## The mechanism, end to end

`analysis_jobs.podcastId` is written by exactly one function,
`AnalysisWorkScheduler.enqueue(episodeId:podcastId:...)`. Its two production callers are
both in `DownloadManager` and both pass `context?.podcastId`:

    DownloadManager.swift:1360   scheduler.enqueue(..., podcastId: context?.podcastId, ...)
    DownloadManager.swift:2105   enqueueAnalysisIfNeeded(..., context:) -> the same

`DownloadContext` is CONSTRUCTED at exactly ONE site in the whole tree —
`PlayheadRuntime.swift:3888`, the streaming-download branch of `performPlayEpisode`.
Everywhere else `context` defaults to `nil`:

    DownloadManager.swift:1210 / :1253 / :1690   `context: DownloadContext? = nil`
    DownloadManager.swift:1672 / :3640           explicit `context: nil`
    DownloadManager.swift:2169                   `func backgroundDownload(episodeId:from:)`
                                                 — no context parameter AT ALL

`backgroundDownload` is the auto-download / prefetch / force-quit-resume entry point
(callers: `EpisodePreparationCoordinator:236`, `BackgroundFeedRefreshService:993`,
`ForceQuitResumeScan:498`). Every episode that arrives that way enqueues with
`podcastId: nil` **even when the show is perfectly well known upstream**.

`EpisodePreparationCoordinator` is the sharpest case: it RECEIVES a podcastId in its
`Request` (from `PlayheadRuntime:3600`), threads it correctly into
`enqueueUserIntentAnalysis`, and then drops it on the floor for the download half.

## Why it matters — the value that names an absence

`AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:3952` builds the range request as:

    podcastId: job.podcastId ?? ""

So a NULL column becomes an EMPTY-STRING show identity inside the analysis pipeline —
the exact defect class of the 07-29 -> 08-01 arc. Anything downstream that keys
per-show state (SponsorKnowledge, per-show trust telemetry, show-scoped priors) is
keyed on `""` for that population, silently pooling every unattributed episode into one
fake show.

## Work

1. Give `backgroundDownload` a `DownloadContext` (or at minimum a podcastId) and thread
   it from the three callers that have an Episode/Request in hand.
2. Then decide what `job.podcastId ?? ""` should be. An empty string is not a show; it
   should either fail closed or be a named absence, not a joinable key.
3. Consider whether `analysis_assets` should carry the column after all — djl0 needed it
   and had to read `analysis_jobs` instead (`AnalysisStore.fetchRecordedPodcastId`,

title: Pre-qs0d day-0 marks are permanently mark-only — .marked is terminal across generations
description:
Found while implementing playhead-96ot (2026-07-31). NOT a 96ot regression — a
pre-existing interaction between playhead-p70f's attempt policy and
playhead-qs0d's mint change. It matters RIGHT NOW because it can make the
96ot/qs0d acceptance test read as a failure on the wrong episode.

THE CHAIN.

1. `DayZeroRediffAttemptPolicy.decide` checks `record.lastExit.isRetryable`
   BEFORE the `policyGeneration` check, and `.marked.isRetryable == false`. So
   an asset day-0 has already marked is suppressed FOREVER, and deliberately
   cannot be reset by bumping `currentGeneration`. The stated reason: "the marks
   are already persisted, so a re-fetch would spend ~108 MB to mint nothing."

2. playhead-qs0d then changed what a mint PERSISTS: a strict byte-exact slot now
   carries `rediffByteExact` on both edges and `eligibilityGate = eligible`.
   Rows minted BEFORE qs0d carry `unanchored`/`unanchored` + `markOnly`.

3. `currentGeneration` is still 1 — qs0d did not bump it (and bumping would not
   help, per 1).

4. Even if day-0 did re-run, `mintByteExactDayZeroMarks` drops every unioned
   slot overlapping an existing AdWindow, so it would exit
   `.allSlotsAlreadyCovered` and mint nothing. Nothing else re-stamps the
   anchors on an existing row: day-0 rows are in
   `reconcileProtectedBoundaryStates`, so backfill neither retires nor rewrites
   them.

CONSEQUENCE. Every episode whose day-0 marks were minted by a pre-qs0d build is
PERMANENTLY mark-only. It will banner and never auto-skip, no matter how the
delivery path (playhead-96ot) behaves. The measurement in the qs0d bead —
episode DE0784D8 on the owner's clean install, "both dayZeroRediffByteExact
windows persisted startEdgeAnchor = endEdgeAnchor = unanchored" — names one such
episode by id.

IMMEDIATE IMPACT ON THE ACCEPTANCE TEST. playhead-96ot's device check is "mint
day-0 on a FIRST listen and confirm a skip fires WITHOUT relaunching". That is
only observable on an episode day-0 has NOT already marked. Re-running it on
DE0784D8 (or any episode played under the pre-qs0d build) will show a BANNER and
no skip, which looks exactly like 96ot failing.

  * Workaround for the test: use an episode with no `rediff_day_zero_attempts`
    row, i.e. one never played on a build with day-0 on.
  * Diagnostic if in doubt: `rediff_day_zero_attempts.lastExit == 'marked'` for
    the asset, plus `ad_windows.startEdgeAnchor == 'unanchored'` on rows whose
    `boundaryState == 'dayZeroRediffByteExact'`.

OPTIONS (Dan's call — each spends bandwidth or changes a documented policy):

  a) A one-shot MIGRATION that re-stamps existing `dayZeroRediffByteExact` rows.
     Costs zero bandwidth, but the STRICT/segment-recovered classification was
     not persisted, so a migration cannot tell which rows earned an anchor —
     it would either under-promote everything or promote 9s6q-recovered slots
     that qs0d deliberately withheld. Persisting the strict flag on the row
     would make this possible for FUTURE mints only.
  b) Make `.marked` retryable ACROSS generations (generation-scoped terminality)
     and bump the generation, plus relax the mint's overlap filter for
     same-provenance day-0 rows so a re-mint can replace its own earlier row.
     Correct, and costs ~108 MB per affected asset that is replayed.
  c) Accept it: only pre-qs0d episodes are affected, and the population shrinks
     to nothing as the library turns over. Document the test caveat and move on.

Not implemented here — playhead-96ot's scope is delivery, and both (a) and (b)
change a persistence/bandwidth policy that CLAUDE.md reserves for an explicit
decision.

## REVIEW ADDENDUM 2026-08-01 — the trap is wider than "pre-qs0d builds"

D9B513CD was day-0 marked 2026-08-01 03:20 **on the post-qs0d build**, and STILL lands in this
bead's trap: all 4 of its slots came out non-strict (one B-side gate-rejected, the survivor
segment-recovered), so they persisted unanchored/markOnly — and `.marked` being terminal means
day-0 will never re-attempt with different personas that might produce a STRICT outcome.
`suppressedCount` will simply grow.

So the accurate statement is: **any degraded day-0 outcome is frozen at its first attempt's
quality.** Pre-qs0d rows are the worst case (unanchored even when strict), but a post-qs0d
non-strict mint is equally permanent. The remediation options below should be evaluated
against BOTH populations — an anchor re-stamp alone fixes only the pre-qs0d half; the
non-strict half needs a bounded retry policy (e.g. one re-attempt with a fresh persona when
the first mint was wholly non-strict, under the bandwidth ledger).

Field inventory on the device right now: DE0784D8 (pre-qs0d, 2 slots) and D9B513CD (post-qs0d
non-strict, 4 slots) — every rediff-marked episode Dan owns is in one of the two populations.
## DECIDED — Dan 2026-08-01: rescue them

> "yes reacue"

Both trapped populations get remediated, not just the pre-qs0d half:
1. **Pre-qs0d rows** (unanchored despite being strict): re-stamp anchors from the persisted
   byte-exact provenance. No re-fetch needed — the geometry is already on disk.
2. **Post-qs0d non-strict rows** (frozen at their first attempt's quality): allow ONE bounded
   re-attempt with a fresh persona when the first mint was wholly non-strict, under the
   rediff_bandwidth_ledger and the new user transport setting ([[playhead-4dqe]]).

Bound it like everything else in this arc: count CONSECUTIVE re-attempts, name the refusal
reasons, and make "permanently frozen" a surfaced state rather than silence. Do not let the
rescue become an unbounded re-fetch loop — that is ~120-250 MB a time.

title: Contract conflict: acceptSuggestedSkip's markOnly refusal must AND must not reach the decision log (ynmk vs the veto source canary)
description:
Found by playhead-d3g0 while running the full gate on 2026-07-31. NOT introduced by d3g0 — reproduced on main c673896b, and absent on ec68e549 (pre-ynmk). d3g0 leaves it untouched deliberately: resolving it means choosing between two tests a human wrote on purpose.

## The failure

    Test Case '-[PlayheadTests.TranscriptPeekViewVetoSourceCanaryTests
      testExplicitBannerFeedbackRoutesDoNotWriteDetailedLogs]' failed
    SkipOrchestratorRevertTests.swift:298: XCTAssertFalse failed
      - func acceptSuggestedSkip( ... must not append exact feedback to the decision log

It is an XCTest, which is why it is easy to miss: every failure-triage script in this repo greps the Swift Testing marker (a leading '✘'), and XCTest prints "Test Case '-[...]' failed". Only ONE XCTest fails in the whole gate and it is this one.

## The two contracts, both deliberate

playhead-ynmk (c673896b) added, inside acceptSuggestedSkip's non-skippable branch:

    logDecision(
        managed: managed,
        decision: .confirmed,
        reason: "Banner confirmation over an unanchored extent -- presence recorded, markOnly"
    )

and a test that REQUIRES it — BannerConfirmationExtentGateTests, ~line 258:

    // The decision log is the audit trail for "the tap was honoured as
    // feedback, and deliberately not as a skip". Without an explicit
    // record, a refused confirmation is indistinguishable from a
    // confirmation that never arrived.
    #expect(await orchestrator.getDecisionLog().contains { ... }, "the refusal must be recorded, not silent")

The pre-existing canary FORBIDS exactly that, for all four explicit-feedback routes:

    /// Exact feedback receipts belong only in the durable correction store.
    /// Pin every explicit route against accidentally reusing the diagnostic
    /// decision logger or interpolating receipt fields into OSLog.

They cannot both hold. Deleting either one deletes a rail somebody wrote on purpose.

## The actual question

Is `decisionLog` a DIAGNOSTIC trace (ynmk's reading: an audit trail, and a refused confirmation must be visible in it) or a RECEIPT surface subject to the privacy contract (the canary's reading: exact feedback belongs only in the durable correction store)? Note `logDecision(managed:)` records the window's exact span, which is the specific thing the canary is about.

## Options

  A. The canary wins. Replace the `logDecision` with a `logger.info` carrying only the window id at `privacy: .public` — ynmk's observability intent survives, the exact span does not reach the diagnostic log, and ynmk's assertion moves to the os_log surface or to the durable row it already writes.
  B. ynmk wins. Add `acceptSuggestedSkip`'s markOnly branch as a named exception in the canary, with the reasoning written down — a refusal is not a receipt.
  C. Split the difference: a `logDecision` variant that carries the id and reason but not the span.

A is the smallest change and preserves both intents; B is the smallest diff. Either is a call about what the decision log IS, so it is Dan's.

## Related

  [[playhead-ynmk]] introduced it. [[playhead-d3g0]] found it and left it alone.

title: Activity's AN bar must express how much of TOTAL analysis is done, not one stage's frontier
description:
Dan, 2026-07-31:

> "an should be how much of total analysis is done"

## The decision

Activity's AN bar currently shows `analysisCoveredSec` — "how much transcribed audio lies at
or before the analysis frontier" (EpisodePreparationStatusModel.swift:24-25). That is ONE
STAGE's throughput. It must instead express **how much of the total analysis for this episode
is done**, across every stage that has to finish before the episode delivers on its promise.

This SUPERSEDES the relabel-only direction in [[playhead-71n6]]. We are not renaming AN to
"Prepared"; we are making AN measure the thing the word already implies. 71n6 stays open only
for whatever copy work survives this change.

## Why the current number is indefensible

Measured on Dan's clean install, 2026-07-31, episode DE0784D8 (92 min):

    features    5522 / 5522 s   100%
    transcript  5522 / 5522 s   100%
    ad scan     0 rows, 0.0 s     0%     <- semantic_scan_results is EMPTY

Activity showed **94% analyzed**. Library showed **0% analyzed**. Both from one model, both
arithmetically correct, both labelled "analyzed". Dan read 94% and reasonably concluded the
work was nearly done. It had not started.

## THE TRAP THIS BEAD MUST NOT FALL INTO

A naive composite AVERAGES THE ZERO AWAY. features 100% + transcript 100% + ad scan 0%, evenly
weighted, is 67% — which still tells the listener two-thirds of the job is done when **none of
the promise has been delivered**. That would be the same defect wearing a new formula, and it
would be worse than today's number because it would look principled.

Design constraints that follow:

1. **The ad scan is the promise; the other stages are means to it.** If ad-scan coverage is
   zero, AN must be at or near zero. A stage that produces no listener-visible value cannot
   carry the bar on its own.
2. Apply the standing check to whatever formula is chosen: *what would this read if the ad
   scan had never run?* If the answer is anything comfortable, the formula is wrong. See
   [[feedback_ask_what_the_quantity_measures_2026-07-29]].
3. Prefer a formula that is MONOTONE and has an honest 100%: AN = 100% must mean "there is no
   further analysis this episode can receive", which is the same condition the readiness ✓
   asserts. AN and the ✓ should agree at the endpoints even though they may differ in between.
4. Do not reconcile AN and adScanFraction into a single scalar — EpisodePreparationStatusModel
   .swift:35 forbids it, and correctly (neither dominates: AN can exceed ad-scan where the
   frontier has passed unscanned audio, and ad-scan can exceed AN where a window read text past
   the frontier, bridging gaps via AnalysisCoverageMath.adScanBridgeableGapSec). AN may be
   DERIVED from several scalars including adScanFraction; it must not BE adScanFraction, and
   the two may still legitimately differ mid-flight.

## Open for Dan (product, not engineering)

How should the stages be weighted? Options, needing a decision rather than a default:
  (a) Gate on the promise — AN = ad-scan coverage, with earlier stages shown as a separate,
      quieter preparation indicator. Simplest and hardest to misread.
  (b) Weighted composite dominated by ad scan (e.g. ad scan worth as much as everything else
      combined), so early stages show SOME movement without ever implying completion.
  (c) Staged/segmented bar — visibly three chunks, so "transcribed but not scanned" is legible
      at a glance rather than collapsed into one percentage.

Recommendation: (c) with (a)'s honesty — a segmented bar cannot average a zero away, and it
shows real progress during long transcription instead of sitting at 0% for many minutes, which
is its own kind of lie. But per [[feedback_peace_of_mind_not_metrics]], first ask whether this
belongs on a user-facing screen at all, or whether it is engine telemetry that should live in
Settings -> Diagnostics.

## Blocked by reality

Note this bead cannot be VERIFIED against a healthy pipeline until [[playhead-ewag]] is fixed —
right now no episode gets ad-scanned at all, so every honest AN would read ~0. Implement and
unit-test the formula independently of the device, and confirm on device after ewag lands.
## DECIDED — Dan 2026-08-01: option (c), the SEGMENTED bar

> "4. c"

AN becomes a **segmented bar** with visibly distinct stages, not a single averaged percentage.

Why this and not (a)/(b): a single number can average a zero away — features 100% + transcript
100% + ad-scan 0% evenly weighted reads 67%, which would be WORSE than today because it looks
principled. Segments cannot hide a zero. And unlike (a) (gate purely on ad-scan) the bar still
shows real movement during a long transcription instead of sitting at 0% for an hour, which is
its own kind of lie.

Requirements that follow:
- **"Transcribed but not scanned" must be legible at a glance** — that is the exact state Dan
  was in when Activity said 94% and Library said 0%.
- The ad-scan segment is THE PROMISE. Its emptiness must be visually obvious, not a thin sliver.
- AN = fully complete must mean the same condition the readiness ✓ asserts; they may differ
  mid-flight but must agree at the endpoints.
- Still do NOT reconcile AN and adScanFraction into one scalar
  (EpisodePreparationStatusModel.swift:35 forbids it, correctly).
- Standing check on whatever is built: what would this render if the ad scan had never run? If
  it looks comfortable, it is wrong.

This supersedes the relabel-only direction in [[playhead-71n6]]; that bead keeps only whatever
copy work survives.

title: Two surfaces both say 'analyzed' and show 94% and 0% for the same episode — the number is right, the word is wrong
description:
Found by Dan on device 2026-07-31, clean install, main @ a4d5ad32.

> "activity page shows 94 transcribed 94 analyzed on that one asset. Is that in any way
> accurate?"  ... "it shows 0% analyzed in the library view."

Same episode. Same moment. Two screens, both using the word "analyzed", showing 94% and 0%.

## The arithmetic is CORRECT. This is not a math bug.

Both surfaces read one model (AnalysisStore.fetchCoverageSummariesByAssetIds) and display
different scalars of it, deliberately, as documented at
EpisodePreparationStatusModel.swift:24-31:

  * Activity's AN bar  -> analysisCoveredSec — "how much transcribed audio lies at or
                          before the analysis frontier" (PIPELINE PROGRESS)
  * Library readiness  -> adScanFraction     — "how much audio was actually read for ads"
                          (THE USER-FACING PROMISE)

Verified against the live device DB at that moment (DE0784D8, 92 min):
    fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime  5522 / 5522 s   (100%)
    featureCoverageEndTime         5522 / 5522 s   (100%)
    confirmedAdCoverageEndTime     0.0 s
    semantic_scan_results          0 ROWS
So adScanFraction = 0 is exactly right, and the Library's 0% is the honest number.
playhead-pz32 did its job here — the readiness glyph refused to resolve on a
non-ad-scan quantity.

## The defect is the WORD, not the number

"Analyzed 94%" is read by a user as "you have looked for ads in 94% of this episode." What
it actually means is "decode and transcription have advanced 94% of the way." Dan — who
WROTE the product and knows the pipeline — read it the wrong way within seconds of seeing
it. No user will do better.

This is the repo's recurring defect class living in the label instead of the computation:
a value that names one thing being read as though it named another. pz32 could not catch
it because pz32 audited the ARITHMETIC behind the glyph, and the arithmetic is fine.

Apply the standard check to the Activity number: what would "94% analyzed" read if ad
analysis had never happened? Answer: 94%. That is the current state. It measures
presence-of-pipeline-work, not amount-of-ad-analysis.

## Constraint that must survive the fix

Do NOT "reconcile" the two surfaces by making one read the other — the file comment at :35
explicitly forbids it, and correctly: neither dominates the other. AN can exceed ad-scan
(the frontier has passed audio the scan has not reached — the usual case) and ad-scan can
exceed AN (a scan window read text past the frontier, bridging sub-ad-width transcript gaps
via AnalysisCoverageMath.adScanBridgeableGapSec). They answer different questions and both
deserve to exist.

The fix is to make the LABELS answer the questions the scalars actually answer. Only one of
these two is a promise to the listener; the other is engine telemetry. Candidate direction:
reserve "analyzed" exclusively for adScanFraction, and rename the Activity bar to something
that plainly means preparation/throughput ("Prepared", "Processed", "Read") — but the copy
is Dan's call, not the implementer's.

Worth deciding at the same time: does the pipeline-progress number belong on a user-facing
screen at all, or is it diagnostics? Per [[feedback_peace_of_mind_not_metrics]] the product
sells the felt experience, not counters — and a counter that reads 94% while the actual
promise sits at 0% is worse than no counter.

Coordinate with [[playhead-1mq1.1]] (banner copy pass) — same voice, same pass.

title: Atom sequence is ordered by chunkIndex, which is not monotone in time (27 of 30 device assets)
description:
FOUND while fixing playhead-csbq. Not fixed there: the fix changes transcriptVersion hashes and prompt content, which is a detection-quality decision.

MEASURED on the 2026-07-30 device pull (scratchpad/db2/analysis.sqlite):

  assets whose chunks are NOT time-monotone when read in chunkIndex order:  27 of 30
  worst backward step:                                                      -1470.8 s
  by transcript shape:  mixed 20/20    all-final 3/4    all-fast 4/6

WHY IT MATTERS. `TranscriptAtomizer.atomize` sorts its input by `chunkIndex` and assigns `atomOrdinal = enumerated index`. So when chunkIndex order != time order, the ATOM SEQUENCE is out of temporal order, and therefore so are the segments `TranscriptSegmenter` builds from it. Two consequences:

 1. The FM prompt for a coarse window contains transcript lines in jumbled time order. The model is asked to reason about ad boundaries over text that does not run forwards.
 2. A scan window's [start,end] is the convex HULL of a temporally scattered segment set, so it claims coverage over audio between the segments that its prompt never contained. playhead-csbq made those bounds valid (min/max instead of first/last, which stopped them INVERTING) but a hull over a scattered set still over-claims. pz32's `adScanCoveredSec` intersects with the transcribed region, which bounds but does not eliminate this.

WHY hc7e DOES NOT COVER IT. `TranscriptChunkCanonicalizer` re-sorts by time and re-indexes ONLY on the mixed fast+final path. Single-pass transcripts (all-fast or all-final) are returned byte-identically — that is its documented no-regression contract. 10 of 30 assets are single-pass and 7 of those have backward steps, so the hole is open today. It is not visible in `semantic_scan_results` yet only because those 7 assets have ~zero coverage-lane rows — they are the un-scanned backlog that playhead-hvk0 / playhead-i7qe are about to drain. Draining them walks straight into this.

Note ordering by chunkIndex is non-monotone EVEN WITH UNIQUE chunkIndex values (asset C25FF8CF: 3281 chunks, 3281 distinct chunkIndex, 54 backward steps), so this is not only the cross-pass chunkIndex collision.

THE FIX IS NOT FREE — that is why it is its own bead:
  * `atomize` computes `transcriptVersion` over the chunkIndex-sorted text. Re-sorting by time changes the hash for every disordered asset, which re-keys `reuseKeyHash` and invalidates cached scan rows (a re-scan).
  * It changes atom ordinals, which are referenced by `evidence_events.atomOrdinals` and friends.
  * It breaks hc7e's pinned "single-pass passes through byte-identically" acceptance tests, deliberately.

OPTIONS: (a) canonicalize by time on ALL paths, not just mixed; (b) sort by time inside `atomize` itself; (c) fix whatever writes non-monotone chunkIndex at the source (SpeechAnalyzer finalization order?) and repair forward only. (c) is the real root cause and is unexamined.

title: transcript_chunks.pass is mis-tagged 'final' for every fast-path chunk after a launch final-pass sweep
description:
FOUND 2026-07-30 by the adversarial review of playhead-se2h. PRE-EXISTING — not introduced by that bead — but se2h's diff initially documented and test-pinned the WRONG side of it, which is how it surfaced.

THE DEFECT: on any device with a final-pass backlog, every fast-path transcript chunk for the rest of the process is persisted with pass='final'.

THE CHAIN, each link verified against current main:
  * Nothing ever resets `activeModelRole` back to `.asrFast`. `FinalPassRetranscriptionRunner` is the only other writer and never restores it.
  * `unloadCurrentModel()` — which would clear it — has ZERO production callers. Grepped across all of Playhead/.
  * `SpeechService.transcribe` derives the pass type from that one field: `activeModelRole == .asrFinal ? .final_ : .fast`.
