  * `TranscriptEngineService` writes `pass: segment.passType.rawValue` straight into the database.
  * The launch sweep runs the FINAL pass at launch on the SAME `SpeechService` instance the playback path later uses.

So the sequence is ordinary, sequential, and needs no race: launch sweep sets `.asrFinal` -> the listener presses play -> `prepareFastModel()` returns `.alreadyLoaded` because a model IS loaded -> the role is never corrected -> every subsequent fast chunk is written as `final`.

WHY THE FIELD IS THE WRONG SHAPE, which is the actual root cause. `AppleSpeechRecognizer.loadModel()` is ROLE-AGNOSTIC: both roles run the identical `assetBootstrapper.prepare()` and set identical `selectedLocale` / `analyzerFormat` / `prepared`. There is no such thing as "the fast model" versus "the final model" at the recognizer level. `ModelRole` is a CALLER-INTENT LABEL, not recognizer state — and it is being read as though it described what is loaded. Any comment asserting "the role must still describe the model actually loaded" is therefore describing something that cannot be true, because the recognizer has no role.

That mislabelling is the defect class this project keeps hitting: a value that names one thing being read as though it named another. See the sibling instances in playhead-i7qe (`!hasCandidateWindows` read as "nothing to do") and playhead-gqx4 (transcript coverage read as ad-scan coverage).

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: commit 94809607 ("canonicalize mixed-pass display rows") landed 2026-07-26, so mixed-pass handling is live territory and a mis-tagged `pass` column feeds it. Any consumer that trusts `pass` to mean "which transcription pass produced this text" is being lied to — including reuse/dedupe keyed on `(assetId, pass, segmentFingerprint)`, which playhead-6av0's V40 unique index now depends on.

WHAT TO DECIDE, do not just patch the symptom:
  * Preferred: stop deriving persisted pass type from mutable actor state. The pass is a property of the REQUEST, not of the engine — thread it through the call rather than reading a field that outlives the call.
  * If the field must stay, it needs an owner and a reset discipline, and `unloadCurrentModel()`'s zero callers must be explained or the method removed.
  * Either way, delete any comment or test asserting the current behaviour is a safety property. se2h's review flagged exactly that; check what se2h shipped and correct it if the assertion survived.

DO NOT fix this inside a bead about something else — it touches the persisted schema's meaning and deserves its own review.

title: Under-scanned episodes have no re-drive: a completed analysis_jobs workKey blocks a new scan pass
description:
SURFACED 2026-07-29 by the adversarial review of playhead-gqx4/i7qe, and independently written down earlier by playhead-pz32 (EpisodePreparationReadiness.swift:233-238, which names gqx4/i7qe as the owner of the re-drive). gqx4/i7qe did NOT deliver it; this bead carries it.

THE MECHANISM. AnalysisJobRunner.shouldSkipSemanticBackfill (playhead-i7qe) governs runs that are ALREADY being dispatched. It does not cause a run to happen. Once an episode's coverage tiers are done, AnalysisWorkScheduler writes analysis_jobs.state='complete' (AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:3816-3823, :3844-3856, :3887-3900); analysis_jobs.workKey is TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE (AnalysisStore.swift:7912) and insertJob is INSERT OR IGNORE (AnalysisStore.swift:12688); only queued/paused/retryable-failed rows dispatch. So no new preAnalysis job is ever minted for that episode at the same analysisVersion. The glo9 relaxation only relaxes admission for EXISTING pending rows; it creates none.

CONSEQUENCE, forward-looking and not merely historical: a NEW episode whose FM windows were thermally deferred or rate-limited finishes all tiers at (say) 40% ad-scan coverage, finalizeBackfill stamps the honest degraded terminal completeAdScanPartial, the library correctly renders it ◐ 'Partly analyzed' — and nothing ever runs the scan again. gqx4 converted a lying checkmark into a truthful one; it did not finish the scan.

MEASURED on the 2026-07-29 device pull (34 assets over 15 minutes): 14 still have a dispatchable job and will benefit from the i7qe fix; the other 20 do not. Of the 6 'completeFull' assets over 15 minutes, only 2 (820134BF, 70EC53D7) carry a queued job.

WHAT TO DECIDE (this is a scheduler terminal-accounting change, so it needs a deliberate design, not a patch):
  * Mint a re-drive job when adScanFraction < episodePreparationCompleteThreshold and the FM job budget is not exhausted. The workKey collision is the obstacle: a new tier workKey, or an analysisVersion-like discriminator, or a distinct jobType.
  * MUST be bounded. The reason gqx4 terminates into a degraded state rather than declining to terminate is that an unbounded retry is a worse bug than the one it fixed. Any re-drive needs a budget with a no-progress guard — shouldRetryCoverageInsufficient's shape is the precedent, and BackfillJobRunner already refuses to re-enqueue past AdmissionController.maxRetries.
  * Consider whether the re-drive belongs to the pre-analysis lane at all, or whether the coverage-lane (backfill_jobs) needs its own resumption path. NOTE: there is currently NO query anywhere that selects queued backfill_jobs rows — grep 'FROM backfill_jobs' returns only fetchBackfillJob(byId:) and a status probe. A backfill_jobs row that outlives its runPendingBackfill invocation is orphaned, and on the device pull several fullEpisodeScan rows have sat 'queued' for six days.

DO NOT re-implement playhead-3xtw or playhead-glo9; both are shipped and neither creates jobs for this shape.

title: The pre-roll clamp can widen a detector window straight over a hand-marked span
description:
SPLIT OUT of playhead-aqo9. Applies to the pre-roll start clamp that SHIPS ON TODAY (playhead-xsdz.66) — a live defect, and a direct violation of Dan's rule that 'a manually marked span should override anything else.'

THE DEFECT, observed rather than reasoned. With the clamp reaching far enough, a fusion window past a user's [35, 55) mark was widened to [0, 60) and ENGULFED it, leaving TWO windows over the marked region:

    acousticRefined/confirmed [0.0, 60.0)  gate=markOnly   startAnchor=unanchored
    userMarked/confirmed      [35.0, 55.0) gate=eligible   startAnchor=unanchored

WHY THE OBVIOUS GUARD IS NOT ENOUGH. Adding `guard first.boundaryState != "userMarked"` inside the clamp does NOT fix this, because THE CLAMP CANNOT SEE THE MARK: `userMarked` rows are persisted separately and are NOT in the `fusionWindows` list the clamp receives. The in-clamp guard only covers the case where a user-marked row happens to be in that list. The clamp must be TOLD about the marks.

Note also that `.unanchored` means 'no DETECTOR anchored this edge' — it does NOT mean 'no human chose it'. A listener's window carries no edge anchor, so it arrives looking exactly like an FM guess. That is why the trustworthy-edge exemption does not cover it either.

THE FIX, implemented on branch bead/playhead-aqo9 (HEAD cca428eb) — salvage from there:
 - a `protectedRegions: [(start: Double, end: Double)]` parameter on the clamp, defaulting to empty;
 - the wire-in reads persisted `userMarked` rows once and passes them;
 - the clamp REFUSES to widen when a protected region intersects the widening path `[0, first.startTime)`, rather than partially extending to the mark's edge. Refusing fails closed and is trivially reasonable about; a partial extension would manufacture a novel adjacency between a detector guess and a human boundary.

THE REFUSAL MUST BE SCOPED. A mark anywhere in the episode must not silently disable the clamp forever — test that a mid-roll mark does NOT veto an unrelated pre-roll clamp. Also test that a degenerate region (zero-width, NaN, infinite) protects nothing and cannot become an accidental global veto.

OPEN, and the reason aqo9 was not merged: bead/playhead-aqo9 has an UNEXPLAINED regression in `AddedMarkSurvivesBackfillTests` 'exactly ONE window over the mark' — fails on the branch in isolation while main passes it in isolation. Ruled out by direct probe: the pre-roll ceiling, the post-roll clamp, the new mid-pipeline await, and the in-clamp userMarked guard. Untested lead: the decision-envelope refresh aqo9 added after the clamps. CONFOUND TO CONTROL FIRST: that same test fails in main's FULL gate while passing in isolation, so establish isolated-vs-full behaviour on both sides before attributing anything. Reverting the post-roll clamp and the ceiling raise (per aqo9's retraction) may well clear it — check that before hunting further.

TRAP for whoever picks this up: `PreRollStartClamp.Configuration.default` is ITSELF 90.0, independent of the service-level `preRollStartClampSeconds`. Editing only the service config may not change what a given test sees. Edit both.

NOTE: shares PreRollStartClamp.swift with the per-edge-eligibility bead; the two will likely land in one PR.

title: Widening one edge must not demote the whole window's auto-skip gate (per-edge eligibility)
description:
SPLIT OUT of playhead-aqo9, whose clamp approach was retracted on measurement. This piece survives independently and applies to the pre-roll start clamp that SHIPS ON TODAY (playhead-xsdz.66), so it is a live defect rather than a property of unlanded work.

THE DEFECT. PreRollStartClamp's copy helper demotes the widened window's `eligibilityGate` to `markOnly`:

    if let existing = eligibilityGate.flatMap(SkipEligibilityGate.init(rawValue:)),
       existing.severity >= SkipEligibilityGate.markOnly.severity { keep } else { markOnly }

WHY THAT IS WRONG. The risk is PER-EDGE, not per-window. This clamp only moves the first slot's START leftward to 0.0 — an OUTER edge, bounded by the episode boundary. The edge that can eat the show is the INNER one (a pre-roll's end), which the clamp never touches. Demoting the whole window for moving the other edge surrenders auto-skip on the part that was already trustworthy.

Dan, 2026-07-29, when told the alternative was more banners: 'does a mark help that much? if its an ad and i click yes i still lose part of the show.' A mark is worth far less than a silent skip AND can itself cost show content when acted on, so 'we demoted it to mark-only' is not a preserved outcome.

TWO REASONS IT IS A RESTORATION, NOT A LOOSENING:
 1. REDUNDANT where it was right — the clamp fires only on `.unanchored` edges, and playhead-2350 is already the independent authority on whether an unanchored edge may auto-skip.
 2. IT BREAKS A REAL CONTRACT where 2350 deliberately permits an unanchored edge to stay eligible: playhead-527u stamps a user-marked window `.eligible` at the listener's own boundaries even though it carries no detector anchor. The demotion overrode the listener.

THE FIX is to pass `eligibilityGate` through verbatim — no severity arithmetic at all. Arithmetic is what would let a later edit start auto-skipping windows the pipeline refused.

CARRYING THROUGH MUST NEVER BECOME RAISING. Required tests, one per direction: `eligible` stays eligible; `markOnly` stays markOnly; a suppressed/blocked gate is preserved; and `nil` STAYS NIL — nil is the case the old arithmetic silently swallowed, mapping it to `markOnly` so an ungated window acquired a gate the pipeline never assigned. Also assert the INNER edge is byte-identical across a firing clamp (bitPattern equality, not `==`).

ALREADY IMPLEMENTED AND TESTED on branch bead/playhead-aqo9 (HEAD cca428eb) — salvage from there rather than rewriting. Existing tests that asserted the demotion were inverted and labelled SPECIFICATION CHANGE with the reasoning inline; keep that framing so the reversal is auditable.

NOTE: shares PreRollStartClamp.swift with the other split-out bead (user-mark protection), so the two will likely land in one PR. That is fine; they are separate findings with separate acceptance criteria.

title: The default gate reports 33 failures on a CLEAN main — it can no longer certify anything
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-29 ~22:30 ET on clean main (0c667b83), single gate, nothing else running, lint clean:

    scripts/fast-gate.sh  ->  exit 65, 9,331 tests / 1,148 suites, 33 distinct failing tests

Failures by owning file:
    10  SilenceCompressionCoordinatorTests
    10  BackgroundProcessingServiceTests
    10  AnalysisPipelineStallInvariantHarnessIntegrationTests
     6  BackgroundProcessingServiceTelemetryTests
     4  BackgroundProcessingServiceLedgerTests
     3  InterruptionHandlingTests
     3  BackgroundFeedRefreshServiceTests
     1  SettingsViewTests

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN BUG RATHER THAN KNOWN FLAKINESS. CLAUDE.md documents these families as load-sensitive and records a DEFERRED decision not to PerfGate them out of the default gate, because they test real behaviours and moving them is a coverage decision for Dan. That deferral is defensible in the abstract. What is not defensible is the consequence measured here: the gate's terminal verdict is RED on a clean tree, every time, so it cannot distinguish 'your change broke something' from 'the usual 33'. Every bead in flight now has to hand-diff its failure set against a 33-item baseline that nobody has written down — which is exactly how a real regression gets waved through as 'looks like the usual flakes'.

CONCRETE HARM, same session: playhead-aqo9's investigation cost SIX extra builds and produced two conclusions I had to retract, because I was comparing failure SETS against an unknown baseline. Specifically 'AddedMarkSurvivesBackfillTests passes on main' was true in ISOLATION and false in the FULL gate, and I only found that out after using the isolated result as evidence. A written baseline would have caught it immediately.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT, cheapest first:
 1. RECORD the baseline. Commit the 33 test names to a file the gate reads, and have fast-gate.sh report 'RED (33 known / 0 new)' vs 'RED (33 known / 2 NEW)'. This makes the gate useful again TODAY without moving a single test or making any coverage decision. Strictly additive and reversible.
 2. Then decide the coverage question per family with data — an isolated pass rate for each of the 8 files. A family that passes 20/20 in isolation and 0/20 under load is a harness problem, not a coverage asset, and PerfGate-ing it loses nothing real. That reframes Dan's deferred decision as eight small evidenced calls rather than one big blind one.
 3. Only then consider fixing or gating individual tests.

DO NOT fix this by adding sleeps, retries, or by deleting the tests.

OPEN QUESTION for step 1: whether the baseline file should hard-FAIL when a known-failing test starts PASSING (i.e. treat the baseline as exact rather than a ceiling). Exact is better hygiene — it stops the list rotting — but it will fire on genuine fixes, so it needs to be easy to update. Recommend exact, with the update being a one-line script.

Related: playhead-be3s (test-health sweep), and CLAUDE.md's 'Load-sensitive measurement tests' + PerfGate sections.
=== DAN DECIDED 2026-07-29: THE BASELINE IS EXACT, NOT A CEILING ===

Asked whether the recorded baseline should hard-FAIL when a known-failing test starts PASSING, Dan: "yes".

So implement it as an EXACT set, not a maximum:
  - a NEW failure not in the baseline  -> FAIL (a regression)
  - a baseline test that now PASSES    -> FAIL (the list has rotted; someone fixed something and the
                                          baseline must shrink to match, or a load flake is
                                          masquerading as fixed)
  - exactly the baseline set           -> report "RED (33 known / 0 new)" and exit 0

The second arm is the one that keeps the list honest — a ceiling-style baseline only ever grows stale,
and a stale allow-list is how a real failure hides behind a name that has been in the file for months.

BECAUSE the pass-direction now fails the gate, updating the baseline MUST be trivial or people will
route around it: ship a one-command refresh (e.g. `scripts/fast-gate.sh --accept-baseline`) that
rewrites the file from the current run, and require the diff to be reviewed like any other change —
the file is the record of what is known-broken, so a shrinking diff is good news and a growing one
needs a reason in the commit message.

NOTE ON FLAKY MEMBERSHIP: at least one baseline member is order/load-dependent rather than
deterministically failing — `AddedMarkSurvivesBackfillTests` "exactly ONE window over the mark" fails
in the FULL gate but PASSES in isolation. An exact-match baseline will flap on tests like that. Handle
it by recording the baseline PER PLAN/INVOCATION MODE (full gate vs isolation are different baselines),
not by softening the exact match. If a test cannot be pinned in either mode, that is itself the finding.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
Step 1 implemented on bead/playhead-voez (branched from a97224fc).

WHAT SHIPPED
- scripts/gate_baseline.py: pure parse/diff/merge + CLI (check|accept).
- scripts/gate-baseline.<plan>.json: the committed record of what is known-broken.
- scripts/fast-gate.sh: verdict is now about the DIFF. RED (N known / 0 new) -> exit 0;
  a NEW failure or a rotted entry -> exit 65, named. Refresh: fast-gate.sh --accept-baseline.
- scripts/mutation-battery-gate-baseline.py: R series, 23 rails + 1 vacuity control.
- 62 unit tests (scripts/tests/test_gate_baseline.py), ~1.4s, no build.

MEASURED HERE, not lifted from the briefed log: 32 distinct failing tests,
9,922 Swift Testing tests / 1,213 suites, 53 issues, ZERO XCTest failures.
22/32 fail purely on 'Time limit was exceeded', 8 mix timeout+assertion, 2 assertion-only.
Families match the ones CLAUDE.md already names load-sensitive: BackgroundProcessingServiceTests 10,
PlaybackInterruptionTests 5, RouteChangeTests 3, the three AnalysisPipelineStall harnesses 6.

CORRECTION to the number this bead was briefed with. The 2026-08-01 reference log was
quoted as '72 Swift Testing failures'. It contains 57 failing TESTS and 15 failing SUITES,
and 57+15=72 — the suite lines are roll-ups of the tests already counted. That log is also
truncated (930 XCTest cases started, 900 reported, no terminal verdict). Hence the parser
refuses to judge any log without a terminal marker.

DAN'S EXACT-BASELINE DECISION, implemented where it is sound. Entries carry seen/failed
counts; failed==seen over >=2 observations is DETERMINISTIC and its PASSING hard-fails the
gate. Anything else is LOAD-SENSITIVE: passing is reported as a removal candidate, not fatal,
because one quiet run is not evidence a starvation flake is fixed. The tolerance is not a hole
because identity includes the failure KIND — a known-timeout test that fails an EXPECTATION is
reported NEW.

STEP 2 IS UNBLOCKED AND CHEAPER NOW: the baseline names the 8 families with per-test kind and
frequency, and PerfGate-ing any of them shows up as 'DID NOT RUN' demanding an explicit
baseline refresh rather than silently shrinking coverage.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
FINAL STATE on bead/playhead-voez (10 commits, a97224fc..2e02651c).

REAL GATE EXIT CODE: 65 on run 3 — 'RED (16 known / 9 NEW)', all nine named, plus 3 FAILS
DIFFERENTLY and 13 load-sensitive passers reported non-fatally. Run 1 self-check: 'RED (32 known
/ 0 new)' exit 0.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT SHAPED THE DESIGN. Two full runs, identical code, before any other agent
started: 32 failures and 28 failures, 19 in common, union 41 — JACCARD 0.46. Fewer than half the
failures recur run to run. A flat exact set is unusable here. Capture-recapture puts the true
population near 47, so the next accept or two will legitimately add names.

CORRECTIONS TO THE BEAD'S OWN FRAMING, with evidence:
1. 'AddedMarkSurvivesBackfillTests exactly ONE window over the mark' — the bead's named
   order/load-dependent example — PASSED in BOTH full-gate runs (121.7s and 153.2s). It did not
   reproduce.
2. The bead prescribes recording per plan/invocation mode 'not by softening the exact match'.
   Per-mode recording is implemented and necessary, but the 0.46 churn is WITHIN one mode, so it
   is not sufficient. Softening was unavoidable; it was confined to the pass direction and paid
   for by making the failure KIND part of identity.
3. The briefed '72 failures' = 57 tests + 15 SUITES in a TRUNCATED log. Double-counted roll-ups.

VERIFICATION: 70 unit tests (~1.3s, no build). 29 mutations: 28 KILLED, 0 SURVIVED, 0 ERROR,
vacuity control OK-SURVIVED. Three rails caught real defects rather than confirming the design —
R18 a weak test, R24 a bytecode-cache bug that made the battery itself mis-report, and R25/R26/R27
after a live run executed ZERO tests and the headline said GREEN.

STATE SHIPPED: 41 entries, 2 observations, all load-sensitive. Dan's pass-direction arm is
implemented and rail-tested but INERT until a third accepted observation; the gate says
'unconfirmed' in words rather than implying more confidence than the evidence supports.

STEP 2 UNBLOCKED: the baseline names the families with per-test kind and frequency, and
PerfGate-ing one now shows up as DID NOT RUN demanding an explicit refresh instead of silently
shrinking coverage.

title: Repeated user ad-corrections create duplicate ad_windows rows
description:
Found during playhead-6av0 review round 1, verifying that bead's decision NOT to dedupe ad_windows.

That decision is CORRECT — the exact-content duplicate groups on the device sit at ADJACENT rowids (one run, written back-to-back), two affected assets have zero transcript duplication so were never merged at all, and 'ad_windows.id' is a fresh UUID that other tables reference. Content equality genuinely cannot separate a merge import from a second legitimate detection, so a V40-style sweep would have been guesswork.

But the evidence that clinched it points at a separate live defect: several of the duplicate groups carry detectorVersion='userCorrection'.

AdDetectionService.recordUserMarkedAd(analysisAssetId:startTime:endTime:podcastId:windowId:) defaults 'windowId' to a fresh UUID().uuidString on EVERY call and does no content dedupe. So a user who marks the same region twice — a double tap, a re-mark after a scrub, a correction repeated across two launches — gets two ad_windows rows with identical (analysisAssetId, startTime, endTime, confidence 1.0, boundaryState 'userMarked', decisionState 'confirmed'). Both are auto-skip-eligible (playhead-527u stamps the gate .eligible at write time), so the region is double-counted in every downstream denominator, exported twice by CorpusExporter, and reaches the skip orchestrator as two overlapping windows.

This is NOT the 0hi9 merge duplication and V40 does not touch it.

Fix direction (needs a product call, not a mechanical dedupe): give a user mark a CONTENT-ADDRESSED id the way playhead-hygc.1.6 did for correction_events — e.g. an id derived from (analysisAssetId, quantised start, quantised end) plus a UNIQUE index, so a repeat mark upserts the existing row instead of minting a sibling. Quantisation width is the judgement call: too tight and a deliberate re-mark of an adjacent region collapses, too loose and two real ads merge.

Repro: call recordUserMarkedAd twice with identical arguments and count ad_windows.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: REPRIORITIZED -> P1 in the 2026-08-11 triage: completion-path work; the binding constraint is completion, not width.

title: Three jobs are permanently superseded and cannot be re-requested — one with a complete transcript
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-29 from a 52 MB device database pull. THREE jobs on Dan's device are in state `superseded` and are PERMANENTLY UN-REQUESTABLE:

  asset     attempts  lastErrorCode                                  duration  transcriptPct  analysisState
  594732D7     5      maxAttemptsReached:cancelMidRun                 4083s        37%        queued
  7A481794     8      maxAttemptsReached:transcription:zeroCoverage   3213s       100%        completeFull
  9AA1FEA2    10      maxAttemptsReached:transcription:zeroCoverage   1826s        69%        queued

`superseded` is not "gave up retrying". analysis_jobs.workKey is UNIQUE (AnalysisStore.swift:7323), insertJob is INSERT OR IGNORE (:11906), and computeWorkKey (:1128) is "<fingerprint>:<analysisVersion>:preAnalysis" — stable across launches. So every future enqueue for these episodes is SILENTLY SWALLOWED. And the one attempt-reset path, requeueOrphanedLease (:13425), guards on `state = CASE WHEN state = 'running'`, so it never touches a superseded row. These three cannot be re-requested at all until an analysisVersion bump ships.

Note 7A481794 has a 100% COMPLETE TRANSCRIPT and is still dead. Whatever failed, it was not transcription reach.

WHY THIS IS NOT playhead-ngev: ngev stopped an INTERRUPTION from spending an attempt, which prevents new dead ends. It does not rescue rows that already reached the cap. These three predate it and will stay dead forever without a deliberate sweep. Same lesson as playhead-0hi9 and playhead-6av0 — prevention does not repair what is already on disk.

WHAT TO DO: a one-shot _meta-gated sweep that resets `superseded` jobs whose asset still has work outstanding. Reset attemptCount to 0 and return the job to `queued`.

ESTABLISH BEFORE BUILDING, do not assume:
 - What "still has work outstanding" means precisely. 7A481794 is completeFull with a full transcript, so a naive "transcript incomplete" predicate would skip it — yet it is exactly the case worth rescuing, since its semantic scan may be far behind. Consider keying on semantic scan reach rather than transcript coverage, and check what playhead-gqx4 concludes about completeFull's honesty first.
 - Whether resetting a job whose failures were GENUINE simply burns five more attempts and returns to superseded. If the underlying cause persists the sweep achieves nothing; it may need to pair with a reason check, or accept one more cycle now that ngev names failures properly.
 - Whether the sweep should run once or become a periodic reaper. Once is safer and matches the existing _meta-gated precedents; a reaper risks masking a real permanent failure.

CAUTION: this touches the same migration machinery that could delete the store on a thrown migrate() (playhead-wvdz). Run inside a savepoint that rolls back and leaves the schema version unchanged, as playhead-0hi9's v39 rung does.

VERIFY AGAINST THE PULLED DATABASE at scratchpad/db2/analysis.sqlite rather than only a synthetic fixture — all three real cases are in it.
=== CHECKED 2026-07-30 05:30 ET at Dan's request ("check y8f3 and close if already fixed"). NOT FIXED — but RESCOPED. ===

VERDICT: the REPAIR half is now out of scope; the PREVENTION half is still live and is the real bug. Do not close.

WHAT IS OUT OF SCOPE NOW. Dan, 2026-07-30: "i dont really care abkjt the existing library as long as the forward looking oicture is fixed." This bead's stated fix — a one-shot _meta-gated sweep resetting the THREE existing superseded rows — is precisely a historical-repair migration, which he has now declined twice (also on playhead-gqx4). Drop the sweep. The three rows on his device stay dead.

WHAT IS STILL LIVE, and why closing would be wrong. `superseded` remains a PERMANENT DEAD END with NO reset path, and new episodes can still reach it:

  * The only attempt-reset, `requeueOrphanedLease` (AnalysisStore.swift:14207), rewrites
        state = CASE WHEN state = 'running' THEN 'queued' ELSE state END
    so a superseded row is explicitly preserved, not rescued. Verified 2026-07-30 against current main.
  * `analysis_jobs.workKey` is still UNIQUE and `insertJob` is still INSERT OR IGNORE, so every future enqueue for that episode is silently swallowed.
  * Multiple `maxAttemptsReached:*` paths still write `superseded` — `cancelMidRun` (AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:3635), `coverageInsufficient` (:3897), `assetResolution` (:3453). playhead-ngev (#293) stopped an INTERRUPTION from spending an attempt, which removes one cause; it does not remove the trap, and the other causes remain reachable.

So the forward-looking statement is: an episode that exhausts its attempts for ANY remaining reason becomes permanently un-analysable, silently, until an analysisVersion bump ships. That is a forward-looking defect by Dan's own test and it survives his scope cut.

RESCOPED ACCEPTANCE:
  * Reaching the attempt cap must not be PERMANENT. Either superseded gains a bounded, principled reset path (e.g. eligible again when the asset still has outstanding work AND some cooling condition holds), or the enqueue path stops silently swallowing a re-request for a superseded workKey. Prefer whichever is smaller.
  * MUST stay bounded — the reason the cap exists is that a poisoned asset must eventually stop consuming budget. An unbounded reset recreates the bug the cap was defending against. Same constraint as playhead-gqx4's degraded terminal and playhead-onn6's re-drive: bound it, and add a no-progress guard.
  * A silently-swallowed re-request is itself the defect shape this project keeps hitting — INSERT OR IGNORE returning success while doing nothing. At minimum the swallow should be observable.
  * NO migration, NO repair sweep, NO _meta-gated one-shot. Existing rows stay as they are.

RELATIONSHIP TO playhead-onn6 (in flight): DIFFERENT TABLE, do not assume overlap. onn6 concerns `backfill_jobs` (35 rows queued, no selector) and the coverage-lane re-drive. This bead concerns `analysis_jobs` and the pre-analysis lane's attempt cap. They share a SHAPE — a UNIQUE workKey plus INSERT OR IGNORE making re-request impossible — so onn6's chosen discriminator may be directly reusable here, and whoever picks this up should read onn6's solution first rather than inventing a second mechanism.

DEVICE STATE 2026-07-30 (unchanged since filing): analysis_jobs = 10 complete, 17 queued, 3 superseded, 1 failed.
acceptance_criteria: The three real superseded jobs on Dan's device are recoverable, verified against the pulled database at scratchpad/db2/analysis.sqlite. The 'still has work outstanding' predicate is established from evidence — note 7A481794 has a 100% transcript and must still qualify. The sweep runs inside a savepoint that rolls back leaving schema_version unchanged. Decided and recorded whether this is one-shot or periodic, with the reasoning. Does NOT mask a genuinely permanent failure: state what happens if the underlying cause persists after the reset.
notes:
=== IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-31 (prevention half only; repair stays out of scope). ===

MEASURED, db4 pull (reproduced the reported deltas exactly: queued 17->1, complete 10->17,
superseded 3->8, failed 1->0; 27 long episodes under 95% transcript; 1 dispatchable job).

lastErrorCode distribution on the 8 superseded rows:
  maxAttemptsReached:transcription:zeroCoverage            6
  maxAttemptsReached:decode: ...Operation Interrupted      1
  maxAttemptsReached:cancelMidRun                          1
All 8 carry transcriptCoverageSec = 0 in the JOB row while their assets are 0-100% transcribed:
updateJobProgress OVERWRITES with the last run's output, it is not a high-water mark. Any
progress guard reading the job column concludes "no progress ever" for a nearly-done episode.

Of the 27 under-95% episodes: 9 have NO job row (8bp2/discoverUnEnqueuedDownloads owns those),
12 have a `complete` job (gqx4's degraded terminal), 6 have a `superseded` job. This bead
reaches those 6.

DOES `superseded` MEAN TWO THINGS? YES, and that is exactly why requeueOrphanedLease preserves
it. Genuine supersession (stale analysisVersion, episode deleted, staleFingerprint:cachedAudioMismatch)
vs attempt cap-out. The discriminator shipped is `state == 'superseded' && lastErrorCode
hasPrefix 'maxAttemptsReached:'`. Both genuine paths go through updateJobState's default, which
NULLs lastErrorCode, so they can never be misread. The 5th maxAttemptsReached writer
(coverageInsufficient, gqx4) terminates `complete` and is excluded by the STATE check.

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S PREMISE: cap-out is NOT literally permanent. AnalysisJobReconciler
step 5 GCs complete/superseded rows older than 7 days, after which step 7 mints a fresh base
job at defaultT0DepthSeconds. The real behaviour is a 7-DAY DEAD WINDOW followed by a restart
from 90 s that discards the tier depth. Still a defect, and still what Dan is watching.

FIX (no migration, no sweep, no existing row touched): on a swallowed re-enqueue in step 7,
mint ONE new row at `<base>:capRetry:<n>` -- playhead-onn6's mechanism, reused rather than
reinvented. maxCapOutRetries = 2. Guards: cap-out discriminator, budget ordinal (UNIQUE
workKey), 1 h cooldown (= exponentialBackoffSeconds' own ceiling), and an outstanding-transcript
predicate that takes the next TIER LADDER rung above the asset watermark (so the retry always
has unread audio; two device rows were already transcribed past their own job's target).
Every refusal is a NAMED reason. New report fields capOutRetriesMinted + reEnqueuesSwallowed;
AnalysisWorkScheduler.enqueue now logs its own swallow (it discarded insertJob's Bool).

BOUNDED IN ROWS, NOT DISPATCHES -- deliberately stated that way: fetchNextEligibleJob has no
attemptCount predicate and requeueOrphanedLease resets it, which is why device rows carry
attemptCount 8 and 10 against a cap of 5. The ledger this holds is 3 rows per
(sourceFingerprint, analysisVersion) per 7-day GC window.

PREDICTED ON DAN'S DEVICE, simulated against db4 with the shipped predicate: 6 of the 8
superseded rows mint a retry on the next reconcile (594732D7 -> 4083 s, 9AA1FEA2 -> 1826,
0992B341 -> 6637, D2B8579A -> 2936, 1B0C0D33 -> 4245, FF3A6A5E -> 90). The other 2 decline
`noOutstandingTranscript` because they are fully transcribed: 25D2294D (onn6's re-drive lane
owns it, 2 resumable backfill rows) and 7A481794 (0 resumable; nothing left to transcribe --
the original bead's headline case is deliberately NOT rescued by this bead).
Dispatchable jobs go 1 -> 7.

TESTS: PlayheadTests/Services/PreAnalysis/CapOutRetryTests.swift, 15 tests. Includes the
seconds-of-audio reach test (asserts fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime rises, not a row state) and
a termination test driving 10 cycles against an always-failing decode. 6 mutations applied and
all killed.

title: The diagnostics legal-checklist guard does not check nested record keys — free text leaked past it in a measured test
description:
CORRECTION TO A WIDELY-REPEATED ASSUMPTION, found during playhead-8ysk review round 1. I have told several agents that DiagnosticsBundleShapeTests is the legal guard on the diagnostics bundle and that it has rejected new keys before. That is only true for TOP-LEVEL and `default`-subtree keys. It does NOT enumerate NESTED RECORD keys.

MEASURED: with the export vocabulary validation removed, a real episode title ("Diary of a CEO — Episode 412") reached the encoded bundle JSON — and DiagnosticsBundleShapeTests PASSED. The leak was caught only by the bead's own adversarial suite. So the checklist that everyone treats as the compliance gate did not gate the thing it exists to gate.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A TEST GAP: this repo has a hard on-device mandate — no audio, transcripts, or episode content may leave the device — and the diagnostics bundle is the ONLY egress path in the app. Its guard is what makes it safe to add fields there. Every future bead that adds a nested diagnostic field will reasonably assume the checklist covers it. Two beads in the last day added nested subtrees (playhead-p70f's rediff_diagnostics, playhead-8ysk's failure_class/failure_code), and in both cases the real protection was a hand-written adversarial test that happened to be written because someone thought to.

WHAT TO ESTABLISH: whether the checklist should recurse over the whole encoded structure, or whether nested records need their own registration. Recursing is the stronger guarantee but will surface every existing nested field at once — measure that count before committing to it, the same way .swiftlint.yml was built by measurement rather than taste.

DO NOT simply add the two new keys to a list. The defect is that the mechanism does not see nested structure at all; enumerating today's nested keys by hand reproduces the same hole for tomorrow's.

CONSIDER ALSO: the strongest form is a test that encodes a bundle populated with poison values — recognisable sentinel strings in every free-text-capable source field — and asserts none appear anywhere in the encoded JSON, at any depth. That is content-based rather than key-based, so it cannot be defeated by a field nobody registered.

Related: playhead-8ysk (where this was found), playhead-p70f (added the other recent nested subtree), and the Addendum A telemetry envelope documentation which records the founder's approval on the basis that the bundle is guarded.
acceptance_criteria: The guard sees nested structure. Proven by the measured case: with a vocabulary validation removed, an episode title reaching the encoded JSON must FAIL the checklist, not pass it. Prefer a content-based poison-value assertion over an enumerated key list, so an unregistered field cannot slip through. If the approach surfaces existing nested fields, measure the count first and tier the work rather than disabling the check. Verify against both recent nested subtrees (rediff_diagnostics, failure_class/failure_code).

title: A job that stops at 84% coverage journals nothing — partial failure is the one shape with no diagnostic
description:
Flagged by the playhead-8ysk implementer as a deliberate scope boundary. It matters because it is DAN'S EXACT REPORTED SYMPTOM.

Dan, 2026-07-29: "transcript and analysis appears stuck at 84%".

playhead-8ysk gives every shard failure a named class and a .failed event, and removes the lie where a loop that failed every shard still reported .completed. But the RUNNER only journals a failure when transcript coverage is ZERO — AnalysisJobRunner.swift:697, "if transcriptCoverage == 0". A job that transcribes 84% of an episode and fails the remaining 16% therefore still reports .completed, journals nothing, and leaves no record that anything went wrong.

So the shape Dan actually sees — analysis parking part-way and staying there — remains the one shape with no diagnostic. Zero-coverage failures are now well instrumented; partial-coverage failures are not instrumented at all. That is backwards relative to how often each occurs: his six-day scheduler_events sample had 147 acquisitions against 9 finalizations, and a job that stops at 84% is far likelier than one that produces nothing.

WHAT TO ESTABLISH FIRST: whether a partial-coverage job is genuinely FINISHED-BUT-INCOMPLETE or whether it is still running and merely appears stuck. Those need different treatments and the current telemetry cannot distinguish them. playhead-8ysk's new .failed events give per-shard classes; the missing piece is a job-level verdict that says "this job stopped with N of M shards failed, dominant class X" even when N < M.

DESIGN NOTE, not a prescription: resist making any nonzero failure count a hard job failure. Partial coverage is often legitimate and better than none — the per-shard catch comment says so explicitly ("partial coverage is better than none"), and the 120s holder watchdog from playhead-8m2w is calibrated on exactly that premise, costing one shard rather than the job. The goal is that a partial failure be VISIBLE, not that it be fatal. A journal row with counts and a dominant failure class, plus a coverage figure, is probably the right shape.

RELATED, and it should be decided together: playhead-pz32 shows the readiness checkmark keys on feature-extraction coverage and the last detected ad's end time, so it can read "ready" on an episode stuck at 84%. Whatever verdict this bead produces is the natural input for an honest indicator.

Related beads: playhead-8ysk (parent), playhead-pz32 (the UI that misreports this state), playhead-3ffk (a swallowed model-load failure that would present as a high partial-failure count).
acceptance_criteria: A job that completes with a materially incomplete transcript emits a job-level verdict carrying the failed-shard count, the total, the dominant failure class and the achieved coverage — visible in a diagnostics bundle without a device attached. Partial coverage is NOT made fatal; a single failed shard must still leave the job useful, per the existing per-shard contract and the 8m2w watchdog calibration. Dan's reported shape (analysis parking at ~84%) is reproducible in a test and produces a record. Coordinate the verdict's shape with playhead-pz32 so the readiness indicator can consume it rather than inventing a second notion of done.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: REPRIORITIZED -> P1 in the 2026-08-11 triage: it is on the completion path, which the queue-6 evidence establishes as the binding constraint (ZERO backfill_jobs have ever reached complete across 33 assets).

title: A failed migration silently deletes the user's entire analysis database, with no error surfaced
description:
SURFACED TWICE during playhead-0hi9's review rounds, and deliberately left for Dan as a product decision rather than fixed inside that bead.

PlayheadRuntime.swift:2109 handles a thrown AnalysisStore.migrate() by deleting the entire store directory and retrying:

    try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: AnalysisStore.defaultDirectory())

The retry then succeeds, because the directory is empty. The user's complete analysis database — every transcript chunk, ad window, semantic scan result, correction they made by hand, fingerprint and learned threshold — is destroyed silently. No error is surfaced, nothing is logged to the user, and the app appears to launch normally. From the outside it is indistinguishable from a fresh install.

HOW IT WAS FOUND: playhead-0hi9's v39 migration originally issued a bare DELETE FROM analysis_assets. Because training_examples.analysisAssetId is ON DELETE RESTRICT, a single fingerprint collision whose losing row carried a training example raised FOREIGN KEY constraint failed, aborting migrate() — and landing directly on this path. Review round 1 caught it; round 2 then hardened the rung structurally by wrapping it in a SAVEPOINT that rolls back and leaves schema_version at 38 so the next launch retries, rather than by enumerating throw sites. So 0hi9 no longer materially raises the chance of reaching this recovery.

WHY IT STILL DESERVES A DECISION: the recovery path is pre-existing and applies to EVERY migration, not just v39. Any future rung that throws for any reason — a constraint, a missing column on an old schema, a disk error, a corrupt page — silently wipes the user's library. That is a very large consequence for a failure mode whose most likely causes are transient or recoverable, and it converts every future migration into a potential data-loss event. It is also invisible in telemetry: the app does not report it, so a fleet-wide wipe caused by one bad rung would look like a sudden drop in analysis coverage with no error signal at all.

OPTIONS TO WEIGH — this is a product call about failure posture, not purely a technical one:
 (a) Keep as-is. Guarantees the app always launches. Accepts silent total loss.
 (b) Move the store aside instead of deleting it (rename to a quarantine path). The app still launches on a fresh store, the data is recoverable, and a diagnostics bundle can report that a quarantine exists. Costs disk until cleaned up.
 (c) Surface it. Let the app launch degraded and tell the user analysis history could not be opened, rather than pretending nothing happened.
 (d) Leave schema_version untouched on failure and retry next launch — what 0hi9's v39 rung now does for itself — so a transient failure resolves instead of escalating to a wipe. Does not cover a genuinely corrupt database.
Options (b) and (d) compose well: retry on the next launch, quarantine only after repeated failures.

Note the on-device mandate makes this worse in one specific way: there is no cloud copy. Whatever is destroyed here is gone permanently, including the user's manual corrections, which are the most expensive data in the app to reproduce because a human produced them one tap at a time.
=== DAN'S DECISION, 2026-07-29: RETRY, THEN SURFACE AND LET THE USER DECIDE ===

Dan, verbatim: "retry then surface to the user and let them decide."

This is a hybrid of the retry option and the surface option, and it is stronger than either alone or than the quarantine-automatically recommendation I gave. THE APP NEVER MAKES THE DESTRUCTIVE CHOICE. It retries what is usually transient, and when that is exhausted it hands the decision to the person whose data it is.

THE SETTLED CORE, which is not open to reinterpretation during implementation:
 1. A migration failure NEVER silently deletes the store. The current behaviour — PlayheadRuntime.swift:2109 answering a thrown migrate() with removeItem(at: AnalysisStore.defaultDirectory()) and retrying on the empty directory — is removed.
 2. First failures RETRY. Roll back, leave schema_version at its prior value, let the next launch try again. Most migration failures are transient. playhead-0hi9's v39 rung already does exactly this for itself (SAVEPOINT, roll back, leave version at 38) — follow that shape rather than inventing a second one.
 3. When retries are exhausted, SURFACE IT and let the user choose. The app does not decide to destroy.

OPEN SUB-QUESTIONS — design these, then confirm with Dan before building the UI:
 - How many failures before surfacing? Consider that each retry costs a launch, so a low number (2-3) surfaces quickly while still absorbing a one-off.
 - What choices does the user get? At minimum "try again" and "start fresh". Consider whether "start fresh" should still QUARANTINE rather than delete — Dan chose to let the user decide, which is about agency, not about making destruction easy to reach by accident. A quarantine that is recoverable respects the decision while keeping the mistake reversible.
 - What does the app do WHILE the decision is pending? Recommend launching DEGRADED — playback works, analysis features report unavailable — rather than blocking launch behind a modal. A listener who opens the app to play a podcast should be able to play a podcast.
 - Where does this live? There is no existing surface for it. Coordinate with playhead-jw63.4 (crash/hang pipeline) and the diagnostics hatch rather than inventing a new one-off alert.

REGARDLESS OF THE UI, DO THIS FIRST AND SEPARATELY: make the failure OBSERVABLE in the diagnostics bundle. Today a migration failure is invisible — no error, no telemetry, and the app looks like a fresh install. A fleet-wide wipe would have presented as an unexplained drop in analysis coverage with no signal at all. The observability half is independent of the UI half, is much cheaper, and should not wait for it.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A TYPICAL FAILURE PATH: the on-device mandate means there is no cloud copy, so anything destroyed is gone permanently. And 54 of the 166 ad windows on Dan's device are HIS OWN MANUAL CORRECTIONS — a third of the total, each produced by a human tapping a button. That is the most expensive data in the app to reproduce and the least defensible to delete without asking.
acceptance_criteria: A migration failure never silently deletes the store — the removeItem-and-retry path at PlayheadRuntime.swift:2109 is gone, proven by a test with a deliberately failing migration rung. Early failures roll back and retry on the next launch, following playhead-0hi9's v39 savepoint shape. When retries are exhausted the user is asked, and the app never chooses destruction on its own. The app launches DEGRADED while a decision is pending rather than blocking playback. The failure is observable in the diagnostics bundle — ship that half FIRST and independently, since a fleet-wide wipe must not be able to present as an unexplained coverage drop. Confirm the retry count and the exact user choices with Dan before building the UI.

title: Diagnostics bundle: the 200-event cap makes rates uncomputable and the dropped metadata hides every failure cause
description:
The diagnostics bundle is now the primary instrument for diagnosing this app on real hardware — tonight it produced playhead-8ysk, playhead-4lcz and the confirmation of playhead-p70f. Two limitations in it cost real accuracy tonight and should be fixed before the next investigation leans on it.

1. THE SCHEDULER-EVENT CAP MAKES RATES UNCOMPUTABLE. DiagnosticsBundleBuilder.swift:95 sets schedulerEventsCap = 200 and :163 takes the last 200 events. Dan's bundle contained exactly 200 (147 acquired + 9 finalized + 20 failed + 24 preempted), i.e. the window was SATURATED. Terminal rows for the older acquisitions had already fallen off the front, so the acquired:finalized ratio inside the window is not a completion rate. I quoted "6% completion" from it and had to correct myself. Either raise the cap materially, or — better — export pre-aggregated counters (acquisitions, finalizations, failures by cause, over a stated window) alongside the tail, so a rate is computable without inferring it from a truncated sample.

2. THE CAUSE FIELD IS PROJECTED WITHOUT ITS DETAIL. DiagnosticsBundle.swift:492-495 deliberately omits WorkJournalRecord.metadata and SchedulerEvent's equivalent on PII grounds — the comment notes callers stash arbitrary JSON there. The privacy instinct is right and should be preserved. But the consequence is that runner_reason ("transcription:zeroCoverage") and stage, which ARE persisted on-device at AnalysisStore.swift:13259, never reach the bundle. That is why asr_failed arrives as a bare label with nine indistinguishable causes behind it. The fix is not to export metadata wholesale: add a NARROW, TYPED, redacted field (error class or domain plus code, drawn from a closed vocabulary) that survives projection — the same shape playhead-p70f used for its day-0 exit taxonomy, which exports a closed enum raw value and never free text.

Both are small, and both multiply the value of every future device pull. Note the bundle already does the hard part correctly: episode and asset ids are hashed via EpisodeIdHasher, and DiagnosticsBundleShapeTests enforces a legal checklist that has already rejected a new key once.

Related: playhead-8ysk (blocked on limitation 2), playhead-4lcz, playhead-p70f (the pattern to follow for a closed-vocabulary diagnostic field).
acceptance_criteria: A completion rate can be computed from a bundle without inferring it from a saturated tail — either via a materially larger cap or via exported aggregate counters over a stated window. A failure cause carries a narrow typed discriminator (error class/domain/code from a closed vocabulary) that survives projection, without exporting free text or arbitrary metadata. The existing privacy guarantees are preserved: ids stay hashed and DiagnosticsBundleShapeTests still passes. Verify against a real device pull that the new fields answer the question 'why did this fail' without a debugger attached.

title: A swallowed launch-time model-load failure permanently disables transcription, with no retry
description:
Found while tracing playhead-8ysk. An independent defect that can permanently disable transcription for the life of an app install, with no retry and no visible error.

loadFastModel() is invoked EXACTLY ONCE, at PlayheadRuntime.swift:2775, and its failure is swallowed by an empty catch at :2776-2779. The catch's own comment claims "the transcript engine will surface failures when first used". IT DOES NOT. Those failures land in the per-shard catch at TranscriptEngineService.swift:555, which logs and continues — so the model-load failure becomes an indistinguishable modelNotLoaded throw on every subsequent shard (TranscriptEngine.swift:674-676 and :1586-1588), forever. Nothing anywhere retries the load.

The consequence: a single transient failure at launch — a locale asset not yet installed, an analyzer format briefly unavailable, a cold-start resource pinch — silently converts every future transcription attempt on that device into a failure, until the user happens to relaunch at a moment when the load would have succeeded. There is no signal to the user, no retry, and no diagnostic.

COMPOUNDING DEFECT in the sibling: loadFinalModel (TranscriptEngine.swift:649-660) calls unloadModel() at :652 BEFORE try await recognizer.loadModel() at :656. A throw between those two lines leaves the device with NO model loaded at all and activeModelRole stale at .asrFast. So a failure while upgrading from the fast model to the final model is strictly worse than not attempting the upgrade — it destroys a working state.

WHY THIS IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY THE CAUSE OF playhead-8ysk, but must be ruled out: Dan's eligibility_snapshot reads fully healthy (appleIntelligenceEnabled, hardwareSupported, languageSupported, modelAvailableNow, regionSupported all true). But that snapshot reports Apple Intelligence availability, NOT SpeechService.activeModelRole — a device can be entirely eligible while this actor holds prepared == false. Against it: his bundle shows 9 finalized jobs interleaved with the failures, which argues against a total model outage. Treat this as a real defect worth fixing on its own merits, and as a hypothesis for 8ysk that the error-propagation work will confirm or eliminate.

FIX SHAPE: do not swallow the load failure. Surface it (the same .failed channel playhead-8ysk adds to TranscriptEngineEvent is the natural carrier), and add a retry — a load failure at launch is frequently transient and there is currently no path back. For loadFinalModel, do not unload until the replacement has loaded successfully, or restore the prior model on failure.
acceptance_criteria: A model-load failure at launch is surfaced rather than swallowed, and is retried rather than being terminal for the install's lifetime. loadFinalModel cannot leave the device with no model loaded — either it does not unload until the replacement is ready, or it restores the previous model on failure, proven by a test that makes the load throw. The modelNotLoaded case is distinguishable in diagnostics from other ASR failures (coordinate with playhead-8ysk's error propagation rather than building a second channel). Explicitly record whether this was a contributing cause of playhead-8ysk once that bead's error propagation lands.

title: iOS filed two MetricKit disk-write exceptions: 1,074 MB written, twice in eight hours
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-29 from Dan's diagnostics bundle (playhead-diagnostics-2026-07-29T03-17-21Z.json). iOS filed TWO MetricKit disk-write exceptions against the app in an eight-hour window, each reporting 1,074 MB written.

  kind: disk_write_exception   writes_caused_mb: 1074   received 2026-07-28 18:47:22 UTC
  kind: disk_write_exception   writes_caused_mb: 1074   received 2026-07-29 03:02:02 UTC
  device iPhone17,2, iPhone OS 27.0 (24A5390f), Release build (is_test_flight false)

A gigabyte of disk writes is a lot for a podcast player, and iOS considered it exceptional enough to report twice.

THE STACK DOES NOT IDENTIFY THE WRITER — do not chase it. Both reports carry frames_truncated=true (64 of 512 frames), and the top frames are the main run loop (dyld -> Playhead -> SwiftUI -> UIKitCore -> GraphicsServices -> CoreFoundation -> libdispatch). MetricKit attributes the exception to the process and samples wherever it happened to be; the writing code is not in this stack. Attribution has to come from instrumenting the write paths, not from reading these frames.

CANDIDATE WRITERS, to be measured rather than assumed:
 - ShardCache PCM persistence (AnalysisAudio.swift, ShardCache.saveShards). Decoded audio is large — mono 16 kHz float32 is ~64 KB/s, so a 30-minute episode is on the order of 115 MB. With 148 job acquisitions in six days (playhead-8ysk), repeated decode-and-persist across retries could plausibly reach this scale on its own.
 - Rediff B-copies. 367.7 MB of full fetches are recorded in rediff_bandwidth_ledger across the device's life, each written to disk and then deleted. Real, but an order of magnitude short of 1,074 MB per report window on its own.
 - Episode downloads themselves, and any re-download after cache eviction.
 - SQLite write amplification — WAL checkpoints, the analysis DB is ~40 MB.
Start by instrumenting the ShardCache path, since it is both the largest per-item writer and the one most likely to repeat under playhead-8ysk's retry loop.

HYPOTHESIS WORTH TESTING, because it would tie together two open beads: iOS deprioritises apps that trigger resource exceptions. Playhead's background task grants are conspicuously poor — the rediff lagged sweep received exactly ONE window in seven days while preanalysis_recovery got 283 and backfill got 93 over the same period (playhead-p70f), and an earlier investigation attributed an overnight analysis stall to iOS granting approximately zero discretionary windows (project_backfill_stall_bgtask_2026-07-22, where the conclusion was that it was NOT a code bug). If disk-write exceptions are causing the scheduler to throttle the app, that would be a shared upstream cause for both, and reducing writes would improve background scheduling as a side effect. This is speculation until measured — MetricKit does not expose the throttling decision — but it is cheap to test by reducing writes and re-observing grant rates.

USER-FACING STAKES beyond scheduling: sustained gigabyte-scale writes drain battery and consume flash endurance. For an app whose pitch is that it respects the listener's attention and runs entirely on-device, being flagged by iOS for excessive disk activity is a credibility problem as well as a technical one.

RELATIONSHIP TO OTHER BEADS: playhead-8ysk (the retry loop that may drive repeated decodes), playhead-0hi9 (partial decodes at the 8 MiB playable threshold, which produce shards that are then written), playhead-p70f (rediff fetch volume, already reduced by that bead's idempotency work — measure whether these numbers fall after it ships).
acceptance_criteria: The dominant writer is identified by instrumenting the candidate write paths, not inferred from the MetricKit stack (which samples the main run loop and does not name it). Total bytes written per listening session is measured and reported as a baseline. Writes are reduced materially, with the reduction verified by a fresh device pull showing either no further disk_write_exception reports or a substantially lower writes_caused_mb. The background-grant hypothesis is tested: re-observe rediff_refetch and backfill BGTask grant rates after the reduction and record whether they improve. Do not close on a code change alone — this bead exists because of a device measurement and needs a device measurement to close.

title: SegmentAggregator dilutes confidence over a wider region than the window it reports
description:
Found 2026-07-28 tracing playhead-8x59. A genuine width/confidence-coherence defect inside the segment aggregator, distinct from the surfacing question.

SegmentAggregator.swift:486-492 includes a sub-continuation trailing window in the SCORE but not in the EXTENT:

    // Below continuation. Include the window in the score
    // (it's still evidence about the region), but advance the
    // end countdown. Note: the emitted endTime still snaps to
    // `lastQualifyingEndTime`, so sub-continuation tail does
    // NOT extend the reported segment boundary.
    seg.include(w)
    seg.belowContinuationSeconds += w.durationSeconds

seg.include() adds to weightedScoreSum and totalDuration (SegmentAggregator.swift:325-337), and meanScore divides by totalDuration. So the denominator grows with region the emitted window does not cover.

WORKED EXAMPLE from the observed device data: a 0.62 seed slot at [1530,1560) followed by a 0.20 sub-continuation slot at [1560,1590) materializes as mean = (0.62*30 + 0.20*30)/60 = 0.41 with endTime = 1560. The persisted row is 30 seconds wide at confidence 0.41, but that 0.41 describes 60 seconds. The strong half is reported at the diluted score of the weak half.

TWO CONSEQUENCES:
 1. Confidence and geometry describe different regions, so any downstream threshold on confidence is reasoning about a span that is not the span it will act on. This matters more once auto-skip widens (playhead-qs0d).
 2. It is a systematic DOWNWARD bias on exactly the segments most likely to be real — a genuine ad followed by a quiet lead-out gets scored as if the lead-out were part of it. Some windows currently sitting at 0.41-0.43 in the markOnly band may be true detections pushed under the 0.55 auto-skip threshold by their own tail.

Consequence 2 means this is NOT purely a precision cleanup — fixing it could RAISE some scores. Do not assume the change is monotone in either direction; measure before and after on the corpus.

DECIDE WHICH INVARIANT IS WANTED (do not assume): either the score is computed only over the reported extent, or the extent grows to cover everything the score consumed. The comment shows the current split was a deliberate choice about boundary snapping, so the fix must preserve whatever the snapping was protecting — check playhead-4xqf, since reporting a NARROWER window than the evidence supports is precisely the boundary-collapse family that bead tracks.

Related: playhead-4xqf (boundary undersizing), playhead-8x59 (the surfacing question on the same producer).
acceptance_criteria: The chosen invariant is stated explicitly and justified against the boundary-snapping intent the current comment records. Confidence and extent describe the same region after the fix. The worked example (0.62 seed + 0.20 tail -> currently 0.41 over a 30s window) is a regression fixture. Corpus measurement before/after is reported, covering BOTH directions — count of windows whose score rises above 0.55 as well as those that fall — since the bias is downward today and the fix is not monotone. Coordinate with playhead-4xqf rather than fixing extent twice.
notes: PR #341 open. 8 KILLED / 0 SURVIVED / 0 ERROR on the PG battery (batches 270-276) after a first pass that found two real holes in the new rails (PG02 blind because the shape ended on a qualifying window; PG05 blind because its witness was global rather than per-exit) and one inert edit (PG07 aimed at meanScore, which every exit reaches only after the tail is settled). Final gate RED (25 known / 22 NEW), all 22 triaged as pre-existing load flakes: 20 time-limit at 138-160s, 2 expectation-kind at 126.6s that are a 10s polling budget under starvation and have failed in 7/22 prior unrelated logs. Filed playhead-eqo8 for the lastQualifyingEndTime regression. Recorded the interaction on playhead-8x59, which this unblocks.

title: Assets stall in 'backfill' with a 100% transcript and never drain — Dan's audited episode sat at 47% scan
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-28 in Dan's dogfood analysis.sqlite. The companion failure to the completeFull bead: where that one declares victory too early, this one never finishes at all.

DAN'S AUDITED EPISODE, asset 820134BF (2113s):
  fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime = 2113.0  -> transcript is 100% COMPLETE
  analysisState                 = backfill
  confirmedAdCoverageEndTime    = NULL
  finalPassCoverageEndTime      = NULL
  semantic scan                 = 12 rows, passA ONLY, reaching 984s = 47%

So the expensive part (transcription) finished, the cheap part (scanning the text we already have) stopped at 47%, and the asset has been parked in backfill ever since. passB never ran at all.

THIS IS WHY DAN SAW WHAT HE SAW. His two denied banners were at 300-330s and 1800-1950s. 1800s is far beyond the 984s the scan reached, so nothing with judgement ever looked at it — the only thing with an opinion out there was the evidence-free shard scorer (playhead-8x59). And his reported MISSES at 2046-2112s are likewise past the scan frontier. Both of his complaints live in the unscanned 53%.

OTHER STALLED ASSETS in the same state: 144C8A80 (3170s, transcript 100%, backfill, scan 39%), 1A9616D1 (3013s, transcript 100%, backfill, scan 10%), D2F6BDA9 (3578s, transcript 57%, backfill, scan 0 rows).

WHY THE EXISTING WORK DID NOT COVER THIS: playhead-3xtw (on-demand download+analyse) and playhead-glo9 (opportunistic backlog drain during playback) are both CLOSED and shipped. Dan's device HAS those builds. They are evidently not sufficient to drain a backfill asset whose transcript is already complete. Do not re-implement them — find out why they do not fire for this asset shape. Candidate directions to CHECK, not assume: the drain's eligibility predicate may key on transcript coverage (already satisfied, so nothing looks pending), the backfill state may not be in the drain's admitted set, or the per-pass budget may exit before making progress. Note playhead-bbut records a drainEligible busy-spin under DB write-lock, which may be related.

REMINDER FROM MEMORY (project_backfill_stall_bgtask_2026-07-22): an earlier 'analysis stalled' report was NOT a code bug — iOS granted ~0 discretionary BGTask windows. Rule that out FIRST for this instance before chasing code, because the signature can look identical. The distinguishing evidence here is that foreground playback sessions did occur (banner_tallies shows two sessions on this asset) and glo9 is supposed to drain during playback, so a foreground drain should have run.
=== DEMOTED P0 -> P1 on 2026-07-29, and WHY — read before acting on this bead ===
This is NOT a judgement that the problem is small. It is a judgement that this bead may be describing a SYMPTOM.

playhead-8ysk measured, from six days of scheduler_events on Dan's device: 147 analysis jobs acquired, 9 finalized. A pipeline where jobs overwhelmingly fail or are preempted before finalizing leaves exactly the debris this bead describes — assets parked mid-analysis, terminal states declared over partial work, coverage watermarks that never advance.

So the instruction is: DO NOT start work here until 8ysk lands, and when it does, RE-MEASURE against a fresh device pull before writing any code. Use scripts/coverage-audit.sh against a newly pulled analysis.sqlite. If the shape this bead describes has evaporated, close it and say so. If it persists, it is a real independent defect and should be promoted back to P0 with the new measurement attached.

Dan approved this reordering on 2026-07-29 after the dogfood audit that produced 8ysk.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause established with evidence, and BGTask starvation explicitly ruled in or out before any code change. An asset with a complete transcript and an incomplete semantic scan is drained to completion, or its failure to drain is surfaced rather than silent. Dan's asset 820134BF (transcript 2113/2113, scan 984/2113, state backfill) is the fixture. A regression covers the specific shape 'transcript complete + scan incomplete + state backfill' since that is the shape both closed beads missed. Verify against the real device database, not only a synthetic fixture.

title: completeFull is declared on transcript/feature coverage while the semantic ad scan reached 3-40% — the asset is then never revisited
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-28 in Dan's dogfood analysis.sqlite pulled off the device. This is the primary cause of Dan's stated #1 problem: 'analysis not reaching where it needs to in time'.

THE EVIDENCE — assets whose analysisState is 'completeFull', with the terminalReason the code itself wrote:

  asset     dur    transcriptEnd  confirmedAdEnd  semanticScanReach  terminalReason
  B10C7BC8  3468s  3466s          1911s (55%)     90s  = 3%          'full coverage: transcript 0.999, feature 1.000'
  41E69CB2  3170s  3170s          1888s (60%)     670s = 21%         'full coverage: transcript 1.000, feature 1.000'
  8FECFDDE  3578s  3576s          3538s (99%)     1426s= 40%         'full coverage: transcript 0.999, feature 1.000'

The terminalReason string is the confession: completion is computed from TRANSCRIPT and FEATURE coverage ratios only. Neither term is the semantic ad scan. So an asset can be declared fully analysed having had 3% of its audio examined for ads — and because completeFull is terminal, no backfill or drain pass will ever return to it.

AGGREGATE (assets over 15 minutes, n=26): exactly ONE reached >=95% semantic scan coverage. TWENTY-TWO of 26 are under 25%. So roughly 85% of Dan's library has had less than a quarter of its audio semantically examined for ads.

WHY THIS OUTRANKS THE DETECTION-QUALITY WORK: every prompt, scorer, fusion and threshold change we have made optimizes a stage that, in production, only ever sees 10-25% of the audio. Recall measured against a corpus where the scan DID run is not the recall Dan experiences. This is a denominator bug and it silently discounts all downstream quality work.

NOTE the distinct sibling failure: Dan's audited episode 820134BF is NOT completeFull — it is stuck in 'backfill' at 47% scan with a 100% transcript. That is a separate drain/resumption failure; see the companion bead. Do not conflate them: one declares victory early, the other never finishes.

WHAT TO ESTABLISH FIRST (do not assume the fix): find where analysisState is promoted to completeFull and which watermarks feed the ratio. Determine whether the semantic scan has a coverage watermark that COULD participate (confirmedAdCoverageEndTime is populated and is clearly lower than transcript on every row above, so a signal exists). Then decide with Dan whether completeFull should require ad-scan coverage, or whether a new state is needed to distinguish 'transcript done' from 'ads analysed'.
=== DEMOTED P0 -> P1 on 2026-07-29, and WHY — read before acting on this bead ===
This is NOT a judgement that the problem is small. It is a judgement that this bead may be describing a SYMPTOM.

playhead-8ysk measured, from six days of scheduler_events on Dan's device: 147 analysis jobs acquired, 9 finalized. A pipeline where jobs overwhelmingly fail or are preempted before finalizing leaves exactly the debris this bead describes — assets parked mid-analysis, terminal states declared over partial work, coverage watermarks that never advance.

So the instruction is: DO NOT start work here until 8ysk lands, and when it does, RE-MEASURE against a fresh device pull before writing any code. Use scripts/coverage-audit.sh against a newly pulled analysis.sqlite. If the shape this bead describes has evaporated, close it and say so. If it persists, it is a real independent defect and should be promoted back to P0 with the new measurement attached.

Dan approved this reordering on 2026-07-29 after the dogfood audit that produced 8ysk.
acceptance_criteria: The promotion site for completeFull is identified by tracing. An asset cannot reach a terminal, never-revisited state while its semantic ad-scan coverage is materially below its transcript coverage. Dan's three measured assets (B10C7BC8 3%, 41E69CB2 21%, 8FECFDDE 40%) are used as fixtures and would not be declared complete under the new rule. Assets already wrongly marked completeFull are re-openable — a migration or re-evaluation path exists, since leaving them terminal preserves the bug for Dan's existing library. Prove the change does not simply stall assets forever: there must still be a defined exit.

title: Acoustic-only segments must earn their banner card: raise the promotion bar without removing the path
description:
DAN'S DECISION, 2026-07-28: keep surfacing acoustic-only (Tier-1-only) segments as banner cards, but make them much harder to earn. Explicitly REJECTED suppressing the path, because over the 75-90% of audio the semantic scan never reaches (see playhead-gqx4/i7qe) this is the only detector running, and losing it would trade false positives for silence. This bead is therefore a CALIBRATION, not a removal. Do not reverse playhead-0usd; tune it.

THE PRODUCER (traced 2026-07-28, all citations verified):
AdDetectionService.swift:10695-10727 constructs every one of these rows. Bounds are 30s-quantized because Tier 1 slices on a fixed grid anchored at 0 (tier1DefaultWindowSeconds = 30.0, AdDetectionService.swift:3193; makeTier1Slots :3305-3322) and SegmentAggregator.materialize (SegmentAggregator.swift:554-570) copies slot edges verbatim. USE THIS AS A DIAGNOSTIC: a 30-aligned window PROVES zero Tier 2 lexical windows participated (Tier 2 candidates are 2s wide, SegmentAggregator.swift:32-37). Any lexical contribution drags an edge off the grid.

WHY THE SCORES CLUSTER AT 0.41-0.43: the Tier 1 synthetic candidate hardcodes confidence: 0.0 (AdDetectionService.swift:3347-3360), which zeroes the LARGEST classifier weight (lexical = 0.40, ClassifierService.swift:355-372). What remains is rmsDrop/spectralChange/speakerChange (quantized) plus a music term that saturates for ~93% of speech candidates (ClassifierService.swift:170-172, 249-262). rawScore for ordinary speech lands ~0.10-0.22, sigmoid ~0.23-0.44 — straddling the promotion floor. Scores are then hard-floored at 0.40 (promotionThreshold) and hard-ceilinged at 0.55 (autoSkipThreshold), so 0.41-0.43 is simply the mass just above the floor. THE IMPLICATION: today's threshold sits inside the noise distribution of ordinary conversation. That is the thing to fix.

THE KNOBS (SegmentAggregator.swift:188-198 unless noted):
  promotionThreshold      0.40   — currently inside the speech noise band
  minAdDurationSeconds    30.0   — one slot; no real ad is one slot
  N-corroboration rule           — the aggregator requires N=2
  boundarySingletonPromotedSegments (AdDetectionService.swift:11104-11178) — BYPASSES corroboration entirely, returns promoted: true UNCONDITIONALLY above a 0.40 floor, for slots within 120s of start / 180s of end.
  InventorySanityFilter (SkipOrchestrator.swift:2131-2147) — has a .tooEarly rule that would already reject start=0 rows; check whether it is actually enabled on this path.

RECOMMENDED SHAPE — ASYMMETRIC BY POSITION, and here is the evidence for it. Dan's two DENIED windows were 300-330 and 1800-1950, both MID-EPISODE, both from the SegmentAggregator branch, and he described both as 'in the middle of the host/guest interchange'. His 0/30/60/90 windows come from the boundary-singleton branch and he did NOT complain about those. Podcast ad load is structurally concentrated at pre-roll, mid-roll breaks and post-roll, so an acoustic blip mid-conversation is far likelier to be false than one at a boundary. Tighten mid-episode promotion substantially; keep boundary promotion permissive. This is a hypothesis to TEST, not a conclusion — measure it.

MEASUREMENT IS MANDATORY AND IS THE HARD PART. Threshold tuning without held-out validation is how this repo has been burned before: project_fm_prompt_program records that a curated eval looked excellent and the held-out set proved it OVERFIT. Requirements:
 - Quantify what this path currently contributes BEFORE changing anything: over the existing corpus, how many true ads are caught ONLY by acoustic-only segments (i.e. would be lost entirely), and what is its standalone precision? Dan is trading precision for that recall and cannot judge the trade without the number.
 - Report precision AND recall at each candidate threshold, not just precision. The whole point of his decision is preserving recall.
 - Validate on held-out shows, not the tuning set. Coordinate with playhead-xdh7 (corpus growth, the activation blocker).
 - Segment results by position (pre-roll / mid-roll / post-roll) since the recommended fix is positional.

INTERACTION — DO NOT TUNE BEFORE READING THIS. playhead-pggn is a confidence-dilution defect in the SAME aggregator: sub-continuation trailing windows are counted in the score denominator but excluded from the reported extent, biasing scores DOWNWARD on segments that have a quiet lead-out. Some windows sitting at 0.41-0.43 may be true detections pushed down by their own tail. Tuning the threshold up before fixing pggn would therefore discard real ads for the wrong reason. Establish the interaction between the two before committing to a number.

ALSO IN SCOPE, cheap and clarifying: AdBoundaryState.segmentAggregated is written at AdDetectionService.swift:10702 and read by NOTHING in the app target. It is the one honest 'this window has no evidence' discriminator and it is inert. Wire it, or whatever replaces it, so downstream consumers (and any future gate) can distinguish an acoustic-only card from a verified one. Note AdBannerView.swift:1488-1492 already guards banner COPY on metadataSource != 'none' — the UI knows the row has no metadata and shows a card anyway.

THREE GREEN TESTS PIN CURRENT BEHAVIOR and will need updating, not deleting: SegmentAggregatorWiringTests.swift df5c1832AggregatorPromotesSingleFusedWindow (:106), boundarySingletonTier1CandidatesPersistMarkOnly (:280), boundarySingletonHighScoreTier1CandidatesStayMarkOnly (:325). They encode 0usd's intent, which Dan has chosen to keep — so they should be retuned to the new bar, and a test asserting an acoustic-only card can still be earned must survive.
=== DEMOTED P0 -> P1 on 2026-07-29, and WHY — Dan approved after the dogfood audit ===
The justification for keeping this path alive, and for making it P0, was Dan's decision that acoustic-only segments are the ONLY detector operating over the 75-90% of audio the semantic scan never reaches. That premise weakened materially on 2026-07-29 for two measured reasons:

1. REDIFF NOW WORKS. Day-0 rediff minted its first real byte-exact ad window on Dan's device (playhead-p70f): 2 B-copies fetched, 1 accepted, 1 divergent slot, exit "marked", rotated_count 1. It also has NO TIME GATE — the 24h figure applies only to the lagged sweep, and the xsdz16 spike's "0/10 at 10 seconds" varied elapsed time when the axis that matters is request context. So a listener CAN be served deterministic ad boundaries minutes after download. The high-certainty lane is alive, which reduces how much weight the evidence-free acoustic path has to carry.

2. THE UNSCANNED FRACTION IS A BUG, NOT A CONSTANT. playhead-8ysk measured 147 jobs acquired against 9 finalized. The reason 75-90% of audio goes unscanned is that analysis jobs almost never complete — not that scanning is inherently unreachable. Calibrating a threshold against today's coverage would tune against a denominator that is about to change, and the tuning would have to be redone.

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE: Dan's decision stands. Do NOT remove the acoustic path. This bead is still a CALIBRATION, not a suppression. The demotion is about ORDER, not about whether it happens.

BLOCKED ON, in order: playhead-8ysk (so coverage is real before a threshold is set against it), then playhead-pggn (the confidence-dilution defect biases these exact scores DOWNWARD, so raising the bar first would discard true detections for the wrong reason), then playhead-xdh7 (corpus, so validation is held-out rather than overfit — this repo has already been burned by a curated eval that looked excellent and did not generalize).
acceptance_criteria: Current contribution of the acoustic-only path is MEASURED before any threshold moves: standalone precision, and the count of true ads it alone catches. Precision and recall are both reported at each candidate threshold. Validation is on held-out shows, not the tuning set. Results are segmented by position (pre/mid/post-roll), and the positional-asymmetry hypothesis is confirmed or refuted with data rather than assumed. Dan's two denied windows (300-330 and 1800-1950 on asset 820134BF, both mid-conversation) no longer promote. Acoustic-only cards are still earnable at boundaries — the path is NOT removed, per Dan's explicit decision. Interaction with playhead-pggn is established before a threshold is fixed.
