AdBoundaryState.segmentAggregated (or a successor) is consumed by something rather than written and ignored. The three SegmentAggregatorWiringTests are retuned, not deleted, and at least one still asserts a legitimate acoustic-only promotion.
notes:
=== THE pggn INTERACTION IS ESTABLISHED (2026-08-03, playhead-pggn merged) ===
This bead's acceptance requires "Interaction with playhead-pggn is established before a threshold is fixed." Here it is, so this blocker is discharged.

WHAT pggn CHANGED. A trailing below-continuation window used to land in `weightedScoreSum` AND in the `totalDuration` denominator while the emitted `endTime` stayed snapped to `lastQualifyingEndTime`. The invariant now shipped is (a): no region outside `[startTime, endTime]` contributes to `segmentScore`. Geometry is byte-identical; only the score and `windowCount` moved.

THE DIRECTION, WHICH IS WHAT THIS BEAD NEEDS. The correction is upward on every segment this bead can see, and that is provable rather than sampled: mu_old is a weighted average of mu_new and the dropped tail's mean, so mu_new can only fall below mu_old when it is already below the tail — and every tail window is under `continuationThreshold` (0.28), hence under `promotionThreshold` (0.40). A segment whose score can FALL is a segment neither run would promote. Measured across ~300k segments in five populations plus 3M unconstrained fuzz streams: score DOWN = 0, everywhere.

SO THE 0.41-0.43 DIAGNOSIS IN THIS BEAD'S BODY IS NOW PARTLY STALE. That band was described as "the mass just above the 0.40 floor". Part of that mass was segments diluted by their own lead-out. After pggn the same acoustic evidence reads higher: in the Tier-1-grid population the count of promoted segments rose 3,511 -> 5,474 and the count at >=0.55 rose 18 -> 255. RE-MEASURE THE DISTRIBUTION BEFORE PICKING A NUMBER — a threshold fitted to the pre-pggn histogram would be fitted to a bias.

DIRECTION OF THE BIAS FOR CALIBRATION PURPOSES: pggn RAISES acoustic-only scores, so the population this bead wants to tighten got LARGER, not smaller. Dan's two denied windows (300-330, 1800-1950 on asset 820134BF) are mid-episode acoustic-only segments; if either had a quiet lead-out its score is now higher than when he denied it. Check that before assuming the same threshold move suffices.

WHAT DID NOT CHANGE. Nothing was admitted to auto-skip. `runSegmentAggregation` hardcodes `extentSupport = .unanchored` and playhead-bllt (#339) demotes every `autoSkip` verdict on this producer to `markOnly` unconditionally, at any score. The 0.55 crossings are crossings of the gate's INTERNAL threshold only. The admission that actually moved is at 0.40, where `promotionThreshold` and `AutoSkipPrecisionGateConfig.uiCandidateThreshold` coincide — i.e. more markOnly MARKER rows, which is exactly the population this bead is about.

ALSO RELEVANT TO THE 30-ALIGNED DIAGNOSTIC THIS BEAD RELIES ON. playhead-eqo8 was filed out of the same investigation: `ingestIntoOpenSegment` assigns `lastQualifyingEndTime` where `openSegment` MAXes it, so on overlapping Tier-1/Tier-2 input the reported extent can move BACKWARDS. That does not affect 30-aligned rows (a 30-aligned window still proves zero Tier-2 participation), but it does mean an OFF-grid row's end edge may be narrower than the evidence supported. If this bead segments results by position using edge geometry, read eqo8 first.

FULL WRITE-UP: docs/investigations/playhead-pggn-score-extent-coherence.md — populations, both directions, the constructed downward witness, and what corpus data does not exist.

title: Repeat 'hearing an ad' on an already-corrected span is silently deduped — reads as broken
description:
Found 2026-07-28 on the dogfood build (add2f623) by Dan, and CONFIRMED IN THE DEVICE DATABASE — it happened twice in one episode.

SYMPTOM (Dan's words): 'hitting hearing an ad didn't work after I had already hit once and skipped part.'

EVIDENCE from analysis.sqlite pulled off the phone, correction_events:
- row at createdAt 1785264176, scope exactTimeSpan:...:0.000:33.750, submissionCount=2, lastSeenAt-firstSeenAt=9s
- row at createdAt 1785265253, scope exactTimeSpan:...:2046.000:2084.500, submissionCount=2, lastSeenAt-firstSeenAt=5s
Both show a SECOND press within seconds of the first, folded into the existing row by the correctionIdentityKey dedupe rather than creating a new correction.

THE DEDUPE IS CORRECT. Re-reporting the same span must not mint a duplicate correction — that is the identity-key behaviour the o4qr / 1mq1.2.1 work deliberately built. THE DEFECT IS THE SILENCE: the listener gets no acknowledgement distinguishing 'already recorded — got it' from 'your tap did nothing'. Having skipped part of the ad in between, Dan reasonably expected the second press to register something new, and the absence of any response read as a broken button.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: this is the exact gesture Phase 2 Trust is built on — 'fixing Playhead's mistake takes one tap' (playhead-1mq1.2). A tap that silently no-ops teaches the listener the correction UI is unreliable, which is worse than the original miss. It also suppresses signal: a listener who believes the button is broken stops pressing it, and these are precisely the reports that would close the coverage gap.

FIX SHAPE (product decision inside it — do not guess): the listener needs feedback on a deduped submission. Options: (a) acknowledge identically to a fresh correction ('Got it — we'll skip this next time'), which is honest since the report WAS received; (b) acknowledge differently ('Already noted'), which is more truthful but may read as a scolding; (c) treat a repeat press at a DIFFERENT playhead position inside the same window as a request to EXTEND the span rather than re-report it — the most useful reading, since Dan had skipped forward and was arguably marking more ad. Note (c) is a real feature, not a message change.

RELATED SIGNAL FROM THE SAME SESSION, worth its own analysis: 5 falseNegative reports (0-33.7, 34.2-59.8, 2046-2084, 2052-2112) and 2 bannerSuggestionDenied (300-330, 1800-1950) in ONE episode. The misses cluster at 0-60s (an entirely uncaught pre-roll pod) and 2046-2112s where a manualVeto at 2044.5-2048.8 sits between two misses — the boundary-collapse signature playhead-4xqf describes.
acceptance_criteria: A repeat 'hearing an ad' on an already-corrected span produces visible acknowledgement rather than silence. The chosen semantics (acknowledge-same / acknowledge-different / extend-the-span) is decided deliberately and recorded. A regression drives two submissions of the same span and asserts the second produces user-visible feedback, with submissionCount still incrementing rather than minting a duplicate row.

title: Injection-wait timeout starves on the actor it must resume: unarmed BGTask expiration window reopens
description:
Found by playhead-c25o, confirmed against current main by playhead-8m2w (which chose NOT to fold it in — see WHY IT IS ITS OWN BEAD below).

SITE. BackgroundProcessingService.handlePreAnalysisRecovery (:1696) awaits awaitPreAnalysisServicesInjected() at :1743 but does not install task.expirationHandler until :1854. Verified 2026-07-28: c25o did not change this ordering (it fixed the getPendingTaskRequests bridge at :156 and armed expiration in a different handler).

THE DEFECT. That await IS bounded — but only by a hand-rolled timer at :596-602 whose Task must hop BACK ONTO the BackgroundProcessingService actor to run timeoutInjectionWaiter(slot:) (:627) and resume the parked waiter. A busy or wedged actor therefore starves its own timeout, the waiter parks unboundedly, and the unarmed-expiration window reopens: no setTaskCompleted, no expirationHandler, so iOS terminates the process and penalises future scheduling. Strictly weaker than Playhead/Support/BoundedContinuation.swift, which arms its timer on a nonisolated unstructured Task precisely to avoid this — see the KEEP THIS METHOD NONISOLATED comment on armTimeout.

WHY IT IS ITS OWN BEAD (not a tail on 8m2w). withBoundedCheckedContinuation cannot be dropped in here. Its \`body\` closure runs OUTSIDE the caller's actor isolation — the helper is a nonisolated async function with no \`isolation:\` parameter — but the body at this site must do two actor-isolated things: re-check analysisJobReconciler (the race the comment at :604-606 documents) and append to pendingInjectionWaiters. Adoption therefore requires one of:

  (a) Adding \`isolation: isolated (any Actor)? = #isolation\` to the shared helper. That changes where body/attach/armTimeout run for the EXISTING c25o call site too, which re-opens the exact starvation question that file's armTimeout doc-comment is dedicated to, and needs c25o's 200-iteration jittered race test re-run against the new signature. A shared-primitive API change, not a drive-by.
  (b) Moving pendingInjectionWaiters off the actor into a lock-protected registry — a rewrite of playhead-8u3i's waiter mechanism, which carries dedicated test seams (triggerInjectionWaitTimeoutForTesting :360, playhead-hv73, playhead-vsot notifyInjectionWaiterObserversForTesting) and tests asserting the current timeout mechanics.

  (c) A third option, which is what 8m2w used at both of ITS sites and is probably the cheapest here: keep the waiter list on the actor and make ACTOR ISOLATION the once guard, but arm the timeout so it does not need the actor to fire. Note WaiterSlot (:563) is already the right shape for this.

Either way it is a design decision plus test churn, and half-doing it is worse than leaving it.

ACCEPTANCE. The injection wait is bounded by a timer that cannot be starved by the BackgroundProcessingService actor it must resume. A test proves a waiter parked in awaitPreAnalysisServicesInjected resumes on timeout while the actor is occupied. No second hand-written once-guard is introduced (double-resuming a CheckedContinuation traps).

Related: playhead-xc6b (failure class), playhead-c25o (the helper), playhead-8m2w (siblings 2 and 3 of 4), playhead-2gka (PlayheadRuntime.swift:33, the fourth site).

Still present on `bead/playhead-mk6z` (HEAD 8780b540). Line numbers have moved since

title: Per-episode banner tally: count cards without watching for them
description:
Dan 2026-07-28, for the dogfood audit: banner cards sometimes fire fast one after another, so counting them by hand during a listening session is unreliable — and the count is the single number the playhead-zkcg decision depends on.

WHAT EXISTS ALREADY (do not rebuild): playhead-jw63.1 landed BannerFeedbackCounterStore, and playhead-jw63.3's five analytics counters include banners_shown/confirmed/denied. But that counter is an AGGREGATE keyed by episode-duration cohort, not per-episode, and it is local-only with the upload gate deliberately shut. The number exists; it is neither per-episode nor readable.

WHAT TO ADD — two surfaces, because they answer different questions:
1. LIVE, via os_log. One breadcrumb per banner presentation carrying: a running per-episode index (1, 2, 3...), the eligibility tier that produced it (markOnly vs suggest vs autoSkip), and the span start/end. Then Console.app with a filter gives a live count and a timeline, and the index means fast consecutive cards are still individually attributable. Reset the index on beginEpisode.
2. AFTER THE FACT, via the diagnostics bundle. A per-episode tally (episode reference, total cards, breakdown by tier) so a session can be audited from an exported bundle rather than requiring Console to have been open. The jw63.5 feedback channel already emails that bundle.

PRIVACY: the os_log breadcrumb is LOCAL and may name the episode plainly, but use the established privacy annotations rather than inventing a convention — check how existing os_log call sites in SkipOrchestrator mark public vs private. The DIAGNOSTICS BUNDLE is an egress surface and the legal checklist applies: use the SAME salted episode reference the bundle already uses (see the jw63.5 envelope and playhead-jw63.4's stability records), never an episode title or feed URL. If in doubt, put less in the bundle and more in the log.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS AUDIT: playhead-2350 demotes unanchored spans to markOnly, markOnly routes to the suggest tier, and the suggest tier emits a card. Since almost no dogfood span carries a rediff slot or stinger snap, this may approach one card per detection — which would cut against 'Respect your attention' and reshape Phase 2. Right now that is a hypothesis nobody can measure. The tally converts it into a number, and it stays useful afterwards as the regression signal if banner volume ever creeps.

SCOPE DISCIPLINE: this is instrumentation, not a behaviour change. Do not alter when a banner is presented, what tier it gets, or any dismissal timing. If the work reveals that the presentation seam is a poor place to count from (e.g. re-presentation after a dismissal would double-count), say so and count where it is honest rather than where it is convenient.
acceptance_criteria: A listener can determine banner cards per episode two ways without manual tallying: live from Console.app via a per-banner os_log breadcrumb carrying a running per-episode index, tier, and span; and after the fact from an exported diagnostics bundle carrying a per-episode total with a per-tier breakdown. The index resets per episode. No behaviour changes — presentation, tier assignment, and dismissal timing are untouched, pinned by a test. The bundle surface uses the existing salted episode reference and carries no title, feed URL, or transcript text, proven by a sentinel test as playhead-jw63.4 did. Re-presentation of the same span does not double-count, or the semantics are documented if it does.
close_reason: Merged to main as add2f623. Two surfaces: a live os_log .notice per on-screen banner presentation (running per-episode index, tier, span, episode, window id) and a banner_tallies array on the diagnostics bundle with the auto-skipped/suggest split. COUNTED AT THE ON-SCREEN BOUNDARY (AdBannerQueue.recordBannerShown), NOT at emission — emissions get de-duplicated, coalesced, host-scope-rejected and discarded on teardown, so an emission count would OVERSTATE what the listener saw. Re-presentation is precise: the same visible presentation being re-notified does not double-count, but a card dismissed and genuinely re-presented does, deliberately. Self-review caught a HIGH issue: the checked-in legal fixture is returned whenever it exists, so adding a field left every item-(a) audit running against a shape that no longer ships AND left the artifact offered to legal misrepresenting the bundle — and deleting the fixture is not an escape hatch because they are BUILD RESOURCES (a missing file fails the build). Privacy proven by a sentinel driving the real store through the real encoder with an episode id containing a title, feed URL and transcript fragment, asserting none survive plus rows.count==1 so it cannot pass by counting nothing. No behaviour change pinned by an instrumented-vs-uninstrumented queue comparison across current card, tier, dwell, both impression-guard returns, post-dismiss state and deferred slide-in scheduling. Budget 5/10. CONSOLE FILTER for the audit: subsystem:com.playhead category:BannerTally — highest index= is the count.

title: PlaybackLifecycleMutex.acquire has no cancellation path and no defer-guaranteed release; shutdown() joins it
description:
Found 2026-07-28 by the continuation audit. Fourth of four AT-RISK continuation sites.

SITE: PlayheadRuntime.swift:33, PlaybackLifecycleMutex.acquire — a FIFO mutex permit, resumed only by release() from the current holder.

THE SHAPE: playEpisode (:3521) and stopPlayback (:4033) each cancel() the previous lifecycle task, spawn a new one that does await mutex.acquire() ... await mutex.release(), then await task.value (:3543 / :4054). shutdown() cancels at :3247 AND JOINS AT :3273. Release is written manually on all three exits (:3530, :3540 / :4042, :4051) — there is NO defer.

VERIFIED vs INFERRED: performPlayEpisode is non-throwing, so a cancellation cannot skip the manual release — the hang requires the holder's body to never return (INFERRED). What IS certain (READ): cancel() on a task parked in acquire() provably does nothing, because there is no cancellation handler. So any stall inside the holder propagates straight into a shutdown() that never returns, and every subsequent play/stop queues behind it on the MainActor transport.

WHY IT MATTERS DESPITE LOW LIKELIHOOD: RuntimeShutdownLifecycleTests exists because this path has bitten before, and a wedge here takes the MainActor playback transport with it.

FIX: give the mutex a withLock-style SCOPED api so release is structurally guaranteed rather than manually written at three exits, and make acquire() cancellation-aware — withTaskCancellationHandler that removes this waiter from  and resumes it on cancel, with the waiter then checking Task.isCancelled and skipping the body. Because the waiter array is actor state, removal must hop to the actor; use the one-shot resolver pattern already proven at LanePreemptionCoordinator.swift:143-158. CHEAPEST PARTIAL HARDENING if the full fix is too invasive: bound shutdown()'s join at :3273 rather than waiting unconditionally.

Related: playhead-xc6b, the P0 BGTask sibling, the transcript-side pair.
acceptance_criteria: acquire() is cancellation-aware: a cancelled waiter leaves the queue and does not run the guarded body. Release is structurally guaranteed by a scoped API rather than three manual call sites. shutdown() cannot wait unconditionally on a wedged holder. A test proves a cancelled waiter unblocks and that shutdown() completes when a holder stalls.
notes:
TEXT REPAIR (2026-07-28): the FIX paragraph above lost a word to shell interpretation — it should read 'removes this waiter from the waiters array and resumes it on cancel'. The waiters array is the actor-isolated queue inside PlaybackLifecycleMutex (PlayheadRuntime.swift ~:33). No other text was affected.
2026-07-28: ADOPT THE HELPER. playhead-c25o (merged ae966824) added Playhead/Support/BoundedContinuation.swift with a proven once-guard — use it rather than hand-rolling. Note this bead ALSO needs the structural release fix (a scoped withLock-style API replacing three manual release sites); the helper solves the cancellation half, not the release half. c25o's precedent for the cheap partial hardening still applies: bounding shutdown()'s join at :3273 is worth doing even if the full scoped-API change is deferred.

title: Process-wide ASR gate and shard-wait can park forever: one stuck Speech call wedges all transcription
description:
Found 2026-07-28 by the continuation audit (see the P0 sibling for the BGTask instance). Two transcript-side sites of the same class, paired because the SAME amplifier turns either into a whole-subsystem stall.

SITE A — TranscriptEngine.swift:328, SpeechRecognitionRequestGate.acquire. requestGate is a private static let (:370) — ONE gate for the entire process. withExclusiveAccess (:310-329) is correct in isolation (release runs on both success and catch paths), but operation() is an Apple Speech call (detectVoiceActivity, transcribe). If one such call never returns, isHeld stays true forever and every waiter — including cancelled ones — stays parked. No timeout on the holder, no cancellation path for waiters. CONSEQUENCE: a single stuck Speech call wedges ALL transcription in the app, permanently, with no recovery short of an app restart.
FIX (two independent changes): (a) withTaskCancellationHandler on acquire() so a cancelled waiter leaves the queue and withExclusiveAccess throws CancellationError — it must NOT call release() in that case, since it never acquired; (b) a watchdog on the HOLDER: race operation() against a generous deadline so a wedged Speech call degrades one shard instead of the whole app's ASR.

SITE B — TranscriptEngineService.swift:669, waitForMoreShards. The drain loop (:553) checks Task.isCancelled at :590, ONE LINE before parking at :591 — a check-then-park race where a cancel landing in that window parks anyway. Well-defended today: every activeTask?.cancel() in the file is paired with resumeAllAppendWaiters() (:210->232, :362->375, :427->444), and AnalysisCoordinator.cancelPipeline calls transcriptEngine.stop() after cancelling shardConsumerTask. RESIDUAL HAZARD: a producer that dies silently — shardConsumerTask stalling inside featureService.extractAndPersist (:1854) so finishAppending (:1875) is never reached — with no stop() following.
FIX: withTaskCancellationHandler around the park, resuming this waiter directly. Closes the check-then-park race AND removes the dependency on every future cancel site remembering the pairing.

THE AMPLIFIER (why these two matter more than they look): AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:3590 does outcome = try await runTask.value, where runTask wraps jobRunner.run(request), which reaches both sites. The withTaskCancellationHandler at :3572 correctly forwards cancel to runTask — but CANCEL CANNOT UNWIND A PARKED CONTINUATION. So a hang at either site surfaces here as a job loop that never advances: currentRunningTask never clears and NO FURTHER ANALYSIS JOB STARTS. Either transcript-side hang becomes a whole-subsystem stall.

Related: playhead-xc6b (failure class), the P0 BGTask sibling, PlayheadRuntime.swift:33 (the fourth site).
acceptance_criteria: A cancelled waiter on the ASR gate leaves the queue and throws CancellationError without calling release(). A wedged holder is bounded by a watchdog so it degrades one shard rather than all transcription. waitForMoreShards has a cancellation handler that closes the check-then-park race. Tests prove each: a cancelled waiter unblocks, and a never-finishing holder does not wedge a subsequent acquire. Do not change what the Speech call does — only how long it may hold the gate.
notes:
2026-07-28: ADOPT THE HELPER. playhead-c25o (merged ae966824) added Playhead/Support/BoundedContinuation.swift — withBoundedCheckedContinuation(timeout:fallback:onFallback:) — a generic cancellable, timeout-bounded continuation wrapper with a proven once-guard. Use it here rather than hand-rolling; a second hand-written once-guard is a second chance to trap on a double resume, and its lock-under-transition / resume-outside-lock ordering plus the resolve-before-attach phase are both non-obvious and already tested (200-iteration jittered race). Choose the timeout from the TIGHTEST caller, as c25o did, not the most generous one.

ALSO FOUND BY c25o, a THIRD instance of the same shape — worth folding into this bead or filing beside it: handlePreAnalysisRecovery (BackgroundProcessingService.swift:1696) awaits awaitPreAnalysisServicesInjected() at :1743 but does not install task.expirationHandler until :1854. That await IS bounded, but only by a hand-rolled timer at :599-602 whose Task must hop BACK ONTO the BackgroundProcessingService actor to resume the parked waiter — so a busy or wedged actor starves the timeout and the unarmed-expiration window reopens. Strictly weaker than the new helper, which arms its timer on a nonisolated unstructured Task precisely to avoid that starvation. Natural next adoption site.
2026-07-28 IMPLEMENTED on bead/playhead-8m2w (4 commits, head eab45c7a; not merged).

SITE A(a) waiter cancellation (8238dcd1). Cancelled waiter leaves the queue and withExclusiveAccess throws CancellationError with NO release() — it never held the permit, and handing the gate to nobody wedges it permanently. ONCE GUARD IS THE ACTOR, not a second hand-written one: abandon() removes a waiter from the queue BEFORE resolving it and release() only hands off to a waiter still in the queue, so the two paths cannot both resume the same continuation. The Waiter box is the same shape as BackgroundProcessingService.WaiterSlot. Gate made internal (was file-private) so tests use a dedicated instance, not the process-wide one.

SITE A(b) holder watchdog (ebaf6fbf), 120 s. Adopts withBoundedCheckedContinuation for the timer + once-guard. Deadline calibrated from BOTH ends: 4x the 30 s shard duration from below (fires only for a call that stopped progressing, not one slow under thermal/.utility), and well inside AnalysisJobRunner's 300 s transcription-stage budget from above (a ceiling >= 300 s protects nothing — the caller has already given up). KEY DESIGN POINT: cancellation is forwarded into the call and then WAITED OUT; only the hard deadline abandons. Releasing the permit while a cancelled Speech call is still unwinding would reintroduce the exact overlap (SFSpeechErrorDomain Code=16) this gate exists to prevent, and cancellation is a common path. That is why the bounded wait sits in its own unstructured Task — the helper also resolves on cancellation, and an unstructured task does not inherit cancellation.

SITE B shard wait (68d2682a + eab45c7a). withTaskCancellationHandler around the park, resuming via the EXISTING resumeAllAppendWaiters() — it drains the list before resuming and runs on the actor, so actor isolation is already the once guard. Plus a Task.isCancelled check inside the continuation body so an already-cancelled loop never parks, which deletes the hop-ordering argument entirely.

HELPER FIT — the one honest limitation. withBoundedCheckedContinuation could NOT be used for either waiter park: its `body` runs OUTSIDE the caller's actor isolation (nonisolated async fn, no `isolation:` parameter), so it cannot touch `waiters` / `appendWaiters`. It fits the holder watchdog perfectly (body only spawns a task). At both waiter sites actor isolation replaced it as the once guard — no second hand-written guard was introduced anywhere.

TESTS: 12 new (9 gate, 3 shard-wait). Each is written so a REGRESSION HANGS rather than mis-asserts. Two DEBUG-only seams on TranscriptEngineService, no production callers: activeTaskForTesting() and appendWaiterCountForTesting. The second is LOAD-BEARING — the first version of the Site B tests used an empty shard list, which the loop early-returns on, so they never reached the park and passed against the bug; the waiter-count probe turned that into a 60 s hang and exposed it.

GATE: lint clean. Full PlayheadFastTests 8946 passed / 52 failed, all in 4 documented load-sensitive suites (pd0q + gy2s pipeline-stall, shpy BG-telemetry, DelegateWorkJournal) at 100-119 s with "Time limit was exceeded: 60.000 seconds". Zero transcript/speech failures, zero sub-second failures. All 4 suites re-run IN ISOLATION: 22 tests pass in 5.4 s. Load starvation, not a regression.

THIRD SITE NOT ADOPTED — filed as playhead-jaa2 (P1) with the precise reason: the helper cannot be dropped into awaitPreAnalysisServicesInjected for the same actor-isolation reason, so adoption needs either an `isolation:` parameter on the SHARED helper (re-opens c25o's starvation question and needs its 200-iteration race test re-run) or a rewrite of playhead-8u3i's waiter mechanism with its live test seams. Design decision + test churn, not a tail. Confirmed still live on current main: await at :1743, expirationHandler at :1854.

title: PerfGate migration is the WRONG fix: the load-sensitive suites are behavioural, not measurement
description:
Analysis for playhead-buge, 2026-07-28, two independent readers. VERDICT: playhead-buge AS FRAMED IS THE WRONG FIX. Do not migrate these suites to PerfGate.

FINDING: across the two largest candidate files (PlaybackServiceActorTests, RuntimeShutdownLifecycleTests) — 50 tests — the category split is ZERO measurement, ZERO timing-is-the-contract, and FIFTY behavioural-with-an-incidental-timeout. Neither file contains a single latency assertion, Task.sleep, pollUntil, ContinuousClock, or Date()-elapsed computation. They assert STATE (a status observed, a row flipped, a count) and merely use a wall-clock deadline as their synchronisation primitive. PerfGate exists for tests whose assertion is meaningless under load; these assertions are perfectly valid under load — only the DEADLINE is too short. Migrating them would leave the behaviour unverified in the default gate to fix a problem that is not the one PerfGate solves.

ROOT CAUSE of the load sensitivity, independently reached by both readers: @PlaybackServiceActor is a single process-wide serial executor (PlaybackTransport.swift:33-36) shared by both files, and RuntimeShutdownLifecycleTests additionally serialises all 18 of its tests on @MainActor. Under a saturated gate the queue behind that executor is what blows the deadline — not the code under test.

THE CORRECTED FIX — cheap, zero coverage loss, strictly more protective than migration:
Tier 1 (~1-2 hours): give every test a FINITE hang backstop, two-sided. RAISE the deadline where a 1-minute .timeLimit exists; ADD .timeLimit(.minutes(3)) where NONE exists. The backstop coverage is currently inverted from what one would assume: 38 of the 50 tests have NO .timeLimit at all, and many await continuation gates or AsyncStream iterators with no deadline of any kind (PlaybackServiceActorTests.swift:163, 368, 407, 459, 532, 585, 641, 866, 869; RuntimeShutdownLifecycleTests.swift:878, 969, 1070, 1097, 1122). A REGRESSION IN THOSE PATHS HANGS THE GATE HOST INDEFINITELY RATHER THAN FAILING A TEST — which is worse than a flake and is happening today.

SEPARATE DEFECTS FOUND, each worth its own treatment:
1. THREE FIXED-YIELD BUDGETS GUARD NEGATIVE ASSERTIONS (RuntimeShutdownLifecycleTests.swift:620-622, PlaybackServiceActorTests.swift:846-848 and :885-887). Under load these FAIL OPEN — the assertion passes VACUOUSLY rather than failing. So these suites are currently WEAKER under load, not merely flakier. Same soundness class as the vacuity work in playhead-ugy4/auz3.
2. TWO TESTS ASSERT NOTHING AT ALL: PlaybackServiceActorTests.simultaneousAccessAndCallbacks (:1108, body ends '_ = loader' at :1146) and interruptionObserverDoesNotCreateRetainCycle (:876, zero #expect — passing means a latch fired). They can only fail by crash or timeout.
3. TEARDOWN HYGIENE: PlaybackService has NO deinit (the only deinit in PlaybackTransport.swift is ProgressiveResourceLoader's at :1649), and MPRemoteCommandCenter.shared() targets are removed only via tearDown() -> removeRemoteCommandTargets() (:348, :1327-1330). 24 of 32 tests in PlaybackServiceActorTests never tear down, each leaving ~8 targets plus a mutation of shared preferredIntervals (:1573) registered for the life of the process. Nuance: leaked closures capture [weak self] and RemoteCommandHandler holds weak service (:1541), so this is unbounded GLOBAL-TOKEN growth, not service retention — which is why the :876 dealloc test still passes. RuntimeShutdownLifecycleTests is by contrast well-behaved (19 of 20 runtimes call shutdown()).
4. A RETAIN CYCLE INSIDE A TEST: RuntimeShutdownLifecycleTests.newestSeekWinsAcrossInEffectSuspension .persistence stage — the handler closure at :954-963 captures runtime STRONGLY while being stored ON runtime, so the runtime and its PlaybackService never deallocate, once per parameter case. Does not affect pass/fail; feeds the leak pile. Same test has a state-ordering race at :987 (persistence.snapshot() == [90] depends on the older handler observing Task.isCancelled at :956, and could observe [90, 90]).

RECOMMENDED ORDER: Tier 1 backstops first (cheap, stops the indefinite hangs). Then the three fail-open yield budgets, since a vacuous pass is worse than a flake. Then teardown hygiene. The two assertion-free tests need a decision — give them assertions or delete them; for those two ONLY, a migration or timeout raise really would leave nothing behind.

playhead-buge should be closed as WONT-FIX-AS-FRAMED with a pointer here, or retitled to this scope.
acceptance_criteria: Every test in the candidate suites has a finite hang backstop (raised where one exists, added where none does), so a regression fails rather than hanging the gate host. The three fail-open yield budgets are replaced with waits that fail closed. A decision is recorded on the two assertion-free tests. Teardown hygiene is addressed or explicitly deferred with reasoning. playhead-buge is closed or retitled so nobody migrates these suites to PerfGate on the original framing.
notes:
2026-07-28 IMPLEMENTED on branch bead/playhead-xc6b (base 89bf541a). Line citations in the analysis were verified against the tree and are accurate; two were off by one line (RemoteCommandHandler weak service is :1540 not :1541, preferredIntervals are :1568/:1577 not :1573) and RuntimeShutdownLifecycleTests:1070 is the closing brace of the held Task, not the await. The COUNTS are all exactly right: 32 + 18 = 50 tests, 12 pre-existing .timeLimit traits (2 + 10), 38 with none, 24 of 32 without teardown.

DONE:
1. BACKSTOPS. 11 one-minute traits raised to 3 minutes; 38 added; plus a suite-level .timeLimit(.minutes(3)) on all 5 suites so future tests inherit one. Per-test traits kept explicitly so coverage is greppable rather than relying on SuiteTrait recursion. No test was exposed as previously-hanging: all 50 pass in 5.3s focused.
2. THREE FAIL-OPEN YIELD BUDGETS replaced with positive-control-plus-barrier, and EACH PROVEN to fail when the guarded behaviour occurs.
3. ASSERTION-FREE TESTS: both KEPT and given real assertions. interruptionObserverDoesNotCreateRetainCycle was under-read by the analysis — it pins a real invariant, and its skipped teardown is correct (teardown joins the observer under test). simultaneousAccessAndCallbacks now requires both concurrent workloads to complete and every snapshot to observe .idle.
4. TEARDOWN HYGIENE: FIXED, not deferred. 22 tests now tear down.
5. Test-local retain cycle fixed with [weak runtime]; the persistence == [90] ordering race closed by waiting for both handler invocations to finish.
6. playhead-buge closed WONT-FIX-AS-FRAMED and retitled.

KEY MEASURED FINDING worth keeping: the intuitive barrier for a NotificationCenter negative — 'post is synchronous, therefore a following actor read is queued behind any live observer' — IS FALSE. Measured with a live observer and an installed item, a single post followed immediately by snapshot() still read the pre-resume state. Resumption of the notification async-sequence is not completed inside post(). The working barrier is a WITNESS subscriber of the same kind on the same executor (postInterruptionUntilWitnessed). Anyone writing a negative assertion about NotificationCenter delivery elsewhere in this repo should reuse that, not the intuition.
2026-07-28 GATE RESULTS + FOLLOW-UPS FOUND.

FULL-GATE EVIDENCE (3 runs, PlayheadFastTests, 8975 tests):
 - main@89bf541a: FAILED, 2 issues — LongFormPlaybackTests + RouteChangeTests, both 'Time limit was exceeded: 60.000 seconds' at 119-121s elapsed.
 - bead/playhead-xc6b (final, dde9adc8+5a08d952): FAILED, 7 issues — ALL in BackgroundProcessingServiceTelemetryTests, none in the two files this bead touched.
 - All 9 PlaybackService*/playhead-7h2 suites PASSED in every branch run.

MAIN IS NOT GREEN UNDER THE FULL GATE ON THIS BOX. The failing population is the documented load-sensitive family and it VARIES RUN TO RUN (an earlier branch run with a review subagent competing for CPU produced 49 issues across SilenceCompressionCoordinator/AnalysisPipelineStall/RouteChange/Interruption/BackgroundProcessing; a clean run produced 7). Anyone gating on the full plan here should expect that and diff the failing SET, not the count.

VALUABLE SIDE-EFFECT: suite wall-clock for the two files under the full gate was 118.7s (PlaybackServiceActor – Isolation) and 124.9s (playhead-7h2). Under the OLD 1-minute limits several of those tests would have tripped in this very run. The raise removed real flakes, it did not merely paper over them. It also gives the repo a MEASURED starvation figure to cite instead of folklore: 60s limits blowing at 119-134s elapsed, on main as well as on the branch.

FOLLOW-UPS WORTH THEIR OWN BEADS:
1. CANCELLATION-AWARE TEST GATES. The .timeLimit backstop reliably bounds the DIAGNOSIS (a named failure) but not always the process: ControlledItemSeek, ControlledSeekSequence, RuntimePlaybackObserverGate, FirstAcceptedRuntimeSeekGate and DeallocLatch all park on withCheckedContinuation with NO cancellation handler, so a body suspended there cannot be forced to unwind when Swift Testing cancels the task. Converting them to withTaskCancellationHandler would make the backstop bound the process too. Not done here — it touches 5 shared primitives and deserves its own change.
2. BackgroundProcessingServiceTelemetryTests IS THE NEXT FAIL-OPEN CANDIDATE, same class as the three fixed here. It passes in ISOLATION in 0.110s and fails under saturation at 96-102s with fire-and-forget telemetry assertions (events.count >= 1, submit != nil), and its recording logger uses a bounded 'try? await Task.sleep(for: timeout)'. Give it a positive-control-plus-barrier wait, not a longer sleep, and do NOT move it to PerfGate — its assertions are behavioural, exactly like these.
3. tearDownOwnsEveryLongLivedResource now DETERMINISTICALLY joins a live, registered NotificationCenter async sequence (the positive control guarantees registration before tearDown). If NotificationCenter.Notifications ever stops honouring cancellation promptly this becomes a deterministic 3-minute stall rather than an occasional flake. Watch-item, not a defect.
close_reason:
Merged to main as 4ab0c897, after one full review round (3 findings, all overclaims in the instrument itself, fixed). CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN NOTES: the tree has 31 of 32 tests tearing down (8 pre-existing + 23 added), not the '22' recorded earlier.

DELIVERED: all 50 tests carry .timeLimit(.minutes(3)) + a suite-level trait so later tests inherit one (11 raised, 38 added — 38 previously had NO deadline, so a regression HUNG THE GATE HOST rather than failing). Three fail-open yield budgets replaced with positive-control-then-barrier, EACH PROVEN by mutation to fail when the guarded behaviour occurs. Both assertion-free tests KEPT with real assertions (one was under-read as vacuous — it pins a real retain-cycle invariant, and its skipped teardown is CORRECT since teardown joins the very observer under test). Teardown fixed, not deferred. Test-local retain cycle + ordering race fixed. playhead-buge closed WONT-FIX-AS-FRAMED.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN STANDING BELIEFS, both measured: (1) 'main is green at 89bf541a' does NOT hold for the full gate on this box — main measures 2-50 failures depending on the run, with the failing SET varying, so gate on the SET not the count; (2) the '~98-131s' starvation range I had been citing across a dozen agent briefs appears NOWHERE in the repo — the measured band is 119-134s, and main's playhead-7h2 suite landed at 134.062s, literally the upper bound.

THE INSTRUCTIVE FAILURE: the implementer's first barrier was WRONG and it found out only because the proof mutation PASSED when it should have failed — it assumed a synchronous center.post orders a following actor read behind a live observer. The review round reproduced this independently: bare post + immediate read passes in 0.025s observing pre-resume state. Without insisting on watching the assertion fail, a barrier that looked correct would have preserved the exact vacuity it was fixing.

HONEST LIMIT, now stated where readers meet it: .timeLimit does NOT unwind every hang — bodies parked on withCheckedContinuation with no cancellation handler cannot be forced to return, so the backstop guarantees a REPORTED NAMED failure, not process recovery. Full gate judged on the failing SET: branch 34 issues vs main 50, same family, all five touched suites passing in both.

title: Unanchored hot-path auto-skips have no last-mile guard: AutoSkipEdgePadding ships OFF
description:
Correctly-framed successor to a concern raised during playhead-2350 and re-diagnosed during playhead-y87g. NOTE THE REFRAMING: 2350's implementer reported this as 'precisionGateLabel's autoSkip literal is broken'. That framing is WRONG and was disproved in y87g — the nil-decode is a documented producer contract whitelisted in three consumers, and nil vs .eligible route identically. Do not chase the label.

THE ACTUAL CONCERN: hot-path rows (runHotPath + the segment-aggregator promotion) are UNANCHORED BY CONSTRUCTION — buildAdWindow never sets the edge-anchor columns. playhead-2350 closed the FUSION path (both edges must carry independent provenance or the span is demoted to markOnly), but the hot path is a SECOND producer that reaches auto-skip eligibility without that gate. The only last-mile per-edge veto is AutoSkipEdgePadding, and AutoSkipEdgePadding.isEnabledByDefault == false (AutoSkipEdgePadding.swift:118) — so it does not run for anyone today.

WHY IT IS NOT A FIRE: this is playhead-98co's deliberate shipped posture, not an accident, and 98co's notes explain why the flag is off — flag-ON auto-skips NOTHING unanchored, which is a large recall change that 98co could not verify at n=44 (2% clip-rate target, per-tier upper bounds 5-39%). So the gap is known and priced; it is simply not written down anywhere as 'the hot path has no edge guard'.

THE DECISION THIS BEAD EXISTS TO FORCE: either (a) extend 2350's presence-vs-extent gate to the hot-path producer so unanchored hot-path rows are demoted to markOnly the way fusion rows now are — consistent, and does not depend on a flag anyone might never flip; or (b) flip AutoSkipEdgePadding on, which is gated on the corpus growth (playhead-xdh7) Dan already decided to wait for (2026-07-28: 'keep both, gated by corpus'); or (c) accept it explicitly and write down why, so the next reader does not rediscover it as a surprise.

(a) is the one that does not depend on a deferred corpus. Note the constraint that governed 2350: any change here must only ever make FEWER things auto-skippable, never more.

Related: playhead-2350 (fusion-path gate), playhead-98co (the padding policy and its off-by-default posture), playhead-y87g (where the label framing was disproved), playhead-qs0d (blocked, would widen auto-skip).
acceptance_criteria: A decision is made among extend-the-2350-gate / flip-the-padding / accept-and-document, and implemented. If the gate is extended, unanchored hot-path rows demote to markOnly with a regression proving a hot-path row with invented edges is not autoSkipEligible, and the change makes strictly fewer things eligible. If accepted as-is, the reasoning is written where a reader of SkipOrchestrator's auto-skip path will find it, not only in a bead.

## QUEUE 2 — EXTENDED to eight (Dan 2026-08-02)

    3nfa(done) -> le02(done) -> bllt -> ug9m -> pggn -> kkzu -> kanf -> 5n8k

**Slots 7 and 8 added on Dan's instruction. Rationale:**

priority 20 (.now lane), but `insertJob` is INSERT OR IGNORE on workKey. If the auto-pipeline
already queued that episode, the user-intent enqueue is a SILENT NO-OP: the row keeps background
priority 0 and the one-shot flag is consumed without promoting. So the tap gives status, not the
promised preemption — and it fails in exactly the case the feature exists for, an
already-queued starving background job. Dan's standing bar is that the work must be finished
BEFORE he presses play; this is a user asking for that explicitly and being ignored.
It sits beside kkzu deliberately: both are the download->analysis path that feeds the
"analyzed before play" population.
NOTE the bead's own judgement: promoting an IN-PROGRESS job is a lease/epoch design decision.
Scope to state='queued' only, never a leased/running row. Coordinate with playhead-glo9.

observer is a `nonisolated(unsafe) static var`; under Swift Testing's in-process parallelism another

which is the shape the triage rule reserves for REAL defects — the >=97s load-flake heuristic does
not apply. So it costs a full triage round every time and looks like a regression in whatever is
under test. Fix direction: per-test scoping (task-local or a confirmation-scoped install that
fails loudly on double-install), not a global that silently interleaves.

Both are device-free and on-box verifiable. Constraint unchanged: Dan is away and cannot install
a build or produce a device pull.
