title: MIXED revert teaches a WEAK signal, not a full false positive (1mq1.2.1 follow-up)
description:
2026-07-28 DAN DECISION on the question playhead-1mq1.2.1 deliberately left open: on a MIXED revert, DOWNGRADE BOTH the per-show trust penalty and the threshold-controller sample to their weak variants.

THE PROBLEM: 1mq1.2.1 fixed the LABEL — a revert whose window contains a real ad no longer writes a whole-span negative. But two effects on the same gesture still fire at FULL strength and still mean 'no ad here': the per-show trust penalty (recordFalseSkipSignal) and the per-show threshold-controller sample. They are per-show scalars rather than span labels, so the implementer left them alone rather than change behaviour unilaterally — but the semantics now disagree with the fix.

WHY IT MATTERS: a width complaint says 'your boundaries were wrong'; a full trust penalty teaches 'you were wrong that there is an ad on this show'. On the THEMOVE fixture the detection was CORRECT — the window merely swallowed 12.7s of show sign-off. Penalising trust there pushes the per-show threshold up, making Playhead MORE conservative about detecting ads on a show where detection is working, i.e. suppressing true positives to punish a boundary error. Boundary errors are systematic (the ~18% width-coverage collapse), so this would fire repeatedly on exactly the shows where detection is healthy.

THE DECISION: weak, not absent. The listener DID revert, so something was wrong and a genuinely over-eager show must still be calibratable — withholding entirely would leave that show uncorrected whenever its errors happen to contain some real ad. recordWeakFalseSkipSignal already exists alongside the full-strength variant, and battery mutation M16 pins the distinction (a silent downgrade of the FULL path is caught), so the two are not interchangeable by accident.

SCOPE:
- On RevertEvidencePartition == MIXED, route the trust penalty through the weak variant and reduce the controller sample correspondingly. CLEAN reverts keep full strength — unchanged.
- Add battery entries pinning BOTH directions: a MIXED revert must not emit the full-strength signal, and a CLEAN revert must not be silently downgraded (the second is the one a future refactor breaks).
- Check whether the controller has a defined reduced sample or whether one must be introduced; if introduced, do NOT change PerShowThresholdController's math, gains or bounds — per playhead-i08e that is off-limits.
- Note the controller is flag-OFF in production (perShowThresholdControlEnabled = false), so its half is latent today; the trust half is live.

Related: playhead-1mq1.2.1 (the label fix and RevertEvidencePartition), playhead-i08e (the controller write path).
acceptance_criteria: A MIXED revert emits the weak trust signal and a reduced controller sample; a CLEAN revert is unchanged at full strength. Both directions are pinned by mutation-battery entries, including the downgrade-a-CLEAN-revert direction. PerShowThresholdController's math, gains and bounds are untouched. A regression uses the THEMOVE sign-off + HAIKS fixture and asserts the show's trust does not take a full-strength penalty for a boundary error.

title: Analytics opt-in toggle in Settings, default ON (jw63.3 follow-up)
description:
2026-07-28 DAN DECISION on the question playhead-jw63.3 deliberately left open: ADD AN OPT-IN TOGGLE, DEFAULT ON.

Envelope v1 permits aggregate-only automatic upload with no opt-in flow, so this is a product choice, not a compliance one. Default ON keeps the sample intact (retention — the one number the bead exists to produce — is easily biased if engaged users opt out), while making the promise legible: an app whose line is 'Respect your attention' should be able to say on its own settings screen exactly what does and does not leave the device.

SCOPE (~20 lines against isUploadPermitted):
- A Settings toggle, default ON, gating AnalyticsService's upload permission. It must AND with the existing AnalyticsUploadGate.legalSignoffRecorded — the toggle can only ever make uploads FEWER, never bypass the counsel gate, which stays shut until Addendum A is signed.
- Copy obeys the external-copy rule: never 'ad detection' or 'AI'. Say concretely what is sent (a handful of anonymous counts, no per-device identifier, nothing about what you listen to) rather than the word 'analytics'. The About screen's existing 'Your podcasts never leave your device' promise is the tone to match.
- Turning it OFF must stop uploads immediately and should not silently keep accumulating an unbounded local delta — decide whether counters keep accruing (so re-enabling resumes) or reset, and write down which.
- A test proving OFF means no outbound record even when the counsel gate is later opened.

WORTH SAYING IN THE COPY, per the CloudKit finding: our payload carries no identifier, but CloudKit stamps a server-side creatorUserRecordID on public-database records, so the platform links a device's uploads even though we do not. That asterisk is already Addendum A's headline question for counsel; do not claim more anonymity than is true.

Related: playhead-jw63.3 (the analytics), the Addendum A counsel gate.
acceptance_criteria: A Settings toggle exists, defaults ON, and ANDs with the counsel gate so it can only reduce uploads. Copy obeys the external-copy rule and describes what is sent concretely rather than abstractly, without over-claiming anonymity given the CloudKit creator-identity caveat. OFF stops uploads immediately, proven by a test that holds even with the counsel gate opened. The accrue-vs-reset behaviour on OFF is decided and documented.

title: subdividedCoarseOutput discards refusalCount — chunk-level refusals persist as a fully-scanned noAds
description:
Found 2026-07-27 by the playhead-qbib implementer; the SAME false-clean defect qbib just eliminated, but one level down and via a different mechanism, so it was deliberately left for its own bead.

FoundationModelClassifier.subdividedCoarseOutput (~line 4300) is the context-overflow path: when a coarse window exceeds the model's context, it is chunked into atoms and classified piecewise. It tracks refusalCount and then DISCARDS it. The only gate is 'guard succeededCount > 0'. So if some chunks refuse and the remainder return noAds, the whole window is persisted as a fully-scanned .noAds — a confident 'no ads here' over audio that was never examined.

This is exactly the class qbib closed at window granularity (a refused window is now an honest hole with its own coordinates, and SemanticScanCoverage can tell 'scanned, clean' from 'could not scan'). At sub-window granularity the same lie is still possible, and it is arguably worse: a window-level refusal is at least visible as a failure row, whereas this one persists as a SUCCESS.

Why it matters beyond tidiness: the same downstream consumers qbib just taught to distinguish examined from unexamined (coverage %, precision measurement, the 0sro watermark invariants, the gold-gap analysis) will trust this row completely. A false clean is worse than a hole because nothing downstream ever revisits it.

FIX SHAPE (small, ~4 lines): when the aggregate would claim clean but at least one chunk was never examined, return nil rather than a .noAds — i.e. refuse to synthesise a verdict the evidence does not support. Consider instead persisting a partial-coverage result carrying the examined sub-ranges, which would let SemanticScanCoverage account for it properly; that is the more complete fix and the reason this deserves its own bead rather than a 4-line patch.

Read qbib's merge (1d263d09) first — SemanticScanStatus.didExamineWindow and SemanticScanCoverage are the vocabulary this fix should reuse rather than reinvent.
acceptance_criteria: A coarse window whose atom chunks partially refuse can no longer persist as a fully-scanned noAds. Either the window returns nil (no synthesised verdict) or it persists partial coverage carrying the examined sub-ranges, accounted for by SemanticScanCoverage. A regression seeds a chunked window where some atoms refuse and the rest return noAds, and asserts the window is NOT recorded as cleanly scanned. Reuse SemanticScanStatus.didExamineWindow rather than inventing a parallel notion of examined.
close_reason: Merged to main as 89bf541a. Premise confirmed TWICE: statically (refusalCount read only in a debug log, gate solely succeededCount>0) and EMPIRICALLY (pre-fix file + new regression = TEST FAILED, 4 issues). Widened the criterion from refusals to qbib's didExamineWindow so decode failures, guardrails, rate limits and cancellations all block a clean claim — with a dedicated test so a future refactor cannot narrow it back. CHOSE THE MINIMUM AFTER PROVING THE BETTER OPTION CANNOT FIT: partial coverage was designed then abandoned on evidence — passA row identity is semanticScanReuseKeyHash keyed on SEGMENT-derived atom ordinals and subdivision only runs on single-segment plans, so every sub-range row hashes identically (two examined sub-rows collide under UNIQUE, and the hole row is silently dropped by the H-1 'a cached success must never be demoted' guard since window rows insert before failure rows). Synthesising partial coverage today would have REPRODUCED THIS BEAD'S OWN DEFECT through the persistence layer. Lost: examined chunks are conceded back into the hole, so coverage under-counts on this rare path and the next scan re-runs them — the safe direction, a hole is revisitable and a false clean is not. Per-chunk permissive recovery reuses qbib's budgets (a subdivided window costs at most the same 3 calls, however many chunks). containsAd aggregates deliberately still return whole-window: not a clean claim, and holing the short-circuited tail would stall the coverage cursor forever since every re-scan short-circuits at the same chunk. Full gate green, 8975 tests, 0 failures. Budget 6/14. FOLLOW-UP FILED: sub-window row identity (see playhead-oyx1).

title: Two source-canary regressions red on main (precision-gate label + user-mark revalidation ordering)
description:
Found 2026-07-27 during the playhead-0sro gate; PRE-EXISTING on main, proven not assumed. Three XCTest source-canary failures:

1. AdDetectionServicePrecisionGateLabelCanaryTests (2 failures) — the canary demands a 'return "autoSkip"' label in AdDetectionService.swift; that string occurs ZERO times in the file, verified in both the bead worktree AND the main checkout.
2. PlayheadRuntimeWiringSourceCanaryTests.testUserMarkLiveInjectionRevalidatesPlaybackAfterPersistence — demands a 'guard currentAnalysisAssetId == expectedAssetId' BEFORE recordUserMarkedAd; PlayheadRuntime.swift has exactly one such guard and it sits AFTER.

PROOF OF PRE-EXISTENCE: git diff --stat over the canaries' target files (AdDetectionService.swift, PlayheadRuntime.swift), the canary files themselves, and SwiftSourceInspector.swift is EMPTY between main and the 0sro branch. Source canaries are deterministic text checks, so byte-identical inputs give identical results — these fail on main today.

WHY IT MATTERS: a source canary encodes an invariant somebody thought worth pinning. Red canaries are either (a) the invariant genuinely regressed and the product is wrong, or (b) the code was deliberately restructured and the canary was never updated. Both need a human decision; neither is served by leaving them red, because a permanently-red canary trains everyone to ignore canary failures — the same dynamic that makes an always-red linter worthless.

Note the second one is adjacent to real work: playhead-o4qr just fixed a producer-revision mismatch in the user-mark injection path, so the ordering the canary demands may have been deliberately changed. Check o4qr's merge (d94c1a2c) before deciding.

METHOD: for each, determine whether the invariant still holds in a different form (update the canary) or was genuinely lost (restore the code). Do NOT delete a canary to make the gate green.
acceptance_criteria: Both canary suites pass on main. For each, a written determination of whether the invariant was restored in code or the canary was updated to match a deliberate restructure, with the reasoning recorded. No canary deleted merely to go green. If a canary is judged obsolete, its removal is justified in writing against what it was pinning.
notes:
2026-07-27 A FOURTH RED-ON-MAIN TEST, and a misfiling corrected: UserMarkedAdPersistenceTests.userMarkLearnsCatalogWithAuthoritativeProvenance() fails DETERMINISTICALLY in 0.04s. I had it on the documented load-flake list; it does not belong there. The jw63.4 implementer checked rather than inheriting the label — it fails identically on base commit 51a5aada with its work entirely absent, and 0.04s does not match the ~60s-timeout starvation signature at all. It is a hard expectation failure, not a flake.

LESSON worth keeping: a test living in a FILE whose other tests are load-flaky gets pattern-matched onto the flake list and stops being investigated. DURATION IS THE DISCRIMINATOR — a sub-second failure is never starvation. Re-check any other member of the documented flake families that fails fast.

Main therefore carries FOUR red tests, not three. Retitle this bead accordingly when picking it up.
close_reason:
Merged to main as a08c0ffa. MAIN IS NOW GREEN. 4/4 resolved as (b) — canary/fixture re-anchored, invariant intact — with ZERO production files changed. All four trace to ONE commit, b072e72f (the playhead-o4qr work), which restructured seams and landed with its canaries and one fixture never re-anchored.

MOST INSTRUCTIVE: PlayheadRuntimeWiringSourceCanaryTests had been silently asserting against the WRONG FUNCTION — o4qr added revertAdWindows at :4615, ABOVE injectUserMarkedAd at :4661, with an identical 'ifCurrentAnalysisAssetId expectedAssetId:' external label, and SwiftSourceInspector.firstBody takes the FIRST match. The canary was pinning a function with no persistence step at all, which is why it failed at the guard-let with a generic XCTFail rather than at a comparison. Re-anchored on the unique 'func injectUserMarkedAd('.

Precision-gate canary: o4qr changed precisionGateLabel's return type String? -> struct, so 'return "autoSkip"' became 'PrecisionGateResult(label: "autoSkip", …)'. Literals unchanged — corroborated by the companion DOC canary staying green throughout. The negative assertion was widened identically; leaving it narrow would have made it VACUOUS, which is worse than red.

User-mark test: failed at #require(catalog.allEntries().first) — catalog EMPTY. o4qr hardened AcousticFingerprint.fromFeatureWindows to the calibrated cohort [1.0,2.0,4.0]s while the fixture still built 6s windows, so every fingerprint came back .zero, correctly suppressing both catalog insert and recurrence write. Product right, fixture testing a shape production refuses. Also ADDED the previously-uncovered anonymous nil-podcastId case — the one Dan's 'accept the receipt, refuse the learning' policy actually governs; every prior call site passed a real show id.

AUTOSKIP LABEL: NOT a defect, verified independently. The 2350 implementer's FACTS were correct ('autoSkip' is not a SkipEligibilityGate raw value, decodes to nil, buildAdWindow sets no edge-anchor columns) but the INFERENCE was wrong — the nil-decode is a documented producer contract whitelisted in three independent consumers (SkipOrchestrator.receiveAdWindows, AnalysisStore+CrossUserSharing, AnalysisJobRunner), and nil and .eligible are behaviourally identical on every branch, so swapping the literal gives byte-identical routing at the cost of a schema migration of on-device rows. The one consumer that does not whitelist it (PreRollStartClamp) fails CONSERVATIVE to .markOnly. Budget 4/14.

title: Truthful coverage watermark suppresses the m1l9 tail-mark affordance on silent-shard postrolls
description:
Found 2026-07-27 by the playhead-0sro implementer; NOT a regression it introduced, but a live product consequence its fix unmasks.

TranscriptPeekViewModel.lastCoveredTime (:272-273) computes max(chunkMax, watermark). The watermark legitimately runs PAST chunk max when the engine advances coverage for a shard that produced ZERO segments (TranscriptEngineService:707-714) — precisely the music-bedded post-roll that m1l9's tail-mark affordance exists for.

CONCRETE: chunks reach 3400s, shards reach 3600s. BEFORE 0sro, the clobbered watermark left lastCoveredTime at 3400, so a listener at 3450s got the 'mark this as an ad' affordance. AFTER 0sro the watermark is truthfully 3600, so lastCoveredTime is 3600, untranscribedTailMarkSpan returns nil, and the ad is unmarkable by EITHER flow.

This is m1l9's documented design finally taking effect rather than a new bug — TranscriptPeekTailMarkTests:138 pins the watermark-dominant branch as intentional. But the premise deserves re-examination: a silent shard means 'we looked and found nothing', which is arguably exactly when the tail affordance SHOULD appear. A music-bedded ad produces no transcript segments by definition, so keying the affordance on transcript absence and then suppressing it on coverage presence closes the one path a listener had to report it.

NEEDS-DAN (product): should the tail-mark affordance key on CHUNK coverage rather than the watermark, so a silent shard still offers 'mark this as an ad'? Options: (a) key on chunkMax only; (b) keep the watermark but treat a zero-segment shard as uncovered for affordance purposes; (c) leave as-is and accept music-bedded postrolls are unmarkable from the transcript peek.

Relates to playhead-0sro (the watermark fix) and the m1l9 tail-mark work.
acceptance_criteria: Decide and implement the affordance's coverage source. A listener at a playhead inside a silent (zero-segment) shard can still mark an ad if that is the decision, with a regression test using the chunks-to-3400 / shards-to-3600 shape. If the decision is to leave it, TranscriptPeekTailMarkTests gets a comment recording why a silent shard counts as covered.
notes:
2026-07-27 DAN DECISION: option (b) — keep the watermark, but treat a ZERO-SEGMENT shard as UNCOVERED for tail-mark-affordance purposes.

The affordance must key on whether we have TRANSCRIPT EVIDENCE at the playhead, not on whether we scanned. The watermark answers 'did we look here?'; the chunks answer 'did we find speech here?'. Keying on the former suppresses the affordance in exactly the case it exists for: we looked, found nothing, and a music-bedded ad is playing.

WHY (b) AND NOT (a) 'key on chunkMax only': (a) collapses the distinction between 'we have not looked yet' (transient — analysis in flight, segments likely imminent, and offering a mark there asks the listener to do work the pipeline was about to do) and 'we looked and found nothing' (the genuine blind spot). Preserve that distinction.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND UI: music-bedded ads are the hardest class — no speech, so no lexical anchors, no FM judgment, nothing for deterministic signals to bite. A listener hearing one is the ONLY reliable signal it exists. Closing that path makes the blind spot structural: Playhead could only ever learn about ads it already partly detected, and the corpus would quietly self-select toward easy cases. It also cuts against Phase 2's metric — a music-bedded postroll the listener manually skips IS a +30s reach, and today it is one we never hear about.

ACCEPTED RISK (stated, not overlooked): a scanned-but-silent region is often just music (outro, interlude, scored segment), so the affordance will sometimes be offered over non-ad audio. Blunted by the affordance being OPT-IN — it only fires when someone actually heard an ad, which is better ground truth than any classifier — and by the existing certainty-tiering for corrections. Weight the resulting correction accordingly rather than suppressing the report.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: before changing anything, VERIFY the path firsthand — this decision rests on the playhead-0sro implementer's reading of TranscriptPeekViewModel.lastCoveredTime (:272-273) and the zero-segment coverage advance at TranscriptEngineService (:707-714), which was not independently confirmed. Confirm a shard can advance coverage while producing zero segments, and that lastCoveredTime is what gates untranscribedTailMarkSpan. Then add the regression with the chunks-to-3400 / shards-to-3600 shape, and update TranscriptPeekTailMarkTests:138 (which currently pins the watermark-dominant branch as intentional) to reflect the new contract.
2026-07-28 DAN DECISION on the question this bead left open: NO — both uncovered states keep offering the tail-mark affordance. The TailCoverage tri-state stays as a named, tested seam with no runtime consequence, NOT as a suppression rule.

Suppressing .notYetScanned would DELETE m1l9's shipped behaviour: that affordance was built for the not-yet-analyzed post-roll, where a listener reaches the end of an episode before analysis catches up, and suppressing it there fails m1l9's own crux test.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER FRAMING (Fable): when recommending option (b) I justified preserving the distinction as 'do not ask the listener to do work the pipeline was about to do'. That assumes analysis will arrive. At the END of an episode, with the listener right there, 'shortly' may be never for their purposes — which is precisely the case m1l9 shipped for. The distinction is still worth NAMING (it makes the two cases discussable, and is a cheap lever if telemetry later shows the transient case is noisy) but it should not gate the affordance.

The tri-state was deliberately NOT deleted: keeping it costs nothing, and it means a future reader can reason about the two cases separately instead of rediscovering that they differ. Anyone tempted to 'fix' the collapsed !=.transcribed check into a suppression rule should read this note first.
close_reason: Merged to main as 2ee6a51b. PREMISE CONFIRMED FIRSTHAND (not inherited): lastCoveredTime was max(chunkMax, watermark) at TranscriptPeekViewModel:272-273; the guard !segments.isEmpty arm at TranscriptEngineService:707-714 calls updateCoverage for a ZERO-SEGMENT shard; both advance and reconcile only ever RAISE the watermark so it stays past the last chunk; untranscribedTailMarkSpan gated on exactly currentTime > lastCoveredTime. Direct proof: the new regression FAILS against the pre-change gate. Dan's option (b) implemented — the affordance keys on transcript evidence (currentTime > lastTranscribedTime) while the watermark is RETAINED, with a TailCoverage tri-state keeping .scannedWithoutSpeech (looked, found nothing — the music-bedded blind spot) distinct from .notYetScanned (transient). Regression silentShardPostRollIsStillMarkable (chunks 3400 / watermark 3600 / playhead 3450) is load-bearing three ways: reverting to the watermark fails the #require, option (a) fails the two-state assertions, and making it unconditional fails the within-transcript nil. Test :138 REWRITTEN not deleted — its fixture had chunks and watermark coinciding so it never discriminated; it pinned a belief that became wrong once 0sro made the watermark truthful, and the file header asserted the exact false premise that caused the bug. Budget 3/12. FLAGGED FOR DAN: the tri-state is a named, tested seam but has NO runtime consequence today (production collapses it via != .transcribed) — both uncovered flavours offer the mark. If the intent was for .notYetScanned to SUPPRESS the affordance, that would delete m1l9's shipped post-roll behaviour and fail its own crux test, so it was not done unilaterally.

title: Two more vacuous SkipOrchestrator tests of the ugy4 class (gateFlipClearsSuggestEntry + directEpisodeReplacementClearsAcceptedSuggestionIDs)
description:
Found 2026-07-27 while fixing playhead-ugy4. Same vacuity class, but outside that bead's stated seven, so deliberately not fixed there. Both verified by mutation: break the contract the test names, the test stays green.

1. gateFlipClearsSuggestEntry (SkipOrchestratorCharacterizationTests.swift:1422) — HIGHEST VALUE. Direct twin of the fusion test repaired in ugy4, same playhead-rfu-sad contract. Vacuous TWICE over: the markOnly row is never inserted into the store, AND its only observable is confirmedWindows(), which filters to .confirmed while applyManualSkip flips a promoted window to .applied — so the accessor structurally cannot observe the promotion the test claims to forbid.

2. directEpisodeReplacementClearsAcceptedSuggestionIDs (SkipOrchestratorRevertTests.swift:5714) — the accept fails at persist, and the catch path removes the id from recentlyAcceptedSuggestIds BEFORE beginEpisode runs. Deleting the removeAll() the test is named for would not redden it.

RULED OUT after checking (do not re-investigate): the whole revertByTimeRange/revertWindow family (~15 apparent hits). persistRevertedAdWindow makes no feedbackAssetMatches call, so the ownership-refusal cause cannot apply there.

METHOD: identical to ugy4. Use scripts/mutation-battery.sh (now on main, 31 anchors, supports --dry-run at 0 builds and --batch N). Break the named contract, confirm the test still passes (proving vacuity), repair the fixture/assertion, re-apply the break, confirm it now fails, restore. Do NOT weaken assertions. Add the repaired contracts to the battery as new entries.

ALSO FOLD IN (recorded during ugy4): the battery's headline status is split — M01-N07 were not re-run after FOCUSED_SUITES was widened with the two characterization @Suite structs (SkipOrchestratorAdDecisionContractTests, SkipOrchestratorSuggestTierTests). There is an explicit 'PARTIAL SINCE THEN' block in the script. The next whole-battery run should fold that back into a single LAST GREEN line.
acceptance_criteria: Both tests fail when the contract they name is broken (prove by mutation: break, see red, restore) and pass otherwise. Fixtures made coherent rather than assertions loosened; where an accessor structurally cannot observe the outcome (confirmedWindows() vs .applied), the assertion is replaced with one that can fail. Both added to scripts/mutation-battery.sh. A full battery run folds the PARTIAL SINCE THEN block back into one LAST GREEN provenance line. Sweep the remaining SkipOrchestrator suites with the same method and report any further vacuous tests.
close_reason: Merged to main as 52987c21. 2/2 PROVED vacuous by mutation before repair (S06+S07 both SURVIVED pre-repair), repaired so the seam is reached, re-broken to confirm both now fail. gateFlipClearsSuggestEntry was vacuous twice over — the markOnly row was never inserted so acceptSuggestedSkip aborted in persistAcceptedSuggestionIfCurrent regardless, AND its only observable confirmedWindows() filters to .confirmed while the forbidden duplicate is minted .applied by applyManualSkip (an accessor structurally unable to see the outcome it asserts against). directEpisodeReplacementClearsAcceptedSuggestionIDs failed at persist and the catch path removed the id while episode 1 was still live, so beginEpisode's removeAll() — the thing the test is named for — had nothing to clear. THE BIGGER FINDING: the full battery exposed N04's EDIT as ROTTEN — it still ANCHORED (so --dry-run swept clean through an entire prior bead) but the mutated tree no longer COMPILED after ingestNegativeFingerprint grew its negativeAttribution parameter, and since a batch aborts on its first failure N02/N03/N06 went down with it: four mutations silently unevaluated behind a green dry-run. Re-cut, batch 8 now 4/4 KILLED. Battery now 35 entries / 34 KILLED / 1 SURVIVED (M17, documented+deliberate); three overlapping status blocks collapsed into one provenance block; M14 and O04 settled as KILLED; every batch re-run since FOCUSED_SUITES widened. NEW LESSON PINNED: --dry-run proves an anchor still APPLIES, not that the mutant still COMPILES or still KILLS. Budget 25/16 — over, deliberately and reported: the full battery is 20 builds by construction at 19 batches, so the acceptance criterion alone exceeded the budget I set from a stale LAST GREEN line; truncating would have left the battery half-run and unable to fold the PARTIAL block. No production file changed.

title: Seven vacuous SkipOrchestrator tests pass for the wrong reason (fixture/setup defects predating i08e)
description:
Found 2026-07-26 by the second independent reviewer during the playhead-i08e loop, verified by mutation testing. Seven tests cannot fail even when the contract they name is broken, so they provide FALSE coverage assurance over correction/suggest seams.

TWO ROOT CAUSES (both predate i08e; the i08e diff neither introduced nor worsened them):
1. Asset/episode fixture mismatch — the asset row carries episodeId 'ep-1' while the test calls beginEpisode with a different id, so AnalysisStore.feedbackAssetMatches refuses persistence on OWNERSHIP grounds before the seam under test is ever reached. The test then observes 'nothing was written' and passes, but it would pass identically if the seam were broken. This is the same defect class that hid the original i08e regression.
2. Suggest windows are never insertAdWindow'd into the store, so acceptSuggestedSkip can never promote — assertions like #expect(activeWindowIDs().isEmpty) and #expect(pushedCues.isEmpty) are unfalsifiable regardless of fixture.

AFFECTED (verified individually by deleting the guard under test and confirming the test still passed):
- SkipOrchestratorRevertTests ~3077 adWindowInvalidations...
- SkipOrchestratorRevertTests ~3169 decisionInvalidations...
- SkipOrchestratorRevertTests ~3268 explicitRetirementRejects...
- SkipOrchestratorRevertTests ~3352 lateInventoryContextRejects...StaleSuggestionYes
- SkipOrchestratorRevertTests ~5075 episodeBoundSuggestActionsRejectStaleIdentity (recoverFailedProvisionalSuggestion restores the entries, so remaining.contains(...) is unfalsifiable)
- SkipOrchestratorCharacterizationTests fusionResultClearsSharedIdSuggestEntry
- SkipOrchestratorCharacterizationTests declineSuggestedSkipDoesNotConfirm

WHY A SEPARATE BEAD: correct repair means reconstructing each test's material-token / producer-revision fixture individually. A blind fix risks making them pass for YET ANOTHER wrong reason — the exact failure mode the i08e loop existed to eliminate. They also sit outside the i08e diff hunks. Three sibling tests with this defect WERE repaired inside i08e because that diff touched them.

METHOD THAT FOUND THESE (reuse it): mutation testing — break the production behavior the test names, confirm the test goes red, restore. Any test that stays green is vacuous.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the seven tests fails when the contract it names is broken (verify by mutation: break the guard/behavior, see red, restore) and passes otherwise. Fixtures are made coherent — asset episodeId matches beginEpisode, and suggest windows are actually inserted where the seam requires it — rather than assertions being loosened. Sweep the rest of the SkipOrchestrator suites with the same mutation-testing method and report any further vacuous tests found.
close_reason: Merged to main as ac5fe4ca. All seven repaired; tests only, ZERO production files changed. Root causes were two fixture defects (asset episodeId 'ep-1' vs a different beginEpisode id, so feedbackAssetMatches refused on ownership before the seam ran; and suggest windows never insertAdWindow'd so acceptSuggestedSkip could never promote) plus a THIRD the bead had not named: confirmedWindows() filters to .confirmed while applyManualSkip flips a promoted window to .applied, so both characterization tests asserted 'no promotion' through an accessor that structurally cannot see one. episodeBoundSuggestActionsRejectStaleIdentity was unfalsifiable by construction (recoverFailedProvisionalSuggestion restores the entry, making refusal and rollback indistinguishable) and was given the inverse fixture so the orchestrator's own activeEpisodeId guard is the only possible rejecter. Five mutations S01-S05 added to scripts/mutation-battery.sh so these contracts stay pinned mechanically. Verification: 98/98 focused pass repaired+unmutated; the same mutations redden exactly the previously-green assertions after repair; full gate 8549 tests / 1094 suites, 0 failures, ZERO flakes. No production bug exposed. Two MORE tests of the same vacuity class found outside this bead's stated seven — filed as a follow-up.

title: Per-show threshold-control write path dead on two correction seams — main is red
description:
Found 2026-07-26 while gating playhead-txq3. main @94809607 (and now @4a4be8ae) FAILS PlayheadFastTests deterministically: SkipOrchestratorThresholdControlTests has 2 failing tests. NOT a load flake — reproduced on a quiescent machine with only 9 tests running, failing in 2.25s.

FAILING:
  - 'Manual "not an ad" revertWindow records a FALSE-POSITIVE signal' (expects integral == +1, gets 0)
  - 'Accepting a suggested (not-auto-skipped) ad records a MISS signal' (expects integral == -1, gets 0)

PASSING siblings (so the write path is only PARTIALLY dead): listen-revert, revertByTimeRange, and the flag-OFF no-store case.

DIAGNOSIS: the test helper awaitSampleCount() polls 40x50ms (~2s) and returns PerShowThresholdControllerState.zero on timeout WITHOUT throwing. Both failures took 2.253s — exactly the timeout — so sampleCount never reached 1: the controller sample is NEVER RECORDED for these two gestures, rather than recorded with a wrong value. (integral==0 is the .zero sentinel, not a miscomputation; PerShowThresholdController's integral math is a straightforward prior.integral + signal.error with error ±1 and looks correct.)

SUSPECT: 5c1a167e 'feat(banners): capture private explicit feedback' rewrote SkipOrchestrator.swift (+1530/-266) and added CorrectionAttribution.swift. The manual-'not an ad' revert seam and the acceptSuggestedSkip seam most likely lost their recordThresholdControlSignal() call or had it gated behind a new unmet condition during that refactor. Verify by checking those two seams against the parent commit b5a9d649.

PRODUCTION IMPACT: LIMITED — recordThresholdControlSignal() no-ops when no PerShowThresholdControllerStore is wired, which is the flag-OFF production default (playhead-xsdz.11). So this breaks a dormant feature plus the learning receipts, not live skip behavior. The immediate cost is that main's gate is RED, which taxes every subsequent bead gate (12 other failures in a full run are genuine load flakes and must not be confused with these 2 real ones).

NOT introduced by txq3 or i6oi — both were verified clean against this baseline.
acceptance_criteria: Both tests pass on a quiescent machine. The two seams (manual not-an-ad revertWindow, acceptSuggestedSkip) record exactly one controller sample with the correct signed error. Add a regression asserting a recorded sample rather than relying on a helper that silently returns .zero on timeout — awaitSampleCount() should THROW on timeout so a dead write path can never again look like a wrong value. Confirm no other correction seam lost its controller write in the 5c1a167e refactor.
close_reason: Merged to main as 85624298. Root cause: 5c1a167e gave each correction seam's CorrectionEvent builder a 'guard correctionStore != nil else { throw }' precondition; SkipOrchestrator.correctionStore defaults to nil, so any orchestrator without one aborted the gesture BEFORE reaching recordThresholdControlSignal(). The observed integral 0 was the .zero sentinel of a test helper that silently returned on timeout, not a miscomputed value — confirmed by the 2.25s failure exactly matching the helper's 2s poll budget. Scope was WIDER than filed: 3 seams were fully dead (incl. denyAutoSkippedBanner, which had zero coverage) and 2 more (recordListenRevert, revertByTimeRange) were conditionally dead — a live-lifecycle guard inserted by the same commit dropped a valid correction AFTER its trust penalty had already landed, leaving trust and corrections permanently out of step. Fix: remove the spurious precondition; hoist receipt/hard-negative/controller-sample above the lifecycle guard; in-loop return -> break; awaitSampleCount() now THROWS on timeout so a dead write path can never again masquerade as a wrong value. Added a DEBUG-only revertPersistenceBarrierForTesting (inert in release, matches the file's existing barrier pattern) so the race is testable behaviourally rather than by scanning source text. 9 review rounds, 58 issues found+fixed; production delta only 39 non-doc lines. Verification: originally-failing suite 12/12 pass in 0.724s (was a 2.25s silent timeout); full gate green apart from the documented RouteChangeTests load flake; scripts/mutation-battery.sh 26/26 KILLED, 0 survivors. Follow-ups filed: playhead-ugy4 (7 pre-existing vacuous tests), playhead-ia2s (swiftlint), plus beads for the view-layer late podcastId read and the unwired listen-revert calibration signal.

title: Fixing Playhead's mistake takes one tap: manual-correction UX polish
description: Customer outcome: when Playhead is wrong, recovery is instant and visibly learned-from. One-tap undo of a wrong skip (jump back + mark false-positive), one-tap 'this was an ad' mark that becomes definitive (auto-skip eligible — already policy), visible acknowledgment ('Got it — we'll skip this next time'). Surfaces the existing correction machinery; the Gate-2 mark-surfacing work folds in here.
notes: 2026-07-26: absorbs the correction-expressiveness requirement split out of child playhead-1mq1.2.1 — the correction UX/data model must let a listener express not-an-ad, start-too-early, end-too-late, and mixed/partial-overlap outcomes (lightweight edge adjustment or inferred retained-subspan). The child keeps only the P0 learning-attribution guard (no whole-span negatives when internal ad evidence exists).

title: Banner words a listener trusts: banner copy pass
description:
Customer outcome: the banner reads as a calm, honest assistant — plain words, no hedging jargon, consistent voice across certainty tiers (certain vs probably vs 'you marked this'). Audit every user-facing detection string. Copy principle: it says exactly what happens ('Skipping in 3s…', 'Skipped 45s of ads', 'Was this right?'). Never 'AI' or 'detected'.
## DIRECTION — Dan 2026-08-01: "whatever you recommend"

Dan delegated the copy direction. Recommendation below; final strings still want his eye before
ship, but implement against this.

### What changed under this bead, and why the old copy no longer fits

1. [[playhead-d3g0]]: the card now arrives when the playhead ENTERS the ad — **before** the
   listener has heard it. Retrospective phrasing ("Was this right?", "Was that an ad?") asks
   about audio they have not heard. It is now a PROSPECTIVE affordance.
2. [[playhead-ynmk]]: on an unanchored span a confirmation MARKS rather than skips, and the card
   must not offer a Skip it cannot perform.

### Recommendation

- **Lead with the action, not the question.** The card's job at that moment is to let Dan get
  past the ad. Something of the shape `Ad detected — [Skip]` (skippable) / `Ad detected —
  [Mark]` (mark-only). The feedback value is a by-product of the tap, not the ask.
- **Never promise in copy what the anchors cannot deliver.** The skippable/mark-only branch is
  already derived once (`confirmationWouldSkip`); the copy must read from that single
  derivation, never re-derive.
- **Dismissal is the negative signal.** No separate "Not an ad" button competing with the
  primary action — dismissing is already recorded and keeps the card to one decision.
- **Keep it to one line.** It appears over playback, at the moment attention is on audio.
- **No numbers, no confidence, no counters** — [[feedback_peace_of_mind_not_metrics]]. The card
  should feel like the app quietly handling something, not reporting a measurement.
- The mark-only string should not read as a downgrade or an apology. "Mark" is a real, useful
  action; phrasing it as a consolation prize teaches the listener to distrust the feature.
notes:
playhead-d3g0 (2026-07-31) added ONE new user-facing string and left it deliberately minimal for this bead to own.

CONTEXT. d3g0 makes the suggest banner fire when the playhead ENTERS the ad span (Dan: "when it enters so I can skip"), which turns the card from a retrospective correction into a PROSPECTIVE SKIP AFFORDANCE. Dan's decision text says the copy here "was written for a different interaction model and should be re-read against this" — specifically that the primary action is SKIP and feedback capture is a side effect of the same tap.

THE SEAM. Everything lives in AdBannerView.feedbackChoiceContent(for:confirmationSkipsPlayback:). Two branches under .suggest:

  confirmationSkipsPlayback == true  -> UNCHANGED, byte-identical to what shipped:
      confirmLabel                 "Yes"
      confirmAccessibilityLabel    "Yes, skip this sponsor break"
      confirmAccessibilityHint     "Confirms this is an ad and skips it"

  confirmationSkipsPlayback == false -> NEW, and the only new copy in d3g0:
      confirmLabel                 "Mark"   (AdBannerView.markOnlyConfirmFeedbackLabel)
      confirmAccessibilityLabel    "Yes, this is a sponsor break"
      confirmAccessibilityHint     "Marks this as an ad; playback continues"

WHY THE SECOND BRANCH EXISTS. playhead-ynmk made a confirmation assert PRESENCE, never EXTENT, so on a span whose edges the detector drew and cannot prove late-safe (both edges unanchored — the entire 2026-07-31 field population, 3 of 3) confirming produces a MARK and playback DOES NOT MOVE. With entry-firing, offering "Yes, skip this sponsor break" there is a button that does nothing at the exact moment the user wants it to do something. The flag is resolved by the orchestrator from the same AutoSkipEdgePadding policy the acceptance transaction consults, and a test compares the card's claim against the durable row so the two cannot drift.

WHAT THIS BEAD SHOULD DECIDE.
  1. Whether the skippable branch should now LEAD WITH THE SKIP ("Skip" rather than "Yes", and the button order). d3g0 deliberately did not pre-empt that.
  2. The mark-only wording. "Mark" is a placeholder chosen to be obviously changeable, not a proposal.
  3. Whether the shared prompt "Was this right?" still fits a card that arrives BEFORE the audio it is asking about. It reads as retrospective and the interaction is now prospective.

Tests that will need their expected strings updated with any change:
  SuggestBannerSkipAffordanceTests "Mark-only copy drops the skip promise and skippable copy is untouched"
  AdBannerQueueTests (the feedbackChoiceContent assertions)
  ListenerFeedbackEntryPointTests

title: Crashes get fixed before anyone reports them: crash + hang pipeline
description: Customer outcome: a listener never has to describe a crash to us. Wire MetricKit (MXCrashDiagnostic, hang + disk-write diagnostics) into a local diagnostics store surfaced via the existing diagnostics-bundle path (respecting docs/plans/diagnostics-bundle-legal-checklist.md), plus App Store Connect opt-in crash reports once distributed. Zero third-party SDKs needed.
notes:
2026-07-27 DAN: implement this bead with the iterative-implementation-with-review-loops skill (implementer subagent, then FRESH reviewer subagents that FIX what they find, until TWO CONSECUTIVE zero-finding rounds; cap 20 per this repo's convention, not the skill's default 5).

APPLY THE COST PROTOCOL learned on playhead-i08e (see memory feedback_review_loop_economics_2026-07-27) — without it rounds balloon to ~85 min each:
- Give every round a HARD BUILD BUDGET (12-16 xcodebuild invocations) and require it to report usage.
- FULL GATE EXACTLY ONCE, at the end of a round, on the final committed state. Validate everything else against focused suites. Running the full gate mid-round adds no information and costs ~5.5 min a time.
- COMMIT AFTER EVERY DISCRETE STEP. Rounds get interrupted; uncommitted work is lost work.
- Don't re-derive known checks by hand — scripts/mutation-battery.sh (on main) runs the established battery in one command.
- MUTATE, DON'T READ: a finding you cannot demonstrate with a surviving mutation probably isn't one; a mutation that survives the gate definitely is. On i08e, three separate rounds found mutations surviving the whole ~8.5k-test gate, and one round's confident 'zero findings' was later proved wrong.
Measured costs on this box: warm no-op focused run 68s; focused run after touching a production file 85s; full gate ~5.5 min; whole battery 10 builds/~17 min.

Every round must set DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode-beta.app/Contents/Developer, never pipe a gate through a mask (a pipeline returns the LAST exit code, so a failed gate reads as 0), and never run two xcodebuild processes concurrently (16 GB box; the loser is OOM-killed with no test failure).
close_reason: Merged to main as 1af54bbc. MXMetricManager -> subscriber -> allowlist-scrubbing projector -> 50-record JSONL ring buffer in Application Support -> stability_diagnostics block of the existing diagnostics bundle the user already chooses to email; scripts/symbolicate-stability-diagnostics.sh turns each frame's binary UUID + __TEXT offset into a symbolicated stack. FIRST-PARTY, NO DEPENDENCY ADDED and none recommended — MetricKit gives crashes AND main-thread hangs with no signal handler, no Mach exception port and no network client, whereas a third-party SDK would add a second egress path to keep honest forever against the on-device mandate. Honest cost: delivery at most once per 24h on the launch after the incident, device-only; live telemetry is the tradeoff to revisit later. PRIVACY: the fields most likely to carry episode content are NEVER READ (exceptionReason.composedMessage/.formatString/.arguments, terminationReason verbatim which embeds the container path, virtualMemoryRegionInfo, frame addresses). Four scrubbing layers incl. re-sanitisation on decode because the buffer outlives app versions. Proven by a hostile fixture seeded with transcript text, an episode title, a feed URL and a container path — sentinels absent from encoded bytes AND records still captured, so scrubbing-by-dropping would not pass; falsifiability confirmed by two mutation runs. Application Support rather than Caches because the OS evicts Caches under exactly the disk pressure that makes a crash interesting. Hangs are a distinct kind with hang_duration_ms. Zero new user-visible strings so the external-copy ban is trivially satisfied. 76 new tests; lint clean; Release build verified separately because the Debug gate never compiles ReleaseDiagnosticsHatch. Budget 14/14.

title: Know whether listeners come back tomorrow: privacy-first analytics (self-built, envelope v1)
description:
DECIDED by Dan 2026-07-24: option (a) — self-built on telemetry-envelope-v1 (docs/legal/telemetry-envelope-v1.md). No third-party SDK. Customer outcome: we learn retention + trust without ever making the user's attention our inventory.

## v1 scope — brutally small, grow only when a question demands it
- FIVE counters, all anonymous aggregate increments (envelope aggregate-only rule): banners shown / banners confirmed ('Was this right?' yes) / banners denied (no) / manual +30s reaches / listening hours.
- North-star metric: manual +30s reaches per listening hour (the incumbent we replace).
- Retention WITHOUT device IDs: each device computes its own return bucket locally (D1/D7/D30 'came back' streak) and uploads an anonymous bucket increment — no per-device identifier ever leaves the device (envelope rule 3 stays satisfied without an opt-in flow).
- Cohort keying per envelope: SLICohortAxes (trigger × analysis mode × execution condition × duration bucket) where meaningful.

## Transport
- CloudKit public database (serverless, $0 at this scale, Apple-native). Write-only anonymous increment records; no user record types, no queries from device.
- Read side: a simple rollup script (weekly report is the v1 'dashboard'). No web dashboards until user count demands it.

## Constraints
- Envelope rules are HARD: no transcript text, no per-device behavior history, aggregate-only automatic upload, default-deny for any field not on the allow-list.
- Counters source: the local aggregate counters landed by jw63.1 (banners shown/confirmed/denied) + playback-side counters for +30s reaches and listening hours.
- No new dependencies of any kind.

## GATE before shipping automatic upload
- telemetry-envelope-v1 is still marked LEGAL REVIEW PENDING — counsel signoff must happen before the first automatic upload ships (the mail-composer diagnostics path is unaffected). Queue with counsel NOW so it is not the release blocker.

Depends on jw63.1 (counter substrate). Considered + rejected: (b) TelemetryDeck — per-device hashed signals = device-keyed behavior history, forbidden by our own envelope without an opt-in flow/envelope v2, plus a dependency; (c) Apple App Analytics alone — no custom events, cannot measure the north star (kept anyway as the free floor).
notes:
2026-07-24: Dan chose option (a) after cost comparison (build 3-5d + ownership vs vendor legal friction vs Apple-only blindness). Deps: jw63.1 counters. CloudKit public DB transport.
2026-07-27 DAN: implement this bead with the iterative-implementation-with-review-loops skill (implementer subagent, then FRESH reviewer subagents that FIX what they find, until TWO CONSECUTIVE zero-finding rounds; cap 20 per this repo's convention, not the skill's default 5).

- FULL GATE EXACTLY ONCE, at the end of a round, on the final committed state. Validate everything else against focused suites. Running the full gate mid-round adds no information and costs ~5.5 min a time.
- COMMIT AFTER EVERY DISCRETE STEP. Rounds get interrupted; uncommitted work is lost work.
- Don't re-derive known checks by hand — scripts/mutation-battery.sh (on main) runs the established battery in one command.
- MUTATE, DON'T READ: a finding you cannot demonstrate with a surviving mutation probably isn't one; a mutation that survives the gate definitely is. On i08e, three separate rounds found mutations surviving the whole ~8.5k-test gate, and one round's confident 'zero findings' was later proved wrong.
Measured costs on this box: warm no-op focused run 68s; focused run after touching a production file 85s; full gate ~5.5 min; whole battery 10 builds/~17 min.

Every round must set DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode-beta.app/Contents/Developer, never pipe a gate through a mask (a pipeline returns the LAST exit code, so a failed gate reads as 0), and never run two xcodebuild processes concurrently (16 GB box; the loser is OOM-killed with no test failure).
2026-07-28 ADDENDUM A APPROVED BY FOUNDER (commit 4d8dccbb). Dan self-approved as principal; documented explicitly as a FOUNDER approval, NOT counsel review, with counsel deferred to first PAID release and the reasoning recorded in a new §4.1.

Answers to the five questions, now founder decisions: (Q1) anonymous-increment accepted as designed — server-side summation satisfies §1(a), a pre-transmission k-floor rejected because a device cannot enforce one without the peer-count query this design exists to avoid; (Q2) k = 20; (Q3) exclude the install-week bucket, accepting a WINDOW rather than cohort retention ratio in exchange for adding no linkage surface; (Q4) CloudKit needs no different treatment under §2.1; (Q5) the platform-stamped creatorUserRecordID accepted as the §4.3 transport-metadata case, mitigated by the rollup reading only the nine counter fields — flagged in the document as the answer most likely to be wrong, with the remedy scoped to one class since the payload would not change.

APPROVED BUT NOT ACTIVATED: legalSignoffRecorded stays false. That is now a v1 PRODUCT decision, not a legal blocker — at v1 user counts the k>=20 floor suppresses most rollup rows, so uploading would make the CloudKit question live while returning little readable. Local accumulation + the diagnostics bundle the jw63.5 feedback channel already ships gives real numbers at zero upload surface. Activation is a submission-time decision alongside the privacy nutrition label and support URL.

STANDING CONDITION: 'anonymous' is barred from user-facing copy about this collection — say concretely what is sent. This binds the opt-in-toggle bead's copy.
close_reason: Merged to main as 34d8a25a. Nine anonymous integer counters (banners shown/confirmed/denied, manual +30s reaches, listening seconds, D1/D7/D30 return buckets computed on-device) accumulate locally and leave only as write-only unlinkable CloudKit public-DB increment records keyed by episode-duration cohort. North star: manual +30s reaches per listening hour. ENVELOPE ENFORCED STRUCTURALLY — every key is an enum case and every string value an enum raw value, so there is no [String: Any] between a counter and a record and an episode title has no representation it could travel in; the allow-list then re-validates against a frozen 12-key set + 6-token vocabulary immediately before CKRecord, rejecting the WHOLE record on surprise, and re-runs on decode so a hand-edited blob cannot smuggle a key in. UPLOAD GATE SHUT (legalSignoffRecorded=false) per envelope §7 — the counters are not on v1's §2 allow-list and the envelope is unsigned; Addendum A is written and ready for counsel. Retention without IDs via a local installDayIndex that never leaves the device. Counters reuse jw63.1's banner store rather than re-counting; +30s instrumented at BOTH disjoint skip paths with a canary pinning the disjointness (a future delegation would double every count while leaving all tests green). Never wakes the device (no BGTask/timer/push/background URLSession) and fails silent with 7-day backoff cap and 30-day drop. 66 new tests incl. egress sentinels seeding transcript text, episode title, feed URL, episode id and show title into the REAL path, asserting absence over the entire rendered payload, at rest, and in a materialized CKRecord. No dependency added. Budget 7/14. TWO OPEN ITEMS FOR DAN: (1) counsel signoff on Addendum A is the gate — queue it now so it is not the release blocker; (2) an opt-in Settings toggle is RECOMMENDED but not built — the envelope permits aggregate-only automatic upload without one, but 'Respect your attention' argues an app whose pitch is not making your attention someone's inventory should say so on its own settings screen (~20 lines, a product decision). Also noted: CloudKit stamps a server-side creatorUserRecordID on public-DB records, so the platform links a device's uploads even though our payload does not — documented at the writer, raised as Addendum A's headline question for counsel, and mitigated on the read side by projecting to the 12 allow-listed fields before aggregating.

2026-07-27 CORRECTION (Dan): the iterative-implementation-with-review-loops skill is NOT needed for this bead, nor for design/copy/content work generally. It is a CODE review-fix loop — its value comes from mutation testing and adversarial review of implementation, which has no analogue in screenshots and product-page copy. Use it for code beads (ia2s, 0sro, jw63.3 analytics, jw63.4 crash pipeline, jw63.5 feedback channel); skip it here.
