title: Trace + fix rediff head over-widening: non-rediff channels flag theme+monologue as ad-like (auto-skip blocker)
notes:
THE AUTO-SKIP BLOCKER (from measurement #2, 2026-07-17). SYMPTOM: with rediff byte-first ON, the conan-2026-07-13-mick-jagger head emitted 2 windows [0-88.3]+[89.6-204.2] (blockedByEvidenceQuorum) spanning ~200s, when the TRUE DAI ad is only [0-60.4] (Progressive + Mint Mobile pre-rolls, transcript+byte-truth+ear all agree). The 144s from 60.4-204 is PURE CONTENT: Mick Jagger cold-open bit (60-82s), the White Stripes theme song (83-100s), and Conan's intro monologue (101-204s). BYTE DIFFER IS INNOCENT: it flagged only [0-60.4] (byte-exact). The over-widening came from the OTHER (non-rediff) channels flagging the theme music + 'welcome to the show' framing as ad-like, surfaced once rediff turned ON. Contained today ONLY by the evidence quorum (blocked, not eligible → not skipped). WHY IT'S THE AUTO-SKIP BLOCKER: 'safe because a second layer blocked it' is fragile; a quorum-tuning change could expose 144s of host content to auto-skip. INVESTIGATE: (1) which channels produce the [60-204] candidate spans (FM? lexical promo-cadence? acoustic music? a stinger/pod-grid boundary?); (2) why rediff-ON surfaces them when baseline didn't (does the byte head-slot [0-60] seed a decoded span that fusion/widening extends?); (3) fix so the WIDTH is clean (doesn't reach into content) rather than relying on the block. Then re-run measurement #2 (byte-first Catalyst treatment → l2f-score-oracle-gold + l2f-bd4xqf eligible-only + all-windows gates); auto-skip flip is the decision AFTER all-windows also lands under budget. REPRO DATA: transcript TestFixtures/Corpus/Transcripts/conan-2026-07-13-mick-jagger.json; treatment dump + composite truth on main.
DIAGNOSIS (2026-07-17, read-only trace — CONFIRMED). PREMISE OVERTURNED: rediff/byte differ did NOT cause the head over-widening. ROOT: the two head windows are FOUNDATIONMODEL-CONSENSUS false positives — FM anchored atoms across the cold-open bit + theme song + monologue → MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder emitted spans [0-88.32] and [89.6-204.24] BEFORE rediff runs (projector:14871 → spans:14877 → byte differ:14884 → rediff:14885). Every other channel byte-identical between baseline/treatment (lexical 5 cand both, acoustic 33 breaks both); only FM swung (2→5 windows). CONFOUND: 'appears only with rediff ON' = FM NON-DETERMINISM — baseline run logged 'Safety guardrails triggered' (the ~40% refusal), runs 2 days apart; FM runs upstream of rediff and never reads the flag. INFER(strong): a baseline re-run where FM doesn't refuse shows the same head windows rediff-OFF. WHAT REDIFF ACTUALLY DID = a MISSED CLIP: it held byte-exact slot [0-60.369] but resolveSpan's minCoreCoverage=0.8 gate refused to snap the FM span [0-88.32] to it (60.369/88.32=0.684<0.8) → span kept FM width. So rediff HAD the truth and DIDN'T USE IT. FRAGILITY CONFIRMED: [89.6-204.24] monologue held back only by quorum needing >=2 evidence kinds (has only FM); if the theme-song music got a musicBed entry → FM+musicBed=2 → eligible → auto-skippable 144s of content. CLASS: conan unique in THIS corpus (only blockedByEvidenceQuorum content-sweep); underlying mode (FM over-anchoring musical/comedic show intros) is a latent class for late-night/variety. RECOMMENDED FIX A: byte-slot CONTAINMENT CLIP in RediffSlotOwnership.resolveSpan — when a byte-exact slot is strictly CONTAINED in the FM span core but coverage<0.8 (span OVERRUNS the byte slot), bypass the coverage gate and clip the span to the byte extent. Clips conan [0-88.32]→[0-60.369] (snaps at the real ad boundary); mid-rolls unaffected (coverage=1.0 branch); non-byte baked-in-ad episodes unaffected (must NOT drop those — recall). LOW risk, one carve-out. FIX B (quorum hardening for the no-byte [89.6-204]) MEDIUM risk (recall). FIX C (upstream FM precision) = the epic's demote-FM long game, separate bead. Cheap confirmatory: re-run baseline dump x3 → head windows in any rediff-OFF run retires the 'only-with-rediff' premise. Sites: RediffSlotOwnership.swift:426-487 (FIX A), BackfillEvidenceFusion.swift:1043-1069 (FIX B), AtomEvidenceProjector.swift:82-140 (FM anchor).
SPLIT (2026-07-17): FIX A (byte-slot containment clip, the WIDTH fix) stays in xsdz.58. The pure-FM over-anchor of the [89.6-204] monologue (no byte slot, held only by evidence quorum, one musicBed-entry from eligible) is FILED SEPARATELY as an FM-precision bead (below) — it's the epic's demote-FM long game, not a width/rediff fix. Dan constraint on FIX A: MUST NOT break other shows (baked-in-ad episodes casefile/ted-business/doac have non-byte eligible windows that must stay untouched).
R1 CLEAN (2026-07-17): all 7 adversarial angles verified; existing suites unmodified+green (94 tests/10 suites incl. veto read-side); FIX A monotonically narrows (can never eat MORE content than the pre-fix over-anchor). CHROMA-RESIDUAL DECISION (Dan): OPTION (a) — clip BOTH byte and chroma slots, ACCEPT the residual. Rationale: (a) reduces content-eating on ALL ~44 rediff episodes (byte-exact on 36, chroma ±sec-fuzz-but-monotonically-narrower on ~8), baked-in-ad shows untouched; (b) byte-only would leave the 8 chroma episodes' FM over-anchors bloated (bug unfixed, quorum-dependent). NOT adding a byte-only gate. FIX A stands as-implemented. (Rejected companion policy: 'auto-skip only on byte-exact widths' — bigger question, not now.)
LANDED on main (2026-07-17) — FIX A byte-slot containment clip. Two-consecutive-clean (R1+R2). Safety invariant proven airtight: persisted width is always the slot extent (⊆ core, narrower) or minted core (status-quo), never wider than the FM over-anchor; holds for byte AND chroma; don't-break-other-shows guaranteed (non-byte spans exit at .noCandidatePairs); veto path inert for clips. Fixes conan [0-88.32]→[0-60.369]. NEXT: re-measure (byte-first + FIX A) with pre/post window diff as the don't-break-shows check.

title: Canonicalize mixed fast/final transcripts and close the final-ASR detection loop
description:
## Problem

runBackfill selects every pass=final chunk as the atomization transcript whenever even one final chunk exists, while FinalPassRetranscriptionRunner creates final chunks only around already-detected candidate windows. The result can be a candidate-local atom timeline instead of full-episode coverage. In the same run, lexical scanning still receives the uncanonicalized mixed-pass chunk array, so overlapping fast/final text can contribute twice. The final-pass runner appends improved chunks but does not trigger detection/revalidation afterward.

## Steps to Reproduce

Persist full-episode pass=fast chunks, then run FinalPassRetranscriptionRunner for one eligible ad candidate so it appends pass=final chunks only around that window. Fetch the mixed chunk set and call runBackfill. Observe that TranscriptAtomizer receives only the final subset while LexicalScanner receives both passes; then complete the final-pass runner and observe no detector revalidation is scheduled.

## Scope

Build one deterministic canonical transcript where final chunks replace overlapping fast coverage and fast chunks remain elsewhere; deduplicate overlaps before every lexical, catalog, FM, and atomization consumer. After final-pass chunks are persisted, enqueue or invoke the appropriate detector revalidation for the affected asset. Add coverage and duplicate-evidence diagnostics so partial replacement cannot silently recur.
acceptance_criteria: A mixed-pass fixture with candidate-local final chunks retains full episode coverage, uses final text only in overlapping intervals, and produces no duplicate lexical evidence; completing final-pass transcription causes a detector re-run/revalidation; an all-fast and an all-final transcript remain behaviorally unchanged; focused unit/integration tests fail on main and pass with the fix.

title: Make backfill authoritative over nonterminal hot-path ad windows
description:
## Problem

The hot path has transactional reconciliation and retirement, but runBackfill creates fresh UUID AdWindows and insertAdWindows only appends them. A hot candidate rejected by backfill can therefore survive beside the authoritative fusion result and can still be promoted by SkipOrchestrator when its confidence clears the orchestrator threshold.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run the hot path on a fixture that emits a candidate above the orchestrator entry threshold. Run backfill on the same asset with evidence that rejects that span or emits a refined overlapping span. Fetch AdWindows and feed them to SkipOrchestrator. Observe that the stale hot candidate remains because backfill only inserts fresh rows and does not retire unmatched nonterminal hot rows.

## Scope

Define the ownership contract between hot and backfill outputs. Atomically reconcile the current detector version's nonterminal hot windows against the final backfill set: preserve terminal/user-owned history, retire stale candidates, reuse stable IDs for matched spans where practical, and deliver retirements to SkipOrchestrator before or atomically with replacement decisions. Make reruns idempotent.
acceptance_criteria: A hot false positive absent from backfill is retired and cannot later auto-skip; a matched hot/backfill span produces one active window; terminal/user-corrected history is preserved; repeated backfills are idempotent; persistence plus SkipOrchestrator integration tests cover add, replace, retire, and rollback behavior.
notes:
DESIGN PROPOSAL (2026-07-20, read-only investigation): ownership contract for backfill-authoritative reconciliation. Full doc in session scratchpad ud4n-ownership-contract-design.md.

RECONCILABLE INVARIANT (correctness backbone): a row is backfill-authoritative iff detectorVersion==config AND decisionState in {candidate,confirmed,suppressed} AND !id.hasPrefix('shared-') AND boundaryState not in {correctionReplay,userMarked,userConfirmedSuggested}. Every reconcilable row absent from the authoritative backfill set is retired -> satisfies FP-retirement AC independent of match quality.

RECOMMENDED = Design B: deterministic content-addressed fusion ids ('fusion-'+hashedId(assetId,detectorVersion,startOrdinal,endOrdinal); hashedId exists BackfillJobRunner:2200) instead of UUID(); reconcile = set-difference; hard-DELETE retirement in one atomic AnalysisStore txn (sibling of upsertHotPathAdWindows:7310, INSERT OR REPLACE + deleteAdWindows:7335); retire-before-replace orchestrator delivery in runBackfill Step 17 (:5371) BEFORE receiveAdDecisionResults. Idempotency by construction, no id-remap plumbing, fixes decision_events orphaning, NO schema migration (ad_windows.id already TEXT PK, no child FK). Fallback = Design A (keep UUIDs, mirror reconcileHotPathWindows:8127, but needs id-remap across fusionWindows/decisionResults/decisionEvents/metadata = main risk).

FILES: AnalysisStore (reconcileBackfillAdWindows), AdDetectionService (buildFusionAdWindow:7196 id, new reconcileBackfillWindows, persist swap :5296, Step 17 retire). AnalysisCoordinator/SkipOrchestrator need NO change. revalidateFromFeatures inherits the fix. 13-case test matrix (add/replace/retire/idempotency/terminal-preserve/correction-replay/imported/other-version/rollback/ordering/suppressed-flip).

6 DECISIONS FOR DAN: (1) MAIN: Design A vs B (fusion id semantics — content-addressed PK ok?). (2) hard-delete vs soft-retire (audit trail via schema v30?). (3) scope current detectorVersion only, or cross-version cleanup? (4) OK to retire/replace algorithmic .suppressed rows? (5) hot->backfill: clean retire+mint-new (one-frame banner re-emit, avoids edge-anchor trap) vs re-stamp anchors on reused id? (6) IoU 0.5 continuity threshold ok given boundary-collapse (10-18% width), or overlap/min-duration? Implementation blocked on these — esp. Q1.
DAN DECISIONS (2026-07-20): Q1 = Design B (content-addressed fusion ids 'fusion-'+hashedId). Q2 = HARD-DELETE retirement (no soft-retire, no migration). Q3-Q6 not explicitly answered → implement with the design doc's recommended defaults (Dan can override): Q3 scope = current detectorVersion only; Q4 = include .suppressed in the reconcilable set; Q5 = hot->backfill uses clean retire+mint-new (edge-anchor-safe, accept one-frame banner re-emit); Q6 IoU 0.5 continuity threshold (not load-bearing for correctness in Design B). READY TO IMPLEMENT with these.

## Scope

(3) Presence-gated oracle emissions PROJECTED — 47/198 tier-a slots carry >=1 independent production presence core (23 episodes, 68.5 min, mean 87.4s/slot); 151 slots correctly gated out (no core -> no emission). Emission set: /Users/dabrams/playhead-baselines/oracle-emissions-20260715.json. STILL OUTSTANDING before go/no-go: Dan's fresh ear audit, xsdz.30 days-gap measurement, xsdz.34 correction read-side, xsdz.28 re-fetch policy, bandwidth/latency accounting, rollback thresholds.
LABEL-TOLERANCE NOTE for the 2026-07-15 oracle ear-audit promotion (Dan, mid-audit): Nikki Glaser show->ad transitions are abrupt enough that his rebound bounds may be off by up to +-0.5s despite aiming for +-0.1s. When the review file is frozen/promoted to evaluation labels, nikki-glaser rows get an explicit boundary_tolerance_seconds=0.5 (others default tighter). Boundary-error scoring against these labels should treat errors within tolerance as zero. Also pending from mid-audit reports: 1 reject so far (~25+ rows in; if it is the nikki-...515 row whose slot end was clamped 81s for a suspected feed-variant mismatch, exclude from the precision denominator with cause rather than counting against the oracle).
CORRECTION (Dan): Nikki Glaser DOES have a stinger — just a very short one. His boundary marks may land in the last ~0.5s of the stinger or the first ~0.5s of the ad; the +-0.5s tolerance is specifically at the stinger->ad seam. CONTRACT AMENDMENT (strategy panel 2026-07-07, high-confidence): rediff is the SOLE production width SETTER. Episodes/intervals WITHOUT rediff coverage fall through to STATUS-QUO transcript-width behavior — NOT to SpliceSlotResolver's acoustic pair-finding. The acoustic channel runs SHADOW/EVAL-ONLY (a chance-level signal, AUC 0.547, cannot safely reweight a good width). Documented reversal bar to ever restore acoustic width authority: AUC>=0.70 AND slot-feasibility>=0.60 at control-FP<=0.10 on the xsdz.24 harness. DESIGN INPUTS FROM xsdz.27 (fingerprint store, converged 2026-07-07) — MUST honor in the integration:
1. CAPTURE SOURCE: the download-time whole-episode PCM buffer (~230MB@16k transient) is why xsdz.27 kept capture behind a default-OFF flag. For xsdz.29, the RECOMMENDED capture source is the iOS 27 AVPlayerItemSampleBufferOutput AS-PLAYED TAP — fingerprints the literally-played (DAI-stitched) bytes, streams incrementally, no whole-episode buffer. Evaluated + documented in EpisodeFingerprintCapture.swift header; build it here.
2. RESAMPLE->FINGERPRINT PATH IDENTITY: the re-fetched B-side MUST reuse the EXACT same resample(16k->11025 linear)->ChromaFingerprinter path xsdz.27 pins, or A/B fingerprints are incomparable. The resampler identity is broader than algorithmVersion (tripwired in xsdz.27) — treat the (resampler + fingerprinter) pair as one versioned unit.
3. sourceAudioIdentity GATE: xsdz.27's fetchEpisodeFingerprints gates on algorithmVersion ONLY. xsdz.29 MUST additionally compare the stored sourceAudioIdentity against the asset's current assetFingerprint before trusting a stored stream as the rediff A-side — else an assetId reused for re-downloaded audio returns a version-matching but audio-mismatched stream. title: Offline ground-truth splice-edge calibration study: score acoustic edges at rediff-true splice points (FM-free)
description:
Answers THE question the illustrative eval surfaced: qualification is floor-limited (edgeBelowFloor 11/28, noCandidatePairs 6/28) — are the floors miscalibrated, is the break detector the bottleneck, or are CDN splices genuinely softer than the design assumed? We can answer FM-FREE because the tier-a rediff gives GROUND-TRUTH splice times: every DAI slot edge in playhead-dogfood-diagnostics-tier-a-rediff.json (41 episodes, adSlots[].startSeconds/endSeconds) is a true server-side splice point in staged audio.

INPUTS (read from PLAYHEAD_CORPUS_ROOT, default /Users/dabrams/playhead): tier-a rediff JSON (episodeId + adSlots with startSeconds/endSeconds + rotated flag); staged audio via TestFixtures/Corpus/Snapshots/manifest.json audioPath mapping; NO cores, NO FM, NO baseline dump needed.

METHOD (per episode, on the iPhone 17 Pro SIMULATOR — proven FM-free chain from xsdz.23's harness): AnalysisAudioService().decode -> FeatureExtractionService(store:).extract -> [FeatureWindow] -> AcousticBreakDetector.detectBreaks -> [AcousticBreak]; edge scoring via the candidate-time API AudioForensicsBoundaryDetector.scoreCandidateEdge (added in xsdz.19). Then per TRUE splice edge (each slot start + end):
1. DETECTOR RECALL: distance to nearest AcousticBreak candidate; report fraction within ±2s / ±5s / ±8s / ±15s. (No candidate near a true splice = detector bottleneck / explains noCandidatePairs.)
2. SCORE AT TRUTH: sigma-normalized edge-step score AT the true splice time AND at the nearest candidate; full distributions (min/p25/median/p75/max + histogram buckets).
3. CONTROLS / SEPARABILITY: score at N random control times per episode (>=60s from any slot edge, uniform over the episode) — if true-splice and control score distributions overlap heavily, lowering floors floods FPs and the fix is detector quality, not floors.
4. FLOOR SWEEP: for floor in 0.05,0.075,0.10,0.125,0.15,0.20,0.25: fraction of true slots where BOTH edges have a candidate within ±8s scoring >= floor (i.e. slot-qualification feasibility ceiling at that floor), AND control false-positive rate at the same floor. Present as a table.
5. Break out rotated vs non-rotated slots if the rediff flag is meaningful.

OUTPUT: gitignored JSON + markdown report at corpus root (playhead-dogfood-diagnostics-splice-calibration.{json,md}) + printed summary. The markdown must END with a data-backed RECOMMENDATION, one of: (a) floors miscalibrated -> proposed new floor values with supporting numbers; (b) detector bottleneck -> which sub-signal/config of AcousticBreakDetector misses true splices; (c) premise problem -> true splices genuinely score at control levels; or a mix. NO code changes to production floors/detector in this bead — measurement only; tuning is a follow-up decision.

HARNESS SHAPE: extend the xsdz.23 pattern — env-gated XCTest (PLAYHEAD_SPLICE_CALIBRATION=1) in the PlayheadSpliceSlotEval test plan (env vars must ride the .xctestplan — command-line env does NOT reach the sim test process, proven in xsdz.23); pure, unit-tested aggregation/report logic (distance calc, sweep table, separability stats) with the live suite as a thin driver. Per-episode soft-skip on missing audio (report skipped list). 41 decode+extract passes unattended is fine (~1-3 min each).

Branch: continue on bead/playhead-xsdz-eval in worktree .worktrees/eval (stacks on the xsdz.23 harness commit 931c3386).
acceptance_criteria: Pure aggregation logic unit-tested (distance-to-candidate, floor-sweep table, separability stats, report rendering); live run covers all rediff episodes with staged audio (skips reported); report contains detector-recall table, true-vs-control score distributions, floor-sweep qualification-feasibility vs control-FP table, rotated breakout, and a data-backed recommendation; JSON+md written to corpus root; no production code changed; committed to bead/playhead-xsdz-eval; no new FastTests failures beyond known corpus-drift + load flakes.
close_reason: Study COMPLETE (commit 9cf10572 on bead/playhead-xsdz-eval). VERDICT: detectorBottleneck — AcousticBreakDetector misses true DAI splices: recall@±8s=20.9% (±2s: 3.7%) over 349 in-range ground-truth edges; near-random separability AUC(bestWithin8)=0.547, scoreAtTruth-vs-control=0.511 (median score AT the true splice time = 0.002); floor sweep proves floors CANNOT fix it (slot-feasibility ceiling 6.0% at floor 0.05 vs 3.6% at production 0.15; control FP within budget at all floors). Drift-guard applied per review caveat: provably drift-free head-anchored edges still only 35.7% recall — the verdict survives drift skepticism, though drift depresses the other buckets somewhat. 34 episodes / 198 slots / 396 edges / 680 seeded controls; 7 episodes skipped (no rediff slots). IMPLICATIONS: (1) do NOT spend the FM/macOS-27 canonical eval — it would re-measure a <=6% feasibility ceiling; (2) xsdz.15 slot machinery is sound but its acoustic width-oracle is too weak to activate; (3) strongest width-oracle candidate is now playhead-xsdz.16 (on-device rediff double-fetch — exact boundaries, zero acoustics); acoustic splice-detection R&D is the longer-shot parallel track. Report: playhead-dogfood-diagnostics-splice-calibration.{json,md} at repo root (gitignored).

title: Backfill slot-ownership integration: post-decode SpliceSlot span rewrite + AnchorRef.spliceSlot + refiner skip (flag-gated OFF)
description:

NEW POST-DECODE SLOT PASS in runBackfill — after decode, after assetAcousticBreaks (:3133-3135), BEFORE the per-span boundary-refine loop (:3177-3248). Do NOT call it 'step 12.5' (doc-comment :2616-2633 numbers decode=11, fusion=12, refine=13, refine physically before fusion) — ADD the pass to that doc-comment with a neutral name.

INTERVAL SEMANTICS (pinned, used UNIFORMLY in every rule below and in bead C's mirrors): OVERLAP = intersection of POSITIVE DURATION; intervals sharing only an endpoint are DISJOINT; FULLY ENCLOSED = subset-or-equal (shared endpoints allowed). This matters concretely: in a pod with a STRONG inner splice, both spans' resolvers draw from the same assetAcousticBreaks array, so slot1=[L,B] and slot2=[B,R] share the bitwise-identical Double B — they are DISJOINT and BOTH keep (full pod coverage, the flagship win). A closed-interval reading would demote half the pod.

PASS ORDER (pinned — ordering changes output, so it is spec): (1) resolve ALL spans' would-be slots; (2) per-span NEGATIVE-BANK VETO; (3) GREEDY COLLISION among veto-survivors; (4) SLOT-vs-MINTED OVERLAP (FIXPOINT, below); (5) apply rewrites. All policies stated on WOULD-BE slot intervals, pre-rewrite. REASON PRECEDENCE for diagnostics/shadow: a span's final disposition is the LAST pass that touched it (bead C relies on this).

RESOLVER INPUT SOURCES (pinned, all four): core interval = the span's CURRENT post-decode [startTime, endTime] (post-Use-A-snap — the same interval the rewrite overwrites; bead C's mintedStart/mintedEnd are this interval); episodeWindows = in-scope featureWindows; breaks = assetAcousticBreaks (:3133-3135); vetoed-time-ranges = intervals of atoms with correctionMask == .userVetoed (MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder.swift:153). HONESTY NOTE: runBackfill projects with NoCorrectionMaskProvider (:2813); no production CorrectionMaskProvider exists, so that source is EMPTY in production today — implement + test with synthetic vetoes; do NOT claim production FP containment until a real provider is wired.

NEGATIVE-BANK VETO (pinned; bank entries are show-scoped token fingerprints, NO time data — NegativeFingerprintBank.swift:44-94): runs AFTER resolve. When crossEpisodeMemoryEnabled and a bank is wired: tokenize atoms of the SLOT interval AND (separately) the CORE interval (same tokenization/clamping as :3313-3342 — NOTE that clamping is a PREFIX truncation at maxTokenCount=100, which is why the absorbee check below exists), bank.bestMatch on each; DISCARD the slot if EITHER matches (>= defaultMatchThreshold) — either-match prevents token DILUTION from defeating today's suppression. Fallback receives today's suppression as before. Dormant when crossEpisodeMemoryEnabled OFF (default) — document.

GREEDY COLLISION (pinned — pairwise 'colliding' is NOT transitive): rank veto-survivors by core-overlap fraction DESC, tiebreak earlier core start; walk the ranking, KEEP a slot iff its would-be interval is disjoint (per INTERVAL SEMANTICS) from every already-KEPT slot, else DEMOTE to minted. (Chain A[0,60] B[50,120] C[110,180], A first: keep A, demote B, KEEP C.)

SLOT-vs-MINTED OVERLAP (pinned FIXPOINT — approved by Dan 2026-07-06 over the conservative one-sweep: overshooting minted extents are NORMAL near inner splices, so a one-sweep ownership-blind check sees phantom conflicts with intervals the rewrite is about to vacate and demotes half a pod): the comparison set for a kept slot EXCLUDES still-KEPT slots' own minted intervals (they are being vacated). Iterate (a)+(b) to a FIXPOINT: (a) a kept slot with >=1 PARTIAL overlap (positive-duration intersection, neither encloses) with any interval in the current comparison set (non-kept spans' minted intervals) is DEMOTED and ABSORBS NOTHING; (b) ABSORPTION IS ALL-OR-NOTHING PER SLOT: for each still-kept slot, collect every OTHER non-kept span whose minted interval it fully encloses (the slot's OWN span is never an absorbee — coreCoverage=1.0 makes self-enclosure the normal case; kept-encloses-other-kept is impossible post-greedy since coreCoverage>=0.8 forces slot-slot overlap that collision already resolved); when crossEpisodeMemoryEnabled with a bank wired, bank-check EACH enclosed span's core tokens BEFORE any absorption (prefix truncation at maxTokenCount=100 defeats the slot-level check for long slots); if ANY enclosed span matches, DEMOTE the slot and absorb NOTHING under it (ALL enclosed spans keep minted; today's suppression runs for each); ABSORPTION IS COMPUTED ONLY AT THE FIXPOINT (pinned): during iteration, (b) only DEMOTES (any-enclosed-bank-match demotes the slot); absorbed dispositions are assigned once, from the FINAL kept set, after the iteration terminates — equivalently, demotion of a would-be absorber reverts its would-be absorbees to their prior-pass disposition. Rationale: per-round absorption lets a slot absorb span P in round r and get demoted in round r+1 (via an interval re-introduced by a DIFFERENT slot's (b) demotion), leaving P dropped with NO surviving span covering it — span loss that also biases the eval pro-treatment (P removed from the treatment arm while the demoted absorber is not substituted). Deferral is behavior-neutral otherwise: an absorbee's minted interval can never positive-overlap any OTHER kept slot (enclosure by K plus overlap with K-prime would force K∩K-prime overlap, impossible post-greedy). At the fixpoint, absorbed spans are dropped pre-fusion; atoms feed the absorber's ledger; log identifiers. EACH DEMOTION (from (a) or (b)) RE-INTRODUCES that span's minted interval into the comparison set and the iteration repeats — the kept-set shrinks monotonically, so the fixpoint terminates deterministically in <=N rounds. NO single-sweep order is sound: a later (b) bank-demotion re-introduces a minted interval that can partially overlap an already-surviving slot. COMPOSITION GUARANTEE (state in code comments, assert in tests): at the fixpoint, final persisted spans are PAIRWISE DISJOINT per INTERVAL SEMANTICS (decoder resolveOverlaps at MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder.swift:385-408 guarantees the minted-minted leg).

EMPTY-ATOM-SET CHECK ORDER (pinned): the INTERSECTS/empty-set check is a PER-SLOT DISQUALIFICATION run BEFORE pass 3 (it needs only the slot interval + atom stream, no cross-span state): reason=emptyAtomSet, minted interval STAYS in every comparison set, ineligible to keep or absorb. Rationale: discovering emptiness at rewrite time (after the fixpoint) would resurrect a minted interval that kept slots were allowed to ignore — breaking the pairwise-disjointness guarantee the tests assert.

SHARED DISPOSITION FUNCTION (pinned structure — the eval's validity rests on shadow == flag-ON by construction, not by hand-written mirror tests alone): TWO-PHASE SHAPE, because NegativeFingerprintBank is an actor (NegativeFingerprintBank.swift:110; bestMatch :350 is awaited at :3336-3342) and a pure synchronous function cannot call it, while pass 4(b) discovers absorbees only mid-fixpoint: (i) run pass 1 (pure resolver) for all spans; (ii) await the bank ONCE for a VERDICT TABLE — core-token match for EVERY span (any span can become an absorbee) and slot-token match for every span with a resolved slot; (iii) invoke the PURE, side-effect-free disposition function — passes 2-4 with the per-slot empty-set check folded in before pass 3, bank checks as table lookups — returning per-span dispositions (final reason + would-be slot). Flag-ON applies them (pass 5); bead C's shadow EMITS them. Do not bury the pass policy inline in runBackfill.

REWRITE (per surviving kept span): 1. startTime/endTime = slot interval; 2. RECOMPUTE ordinals — atoms whose interval INTERSECTS (positive-duration) the slot (cannot be empty here: the per-slot empty-set disqualification ran before pass 3; keep a defensive assert); 3. append AnchorRef.spliceSlot (case ships in playhead-xsdz.22; presence IS the marker); 4. recompute id via DecodedSpan.makeId (DecodedSpan.swift:30) and RE-PERSIST: either move the post-decode upsert (upsertDecodedSpans :2822) to after this pass (absorbed spans then never upserted), or re-upsert rewritten spans AND delete superseded-id rows AND delete ABSORBED spans' rows (no successor id; surviving row = ghost nested in the slot span). Unchanged-ordinal shape: makeId unchanged, no superseded row — handle both.

USER CORRECTIONS: ordinal-range-scoped (CorrectionScope.exactSpan, UserCorrectionStore.swift:26-42). Tests: (i) .exactSpan correction against a slot-owned span resolves next run; (ii) synthetic-span path (:916-939) unaffected; (iii) ABSORPTION ORPHANS .exactSpan corrections on the absorbed span — PINNED v1: document + test the orphaning; when a real CorrectionMaskProvider lands, not-an-ad corrections must flow into vetoed-time-ranges so .vetoNewlyEnclosed prevents the absorption (note forward path in comment).

REFINER SKIP (approved): spans carrying .spliceSlot bypass BracketAwareBoundaryRefiner AND BoundaryRefiner (±3s clamps would blur physical splices). Non-slot spans keep today's exact path.

CLOBBER GUARD (pinned): the Phase 5 projector (runPhase5ProjectorPhase, upsert :5476) upserts FRESHLY decoded spans which never carry .spliceSlot — a per-row provenance filter can NEVER fire; worse, in the changed-ordinal shape a fresh decode re-mints the ORIGINAL ordinals -> original makeId -> RE-INSERTS the superseded-id row this bead just deleted (resurrecting the ghost row). Required: either (a) confirm + document that the projector never runs post-backfill for the same asset, or (b) skip/filter the projector's ENTIRE upsert for any asset that has persisted slot-owned rows (query .spliceSlot provenance per asset). Test must assert no superseded-id row reappears after a Phase-5 run over a slot-owned asset.

DOUBLE-COUNTING (pinned): slot width evidence and the .audioForensics entry (:4809-4815) derive from the SAME discontinuity — SUPPRESS .audioForensics on slot-owned spans. Revisit in bead C.

FLAG: spliceSlotOwnershipEnabled on AdDetectionConfig, default OFF (pattern: audioForensicsEnabled, false at :483). OFF: slot pass never invoked; OUTPUT byte-identical — test-proven. (Bead C's shadow separately gated, exempt.)

SCOPE: backfill only. Hot path/Tier-1 and BoundaryExpander untouched.

INTERACTIONS: DecisionMapper duration-prior on wider spans; SpanFinalizer >180s split cannot trigger (slot capped <=180); fusion over slot interval picks up additional entries (assert ledger-mass increase).

TESTS (Swift Testing): unit — rewrite + INTERSECTS ordinals + makeId (changed AND unchanged shapes); empty-atom-set fallback; persistence (slot-owned row correct; no orphaned superseded row; absorbed row absent — row-count + makeId-absence); refiner-skip keyed on .spliceSlot only; .audioForensics suppression on slot-owned only; negative-bank veto (core-matches -> DISCARDED + suppression fires; widened-only -> discarded; neither -> allowed; flag OFF -> skipped); ABSORBEE bank check ALL-OR-NOTHING (slot enclosing one bank-CLEAN + one bank-MATCHED span -> slot DEMOTED, BOTH survive as minted, NOTHING absorbed, suppression runs for the matched one as today); PASS-ORDER (A+B collide, A wins, A vetoed -> B keeps); GREEDY-CHAIN (keep A+C, demote B); STRONG-INNER-SPLICE POD (slot1=[L,B], slot2=[B,R] share bitwise-identical B -> BOTH kept, both rewritten); OVERSHOOT POD (span1 minted crosses B by ~5s, both slots meet at B -> fixpoint excludes kept slots' minted intervals, BOTH still kept and rewritten — no phantom demotion); ABSORBER-DEMOTED-AFTER-ENCLOSING (K2 encloses clean span P and would absorb it; K2 is demoted in round 2 by K1's re-introduced interval -> P SURVIVES as minted with its prior-pass reason, row NOT deleted); FIXPOINT RE-INTRODUCTION (slot K1 demoted in (b) by a bank-matched absorbee -> K1's minted interval re-enters the set and partially overlaps surviving slot K2 -> K2 demoted in the next round; assert 2-round convergence); ENCLOSES-AND-CLIPS (S demoted, X survives, nothing absorbed); enclosure absorb (dropped, logged, row deleted); FINAL-DISJOINTNESS (positive-duration semantics) asserted on every integration fixture; absorbed-span-with-correction orphaning; weak-inner-splice pod (one kept slot, loser disposed per pass order, distinct makeIds); flag OFF byte-identical; .exactSpan re-match; Phase-5 guard (no superseded-id reappearance). Integration: qualifying widens correctly; non-qualifying byte-identical; mixed episode.

CONSTRAINTS: DEVELOPER_DIR=Xcode-beta required; PlayheadFastTests plan; known 3 corpus-drift fails + load flakes pre-existing.
acceptance_criteria: Flag OFF: OUTPUT byte-identical, slot pass never invoked (bead C's shadow exempt). Flag ON: interval semantics (touching=disjoint) proven by the strong-inner-splice pod fixture (BOTH kept); pass order proven (A-vetoed-B-keeps); greedy collision proven (chain: keep A+C); overlap FIXPOINT proven (encloses-and-clips: S demoted, X survives; OVERSHOOT pod: both kept, no phantom demotion; re-introduction fixture converges in 2 rounds; absorbee bank check ALL-OR-NOTHING: one-clean-one-matched -> slot demoted, both survive minted; absorbed rows deleted); FINAL persisted spans pairwise disjoint (positive-duration) on every integration fixture; INTERSECTS ordinals + makeId + persistence for changed/unchanged shapes; empty-atom-set disqualification runs pre-pass-3 (fixture proves minted interval remains in comparison sets); absorbed-correction orphaning pinned; refiners skipped ONLY on slot-owned; .audioForensics suppressed only on slot-owned; EITHER-matches veto incl. dormant-when-OFF; Phase-5 guard proven by no-superseded-id-reappearance test; no new FastTests failures beyond known 3 + flakes. (AnchorRef case itself: see playhead-xsdz.22.) Passes 2-4 (including the pre-pass-3 empty-set check) live in a pure, synchronous shared disposition function taking pass-1 resolver outputs and the pre-awaited bank verdict table as inputs; flag-ON pass 5 and bead C shadow both consume its per-span dispositions. Absorption computed only at the fixpoint (absorber-demoted fixture: enclosed span survives). Disposition function is two-phase (pre-awaited bank verdict table; pure synchronous passes 2-4) and absorbee domain excludes self/kept spans.

title: SpliceSlot + SpliceSlotResolver: pure slot-resolution engine (types, edge scoring, pair selection, qualification gates)
description:
Bead A of approved xsdz.15 — the pure slot-resolution engine. NO pipeline wiring (bead B = playhead-xsdz.20). SELF-CONTAINED: do NOT rely on docs/xsdz15-boundary-authority-inversion-design.md (untracked — absent from bead worktrees); this description carries the design.

WHY: playhead-4xqf — pipeline covers ~18% of true DAI ad width. Root cause (code-traced 2026-07-05): span width is minted at MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder.formRuns (MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder.swift:147-192) as the anchored-atom run extent; downstream can only nudge edges ±8s (Use-A snap, snapRadiusSeconds=8) + ±3s (refiner maxBoundaryAdjust). DAI ads are spliced server-side — splices ARE the true boundaries. Approved inversion: when a qualifying splice pair encloses enough of a presence core, the slot owns WIDTH; transcript/FM keep owning PRESENCE.

INTERVAL SEMANTICS (pinned, same convention playhead-xsdz.20 pins pipeline-wide): interval intersection means POSITIVE-DURATION overlap; intervals sharing only an endpoint do NOT intersect.

DELIVERABLES (new Playhead/Services/AdDetection/SpliceSlotResolver.swift):
1. struct SpliceSlot: Sendable, Equatable {startTime, endTime, startEdge, endEdge, slotConfidence, coreCoverage} + SpliceEdgeEvidence {time, stepScore, contributingSignals}.
2. SpliceSlotResolver.Configuration with DOCUMENTED defaults: searchRadiusSeconds=120 (outward per side); inwardToleranceSeconds=8 (mirrors snapRadiusSeconds — minted extents can OVERSHOOT the true splice); slotDuration 5...180s; spliceEdgeFloor + slotConfidenceFloor (calibrate against synthetic fixtures, document rationale); minCoreCoverage=0.8; contentCutPenalty=1.5.
3. API: resolveWithDiagnostics(core interval + vetoed-time-ranges, breaks: [AcousticBreak], episodeWindows: [FeatureWindow]) -> (slot: SpliceSlot?, diagnostics: SpliceSlotDiagnostics); resolve(...) -> SpliceSlot? thin wrapper. SpliceSlotDiagnostics: Sendable, Equatable {bestGeometryValidPair: SpliceSlot?, failureReason: FailureReason?}. POPULATION CONTRACT (pinned): failureReason set on every non-qualifying outcome, nil when qualified; bestGeometryValidPair populated whenever >=1 geometry-valid pair exists (the champion, pre-qualification), nil otherwise (.noCandidatePairs, .degenerateCore, .durationOutOfRange); on QUALIFIED outcomes it equals the returned slot. FailureReason: .degenerateCore, .noCandidatePairs, .durationOutOfRange, .edgeBelowFloor, .slotConfidenceBelowFloor, .coreCoverageBelowMinimum, .vetoNewlyEnclosed. Pure, deterministic, no I/O, no actor hops, token-free (the negative-bank veto is bead B's, layered after resolve). Inputs caller-supplied; bead B pins sources.
   Algorithm: (0) GUARD: zero-/negative-length core -> (nil, .degenerateCore) before any coverage math; (a) candidate edges per side = AcousticBreaks (AcousticBreakDetector.swift:22-29) in [coreEdge − inwardToleranceSeconds, coreEdge + searchRadiusSeconds] (mirrored for start side); (b) score each candidate time with the sigma-normalized edge-step math from AudioForensicsBoundaryDetector (loudness/RMS + spectral-flux + noise-floor + musicProbability/environment steps; AcousticFeatures/AudioForensicsBoundaryDetector.swift:272-353); (c) PINNED CHAMPION-SCAN (total order — the naive pairwise 'wider beats tighter at >=1.5x' relation is NON-TRANSITIVE with 3+ pairs and is NOT the spec): geometry-valid pairs = {slotStart < slotEnd, slot ∩ core has POSITIVE DURATION (a pair sharing only an endpoint with the core is NOT geometry-valid), duration in slotDuration range}; DURATION DIAGNOSTIC (pinned): geometry-valid set EMPTY but >=1 pair failed ONLY the duration bound -> (nil, .durationOutOfRange, nil pair); empty otherwise -> (nil, .noCandidatePairs). Sort geometry-valid pairs by non-core seconds ASC, ties by higher pairScore = min(edge stepScores), then earlier startTime, then earlier endTime; champion = first; scan remaining in order — candidate REPLACES champion iff pairScore(candidate) >= contentCutPenalty × pairScore(champion); final champion wins. contentCutPenalty=1.5 mirrors AsymmetricSnapScorer editorial-clip weighting (AsymmetricSnapScorer.swift:72-85); (d) qualification gates on the FINAL CHAMPION ONLY (pinned: do NOT pre-filter sub-floor edges, do NOT search for another qualifying pair — a disqualified champion means fallback BY DESIGN): both edges >= spliceEdgeFloor, slotConfidence (min edge) >= slotConfidenceFloor, coreCoverage = |slot ∩ core| / |core| >= minCoreCoverage, NO vetoed time-range newly enclosed beyond those already intersecting the core. Gate failure -> (nil, reason) with bestGeometryValidPair = the champion.
4. REFACTOR AudioForensicsBoundaryDetector to expose candidate-time edge scoring WITHOUT changing existing buildEntries(span:episodeWindows:fusionConfig:) fusion behavior (:155-216) — regression test: identical inputs -> identical EvidenceLedgerEntry pre/post refactor.

TESTS (Swift Testing, PlayheadTests/Services/AdDetection/SpliceSlotResolverTests.swift): qualifying DAI-like fixture -> exact slot AND bestGeometryValidPair == slot; no-breaks -> (nil, .noCandidatePairs, nil pair); TOUCHING-ONLY pair (shares only an endpoint with core) excluded from geometry-valid -> (nil, .noCandidatePairs); only-pair-too-long -> (nil, .durationOutOfRange, nil pair); edge below floor -> (nil, .edgeBelowFloor) with champion populated; DISQUALIFIED-CHAMPION-SHADOWS: near-core champion pairScore 1.4 (floor 1.5), true pair 2.0 < 1.5×1.4 -> (nil, .edgeBelowFloor), NOT rescued; coreCoverage < 0.8 -> (nil, .coreCoverageBelowMinimum); veto newly enclosed -> (nil, .vetoNewlyEnclosed), veto already intersecting core -> allowed; CHAMPION-SCAN: 2-pair 1.4x LOSES / 1.6x WINS; 3-pair cycle (T 2s score 1.0, M 10s 1.4, W 20s 2.0 -> deterministically W via T->W); equal non-core + equal pairScore -> earlier startTime; zero-length core -> (nil, .degenerateCore); inward-tolerance edge (coreEdge − 8s accepted, beyond rejected); determinism incl. diagnostics; degenerate (empty windows, single break). Plus detector-refactor regression test.

CONSTRAINTS: no new frameworks; match surrounding idiom; Sendable-clean; iOS 27 floor (#222); DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode-beta.app/Contents/Developer required. PlayheadFastTests plan, iPhone 17 Pro sim; known 3 corpus-drift fails + load flakes — do not chase.
acceptance_criteria: All unit tests green incl. 3-pair cycle, disqualified-champion-shadows, and touching-only-pair fixtures; detector regression test proves byte-identical fusion entries; diagnostics population contract exact; positive-duration geometry semantics proven; resolver pure + deterministic; ZERO production call sites; no new FastTests failures beyond known 3 + flakes.

Round-8 pin folded 2026-07-06: positive-duration slot∩core in the geometry-valid predicate + touching-only fixture. Description is the single source of truth.

title: SPIKE: Core AI custom model — own the ad classifier (toolchain proof, then golden-corpus fine-tune vs FM head-to-head)
description:
RE-SCOPED 2026-07-06 (Dan-approved) from the dead LoRA-adapter spike: Apple's adapter toolkit is discontinued at 26.0.0 and SystemLanguageModel.Adapter is obsoleted in iOS 27. The successor is Core AI: on-device inference of OUR OWN compiled models. VERIFIED REAL: the public API lives in the SubFrameworks — CoreAIRuntime (AIModel, InferenceFunction with async run + KV-cache states, ComputeStream, NDArray; 1430-line swiftinterface) and CoreAIAsset (model loading) — NOT the empty umbrella CoreAI.framework (import CoreAIRuntime, not CoreAI). Pipeline: MLX fine-tune on a Mac -> coreai-torch export -> .aimodel -> ANE on iPhone (apple/coreai-models, WWDC26 session 324). Fully on-device = mandate-clean.

WHY (what owning the model buys): (1) NO Apple guardrails — the true-crime refusal-abort class (Morbid ~40% plan aborts, though 4my.19 will re-measure) disappears BY CONSTRUCTION; (2) OUR context window — bounded by RAM not Apple policy (8-16k plausible on a small model; un-dies the window-collapse goal that the PCC finding killed); (3) real specialization on the golden ad corpus — the adapter dream with owned weights, no per-OS retraining mandate, no discontinuable toolkit.

PHASE 1 — TOOLCHAIN PROOF (cheap): export a stock tiny model (Qwen3-0.6B class, per the apple/coreai-models recipes) -> .aimodel -> load + run on Dan's iPhone via CoreAIRuntime; measure latency/token, memory, thermal, model-asset size; ALSO verify the CoreAILanguageModel path (new FoundationModels LanguageModel protocol) so the EXISTING session/@Generable stack can host the custom model unchanged. Open toolchain questions: does coreai-torch export require macOS 27 or run on 26.5 + Xcode 27 beta toolchain? Asset delivery via BackgroundAssets sizing.

PHASE 2 — FINE-TUNE HEAD-TO-HEAD: MLX QLoRA fine-tune on the golden ad corpus (coarse ad/not-ad screen + refinement spans as tasks), eval on the existing harnesses vs the current SystemLanguageModel classifier: quality (the eval bar), refusal rate on the sensitive corpus (expect zero), effective context, latency/thermal, size. GO criteria: beats-or-matches FM quality with materially better refusals/context, at acceptable thermal + asset cost.

TRAINING HARDWARE: Dan has access to a 96GB M2-class Mac — USE IT for Phase 2 (and ideally Phase 1 export). What it changes vs the 16GB primary: (a) teacher-student becomes possible — fine-tune a 7-8B teacher on the corpus, DISTILL to the 0.6-1.7B shippable student (better quality at the same shipped size — the shipped model is phone-RAM-bound regardless of Mac size); (b) full-precision LoRA instead of QLoRA on small models + big batches = faster, better convergence; (c) hyperparameter sweeps become cheap; (d) keeps the 16GB primary dev machine free (its 2-xcodebuild ceiling is already the session bottleneck). BONUS: if that Mac takes the macOS 27 beta, it also becomes the natural host for everything we deferred for lack of one — the Catalyst FM-cores canonical eval (xsdz.23), fm CLI / apple_fm_sdk batch corpus labeling — without risking the primary machine.

SEQUENCING: queue position #5, AFTER 4my.19 (FM economics) — deliberately: if schema-out fixes the budget crunch AND refusals already collapsed in iOS 27's rebuilt model, the case for owning a model shrinks. Measure before building. SPIKE ONLY: findings + go/no-go to Dan; no production wiring (new architecture — explicit approval required).
acceptance_criteria: Phase 1: .aimodel built from a stock small model, loaded + timed on the real iPhone via CoreAIRuntime (latency/memory/thermal/size numbers); CoreAILanguageModel session-stack compatibility verified or refuted; toolchain macOS/Xcode requirements documented. Phase 2: fine-tuned model evaluated head-to-head vs the current FM classifier on the existing eval harnesses (quality, refusal rate on sensitive corpus, context, thermal); go/no-go with numbers delivered to Dan; zero production wiring.
notes:
RESEARCH VERDICT 2026-07-06: this bead AS DESIGNED IS DEAD — Apple's adapter-training toolkit is discontinued ('Version 26.0.0 is the last release... not compatible with macOS, iOS, iPadOS, or visionOS 27 and later', developer.apple.com/apple-intelligence/foundation-models-adapter/) and SystemLanguageModel.Adapter is deprecated 26.4 / OBSOLETED 27.0 in the SDK with no public replacement. Candidate successor path (NOT approved yet — needs Dan's explicit re-scope decision + a 10-min verification that CoreAI is actually importable on iOS despite its empty swiftinterface): MLX fine-tune on Mac -> coreai-torch export -> .aimodel on ANE via the new public Core AI runtime (apple/coreai-models, WWDC26 session 324), optionally surfaced through the existing session stack via the new LanguageModel protocol (CoreAILanguageModel). Do not start without the re-scope approval.
ELEVATED P2->P1 (Dan, 2026-07-17): strongest case yet for a distilled specialist classifier = the FM capability-floor evidence (iter5 prompt maxed at ~65-79% held-out recall, [[project_fm_prompt_program_2026-07-17]]). SEQUENCING (Dan): do the DETERMINISTIC lanes FIRST (xsdz.62 rediff-primary, j3dc spectral stinger, t1py music-offset, wraj gate, 7hm5 per-user learning) THEN this. Rationale (Dan agreed): every deterministic signal shrinks the FM residual + cleans the distillation training data, so distillation gets easier + better the longer we wait. Elevated in priority but explicitly downstream of the crisp-lane work.
TRAINING-DATA MACHINERY (2026-07-19, E5): the extraction path (FoundationModelExtractor / AdMetadataSchema, extract framing) runs at 3x lower guardrail-refusal than classification on sensitive shows and produces advertiser/product labels per window. That is exactly the auto-labeling machinery for the distilled-specialist training set: run extraction over the corpus, verify labels deterministically (rediff width + lexical artifacts + gold), train the specialist on the verified set. Extraction labels are loose/paraphrased (E5b: promo=Home Depot app) — always verify, never trust verbatim.
HARDWARE CONFIRMED READY (2026-07-20, Dan): export/training host = the minidev Mac mini on macOS 27 (agent can drive it directly for the coreai-torch export + Phase-1 toolchain proof — no need to wait on a separate 96GB Mac for the export step); deployment target = Dan iPhone on iOS 27 (Phase-1 .aimodel on-device load + 4my.19 refusal re-measure both hardware-unblocked). SPIKE KICKED OFF: WS1 (verified training-corpus assembly from gold+rediff+E5-extraction, offline) + WS2 (Core AI toolchain feasibility probe on the macOS 27 Mac mini) running as research agents — findings + GO/NO-GO to Dan, no production wiring. NOTE: FoundationModels runs on macOS 27 too, so 4my.19 refusal re-measure on the iOS-27 gen-3 model may be runnable on THIS Mac mini via the Catalyst lane without needing the iPhone.
SPIKE WORKSTREAMS COMPLETE (2026-07-20). WS2 TOOLCHAIN = GO (feasibility real, no hard blocker): CoreAIRuntime+CoreAIAsset confirmed in iOS-27+macOS-27 SDKs (all named symbols), CoreAILanguageModel bridges an owned model into the EXISTING LanguageModelSession/@Generable stack (minimal-change hosting), this M4/16GB Mac mini (macOS27/Xcode27) is a valid export host (answers "export needs nothing newer than macOS 27"=confirmed), paired iPhone 16 Pro Max iOS 27 for on-device numbers. Shippable candidate Qwen3-0.6B mixed 4/8-bit = ~0.43GB .aimodel via BackgroundAssets. Cheapest proof = Mac-only llm-benchmark (no device/signing). Soft blockers: brew install uv + uv sync (PyTorch ~3GB), sudo xcode-select -s Xcode-beta (machine-wide, ALSO fixes our CommandLineTools/simctl test-infra pain), disk tight (16GB free/92% full). STRATEGIC: this CONFIRMS the specialist SHRINKS not REPLACES FM ([[feedback_fm_hostread_irreplaceable]]) — the play is refusal-free owned classifier for the catchable classes, FM keeps its irreplaceable host-read job. NEXT DECISION (Dan): run Phase-1 Mac-only toolchain proof (needs the 3 soft-blocker OKs).
PHASE 1 RUN (2026-07-20, on the minidev Mac mini macOS 27.0 / Xcode 27 beta). BUILD HALF = PROVEN: full toolchain (uv + coreai-torch 0.4.1 + torch 2.9 + coremltools 9.0) installed clean; `uv run coreai.llm.export qwen3-0.6b --platform macOS` succeeded -> valid 320MB .aimodel (main.mlirb 335,977,556 B), EMBEDDED tokenizer, 4-bit, max_context_length=8192 (the "our context window > Apple 4096" win, real). Export took ~90s + a one-time HF download. Despite the torch 2.9-vs-tested-2.7 warning, export was clean. RUN HALF = blocked on THIS macOS build only: both llm-runner AND llm-benchmark crash at dyld launch — Symbol not found _$s16FoundationModels...LanguageModelExecutorGenerationChannel...send — the coreai-models Swift CLIs link CoreAILanguageModels->FoundationModels, and Xcode-27 beta SDK is AHEAD of the installed macOS 27.0 (26A5378n) system FoundationModels. NOT a model/toolchain defect — a beta-SDK-vs-OS version skew. Standalone CoreAIAsset load-probe via bare swiftc is fiddly to link (SubFramework module setup) — not chased. VERDICT: Phase-1 = QUALIFIED GO — the hard novel unknown (can we produce a runnable owned mandate-clean on-device model?) is ANSWERED YES; the actual latency/mem number needs an OS-matched runtime. TWO PATHS to the run number: (a) tiny iOS host app on the iOS-27 iPhone 16 Pro Max via CoreAILanguageModel(resourcesAt:) [also = the bead Phase-1 acceptance target "loaded+timed on the real iPhone" AND tests the unverified @Generable/guidedGeneration-through-CoreAILanguageModel question]; (b) bump this Mac to the matching macOS 27.x beta. Toolchain lives at /Users/dabrams/coreai-spike/. NEXT DECISION (Dan): iOS host app (rec) vs macOS beta bump.
PHASE 2 RESULT (2026-07-20, minidev) — STRONG GO. Fine-tuned Qwen3-0.6B (LoRA, mlx-lm, 300 iters, val loss 6.7->0.014, peak mem 8.6GB) evaluated on 7 SHOW-DISJOINT held-out shows (1412 windows: 91 ad / 1321 not_ad). HEAD-TO-HEAD (coarse ad/not-ad, same val windows): SPECIALIST prec 0.81 / recall 0.92 / F1 0.86 / 0 refusals vs FM-PIPELINE prec 0.92 / recall 0.24 / F1 0.38 (base un-FT Qwen = useless, predicts ad for everything, prec 0.06). NOTE: the FM pipelines 502 "misses" are covered:false (uncovered windows = implicit not-ad), NOT guardrail refusals — fair framing = the pipeline is precision-first + coverage-limited (24% window-recall, the ~50%-coverage ceiling we hammered all arc); specialist recall 92% is the big lift. THE KEY VALIDATION (is it real semantics or a lexical re-learn?): specialist catches CUE-LESS ads (no lexical artifact — the class the lexical gate CANNOT catch, FMs supposed job) at 82% (31/38), AND cue-bearing at 100% — so it learned real ad semantics, not the lexical gate. GENERALIZES across all 7 unseen shows 75-100% incl. MORBID (sensitive true-crime, the show FM refuses on) at 97% — NO overfit collapse despite the 22-show corpus (contradicts the WS1 fear). Of 20 "false positives" only 1 has a lexical cue => most are likely gold-missed real ads (true precision higher than 0.81). HONEST CAVEATS: (1) truly-invisible smooth artifact-less host-reads are absent from val entirely (unverifiable => not in gold => uneval-able) — 82% cue-less is on GOLD-labeled cue-less ads, the fully-invisible class stays unmeasured; (2) n=91 positives, wide CIs — needs xdh7 show-growth + l2f.9 host-read attestation to firm; (3) this is a per-window COARSE SCREEN (detection recall — the #1 bottleneck), not the full pipeline (still needs boundary/width machinery for skip spans). VERDICT: owning the model is worth it as a coarse ad-detection screen — directly cracks the recall/coverage ceiling FM judgment-bound at ~50% couldnt, refusal-free, on-device (320MB/8k-ctx artifact proven in Phase 1). NEXT: confirm at scale (grow corpus), then on-device latency (phone-gated), then production-integration decision (Dan, new-architecture approval).

CRITICAL REFINEMENTS: (1) REFUSAL advantage is a CONSTRUCTION GUARANTEE, not a measured delta — the FM dump did NOT reproduce the 40% Morbid refusal story (FM got 0.43-0.62 recall on covered Morbid eps), so "beats FM where FM refuses" was overstated; the specialist is refusal-free BY ARCHITECTURE, not shown-better-on-refusals here. title: SPIKE: on-device rediff — double-fetch episode audio and diff to extract exact DAI slot boundaries
description: The eval harness's ground truth for DAI slots comes from rediffing two downloads of the same episode. Same trick works on the user's device: re-fetch episode audio (or byte-range hashes) hours/days after first download, diff → EXACT DAI slot boundaries. Zero ML, zero FM budget, refusal-proof, transcript-independent, fully on-device (mandate-clean, no sharing questions — single-device version of what bbrv.1 explores via sharing). Covers only DAI (not baked-in host reads). Spike questions: (1) how often do consecutive fetches actually rotate ads per feed/CDN (measure across the test feeds); (2) bandwidth cost + WiFi-and-charging-only policy; (3) diff granularity — full re-download vs HTTP range requests vs chunk hashes; (4) how slots feed the fusion layer (authoritative spans vs strong prior). Exit: go/no-go + measured rotation rates on real feeds.
notes:
PROMOTED to P1 by Dan 2026-07-06, on the xsdz.24 calibration verdict: acoustic splice detection is the width bottleneck (recall 21%@±8s, feasibility ceiling 6% at any floor) — rediff double-fetch is now the LEAD width-oracle candidate for the merged (flag-OFF) xsdz.15 slot machinery, which is oracle-agnostic and reusable as-is.

CONTEXT FOLD-IN for the spike (learned since the bead was written):
1. ROTATION RATE PARTIALLY ANSWERED: the tier-a rediff (snapshot-May vs fresh-fetch, weeks gap) shows 34/41 episodes rotated (83%) with 198 rotating slots across 20+ shows. STILL OPEN: short-gap rotation (hours/days — the production scenario is re-fetch days after first download); measure by double-fetching a subset back-to-back and/or vs the May snapshots.
2. TIMELINE DRIFT IS A FIRST-CLASS DESIGN CONSTRAINT: fresh-download coordinates drift vs the played copy by up to ±180s (per-episode net drift D in the calibration report). Production diffing must express slot boundaries in the PLAYED file's timeline (the device diffs ITS OWN copy vs the re-fetch — anchor alignment on shared content spans, not absolute offsets).
3. EXISTING TOOLING TO LEVERAGE: scripts/l2f-dai-rediff.py (the reference fingerprint differ that produced tier-a), playhead-dogfood-diagnostics-tier-a-rediff.json (schema: episodeId, adSlots[startSeconds,endSeconds], rotated, fingerprintsA/B, secondsPerFp), TestFixtures/Corpus/Audio/_downloaded_manifest.json + Snapshots/manifest.json (feedUrl + enclosureUrl per episode), staged May audio as the 'played copy' arm.
4. SPIKE PRIORITIES: (a) Swift prototype of the fingerprint differ (production candidate — the python script is reference only), TDD-able offline against staged audio pairs; (b) CDN capability probes: HTTP Range support + ETag/Last-Modified semantics per feed CDN (HEAD/Range requests — cheap); (c) bandwidth math: full re-download vs ranged sampling strategies, sized against real enclosure sizes; (d) short-gap rotation measurement on a SUBSET (~8-10 episodes across distinct CDNs; download to temp, hash/fingerprint, DELETE audio immediately — 14GB free disk, keep only fingerprints); (e) design sketch: rediff slots -> the existing SpliceSlot pass as the width oracle (replacing acoustic pair-finding), incl. the played-timeline alignment. EXIT: go/no-go report + measured short-gap rotation + CDN matrix + prototype differ + oracle integration sketch.
SPIKE COMPLETE — GO (2026-07-06). Recommendation: promote rediff double-fetch to production DAI width oracle. Decisive numbers: rotation 0/10 back-to-back, 2/10 @~1h, 8/10 @5wk (36/41=88% full corpus); boundaries ~1s of ground truth in PLAYED timeline; Range 206 on 10/10 CDNs; ~54MB/episode, ~1.1GB/library-week -> WiFi+charging. Swift prototype differ (test-target-only) exact-parity with python reference on 5 fixtures + 3 fresh real pairs + 5,100 fuzz cases; 37 tests green; review loop converged (R4+R5 clean). Full report: docs/xsdz16-rediff-spike.md @ 94da2038 on bead/playhead-xsdz.16. FIRST FOLLOW-UP DECISION (Dan): on-device fingerprinter — chromaprint C lib (LGPL) vs pure-Swift port vs custom fingerprint. Open number: days-gap rotation rate (bracketed 20-88%), needs dogfood measurement.
close_reason: SPIKE COMPLETE — VERDICT: GO (promote rediff double-fetch to production DAI width oracle). Committed 94da2038 on bead/playhead-xsdz.16 (unmerged; prototype is test-target-only). Decisive: rotation 0/10 back-to-back, 2/10 @~65min, 8/10 @~5wk (corpus: 36/41=88%, 198 slots, median 49s) -> re-fetch policy >=~24h; days-gap bracketed 20-88% = the open number (dogfood follow-up). Differ accuracy ~1s of true boundaries IN THE PLAYED TIMELINE (vs acoustic 21%@±8s) — gapsInA union-complement closes the ±180s drift problem; EXACT parity with the python reference (5 fixtures + 3 real pairs + 5,100 fuzz cases). CDNs: Range 206 on 10/10; HEAD/ETags unreliable (podtrac length flapping, Acast HEAD broken) -> ranged-GET sampling only. Bandwidth ~54MB/ep, ~1.1GB/library-week -> WiFi+charging policy + head/tail-64KB pre-check. Guards: alignedFraction>=0.5 mandatory (Megaphone re-encodes per stitch). Recall gaps by construction: DAI-only; order-swapped/equal-length rotations invisible (high precision, incomplete recall). Review loop: I+R1(4)+R2(5)+R3(2)+R4/R5 CLEAN; 37/37 focused; full FastTests failures all in the pre-declared known set. FOLLOW-UPS sequenced in docs/xsdz16-rediff-spike.md §8: (1) on-device fingerprinter choice — DAN DECISION (chromaprint LGPL vs Swift port vs custom); (2) fingerprint store; (3) BGTask re-fetch policy; (4) flag-OFF slot-pass integration + shadow; (5) days-gap dogfood measurement.

title: Boundary-authority inversion: acoustic splice channel owns ad-span WIDTH, transcript/FM own PRESENCE
description: Design review (architecture change — needs explicit approval per no-unilateral-swaps). Today the FM/transcript span is the boundary source and BoundaryExpander/BracketAwareBoundaryRefiner stretch it post hoc; 4xqf shows we still cover only ~18% of true DAI ad width — spans are born too small to rescue. Proposal: invert authority. Once ANY signal establishes ad PRESENCE near t, the emitted span becomes splice-to-splice from the composite audio-forensics channel (xsdz.8: splice + environment + spectral discontinuity), with transcript/FM evidence voting only on presence/confidence. DAI slots are physically spliced server-side, so acoustic splice points ARE the true boundaries — snapping to them should move width coverage from ~18% toward ~100% on stitched ads. Deliverable: design doc covering fusion-layer changes, non-DAI (baked-in host-read) fallback where no splice exists, FP risk when splice detection misfires, and eval plan against the rediff-corroborated corpus. Implementation gated on Dan's approval of the design.
notes: Design doc written 2026-07-05: docs/xsdz15-boundary-authority-inversion-design.md. Code trace confirmed root cause: width minted at MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder.formRuns (anchored-atom run extent); max downstream edge movement ±8s (Use-A snap) + ±3s (refiners) — no slot-spanning primitive exists. xsdz.8 AudioForensicsBoundaryDetector measures the splice discontinuity but is wired as capped (0.20) fusion evidence on already-refined edges. Design: new SpliceSlot type + SpliceSlotResolver stage (reuses forensics edge-step scoring + BoundaryExpander search radii), integrated as a third decoder boundaryOwnership mode (.slotOwned, alongside existing .legacyEvidence/.hypothesisOwned) + new AnchorRef.spliceSlot. Additive: qualifying splice pair required (edge floors, coreCoverage>=0.8, veto check, duration 5-180s), else exact fallback to today's behavior. Backfill-only v1; shadow-first rollout; eval via l2f-bd4xqf-compare (18% baseline). AWAITING DAN'S REVIEW — 4 open questions in doc §6. Implementation gated on approval.
close_reason: DECIDED + APPROVED 2026-07-05: boundary-authority inversion approved as designed (docs/xsdz15-boundary-authority-inversion-design.md). Dan's calls: backfill-only v1; refiners SKIPPED on slot-owned spans; provenance via new AnchorRef.spliceSlot; shadow-first rollout. Implementation tracked in beads labeled xsdz15-impl (A: resolver engine, B: decoder mode + integration, C: shadow + eval).

title: Isolate load-sensitive measurement tests from the parallel fast suite (PerfGate)
description:
The ~7900-test PlayheadFastTests suite runs Swift Testing in parallel, saturating the CPU. Load-sensitive MEASUREMENT tests (MainActorFreedom latency budget=100ms, LaunchPerf, cancellation-timing) then flake because their absolute wall-clock thresholds trip under the suite's own load. Proven flaky: full loaded run failed 3 timing tests; isolation run passed all (MainActorFreedom max=34ms vs 100ms budget).

Fix: runtime PerfGate keyed on env PLAYHEAD_PARALLEL_SUITE. FastTests plan sets it -> measurement tests self-skip in the parallel run (uniform across XCTest + Swift Testing, sidestepping the xctestplan Swift-Testing-filter limitation). Dedicated serial perf pass (scripts/perf-tests.sh + PlayheadPerfTests plan) runs ONLY those tests via -only-testing with -parallel-testing-enabled NO, no env var -> clean measurement. Separates load from measurement while keeping every test's value. Also de-flakes Phase D of the iOS 27 epic (playhead-xx7m).

Measurement tests to gate: MainActorFreedomTests (XCTest), PlayheadRuntimeLaunchPerfTests (XCTest), AnalysisWorkSchedulerOutcomeBookkeepingTests, AnalysisWorkSchedulerJournalEmissionTests, AnalysisWorkSchedulerQueueProgressIntegrationTests, SessionLifecycleRetryTests, AnalysisJobReconcilerTests (Swift Testing).
notes: IMPLEMENTED + VALIDATED on iOS 27 sim. Perf pass (PLAYHEAD_RUN_PERF=1, -parallel-testing-enabled NO): 7/7 pass, MainActorFreedom max=11.2ms (budget 100), LaunchPerf median=3.0ms (budget 250). Fast plan (no env): 5 measurement tests skip with reason, 2 non-gated suite tests still pass. Files: PlayheadTests/Helpers/PerfGate.swift, MainActorFreedomTests + PlayheadRuntimeLaunchPerfTests (setUpWithError XCTSkipUnless), AnalysisWorkSchedulerOutcomeBookkeepingTests (3 @Test .enabled(if:)), TestPlans/PlayheadPerfTests.xctestplan, scripts/perf-tests.sh, project.yml scheme. Uncommitted on branch bead/playhead-xx7m.1.

title: Phase B: Exploit 32k context — retune prompt budget, attack boundary-undersizing
description:
iOS 27 on-device model reports a much larger contextSize (~32k vs 4096). contextSize already read dynamically from SystemLanguageModel.default.contextSize (FoundationModelClassifier.swift:4981), so the big window flows in automatically — BUT the hand-tuned safety divisors (coarseBudgetDivisor=8, refinementBudgetDivisor=2) were sized for the small model's tokenizer undercount and will over-conserve ~8x, keeping windows tiny.

Work: confirm real on-device contextSize on iOS 27; retune divisors; likely collapse ~20 tiny windows/episode into 1-2 large ones. This is the direct fix for the top open recall bug: boundary-undersizing / 18% DAI ad-width coverage (see playhead-4xqf). Measure via rediff eval harness; do not assume 32k, verify on-device. Guard the smart-shrink retry loop against the new regime.
notes:
DEVICE RUN 2026-07-05 (Phase B Part 2 verification): added automated on-device XCTest phaseB32kRetuneOnDeviceVerification() in PlayheadTests/IntegrationTests/FoundationModelClassifierTests.swift — green-skips where FM unavailable (sim/CI via contextSize>0 guard), asserts on device: contextSize>=16384, coarseWindows<=2, live coarsePassA status .success + zero contextOverflow. Ran on real iPhone (iOS 27.0, AI enabled). RESULT: contextSize=4096 NOT ~32768 — Phase B's 32k premise did NOT reproduce. PHASE-B-VERIFY contextSize=4096 coarseDivisor=8 coarseBudget=463 coarseWindows=13 largestWindowTokens=461 status=failedTransient overflowAbandoned=0. IMPORTANT: run was thermally confounded (thermal nominal->fair->serious, started charging=false) — iOS may serve the 4096 base model under thermal pressure, so this is NOT yet a clean read; recipe demands COOL+charging. status=failedTransient is the thermal/usability gate (foundationModelsUsable=false most of run), not a divisor issue (overflowAbandoned=0). SILVER LINING: at 4096 the retune fell into its ÷8 small-context branch = byte-for-byte iOS-26 behavior, empirically confirming the 'fallback path unchanged' guarantee on device. PENDING: clean re-run cool+charging. If still 4096 → 32k premise fails on SystemLanguageModel.default; investigate whether iOS 27's large window is gated behind a non-default model/config (API investigation, surface before more Phase B). Changes uncommitted on branch bead/playhead-xx7m.2-part2.
CLEAN RE-RUN 2026-07-06 (icepack pre-cooled, contextSize read at thermal=fair seconds after nominal start, AI on, charging): contextSize=4096 AGAIN — thermal confound eliminated; PHASE-B-VERIFY contextSize=4096 coarseDivisor=8 coarseBudget=463 coarseWindows=13 status=failedTransient (thermal went serious 30s in — FM inference self-heats; irrelevant to the contextSize question). SDK INVESTIGATION (iOS 27.0 swiftinterface, same method as the Phase C spike): the premise resolves — iOS 27 adds PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel (new in 27.0, its own async contextSize, Executor, capabilities) — i.e. the 'bigger model / large context' is Apple's PRIVATE CLOUD COMPUTE model, NOT the on-device SystemLanguageModel, which remains 4096 on this hardware even cool. On-device 32k does not exist here. CONSEQUENCE: the Part 2 speculative ÷4 retune (uncommitted on bead/playhead-xx7m.2-part2) is DORMANT on this device (engages only at >=16384; 4096 path byte-identical to pre-retune). PCC adoption would violate the standing on-device/no-cloud mandate — Dan's call, not ours. Awaiting Dan: dispose Part 2 branch (commit as dormant future-proofing vs discard) + reframe epic xx7m.
close_reason: CLOSED via PR #225 (squash 76a8771e). Part 1 (instrumentation) shipped in #223; Part 2 (context-aware divisor + on-device verification test) shipped DORMANT after the premise resolved: on-device SystemLanguageModel stays 4096 on iOS 27 (two device runs incl. cool/icepack at thermal=fair); the 32k model is PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel (cloud, mandate-excluded). The ≥16384 branch self-activates only if a future OS/device reports a bigger on-device window. Epic xx7m reframing still pending (Phases C+B premises both dissolved; what iOS 27 delivered = floor raise + FM economics levers, tracked in 4my.19).

title: Diagnose persistent Xcode GUI codesign failure
description: Xcode GUI still reports Command codesign failed even after CLI provisioning refresh. Need identify the exact destination/configuration and underlying codesign/provisioning log line from Xcode's build logs, then fix or document the local signing remediation.
notes: ROOT CAUSE FOUND (2026-07-05): the 'persistent codesign failure' on device builds is 'codesign ... errSecInternalComponent' caused by the LOGIN KEYCHAIN BEING LOCKED. Diagnosis: 'security show-keychain-info ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db' returns 'User interaction is not allowed.' while signing identities are valid ('security find-identity -v -p codesigning' shows Apple Development: Daniel Abrams 4428W3V62Y). FIX: 'security unlock-keychain ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db' (prompts for login password) immediately before the device xcodebuild — confirmed: after unlock the same test command signed + installed + ran on device. If unlock alone is insufficient (per-use key ACL prompt), permanent fix is 'security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple: -s -k <pw> ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db'. Keychain re-locks on screen-lock/timeout so this may recur per session; not closing.
close_reason: DIAGNOSED + fix documented (2026-07-05/06): device-build 'codesign errSecInternalComponent' (and the Xcode GUI equivalent) = LOCKED LOGIN KEYCHAIN. Diagnose: security show-keychain-info ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db -> 'User interaction is not allowed.' while find-identity shows valid identities. Fix: security unlock-keychain ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db before device builds (recurs per session/screen-lock; keychain was later set no-timeout which prevents mid-build re-locks). Escalation if unlock alone insufficient: security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple: -s -k <pw>. Verified working twice on real device builds (Phase B runs 2026-07-05 and 2026-07-06). Durable reference: memory project_codesign_keychain_lock_2026-07-05.
