title: Noise-aware A/B: multi-run FM aggregation + CIs in the activation harnesses
description:
The 2026-05-29 activation campaign (7 live A/Bs of the xsdz precision signals on Catalyst) quantified FM intra-run non-determinism on the 12-episode dogfood corpus: ~±2 FP (span-level) and ~±0.14 (coverage precision), even within a single warm build. A SINGLE 2-arm run therefore cannot distinguish a real ≤±2 FP signal effect from noise. Proven twice over: xsdz.11 changed ZERO spans (offset 0 everywhere, span TP/FP/F1 byte-identical) yet covP still swung −0.142; xsdz.13 looked like a −2 FP "winner" while its channel fired 0 times. au2v.1.27 explored multi-run aggregation but was CHAPTER-signal-specific and is CLOSED.

Harden the 5 merged activation A/B harnesses (FragilityGate #187, BrandAppearance #188, Actempo #189, Fbsignals #190, LexicalScorer) so each ARM runs N times (configurable) and reports median + variance / confidence interval per metric (FP, spanF1, coverage P/R), not a single point. Define a MATERIAL-LIFT BAR in aggregate terms (e.g. non-overlapping IQR, or median delta beyond the measured ±2 FP / ±0.14 covP noise band). Keep the existing per-channel FIRE-COUNT instrumentation and surface it alongside the aggregates so "fired but within noise" vs "real effect" is decidable.

Cost note: each Catalyst arm is ~12 min; N=5 over 2 arms ≈ ~2 hrs/signal — design for overnight/background runs and cache where safe.

ACCEPTANCE: re-running any activation signal yields noise-aware aggregate metrics that distinguish a real effect from the FM noise floor; a documented material-lift bar; fire-count + aggregate jointly reported. Prereq (with corpus growth) for re-judging the 7 off-by-default signals and for xsdz.4.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: Joint prerequisite with playhead-xdh7 (corpus growth): xdh7 gives statistical power + makes 4 inert signals fire; xsdz.14 makes the metrics noise-aware. BOTH are needed before re-judging the 7 off-by-default xsdz signals. Activation campaign detail in memory project_ad_detection_duel_2026-05-27 + JSON dumps playhead-dogfood-diagnostics-*.json.

title: Evidence-fragility / ablation precision gate (deterministic FP suppression over the existing ledger)
description:
CONSENSUS #1 from the 2026-05-27 dueling-idea-wizards duel (cc vs cod) — the single strongest idea: cod scored cc's version 935/1000 (its highest of the whole duel); cod's own #11 (counterfactual ablation) is the same insight (cc 640). BOTH models ranked it #1 in their post-reveal stacks.

MECHANISM: FPs clear threshold on thin/brittle evidence (one dominant channel, narrow margin, few distinct families); TPs are robust across many channels. Compute a fragility score from existing ledger geometry: margin = proposalConfidence − effectiveThreshold; concentration = maxSingleEntryWeight / proposalConfidence; depth = #distinct evidence families with weight>0. fragility = concentration / max(margin,ε) / depth. Apply as a SOFT multiplicative penalty on skipConfidence (or an additional quorum gate) before hard gates. The existing 2+-distinct-kinds quorum is a binary version of this; fragility is the continuous form.

ON-DEVICE: ~15-25 lines in BackfillEvidenceFusion / DecisionMapper. Deterministic, zero new infra, zero new data, universal coverage (all detections, not a subset).

RISKS (opponent critique): fragility may correlate with raw score (redundant) → validate it adds info CONDITIONAL on score (among similar-score detections, do fragile ones have higher FP rate?); overfitting the threshold on 41 examples → LOO cross-val, prefer a continuous feature over a binary gate; small recall risk for borderline TPs.

SUCCESS: measured span-precision lift on the 12-episode dogfood golden via LexicalScorerLiveABTests (xsdz.5) beyond the ±1 FP noise floor, without recall regression. Ship as a soft, off-by-default signal first.

title: Gate xsdz.1 lexical-auto-ad OFF by default (per-feature A/B: net-adds a FP, no recall gain)
description:
The 2026-05-27 per-feature live A/B (playhead-xsdz.5 LexicalScorerLiveABTests, one Catalyst build, 12 dogfood episodes, real runBackfill + fmBackfillMode .full) showed: recall is FLAT at 20/24 (0.833) across all four arms — no xsdz feature catches an ad the baseline misses. The only span-level movement is false positives: baseline 17, xsdz.1-only 16, xsdz.2+3-only 17, all-on 18. xsdz.1 alone removes a FP, xsdz.2+3 alone is span-neutral, but COMBINED (= current main, all default-ON) they net-add one FP — an interaction at no recall gain. xsdz.2+3 alone also lifts coverage-seconds recall 0.114->0.142.

The "21% recall" that launched the xsdz program was the chapter LABELER's standalone number, never the product's (baseline full pipeline already 0.833 span recall). Decision (product owner, 2026-05-27): keep xsdz.2+3 (region tightening — span-neutral coverage gain), gate xsdz.1 OFF.

Implementation: add AdDetectionConfig.lexicalAutoAdEnabled: Bool (default false), guard the LexicalAutoAdEvidenceBuilder.buildEntries call in buildEvidenceLedger so no .lexicalAutoAd entry is built when off — removing both the lexicalAutoAdQualified auto-skip track AND the entry's fusion mass (strictly more conservative than raising the threshold). One-line rollback (flip to true) keeps the fully-tested rule available for future corpus-gated work. xsdz.2+3 (NarrowingConfig.lexicalClusterSnapEnabled) stays default true.

title: Lexical auto-ad rules: sponsor-disclosure + promo/URL in a tight span -> adBreak, with negative-evidence guardrails
description:
Cheapest, highest-ROI first conversion of LexicalScanner coverage into ad RECALL (idea C1; cod 870, aligns with cc's #3=880 in spirit — see DUELING_WIZARDS_REPORT.md). Today the scanner detects 'today's sponsor', promo codes, URLs, 'brought to you by' but the FM vetoes/ignores them and labels the region content. Instead: when a local window contains a sponsor disclosure PLUS a promo-code/URL/offer within a tight span, classify it as adBreak directly (do not route through the FM), UNLESS negative-evidence patterns fire (e.g. the brand is discussed non-commercially, news/review context). Start conservative for auto-skip; lower-confidence regions remain review/fusion candidates. Explainable + deterministic. Measure on the au2v.1.27 SpanMetrics harness against the 12-episode golden set.

Cross-model: cc emphasized the prompt-prior framing (#3=880) but cod's sharper critique (#3=430) is that priming a model which already ignores visible cues is low-leverage — convert the coverage to labels directly instead. This bead is that direct conversion.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic lexical auto-ad rule fires adBreak on strong sponsor+promo/URL co-occurrences; negative-evidence guardrails suppress non-commercial brand mentions; measured ad-region recall materially above the 21% FM baseline on the golden corpus with controlled false-positive rate; rule is explainable and unit-tested.
close_reason: Merged. Lexical auto-ad rule live; corpus eval: ad-region recall 0.21->0.375 at 0.90 span / 1.0 coverage precision, 0 content FPs. R1-R3 two-consecutive-clean; no regression. Boundary tightness deferred to xsdz.2.

title: [epic] Multi-signal local ad scorer — demote FM from primary ad classifier
description:
Dueling-idea-wizards (cc=Claude + cod=Codex/gpt-5.5, 2026-05-26) and the au2v.1.27 fusion-lift A/B converge on the same conclusion: the on-device FoundationModels labeler is the WRONG primary tool for ad classification. It reads blatant ad copy ('today's sponsor', promo codes, URLs) as 'content' (~21% ad-region recall; few-shot HURT; full A/B = zero lift). Meanwhile the existing LexicalScanner already covers ~92% of golden ad spans — it just never converts that coverage into ad LABELS.

Strategy: build a deterministic multi-signal LOCAL ad scorer (lexical cues + acoustic/music windows + episode-position priors + speaker/production shifts) calibrated against the golden corpus, with SEPARATE thresholds for recall (planning/coverage) vs precision (auto-skip UX). The FM is demoted to an optional confirming-evidence layer (never a veto), or dropped from ad classification entirely.

Cross-model validation: this is idea N2 — cc 830 / cod 900 (the single strongest consensus pick). See DUELING_WIZARDS_REPORT.md. Both models independently reached it from only the measured facts.

Children: high-precision lexical auto-ad rules (the cheapest first recall conversion), tighter ad-candidate regions, lexical-recall->FM-precision two-stage, and an evidence-window CoreML ranker (durable medium-term). The reusable A/B + diagnostic harness (ChapterFusionLiftABTests / the SpanMetrics scorer from au2v.1.27 Phase A) measures each change against the same bar.
acceptance_criteria: A calibrated local ad scorer beats the FM-only baseline on the dogfood corpus (span precision/recall/F1 measured via the au2v.1.27 SpanMetrics harness) without cloud; recall and precision thresholds tunable for planning vs auto-skip; FM no longer the sole ad-classification authority.
notes:
Baseline correction from the 2026-07-10 accuracy audit: the often-cited ~21% recall is the standalone chapter FM labeler (10/47 overlap), not the end-to-end detector. The closest comparable 12-episode full-pipeline live-FM baseline is 20 TP / 17 FP / 4 misses (span precision 0.541, recall 0.833, F1 0.656) with only ~0.142 ad-seconds recall because spans are narrow. Treat the current program as two separate problems: improve presence precision while preserving recall, and recover DAI width without allowing rediff to mint ad presence.
WIDTH-PROGRAM SEQUENCING (recommended 2026-07-17, Dan-requested). ONGOING/CRITICAL PATH (nothing jumps it): xsdz.36.1 activation measurement harness (Piece A done+pilot-validated; Piece B committing; then full re-fetch -> pilot treatment -> full Catalyst treatment -> score vs gold v6 + 90s gate) -> auto-skip go/no-go. TIER 1 NEXT (cheap, high-payoff, and NONE compete for xcodebuild slots — all Python/curl over on-disk data): (1) xsdz.44+43+51 as ONE batch spike (one mp3-frame parser, three verdicts: byte rediff alignment / codec splice scars / within-show dedup) — 44 directly de-risks the measurement (Morbid alignment failures cap N); (2) xsdz.50 HLS manifest probe (P1, per-platform verdict); (3) xsdz.46+53 feed-facts scripts (duration arithmetic + enclosure-length telemetry). TIER 2: xsdz.45 dual-persona fetch matrix; xsdz.56 ad-atlas DESIGN DOC (biggest strategic multiplier; design-first, Dan reviews before any code; write after Tier-1 verdicts since which teachers survive shapes the fact schema); xsdz.47 creative dictionary (after 51's verdict picks byte vs acoustic substrate). TIER 3 (sequenced/blocked): xsdz.49 transcript rediff (backstop if 44 fails on re-encode CDNs); xsdz.55 splice templates (after 43 verdict + activation labels); xsdz.48 speaker islands (BLOCKED on Dan model/framework decision); xsdz.52 premium-diff (exploratory + ToS sub-check; near-term dev-side variant = Dan subscribes Wondery+ for Morbid gold); xsdz.54 watermarks (day-scale lark, run whenever idle).

title: Harden chapter-signal eval harness: multi-run aggregation + determinism so prompt/labeling tweaks are measurable over FM + SoundAnalysis noise
description:
Surfaced 2026-05-26 validating playhead-au2v.1.26 (few-shot exemplars). The chapter-label diagnostic (ChapterLabelingDiagnosticTests) is a SINGLE live Catalyst run, but the pipeline is non-deterministic on two axes: (1) SoundAnalysis feature extraction (candidate count moved 49→47 between runs of the same audio), and (2) the FM labeler itself. So a single-run A/B cannot distinguish a real small effect (e.g. ±1-2 adBreak out of ~48) from run-to-run jitter — au2v.1.26's 9/47 vs au2v.1.25's 10/49 is within noise and tells us nothing.

This blocks evaluating ANY further chapter-labeling prompt/strategy tweak (1.26 follow-ups, region tightening, binary pass) and the disposition-accuracy floor itself.

Scope:
- Multi-run aggregation: run the diagnostic N times (configurable) and report median/mean adBreak rate + variance per config, so A/B comparisons are noise-aware. Consider a small CLI/test entry that loops and emits an aggregate JSON.
- Determinism: investigate pinning SoundAnalysis output (does the builder expose a seed / cache? the ChapterFeatureSnapshotBuilder header notes SoundAnalysis is non-deterministic across runs) so candidate sets are stable across runs; if not pinnable, document and rely on aggregation.
- Possibly widen the corpus beyond 12 episodes for statistical power.
- Define a 'material lift' bar in aggregate terms (e.g. median adBreak rate +X over N runs, non-overlapping IQR).

Acceptance: a documented, repeatable way to A/B a chapter-labeling change that distinguishes a real effect from pipeline noise; au2v.1.26 (and future tweaks) can then be evaluated against it.
acceptance_criteria: Diagnostic can be run N times with aggregated (median/mean + spread) adBreak-rate output per config; A/B of two configs is noise-aware; determinism investigated + documented; a 'material lift' threshold defined in aggregate terms.
notes:
2026-05-26 nuance: within a FIXED warm-Catalyst build the diagnostic is actually DETERMINISTIC — few-shot and baseline each gave identical numbers across 5 runs (9/47 and 10/47 respectively; candidate count stable at 47). The earlier 49-vs-47 candidate discrepancy was a CROSS-BUILD artifact (different branch/build state), not run-to-run jitter. So the harness need is less about FM/SoundAnalysis noise-aggregation and more about: (1) controlled, comparable builds for A/B (same derivedData discipline, measure both arms in one session), and (2) defining a material-lift bar. Determinism on device / cold builds is still unverified — investigate before relying on single runs there.
2026-05-26 PIVOT: scoping showed the narl-eval FrozenTrace harness is the WRONG instrument — the inferred chapter signal acts via CoveragePlanner audit-window steering (online), not the post-fusion ledger. Worse, the signal is DARK in production: (gap #1) runShadowFMPhase builds CoveragePlannerContext WITHOUT chapterSignalMode/chapterEvidence (verified AdDetectionService.swift:4167), so the au2v.1.14 chapter branch is unreachable from live backfill; (gap #3) no production call site injects chapterGenerationPhaseFactory and chapterSignalMode defaults .off. So 1.24/1.25 improved a labeler whose output is currently consumed nowhere. This bead is now the ONLINE fusion-lift A/B eval, 3 phases: A) hermetic scorer foundation (reuse SpanMetrics + CorpusAnnotation bridges + FusionLiftResult); B) safe .enabled-gated wire-in of cached ChapterPlan -> CoveragePlannerContext (production-neutral at default .off); C) Catalyst A/B harness running real runBackfill x12x2 vs ground truth (heavy, follow-on). Phase A+B = first PR (this swarm). Multi-run aggregation framing superseded (pipeline is deterministic within a build).
2026-05-26 Phase A+B LANDED (PR #172, merged): hermetic scorer foundation (SpanMetrics bridges + SpanF1 + FusionLiftResult) + the safe .enabled-gated cached-ChapterPlan->CoveragePlannerContext wire-in (proven byte-identical at .off; production-neutral). Reviewed R1-R2 two-consecutive-clean, sim-verified (6775 tests). Bead STAYS OPEN for Phase C: the Catalyst A/B harness (ChapterFusionLiftABTests) that runs the real AdDetectionService.runBackfill x12 dogfood episodes x2 modes (.off vs .enabled), persists feature windows + transcripts + wires chapterGenerationPhaseFactory in-test, fetches predicted ad windows, scores vs CorpusAnnotation ground truth via the Phase-A scorer, and emits the real fusion-lift delta. That number is the gate for flipping ChapterSignalMode. Phase C is heavy (~2-3 days, FM/Catalyst, store + feature-extraction-persist the big lift) and only partly swarm-verifiable (live A/B is an orchestrator Catalyst run).
close_reason: Fusion-lift A/B complete (Catalyst, 12 dogfood episodes, off vs enabled, fmBackfillMode .full, live FM). RESULT: NO ad-detection lift. Span-level metrics IDENTICAL between arms — both 20 TP / 17 FP / 4 miss, spanPrecision 0.541, spanRecall 0.833, spanF1 0.656 (deltas exactly 0). Only difference: coverage-precision +0.17 (0.37->0.54) with coverage-recall -0.006 — i.e. the chapter signal marginally TIGHTENS detected-ad boundaries but catches the exact same ads and removes no false positives. Net detection benefit ~= 0; F1 flat. The epic's eval bar ('measurable lift on recall or precision without regression') is NOT met. RECOMMENDATION: do NOT flip ChapterSignalMode to enabled — it costs FM budget for no detection gain. Phase A+B (#172) + Phase C harness (#173) merged; harness is reusable for any future chapter-labeling improvement. Likely root cause: 21% standalone ad-labeling quality (au2v.1.25/.26) means the inferred plan rarely steers the FM toward ad windows it would have missed.

title: Chapter FM labeler misreads obvious host-read/programmatic ads as content (prompt + schema fix)
description:
Diagnosed 2026-05-25 via ChapterLabelingDiagnosticTests (direct detector+labeler, no phase). DOMINANT cause of the chapter signal missing the eval bar.

Boundary detection is fine: 22/24 (92%) golden adBreak spans have an overlapping detected candidate. But of 49 candidates overlapping a golden ad span, 45 get a SUCCESSFUL FM label and only 5 map to adBreak. Region-text inspection confirms the FM is handed blatant host-read ad copy — sponsor names, URLs, promo codes, CTAs (e.g. 'Lufthansa, today's sponsor', 'sign up for your $1/month trial at Shopify dot com slash...', 'Visit Lufthansa.com and search for Allegris') — and labels it 'content'. Not region dilution; the region text IS the ad.

Root cause: the labeling prompt gives no ad-detection guidance. Current ChapterLabelingService.buildPrompt is just 'Classify this podcast chapter region. Output disposition, confidence, brief topic descriptor.' + chapter context + region transcript. The ChapterDispositionRaw cases hostReadAd/programmaticAd likely lack @Guide descriptions telling the FM what distinguishes an ad (sponsor mentions, calls-to-action, promo codes, URLs, 'today's sponsor', 'this episode is brought to you by').

Scope (the fix):
- Strengthen ChapterLabelingService.buildPrompt with explicit ad-classification guidance + the disposition taxonomy meaning.
- Add @Guide descriptions to the ChapterDispositionRaw / ChapterLabel @Generable schema fields.
- Update ChapterLabelingServiceTests.testPromptShape... to match the new prompt.
- Keep PlayheadFastTests green.

Distinct from playhead-au2v.1.24 (guardrail aborts on editorial content — only 4/49 ad regions affected, separate problem).

VALIDATION: prompt efficacy can ONLY be confirmed by a live Catalyst diagnostic re-run (keychain-unlocked). Unit tests verify prompt shape + compile only. Target: ad-overlapping candidates mapping to adBreak rises materially from the 5/45 baseline.
acceptance_criteria: buildPrompt + schema carry explicit ad-classification guidance; prompt-shape tests updated + green; PlayheadFastTests green; live Catalyst diagnostic re-run shows ad-overlapping→adBreak rate materially above the 5/45 (11%) baseline (re-run done by Dan/orchestrator, not the swarm).
close_reason: Merged PR #170. Prompt + @Guide ad-classification guidance landed; reviewed R1-R5 (two-consecutive-clean). Live Catalyst diagnostic: ad-overlap→adBreak doubled 5/45→10/47 (11%→21%), operational failures 4→2, no regression. Acceptance ('materially above 5/45 baseline') MET. Remaining gap (FM still misreads ~79% of ad regions) tracked in follow-up.

title: FM safety guardrails refuse chapter labeling on sensitive content → ~40% plan-abort coverage gap
description:
Surfaced 2026-05-25 during the first real-corpus ChapterPlan capture (bead playhead-au2v.1.23 / au2v.1.25 tooling).

When ChapterLabelingService.live is given real region transcript text, the on-device FoundationModels model throws 'Safety guardrails were triggered' on regions discussing heavy themes (war, violence, true-crime, paranormal). Each refusal becomes a LabelingResult with failureMode == .operational. ChapterPlanAssembler aborts the whole plan when operational rate > 0.3.

Observed on the 12-episode dogfood corpus: 5/12 episodes aborted on operationalRateExceeded — doac 'WW3/global starvation' (0.66), hard-fork (0.60), 99pi (0.36), ghost-machine 'we will catch you' (0.36), rest-history (0.30). So ~40% of episodes get NO inferred chapter plan (graceful fallback to today's pipeline, but a real coverage gap). Additionally, successful labels never emitted adBreak — all 'content'.

This is a PRODUCTION behavior, not a capture artifact: production calls the same ChapterLabelingService.live with the same region text.

Investigation directions:
- Confirm guardrail-refusal cause via the operationalResult cause= debug logs (timeout vs decoding vs guardrail).
- Consider prompt reframing (e.g. classification-only framing, content sanitization, neutral system instructions) to reduce false guardrail trips on editorial content.
- Evaluate whether operational (guardrail) failures should be treated distinctly from other operational failures in the abort gate.
- Separately investigate why successful labels never produce adBreak (prompt/disposition-parse/boundary-alignment).
acceptance_criteria: Root cause of guardrail trips confirmed; mitigation evaluated; operational-abort rate on the dogfood corpus brought under the 0.3 gate OR a documented decision that guardrail-refused episodes fall back cleanly; adBreak labels demonstrably produced on known-ad regions.
notes: 2026-05-25 diagnosis (ChapterLabelingDiagnosticTests): guardrails are a SEPARATE problem from the missing-adBreak issue. Only 4/49 ad-overlapping candidates fail operationally; guardrails trip broadly on EDITORIAL content (war/violence/true-crime), causing the episode-level operationalRateExceeded aborts (~40% coverage gap). The dominant eval-bar problem (FM labeling obvious ads as content) is tracked separately — see the new sibling bead. This bead remains scoped to the guardrail/abort coverage gap.
close_reason: Merged PR #171. Distinct LabelFailureMode.guardrail, classified from refusal/guardrailViolation, not retried, excluded from the abort numerator. Live Catalyst capture: 7/12→12/12 episodes assemble, 5→0 operationalRateExceeded aborts — ~40% coverage gap closed. Reviewed R1-R3 (two-consecutive-clean). Fully unit-tested + no regression.

description: The current transcript-to-draft generator marks cue snippets such as URLs, promo codes, and sponsor phrases, but it usually does not mark the full ad pod. Improve scripts/l2f-draft-annotation.swift so it groups nearby cue hits and surrounding ad-like transcript segments into review-only candidate ad pods. This should keep output under TestFixtures/Corpus/Drafts and must not promote anything into TestFixtures/Corpus/Annotations.

title: Add an actionable no-progress summary to dogfood diagnostics exports
description:
## Problem

The May 6 diagnostic export had enough raw ingredients to diagnose the situation, but the answer required manual SQLite and JSONL mining. A user looking at Activity saw download working, many rows not fully transcribed, DL/ad often `--%`, and no obvious progress after days of dogfooding.

The exported diagnostics should answer this directly:
- Is anything running now?
- Is background work being scheduled?
- Is background work actually advancing coverage?
- Which assets are stale, blocked, failed, deferred, complete, or partially complete?
- Why is a progress field unknown or `--%`?
- What is the next useful action: wait, plug in, open app, retry, clear stale lease, export diagnostics, or file a bug?

## Scope

Extend dogfood diagnostics with an actionable analysis health section:
- Global summary: generated_at, total assets, running count, queued count, stale count, failed count, latest background run outcome, latest durable job update, latest transcript/ad artifact update.
- Per-asset summary: state, canonical coverage percentages, stale persisted watermark deltas, cached audio presence, latest session/job/final-pass/backfill status, latest failure/defer/no-op reason, and recommended next action.
- Progress provenance: why each percent is shown, e.g. cached audio, chunk max, final-pass chunks, asset watermark, ad windows, unknown/no artifacts.
- Staleness checks: flag rows where `analysisState` says terminal but canonical coverage or durable jobs disagree.
- Duplicate checks: count duplicate correction scopes and duplicate final-pass windows.
- Learning checks: raw corrections, deduped corrections, shadow FM responses, ingested learning artifacts, skipped ingestion reasons.

## Design considerations

This should be compact enough to attach or inspect quickly. Put large raw logs behind file references/counts, not inline megabytes.

Diagnostics should not leak raw transcript text, audio paths, or private source URLs unless explicitly already safe under the existing diagnostics policy. Prefer hashes/synthetic IDs and counts.

The summary should be deterministic and schema-versioned so future tooling can compare dogfood exports across builds.

## Test plan

Add tests for diagnostics generation using the sanitized May 6 fixture:
- Global summary says zero running rows when all Activity rows have `is_running=false`.
- Per-asset summary flags stale transcript watermark gaps.
- Per-asset summary flags terminal-state contradictions.
- Progress provenance explains non-unknown transcript/ad progress when artifacts exist.
- Duplicate correction/final-pass counts are present.
- Learning summary reports nonzero raw signal and zero ingested artifacts for the May 6 fixture.
design: Bump or extend DogfoodDiagnosticsArchive with an optional analysis_health object built from the read models in .1.2, .1.3, and .1.4. Include per-row and aggregate counts: unknown download/transcript/analysis percent, stale watermark vs real chunks, terminal-state contradictions, queued/running/deferred/failed job counts, last run outcome, last progress timestamp, no-progress duration, defer/expiration cause, final-pass pending/deferred count, correction duplicate count, and top recommended next action. Keep raw JSONL support-safe files as files; summarize bg-task-log, asset-lifecycle-log, shadow-decisions, and corpus-export only through privacy-safe counts unless the user opts into a deeper export.
acceptance_criteria: A dogfood export from the May 6 fixture contains analysis_health and can answer: download done or unknown, transcript artifact coverage, analysis/ad coverage, terminal-state truth, background task admission/expiry/defer state, final-pass queue state, and duplicate correction count. Tests in DiagnosticsExportServiceTests decode schema v2 or optional extension, preserve schema v1 compatibility, verify redaction/no raw transcript, and prove no-surface-status failure behavior remains clear or intentionally replaced. The Settings/export flow still lets the user choose Mail/Files without forcing email.
notes:
2026-05-07 codebase audit: dogfood diagnostics export is intentionally small today. DogfoodDiagnosticsArchive schema v1 contains files plus optional activity_snapshot. DogfoodDiagnosticsExporter.isExportableDogfoodDiagnosticsFile only includes surface-status JSONL files and refuses export when no surface-status log exists. Activity snapshots already include pipeline fractions, sources, analysis asset state, latest session, latest job, and latest terminal work journal. DiagnosticsExportServiceTests pin that transcriptPercent can be --% and that transcript-shadow-gate.jsonl is excluded.

The missing artifact is not more raw logs by default. It is a structured analysis_health summary that answers the support question directly: why did this episode not progress overnight, which subsystem owns the block, what was the last durable work event, and what changed since the previous snapshot.

title: Improve remaining dogfood ad recall after boundary-singleton recovery
description:
## Problem

The boundary-singleton fix recovered an important class of dogfood false negatives, but the May 6 data still shows many user-marked ads that were not detected as ads.

Known dogfood facts from the May 6 analysis:
- 65 userMarked ad windows covering about 44.6 minutes.
- 41 of 65 userMarked windows had no overlapping algorithmic `ad_windows` before the boundary singleton work.
- Boundary singleton recovery was estimated to surface 24 of 65 userMarked windows, about 20.8 minutes of the 44.6 marked minutes.
- The remaining misses include lower-confidence/no-decision windows and midroll spans, not just pre/post-roll boundary candidates.
- Production activation flags in decision logs were mostly off: lexical injection false, classifier prior shift false, FM scheduling false, while counterfactual gate was open.
- Shadow FM evidence exists at scale: 1,321 shadow responses, many with `isAd=true`, but this signal is not feeding durable learning tables yet.

## Scope

Design the second recall wave after boundary-singleton recovery:
- Replay dogfood false negatives against current detection code and classify each remaining miss into buckets: no transcript coverage, no candidate generated, candidate below threshold, candidate blocked by policy, no decision log, correction-blocked, or metadata/FM signal present but inactive.
- Use deduped corrections and shadow FM artifacts from `playhead-hygc.1.7` to propose conservative recall improvements.
- Prefer mark-only/detect-only surfacing for uncertain windows. Do not silently expand auto-skip eligibility without precision evidence.
- Evaluate lexical/metadata/FM activation components independently rather than enabling all gates blindly.
- Add per-window explanations so a recovered ad says which evidence family moved it.

## Design considerations

Recall improvements should be staged:
1. Surface more mark-only candidates for review and UI visibility.
2. Use confirmed corrections and high-confidence repeated evidence to promote to stronger candidates.
3. Only expand auto-skip after replay proves precision holds.

The app must continue treating false positives as first-class. The same corpus that finds missed ads should verify that wrongly skipped content does not increase.

## Test plan

Build replay/golden tests from the sanitized dogfood fixture:
- Boundary singleton recovered windows remain recovered.
- Remaining false negatives are bucketed with stable reason codes.
- At least one non-boundary miss is recovered into mark-only/detect-only by correction-aware or shadow-FM-aware evidence.
- False-positive corrections suppress or demote matching windows.
- Auto-skip count does not increase unless the fixture contains explicit precision evidence for that window class.
- Metrics report recall delta, precision risk, and examples by bucket.
design: Add a fixture-backed NARL analysis pass for the May 6 dogfood export from .1.1. Generate a miss taxonomy report before changing detector behavior. Candidate fixes should be evaluated through default vs allEnabled and terminal-reason stratified reports. Prefer improvements that increase recall in completeFull/completeTranscriptPartial assets without increasing auto-skip false positives; recall-only candidates can surface as review banners or shadow evidence before autoskip.
acceptance_criteria: May 6 dogfood misses are categorized with counts and examples. At least one targeted detector/pipeline change improves recall on the dogfood fixture and existing NARL corpus, with precision and false-skip risk reported. NarlThresholdSweepTests/NarlEvalHarnessTests or a new dogfood-specific NARL test asserts the chosen config. CorrectionNormalizer handles duplicate/near-duplicate user corrections from .1.6. No autoskip policy change ships without an explicit precision gate result.
notes:
2026-05-07 codebase audit: use the existing NARL harness and ad-detection seams. The repo already has FrozenTrace fixtures under PlayheadTests/Fixtures/NarlEval, NarlEvalHarnessTests, NarlThresholdSweepTests, NarlEvalReport with terminalReasonBuckets, CorrectionNormalizer, NarlGroundTruth, and optional shadow-decisions ingestion. Production seams include AdDetectionService, SegmentAggregator, RegionProposalBuilder, BackfillEvidenceFusion, MetadataActivationConfig, AutoSkipPrecisionGate, ShadowDecisionsExporter, TrainingExampleMaterializer, and correction/rewind feedback paths.

Do not treat this as a generic threshold tweak. The user observed missing ads after boundary-singleton recovery, so the first implementation step is to bucket remaining misses by evidence shape: transcript/analysis coverage gap, FM not scheduled, FM negative, lexical miss, metadata-only candidate dropped, boundary clipped too tight, final-pass unavailable, user correction not replayed, or precision gate rejected. Then change the narrowest stage that explains the largest bucket.

title: Persist dogfood corrections and shadow FM evidence into durable learning artifacts
description:
## Problem

The app is collecting high-value dogfood signal but is not converting it into durable learning state.

Evidence from the May 6 export:
- Corpus export contains 88 correction records.
- SQLite contains 1,321 `shadow_fm_responses`.
- `semantic_scan_results` has only 1 failed transient scan.
- `evidence_events` has 0 rows.
- The following learning/knowledge tables are empty: `sponsor_knowledge_entries`, `training_examples`, `ad_copy_fingerprints`, `fingerprint_source_events`, `implicit_feedback_events`, `knowledge_candidate_events`, `music_bracket_trust`, `boundary_priors`, `source_demotions`.

This means dogfooding helps offline diagnosis but does not yet improve the on-device product through persisted learning artifacts.

## Scope

Build the ingestion path from real dogfood signals to durable learning artifacts:
- Consume deduped `correction_events` as feedback examples with explicit type, asset, span, source, and confidence/provenance.
- Convert eligible false negatives into training examples or knowledge candidates that can inform future ad detection recall.
- Convert eligible false positives into demotion/suppression examples so recall improvements do not blindly increase false skips.
- Persist shadow FM responses in a queryable form that can be compared against production decisions without decoding opaque payloads at analysis time.
- Create or update sponsor knowledge/fingerprint/boundary-prior tables only when the evidence meets a documented threshold.
- Add diagnostics counters showing raw corrections, deduped corrections, ingested examples, skipped examples, and skip reasons.

## Design considerations

Privacy and minimization are load-bearing. Do not persist raw transcript text into learning tables unless the table is explicitly designed for user-private local-only data. Prefer span refs, normalized token hashes, category labels, timing, source families, and provenance.

This is an on-device learning pipeline first. Any future shared corpus or cloud learning must be a separate privacy/product decision.

The ingestion path must be correction-aware and precision-aware. False positives should have equal first-class treatment so the model learns what not to skip.

## Test plan

Add tests for:
- Deduped false negatives become training examples or knowledge candidates with stable provenance.
- Deduped false positives become demotion/suppression examples.
- Duplicate corrections do not produce duplicate learning artifacts.
- Shadow FM responses are summarized into durable, queryable artifacts without requiring raw base64 payload decoding at read time.
- Empty or low-confidence signals are skipped with diagnostic reasons.
- May 6 fixture produces nonzero eligible learning artifacts while preserving zero raw private text in the fixture.
design: After .1.6 canonicalizes corrections, feed canonical correction signals into TrainingExampleMaterializer and any SponsorKnowledgeStore promotion/demotion path that can safely learn show-level sponsor facts. Summarize shadow FM rows using ShadowDecisionsExporter.decodeShadowSummary or equivalent so learning can use isAd/confidence without requiring raw prompt/response text. Keep raw opaque blobs for export/replay only. Add an explicit materialization trigger after backfill/final-pass/correction ingestion rather than depending on opportunistic test-only calls.
acceptance_criteria: A false positive listen revert and a false negative user-marked ad both persist to canonical corrections, materialize into training_examples with the expected bucket, and can be exported into NARL without duplicates. Shadow FM rows produce stable summary signals and do not require decoding raw text in diagnostics. SponsorKnowledgeStore tests cover promotion/demotion from correction-backed evidence where applicable. TrainingExamplePersistenceTests, TrainingExampleMaterializerTests, TrainingExampleBucketerTests, SponsorKnowledgeStoreTests, FoundationModelsFeedbackStoreTests, ShadowCaptureStorageTests, and ShadowDecisionsExporterTests stay green.
notes:
2026-05-07 codebase audit: durable learning storage already exists. AnalysisStore has training_examples, sponsor_knowledge_entries, and shadow_fm_responses tables plus CRUD. TrainingExampleMaterializer joins semantic_scan_results with evidence_events, decision_events, correction_events, and ad_windows, then uses TrainingExampleBucketer. ShadowDecisionsExporter exports shadow_fm_responses with decoded isAd/shadowConfidence summaries while retaining fmResponseBase64. SponsorKnowledgeStore and FoundationModelsFeedbackStore already have tests and runtime seams.

Therefore this bead should wire and harden existing stores, not add brand-new learning tables. The dogfood gap is that corrections and shadow evidence need to become durable training/knowledge artifacts on the actual production paths, with privacy and dedupe constraints from .1.6. Pay attention to DEBUG-only FoundationModelsFeedbackStore: production learning should rely on AnalysisStore-backed artifacts, not a DEBUG-only feedback file.

title: Make correction event writes idempotent and dedupe existing duplicate scopes
description:
## Problem

The May 6 dogfood database has duplicate correction rows.

Evidence:
- `correction_events` contains 76 `falseNegative` rows but only 61 distinct scopes.
- It contains 12 `falsePositive` rows but only 7 distinct scopes.
- Exact false-negative spans repeat 2-4 times, including `C75C2E85:3386.000:3394.140` repeated 4 times and `C75C2E85:3394.140:3395.652` repeated 4 times.
- Exact false-positive spans also repeat, including scopes on `631931BA`, `C75C2E85`, `DCE6AA97`, and `F3CB8FBF`.

Duplicated corrections distort recall/precision analysis, can cause repeated final-pass work, and will poison learning tables if corrections are ingested as training examples without dedupe.

## Scope

Make correction ingestion idempotent:
- Define the semantic correction identity key. Candidate key: analysisAssetId + correctionType + normalized exact time span + target refs/version, with a tolerance for floating-point span jitter where appropriate.
- Enforce the key at write time using upsert or uniqueness constraints.
- Preserve an audit count or last-seen timestamp when the same correction is submitted again.
- Ensure corpus export can choose distinct semantic corrections by default, while still allowing raw-event export for debugging.
- Add read-side dedupe for existing local databases that already contain duplicates.
- Verify user actions such as add, adjust, save, replay, app relaunch, and export/import do not multiply the same correction.

## Design considerations

Do not silently discard meaningful edits. If the user changes a correction span or changes falseNegative to falsePositive, that should be treated as a new semantic correction or a superseding correction according to an explicit rule.

The dedupe key should be stable across app launches and exports. Avoid relying only on generated UUIDs.

## Test plan

Add tests for:
- Submitting the exact same false-negative correction twice yields one semantic correction with updated audit metadata.
- Submitting the same span with small float jitter dedupes if within tolerance.
- Changing span boundaries beyond tolerance creates a distinct or superseding correction according to the chosen rule.
- FalsePositive and falseNegative for the same span do not collapse incorrectly.
- Corpus export emits distinct corrections by default.
- Learning ingestion receives deduped corrections, not raw duplicate rows.
design: Add semantic identity for corrections while preserving raw audit intent. Candidate: a correctionSemanticKey derived from analysisAssetId, normalized CorrectionScope, correctionType, source family, and targetRefs/adWindow where relevant. Store it on correction_events with a unique index, or add a separate canonical_corrections view/table fed by raw events. Normalize exactTimeSpan edges to the same precision used by CorrectionScope.serialized and NARL CorrectionNormalizer so duplicate/near-duplicate dogfood rows collapse predictably. Preserve createdAt/event id for audit, but expose canonical corrections to TrainingExampleMaterializer, SponsorKnowledgeStore inputs, and NARL export.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated identical false positive/false negative gestures do not create duplicate canonical corrections. Separate meaningful corrections are not collapsed across asset, type, source family, or materially different spans. Existing tests for recordUserMarkedAd, recordListenRevert, revertByTimeRange one-per-gesture, UserCorrectionStore, CorrectionSuppression, FalseNegativeCorrection, CorrectionAttribution, and NARL CorrectionNormalizer still pass. A migration/dedupe test seeded with duplicate May 6 scopes proves canonical correction count is stable.
notes:
2026-05-07 codebase audit: correction_events persistence is present but UUID-idempotent only. AnalysisStore.appendCorrectionEvent uses INSERT OR IGNORE on id; indexes exist for analysisAssetId and scope, but there is no unique semantic key for repeated user actions over the same asset/scope/type/source. Helpers hasAnyCorrectionEvent(withScope:) and correctionScopesPresent(from:) exist, but they only answer presence and are not a full dedupe contract.

UI paths already write precise exactTimeSpan corrections: UserCorrectionStore.recordVeto(startTime:endTime:) and SkipOrchestrator.revertByTimeRange funnel into CorrectionEvent; UserMarkedAdInjectionTests and SkipOrchestratorRevertTests cover exactTimeSpan behavior and one correction per gesture. The missing layer is cross-gesture semantic idempotency and a clean canonical view for learning/NARL.

title: Make final-pass job fanout idempotent and recover thermal-deferred/running windows
description:
## Problem

The May 6 store contains duplicate final-pass job rows for identical windows and stale deferred/running windows.

Evidence from `final_pass_jobs`:
- Asset `C75C2E85` has duplicated thermal-deferred windows, including exact spans `3386.0-3394.14` repeated 4 times and `3394.14-3395.652` repeated 4 times.
- The same asset has a `running` final-pass job for `21.6-22.6` minutes with deferReason `thermalThrottled`, plus nearby deferred rows, all created around 2026-05-01.
- Asset `1874D961` has the exact `24.0-38.16` second final-pass span repeated 4 times as complete.
- Some complete rows have zero-length or near-zero windows, which may be valid boundary refinements or may be a fanout artifact; the contract is not explicit.

These duplicate rows make it harder to tell what final-pass transcription actually completed and may contribute to stale progress or repeated background no-ops.

## Scope

Fix the final-pass job identity and recovery model:
- Define the unique key for a final-pass job, likely asset ID + ad window ID or asset ID + normalized start/end + phase/policy.
- Prevent duplicate creation under concurrent/resubmitted background runs.
- Add migration/recovery logic to collapse or ignore duplicates safely in read models.
- Make stale `running` rows recoverable after app relaunch or BGTask expiration.
- Ensure `thermalThrottled` deferrals record a next eligibility or recovery path.
- Decide whether zero-length and near-zero windows are valid; if valid, document and handle them explicitly. If invalid, reject at creation.

## Design considerations

Do not delete historical dogfood evidence during recovery. Prefer idempotent upsert/read-side dedupe or a migration that preserves enough audit information.

Final-pass coverage should be derived from successful, non-duplicate completed spans. Deferred/running spans should not count as coverage, but they should explain why coverage stopped.

## Test plan

Add tests for:
- Repeated enqueue of the same asset/window produces one durable job or one active job plus merged audit history.
- Concurrent enqueue attempts are race-safe.
- Stale running job is reset/requeued by recovery with a clear reason.
- Thermal-deferred job resumes when eligible and does not create duplicates.
- Final-pass progress computation ignores duplicate completed rows.
- Invalid zero-length windows are rejected, or valid near-zero windows are preserved with documented semantics.
design: Keep final_pass_jobs, but add semantic dedupe around eligible AdWindow materialization. Normalize each candidate by analysisAssetId plus canonicalized windowStart/windowEnd with a small tolerance or by interval-overlap coverage, and either collapse duplicates before insert or add a durable semantic key/unique index that does not rely only on adWindowId. Preserve audit visibility for the contributing adWindowIds. Continue to support thermal-deferred retry and stranded-running reaper behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated final-pass drains with the same windows are no-op. Distinct adWindowIds with identical or near-identical spans produce one final-pass ASR pass and one semantic job outcome. Overlapping but non-identical windows do not lose needed uncovered audio. Thermal top-level deferral, mid-window deferral with partial chunks, recovered deferred rows, cancellation, and stranded-running reset stay covered by FinalPassRetranscriptionRunnerTests, FinalPassThermalRecoveryObserverTests, and AnalysisJobReconcilerTests. May 6 fixture proves duplicate dogfood windows stop fanning out.
notes:
2026-05-07 codebase audit: final_pass_jobs already has durable retry state and basic idempotency. AnalysisStore schema comments document jobId = fpj-<analysisAssetId>-<adWindowId>, insertOrIgnoreFinalPassJob uses INSERT OR IGNORE, markFinalPassJobRunning/Deferred/Complete/Failed update status/updatedAt, and resetStrandedFinalPassJobs is wired through AnalysisJobReconcilerTests. FinalPassRetranscriptionRunner also carries in-drain interval coverage so overlapping windows do not re-run ASR within one drain, and FinalPassThermalRecoveryObserver wakes deferred rows after capability recovery.

The dogfood duplicate risk is semantic, not simple row-idempotency: if two AdWindow rows represent the same or nearly same time span with different adWindowId values, current job ids differ and both jobs can be enqueued. Watermark filtering by finalPassCoverageEndTime can also be too coarse for out-of-order windows. This bead should dedupe at normalized window/span level before or during job creation.

title: Make background backfill and preanalysis runs durably explain progress, no-op, deferral, and expiry
description:
## Problem

The May 6 dogfood data shows background task churn without enough durable explanation.

Evidence from `bg-task-log.jsonl`:
- 981 total `submit` events.
- 470 `start` events.
- 407 `complete` events.
- 78 `expire` events.
- Analysis-specific events include 298 `com.playhead.app.analysis.backfill` submits, 197 starts, 153 completes, and 23 `backfill-task-expired` rows.

But the durable `analysis_jobs` table has only 15 rows and no real updates after 2026-05-01. Many Activity rows still show queued/up_next/waiting_for_time on 2026-05-06 even though background tasks had been firing.

This means a user can plug in the phone overnight and the app may wake repeatedly without making visible progress, while diagnostics cannot say whether it found no work, got throttled, expired, lost leases, skipped due to capability, or completed a tiny no-op.

## Scope

Instrument and repair the background analysis/preanalysis run contract:
- Each BGTask execution must create or update a durable run record with start time, end time, task identifier, scene/background state, claimed work count, advanced work count, and outcome.
- Backfill runs must distinguish: no eligible work, work claimed, work advanced, thermal deferral, capability deferral, expired, cancelled, failed, and rescheduled.
- Preanalysis recovery must distinguish: recovered work, found no stale work, repaired leases, resubmitted backfill, or no-op.
- Expiration handlers must persist a final outcome before returning.
- Activity/diagnostics should surface the latest durable outcome per asset and globally.
- Avoid double-submit storms: repeated submits should be coalesced or explained with a reason.

## Design considerations

Do not rely only on JSONL logs. JSONL is useful support evidence, but the app needs durable state in SQLite so Activity and diagnostics can answer the user question: is anything actually working?

Keep BGTaskScheduler constraints in mind. A task may legitimately run for a few seconds and complete with no work; that should be an explicit outcome, not indistinguishable from success.

## Test plan

Use dependency-injected schedulers/task runners where possible:
- Run with eligible work: durable outcome says work claimed and advanced.
- Run with no eligible work: durable outcome says no eligible work and does not imply progress.
- Expiration callback fires: durable outcome says expired and records partial advancement if any.
- Thermal/capability deferral: durable outcome records defer reason and next eligibility.
- Recovery task repairs stale/running leases and records what it did.
- Diagnostics snapshot includes latest global and per-asset background outcomes.
design: Add a small durable run-outcome model instead of depending on os_log or raw JSONL. Candidate: analysis_run_events or background_task_runs in AnalysisStore with runId, entryPoint, startedAt, finishedAt, outcome, deferReason/cause, jobsSeen, jobsAdmitted, jobsCompleted, jobsDeferred, coverageBefore/After where available, taskIdentifier, taskInstanceID, expiration flag, and lastErrorCode. Wire BackgroundProcessingService, AnalysisWorkScheduler, BackfillJobRunner, and FinalPassRetranscriptionRunner at their existing RunResult/markComplete seams. Keep BGTaskTelemetryLogger as lifecycle telemetry; this bead adds queryable progress accounting.
acceptance_criteria: A dogfood overnight run can be classified without reading raw logs: admitted work, no eligible work, deferred by thermal/power/LPM, expired, cancelled, failed, or made zero progress. Tests cover backfill start/complete, expiration, QualityProfile deferral, queue-empty no-op, scheduler wake with admitted jobs, final-pass top-level and mid-window deferral, and persistence across process restart. The summary feeds .1.9 diagnostics export and does not duplicate or remove BGTaskTelemetryLogger JSONL.
notes:
2026-05-07 codebase audit: background observability exists but is split. BGTaskTelemetryLogger writes append-only Documents/bg-task-log.jsonl for submit/start/complete/expire/appPhase and BackgroundProcessingServiceTelemetryTests cover those rows. BackgroundProcessingService.handleBackfillTask wakes AnalysisWorkScheduler and runPendingBackfill, has expiration handling, and emits BG telemetry. AnalysisStore job tables already have updatedAt fields and reapers for backfill_jobs and final_pass_jobs, and AnalysisWorkSchedulerOutcomeBookkeepingTests pin attempt-count bookkeeping for task expiration.

What is missing for the dogfood question is a durable run summary that answers: was work admitted, deferred, expired, no-op because queue empty, no-op because store unopened, or did jobs run but make zero coverage progress? JSONL lifecycle telemetry alone is useful forensic material but not a queryable per-run progress ledger and is not currently included in dogfood diagnostics except indirectly if a human pulls the file.

title: Fix completeFull/backfill terminal-state consistency against real coverage
description:
## Problem

Several May 6 assets have terminal states that overstate the actual persisted coverage contract.

Examples:
- `3B96D187` is `completeFull` with terminalReason `full coverage: transcript 1.000, feature 0.999`, but asset fast transcript watermark is 1.5 minutes on a 36.4 minute episode and no final-pass coverage is stored.
- `8A9DFC82` is `completeFull` with terminalReason claiming transcript 1.163 and feature 1.724, but stored feature coverage is 21.5 minutes on a 94.1 minute episode and fast transcript watermark is 1.5 minutes.
- `9C109975` is `completeFull` with fast transcript watermark 1.5 minutes on a 66.0 minute episode, though transcript chunks later prove more coverage exists.
- `E8F0F867` terminalReason says transcript 6.891 and feature 8.106, ratios above 1.0, which suggests the terminal-reason math is using mismatched denominators or stale duration/coverage values.

This undermines both the UI and the user mental model. `completeFull` must be a meaningful state, not just a historical transition label.

## Scope

Audit and repair the analysis asset state transition logic:
- Define the exact invariant for `completeFull`, `completeTranscriptPartial`, `backfill`, `queued`, and `failed`.
- Use the same canonical coverage computation as Activity wherever possible, or explicitly explain why a persisted state differs from derived read-model coverage.
- Clamp and validate terminal reason ratios so values like transcript 6.891 or feature 8.106 cannot be emitted unless there is a deliberate documented meaning.
- Reconcile existing stale rows on startup or during recovery where safe, without destroying evidence needed for diagnosis.
- Ensure terminal states do not strand rows in `up_next` when they should be terminal/ready/paused elsewhere in the Activity model.

## Design considerations

This should not paper over incomplete work by renaming states. The point is to make states true enough to drive UI, scheduling, diagnostics, and user support.

If an asset has complete transcript chunks but stale watermarks, the reconciler may treat progress as complete while this bead decides whether and how to persist repaired state/watermarks.

If an asset has feature coverage but not transcript coverage, it should stay in a backfill/partial state with a reason that says exactly what is missing.

## Test plan

Add tests for:
- `completeFull` requires transcript and feature coverage to satisfy thresholds after canonical reconciliation.
- Ratios in terminalReason are clamped or computed from consistent denominators.
- Stale watermark with complete chunks can be repaired or represented consistently.
- Partial transcript assets remain `completeTranscriptPartial` with accurate reason text.
- Failed assets retain actionable failureReason and do not present as queued work without a recovery path.
design: Add a narrowly scoped reconcile step, likely in AnalysisStore or AnalysisCoordinator startup recovery, that scans terminal completion assets for impossible or contradictory coverage: completeFull with transcript coverage below threshold against resolved episodeDurationSec, terminalReason ratios > expected bounds, feature shortfall, or missing duration. Reclassify only rows that fail the invariant using the existing classifyBackfillTerminal semantics, and preserve an audit trail via terminalReason or lifecycle/journal entry. Do not change the existing live threshold rules without updating ClassifyBackfillTerminalTests.
acceptance_criteria: May 6 fixture rows that were falsely completeFull are repaired or explicitly flagged. Good completeFull rows remain completeFull. Tests cover old bad persisted rows, healthy rows, unknown duration fail-safe, and no regression to FinalizeBackfillDenominatorFixTests/ClassifyBackfillTerminalTests/SessionStateContractTests. Activity and dogfood diagnostics no longer present a repaired partial/failed row as fully analyzed.
notes:
2026-05-07 codebase audit: the live backfill classifier is already much stronger than the original dogfood symptom. AnalysisCoordinator.finalizeBackfill resolves episode duration once with max(liveDuration, persistedDuration), passes that duration into runBackfill, and classifies terminal state via classifyBackfillTerminal. Tests already pin the stale denominator regression: FinalizeBackfillDenominatorFixTests has the 8A9DFC82 reproduction and healthy cases; ClassifyBackfillTerminalTests pins completeFull, completeFeatureOnly, completeTranscriptPartial, failedFeature, failedTranscript, and cancelledBudget; SessionStateContractTests pins terminal transitions.

This bead should therefore focus on persisted historical bad rows and Activity/export consistency, not reimplementing the classifier. The dogfood data can still contain rows stamped completeFull with terminalReason ratios > 1 or with true coverage far below episodeDurationSec from older builds. Those rows need a repair/reconcile path and a diagnostic flag so support output is truthful.

title: Reconcile Activity progress from canonical artifacts instead of stale watermarks
description:
## Problem

The May 6 dogfood export shows Activity progress being driven by stale asset-level fields even though richer canonical artifacts exist in the store.

Concrete evidence:
- Asset `9C109975` is `completeFull`; transcript chunks extend to 66.0 minutes, but `analysis_assets.fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime` is only 1.5 minutes.
- Asset `C75C2E85` is `backfill`; fast chunks extend to 57.1 minutes, but the asset fast watermark is 1.0 minute and final-pass watermark is 5.0 minutes.
- Asset `3B96D187` is `completeFull`; fast chunks extend to 36.4 minutes, but the asset fast watermark is 1.5 minutes.
- Asset `F3CB8FBF` has fast chunks through 48.4 minutes and final pass through 48.4 minutes, but the fast watermark is 15.0 minutes.
- The Activity snapshot reports rows with transcript percentages such as 2%, 4%, 9%, 15%, or 39% even when chunk tables prove much more transcript exists.

This makes the user-visible Activity screen look stalled or incomplete even when transcription has happened.

## Scope

Define and implement a single canonical progress reconciliation path used by Activity/diagnostics surfaces.

The reconciler should derive:
- Download progress from cached audio state when available.
- Feature/analysis progress from feature windows or feature coverage, choosing the most trustworthy persisted artifact.
- Fast transcript coverage from the maximum transcript chunk end time for `pass = fast`, falling back to the asset watermark only when chunks are unavailable.
- Final transcript coverage from the maximum final-pass chunk end time and/or `finalPassCoverageEndTime`.
- Display transcript progress from the best available transcript coverage, while preserving enough metadata to show whether it is fast or final.
- Ad/DL progress from ad windows and confirmed/ad coverage artifacts instead of returning `--%` solely because the asset watermark is nil.

The implementation should also report provenance for each displayed percentage, e.g. `fast_transcript_chunks`, `final_pass_chunks`, `asset_watermark`, `ad_windows`, `cached_audio`, so diagnostics explain why a number appears.

## Design considerations

Do not merely bump watermarks on read without understanding write semantics. It is acceptable for the Activity read model to derive truth from canonical child artifacts, but long-term persisted watermarks should also be repaired by a separate state-machine bead.

Avoid showing false precision. If ad windows exist but full episode ad coverage is unknown, show a bounded/provenance-aware progress value or explicit partial state rather than pretending the whole episode is analyzed.

## Test plan

Use the sanitized May 6 fixture from `playhead-hygc.1.1` plus focused unit tests:
- Stale fast watermark, complete fast chunks: displayed transcript coverage follows chunk max.
- Missing final-pass watermark, final chunks present: final coverage follows chunk max.
- Ad windows present, confirmed ad watermark nil: Activity does not show `--%` blindly; it exposes partial/ad-window-derived provenance.
- Cached audio present: download shows complete even if download job state is absent.
- No artifacts present: progress remains unknown with an explicit unknown reason.
design: Introduce an AnalysisCoverageSummary read model in AnalysisStore, or equivalent, that returns per asset: episodeDurationSec, fastTranscriptCoveredSec as interval-unioned seconds, fastTranscriptCoverageEndSec as max end, featureCoverageEndSec, confirmedAdCoverageEndSec, finalPassCoverageEndSec, and provenance/source strings. Use that read model from ActivitySnapshotProvider for both UI rows and dogfood snapshots. Keep display clamped to [0, 1] and keep unknown as nil/--%, not synthetic 0%.
acceptance_criteria: Activity progress uses canonical artifact coverage rather than stale watermarks. Tests cover overlapping fast chunks, gapped fast chunks, stale asset watermark with real chunks, cached download 100%, feature-only analysis coverage, confirmed-ad coverage exceeding feature coverage, and final-pass coverage appearing in dogfood provenance. Existing ActivitySnapshotProviderTests remain green and add May 6 fixture-backed assertions from .1.1.
notes:
2026-05-07 codebase audit: Activity already bulk-loads real fast transcript rows. LiveActivitySnapshotProvider.loadInputs and loadDogfoodDiagnosticsSnapshot call AnalysisStore.fetchFastTranscriptCoveredSecondsByAssetIds and fall back to analysis_assets.fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime. Existing tests in ActivitySnapshotProviderTests already cover fast chunks overriding stale watermarks and cached downloads showing 100%.

The remaining risk is semantic accuracy. fetchFastTranscriptCoveredSecondsByAssetIds currently SUMs fast chunk durations (endTime - startTime), while other terminal logic often reasons about coverageEnd = max(endTime). Summing can overstate overlapping chunks and under-explain gaps. The dogfood symptom needs a canonical coverage summary that can report both covered interval seconds and high-water end time, not just one ambiguous number.

Activity has downloadFraction, transcriptFraction, and analysisFraction only. There is no explicit ad-detection percent field. DogfoodDiagnosticsPipelineSnapshot emits analysisPercent/analysisSource from max(featureCoverageEndTime, confirmedAdCoverageEndTime) and also includes finalPassCoverageEndSec, but final pass is not currently part of analysisFraction.

title: Create sanitized regression fixtures for the May 6 dogfood export
description:
## Background

The May 6 dogfood export is rich enough to drive several fixes, but the raw `.xcappdata` and diagnostics files are local user data and must not be committed. We need a small, scrubbed regression fixture that preserves the structural facts needed for tests.

Local source evidence:
- `playhead-dogfood-diagnostics-2026-05-06T23-46-51Z.json`
- `com.playhead.app 2026-05-06 18:39.47.688.xcappdata/AppData/Documents/ExportedAnalysisStore/analysis.sqlite`
- `bg-task-log.jsonl`, `asset-lifecycle-log.jsonl`, `shadow-decisions.jsonl`, `corpus-export.2026-05-01T18-09-08.190Z.jsonl`

## Scope

Create a compact fixture format for dogfood regression tests. Include only the fields needed to reproduce the bugs:
- Activity rows with section/status/is_running/queue_position/cached_audio_present/pipeline fields.
- Analysis asset rows with state, duration, feature/fast/final/ad coverage watermarks, terminalReason.
- Transcript chunk maxima by asset and pass.
- Ad-window maxima/counts by asset, including userMarked vs algorithmic counts.
- Background task event counts and representative submit/start/complete/expire rows.
- Correction rows reduced to correctionType plus scope hashes/spans sufficient to prove duplication.
- Empty learning table counts plus shadow FM response counts.

Scrubbing rules:
- Replace episode IDs, URLs, hashes, and transcript text with stable synthetic IDs.
- Do not include audio paths, source URLs, prompt text, FM response payload text, or raw transcript snippets.
- Preserve timing, counts, states, coverage values, and duplicate-key structure exactly enough for assertions.

## Test plan

Add fixture-loader tests that assert the fixture contains these facts:
- 22 Activity rows, all queued/up_next/waiting_for_time and not running.
- Cached audio present for all rows and download progress at 100%.
- At least one asset has chunk transcript coverage far beyond asset watermark coverage; use `9C109975`-equivalent synthetic ID with 66.0 min chunks vs 1.5 min asset watermark.
- At least one `completeFull` asset has contradictory stored coverage/terminal state.
- Correction scopes contain duplicates, including one falseNegative scope repeated 4 times.
- Learning artifact counts are zero while shadow FM response count is nonzero.

## Notes

This bead is a foundation for the child implementation beads. Keep the fixture boring and explicit; this is a regression harness, not a replay of private user content.
design: Add the smallest fixture bridge that captures the May 6 failures as structured, privacy-safe facts: activity row pipeline percentages/sources, terminal states and reasons, job/session states, correction scopes after dedupe normalization, and NARL replay spans. Prefer extending NarlEvalCorpusBuilderTests and adding a tiny DogfoodAnalysisHealth fixture loader over parsing production diagnostics ad hoc inside multiple tests.
acceptance_criteria: A committed sanitized fixture set exists for the May 6 dogfood export and contains no raw transcript/audio or unsalted identifiers. Unit tests load it deterministically. At least one Activity/diagnostics test and one NARL/correction test can consume it without requiring a live .xcappdata bundle. The fixture README documents source files used, fields retained, fields redacted, and how to regenerate.
notes:
2026-05-07 codebase audit: reuse existing fixture systems. The repo already has NARL FrozenTrace fixtures under PlayheadTests/Fixtures/NarlEval, diagnostics fixtures under PlayheadTests/Fixtures/Diagnostics, and corpus fixtures under PlayheadTests/Fixtures/Corpus. Do not invent an unrelated dogfood format unless it is a small manifest that points into those existing shapes.

Target artifact shape: a sanitized May 6 fixture set that can feed both Activity/diagnostics assertions and NARL replay metrics. Good candidates are PlayheadTests/Fixtures/Dogfood/2026-05-06/analysis-health.json for pipeline/status summaries and additional FrozenTrace rows under PlayheadTests/Fixtures/NarlEval/2026-05-06/ for ad-recall replay. Exclude raw audio, raw transcript text, full episode titles, raw episode ids in support-safe diagnostics, install salts, and device-specific paths.

Relevant builders/tests: PlayheadTests/Services/ReplaySimulator/NarlEval/NarlEvalCorpusBuilderTests.swift already converts .xcappdata Documents files into FrozenTrace fixtures from corpus-export JSONL, decision-log.jsonl, optional shadow-decisions.jsonl, and asset-lifecycle-log.jsonl. DiagnosticsExportServiceTests already has dogfood archive fixture expectations.

title: Dogfood 2026-05-06 follow-up: truthful progress, live work, and learning ingestion
description:
## Background

Dan dogfooded Playhead for more than two weeks and exported a fresh diagnostic bundle plus `.xcappdata` on 2026-05-06. The export shows that download is no longer the main blocker. Cached audio is present and the Activity snapshot reports download at 100%, but the analysis/transcript/ad progress contract is not truthful enough to explain what is happening.

Primary local evidence inspected read-only:
- `playhead-dogfood-diagnostics-2026-05-06T23-46-51Z.json`
- `com.playhead.app 2026-05-06 18:39.47.688.xcappdata/AppData/Documents/ExportedAnalysisStore/analysis.sqlite`
- `decision-log*.jsonl`, `shadow-decisions.jsonl`, `bg-task-log.jsonl`, `asset-lifecycle-log.jsonl`, and `corpus-export.*.jsonl` inside the app container

Do not commit the raw diagnostic exports or raw `.xcappdata` contents. Any regression fixtures created from this evidence must be minimized, scrubbed, and purpose-built.

## Findings to remediate

1. Activity looks busy but no work is running. All 22 rows in the 2026-05-06 Activity snapshot are `up_next`, `queued`, `waiting_for_time`, `is_running=false`, with cached audio present.

2. Background tasks are firing but not durably advancing enough work. `bg-task-log.jsonl` has 981 submits, 470 starts, 407 completes, and 78 expirations. For analysis specifically, there are 298 backfill submits, 197 starts, 153 completes, and 23 expirations. The durable `analysis_jobs` table has no real new updates after 2026-05-01, which suggests many runs are no-op, stale, or invisible in the durable job model.

3. Transcript progress watermarks are stale relative to transcript chunks. Example: asset `9C109975` has fast transcript chunks through 66.0 minutes but `analysis_assets.fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime` is 1.5 minutes. Similar gaps exist for `C75C2E85`, `3B96D187`, `F3CB8FBF`, `FCFD51EB`, `58F57D4E`, `F920C21E`, `45501B10`, and `8A9DFC82`.

4. Terminal states overstate reality. Several assets are `completeFull` even though asset-level transcript/ad coverage fields are missing, tiny, or inconsistent with chunk/ad-window evidence. `completeFull` currently cannot be treated as a user-visible promise of full transcript plus ad analysis coverage.

5. The ad/DL field is underreported. Most assets have ad windows, but only 3 of 22 Activity rows expose confirmed ad coverage. The UI can therefore show `--%` even when algorithmic and user-marked ad windows exist.

6. Dogfood corrections are duplicated. The database contains 76 false-negative correction rows over 61 distinct scopes and 12 false-positive rows over 7 distinct scopes. Several exact spans repeat 2-4 times.

7. Learning tables are empty despite useful signal. The corpus export contains 88 corrections and the store has 1,321 shadow FM responses, but `sponsor_knowledge_entries`, `training_examples`, `ad_copy_fingerprints`, `boundary_priors`, `implicit_feedback_events`, `knowledge_candidate_events`, `music_bracket_trust`, and related learning tables are all empty.

8. Ad recall still needs a second wave after the boundary-singleton fix. The recent boundary singleton patch recovers a meaningful bucket, but the remaining false negatives include lower-score/no-log windows and midroll cases that need correction-aware learning and replay validation.

## Goal

Make the app honest and self-improving under real dogfood usage:
- Activity must show progress derived from canonical artifacts, not stale watermarks.
- Analysis/background jobs must report whether real work was claimed, advanced, deferred, expired, or no-op.
- Corrections and final-pass jobs must be idempotent.
- Dogfood corrections and shadow FM evidence must feed durable learning artifacts.
- Every fix must be covered by a minimized dogfood regression harness.

## Non-goals

- Do not blindly lower ad thresholds in production.
- Do not commit raw user transcripts/audio/diagnostic bundles.
- Do not treat `completeFull` as fixed by copy changes alone; the state machine and persisted coverage contract must be corrected.
design: Treat the May 6 dogfood export as a product feedback loop: fixture, explain, repair, learn, then export better diagnostics. Keep user privacy constraints intact: no raw audio, no raw transcript text, no install salt, and hashed episode ids only in support-safe artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: All child beads carry codebase-specific implementation seams, test seams, and explicit non-goals. Dependency graph remains acyclic. A future implementer can start each child without redoing this investigation.
notes:
2026-05-07 codebase audit: this epic is valid but should be implemented by extending existing Playhead seams, not by building parallel dogfood machinery. Key files: Playhead/Services/Activity/ActivitySnapshotProvider.swift, Playhead/Support/Diagnostics/DiagnosticsExportService.swift, Playhead/Persistence/AnalysisStore/AnalysisStore.swift, Playhead/Services/AnalysisCoordinator/AnalysisCoordinator.swift, Playhead/Services/AnalysisCoordinator/BackgroundProcessingService.swift, Playhead/Services/AdDetection/FinalPassRetranscriptionRunner.swift, Playhead/Services/AdDetection/UserCorrectionStore.swift, Playhead/Services/AdDetection/TrainingExampleMaterializer.swift, and PlayheadTests/Services/ReplaySimulator/NarlEval.

Recommended order after audit:
1. Build the sanitized May 6 fixture bridge in .1.1 so every downstream fix has stable input.
2. Reconcile Activity progress in .1.2, especially canonical transcript coverage semantics.
3. Add persisted terminal-state repair in .1.3 only for old/bad rows; the live classifier already has strong denominator tests.
4. Add durable background/run outcome summaries in .1.4; existing BGTaskTelemetryLogger is JSONL lifecycle telemetry, not durable no-progress accounting.
5. Tighten final-pass semantic dedupe in .1.5; current job idempotency is by adWindowId only.
6. Tighten correction semantic dedupe in .1.6; current INSERT OR IGNORE dedupes UUID only.
7. Wire existing training/knowledge/shadow stores in .1.7.
8. Use NARL to improve remaining ad recall in .1.8.
9. Export a structured analysis_health summary in .1.9 so the next dogfood file answers why nothing moved.

title: FrozenTrace v3: listen-rewind event capture
description:
## Problem

`recordListenRewind` (AdDetectionService.swift:3353) only mutates `AdWindowDecision.reverted` + profile counters. There is no persisted event log of listen-rewind taps. FrozenTrace v2 corpus therefore cannot supply listen-rewind evidence to the q45f counterfactual gate; the gate is structurally unsatisfiable today.

## Scope

1. Persist a `FalseSkipSignal` row at every `recordListenRewind` (windowId, podcastId, timestamp; new SQLite table OR append to existing capture log).
2. Extend `FrozenTrace` to v3: optional `listenRewindEvents: [FrozenListenRewindEvent]` (windowId, time, podcastId). Strictly additive; older fixtures decode `[]`.
3. Capture-time builder (FrozenTrace producer) reads the new rows into `listenRewindEvents`.
4. Round-trip + back-compat tests. 3-cycle skeptical review.

## Out of scope

- Re-capturing real-device fixtures (separate calendar-bound effort).
- q45f's option-C wiring (parent bead, blocked on this + fresh fixtures).

## Acceptance

- New persistence table/JSONL captures every `recordListenRewind` call atomically with the existing `updateAdWindowDecision`.
- `FrozenTrace.listenRewindEvents` round-trips through Codable with no schema-version bump in older fixtures.
- All existing FrozenTrace fixtures (2026-04-22..04-25) decode unchanged with `listenRewindEvents == []`.
- PlayheadFastTests green.
- 3-cycle skeptical review verdict: ship.

title: C26 H-1: doc-only fix for recordListenRewind trust-score writer policy
description:
Fix the misleading 'sole writer' doc claims in AdDetectionService.swift. The C26 reviewer flagged that AdDetectionService.recordListenRewind directly decrements skipTrustScore by 0.05, bypassing TrustScoringService's state machine. Two doc sites (lines 4949 and 5187) claim TrustScoringService is the 'sole writer', which is false.

Per user decision (option B): keep the 0.05 magnitude (deliberate weaker signal vs 0.10 explicit revert) and the state-machine bypass, but document the actual policy honestly:
- recordListenRewind: weaker FP signal, decrements 0.05, increments recentFalseSkipSignals, does NOT run demotion check
- TrustScoringService.recordFalseSkipSignal: stronger FP signal, decrements 0.10, runs demotion check

Followup playhead-q45f tracks the eval question of whether listen-rewind should feed demotion counter (option C deferred pending eval data).

Acceptance: doc claims at lines 4949 and 5187 reflect actual policy; recordListenRewind has a docstring explaining the deliberate divergence; PlayheadFastTests green; PR opened and merged.

title: Promotion-gate score path for classifier-seeded candidates (post-9.4.1 ceiling)
description:
## Problem

After `playhead-gtt9.4.1` (boundary expansion, merged d3bb935 on 2026-04-24) and the `a4ea4ca` classifier-seeding fix shipped, the 04-25 dogfood capture of episode 71F0C2AE shows the [7006, 7037.34] GT span FN reason changed from 'no scored windows overlap' → 'candidate windows present but none were promoted to auto-skip'. **Sec-F1 movement was zero on this episode** despite both fixes.

This means classifier-seeded candidates now reach BackfillEvidenceFusion but score below the `autoSkipConfidenceThreshold` (0.80) post-fusion. They don't become AdWindows, so 9.4.1's boundary-expansion logic never fires on them.

## Investigation needed

For the [7006, 7037.34] span on 71F0C2AE specifically:
1. What does the fusion pipeline actually score these candidates? (Read `shadow-decisions.jsonl` and the per-asset evidence ledger.)
2. Are the classifier-seeded candidates short (~2s) and isolated, or do they have neighboring evidence the fusion isn't picking up?
3. Does the post-9.4.1 boundary-expanded span (had it been admitted) overlap an acoustic-break envelope that could have been used as evidence?

## Proposed paths (pick after investigation)

1. **Score-boost via additional evidence** — give classifier-seeded candidates an acoustic-break alignment bonus or transcript-coverage confidence multiplier so borderline regions clear 0.80 without changing the global threshold.
2. **Second-tier promotion path** — separate eligibility track for classifier-seeded candidates with looser thresholds but tighter precision (e.g., require both classifier ≥0.70 AND acoustic-break alignment within a small radius).
3. **Threshold tuning** — lower the global auto-skip threshold conditionally (high-trust shows, fully-transcribed episodes). Bigger architectural move; precision risk.

Start with (1) — narrowest scope, doesn't change architecture.

## Acceptance

- For the 71F0C2AE 04-25 fixture, the [7006, 7037.34] GT span flips from FN to TP under `allEnabled` config without DoaC `allEnabled` Sec-F1 dropping >2pt.
- Cross-episode rollup ScoredCov stays flat or improves; AutoSkip Precision doesn't drop below 0.25.

## Reference

- Doc: `docs/narl/2026-04-24-real-data-findings.md` (post-correction section: 'Actual next ceiling')
- Pre-fix evidence: 04-24 fixture, FN reason 'no scored windows'
- Post-fix evidence: 04-25 fixture, FN reason 'candidate windows present but none promoted'
- Harness run: `.eval-out/narl/20260504-174000-93AB6B/`
- Code touchpoints: `AdDetectionService.makeClassifierProposals`, `BackfillEvidenceFusion`, `emitHotPathDecisionLogs`
