SkipOrchestrator.receiveAdWindows: block fusion-path-blocked-gate values symmetric with receiveAdDecisionResults
description: AdWindow rows persisted with eligibilityGate stamped from the fusion path (e.g. "blockedByPolicy", "blockedByEvidenceQuorum", "blockedByUserCorrection", "cappedByFMSuppression") fall through SkipOrchestrator.receiveAdWindows into the standard managed path. The cycle-2 type-decode pins ONLY the .markOnly branch; every other SkipEligibilityGate raw value decodes to a non-.markOnly result and reaches evaluateAndPush. By contrast, receiveAdDecisionResults explicitly guards `result.eligibilityGate == .eligible`. The asymmetry is caller-independent: receiveAdWindows is invoked from the cross-launch preload (SkipOrchestrator.beginEpisode), the live hot-path post-classification push (AnalysisCoordinator.handlePersistedTranscriptChunks at line 1885), AND the final-pass backfill push (AnalysisCoordinator.finalizeBackfill at line 1996) — every caller hits the same decode. Fusion stamps originate only in AdDetectionService.runBackfill via buildFusionAdWindow (writes decision.eligibilityGate.rawValue at line 2569; persists with decisionState == .candidate when policyAction == .autoSkipEligible AND decision.eligibilityGate != .eligible at line 2534). They surface to all three callers via: (a) store reads on relaunch for the preload; (b) reconcileHotPathWindows.preservedWindow copying existing.eligibilityGate at line 3291 from a matched candidate row for the hot-path push; (c) AdWindow refresh for finalizeBackfill. Cycle-6 corrected the in-code Producer note (cycles 4 and 5 had wrongly framed the hot-path push as benign). Symmetric guard needed in receiveAdWindows OR a documented justification for the asymmetry. Surfaced by cycle-3 skeptical review (H-1) and re-confirmed in cycles 4–6.

title: Episode summaries via on-device Foundation Model
description:
## Background

On-device episode summaries via the FoundationModelClassifier pattern. Sample first 3 min + middle segment + last 3 min of transcript, feed to FM via schema-bound `@Generable` struct (`summary: String`, `mainTopics: [String]`, `notableGuests: [String]`), persist to a new `episode_summaries` table in AnalysisStore, surface in EpisodeListView as expandable subtitle below the episode title with topic tags as small Soft Steel pills.

This is the highest-value novel idea from the 2026-04-29 dueling-idea-wizards run (DUELING_WIZARDS_REPORT.md). It is the only top-5 idea from either agent that is not already shipping or already in the backlog. CC ranked it #3 with score 650; COD scored it 755 cross-model.

## Cross-Model Validation

- CC self-score: 650 — "Leverages the FM advantage in a way that's daily-useful for backlog triage"
- COD cross-score: 755 — "Solves real backlog triage pain; uses on-device FM advantage in a user-facing way that can feel premium when done well"
- Verdict: CONSENSUS WIN, novel against backlog (no overlapping bead found)

## Goals

- Generate a 2-3 sentence verbatim-grounded summary per analyzed episode using on-device FM
- Extract main topics (3-5 keyword phrases) and notable guests
- Surface subtly in EpisodeListView for daily backlog triage
- Degrade gracefully when FM unavailable (CapabilitiesService gating)

## Implementation Approach

1. New `EpisodeSummaryExtractor` service (~200 lines) following FoundationModelClassifier patterns: schema-bound `@Generable` struct, `LanguageModelSession`, capability gating via `CapabilitiesService`, permissive-content fallback path for guardrail refusals on sensitive episodes.
2. Sampling strategy: first 3 min + middle segment + last 3 min of transcript chunks. Avoids feeding full transcripts (50K+ tokens) and bounds processing cost.
3. New `episode_summaries` table in `AnalysisStore` keyed by `analysisAssetId` (3 columns + FK).
4. Trigger: backfill scheduling pass after transcription reaches ≥80% coverage. Uses existing AnalysisWorkScheduler Background lane.
5. UI: `EpisodeListView` cell expansion shows summary in editorial serif font; topic tags as Soft Steel pills (matches existing design tokens). Falls back to standard show-notes excerpt when summary unavailable.

## Risks and Concerns

(Aggregated from COD's cross-scoring critique — the opponent's risk-list is the most honest assessment.)

- **Hallucination/over-summary risk** can erode trust fast. Mitigations: confidence gating on FM output, explicit fallback copy ("No summary available"), regression tests on known-episode fixtures.
- **FM availability variability** by device/locale (CapabilitiesService already handles this — graceful degradation).
- **FM guardrail refusals** on sensitive content (use the PermissiveAdClassifier permissive-content path as fallback).
- **Persistent artifact maintenance** — versioning, invalidation on transcript regeneration, schema migration. Use the existing artifact-versioning pattern from analysis_assets.
- **Design-identity drift** if summaries become "AI summary cards everywhere." Mitigation: subtle expandable subtitle, no badge, no "AI" wording in user-facing copy. Match the restraint of "small copper numeral, not a badge" from PLAN.md §4.8.

## Success Criteria

- Summaries generated for ≥90% of episodes with ≥80% transcript coverage on FM-capable devices
- 0 hallucination incidents on regression-test fixture set (baseline of 20 known episodes)
- EpisodeListView cell renders summary or graceful fallback in <50ms (cached)
- No design-identity violations: no "AI" wording, no metrics counter, no quantified confidence scores
- Optional toggle in Settings to disable summary generation entirely

## Provenance

- Source: 2026-04-29 dueling-idea-wizards run, CC #3
- Cross-model verdict: novel + high-value (no existing bead overlap)
- Full context: DUELING_WIZARDS_REPORT.md, WIZARD_IDEAS_CC.md (idea #3), WIZARD_SCORES_COD_ON_CC.md (score 755)

title: AnalysisStore production-safe paginated asset iteration
description:
gyvb.2 introduced a production call to AnalysisStore.fetchAllAssets() in runEpisodeDurationBackfillIfNeeded, but fetchAllAssets is #if DEBUG-gated (loads every analysis_assets row in one pass; can OOM on real listener libraries).

Symptom: Release archive (TestFlight) fails with 'value of type AnalysisStore has no member fetchAllAssets' at AnalysisCoordinator.swift:2520. Debug builds and tests succeed because the gate lets fetchAllAssets through.

Fix: Add a non-DEBUG paginated fetchAssets(limit: Int, offset: Int) and rewrite the sweep to iterate page by page (LIMIT/OFFSET ordered by createdAt DESC, rowid DESC), exiting when a page returns < limit.

Reason it must not stay #if DEBUG: the duration-watermark recovery is the whole point of the gyvb.2 backfill — gating it loses the fix on real users.

title: Use on-disk audio duration as source of truth, plus backfill sweep
description:
# Problem

Real-world incident, 2026-04-27. Cross-checked persisted
`episodeDurationSec` vs actual MP3 duration via `afinfo`:

| Asset | declared | actual | factor |
|---|---|---|---|
| F920C21E (running, stuck) | 704.48 s | 9700.78 s | **13.8×** |
| 78FE9F65 (backfill) | 709.93 s | (~6482 s feature watermark observed) | **~9×** |
| DCE6AA97 (queued) | 3225 s | 3226 s | ≈1× |

Feed-metadata duration (parsed from `<itunes:duration>` in
`PodcastFeedParser.swift:371`) is unreliable for some
libsyn/flightcast feeds. Today this value flows through
`PodcastDiscoveryService.persist()` into SwiftData
`Episode.duration`, then into the analysis pipeline as
`episodeDurationSec` (when the spool path doesn't yet have a
measured value).

The disposition reducer reads `episodeDurationSec` as truth in
coverage-ratio gates (`AnalysisCoordinator.classifyBackfillTerminal`,
~line 2091). If transcript/feature watermarks exceed the (wrong)
declared duration, classification logic is permanently confused and
the episode can't reach `.completeFull`.

# Fix

User directive: \"Once we have the real runtime from the file that
should be the source of truth.\"

Two changes:

## Change A — measure-on-download

After a download completes (file lands in
`AudioCache/complete/<id>.mp3`), probe the file's actual duration
via `AVURLAsset` (cheap; reads container metadata, no full decode)
and persist it to `analysis_assets.episodeDurationSec` via
`AnalysisStore.updateEpisodeDuration(id:durationSec:)`.

Source-of-truth ordering: **measured file duration > feed metadata**.
If the measured value is non-nil and finite, write it
unconditionally, overriding any prior feed-derived value.

The natural seam is in `DownloadManager` (or wherever the
download-complete transition fires) — but the implementer should
confirm a clean integration point before settling on a location. A
separate small helper (e.g. `AudioFileDurationProbe`) is fine.

`AnalysisCoordinator.runFromSpool()` (Playhead/Services/AnalysisCoordinator/AnalysisCoordinator.swift:1200-1227)
already persists a duration measured from decoded shards. After this
fix the on-download value should pre-empt that path; if the spool
later measures a different value, the spool measurement wins
(decoded sample count is more authoritative than container metadata
for actual playable length, and matches what feature/transcript
watermarks are expressed in).

## Change B — one-time backfill sweep

At app launch (or first time the analysis store opens this version),
run a one-shot sweep over `analysis_assets`:

- For each row where the on-disk audio file exists AND
  (`featureCoverageEndTime > episodeDurationSec` OR
  `transcriptCoverageEndTime > episodeDurationSec` OR
  `episodeDurationSec` is null/<= 0), re-probe the file with
  `AVURLAsset` and rewrite `episodeDurationSec`.
- Gate behind a SQLite-level migration marker or
  `AnalysisStore.didDurationBackfillRunV1` so it runs exactly once
  per install.

# Test plan

`PlayheadTests/Services/AnalysisCoordinator/EpisodeDurationPersistenceTests.swift`
already pins the resolver; mirror that style.

Unit:

- Probe helper given a real fixture .m4a/.mp3 returns finite
  duration matching `afinfo` (within 0.5 s tolerance).
- Probe helper on a non-audio file returns nil, doesn't throw.
- DownloadManager (or whichever seam) persists the probed duration
  to `analysis_assets.episodeDurationSec` after a stubbed download
  completes.
- If feed says 704 and probe returns 9700, persisted value is 9700.
- If feed is nil and probe returns 3226, persisted value is 3226.
- If probe fails, persisted value is whatever feed said (no
  regression).

Integration:

- A backfill suite that seeds an `analysis_assets` row with
  `episodeDurationSec=704` and `featureCoverageEndTime=9000`,
  triggers the sweep, asserts the row's duration is rewritten to
  the actual file value (>= 9000).
- The sweep marker prevents a second run from re-doing the work.

# Acceptance

- New unit tests fail on `main`, pass after the fix.
- Backfill integration test green.
- `xcodebuild test -scheme Playhead -testPlan PlayheadFastTests
  -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17 Pro'` green.
- No regressions in existing
  `EpisodeDurationPersistenceTests` / `AnalysisCoordinatorTests`.

# Out of scope

- Changing `Episode.duration` (SwiftData) source of truth — leaving
  feed metadata in the human-facing field is fine; only the
  analysis-pipeline `episodeDurationSec` needs to be measured-truth.
- Re-running classification on already-terminal episodes — the
  backfill only rewrites duration; downstream re-classification is
  the natural job of the existing `gtt9.1.1` failsafe pathway.

title: P1: FeatureExtraction in-memory window accumulator redundant with SQLite
description:
# P1: FeatureExtraction in-memory window accumulator redundant with SQLite persistence

## Problem

`Playhead/Services/FeatureExtraction/FeatureExtraction.swift:506` declares `allWindows: [FeatureWindow]` and the loop at 516-592 appends per-shard windows. Each window is persisted to SQLite at line 569 (synchronously inside the loop). Then line 594 returns the entire `allWindows` array.

The in-memory accumulator is **redundant** — the windows are already in the AnalysisStore, callers can fetch them via `fetchFeatureWindows(assetId:from:to:)`. The double-storage means peak RAM scales with episode duration even though the bounded SQLite copy is the source of truth.

For a 5-hour episode: ~9000 windows × ~120 bytes ≈ 1.1 MiB. Not a P0 OOM risk but inefficient and creates unclear data ownership.

## Fix

1. Audit callers of `extractFeatures(...)` (or whatever the entry point is). For each caller:
   - If it consumes the returned array immediately → fine to keep, or change caller to fetch from store
   - If it discards the return value → drop the in-memory accumulation entirely
   - If it iterates → consider an `AsyncStream<FeatureWindow>` return type that yields per-window
2. Remove `allWindows` if no caller needs the in-memory copy. Otherwise, document why both representations exist.

## Acceptance

- Peak in-flight RAM for FeatureExtraction proportional to **one window**, not the whole episode.
- All callers updated and tests green.
- No double-source-of-truth concern in code review.

## Out of scope

- Streaming feature extraction proper (separate bead if a caller really needs windows as they're produced).

## Dependencies

- None. Lower priority than P0 OOM beads.

title: gtt9.1.1: install JSONL sink for transcript shadow-gate decisions
description:
# gtt9.1.1: install JSONL sink for transcript shadow-gate decisions

## Problem

playhead-dzmu (gtt9.1) shipped the shadow-mode acoustic transcript gate but only wires `NoOpTranscriptShadowGateLogger` in production. Every shard's gate decision is computed and dropped on the floor. Without a real sink, the bead's eval procedure (replay against decision-log to compute would-skip-rate + host-read miss-rate) cannot run.

## Fix

Implement a concrete `TranscriptShadowGateLogging` that writes to `Documents/transcript-shadow-gate.jsonl`. Schema (per row):

- `episodeId` (string)
- `analysisAssetID` (string)
- `shardStart` (double, seconds)
- `shardEnd` (double, seconds)
- `decision` (string enum: `aboveThreshold` | `wouldSkip` | `safetySampleKeep` | `qualityPreconditionKeep` | `scoreUnknown`)
- `likelihood` (double, nullable when `scoreUnknown`)
- `threshold` (double, the active threshold at decision time)
- `transcribed` (bool, what actually happened)
- `timestamp` (ISO 8601)
- `buildCommitSHA` (for replay correlation)

Match the existing logger pattern from `DecisionLogger` / `BGTaskTelemetryLogger` (lazy bootstrap, periodic rotation at 10MB, jsonl format).

Wire the real logger in `PlayheadRuntime.swift` (production path) — keep `NoOpTranscriptShadowGateLogger` for previews and tests.

## Acceptance

- File appears in Documents during dogfood with non-empty rows.
- One row per gate-eligible shard.
- Rotation at 10MB.
- Eval tooling at `scripts/narl/gtt91-eval.swift` (or wherever the existing replay scripts live) can join shadow-gate.jsonl × decision-log.jsonl on `(analysisAssetID, shardStart, shardEnd)` and produce would-skip-rate + host-read miss-rate metrics.
- Source-canary test pinning the wiring (production runtime constructs the real logger, not the no-op).

## Out of scope

- Flipping `skipEnabled=true` (separate bead once eval data exists).
- The eval tooling itself can be a separate sibling bead if it grows.

## Dependencies

- gtt9.1 (playhead-dzmu) — shipped.

title: gtt9.1: acoustic-likelihood-driven transcript scheduling
description:
# gtt9.1: acoustic-likelihood-driven transcript scheduling

## Problem

Recent dogfood (2026-04-26 capture, ~hours of listening) shows **105,839 decision-log entries but only 147 fusion-scored windows (0.14%)**. Most windows are dropped at `BackfillEvidenceFusion.quorumGateForFMConsensus()` (line 492-495) because they have a single evidence kind (FM verdict OR acoustic break) but **no transcript** — `distinctKinds.count >= 2` blocks them. Transcript is *also* the dominant CPU/battery cost in the analysis pipeline.

Currently transcript runs unconditionally in `AnalysisJobRunner.run()` at line 238 (`await transcriptEngine.startTranscription(shards:...)`). All shards in `[0, desiredCoverageSec]` are passed to the engine — no per-window gating, no acoustic prefilter. The decision is made by `desiredCoverageSec` at job-enqueue time, not by per-window acoustic likelihood.

## Proposal

Gate transcript work on acoustic likelihood. Run transcript on windows where pre-computed acoustic features (music-bed onset/offset, speaker-change proxy, music-bed level) suggest ad-likely; skip the rest. This simultaneously **increases accuracy** (more borderline windows reach 2-kind quorum and can promote) and **reduces processing time** (fewer transcript cycles on quiet/non-ad audio).

Reuse existing `AcousticLikelihoodScorer.scoreOne()` (`Playhead/Services/PreAnalysis/AcousticLikelihoodScorer.swift:112-124`) which already combines these signals into `[0,1]` ad-likelihood per window. The scorer was built for gtt9.24 and is currently used only for "promote one window past T2" escalation, not in-job shard gating.

## Implementation sketch

1. **Single change site**: `AnalysisJobRunner.run()` at `Playhead/Services/AnalysisJobRunner/AnalysisJobRunner.swift:129` (shard filter) and `:238` (transcript dispatch).
2. **Add per-shard acoustic gate**: post-filter the `[0, desiredCoverageSec]` list to retain shards whose `AcousticLikelihoodScorer.scoreOne()` ≥ threshold (initial threshold from a configurable constant, default to be tuned via shadow eval).
3. **Pass the gated set** to `transcriptEngine.startTranscription(shards:)`. Engine logic unchanged.
4. **Shadow mode first**: gate selection but don't actually skip transcript — compute the gate, log "would-have-skipped" decisions, measure recall on the dogfood corpus before flipping a production switch.

## Mitigations for known risk

**Risk**: acoustic-quiet ad reads (host-read endorsements with no music bed) get missed.

- M1: require `transcriptQuality == .good` precondition — if transcript is already running for this episode, skip the gate (don't kill mid-stream).
- M2: low-confidence safety sample — keep transcribing 10% of low-likelihood windows as a calibration corpus; bead to make this configurable.
- M3: shadow-mode first; measure host-read miss rate on the dogfood corpus before enabling production skip.

## Acceptance

- Fusion-scored windows ratio rises from 0.14% to ≥5% on the 2026-04-26 dogfood corpus replay.
- Transcript wall-time per episode drops by ≥30% on a quiet-episode fixture.
- Held-out test set ad-detection recall ≥95% of pre-bead baseline (no regression on host-reads).
- Shadow-mode telemetry written for ≥1 dogfood capture before flipping production gate.
- PlayheadFastTests green; new unit tests for the gate logic pass.

## Out of scope

- MusicBed weight tuning (separate follow-up if shadow eval suggests).
- FM Positive-Only Rule loosening (lower-leverage; deprioritized).
- Per-gate metadata activation flag flips (separate bead).
- Decision-log volume (97MB/few-hours capture is excessive — separate sampling bead).

## Dependencies

- gtt9.24 (AcousticLikelihoodScorer infrastructure) — already shipped.
- Working preanalysis.recovery pipeline — blocked by the bgrace bug; gtt9.1 can be implemented but its production eval depends on the recovery fix.

title: preanalysis.recovery silent-fails on cold-launch BG wake (race with reconciler injection)
description:
# Bug: preanalysis.recovery silent-fails on cold-launch BG wake (race with reconciler injection)

## Symptom

User left phone plugged in overnight (~7 hours). **0 episodes finished processing.** `bg-task-log.jsonl` from the 2026-04-27 05:33Z dogfood capture shows preanalysis.recovery firing every ~30 minutes but every fire after the initial successful 23:19Z run completes with `success=false` and microsecond execution time.

| Timestamp | Exec time | Status |
|-----------|-----------|--------|
| 2026-04-26 23:19:32Z | 1074.57 sec | success (1 long active session) |
| 2026-04-27 02:04:57Z | 0.25 sec | **FAIL** |
| 2026-04-27 03:04:59Z | 6 µs | **FAIL** |
| 2026-04-27 03:35:25Z | 570 µs | **FAIL** |
| 2026-04-27 04:05:29Z | 23 µs | **FAIL** |
| 2026-04-27 04:35:37Z | 68 ms | **FAIL** |
| 2026-04-27 05:05:47Z | 1.7 ms | **FAIL** |
| 2026-04-27 05:35:57Z | 4.8 ms | **FAIL** |

decision-log.jsonl + asset-lifecycle-log.jsonl stayed flat across the same window.

## Root cause

`BackgroundProcessingService.handlePreAnalysisRecovery` at `Playhead/Services/AnalysisCoordinator/BackgroundProcessingService.swift:1083-1095`:

```swift
guard let reconciler = analysisJobReconciler else {
    logger.warning("Pre-analysis recovery: no reconciler available")
    markComplete(task, success: false)
    return
}
```

`analysisJobReconciler` is injected via `setPreAnalysisServices(scheduler:reconciler:)` at line 290, which is awaited from `PlayheadRuntime.init`'s deferred `Task { ... }` block at `PlayheadRuntime.swift:948-1085`. That block runs **8+ awaits** before injection: analysisStore.migrate (with retry), adCatalogStore.migrate, 4 logger migrations, recoverCoverageGuardFailures, pruneOrphanedScansForCurrentCohort, shadowRetryObserver, then setPreAnalysisServices.

When iOS wakes the app cold for a BGProcessingTask, the registered handler (`BackgroundProcessingService.swift:391-398`) fires **before** that deferred chain completes. Handler hits `guard` → `success=false` → microsecond exit.

## Why now

The 23:19Z task wrote 1074 seconds of data to the analysis store. Subsequent cold-launch migrate / pruneOrphanedScansForCurrentCohort / recoverCoverageGuardFailures wall-time grows with row count, widening the race window relative to BG-task fire timing. Pre-jndk this was masked because migrate was synchronous in init body; jndk + 6boz pushed it into the deferred Task to fix main-thread blocking, opening this race.

## Fix options

**Option A — buffer the task until injection lands.** In `handlePreAnalysisRecovery`, if reconciler is nil, suspend on a continuation set by `setPreAnalysisServices`. Add a 20s timeout (BGProcessingTask deadline is ~30s).

**Option B — inject reconciler eagerly in init body.** Reconciler is constructed in init at `PlayheadRuntime.swift:850`. If `setPreAnalysisServices` doesn't depend on analysisStore.migrate having completed (which it shouldn't, since AnalysisStore.ensureOpen is lazy after 6boz), call it synchronously after construction. The deferred Task only does the migrate chain, and the reconciler is available the moment the handler fires.

**Option C — defer registration until injection.** Risky: Apple requires registration before applicationDidFinishLaunching returns. Skip.

Lean toward **Option B** as most robust (no buffering, no race, no timeout), with a fallback to **Option A** if there's a hidden ordering dependency.

## Acceptance

- preanalysis.recovery cold-launch fires complete with `success=true` even when the deferred migrate chain hasn't finished yet.
- Source-canary or unit test pinning the new ordering — handler must succeed even if `analysisStore.migrate` hasn't been called.
- Race test: spin up BackgroundProcessingService, fire a fake BG task immediately, assert it doesn't instant-fail.
- Manual: after fix, re-capture overnight dogfood; expect preanalysis.recovery completions with non-trivial wall times (>>1s) and decision-log activity.

## Out of scope

- The 30-min BG fire cadence itself (iOS-controlled).
- The 23:19Z task's 18-min wall time (legit work; unrelated).
- gtt9.1 (acoustic-gated transcript scheduling) — separate bead.

title: gtt9.4 follow-up: wire MusicBedLevel + flip metadata activation
description:
# gtt9.4 follow-up: wire MusicBedLevel + flip metadata activation

## Problem

The 2026-04-24 spike under gtt9.4 found two evidence sources silent for **non-tuning reasons** — they're either disconnected or shipped disabled. Both are infrastructure-level, not gate-tuning, fixes.

## Change 1: Wire `MusicBedLevel` into `buildAcousticLedgerEntries`

**File:** `Playhead/Services/AdDetection/AdDetectionService.swift:1368-1387`

Currently `buildAcousticLedgerEntries` uses only `RmsDropScore` and early-exits via `guard breakStrength > 0 else { return [] }`. `MusicBedLevel` is computed in `FeatureWindow` but never threaded into `EvidenceLedgerEntry`. `BracketDetector` already consumes it for boundary refinement; the data is computed and discarded before reaching fusion.

**Fix:** Thread `MusicBedLevel` into `EvidenceLedgerEntry` as a second acoustic signal alongside RMS-drop. Drop the unconditional early-exit when MusicBedLevel is present. Estimated firing impact: acoustic 2% → 15-20% on the 2026-04-23 corpus.

## Change 2: Flip `counterfactualGateOpen` on in `MetadataActivationConfig.default`

**File:** `Playhead/Services/AdDetection/MetadataActivationConfig.swift:64-75`

`MetadataActivationConfig.default` ships with all gates false, including the master `counterfactualGateOpen=false`. The master kill makes **every** NARL metadata-activation knob inert (priorShift, metadata fusion, etc.) regardless of how it's tuned.

**Fix:** Set `counterfactualGateOpen = true` in the default config. Audit the per-gate flags below it — leave them as-is unless the spike notes an obvious correctness reason to flip them too. Add a unit test pinning the activation state so future config changes are intentional.

## Why both in one bead

Both fixes are "wire up signal that exists but isn't reaching production." Neither is a tuning knob. Bundling minimizes context-switch cost and produces one cohesive PR for cross-review.

## Acceptance

- `MusicBedLevel` appears as a distinct evidence kind in at least one ledger entry on the 2026-04-23 corpus when re-run via NARL harness.
- `MetadataActivationConfig.default.counterfactualGateOpen == true`.
- Pinned unit test asserts the activation default.
- PlayheadFastTests green.
- NARL harness re-run on the 2026-04-23 fixture set documents source-firing deltas in a brief markdown writeup at `docs/narl/2026-04-26-gtt9.4-followup-deltas.md`.
- Source-firing percentages updated in the gtt9.4 bead body or a follow-up note.

## Out of scope

- Tuning MusicBed weights or thresholds beyond what's needed to make it fire (separate bead if needed).
- Loosening the FM Positive-Only Rule (lower leverage; explicitly deprioritized).
- Per-gate metadata activation flag audit beyond `counterfactualGateOpen` (file a follow-up bead if any per-gate flag also needs flipping).

title: AnalysisStore lazy-init with schema-readiness signaling
description:
# AnalysisStore lazy-init with schema-readiness signaling

## Problem

`AnalysisStore.init` opens a SQLite handle and runs CREATE TABLE / migration DDL synchronously. After 2026-04-26's jncn refactor, the 5 logger stores (DecisionLogger, FoundationModelsFeedbackStore, AssetLifecycleLogger, BGTaskTelemetryLogger, SurfaceStatusInvariantLogger) all deferred their `migrate()` to a Task block in PlayheadRuntime.init, but **AnalysisStore is still synchronously constructed in init** — its DDL is the largest remaining sync I/O on the launch path.

This bead applies the same pattern to AnalysisStore: lightweight init (record the directory, nothing else), `ensureOpen()` lazy-opens at every public entry. But unlike the loggers, AnalysisStore is hot — it's read by ActivitySnapshotProvider, BackfillJobRunner, and AdDetectionService. Several of those callers race init: if they hit AnalysisStore before its DDL is ready, they get a confusing empty-result rather than a structured "not ready yet" signal.

## What this bead is

1. Refactor `AnalysisStore.init` to be lightweight (URL only).
2. Add `ensureOpen()` at each public entry point (open + migrate idempotent under WAL).
3. Add a schema-readiness signal callers can poll/await:
   - Either `var isOpen: Bool { get }` for callers that should treat unopened as "no data yet"
   - Or `func awaitReady() async` for callers that genuinely need to block until DDL completes.
4. Audit existing callers and route each to the right signal:
   - **ActivitySnapshotProvider.loadInputs**: should treat unopened as empty (UI shows the empty state, not a spinner).
   - **BackfillJobRunner**: should `awaitReady()` (it's already on a background actor; waiting is fine).
   - **AdDetectionService**: TBD — need to verify it can tolerate empty-result without misclassifying.
5. Source-canary tests asserting AnalysisStore.init body contains no `sqlite3_open` / `try .write(` / `FileManager.default.createDirectory` calls.
6. Race test: spawn N concurrent `ensureOpen()` callers, assert exactly one DDL pass runs.

## Why now

Two emergency main-thread fixes in 24 hours (jndk + hkn1) traced to sync I/O in init. AnalysisStore is the largest remaining offender. The os_signpost interval added in jndk will start showing AnalysisStore as the dominant init cost once the other fixes ship to dogfood — better to land this proactively than firefight after the next freeze report.

## Acceptance

- AnalysisStore.init does no I/O (directory existence check is OK; DDL is not).
- Every public entry calls `ensureOpen()` first.
- Source-canary test pins the new state.
- Race test confirms ensureOpen is idempotent.
- All existing AnalysisStore callers updated to the new contract.
- PlayheadFastTests green; integration tests green on simulator.
- os_signpost shows AnalysisStore.init time drops to near-zero; first-call latency is bounded and measured.

## Out of scope

- Connection pooling (single shared handle is fine).
- Migrating the 5 logger stores back to AnalysisStore's lazy pattern (jncn already did the equivalent for those — the patterns should converge later but not in this bead).

title: LibraryView PodcastGridCell.unplayedCount filter on every redraw
description:
P1 from 2026-04-26 main-thread blocking audit.

LOCATION: Playhead/Views/Library/LibraryView.swift:148-150

PROBLEM: Computed property unplayedCount runs .filter { !$0.isPlayed }.count on podcast.episodes inside a SwiftUI computed property that re-evaluates on every cell body redraw. With shows that have 50+ episodes per podcast and many podcasts in the library grid, this is O(N) per cell × N cells per frame = visible jank during scroll/animation on the Library tab.

FIX OPTIONS:
1. Cache as a derived property on the Podcast SwiftData model (with invalidation when episode.isPlayed changes).
2. Precompute once in the parent view (LibraryView) into [Podcast.id: Int] dict; pass into PodcastGridCell.
3. Use a @Query with #Predicate and grouping if SwiftData supports the aggregation (may not).

Option 2 is lowest-risk: single fetch in the grid parent, no schema change, no model invalidation logic.

ACCEPTANCE:
- LibraryView grid renders a 50-podcast × 50-episodes-per-podcast synthetic dataset under the Activity tab's 250ms wall-clock budget per the hkn1 perf-test pattern.
- Regression test pinning the budget at N=50×50.

CONTEXT:
- Audit ran 2026-04-26 against changes since git tag phase-2-review-complete (8fa7f4b, 220 commits).
- Found alongside the Activity N+1 (shipped as playhead-hkn1).

title: Lazy PermissiveAdClassifier + AdCatalogStore DDL deferral (launch-freeze fix)
description:
Root cause of multi-minute launch freeze (snapshot 2026-04-25 22:42).

PRIMARY: PlayheadRuntime.swift:467 instantiates PermissiveAdClassifier() synchronously inside PlayheadRuntime.init (which runs on main as part of PlayheadApp init, before SwiftUI's first frame). PermissiveAdClassifier.init at PermissiveAdClassifier.swift:660-664 calls SystemLanguageModel(guardrails: .permissiveContentTransformations). On iOS 26 this triggers FoundationModels framework init + locale probe + on-device model availability check — minutes of main-thread blocking.

SECONDARY: AdCatalogStore.init at AdCatalogStore.swift:156-182 runs PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL, foreign_keys, secure_delete, and migrate synchronously. Snapshot showed ad_catalog.sqlite-wal at 424 KB on a 4 KB DB — uncheckpointed write batches force WAL replay every launch. AnalysisStore.swift:778-841 already defers DDL to await migrate(); AdCatalogStore should do the same.

FIX:
1. Convert bd1enPermissiveBox in PlayheadRuntime.swift:465-470 from value-holding PermissiveClassifierBox(PermissiveAdClassifier()) to @Sendable () -> PermissiveAdClassifier factory closure. Box invokes lazily on first call (off main, inside detection pipeline).
2. Move AdCatalogStore PRAGMA + schema migration out of init into await migrate() / first-use path, mirroring AnalysisStore pattern.
3. Add os_signpost interval named PlayheadRuntime.init for measurement.
4. Source-canary test asserting PermissiveAdClassifier() is not constructed inside PlayheadRuntime.init body.

title: Defensive launch UX: hard splash dismiss + activity skeleton + sync-work audit
description:
## Problem

Tonight (2026-04-26) Dan reported the new build (`204d0ec`) freezes on a blank launch screen for several minutes. Investigation shows reconcile/recovery is already in a detached `Task { … }`, so it isn't structurally on the render path — but the splash still appears stuck. Root cause is a still-unknown contention path (likely SwiftData `@Query` / SwiftDataStore actor / SQLite WAL) feeding the main thread.

Even after we find the root cause, **a splash screen that depends on background work to dismiss is a latent UX bug**. Users will hit any future regression of this same shape and stare at a frozen logo. The defensive fix is to make the splash, the activity screen, and the launch path resilient to slow recovery — independent of whatever blocker we eventually find.

## What this bead is

Three independent UX defenses, one bead:

1. **Hard splash dismiss**: `RootView` flips `showSplash = false` after a fixed 1.0–1.5 s timer that runs on the **main runloop scheduler**, never on a Task that could be starved by recovery work. No dependency on runtime state, init, store readiness, or any `@Published`. Splash never lingers past the timer regardless of what's happening underneath.
2. **Activity-screen skeleton**: when the underlying store hasn't yet returned data (e.g. reconcile holding the writer), show a skeleton/loading state instead of an empty list or a spin-forever. Acceptance: when store calls take >250 ms, the user sees a non-frozen UI.
3. **Audit + relocate any synchronous work** off the critical path:
   - `PlayheadRuntime.init` — anything that does I/O, DB migration, or SQLite open synchronously needs to move to the existing detached Task or a separate Task.
   - Any `@Query` in `RootView` / `ContentView` / `ActivityView` that runs on the main thread against a contested store — wrap in a model that reads off-main and publishes a value, or use a paginated/lazy query.
   - `analysisStore.migrate()` — confirm it's already in the detached Task at `PlayheadRuntime.swift:762`. If not, move it.

This is purely additive UI defense. No behavioral change to recovery, scheduler, or analysis pipeline.

## Why now

We can't ship users a build that hangs on launch. Even if the underlying blocker turns out to be cheap to fix, this defense prevents the next regression from turning into the same crisis. Shipping this before the root-cause investigation lands means Dan's next dogfood install is bounded — at worst, splash dismisses in 1.5 s and the activity screen shows skeleton while reconcile finishes in the background. Shipping this also gives the next investigation a stable canvas.

## Acceptance

- New `RootView` splash timer using `DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter` or equivalent main-runloop scheduler, NOT a `Task`. 1.0–1.5 s, configurable via constant.
- Splash dismisses even if `runtime` is not yet finished initializing — confirm by manually delaying init by 5 s in a debug-only path and verifying splash still dismisses on schedule.
- Activity screen renders a skeleton (placeholder rows / shimmer / "Catching up…" copy — pick the simplest) when its data source returns no rows yet AND a flag indicating recovery is in progress is true. Recovery flag exposed by `PlayheadRuntime` or whoever owns the launch Task.
- All synchronous I/O / SQLite / SwiftData open in `PlayheadRuntime.init` audited and relocated off the critical path. Any unavoidable sync work documented in code comments with rationale.
- Test: assert that with `runtime.isLaunchRecoveryComplete == false` for 3 s, the splash still dismisses at 1.0–1.5 s.
- Test: activity-screen view-model returns skeleton state when its store-read promise hasn't resolved within 250 ms.

## Out of scope

- Fixing the underlying blocker that makes recovery slow on this device — that's the next bead, after we audit `ActivityViewModel`, `migrate()`, and `@Query` usage with a fresh investigation.
- Reworking the recovery pipeline itself.
- Changing splash visual design.

## References

- 2026-04-26 frozen-launch snapshot: `/Users/dabrams/playhead/com.playhead.app 2026-04-25 22:42.28.954.xcappdata/`
- Investigation report (this session): reconcile is already detached at `PlayheadRuntime.swift:762`; splash dismiss in `RootView.onAppear` is unconditional but still doesn't fire — root cause TBD.
- btwk (`204d0ec`) — the recovery sweep we shipped tonight that highlighted this latent UX issue.

title: Reconciler sweep: recover stranded backfill/running/paused jobs from prior sessions
description:
## Problem

Tonight (2026-04-26) Dan installed a fresh build (`1b1fa47`, contains gjz6 + 5uvz tail). 6 episodes from yesterday's broken-build session are parked in `backfill` state (e.g. `F5F027F7` at 89s/3695s = 2.4% coverage). 16 minutes of foreground time after install: zero scheduler activity, zero state transitions, decision-log mtime unchanged.

Root cause traced to a reconciler gap:

1. `AnalysisJobReconciler.discoverUnEnqueuedDownloads()` calls `fetchActiveJobEpisodeIds()`, which returns "everything not `complete`/`superseded`". So `backfill`-state jobs count as "active" and the reconciler **skips re-enqueueing them**.
2. `AnalysisWorkScheduler.fetchNextEligibleJob()` only picks jobs in `queued`/`paused`/`failed`. A `backfill`-state job is **not eligible for dispatch**.
3. Result: stranded `backfill` jobs are simultaneously "already covered" (per reconciler) and "not pickable" (per scheduler) — invisible.

5uvz.8 only re-enqueues across `analysisVersion` bumps (supersession). Today's `3144f6a` auto-recovery sweep only handles **coverage-guard-stranded** sessions. Same shape of bug, different stranding cause: **build replacement**.

## Fix

Add a step in `AnalysisJobReconciler.reconcile()` that sweeps jobs in `backfill` / `paused` / `running` whose `sessionID` does not match the current session, and marks them as `queued` while preserving their `transcriptCoverageEndSec` (so we resume from where the previous build left off, not restart from zero).

Place between `recoverExpiredLeases()` (current step 1) and `unblockMissingFiles()` so reaper has already run; sweep then catches any survivors.

## Acceptance

- New step in `reconcile()`: `recoverStrandedSessionJobs()` (or similar name).
- TDD: regression test creates a synthetic `backfill`-state job with a stale `sessionID`, runs reconcile, asserts the job is now `queued`, has a fresh `sessionID`, and `transcriptCoverageEndSec` is preserved.
- Second test: a `running`-state job with stale `sessionID` is also recovered (matches the lease-expiry path's intent but for state-transitions, not lease-expiry).
- Third test: a `running`-state job with the **current** sessionID is NOT touched (do not yank legitimate in-flight work).
- Fourth test: a `complete`/`superseded` job is not touched.
- PlayheadFastTests pass.

## Out of scope

- Changing `fetchNextEligibleJob` to consider `backfill` eligible (would create dispatch races with currently-running backfill loops).
- Refactoring `fetchActiveJobEpisodeIds` semantics (broader change; this bead's approach is upstream of that).
- Build-version stamping on jobs to auto-detect "stale build" (separate, useful, but not this bead).

## References

- 2026-04-26 device snapshot showing 6 stranded backfill jobs invisible to new build's scheduler
- 5uvz.8 (`6125071`) — re-enqueue at current version inside the same reconcile (handles version bump)
- 3144f6a — auto-recover sessions stranded by coverage guard (handles guard, not build-replace)
- gjz6 (`b70c601`) — rearm BG task on enqueue when backgrounded (the fix that should now run, but can't because nothing enqueues)

title: BG-task telemetry: stamp BGTaskScheduler events into bg-task-log.jsonl
description:
## Problem

The 2026-04-25 device snapshot showed background processing stalled all day with zero forward progress on backfill. We had to *infer* the failure mode from activity-blackout shape in `decision-log.jsonl` because **no log carries direct `BGTaskScheduler` / `BGProcessingTask` events**. That inference took a multi-step subagent investigation; with direct telemetry it would have been a 5-second jq query.

## What this bead is

Add a dedicated `bg-task-log.jsonl` under `Documents/` capturing every BG-task lifecycle event:

- `BGTaskScheduler.submit` attempts: success/failure + `error` + `taskRequest.identifier` + `earliestBeginDate`
- `BGProcessingTask.start`: identifier, scenePhase, time-since-submit
- `BGProcessingTask.setTaskCompleted` calls: identifier, success bool, work-done summary
- `BGProcessingTask.expirationHandler` fires: identifier, time-into-task, what-was-running

Also stamp `appLifecycle` events: `applicationDidEnterBackground`, `applicationWillEnterForeground`, `sceneWillEnterForeground` so we can correlate.

## Why now

Tonight (2026-04-25), we had to root-cause from indirect signals when Dan reported BG processing broken. The actual cause turned out to be a missing fix already shipped (`gjz6`), not a regression — but we couldn't tell that without a 700-word forensic exercise. The next dogfood run will produce the same diagnostic burden if we don't fix the observability gap now.

## Acceptance

- New `BGTaskTelemetryLogger` (or extension to existing diagnostics writer) emits to `Documents/bg-task-log.jsonl` (rolling, capped at e.g. 5 MB).
- Wired at every BG-task surface point: registration, submission, callback start, completion, expiration.
- One-line jq cookbook in module doc-comment showing how to extract: submitted-vs-fired ratio, expiration rate, mean-time-in-task.
- Unit test asserts each event type writes a parseable JSON line with the expected schema fields.
- No production behavior change — purely additive observability.

## Out of scope

- Reconcile-trigger debouncing (separate bead).
- Fancy UI for browsing the log.
- Remote upload / Sentry-style aggregation.

## References

- 2026-04-25 forensic root-cause: device on 2c099de showed all-day BG stall; cause was missing gjz6 (b70c601) fix
- gtt9.21 (detectorVersion + buildCommitSHA stamping in FrozenTrace) — same observability philosophy
- gjz6 (b70c601) "rearm BG task on enqueue when backgrounded" — the fix this telemetry would have surfaced instantly

title: Surface AdCatalogStore match telemetry in corpus export so NARL can measure the correction loop
description:
## Problem

AdCatalogStore (gtt9.13/9.17) emits per-span match similarities at fusion time and adds an EvidenceLedgerEntry with source `.catalog`, but the corpus export pipeline does not surface this signal in any analyzable form. Two distinct gaps cause the loop to be empirically invisible:

1. **Schema collision in FrozenTrace.evidenceCatalog**: `FrozenEvidenceEntry` has only `source: String`, and BOTH the in-pipeline `EvidenceCatalogBuilder` (transcript sponsor tokens) and `AdCatalogStore` matches use the source string `.catalog`. NARL replay cannot distinguish them.

2. **Match telemetry not exported**: `AdDetectionService.lastCatalogMatchSimilarityForTesting()` is the only reader of the per-backfill top similarity. The value is not persisted to AdWindow rows, decision logs, or the corpus export.

## Why this matters

The 2026-04-25 correction-loop audit (`docs/narl/correction-loop-audit-2026-04-25.md`, gtt9.25) could not measure the catalog firing rate on real corpora, because:

- 11 corrections exist in the 04-25 capture (8 on Conan asset E8F0F867, 3 on DoaC) — `recordUserMarkedAd` should have inserted ≥ 11 catalog rows on the capturing device.
- Zero fingerprint catalog matches show up in any FrozenTrace fixture (all 20 `.catalog` entries across 64 fixtures are sponsor tokens, not store hits).
- We cannot tell if the loop is tight, loose, or broken.

This blocks any bead that wants to tune the 0.80 similarity floor, the 0.20 catalogCap, or the show-scoping semantics — none of those decisions can be made without telemetry.

## Concrete fix

Two-part change, additive only:

### A. Per-span catalog match similarity field

Add `catalogStoreMatchSimilarity: Double?` (nullable Double) to:

- `AdWindow` (or a sibling table `ad_window_catalog_match` keyed by windowId) so the value persists with the decision.
- The corpus export JSONL row schema (`CorpusExporter.swift`).
- `FrozenWindowScore` in `PlayheadTests/Services/ReplaySimulator/ReplayMetrics.swift` so NARL replay can read it.

`AdDetectionService.runBackfill` already computes `spanTopCatalogSimilarity` per span (`AdDetectionService.swift:1747-1758`); plumb that into the new field.

### B. Disambiguate source label OR add a sub-source

Either:

- (B1) Split the source label: rename the in-pipeline transcript catalog to `.transcriptCatalog` and keep `.catalog` for AdCatalogStore (preferred — better names align with what each is).
- (B2) Keep `.catalog` shared but add a `subSource: String?` field on `EvidenceLedgerEntry` and `FrozenEvidenceEntry`. `AdCatalogStore` matches set `subSource = "acousticStore"`, transcript catalog leaves it nil.

(B1) is cleaner. Either is acceptable.

## Acceptance

- New corpus exports include per-span `catalogStoreMatchSimilarity`.
- NARL eval report breaks out a column `AdCatalogStoreFireRate` (windows where catalogStoreMatchSimilarity >= 0.80 / total windows).
- An older capture re-replayed against the 04-25 corpus shows: a Conan ad span on a SECOND captured episode after the original correction lands either a) a non-zero similarity, or b) a documented zero (loop is loose, escalate).
- All existing `.catalog` source-label assertions across the test suite still green (or are intentionally re-pointed to whichever new label).

## Out of scope

- Adding a `catalog-export.jsonl` artifact alongside corpus export (gap 2 of the audit; separate bead if needed).
- Changing the dedup semantics to make replays idempotent (gap 3; tech debt).
- Cross-show fingerprinting (separate bead, originally lever D).
- Tuning the floor or cap based on the new telemetry — that is a follow-up after we can measure.

## References

- `docs/narl/correction-loop-audit-2026-04-25.md` (gtt9.25)
- `Playhead/Services/AdDetection/AdDetectionService.swift:1737-1772` (egress site)
- `Playhead/Services/AdDetection/AdDetectionService.swift:2097-2118` (ledger build)
- `Playhead/Views/Settings/CorpusExporter.swift`
- `PlayheadTests/Services/ReplaySimulator/ReplayMetrics.swift:680-944`

title: Banner-gradient UX: tier auto-skip / suggest / silent thresholds for skip-worthiness gradient
description:
## Problem

The product philosophy (per memory `project_ad_gradient`) treats ads as existing on a skip-worthiness gradient: clear-cut sponsor reads at one end, borderline cross-promo content in the middle, host-read ads with content value at the other end. The current banner UX shows up only when the detector clears the auto-skip precision threshold (currently 0.55). Everything below that is invisible to the user — even though the user might want agency over the gradient.

In the latest NARL eval, AutoSkip Recall on `completeFull` cohort = 14%. Six of seven ads are NOT auto-skipped under the current threshold. Of those six, many sit in the 0.30–0.50 confidence band — high enough that we have an opinion, low enough we don't trust auto-skip. The user has no way to see those.

## What this bead is

Lower the threshold for *showing a banner* well below the auto-skip threshold. Banner precision can be substantially lower than auto-skip precision because the user is the gate: they swipe to skip if they agree, ignore if not. Wrong banner = mild noise; wrong auto-skip = deleted content.

Tier the UX:

1. **High-confidence (≥ 0.55, current)** — auto-skip + visible banner ("Skipped sponsor break").
2. **Medium-confidence (~0.35–0.55, NEW)** — visible banner ("This may be a sponsor break. Swipe to skip.") with an obvious skip affordance. NO auto-skip.
3. **Low-confidence (< 0.35)** — silent. Maybe a subtle indicator on the seek bar but no banner.

This converts the 14% auto-skip recall ceiling into "the user has direct control on most of the remaining ads they're hearing."

## Why now

This is the highest-leverage change for *felt experience* per unit of engineering cost. It doesn't require any classifier improvement, any pipeline-coverage fix, any new evidence channels. It's a UX decision about how to surface what we already detect.

## Design questions

1. **Thresholds**: what bands? Hard numbers or per-show-calibrated?
2. **Banner content**: what exactly does the medium-confidence banner say? (User memory: "peace of mind, not metrics" — avoid quantified language like "73% confidence.")
3. **Persistence**: banner stays visible until user swipes / dismisses, or auto-fades?
4. **Skip affordance**: same gesture as auto-skip? Different? More prominent?
5. **Telemetry**: do we record user accepts/declines on medium-confidence banners? That signal is exactly what calibrates future thresholds (and feeds the user-correction loop).

## Acceptance

- Three-tier banner system implemented with clear thresholds.
- Unit test fixture: medium-confidence detection produces banner+skip-affordance, no auto-skip.
- User-action telemetry on medium-confidence banner (accepted swipe / ignored) captured into FrozenTrace.
- Visual review with the user before merging — this is a UX-shaping change.

## Out of scope

- Auto-skip threshold recalibration (`gtt9.3`).
- Per-show banner customization (Phase 10+).
- Audio ducking on sponsor reads (different feature).

## References

- Memory: `project_ad_gradient` ("Ads exist on a skip-worthiness gradient; banner UX handles borderline cases")
- Memory: `feedback_peace_of_mind_not_metrics`
- Existing banner: `playhead-vjxc` (banner evidence catalog, shipped)
- E2E test: `playhead-e8z` (banner accuracy testing — separate from gradient design)
- 2026-04-25 NARL eval: `.eval-out/narl/20260425-160022-E1D7EB/report.md`

title: Show-notes / iTunes chapter ingestion: parse RSS chapter markers as ad evidence
description:
## Problem

Many podcasts label sponsors directly in their RSS show notes, `<itunes:chapters>` markers, or both. The current ad-detection pipeline ignores this entirely and pays full transcription cost to rediscover information the publisher already disclosed. For cooperative shows, this is the lowest-cost evidence we can get — zero CPU, zero battery, deterministic.

## What this bead is

Parse RSS-feed metadata (`<itunes:chapters>`, `<podcast:chapters>`, structured show-notes HTML) at feed-refresh time. Extract:

1. **Chapter markers** with timestamp + title — chapters titled "Sponsor", "Ad break", "[ad]", or matching known patterns become high-precision ad-evidence anchors.
2. **Sponsor-list mentions in show notes HTML** — many shows include "This episode is sponsored by X. Use code Y." Treat these as classifier hints (sponsor name + likely host-read pattern).
3. **External chapter feeds** (PodcastIndex `<podcast:chapters>` JSON URL) — same parse, just a separate fetch.

## Why now

The 2026-04-25 NARL eval shows 2914 s of pipeline-FN time across the corpus, of which the long-episode shows (Conan, etc.) dominate. Show-notes ingestion can short-circuit transcript dependency entirely on cooperative shows — the pipeline still runs for the un-labeled regions, but the labeled regions get instant high-precision evidence.

## Design questions

1. **Confidence weighting**: how strongly do publisher-supplied chapter markers seed the fusion? Treat as ground-truth (auto-skip eligible) or as one evidence channel among many?
2. **Fallback when chapter timestamps are imprecise**: many feeds have chapter starts but no ends, or have rounded-to-the-second timestamps off by ±2 s. Need a snap-to-acoustic-boundary pass.
3. **Cooperative-share heuristic**: not every show provides usable metadata. Detect once per show whether chapters are reliable and remember.
4. **Dynamic content**: some feeds rewrite show notes after publish (e.g., to add the sponsor list later). Re-fetch on cadence or only on first-fetch?
5. **Privacy/network**: feed metadata is already fetched as part of refresh; this is a pure parser, no new network calls. Verify.

## Acceptance

- Parser handles `<itunes:chapters>`, inline chapter markers in description CDATA, and `<podcast:chapters>` JSON URL.
- Chapter markers tagged "sponsor" / "ad" / "[ad break]" feed `AdCatalogStore` or `BackfillEvidenceFusion` as a new evidence channel.
- Regression test fixture: a feed with known sponsor chapters; assert detection picks them up without transcript.
- Telemetry: chapter-derived evidence distinguishable in FrozenTrace (`evidenceSource=metadata.chapters`).

## Out of scope

- Inferring chapters via on-device LLM from transcript — that's `playhead-w7oi`.
- Ingesting Spotify / YouTube / external sponsor databases.
- Cross-show sponsor-name fingerprint matching (separate bead, lever D).

## References

- 2026-04-25 NARL eval: `.eval-out/narl/20260425-160022-E1D7EB/report.md`
- Existing AdCatalogStore (gtt9.13)
- `<podcast:chapters>` spec: https://podcasting2.org/podcast-namespace/tags/chapters

title: Foreground transcript catch-up: playhead-aware escalation for long-episode pipeline coverage
description:
## Problem

Long episodes (Conan ≈ 117 min, similar long-form podcasts) consistently fail to reach pipeline-coverage completion via background-only transcription. From the 2026-04-25 NARL eval (run `E1D7EB`):

- 12 of 21 Conan episodes flagged `pipelineCoverageFailureAsset`
- 2714 s of pipeline-driven false-negative time on Conan alone (vs 200 s on DoaC)
- Pipeline FN dominates classifier FN by ~5× (2914 s vs 570 s across all shows)
- Even on episodes where transcription DID complete (`completeFull` cohort), AutoSkip Recall = 14% — but that's a separate, smaller lever (see gtt9.4 family)

The root coverage problem is that iOS BG-task budget can't realistically chain enough wakeups to transcribe 90+ minute episodes before the user wants to listen. The user is then playing audio that has been transcribed for ~90 s out of 7000 s. No amount of classifier tuning helps audio that was never scored.

## What this bead is

A **playhead-aware foreground transcription escalation**: when the user is actively playing an episode and the playhead is approaching the un-transcribed region, transcribe the upcoming N minutes ahead of playhead at user-foreground priority (not BG-task priority). This converts "Conan didn't get backfilled overnight" into "Conan finishes transcribing as you listen."

This complements (does NOT replace) the BG-task-chained backfill path. BG continues opportunistically as today; foreground catch-up is the safety net that guarantees the user always has scored audio in front of the playhead.

## Design questions to resolve

1. **Trigger condition**: how close to the un-transcribed region should the playhead get before catch-up kicks in? Candidates:
   - Distance-based: < 60 s of transcribed audio remaining ahead of playhead
   - Time-to-empty-based: at current playback rate, transcribed audio runs out in < 30 s
   - Always-on while playing: continuously transcribe ahead at lower priority (probably wrong — defeats battery wins of scheduled BG work)
2. **Lookahead window**: how far ahead should foreground catch-up transcribe? Candidates:
   - Fixed (e.g., 5 min)
   - Relative to playback speed (e.g., 5 min × playback rate)
   - Until end of episode if BG already gave up
3. **Priority interaction with hot path**: AdDetectionService already has a hot-path transcript for "lookahead near current playhead." Is the proposal a new pass or a re-prioritization of the existing one? Need to read `AdDetectionService.runHotPathResult` and `AnalysisCoordinator.handlePersistedTranscriptChunks` to know.
4. **Backpressure on classifier/fusion**: foreground catch-up will dump transcripts faster than today's BG-driven cadence. Does the classifier path scale to that ingestion rate, or do we need batching / gating?
5. **Battery / thermal**: foreground transcription on a long episode is a significant CPU draw. Should it pause when battery is low / device is thermally throttled? (Likely yes — defer to existing `BatteryStateProviding` / capability gates the pipeline already uses.)
6. **User-perceptible latency**: if the user fast-forwards past the transcribed region, what UX shows? "Skipping ad ▸ analyzing…" indicator? Block skip until catch-up reaches that region?

## Why now

The 5uvz.* tail (in flight) and the existing gtt9.1.1 fix close the BG-task reliability gaps but cannot raise the BG-task budget ceiling — that's an iOS limit, not ours. Foreground catch-up is the only path that bypasses the BG ceiling for a user who actually starts listening.

This is the highest-leverage net-new pipeline-coverage work currently un-bedded.

## Acceptance

- Design doc enumerating decision matrix for the 6 questions above (committed to `docs/narl/` or similar).
- Concrete thresholds chosen for trigger / lookahead.
- Implementation: foreground transcription pass triggered by playhead position, gated on capability + battery checks, integrating with existing AdDetectionService hot path (no double-decoding the same audio).
- Telemetry: distinguishable in FrozenTrace as `foregroundCatchUp` so we can verify it actually moved Conan pipeline coverage in the next NARL capture.
- Regression test: unit test that simulates a partial-transcript-coverage asset, plays past the transcribed region, asserts foreground catch-up was invoked and converted the asset to scored audio.

## References

- 2026-04-25 NARL eval: `.eval-out/narl/20260425-160022-E1D7EB/report.md`
- gtt9.1.1 (closed): persistEpisodeDuration + fail-safe coverage-guard shortcuts
- 5uvz.4 (just shipped, PR #15 → bc1c084): rearm BG task post-feed-refresh — a slice of the BG-chain reliability story
- Memory: `project_ad_detection_weak_on_conan` (2026-04-23)

## Out of scope

- Classifier/recall ceiling on already-complete episodes (separate work, gtt9.4 family).
- Threshold recalibration (gtt9.3, pending dogfood data).
- BG-task scheduling improvements not driven by the playhead position.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc + impl + telemetry + regression test, per body

title: NARL threshold sweep: pre-dogfood calibration of segmentAutoSkipThreshold
description:
Pre-dogfood threshold sweep against the existing NARL frozen-trace corpus.

**Goal:** Sweep `AdDetectionConfig.segmentAutoSkipThreshold` over `[0.40, 0.45, 0.50, 0.55, 0.60, 0.65, 0.70]` (current default 0.55) to find the precision/recall knee on the existing labeled fixtures.

**Why pre-dogfood:** Threshold gating is applied at the END of the replay pipeline (`AutoSkipPrecisionGate.classify`), so re-scoring frozen predictions against varied thresholds requires zero re-detection. Cheap to run, gives us a starting point before dogfood data lands.

**Implementation outline (per Explore agent's survey):**
1. Extend `PlayheadTests/Services/ReplaySimulator/NarlEval/NarlEvalHarnessTests.swift:634-783` with a sweep over thresholds.
2. Per (show, threshold) pair, recompute precision/recall/F1 against labeled spans.
3. Hold `segmentUICandidateThreshold` fixed at 0.40 for this sweep.
4. Emit a sweep report to `.eval-out/narl/<ts>/sweep.csv` with columns: show, threshold, P, R, F1.

**Caveats:**
- Frozen traces predate kgby (boundary timing changed today). Thresholds operate on segment scores, not boundaries, so sweep is still valid.
- Successor to playhead-gtt9.3 (threshold recalibration) — gives that bead a calibrated starting point.

title: Wire AnalysisCoordinator.recoverOrphans into cold-launch path (Gap-2)
description:
**From audit playhead-5uvz Gap-2 (HIGH).**

`AnalysisCoordinator.recoverOrphans(now:graceSeconds:)` is the bead-spec'd lease reaper that:
- inspects the last `work_journal` entry for each stranded `analysis_jobs` row;
- treats .finalized / .failed as terminal → clear lease, no requeue;
- treats .checkpointed / .acquired / .preempted / no-entry as recoverable → bump scheduler epoch, mint fresh generationID, re-queue, demote Now-lane jobs stale > 60s to Soon.

**Confirmed by grep:** `recoverOrphans` has zero production call sites (only the definition + one test file + one journal append site).

What runs instead at startup: `AnalysisJobReconciler.reconcile()` via `PlayheadRuntime.swift:775`, whose `recoverExpiredLeases` step is a blind sweep — requeues running|queued|paused rows whose lease expired with no journal-aware policy. No Now→Soon demotion, no scheduler-epoch bump, no generation rotation.

**Fix scope:** Call `AnalysisCoordinator.recoverOrphans` at app launch (in `PlayheadRuntime.startSchedulerLoop`, before `reconciler.reconcile()`). Reduce `AnalysisJobReconciler.recoverExpiredLeases` to a fallback for jobs the journal-aware path skipped (e.g. corrupt epoch).

**Depends on:** playhead-5uvz.1 (Gap-1) — without journal rows in production, recoverOrphans degrades to the same blind-sweep behavior as the current Reconciler. Wire the journal first OR ship Gap-2 at the same time so the journal-aware policy starts mattering.

**Files:** `Playhead/Services/AnalysisCoordinator/AnalysisCoordinator.swift` (lines 805-902), `Playhead/App/PlayheadRuntime.swift` (line 775), `Playhead/Services/PreAnalysis/AnalysisJobReconciler.swift`.

See: `docs/audits/2026-04-25-episode-job-dag-audit.md`

title: Wire WorkJournal-emitting lease API into scheduler dispatch (Gap-1)
description:
**From audit playhead-5uvz Gap-1 (HIGH).**

Production scheduler claims jobs via the lightweight `AnalysisStore.acquireLease(jobId:owner:expiresAt:)` (bare UPDATE, no journal write). The richer `AnalysisStore.acquireEpisodeLease(...)` — which atomically appends a `work_journal` row with eventType=`acquired` inside the same SQL transaction — is reachable only through `AnalysisCoordinator.acquireLease(episodeId:)`, which has zero production call sites. Confirmed by grep.

Also: `AnalysisWorkScheduler.setWorkJournalRecorder` is wired to inject a recorder, but `PlayheadRuntime` never calls it. The default is `NoopWorkJournalRecorder`. The single `recordPreempted` site at processJob:1622 is a no-op in production.

**Consequence:** the production work_journal table never accumulates acquired/finalized/failed/checkpointed/preempted rows from the scheduler-driven pipeline. Every diagnostic, orphan-recovery decision, and operator triage tool that reads work_journal sees an empty journal. Gap-2 (recoverOrphans dead code) is enabled by this gap.

**Fix scope:** Either (a) wire `AnalysisCoordinator.acquireLease(episodeId:)` into the scheduler dispatch path replacing the bare `acquireLease` call, OR (b) extend the bare API to append a `work_journal` row in the same transaction, OR (c) wire `PlayheadRuntime` to inject a real `WorkJournalRecorder` into the scheduler. Pick the simplest that gets journal rows into production.

**Files:** `Playhead/Services/PreAnalysis/AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift` (lines 1001 and 1440), `Playhead/Persistence/AnalysisStore/AnalysisStore.swift` (lines 4611 and 4934), `Playhead/App/PlayheadRuntime.swift`.

See: `docs/audits/2026-04-25-episode-job-dag-audit.md`

title: Investigate overnight background-processing gap (04-24 20h → 04-25 07h)
description:
## Evidence

Capture bundle: `.captures/2026-04-25/com.playhead.app 2026-04-25 07:43.49.095.xcappdata/`

Decision-log histogram (events per hour):
- 04-24 19h: 10,680 events (foreground use; user queueing 4 episodes)
- 04-24 20h–23h: **0 events**
- 04-25 00h–06h: **0 events**
- 04-25 07h+: morning resume after user reopened the app

User report: queued 4 episodes overnight while device was charging; none finished analyzing.

## Asset-lifecycle log corroborates

Only ONE terminal coverage event between 20:34 and 07:21 — at 07:21:05 AM, a 4482s feature episode reaches full coverage. No intermediate state transitions logged for ~10.5 hours despite the device being plugged in.

## Likely areas

1. **BGTaskScheduler** — submitted tasks not actually running (iOS deferral, expiration, or registration mismatch).
2. **AnalysisCoordinator gate** — scheduler may require `activePlaybackEpisodeId != nil` (gtt9.14 noted this); paused-but-loaded prevents progress, but here the episodes were queued not playing.
3. **Power-source heuristic** — possible inverted condition that pauses on AC vs battery.
4. **Foreground-only path** — analysis pipeline may not actually run in the background.

## Acceptance

- Reproduce the gap on a controlled overnight run (queue N episodes, plug in, leave); confirm scheduler logs match expectation
- Identify root cause (which gate / which scheduler API path)
- File fix bead with proposed change

## Reference

asset-lifecycle-log.jsonl + decision-log.1.jsonl in the bundle linked above.

title: NARL corpus builder: detectOnly + autoSkipEligible must map to isAdUnderDefault=true
description:
## Root cause
NarlEvalCorpusBuilderTests.swift:527-529 derives isAdUnderDefault via substring match on 'autoskip'/'markonly'/'skip'.

```swift
let isAdUnderDefault = action.contains("autoskip")
    || action.contains("markonly")
    || action.contains("skip") && !action.contains("suppress")
```

## Why this is wrong
1. `detectOnly` is a legitimate positive ad determination (SkipPolicyMatrix). For owned/affiliate/unknown-unknown (all common in Conan), the matrix emits detectOnly by design. These are real ad detections the harness silently discards.
2. `autoSkipEligible` already matches the substring check — but the substring is fragile; anything renamed will silently degrade.

## Evidence
Conan 71F0C2AE episode (117 min, 2026-04-24 capture):
- Baseline ads at [0, 29.82] and [5670.6, 5690.52] confidence=1.0 logged as 'detectOnly' → dropped.
- Hot-path [7006, 7008] confidence=0.815 logged as 'hotPathCandidate' (pre-6e37335) → dropped.
- Harness scored GT=3, Pred=0, Sec-F1=0 — the detector actually caught 2 of 3 ads correctly.

## Fix
Switch to an exact-match enumeration against SkipPolicyAction raw values:
- `autoSkipEligible` → true
- `detectOnly` → true
- `logOnly` → false (telemetry only, not a positive)
- `suppress` → false
- `markOnly` (if still emitted anywhere) → true
- hotPath- prefixes other than autoSkipEligible → false

## Acceptance
- Re-run NARL harness against 2026-04-24 fixtures with no other changes.
- Conan 71F0C2AE Sec-F1 rises from 0 to ≥ 0.4.
- ALL-episode default Sec-F1 rises by ≥ 5 points.
- Unit test covers each SkipPolicyAction enum case.

## Parent
Diagnosis: docs/narl/2026-04-24-finding1-conan-classifier-diagnosis.md (investigation/gtt9.18).

title: Investigate classifier+fusion failure on long conversational shows (Finding 1)
description:
## Why
2026-04-24 real-data eval Finding 1: Conan episode 71F0C2AE (117 min, episodeId ...01KM20WJPKVFHRVJZWTNA6Q1XT) completed with terminalReason 'full coverage: transcript 1.000, feature 1.000' — gtt9.1.1 worked, 90s ceiling gone. But harness scored GT=3, Pred=0, Sec-F1=0. Detector missed ALL 3 user-marked ads despite full transcription.

First real measurement of detection quality with transcript coverage as a non-issue. Classifier + promotion + fusion fail on a real 2-hour show. This is the next ceiling — improving acoustic features (gtt9.12) + catalog (gtt9.13) + threshold calibration (gtt9.3) won't move this metric until we understand why no candidates promoted.

## Repro case
- Episode: flightcast:01KM20WJPKVFHRVJZWTNA6Q1XT (Conan 117-min)
- Fixture: PlayheadTests/Fixtures/NarlEval/2026-04-24/71F0C2AE/
- Expected: 3 ad windows
- Actual: 0 AdWindows emitted

## Investigation checklist
1. Replay the fixture; instrument which candidates get built (transcript / acoustic / lexical).
2. Does SlotScoringClassifier see them? What scores does it emit?
3. Do any clear the candidateThreshold (0.35)? continuationThreshold? promotionThreshold (0.40)?
4. If scores are low, is it the MusicBedLevel disconnection surfaced in gtt9.4? Still unwired in production?
5. Check prior ads' lexical / acoustic evidence in fixture — are the signals there at all?
6. If no signals: is the episode simply too conversational for current feature set? (Feeds gtt9.12 priorities.)
7. If signals are there but gated out: where is the gate too strict? (Feeds gtt9.3.)

## Acceptance
- Root-cause diagnosis written to docs/narl/ with fixture evidence.
- Follow-up bead(s) filed for whatever is broken.
- Ideally: hypothesis that can be re-tested against 2026-04-25 or later capture.

title: Wire AdCatalogStore ingress + fusion egress into production
description:
## Why
gtt9.13 shipped AdCatalogStore + AcousticFingerprint + catalogMatch safety signal but the store is never populated and never queried in the hot path. Blocks real-corpus firing-rate validation and gtt9.3 calibration.

## Scope

2. **Egress**: AdDetectionService fusion path queries AdCatalogStore.matches(...) for candidate windows, emits catalog evidence with similarity score, and threads catalogMatchSimilarity into AutoSkipPrecisionGate inputs.
3. Wire RepetitionFingerprint feature (from gtt9.12) to query the catalog.

## Acceptance

- PlayheadFastTests green.

title: Wire AcousticFeaturePipeline into AdDetectionService hot path
description:
## Why
gtt9.12 shipped AcousticFeaturePipeline + 7 features but deferred the hot-path wiring. Features compute nothing in production until called. Blocks gtt9.3 calibration.

## Scope
1. Inject AcousticFeaturePipeline into AdDetectionService.
2. Call the pipeline during hot-path feature computation per window.
3. Feed each feature score into the fusion evidence array with default priors.
4. Verify funnel counters increment in production (extend an integration test).
