title: wire-segment-aggregator-into-production
description:
## Why

gtt9.10 shipped `SegmentAggregator` as a unit-tested state machine but did NOT wire it into production. The aggregator currently produces nothing for the user. Shipping gtt9.10 without wiring wastes the bead's value — window scores continue to flow directly to the promotion gate, and the [0.30, 0.40) evidence that the aggregator was designed to fuse is still being dropped on the floor.

## Goal

Integrate `SegmentAggregator` into the AdDetection pipeline so per-window scores (from Tier 1 gtt9.9 + Tier 2 transcript/FM path) are aggregated into coherent segments before reaching the promotion gate.

## Contract

- Aggregator sits between window scoring and promotion: `windows → aggregator → segments → promotion`
- Existing single-window promotion must still happen for the high-confidence fast path (one `adProbability >= 0.60` window alone can still promote via the pre-existing logic) — aggregator ADDS coverage for low-corroboration cases, doesn't replace existing routes
- Persisted `AdWindow` extents come from the segment, not the individual window, for aggregator-emitted segments (so gtt9.4.1's boundary expansion and this change compose additively)
- Telemetry: distinguish "promoted via single-window path" vs "promoted via aggregator" in evidence-ledger / decision logs for observability

## Acceptance

1. When the pipeline runs on a synthetic episode with the DF5C1832-equivalent pattern (two sub-threshold spikes 64s apart), exactly one `AdWindow` is persisted covering the segment span — not two separate 1-s windows
2. When the pipeline runs on a single high-confidence window (0.85, isolated), an `AdWindow` is still persisted (fast path preserved)
3. When the pipeline runs on the C22D6EC6-equivalent pattern (single 0.597 window alone), NO `AdWindow` is persisted (single borderline spike doesn't escalate)
4. `PlayheadFastTests` passes with no regression
5. Existing corpus of Tier-2 tests still green — aggregator doesn't break the transcript-refined path

## Scope guardrails

- Do NOT calibrate thresholds (gtt9.3's job)
- Do NOT split auto-skip from detection (gtt9.11)
- Do NOT modify `SegmentAggregator` internals — only wire the existing API
- Do NOT touch boundary expansion (gtt9.4.1) — segments and boundary expansion should compose independently

## Source

Flagged by gtt9.10 agent's GREEN ship report, 2026-04-24: "The aggregator is not yet wired into production. The bead is explicit: this lands the state machine with unit tests; integration into AdDetectionOrchestrator / promotion gate is a separate follow-up."
close_reason: Wired SegmentAggregator hysteresis state machine into AdDetectionService production hot path. Additive to single-window promotion; distinguishing boundaryState (.segmentAggregated) and decision-log action (segmentAggregatorPromoted). 4 RED-then-GREEN wiring tests + fast suite (3960/3960) green. Scope guardrails honored.

title: narl-corpus-backfill-historical-lifecycle
description:
## Goal
Shrink the 54 "unknown" bucket in NARL pipeline-coverage rollups by re-running the corpus builder against historical capture sessions where `asset-lifecycle-log.jsonl` already exists, so their FrozenTrace fixtures get populated with the 5 lifecycle fields (terminalReason, analysisState, durationSec, fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime, featureCoverageEndTime).

## Context
gtt9.15 added pipeline-coverage bucketing to the NARL harness. Fixtures generated before gtt9.8-corpus-thread landed lack lifecycle fields and classify as `unknown`. As of 2026-04-24 that's 54 of 58 traces.

Some of those pre-gtt9.8 captures do have `asset-lifecycle-log.jsonl` on disk under `.captures/*/com.playhead.app*.xcappdata/` — the corpus builder just didn't thread the fields at build time. Re-running the builder against those bundles should backfill the fixtures.

## Scope
- Identify which historical capture bundles have `asset-lifecycle-log.jsonl` populated
- Re-run `NarlEvalCorpusBuilder` against them (or the subset that still matches a fixture by assetId)
- Commit regenerated FrozenTrace JSON so `unknown` shrinks into `scoringLimited` / `pipelineCoverageLimited`
- Expected to be a one-shot data regeneration; no product code change

## Out of scope
- Capturing new sessions
- Classifier/promotion work (that's gtt9.4 family)

## Success
- Next NARL eval run shows materially fewer `unknown` traces, with the shifts landing in the right buckets
- No regression in Sec-F1 / AutoSkip numbers (since ground truth doesn't change)

## Source
Flagged as follow-up #2 from gtt9.15 GREEN report, 2026-04-24.
close_reason: Infeasible: data audit found 16 of 19 historical asset IDs have no lifecycle telemetry in any capture bundle (JSONL or SQLite). Only 3 assets recoverable (34C7E7CF and 71F0C2AE already populated by gtt9.15; AA8DCCA6 has partial sqlite data but builder deliberately avoids sqlite). Bucket count goes 54 -> 51 at best — not material vs <10 goal. Findings doc at docs/narl/2026-04-24-pc0t-backfill-audit.md. Recommendation: let new dogfood captures naturally replace the prior via regular test cycles, or delete pre-gtt9.8 fixture dirs if visual noise becomes actionable (separate policy call).

title: Post-classify boundary expansion for high-confidence classifier windows
description:
## Problem

Captured by gtt9.4 follow-up spike (2026-04-24) on episode 71F0C2AE (Conan, 117 min):

- Classifier scored only 6 distinct windows in a 117-min episode (it runs only on `LexicalCandidate`s, not as a sweep).
- For the GT ad span [7007.34, 7037.34] (30 s), only [7006, 7008] (a 2-s lexical hit) was scored — at adProbability 0.815.
- Even with the 6e37335 labelling fix (autoSkipEligible promotion) and a4ea4ca seeding fix shipped in this build, the **persisted AdWindow span remains ~2 s wide vs a 30 s GT ad** → Sec-F1 ≈ 0.04, near-miss.

## Proposed fix

When the classifier returns `adProbability >= autoSkipConfidenceThreshold` (default 0.80) on a `LexicalCandidate` of duration shorter than `priors.typicalAdDuration / 2`, expand the persisted `AdWindow.[startTime, endTime]` (NOT the classifier candidate, NOT the score) outward to the nearest `AcousticBreak` within `BoundaryExpander.ExpansionConfig.neutral` radii (or to `priors.typicalAdDuration` extent as fallback).

Two reasonable scope options:
1. **Surface fix only**: expand the persisted AdWindow extents at AdWindow construction time. Doesn't change scoring, doesn't re-score, doesn't change ledger. Just makes the persisted span match where the ad actually is in audio.
2. **Re-score + expand**: classify the expanded span as a second pass to confirm.

Start with (1) — cheaper, lower risk, and validated against the 71F0C2AE 7006-7037 case directly.

## Acceptance

- A new test: given a synthesized ClassifierResult with adProbability 0.85 on a 2-s candidate inside a 30-s acoustic-break envelope, the resulting persisted `AdWindow` spans the full envelope.
- Re-running the harness on a fresh capture of 71F0C2AE shows Sec-F1 > 0.5 for that episode (currently 0).

## Reference

- Spike notes appended to playhead-gtt9.4 (2026-04-24 follow-up section).
- Fixture: `PlayheadTests/Fixtures/NarlEval/2026-04-24/FrozenTrace-71F0C2AE-7260-4D1E-B41A-BCFD5103A641.json`
- Code touchpoints: `Playhead/Services/AdDetection/AdDetectionService.swift:2858` (`buildAdWindow`), `BoundaryExpander.swift` (existing radii consts).
close_reason: Shipped post-classify boundary expansion (merge d3bb935). High-confidence (>=0.80) narrow classifier hits now expand persisted AdWindow extents to nearest AcousticBreak within BoundaryExpander.ExpansionConfig.neutral radii, with fallback to priors.typicalAdDuration.lowerBound/2 per side. Does not re-score, does not touch classifier score, does not modify ledger beyond persistence. 4 helper tests green + full PlayheadFastTests plan green (4530 passed, 9 skipped).

title: Pull-to-refresh on per-show episode list
description:
LibraryView (the grid of shows) has pull-to-refresh via .refreshable { await refreshAllFeeds() }. But EpisodeListView (the per-show episode list the user scrolls to find unplayed episodes) has NO .refreshable modifier, so the user cannot refresh a single show's feed from its own screen — they must navigate back to Library and pull-to-refresh the entire grid.

Fix: add .refreshable on the EpisodeListView's scroll container that calls discoveryService.refreshEpisodes(for: podcast, in: modelContext). Mirror the LibraryView.refreshAllFeeds pattern (silent partial-refresh tolerance). Tiny scope.
acceptance_criteria:
1. EpisodeListView has .refreshable modifier on its scrollable list.
2. Pull-to-refresh triggers discoveryService.refreshEpisodes(for: podcast, in: modelContext).
3. New episodes discovered by refresh appear in the list without a reload.
4. Errors are swallowed silently (match LibraryView pattern).
5. Unit/snapshot test verifies the modifier is present and fires refreshEpisodes exactly once per pull.
close_reason: Landed in merge 15aceda, pushed to origin/main. All 5 pull-to-refresh tests green.

title: Background feed refresh for new episodes
description:
App currently has no automatic way to discover new episodes. The only refresh path is user-initiated pull-to-refresh on LibraryView. This makes the 'auto-download next N on subscribe' feature (AutoDownloadOnSubscribe in SettingsL274) effectively one-shot — new episodes published after the initial subscribe are never detected or downloaded until the user manually refreshes.

Fix: register a BGAppRefreshTask at launch that periodically calls discoveryService.refreshEpisodes(for:in:) across all subscribed podcasts, then feeds newly-discovered episodes into the existing auto-download path. Task identifier pattern follows existing BackgroundProcessingService convention. iOS schedules the cadence; we request a minimum interval (e.g. 1-2h).
acceptance_criteria:
1. BGTaskScheduler registered at launch for a new bg-refresh identifier.
2. Handler iterates subscribed podcasts, calls refreshEpisodes for each, and triggers auto-download for new episodes when AutoDownloadOnSubscribe is enabled.
3. Next refresh re-scheduled at handler end (even on cancel).
4. Unit tests cover: handler iterates podcasts; handler schedules next refresh; handler respects user's AutoDownloadOnSubscribe setting.
5. UIBackgroundModes updated in Info.plist to include 'fetch' (or equivalent for BGAppRefreshTask) if not already present.
6. Does NOT collide with existing BGProcessingTask identifiers.
close_reason: Landed in 5463918. BGAppRefreshTask com.playhead.app.feed-refresh drives periodic feed refresh + auto-download when enabled. Review added idempotent completeTaskOnce so expiration-path setTaskCompleted (iOS contract) can't race with normal-exit path; +1 regression test.

title: Scene-phase + playback-state aware analysis scheduling
description:
## Why

`AnalysisWorkScheduler` currently blocks deferred work whenever `activePlaybackEpisodeId != nil` — i.e., whenever *any* episode is loaded, regardless of whether it's playing, paused, or idle. This conflates "user cares about this episode" with "scheduler must not run deferred work," which is backwards for foreground-paused.

Scene phase is also invisible to the analysis pipeline. Only `PlayheadApp.swift:9/171-188` observes `scenePhase`, and it's used only to persist playback position. `AnalysisWorkScheduler` / `AnalysisCoordinator` / `BackgroundProcessingService` have zero awareness of foreground vs background.

Concrete symptom from 2026-04-23 real-data eval (`docs/narl/2026-04-23-real-data-findings.md`):
- Asset `DF5C1832` (4262s episode) got feature/transcript coverage to 1619s, then stopped.
- Most plausible explanation: user played ~27 min, paused, episode stayed active → scheduler blocked deferred work thereafter.
- 9.8's `terminalReason` telemetry on the next capture will confirm whether paused-with-episode-loaded is a common real-user stall reason.

## Current state (from investigation 2026-04-23)

The scheduler distinguishes:
- Is an episode active? (`activePlaybackEpisodeId != nil`)
- Device thermal state (`QualityProfile`)

It does NOT distinguish:
- `PlaybackState.Status` (`.playing` vs `.paused` vs `.idle`)
- `scenePhase` (`.active` / `.inactive` / `.background`)

State matrix today:
| State | Thermal gate | T0 eligible | Deferred eligible |
|---|---|---|---|
| foreground + playing | `.critical` pauses | yes | NO (episode active) |
| foreground + paused | `.critical` pauses | yes | **NO (episode active — wrong!)** |
| foreground + idle (no episode) | `.critical` pauses | n/a | yes |
| background | `.fair` / `.serious` pauses progressively | yes | yes |

Foreground-paused should be the *most aggressive* mode (device awake, user engaged, no OS time limit, audio idle).

## Proposal

Extend the scheduler with two new signals and a richer admission filter:

1. **Add `playbackContext` enum** — `playing` | `paused` | `idle` — threaded from `PlaybackState.Status` into `QualityProfile` or the scheduler directly.
2. **Add `scenePhase` signal** — observe SwiftUI `scenePhase` in `PlayheadRuntime` and forward into `AnalysisWorkScheduler`.
3. **Refine admission filter** at `AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:818` (current `if activePlaybackEpisodeId != nil { continue }`):
   - `foreground && playing` → current behavior (block deferred, drain T0 only)
   - `foreground && paused` → **unblock deferred; allow full concurrency; permit `.serious` thermal** (more aggressive than background)
   - `foreground && idle` → same as foreground-paused
   - `background` → current behavior (OS-scheduled window, current thermal gates)
4. **Optional (consider)**: tune `QualityProfile.schedulerPolicy` slices per state. Foreground-paused could run at 100% of Now+Soon lanes simultaneously.

## Acceptance

1. New signals observable in `AnalysisWorkScheduler`: `playbackContext`, `scenePhase`.
2. Admission filter differentiates the four states above; unit tests cover each transition.
3. `QualityProfile` or equivalent emits a distinct policy for foreground-paused.
4. When user pauses a loaded episode while app is foregrounded, deferred transcript / feature work resumes within one scheduler tick.
5. No regression in thermal protection — `.critical` still pauses everything in all states.
6. `AssetLifecycleLogger` (gtt9.8) records scheduler state on chunk-start events so we can observe the distribution empirically post-ship.

## Related

- Depends on: gtt9.8 (landed) — telemetry to diagnose real stalls and validate fix post-ship.
- Pairs with next dogfood capture.
- Corrects the incorrect claim in `docs/narl/2026-04-23-real-data-findings.md` that "Lane A gates on `status == .playing`" — it actually gates on episode presence.

## Investigation references (2026-04-23)

- `Playhead/Services/PreAnalysis/AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:209` — `activePlaybackEpisodeId`
- `Playhead/Services/PreAnalysis/AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:818` — blocking filter
- `Playhead/App/PlayheadApp.swift:9,171-188` — only `scenePhase` consumer today (UI-only)
- `Playhead/Services/PlaybackTransport/PlaybackTransport.swift` — `PlaybackState.Status` enum
- `Playhead/App/PlayheadRuntime.swift:755` — where `timeUpdate` events already flow; natural point to also forward status+phase

title: Segment-level candidate aggregator with hysteresis
description:
## Why

Per the 2026-04-23 expert review (§4): several real-data FNs are one-second scored windows *inside* much longer user-marked ad spans. The pipeline makes local window decisions but doesn't assemble them into coherent ad segments. Current confidence mode is `[0.30, 0.40)` — lots of evidence sitting just below the nominal 0.40 action threshold, individually inconclusive but collectively strong.

## Scope

Introduce a segment-level state machine that sits between per-window scores and the promotion gate:

```
window scores → candidate run → merged segment → promotion gate
```

Logic:

```
Start segment when:
  score >= candidateThreshold for N nearby windows
  OR score >= highConfidenceThreshold once
Continue while:
  score >= continuationThreshold
  OR gap <= maxInternalGapSeconds
End when:
  score < continuationThreshold for M seconds
Promote when:
  segmentScore >= promotionThreshold
  AND duration >= minAdDuration
  AND safety signals pass (see gtt9.11)
```

Hysteresis starting points (calibrate in gtt9.3 after gtt9.6 eval lands):

```
candidateThreshold   = 0.35
continuationThreshold = 0.28
promotionThreshold   = 0.40  (keep current)
```

## Acceptance

1. New `SegmentAggregator` component consumes window scores and emits merged candidate/promoted segments.
2. `segmentScore` uses a defensible aggregation (e.g., duration-weighted mean with time-decay) — document the choice.
3. Re-running on the 2026-04-23 DF5C1832 asset: the [1612,1613] @ 0.45 and [1676,1677] @ 0.46 windows now participate in coherent segments that cover the user-marked FN spans.
4. No regression on C22D6EC6 (the 0.597 window in a user-marked FP region must still not promote).

## Related

- Depends on: gtt9.9 (feature-only path gives the aggregator a complete window stream).
- Pairs with: gtt9.2 (promotion reject reasons) — aggregator may itself emit reasons like `segmentDurationBelowMin`.
- Pairs with: gtt9.11 (split detection/auto-skip) — segment score feeds both layers.
close_reason: Shipped: SegmentAggregator hysteresis state machine with duration-weighted-mean segmentScore; DF5C1832 FN shape coalesces into one segment, C22D6EC6 lone 0.597 window does not promote; 13 new tests green, full fast plan TEST SUCCEEDED

title: Full-audio feature-only scoring path (decouple scoring from transcript progress)
description:
## Why

Per the 2026-04-23 expert review (§2): **ad detection should have a feature-only baseline path that scans the whole episode using cheap local signals**, rather than depending on transcript progress to decide whether a region gets scored at all.

On the 2026-04-23 capture, 13 of 21 user-confirmed ad spans had zero scored windows because transcript coverage stopped at 90s. Even if the transcript-coverage bug (gtt9.1.1, gtt9.8) is fully fixed, **long-form content will always have regions where transcript is slow or unavailable**; the detector should still score them.

## Scope

Introduce a two-tier scoring architecture:

```
Tier 1 — full-audio cheap pass (always covers whole episode)
  ├─ classifier score (already runs per window)
  ├─ acoustic features (gtt9.12 expanded set)
  ├─ boundary / change-point detection
  └─ metadata time-position prior (pre/mid/post-roll)

Tier 2 — expensive refinement (scoped by Tier 1 candidates)
  ├─ transcript lexical pass
  ├─ FM classification
  ├─ catalog matching
  └─ promotion decision
```

Key contract: **Tier 1 emits decisions for every episode second regardless of transcript state.** Transcript refinement is Tier 2 and modifies scores, never gates whether a region is evaluated.

## Acceptance

1. `scoredCoverageRatio` (gtt9.6) ≥ 0.95 on every downloadable episode, even when transcript coverage is 0%.
2. A deliberately transcript-disabled run still produces `hotPathCandidate`-or-above windows in plausible pre/mid/post-roll positions.
3. Tier 2 still fires when transcript is available; detection quality does not regress on the fast-track cases.

## Related

- Depends on: gtt9.8 (coverage contract + telemetry).
- Blocks: gtt9.11 (split detection/auto-skip needs a reliable candidate stream).
- Complemented by: gtt9.12 (acoustic features give Tier 1 something to stand on).
close_reason: Tier 1 transcript-independent feature-only scoring landed. Stage 4 now emits a scored DecisionLogEntry for every non-overlapping 30s slot across the full episode regardless of transcript state. Tested: 4 new tests in Tier1FeatureOnlyScoringTests (100% coverage on empty-transcript episodes, hotPathCandidate/autoSkipEligible at plausible pre/mid/post-roll, Tier 2 does not remove Tier 1 entries, runHotPath with empty chunks still emits Tier 1 entries). Full PlayheadFastTests green: 4,488 passed, 0 failed, 9 skipped. Merge e1d41fc on main. Unblocks gtt9.10 (SegmentAggregator). Followup: gtt9.10 aggregator should consume Tier 1 + Tier 2 decision-log entries into coherent spans; gtt9.3 can now tune thresholds against real full-coverage data; gtt9.11 auto-skip eligibility gate remains sole skip authority.

title: analysisState contract + per-asset/per-job coverage telemetry
description:
## Why

gtt9.1.1 fixed the specific `activeShards` rehydration bug that let 4 assets be stamped `.complete` with 90s of transcript covering hours of audio. Per the 2026-04-23 expert review (§1), that bug was a symptom of a broader architectural gap: **`analysisState = .complete` today doesn't actually contract that scoring, decisions, or transcript finished.**

This bead delivers the coverage contract + telemetry the expert recommends.

## Scope

### Expand the `analysisState` enum

Replace the monolithic `.complete` with explicit terminal states:

```
completeFull             // feature + transcript + decisions all covered
completeFeatureOnly      // feature covered, transcript never advanced
completeTranscriptPartial // transcript-dependent sources partial
failedTranscript
failedFeature
cancelledBudget
waitingForBackfill
```

Invariant: `completeFull` requires feature-scored range, decision windows emitted over it, AND transcript either complete or explicitly marked partial/unavailable.

### Per-asset coverage telemetry

On every finalize, log (persist to `analysis_assets` + emit to decision log):

```json
{
  "assetId": "...",
  "audioDuration": 7036,
  "featureCoverageEnd": 7036,
  "transcriptCoverageEnd": 90,
  "scoredCoverageEnd": 90,
  "analysisState": "completeTranscriptPartial",
  "terminalReason": "transcriptionBudgetExceeded",
  "unscoredRanges": [[90, 7036]]
}
```

### Per-job telemetry

Every transcript/scoring chunk lifecycle event logs:

```json
{
  "assetId": "...",
  "chunkStart": 90,
  "chunkEnd": 180,
  "jobState": "cancelled",
  "reason": "budgetLimit | appBackgrounded | timeout | noAudio | speechUnavailable | unknown"
}
```

Turn "coverage mysteriously stopped" into a specific `terminalReason`.

### Investigation targets

- Search codebase for any other hard caps near 90 / preview / headOnly / firstChunk / initialWindow paths that could silently truncate long-form.
- Verify the fast-pass + backfill state machine can emit each new state.

## Acceptance

1. New `analysisState` enum with distinguishable terminal reasons.
2. Per-asset telemetry persisted and queryable by harness.
3. Per-job telemetry surfaced in decision log or a new lifecycle log.
4. Harness can compute `scoredCoverageRatio` (gtt9.6 metric) directly from telemetry.
5. No asset can reach `completeFull` unless the coverage invariant passes.

## Related

- Depends on: gtt9.1.1 (already landed).
- Blocks: gtt9.6 (metric split consumes this telemetry), gtt9.9 (feature-only path needs this state machine).

title: Normalize user corrections before use as ground truth
description:
## Why

Per the 2026-04-23 expert review (§11): the correction set mixes whole-asset toggles, span-level FPs, and span-level FNs. **9 of 10 "FP corrections" are whole-asset manual vetoes, not span-level FPs.** Feeding these raw into eval or training yields garbage numbers.

Pairs with gtt9.6 (eval metric split): together they make the GT side of NARL evaluation trustworthy.

## Scope

Introduce a correction-normalization pass that runs before the harness consumes `corpus-export.*.jsonl`:

1. **Separate correction types.** Tag each correction as `wholeAsset` / `spanFN` / `spanFP` / `unknown`.
2. **Merge adjacent FN spans.** Adjacent (gap ≤ 5 s) FN spans on the same asset collapse into one span.
3. **Deduplicate.** Identical corrections (same asset + same span type + same ~time) count once.
4. **Preserve uncertainty.** When correction type is genuinely ambiguous, keep an `unknown` bucket and exclude from precision/recall.
5. **Handle whole-asset vetoes properly.** Exclude from span-level precision/recall unless explicitly converted (e.g., whole-episode FP → synthesized span covering whole episode).

## Acceptance

1. New `CorrectionNormalizer` (Swift or harness-side Python) produces a normalized view of the correction corpus.
2. Harness consumes normalized corrections; eval metrics change in predictable ways (FP counts drop because whole-asset vetoes no longer inflate per-span FPs).
3. Per-asset correction counts before/after normalization logged in the report so we can see the delta.

## Related

- Blocks: gtt9.3 (PriorShift retune).
- Paired with gtt9.6.

title: Fix: persist episodeDuration + fail-safe unknown-duration coverage-guard shortcuts
description:
## Problem

Per the investigation under `playhead-gtt9.1`: the coverage guard in `AnalysisCoordinator` silently bypasses the 95%-transcript-coverage check when `currentEpisodeDuration()` returns 0 (which happens on any resume-from-persisted-`.backfill` path, because `activeShards` is only written during `spool` and is never rehydrated). Result: assets get stamped `analysisState='complete'` with only the T0 tier's 90s of fast-pass transcript and zero final-pass coverage.

**Full diagnosis:** `playhead-gtt9.1` notes.

## Fix — Option B + C together

### Option B — persist episode duration on the asset row

Make the asset's total duration a durable field on the `analysis_assets` SQLite row, written at `spool` time when the audio is decoded. Have `currentEpisodeDuration()` fall back to this persisted value when `activeShards == nil`.

Concrete changes:
- Add `episodeDurationSec: Double?` column to `analysis_assets` (plus migration).
- In `AnalysisCoordinator` spool path, after `activeShards = shards` and before `runFromFeaturesReady`, persist: `store.updateEpisodeDuration(assetId, totalAudio)` where `totalAudio = shards.map(\.duration).reduce(0, +)`.
- Rewrite `currentEpisodeDuration()` to consult `activeShards` first; fall back to a cached copy of the persisted asset's `episodeDurationSec`; finally fall back to 0.
- On resume-from-backfill paths, load the asset row first so the cached value is populated before the guards run.

### Option C — fail-safe unknown-duration shortcuts

In `AnalysisCoordinator.swift`:
- `finalizeBackfillVerdict` line 1706: change `guard episodeDuration > 0 else { return .allowComplete }` to `.blockComplete(coverageEnd: chunks.map(\.endTime).max() ?? 0, episodeDuration: 0, ratio: 0)`. Pick a sentinel for the ratio field or refactor the enum to represent unknown-duration explicitly.
- `resumeBackfillDecision` line 1756: change `guard episodeDuration > 0 else { return .finalize }` to `return .restart`.

When even the persisted duration is missing, "restart" is the safe fallback (the pipeline re-decodes and re-populates `activeShards`).

## TDD plan

Write tests FIRST, watch them fail, then implement.

### Test 1 — finalizeBackfillVerdict unknown-duration fails safe
Pure-function test in `AnalysisCoordinatorTests` (or similar existing file):
```swift
@Test("finalizeBackfillVerdict blocks complete when episodeDuration is 0")
func test_unknownDurationBlocks() {
    let chunks = [makeTranscriptChunk(pass: "fast", startTime: 0, endTime: 90)]
    let verdict = AnalysisCoordinator.finalizeBackfillVerdict(chunks: chunks, episodeDuration: 0)
    #expect(verdict != .allowComplete)
}
```

### Test 2 — resumeBackfillDecision unknown-duration restarts
```swift
@Test("resumeBackfillDecision restarts when episodeDuration is 0")
func test_resumeUnknownDurationRestarts() {
    let chunks = [makeTranscriptChunk(pass: "fast", startTime: 0, endTime: 90)]
    #expect(AnalysisCoordinator.resumeBackfillDecision(chunks: chunks, episodeDuration: 0) == .restart)
}
```

### Test 3 — currentEpisodeDuration falls back to persisted value
Integration-style test with a stubbed `AnalysisStore` returning a persisted `episodeDurationSec`:
- activeShards = nil
- store returns asset with episodeDurationSec = 1800
- Assert `currentEpisodeDuration()` returns 1800

### Test 4 — end-to-end: resume-from-backfill with stale fast-pass doesn't stamp .complete
Existing `CoverageGuardRecoveryTests.swift` has the right shape. Add:
- Seed asset with fastCov=90, featCov=1800, persisted duration=1800, 3 fast chunks covering 0-90s, session state=`.backfill`
- Clear `activeShards`
- Kick runFromBackfill
- Assert session transitions to `.failed` (with coverage-guard reason), NOT `.complete`

### Test 5 — normal spool path persists duration
Integration test: spool → assert `analysis_assets.episodeDurationSec` equals the sum of shard durations.

## Acceptance

- All 5 tests pass (red → green → refactor).
- `PlayheadFastTests` test plan fully green.
- `bd close playhead-gtt9.1.fix` only after PR merge and disk cleanup per CLAUDE.md.
- Manual-verification step: re-build and sanity-check against the existing 2026-04-23 bundle — the re-analysis should transition the affected assets to `.failed` on the next coordinator run (not silently stay `.complete`).

## Reference

- Diagnosis: `playhead-gtt9.1` (notes)
- Full writeup: `/Users/dabrams/playhead/docs/narl/2026-04-23-real-data-findings.md`
- Expert report: `/Users/dabrams/playhead/docs/narl/2026-04-23-expert-report.md`

title: Instrument promotionRejectReasons — explain every non-promotion
description:
## Problem

Across 147 real-data scored windows (2026-04-23 capture), **41 reached `hotPathCandidate` but only 3 ever reached `autoSkipEligible`**. All 3 promoted windows had `fusedConfidence=1.000`. No window in the half-open band `(0.40, 0.999)` was ever promoted — even though the nominal classifier promotion threshold is 0.40.

Two DF5C1832 windows @ 0.45 and 0.46 overlap user-confirmed ad spans and never escalate. A C22D6EC6 window @ 0.597 correctly holds because it overlaps a user-marked FP. **Promotion behaviour is context-dependent — we cannot tell if the current gating is intentionally conservative or accidentally requires near-certainty.**

## Scope (post expert review — 2026-04-23)

**Do NOT lower the 0.40 threshold.** The correct fix is to make every non-promotion *explainable*, so we can distinguish intentional selectivity from a bug before touching the gate logic.

Per the expert review (`docs/narl/2026-04-23-expert-response.md` §3):

For each candidate window that could have been promoted but wasn't, record structured rejection reasons in the decision log:

```json
{
  "window": [1612, 1613],
  "skipConfidence": 0.45,
  "nominalPromotionThreshold": 0.40,
  "promotionEligible": false,
  "promotionRejectReasons": [
    "insufficientSegmentDuration",
    "missingTranscriptAnchor",
    "noEvidenceDiversity",
    "cooldownActive"
  ]
}
```

Enumerate every branch in the promotion pipeline that can cause a non-promotion:
- `belowConfidenceThreshold`
- `insufficientDuration`
- `insufficientHotPathStreak`
- `missingTranscriptAnchor`
- `missingAcousticSupport`
- `missingMetadataSupport`
- `cooldownActive`
- `nearManualVeto`
- `wholeAssetVetoed`
- `insideKnownFalsePositiveRegion`
- `lowCoverage`
- `sourceUnavailable`

Every existing `return`/`continue`/`guard` in the promotion path should emit one of these reasons.

## Acceptance

1. Every `hotPathCandidate` window above `nominalPromotionThreshold` has at least one `promotionRejectReasons` entry when it fails to promote.
2. Entries are persisted to the decision log alongside the confidence + evidence breakdown.
3. Re-running the NARL eval on the 2026-04-23 capture explains the DF5C1832 0.45/0.46 misses with specific reason(s) — not just "below 1.0 fused confidence".
4. The C22D6EC6 0.597 counter-case surfaces the same or a different reason — we can compare and confirm the gate is doing the right thing for that case.

## Out of scope

- Changing the threshold itself (any re-tune belongs in gtt9.3).
- Segment-level aggregation (that's gtt9.8).
- Anchor-density (gtt9.4 — relates to *why* multi-source windows never form in the first place, a separate root cause).

## Related

- Supersedes closure note that rolled this up into gtt9.4. Anchor-density is still a real issue, but the expert review reframes this bead as a prerequisite for trustworthy tuning.
- Pairs with gtt9.4 (source funnel): once we know *why* non-promotion happens per window, we can see whether the cause is source-silence (→ 9.4) or gate-logic (→ this bead).
notes:
**Full writeup:** `/Users/dabrams/playhead/docs/narl/2026-04-23-real-data-findings.md` — Finding 2

## 2026-04-23 Investigation findings

The "promotion gap" as originally framed does not exist. It's a two-phase architecture working as designed; the user-visible symptom (ads missed despite decent classifier confidence) has a different root cause. Recommendation: close this bead as "explained / subsumed" and hand the symptom to `playhead-gtt9.4`.

### Architecture (design, not bug)

**Hot-path (`AdDetectionService.emitHotPathDecisionLogs`, ~line 2732):**
- Runs during fast-pass chunk arrival
- Classifier-only evidence (pre-fusion)
- Emits `hotPathCandidate` as a *flag*, never `autoSkipEligible`
- Purpose: drive real-time skip banners/cues; it's log-only for detection

**Backfill (`AdDetectionService.runBackfill`, ~lines 715-1092):**
- Runs on `.completed` via `AnalysisCoordinator.finalizeBackfill`
- Generates fusion windows via `RegionShadowPhase.run` → `RegionProposalBuilder.build` → `AtomEvidenceProjector.project` → `MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder.decode`
- Window candidates are formed from **anchored atoms**: atoms anchored by FM consensus (strength ≥ .medium), lexical patterns (url, promoCode, disclosurePhrase, ctaPhrase — `AtomEvidenceProjector.swift:32-34`), acoustic breaks, or Use-C corroboration (single-window FM + nearby acoustic)
- Per-fusion-window `decisionLogger.record(logEntry)` writes the multi-source decision-log entry
- Only this phase can emit `autoSkipEligible`

### Data confirms the architecture

| Action | Windows | Sources |
|---|---:|---|
| hotPathBelowThreshold | 101 | classifier-only |
| hotPathCandidate | 41 | classifier-only |
| autoSkipEligible | 3 | 4–6 sources (all contain `metadata` with authority=strong) |
| detectOnly | 2 | 5 sources |

All 41 hotPathCandidates are pre-fusion classifier-only logs. They were never *candidates for promotion* — they're telemetry of where the classifier fired. Promotion is a separate backfill-only decision.

### The real symptom: anchor sparsity in backfill

For DF5C1832 (72-minute DoaC episode):
- 7 user-confirmed FN ad spans
- **1** backfill fusion window ([1609.62, 1619.28], autoSkipEligible, conf=1.000)
- **6 of 7 FN spans have zero overlapping backfill window** — they were never considered for fusion at all

Corpus-wide: 5 of 147 decision-log rows are multi-source (3.4%). The fusion pipeline produces ~5 windows across 16 assets — far below what you'd expect if it scored every segment.

### Why so few fusion windows

Per the code trace: backfill's window set comes from the span decoder applied to **anchored atoms**. If a region has no lexical ad-marker (url, promo code, disclosure phrase, CTA phrase), no FM consensus hit, and no acoustic break, the decoder forms no candidate span there, and the fusion loop never runs on it.

The 6 missed DF5C1832 FN spans all lack these anchors in the transcript/audio. This is gtt9.4's territory:

- Lexical firing: 5 of 147 windows (3%) — patterns probably too narrow
- FM firing: 2 of 147 (1%) — scheduling/cooldown likely very conservative
- Acoustic firing: 3 of 147 (2%) — MusicBedLevel etc. underutilized
- Metadata firing: 5 of 147 (3%)

### Re-examined claim on DF5C1832 [1612, 1613] @ 0.451

The original framing said this hotPathCandidate "should have promoted." Incorrect: there is no path by which a hot-path entry promotes. However, the backfill DID promote a *broader* window [1609.62, 1619.28] that overlaps this one. So for THIS span, the system actually worked — an ad was caught. The promoted window just has different bounds than the hot-path log entry because backfill's decoder snaps to acoustic/atom boundaries.

### Re-examined claim on DF5C1832 [1676, 1677] @ 0.456

No overlapping backfill window exists. This FN span [1624.3, 1688.6] was missed by backfill — root cause: no anchor atoms in that region. This is an anchor-density / evidence-fusion problem (gtt9.4), not a promotion problem.

### Re-examined claim on C22D6EC6 [74, 83.4] @ 0.597

Correctly held at `hotPathCandidate` because the user marked [77.1, 85.0] as a falsePositive. If this had an auto-promote-classifier-only path, it would have become an FP. Current architecture is conservative here in a way the user prefers.

### Recommendation

**Close gtt9.2 as "explained — rolls up to gtt9.4."** Three justifications:

1. The architecture is intentional. Adding a classifier-only auto-promotion path is high-risk (C22D6EC6 case shows the FP hazard).
2. The symptom (missed FN ads on DF5C1832 etc.) has a different root cause: backfill's anchor-gated window generation. That belongs to gtt9.4 (evidence-source firing rates), which should be re-scoped to "anchor-atom density in backfill fusion."
3. Fixing gtt9.4 (more/better anchors) automatically exercises the existing promotion path correctly — no change needed to the promotion gate.

### File:line citations

- `Playhead/Services/AdDetection/AdDetectionService.swift:2732` — hot-path log emit (classifier-only)
- `Playhead/Services/AdDetection/AdDetectionService.swift:715-1092` — backfill window generation + fusion loop
- `Playhead/Services/AdDetection/AdDetectionService.swift:1070-1092` — per-window multi-source log write
- `Playhead/Services/AdDetection/RegionShadowPhase.swift:154` — RegionProposalBuilder.build entry
- `Playhead/Services/AdDetection/RegionProposalBuilder.swift:107-115` — the five proposal sources (lexical/FM/sponsor/fingerprint/acoustic)
- `Playhead/Services/AdDetection/AtomEvidenceProjector.swift:32-34, 82-92` — atom anchoring rules
- `Playhead/Services/AdDetection/MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder.swift:66-191` — span decoder (only anchored atoms form runs)
[2026-04-23] Closed pre-instrumentation based on source grep — the expert review's "instrument first" recommendation turned out to be answerable directly from the code.

Root cause of the 1.0 cliff:
- Promotion site: Playhead/Services/AdDetection/AdDetectionService.swift:995-1007. Requires all of: (1) raw policy ∈ {detectOnly, logOnly}, (2) eligibilityGate == .eligible, (3) finite skipConfidence, (4) skipConfidence >= autoSkipConfidenceThreshold (default 0.80, not 0.40).
- Real blocker: Playhead/Services/AdDetection/BackfillEvidenceFusion.swift:452-471 — blockedByEvidenceQuorum. FM-consensus path requires distinctKinds.count >= 2 (multi-source corroboration), duration ∈ [5, 180]s, transcript quality == .good. FM-acoustic path needs external corroboration from a non-FM source. Metadata-only cannot skip alone.

The (0.40, 0.999) band doesn't fail a threshold check — it fails the evidence-quorum gate before ever reaching the 0.80 promotion threshold. The 1.0 cliff is emergent: only windows where multiple sources agree can both clear quorum and hit 0.80. No literal >= 1.0 anywhere in the path.

Why this is not a bug. The quorum gate is working as designed — conservative, prefers holding over auto-skipping single-source evidence. The "41 hotPathCandidate → 3 autoSkipEligible" numbers are an artifact of the 2026-04-23 capture's coverage bottleneck (Finding 1 / gtt9.1): most windows lack transcript coverage, so lexical/fm/catalog evidence can't fire, so single-source classifier hits are the only signal, so quorum correctly rejects them.

What replaces this bead. gtt9.6 landed coverage + FN-decomposition metrics that split unscoredFN from classifierFN from promotionFN. Once gtt9.8 tightens transcript-coverage, the promotionFN number on transcript-covered windows will tell us directly whether the quorum gate is starving real promotions. If it is, open a new bead to debate loosening quorum (e.g., allow classifier >= 0.90 alone on transcript-covered good-quality windows). Until then, don't touch the gate.

title: Investigate why fastTranscriptCoverage maxes at 90s on assets marked 'complete'
description:
**Source:** 2026-04-23 real-data eval (parent playhead-gtt9).

**Observed:** In the exported analysis.sqlite from the 2026-04-23 capture, four episodes are marked `analysisState='complete'` yet have `fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime=90` despite `featureCoverageEndTime` in the 1800–7000s range:

| assetId | episodeId_tail | fastTxCov | featCov | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 99E86F79 | flightcast:01KNF6VSZK1MXKZRCKT9PQKSZW | 90 | 5704 | 1.6% |
| 5951989F | flightcast:01KM20WJPKVFHRVJZWTNA6Q1XT | 90 | 7036 | 1.3% |
| A53E3CE0 | flightcast:01KP9HAYP5R81VSSVBEPE3C926 | 90 | 2370 | 3.8% |
| D787EAA8 | flightcast:01KMZRVEW8TBWD8QTDH5GJQWE6 | 90 | 1830 | 4.9% |

The 90-second ceiling is suspiciously uniform — strongly suggests a hard-coded limit or early-exit condition fires after the first chunk.

**Impact:** This single bug explains **63 of 72 user corrections** on this corpus — the detector never scored those windows because the transcript never reached them. No classifier change or NARL activation will fix ads missed in un-transcribed audio.

**Investigation asks:**
1. Why is `fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime=90` a common ceiling? Hard-coded limit, budget exhaustion, task-skip after Nth chunk, or some other early-terminate?
2. What transitions an asset to `complete` when 95%+ of the audio hasn't been fast-transcripted?
3. Is the slow-transcript coverage completing the gap, or is it also stuck?
4. Does the background-processing budget cut off fast-transcript early?

**Acceptance:**
- Root cause identified and documented
- Either fast-transcript coverage genuinely runs to end-of-feature, or the `analysisState='complete'` label is renamed to reflect partial coverage so downstream telemetry/metrics aren't misled
- Re-run NARL eval on a corpus that has closer parity between fast-transcript and feature coverage, confirm a meaningful drop in "windows never scored"

**Reference:** `.xcappdata` bundle in working dir; eval output at `.eval-out/narl/20260423-175930-22C2B0/`.
notes:
**Full writeup:** `/Users/dabrams/playhead/docs/narl/2026-04-23-real-data-findings.md` — Finding 1
**Expert-evaluation report (detailed data):** `/Users/dabrams/playhead/docs/narl/2026-04-23-expert-report.md`

## 2026-04-23 Investigation findings

Traced the field through `AnalysisCoordinator`, `TranscriptEngineService`, `AnalysisJobRunner`, `PreAnalysisConfig`. Result:

### The 90s ceiling itself is by design

`PreAnalysisConfig.swift:16` declares `defaultT0DepthSeconds: Double = 90`. This is the first tier (T0) of a three-tier coverage system (T0=90s, T1=300s, T2=900s). `AnalysisJobRunner.swift:129` filters shards: `allShards.filter { $0.startTime < request.desiredCoverageSec }`. With 30s default shard duration, T0 processes shards [0-30, 30-60, 60-90] and stops. That ceiling is intentional.

### The bug is NOT the 90s ceiling; it's that assets still reach `analysisState='complete'`

The coverage guard at `AnalysisCoordinator.finalizeBackfillVerdict` (line 1702) SHOULD block completion when transcript coverage ratio < 0.95. For the four affected episodes (fastCov=90s on 1800–7000s episodes), ratio is 1–5% — well below the 0.95 threshold, so `.failed` should result, not `.complete`.

### Root cause: `currentEpisodeDuration()` returns 0 on crash/resume

`currentEpisodeDuration()` (line 1720-1725) derives duration from `activeShards`. `activeShards` is only populated during `spool` (line 1045) — never rehydrated. On a fresh process where the session resumes from persisted `.backfill` state (`runFromBackfill` with `transcriptEventTask == nil`, line 1129):

1. `currentEpisodeDuration()` returns 0
2. `resumeBackfillDecision(chunks, 0)` hits `guard episodeDuration > 0 else { return .finalize }` (line 1756-1758) → bypass the ratio check → route to finalize
3. `finalizeBackfill` calls `finalizeBackfillVerdict(chunks, 0)` which hits `guard episodeDuration > 0 else { return .allowComplete }` (line 1706) → bypass the ratio check → allow complete
4. `transition(..., to: .complete)` stamps the asset as complete with only fast-pass 90s of data

This explains all five observed symptoms:
- `fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime=90` (T0 tier ran exactly once during a prior session)
- `analysisState='complete'` (coverage guard bypassed on resume)
- `featureCoverageEndTime` in the thousands (feature extraction persisted earlier)
- Zero decision-log rows on those assets (fast-pass never triggered scoring far enough; backfill runBackfill probably ran but had no windows to score past the 90s chunk range)
- Uniform 90s across four independent episodes (deterministic — same T0 constant, same bypass path)

### Scoring-trigger secondary finding

Relevant to gtt9.4 but surfaced here: decision-log writes happen on two paths only:
1. **Hot path**: `AnalysisCoordinator.handlePersistedTranscriptChunks` (line 1559) → filters for fast-pass only (line 1563) → `AdDetectionService.runHotPathResult` → `emitHotPathDecisionLogs` (AdDetectionService.swift:2732)
2. **Backfill**: `AnalysisCoordinator.finalizeBackfill` (line 1591) → `AdDetectionService.runBackfill` → logs per-fusion-window (AdDetectionService.swift:1070-1092)

If `finalizeBackfill` is called via the bypass path above with only 90s of fast-pass chunks, `runBackfill` will still execute but has nothing further to score. If `finalizeBackfill` never runs (crashed mid-backfill, no resume), decision-log stays empty.

### Proposed fixes (not yet implemented — for gtt9.1's fix bead)

Option A — rehydrate `activeShards` on resume: re-decode/cache the audio shards when resuming from `.backfill` so `currentEpisodeDuration()` returns real values and both coverage guards function.

Option B — persist episode duration: store the total duration on the asset row at spool time. Have `currentEpisodeDuration()` fall back to that persisted value when `activeShards == nil`. Cheaper than re-decoding.

Option C — tighten the guards: change the "episodeDuration <= 0" shortcuts in `finalizeBackfillVerdict` and `resumeBackfillDecision` from `.allowComplete / .finalize` to `.blockComplete / .restart` so unknown-duration forces a safe restart rather than a silent bypass.

Option B + C together look best: persist duration as the durable source of truth, and make the guards fail-safe when even the persisted value is missing.

### File:line citations

- `Playhead/Services/PreAnalysis/PreAnalysisConfig.swift:16` — T0=90s constant
- `Playhead/Services/AnalysisJobRunner/AnalysisJobRunner.swift:129` — shard filter by desiredCoverageSec
- `Playhead/Services/AnalysisCoordinator/AnalysisCoordinator.swift:1045` — activeShards write (spool only)
- `Playhead/Services/AnalysisCoordinator/AnalysisCoordinator.swift:1720-1725` — currentEpisodeDuration
- `Playhead/Services/AnalysisCoordinator/AnalysisCoordinator.swift:1706` — finalizeBackfillVerdict bypass
- `Playhead/Services/AnalysisCoordinator/AnalysisCoordinator.swift:1749-1765` — resumeBackfillDecision bypass
- `Playhead/Services/AnalysisCoordinator/AnalysisCoordinator.swift:1563-1574` — hot-path fast-pass filter
- `Playhead/Services/AdDetection/AdDetectionService.swift:1070-1092` — backfill decision-log write

### Recommendation

Split this bead:
- **gtt9.1 stays as an investigation bead** (this document is the deliverable)
- **Spawn a gtt9.1.fix bead** to implement Option B + C and add a regression test: create a session persisted at `.backfill` with activeShards unset and 90s of fast chunks, verify coverage guard blocks `.complete`

title: narl Phase 2: post-capture findings from 2026-04-23 real-data eval
description:
Ran the NARL harness on the first real .xcappdata capture (2026-04-23, 16 episodes, 0 shadow rows but 72 corrections, 147 decision-log windows). The numerical findings reframe what "improving detection" actually means.

## Key findings from real-data eval

Against synthetic fixtures the story looked like "allEnabled regresses F1." Against real data it's much more interesting:

**1. Pipeline completion dominates — 63 of 72 user corrections are in windows the detector never scored.**
   Only 9 corrections have causalSource="foundationModel" (i.e., FM made an actual wrong call). The rest are user-adds filling in analytical gaps. Asset table shows the root cause: fastTranscriptCoverage maxes at 90s on four episodes marked `complete` with featureCoverage of 1800–7000s (1.3–4.9% transcript coverage). You cannot miss-classify what was never classified.

**2. The "0-of-8 Conan catastrophe" is not a detection failure — it's a partially-scored episode with a promotion bug.**
   Decision log shows C22D6EC6 actually scored 3 distinct windows out of ~73 expected. One window at [74.0, 83.4] hit classifier confidence **0.597** and overlapped GT at [77.1, 85.0] — but was tagged `hotPathCandidate` (flagged-not-promoted) instead of `autoSkipEligible`. Something in the promotion path gated it off despite strong evidence.

**3. PriorShift as configured is inert on real data.**
   Default midpoint 0.25, shifted midpoint 0.22. Across all 147 scored windows, **zero** land in the (0.22, 0.25] band that priorShift targets. Confidence mode is 0.30–0.40 (78 of 147 windows, 53%). The synthetic fixtures placed windows in the priorShift band artificially; real classifier output doesn't cluster there.

**4. Classifier-dominance — other evidence rarely fires.**
   Evidence source counts across 147 windows: classifier=147 (100%), metadata=10 (7%), fm=8 (5%), lexical=5 (3%), catalog=5 (3%), acoustic=3 (2%). The metadata-activation machinery NARL gates touches <10% of decisions; the classifier drives everything else.

**5. Show-label heuristic misses real-world podcastIds.**
   Eight episodes rolled up as "unknown" in the report because podcastId is the raw feed URL like `https://feeds.simplecast.com/dHoohVNH::311e3daa-...` which the existing heuristic doesn't pattern-match. Hides per-show signal in rollups.

## What this epic covers

Child beads on each of the five findings above, scoped to be individually useful:
- Transcript completion investigation (biggest lift, clearest root cause ask)
- Promotion-gap investigation (smallest lift, specific test case: C22D6EC6 window [74, 83.4])
- PriorShift retune against real-data confidence distribution
- Evidence-fusion rebalancing review (if classifier-dominance is by design, NARL can't help; if it's symptom, fix it)
- Show-label heuristic patch (minor polish)

## Referenced source data

- `.xcappdata`: `/Users/dabrams/playhead/com.playhead.app 2026-04-23 13:54.43.748.xcappdata` (gitignored; dev-only)
- Generated fixtures: `PlayheadTests/Fixtures/NarlEval/2026-04-23/` (16 FrozenTrace-*.json)
- Harness output: `.eval-out/narl/20260423-175930-22C2B0/`

**Expert-evaluation report (detailed data):** `/Users/dabrams/playhead/docs/narl/2026-04-23-expert-report.md`

title: [epic] Personal dogfood corpus → metadata activation
description:
## Goal

Build a labeled corpus from Dan's personal listening (N=1 dogfooding) that is precise enough to counterfactually validate the metadata-activation gate flip on `playhead-narl` without waiting for an external corpus.

Dan is pre-launch sole user. Waiting for a 200+ episode external corpus to unblock `narl` is premature-optimization; live dogfooding already generates labeled data *if* we (a) record what the system decided, (b) record what the user corrected with per-window precision, and (c) export the joined data in a reviewable form.

## Why this is an epic, not a single bead

The three enabling beads have to land in order before `narl` can flip:

1. **narL (playhead-8em9)** — DecisionLogger writing per-window JSONL so we can replay any config offline. Precondition: without decision logs, corrections have nothing to grade against.
2. **narP (playhead-zskc)** — Fix the `0...Int.max` scope fallback so user corrections carry window-precision, not whole-episode. Precondition: without narP, every correction in the corpus collapses to episode-level — insufficient for precision/recall/IoU metrics.
3. **narE (playhead-dgzw)** — Debug-menu export combining the decision log and correction events into a single reviewable JSONL. Consumer of both narL and narP.
4. **narl (playhead-narl)** — Activate the metadata lexical injection + prior shift + FM scheduling trio (counterfactual gate flip). Graduation target: enabled once the corpus validates that activation does not regress precision.

## Sequencing

- narL and narP can be done in parallel (independent fixes; narP is a bug, narL is new logging infra).
- narE blocks on BOTH narL and narP (it's the export that joins their outputs).
- narl blocks on narE (and on Dan having tagged enough episodes via the corpus to counterfactually validate activation).

## Status snapshot (2026-04-21)

- narP: **implemented on branch `bead/playhead-zskc`** (commit 5e28f09). Not yet merged; Dan plans to tag 3–4 more episodes tonight, but those fresh tags will still carry the coarse `0...Int.max` scope until the branch lands on-device.
- narL: open, not started.
- narE: open, not started.
- narl: parked — the counterfactual gate remains `.default` until narE yields a validated corpus.

## Acceptance (epic-level)

- Decision logs accumulate during real listening (narL).
- New corrections persist with window-precise scope, never `0...Int.max` (narP).
- Debug menu exports a single joined JSONL with enough fidelity to replay `.default` decisions offline (narE).
- Dan makes a confident call to flip the counterfactual gate based on the export (narl), or deliberately parks `narl` with evidence-backed reasoning.

## Non-goals

- Not a product-level feature-flag system. Debug gate and logging are DEV-only; release build strips both.
- Not a privacy surface change. All logs are on-device; no telemetry.
- Not a scoring-policy change. The epic enables the decision to activate metadata; it does not itself change detection.

title: narP: Fix 0...Int.max fallback — carry precise window scope into CorrectionEvent
description:
## Background

Discovered 2026-04-21 while inspecting the on-device analysis.sqlite from personal dogfooding. All 19 \`CorrectionEvent\` rows captured by the existing \"Not an ad\" / \"I'm listening to an ad\" buttons persisted with scope \`exactSpan:<assetId>:0:9223372036854775807\` — i.e. the \`0...Int.max\` whole-episode fallback.

This is exactly the failure mode COD blind-spot idea #4 from the 2026-04-21 dueling-wizards session called out (\"Correction Anchor Precision — Kill the 0...Int.max Fallback\"), and it's actively blocking the personal-corpus path: without per-window scope, we have episode-level labels only, which is insufficient for precision/recall/IoU metrics on the \`playhead-8xap\` (nar0) harness.

## Symptoms

All 19 real-world correction rows on Dan's device share scope pattern \`exactSpan:C25A058C-778B-44A8-9145-D83AA7AF297E:0:9223372036854775807\`, across both \`manualVeto\`/\`.falsePositive\` (\"Not an ad\") and \`.falseNegative\` (\"I'm listening to an ad\") sources.

Expected, per \`PersistentUserCorrectionStore\`:
- \`recordVeto(span:)\` should persist \`span.fullOrdinalRange\` (= \`firstAtomOrdinal...lastAtomOrdinal\`).
- \`recordFalseNegative(assetId:reportedTime:)\` should persist synthetic negative ordinals (\`syntheticFirst...syntheticLast\` derived from SHA256 hash).

Neither should produce \`0...Int.max\`. Something in the call chain is either (a) substituting a coarse span before it reaches \`recordVeto\`, (b) calling \`record(_:)\` directly with a pre-constructed \`0...Int.max\` scope, or (c) failing a guard and falling back somewhere.

## Investigation plan

1. \`grep -n 'Int.max\\|9223372036854775807\\|0...Int' Playhead/\` — find hardcoded fallbacks in correction/decoded-span paths.
2. Find all call sites of \`recordVeto\`, \`recordFalseNegative\`, and direct \`record(_:)\` calls.
3. For each: trace the \`DecodedSpan\` / \`CorrectionEvent\` being passed; confirm its ordinal range matches actual user intent (the tapped span / synthetic window) rather than a coarse fallback.
4. For the \"I'm listening to an ad\" button in particular: verify \`recordFalseNegative\` actually uses the negative-ordinal synthetic range it computes — not a second sanitization step that widens to \`0...Int.max\`.
5. Write the root-cause and fix plan into this bead before coding.

## Fix

Depends on root cause:
- If coarse spans are being constructed at the UI layer: fix UI code to pass the actual tapped/contextual span.
- If \`record(_:)\` is being called directly with a fallback scope: replace with typed \`recordVeto\` / \`recordFalseNegative\` or surface the ordinal range at the call site.
- If a serialization path collapses finite ordinals to \`Int.max\`: fix the serializer.

Also add:
- Unit test: a \`recordVeto\` with concrete ordinals \`100...200\` must persist scope \`exactSpan:<asset>:100:200\`, NOT \`0:Int.max\`.
- Unit test: \`recordFalseNegative\` must persist a scope with a negative first ordinal.
- Optional: a migration / tagger that marks existing coarse-scope corrections as \`boundaryPrecision: .episode\` vs. new ones as \`.window\`, so nar0 can filter.

## Acceptance

- New \`manualVeto\` corrections persist with the actual tapped span's ordinal range.
- New \`falseNegative\` corrections persist with the synthetic negative-ordinal range that matches the DecodedSpan synthesized by \`recordFalseNegative\`.
- No code path can silently substitute \`0...Int.max\` unless explicitly requested for a whole-episode veto (if such a thing even exists).
- Regression tests added for both.

## Relationship to other beads

- Unblocks meaningful use of \`playhead-dgzw\` (narE corpus export) and \`playhead-8xap\` (nar0 harness).
- Complementary to \`playhead-8em9\` (narL decision logger) — narL captures *what the system decided*; narP ensures *what the user corrected* is scoped precisely. Both needed for counterfactual replay.
- Retroactive: Dan's existing 19 coarse corrections don't become more precise after the fix. Going forward, new ones will — which is why this bead gates continued corpus growth.
notes:
## Root-cause analysis (2026-04-21)

**Six hardcoded `0...Int.max` call sites identified:**

1. `Playhead/Services/SkipOrchestrator/SkipOrchestrator.swift:594` — `recordListenRevert` ("Listen" button). Has `managed.snappedStart`/`snappedEnd` (times) but AdWindow carries no ordinals. Explicit comment admits coarseness.
2. `Playhead/Services/SkipOrchestrator/SkipOrchestrator.swift:659` — `revertByTimeRange` ("Not an ad" banner / popover by time range). Has `start`/`end` params directly.
3. `Playhead/Services/SkipOrchestrator/SkipOrchestrator.swift:727` — `revertWindow` (by ID). Has `managed.snappedStart`/`snappedEnd`.
4. `Playhead/Views/NowPlaying/TranscriptPeekView.swift:614` — transcript modal "Not an ad". Synthesizes a `DecodedSpan` from selected chunks with actual times but stub ordinals `0...Int.max`.
5. `Playhead/Views/NowPlaying/NowPlayingView.swift:100` — banner "Not an ad" (`onNotAnAd`). Constructs CorrectionEvent directly with coarse scope. The AdBannerItem has no ordinal info.
6. `Playhead/Services/AdDetection/AdDetectionService.swift:402` — `recordUserMarkedAd` ("I'm listening to an ad"). Ironically, the caller (`NowPlayingViewModel.reportHearingAd`) uses `BoundaryExpander` to compute real start/end times and injects a proper AdWindow, but then discards the boundary when persisting the CorrectionEvent.

## Why the fallback exists

All six sites have **time** info but no **ordinal** info. `AdWindow` doesn't carry atom ordinals. `TranscriptChunk.atomOrdinal` is `Int?` and nil during fast-pass transcription (populated only on final pass). `CorrectionScope.exactSpan` only accepts ordinals, so callers without ordinals stubbed `0...Int.max`.

## `BoundaryExpander` is already the right tool — just not wired all the way through

`BoundaryExpander.expand(seed:featureWindows:transcriptChunks:adWindows:) -> ExpandedBoundary` turns a seed time into `(startTime, endTime, boundaryConfidence, source)`. The file's header comment literally says "instead of logging a whole-episode correction (scope 0...Int.max), this finds the ad's actual start and end boundaries." It's used by the "I'm listening to an ad" UI path to compute the AdWindow. But the persistence of CorrectionEvent still throws those times away.

## Proposed fix

**Add a time-based case to `CorrectionScope`:**

```swift
case exactTimeSpan(assetId: String, startTime: Double, endTime: Double)
```

Serialize as `exactTimeSpan:assetId:<startTime>:<endTime>` with fixed-precision (e.g. 3 decimals) to avoid FP drift, matching the existing scheme.

**Call-site changes:**
- All 6 sites above: replace `.exactSpan(assetId:, ordinalRange: 0...Int.max)` with `.exactTimeSpan(assetId:, startTime:, endTime:)` using the times already in scope.
- TranscriptPeekView: stop synthesizing a coarse DecodedSpan; either (a) pass the time range directly to a new correction-recording API on UserCorrectionStore, or (b) keep the DecodedSpan but let `recordVeto` detect when `lastAtomOrdinal == Int.max` and fall back to emitting `.exactTimeSpan` using the span's `startTime`/`endTime`.

**Downstream consumer changes:**
- `correctionPassthroughFactor`, `hasActiveCorrection`, scope matching in `BroadCorrectionEvaluator` must handle the new case. Deserialization is additive. Match logic needs to compare time ranges when the scope is time-based.

**Optional late-binding resolution:** when atom ordinals become available (e.g., after final-pass transcript completes), a background job could upgrade `exactTimeSpan` corrections to `exactSpan` by looking up `TranscriptChunk` rows in the stored time range. Not required for the fix, but a nice follow-up.

## Effort

Moderate. ~300–500 lines touched across UserCorrectionStore, the 6 call sites, and downstream matchers. 20–30 new/updated tests. Not a one-line fix because the scope type is load-bearing.

## Retroactive data

Dan's 19 existing coarse corrections on `C25A058C-...` are lost for precision purposes; they remain as episode-level labels only. New corrections post-fix will carry window-precision. No migration possible — the information was never captured.

title: narL: Debug-scoped activation override + decision logger
description:
## Background

Dogfooding posture: Dan is the only user pre-launch, so `MetadataActivationConfig.counterfactualGateOpen` over-protects. We want `.allEnabled` driving real skips in dev builds AND rich per-window logging so decisions can be replayed offline under any config once a labeled corpus exists.

This is NOT flipping the production gate — shipping release stays `.default`.

## Scope

### 1. Debug-scoped gate override
- Add mechanism to override `counterfactualGateOpen` in dev builds only. Options (pick one):
  - Build-config flag (`#if PLAYHEAD_DEV` in personal scheme)
  - Launch argument parsed by `MetadataActivationConfig`
  - Settings bundle toggle (nice but heavier)
- Production release build MUST ignore the override — assert this with a test.

### 2. `DecisionLogger` service
- New actor/service subscribing to ad-detection pipeline output.
- Writes JSONL to `FileManager.default.urls(for: .documentDirectory)[0].appendingPathComponent(\"decision-log.jsonl\")`.
- One record per window decision:
  - episodeID, timestamp, windowBounds (start/end seconds)
  - `MetadataActivationConfig` snapshot
  - Evidence inputs: metadata lexicon hits, prior-shift deltas applied, FM scheduling adjustments, acoustic/ASR evidence components
  - Fused confidence breakdown (per-component contributions to final score)
  - Final decision (skip/keep/banner) + threshold crossed
- Append-only, rotate on 10MB chunks (`decision-log.1.jsonl`, `.2.jsonl`, ...).
- Rich enough that offline replay can reconstruct `.default` decisions without re-running the pipeline.

### 3. Info.plist file-sharing
- Add `UIFileSharingEnabled = YES` and `LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace = YES` — dev scheme only.
- Document pull paths in README or debug menu:
  - Finder: device → Files tab → Playhead → drag `decision-log.jsonl` out
  - Xcode: Devices and Simulators → Download Container → unwrap `.xcappdata` → `AppData/Documents/`

## Acceptance

- On dev build, `.allEnabled` is actively driving skip decisions (verify with a test-level assertion or debug overlay).
- `decision-log.jsonl` accumulates records during real listening sessions.
- A shipping release build cannot enable the override (assertion test).
- Logs are retrievable via Finder in under 30 seconds.
- Log records contain enough inputs to compute `.default`-equivalent decisions offline.

## Risks and concerns

- **Log volume**: ~hundreds of windows per 60min episode × ~200 bytes = tens of KB. Rotation at 10MB is generous.
- **PII / privacy**: logs include episode IDs and show metadata — fine for personal device, but never enable in release build.
- **Performance**: logging must be non-blocking (async file writes, bounded queue). Don't let logging back-pressure decisions.
- **Schema stability**: add a `schemaVersion` field up front so future replay tools can handle drift.

## Why now

Unblocks personal dogfooding of the metadata trio without committing to a product-level activation decision. Every listening session grows the replayable dataset for the eventual `playhead-narl` activation gate.

## Depends on / blocks

- Precursor to `playhead-narl` (metadata activation for all users) — that bead remains parked pending corpus.
- Pairs with `playhead-narA` (correction annotator) which stamps labels into the same-directory `corrections.jsonl`.

title: Activate BracketDetector + FineBoundaryRefiner (shadow → live)
description: Promoted idea from the 2026-04-21 dueling-wizards synthesis. COD originated at #4 of its own list; after the reveal, COD self-reranked above its own top ideas ('Claude is right and this should have ranked higher'). Same structural pattern as playhead-rxuv (activate chapter evidence): sophisticated shadow infrastructure already built; graduation pending.
design:
Current state:
- BracketDetector is a deterministic finite-state envelope scanner with full template taxonomy (stingInBedDryOut, dryInStingOut, hardInFadeOut, symmetricBracket, partialOnset, partialOffset). Emits BracketEvidence with onset/offset times, template class, confidence, and per-show musicBracketTrust (Beta posterior).
- FineBoundaryRefiner provides local search ±3s around candidate boundaries at 100-250ms hops with multiple cue types (silenceGap, energyValley, spectralDiscontinuity, coarseFallback).
- Both are deployed in SHADOW MODE — logging evidence but not influencing live skip decisions.

Activation work:
1. Wire BracketEvidence from the scanner into the live boundary-resolution pipeline (TimeBoundaryResolver / BoundaryRefiner upstream of SkipOrchestrator).
2. Graduate FineBoundaryRefiner from shadow to live with an activation flag.
3. Gate on per-show musicBracketTrust (Beta posterior) so shows with insufficient confidence stay conservative.
4. Validate against accumulated shadow logs before flipping activation.

Coverage caveat: music-envelope bracketing helps when the episode HAS a music bed (common in produced podcasts, absent in host-read integrations). Orthogonal and complementary to the transcript boundary cue (playhead-kgby) and chapter evidence (playhead-rxuv). Together these three form a coherent boundary-quality work package.

Pattern match to playhead-rxuv: both beads graduate sophisticated shadow systems. Expect similar sequencing — wire, shadow-compare, flip with trust gate.
acceptance_criteria:
- BracketEvidence feeds live boundary resolution as a scored cue, not an override
- FineBoundaryRefiner activation flag introduced with default conservative gate
- Per-show musicBracketTrust controls activation threshold
- Shadow-log validation pass before live flip
- Boundary quality improves on produced podcasts (shadow-vs-live comparison)
- Graceful no-op for host-read segments without music beds
notes: Related infrastructure — FineFeatureBandCache (Playhead/Services/AdDetection/FineFeatureBandCache.swift) carries an explicit 'SHADOW MODE only — not wired into live skip pipeline' comment and has no external caller in production. It is the ±3s feature-band cache that FineBoundaryRefiner was built to use. This activation bead implicitly brings FineFeatureBandCache live as well; confirm it is wired when the refiner is graduated. No separate bead needed.

title: Banner transparency: wire EvidenceCatalogBuilder into AdSkipBannerItem with user-facing copy
description: Consensus winner #3 from the 2026-04-21 dueling-wizards synthesis (cross-model avg 712, both agents agreed on mechanism). Always-intended Playhead feature per user: banner today shows WHAT was skipped; this adds WHY. For an AI-driven product that makes decisions about what users hear, transparency is not polish — it is the trust architecture.
design:
Current state (verified):
- AdSkipBannerItem.evidenceCatalogEntries is an empty array [] with a Phase 7 deferral comment in the code.
- EvidenceCatalogBuilder exists; evidence is persisted; the hard work is done — it is just not wired into banner emission.

Three-part scope (can be done as one epic with sub-beads, or sequentially):

1. PLUMBING — wire EvidenceCatalogBuilder output into ManagedWindow and through to AdSkipBannerItem.evidenceCatalogEntries. Ensure the banner emission path carries the evidence across the threading boundary. Low risk, mostly mechanical.

2. COPY ABSTRACTION — the real design work. Raw evidence entries are debug output ('Lexical match on pattern sponsorPhrase weight 0.82'), not user language. Build a translation layer turning evidence types into human-readable explanations:
  - 'Heard sponsor language: "use code PODCAST for 20% off"'
  - 'Music transition detected at boundaries'
  - 'Matches sponsor pattern from 3 other episodes of this show'
  - 'Chapter marked Sponsor: BetterHelp' (once playhead-rxuv lands)
  This is a taste problem, not a tech problem. Needs iteration with real episodes.

3. EXPAND-TO-DETAIL UI — banner stays minimal by default (existing look), tap-to-expand reveals the evidence list. Must not destabilize current banner ergonomics.

Sequencing note: ship plumbing + copy together as one shippable unit; UI can follow or ship with them. First-Encounter Trust Choreography (separate future bead from blind-spot list) should reuse this copy abstraction as its content.
acceptance_criteria:
- EvidenceCatalogBuilder output reaches AdSkipBannerItem.evidenceCatalogEntries on the live banner emission path
- Human-readable copy layer translates all current evidence types into user-facing strings
- Expand-to-detail interaction reveals the evidence list without disrupting default banner ergonomics
- No regression on existing banner behavior when the evidence list is empty (graceful absence)
- Copy reviewed for tone consistency with Playhead's design-forward aesthetic
notes:
Refinement (2026-04-21): expanded banner detail MUST include advertiser identity when available.

- The ad_windows table already has an advertiser field populated by the detection pipeline.
- When advertiser name is present with sufficient confidence, surface it as the PRIMARY copy element: 'Skipped · BetterHelp sponsor read' — more concrete and trust-building than any abstract evidence explanation.
- When absent or low-confidence, fall back to the abstract evidence copy ('Heard sponsor language: …').
- This feature intersects naturally with the Cross-Show Ad Repetition blind-spot idea (CC-BS3): advertiser name is the join key that enables 'heard on 3 other shows this week' copy once that data is aggregated.

Updated acceptance:
- When advertiser is confidently identified, display advertiser name as primary copy.
- Graceful fallback to abstract evidence copy when advertiser is absent or low-confidence.
- Advertiser name rendered consistently with design-forward aesthetic (no ALL CAPS, no overzealous branding).

title: Activate chapter evidence in AdDetectionService fusion (creator-provided chapters)
description: Consensus winner #2 from the 2026-04-21 dueling-wizards synthesis (cross-model avg 745). Exit shadow mode for Podcasting 2.0 chapter evidence: wire ChapterEvidence into AdDetectionService's evidence fusion, add chapter-based confidence adjustments to the hot-path scorer, and implement content-chapter suppression for false-positive reduction.
design:
Current state (verified):
- ChapterParser and quality scoring exist and are tested.
- Production consumption is thin: CandidateWindowSelector is the sole real consumer; cascade is optional with nil default.
- Effectively shadow-mode for the hot path.

What 'activation' means (real work, not a toggle):
- Wire ChapterEvidence into AdDetectionService evidence fusion as a proposal source.
- Add chapter-based confidence adjustments to the hot-path scorer.
- Content-chapter SUPPRESSION in the decision mapper: penalize ad proposals inside chapters labeled 'Interview', 'Q&A', etc. (this is the false-positive reducer).
- Validate against accumulated shadow logs before flipping activation flag.

Trust tier for this bead: creator-provided chapters only (Podcasting 2.0). These are treated as near-ground-truth. LLM-inferred chapters are a separate follow-on bead with a lower trust weight.

Why it's consensus #2 despite minority coverage: for episodes that DO ship chapters, signal quality is categorical (creator-labeled 'Sponsor: X' is not statistical inference). One prevented false positive per user per week > marginal recall gains.
acceptance_criteria:
- ChapterEvidence wired into AdDetectionService fusion with distinct provenance tag ('creatorChapter')
- Content-chapter suppression reduces false-positive ad proposals inside non-ad chapters
- Shadow-log validation pass before activation
- Graceful no-op when episode has no chapter markers
- No regressions on episodes without chapters

title: Transcript-aware boundary cue in TimeBoundaryResolver
description: Add a probabilistic transcript sentence-boundary cue to the multi-cue resolver in AdDetectionService (TimeBoundaryResolver / BoundaryRefiner), weighted by ASR quality. Winner of the 2026-04-21 dueling-wizards synthesis (cross-model avg 827).
design:
NOT SkipOrchestrator — that consumes precomputed spans. Integrate upstream in TimeBoundaryResolver / BoundaryRefiner as a new cue type that competes with silenceGap, energyValley, spectralDiscontinuity, coarseFallback.

Design (refined through adversarial duel):
- New cue type: transcript sentence-terminal boundary (derived from ASR punctuation + pause-probability peaks)
- Weight = f(punctuation reliability, local ASR confidence, chunk quality)
- Graceful degradation: when ASR is noisy (music under speech), weight drops and acoustic cues win
- Competes in existing multi-cue resolver; does not override

Risk: if shipped as a hard snap rule, becomes 'fancy boundary jitter'. MUST be probabilistic, not deterministic.

Why it's #1: only idea in the dueling-wizards synthesis that adds a qualitatively new KIND of information to the boundary stack. All other picks optimize or activate existing signals.
acceptance_criteria:
- Transcript cue type defined and emitted from TranscriptChunk data
- Weight function responsive to ASR quality signals
- Fusion weights tuned so cue degrades gracefully under poor ASR
- Boundary quality improves on produced podcasts (regression + shadow-mode comparison)
- No regressions when transcript is absent or low-confidence

title: zp0x-followup: wire per-episode SurfaceReason into BatchChildSurfaceSummary
description:
zp0x landed BatchNotificationEligibility/Reducer/Service/Coordinator/Evictor with the full enum surface (tripReady + blockedStorage + blockedWifiPolicy + blockedAnalysisUnavailable). However `PlayheadApp.makeBatchSummaryBuilder` derives `BatchChildSurfaceSummary` only from `Episode.downloadState` and `analysisSummary?.hasAnalysis` — every non-ready child is stamped with `reason: .waitingForTime, userFixable: false`. As a result, `tripReady` notifications fire correctly in production, but `blocked*` notifications never trigger because real `SurfaceReason` data is never plumbed in.

## Scope

Wire the full per-episode `EpisodeSurfaceStatus` reducer (CapabilitySnapshot + AnalysisEligibility + the dfem/sueq SurfaceReason machinery) into the BatchChildSurfaceSummary path in `PlayheadApp.makeBatchSummaryBuilder` so that non-ready children carry their actual SurfaceReason / AnalysisUnavailableReason / userFixable.

## Acceptance

- A child whose download is blocked because the device is over the storage cap reports `reason: .storageFull, userFixable: true` → coordinator emits `blockedStorage` after the persistence rule fires.
- A child blocked by `analysisUnavailable` with `appleIntelligenceDisabled` or `languageUnsupported` → coordinator emits `blockedAnalysisUnavailable`.
- A child blocked by `analysisUnavailable` with `hardwareUnsupported` or `regionUnsupported` → continues to report `userFixable: false` → coordinator stays at `.none` (correct — not user-actionable).
- Test in `BatchNotificationCoordinatorTests` that exercises the production builder path against a seeded SwiftData store with each blocker shape.

## Cross-refs

- Spec source: zp0x bead + Phase 2 deliverable 8 (blocker eligibility cases).
- Existing inline note: `Playhead/App/PlayheadApp.swift` `makeBatchSummaryBuilder` doc-comment.
- Depends on already-shipped: dfem (SurfaceReason mapping), sueq (AnalysisUnavailableReason wiring), zp0x (notification surface itself).

description:
