title: A5: TimeBoundaryResolver — Multi-cue boundary snapping in seconds
description:
## Background
Current boundary operations use atom counts (mergeGapAtoms=3, boundarySnapRadiusAtoms=15) which are unstable because atoms vary 1–5 per second. Boundary snapping also relies only on silence, but host-read ads often transition on speaker turns, music beds, or compression changes. TimeBoundaryResolver replaces all of this with seconds-based, multi-cue, distance-aware, asymmetric snapping.

## What to build
New file: Playhead/Services/AdDetection/TimeBoundaryResolver.swift

TimeBoundaryResolver is the ONLY component allowed to snap or relocate boundaries.

### Inputs
The `snap()` method accepts:
- `candidateTime: Double` -- the boundary time to snap
- `boundaryType: BoundaryType` (.start or .end)
- `anchorType: AnchorType` -- for asymmetric snap distance lookup
- `featureWindows: [FeatureWindow]` -- acoustic/music/speaker cues
- `lexicalHits: [LexicalHit]` -- for lexical density delta (start) and return markers (end)
- `config: BoundarySnappingConfig`

### Boundary-type-aware scoring
Separate cue weights for .start and .end boundaries:

Score formula:
`score = cueBlend(boundaryType) - lambda * normalizedDistance`

where `normalizedDistance = abs(candidateWindowTime - originalTime) / maxSnapDistance` (0-1 range).

Note: The original spec included `+ continuityBonus - contradictionPenalty` terms in the formula, but these were removed because they lacked definition and could not be implemented without further design. If needed, they can be added in a follow-up bead once their computation is specified.

Start boundary weights:
- Pause/VAD: 0.25, Speaker change proxy: 0.20, Music bed change: 0.15, Spectral change: 0.20, Lexical density delta: 0.20

End boundary weights:
- Pause/VAD: 0.25, Speaker change proxy: 0.20, Music bed change: 0.15, Spectral change: 0.15, Explicit return marker: 0.25

### Cue computation details

**Lexical density delta (start weight 0.20):** Computed inside TimeBoundaryResolver from `lexicalHits`. For each FeatureWindow, count the number of ad-category LexicalHits whose time overlaps that window and the preceding window. The delta is `|count[t] - count[t-1]|` normalized to 0-1 (capped at e.g. 3 hits). A sharp increase in ad-like lexical hits indicates an ad boundary.

**Explicit return marker (end weight 0.25):** Computed from `lexicalHits`. If any LexicalHit with category `.transitionMarker` overlaps the FeatureWindow's time range, this cue is 1.0; otherwise 0.0. LexicalScanner already emits `.transitionMarker` hits for "back to the show", "back to the episode", etc.

**Spectral change:** `spectralFlux` from FeatureWindow, normalized against a local baseline (e.g., mean spectralFlux within the search radius). Score = min(1.0, spectralFlux / localMeanSpectralFlux) or similar.

**All other cues** come directly from FeatureWindow fields: `pauseProbability`, `speakerChangeProxyScore`, `musicBedChangeScore`.

### Distance penalty
lambda (default 0.3, configurable in BoundarySnappingConfig) * normalizedDistance ensures the resolver prefers the NEAREST plausible boundary, not the absolute best cue anywhere in the radius. Prevents snapping to unrelated speaker changes or pauses.

### Asymmetric snap distance by anchor type
| Anchor Type | Max Start Snap | Max End Snap |
|-------------|----------------|---------------|
| disclosure (startAnchored) | 5s | 15s |
| CTA/URL (endAnchored) | 15s | 5s |
| fmPositive (neutral) | 10s | 10s |

Configurable via maxSnapDistanceByAnchorType in BoundarySnappingConfig.

### Algorithm
1. Determine maxSnapDistance from anchorType + boundaryType
2. Scan FeatureWindows within search radius
3. For each window, compute cueBlend from boundary-type weights + lexical signals
4. Apply distance penalty: score = cueBlend - lambda * normalizedDistance
5. Return nearest local maximum exceeding BOTH minBoundaryScore (0.3) AND minImprovementOverOriginal (0.1)
6. If nothing qualifies, return original time unsnapped

### Scope clarification
This bead creates TimeBoundaryResolver and BoundarySnappingConfig only. It does NOT modify existing snap logic in SkipOrchestrator.snapBoundary() or MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder.applyBoundarySnap(). Those replacements happen in playhead-gji (A5: Wire TimeBoundaryResolver into existing components).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] New file TimeBoundaryResolver.swift with snap() method
- [ ] New file/struct BoundarySnappingConfig with all tunable weights and defaults
- [ ] All boundary math in seconds, no atom counts
- [ ] Separate start/end cue weights (totaling 1.0 each)
- [ ] snap() accepts FeatureWindows AND LexicalHits as inputs
- [ ] Lexical density delta computed from LexicalHit overlap counts per window
- [ ] Return marker cue computed from .transitionMarker LexicalHits
- [ ] Spectral change normalized against local baseline
- [ ] Distance penalty with configurable lambda (default 0.3), normalizedDistance = abs(delta) / maxSnapDistance
- [ ] Asymmetric snap distance by anchor type
- [ ] minBoundaryScore and minImprovementOverOriginal thresholds enforced
- [ ] Falls back to unsnapped when no good candidate
- [ ] Comprehensive unit tests for scoring formula
- [ ] Tests for distance penalty behavior (nearer candidate wins over higher-cue distant candidate)
- [ ] Tests for asymmetric snap distances (startAnchored uses 5s start / 15s end, etc.)
- [ ] Tests for fallback-to-original behavior
- [ ] Tests for lexical density delta cue
- [ ] Tests for return marker cue
- [ ] Does NOT modify SkipOrchestrator or MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder (that's playhead-gji)

title: A1: Add speakerChangeProxyScore and music signals to FeatureWindow
description:
## Background
FeatureWindow (AnalysisStore.swift:72) already has: rms, spectralFlux, pauseProbability, musicProbability (hardcoded to 0 — FeatureExtraction.swift:229), speakerClusterId (always nil), and jingleHash. The musicProbability and speakerClusterId fields exist in both the struct and the SQLite schema but are unpopulated placeholders.

Multi-cue boundary snapping (A5) and SpanHypothesisEngine (A2) need these signals populated, plus two new derivative/proxy fields, to find ad boundaries that don't start/end on silence.

## What to build

### Populate existing fields
- `musicProbability` — Currently hardcoded to 0 in FeatureExtraction.swift:229. Wire a SoundAnalysis pass (SNClassifySoundRequest with SNClassifierIdentifier.version1) to populate it with real values on-device.
- `speakerClusterId` — Remains nil in Phase A (no change needed). Note: the existing field is named `speakerClusterId`, NOT `speakerId`. Do not rename it.

### Add two new fields to FeatureWindow
- `speakerChangeProxyScore: Double` (0–1) — Acoustic turn-change proxy: pause probability spike + spectral flux spike + timbre shift. Falls back gracefully when speakerClusterId is nil. Smoothed +/-1 window. In future Phase B, becomes 1.0 at actual speaker turn boundaries.
- `musicBedChangeScore: Double` (0–1) — Derivative of musicProbability: |musicProbability[t] - musicProbability[t-1]|. Spikes on music onset/offset.

Both new fields must be added to: FeatureWindow struct, SQLite CREATE TABLE schema, INSERT/SELECT statements in AnalysisStore.swift, and all test helper factory functions.

## Implementation notes
- SoundAnalysis pass runs in parallel on the same audio buffer, on-device, no new dependencies beyond the SoundAnalysis framework (already available on iOS 13+)
- `import SoundAnalysis` does not currently exist anywhere in the project — this is new
- speakerChangeProxyScore smoothed +/-1 window: computed from acoustic features (pause probability spike + spectral flux spike + timbre change)
- musicBedChangeScore = |musicProbability[t] - musicProbability[t-1]| (or similar derivative)
- Music is an AUXILIARY cue, not a primary boundary owner
- All of Phase A must work when speakerClusterId is nil
- DB migration: bump featureVersion so existing rows are invalidated/re-extracted

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] musicProbability populated from SoundAnalysis on real audio (no longer hardcoded 0)
- [ ] Two new fields (speakerChangeProxyScore, musicBedChangeScore) added to FeatureWindow struct
- [ ] SQLite schema updated with new columns + migration path
- [ ] AnalysisStore INSERT/SELECT updated for new columns
- [ ] All existing test helpers/factories updated (there are ~15+ call sites constructing FeatureWindow in tests)
- [ ] speakerChangeProxyScore produces nonzero values from acoustic proxy when speakerClusterId is nil
- [ ] musicBedChangeScore derivative computed correctly
- [ ] Existing tests still pass (changes are additive, defaults preserve behavior)
- [ ] Unit tests for acoustic proxy score computation
- [ ] Unit tests for music derivative computation
- [ ] featureVersion bumped

title: B9: Retask FM into structured boundary extraction
description:
## Background
Current FM usage: ~3,700 token overhead per call, 300s scan budget. Two generic passes (coarse yes/no, then refinement) over broad windows. Most budget confirms what lexical + acoustic already found. Expert recommendation: stop spending FM budget on generic classification; use it for targeted boundary extraction.

## What to build

### Remove generic FM scanning
- coarsePassA() removed — suspicious regions now come from SpanHypothesisEngine (as CandidateAdSpan objects)
- refinePassB() removed — replaced by extractBoundaries()
- planPassA() replaced with planBoundaryExtractionWindows() — selects CandidateAdSpan regions for FM processing
- CoveragePlanner simplified — processes hypothesis-flagged regions only

### New extractBoundaries() method
For each CandidateAdSpan region:
1. Pre-segment transcript into sentence-like / discourse units (2–8s each, pause- and punctuation-aware). NOT atom-level — atoms vary 1–5/s making hundreds of labels token-heavy.
2. Ask FM to return 1..N contiguous labeled spans over those units
3. Schema: FMBoundarySchema with spans array + explicit abstain: Bool
4. SpanRole enum: show, adIntro, adBody, adCTA, returnToShow
5. Each span includes commercialIntent: CertaintyBand and ownership: OwnershipType
6. Each span includes evidenceRefs back to evidence catalog

### Prompt design
- 1 positive host-read ad example
- 1 negative lookalike example (show recommendation / self-promo / content CTA)
- Optionally 1 produced-ad example if budget allows
- Exclude schema framing when examples present (saves ~3,500 tokens)
- Prewarm session before extraction per Apple guidance

### Budget reallocation
Full 300s budget → fewer targeted calls on CandidateAdSpan regions (~30–120s each)

### Guardrail
If FM span crosses strong contradiction from hypothesis engine, treat as uncertain.

## Acceptance criteria
- coarsePassA() removed, refinePassB() removed, extractBoundaries() implemented
- planPassA() replaced with planBoundaryExtractionWindows()
- Pre-segmentation into discourse units (not atoms)
- FMBoundarySchema includes commercialIntent and ownership fields
- Explicit abstain path works
- One-shot examples in prompt
- FM contradiction guardrail implemented
- Token budget stays within 300s allocation
- Unit tests for discourse unit segmentation
- Tests for FM schema parsing including abstain
- Integration test with SpanHypothesisEngine CandidateAdSpan regions

title: Phase B: Span Expansion — Heavier Signal / Model Work
description:
Epic for Phase B of the span expansion initiative. Builds on Phase A's span construction with deeper signal and model improvements: validated speaker diarization, music-bed detection tuning, FM retasked from generic scanning to structured boundary extraction on suspicious regions, fingerprint full-span recovery via anchor-aware alignment, and selective typed redaction.

Phase B items have higher implementation risk or depend on Phase A infrastructure being in place. Expert-reviewed design in docs/plans/2026-04-12-span-expansion-design.md.

title: A4: ASRVocabularyProvider — Sponsor vocabulary biasing for ASR
description:
## Background
Many anchor misses are ASR misses — the speech recognizer doesn't know sponsor names, domain stems, or promo codes. Apple's Speech framework may expose vocabulary biasing through contextualStrings on SFSpeechRecognitionRequest (legacy path). However, the Playhead codebase uses the iOS 26+ SpeechAnalyzer / SpeechTranscriber API exclusively — whether SpeechTranscriber supports contextualStrings or an equivalent biasing mechanism needs verification against actual iOS 26 SDK headers before building this.

## BLOCKERS — must verify before implementation
1. **Does SpeechTranscriber (iOS 26+) support contextualStrings or vocabulary biasing?** The codebase uses SpeechTranscriber(locale:preset:), not SFSpeechRecognitionRequest. Check iOS 26 SDK headers for SpeechTranscriber, SpeechAnalyzer, or related types for any contextualStrings / customVocabulary / biasing API. If no biasing API exists on SpeechTranscriber, this bead may be infeasible on the current ASR path.
2. **AnalysisContext is NOT a real type** — the bead originally referenced AnalysisContext.contextualStrings, which does not exist in Apple's Speech framework or anywhere in the codebase. Remove from scope.

## What to build (contingent on blocker #1)
New file: Playhead/Services/TranscriptEngine/ASRVocabularyProvider.swift

Pulls vocabulary from knowledge stores and compiles into contextualStrings for the active ASR path (SpeechTranscriber, not SFSpeechRecognitionRequest).

Strict priority budget (active sponsors first, in case Apple caps the number):
1. Active sponsor names for this show (from SponsorKnowledgeStore.activeEntries(forPodcast:) -> [SponsorKnowledgeEntry].entityValue + .aliases)
2. Current sponsor lexicon for this podcast (from PodcastProfile.sponsorLexicon, comma-separated string)
3. Domain stems and spoken URL templates ('betterhelp', 'betterhelp dot com slash podcast')
4. ~~Show title + host names (from PodcastProfile)~~ — PodcastProfile does NOT have title or host fields. Would need to source from elsewhere (runtime? podcast RSS metadata?) or defer.
5. ~~Top historical sponsors from fingerprint store~~ — AdCopyFingerprintStore.activeEntries(forPodcast:) returns FingerprintEntry with normalizedText (full ad copy) and fingerprintHash, NOT structured sponsor names. Extracting sponsors from ad copy text would require NLP/heuristics. Consider using SponsorKnowledgeStore entries in .decayed state instead.
6. Promo-code templates (only when podcast-specific) — no existing source for promo codes; would need to be extracted from SponsorKnowledgeStore metadata or a new field.

## Codebase facts
- TranscriptEngine.swift uses SpeechAnalyzer + SpeechTranscriber (iOS 26+), NOT SFSpeechRecognitionRequest
- SpeechTranscriber is created per-shard in AppleSpeechRecognizer.transcribe(shard:) at line 426
- SponsorKnowledgeStore (actor) at Playhead/Services/AdDetection/SponsorKnowledgeStore.swift
- PodcastProfile (struct) at Playhead/Persistence/AnalysisStore/AnalysisStore.swift:180 — has sponsorLexicon: String? but NO showTitle or hostNames
- AdCopyFingerprintStore at Playhead/Services/AdDetection/AdCopyFingerprintStore.swift — has activeEntries(forPodcast:) returning [FingerprintEntry] with normalizedText, not sponsor names
- CompiledSponsorLexicon at Playhead/Services/AdDetection/CompiledSponsorLexicon.swift — compiles active SponsorKnowledgeStore entries into regex patterns
- contextualStrings is not used anywhere in the codebase currently

## Integration point
ASRVocabularyProvider would be called in AppleSpeechRecognizer.transcribe(shard:) before creating the SpeechTranscriber — but only if the SpeechTranscriber API accepts vocabulary hints.

## Acceptance criteria
- Verify SpeechTranscriber supports vocabulary biasing (blocker)
- Provider compiles vocabulary from available sources (SponsorKnowledgeStore, PodcastProfile.sponsorLexicon)
- Priority ordering is correct (active sponsors first)
- Integration with TranscriptEngine wired (if API supports it)
- Unit tests for vocabulary compilation and priority ordering
- Test that empty knowledge stores produce empty vocabulary gracefully

title: Phase A: Span Expansion — Fast, Low-Risk Wins
description:
Epic for Phase A of the span expansion initiative. The current ad detection pipeline seeds on strong CTA evidence (URLs, promo codes, disclosure phrases) and never grows that seed into the full ad span. Host-read ads commonly run 45–90s, but the 30s lexical merge window means the sponsor intro and CTA land in separate clusters — only the CTA cluster becomes a candidate. Result: detecting the last 10–20% of most host-read ads.

Phase A fixes this with fast, low-risk wins: auto-expanding machine seeds, hypothesis-based span construction, ASR vocabulary biasing, seconds-based multi-cue snapping, and metrics to measure it all. Expert-reviewed design in docs/plans/2026-04-12-span-expansion-design.md.

Key design principle: SpanHypothesisEngine is the single owner of provisional span boundaries. TimeBoundaryResolver is the only component allowed to snap.

title: A3: Wire hypothesis windows into LexicalScanner output path
description:
## Background
LexicalScanner stays stateless — it keeps emitting LexicalHits. The 30s merge logic remains as a fallback for when no hypothesis is active. But the primary merge path now flows through SpanHypothesisEngine.

## What to build

### Hypothesis lifecycle wiring
1. When LexicalScanner emits a hit with category .sponsor (including sponsor lexicon matches at weight 1.5), .promoCode, or .urlCTA, route it to SpanHypothesisEngine as a seed event. Note: LexicalPatternCategory does NOT have .disclosurePhrase — disclosure patterns are .sponsor category in LexicalScanner. The separate EvidenceCategory.disclosurePhrase in EvidenceCatalogBuilder is a different pipeline stage and not relevant here.
2. While hypothesis is open, ALL incoming lexical hits contribute as body evidence — including weaker ones (e.g. .purchaseLanguage, .transitionMarker) that normally fall below the 2-hit minimum
3. On closing anchor (CTA, URL, promo code): engine transitions to confirmed, then boundary refinement produces the final span edges. Note: BoundaryExpander.expand() currently takes (seed:featureWindows:transcriptChunks:adWindows:) -> ExpandedBoundary. This API was designed for single user-tap expansion, not hypothesis-window closing. Either adapt the existing API or introduce a new boundary resolution path for hypothesis windows. TimeBoundaryResolver does not exist yet — if needed, create it or clarify whether BoundaryExpander covers this.
4. On explicit return marker (.transitionMarker hits like "back to the show"): close immediately, snap backward
5. On timeout/idle-gap: apply fallback rules from A2

### Disclosure single-hit bypass
When a .sponsor hit (which includes built-in disclosure phrases like "brought to you by", "sponsored by", etc.) co-occurs with a sponsor lexicon match (weight 1.5) in the same hypothesis window, bypass the 2-hit minimum (minHitsForCandidate = 2, enforced in LexicalScanner.buildCandidate). This improves recall on sponsor intros that currently get dropped as isolated single hits. Note: LexicalScanner already has a highWeightBypassThreshold (0.95) that promotes single high-weight hits — sponsor lexicon hits at weight 1.5 already bypass this. The new bypass here targets the case where a built-in .sponsor hit (weight 1.0) co-occurs with a lexicon hit, reinforcing each other.

### Integration into AdDetectionService
Wire SpanHypothesisEngine into AdDetectionService.swift. Clarify the integration point:
- **Hot path** (runHotPath): LexicalScanner -> classifier -> AdWindows. SpanHypothesisEngine could sit between LexicalScanner output and the classifier to improve candidate region quality.
- **Backfill pipeline**: LexicalScanner is NOT directly upstream of MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder. The backfill flow is: TranscriptAtomizer -> EvidenceCatalogBuilder -> RegionProposalBuilder -> RegionFeatureExtractor -> AtomEvidenceProjector -> MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder. LexicalScanner feeds the hot path and BoundaryExpander's lexical signal, but not the backfill span decoder chain.
- Decide whether SpanHypothesisEngine wires into the hot path, the backfill path, or both.

## Output type
The spec originally referenced CandidateAdSpan as the output type. This does not exist in the codebase. Candidate types that DO exist: LexicalCandidate (from LexicalScanner), AdWindow (from AdDetectionService), DecodedSpan (from MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder). Define the output type or map to an existing one.

## Acceptance criteria
- LexicalScanner output routes to SpanHypothesisEngine when hypothesis is active
- 30s merge fallback still works when no hypothesis is active
- Disclosure + sponsor lexicon bypass fires correctly
- Body evidence accumulates during open windows
- Output spans emitted with correct boundaries (type TBD — see output type note)
- AdDetectionService pipeline wired correctly (hot path, backfill, or both — see integration note)
- Integration tests: synthetic episode with known sponsor intro -> body -> CTA pattern produces full-span detection
- Regression tests: existing detection behavior preserved when no hypothesis fires

title: A4: Alternative transcript rescans for weak-anchor recovery
description:
## Background
Even with vocabulary biasing, the top transcript may miss sponsor names. When the primary scan finds nothing but context suggests an ad (e.g., open hypothesis, sponsor neighborhood), rescanning low-confidence regions can recover missed anchors.

## What to build

### 1. Investigate SpeechTranscriber alternative-transcription surface
The codebase uses iOS 26+ SpeechAnalyzer / SpeechTranscriber — NOT SFSpeechRecognizer / SFSpeechRecognitionResult. The old SFSpeechRecognitionResult exposed a `transcriptions` array with alternatives; the new SpeechTranscriber.Result uses AttributedString runs with per-run `transcriptionConfidence`.

**Before implementing**: verify whether `SpeechTranscriber.Result` exposes alternative transcriptions at all. If it does not, pivot strategy to use per-word/per-run confidence scores as the weak-anchor signal (low-confidence runs are the regions most likely to have misrecognized sponsor names).

### 2. Add weak-anchor metadata to TranscriptChunk
Add a field to `TranscriptChunk` (in `Playhead/Persistence/AnalysisStore/AnalysisStore.swift:85`) carrying ASR confidence or alternative data from `SpeechTranscriber.Result`. The field must be:
- A proper `Sendable`, `Codable` struct (not a bare tuple — TranscriptChunk is Sendable and persisted to SQLite)
- Populated in `TranscriptEngineService.transcribeShard()` (`TranscriptEngineService.swift:404`) where TranscriptChunks are created from TranscriptSegments
- The upstream data flows: `SpeechTranscriber.Result` → `extractWords()` (TranscriptEngine.swift:642) → `RecognitionSnapshot` → `TranscriptSegment` → `TranscriptChunk`. The alternative/confidence data must be threaded through this chain.

### 3. Add `rescanAlternatives(chunks:nearTime:radius:)` to LexicalScanner
LexicalScanner (`Playhead/Services/AdDetection/LexicalScanner.swift`) currently has `scan(chunks:analysisAssetId:)` and `scanChunk(_:)`. Add a method that re-scans only alternative/low-confidence text from chunks within a time window. This must use the same pattern-matching pipeline (built-in patterns, strong URLs, show sponsor patterns, compiled lexicon).

### 4. SpanHypothesisEngine scoped rescans (depends on playhead-y9u)
SpanHypothesisEngine (not yet implemented — dependency playhead-y9u) calls rescanAlternatives() ONLY inside:
- Open confirmed hypotheses (looking for closing anchor)
- Sponsor/disclosure neighborhoods (looking for missed intro)
- Low-confidence likely-ad regions
Never rescan alternatives globally — that would be expensive and noisy.

## Acceptance criteria
- Investigation of SpeechTranscriber alternative-transcription API documented
- TranscriptChunk carries weak-anchor metadata (confidence or alternatives) from ASR result
- Metadata field is a proper Codable/Sendable struct, not a bare tuple
- Data threaded through the full chain: SpeechTranscriber.Result → RecognitionSnapshot → TranscriptSegment → TranscriptChunk
- LexicalScanner rescanAlternatives() finds patterns in alternative/low-confidence texts
- Rescans are scoped (not global)
- SpanHypothesisEngine triggers rescans at appropriate moments (after playhead-y9u lands)
- Unit tests for alternative rescan with synthetic chunks
- Test that global rescan is not possible (scoping enforced)

title: A2: SpanHypothesisConfig — Anchor-type-aware configuration
description:
## Background
The SpanHypothesisEngine needs configurable, anchor-type-aware parameters for rapid iteration. These were explicitly requested to live in a config struct rather than hardcoded.

## What to build
New file: Playhead/Services/AdDetection/SpanHypothesisConfig.swift

### Types defined in this file

**AnchorType enum** (consumed by both config and engine):
```swift
enum AnchorType: Sendable {
    case disclosure
    case sponsorLexicon
    case url
    case promoCode
    case fmPositive
    case transitionMarker
}
```

**AnchorPolarity enum** (consumed by both config and engine):
```swift
enum AnchorPolarity: Sendable {
    case startAnchored   // disclosure, sponsor intro — search forward
    case endAnchored     // CTA, URL, promo code — search backward
    case neutral         // FM-positive — search both directions
}
```

**AnchorTypeConfig struct** — per-anchor-type parameters:
```swift
struct AnchorTypeConfig: Sendable {
    let polarity: AnchorPolarity
    let windowDuration: TimeInterval
    let backwardSearchRadius: TimeInterval
    let forwardSearchRadius: TimeInterval
}
```

**SpanHypothesisConfig struct** — top-level config (Sendable, with static let `default`):

Per-anchor-type configuration table (via `[AnchorType: AnchorTypeConfig]`):
| Anchor Type | Polarity | Window Duration | Backward Search | Forward Search |
|-------------|----------|----------------|-----------------|----------------|
| disclosure / sponsorLexicon | startAnchored | 90s | 15s | 90s |
| url / promoCode | endAnchored | 75s | 75s | 15s |
| fmPositive | neutral | 60s | 30s | 30s |
| transitionMarker | endAnchored | 60s | 60s | 5s |

Global parameters:
- maxIdleGapSeconds: 20s
- evidenceDecayRate: 0.95/s
- minConfirmedEvidence: 2.5
- minBodyWeight: 1.5 (for timeout-emitted backfill candidates)

### Codebase conventions to follow
- All config structs in AdDetection use `Sendable` conformance
- Provide `static let default` with the design-doc values
- Use `TimeInterval` for durations (matching existing patterns like LexicalScannerConfig)
- Provide a convenience method `config(for anchorType: AnchorType) -> AnchorTypeConfig` for lookup

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AnchorType and AnchorPolarity enums defined with Sendable conformance
- [ ] AnchorTypeConfig struct defined with polarity, windowDuration, backwardSearchRadius, forwardSearchRadius
- [ ] SpanHypothesisConfig struct with per-anchor-type dictionary and global parameters
- [ ] All values configurable (init with defaults, not hardcoded)
- [ ] `static let default` matches the design doc table values exactly
- [ ] Convenience lookup method for per-anchor-type config
- [ ] Unit test validates all default config values against design doc
- [ ] Unit test validates lookup for each anchor type returns expected config

title: A5: Wire TimeBoundaryResolver into existing components
description:
## Background
TimeBoundaryResolver replaces boundary logic in multiple existing components. This bead handles the wiring.

## What to change

### MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder.swift
- Convert mergeGapAtoms (3) → mergeGapSeconds (config, default ~3s)
- Convert boundarySnapRadiusAtoms (15) → snapRadiusSeconds (config, default ~8s)
- **Note**: atoms are variable-length transcript segments (1–5 per second), so the current atom-count approach was chosen for transcript-density invariance (see DecoderConstants comment at DecodedSpan.swift:47). Converting to seconds sacrifices this invariance — accepted tradeoff per design doc.
- Remove Step 4 (applyBoundarySnap) entirely when operating on hypothesis-owned spans. Requires new parameter or code path to distinguish hypothesis-owned vs legacy evidence, since the decoder currently has no hypothesis concept.
- Becomes fallback reducer for legacy / non-hypothesis evidence only

### SkipOrchestrator.swift
- Remove snapBoundary() method (line 933–971) and SnapDirection enum (line 927–929)
- Remove config fields: boundarySnapMaxDistance, silenceThreshold (lines 81, 83, defaults at 95–96)
- Update 3 call sites that use snapBoundary(): receiveAdWindows (line 402–403), receiveAdDecisionResults (line 447–448), injectMarkAsAdWindow (line 1044–1045) — pass times through unsnapped
- Consume finalized spans only — does not discover or move boundaries

### BoundaryExpander.swift
- Delegate silence scoring (scoreFeatureWindow at line 221–225: pause * 0.7 + rms * 0.3) to TimeBoundaryResolver.snap() with boundary type and distance penalty
- Replace findAcousticBoundary (line 228–265) and snapToNearestSilence (line 344–373) with TimeBoundaryResolver calls
- Accept anchor-type config for asymmetric radii (overlap with A3 auto-expand)

### NOT in scope but needs tracking
- **BoundaryRefiner.swift** (line 6–65): Separate boundary-snapping helper used by ClassifierService (line 378) and AdDetectionService (lines 640, 1048). Not mentioned in design doc or any bead. Needs its own bead or inclusion here to satisfy "no component other than TimeBoundaryResolver performs snapping."
- **TargetedWindowNarrower.swift**: Performs acoustic-break-based edge snapping (acousticBreakSnapMaxDistanceSeconds, line 494+). Not mentioned in design doc or any bead. Same ownership concern.

## Boundary ownership principle
- SpanHypothesisEngine: owns provisional boundaries
- TimeBoundaryResolver: only snapper
- MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder: fallback reducer, no snapping
- SkipOrchestrator: consumer only
- **Gap**: BoundaryRefiner and TargetedWindowNarrower also snap boundaries today but are not addressed in any bead

## Acceptance criteria
- MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder uses seconds not atoms for merge gap and snap radius
- MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder skips boundary snap (Step 4) for hypothesis-owned spans
- SkipOrchestrator.snapBoundary() removed along with config fields
- BoundaryExpander delegates to TimeBoundaryResolver
- Existing tests updated: MinimalContiguousSpanDecoderTests, BoundaryExpanderTests, SkipOrchestratorRevertTests
- No component other than TimeBoundaryResolver performs snapping (requires BoundaryRefiner + TargetedWindowNarrower beads)
- Regression tests: skip orchestrator still works with finalized spans
notes: Created follow-up beads playhead-9ua.1 and playhead-9ua.2 for the remaining BoundaryRefiner and TargetedWindowNarrower snapping debt. Also hardened finalized-span pass-through coverage in UserMarkedAdInjectionTests before closeout.

title: A3: Auto-apply BoundaryExpander to machine-found seeds
description:
## Background
BoundaryExpander already has the logic to expand a single point into a fuller ad span using ±60s acoustic and ±90s lexical search (hardcoded private let properties at lines 40-43 of BoundaryExpander.swift). Today its only production caller is NowPlayingViewModel.swift line 230 (user-tap "hearing an ad" flow). The expert recommendation: whenever a strong anchor fires, treat it as a seed and immediately expand it.

## What to build

### Part 1: Configurable asymmetric radii (API change)
Add an ExpansionConfig struct to BoundaryExpander.swift with:
- backwardAcousticRadius / forwardAcousticRadius (default: 60s each, preserves current behavior)
- backwardLexicalRadius / forwardLexicalRadius (default: 90s each, preserves current behavior)
- fallbackHalfWidth (default: 30s)

Modify expand() to accept an optional ExpansionConfig parameter (nil = use defaults for backwards compatibility). Wire the per-direction radii into findAcousticBoundary() and findLexicalBoundaries().

Anchor-type presets (static factory methods on ExpansionConfig):
- .endAnchored (CTA/URL/promo): backward acoustic 90s, forward acoustic 20s; backward lexical 120s, forward lexical 30s
- .startAnchored (disclosure): backward acoustic 20s, forward acoustic 90s; backward lexical 30s, forward lexical 120s
- .neutral (fmPositive): symmetric 60s/90s (same as current defaults)

NOTE: These radii are BoundaryExpander's own search radii, distinct from SpanHypothesisConfig's window/search parameters in playhead-dza. BoundaryExpander radii control how far expand() looks for silence and lexical markers around a seed point.

### Part 2: Auto-expand on confirmed hypothesis (wiring)
When SpanHypothesisEngine emits a confirmed hypothesis, call BoundaryExpander.expand() with:
- seed = the hypothesis's best candidate time (startCandidateTime for startAnchored, endCandidateTime for endAnchored)
- config = ExpansionConfig preset matching the hypothesis's polarity
- Feed result back to the hypothesis as expandedBoundary

## Acceptance criteria
- ExpansionConfig struct with asymmetric radii and static presets
- expand() accepts optional config, defaults to symmetric (backwards compatible)
- Existing NowPlayingViewModel caller unchanged (still works without config)
- SpanHypothesisEngine calls expand() on confirmed hypotheses with polarity-matched config
- Unit tests for asymmetric expansion (endAnchored searches further backward, startAnchored searches further forward)
- Unit tests confirming default config matches current 60/90 behavior exactly
- Integration test: CTA-only seed with .endAnchored config expands backward further than forward

## Dependency note
Depends on playhead-y9u (SpanHypothesisEngine, the caller) and playhead-dza (SpanHypothesisConfig, polarity definitions). The dependency on playhead-348 (TimeBoundaryResolver) should be REMOVED. TimeBoundaryResolver handles multi-cue snapping which is a separate concern wired by playhead-gji. BoundaryExpander has its own acoustic+lexical search that does not use TimeBoundaryResolver.

title: A2: SpanHypothesisEngine — Core state machine with sponsor identity and polarity
description:
## Background
This is the centerpiece of the span expansion work. Today, LexicalScanner merges hits within a fixed 30s gap and the pipeline only detects the CTA tail of host-read ads. SpanHypothesisEngine replaces this with an explicit hypothesis lifecycle that tracks sponsor identity, anchor polarity, idle gaps, and evidence decay.

## What to build
New file: Playhead/Services/AdDetection/SpanHypothesisEngine.swift

### Types this bead creates (all in the same file unless they grow large)

**AnchorType** enum: disclosure, sponsorLexicon, url, promoCode, fmPositive, transitionMarker

**AnchorPolarity** enum: startAnchored, endAnchored, neutral — controls asymmetric search direction per anchor type.

**AnchorEvent** struct: wraps an incoming signal that can seed or close a hypothesis. Fields: anchorType (AnchorType), matchedText (String), startTime (Double), endTime (Double), weight (Double), sponsorEntity (NormalizedSponsor?). Constructed from LexicalHit (mapping LexicalPatternCategory → AnchorType) or from FM/fingerprint results in later beads.

**NormalizedSponsor** struct (or enum with associated value): a lowercased, whitespace-trimmed sponsor identity string used for entity-aware merging. Extraction logic: when a LexicalHit has category .sponsor, extract the sponsor name from matchedText by stripping the disclosure prefix (e.g. "brought to you by X" → "X"). When category is .promoCode, extract from "use code X at Y" → "Y". When no entity can be extracted, sponsorEntity is nil. Keep extraction simple — it will be refined in later beads.

**BodyEvidenceItem** struct: fields: matchedText (String), timestamp (Double), weight (Double), category (LexicalPatternCategory). Represents a non-anchor lexical hit that corroborates an open hypothesis.

**CandidateAdSpan** struct: the output type emitted when a hypothesis closes. Fields: id (String), analysisAssetId (String), startTime (Double), endTime (Double), confidence (Double), evidenceScore (Double), anchorType (AnchorType), sponsorEntity (NormalizedSponsor?), isSkipEligible (Bool), evidenceText (String), closingReason (ClosingReason). This replaces LexicalCandidate as the downstream type in the span-expansion pipeline.

**ClosingReason** enum: explicitClose (CTA/URL/promo), returnMarker, timeout, idleGap.

### Types this bead consumes from existing code
- **LexicalHit** (LexicalScanner.swift:72): category, matchedText, startTime, endTime, weight. The engine maps these to AnchorEvent or BodyEvidenceItem based on category and weight.
- **ExpandedBoundary** (BoundaryExpander.swift:23): startTime, endTime, boundaryConfidence, source. Note: the current BoundaryExpander.expand() API is designed for user-tap seeds, not hypothesis-engine use. This bead stores an optional ExpandedBoundary on the hypothesis struct but does NOT call BoundaryExpander directly — that wiring happens in playhead-gji (A5: Wire TimeBoundaryResolver).
- **SpanHypothesisConfig** from dependency playhead-dza. Until that lands, use hardcoded defaults matching the design doc table.

### State machine: idle → seeded → accumulating → confirmed → closed

**AdHypothesis** struct with:
- seedAnchor: AnchorEvent, seedTime: Double, anchorType: AnchorType
- sponsorEntity: NormalizedSponsor? — extracted sponsor identity for entity-aware merging
- polarity: AnchorPolarity — controls search direction
- bodyEvidence: [BodyEvidenceItem] with timestamps and weights
- closingAnchor: AnchorEvent?, windowDuration: Double
- expandedBoundary: ExpandedBoundary? — populated later by TimeBoundaryResolver (not this bead)
- evidenceScore: Double, confidence: Double, lastEvidenceTime: Double
- startCandidateTime: Double, endCandidateTime: Double

### Key behaviors
- Consumes AnchorEvents (mapped from LexicalHits via a mapping function this bead provides)
- Opens hypothesis on strong anchor (disclosure, sponsor lexicon, URL, promo code)
- Polarity determines asymmetric search direction
- maxIdleGapSeconds (default 20s): close if no evidence arrives
- evidenceDecayRate (default 0.95/s): older evidence contributes less
- Sponsor-entity compatibility: evidence mentioning a different sponsor does not contribute
- Close explicitly on CTA/URL/promo hit → confirmed → emit CandidateAdSpan with isSkipEligible=true
- Close on explicit return markers only ('back to the show', 'back to the episode'). Generic markers (anyway, moving on) are weak evidence, never close alone.
- Close on timeout: emit CandidateAdSpan with isSkipEligible=false UNLESS evidenceScore > minConfirmedEvidence AND has plausible start+end
- Close on idle gap: emit CandidateAdSpan with whatever has accumulated
- Overlapping hypotheses: merge only if sponsor entity matches OR one side lacks entity and overlap exceeds stricter threshold

### LexicalHit → AnchorEvent mapping
Provide a static function mapToAnchorEvent(_ hit: LexicalHit) -> AnchorEvent? that:
- .sponsor with weight >= 1.0 → AnchorType.sponsorLexicon (or .disclosure if matchedText contains disclosure phrases like "brought to you by", "sponsored by", etc.)
- .promoCode → AnchorType.promoCode
- .urlCTA with weight >= 0.95 → AnchorType.url
- .transitionMarker → AnchorType.transitionMarker
- .purchaseLanguage, weak .urlCTA → nil (these become BodyEvidenceItem, not anchors)

### Design principle
SpanHypothesisEngine is the SINGLE OWNER of provisional span boundaries. No other component discovers or relocates boundaries.

### NOT in scope for this bead
- Calling BoundaryExpander or TimeBoundaryResolver (that is playhead-gji)
- Wiring into LexicalScanner output path (that is playhead-c0e)
- FM result consumption (that is playhead-5p7)
- Fingerprint match consumption (that is playhead-nqx)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All new types (AnchorType, AnchorPolarity, AnchorEvent, NormalizedSponsor, BodyEvidenceItem, CandidateAdSpan, ClosingReason) defined with Sendable conformance
- [ ] LexicalHit → AnchorEvent mapping function works for all LexicalPatternCategory values
- [ ] NormalizedSponsor extraction from sponsor disclosure matchedText
- [ ] State machine transitions work correctly for all paths (idle→seeded→accumulating→confirmed→closed)
- [ ] Polarity correctly biases search direction (startAnchored searches forward, endAnchored backward)
- [ ] Sponsor entity tracking prevents cross-sponsor merging
- [ ] Idle gap (20s default) closes hypotheses appropriately
- [ ] Evidence decay reduces stale evidence weight (0.95/s)
- [ ] Generic discourse markers ('anyway', 'moving on') contribute weak evidence but never close alone
- [ ] Explicit return markers ('back to the show', 'back to the episode') close immediately
- [ ] Timeout-only spans emit CandidateAdSpan with isSkipEligible=false unless evidence threshold met
- [ ] CandidateAdSpan.closingReason correctly reflects how the hypothesis closed
- [ ] Comprehensive unit tests for each state transition
- [ ] Tests for overlapping hypothesis merging logic
- [ ] Tests for sponsor-entity compatibility filtering
- [ ] Tests for LexicalHit → AnchorEvent mapping

title: Transcript peek: select range to mark as 'not an ad'

title: Boundary expansion for user-marked ad corrections
description:
When a user marks a point as "hearing an ad" (single playback position, no chunk selection), the system should automatically find the ad's start and end boundaries rather than logging a whole-episode correction.

## Current state

"Hearing an ad" (NowPlayingViewModel.swift:201) records a CorrectionEvent with scope exactSpan(assetId, 0...Int.max) — the entire episode. The comment at lines 214-217 acknowledges this gap: "mapping playback time to an atom ordinal requires the atom index, which isn't available here." No boundary detection runs.

## Approach: multi-signal boundary search

Given the user's current playback position as the seed point, search outward in both directions using existing infrastructure:

### Signal 1: Acoustic boundaries (FeatureWindow)
- SkipOrchestrator.snapBoundary(time:direction:) finds silence/low-energy points using cached FeatureWindow data. NOTE: snapBoundary and SnapDirection are both **private** — BoundaryExpander cannot call them directly. Either change access to internal, or extract the scoring logic (pauseProbability * 0.7 + quietScore * 0.3) into a shared utility.
- snapBoundary scores candidates using **pauseProbability and RMS only** (combined = pauseProbability * 0.7 + quietScore * 0.3, where quietScore = max(0, 1 - rms * 10)). It does NOT use spectralFlux or musicProbability. musicProbability is hardcoded to 0 in FeatureExtraction.swift:229 ("Requires ML model — deferred") and cannot be used as a signal.
- Search backward from seed for ad start: find nearest high-pauseProbability/low-RMS point within ±60s
- Search forward from seed for ad end: same criteria
- This gives a rough boundary estimate

### Signal 2: Transcript pattern matching (LexicalScanner)
- Run LexicalScanner on transcript chunks near the seed point (±90s window)
- Look for sponsor intro patterns ("brought to you by", "this episode is sponsored") backward from seed
- Look for transition patterns ("now back to", "let's get back") forward from seed
- Narrow the acoustic boundaries if lexical markers are found

### Signal 3: Existing ad windows
- Check if any existing AdWindows (even suppressed/candidate ones) overlap or adjoin the seed point
- NOTE: AnalysisStore.fetchAdWindows(assetId:) returns ALL windows for an asset with no time-range filter parameter. Must filter in memory after fetching, or add a new fetchAdWindows(assetId:inRange:) method.
- If overlapping windows exist, adopt their boundaries rather than computing new ones
- This handles the case where the system detected something but didn't have enough confidence to act

### Fallback
- If no clear boundaries found, use a default window: seed ± 30s, snapped to nearest silence points
- Mark with low boundary confidence so the system doesn't over-trust the estimate

## Output
- Expanded time range (startTime, endTime) with boundaryConfidence
- Fed into sibling bead (playhead-98q) for immediate skip cue injection
- Persisted as AdWindow with boundaryState="userExpanded"

## Files
- NEW: BoundaryExpander.swift in Services/AdDetection/ — stateless utility that takes seed time + [FeatureWindow] + [TranscriptChunk] and returns expanded boundaries. Must either duplicate snapBoundary's scoring logic or consume a shared extraction of it.
- NowPlayingViewModel.swift — reportHearingAd() calls BoundaryExpander before injecting the skip cue
- SkipOrchestrator.swift — snapBoundary exists at line 799 (private); access or logic extraction needed

## Acceptance criteria
- User taps "Hearing an ad" at 5:30 in an episode with a host-read ad from 5:00-6:00 → system finds boundaries near 5:00 and 6:00
- Boundaries snap to silence/low-energy transitions using pauseProbability + RMS (not musicProbability or spectralFlux)
- If lexical markers exist ("brought to you by" at 4:58), start boundary uses them
- If an existing suppressed AdWindow covers 4:55-6:05, those boundaries are adopted instead (fetched via fetchAdWindows(assetId:), filtered in memory)
- Fallback (no signals): window is seed ± 30s snapped to silence, with low boundaryConfidence
- Expanded boundaries fed to immediate skip cue injection (playhead-98q)
- Works with available data only — does not block on backfill or trigger new transcription
notes:
Code review of existing infrastructure references (2026-04-10):

1. snapBoundary is PRIVATE — BoundaryExpander cannot compose it without changing access level. SnapDirection enum is also private.

2. The type is FeatureWindow (singular), not 'FeatureWindows'. musicProbability is hardcoded to 0 (deferred ML model) so using it as a signal is useless. snapBoundary only uses pauseProbability and rms — not spectralFlux or musicProbability as the bead describes.

3. LexicalScanner API is accurately described — scan(chunks:analysisAssetId:) accepts any [TranscriptChunk] subset. ACCURATE.

4. reportHearingAd() exists at line 201 and does what the bead says. The atom-ordinal comment is at lines 214-217 (not 215-218). Minor line number error.

5. No time-range query for AdWindows exists. fetchAdWindows(assetId:) returns ALL windows for an asset. In-memory filtering is needed.

6. Services/AdDetection/ directory exists. ACCURATE.

Action items before implementation:
- Either make snapBoundary (and SnapDirection) internal/public, or duplicate the logic in BoundaryExpander
- Remove musicProbability from the signal design (always 0)
- Add a fetchAdWindows(assetId:inRange:) method to AnalysisStore, or plan for in-memory filtering
- Fix line number reference: 214-217 not 215-218
close_reason: BoundaryExpander.swift + 12 tests. Multi-signal boundary expansion: existing windows > acoustic+lexical > acoustic > fallback.

title: Real-time 'not an ad' correction with immediate revert + UI update
description:
When a user marks a segment as NOT an ad (via banner 'Not an ad' button or AdRegionPopover 'This isn't an ad'), the system should immediately:

1. **Remove the skip cue** — call SkipOrchestrator to revert the ManagedWindow and remove it from active cues
2. **Update timeline markers** — broadcastAppliedSegments() so TimelineRailView removes the ad segment immediately
3. **Update transcript peek** — the region should no longer appear as an ad span
4. **Update database** — set AdWindow.decisionState to .reverted, same as "Listen" does
5. **Feed trust scoring** — record false-positive signal on PodcastProfile

## Current state

"Not an ad" from banner (NowPlayingView.swift:92-113) only records a CorrectionEvent with .manualVeto source. The skip cue remains active, timeline still shows the ad, transcript still highlights it. The correction only suppresses confidence on the next backfill run.

"This isn't an ad" from AdRegionPopover (AdRegionPopover.swift button UI at lines 88-101, actual veto call at line 38 inside the .alert confirm handler) has the same problem — calls correctionStore.recordVeto(span:) which records CorrectionEvent(s) but no immediate UI/playback effect.

**Critical finding: "Listen" has the same gap.** NowPlayingViewModel.handleListenRewind (line 180) calls runtime.recordListenRewind() (PlayheadRuntime.swift:848) → adDetectionService.recordListenRewind() (AdDetectionService.swift:1503), which updates SQLite (AdWindow.decisionState -> .reverted, PodcastProfile trust scoring) but does NOT call SkipOrchestrator. The skip cue is NOT removed from memory, broadcastAppliedSegments() is NOT called, and the timeline is NOT updated in real-time.

SkipOrchestrator.recordListenRevert() (line 514) exists and DOES the right thing — reverts in-memory state (lines 517-519), persists to SQLite (line 529), signals trust via TrustScoringService (lines 538-539), persists CorrectionEvent (lines 542-566), and calls evaluateAndPush() (line 570) which internally calls broadcastAppliedSegments() (line 686). But it is never called from production code. It is only exercised in tests. The runtime.recordListenRewind -> adDetectionService.recordListenRewind path is a parallel SQLite-only path that lacks the real-time orchestrator effects.

The seek in handleListenRewind temporarily suppresses skips via recordUserSeek (2s stability window), but after that window the orchestrator re-evaluates and the still-.applied window re-activates.

## Implementation approach

### Wire SkipOrchestrator.recordListenRevert into the "Listen" path (pre-requisite fix)
- PlayheadRuntime.recordListenRewind (line 848) should ALSO call skipOrchestrator.recordListenRevert(windowId:podcastId:). This fixes the existing "Listen" gap where the orchestrator state is never updated.
- Alternatively, replace the adDetectionService.recordListenRewind call entirely since recordListenRevert already persists via store.updateAdWindowDecision and signals trust via TrustScoringService.recordFalseSkipSignal. However, recordListenRevert does NOT update PodcastProfile.implicitFalsePositiveCount/skipTrustScore/recentFalseSkipSignals (that's in AdDetectionService.recordListenRewind). Need to reconcile these two paths.

### Banner "Not an ad" path
- NowPlayingView.swift onNotAnAd closure: after recording CorrectionEvent, also call SkipOrchestrator.recordListenRevert() (or a new recordNotAnAdRevert() that skips the seek-back)
- Key difference from "Listen": do NOT rewind playback — user has already moved past it. Just revert the window state and remove the cue.

### AdRegionPopover "This isn't an ad" path  
- After correctionStore.recordVeto(span:), also call SkipOrchestrator to revert the matching ManagedWindow
- Need to find the ManagedWindow that overlaps the DecodedSpan's time range

### SkipOrchestrator additions
- New method: `revertByTimeRange(start: CMTime, end: CMTime)` — finds overlapping ManagedWindow(s), sets decisionState=.reverted, removes from active cues, broadcasts
- Or reuse recordListenRevert() with an option to skip the seek

### Trust path reconciliation
- SkipOrchestrator.recordListenRevert uses TrustScoringService.recordFalseSkipSignal (if trust service wired)
- AdDetectionService.recordListenRewind manually updates PodcastProfile fields (implicitFalsePositiveCount, skipTrustScore, recentFalseSkipSignals)
- These are redundant/divergent. Consolidate into one path, likely through TrustScoringService.

## Files
- SkipOrchestrator.swift (add revertByTimeRange or extend recordListenRevert)
- PlayheadRuntime.swift (wire skipOrchestrator.recordListenRevert into recordListenRewind at line 848)
- NowPlayingView.swift (update onNotAnAd closure)
- NowPlayingViewModel.swift (add revert method for popover path)
- AdRegionPopover.swift (call revert after veto)
- AdDetectionService.swift (reconcile recordListenRewind with SkipOrchestrator path)

## Acceptance criteria
- Tapping "Not an ad" on banner removes ad marker from timeline within 1 frame
- Tapping "This isn't an ad" in popover removes ad marker from timeline
- Tapping "Listen" on banner removes ad marker from timeline (fixing existing gap)
- Transcript peek no longer shows the region as an ad span
- AdWindow.decisionState set to .reverted in SQLite
- Skip cue removed — if another ad would have been auto-skipped in that range, it no longer is
- Playback does NOT rewind for "Not an ad" (unlike "Listen" which seeks back)
- Trust scoring receives false-positive signal through a single consolidated path
- CorrectionEvent still recorded (existing behavior preserved)
notes:
Code review pass 1 (2026-04-11): Fixed 1 inaccuracy in description:
1. Line reference 'adDetectionService.recordListenRewind() at line 1446' was wrong — runtime method is at PlayheadRuntime.swift:848 (calls at line 850), adDetectionService method is at AdDetectionService.swift:1503. Fixed both references.
Also clarified that broadcastAppliedSegments() is called indirectly via evaluateAndPush() (line 570→686), not directly from recordListenRevert.
close_reason: Wired SkipOrchestrator revert into Listen/Not-an-ad/Popover paths. Fixed existing gap. 7 tests. Trust signal consolidated.

title: Real-time 'mark as ad' correction with immediate skip + UI update
description:
When a user marks a segment as an ad (via 'Hearing an ad' button or transcript chunk selection), the system should immediately:

1. **Create a synthetic skip cue** — inject a ManagedWindow into SkipOrchestrator with high confidence and decisionState=.confirmed, keyed as user-corrected
2. **Skip playback** — if playhead is inside the marked region, seek past it with duck/seek/release smoothing (executed by PlaybackService.duckSeekRelease(to:) in PlaybackTransport.swift:367, NOT SkipOrchestrator)
3. **Update timeline markers** — broadcastAppliedSegments() so TimelineRailView shows the new ad segment immediately
4. **Update transcript peek** — the marked region should appear as an ad span in TranscriptPeekView
5. **Persist to database** — create an AdWindow with decisionState=.confirmed and metadataSource="userCorrection", plus the existing CorrectionEvent

## Skip execution chain

SkipOrchestrator does NOT directly control playback. The chain is:
- SkipOrchestrator.evaluateAndPush() → pushMergedCues() → pushSkipCues() → calls skipCueHandler callback (line 880)
- PlayheadRuntime wires the callback (PlayheadRuntime.swift:512) to PlaybackService.setSkipCues()
- PlaybackService.setSkipCues() (PlaybackTransport.swift:336) stores cues in a property; skip detection uses polling via checkSkipCues(currentTime:) (PlaybackTransport.swift:341) during periodic time observation
- When playhead enters a cue range, performSkipTransition() → duckSeekRelease(to:) executes the smooth skip (duck volume, seek, restore volume)

## Current state

"Hearing an ad" (NowPlayingViewModel.swift:201) and "Mark ad" transcript selection (TranscriptPeekView.swift:432) only record a CorrectionEvent with .falseNegative source and 0...Int.max scope. No skip cue is created, no timeline update, no transcript highlight. The correction only takes effect on the next backfill run.

## Implementation approach

### SkipOrchestrator additions
- New method: `injectUserMarkedAd(start: CMTime, end: CMTime, analysisAssetId: String)` 
- Creates a ManagedWindow wrapping an AdWindow with confidence=1.0 on adWindow.confidence, decisionState=.confirmed (note: confidence lives on the nested adWindow, not as a direct ManagedWindow field; ManagedWindow has no `source` field)
- Calls evaluateAndPush() to merge into active cues and broadcast via skipCueHandler callback
- PlaybackTransport handles the actual skip execution through the existing cue mechanism

### AdDetectionService additions
- New method: `recordUserMarkedAd(analysisAssetId:, startTime:, endTime:, podcastId:)`
- Creates AdWindow row with metadataSource="userCorrection", decisionState=.confirmed
- Records CorrectionEvent with proper atom ordinal scope (not 0...Int.max)

### UI wiring
- NowPlayingViewModel.reportHearingAd() → call SkipOrchestrator.injectUserMarkedAd() + AdDetectionService.recordUserMarkedAd()
- TranscriptPeekView.submitMarkedChunks() → same, using chunk start/end times for boundaries

### Scope precision fix
- Map selected transcript chunks to actual atom ordinal ranges for the CorrectionEvent scope (TranscriptPeekView already has chunk start/end times)
- For "Hearing an ad" button (no chunk selection), use boundary expansion (see sibling bead) to determine range

## Files
- SkipOrchestrator.swift (add injectUserMarkedAd — pushes cues via callback, does not seek directly)
- PlaybackTransport.swift (no changes needed — existing duckSeekRelease handles skip smoothing)
- AdDetectionService.swift (add recordUserMarkedAd)
- NowPlayingViewModel.swift (update reportHearingAd)
- TranscriptPeekView.swift (update submitMarkedChunks)
- NowPlayingView.swift (update wiring)

## Acceptance criteria
- Tapping "Hearing an ad" creates visible ad marker on timeline within 1 frame
- If playhead is inside marked region, playback skips forward immediately (via PlaybackTransport.duckSeekRelease)
- Transcript peek shows marked region as ad span
- AdWindow persisted in SQLite with metadataSource="userCorrection"
- CorrectionEvent recorded with proper scope (not 0...Int.max when chunk data available)
- Banner appears for the new skip (showing "Skipped sponsor segment" generic copy)
- Works in .manual and .auto trust modes
notes:
Code review pass 1 (2026-04-11): Fixed 2 inaccuracies in description:
1. setSkipCues() does NOT register CMTimeRange boundary observers — it stores cues in a property; skip detection uses polling via checkSkipCues(currentTime:) at PlaybackTransport.swift:341. Fixed.
2. ManagedWindow has no direct 'confidence' or 'source' fields — confidence lives on adWindow.confidence (nested AdWindow), and there is no 'source' field on either type. Fixed description to clarify nested access pattern.

title: Fix transcript truncation: capture partial results at shard boundaries
description:
TranscriptEngine.collectSegments (line 557) discards all partial speech recognition results with 'guard result.isFinal else { continue }'. When finalizeAndFinish() is called at a shard boundary, the tail audio may still be partial and gets silently dropped — losing the last 30-60 seconds of transcript, sometimes mid-sentence.

Fix: track the latest partial result as results stream in. When a final result arrives, clear the partial (superseded). When the stream ends, if a partial remains, promote it to a segment. Only uses partials that were never finalized — no risk of duplicates.

File: Playhead/Services/TranscriptEngine/TranscriptEngine.swift, collectSegments function.

Impact: recovers lost transcript at episode/shard boundaries. Directly improves detection recall for ads in uncovered audio. Root cause contributor to issues 2 and 3 as well.
notes: Code review 2026-04-10: Description verified accurate against current codebase. TranscriptEngine.swift exists at Playhead/Services/TranscriptEngine/TranscriptEngine.swift. collectSegments is at line 549. The guard result.isFinal else { continue } pattern is at exactly line 557. finalizeAndFinish() is called at line 430. The truncation bug description accurately reflects the code behavior. No corrections needed.

title: Phase 6.5b: Confidence-gated autoSkipEligible promotion (no SponsorKnowledgeStore required)
description:
Phase 8 is the full SponsorKnowledgeStore that populates CommercialIntent + AdOwnership and unlocks autoSkipEligible via SkipPolicyMatrix. But users can't correct skips in Phase 7 if nothing is being skipped. This bead extracts just the autoSkip promotion from Phase 8 — gated purely on fusion confidence + eligibilityGate, requiring no intent/ownership data — so Phase 7 ships with a live skip loop.

**The gap:**
Even after playhead-4my.16 (detectOnly for unknown spans + runBackfill wiring), all banners are confirm-only. SkipPolicyMatrix needs (.paid, .thirdParty) to return .autoSkipEligible, and FM never classifies CommercialIntent in Phase 6. So no auto-skips fire until Phase 8.

**The insight:**
The fusion pipeline already produces a calibrated skipConfidence and an eligibilityGate. A span with gate=.eligible and skipConfidence >= threshold is, by definition, a high-confidence ad detection. That is sufficient signal to auto-skip, even without intent/ownership attribution — the attribution affects *which* policy applies, but at high enough confidence the policy outcome is the same regardless.
design:
**Mechanism: post-policy confidence promotion**

After SkipPolicyMatrix.action(for:ownership:) returns in runBackfill, apply a second promotion pass:

  if policyAction == .detectOnly || policyAction == .logOnly,
     decision.eligibilityGate == .eligible,
     decision.skipConfidence >= config.autoSkipConfidenceThreshold {
      effectiveAction = .autoSkipEligible
  }

This keeps SkipPolicyMatrix clean (policy layer, not confidence layer) and makes the threshold an explicit, tunable config parameter rather than a hardcoded constant.

**Config change:**
Add autoSkipConfidenceThreshold: Double = 0.75 to AdDetectionConfig. Default is conservative — only very high-confidence detections auto-skip. Can be lowered via config as we gain confidence in calibration.

**What does NOT change:**
- SkipPolicyMatrix logic is unchanged (Phase 8 still owns the full matrix)
- .suppress still suppresses (promotion never overrides suppress)
- .autoSkipEligible from the matrix (Phase 8) still works as before
- Gate-blocked spans (blockedByEvidenceQuorum, blockedByPolicy, etc.) never promote

**Sequencing with playhead-4my.16:**
This bead depends on 4my.16 (detectOnly wiring + runBackfill → receiveAdDecisionResults). The promotion promotion happens inside runBackfill after the policy step, so the orchestrator call from 4my.16 carries the promoted action.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A backfill run with eligibleGate=.eligible and skipConfidence >= 0.75 results in an auto-skip firing (no user tap required).
2. A span with skipConfidence < 0.75 and gate=.eligible gets a banner (detectOnly) but no auto-skip.
3. A span with gate=blockedByEvidenceQuorum never auto-skips regardless of skipConfidence.
4. .suppress policy action is never overridden by confidence promotion.
5. autoSkipConfidenceThreshold is configurable in AdDetectionConfig and defaults to 0.75.
6. Shadow invariant test still passes.
7. Existing Phase 6 tests (SkipPolicyMatrixTests, BackfillFusionPipelineTests) still pass unchanged — the promotion is additive, not a matrix change.

title: Phase 6.5: Wire fusion decisions to SkipOrchestrator + detectOnly for unknown-intent spans
description:
Phase 6 built and persisted the fusion pipeline but left two gaps that prevent Phase 7 (User Corrections) from having real signal to learn from:

**Gap 1 — SkipPolicyMatrix blocks all decisions:**
SkipPolicyMatrix.action(for:ownership:) is hardcoded to (.unknown, .unknown) in AdDetectionService.runBackfill, which returns .logOnly for every span. FM does not classify CommercialIntent in Phase 6 and Phase 8 provides AdOwnership, so the policy gate produces no actionable output. Users never see a banner; no correction signal is ever generated.

**Gap 2 — runBackfill never calls receiveAdDecisionResults:**
AdDetectionService.runBackfill saves fusion AdWindows to the store and logs DecisionEvents, but does not call SkipOrchestrator.receiveAdDecisionResults. The method exists and guards correctly on eligibilityGate, but nothing triggers it after a backfill completes.
design:
**Fix 1 — detectOnly for unknown-intent spans:**
Change SkipPolicyMatrix so that (.unknown, .unknown) → .detectOnly instead of .logOnly. A detected span with unknown provenance gets a banner (host can dismiss, user can confirm). No auto-skip. This is safe: worst case is a false-positive banner the user dismisses.

**Fix 2 — Wire runBackfill → SkipOrchestrator:**
After backfill completes, pass eligible fusion results (eligibilityGate == .eligible) to SkipOrchestrator.receiveAdDecisionResults. The AdDecisionResult conversion is straightforward; the guard in receiveAdDecisionResults already filters blocked gates.

The orchestrator path is the right channel — it handles idempotency keys, hysteresis (ManagedWindow), and snap boundaries. Bypassing it would duplicate logic.

**What this unlocks for Phase 7:**
- Banner impressions = confirmation opportunities
- 'Listen' taps = correction signal
- Without this, UserCorrectionStore has nothing to correct against.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A backfill run on an episode with confident fusion detections (eligibilityGate=eligible) results in a banner being shown to the user.
2. SkipPolicyMatrix returns .detectOnly for (.unknown, .unknown) — verified by test.
3. AdDetectionService.runBackfill calls skipOrchestrator.receiveAdDecisionResults with eligible results — verified by shadow mode integration test confirming orchestrator receives the results.
4. No auto-skips fire for unknown-intent spans (eligibilityGate blocks are never promoted to applied).
5. Shadow invariant test still passes (no AdWindow rows written directly from FM in shadow mode).

title: Phase 4: shape TargetedWindowNarrower windows using AcousticBreakDetector output
description:
Use AcousticBreakDetector output to shape TargetedWindowNarrower's window selection. After per-anchor interval merging, snap outer edges of each merged interval to the nearest acoustic break within 2.0s (one FeatureWindow duration, matching the detector's own grouping tolerance). Option D: conservative edge-snap, never drift more than perAnchorPaddingSegments, never cause cap abort.

Acceptance criteria:
- New code reads AcousticBreakDetector.detectBreaks(...) output and uses it to influence TargetedWindowNarrower window selection per Option D
- Conan smoke test recall remains at 4/4 (no regression)
- New unit tests in TargetedWindowNarrowerTests.swift pin snap/extend behavior
- Existing TargetedWindowNarrowerTests still pass
- BoundarySpanExpansionTests (bd-1my) still pass

Related: playhead-8jd (acoustic-origin fix).
notes: Snap may move an edge in EITHER direction. Outward widening is bounded by `perAnchorPaddingSegments` (the original padding distance) and is re-checked by the merged-segment cap. This means snap can't blow the cap on its own — if the bounded widening would exceed the cap, the existing cap-abort logic falls back to the full segment list.

title: Phase 4: surface AcousticBreakDetector output as .acoustic region origin
description:
## Bug

On real audio (Conan Fanhausen Revisited episode, 915s, decoded from `/tmp/conan.mp3`), `AcousticBreakDetector` correctly produces 3 acoustic breaks (0 energy transitions, 2 spectral spikes, 1 pause cluster). However, `RegionProposalBuilder` does NOT promote these acoustic breaks into regions with `origins=acoustic`. All resulting regions remain `origins=lex` only.

In plain English: the acoustic-break signal is wired into `RegionProposalBuilder` as an *associator* for regions that already exist from other sources (lexical, FM, sponsor, fingerprint) — but there is no path that turns a free-standing acoustic break into its own region. If a break doesn't happen to land within ~1s of an existing proposal edge, it is silently dropped on the floor.

## Empirical Evidence

Stage C real-audio benchmark on 2026-04-09 confirmed:
- Real features: 3 acoustic breaks detected by `AcousticBreakDetector` (0 energy transitions, 2 spectral spikes, 1 pause cluster)
- Synthetic features (no acoustic signal): identical 15% ad-second coverage, identical 3 lex-only regions
- Zero regions surfaced with `.acoustic` origin in either run

This was demonstrated by comparing real-features vs synthetic-features runs in the Phase 4 shadow benchmark — with the real acoustic signal available, output was bit-identical to the synthetic-feature run, proving the acoustic pipeline is dead downstream of the detector.

## Where the Bug Lives

`Playhead/Services/AdDetection/RegionProposalBuilder.swift`:

1. `build(_:config:)` at lines 78–155: proposals are constructed from FM, lexical, sponsor, and fingerprint sources only (lines 97–104). There is no `makeAcousticProposals` analog.
2. Acoustic breaks are used only at lines 121–130 inside the final `.map` — `associateAcousticBreaks` filters `input.acousticBreaks` to those within `acousticBreakAssociationTolerance` (default 1.0s, line 74) of an *existing* proposal's start/end. If `!associatedBreaks.isEmpty`, `.acoustic` is inserted into that proposal's origins. Otherwise the break is discarded.
3. `associateAcousticBreaks` at lines 354–363: simple edge-proximity filter. Free-standing acoustic breaks that don't overlap a lexical/FM/sponsor/fingerprint proposal have no path to become a region.

Result: acoustic breaks can only ever *decorate* existing regions with an extra origin flag; they cannot spawn one.

## Why Fixing It Broadens Phase 5

Phase 5's anchor-based decoder (see `docs/plans/2026-04-09-phase-5-design.md`) currently sources anchors from FM consensus + `EvidenceEntry` only. The `.acoustic` origin path is effectively dead, so shows where FM is unavailable or under-running are starved of fallback anchors. Surfacing acoustic breaks as first-class regions (or at minimum as standalone proposals) would give Phase 5 an automatic backup anchor source with zero additional wiring on the Phase 5 side.

This is a Phase 4 bug, not a Phase 5 issue. Phase 5 can ship without the fix; they are independent. But fixing this bug broadens Phase 5's anchor set for free.

## Cross-References

- Phase 5 design doc: `docs/plans/2026-04-09-phase-5-design.md`
- Regression test fixture: `PlayheadTests/IntegrationTests/Phase4ShadowBenchmarkTests.swift` — the `phase4OnRealFeatures()` method is the empirical demonstration and should become the regression test once the fix lands.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `RegionProposalBuilder` produces at least one region with `.acoustic` origin when `AcousticBreakDetector` returns at least one break on the input
- The Stage C real-audio benchmark (`Phase4ShadowBenchmarkTests.phase4OnRealFeatures`) shows non-zero `.acoustic`-origin regions
- A unit test pins the wiring: feed RegionProposalBuilder a synthetic AcousticBreak set + minimal lexical input, assert at least one bundle has `.acoustic` in its `region.origins`
- No regression: existing `RegionProposalBuilderTests` still pass

title: Kelly Ripa: try includeSchemaInPrompt: false + one-shot example experiment
description: The Kelly Ripa #1 refinement window refuses every run with 'May contain sensitive content' on the default-guardrails @Generable path despite the visible prompt containing zero pharma trigger vocabulary. Apple expert diagnosis: classifier checks the FULL augmented input including framework-injected schema text. Reference: docs/fm-safety-classifier-kelly-ripa-mystery.md sections 'Expert response (2026-04-08)' and 'The experiment that should answer this fastest'. Failing call: Playhead/Services/AdDetection/FoundationModelClassifier.swift refinePassB (the @Generable RefinementWindowSchema path). Test fixture: PlayheadTests/Services/AdDetection/PlayheadFMSmokeTests.swift Conan boundary expansion test, the Kelly Ripa #1 window specifically.
acceptance_criteria: Run the failing Kelly Ripa #1 refinement A/B-style: (a) baseline default-path call (expected: refusal), (b) same call with includeSchemaInPrompt: false + a one-shot example in instructions + manual schema preamble removed. Document outcome in fm-safety-classifier-kelly-ripa-mystery.md. If refusal disappears, hidden schema text was the trigger and we have a clean fix path. If refusal persists, schema-injection is ruled out and we should switch to automatic permissive fallback (separate bead).
notes: Filed during Phase 5 brainstorm. See docs/plans/2026-04-09-phase-5-design.md (Related work section). Original mystery doc: docs/fm-safety-classifier-kelly-ripa-mystery.md

title: Kelly Ripa: auto-retry default-path FM refusals via permissive path regardless of vocabulary
description:
Currently the SensitiveWindowRouter dispatches sensitive plans to PermissiveAdClassifier based on a vocabulary dictionary (RedactionRules.json). The Kelly Ripa #1 mystery shows the router can fail to detect sensitive content because Apple's classifier inspects framework-injected schema text the router doesn't see.

The Apple expert's recommendation if the includeSchemaInPrompt experiment doesn't fix Kelly Ripa: 'stop trying to extend the routing dictionary. Apple staff explicitly says guardrails usually cannot be suppressed by extra prompts/rules, and permissive mode is the supported escape hatch.'

Two options the expert presents:
  1. Make all refinement use the permissive string path (heavy)
  2. At minimum, automatically retry any default-path refinement refusal through the permissive string path, regardless of vocabulary (lighter)

This bead implements option 2 — it preserves the @Generable guided-generation path as the fast/preferred route and uses permissive as a safety net.

Implementation:
  - In FoundationModelClassifier.refinePassB, catch GenerationError.refusal and immediately retry via PermissiveAdClassifier.refine
  - Same for coarsePassA if applicable
  - Surface both attempts in SemanticScanResult so the retry is observable
  - The vocabulary router stays in place as a fast-path optimization (skip the @Generable attempt entirely when vocabulary matches), but is no longer load-bearing for correctness

Depends on: kr-2 (refusal.explanation diagnostic capture) for clearer failure logging when both paths fail.

Reference: docs/fm-safety-classifier-kelly-ripa-mystery.md 'Production recommendation' section
acceptance_criteria: Any GenerationError.refusal caught on the default @Generable path (coarse OR refinement) is automatically retried via the corresponding PermissiveAdClassifier method. The vocabulary-based router becomes a fast path optimization, not a correctness gate. The Conan smoke test catches Kelly Ripa #1 directly (not just via outward expansion sibling-window leakage). The 'load-bearing on luck' fragility called out in the mystery doc is removed.
notes: Filed during Phase 5 brainstorm. See docs/plans/2026-04-09-phase-5-design.md (Related work section). Original mystery doc: docs/fm-safety-classifier-kelly-ripa-mystery.md

title: Transcript ad-region overlay UI
description:
[REVISED 2026-04-09 after Phase 5 cycle-1 review]

Surface decoded ad spans from MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder (5.2) in the transcript view layer. Decoupling visualization from skipping is the load-bearing UX win — it builds user trust and enables future correction gestures without committing to automatic skipping in v1.

INTEGRATION TARGET (pinned cycle-1): Extend TranscriptPeekView and TranscriptPeekViewModel in place. Do NOT fork a new screen.

READ PATH (pinned cycle-1):
  - Read DecodedSpans via AnalysisStore.fetchDecodedSpans(assetId:) (added in 5.2)
  - Subscribe / poll for updates as backfill progresses and decoded_spans rows land
  - Map DecodedSpan → transcript chunk overlay by TIME OVERLAP:
      use DecodedSpan.startTime / endTime vs TranscriptChunk.startTime / endTime
      do NOT route through atom ordinals in the UI layer
  - This sidesteps atom-ordinal stability across re-runs

DUAL-SOURCE RENDERING (pinned cycle-1):
  During the Phase 5/6 transition, BOTH ad-styling sources render simultaneously:
    - Existing: italic + 0.45 opacity + AD% from AdWindow stays as-is
    - New (this bead): background tint + left-edge bar + AD badge sourced from DecodedSpan
  Phase 6 reconciles these when DecodedSpan becomes the source of truth.

VISUAL SPECIFICATION (pinned cycle-1):
  Background tint:
    - AppColors.accentSubtle at 100% opacity (not pre-multiplied with content opacity)
  Left-edge bar:
    - 3pt wide x full row height
    - Color: AppColors.accent (Copper)
    - Same geometry as existing active-chunk bar but DIFFERENT positioning: overlays the left edge of ALL rows in the span, not just the active row
    - When user is currently scrubbed inside an ad span, existing active-chunk bar keeps its highlight; ad edge bar renders underneath at lower z-order
  AD badge:
    - Pill shape
    - Background: AppColors.accent
    - Text color: AppColors.surface
    - Typography: sans(size: 10, weight: .semibold)
    - Leading-aligned at the start of the first row in the span, vertical-center
  Dark mode:
    - Tint adapts via existing AppColors.accentSubtle token (already dark/light aware)
  Accessibility:
    - accessibilityLabel includes 'Ad segment, n seconds, detected from <provenance summary>'

TAP BEHAVIOR:
  - Tap on highlighted region → read-only provenance popover derived from DecodedSpan.anchorProvenance (e.g., 'FM consensus + 2 EvidenceEntries: cvs.com URL, promo code CONAN10')
  - 'This isn't an ad' gesture PRESENT AND VISIBLE in popover but NOT WIRED to real state. Calls a stub method on UserCorrectionStore protocol with a NoOp default impl. Phase 7 will conform a real store.

CORRECTION PROTOCOL SPLIT (pinned cycle-1):
  - CorrectionMaskProvider = READ path (consumed by 5.1 projector)
  - UserCorrectionStore    = WRITE path (called by this UI gesture stub)
  - Both have NoOp default implementations in Phase 5
  - Phase 7 conforms a real store to BOTH protocols
  - Document the relationship in u4d and 5.1

What flows through the gesture:
  - The DecodedSpan reference (with anchorProvenance for context)
  - The time range that the user is rejecting
  - Should NOT mutate any state in v1 — just log the gesture for diagnostics

Files:
  - EXTEND: Playhead/Views/NowPlaying/TranscriptPeekView.swift
  - EXTEND: Playhead/Views/NowPlaying/TranscriptPeekViewModel.swift
  - NEW: AdRegionPopover.swift (the tap-to-explain provenance display)
  - NEW: Playhead/Services/AdDetection/UserCorrectionStore.swift (protocol + NoOp default impl)

Out of scope (Phase 7):
  - Persisting user corrections
  - Negative-feedback decay
  - Sponsor-specific blocking from corrections
  - Cross-episode correction propagation

Estimated size: ~150 lines of UI additions + ~30 lines of stub.

Acceptance:
  - DecodedSpans rendered in TranscriptPeekView as background tint + left-edge bar + inline AD badge per visual spec above
  - Legacy AdWindow italic/opacity/AD% styling still renders in parallel during transition
  - TranscriptPeekViewModel reads DecodedSpans via AnalysisStore.fetchDecodedSpans(assetId:) and maps them to chunks by time overlap (no atom-ordinal routing in the UI)
  - Tap → provenance popover
  - 'This isn't an ad' gesture wired to NoOp UserCorrectionStore
  - Accessibility label present
  - Snapshot test for visual regression

Design doc: docs/plans/2026-04-09-phase-5-design.md
acceptance_criteria: Decoded spans visible in transcript view as background tint + left-edge bar + inline AD badge. Tap on highlight surfaces provenance popover (which evidence flagged it). Tap-to-veto gesture is present but stubbed (no-op call to a future UserCorrectionStore protocol). Highlights render regardless of whether skipping is enabled. Snapshot test for visual regression.
