title: Thread podcastProfile through RegionShadowPhase to enable per-show sponsor scoring
description:
Current behavior: `RegionShadowPhase.run` passes `podcastProfile: nil` into `RegionFeatureExtractor.Input` (Playhead/Services/AdDetection/RegionShadowPhase.swift:~129).

Impact: `LexicalScanner` (Playhead/Services/AdDetection/LexicalScanner.swift:276-295) skips per-show sponsor patterns when the profile is nil, so shadow lexical scores silently under-report on shows that have custom sponsors. The Phase 4 shadow output therefore diverges from the live path on any show where the podcast profile carries sponsor signals.

Fix direction: persist `podcastProfile` on `AdDetectionService` (or fetch it during `runRegionShadowPhase`) and thread it through `RegionShadowPhase.Input.podcastProfile` into the feature extractor call.

Acceptance: shadow output reflects per-show sponsor matches identically to the live path — given the same episode and profile, the shadow `RegionFeatureBundle` lexical scores match the live backfill lexical scores on shows with custom sponsor patterns.

Reference: commit 913bff6 (acknowledged but untracked), RegionShadowPhase.swift:~129, LexicalScanner.swift:276-295.

title: Wire Phase 4 RegionProposalBuilder+RegionFeatureExtractor into production in shadow mode
description: RegionProposalBuilder and RegionFeatureExtractor have zero production call sites. Wire them into AdDetectionService.runBackfill as a DEBUG-only shadow phase that records RegionFeatureBundles to a new RegionShadowObserver, mirroring the FM shadow pattern. No live behavior changes; FM-origin clustering stays unexercised until BackfillJobRunner.RunResult surfaces FMRefinementWindowOutput.
notes: Wire-up landed. RegionShadowObserver + RegionShadowPhase helper added. AdDetectionService.runBackfill now invokes Phase 4 pipeline in shadow mode when a non-nil observer is injected. PlayheadRuntime constructs the observer only in DEBUG, mirroring FoundationModelsFeedbackStore gating. FM-origin region clustering still unexercised because BackfillJobRunner.RunResult does not surface FMRefinementWindowOutput — follow-up work. 3 new integration tests + full suite (973) green.

title: Make ShadowRetryObserver/runBackfillPollingLoop test deadlines injectable
description:
Current: tests exercising ShadowRetryObserver and runBackfillPollingLoop use hard-coded wall-clock deadlines (~5ms, 100-500ms) that assume a lightly-loaded cooperative pool. Under parallel test execution or on loaded CI hosts these flake intermittently because the cooperative pool doesn't schedule the continuation inside the deadline.

Workaround: commit 17b6c7c set parallelizable: false in project.yml (see playhead-86s). Must be reverted once deadlines are deterministic.

Root cause: deadlines are literal constants compiled into production code paths; tests cannot substitute a faster/virtual clock.

Acceptance:
- Deadline values are injected via constructor/config, or driven by a mockable/virtual clock abstraction.
- Tests use a logical clock (no wall-clock sleeps for timing assertions).
- project.yml re-enables parallelizable: true.
- Suite green parallelized on a loaded host across repeated runs.

Owner: TBD
Related: 17b6c7c, playhead-86s
acceptance_criteria: Deadline values in ShadowRetryObserver and runBackfillPollingLoop are injectable (or driven by a mockable clock); tests use a logical/synthetic clock rather than wall-clock sleeps; suite green parallelized on loaded CI hosts.

title: Inject AVAudioSession + MPNowPlayingInfoCenter to remove PlaybackService singleton coupling
description:
Current: PlaybackService writes to process-global AVAudioSession.sharedInstance() and MPNowPlayingInfoCenter.default() on every init, and subscribes to AVAudioSession interruption notifications. Two PlaybackService instances clobber each other, causing cross-suite races during parallel test execution.

Workaround: commit 17b6c7c set parallelizable: false in project.yml (lines 47-63). This adds wall-clock cost to the test suite and must be reverted once the underlying coupling is fixed.

Root cause: hard dependency on two process-global singletons with no seam for tests to substitute fakes.

Acceptance:
- PlaybackService constructor accepts injectable AVAudioSession-like and MPNowPlayingInfoCenter-like dependencies (protocol seams).
- Test fixtures pass in-memory fakes; no test touches the real shared instances.
- project.yml re-enables parallelizable: true.
- Full suite passes green parallelized on a loaded host.

Owner: TBD
Related: 17b6c7c, project.yml
acceptance_criteria: PlaybackService takes injectable seams for AVAudioSession and MPNowPlayingInfoCenter; test fixtures pass fakes; project.yml can re-enable parallelizable: true without flakes; full test suite passes parallelized.

title: Stop stale transcript/streaming work on coordinator session switch
description: Resume/playback session switches currently call AnalysisCoordinator.cancelPipeline() but do not stop TranscriptEngineService or clean up the active StreamingAudioDecoder. In device logs this leaves the old episode transcribing after a new play event and can trigger zero-shard / appended-shard cleanup oddities (e.g. 'Starting transcription loop: 0 shards', silent appended shard failure). Fix session-switch teardown so old transcript/decode work cannot leak across episodes or resumes, add regression coverage, verify targeted tests, and push main.

title: Skip stale runner detection work when transcript pass adds nothing
description: AnalysisJobRunner still runs hot-path and backfill once on duplicate pre-analysis passes that write zero transcript chunks. This wastes CPU and can append duplicate suppressed windows even though the scheduler now terminates the job after the pass.
acceptance_criteria: Runner skips hot-path when a no-new-chunks pass already has persisted AdWindows; runner skips backfill on the same pass when no candidate windows remain; retries after missing windows or unresolved candidates still execute the necessary detection stages; regression tests cover all three cases.

title: Stop zero-progress pre-analysis requeue loops
description: Pre-analysis jobs can requeue repeatedly after a bounded run returns reachedTarget with unchanged feature/transcript/cue coverage. On-device this shows up as repeated 3-shard transcription loops that only skip duplicate transcript segments, rerun hot path/backfill, and accumulate suppressed windows until maxAttemptCount is hit.
acceptance_criteria: A pre-analysis job that returns reachedTarget without increasing stored coverage is completed instead of requeued; repeated duplicate transcription loops stop after a single no-progress pass; regression tests cover the scheduler behavior.

title: Persist partial FM guardrail failures in shadow backfill
description: Device logs show Foundation Models can trip a safety/guardrail stop after earlier coarse/refinement windows have already succeeded. BackfillJobRunner currently persists the success rows but drops the terminal guardrail failure whenever the pass returns partial output, so shadow telemetry undercounts scans and loses the reason the pass stopped. Update the runner/classifier persistence path so partial non-graceful FM failures (at least guardrailViolation, and likely any non-success partial pass) persist an explicit failure scan row alongside surviving success rows, and add regression coverage for coarse and refinement partial-failure cases.

title: Degrade shadow FM rate limits instead of aborting backfill
description:
Why this issue exists and what needs to be done

Device logs on 2026-04-07 show the shadow Foundation Models coarse pass still aborting the entire FM backfill job when a window hits LanguageModelSession.GenerationError.rateLimited after the built-in retry. Foreground lexical analysis completes, but the shadow FM job is marked failed and we lose the rest of the scan.

Fix the classifier/runner path so FM rate limits degrade predictably instead of killing the whole shadow job. Preserve useful telemetry and add regression coverage for the rate-limited window case.

title: Harden FoundationModelClassifier retry session lifecycle
description: Review found that coarse and refinement retry paths reuse the same per-window session across multiple respond attempts. That can reintroduce conversation-history accumulation on retries and violates the intended single-use session lifecycle for LanguageModelSession. Update retry paths to mint a fresh prewarmed session per attempt and add targeted tests.
notes:
Investigated 2026-04-07 device logs. The remaining issue does not fit this retry-session-lifecycle bug; logs point to partial FM pass termination on safety/guardrail after some window successes. Handling separately.
Code review 2026-04-10: The session-reuse bug described in this bead has been fully fixed in the current codebase. All retry paths (coarse shrinkWindowAndRetryOnce at line 2897, coarse backoffAndRetry at line 2839, refinement shrinkWindowAndRetryOnce at line 3165, refinement backoffAndRetry at line 3189, and smart-shrink retry at line 2999) now call makePrewarmedSessionBox() to mint a fresh SessionBox per attempt. description:

## Test File

## Test Suites

### Fingerprint Generation
- Confirmed ad span produces MinHash fingerprint from normalized text
- Fingerprint is deterministic (same input → same hash)
- Different ad copy produces different fingerprints
- Normalization strips punctuation, filler words, lowercases
- Unicode text handled correctly (accented chars, CJK, emoji)
- Empty/whitespace-only text produces no fingerprint

### Near-Duplicate Matching
- Same ad script with slight word variation matches (Jaccard >= 0.6)
- Same ad script with different filler words matches
- Completely different editorial content does not match (Jaccard < 0.6)
- Similarity score reflects actual Jaccard distance
- High similarity (>= 0.9) vs moderate similarity (0.6-0.9) ranked correctly
- Near-threshold cases: 0.59 rejected, 0.61 accepted

### Lifecycle Transitions
- New fingerprint starts as candidate
- First confirmation promotes to quarantined
- Second confirmation (low rollback) promotes to active
- Only active fingerprints are returned by matcher
- Rollback spike demotes active → decayed
- Persistent rollback demotes to blocked
- Decayed can recover to active with new confirmations
- Empty store returns no matches gracefully

### Store → Matcher → Evidence Pipeline Integration
- AdCopyFingerprintStore produces fingerprints, matcher reads and returns ranked matches
- RegionShadowPhase.Input receives fingerprintStore, calls store-backed matcher overload
- FingerprintMatch flows through RegionProposalBuilder as .fingerprint origin
- FingerprintMatch produces EvidenceLedgerEntry with source .fingerprint
- Fingerprint evidence contributes to "2+ distinct evidence kinds" quorum gate
- Fingerprint weight is capped by FusionWeightConfig.fingerprintCap
- Empty fingerprint matches produce no ledger entries

### Backfill-Only Structural Guarantee
The hot-path (runHotPath, AdDetectionService.swift:309) structurally cannot call fingerprint matchers — it only runs LexicalScanner + ClassifierService. This is an architectural invariant verified by code review, not a behavioral test. Include a single structural assertion:
- RegionShadowPhase is not referenced in runHotPath code path

### Rollback Decay
- User correction triggers rollback on matching fingerprint
- Active entry decays on rollback spike (rate > 0.5)
- Decayed entry stops contributing matches until re-confirmed
- Cross-episode: fingerprint confirmed in ep1+ep2, rollback in ep3, decayed — no match in ep4

### Provenance Events
- Fingerprint creation logs source event with adWindowId
- Source events are append-only (INSERT OR IGNORE)
- Source events loadable by analysisAssetId

description:

**Entry point 1: Listen revert (existing flow, add correction write)**
SkipOrchestrator.recordListenRevert() currently updates decisionState to .reverted and signals TrustScoringService. Add: also write CorrectionEvent with source=.listenRevert. Infer correction scope from AdWindow's evidenceSources and metadata (sponsor name, phrase matches, campaign ID).

**Entry point 2: Manual veto (existing flow, replace NoOp)**
AdRegionPopover's "This isn't an ad" currently calls NoOpUserCorrectionStore.recordVeto(). Wire to persistent UserCorrectionStore. Source=.manualVeto. Typically only exactSpan scope (less metadata available from DecodedSpan).

**New UX surfaces:**
1. "Not an ad" button on AdBannerView — new button alongside "Listen". Records correction with source=.manualVeto without rewinding. Uses AdWindow metadata for scope inference (richer than popover path).
2. Timeline rail tap target — tapping an ad segment on TimelineRailView pops AdRegionPopover. Requires: hit testing on ad segment ranges, presenting popover anchored to tap point.

**Suppression wiring:**
BackfillEvidenceFusion eligibility gate checks UserCorrectionStore for matching scopes. title: UserCorrectionStore
description:
Persistent UserCorrectionStore replacing NoOpUserCorrectionStore stub.

## Data Model

**CorrectionScope enum:**
- exactSpan(assetId, ordinalRange) — this specific time range on this episode
- sponsorOnShow(podcastId, sponsor) — this sponsor on this show
- phraseOnShow(podcastId, phrase) — this phrase pattern on this show
- campaignOnShow(podcastId, campaign) — this campaign on this show

All four scopes implemented. phraseOnShow/campaignOnShow gracefully no-op when upstream metadata is insufficient; Phase 8 SponsorKnowledgeStore will enrich.

**CorrectionEvent (append-only ledger row):**
- id (UUID), analysisAssetId, podcastId
- source: .listenRevert | .manualVeto
- correctionScope (serialized enum)
- atomOrdinalRange (JSON [first, last] — always present for exactSpan, nil for broader scopes)
- evidenceJSON (snapshot of what triggered the original detection)
- createdAt (epoch)

**Query-time weight function:**
weight(age) = max(0.1, 1.0 - (ageDays / 180.0))
Fresh = 1.0 (hard block). 3 months = 0.5. 6 months = 0.1 floor.

**Storage:** Uses existing correction_events table in AnalysisStore. correctionScope column gets serialized enum.

**Scope inference logic:**
- Always record exactSpan
- If AdWindow has canonicalized sponsor name → also record sponsorOnShow
- If evidence contains matched phrase pattern → also record phraseOnShow
- If evidence contains campaign identifier → also record campaignOnShow

**Integration points:**
- BackfillEvidenceFusion: check active correction scopes in eligibility gate, apply decay-weighted suppression (effectiveConfidence = rawConfidence * (1.0 - correctionWeight))
- AtomEvidenceProjector: exactSpan corrections become decay-weighted masks on atom timeline
- SponsorKnowledgeStore: corrections feed negative memory (Phase 8)

Files: UserCorrectionStore.swift (replace NoOp with persistent impl), AnalysisStore.swift (query methods for correction lookup by scope)

Acceptance: Corrections stored with scope and source. Query-time decay works. Broader scopes inferred from evidence. Scope matching queries return weighted results.

title: Phase 7: User Corrections
description:
Scoped correction memory that feeds back into the pipeline. When a user taps 'Listen' (reverts a skip) or 'This isn't an ad' (veto from popover/timeline), the correction is stored with scope — not just the exact time range, but potentially the sponsor, phrase, or campaign on that show. This prevents FM from re-promoting corrected spans.

## Design Decisions (2026-04-10 brainstorm)

**Correction scopes:** All four implemented now (exactSpan, sponsorOnShow, phraseOnShow, campaignOnShow). phraseOnShow and campaignOnShow are defined and functional when upstream data exists; they gracefully no-op when metadata is insufficient. Phase 8 SponsorKnowledgeStore will provide richer data for broader scopes.

**Decay model:** Query-time decay, not TTL. Corrections stored permanently in append-only ledger. Weight function: `max(0.1, 1.0 - ageDays/180.0)`. Fresh corrections = hard block (1.0). 6+ months = faint memory (0.1 floor). Rationale: users may gesture accidentally; corrections should self-heal as shows evolve.

**Suppression behavior:** Hard suppress with decay expiry. Fresh corrections fully block re-detection. As corrections age and weight decays, strong new evidence (e.g., FM at 0.99) can break through. Effective confidence = rawConfidence * (1.0 - correctionWeight). Consistent with decay model.

**Single ledger:** Both "Listen" reverts and "This isn't an ad" vetos write to the same CorrectionEvent ledger with a `source` field (`.listenRevert` vs `.manualVeto`). Scope inference naturally produces broader scopes for Listen reverts (richer AdWindow evidence) and narrower scopes for manual vetos (less metadata). Source field is for analytics, not branching behavior.

**UX surfaces:**
1. Banner "Listen" button (existing) — records correction + rewinds
2. Banner "Not an ad" button (NEW) — explicit correction without rewind, alongside Listen
3. Timeline rail tap (NEW) — tapping ad segment on TimelineRailView pops AdRegionPopover with "This isn't an ad"
4. Transcript overlay popover (existing) — "This isn't an ad" in AdRegionPopover

Verification: User 'Listen' tap records scoped correction. 'Not an ad' button records correction. Timeline tap opens correction popover. Future backfills respect correction scopes with decay weighting. Broader scopes inferred when evidence supports it.

title: SkipPolicyMatrix + DecisionCohort
description:
Map (commercialIntent, ownership) → SkipPolicyAction and track decision provenance separately from scan provenance.

SkipPolicyMatrix:
- (.paid, .thirdParty) → autoSkipEligible
- (.owned, .show) → detectOnly
- (.owned, .network) → detectOnly
- (.affiliate, *) → detectOnly
- (.organic, *) → suppress
- (.unknown, *) → logOnly

For v1, everything defaults to (.unknown, .unknown) → .logOnly. The types (CommercialIntent, AdOwnership) and matrix are defined now so Phase 8 (SponsorKnowledgeStore) can populate them later. FM does NOT classify commercial intent in Phase 6 — that requires business context FM doesn't have.

SkipPolicyAction enum:
- .autoSkipEligible — fusion can promote to skip
- .detectOnly — show banner, never skip
- .suppress — don't even show
- .logOnly — record for telemetry only

DecisionCohort: featurePipelineHash, fusionHash, policyHash, stabilityHash, appBuild. Changes here recompute decisions from cached scan results WITHOUT triggering FM rescans.

DecisionStabilityPolicy: removing a previously-applied skip cue requires BOTH:
(a) score drops below stayThreshold AND
(b) at least one of: user correction, FM negative with strong certainty + good transcript quality, or transcript content materially changed (transcriptVersion differs).
Cohort-only changes (same transcript, new OS model) cannot remove cues unless the new cohort produces a score below suppressionThreshold (0.25).
User explicit correction always overrides everything.

Files: SkipPolicyMatrix.swift (NEW), CommercialIntent.swift (NEW), AdOwnership.swift (NEW), DecisionCohort.swift (NEW), DecisionStabilityPolicy.swift (NEW)

Acceptance: Policy matrix maps correctly. v1 defaults everything to logOnly. Decision recomputation from cached scans works. Stability policy prevents cue removal without strong counterevidence.
notes:
DecisionStabilityPolicy 'strong counterevidence' defined as:
- For cue removal: requires BOTH (a) score drops below stayThreshold AND (b) at least one of: user correction, FM negative with strong certainty + good transcript quality, or transcript content materially changed (transcriptVersion differs).
- Cohort-only changes (same transcript, new OS model) cannot remove cues unless the new cohort produces a score below suppressionThreshold (0.25).

title: Phase 6: Evidence Fusion + Current-Episode Decisions
description:
The decision layer. Fusion is the SINGLE decision authority — the old promote/suppress path is removed. All evidence sources (including the old RuleBasedClassifier score) contribute entries to an evidence ledger, and fusion is the only decision maker.

Key design decisions from brainstorming (2026-04-09):
1. FMBackfillMode: 5-case enum (off/shadow/rescoreOnly/proposalOnly/full) replacing old 3-case. Mode controls which evidence sources contribute to the ledger, not which decision path runs.
2. SkipPolicyMatrix: v1 defaults everything to (.unknown, .unknown) → logOnly. FM does not classify commercial intent — that's Phase 8's job.
3. Evidence quorum reads anchorProvenance from DecodedSpan (Phase 5), does not re-derive multi-window consensus.
4. SkipOrchestrator updated to consume AdDecisionResult (not raw AdWindows). Write SkipOrchestrator tests FIRST.
5. Old promote/suppress (resolveDecision) removed entirely. Classifier score is one ledger entry alongside FM/lexical/acoustic/catalog.
6. Gate blocks at decision level, not score clamping.

FM contributes positive evidence only in v1. FM noAds/low-confidence/abstain = 'no ledger entry', never negative evidence.

Verification: FM-assisted rescoring promotes borderline candidates above skip threshold. FM-only regions with evidence quorum become skip-eligible. FM-only regions without quorum stay blocked. User-reverted spans not re-promoted. Existing materialized cues stable across decision recomputation.

title: BackfillEvidenceFusion + DecisionMapper
description:
Evidence ledger accumulation and decision mapping over decoded spans. Fusion is the SINGLE decision authority — the old RuleBasedClassifier promote/suppress path is removed. All evidence sources (including the old classifier score) contribute ledger entries.

Each evidence source contributes a capped, trust-scaled EvidenceLedgerEntry to the ledger:
- source: EvidenceSourceKind (.classifier, .fm, .lexical, .acoustic, .catalog)
- weight: Double — capped, trust-scaled per source
- detail: EvidenceLedgerDetail — enum with source-specific metadata

The old RuleBasedClassifier score becomes a .classifier entry. FM certainty bands become .fm entries mapped through a cohort-specific calibrator (CertaintyBand.strong from ScanCohort X maps to a different numeric weight than from ScanCohort Y).

DecisionMapper converts the accumulated ledger into:
- proposalConfidence: raw estimate from all evidence
- skipConfidence: calibrated score for SkipOrchestrator (mapped to 0-1 scale)
- eligibilityGate: SkipEligibilityGate enum (.eligible/.blockedByEvidenceQuorum/.blockedByPolicy/.blockedByUserCorrection)

Gate blocks at the DECISION level, not by clamping the score. A span can have skipConfidence=0.85 but eligibilityGate=.blockedByEvidenceQuorum — the score is honest, the gate prevents action.

FM positive-only in v1: FM noAds/low-confidence/abstain contribute NO ledger entries. They affect scan scheduling and diagnostics only.

Evidence quorum for FM-only regions reads anchorProvenance from DecodedSpan (does NOT re-derive multi-window consensus):
- anchorProvenance contains .fmConsensus → multi-window consensus satisfied → check remaining: 2+ distinct evidence kinds + good transcript quality + boundary precision
- anchorProvenance only has .fmAcousticCorroborated (Use C) → needs external corroboration via path (b)
- No FM provenance → non-FM path, quorum N/A

Until quorum satisfied, eligibilityGate = .blockedByEvidenceQuorum (score NOT clamped).

FMBackfillMode controls which evidence SOURCES contribute to the ledger, not which decision path runs:
- off → ledger has classifier + lexical + acoustic (no FM entries)
- shadow → same as off for decisions, FM entries persisted for telemetry only
- rescoreOnly → FM entries join ledger for existing candidates
- proposalOnly → FM can propose new regions
- full → all of the above

Files: BackfillEvidenceFusion.swift (NEW), EvidenceLedgerEntry.swift (NEW)

Acceptance: Evidence ledger accumulates correctly from all source types. Old classifier score is one ledger entry among many. DecisionMapper produces proposalConfidence + skipConfidence + eligibilityGate. FM-only regions blocked until quorum. FM negatives do not suppress. Quorum reads anchorProvenance, does not re-derive consensus.

title: Phase 5 tests
description:
[REVISED 2026-04-09 after Phase 5 cycle-1 review — acoustic break hint tests added]

Tests for AtomEvidenceProjector (5.1), MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder (5.2), decoded_spans persistence, and the transcript ad-region overlay UI (u4d). The test surface is what protects the zero-shot guarantee and the precision-first invariant.

Test categories:

(1) AtomEvidenceProjector unit tests:
  - Every input atom produces an output AtomEvidence record with startTime/endTime populated
  - Anchored atoms reflect upstream Phase 4 FM-origin regions with fmConsensusStrength >= .medium
  - Trustworthy EvidenceEntry categories (.url, .promoCode, .disclosurePhrase, .ctaPhrase) anchor; .brandSpan does NOT anchor alone
  - Multiple anchor sources on same atom merge into anchorProvenance
  - NoCorrectionMaskProvider leaves all atoms unmasked
  - Test CorrectionMaskProvider with vetoed range marks atoms .userVetoed
  - CorrectionMaskProvider is queried once in bulk (async, ordinals: ClosedRange<Int>)
  - hasAcousticBreakHint: atoms covered by .acoustic-origin Phase 4 regions have hasAcousticBreakHint=true; atoms without coverage have hasAcousticBreakHint=false
  - Use C — corroboration anchors: atom covered by single-window FM (fmConsensusStrength >= .low AND < .medium) + acoustic break (breakStrength >= 0.5) within ±2 atoms → isAnchored=true AND anchorProvenance contains .fmAcousticCorroborated
  - Use C — without break: same single-window FM atom with NO co-located acoustic break → isAnchored=false (the single FM window alone does not anchor)
  - Use C — without FM: acoustic break alone (no FM coverage) → isAnchored=false (precision-first invariant; the break alone does not anchor)
  - Use C — break too far: single-window FM atom + acoustic break 3+ atoms away → isAnchored=false (±2 atom boundary is strict)
  - Use C — weak break: single-window FM atom + acoustic break with breakStrength < 0.5 → isAnchored=false

(2) MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder unit tests:
  - Contiguous run of anchored atoms → single span
  - Non-anchored atoms break runs
  - Sub-MIN_DURATION spans dropped
  - Above-MAX_DURATION spans split at longest internal unanchored gap
  - 100%-anchored over-max span splits at midpoint ordinal
  - Tied longest gaps → argmin(ordinal) deterministic tiebreak
  - Recursive split: pathological ultra-long span recurses to all <= MAX_DURATION
  - Adjacent spans within MERGE_GAP_ATOMS merge; anchorProvenance is union-deduped
  - Split preserves only provenance whose atom range overlaps each half
  - .userVetoed atom between two near-adjacent spans BLOCKS merge
  - .userConfirmed does NOT create a span without an anchor (precision invariant)
  - Refuses to emit any span when there are zero anchors in the input
  - Use A — boundary snap with break: span anchored by lex hit, atom with hasAcousticBreakHint at ordinal 0 within ±3 of span's firstAtomOrdinal → assert span's firstAtomOrdinal and startTime snap to that atom
  - Use A — boundary snap WITHOUT break: same span, no hasAcousticBreakHint atoms in range → assert span keeps default boundaries
  - Use A — snap on both sides: breaks within ±3 of both left and right edges → both edges snap
  - Use A — snap out of range: nearest break is 4+ atoms away → no snap
  - Use B — anti-merge across break: two anchored runs separated by 1 unanchored atom that has hasAcousticBreakHint=true → assert no merge (two distinct spans survive)
  - Use B — merge across non-break gap: two anchored runs separated by 1 unanchored atom WITHOUT hasAcousticBreakHint → assert merge happens (control case)
  - Use B + .userVetoed: gap contains a .userVetoed atom AND a hasAcousticBreakHint atom → no merge (both conditions independently block)

(3) Mutation / precision invariants (added cycle-1):
  - Take Conan fixture, run projector, then STRIP all anchors from projected output → decoder emits zero spans
  - STRIP all hasAcousticBreakHint flags → decoder still emits the same spans as the anchor-only path (Use A/B only refine; they never create spans)
  - decode(decode(x)) == decode(x)  (idempotency, including Use A snap and Use B gate)

(4) Robustness (the zero-shot rail):
  - No-ads synthetic episode (zero anchors) → zero spans, even with hasAcousticBreakHint flags present
  - 80%-runtime single ad → does not collapse into one mega-span when split conditions hit
  - Two adjacent ads separated by 5-atom host transition → split, not merged
  - Lex-noisy but anchor-free adversarial episode → zero spans
  - Same input twice → identical output (determinism)

(5) Performance (added cycle-1):
  - Decode 15,000 atoms with ~50 anchors + ~100 hasAcousticBreakHint atoms in < 200ms on simulator

(6) Phase 4 → Phase 5 integration (Conan fixture):
  - Run RegionShadowPhase, feed bundles + EvidenceCatalog to projector + decoder
  - Report recall, precision, ad-second coverage against ground truth
  - CONCRETE FLOOR (pinned cycle-1): ad-second coverage >= 30% on Conan (2x Phase 4 baseline of 15%)
  - 80% is a Phase 12 goal, not a Phase 5 gate
  - Lenient recall: does not regress below Phase 4's 75%
  - With playhead-8jd landed: Use A snap on the CVS ad should close the 0:00 → 0:21 gap (lex anchor at 0:21, acoustic break at 0:00)

(7) Materialization tests:
  - DecodedSpan persisted to decoded_spans round-trips via fetchDecodedSpans(assetId:)
  - Re-running decoder is idempotent at the persistence layer (upsert by id, no duplicates)
  - Existing ad_windows rows continue to load (additive migration)

(8) Transcript overlay UI tests (u4d):

  - Tap on highlighted region surfaces AnchorRef provenance popover (including .fmAcousticCorroborated case)
  - 'This isn't an ad' gesture present, tappable, calls NoOp UserCorrectionStore stub
  - Highlights render whether or not skipping is enabled
  - Snapshot/golden test on one fixture episode

title: AtomEvidenceProjector
description:
[REVISED 2026-04-09 after Phase 5 cycle-1 review — acoustic break hints added]

Project Phase 4 region anchors and EvidenceEntry catalog onto the per-atom timeline. Per-atom annotations consumed by MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder (5.2).

ZERO-SHOT CONSTRAINT: Must work on unseen podcasts, no per-show calibration, no labeled training data, no fitted distributions, no score thresholds, no percentile normalization.

PROJECTOR SIGNATURE (pinned in cycle-1):
  AtomEvidenceProjector.project(
    regions: [RegionFeatureBundle],
    catalog: EvidenceCatalog,
    atoms: [TranscriptAtom],
    correctionMaskProvider: any CorrectionMaskProvider
  ) async -> [AtomEvidence]

ATOM EVIDENCE SHAPE:
  struct AtomEvidence {
    let atomOrdinal: Int
    let startTime: Double                // added cycle-1 so decoder has no second input
    let endTime: Double                  // added cycle-1
    let isAnchored: Bool
    let anchorProvenance: [AnchorRef]
    let hasAcousticBreakHint: Bool       // NEW — drives Use A boundary snap + Use B anti-merge
    let correctionMask: CorrectionState  // .none / .userVetoed / .userConfirmed
  }

ANCHOR REF ENUM (extended):
  enum AnchorRef: Sendable, Equatable {
    case fmConsensus(regionId: String, consensusStrength: Double)
    case evidenceCatalog(entry: EvidenceEntry)
    case fmAcousticCorroborated(regionId: String, breakStrength: Double)  // NEW — Use C
  }

isAnchored = true iff ANY of:
  - a region with .foundationModel origin AND fmConsensusStrength >= .medium covers this atom
  - an EvidenceEntry of a TRUSTWORTHY category covers this atom
  - Use C — a single-window FM region (.foundationModel origin, fmConsensusStrength >= .low AND < .medium) covers this atom AND an acoustic break with breakStrength >= 0.5 falls within ±2 atoms. Provenance gets a .fmAcousticCorroborated entry.

TRUSTWORTHY EVIDENCE CATEGORIES (anchor-eligible):
  .url, .promoCode, .disclosurePhrase, .ctaPhrase
NOT anchor-eligible on its own:
  .brandSpan  (too noisy, appears in editorial context)

ACOUSTIC BREAK HINT POPULATION:
  - The projector reads .acoustic-origin regions from Phase 4 (per playhead-8jd RegionProposalBuilder fix) and marks every atom covered by an acoustic break with hasAcousticBreakHint = true.
  - hasAcousticBreakHint is a hint, not an anchor source. It is consumed by the decoder for Use A (boundary snap) and Use B (anti-merge) in 5.2, and by the projector itself for Use C corroboration.
  - Use C precision-first invariant: neither the single-window FM hit alone nor the acoustic break alone anchors. Both must be present within ±2 atoms.
  - breakStrength >= 0.5 cutoff uses the midpoint of the AcousticBreak.breakStrength 0..1 range produced by AcousticBreakDetector.computeStrength.

NO score field. NO per-feature vector. NO calibration math.

CORRECTION MASK PROVIDER (pinned in cycle-1):
  protocol CorrectionMaskProvider {
    func correctionMasks(
      for ordinals: ClosedRange<Int>,
      in assetId: String
    ) async -> [Int: CorrectionState]
  }
Bulk, async, asset-scoped. Phase 5 ships NoCorrectionMaskProvider returning empty dict. Phase 7 UserCorrectionStore conforms with a real impl.

PROPOSED REGION STABLE ID (pinned in cycle-1):
  "\(analysisAssetId)#\(firstAtomOrdinal)-\(lastAtomOrdinal)"

title: MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder
description:
[REVISED 2026-04-09 after Phase 5 cycle-1 review — acoustic break hints added]

Linear-walk decoder over the per-atom timeline produced by AtomEvidenceProjector. Produces contiguous DecodedSpans with user-correction masks applied and universal duration constraints enforced. Persists via new decoded_spans table.

ZERO-SHOT CONSTRAINT: No score thresholds, no calibration, no tunable parameters that depend on a specific show. Universal hyperparameters only (duration constraints + boundary snap radius).

DECODER INPUT: [AtomEvidence]  (AtomEvidence now carries startTime/endTime + hasAcousticBreakHint, so no secondary input required)

RULE ORDER (pinned in cycle-1, idempotent: decode(decode(x)) == decode(x)):
  1. Form runs: walk atoms left to right; a contiguous run of atoms where (isAnchored && correctionMask != .userVetoed) is a candidate span
  2. Boundary snap (Use A): for each candidate span, look for atoms with hasAcousticBreakHint within ±BOUNDARY_SNAP_RADIUS_ATOMS of the span's first and last ordinals. If found, snap the boundary to that atom's ordinal/time.
  3. Merge: two adjacent candidate spans merge if separated by < MERGE_GAP_ATOMS unanchored atoms AND no .userVetoed atom sits between them AND (Use B) no atom in the gap has hasAcousticBreakHint
  4. Split: spans above MAX_DURATION split (see rule 4 edge cases)
  5. Drop: spans below MIN_DURATION dropped

UNIVERSAL CONSTANTS:
  - MIN_DURATION = 5 seconds (industry convention — no ad shorter)
  - MAX_DURATION = 180 seconds (cap against runaway merges)
  - MERGE_GAP_ATOMS = 3  (~2s of speech; small enough to merge micro-gaps within an ad, large enough not to bridge non-ad content; picked from first principles, not tuned)
  - BOUNDARY_SNAP_RADIUS_ATOMS = 3  (NEW — same magnitude as MERGE_GAP_ATOMS; ~2s radius is tight enough to be a refinement but wide enough to catch breaks that landed slightly off the lex/FM hit)

USE A — BOUNDARY SNAP (NEW):
  - When a candidate span's firstAtomOrdinal is within ±3 atoms of an atom with hasAcousticBreakHint, snap firstAtomOrdinal (and startTime) to that atom. Same for lastAtomOrdinal / endTime.
  - Applies only to already-anchored candidate spans. Never creates a span.
  - Concrete example (Conan): CVS ad spans 0:00–0:26. Lex anchor fires at 0:21. Default-widened span is 0:21–0:26 (5s). Acoustic break at 0:00 → snap left edge to 0:00 → final span 0:00–0:26 (26s). Precision-preserving because the anchor didn't change.

USE B — ANTI-MERGE TIE-BREAKER (NEW):
  - Before merging two adjacent candidate spans across a gap of fewer than MERGE_GAP_ATOMS (3) unanchored atoms, check if any atom in the gap has hasAcousticBreakHint. If yes, do NOT merge.
  - Prevents "two adjacent ads separated by a 2s host transition get glued into one mega-ad" failure mode.
  - Never creates a span; only blocks an inappropriate merge.

Use C (weak-FM corroboration) is evaluated in the projector (5.1), not the decoder. By the time the decoder runs, Use C atoms already have isAnchored=true and .fmAcousticCorroborated in anchorProvenance. The decoder treats them identically to any other anchored atom.

RULE 4 EDGE CASES (pinned in cycle-1):
  - 100%-anchored over-max span → split at midpoint ordinal
  - Tied longest gaps → argmin(ordinal) for determinism
  - Recurse: split repeatedly until all resulting spans <= MAX_DURATION

ANCHOR PROVENANCE MERGE/SPLIT SEMANTICS (pinned in cycle-1):
  - Merge → union of both anchorProvenance lists, deduplicated by AnchorRef
  - Split → each half keeps anchors whose atom range overlaps that half

USER CORRECTION SEMANTICS (pinned in cycle-1):
  - .userVetoed: atom is removed from candidate runs (cannot appear in any span)
  - .userConfirmed: in v1 does NOT force a span without an upstream anchor (precision-first invariant holds). It only prevents future re-vetoing via user gesture (relevant in Phase 7). Document explicitly.

NO FM CALLS. FM has already happened upstream. Decoder is pure structural Swift.

PRECISION-FIRST: refuses to emit a span without an anchor — no anchor, no span. False positives are worse than false negatives in v1. Uses A and B are precision-preserving: neither can create a span; they only refine boundaries or block a merge.

DECODED SPAN SHAPE:
  struct DecodedSpan {
    let id: String                          // SHA256 prefix of "\(assetId):\(firstAtomOrdinal):\(lastAtomOrdinal)"
    let assetId: String
    let firstAtomOrdinal: Int
    let lastAtomOrdinal: Int
    let startTime: Double
    let endTime: Double
    let anchorProvenance: [AnchorRef]
  }

MATERIALIZATION (pinned in cycle-1):
  - NEW table 'decoded_spans' in AnalysisStore (NOT extending 'ad_windows')
  - Rationale: existing AdWindow consumers (skip engine, banner UI) read fields Phase 5 does not populate. Keeping tables separate avoids coupling. Phase 6 will reconcile.
  - 5.2 adds: fetchDecodedSpans(assetId: String) async throws -> [DecodedSpan]
  - Migration: additive only — creates decoded_spans table; ad_windows untouched.
  - Re-running decoder is idempotent: same input → same persisted rows, no duplicates (upsert keyed on DecodedSpan.id).

Out of scope: hysteresis, enter/exit thresholds, score-based decoding, multi-state HMM / Viterbi (Phase 12), FM invocation, calibration.

Files (NEW): MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder.swift, DecodedSpan.swift, and AnalysisStore migration + fetchDecodedSpans impl.

Estimated size: ~180 lines of production code + persistence glue (slightly larger than pre-cycle-1 estimate to cover Use A snap + Use B gate).

Acceptance:
  - No micro-fragment spans below MIN_DURATION
  - Spans capped at MAX_DURATION via recursive split
  - Correction-masked atoms cannot appear in spans
  - .userConfirmed does NOT create a span without an anchor (v1 invariant)
  - No span emitted without an upstream anchor
  - Use A: anchored span with an acoustic break within ±3 atoms of its boundary snaps to that break; without a break, default boundaries used
  - Use B: two near-adjacent candidate spans do NOT merge when a hasAcousticBreakHint atom sits in the gap; DO merge when the gap is clean
  - decode(decode(x)) == decode(x) (idempotency, including Use A + B — snapping and anti-merge are both idempotent)
  - DecodedSpan rows persist and round-trip via fetchDecodedSpans
  - All parameters are universal constants (MIN_DURATION, MAX_DURATION, MERGE_GAP_ATOMS, BOUNDARY_SNAP_RADIUS_ATOMS)

Design doc: docs/plans/2026-04-09-phase-5-design.md (sections: Decoder algorithm; Acoustic break hints (Uses A/B/C); Materialization)
notes: Design doc: docs/plans/2026-04-09-phase-5-design.md (sections: Decoder algorithm; Materialization)

title: Phase 5: Timeline Projection + Minimal Decoder
description:
Project evidence onto the atom timeline and decode contiguous spans. Prevents fragmented micro-spans and over-merging that region-based heuristics produce.

Ads are temporal states with continuity, duration priors, and transition cues. A minimal duration-constrained decoder encodes these facts structurally rather than relying on overlap thresholds, center-separation rules, and IoU cutoffs.

SCOPE (post cycle-1 review):
- 5.1 AtomEvidenceProjector: projects Phase 4 regions + EvidenceEntry catalog onto per-atom timeline
- 5.2 MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder: linear decoder producing DecodedSpan values, persists via new decoded_spans table
- 5.3 Phase 5 tests: unit + integration + mutation + idempotency + performance + snapshot
- u4d Transcript ad-region overlay UI: extends TranscriptPeekView/TranscriptPeekViewModel in place

RUNTIME WIRING: Phase5Projector injected into AdDetectionService.runBackfill as a new step 11 (after runRegionShadowPhase step 10), gated on non-nil injection. DEBUG-only injection pattern mirrors RegionShadowObserver.

PERSISTENCE: New AnalysisStore table 'decoded_spans' distinct from legacy 'ad_windows'. 5.2 adds fetchDecodedSpans(assetId:) async throws -> [DecodedSpan]. Existing AdWindow consumers (skip engine, banner UI) unaffected. Phase 6 reconciles.

Verification: Decoded spans are contiguous (no micro-fragments). Duration constraints prevent implausible spans. Correction masks prevent re-detection of user-reverted spans.

See docs/plans/2026-04-09-phase-5-design.md for full design.
acceptance_criteria:
Phase 4 baseline (Conan Fanhausen Revisited fixture, sim, fmBackfillMode: .disabled, synthetic flat features):
  - 3 lexical-origin regions
  - 75% recall (3/4 ads, ±10s grace)
  - 66% precision
  - 15% ad-second coverage  <-- the key number to lift
  - regions are point-like (5-7s) anchored on single-atom lexical hits

Phase 5 success criteria:
  1. Phase4ShadowBenchmarkTests on the same fixture shows ad-second coverage moving from 15% toward 80%+ as the doc claims
  2. Decoded spans are contiguous (no micro-fragments < 5s)
  3. Duration constraints prevent implausible spans (no 30-minute "ads")
  4. Correction masks prevent re-detection of user-reverted spans
  5. Lenient region-recall does NOT regress below 75%
  6. Zero new test flakes when run parallelized (parallelizable: true is now standard)

title: RegionFeatureExtractor
description:
Compute a uniform feature bundle for every proposed region, regardless of origin. This eliminates source asymmetry: FM-origin regions get lexical/acoustic treatment, lexical-origin regions get FM evidence.

Feature bundle per region (RegionFeatureBundle struct, defined in this file):
- Lexical score: re-run LexicalScanner patterns over region transcript text
- Acoustic features: fetch overlapping FeatureWindows, compute RMS drop, spectral change, music, speaker change scores
- Transcript quality: from FM scan or heuristic
- Prior score: PodcastProfile slot positions, sponsor knowledge hits
- FM evidence: commercial intent, ownership, consensus strength, evidence anchors, alternative explanation, boundary precision, certainty band, reason tags

Extract shared region-scoring helpers from ClassifierService.RuleBasedClassifier:
- computeRmsDropScore(windows:) → Double
- computeSpectralChangeScore(windows:) → Double
- computeMusicScore(windows:) → Double
- computeSpeakerChangeScore(windows:) → Double
- computePriorScore(candidate:episodeDuration:priors:) → Double

These become free functions or a shared RegionScoring enum so both RuleBasedClassifier (hot path) and RegionFeatureExtractor (backfill) use the same logic.

Files: RegionFeatureExtractor.swift (NEW — includes RegionFeatureBundle struct), ClassifierService.swift (extract helpers into shared RegionScoring)

Acceptance: Every ProposedRegion gets a complete RegionFeatureBundle. FM-origin regions have lexical scores. Lexical-origin regions have FM evidence. Extracted helpers produce identical output to original ClassifierService methods.
notes:
Specific helpers to extract from ClassifierService (RuleBasedClassifier):
- computeRmsDropScore(windows:) → Double
- computeSpectralChangeScore(windows:) → Double
- computeMusicScore(windows:) → Double

- computePriorScore(candidate:episodeDuration:priors:) → Double

title: RegionProposalBuilder
description:
Normalize all cue harvester + FM proposals into source-agnostic canonical regions.

- Lexical candidates (from LexicalScanner)

- Sponsor knowledge matches (from SponsorKnowledgeMatcher, initially empty)

FM consensus clustering:
- Cluster overlapping positive/uncertain FM spans
- Require anchor-consistent consensus: >=2 windows with aligned spans, sufficient center separation, IoU agreement
- Union evidence across overlapping windows
- Single FM positive without overlap → low-consensus proposal (enters fusion at reduced weight)

Output: [ProposedRegion] with:
- Canonical start/end atom ordinals and times
- Origin flags (which sources proposed this region)
- FM consensus strength
- Canonicalized evidence (from CommercialEvidenceResolver)
- Lexical/sponsor/fingerprint match references

From this point forward, pipeline does not distinguish between sources.

title: CommercialEvidenceResolver
description:
Maps FM evidence output back to deterministic catalog entries. This is the firewall between FM output and the SponsorKnowledgeStore.

For each FM EvidenceAnchor:
1. Prefer evidenceRef resolution (FM pointed to a catalog entry)
2. Fall back to lineRef-based extraction (look up atom text, apply deterministic extraction rules)
3. Only deterministically resolved spans are eligible for SponsorKnowledgeStore writes

If FM says 'sponsorName at line 5' but no extractable brand name exists in that atom's text, the evidence anchor is still valid for classification scoring but does NOT write sponsor memory.

title: CoveragePlanner + BackfillJob
description:

CoveragePlanner selects policy:
- fullCoverage: cold-start shows (<5 episodes), first episode after cohort invalidation, degrading recall
- targetedWithAudit: mature shows (>=5 episodes, stable precision) — scan harvester proposals, likely ad slots, mandatory random audit windows (10-15% sampled)

Each phase is idempotent — re-entering after crash resumes from progressCursor. Phase transitions are atomic.

AdmissionController: schedules by listener value (cold-start > frequently played > backlog). Respects thermal state, battery, charging. Serial by default.

title: ScanCohort + SemanticScanStatus models
description:
Create the provenance and failure models for FM scanning.

ScanCohort captures what produced the FM scan results — changes here trigger FM rescan:
- promptLabel (human-readable), promptHash (rendered prompt hash), schemaHash, scanPlanHash, normalizationHash, osBuild, locale, appBuild

SemanticScanStatus covers the real Apple Foundation Models runtime error surface:
- queued, running, success
- unavailable, unsupportedLocale, exceededContextWindow, decodingFailure
- refusal, guardrailViolation, assetsUnavailable, rateLimited
- thermalDeferred, cancelled, failedTransient

Retry policy per status (documented in code):
- exceededContextWindow → shrink window, retry once
- decodingFailure → simplify schema (fall back to coarse), retry once
- refusal/guardrailViolation → persist, never reinterpret as 'not an ad'
- assetsUnavailable → defer, retry later
- rateLimited → backoff, retry
- thermalDeferred/cancelled → resume from checkpoint

title: Phase 3: FM Semantic Scanner + Shadow Logging
description:
The core FM scanning pipeline, running in shadow mode only. This is where Foundation Models enters the picture. Three-pass scanning (coarse → zoom → refine) with token budgeting, certainty bands (not raw doubles), and grounded evidence anchors that point to deterministic catalog entries.

Key architectural choices:
- ScanCohort provenance (separate from DecisionCohort) so policy tweaks don't trigger rescans
- Certainty bands (weak/moderate/strong) instead of raw confidence floats — FM self-reported numbers drift across cohorts
- BoundaryPrecision (rough/usable/precise) instead of boundaryConfidence double
- ReasonTag enums instead of free-text reasoning — production decisions use structured tags only
- Evidence catalog refs in FM prompts so FM can point to deterministic entries
- Fresh LanguageModelSession per window (no context accumulation)
- Prewarm once per job via prewarm(promptPrefix:)
- Approved cohort gating: unknown (osBuild, ScanCohort) defaults to shadow

Failure handling mirrors real Apple Foundation Models runtime: exceededContextWindow, decodingFailure, refusal, guardrailViolation, assetsUnavailable, rateLimited, thermalDeferred, cancelled.

Verification: FM produces classifications on test episodes in shadow mode. Coarse pass covers full transcript. Refinement produces grounded evidence anchors resolving to catalog entries. Operational metrics within budget. Replay harness produces stable results within a cohort.
close_reason: All Phase 3 child beads are closed; FM semantic scanner and shadow logging coverage are complete and verified on the focused simulator suite.

title: EvidenceCatalogBuilder
description:
Deterministic extraction of commercial evidence entities from transcript atoms BEFORE FM runs. This is the critical firewall between raw transcript text and FM-visible evidence handles.

Extracts and catalogs:
- URLs / vanity URLs (pattern: 'X.com/Y', 'X dot com slash Y', domain patterns)
- Promo codes (pattern: 'code X', 'promo code X', alphanumeric sequences near purchase language)
- CTA phrases ('get started today', 'sign up now', 'click the link', etc.)
- Disclosure phrases ('brought to you by', 'sponsored by', 'partnered with', etc.)
- Brand-like spans (capitalized multi-word sequences, proper nouns near commercial context)

Each catalog entry gets a stable evidenceRef integer that can be injected into FM prompts:
[E0] "betterhelp.com slash" (url, line 2)
[E1] "BetterHelp" (sponsorName, line 1)

FM refinement schema includes an evidenceRef field so the model can point to catalog entries rather than authoring free-text. CommercialEvidenceResolver (Phase 3) maps FM output back to these deterministic entries.

Files: EvidenceCatalogBuilder.swift (NEW)

Acceptance: Catalog entries match manual inspection on test episodes. All extractable URLs, promo codes, and known sponsor phrases are captured. Evidence refs are stable within a transcript version.

title: AcousticBreakDetector
description:
Scan all FeatureWindows for energy drops, spectral flux spikes, and pause clusters that suggest segment boundaries across the full episode.

This produces candidate BREAK POINTS, not ad regions — these seed RegionProposalBuilder as potential ad boundaries. Runs in milliseconds over pre-computed features already in SQLite (FeatureWindow table).

Detection signals:
- RMS energy drops > 35% between adjacent windows
- Spectral flux spikes above 80th percentile
- Pause probability clusters (consecutive windows with pauseProbability > 0.6)
- Combined score for multi-signal transitions

Output: array of AcousticBreak (time, breakStrength, signals)

Files: AcousticBreakDetector.swift (NEW)

Acceptance: Detects known ad boundaries in test episodes. Runs in <100ms for a 60-minute episode. No false positives from normal speech pauses.
notes: Note: AcousticBreakDetector reads directly from FeatureWindow table (existing), not TranscriptAtom. No dependency on 1.1 needed. Output is consumed by RegionProposalBuilder (Phase 4).

title: Phase 2: Cue Harvesters + Evidence Catalog
description:
Build the deterministic evidence layer that runs before FM. These are cheap, fast, and broad — bridging the gap between regex (narrow but fast) and FM (broad but slow). The EvidenceCatalogBuilder is particularly important: it builds a deterministic catalog of URLs, promo codes, CTA/disclosure phrases, and brand-like spans BEFORE FM runs. FM refinement then points to evidence catalog refs rather than authoring free-text sponsor names. This is the firewall that prevents FM hallucinations from poisoning the SponsorKnowledgeStore.

Harvesters run in parallel, all deterministic, all complete in milliseconds.

Verification: Harvesters produce candidate regions on test episodes. Evidence catalog contains extractable entities matching manual inspection. Coverage is broader than LexicalScanner alone.

title: TranscriptQualityEstimator
description:
Estimate transcript quality per segment before FM scanning. Low-quality segments can be skipped or deferred by the CoveragePlanner, and quality scores feed into FM evidence weighting.

Quality signals:
- Punctuation density (low = likely ASR without post-processing)
- Token density per second (abnormally high/low = ASR artifacts)
- Overlap/OOV rate (repeated words, unusual tokens)
- Confidence proxy (if ASR provides per-word confidence, aggregate it)

Output: per-segment TranscriptQuality enum (good / degraded / unusable) plus a numeric qualityScore for finer-grained decisions.

Files: TranscriptQualityEstimator.swift (NEW)

Acceptance: Quality scores correlate with known-bad transcript regions on test episodes. degraded/unusable segments align with audibly noisy audio.
notes: Dependency on 1.2 (TranscriptSegmenter) is intentional: quality is estimated per-segment, not per-atom. The segmenter's boundaries define the evaluation units.

title: TranscriptAtom model + TranscriptVersion
description:
Create the TranscriptAtom model with versioned ordinal identity and TranscriptVersion tracking.

TranscriptAtomKey is the durable primary key: (analysisAssetId: String, transcriptVersion: String, atomOrdinal: Int). contentHash is retained for matching/debugging but is NOT the primary key — it breaks on timing drift, repeated phrases, and normalization changes.

TranscriptVersion tracks: transcriptVersion (hash of atom sequence), normalizationHash (transcript normalization pipeline), sourceHash (ASR model / source identity).

CueAnchor is a stable anchor for materialized cues: (analysisAssetId, transcriptVersion, firstAtomOrdinal, lastAtomOrdinal, approxStartTime, approxEndTime, boundaryFingerprint).

FM prompts will use compact lineRef integers that resolve back to atom keys — never expose atom IDs/hashes to the model (wastes tokens).

Files: TranscriptAtom.swift (NEW), update TranscriptChunk to add transcriptVersion + atomOrdinal fields.

Acceptance: TranscriptAtomKey is Hashable, Codable, Sendable. Every TranscriptChunk can produce a TranscriptAtom. Atom ordinals are sequential within a transcript version.
notes: CueAnchor acceptance criteria: CueAnchor is Codable, Sendable. Round-trip encoding test passes. boundaryFingerprint is computed from audio features at boundaries. CueAnchor can fuzzy-match across transcript versions using approxStartTime/approxEndTime + boundaryFingerprint.

title: TranscriptSegmenter
description:
Segment episodes into coherent regions using pauses, speaker turns, punctuation, and discourse markers. This produces natural semantic boundaries BEFORE token-budgeted FM windowing — so FM windows pack coherent segments rather than arbitrary time slices.

Inputs: array of TranscriptAtom (time-ordered)
Outputs: array of TranscriptSegment (startAtomOrdinal, endAtomOrdinal, segmentType, boundaryConfidence)

Segment boundary signals (in priority order):
1. Long pauses (>1.5s silence) — strongest boundary signal
2. Speaker changes (from existing speakerClusterId in FeatureWindow)
3. Punctuation clusters (period/question mark followed by capitalization)
4. Discourse markers ('anyway', 'so', 'moving on', 'let me tell you about')

The segmenter is cheap and deterministic — no ML, just pattern matching on existing features. Segments are the packing unit for FM token-budgeted windows.

Files: TranscriptSegmenter.swift (NEW)

Acceptance: Segments align to natural boundaries on test episodes. No segment spans more than 120s. Every atom belongs to exactly one segment.
notes: Pre-existing infrastructure: FeatureWindow table already exists in AnalysisStore with speakerClusterId, pauseProbability, rms, spectralFlux per 2s window. The segmenter reads these via AnalysisStore.fetchFeatureWindows().

title: Phase 1: Transcript Identity + Segmentation
description:
Establish the stable transcript identity foundation that all subsequent phases build on. Every FM output, user correction, sponsor memory write, and training example will be keyed by versioned TranscriptAtom ordinals — (analysisAssetId, transcriptVersion, atomOrdinal). This MUST land before the first FM scan because retrofitting identity after semantic references exist creates migration tax across the entire system.

Key deliverables:
- TranscriptAtom with versioned ordinal identity
- TranscriptVersion tracking (normalization hash, source hash)  
- TranscriptSegmenter for coherent region boundaries (pauses, speaker turns, punctuation, discourse markers)
- TranscriptQualityEstimator (ASR confidence proxy, punctuation density, overlap/OOV rate)
- TranscriptChunk gains transcriptVersion and atomOrdinal fields

Why versioned ordinals over content hashes: hash(normalizedText + startTime) breaks on ASR timing drift, punctuation restoration, normalization tweaks, and repeated identical phrases. The compound key (assetId, transcriptVersion, ordinal) is stable within a version and cross-version continuity is handled by TranscriptAlignmentMap (Phase 13).

Verification: Every transcript chunk has a stable atom key. Segments align to natural boundaries. Quality scores correlate with known-bad transcript regions.

title: Foundation Model Ad Classifier
description: Multi-phase project to add Foundation Models-based semantic scanning to the backfill pipeline for ad detection. Fixes the core architectural gap where the entire detection pipeline is gated on LexicalScanner regex hits, missing conversational ad reads entirely. Scores land ~0.42 for real ads (below 0.65 skip threshold) because the lexical scanner produces zero hits for host-read ads like 'I've been using BetterHelp for months...' — no sponsor phrases, no promo codes, no URL patterns. The FM scanner covers the full transcript, catches conversational ads, and feeds discovered sponsors back into the hot path via a compiled lexicon for future episodes. Key architectural principles: (1) FM produces grounded evidence, not sponsor facts — deterministic EvidenceCatalogBuilder runs before FM, FM points to catalog refs, CommercialEvidenceResolver maps back to transcript text. (2) Evidence quorum, not blanket non-FM corroboration — multi-window consensus + 2+ evidence kinds can satisfy current-episode skip eligibility. (3) Scan-time evidence and decision-time policy are separate artifacts (ScanCohort vs DecisionCohort) so policy tweaks don't trigger FM rescans. (4) Certainty bands, not raw doubles — FM outputs are CertaintyBand enums calibrated externally per cohort. (5) Append-only event ledger with derived stores for replay and postmortems. (6) Knowledge quarantine lifecycle (candidate→quarantined→active→decayed→blocked). (7) Unknown model cohorts default to shadow. 15 implementation phases, each end-to-end verifiable.
notes: Deferred 2026-07-24 (founder reorder): retention-phase work — revisit at ~$5k MRR / after listeners love the core. Not deleted, just not now. Categories: Mac, TTS, chapters, federation, ad-atlas, specialist/fancy-AI, detection improvements users won't notice.

The actual baseline breakage today was Swift Testing parallel execution flakiness. 950 tests running in parallel collided on: (a) process-global singletons — AVAudioSession interruption notifications cascading self.pause() into every live PlaybackService instance, and MPNowPlayingInfoCenter.default() clobbered across concurrent writers — and (b) cooperative thread-pool starvation inflating Task.sleep(5ms) to 4+ seconds under 950-way parallelism, which blew polling-loop deadline budgets. Diagnose the exact asset catalog or project configuration problem, fix it without disturbing unrelated workspace changes, and verify the build gets past the asset compilation step.
notes: Root cause: the apparent actool asset failure was sandbox/CoreSimulator visibility, not a broken asset catalog. An unsandboxed xcodebuild build-for-testing run got past asset compilation, then uncovered and we fixed two real test-build blockers: a missing try on makeTempDir() in PipelineIntegrationTests and missing Sendable conformance for the IgnoringRangeHTTPServer helper in DownloadManagerTests. Verified with xcodebuild build-for-testing -scheme Playhead -destination generic/platform=iOS\ Simulator CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO outside the sandbox, which now succeeds.

title: Guard against invalid SwiftData descendant predicates on URL fields
description: Why this issue exists and what needs to be done: add a repo-level regression test or lint-style guard that fails when SwiftData #Predicate blocks descend through stored URL properties such as .absoluteString, which triggers runtime fatal errors during fetches. Scope includes implementing the guard, covering current predicate usage, and documenting the failure mode in test intent.
notes: Added a source-level SwiftData predicate guardrail test in CoreServiceTests. It discovers URL-typed SwiftData model properties from Playhead/Models, scans app #Predicate blocks, and fails if any predicate descends through those URL properties (for example .feedURL.absoluteString), which is the runtime crash pattern we hit in subscribe flow.

title: E2E: Analysis State Machine Recovery
description:
Prove that the AnalysisCoordinator state machine is robust under interruption and recovers correctly. This is the hardest thing to get right in a multi-pipeline system.

## Test: Crash at Each State Transition
For each AnalysisSession state (.queued, .spooling, .featuresReady, .hotPathReady, .backfill):
1. Start analysis, wait until session reaches target state
2. Force-kill app
3. Relaunch, play same episode
4. Verify: session resumes from persisted state (not from scratch)
5. Verify: no duplicate work (chunks, features, windows not re-created)
6. Verify: final skip behavior identical to uninterrupted run

## Test: Scrub During Active Analysis
1. Play episode, analysis running at ~3 minutes ahead
2. User scrubs to 30 minutes
3. Verify: AnalysisCoordinator reprioritizes to new region
4. Verify: previous work preserved (not deleted)
5. Verify: hot-path now targets region around 30 minutes
6. Verify: skip cues near 30 minutes arrive within safety margin

## Test: Rapid Scrub (Stress)
1. Play episode
2. Scrub to 10 min, then 40 min, then 5 min, then 50 min (4 rapid scrubs)
3. Verify: no crash, no deadlock, no orphaned sessions
4. Verify: analysis settles on final position (50 min)
5. Verify: previous positions' work preserved for potential future use

## Test: Speed Change During Analysis
1. Play at 1x, analysis running
2. Switch to 3x
3. Verify: hot-path safety margin recalculated (wall-clock margin, not audio minutes)
4. Verify: analysis speeds up prioritization to stay ahead of 3x playback
5. Switch back to 1x → verify graceful adjustment

## Test: Concurrent Episodes (Queue)
1. Play episode A, analysis starts
2. Queue episode B
3. When episode A finishes, episode B auto-plays
4. Verify: episode B gets its own AnalysisAsset and AnalysisSession
5. Verify: episode A's completed analysis preserved
6. Verify: no state leakage between sessions

## Test: Corrupt Analysis State Recovery
1. Manually corrupt an AnalysisSession record (set invalid state)
2. Play the affected episode
3. Verify: AnalysisCoordinator detects corruption, creates fresh session
4. Verify: no crash, analysis proceeds normally
5. Verify: corrupt record marked as .failed with reason logged

Acceptance criteria:
- Zero data loss across all crash/recovery scenarios
- No duplicate analysis work after recovery
- Scrub/speed changes handled within 2 seconds
- Concurrent episodes isolated correctly
- Corrupt state detected and recovered gracefully

title: E2E: Privacy & Network Isolation
description:
Prove that zero audio or transcript data ever leaves the device. Maps to Success Criterion #11 and the core privacy promise.

## Test: Network Monitor During Full Pipeline
1. Install a URLProtocol intercept that logs ALL outbound network requests
2. Play episode from locally cached audio
3. Run full analysis pipeline: decode → ASR → detect → skip → banner
4. Assert: ZERO network requests during transcription
5. Assert: ZERO network requests during ad classification
6. Assert: ZERO network requests during skip orchestration
7. Assert: ZERO network requests during banner rendering
8. Only allowed network: feed refresh, iTunes Search, audio download (all user-initiated)

## Test: No Data in Shared Containers
1. Run full analysis pipeline
2. Inspect: App Group containers, shared UserDefaults, Keychain
3. Assert: no transcript text stored in any shared location
4. Assert: no audio data in any shared location
5. Assert: analysis DB and models in app-private container only

## Test: File Protection
1. Verify: analysis SQLite DB has NSFileProtectionComplete
2. Verify: transcript store has NSFileProtectionComplete
3. Verify: model files have NSFileProtectionComplete
4. Verify: cached audio has NSFileProtectionComplete

## Test: Export Redaction
1. Trigger diagnostic export
2. Verify: transcript text redacted by default
3. Verify: no raw audio in export
4. Verify: only aggregate metrics, no PII

Acceptance criteria:
- Zero outbound requests during analysis (verified by network intercept)
- No data leakage to shared containers
- File protection applied to all sensitive data
- Export redaction verified

title: E2E: Feed & Discovery
description:
Prove podcast search, subscribe, and feed refresh work correctly. Maps to Success Criterion #1.

## Test: Search and Subscribe
1. Search "The Daily" → verify results appear
2. Tap result → verify podcast detail shows title, author, artwork
3. Subscribe → verify podcast appears in Library
4. Verify: episodes loaded with titles, dates, durations
5. Verify: Podcast and Episode records in SwiftData

## Test: Feed Refresh
1. Subscribe to podcast
2. Simulate new episode added to feed
3. Pull-to-refresh in Library
4. Verify: new episode appears in episode list
5. Verify: existing episodes not duplicated

## Test: GUID-Based Deduplication
1. Refresh feed that reorders items but keeps same GUIDs
2. Verify: no duplicate episodes created
3. Verify: episode metadata updated if changed

## Test: Malformed Feed Handling
1. Parse feed with: missing GUIDs, relative URLs, malformed dates
2. Verify: no crash
3. Verify: episodes with parseable data are created
4. Verify: unparseable episodes skipped with logged warning

## Test: Search Rate Limiting
1. Fire 30 search requests in rapid succession
2. Verify: no crash, no hang
3. Verify: rate limiting kicks in gracefully (debounce + backoff)
4. Verify: cached results returned where available

## Test: Offline Search
1. Disable network
2. Search for previously searched term
3. Verify: cached results returned
4. Search for new term → verify: appropriate error shown, no crash

Acceptance criteria:
- Search → subscribe → refresh works end-to-end
- No duplicate episodes under any feed refresh scenario
- Malformed feeds don't crash the app
- Rate limiting transparent to user

title: E2E: Degraded Conditions
description:
Prove the app remains useful under adverse conditions. Maps to Success Criteria #12 (no background dependency), #13 (works without Foundation Models).

## Test: No Foundation Models
1. Mock CapabilitiesService: foundationModelsAvailable = false
2. Play episode with known ads
3. Verify: hot-path detection works (lexical scanner + classifier)
4. Verify: skips fire at correct times
5. Verify: banners show generic copy (no metadata extraction)
6. Verify: CapabilitySnapshot persisted correctly

## Test: Thermal Throttling
1. Play episode, simulate thermalState = .serious
2. Verify: hot-path window reduced (fewer chunks ahead of playhead)
3. Verify: backfill paused
4. Verify: playback continues unaffected
5. Verify: existing skip cues still fire
6. Simulate thermalState = .critical
7. Verify: all analysis paused
8. Verify: playback still works, existing cues still fire
9. Thermal recovers to .nominal → verify analysis resumes

## Test: Low Power Mode
1. Enable Low Power Mode
2. Play episode
3. Verify: hot-path lookahead window reduced
4. Verify: backfill entirely deferred
5. Verify: skip quality acceptable (may miss some ads, but no false positives)
6. Disable Low Power Mode → verify full analysis resumes

## Test: Low Battery (< 20%, Not Charging)
1. Mock battery level at 15%, not charging
2. Play episode
3. Verify: non-critical analysis paused
4. Verify: playback continues
5. Simulate plugging in charger → verify analysis resumes

## Test: Foreground-Only Reliability
1. Play episode entirely in foreground
2. Never grant background processing time
3. Verify: hot-path analysis stays ahead of playback
4. Verify: skips fire correctly
5. Verify: this proves skip reliability does NOT depend on background runtime

## Test: App Backgrounded During Playback
1. Play episode, send app to background
2. Verify: audio continues
3. Verify: hot-path analysis continues (BGContinuedProcessingTask or audio session keeps app alive)
4. Return to foreground → verify: analysis state consistent, no gaps

## Test: Slow/No Network
1. Episode fully cached locally
2. Disable network
3. Verify: playback works, analysis works, skips fire
4. Verify: no network calls attempted for transcription/classification
5. Verify: this proves Success Criterion #11 (zero network for analysis)

## Test: Low Storage
1. Mock available storage at 100MB (below model download threshold)
2. If models already downloaded: verify analysis works normally
3. If models not downloaded: verify graceful error, no crash
4. Verify: user directed to storage management in Settings

Acceptance criteria:
- App never crashes under any degraded condition
- Playback never interrupted by analysis failures
- Existing skip cues survive all degradation scenarios
- Clear degradation hierarchy: backfill drops first, then hot-path reduces, playback never affected

title: E2E: Playback Reliability
description:
Prove that the podcast player works reliably as a player, independent of ad detection. Maps to Success Criteria #2 (standard controls) and #8 (clean transitions).

## Test: Basic Controls
1. Play → verify audio output and time advancing
2. Pause → verify audio stops, time frozen
3. Resume → verify audio resumes from exact position
4. Seek to 50% → verify playback at correct position (±1s)
5. Skip +15s → verify position advances 15s (±0.5s)
6. Skip -30s → verify position retreats 30s (±0.5s)
7. Skip -30s near start → verify clamps to 0, doesn't go negative

## Test: Speed Control
1. Set speed to each value: 0.5x, 1.0x, 1.5x, 2.0x, 2.5x, 3.0x
2. At each speed: verify audio is audible and not distorted
3. Verify: playback position advances at correct rate (±5%)
4. Change speed mid-playback → verify smooth transition (no gap, no repeat)

## Test: Interruptions
1. Play audio, simulate phone call interruption
2. Verify: audio pauses
3. End call → verify: audio resumes (if user had been listening)
4. Play audio, simulate Siri activation
5. Verify: audio ducks or pauses
6. Siri dismisses → verify: audio resumes

## Test: Route Changes
1. Play with headphones connected
2. Disconnect headphones
3. Verify: audio pauses immediately (Apple policy)
4. Reconnect headphones, tap play
5. Verify: audio resumes

## Test: Background Audio
1. Play audio, send app to background
2. Verify: audio continues playing
3. Verify: Now Playing info center shows correct title/artwork/controls
4. Verify: lock screen controls (play/pause/skip) work
5. Return to app → verify: UI state matches playback state

## Test: Skip Cue Smoothing
1. Set up skip cue CMTimeRange at known position
2. Play through the skip cue
3. Streamed audio: verify duck → seek → release (no audible pop or silence gap > 300ms)
4. Cached audio: verify micro-crossfade is smooth
5. Measure: skip transition duration < 500ms

## Test: Long-Form Playback
1. Play a 90-minute episode from start
2. Simulate 2x speed (effectively 45 min wall-clock)
3. Verify: no memory leaks (check memory at 0, 15, 30, 45 min marks)
4. Verify: playback position tracking stays accurate throughout
5. Verify: Now Playing info stays in sync

Acceptance criteria:
- All test scenarios pass on iPhone 15 Pro simulator
- No audio glitches detected via automated waveform analysis
- Memory usage stays flat (no leaks over long playback)
- Every assertion has specific numeric tolerance

title: App Navigation Structure
description:
Tab-based app navigation composing all views into a coherent structure. The structural shell that hosts all screens.

Structure:
- TabView with 3 tabs: Library (square.stack icon), Browse (magnifyingglass icon), Settings (gearshape icon)
- Tab bar: uses .tint(AppColors.accent) for Copper active state; inactive icons use SwiftUI default styling
- NavigationStack within all three tabs (Library, Browse, Settings) — each view owns its own NavigationStack internally
- Now Playing: presented via .fullScreenCover (not a tab) — triggered by tapping the mini player (showNowPlaying binding)
- Mini player slot: positioned above tab bar via safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom, spacing: 0) in a shared tabRoot helper. Renders NowPlayingBar when audio is playing.
- Tab switch animation: .animation(Motion.standard, value: runtime.isPlayingEpisode) on the TabView

Navigation flows:
- Library tab → Podcast detail (Episode List) → tap episode → Now Playing (fullScreenCover)
- Browse tab → Search → tap result → Podcast detail → Subscribe → Library tab
- Any tab → tap Mini Player → Now Playing (fullScreenCover)

State management:
- Selected tab: NOT persisted across launches (no UserDefaults/AppStorage) — uses SwiftUI default
- NowPlayingViewModel lifecycle: created on first isPlayingEpisode=true, startObserving() called; on isPlayingEpisode=false, stopObserving() then nilled, showNowPlaying set to false
- Mini player visibility driven by runtime.isPlayingEpisode AND nowPlayingViewModel existence (both checked in miniPlayerInset)
- .onChange(of: runtime.isPlayingEpisode) syncs the viewModel lifecycle

Acceptance criteria:
- All three tabs navigate correctly with proper icons and labels
- Navigation stack push/pop works within Library, Browse, and Settings tabs
- Mini player persists across tab switches (rendered via safeAreaInset in tabRoot helper)
- Tab bar uses Quiet Instrument aesthetic (Copper active tint verified against design tokens)
- VoiceOver: mini player announces "Now playing: [title]. Tap to open full player" with combined children
- No duplicate NavigationStack wrapping (NavigationStack lives inside each tab view, not in ContentView)
- Rotation: portrait only in MVP (no landscape layout needed)

NOT YET IMPLEMENTED:
- Deep link resolution
- Tab persistence across launches
notes: Code review audit (2026-04-10): Corrected 3rd tab from 'Now Playing (waveform)' to 'Settings (gearshape)'. Library icon is square.stack not house. NavigationStack is used in all 3 tabs (not just Library+Browse). Now Playing is fullScreenCover, not a tab. Tab persistence and deep links are not implemented — added to NOT YET IMPLEMENTED section.

title: Labeled Test Corpus
description:
Curated set of podcast episodes with human-verified ad boundary annotations. Ground truth for the replay simulator and all quality metrics. This corpus is pre-curated — episodes are manually selected, downloaded, and annotated offline. No runtime services needed to build it.

## Corpus Composition (minimum 15 episodes)

Category 1 — Clear host-read ads (5 episodes):
- Episodes where host reads sponsor copy in their own voice
- Clear transitions ("And now a word from our sponsor")
- Well-defined start/end boundaries
- From 5 different shows across genres

Category 2 — Dynamic insertion ads (3 episodes):
- Pre-roll and mid-roll dynamically inserted by ad tech
- Often have music beds, different production quality from main show
- Include 2 variants of the same episode with different ad fills

Category 3 — Blended/ambiguous ads (3 episodes):
- Host weaves sponsor mention into content naturally
- No clear transition markers
- Hardest to detect — these test fail-open behavior

Category 4 — Edge cases (4 episodes):
- Episode with zero ads (verify no false positives)
- Episode with 5+ ads (high ad density)
- Episode with very short ad (< 15s promo mention)
- Episode with back-to-back ads (no content between sponsors)

## Annotation Format (JSON per episode)
{
  "episode_id": "corpus-001",
  "show_name": "Example Podcast",
  "duration_seconds": 3600,
  "ad_windows": [
    {
      "start_seconds": 180.0,
      "end_seconds": 240.0,
      "advertiser": "Squarespace",
      "product": "Website builder",
      "ad_type": "host_read",
      "transition_type": "explicit",
      "confidence_notes": "Clear brought to you by intro"
    }
  ],
  "content_windows": [
    {
      "start_seconds": 0.0,
      "end_seconds": 180.0,
      "notes": "Interview content — must NEVER be skipped"
    }
  ],
  "variant_of": null,
  "audio_fingerprint": "sha256:abc123..."
}

## Annotation Process
1. Human listens to full episode
2. Marks ad start/end times (±0.5s precision)
3. Labels advertiser, product, ad type
4. Marks content windows that must never be skipped (false-positive traps)
5. Second human verifies annotations
6. Audio cached alongside annotations in test fixtures

## Storage
- Audio files: TestFixtures/Corpus/Audio/
- Annotations: TestFixtures/Corpus/Annotations/
- Variant pairs stored with cross-references
- Total size estimate: ~2-3GB (15 episodes × 30-90 min each)

Acceptance criteria:
- Minimum 15 episodes across all 4 categories
- Every annotation verified by at least one human listener
- Content windows explicitly marked (false-positive traps)
- Replay simulator consumes corpus without errors
- At least one variant pair for dynamic ad insertion testing
- Annotations at ±0.5s precision
notes:
Added local corpus bootstrap tooling: whisper.cpp transcript wrapper, transcript-to-draft annotation generator, ignored Transcripts/Drafts directories, model ignore rules, and docs. This reduces labeling effort but does not satisfy human-verified corpus acceptance yet.
Generated local corpus bootstrap artifacts for 15 public RSS episodes: 15 audio files, 15 whisper.cpp transcript JSON files, and 15 draft annotation JSON + 15 review markdown files under ignored TestFixtures/Corpus/{Audio,Transcripts,Drafts}. Drafts are heuristic only and still need human review/promotion before acceptance.
Codex transcript-only review completed for the 15 local draft episodes. Wrote ignored review artifacts to TestFixtures/Corpus/Drafts/codex-transcript-review.json and codex-vs-draft-comparison.json. Codex marked 29 transcript-level ad/promo pods vs 56 generator cue windows; generator covers only 754.7s vs 3173.2s Codex-marked ad time, with 5 apparent draft false positives and 26 undercovered Codex pods. Still requires audio boundary verification before promotion.
Closed playhead-l2f.3 and playhead-l2f.4 after the first audio-reviewed slice: 15 selected episodes reviewed, 12 annotation JSON files committed, 3 ordinary false-positive-only episodes intentionally skipped, and coverage documented in TestFixtures/Corpus/README.md. Parent remains open for any broader replay-simulator/second-pass acceptance that should not be conflated with the promoted slice.
