title: Now Playing Skip Markers
description:
Visual treatment of detected ad segments in the timeline rail on the Now Playing screen.

Design:
- Ad segments rendered as recessed blocks within the progress rail via adSegmentBlock() helper
- Color: Palette.charcoal fill with RoundedRectangle cornerRadius 1
- Recessed look: two overlays — (1) inner stroke Color.black.opacity(0.3), lineWidth 0.5; (2) top inset 1pt Color.black.opacity(0.15) bar for depth illusion. Clipped.
- Minimum block width: 2pt (clamped via max(w, 2))
- Visual height: railHeight (4pt), but frame expanded to touchTargetHeight (44pt) with contentShape(Rectangle()) for accessible tap targets
- Segments positioned via offset(x:) based on segment.lowerBound * width

Data source:
- NowPlayingViewModel.adSegmentRanges: [ClosedRange<Double>] — fractional 0...1 ranges
- Fed by SkipOrchestrator.appliedSegmentsStream() — an in-memory AsyncStream of (start, end) tuples in seconds, converted to fractional ranges by NowPlayingViewModel. NOT a direct SQLite query.

Skip animation:
- Detects skip when progress jumps > skipJumpThreshold (0.02 = 2%)
- Sets isGliding=true, which activates glideAnimation: .easeInOut(duration: 0.45)
- Glide state auto-resets after 500ms via glideResetTask (cancellable Task with Task.sleep)
- Normal playback: glideAnimation returns nil (no animation, continuous updates)
- Playhead line: Rectangle 2pt wide, AppColors.accent, height 12pt (18pt when dragging)

Scrub gesture:
- DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0) on the rail
- Scrub begin: hapticPlayer.play(.control) via handleScrubBegin()
- Scrub end: onSeek(fraction) then hapticPlayer.play(.control) via handleScrubEnd()
- Haptic player injectable (defaults to SystemHapticPlayer, tests use RecordingHapticPlayer)

Tap-to-explain (Phase 7.2):
- onAdSegmentTap: ((Int) -> Void)? callback fires with segment index when user taps an ad block
- Hit target expanded to 44pt height via frame + contentShape for accessibility
- Caller maps index to DecodedSpan for AdRegionPopover

Accessibility:
- Each ad segment: accessibilityLabel "Ad segment N of M", hint "Tap to see details about this ad segment", trait .isButton
- Timeline scrubber: accessibilityLabel "Timeline scrubber", value "N percent"
- Adjustable action: ±5% increment/decrement via accessibilityAdjustableAction

Acceptance criteria:
- Ad segments visible as recessed blocks in timeline rail (visually distinct but not aggressive)
- Segments update as new segments stream in (no full-rail re-render)
- Skip animation smooth at 60fps (no dropped frames)
- Skip animation duration 0.45s easeInOut
- Multiple ad segments render correctly without overlapping
- Scrub haptics fire on begin and end (.control events)
- Tap-to-explain fires onAdSegmentTap with correct segment index

NOT YET IMPLEMENTED:
- Haptic on skip initiation (no haptic fires when a skip jumps the playhead — only scrub begin/end use haptics)
- VoiceOver time-range announcements ("Ad segment from [time] to [time]")
- Filtering by decisionState (.reverted segments — currently shows whatever appliedSegmentsStream provides)
notes: Code review audit (2026-04-10): Corrected recessed block color from Ink to Palette.charcoal. Skip animation is 0.45s easeInOut (not 0.3s custom ease). Skip haptic is NOT implemented — no haptic fires on skip. Data source is SkipOrchestrator.appliedSegmentsStream() (in-memory AsyncStream), not a direct SQLite AdWindows query. VoiceOver says 'Ad segment N of M' (not time ranges). Added tap-to-explain (Phase 7.2) detail.

title: Banner Evidence & Copy Logic
description:
Wire banners to AdWindow metadata with strict evidence-bound copy rules.

Copy rules (implemented in AdBannerView.bannerCopy(for:)):
- metadataSource != "none" AND metadataConfidence >= 0.60 AND advertiser present → "Skipped · [advertiser] · [product]"
- Evidence weak or missing → generic: "Skipped sponsor segment"
- Never surface brand solely because model guessed it
- Template-driven via BannerCopyLine struct, never free-form generated copy
- metadataSource is a String field on AdSkipBannerItem (not an enum). Known values: "fusion-v1", "foundationModels", "none"
- Confidence threshold hardcoded as AdBannerView.metadataConfidenceThreshold = 0.60

Listen behavior (NowPlayingViewModel.handleListenRewind):
- Rewinds to snapped start boundary (item.adStartTime)
- Calls runtime.recordListenRewind which sets decisionState → .reverted so auto-skip ignores that span
- Feeds false-positive signal to PodcastProfile via TrustScoringService

Acceptance criteria:
- High-confidence shows advertiser/product
- Low-confidence shows generic copy
- Listen rewinds and plays through
- Listen tap updates trust scoring
- No hallucinated sponsor names
notes:
Code review (2026-04-10): Checked AdBannerView.swift and NowPlayingViewModel.swift against description.

1. Evidence-bound copy logic EXISTS and is implemented in AdBannerView.bannerCopy(for:). Confidence threshold is 0.60 (hardcoded in AdBannerView.metadataConfidenceThreshold). High confidence shows "Skipped · [advertiser] · [product]"; low/missing shows "Skipped sponsor segment". Matches description.
2. metadataSource is a String field on AdSkipBannerItem, NOT an enum. Values are string literals like "fusion-v1", "foundationModels", "none". Description says "metadataSource enum" but it's stringly-typed. No MetadataSource enum exists.
3. Listen behavior EXISTS in NowPlayingViewModel.handleListenRewind(): rewinds to snapped adStartTime, calls runtime.recordListenRewind which sets decisionState→.reverted. Matches description.
4. Trust feedback EXISTS: recordListenRewind feeds false-positive signal to PodcastProfile via TrustScoringService. Matches description.
5. Template-driven copy is accurate: BannerCopyLine struct enforces template, never free-form.
6. "Never surface brand solely because model guessed it": enforced by checking metadataSource != "none" AND confidence >= 0.60.

title: Banner UI Component
description:
Banner appearing when ad is skipped. Calm margin note, not alert.

Layout: "Skipped · [Advertiser] · [Description]" with [Listen], [Not an ad], and [Dismiss x]

title: Per-Show Trust Scoring
description:
Per-show trust policy controlling skip mode. Key product-level trust protection. Prevents aggressive auto-skipping on shows where detection is unreliable.

Modes:
- .shadow: detection runs, results logged to SQLite, NO visible skip or UI. Used for observation.
- .manual: user sees "Skip Ad" button when ad detected. User decides.
- .auto: full auto-skip with duck/seek/release smoothing. Earned trust only.

## Promotion/Demotion Thresholds (from TrustScoringConfig.default)

New show initialization:
- Default: .shadow
- Exception: if first episode's averageConfidence >= 0.92 → start .manual with skipTrustScore = 0.5 (shadowToManualTrustScore + 0.1). Otherwise start .shadow with skipTrustScore = 0.2.

.shadow → .manual:
- Requires: >= 3 observations AND skipTrustScore >= 0.4
- Trust score increments by +0.10 per successful observation (correctObservationBonus), capped at 1.0

.manual → .auto:
- Requires: >= 8 observations AND skipTrustScore >= 0.75 AND recentFalseSkipSignals == 0
- Note: checks observation count (episodes processed), not skip taps. Zero false signals is a lifetime check on the counter, not windowed.

.auto → .manual (demotion):
- Trigger: recentFalseSkipSignals >= 2 (autoToManualFalseSignals)

.manual → .shadow (demotion):
- Trigger: recentFalseSkipSignals >= 4 (manualToShadowFalseSignals)

There is no separate "immediate demotion at 3" path — demotion only fires at the configured thresholds above.

False-skip signal handling:
- Each false signal (user tapped "Listen" or rewound after skip): skipTrustScore -= 0.10 (falseSignalPenalty), clamped to 0. recentFalseSkipSignals incremented by 1. implicitFalsePositiveCount also incremented.

Score decay:
- decayFalseSignals() halves recentFalseSkipSignals via integer division (signals / 2) after each clean episode. Called externally; no episode-counting gate inside the method.

False-negative signal handling:
- recordFalseNegativeSignal() boosts skipTrustScore by half the normal observation bonus (+0.05). Does not change mode or false signal count.

User override:
- setUserOverride() writes mode directly to PodcastProfile. No explicit override/lock flag — subsequent calls to recordSuccessfulObservation will still evaluate promotion and may change the mode. Trust score is not modified by the override itself.

Stored in PodcastProfile (SQLite): skipTrustScore, observationCount, mode (String, SkipMode rawValue), recentFalseSkipSignals, implicitFalsePositiveCount.

Acceptance criteria:
- New shows start .shadow (verified)
- Exceptional first episode (avgConfidence >= 0.92) starts .manual
- Promotion .shadow→.manual after >= 3 observations with score >= 0.4
- Promotion .manual→.auto after >= 8 observations with score >= 0.75 and zero false signals
- Demotion .auto→.manual after 2 false-skip signals
- Demotion .manual→.shadow after 4 false-skip signals
- Score decay: false signal count halved (integer division) per clean episode
- User override sets mode but does not prevent future automatic mode changes
- Trust score bounded [0.0, 1.0]
- All transitions logged with: old mode, new mode, trigger event, score at transition
notes:
Code review (2026-04-10): Checked TrustScoringService.swift against description. Several threshold mismatches between description and implementation:

1. shadow→manual: description says 5 obs + score≥0.6; code uses 3 obs + score≥0.4 (TrustScoringConfig.default)
2. manual→auto: description says score≥0.85; code uses score≥0.75. Description says "8 manual skip taps with zero Listen reversions in last 10" but code checks observations≥8 (episodes, not skip taps) + recentFalseSignals==0 (all-time, not windowed)
3. First-episode exception: description says "≥3 high-confidence detections (confidence>0.9) with zero ambiguous regions"; code checks single averageConfidence≥0.92 to start in .manual
4. manual→shadow: description says 5 false signals; code uses 4
5. "Immediate: recentFalseSkipSignals≥3" in description has no separate code path; demotion only fires at the threshold counts
6. Score decay: description says "decremented by 1 after every 3 clean episodes"; code halves recentFalseSkipSignals after each clean episode (integer division by 2)
7. User override: code sets mode directly but has no explicit override flag preventing automatic mode changes; trust scoring continues updating the profile including mode on next observation

PodcastProfile fields (skipTrustScore, observationCount, mode, recentFalseSkipSignals) all exist as described in AnalysisStore.swift.

Per-show priors from PodcastProfile (ad slot timing, sponsor patterns).

title: Feature Extraction Service
description:
Extract acoustic features from decoded audio shards for ad detection hot path.

Features per window: RMS energy, spectral flux, music probability, pause probability, speaker cluster ID, jingle hash.

Note: Exact feature set needs validation through prototyping. Start with RMS, spectral flux, and pause detection — cheapest and most likely useful. Jingle hashing and speaker clustering may be deferred.

- Runs faster than real-time on target devices
- Features persisted, no recomputation needed
- Windows align with transcript chunk boundaries

title: Background Processing Strategy
description:
Background processing based on iOS reality. Foreground hot-zone analysis is the reliability path; background only improves completeness.

Implementation:
- Hot-path: foreground during playback. Rolling hot zone adapts to rate and thermal state.
- BGProcessingTask: idle/charging backfill (final-pass, metadata, show-priors). Opportunistic.
- BGContinuedProcessingTask: ONLY for user-initiated long-running work (model download). Not analysis.
- Checkpoint after every feature block and transcript chunk.

Thermal: .nominal/.fair = full; .serious = reduce window, pause backfill; .critical = pause all.
Battery: Below 20% not charging = pause non-critical. Low Power Mode = reduce lookahead, defer backfill.

Acceptance criteria:
- Hot-path runs during foreground playback
- BGProcessingTask registered and runs during idle/charging
- Thermal throttling reduces work without crashing
- Analysis resumes after suspension/termination
close_reason: Gap analysis confirms fully implemented: hot-path, BGProcessingTask, thermal throttling, battery gating, checkpoint watermarks, resume after suspend. BGContinuedProcessingTask no-op deferred by design.

title: PodcastDiscoveryService
description:
Discovery service using iTunes Search API as single MVP provider. Bridges search/discovery to SwiftData library.

API:
- searchPodcasts(query:) async throws -> [SearchResult] — returns search results (not yet subscribed)
- fetchFeed(url:) async throws -> Podcast — parses feed, creates/updates Podcast + Episodes in SwiftData
- refreshEpisodes(for podcast:) async throws -> [Episode] — re-fetches feed, updates episodes
- subscribe(to searchResult:) async throws -> Podcast — fetches feed + marks as subscribed

Implementation:
- iTunes Search API: https://itunes.apple.com/search?term={query}&media=podcast&limit=25
- JSON response parsing: trackName, artistName, artworkUrl600, feedUrl
- Search debounce: 300ms after last keystroke before firing request
- On-device cache: LRU cache of last 50 search queries + results (in-memory, not persisted)
- Rate limit handling: if HTTP 429 or >20 req/min, backoff with exponential delay (1s, 2s, 4s)
- Provider abstraction: PodcastSearchProvider protocol retained for future Podcast Index
- Defer Podcast Index until skip loop is stable

Error handling:
- Network unreachable: return cached results if available, show "Offline" indicator
- Rate limited: show "Please wait" with retry countdown, no crash
- Feed parse failure: show error on podcast detail, do not corrupt existing data
- Invalid feed URL: show user-facing error, log details

Acceptance criteria:
- Search returns results for common podcast names (verified: "The Daily", "Serial", "Radiolab")
- Feed fetch populates Podcast + Episode models in SwiftData correctly
- Debounce prevents rapid-fire API calls (verified: 10 keystrokes produce ≤ 2 API calls)
- Rate limiting does not crash or hang UI
- Cache returns previously searched results instantly
- Offline search returns cached results
- Subscribe flow: search → select → fetch feed → podcast in Library with episodes
notes: Fixed subscribe-path crash caused by an invalid SwiftData predicate that descended through feedURL.absoluteString. persist() now fetches podcasts and matches on the stored URL value directly, and CoreServiceTests now includes an in-memory SwiftData regression test covering persist upsert behavior for the same feed URL.

title: Design Token Files
description:
Design system foundation implementing the "Quiet Instrument" aesthetic. These tokens are the single source of truth for all visual styling across the app.

Design brief: "Make it feel like a precision listening object, not an app with AI features."
Core idea: Editing, not blocking. The product is a beautifully made listening instrument — half editorial system, half studio transport. Not a hacker tool, not a generic podcast app, not an "AI" brand. It respects the conversation rather than attacking the ecosystem.

The product should feel like it was designed by an editorial art director, a music software designer, and a person who hates noisy interfaces. Calm, adult, exact, slightly luxurious.

## Files

Theme.swift:
- Spacing scale: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48 (based on 4pt grid)
- Corner radii: .small (4), .medium (8), .large (12) — restrained, not bubbly
- Shadow definitions: subtle only, Ink-tinted, for elevation hierarchy
- Animation curves: .preciseEase (custom, fast settle, no bounce), .transport (linear for scrubber)
- Animation duration: .quick (0.15s), .standard (0.25s), .deliberate (0.4s)
- Haptic definitions: .skip (medium impact), .control (light impact), .save (success notification)

Typography.swift:
- UI sans: Instrument Sans preferred, Inter Tight fallback, system font last resort
- Editorial serif: Newsreader preferred, Source Serif 4 fallback
- Mono: IBM Plex Mono preferred, Geist Mono fallback
- Semantic roles with Dynamic Type scaling:
  - .title (sans, 28pt scaled)
  - .headline (sans, 20pt scaled)
  - .body (sans, 17pt scaled)
  - .caption (sans, 13pt scaled)
  - .timestamp (mono, 13pt scaled)
  - .transcript (serif, 17pt scaled)
  - .transcriptCaption (serif, 13pt scaled)

Colors.swift:
- Ink: #0E1116 (primary background, dark surfaces)
- Charcoal: #1A1F27 (elevated surfaces, cards)
- Bone: #F3EEE4 (primary text on dark, light mode background)
- Copper: #C96A3D (signal accent — playhead line, key actions)
- Muted Sage: #8C9B90 (calm secondary states)
- Soft Steel: #95A0AE (metadata, timestamps, tertiary text)
- Semantic aliases: .background, .surface, .surfaceElevated, .textPrimary, .textSecondary, .textTertiary, .accent, .accentSubtle
- Light mode variants: Ink↔Bone swap, Charcoal→light gray, Copper stays

## Design Rules (enforce in every view)
- Copper used sparingly — signal accent only, so the interface feels expensive
- No spring/bounce physics on UI elements
- No parallax effects on artwork
- No gradient mesh backgrounds
- No shimmer loading states
- No motion that draws attention to itself
- Cards use long horizontal proportions (cut strips / cue sheets, not squares)
- De-emphasize cover art: stamp-sized, not poster. Privilege time, transcript fragments, and useful moments over show art.
- Skipped ad segments: recessed, muted treatment (never highlighted or aggressive)
- No purple anything, no sparkle icons, no "AI" visual language

Acceptance criteria:
- All 6 colors render correctly in both light and dark mode
- Typography scales correctly with Dynamic Type from AX1 through AX5
- No text truncation at AX3 on iPhone SE (smallest supported screen)
- All Copper-on-Ink and Bone-on-Ink combinations meet WCAG AA contrast ratio (≥ 4.5:1)
- Custom fonts load correctly; fallbacks render without layout shift
- Preview catalog view exercises all tokens (colors, type, spacing, animations)
- Animation curves produce no bounce (verified visually)
- No purple, no gradients, no shimmer anywhere in the token set

title: settleWaitDoesNotLie is a third 'the wall-clock quantity IS the assertion' test and was not gated
description:
Found at playhead-o89d review, 2026-08-13.

o89d gated "the two tests whose wall-clock quantity IS the assertion" and stated the
enumeration found "exactly 2 in the measured load-sensitive population". Re-enumerated
independently at review, there are THREE.

    PlayheadTests/Services/PreAnalysis/BackgroundGrantBudgetTests.swift:812
    struct ExpiredWindowAttemptAccountingTests
    @Test("awaitJobsSettled waits for a running job and times out rather than lying",
          .timeLimit(.minutes(1)))
    func settleWaitDoesNotLie() async throws { …
        let unrelatedStart = ContinuousClock.now
        let unrelated = await scheduler.awaitJobsSettled(
            ["a-job-nobody-cancelled"], within: .seconds(5), pollInterval: .milliseconds(20))
        #expect(unrelatedStart.duration(to: ContinuousClock.now) < .seconds(2),
                "and it must return AT ONCE. …")

That is the SAME SHAPE as `expirationWaitIsBoundedByTheGraceNotTheReserve`, which o89d did
gate: a clock read, then a bound whose job is to separate "returned at once" (correct) from
"burned the whole budget" (the bug). The gated one separates ~0 s from 60 s with a 20 s
bound. This one separates ~0 s from 5 s with a 2 s bound — a TIGHTER margin, so it is more
load-fragile, not less. Both live in the same file.

IT IS IN THE POPULATION, not a hypothetical:

    scripts/gate-baseline.PlayheadFastTests.json
    "swift-testing::awaitJobsSettled waits for a running job and times out rather than lying"
      seen_runs 2, failed_runs 1, kinds ["assertion"], source BackgroundGrantBudgetTests.swift

`assertion`, not `timeout` — i.e. what tripped is the 2 s bound itself, which is exactly the
claim this bead is about.

NOT FIXED AT REVIEW, DELIBERATELY. Gating it makes its baseline entry report `DID NOT RUN`,
which hard-fails the gate and forces a second `--accept-baseline` inside one branch. The
review's standing instruction is to stop and report rather than take a second accept.

WHAT TO DO: gate it with PerfGate, add it to MEASUREMENT_TESTS, verify it runs and passes in
the serial pass, and take ONE accept covering it. Note that `scripts/perf-tests.sh` is
currently RED for unrelated reasons (playhead-1och) — read both output formats.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
R2 REVIEW: the deferral is CORRECT, but for a better reason than the one recorded, and it
now has an ordering rather than an open question.

R1 declined because gating this forces a second `--accept-baseline` inside one branch. True,
and a real cost — but not decisive on its own; an accept is one gate run.

THE DECISIVE REASON is sequencing. `scripts/perf-tests.sh` is the ONLY place a PerfGate'd
test runs, and it is RED TODAY on two XCTest tests, one of which takes the host down
(playhead-1och). Moving a third test into that pass now puts its result somewhere nobody
reads — which is the same defect this bead already found once, where the pass could not
START for six weeks and "gated" and "deleted" were the same thing for every test admitted
since playhead-zx0l. Doing it in that order would be committing the defect one turn after
documenting it.

So: BLOCKED ON playhead-1och. Do it when the serial pass has a verdict a reader can trust,
and do it in the same branch as whatever else owes an accept, so the DID NOT RUN entry and
the accept that absorbs it are one justified diff rather than two.

Second-order cost of waiting, stated so it is not free: the entry stays in the baseline as
an `assertion` failure (seen 2 / failed 1) and keeps contributing roughly one assertion-kind
failure every other full-plan run. That is the price of the ordering, and it is small.

title: a late background URLSession is discarded with invalidateAndCancel(), which cancels transfers it did not start
description:
FOUND by playhead-gpdb R1 review, 2026-08-13. Filed rather than fixed: the remedy is a behaviour choice between three dispositions, and gpdb's ceiling is the call site's correctness.

WHAT gpdb SHIPPED. `DownloadManager.createBackgroundSession(role:)` submits the construction through `BackgroundSessionIO.perform` with

    discardingLateResult: { $0.invalidateAndCancel() }

so a session that `nsurlsessiond` hands back AFTER the 10 s bound has expired is invalidated instead of leaked. Its own comment argues the analogy: "for the same reason a late `downloadTask` is cancelled".

WHY THE ANALOGY DOES NOT HOLD, and this is the "ask what the quantity measures" class. A late `URLSessionDownloadTask` handle names exactly ONE transfer — the one this call just created — so cancelling it destroys nothing that existed beforehand. A late background `URLSession` handle names EVERY transfer registered on that background identifier, including transfers started by an EARLIER PROCESS. `invalidateAndCancel()` is documented as "cancels all outstanding tasks and then invalidates the session", so discarding the late arrival cancels the user's in-flight overnight downloads.

WHEN IT FIRES IS THE BAD PART. Construction is memoized, so the one crossing per process happens at the first session request — and the sites that make that request first are exactly the ones where transfers are already running in the daemon:
  * `resumeSession(identifier:)`, i.e. iOS relaunched us BECAUSE this identifier has pending events;
  * `retireBackgroundTransfers` and `resumeSuspendedTransfer`, which exist to find transfers a previous process left behind.
So the discard hook fires precisely when there is something to lose.

DAMAGE, and it is partly recoverable. The late session carries the real `sessionDelegate`, so each cancelled task reaches `urlSession(_:task:didCompleteWithError:)` (DownloadManager.swift:5025), which harvests `NSURLSessionDownloadTaskResumeData` when URLSession supplies it and routes to `handleBackgroundDownloadFailed`, which persists the blob and releases the in-flight slot. Plain `cancel()` is NOT documented to produce resume data (that is `cancel(byProducingResumeData:)`), so whether the bytes survive is per-task luck.

NOT MEASURED, and say so: nobody has confirmed on-device that a freshly-constructed background session has finished reattaching to the daemon's tasks by the time `invalidateAndCancel()` reaches it. Reattachment is asynchronous (that is why `getAllTasks` is a callback). URLSession serialises on its own work queue, so the cancel very likely lands after reattachment — but this bead is reasoning, not evidence. MEASURE THAT FIRST.

THE THREE DISPOSITIONS:
  1. `invalidateAndCancel()` (shipped) — frees the identifier immediately, destroys in-flight transfers.
  2. `finishTasksAndInvalidate()` — outstanding transfers run to completion and their callbacks still reach the delegate, then the session invalidates. Keeps the bytes; the identifier stays occupied until they finish, so a retry inside that window still collides.
  3. drop it — leaks a live second session on the identifier, which is the state URLSession does not support.

RELATED: playhead-g5bh already records that no rail proves production passes `discardingLateResult` at the two task-creation sites. gpdb adds a THIRD site with the same hole: deleting the hook outright was measured GREEN across 39 download suites (R1 mutant M4). The gap is structural — `BackgroundSessionIO`'s deadline path checks `mayRunBody()` before running, so a body that has not started is never started, and there is no seam that makes a body start and then finish late. Covering any of the three sites needs that seam.

title: a background relaunch whose session the daemon refuses never invokes the OS completion handler
description:
FOUND while implementing playhead-gpdb, 2026-08-13. Filed rather than fixed because it is a behaviour question about PlayheadAppDelegate, outside gpdb's call-site ceiling.

iOS relaunches the app and calls `application(_:handleEventsForBackgroundURLSession:completionHandler:)`. PlayheadAppDelegate.swift:133 stashes the completion handler keyed by identifier, then asks DownloadManager to wake the matching session (:137-139). The handler is invoked later, from EpisodeDownloadDelegate's `urlSessionDidFinishEvents` -> `invokePendingBackgroundCompletionHandler`.

AFTER playhead-gpdb that wake can FAIL: `resumeSession(identifier:)` now returns false when nsurlsessiond will not hand back a session inside the 10s bound. On that path no session exists, so no delegate callback ever fires, so `urlSessionDidFinishEvents` never runs, so THE STORED COMPLETION HANDLER IS NEVER INVOKED. iOS documents not calling it as costing the app its background scheduling budget — which is exactly the currency the overnight 'wake up to analyzed episodes' behaviour is paid in.

Note this is NOT a regression gpdb introduced: before gpdb the same wake would have PARKED forever on the unbounded construction, which also never invokes the handler and additionally deadlocks the cooperative pool. gpdb converts an invisible hang into a reported, recorded failure; what it does not do is decide what to tell iOS afterwards.

THE QUESTION, which needs a decision rather than a patch: should an app that could not open the session still call the completion handler? Arguments both ways.
  - CALL IT: the handler's contract is 'tell iOS you are done processing these events'. We are done — we processed none and never will in this launch. Not calling it is the documented way to lose budget, and losing budget makes the NEXT wake less likely, which compounds.
  - DO NOT CALL IT: calling it claims the events were handled when they were not. Whether iOS re-delivers them on a later launch (and whether an uninvoked handler is what triggers that) was not verified here.

WHAT TO MEASURE FIRST: whether iOS re-delivers `handleEventsForBackgroundURLSession` for the same identifier on a later launch when the handler was never invoked. That single fact decides it, and it is testable on device (playhead-gpdb's refusal is now RECORDED on the surface-status invariant stream as `background_session_creation_refused` with `site=background_relaunch_wake`, so a device pull can tell the two launches apart).

Whatever is decided, the refusal is already visible: DownloadManager logs it and records it. The gap is only what the app tells iOS.

title: correctionReplayCandidates is a FOURTH direct ad_windows producer bypassing both extent gates — and it sets no anchor columns at all
description:
FOUND 2026-08-13 by playhead-mqqd R1's independent hunt, reported rather than filed by the reviewer because the tracker is mine.

WHAT IT IS. AdDetectionService.correctionReplayCandidates (AdDetectionService.swift:11899-11921) writes ad_windows rows directly, carrying the same hard-coded literal playhead-mqqd just removed from the other two composers:

    eligibilityGate: SkipEligibilityGate.markOnly.rawValue

and it sets NO anchor columns at all — neither startEdgeAnchor nor endEdgeAnchor.

WHY THAT IS THE SAME SHAPE mqqd FIXED. boundaryState 'correctionReplay' is not a UserSpanAssertion, so SkipDetectorClass.classify routes it to .fusion — which on a trusted show resolves .auto. mqqd's mutant M3 measured what that costs for the sibling producers: rule set to a bare .eligible with both anchors unanchored, driven through the real SkipOrchestrator at trust 0.95, and the marks reached the MANAGED tier and were SKIPPED. The literal is the only runtime mechanism holding this row back, exactly as it was for semanticSweepMark and podContinuation.

IT IS NOT AN EMERGENCY, and the reason is worth stating so nobody over-reacts: the literal is correct TODAY and nothing promotes it. This is latent drift, not a live cut — the same posture playhead-9uxm has. What makes it worth a bead is that the row's stamp and its (absent) evidence are independent, so the next person who has a reason to promote correction replay has nothing stopping them from doing it wrong.

THE FIX IS THREE LINES, against the mechanism playhead-mqqd shipped: derive one SpanExtentSupport, write it to both anchor columns, hand the same value to ComposedMarkGate.eligibility(for:). Same value out; the columns stop being able to disagree.

CONTEXT — THE FULL INVENTORY, from that same hunt, so the next reader does not have to rediscover it. There are FIVE direct ad_windows producers, and NONE passes an extent gate:
  1. SemanticSweepMarkComposer  — FIXED by mqqd (derives)
  2. AdPodContinuation          — FIXED by mqqd (derives)
  3. SpecialistMarkComposer     — [[playhead-9uxm]] (P2); can auto-skip if promoted, but has a delivery-level guard AND sits behind specialistMarkComposeEnabled defaulting FALSE, so 0 of 45 device rows
  4. correctionReplayCandidates — THIS BEAD; no anchors at all
  5. recordUserMarkedAd         — AdDetectionService.swift:3170, stamps .eligible with no anchors. DELIBERATE and documented at length ([[playhead-527u]]); classify routes userMarked to .userAsserted. NOT a defect, listed only so the inventory is complete.

Also worth knowing, because mqqd's own doc understates it: the sweep and specialist lanes ALSO persist from BackfillJobRunner.swift:5334 and :5354, not only from AdDetectionService. Any audit of 'who writes ad_windows' that greps one file will miss them.

title: [bug] SpecialistMarkComposer still stamps eligibilityGate + both edge anchors as three independent literals — the third composed producer, uncovered by either half of the extent gate
description:
FOUND while implementing playhead-mqqd, which fixed the identical defect in the OTHER two composers. Out of mqqd's scope by its stated ceiling ("these two composers"), filed rather than fixed.

`SpecialistMarkComposer.makeMark` (Playhead/Services/AdDetection/SpecialistMarkComposer.swift:219-249) stamps THREE hard-coded literals that must agree and that nothing checks:

    // ALWAYS markOnly — hard-coded literal, never a policy switch.
    eligibilityGate: SkipEligibilityGate.markOnly.rawValue,
    ...
    // Belt+suspenders: unanchored auto-skips nothing.
    startEdgeAnchor: AutoSkipEdgeAnchor.unanchored.rawValue,
    endEdgeAnchor: AutoSkipEdgeAnchor.unanchored.rawValue

This is byte-for-byte the shape mqqd removed from `SemanticSweepMarkComposer` and `AdPodContinuation`. The fix there is three lines: derive one `SpanExtentSupport` value, use it for both anchor columns, and hand the same value to `ComposedMarkGate.eligibility(for:)` (Playhead/Services/AdDetection/ComposedMarkGate.swift), which mqqd added for exactly this producer family.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING TIDINESS — MEASURED, not argued. mqqd's mutant M3 set the gate rule to `.eligible` while leaving both anchors `.unanchored`, and drove the real `SkipOrchestrator` in `auto` mode at trust 0.95: BOTH composed marks reached the managed tier and were SKIPPED (`bannerTier == .suggest` failed AND `!wasSkipped` failed). So for this producer family the eligibility literal is the ONLY thing standing between the row and a silent cut:

  * playhead-2350's `DecisionResult.withExtentSupport` runs in `runBackfill`'s FUSION emission loop — a composed mark never passes through it.
  * playhead-bllt's `HotPathExtentGate` runs at the two HOT-PATH sites — same.
  * `SkipDetectorClass.classify` sends an unanchored `specialistMark` row to `.fusion`, which in a trusted show is `.auto`.

A composed mark is a THIRD producer of `ad_windows` covered by neither half of the extent gate. mqqd closed that for two of the three. This is the third.

SCOPE: three lines in `makeMark` plus a self-consistency assertion modelled on `ComposedMarkGateTests.composedMarksAreSelfConsistent` / `sweepMarkGateTracksItsDeclaredExtent`. The specialist lane's own reason for being unanchored needs stating in a named `extentSupport` the way the other two now do — do not copy the sweep lane's reason, which is about FM window geometry and does not describe this producer.

NOT A LIVE FIELD DEFECT TODAY: `specialist-ft-v2` contributed 0 of the 45 rows on db-morning7, and the value the derivation computes is the literal it replaces. The bead is about the drift, not the current value.

title: the day-0 instruments write to Library/Caches, which iOS evicts — and oa82 makes every launch consume one of only 200 session-file slots
description:
ESTABLISHED 2026-08-13 in playhead-oa82 R1 review, answering "will the evidence survive to a pull hours later?". Usually yes. The two ways it does not are both invisible when they happen.

1. THE DIRECTORY IS EVICTABLE, AND THE REPO ALREADY KNOWS IT. SurfaceStatusInvariantLogger writes to Caches/Diagnostics/ (SurfaceStatusInvariantLogger.swift:615-626). Its sibling StabilityDiagnosticsStore deliberately chose the OTHER directory and says why in its own header: "Application Support, not Caches: the OS evicts Caches under disk pressure" (StabilityDiagnosticsStore.swift:31, :60-63). An eviction takes the JSONL files AND the .surface-status-install-id salt with them, silently, and a new salt makes every subsequent hash incomparable with every earlier one.

2. RETENTION IS 200 SESSION FILES, AND oa82 JUST MADE EVERY LAUNCH USE ONE. maxSessionFiles = 200 (SurfaceStatusInvariantLogger.swift:82); eviction is newest-first by filename timestamp, run lazily on the first write of each session (:557-578). A session file is created only if the session writes something (:281-283, :526-550). Before playhead-oa82 a scene-less background relaunch with no anomaly and no ready_entered wrote NOTHING and consumed no slot. oa82 adds two lines that fire on EVERY non-preview launch — rediff_day_zero_background_observer_installed, or rediff_day_zero_kickoff_coordinator_absent (PlayheadRuntime.swift:3134-3168, :5627-5633) — so the window is now literally "the last 200 launches". The 08-12 bg-task-log showed 64 BGTask starts in the observed period; at a few dozen wakes a day that is days, not weeks.

Neither is an argument against the instruments — a line that is always present is exactly what makes an absence readable, which is oa82's whole design. It is an argument that the CHANNEL is not durable evidence, and that a pull scheduled a week out may find the moment already rotated away.

THREE FURTHER SILENCES ON THE SAME PATH, for whoever reads "no attempted line" as proof:
  * writeLocked's `catch { }` is empty (:508-522) — an I/O failure drops the entry with no trace anywhere;
  * every write is writeQueue.async at .utility QoS (:478), so a process killed between invariantViolated() returning and the queue draining loses the line — and a background-wake process being cut short is exactly oa82's own hypothesis space;
  * once the queue DOES run, FileHandle.write(contentsOf:) is an unbuffered write(2), so the bytes are in the page cache and survive app termination without an fsync. That half is fine.

OPTIONS, none chosen here: move the day-0 codes (or the whole stream) to Application Support alongside StabilityDiagnosticsStore; raise maxSessionFiles now that every launch consumes one; or cap by AGE rather than by file count so the window is stated in days.

title: the wq34 .applied exclusions are keyed on decisionState, not on 'is this the applied material' — a REVISION of an applied row still goes silent
description:
FOUND 2026-08-13 by the R1 review round on playhead-wq34, answering the CONVERSE of the question wq34's own comment raises about its two `.applied` exclusions.

THE EXCLUSION IS RIGHT, AND MEASURED. `SkipOrchestrator.managedTierWouldBeSilent` refuses to divert whenever `incomingState == .applied || existingState == .applied`, because an already-applied row is a durable RECEIPT for a skip that happened, and `forwardPersistedAdWindows` pre-populates `banneredWindowIds` for durably-applied rows — so a diverted one lands on `.droppedAlreadyBannered`, producing no card AND no cue. Deleting both exclusions (R1 mutant M4) killed `appliedReceiptIsNotDivertedToSuggest`, `inSessionAppliedWindowIsNotDivertedToSuggest`, four `SkipOrchestratorPreloadTests`, one revert test, and HUNG a sixth. That half needs no change.

THE DEFECT IS THE OTHER DIRECTION. The exclusion is keyed on a decision STATE, but "this row is a receipt" is a claim about MATERIAL. Two reachable cases keep a row in the managed tier that should divert, and it goes silent there — the exact inversion wq34 closed, surviving inside wq34's own guard. Both MEASURED on `bead/playhead-wq34` @ d486be9e with temporary probes.

CASE 1 — a materially changed revision of an applied row (`receiveAdWindows`).
  A durably-`.applied` row on a `.manual` show is admitted managed and re-cues (correct — cross-launch continuity). A later producer revision for the SAME id with new geometry has `existingState == .applied`, so `managedTierWouldBeSilent` returns false. Control falls to SkipOrchestrator.swift:3181, whose `bannerMaterialRevisionToken` comparison finds the material CHANGED, retires the receipt (`retireAllNonRevertedWindowStateIfPresent`, which also clears `banneredWindowIds`), and installs the new revision managed at `.confirmed`. `evaluateWindow`'s `.manual` arm then returns a silent `.confirmed`.
  Measured: `managed=["r1p1"] suggest=[] banners-for-r1p1=[autoSkipped (the first delivery's)] cues=0`. The listener HAD a skip for [60,120]; after the revision they have no skip, no card, and the cue list is empty. The identical revision stamped `.markOnly` would have carded.
  Reachable: rediff/backfill revising the geometry of an ad the listener already skipped in an earlier session, on a show whose class has since demoted (which post-playhead-lqcp is the default for the three show-governed classes).

CASE 2 — an applied producer revision with no managed twin (`receiveAdDecisionResults`).
  That door FORCES `decisionState: .confirmed` when it builds its `ManagedWindow` (SkipOrchestrator.swift:3641), so an incoming `.applied` producer revision never becomes an applied receipt there. The `incomingState == .applied` exclusion therefore protects nothing and costs the card: with `existingState == nil` the row is admitted managed as `.confirmed` and is silent on a non-auto show. If door 1 had already carded the same id, `retireSuggestedWindowIfPresent` (:3631) takes the card away first.
  Measured: `managed=["r1p2"] suggest=[] cues=0`.

WHY NOT FIXED IN wq34: it is a UX-visible change (a revised applied span becomes a card, which is Dan's call in the same way wq34's "more cards" was), and the tight predicate is not the same expression in the two doors — door 1 already computes `bannerMaterialRevisionToken` equality at :3181 and door 2 at :3649, while `managedTierWouldBeSilent` is asked BEFORE either. Filed alongside playhead-d2it and playhead-4xw4, which are the same defect through the other two doors.

FIX SHAPE, not decided:
  * door 1: keep the `incomingState == .applied` exclusion; make the `existingState == .applied` exclusion conditional on the incoming material MATCHING the applied one (the `bannerMaterialRevisionToken` equality :3181 already computes, or `!replacesManagedMaterial` which is now hoisted and in scope at the routing site).
  * door 2: drop the `incomingState == .applied` exclusion, since that door cannot produce an applied receipt from it; keep `existingState`, conditioned the same way.
Either change needs a rail per case; the R1 probes are recorded verbatim in the round's transcript and can be lifted into `EligibilityLadderMonotonicityTests`.

title: a user-DRAWN span loses its extent authority when confirmed from a suggest card: confirmationWouldSkip never asks assertsExtent
description:
FOUND 2026-08-13 implementing playhead-wq34, which is what makes it REACHABLE.

`UserSpanAssertion` exists to separate two claims (playhead-ynmk): `.userMarked` asserts PRESENCE **and** EXTENT — the user drew the edges — while `.userConfirmedSuggested` asserts presence only, because the banner asked "is this an ad?" about a span the DETECTOR drew. `assertsExtent` is the property, and `isUserInitiatedSkip` reads it so a user-drawn span is exempt from `AutoSkipEdgePadding`.

TWO PLACES DO NOT ASK IT.

  1. `SkipOrchestrator.confirmationWouldSkip` calls `AutoSkipEdgePadding.skipWindow(...)` on the row's anchors with no `assertsExtent` check at all. `AdDetectionService.recordUserMarkedAd` writes its row with the DEFAULT `startEdgeAnchor`/`endEdgeAnchor`, i.e. `.unanchored` on both edges — so `skipWindow` returns nil and the card is built with `confirmationSkipsPlayback: false`.
  2. `acceptSuggestedSkip` restamps the promoted row `boundaryState: UserSpanAssertion.userConfirmedSuggested.rawValue`, discarding `.userMarked`. Even if (1) were fixed, the promoted row would no longer claim the extent.

NET: after wq34 routes a user-marked region to the suggest tier on reload, the listener is shown a card about their OWN mark that says it cannot skip, and a Yes records a mark rather than moving playback. They drew the edges; the policy treats them as the detector's.

WHY THIS IS NOT A wq34 REGRESSION: before wq34 that row produced nothing at all, so a card that records a mark is still strictly more. But it is an incomplete win, and it contradicts the fidelity ladder Dan set on 2026-07-29 (transcript marking > banner response > inferred listenRevert) — here a transcript mark is demoted to a banner response by the act of confirming it.

WHAT IT IS NOT: this is not an argument for widening edge padding. ynmk's refusal is correct for a DETECTOR-drawn extent and must stay. The question is only whether `assertsExtent == true` should carry through the suggest tier the way it carries through `isUserInitiatedSkip`.

title: injectUserMarkedAd bypasses both admission doors, so a user's own in-session ad mark is still silent on a non-auto show until the next launch
description:
FOUND 2026-08-13 implementing playhead-wq34. It is the same inversion through a THIRD door, and it is the one the listener actually touches.

`SkipOrchestrator.injectUserMarkedAd` (the "Hearing an ad" button and the transcript mark) synthesizes an `AdWindow` stamped `eligibilityGate: .eligible` and writes it STRAIGHT INTO `windows[]` with `decisionState: .confirmed`, then calls `evaluateAndPush()`. It never passes through `receiveAdWindows`, so wq34's fallback — which lives at the admission doors — never sees it.

CONSEQUENCE. On any show whose classes are not `.auto` (which post-playhead-lqcp is every show, for `.userAsserted`, without an explicit override), the user taps "Hearing an ad", the app agrees with them completely, and NOTHING happens: `evaluateWindow` returns a silent `.confirmed`, no skip, no card. The mark only becomes visible after a relaunch, when `beginEpisode` preloads the durable row through `receiveAdWindows` and wq34 cards it.

"Works, but only after you quit the app" is the same shape as the playhead-o4qr defect that motivated stamping the gate on this row in the first place — see the long comment at `injectUserMarkedAd`'s `eligibilityGate:` argument.

THIS IS playhead-527u's OWN GESTURE, which is why it is P2 rather than P3. wq34 revived 527u's product-owner AC for the RELOAD path and left the live path where it was.

FIX SHAPE, not decided: either route the synthesized window through the same `managedTierWouldBeSilent` question before inserting it, or (better, if it holds) stop synthesizing an in-memory twin at all and let the durable writer's row come back through `ingestPersistedAdWindows`, which is the door playhead-96ot added for exactly this "a row landed mid-session" case. The second removes a whole class of twin-divergence bugs; the first is smaller.

SEE ALSO the sibling filed alongside this one: a user-drawn span that DOES reach the suggest tier loses its extent authority on confirmation, so even the reload path does not yet honour the mark fully.

title: retireBackgroundTransfers cancels enumerated OS tasks with a bare task.cancel() on the actor — the one crossing in this family nsjn never bounded
description:
FOUND in playhead-rouw R2 review, 2026-08-13, hunting the diff for the next instance of the class the bead fixes. PRE-EXISTING — unchanged by playhead-rouw, and unchanged in reachability by it — so it is filed, not fixed.

`retireBackgroundTransfers` (DownloadManager.swift:2822, inside the `for task in tasks` loop) calls

    task.cancel()

directly, on the `DownloadManager` actor, i.e. on the fixed-width Swift Concurrency cooperative pool, with no bound. It does this once per matching task, per session, for up to three sessions.

WHY THAT IS THE SAME DEFECT CLASS, from the repo's own position rather than theory. Two of the three places this codebase cancels a BACKGROUND-session task already treat the cancel as a blocking XPC crossing that must not run on the cooperative pool:

  * `abandonUnstartedTransfer` (DownloadManager.swift:2613-2629) wraps it: `Task.detached { _ = await io.perform(label: "cancel unstarted transfer for ...", running: { task.cancel() }) }`, with the comment "on this branch the cancel is exactly as likely to go unanswered as the resume was".
  * `ForceQuitResumeScan.swift:551` passes `discardingLateResult: { $0.cancel() }` — so the late-result cancel runs inside `perform`'s body, on the dedicated queue.

DownloadManager.swift:2822 is the third, and it is the bare one. (The other `task.cancel()` calls in this file — 1654, 1662, 2643, 3763 — are Swift `Task`s or streaming tasks, not background-session tasks. `activeDownloads` is `[String: Task<URL, Error>]`.)

WHAT playhead-rouw CHANGED AND DID NOT. It bounded the ENUMERATION that produces `tasks`. It did not bound what the loop then does with them. Reachability is identical before and after: pre-fix the enumeration either answered (and you reached the loop) or hung (and you did not); post-fix the same, with a 10 s ceiling on the hang. So this is not a regression the fix introduced — it is the crossing immediately downstream of the one it fixed, still on the cooperative pool.

EXPOSURE. `removeCache`, `clearCache` and `cancelDownload` all reach it. A `clearCache` on a slow daemon with N live transfers is N unbounded synchronous XPC round-trips in a row on an actor — the exact shape playhead-nsjn sampled (10 of 10 cooperative threads parked, 10,022 tests started and none finished). It is plausibly one of the remaining sources of the host restart that playhead-rouw's own merge gate still shows (1 restart, 2 no-verdict casualties, down from 11).

THE FIX IS THE MECHANISM THAT ALREADY EXISTS, and the shape is `abandonUnstartedTransfer`'s: submit the cancels through `enumerationIO` (they are already sequenced behind that queue's enumeration anyway) rather than the download path's `sessionIO`. Whether to await them is the design question — `abandonUnstartedTransfer` deliberately does NOT, on the grounds that making the caller pay a second bound to clean up after the first doubles the stall. That reasoning applies here too, so a detached submission is probably right, but it changes when `retiredAny` can be computed and that is a decision, not a patch.

NOT COVERED BY THE CANARY. `BackgroundSessionEnumerationSourceCanaryTests` bans unbounded ENUMERATION only; `cancel()` is a different verb and no rail sees it.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: DUPLICATE of playhead-zq2g, which filed the same call site from playhead-nsjn R2 on 2026-08-11 and states the premise more honestly (the j4wi sample has zero cancel frames, so whether -[__NSURLBackgroundSessionTask cancel] takes the barrier is UNPROVEN either way). Closing this one. The only thing R2's independent re-derivation adds, and it is already implicit in zq2g: playhead-rouw does not change this site's REACHABILITY — pre-fix the enumeration either answered and you reached the loop, or hung and you did not; post-fix the same with a 10 s ceiling. So rouw neither introduced nor worsened it. Read zq2g.

title: cancelDownload's attribution reap is conditional on an enumeration that is now allowed to fail
description:
FOUND in playhead-rouw R1 review, 2026-08-13, attacking the bead's own safety argument.

playhead-rouw bounded `retireBackgroundTransfers`'s task enumeration, so an unanswered `nsurlsessiond` now returns nil instead of hanging forever. The bead's claim for why failing open is acceptable is: an unanswered enumeration is 'a lost SOURCE of identities, never a lost deletion'.

THE DATA-INTEGRITY HALF OF THAT CLAIM HOLDS, and R1 verified it by reading all three routes. `removeCache`, `clearCache` and `cancelDownload` all reach `retireBackgroundTransfers`, and all three arm an identity-required guard that needs no daemon — `backgroundIdentityRequiredEpisodes.insert(episodeId)` for a single episode, `requireRegisteredBackgroundIdentityAfterBulkClear = true` for a bulk clear — BEFORE returning, unconditionally on the enumeration's outcome. `backgroundCallbackIsRetired` consults both. So a late completion for a deleted episode is discarded whether or not the daemon answered, and the bytes cannot be resurrected. That is the property that makes the fix's fail-open defensible and it is genuinely there.

WHAT IS NOT COVERED. `cancelDownload` (DownloadManager.swift:2630) is the one caller that READS the return value:

    if await retireBackgroundTransfers(episodeId: episodeId) { cancelled = true }
    ...
    if cancelled { deleteDownloadAttribution(episodeId: episodeId) }

`retiredAny` is false when the enumeration was the ONLY source of the identity and it was lost. That happens for a transfer this process never admitted: started before a force-quit, reattached by the OS on relaunch. `activeBackgroundTransfers` is in-memory and is not repopulated for such a task until its COMPLETION callback arrives (DownloadManager.swift:3938), so between relaunch and completion the admitted-identity map is empty for it.

So: user force-quits mid-download, relaunches, taps Cancel, the daemon is slow, and (a) the OS transfer is never `cancel()`ed and runs to completion over cellular for an episode the user cancelled, and (b) the attribution sidecar playhead-kkzu says an explicit cancel must reap is left on disk.

SEVERITY IS GENUINELY LOW AND SHOULD BE STATED AS SUCH. Both residues are self-healing: the transfer's eventual completion hits the retired-discard branch (DownloadManager.swift:3917), which deletes the staged bytes AND calls `deleteDownloadAttribution` itself. The leak is permanent only if that transfer never terminates at all. This is filed because the bead's prose says 'never a lost deletion' without qualification, and that sentence is what a future reader will reason from.

THE FIX, IF IT IS WORTH ONE, is not to make the enumeration mandatory — that is the hang this bead removed. It is to decide what `cancelDownload` means by 'cancelled'. Arming `backgroundIdentityRequiredEpisodes` is itself a terminal act for the episode, so the attribution arguably goes with it regardless of what the enumeration found. That is a one-line change to a conditional and a decision about what the flag means, which is why R1 filed it rather than making it.

Not reproducible from a test today: no seam makes the enumeration fail while a task exists that only the enumeration knows about. Adding one means the suite registering a real transfer with the simulator's nsurlsessiond, which is playhead-ornc's residue class.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
R2 VERIFIED THE BOUNDARY, and it is one step wider than this bead says (playhead-rouw R2, 2026-08-13).

R1 wrote 'Losing it costs the OS-side cancel() for a transfer this process never admitted'. That understates the population. Read DownloadManager.swift:2830-2837: the admitted-identity sweep is

    let tracked = activeBackgroundTransfers.filter { episodeId == nil || $0.value == episodeId }
    for (identity, _) in tracked { retiredBackgroundTransfers.insert(identity); activeBackgroundTransfers.removeValue(forKey: identity); retiredAny = true }

It holds BackgroundTransferIdentity values. It never holds a URLSessionTask, so it cannot call cancel() on anything. The enumeration is the ONLY source of task handles in this method. A lost enumeration therefore loses the OS-side cancel() for EVERY matching transfer, admitted or not — the admitted ones are merely retired without being stopped.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT CHANGE.
* It does NOT change this bead's fix or its severity. The self-healing argument is unaffected: an uncancelled transfer runs on, and its completion hits the retired-discard branch (:3917) which deletes the staged bytes and calls deleteDownloadAttribution itself. The wasted-bytes cost just applies to a larger population than stated.
* It does NOT change the retiredAny analysis, which R2 re-derived and confirms. retiredAny is true whenever tracked is non-empty, so cancelDownload's 'cancelled' flag is false only for an episode with NO admitted identity AND a lost enumeration — exactly the force-quit-and-reattach case this bead names. That half of the bead is exactly right.
* The comment in production has been corrected in the rouw branch itself (it was the sentence a future reader would reason from, which is this bead's own stated reason for existing).

AND THE REGRESSION QUESTION THE REVIEW REMIT ASKED, answered: is there a case where the PRE-FIX code would have cancelled an OS-side transfer and the post-fix code does not? Yes, exactly one — a daemon that answers LATER than io.timeout (10 s) rather than never. Pre-fix: block 10+ s on a cooperative thread, get the list, cancel. Post-fix: give up at 10 s, cancel nothing. That window is real and it is the trade the bead deliberately makes; it is not a defect introduced by an oversight. Note that the pre-fix behaviour in that window is itself the nsjn wedge (a parked cooperative thread), so 'what the pre-fix code would have done' is not a baseline worth preserving. Measured in the R2 merge gate: 'allTasks for com.playhead.episode-downloads: the background transfer daemon did not answer within 10.000000s' fired 3 times in one full plan.

title: the force-quit scan's 2s SLA is now bounded at 10s, and the number was never measured for that call site
description:
FOUND in playhead-rouw, 2026-08-13.

`ForceQuitResumeScan.liveBackgroundDownloadEpisodeIds` documents a 2 s SLA — it runs inside the AppDelegate's cold-launch scan, and its own comment says instantiating a background URLSession from cold "can take hundreds of ms", which is why it only queries sessions already brought up.

playhead-rouw routed its `await session.allTasks` through `DownloadManager.boundedAllTasks`, which uses `io.timeout` = `BackgroundSessionIO.defaultTimeout` = 10 s. That is strictly better than the unbounded await it replaced (which could stall a cold launch forever), but it is 5x the SLA this call site states, and the 10 s was chosen for `downloadTask(with:)` — "the line between slow and never" for a call a user is waiting on — not for a best-effort dedup whose documented cost of failing is "at most one dismissable phantom prompt, reconciled by the next scan".

THE QUESTION, and it wants a measurement rather than a taste: what does a healthy `getAllTasks` on an already-instantiated background session actually cost on device, and is a separate, shorter bound for the scan justified? A second number in the file needs evidence, which is why playhead-rouw did not invent one (CLAUDE.md: do not add a threshold without measuring it).

Cheap enough to answer: instrument the scan's own elapsed time on device across a few cold launches, then decide.

title: verification artefacts that live only in a session scratchpad are not verification — the committed R-series battery went unrun for two rounds
description:
FOUND 2026-08-13 in playhead-tl6l R2 review, while trying to run the committed mutation battery for the module the bead changes.

scripts/mutation-battery-gate-baseline.py REFUSES TO START when an anchor no longer matches its source exactly once — deliberately, and that refusal is what surfaced this. Three anchors (R06, R14, R27) had been dead since 40ac7dcc, playhead-tl6l's IMPLEMENTATION commit, because tl6l added `skipped` as a third XCTest outcome, inserted a carry-forward clause inside the prune branch, and added `and not self.crashed_host` to the GREEN condition. Every one of those is a legitimate change; none of them updated the rail that anchors on it.

So for two consecutive rounds the repo's own committed battery for gate_baseline.py could not run at all, and nobody noticed — because BOTH ROUNDS RAN A DIFFERENT BATTERY. The implementer's commit reports "17-rail mutation battery over the new code, ALL KILLED"; R1's reports "37 rails, 36 killed, control green". Neither set is in the repository. They were ad-hoc scripts in a session scratchpad, and they are gone.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE THREE ANCHORS. A scratchpad battery verifies the diff that existed the day it ran and protects nothing afterwards. Its rails cannot be re-run by a reviewer, cannot fail when a later edit removes the behaviour they pinned, and cannot even be READ once the directory is wiped. That is the same defect class as playhead-fer3 (a test that skips itself and reports OK) one level up: the artefact reports success and then ceases to exist.

Concretely: R1's own commit says three safety properties "were asserted NOWHERE" and that deleting each left all 117 tests green. R1 then pinned them as unit tests — correctly — but the RAILS proving those tests actually bite lived only in the scratchpad. R2 has now added them to the committed battery (RB1-RB5).

WHAT TO DECIDE.
1. Is a scratchpad battery ever acceptable as a round's verification, or must rails be committed to count? The cheap rule: a round that reports "N rails, all killed" must be able to name the file they live in.
2. Should anchor drift be caught EARLIER than "the next person tries to run the battery"? The refusal works, but it fires on whoever comes next rather than on the author. A cheap CI-ish check — `mutation-battery-gate-baseline.py --check-anchors`, buildless, run alongside `python3 -m unittest scripts.tests.test_gate_baseline` — would put it on the author. Note scripts/mutation-battery-untypeable.py already has exactly this shape in `--check-inventory`.
3. Whether the same drift exists in the D/E/J/K/L/Q series in scripts/mutation-battery.sh and in the P and TY series. NOT CHECKED — those need a build and were out of scope for tl6l.

Repaired in tl6l R2: the three anchors, with a comment at each saying what moved and when. Battery is 51 rails, 50 killed, control survived, restore byte-exact.

title: gate_baseline's only REAL-LOG rails silently skip outside the session that made them
description:
`RealCrashedRunTests` in scripts/tests/test_gate_baseline.py — the five rails that parse the two preserved 7.2 MB full-plan logs — hardcode a path under

    /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-dabrams-playhead/bee44b12-4e4b-4bbd-ada7-8d211ef3d4e6/scratchpad

which is a SESSION-SPECIFIC scratchpad directory. When it is gone the rails call `self.skipTest(...)` and the suite still reports OK. Their own docstring says they 'are the only rails that prove the module reads a real crash rather than a fixture built to match its own parser' — so the highest-value tests in the file are the ones guaranteed to disappear, and the suite gives no signal when they do (117 tests, 1 skipped, OK).

This is not hypothetical damage: the census assertions those rails carry (30 on main, 14 on mn5e) are exactly the numbers R1 review had to correct, and after this session nobody can re-verify them from the test suite.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN tl6l R1. Committing the logs is wrong (14 MB), and distilling them into a small faithful fixture is real work with its own risk of encoding the parser's assumptions — which is the thing these rails exist to avoid. R1 instead added `TruncatedOutcomeLineTests` and `CrashedHostSafetyPropertyTests`, which are synthetic and pin the same behaviours, so the loss when the scratchpad goes is bounded to 'no rail reads a genuine 7 MB log' rather than 'the defect class is unpinned'.

OPTIONS, ROUGHLY IN ORDER OF APPEAL.
1. Commit a distilled fixture: every line either parser touches (start/pass/fail/issue/skip/restart/Failing-tests/terminal) from both logs, with app-log noise dropped EXCEPT the handful of truncated lines, which must be kept byte-exact. Estimated well under 1 MB. The census numbers must come out unchanged, which is the acceptance test.
2. Keep the logs somewhere durable in-repo-adjacent and gitignored, with the path in an env var.
3. Make the absence LOUD rather than silent — fail if neither the fixture nor the logs are present — so the suite cannot report OK while its only real-data rails are inert.

Option 3 is worth doing regardless of 1 or 2: a rail that reports OK when it did not run is the same defect class as the gate reporting an all-clear for a run that lost part of the plan.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
FIXED 2026-08-13 on bead/playhead-tl6l (R2), by option 1 + option 3 together. Closing.

OPTION 1 — a distilled fixture, committed. scripts/tests/fixtures/crashed-run-main-76b0a09a.log (74 KB) and crashed-run-mn5e.log (59 KB), from the two 7.2 MB originals. The reduction is chosen so the numbers come out UNCHANGED: every failure, issue, skip, casualty and SPLICED line is kept byte-exact, together with the line carrying each splice's displaced tail; every line belonging to a test the committed baseline names is kept even when it merely passed; and a start/pass PAIR for an uninteresting test is dropped WHOLE, which is what leaves `started - ran - skipped` untouched and is where all 7 MB of the saving comes from.

Verified against the full logs on every quantity the module computes, not just the census: no_verdict set, failures, known, new, ABSENT, kind_changed, deterministic_passed, load_sensitive_passed, blamed entries/distinct/unmatched, host restarts, and the EXIT CODE. All identical.

The generator is committed too — scripts/tests/make_crashed_run_fixture.py — and it REFUSES to write a fixture whose census, failure set or absent set differs from its source. Keeping the baseline members was not in the original plan and is the one thing a naive distillation gets wrong: without it the fixture reads 32 recorded members as ABSENT where the full log reads none, and ABSENT is FATAL, so the fixture would have claimed a regression the real run did not have.

OPTION 3 — absence is LOUD. RealCrashedRunTests no longer calls skipTest at all. A missing fixture is an assertion failure naming the file and the regeneration command. The one rail still permitted to skip is the new test_the_fixture_still_agrees_with_the_FULL_LOG_it_came_from, which only cross-checks the distillation against the 7.2 MB originals when whoever is running still has them (PLAYHEAD_GATE_LOG_DIR overrides the path); it adds nothing the committed fixtures do not already assert.

A SECOND INSTANCE OF THE SAME DEFECT WAS FOUND IN THE SAME FILE and fixed with it. CompletenessTests.test_the_real_truncated_reference_log_is_reported_incomplete read the 2026-08-01 combined-main log out of a session scratchpad and skipTest'd when it was gone — which it has been ever since, so that rail had never run for anyone. It does not need THAT log: any real log with its tail cut is a fragment, so it is now built by cutting the terminal marker off a committed fixture, and it runs. The suite is 151 tests with ZERO skips.

AND THE RAILS THEMSELVES ARE NOW PROTECTED. Rail RF1 in scripts/mutation-battery-gate-baseline.py points FIXTURES at a directory that does not exist and requires the real-data rails to FAIL — a rail that reports OK without running is exactly what this bead was filed for, and now something notices.

RELATED FINDING, filed as its own bead: the committed R-series battery had three DEAD ANCHORS (R06, R14, R27) from tl6l's implementation commit, and the battery REFUSES TO START on a drifted anchor. So neither the implementer's round nor R1's ever ran it — both ran ad-hoc scratchpad batteries (17 rails and 37 rails) whose rails are gone with the scratchpad. That is this bead's defect class one level up: a verification artefact that lives only in a session directory. The three anchors are repaired and the battery is 51 rails, 50 killed, control survived.

title: ARM the gate's NO VERDICT category once the host crash is fixed — it is reported but not fatal today
description:
playhead-tl6l made a crashed test host VISIBLE — the headline now reads `RED (85 known / 0 new) — 33 tests got NO VERDICT (crashed host)` and GREEN is unreachable while that count is non-zero — but it deliberately did NOT change the exit code. This bead is the other half.

WHY IT WAS NOT ARMED THEN. It fires on main today: both full-plan control runs on 2026-08-12 (main @ 76b0a09a and bead/mn5e) lost 33 and 15 tests to a dead host, on a pre-existing crash owned by playhead-rouw. Arming it would have made every full-plan gate on this box exit 65 for a reason nobody in the middle of an unrelated bead can fix, and CLAUDE.md is explicit that this is the worse trade — 'one red rule and everyone learns to route around the gate, which is strictly worse than having no linter'. The repo's own answer to 'red for a pre-existing reason' is to RECORD it and diff against the record, and tl6l was not permitted to refresh the baseline.

WHAT TO DO, IN ORDER.

1. Wait for playhead-rouw. Do not start before it is closed.
2. Run the full plan and read the verdict line. `0 tests got NO VERDICT` and no HOST RESTART line is the precondition. One quiet run is weak evidence given the measured 0.46 run-to-run Jaccard — take two.
3. Then it is a one-line change: add `or self.no_verdict` to `Verdict.exit_code` in scripts/gate_baseline.py. The comment there names this bead and says why it is absent.
4. Decide, and say which in the commit message, whether `host_restarts` alone should also be fatal. A restart with nothing silent means everything got re-run and no test lost a verdict — arguably fine, arguably still worth stopping for, since a host that dies once can die again mid-suite.
5. The unit rail `test_it_is_REPORTED_but_does_NOT_by_itself_fail_the_gate` encodes today's decision and will go RED. That is the point — flip it, do not delete it, and keep `test_a_crashed_run_that_ALSO_regressed_still_exits_65` as is.

SECOND, SEPARABLE ITEM — the limit tl6l wrote down rather than papered over. xcodebuild's `Failing tests:` summary spells a test `SuiteType.function()`; Swift Testing's console prints its @Test DISPLAY NAME. The two share nothing, so a summary entry can be reconciled only for XCTest and for un-display-named Swift Testing tests. On the two real logs that leaves 15 of 15 and 14 of 14 entries unmatched — one of which (main's SkipOrchestratorRevertTests.failedSuggestNoRestoresLatestBufferedRevision()) was a genuine casualty that never printed a line at all, and is therefore invisible to the started-set census too. Resolving them needs a source scan of PlayheadTests/**.swift for @Test attributes. That was considered and NOT taken: it trades a sound log-only tool for a source-coupled heuristic whose every mapping miss is a false crash alarm. If somebody wants it, the bar is that a miss must be reported as UNRESOLVED rather than as a casualty.
acceptance_criteria:
1. playhead-rouw closed and two consecutive full-plan runs observed at '0 tests got NO VERDICT' with no HOST RESTART line.
2. scripts/gate_baseline.py: no_verdict participates in exit_code; the module docstring's 'WHAT NO VERDICT DOES TO THE EXIT CODE' section rewritten to state the new policy and why it changed.
3. The host_restarts question decided explicitly in the commit message, either way.
4. test_it_is_REPORTED_but_does_NOT_by_itself_fail_the_gate flipped (not deleted); the rest of CrashedHostVerdictTests still green.
5. CLAUDE.md's gate section updated: 'deliberately NOT fatal' is no longer true.
notes:
R1 REVIEW OF tl6l (2026-08-12) — TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS BEAD.

1. THE NUMBERS ARE 30 AND 14, NOT 33 AND 15. Re-derived independently by two routes (a global set-difference and an order-sensitive, launch-partitioned walk that subtracts xcodebuild's retries explicitly); both converge on 30 on main @ 76b0a09a and 14 on bead/mn5e. The 33/15 first reported counted four tests that DEMONSTRABLY PASSED: three of main's 10,910 `passed after` lines and one of mn5e's were truncated mid-token by interleaved app output (`passed after 100.732 secon` + a spliced log line), and the pattern required the literal word `seconds`. Fixed in tl6l R1 — every outcome pattern now matches on the VERB and treats the duration as optional. Step 2 of this bead ('observe 0 tests got NO VERDICT') is unaffected; the target is still zero.

2. THE HOLE THIS BEAD CLOSES IS BIGGER THAN 'main is red today'. All four of tl6l's mitigations (headline, GREEN foreclosed, ABSENT still fatal, accept carries forward) are addressed to a HUMAN READER. None is an exit code. So the regression class the gate CANNOT catch today is a change that CRASHES THE TEST HOST: the tests it kills are healthy ones that are in nobody's baseline, so `new_failures` is empty, `absent` is empty (that arm covers only ALREADY-KNOWN-BROKEN tests), and the gate exits 0 — the crash destroys the evidence of itself, which is the exact shape tl6l was filed against. Verified as a rail in CrashedHostSafetyPropertyTests, not reasoned about.

3. A MIDDLE PATH TO WEIGH BEFORE TAKING THE ONE-LINER. tl6l's argument for not arming was 'it fires on main today and the repo's answer to red-for-a-pre-existing-reason is to RECORD it and diff against the record — but this bead may not refresh the baseline'. That is an argument against arming it FLAT, not against arming it at all. Recording the no-verdict count in the baseline file and failing only when the run EXCEEDS the record would be quiet on today's pre-existing crash and fatal on a worse one, which is what this module already does for every other category. It does not require rouw to be closed first. Consider it against the flat one-liner in step 3.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
SHIPPED 2026-08-13 on bead/playhead-tl6l (R2). This bead is DONE and is superseded by what landed; closing it.

WHAT SHIPPED — the middle path, not the flat one-liner. The crashed-host census is recorded in the per-plan baseline file under `no_verdict` and the gate is armed on the DIFF, exactly as every other category in the module is:

    a name that lost its verdict and is NOT recorded  -> NEW CASUALTY, exit 65, named
    a recorded name that reported again               -> REPORTED AGAIN, exit 0, good news
    the count alone, or a bare host restart           -> exit 0

That closes the hole R1 named and verified as a rail: a change that CRASHES the test host used to exit 0, because its victims are healthy tests in nobody's failure baseline — `new_failures` empty, `absent` empty (that arm covers only already-recorded tests) — so the crash destroyed the evidence of itself.

A SET OF NAMES, NOT A COUNT, and it is a measurement rather than a preference. A count is blind to substitution: eleven tests die, eleven different ones recover, total unchanged, gate silent. The churn that would make a set noisy was measured and is ZERO — the two 2026-08-12 full-plan runs, on DIFFERENT trees, lost THE SAME ELEVEN TESTS (Jaccard 1.00, against 0.46 for the failure set on identical code). So the set costs nothing and catches the one event a count cannot. It is REPLACED on each accept, not unioned: a union can only grow, so a crash that is genuinely fixed would stay recorded forever. Rail: test_BOTH_runs_lost_THE_SAME_ELEVEN_TESTS is what reopens the question if it ever stops holding.

WHAT THE SET CANNOT SEE, named rather than glossed:
- a test the host killed BEFORE its start line is in no set at all (census is `started - ran - skipped`). It surfaces, if at all, as an unmatched `Failing tests:` entry — a LEAD, and deliberately never armed (rail RA7).
- identity is the DISPLAY NAME, so two same-named tests in different suites share a key (0.57% of names, measured).
- a RENAME reads as one recovery plus one new casualty, i.e. a false RED. Remedy is the refresh a rename already demands of the failure baseline.
- HOW MUCH was lost. Eleven names may be eleven tests or the visible edge of a suite that died before any of it started.

UNRECORDED IS NOT ZERO, and that is what let this land without step 1. A baseline with no `no_verdict` key has never recorded the population: the arm is INERT and the verdict SAYS SO out loud. A key present but EMPTY is a positive claim and is armed. So this does NOT turn main red today for the pre-existing crash playhead-rouw owns, and it did not need rouw closed first. The first `--accept-baseline` records the set and arms it; the accept prints `CENSUS NOW LIVE: N crashed-host name(s) recorded` and names them, the same way tier promotions print `ARMED:`. scripts/gate-baseline.PlayheadFastTests.json is byte-identical to main's (4d300374…) — this bead was not permitted to refresh it, and did not.

STEP 4 DECIDED EXPLICITLY: a HOST RESTART alone is NOT fatal. A restart that costs nobody a verdict means every test was re-run and no information was lost. It is reported and it forecloses GREEN; it does not fail the gate. Rail: test_a_HOST_RESTART_that_costs_nobody_a_verdict_is_NOT_fatal.

STEP 5 done as described: test_it_is_REPORTED_but_does_NOT_by_itself_fail_the_gate was FLIPPED, not deleted — it now pins the INERT (unrecorded) path, which is the half of tl6l's decision that stands.

AND THE NUMBER IS 11 AND 11, NOT 30 AND 14. R2 re-derived the census a third way and found R1's own correction incomplete in the same defect class. The splice does not stop at the duration: it lands inside the NAME (`✔ Test "a b` + `yte-exact span…`), inside the verb (`" pa` + `ssed after 107.082 seconds.`), and once inside the word `Test` itself (`✔ Tes` + `t "watermark…`), because the app-log intrusion carries its OWN NEWLINE and splits one logical verdict into two physical lines. Eighteen such lines on main and three on mn5e, EVERY ONE a passing test. No pattern over `Test "` can ever see them — R1's widening handles only the four where the cut fell after ` after`. gate_baseline.py now REJOINS the halves before parsing (`rejoin_spliced_lines`), which fixes start, pass, fail, issue, skip and XCTest at once.

That correction is load-bearing for THIS bead, not trivia: 19 of main's 30 were an artefact of how chatty the app happened to be on that run, so arming on the unrepaired census would have been arming the gate on log interleaving.

title: the manual->auto closure stranded a floor of machinery, config, metrics and user-facing copy — the full ledger
description:
FOUND 2026-08-12 by the R6 verify round on playhead-mn5e. The brief was "enumerate every mechanism whose correctness depended on the deleted `manual -> auto` clauses"; R5 had traced three (gard's seed, qs0d's day-0 mint, zf2t). This is the rest.

FRAMING FIRST, so nobody reads this as a regression report. On `main`, `recordSuccessfulObservation` had ZERO production callers (`git grep recordSuccessfulObservation main -- Playhead/` returns only the declaration), so `skipTrustScore` was frozen and `manual -> auto` never fired in the shipped app either. playhead-lqcp did not remove a live behaviour; it removed a rung that this branch's own self-promotion wiring would have MADE live. So nothing below is a behaviour regression against main. What they are is machinery, config, metrics and copy that were all built for a rung that is now explicitly and permanently closed — and which now say things that are not true.

DEAD PERMISSIONS (nothing can exercise them)
  * `AutoSkipEdgePadding` (:232-241, :259, :265-298) — `.stingerSnapped` resolves `ExtentAnchorTier.corroborated`, which `SkipDetectorClass.classify` does NOT route to `.rediffByteExact` (:156 requires `.deterministic`). Since the only self-reachable `.auto` class always has both edges byte-exact, `startMarginStingerSnappedSeconds` (0.75), `endMarginStingerSnappedSeconds` (0.75), `endMarginUnanchoredSeconds` (10.25) and `stingerStartDemotedShowKeys` (the nikki-glaser list) are unreachable from the auto path. They stay live only through playhead-ynmk's accepted-suggestion path (SkipOrchestrator :6634-6652) and under a user override.
  * `SpanExtentSupport.isFullyAnchored` (:116-118) admits `.corroborated` to auto-skip under playhead-2350, and the trust gate then refuses it forever. The three-tier design has collapsed to two-valued as far as ACTUATION is concerned.
  * `AutoSkipPrecisionGate.AutoSkipClassification.autoSkipEligible` (:133), its `SafetySignal` set, `MarkOnlyReason.belowAutoSkipThreshold`, and `AdDetectionConfig.bandThresholds.autoSkip` — every span they promote is `.fusion` or `.segmentAggregated` and lands on a silent `.confirmed`. The whole precision ladder now only decides banner-or-nothing.
  * `SkipOrchestrator.applyManualSkip`'s audit gate `if skipMode(for:) != .shadow && !isExplicitBannerFeedback` (:6329) is unreachable: `applyManualSkip` has exactly one production caller (`acceptSuggestedSkip` :5977) and it passes `isExplicitBannerFeedback: true`. There is no "Skip Ad" button anywhere in `Playhead/Views/`, contrary to BEADS.md:781.
  * `PerShowThresholdController` (flag-off by default) would tune a threshold whose downstream is the dead branch.

DEAD CONFIG / API
  * `TrustScoringConfig.manualToAutoObservations` (8) and `manualToAutoTrustScore` (0.75) have ZERO production readers.
