Every remaining read is a test, four of them only to pass the values back into a custom config, and they sit in the synthesized memberwise initializer so they cannot be deleted without touching those four call sites.
  * `TrustScoringService.effectiveMode(podcastId:)` has no production caller; `resolveDetectorModes` is the only production reader of trust mode.

METRICS / EVAL THAT NOW MEASURE THE CLOSURE
  * `false_ready_rate` (`SurfaceStateTransitionEntry.swift:60-76`) = readyEntered \ autoSkipFired / readyEntered. `auto_skip_fired` has one live producer, the `.applied` path (SkipOrchestrator :6875); the second (:6329) is unreachable. For any show without day-0 byte-exact marks every ready episode is a "false ready" by construction and the metric saturates at ~1.0. The Wave-4 dogfood audit will read the trust closure as a surface-status regression.
  * The NARL q45f counterfactual (`NarlQ45fCounterfactual.swift:61-93`, :319-324) seeds every trace at `Q45fReplayGate.State(trustScore: 0.90, mode: .auto)` and documents it as "earned via repeated promotions". Both sentences are now false; the harness asks "when would trust have flipped this show out of auto?" about a population of size zero. `NarlQ45fCounterfactualTests.swift:727-738` pins `freshDefault.trustScore >= manualToAutoTrustScore` — one of the two things keeping the dead constant alive.
  * Eight E2E suites hand-write `mode: "auto"` into `podcast_profiles` (NetworkIsolationTests, BackgroundedPlaybackTests, ForegroundOnlyReliabilityTests, NoFoundationModelsTests, PipelineIntegrationTests, SurfaceStatusCrossProducerHashAgreementTests, CorrectionAttributionCaptureTests, SkipModePillPresentationTests). Their end-to-end auto-skip coverage no longer corresponds to a state a shipped device reaches on its own.

USER-FACING COPY THAT NOW OVER-PROMISES (the highest-severity item here)
  * `FirstSubscriptionOnboardingView.swift:30-31` — "we'll skip them automatically while you listen" — and :38-39 "Tap play and we'll handle the rest." True today only for the narrow day-0 byte-exact rediff population. For every ordinary fusion/FM detection it is false forever, on every show, at every episode count. These strings are pinned verbatim by `FirstSubscriptionOnboardingCopyTests`, so the promise is ENFORCED while the mechanism is closed.
  * `SettingsView.swift:551-558` — the "Auto Skip" footer, "Detected ads are skipped automatically during playback." Its `UserPreferences.skipBehavior` (default `.auto`) is read by NOTHING outside SettingsView.
  * There is no per-show skip control in Settings at all. `setUserOverride` is reachable only from the Now Playing pill menu (`PlayheadRuntime.setShowSkipMode` :5273-5297 <- NowPlayingView :874-885), only while an episode with a resolved show identity is playing. BEADS.md:793 says otherwise.

STALE PROSE OUTSIDE THE BRANCH'S OWN DIFF (the four inside it were corrected in the R6 commit)
  `SkipOrchestrator.swift:6816-6818` ("auto mode (trusted show)"); `AdPodContinuation.swift:130-139` (an asymmetry argued from "spans that DO auto-skip"); `SkipDetectorClass.swift:70-77` (premises that the ladder measures the right thing for the other three classes); `SkipMode.auto`'s own doc "Only for shows with proven local precision"; `PLAN.md:81, 431-435, 767, 780`; `BEADS.md:781, 786-787, 793`.

SUGGESTED ORDER: the onboarding copy first (it is a promise to a paying user), then the false_ready_rate denominator (it will be read as a regression), then the dead knobs. The dead permissions are best resolved by the eligibility-inversion bead rather than by deleting them.

title: an explicit user override can still be walked back to the seed by a veto-then-decay cycle (playhead-u0vv follow-up)
description:
FOUND 2026-08-12 while implementing playhead-u0vv (seed restoration on decay), which is where the reachability comes from — filed rather than fixed because the answer is a policy decision about how permanent an explicit user instruction is, and that is Dan's.

WHAT IS SAFE TODAY. `setUserOverride(podcastId:mode:)` writes EVERY detector class's ledger entry with the chosen mode and `falseSkipWeight: 0` (TrustScoringService.swift:761-775, playhead-gard). u0vv's restoration deliberately keys on a DISCHARGE (`weightBefore > 0 && weightAfter <= 0`), not on the state `weight == 0`, precisely so the listener's very next banner Yes cannot overwrite that instruction with the seed. That case is pinned: `SeedRestorationTests."A listener who turned auto-skip OFF is not overruled by their next Yes"`, and a mutant that drops the `weightBefore > 0` clause reddens it (M3, exit 65).

WHAT IS STILL REACHABLE, in five gestures:

  1. listener sets the show to `manual` (or `shadow`) — every entry now carries that mode at weight 0;
  2. two "Listen" taps on byte-exact rediff banners — the `.rediffByteExact` entry charges to 3.0 (1.5 per deterministic-tier veto). NOTE the class was already at `manual`, so `evaluateDemotion` changes nothing: these vetoes demote NOTHING, they only accumulate debt;
  3. three banner Yeses on rediff spans — 2.0, 1.0, then 0.0. The third is a genuine discharge, so `DetectorTrustLedger.restoredMode` returns `SkipDetectorClass.showIndependentSeedMode`, i.e. `.auto`.

The class is now auto-skipping on a show the listener explicitly told not to. The restoration is a RETURN TRIP by construction, but here it returns the class to a mode it never left by demotion — the tell that the discharge rule cannot, on its own, distinguish "paid off a demotion" from "accumulated and paid off a debt while sitting at a mode somebody chose".

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN u0vv. Distinguishing the two needs provenance the entry does not carry — either a per-entry "this mode was set by an explicit user instruction" flag (a persisted field on `DetectorTrustEntry`, hence a Codable/back-compat change) or a record of what the mode was before the debt was taken. Both are new state, and which one is right depends on a question only Dan can settle: does an explicit per-show override PIN a class permanently (undoable only by another explicit override), or is it a starting point that evidence may move? The existing system already answers "a starting point" in the OTHER direction — an override to `.auto` is undone by four vetoes today, and `ManualModeEscapabilityTests."An explicit user override clears the stale evidence against every detector"` documents that as intended — so u0vv did not unilaterally invent the opposite answer for the return direction.

RELEVANT PRIOR: `feedback_manual_marks_override_2026-07-29` (the fidelity ladder — transcript marking > banner response > inferred listenRevert — applied as precedence in BOTH directions), and `SkipDetectorClass.consultsShowTrust`'s own doc: "a show that serves personalised non-ad material ... is a real failure mode the user must be able to shut off."

IF THE ANSWER IS "PIN IT": the cheapest expression is a fourth guard on `DetectorTrustLedger.restoredMode` fed by a new `DetectorTrustEntry` field written only by `setUserOverride`, cleared only by another `setUserOverride`. Note the same field would also give playhead-zf2t a place to stand.
notes:
--- R6 VERIFY ROUND, 2026-08-12: CONFIRMED, and the bound is looser than filed ---

MEASURED, not reasoned. Three throwaway probes drove the real `TrustScoringService`; all three reproduced the walk-back, and all three are reported below with the mode the class actually ended in.

1. THE SEQUENCE AS FILED IS EXACTLY RIGHT (probe P1a). `setUserOverride(.manual)` -> two `.deterministic`-tier vetoes attributed to `.rediffByteExact` -> three banner Yeses. The class ends at `.auto`. The bead's middle step is confirmed too: after the two vetoes the class is still `.manual` — `evaluateDemotion(.manual, 3.0)` needs 4.0 — so the vetoes really do demote nothing and only accumulate debt.

2. THE MINIMUM IS THREE GESTURES, NOT FIVE (probe P1b). One WEAK veto is enough. `recordWeakFalseSkipSignal` halves the tier weight, so a listen-rewind on a byte-exact span charges 1.5 x 0.5 = 0.75, and a single banner Yes (which decays a full 1.0) discharges it. `setUserOverride(.manual)` -> one listen-rewind -> one Yes -> `.auto`. It is fully production-reachable: `AdDetectionService.recordListenRewind` (:10238-10248) builds its attribution as `(detector: correctedWindow.detectorClass, tier: SpanExtentSupport(...).tier)` off the same row columns, so a byte-exact row yields exactly `(.rediffByteExact, .deterministic)`.

3. `setUserOverride(.shadow)` IS WALKED BACK THE SAME WAY (probe P1c) — the bead says "(or `shadow`)" in step 1, and it holds: three gestures take a listener who turned skipping OFF to a class that auto-skips. This is the strictly worse case and is worth naming in the title rather than in a parenthesis.

4. THE SURFACE DISAGREES WITH THE GATE WHILE IT HAPPENS. Only `.rediffByteExact` has a `modeAuthority`, so only it is restored; `profile.mode` stays at the override because `applyCorrectObservation`'s `evaluatePromotion(.manual, ...)` is a no-op post-lqcp. `SkipOrchestrator` publishes `activeSkipMode = resolved.showMode` (:1974), which is what the Now Playing pill renders. So the pill reads "Manual" (or "Shadow") on a show that is cutting audio unasked. That is not a second defect — it is this one, seen from the surface — but it is the form the listener will actually report it in.

WHAT R6 DID NOT CHANGE. Nothing. The remedy is still a policy decision about whether an explicit override PINS a class, exactly as filed. The three probes were run and deleted; they are recorded here so the next hand does not have to re-derive the arithmetic.

title: playhead-lqcp made a detector's demotion PERMANENT: two vetoes disable byte-exact rediff auto-skip on a show forever, with no route back
description:
FOUND 2026-08-12 (playhead-mn5e R5). An interaction between playhead-lqcp (close the auto rung) and playhead-gard (per-class demotion) that neither bead's reasoning covers.

DAN'S RULING, as recorded on playhead-mn5e: "Rediff is incredibly high confidence, it should always be auto. But other evidence isn't as strong."

HOW THE EXEMPTION IS IMPLEMENTED. `SkipDetectorClass.showIndependentSeedMode = .auto` (SkipDetectorClass.swift:112) is a SEED. `DetectorTrustLedger.seed(for:from:)` returns it only for a class with NO STORED ENTRY. So the exemption is a default, not a floor.

WHY THAT DEFAULT STOPS APPLYING IMMEDIATELY. `TrustScoringService.applyFalseSkipSignal` MATERIALIZES ALL FOUR CLASSES (`Self.materialized(ledger, from: profile)`, :1131) on the first ATTRIBUTED gesture of any kind — deliberately, so blame cannot leak through the seed. Every production veto site passes attributions (SkipOrchestrator:4555, 4994, 4999, 5232, 5377; AdDetectionService:10256, 10265). So from the listener's first veto of ANY window on a show, `.rediffByteExact` has a stored entry forever and the seed is never consulted again.

THE DEMOTION IS REACHABLE. `DetectorVetoWeight.weight(.deterministic) = 1.5` and `autoToManualFalseSignals = 2`, so TWO vetoes of byte-exact spans give weight 3.0 >= 2 and `evaluateDemotion(currentMode:falseSkipWeight:)` returns `.manual`. That is by design (gard: "A class nobody can demote would be the same shape of defect as one scalar for everybody, pointed the other way") and is not what this bead disputes.

WHAT playhead-lqcp REMOVED. Before it, the weighted `evaluatePromotion` (TrustScoringService.swift:1501) carried `observations >= manualToAutoObservations (8) && trustScore >= manualToAutoTrustScore (0.75) && falseSkipWeight <= 0 -> .auto`. That was the route back: `applyCorrectObservation` decays the entry's weight by 1.0 per banner Yes and adds +1 observation / +0.10 trust, so eight Yeses on rediff spans restored the class. lqcp deletes those clauses in BOTH `evaluatePromotion` overloads.

THE RESULT. There is now no path from `manual` to `auto` for any detector class by any evidence. `setUserOverride` is the one remaining route to `auto` and it writes `podcast_profiles.mode` — the SHOW scalar — which a forked ledger does not read. So two gestures permanently disable byte-exact auto-skip on that show, and the day-0 byte-exact mint (playhead-qs0d) — the one signal that works on a FIRST listen, before any transcript exists — is off for good on exactly the shows the listener has touched.

Note this is the same show state R4's own probe used: "a fresh show, ONE veto of a day-0 byte-exact auto-skip". One more such veto and it is permanent.

RELATED: playhead-zf2t (a persisted `showIndependentSeedMode` can never be retuned) is the same root — the stored entry wins over the seed — with a different symptom.

DIRECTION, and it is a DECISION FOR DAN rather than a fix to improvise. Options: (a) let a class with `consultsShowTrust == false` return to `showIndependentSeedMode` once its `falseSkipWeight` decays to 0 — a RESTORATION to its seed, which is not the self-certification lqcp closed; (b) give `setUserOverride` a per-class form so the listener can re-enable the one instrument that works on a first listen; (c) accept permanence and say so in `AutoPromotionConfidenceEvidence`, which currently does not mention that closing the rung also closed the only route back.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
DAN'S DECISION 2026-08-12: OPTION (a) — RESTORE TO SEED ON DECAY.

A detector class with consultsShowTrust == false returns to its showIndependentSeedMode once its falseSkipWeight has decayed to 0. Vetoes still demote it exactly as gard designed; banner Yeses earn it back. 'Always auto' becomes a floor the class can RETURN to, rather than a default it loses permanently on the first gesture.

Dan was given four options — restore-on-decay, never-demotable, a per-class user override, and accept-permanence-and-document — and chose restore-on-decay.

WHY THIS IS BEING FIXED INSIDE playhead-mn5e RATHER THAN AS A FOLLOW-UP, stated because the repo's standing rule is that a bead's acceptance criteria are the ceiling and outside findings get FILED, not fixed: this is not an outside finding. playhead-lqcp — this branch's own auto-rung closure — is what deleted the restoration clauses from both evaluatePromotion overloads. The branch introduced the regression, so the branch closes it.

THE DESIGN CONSTRAINT THAT MATTERS, and the implementer must not blur it: RESTORATION IS NOT PROMOTION. lqcp closed self-certification — the route by which a class accumulates its own observations and declares itself trustworthy. Returning a class to a seed that some OTHER authority set (SkipDetectorClass.showIndependentSeedMode, which encodes 'byte-exact rediff is deterministic') is a different act, and it must be expressible without reopening the clause lqcp removed. The existing AutoPromotionConfidenceEvidence one-case enum is the precedent for naming why an auto is permitted; restoration should route through that concept rather than around it.

BOUNDS THE FIX MUST HOLD:
  - A class whose seed is NOT .auto must never reach .auto by this path.
  - A class with consultsShowTrust == true must never reach .auto by this path.
  - Restoration restores the MODE only. It must not fabricate observationCount or trustScore the class did not earn.
  - A subsequent veto must still demote. Restoration is a return trip, not immunity.

NOTED INTERACTION WITH playhead-zf2t (a persisted showIndependentSeedMode can never be retuned, because a stored entry beats the seed): a restoration path RE-READS showIndependentSeedMode, so it partially mitigates zf2t for any class that has decayed to 0 weight. It does not close zf2t — a class sitting at a stored .auto never takes the restoration path at all — so zf2t stays open.

title: DetectorTrustEntry.observationCount counts banner TAPS, not episodes — three Yeses in one episode promote a class, and the source comment says this was filed when it was not
description:
FOUND 2026-08-12 (playhead-mn5e R5). This bead exists because the production comment SAYS it exists and it did not.

THE CLAIM IN THE SOURCE. `TrustScoringService.applyCorrectObservation`'s doc comment (TrustScoringService.swift:1266-1278) argues at length that the per-detector entry's `observationCount` is deliberately NOT gated on the `trust_episode_observations` claim that gates the show column two lines below it, and closes with: "The right fix is a per-detector claim axis; filed, not improvised here." NO SUCH BEAD EXISTED. Checked `bd list` and `.beads/issues.jsonl` on 2026-08-12; playhead-mn5e's ten DISCOVERED children are 2qz6, 5b5b, 89x6, fh5v, kfts, lqcp, mqqd, scc6, zeh0, zf2t, and none of them is this. This bead is it.

THE DEFECT. `applyCorrectObservation` gates the SHOW column on the claim — `profile.observationCount + (countsAsEpisode ? 1 : 0)` (:1286) — and then increments the per-class entry unconditionally: `entry.observationCount + 1` (:1304). The consumer reads that entry counter as EPISODES: `evaluatePromotion(config:currentMode:trustScore:observations:falseSkipWeight:)` compares it against `TrustScoringConfig.shadowToManualObservations`, which is 3. So THREE banner Yeses inside ONE episode take a detector class from `shadow` to `manual`.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE SHOW COLUMN IT MIRRORS. playhead-fh5v is exactly this defect on `podcast_profiles.observationCount`, and it was fixed. But the show column is what the PILL reads; the per-class entry is what the SKIP GATE reads — `SkipOrchestrator.skipMode(for:)` (SkipOrchestrator.swift:6714) resolves `activeDetectorSkipModes.mode(for:)`, and a ledger forked by any attributed gesture no longer tracks the scalar at all. So fh5v was fixed on the quantity the user can see and left unfixed on the quantity the app acts on.

THE ARGUMENT FOR LEAVING IT, AND ITS EXPIRY DATE. The comment's reasoning is real: gate the entry counter on the same claim and it FREEZES, because the backfill path claims almost every episode without ever touching the ledger, so an entry materialized early would sit at its seed forever and that class could never leave `shadow` on its own evidence. Under-crediting a user-driven escape is genuinely worse than over-crediting a banner. The bound on the harm is playhead-lqcp: with `manual -> auto` closed, the over-count reaches at most `manual`, which is a banner. THAT BOUND DISAPPEARS the moment playhead-yhfr reopens the auto rung — at which point three taps in one episode buy an unasked skip. This bead must be resolved before yhfr lands, not after.

DIRECTION. A `(podcastId, analysisAssetId, detectorClass)` claim axis, so the entry counter is per (episode, class) rather than per gesture, and the backfill's own credit takes the same per-class claim.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
CLOSED AS A DUPLICATE of playhead-jh4y (filed by mn5e R2, 2026-08-12), which describes the same defect — DetectorTrustEntry.observationCount seeded in EPISODES and incremented per GESTURE, read by evaluatePromotion against an episode-unit threshold — and proposes the same fix, a per-detector claim axis.

This bead's premise was that the source comment's 'filed, not improvised here' named a bead that did not exist. It does exist; R5 checked only mn5e's discovered-from children, and jh4y is not linked that way.

The two things this bead added that jh4y did not state — that the per-class entry is what the SKIP GATE reads (so it outranks the show column fh5v fixed), and the verified file:line pair — have been folded into jh4y as a comment. Work the fix there.

title: a veto's EXTENT TIER has no behavioural coverage: forcing every veto to .none passes the whole plan, a 3x change in demotion speed
description:
FOUND IN playhead-mn5e R4, generalizing R3's finding that an argument absent from a `…ForTesting` seam's signature is untested by construction.

THREE SEAMS OMIT AN ARGUMENT THEIR PRODUCTION CALL SITE PASSES:

  * `SkipOrchestrator.falseSkipSignalHandlerForTesting` is `(String) async -> Void`; production calls `recordFalseSkipSignal(podcastId:attributions:privacy:)` (SkipOrchestrator.swift:5232, 5377). `attributions` and `privacy` are invisible to any test using the seam.
  * `SkipOrchestrator.falseNegativeSignalHandlerForTesting` is `(String)`; production passes `privacy: .explicitBannerFeedback` (5900).
  * `AdDetectionService.listenRewindTrustHandlerForTesting` is `(String)`; production passes `attributions: [rewindAttribution]` (10258/10267), an attribution the method derives itself from the persisted row's `detectorClass` and edge anchors.

TWO OF THE THREE AXES TURN OUT TO BE COVERED BY SOMETHING THAT BYPASSES THE SEAM, so the incomplete signature is not by itself the hole R3's was:

  * WHICH DETECTOR a veto blames: covered. `PerDetectorSkipGateTests.revertAttributesToTheDrawingDetector` drives `orchestrator.revertWindow` with a REAL `TrustScoringService` and asserts the persisted ledger. Mutant M-B1 — `vetoAttribution(for:)` forced to return `(.fusion, .none)` — was KILLED there (exit 65, 1 issue, 203 tests / 16 suites).
  * `privacy: .explicitBannerFeedback`: covered by a SOURCE canary, `TranscriptPeekViewVetoSourceCanaryTests` (SkipOrchestratorRevertTests.swift:315/344), which asserts the literal appears in the method body. Text, not behaviour, but it does pin it.

THE HOLE THAT IS REAL — THE EXTENT TIER. Mutant M-B2 replaced only the tier: `tier: support.tier` -> `tier: .none` in `SkipOrchestrator.vetoAttribution`, leaving the detector correct. It SURVIVED the full PlayheadFastTests plan.

HOW THAT VERDICT WAS ATTRIBUTED, since M-B2 rode a run that carried two other mutants. `falseSkipWeight` is asserted in exactly ONE test file in the tree (PerDetectorTrustTests.swift), and within it only `revertAttributesToTheDrawingDetector` reaches the orchestrator's own derivation — every other site calls `TrustScoringService.recordFalseSkipSignal(attributions:)` with a hand-built tier, which cannot observe what the orchestrator computed. That test's tier assertion (line 1161) EVALUATED AND PASSED under the mutant; the test failed one line later, at 1166, on an unrelated assertion belonging to a different mutant in the same run. So the one assertion that could have caught M-B2 saw it and did not.

WHAT THAT MEANS. `DetectorVetoWeight.weight(for:)` is 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.5 for `.none` / `.corroborated` / `.deterministic`, and the weight is what `evaluateDemotion` reads. Under the mutant every veto in the app weighs 0.5, so a class that today demotes after two deterministic vetoes needs six unanchored-equivalent ones — a 3x change in how fast the app stops trusting a detector the listener has told it is wrong, with no test anywhere noticing. `revertAttributesToTheDrawingDetector` cannot see it: its fixture is an unanchored aggregator span whose true tier IS `.none`, so the mutant's value matches the expected one.

The same gap covers `AdDetectionService.recordListenRewind`: no test drives it end-to-end and inspects the resulting per-class weight — only a source canary that the CALL exists (AdDetectionServiceUpdatePriorsAtomicityCanaryTests:203).

WHY IT IS FILED AND NOT FIXED HERE. The derivation is correct today; this is a coverage hole, not a production defect, and it is playhead-gard's surface rather than mn5e's. mn5e's ceiling is the observation counter.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT. One behavioural test per tier through the real orchestrator seam — veto a `rediffByteExact` window with both edges deterministically anchored, assert the class's `falseSkipWeight` is `weight(for: .deterministic)` and not `weight(for: .none)`. `rediffWindow()` in PerDetectorTrustTests.swift already builds exactly such a fixture. Widening the three seam signatures to carry what production passes is the structural half, and is what stops the next argument going dark.

title: a persisted showIndependentSeedMode can never be retuned: the stored entry wins over the seed, so changing the constant misses every forked ledger
description:
FOUND IN playhead-mn5e R4 while attacking "does any reader treat a PERSISTED `auto` differently from a DERIVED one?".

The answer to that question is NO — persisted and derived are byte-identical for `.rediffByteExact`, because `DetectorTrustLedger.seed` ignores the profile entirely for a class with `consultsShowTrust == false` and returns a CONSTANT: trust 0.5, mode `SkipDetectorClass.showIndependentSeedMode`, weight 0, observations 0. So today there is no defect.

WHAT IS NOT SAFE IS TOMORROW. `entry(for:seededFrom:)` returns the STORED entry in preference to the seed. The moment a ledger is materialized — which `applyFalseSkipSignal` does on any attributed veto and `applyCorrectObservation` does unconditionally — `"rediffByteExact": {"mode":"auto",...}` is written to `detectorTrustJSON`, and from then on that device's answer for the class is the persisted string, not the seed.

Therefore: CHANGING `showIndependentSeedMode` DOES NOT REACH ANY DEVICE THAT HAS ALREADY FORKED ITS LEDGER. A future safety retune — "byte-exact should mark, not skip, until the show has some history" is the obvious one — would look like a one-line constant change, would pass every test (fixtures start from an empty ledger), and would silently not apply to exactly the users who have interacted with the app most.

CONFIRMED BY MUTANT. `materialized` was changed to skip classes with `consultsShowTrust == false`, so rediff's `.auto` is never persisted and every read falls through to the seed. See the R4 report for the verdict. The point of the mutant is that persisted and derived are indistinguishable TODAY — which is the same fact that makes the divergence invisible when the constant later changes.

NOT INTRODUCED BY mn5e. `materialized` has been called from both `applyFalseSkipSignal` and `applyCorrectObservation` since playhead-gard. What mn5e changes is the field state: `detectorTrustJSON` is NULL on both shows in the 2026-08-12 device pull, so no shipped device has yet persisted the string.

REMEDIES, cheapest first:
  (a) Do not materialize entries for classes that do not consult show trust. Their seed is a constant, so there is nothing to pin and nothing to protect from leaking through it — the entire argument in `applyFalseSkipSignal`'s comment for materializing ("blame would leak through the seed") applies only to the show-governed classes. A veto that names rediff still writes rediff's own entry through `ledger.set`, so demotion is unaffected. This is the mutant above, promoted from probe to fix.
  (b) Version the seed: store the `showIndependentSeedMode` a row was written under and re-seed when the constant moves.
(a) is a behaviour change for `encoded()` (a ledger with only rediff materialized would now encode as empty), so it needs its own round.

title: podcast_planner_state.observedEpisodeCount counts BACKFILLS, not episodes — the untreated twin of playhead-2qz6
description:
playhead-mn5e R3 review. The V49 migration comment in AnalysisStore.createTables names this column explicitly as having THE SAME defect playhead-2qz6 fixed on podcast_profiles.observationCount: 'podcast_planner_state.observedEpisodeCount has the SAME bug (21 and 6 for the same ~4 episodes on that pull)'.

2qz6 gave podcast_profiles.observationCount a claim ledger (trust_episode_observations, keyed (podcastId, analysisAssetId)) and V49 reset every row to 0. Nothing was done for observedEpisodeCount: it is still incremented per completed backfill, is still ~9x inflated on a field device, and still names 'episodes' to every reader.

Not fixed in mn5e deliberately — scope. Filed so the unit defect is tracked rather than living only in a code comment.

What a fix probably looks like: reuse the existing trust_episode_observations claim, or give the planner its own claim axis if its unit event is genuinely different from the trust one (it may be: the planner may want 'an episode was PLANNED', not 'an episode contributed a trust observation'). Decide which quantity it means before wiring it to either.

Evidence: 2026-08-12 device pull, 21 and 6 observedEpisodeCount for the same ~4 episodes.

title: DetectorTrustEntry.observationCount mixes episodes and gestures at its seed
description:
playhead-fh5v put podcast_profiles.observationCount behind the trust_episode_observations claim, so the SHOW column now counts episodes and has a ledger that says so. The per-detector entry's own observationCount was deliberately left ungated, and the asymmetry is a real unit mismatch worth closing separately.

THE MISMATCH. DetectorTrustLedger.seed (DetectorTrustLedger.swift:180-185) initialises an entry with observationCount: profile.observationCount — an EPISODE count. From then on TrustScoringService.applyCorrectObservation increments it once per banner Yes — a GESTURE count. Four Yes taps in one episode move it by 4. Both numbers are then read by the weighted evaluatePromotion against thresholds documented in episodes (shadowToManualObservations 3, manualToAutoObservations 8).

WHY IT WAS NOT GATED IN fh5v. Gating it on the same (podcastId, analysisAssetId) claim FREEZES it: the backfill path claims almost every episode without ever touching the ledger, so an entry materialized early would sit at its seed forever and that class could never leave shadow on its own evidence — the escape hatch playhead-gard exists to provide. Under-crediting a user-driven escape is worse than over-crediting a banner.

WHY IT IS BOUNDED TODAY. With playhead-lqcp's manual->auto rung closed, an over-counted entry reaches at most shadow->manual, which unlocks a banner and cuts no audio. If lqcp's successor reopens the auto rung, THIS becomes a safety issue and must be closed first.

THE FIX IS A PER-DETECTOR CLAIM AXIS: extend trust_episode_observations with a detector column (or add a sibling table) so an entry can count 'episodes on which THIS class was confirmed' rather than inheriting the show's count and then counting taps.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
CONFIRMED AND SHARPENED 2026-08-12 by playhead-mn5e R5, which independently rediscovered this and filed it as playhead-p1w3 before finding this bead. p1w3 is CLOSED AS A DUPLICATE; its two genuinely new contributions are folded in here.

WHY R5 MISSED IT, worth recording so the next round does not make a third copy: it checked playhead-mn5e's DISCOVERED-FROM children (2qz6, 5b5b, 89x6, fh5v, kfts, lqcp, mqqd, scc6, zeh0, zf2t) and this bead is not among them, so it concluded from the absence that the source comment's 'filed, not improvised here' was a false claim. The comment is TRUE; this is the bead. A finding is not absent because it is not linked.

NEW CONTRIBUTION 1 — WHY THIS OUTRANKS THE SHOW COLUMN IT MIRRORS, established by R4's Finding 1 rather than by argument. The show column is what the PILL reads. The per-class entry is what the SKIP GATE reads: SkipOrchestrator.skipMode(for:) (SkipOrchestrator.swift:6714) resolves activeDetectorSkipModes.mode(for:), and a class tracks profile.mode ONLY while it has no stored ledger entry. Every production veto site passes an attribution, and an attributed veto makes applyFalseSkipSignal materialize the WHOLE ledger — so the first gesture a listener makes forks every class off the scalar permanently. From that moment the show column governs nothing the app acts on.

So playhead-fh5v fixed the unit on the quantity the user can SEE and left it unfixed on the quantity the app ACTS ON. That is the same shape as the defect fh5v itself fixed, one layer down.

NEW CONTRIBUTION 2 — THE EXACT LINES, verified directly 2026-08-12 rather than quoted:
  TrustScoringService.applyCorrectObservation, show column, GATED:
      let newObservations = profile.observationCount + (countsAsEpisode ? 1 : 0)
  three lines later, per-class entry, UNGATED:
      let entryObservations = entry.observationCount + 1
  Both are then passed as 'observations:' to evaluatePromotion, which compares against shadowToManualObservations = 3 — a threshold whose unit is EPISODES. Three banner Yeses inside one episode take a class shadow -> manual.

THE EXPIRY DATE IS NOW CONCRETE, and this is the operational point. This bead's own 'bounded today' argument rests on playhead-lqcp having closed the manual->auto rung. Dan ruled on 2026-08-12: 'yes it should go all the way to auto if it is high confidence' and 'Rediff is incredibly high confidence, it should always be auto. But other evidence isn't as strong.' That ruling IS playhead-yhfr, and it reopens the rung for non-rediff evidence. So the bound expires by decision already taken, not by hypothesis.

THIS BEAD MUST CLOSE BEFORE yhfr LANDS. A dependency has been recorded rather than left as prose, because the whole reason this is survivable today is a bound that a future bead removes.

title: podcast_planner_state.observedEpisodeCount counts BACKFILLS, not episodes
description:
Confirming the call playhead-mn5e/2qz6 made and correctly left alone (AnalysisStore.swift:9313 names it in the V49 block comment as having 'the SAME bug', measured 21 and 6 for the same ~4 episodes on the 2026-08-12 device pull).

VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY:
- AnalysisStore.recordPodcastEpisodeObservation (:14507) increments unconditionally: L14528 'let newObservedCount = (prior?.observedEpisodeCount ?? 0) + 1'. Its own doc, L14465: 'observedEpisodeCount is incremented by 1 on every call.'
- Its single production caller is BackfillJobRunner.swift:1674, inside the per-backfill-job completion path. There is no per-episode dedupe of any kind -- no claim row, no watermark check.
- So the column is a count of BACKFILL RUNS wearing the name 'observed EPISODE count'. Same ~9x inflation as podcast_profiles.observationCount had.

CONSUMER THAT ACTS ON IT: computePlannerStableFlag (:14652-14655) gates on 'observedEpisodeCount >= plannerStableObservedEpisodeFloor' (5). The planner therefore declares a show recall-stable after ~5 backfill runs -- roughly half an episode -- rather than after 5 episodes.

NOT fixed in mn5e: correctly out of scope there (mn5e's ceiling was podcast_profiles.observationCount and the trust ladder). Filed so the second half of the same defect class is not lost.

Fix shape (not decided): the trust_episode_observations claim table mn5e added is the obvious reusable dedupe seam, but the planner's unit may legitimately be 'scan runs' for some of its other counters -- decide per column rather than resetting the row wholesale.

title: [bug] evaluatePromotion's shadow->manual arm ignores recentFalseSkipSignals — a vetoed show re-earns its banner while the veto counter still reads 4
description:
FOUND 2026-08-12 while implementing playhead-mn5e's safety verification.

TrustScoringService.evaluatePromotion (TrustScoringService.swift:1166-1189) takes `recentFalseSignals` and reads it in exactly ONE arm:

  case .shadow:  observations >= N && trustScore >= T                       -> .manual
  case .manual:  observations >= N && trustScore >= T && recentFalseSignals == 0  -> .auto

The shadow -> manual arm does not consult it. The weighted sibling (:1230-1253) has the same asymmetry.

WHY IT WAS INERT AND IS NOT ANY MORE. Before playhead-mn5e, evaluatePromotion had one production caller — the banner Yes tap — and that path (recordCorrectObservation) DECAYS a unit of false-signal evidence as it goes, so the counter and the promotion moved together. mn5e adds a caller that does NOT decay: recordSuccessfulObservation carries `recentFalseSkipSignals` forward untouched and adds +0.10 trust. So self-observation can now walk a show back up past the shadow -> manual rung while the user's veto counter still reads non-zero.

THE ARITHMETIC. manualToShadowFalseSignals = 4, falseSignalPenalty = 0.10, correctObservationBonus = 0.10. A show demoted manual -> shadow by 4 vetoes has lost 0.40 trust — but each subsequent backfill returns 0.10. shadowToManualTrustScore is 0.4, so within a few backfills it clears the bar again and returns to .manual with recentFalseSkipSignals still at 4. The user has to veto FASTER THAN THE APP ANALYSES to hold a show down.

THE AUTO RUNG IS SAFE, and that is verified by test in mn5e (`vetoedShowCannotSelfPromoteBackToAuto`): manual -> auto genuinely requires the counter at 0, and only a banner Yes can decay it. So this is bounded to "a vetoed show re-earns its BANNER" — not "re-earns audio cutting". That is why it is filed rather than fixed inside mn5e: it is a policy question (is a banner something a veto should revoke durably?) and mn5e's scope was the missing caller.

WHAT TO DECIDE: either add `recentFalseSignals == 0` (or a weaker bound) to the shadow -> manual arm, or give recordSuccessfulObservation the decay that decayFalseSignals was written for and never wired to do — note decayFalseSignals STILL has zero production callers after mn5e.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
=== NOT MADE WORSE by playhead-2qz6's counter fix — measurably BETTER (2026-08-12) ===

zeh0 is that `evaluatePromotion`'s `shadow -> manual` arm never reads
`recentFalseSkipSignals`, so a show a user demoted all the way to shadow climbs
back to manual as soon as trust recovers. The severity of that depends entirely
on HOW FAST trust recovers, and 2qz6 changed exactly that.

  BEFORE: +0.10 per BACKFILL, ~9 backfills per episode. A 4-veto demotion costs
          0.40 and was repaid in ~4 backfills — under half an episode. The user
          had to veto faster than the app analysed.
  AFTER:  +0.10 per EPISODE. The same 0.40 takes 4 EPISODES to repay.

The exchange rate is now 1 veto : 1 episode instead of 1 veto : 1 backfill — an
~9x reduction in how quickly a vetoed show re-earns its banner. The missing
clause is still missing and this bead stays open, but it is no longer a
same-session effect.

The `manual -> auto` rung was and remains safe: it requires
`recentFalseSkipSignals == 0`, `recordSuccessfulObservation` carries that
counter forward untouched, and only a banner Yes (`recordCorrectObservation`)
decays it. Pinned by `vetoedShowCannotSelfPromoteBackToAuto`, with
`cleanManualShowReachesAuto` as the non-vacuity control.

title: the day-0 readiness probe resolves the asset row by EPISODE, so a stale registration wins after a re-download with different bytes
description:
playhead-fzrw R5 finding F-B (verified, filed not fixed — outside fzrw's scope).

THE PROBE. Playhead/App/PlayheadRuntime.swift:1755-1765 returns .ready(analysisAssetId: asset.id) as soon as store.fetchAssetByEpisodeId(episodeId) yields any row. That resolver (AnalysisStore.swift:10020) means 'newest row for this EPISODE', not 'the row for THIS download''s bytes'. Same defect class as fzrw's F1/F3: a value that names one thing read as though it named another — here an episode-scoped identity read as a byte-scoped one.

WHY fzrw WIDENS IT. Before the bead, the only row an un-played episode could have was one processJob had just minted FOR THIS JOB'S FINGERPRINT, so on the download path the probe was right by construction. Now a registration from an EARLIER download of the same episode id satisfies the probe immediately, and registerDownloadedAssetRowIfAbsent declines to add a corrected row because its precondition 3 (AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:6619) refuses when the episode already has any row.

SCENARIO (requires the bytes to change across two downloads of one episode id — a feed correction, a publisher re-cut, or a delete/re-download):
1. Download #1 lands => row registered, assetFingerprint = SHA1, analysisState 'new'.
2. Audio is deleted or replaced; the row survives (see playhead-ve27 — nothing deletes it).
3. Download #2 lands with SHA2. Registration bails at precondition 3.
4. The background-download kickoff probe returns .ready on the FIRST poll carrying row #1's id.
5. DayZeroRediffTrigger spends the k-way re-fetch budget and mintByteExactDayZeroMarks writes ad windows against the STALE asset id.
6. resolveAnalysisAssetId then takes its changed-canonical-bytes branch (AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:~6825) and mints a SECOND row for SHA2. Playback, the skip orchestrator and the pipeline all read windows off row #2, so day-0's marks are invisible.
7. rediff_day_zero_attempts is keyed by asset id, so the suppression/backoff record lands on row #1 and row #2 starts with a clean slate — the play-time trigger can spend the whole fetch again.

Pre-bead the probe found no row and gave up 'no_analysis_asset' having spent zero bytes. The wrong-row shape did already exist once the lane had run for download #1; fzrw widens the window from 'the lane already ran' to 'the bytes merely landed'.

CANDIDATE REMEDY: give the probe the fingerprint it actually means — resolve with fetchAssetByEpisodeId(_:assetFingerprint:) against the pinned file's canonical SHA, and return .awaitingAnalysisAsset when only a differently-fingerprinted row exists.

NOTE: when the two downloads carry the SAME bytes the exact-fingerprint reuse arm (AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:6778-6791) resolves the registered row correctly and nothing is wrong.

title: [bug] nothing ever deletes an analysis_assets row, so a deleted download leaves a phantom episode on the Activity screen reported as 'queued' with no job behind it
description:
FILED BY playhead-fzrw R4 review. PRE-EXISTING shape; fzrw WIDENS THE POPULATION
from "episodes that were played or reached by the analysis lane" to "every
downloaded episode with a canonical-SHA fingerprint". Outside fzrw's ceiling.

`AnalysisStore.deleteAsset(id:)` (AnalysisStore.swift:10206) has ZERO production
callers -- verified by grep across Playhead/ -- and there is no asset GC/prune
sweep. The only other removal is the one-shot duplicate-asset fold's private
`deleteAssetRow` (:19587). So an `analysis_assets` row is permanent once minted.

`DownloadManager.removeCache(for:)` (DownloadManager.swift:3757) calls
`AnalysisWorkScheduler.retireDownloadAnalysis`, which bumps the retirement
generation, cancels running jobs and calls
`store.deleteAnalysisJobsForRemovedDownload` -- JOBS only. The asset row survives
with a `sourceURL` pointing at bytes that no longer exist.

WHY fzrw MAKES THIS BITE. Before the bead, an unplayed episode the lane had not
reached had no asset row at all, so deleting its download left nothing behind.
fzrw registers the row at download completion, so every deleted download now
leaves one.

THE VISIBLE EFFECT. `ActivitySnapshotProvider` takes its episode population from
`store.fetchLatestAssetByEpisodeIdMap()` keys (ActivitySnapshotProvider.swift:182
for the UI, :470 for the dogfood snapshot) intersected with SwiftData `Episode`
rows, which survive a download deletion. There is no `isDownloaded` filter in
`loadInputs` (:297-441). The row's state is fzrw's registration token `'new'`,
which `EpisodeSurfaceStatusObserver.analysisState(from:)` projects to
`PersistedStatus.new`; with no live cause the reducer's Rule 5
(EpisodeSurfaceStatusReducer.swift:205) returns the `.queued` disposition
("waiting for its turn"). That was TRUE while the download existed and is FALSE
afterwards -- `retireDownloadAnalysis` deleted the job. `downloadFraction`
resolves to nil (`DL --%`), `finishedOutcome` is nil and `isTerminal` is false,
so the row sits in the in-progress section permanently.

The LIBRARY control is NOT affected: with `isDownloaded == false` and a `'new'`
row, `episodePreparationAnalysisInputs` returns all-false and
`deriveEpisodePreparationReadiness` gives `.idle` -- resting and tappable, the
same answer as no row at all. This is an Activity-surface bug only.

REMEDY IS A DECISION, NOT A PATCH. Deleting the row is the wrong fix and the
codebase already says so (AnalysisStore.swift:7395: "`DELETE FROM
analysis_assets` here is two defects at once") -- transcript chunks, ad windows
and day-0 attempt records are FK'd to it. The candidates are: filter the Activity
population by download presence (`downloadedEpisodeIds` is already fetched at
:484), or mark the row retired and have the reducer read that.

Related: playhead-6zu7 (the same population widening seen from the library
coverage batch's cost model).

title: Activity 'Up Next' strands an episode whose download was deleted before analysis
description:
Nothing in production ever deletes an `analysis_assets` row — `AnalysisStore.deleteAsset(id:)` has ZERO callers — and `AnalysisWorkScheduler.retireDownloadAnalysis` deletes only `analysis_jobs`. So an episode whose download the user removes keeps its asset row forever, and `ActivitySnapshotProvider` filters to asset-bearing episodes: the row reduces to disposition .queued with no live cause, which `dogfoodActivitySection`/the UI aggregator place under `up_next`, with DL --% and no job behind it.

This is PRE-EXISTING (it already happens for any episode the analysis lane reached before the download was deleted), but playhead-fzrw widens the population sharply: the asset row is now minted when the BYTES LAND rather than when the serial lane arrives, so download-then-delete-before-analysis — previously invisible because no row existed — now strands too.

Filed rather than fixed in fzrw R3: the fix belongs to the retirement path (decide whether retirement should delete a never-analysed asset row, and what that means for a row the day-0 rediff kickoff has already minted attempt records against), which is outside fzrw's acceptance criteria.

Evidence: Playhead/Services/PreAnalysis/AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:1505 retireDownloadAnalysis; Playhead/Persistence/AnalysisStore/AnalysisStore.swift:10206 deleteAsset (no callers); Playhead/Services/Activity/ActivitySnapshotProvider.swift:664 dogfoodActivitySection.

title: AnalysisCoordinator.resolveSession's placeholder insert is still a check-then-insert across actors — the mirror of the window playhead-fzrw R2 closed
description:
FILED BY playhead-fzrw R2 review (outside that bead's ceiling, which is "the
analysis_assets row is registered when the bytes land").

fzrw R2 closed ONE ordering of a two-writer race by giving the download-time
registration an atomic conditional insert
(`AnalysisStore.insertAssetIfEpisodeHasNone`, used by
`AnalysisWorkScheduler.registerDownloadedAssetRowIfAbsent`). The mirror window is
untouched and is pre-existing.

THE SHAPE. `AnalysisCoordinator.resolveSession` (AnalysisCoordinator.swift:2211
fetch, :2351 insert) reads `fetchAssetByEpisodeId`, then suspends twice —
`capabilitiesService.currentSnapshot` (:2308) and
`downloadManager?.fingerprint(for:)` (:2332) — before `store.insertAsset`. It runs
on the coordinator actor; the scheduler's registration runs on the scheduler
actor. Both are check-then-insert, so of the two interleavings:

  * registration check -> resolveSession check -> resolveSession insert ->
    registration insert   = CLOSED by fzrw R2 (the conditional insert refuses).
  * registration check -> resolveSession check -> registration insert ->
    resolveSession insert = STILL OPEN (resolveSession inserts unconditionally).

The V39 uniqueness index cannot catch either: it is on
`(episodeId, assetFingerprint)` and the placeholder writes its own UUID as the
fingerprint (:2337), so the indexed pair differs and BOTH rows survive. That is
playhead-0hi9's duplicate, whose one-shot repair sweep
(`did_duplicate_asset_reconcile_v1`, :4113) is already spent on shipped devices.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN fzrw. The remedy is not symmetric. When the conditional
insert refuses, `resolveSession` must adopt the OTHER row's id — but it has
already skipped the session-resume logic that runs for a known asset (:2232-2287),
so a naive adoption can create a second `analysis_sessions` row for an asset that
already has one, and can return a `resumeState` that does not describe the row it
handed back. That is a change to the play-start path, which is a poor thing to
make in passing during a P1 fix round.

WHAT MAKES IT WORSE THAN BEFORE fzrw. Nothing about the coordinator changed, but
the coincidence window widened: `analysis_assets` now has a THIRD writer that
fires at download completion, and `DownloadManager` awaits `enqueue` (:4064)
before announcing the completion that requests the day-0 kickoff — so a download
landing while the user presses play is a routine pairing rather than a rare one.

SUGGESTED SHAPE (not a decision): route `resolveSession`'s insert through
`insertAssetIfEpisodeHasNone` too, and on refusal RESTART the existing-asset arm
from the top (re-fetch, reconcile coverage, resume the existing session) rather
than adopting mid-flight. A rail exists to copy: `PlaceholderRacer` in
`DownloadTimeAssetRegistrationTests.swift` plants a competing row from inside the
one suspension point that lies within the window, with an anti-vacuity assertion
that the seam actually fired.

title: the library coverage batch's 'most rows have never been analysed' premise is false once every download registers an asset row
description:
playhead-fzrw R1 finding, OUT OF SCOPE for fzrw itself.

EpisodePreparationStatusModel.swift:134-140 documents the cost model for the library refresh's coverage batch:

  'It is bounded by the number of episodes that have an analysis_assets row -- NOT by the list length ... Most library rows have never been analysed and cost nothing here. If that ever stops being true (a user with thousands of analysed episodes on screen), the fix is to narrow the fetch to the visible window, not to go back to reading a cheaper wrong number.'

playhead-fzrw makes AnalysisWorkScheduler.enqueue register an analysis_assets row at DOWNLOAD time, so the premise is now false: coverageAssetIds (line 141) becomes every DOWNLOADED episode rather than every ANALYSED one. fetchCoverageSummariesByAssetIds runs four prepared statements per 500-id chunk (see the cost note at :126-133).

Per-row cost for a freshly registered row is small (no transcript chunks yet), so this is a set-size regression rather than a per-row one -- but the comment names the remedy in advance: narrow the fetch to the visible window.

Related: ActivitySnapshotProvider.swift:182/:470 uses fetchLatestAssetByEpisodeIdMap() keys as its episode population (contract stated at AnalysisStore.swift:9962-9964), so the Activity screen's row set grows the same way, and the unbounded SCAN + TEMP B-TREE noted in the TODO at AnalysisStore.swift:9965-9976 now walks 'every downloaded episode'.

title: a test that indexes past an array a mutant shrank CRASHES the runner and prints a green summary
description:
FOUND IN playhead-3zxd R3 review (2026-08-11), measured.

THE HAZARD. A literal subscript after an #expect(x.count == n) traps when a mutant changes the count. In Swift Testing a trap kills the whole runner process; xcodebuild restarts it and CONTINUES, and the final summary counts only the surviving launch. R2's MQ mutant (a widened fragment-merge window) crashed a 20-suite run five times. In this round's re-run the truncated run's LAST LINE READ:

    Restarting after unexpected exit, crash, or test timeout
    ...
    ✔ Test run with 13 tests in 3 suites passed after 1.412 seconds.

191 tests were requested. A crash therefore does not merely cost a verdict, it PRINTS A GREEN ONE -- and 'GATE_EXIT=65 but the last line says passed' is exactly the shape a tired reader mis-triages. (This is the 2026-07-31 gate-triage lesson one layer down: it is not only which FORMAT you grep, it is whether the summary you grepped covers the population you asked for.)

DONE IN 3zxd R3, SO THIS IS THE REMAINDER. Ten sites in the rediff suites were converted to try #require, found by scanning for the pattern rather than by eye:
  RediffSlotOwnershipTests.swift (5), RediffByteAlignerTests.swift (4),
  RediffDayZeroAutoSkipPromotionTests.swift (1).
The same pattern is expected across the other ~1,100 test files and was NOT swept -- out of that bead's scope.

SUGGESTED SHAPE. The scanner is mechanical: find '#expect(<name>.count ==' and any '<name>[<literal>]' within the next few lines. Either sweep it as a one-off (test-only, no production risk) or, better, make it a lint rule so the pattern cannot come back. Note that many literal subscripts are SAFE -- an index-aligned output (candidates/diagnostics/dispositions vs decodedSpans) has a length fixed by the input, not by the code under test -- so a blanket ban would be noise. The discriminator is whether the COUNT is a function of what is being tested.

title: the day-0 invariant witness measures each persona's OWN slots, but what SHIPS is the k-way UNION
description:
FOUND IN playhead-3zxd R3 review (2026-08-11). Not a phantom; a LIMIT of the witness, stated so nobody over-reads a clean column.

RediffSlotOwnership.byteDiagnostics computes alignedSecondsInSlots over ONE persona's acceptance.playedSlots against THAT persona's foundRunASpans, and its doc says it is measured 'over the slots as they SHIP ... because a banner the listener can tap is the thing at stake'. What actually reaches a banner is RediffSlotOwnership.unionedPlayedSlots(perBSideSlots) -- the k-way UNION, re-run through mergedAndCapped -- which can be strictly WIDER than any single persona's slot (it merges across personas, and can bridge two slots that were >3s apart in each list).

So a minted window can contain A-seconds that persona A's found runs proved matched, while lastAlignedSecondsInSlots reads 0. A device pull reading that column as 'no shipped banner contains matched audio' is reading something narrower than it thinks.

WHY IT IS NOT A DEFECT TODAY. Under quorum-1 union semantics (playhead-wybg) that region IS divergent -- persona B diverged on it -- so the banner is correct and measuring the union against persona A's runs alone would flag genuine ads. The honest stronger invariant is the union slot measured against the INTERSECTION of the personas' run coverages ('matched in EVERY persona'), which is a design decision about what the witness should assert, not a bug fix.

SCOPE. Either extend the witness to the union with intersection-of-runs coverage, or correct the two doc comments (RediffSlotOwnership.ByteDiagnostics.alignedSecondsInSlots and RediffByteMintDiagnostics.alignedSecondsInSlots) to say per-persona rather than 'as they SHIP'.

title: the six V48 byte-diff columns are invisible to the diagnostics bundle — the capture harness has no supported readout
description:
FOUND IN playhead-3zxd R2 REVIEW. Not a defect — a gap between what the bead delivers and how it can be read.

playhead-3zxd's premise (RediffByteMintDiagnostics.swift header) is that the PHONE is the capture harness: "day-0 rediff already runs on every download, on the real CDN, with the real personas — so every episode Dan adds is a real observation if, and only if, the diff leaves something behind."

It does leave something behind — six new columns on `rediff_day_zero_attempts` (V48):

    lastRunsFound, lastRunsAOverlapping, lastOverlapSecondsRecovered,
    lastAlignedSecondsInSlots, lastMaxAlignedSecondsInSlot, lastAlignedRunSpans

But `DiagnosticsBundle.RediffDayZeroAttemptSummary` projects NONE of them. It carries the p70f census (attemptCount, lastExit, lastMarkCount, the four per-B counters, lastDivergentSlotCount, the byte totals, policyGeneration) and stops. So the only way to read the phantom evidence off a device is a raw sqlite pull over `devicectl` — not the export path the app already ships and the one a support flow would use.

The V48 migration note does say "Local only: this is written to the on-device store and read by a device pull", so the scoping is deliberate and the on-device mandate is unaffected either way (these are A-timeline seconds and counts, no B offsets, no audio, no transcript — the same disclosure class as `lastDivergentSlotCount`, which IS already exported).

WHAT TO ADD, if this is taken: the five scalars are unambiguously safe to project alongside the existing census. `lastAlignedRunSpans` is a per-episode A-timeline structure rather than a scalar and is capped at 48 spans / <1 KB; decide separately whether it belongs in an export or stays pull-only.

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING: the invariant witness is `lastAlignedSecondsInSlots == 0` and the opportunity counter is `lastRunsAOverlapping > 0`. Without them in the bundle, "did the phantom fire on real audio, and did the fix hold?" cannot be answered from a support export — which is the exact question the bead built the instrument to answer.

title: day-0 free exit ZEROES the per-B census while keeping the earlier attempt's timestamp
description:
FOUND IN playhead-3zxd R2 REVIEW, adjacent to F1 (which fixed the SAME shape for the six V48 byte-diagnostics columns and is the reason this one is now visible on its own).

THE SHAPE. `DayZeroRediffAttemptPolicy.advance` deliberately does NOT move `attemptCount` or `lastAttemptAt` on a FREE exit (`spentBandwidth == false`) — the budget bounds BANDWIDTH, and an exit that spent none must consume none. That is correct and load-bearing (p70f change 3). But it DOES overwrite, from the free outcome:

    lastMarkCount, lastBSideCount, lastBSidesAccepted,
    lastBSidesGateRejected, lastBSidesUnreadable,
    lastDivergentSlotCount, lastFullFetchBytes

and `upsertRediffDayZeroAttempt`'s ON CONFLICT sets every one of them from `excluded`. So after a free exit the row reads: "at time T (the EARLIER attempt's timestamp), attemptCount N, the mint produced 0 marks / 0 divergent slots / spent 0 bytes." Every one of those quantities describes an event that is NOT the event `lastAttemptAt` names.

WHY IT MATTERS. `lastDivergentSlotCount` and `lastMarkCount` are BOTH in the day-0 validation query (see the header of PlayheadTests/Services/AdDetection/RediffRefetch/RediffByteMintDiagnosticsTests.swift), read alongside `datetime(lastAttemptAt,'unixepoch')`. `RediffDayZeroAttemptSummary` in the diagnostics bundle projects all of them the same way.

REACHABLE, and the worst case is a SUCCESS being erased. The ug9m rescue grants one re-attempt over a `.marked` row. If that rescue is then blocked locally — the A-side was deleted after listening, so `byteDifferASideURL` no longer resolves — the exit is `.aSideNotAnchored` (FREE), and the row's `lastMarkCount` falls 4 -> 0 while `lastAttemptAt` still points at the attempt that minted those 4. A support pull then reads "day-0 ran at T and marked nothing" for an asset day-0 marked successfully.

TENSION TO RESOLVE, not an obvious bug. p70f's own doc says the census updating is deliberate: "`lastExit` and the per-B census still update, so the decline stays diagnosable." That is a real requirement — a decline with no trace is what p70f exists to kill. So the fix is NOT simply "carry them all forward". Options:

  (a) carry the census forward with `lastAttemptAt` (as 3zxd R2 did for `byteDiagnostics`) and let `lastExit` + the suppression/retry-claim counters carry the decline. Cheapest, but loses "how many B-copies were on hand when the decline fired", which the in-mint A-side path does record.
  (b) split the columns: a `lastDeclineExit` / `lastDeclineAt` pair owned by free exits, leaving every `last*` measurement pinned to the last attempt that RAN. Most honest, one migration.
  (c) leave the write and fix the READER: state in the validation query's legend that a row whose `lastExit` is a free exit describes a decline, and the measurements are stale by construction. Zero code, but a legend is not a guard.

3zxd R2 took (a) for `byteDiagnostics` only, because those six columns are a MEASUREMENT of a diff (a decline measured nothing, so overwriting destroys an observation and substitutes a fabricated one — `lastRunsFound = 0` reads as "re-encoding CDN"). The census is a weaker case: its zeroes are at least true OF THE DECLINE. Deliberately left in place and filed rather than widened, because changing it changes p70f's contract.

title: 9s6q segmented chainedFractionB is an A-union over a B denominator — it can exceed 1.0, and it is the re-encode floor
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-11 in playhead-3zxd R1 review, against the shipped RediffByteAligner.segmentDivergentSlots.

THE QUANTITY. SegmentRecovery.chainedFractionB = (sum of accepted run BYTES) / (B audio bytes). After the accept loop, the accepted runs are A-disjoint, so the numerator is the byte-measure of the UNION OF THE FOUND RUNS' A-SPANS. The denominator is B's audio bytes. Those two agree only if the accepted set is injective into B — i.e. no two accepted runs claim overlapping B regions. The accept loop de-conflicts A ONLY; nothing constrains B.

MEASURED. Two A-disjoint runs claiming a 200-frame overlapping B region give chainedFractionB = 1.3333. A fraction of B that exceeds 1 is not a fraction of B.

WHY IT MATTERS. RediffSlotOwnership.segmentRecoveredByteGate compares this to minAlignedFractionB (0.5) as the RE-ENCODE FLOOR. An inflated numerator moves a fetch over the floor that its true B-coverage would not.

REACHABILITY. Two accepted runs overlap in B exactly when A carries a repeated content block that two different byte deltas both extend into (A = [U][C][X][C][V], B = [U][C][V]: the U-anchored run extends right through the first C and the V-anchored run extends LEFT through the second, so both claim B's single C). Repeated >=65536-byte blocks in a podcast are plausible (a repeated sponsor creative, a repeated stinger, long digital silence). NOT constructed from real bytes here — the measurement above drives segmentDivergentSlots directly.

PROVENANCE. This is playhead-9s6q's, not playhead-3zxd's: pre-3zxd the same two A-disjoint runs were both accepted whole and produced the same 1.3333. 3zxd is orthogonal (it raises the numerator by keeping A-overlappers) but the two effects compound.

FIX SHAPES (unranked): make the numerator the B-side union rather than the A-side sum; or clamp/assert; or de-conflict B as well as A in the accept loop and account for what that drops.

DISCOVERED BY playhead-3zxd R1 review.

title: fragment-merge can join a rediff slot ACROSS a byte-verified run at >=192 kbps
description:
Found while fixing playhead-3zxd (a byte-matched run reported as an ad). Same
defect CLASS, two orders of magnitude smaller, and NOT fixed there because it
is outside that bead's scope and its remedy is a different decision.

WHAT. `RediffSlotOwnership.mergedAndCapped` merges two played slots whose gap is
<= `fragmentMergeGapSeconds` (3.0 s), to repair chroma fingerprint dropouts
around splices. On the BYTE path the thing separating two gaps is an accepted
RUN — bytes the aligner proved identical in both copies. So a merge that joins
across one produces a slot containing matched audio: exactly the shape 3zxd
removed from `segmentDivergentSlots`.

WHETHER IT CAN FIRE — arithmetic, not measurement. A run is >= `minRunBytes`
(65536) by construction, so its duration is 65536 / (kbps * 125) seconds:

    128 kbps -> 4.10 s   > 3.0  CANNOT be joined over
    192 kbps -> 2.73 s   < 3.0  CAN
    256 kbps -> 2.05 s   < 3.0  CAN
    320 kbps -> 1.64 s   < 3.0  CAN

So it is impossible on a 128 kbps CBR podcast (which is what every synthetic
fixture in the 3zxd/pyq7 suites is) and possible on a 192+ kbps one. Whether any
show Dan subscribes to is 192+ is UNMEASURED.

BOUND. <= `fragmentMergeGapSeconds` (3 s) per join, versus the 470 s 3zxd
measured. A banner 3 s wide at the wrong place is a different order of harm from
one that eats a content block, which is why this is P2 and 3zxd was P0.

ALREADY OBSERVABLE, NO NEW INSTRUMENTATION NEEDED. playhead-3zxd persists
`rediff_day_zero_attempts.lastAlignedSecondsInSlots` and
`lastMaxAlignedSecondsInSlot`, measured over the slots as they SHIP (post-merge)
precisely so this is not hidden. After 3zxd the 3zxd phantom contributes 0, so
any non-zero value on a device pull is either this or a 3zxd regression, and the
magnitude tells them apart: <= 3 s per join is this; minutes is that.

DO NOT "FIX" IT BY LOWERING `fragmentMergeGapSeconds`. That is the same
bound-the-damage move 3zxd rejected for `maxSlotSeconds`, and it would also
weaken the chroma path's dropout repair, which is what the constant is FOR. The
honest options are (a) make the byte path's merge refuse to join across an
interval covered by a found run — the run spans are now on `Alignment.foundRun
ASpans`, so the information is present; or (b) leave it and rely on the
instrumentation. (a) is preferred but it splits a constant the two differs
currently share, which is a design decision, not a bug fix.

FIRST STEP: read `lastMaxAlignedSecondsInSlot` off a device pull before writing
any code. If it is 0 across the library, no show in it is 192+ kbps with an
adjacent-gap shape and this can wait.

title: the day-0 kickoff ledger's lastWaitedSeconds excludes the serial-drain queue wait — the very 33 minutes that motivated the durable claim
description:
FOUND IN playhead-kg8h R3 (Job 4, standing defect class: a value that names one thing read as though it named another). OUT OF kg8h's SCOPE — the code is playhead-4dqe's and untouched by kg8h's diff — so it is filed, not fixed.

THE QUANTITY. `rediff_day_zero_kickoffs.lastWaitedSeconds`, documented on `RediffDayZeroKickoffRecord` as 'Wall-clock seconds the most recent kickoff waited'. It is written in `RediffDayZeroKickoffCoordinator.settle` as `max(0, settledAt - startedAt)`, and `startedAt` is taken at the head of `process(_:)` — i.e. AFTER the request has already been popped off `pending`.

THE TEST (what would this read if the thing it claims to measure had never happened?). A kickoff that sat 33 minutes in the strictly-serial drain and then fired on its first probe reads ~0. That 33-minute figure is not hypothetical: it is playhead-kxgh's own measurement of five day-0 requests through this drain, and it is quoted in `requestKickoff`'s doc comment as loss #3 — the reason the durable claim exists at all. So the row records the ONE component of latency the bead family already knows is the big one as zero.

WHY IT IS NOT RECOVERABLE TODAY. The claim stamps `updatedAt = claim.at` and the settle overwrites it with `settledAt`. Once a kickoff settles, nothing in the row dates its enqueue, so `settledAt - claimedAt` cannot be reconstructed. Only rows still carrying an OUTSTANDING claim (lastOutcome = 'requested') can be aged, and those are exactly the ones that never settled.

SHAPE OF A FIX (not decided). A `claimedAt REAL` column written by `noteRediffDayZeroKickoffClaim` and never overwritten by the settle would make `updatedAt - claimedAt` the end-to-end latency, with `lastWaitedSeconds` left alone as the readiness-poll component. Two honest numbers instead of one number read as the other.

BLAST RADIUS TODAY: diagnostics only — no production code reads `lastWaitedSeconds` (scanned: the only readers are `AnalysisStore.readRediffDayZeroKickoffRow` and tests). The cost is paid by whoever next investigates 'why was day-0 late' from a device pull and concludes the wait was instant.

title: the day-0 kickoff ledger is not in the diagnostics bundle — the only way to read it is a raw DB pull
description:
Found while reviewing playhead-kg8h (R2), OUTSIDE that bead's scope — filed, not fixed.

`AnalysisStore.fetchRediffDayZeroKickoffs(limit:)` has ZERO callers anywhere in the
repo: not in production, not in tests. Its own doc comment calls it 'the
diagnostics-bundle surface', and `rediff_day_zero_kickoffs` appears nowhere under
`Playhead/Support/` (the whole diagnostics tree, including
`DiagnosticsBundleBuilder`).

Why it matters. playhead-4dqe built this table so a silent day-0 give-up would be
impossible, and playhead-kg8h added the durable CLAIM so that
`kickoffCount - (firedCount + gaveUpCount)` is the queryable count of kickoffs
owed and never settled. Both beads describe that number as 'measurable from a
device pull rather than inferred from an absence'. It is not measurable from the
diagnostics bundle a user can actually send — only from pulling the sqlite file
off the device by hand (the Away-Plan devicectl recipe). The give-up path DOES
reach the field, via the JSON Lines invariant stream (`reportViolation`), but that
stream carries only `noPinnedFile` / `noAnalysisAsset`. The two states the claim
was added to distinguish — 'requested and still owed' and 'requested and fired' —
have no field surface at all.

Suggested shape: export the kickoff rows (or a roll-up: episodes, kickoffs,
fired, gaveUp, owed) into the diagnostics bundle alongside the existing analysis
health records. Episode ids must go through `EpisodeIdHasher`, as every other
producer on that surface does.

Note the limit: `fetchRediffDayZeroKickoffs` defaults to the 200 most recently
UPDATED rows. An outstanding claim's `updatedAt` is its REQUEST time and is never
rewritten, so on a busy device the rows that get truncated first are exactly the
owed kickoffs this measurement is for. Worth deciding deliberately when wiring
it up.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: DUPLICATE of playhead-njkw, filed minutes apart by R1 and R2 of the same bead. Closing in favour of njkw, which carries both writeups.

title: the day-0 kickoff ledger never reaches the diagnostics bundle — its only reader is dead code
description:
FOUND IN REVIEW OF playhead-kg8h (R1), OUTSIDE THAT DIFF — filed, not fixed.

`AnalysisStore.fetchRediffDayZeroKickoffs(limit: Int = 200)` (AnalysisStore.swift:7056) carries the doc comment 'Every kickoff record, most recent first — the diagnostics-bundle surface.' It has ZERO callers anywhere in the repo: not production, not tests, not scripts. Verified with a repo-wide grep for the symbol; the only hit is its own declaration.

The singular `fetchRediffDayZeroKickoff(episodeId:)` is likewise called only from PlayheadTests.

CONSEQUENCE. `rediff_day_zero_kickoffs` — including the `.requested` durable claims playhead-kg8h just shipped, and the `kickoffCount - (firedCount + gaveUpCount)` reading that is that bead's whole deliverable — is reachable ONLY by pulling the sqlite file off a device by hand. DiagnosticsBundleBuilder does not ship the analysis DB (grep for sqlite/.db/storeURL in that file returns nothing). So the ledger cannot be read from a support bundle, a TestFlight report, or anything a user can send.

That is a reach gap in the exact instrument the kickoff ledger exists to be: kg8h's premise is that the loss should be QUERYABLE, and today it is queryable only with the phone in hand.

ORIGIN: pre-existing since playhead-4dqe, which added both the plural fetch and its doc comment. Not introduced by kg8h.

SUGGESTED: either wire fetchRediffDayZeroKickoffs into DiagnosticsBundleBuilder (and pin it with a test, since a dead reader is how this happened), or delete it and correct the prose so nobody believes the surface exists.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: MERGED playhead-rrr9 into this bead 2026-08-11 — R1 and R2 of playhead-kg8h independently filed the same finding, which is itself weak corroboration that it is real. rrr9's wording adds one fact worth keeping: the zero-callers claim covers PRODUCTION AND TESTS, not just production. Both 4dqe and kg8h describe this number as 'measurable from a device pull', and it is in no diagnostics bundle, so only a raw DB pull off the handset reaches it. That is the gap: kg8h's whole contribution is a durable claim row, and the claim row cannot be read in the field.

title: a completed background download whose URL resolves nowhere is dropped with no kickoff row — the last silent return on the day-0 hand-off
description:
FILED BY playhead-kg8h (outside its ceiling).

`PlayheadRuntime.installDayZeroBackgroundDownloadKickoff`'s observer ends with:

    guard let request = DayZeroBackgroundKickoff.request(
        episodeId: episodeId, facts: facts,
        fallbackURL: fallbackURL, enqueuedAt: ...
    ) else { return }

`DayZeroBackgroundKickoff.request` returns nil when `facts?.enclosureURL ?? fallbackURL`
is nil, and the observer's `fallbackURL` is
`originalURL ?? URL(string: loadPin(for: episodeId)?.sourceURL ?? "")`
(`DownloadManager.swift`, the `notifyBackgroundDownloadCompleted` call at the end
of `handleBackgroundDownloadComplete`) — `URL(string: "")` is nil, so a
completion with no `originalURL` AND no pin `sourceURL` produces nothing: no
kickoff, no counter, no row, no invariant line.

It is a narrow case and the doc calls it "the one case where there is genuinely
nothing to re-fetch" — which is true about the RE-FETCH and false about the
RECORD. playhead-kg8h's claim covers every kickoff that reaches
`requestKickoff`; this one never gets there. The remedy is the same shape as the
rest of playhead-4dqe: name it and count it rather than returning.

title: The FM prologue atomizes the transcript and builds the evidence catalog TWICE per scan
description:
Established while implementing playhead-15d0 (source trace). Cheap, mechanical, and it sits in the one stretch of the scan that must complete before anything durable is written.

`AdDetectionService.runBackfill` does whole-episode work, then `runShadowFMPhase` does the same work again on the same chunks:

  * `TranscriptAtomizer.atomize` at AdDetectionService.swift:4238 and AGAIN at :9604
  * `EvidenceCatalogBuilder.build` at :4247 and AGAIN at :9611

Both are pure functions of `canonicalChunks` (+ assetId/version), and `runShadowFMPhase` is handed `chunks: canonicalChunks` — the same array — at :4342. Neither call is guarded by a branch that could make the inputs differ.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE RATHER THAN AS TIDINESS. playhead-15d0 measured that a `fullEpisodeScan` writes nothing durable until (probe + `promptBudget` + `planPassA`'s per-candidate `tokenCount` XPC round trips + one full `respond`) have all completed, and that six of the eight background windows iOS granted on the measured evening were shorter than the 30 s metadata bound on ONE of those round trips. Everything in that prologue is paid before the first row and discarded if the window ends. A duplicated whole-episode atomization + catalog build is pure prologue.

NOT MEASURED: how long the duplicate actually costs on device. It is CPU over the whole transcript (1,883 chunks on the measured asset), not I/O, and it is not an XPC round trip — so it is very likely small next to the tokenizer sweep. File and measure before assuming it is worth the churn; the reason to do it is that it is a pure deletion with no behaviour change, not that it is known to be the bottleneck.

title: final_pass_jobs retains complete rows for spans no AdWindow holds any more
description:
Found while reviewing playhead-jzj0 (R1). OUT OF SCOPE for that bead — filed, not fixed.

An AdWindow id is stable across a span change by design (AdDetectionService.reconcileHotPathWindows reuses existing.id with fresh startTime/endTime; AnalysisStore.updateAdWindowHotPathCandidate writes the new bounds onto the same row). playhead-jzj0 R1 made the final-pass runner mint a span-qualified jobId when the natural id is already held by a different span, so the NEW span gets its own row and the OLD span's completed row is left intact.

That is right for history but it means canonicalCompleteFinalPassSpans(forAsset:) can return spans that no AdWindow holds any more. Anything that derives progress from that set alone counts a span nobody is asking about.

Name the quantity: numerator = distinct canonical spans with a complete final_pass_jobs row; denominator = ??? — it is NOT 'distinct spans among today's confidence-cleared AdWindows', which is what a progress UI means. The two diverge by exactly the retired spans.

Not urgent: nothing today routes on it (the runner keys eligibility off the per-span lookup, not off this set), so the exposure is diagnostics/progress reporting. Decide whether the answer is (a) join against ad_windows when deriving progress, or (b) retire rows whose span no longer matches any AdWindow — (b) loses the audit trail the alias table exists to preserve, so (a) looks right.

title: FinalPassRetranscriptionRunner.coversWindow is a per-CHUNK containment test and can essentially never fire for a real window
description:
FOUND during playhead-jzj0 while establishing which rails actually stop redundant final-pass ASR.

FinalPassRetranscriptionRunner.retranscribeWindow documents an 'inner idempotency rail': skip the window if existing pass='final' chunks already cover it. The test is

    existingFinalChunks.contains { chunk in
        chunk.startTime <= job.windowStartTime && chunk.endTime >= job.windowEndTime
    }

That asks whether some SINGLE chunk contains the whole window. Transcript chunks are per-segment — roughly 1-5 s on the device pulls — and ad windows are 8-150 s. On db-evening2 the largest final chunk span for asset 66D32039 is well under any window's width, so no single chunk can contain one. The rail is documented as 'defense' but in practice fires only for a window shorter than one ASR segment.

The same shape appears in the in-drain companion, inDrainCoveredIntervals — that one CAN fire, because its intervals are whole windows.

What the check presumably wants is INTERVAL UNION coverage: does the union of final chunks cover [windowStart, windowEnd]. AnalysisCoverageMath already has union machinery (playhead-hygc.1.2 / sd71).

Impact is bounded — it is the third of three rails, behind the per-window final_pass_jobs status guard (the primary, and after playhead-jzj0 the only one that matters for eligibility) and per-segment fingerprint dedupe (which prevents duplicate ROWS but not duplicate ASR). So this is wasted compute in the case where a span's job row is missing or non-complete but its audio was already transcribed, not a correctness bug.

Deliberately NOT fixed in playhead-jzj0 — out of that bead's scope, and changing it alters when ASR is skipped, which wants its own measurement.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: REPRIORITIZED -> P2 in the 2026-08-11 triage.

title: The canonical bead-close sequence destroys the gate log that authorised the merge
description:
FOUND 2026-08-11 by the playhead-fzpj closer, after its own log had already been deleted. Applies to ALL 13 beads merged on 08-10/11.

THE GAP. scripts/fast-gate.sh writes its log wherever it is invoked, which is the bead worktree. CLAUDE.md's canonical close sequence then runs 'git worktree remove' and 'rm -rf .derivedData'. The gate log goes with it. So the artifact that justified a merge stops existing at the moment the merge completes.

WHY IT MATTERS EVEN WHEN THE VERIFICATION WAS SOUND. On fzpj the log was read twice independently — by the closer, and by me before merging (greps for XCTest failures, sub-97s Swift Testing failures, DID NOT RUN, and failures naming a touched file; all four came back zero). Two parties, same numbers, decision correct. But nobody can re-open it now. Every verbatim line in the merge record rests on transcription. That is acceptable for a decision already made and poor for one anyone later wants to audit — and this project's whole gate discipline (playhead-voez) exists because a verdict you cannot inspect is a verdict you cannot trust.

THE FIX, one line, before 'git worktree remove' in the canonical sequence:

  cp "$WT"/gate-*.log "$SCRATCHPAD/gate-logs/<bead>/" 2>/dev/null

The closer's log is the minimum. The review-round and mutant logs are cheap to keep too, and the mutant logs are what prove a delete-the-call-site probe actually reddened — currently that evidence is destroyed as well.

PARTIAL SUBSTITUTE when a log is already gone, and worth doing routinely regardless: 'git diff <reviewed-tip> <merged-commit>' over the whole tree. Empty means the merged code is byte-identical to what was reviewed and gated, which rescues the ATTRIBUTION of the verdict even though its evidence is lost. The fzpj closer used exactly this (2861f365 vs b196e938, empty).

SCOPE: this is a CLAUDE.md edit to the 'Canonical bead-close sequence' block, plus optionally a line in scripts/fast-gate.sh's own docs pointing out that its log is worktree-local and ephemeral. Filed rather than done because CLAUDE.md is the operating manual for every agent on this repo and Dan should see the change.
