title: recordVeto scopes a sponsor to an EPISODE, not a show: sponsorOnShow(podcastId:) is handed span.assetId
description:
Found while establishing the read topology for playhead-fzpj (verified from source).

`PersistentUserCorrectionStore.recordVeto(span:ledgerEntries:)`
(UserCorrectionStore.swift:877-891) writes, for every brandSpan evidence entry:

    CorrectionScope.sponsorOnShow(
        podcastId: span.assetId,  // best available show-level key without podcastId
        sponsor: entry.normalizedText
    )
    CorrectionEvent(..., podcastId: nil, ...)

An `analysisAssetId` is a per-EPISODE UUID (device DB, correction_events.analysisAssetId
— 6 distinct values in db-corrected2, all UUIDs). A `podcastId` is a FEED URL. So the
field named podcastId holds an episode identity, and the scope that means 'this sponsor,
across every episode of this show' is silently narrowed to one episode. The standing
defect class: a value that names one thing read as though it named another.

CONSEQUENCE. The derived sponsor_knowledge_entries row is keyed
(podcastId=<episode UUID>, .sponsor, <normalizedText>) — UNIQUE(podcastId, entityType,
normalizedValue). `SponsorKnowledgeMatcher.match(podcastId:)` and
`activeEntriesWithNegativeMemory(forPodcast:)` are both called with the FEED URL
(AdDetectionService.swift:4431 -> RegionShadowPhase.swift:249), so the row can never be
found. Every veto also mints a fresh row rather than confirming one, so
confirmationCount can never climb to the .active promotion threshold.

NOT a duplicate of playhead-fzpj. fzpj is about the SPLIT of the wire string being
unrecoverable; this row parses perfectly (a UUID has no colon) and is simply the wrong
identity. fzpj's resolver takes the parsed pair here precisely because the split IS
exact — it cannot tell an episode id from a show id, and should not try.

FIX SHAPE. DecodedSpan does not carry a podcastId (the inline comment says so). Either
thread the show identity into recordVeto(span:) from the caller, or stop emitting a
sponsorOnShow scope from this site and let the banner path be the only writer. Needs a
look at who calls recordVeto(span:) and whether a show identity is in scope there.

BLAST RADIUS TODAY: zero. sponsor_knowledge_entries = 0 rows and sponsorOnShow scopes = 0
across five device pulls (db-corrected2/marked/vtjxverdict/night1/evening2).

title: BackgroundSessionIO's 10s bound measures QUEUE WAIT + daemon time, not daemon time — under contention it fires for the wrong reason (15 occurrences in one full plan)
description:
FOUND by the orchestrator verifying the playhead-nsjn closer gate, 2026-08-11. NOT a merge blocker and NOT a reason to revert nsjn — a bound that occasionally fires early is strictly better than the unbounded deadlock it replaced. But the quantity it measures is not the quantity it names, which is this project's standing defect class.

WHAT WAS MEASURED. In the nsjn closer's full plan (gate-nsjn-closer.log, the first full plan in four attempts to reach a terminal verdict):

  numerator   15 log lines reading 'the background transfer daemon did not answer'
  denominator one full-plan run

Those 15 are the new 10s bound firing. Two of them turned into test failures the closer attributed to this branch (ForceQuitResumeTests.swift, 4 issues across 2 tests: skipsHarvestWhenResumeDataAbsent is genuinely NEW; the other is the FAILS DIFFERENTLY entry, baseline kind 'timeout', this run 'assertion'). Both fail the same pre-existing assertion, admissionCount == admissions + 1, immediately after the new log line — i.e. backgroundDownload took the daemon-unavailable branch and never admitted the transfer.

THE MECHANISM, and why the name is wrong. BackgroundSessionIO.shared is ONE process-wide serial queue. The 10s deadline is armed at the CALLER's start, but the body cannot run until the queue drains ahead of it. So the interval the bound actually measures is (queue wait) + (daemon round trip). It is named, logged and reported as though it measured only the second. Under contention a perfectly healthy daemon answering in milliseconds can still blow the bound because nine other callers were ahead.

Apply the standing check — what would this read if the thing it claims to measure had never happened? If the daemon were instantaneous, the bound would STILL fire whenever queue depth x per-call latency exceeded 10s. That is a value that names one thing and reads another.

WHERE IT BITES TODAY: the test host, where many DownloadManagers funnel through the single shared instance while ~10,000 tests run concurrently. Production is milder (one manager, fewer concurrent downloads) but not immune — playhead-byfd already records the auto-download loop paying the bound per episode inside a ~30s BGTask window, which is the same arithmetic.

CANDIDATE REMEDIES, none obviously right, all needing measurement first:
1. Arm the deadline when the BODY STARTS rather than when the caller submits, so it measures the daemon. Cost: an unbounded queue wait reappears, which is most of what nsjn removed — probably wrong alone.
2. Two bounds: a short one on the daemon round trip and a longer one on total admission, reported distinctly so a queue-starved caller is not blamed on the daemon.
3. Per-role or per-manager IO instances instead of one process-wide queue. Fixes the test host cleanly and reduces production coupling; is a service-architecture change, so Dan's call.
4. Test-host only: give each test DownloadManager its own BackgroundSessionIO. Cheapest, fixes the 2 red tests, leaves the production naming defect standing.

DO NOT simply raise 10s to a bigger number. That trades a wrong-reason refusal for a longer wrong-reason refusal and moves nothing that matters.

RELATED: playhead-byfd (sequential awaits inside the BGTask window), playhead-ola7 (session creation still inline), playhead-zq2g (retire cancels inline). nsjn's own bead records that the 10s value is chosen, not measured — this bead is about WHAT it measures, which is the prior question.

title: backgroundDownload's creation-timeout interleave has no rail; a deterministic seam makes one possible
description:
playhead-nsjn R3 named this its own weakest link and R4 agrees it is unrailed, but disagrees with the stated reason (flake risk). A deterministic rail IS achievable without any wall clock.

WHAT IS UNRAILED. DownloadManager.swift:2505 — backgroundDownload's creation-timeout branch calls releaseInFlightReservationIfUnclaimed. Its CONDITIONAL behaviour (another claimant registered during the suspension must keep the slot) is pinned only at the helper level, by abandonKeepsTheSlotAnotherLiveTransferStillHolds, which drives abandonUnstartedTransfer. A regression that reverted ONLY line 2505 to an unconditional bgInFlightEpisodes.remove(episodeId) survives every rail in the tree.

WHY R3's REASON DOES NOT HOLD. R3 declined because reproducing it 'needs a genuine race between the suspension and a reattached completion'. It does not. perform() is nonisolated, so an actor caller has genuinely released itself for the whole call — a test-supplied hook running inside that window can re-enter the actor deterministically.

PROPOSED SEAM (DEBUG-only, BackgroundSessionIO.Behavior):
    case refusesCallsLabelledAfter(String, hook: @Sendable () async -> Void)
handled in perform's existing #if DEBUG switch as: await hook(); return nil.

PROPOSED RAIL: a lock-box holds the manager (broken circularity: hook is built before the manager, box filled after). Hook body: await manager._registerBackgroundTransferForTesting(episodeId:). Marker 'downloadTask(with:)' — note this does NOT match 'downloadTask(withResumeData:)', so the resume path is unaffected. Then assert the slot is still held, admission count is 0, and that finishing the reattached identity releases it (proving the retain is a deferral, not a leak).

WHY NOT DONE AT R4. It needs new production seam surface, and nsjn was unblocking every merge gate with four wedged closer runs. Landing new production code in the final review round is what restarts the loop. Scope ceiling.

title: retireBackgroundTransfers cancels background-session tasks INLINE on the cooperative pool
description:
playhead-nsjn R2 finding (filed, not fixed - unproven premise).

playhead-nsjn routed downloadTask(with:), downloadTask(withResumeData:) and resume() through BackgroundSessionIO so they run off the Swift Concurrency cooperative pool under a 10s bound. One call of the same family was left inline on the actor:

  DownloadManager.swift:2691, inside retireBackgroundTransfers(episodeId:)
      for task in tasks { ... task.cancel() ... }

'tasks' comes from 'await session.allTasks' over the three BACKGROUND sessions (.interactive/.maintenance/.legacy), and the loop runs on the actor - i.e. on a cooperative thread, unbounded, once per matching task. Reachable from cancelDownload(episodeId:) (user taps Cancel) and clearCache() (:3611, episodeId: nil - every task in every session).

If -[NSURLSessionTask cancel] on a background session takes the same barrier + synchronous XPC round-trip that -[__NSURLBackgroundSession _downloadTaskWithTaskForClass:] does, this reproduces exactly the wedge nsjn exists to fix, on a production user-initiated path.

EVIDENCE STATUS - the premise is UNPROVEN either way. The j4wi sample has 10 distinct stacks and every one is _downloadTaskWithTaskForClass:; there are zero cancel and zero resume frames in it. nsjn already bounds resume() on the same by-analogy reasoning, and abandonUnstartedTransfer deliberately routes ITS cancel through the bounded queue (DownloadManager.swift:2576-2582) - so the codebase already treats cancel as belonging to this family, and :2691 is the inconsistency.

FIRST STEP is measurement, not a fix: determine whether -[__NSURLBackgroundSessionTask cancel] routes through performBlockOnQueueAndRethrowExceptions (disassemble CFNetwork, or sample a deliberately-stalled daemon while cancelling). If it does, route the loop through BackgroundSessionIO - note it is N cancels, so it needs a shape decision (one bounded submission for the whole loop vs one per task).

Also in the same family and same file: cancelDownload(:2594) and clearCache(:3608) cancel foreground activeDownloads inline; those are a normal URLSession, so lower risk.

title: The test suite registers REAL background transfers with the simulator's nsurlsessiond, on three process-global identifiers
description:
Every `DownloadManager` a test constructs instantiates a genuine
`URLSessionConfiguration.background(withIdentifier:)` session on one of
three PROCESS-GLOBAL identifiers — `com.playhead.transfer.interactive`,
`com.playhead.transfer.maintenance`, `com.playhead.episode-downloads` — and
then starts real transfers against `https://cdn.example.com/...` and hands
garbage `Data` blobs to `downloadTask(withResumeData:)`.

Counted in the current tree: 19 `await manager.backgroundDownload(...)`
call sites across 5 test files, of which 13 are in tests; plus the
`ResumeSuspendedTransferTests` resume paths.

Three consequences, all measured or observed:

1. Those registrations are DURABLE. `nsurlsessiond` persists background
   session state outside the app container, which is why the documented
   recovery for the playhead-nsjn hang was `simctl erase` of the whole
   device and why the residue survived ordinary test-scratch cleanup.
2. Ten tests running concurrently in Swift Testing's in-process pool all
   hit the same daemon through the same three session identifiers. That
   concurrency is what turned one slow XPC reply into ten simultaneously
   blocked cooperative threads (playhead-nsjn).
3. `invalidateBackgroundSessionsForTesting()` exists precisely because
   these leak — but it is opt-in, and only some tests call it.

playhead-nsjn contained the SYMPTOM (a stalled daemon can no longer
deadlock the runtime, and its recovery branches are now reachable and
tested). It did not remove the cause: tests should not be talking to the
real background-transfer daemon at all.

Direction, not a decision — needs Dan's call because it touches the
service architecture: inject a session factory into `DownloadManager` so
tests get either per-test identifiers (isolates them from each other but
still uses the real daemon) or a fake (no daemon at all, but then the
tests stop covering the real URLSession plumbing and something else must).

Related: playhead-be3s / playhead-2x8z (test-health cleanup), and the
ForceQuitResume load-flake family in `scripts/gate-baseline.*.json`.

title: Vanity URLs on long-tail TLDs (.store/.energy/.edu) are invisible to the evidence catalog
description:
Found while reviewing playhead-absa (R1). OUT OF SCOPE for absa, which named
.ai/.co/.fm/.tv only — filed rather than fixed.

A census of every `<word>.<word>` no-space period in the absa eval corpus
(94,692 transcript_chunks, 31 assets, db-vtjxverdict) shows 259 occurrences
whose right-hand token is, essentially without exception, a real TLD or a
decimal number. `EvidenceCatalogBuilder` covers .com (112 hits), .ai (44),
.co (12) and — path-only — .org/.io. What it does NOT cover, all measured in
that same corpus, all in commercial-looking context:

  fyc.appletv.com   x7   (caught, but only via .com)
  pro.fiver.com     x6   (caught, but only via .com; ASR for Fiverr)
  coach.stand.store x1   MISSED
  martinpicard.energy x1 MISSED — "website, martinpicard.energy."
  leakentech.edu    x1   MISSED
  osb.org           x1   MISSED — bare .org is path-only by playhead-onnk

So the miss rate for non-.com/.ai/.co vanity URLs on this corpus is 4 of 4.
Small in absolute terms, but the population is real and is exactly the
host-read / guest-plug class where boundary evidence is scarcest.

Two things worth knowing before picking this up:

1. The bare-.org case is a DELIBERATE prior decision (playhead-onnk made
   .org/.io path-only). Re-opening it needs its own justification, not a
   sweep.

2. There is now a measurement recipe for admitting a bare TLD, recorded in
   EvidenceCatalogBuilder.swift under playhead-absa: the two-character
   right-hand-token census. On this corpus that surface is 60 tokens — 56
   sponsor URLs and 4 decimals ("5.30", "99.99", "2.00"), no English words.
   That bound is what makes a bare two-letter TLD safe. A LONGER TLD
   (.store, .energy) has NOT been bounded that way and needs its own census
   before shipping, because the longer the token the likelier it collides
   with an ordinary word after an ASR run-together period (the corpus already
   contains one such artifact, "knives.wake").

Do not treat this as a licence to add TLDs by list. Measure the population
first; the whole point of the absa record is that "family symmetry" is not
evidence.

title: provenance-blind splice absorption destroys the absorbee's presence evidence, so a music-only absorber can silence a corroborated ad
description:
FILED FROM playhead-d666 R5 review (outside that bead's scope: detection pipeline, not display).

`SpliceSlotDispositionEngine` (Playhead/Services/AdDetection/SpliceSlotDisposition.swift:255-262) picks the absorber by slot geometry alone — "each kept slot absorbs every OTHER non-kept span whose minted interval it fully encloses" — with no reference to provenance. At :398 the survivor is rebuilt as the ABSORBER's own `anchorProvenance` plus the width marker:

    var newProvenance = span.anchorProvenance
    if !newProvenance.contains(provenance) { newProvenance.append(provenance) }

The absorbee's anchors are dropped and its row is deleted downstream. Contrast `SpanFinalizer.toFinalized()` (SpanFinalizer.swift:517-522), which UNIONS provenance across `sourceSpans` — that is the correct pattern and it is right there in the same subsystem.

## Why it matters after playhead-d666

`.spliceSlot` / `.rediffSlot` / `.rediffSlotChroma` are deliberately NOT corroboration (they set WIDTH, not PRESENCE). So a music-only absorber that swallows an FM-corroborated or evidence-catalog-anchored span yields a survivor that still satisfies `carriesOnlyMusicPresenceHint` — the merged row is demoted to `.markOnly` in fusion AND (post-d666) silenced in the transcript, while the row that carried the real presence evidence no longer exists. A real ad becomes invisible on both surfaces through a merge that was only ever meant to fix boundaries.

The same engine is reused by rediff via `RediffSlotOwnership.candidates` (RediffSlotOwnership.swift:520-566).

## Fix shape

Union the absorbee's presence anchors into the survivor at the absorption site, the way `SpanFinalizer` already does. NOT MEASURED against the corpus — no witness is claimed here; this was found by reading, and the first step should be to count absorptions where the absorbee carried presence evidence the absorber lacked.

title: the episode summarizer excises every decoded span 'by construction' — 27 music-only spans / 500.9 s of the show's own words deleted from the summary
description:
FILED FROM playhead-d666 R5 review (outside that bead's scope: a non-display consumer).

`EpisodeSummaryBackfillCoordinator.confirmedAdRanges` (Playhead/Services/EpisodeSummaries/EpisodeSummaryBackfillCoordinator.swift:217) excludes ad ranges from the summarizer input:

    let spanRanges = try await store.fetchDecodedSpans(assetId: assetId)
        .map { EpisodeSummaryAdRange(start: $0.startTime, end: $0.endTime) }

with the doc comment "the decoder's contiguous ad spans (which are ad spans by construction)". That premise is exactly what playhead-d666 disproved: a `DecodedSpan` whose only anchor is `.sustainedMusicOffset` is a TARGETING hint ("an ad begins right AFTER this music"), never a verdict about the audio it covers. `BackfillEvidenceFusion.DecisionMapper` demotes such a span to `.markOnly`; `[AnchorRef].carriesOnlyMusicPresenceHint` is the one definition.

The asymmetry makes it plain: the `ad_windows` half of the same function is deliberately strict — only `confirmed`/`applied`, with `candidate`/`suppressed`/`reverted` explicitly excluded because "only confirmed ads should shrink the editorial text" — while the span half accepts everything unconditionally. A bare music bed therefore outranks a `candidate` ad window.

## Measured (db-corrected2)

- 27 of 66 decoded spans are music-only, totalling **500.9 s** (avg 18.6 s). The claiming 39 total 1,352.5 s.
- **493 of 94,099** transcript_chunks rows sit under a music-only span and under NO claiming span — text that is show content by the app's own policy and is currently deleted from the summarizer input.
- The canonical instance is the clip outro on 48E903D7 / 0C2FC22E / F4CE7F47: "to that full episode, I've linked it down below. Check the description. Thank you." — which is the outro of every episode of that show, so the summary loses the same sentence every time.

## Fix

Filter with `carriesOnlyMusicPresenceHint` at the read, matching the transcript's `adClaimingSpansByChunkIndex`:

    .filter { !$0.anchorProvenance.carriesOnlyMusicPresenceHint }

and correct the doc comment, which is where the wrong premise is actually recorded.

title: A transcript row covered by several decoded spans explains itself with an arbitrary one (overlappingSpans.first)
description:
FOUND in playhead-d666 R1 review. PRE-EXISTING (predates that branch); filed, not
fixed, because changing it has a reachability tradeoff that is a product call.

TranscriptPeekView builds BOTH the popover tap target and the VoiceOver label
from `overlappingSpans.first` — the first decoded span in snapshot order that
overlaps the row:

  Playhead/Views/NowPlaying/TranscriptPeekView.swift
    let primarySpan = overlappingSpans.first            // popover
    if makesAdClaim, let span = overlappingSpans.first  // spoken label

A transcript row is ~1-3 s wide and spans abut, so a row straddling the join
between two spans overlaps both. After playhead-d666 the interesting case is a
row covered by a SILENCED music-only span and a corroborated one: the row is
painted as an ad because of the corroborated span, and then explains itself with
the music-only one — "Ad segment, 12 seconds, detected from sustained music",
and the same in the popover. Duration and provenance both belong to a span the
app has just decided makes no claim.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN d666. The obvious fix — prefer a CLAIMING span for both
surfaces — can make a music-only span unreachable: the popover is the only way
to open it, and the veto path (`SkipOrchestrator.revertByTimeRange`, the
playhead-u45d window-less branch) needs an overlapping decoded span to exist
before it will record a veto at all. A music-only span every one of whose rows
also carries a claiming span would then have no tap target anywhere. d666
deliberately kept every overlap read intact for exactly that reason.

WHAT TO DECIDE (not decided here): whether the row-level explanation should
(a) prefer the claiming span and accept the reachability loss, (b) offer all
overlapping spans (a list in the popover), or (c) stay as-is. (b) is the only
one that is strictly better on both axes and it is a UI design change.

NOT a regression from d666 and not load-bearing for it: before that branch both
spans were painted as ads, so `.first` picked between two things the app was
equally claiming.

title: hyht's force-quit resume scan has been DEAD in production since it shipped — cnql R1 silently turns it on
description:
FOUND in the playhead-cnql R2 review as O1. Dan's call whether the activation is wanted now.

THE FACT. Before cnql R1, DownloadManager.registerShared had exactly one call site — PlayheadApp.swift:127, inside a SwiftUI .task, which runs AFTER didFinishLaunchingWithOptions. So DownloadManager.shared was nil at didFinishLaunching on EVERY launch, not only headless ones, and playhead-hyht's force-quit scan (PlayheadAppDelegate.swift:99) logged 'scanForSuspendedTransfers skipped — no DownloadManager registered' universally. hyht has therefore never run in production.

WHAT CHANGES. cnql R1 publishes the manager from PlayheadRuntime.init on the launch path, so the scan starts running on every cold launch. That is a behaviour ACTIVATION riding in on a bead about day-0 rediff, which is why it is being surfaced rather than absorbed.

BOUNDED RISK, established by reading it: the scan is report-only (ForceQuitResumeScan.swift:244) — it emits WorkJournal preempted/failed rows and deletes corrupt blobs, and resumes nothing. So the exposure is not data loss. The visible consequence is that the FIRST launch after this ships will emit a burst of paused/resumeInApp Activity rows for however many stale resume blobs have accumulated since the app started shipping with hyht dead.

WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: suppressing it would be un-asked-for scope, and letting it ship silently is how an activation becomes a mystery bug report. Two options for Dan — (a) let it activate and accept one noisy first launch, or (b) gate the first post-upgrade scan so old blobs are reaped quietly.

ALSO FIX WHEN THIS IS TOUCHED: the in-source comment at PlayheadRuntime.swift:3025-3027 says the skip was logged 'on exactly those launches' (headless). That understates it — it was every launch — and the understatement is precisely what would hide this activation from the next reader.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: KILLED 2026-08-11 in the full-backlog triage. DECIDED BY DEFAULT. cnql merged as #367 (ff338693), so option (a) already happened and option (b) can no longer prevent the burst it was written to prevent. The surviving comment fix at PlayheadRuntime.swift:3044 is re-filed as its own P3.

title: Day-0 daily-budget admission estimate is 65 MB/B-copy but measured attempts spend up to 103 MB/copy — the 1 GB cap can be overshot
description:
FOUND in the playhead-cnql R1 review. NOT a cnql regression — cnql is what
makes it REACHABLE, by roughly tripling the number of day-0 attempts per day.

`RediffDayZeroDailyBudget.allows` admits an attempt against
`estimatedAttemptBytes(kWayFetchCount:)` = `kWayFetchCount *
estimatedBytesPerBCopy`, with `estimatedBytesPerBCopy = 65_000_000` and
`RediffActivation.dayZeroKWayFetchCount = 2` — so an attempt is admitted as
costing 130 MB. That is the ONLY pre-flight bound on spend; the cap is
enforced on the estimate, and the ACTUAL spend is folded in afterwards.

MEASURED on db-vtjxverdict (`rediff_day_zero_attempts`, 11 rows, every one
`attemptCount = 1`, so per-row == per-attempt):

  numerator   sum(totalFullFetchBytes) over the 8 rows with lastExit='marked'
              = 1,076,150,061 B
  denominator 8
  mean        134.5 MB per marked attempt   (vs the 130 MB admitted)
  max         206,620,527 B = 206.6 MB      (103.3 MB per B-copy at K=2)
  min         50,172,973 B  = 50.2 MB

So the admission estimate is 3% low at the mean and 37% low at the worst
observation. Seven attempts are admitted before the 8th is denied
(7 x 130 = 910 MB, 8 x 130 = 1,040 MB > 1,000 MB). Seven attempts at the
observed WORST size would spend 1.45 GB against a 1 GB cap — a ~45%
overshoot, on a user's data plan if they have opted into cellular.

WHY IT HAS NOT BITTEN: the same device actually spent 1,125.3 MB over 8.81
days = 128 MB/day, nowhere near the cap. cnql's projection is 383-412 MB/day
(see below), still under. The cap only binds on a subscription batch day,
which is exactly the day the overshoot would be largest.

RE-DERIVED cnql projection, for the record (same pull):
  27 analysis_assets created 2026-08-01 15:12:01 -> 2026-08-10 10:31:18
  = 8.805 days -> 3.07 downloads/day
  x 125.0 MB/fetching-attempt (1,125,288,584 / 9; two `fetch_failed` rows
    spent zero bytes and are excluded from the denominator)
  = 383 MB/day, 38% of the 1 GB rolling-24h cap.
  Using the MARKED-attempt mean of 134.5 MB instead gives 413 MB/day (41%).

NOT FIXED HERE because the remedy is a policy constant, not a defect:
raising `estimatedBytesPerBCopy` to the observed p100 (~105 MB) would make
the cap admit 4 attempts a day instead of 7, which is a product decision
about how many episodes a heavy subscriber gets prepared. Dan's call.
Options, in increasing order of intrusiveness:
  a. raise `estimatedBytesPerBCopy` to ~105 MB (admits 4/day, never overshoots)
  b. keep the estimate but re-check the budget between the K fetches so a
     large attempt cannot complete past the ceiling
  c. leave it, and accept a bounded overshoot on batch days

Related: playhead-4dqe (built the cap), playhead-p70f (the per-asset
backoff), playhead-cnql (tripled the attempt rate).

title: [bug] a permissive-bypass COARSE row's certainty band is runner-fabricated and INDISTINGUISHABLE at rest — usedPermissiveFallback has no column
description:
Found and half-fixed in playhead-92im. The refined half is closed there; this is the coarse half, which needs a schema change and so is its own bead.

THE FABRICATION. `PermissiveAdClassifier.parse` (PermissiveAdClassifier.swift:363-369) returns

    CoarseScreeningSchema(
        disposition: .containsAd,
        support: CoarseSupportSchema(supportLineRefs: supportLineRefs, certainty: .strong)
    )

on the permissive bypass. The `.strong` is HARDCODED by the runner; the model never graded anything. Its sibling `makeAnchorlessSpan` (:128-143) does the same for refinement and says so plainly: "the FM never inferred these classification dimensions, the runner is hardcoding them."

WHY THE REFINED HALF WAS FIXABLE AND THIS IS NOT. `makeAnchorlessSpan` also stamps `ownershipInferenceWasSuppressed: true`, which IS persisted inside `spansJSON` and is already the documented discriminator (`BackfillJobRunner.EncodedRefinedSpan`'s header: Phase-8 sponsor-memory writers MUST skip suppressed spans "because their classification dimensions are not real signals"). `SemanticSweepMarkComposer.certaintyFactor(of:)` now reads it too — measured, 9 of the 11 refined containsAd rows in the 2026-08-10 pull are permissive spans carrying a fabricated `strong`.

The coarse payload has NO such flag. `SemanticScanResult.usedPermissiveFallback` exists on the struct (SemanticScanResult.swift:121) but there is no `usedPermissiveFallback` column in `semantic_scan_results` — confirmed against the pull's schema. A permissive coarse row is therefore byte-identical at rest to one the model actually graded, and no reader can tell them apart.

BLAST RADIUS. Any consumer that reads `spansJSON.certainty` on a passA row is reading a value that may be manufactured:
  * `SemanticSweepMarkComposer.certaintyFactor(of:)` — the mark confidence this bead's parent just built. Over-grades a permissive coarse verdict to the ceiling.
  * playhead-yx0f will make `buildFMLedgerEntries` read the same field, inheriting the same hole.
  * `TrainingExampleMaterializer.certaintyBandToDouble` maps the band to 0.3/0.6/0.9 for the training corpus.

HOW BIG IS IT? UNKNOWN, and that is the point — it is not measurable from the pull for exactly the reason this bead exists. The 40 `strong` / 15 `moderate` split over 55 coarse containsAd rows cannot be decomposed into genuine vs fabricated. (A weak circumstantial signal: `parse` always writes `.strong`, never `.moderate`, so the 15 `moderate` rows are certainly genuine — but the 40 `strong` are a mixture of unknown proportions.)

FIX. Persist `usedPermissiveFallback` (schema migration, additive BOOL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0), thread it through `AnalysisStore.insertSemanticScanResult` / `readSemanticScanResult`, and have the certainty readers treat a permissive row's band as ungraded. Historical rows stay unattributable and must read as ungraded rather than as `strong` — under-claim, per this repo's standing rule.

title: Specialist + pod-continuation marks are CENSORED at exactly 0.70 (the preload floor) — not the 92im constant, but the same gate-shaped pin
description:
Recorded from playhead-92im's establish round, which was asked to decide whether SpecialistMarkComposer and AdPodContinuation share the sweep's defect. THEY DO NOT, and the bead's premise that "three detectors mint a flat 0.70" is true of the sweep only. Correcting the record here so nobody re-derives it.

MEASURED on the 2026-08-10 pull (db-vtjxverdict, ad_windows):
  semantic-sweep-v1     22 rows   0.70 .. 0.70   <- ONE value. This was 92im.
  pod-continuation-v1    7 rows   0.464 .. 0.70  <- a real distribution
  detection-v1          74 rows   0.346 .. 1.0
  userCorrection        12 rows   1.0 .. 1.0

WHAT THE CODE ACTUALLY DOES:
  * SpecialistMarkComposer.swift:66 -- `static let tau = 0.70` is a DECISION THRESHOLD, not a minted value. The emitted confidence is `row.probabilityOfAd`, merged as max (MergedSpan.confidence, line ~226). The population is censored from BELOW at 0.70 because sub-tau rows are dropped, but it varies above it.
  * AdPodContinuation.swift:209 -- `markConfidenceCeiling` is a CAP. The mark INHERITS the strongest seed's presence confidence and is capped: `min(confidence, config.markConfidenceCeiling)` (line ~930). Censored from ABOVE. The pull shows 0.464 / 0.613 / 0.643 / 0.683 x2 / 0.70 x2 -- 5 of 7 below the cap.

SO THE RESIDUAL IS NOT "a constant". It is that both pins are placed AT SkipOrchestrator.preloadConfidenceThreshold for the same stated reason the sweep constant was -- so the mark survives cross-launch preload -- which piles both populations up on exactly the gate value from opposite sides. 2 of 7 pod-continuation rows sit exactly at 0.70 having been capped there from higher seeds; every specialist mark is >= 0.70 by construction.

WORTH ASKING, NOT WORTH GUESSING:
  * Is a seed's presence confidence the right thing for a CONTINUATION to inherit at all? The claim a continuation mark makes is "this is the same pod", which is a different proposition from "this is an ad", and the cap hides how strong the seed actually was.
  * tau == the preload floor means the specialist lane can never express "an ad, but a weak one". Whether that is right depends on the tiering decision that playhead-atr3 settled for actuation and that 92im left open for the sweep.

BLOCKED ON THE SAME DECISION as 92im's stated consequence: what the 0.70 preload floor should do with mark-only rows. Do not move either pin before that is answered.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: KILLED 2026-08-11 in the full-backlog triage. PREMISE SEVERED. Its thesis — both pins sit at the preload floor so the mark survives cross-launch preload — died with ar60 (#363) + atr3: preloadAdmissibleWindows now filters on actuationConfidence, so the DETECTION confidence these composers mint no longer governs preload at all. The bead also self-describes as 'correcting the record here so nobody re-derives it' — a record, not a task. The two now-false source comments are re-filed as their own P3.

title: [bug] three correction-path entry points have ZERO production callers: recordVeto(span:), recordVeto(span:ledgerEntries:), and all of BroadCorrectionEvaluator
description:
NOTICED WHILE FIXING playhead-q6y3 (its scope 3 asked me to verify the second writer's callers). Filed, not fixed — deleting or wiring live code is a decision, not a cleanup.

MEASURED, on 0ad56882:

1. PersistentUserCorrectionStore.recordVeto(span:) — UserCorrectionStore.swift:810. playhead-ar60 R2 already established this has no production callers. Confirmed: every reference is PlayheadTests (UserCorrectionReadSideTests, SpliceSlotOwnershipCorrectionTests, CorrectionAttributionTests) or a test double (AsyncTestSignals, SkipOrchestratorRevertTests).

2. PersistentUserCorrectionStore.recordVeto(span:ledgerEntries:) — UserCorrectionStore.swift:815. NEW finding, extending ar60 R2 to the ledger variant. Its only non-test mention in Playhead/ is a COMMENT in AdDetectionService.swift:8856 that names it as a second writer of sponsorOnShow + .falsePositive. That comment is load-bearing prose in ar60's justification for the hasSpanScopedSuppressor arm, and it describes a path nothing calls.

3. BroadCorrectionEvaluator — shouldPromote and shouldActAloneSuppress (BroadCorrectionEvaluator.swift). ZERO production callers; every reference is BroadCorrectionEvaluatorTests. This is the whole Layer-B promotion evaluator, including the playhead-xsdz.34 'act-alone suppress' authority that was designed with explicit guardrails and Dan-included reasoning. It is a fully-tested pure evaluator that nothing consults.

WHY IT MATTERS. Not because dead code is untidy — because it is being CITED. q6y3's own investigation had to establish that (2) is the remaining show-wide .falsePositive writer in order to justify leaving it alone, and the honest answer is that it writes nothing today. A reviewer reading AdDetectionService:8856 will believe the pipeline has two show-wide veto writers when it has none reachable from the UI. Same for BroadCorrectionScope's per-scope thresholds (sponsorOnShow: 2 corrections, 2 distinct episodes, 180-day decay) which read like live policy.

DECISION NEEDED: for each of the three, either wire it to the gesture it was written for, or delete it and the prose that cites it. Do NOT do this as a silent cleanup — (3) in particular encodes a Dan-included design decision, and deleting it discards that record.

Related: playhead-q6y3, playhead-ar60 (R2), playhead-xsdz.34.

title: V47 side effect: the 0.7 cross-launch preload floor now admits fusion rows it used to exclude
description:
FILED FROM playhead-ar60 R1 REVIEW — not fixed there, because it is a reach/skip-eagerness call, not a defect in the bead's own change.

ar60 deliberately left `SkipOrchestrator.preloadAdmissibleWindows`'s 0.7 floor reading `AdWindow.confidence`, on the grounds that playhead-ynmk's own comment calls it "a DETECTOR-confidence filter". That is defensible on its own terms and I did not change it. But it is not behaviour-preserving for FUSION rows, and the bead comment does not name the direction.

WHAT CHANGED. Before V47 a fusion row's `confidence` WAS its actuation number, so the floor compared 0.7 against actuation. Since V47 `confidence` is detection, which for a corrected or calibration-discounted span is HIGHER. So more fusion rows are admitted to the cross-launch preload.

THE BAND, exactly. `preloadConfidenceThreshold` is 0.7 and `SkipPolicyConfig.default.enterThreshold` is 0.65. A row with

  * detection >= 0.70, and
  * actuation in [0.65, 0.70), and
  * `eligibilityGate == .eligible`, and
  * `decisionState` in {candidate, confirmed, applied}

was NOT preloaded before (actuation < 0.7) and so could not auto-skip on relaunch. It is preloaded now, and `evaluateWindow` — which ar60 correctly rerouted to `actuationConfidence` — sees >= 0.65 and skips.

WHY IT MAY BE FINE. In-session the same span already auto-skips: `receiveAdDecisionResults` carries `AdDecisionResult.skipConfidence` (the actuation number) and the same 0.65 enter threshold. So the pre-V47 cross-launch path was accidentally MORE conservative than the in-session path for fusion rows only, and V47 unified them. Reading actuation at the floor instead would re-open the opposite question, since ar60's own headline finding was that five spans crossed this floor on correction INFLATION alone (per-span scoping already removes most of that).

WHY IT IS WORTH A DECISION ANYWAY. It is a widening in the auto-skip direction on Dan's device, and the standing rule is that eating show costs more than missing an ad. The choice is one line in `preloadAdmissibleWindows`; what it needs is a call on which quantity that floor is FOR, made once and written down, not another reader-by-reader judgement.

Adjacent to playhead-4obf (the deferred fusion emission floor) — both are about which population reaches the user, and they should probably be decided together.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
DAN'S DECISION 2026-08-09: READ ACTUATION. Principle he gave: 'the highest quality signal we have is a user correction' — reading raw detection where a corrected number exists discards the best evidence.

REFRAMING THAT CHANGES THE OWNER: pre-ar60 ad_windows.confidence HELD the actuation number, so this floor ALREADY read actuation. ar60's column split silently switched it to raw detection. This is therefore not a new enhancement — it is an UNINTENDED BEHAVIOUR CHANGE INTRODUCED BY ar60, in the direction Dan has now rejected. Fix belongs IN ar60 (restoring the pre-existing, now-endorsed semantics), not in a follow-up, even though that costs ar60 a review round.

WHY IT IS SAFE NOW (and was not before): the reason detection looked defensible is ar60's own measurement — an ASSET-WIDE blanket where 5 spans crossed 0.7 on inflation from marks that did NOT overlap them. That was one good signal smeared onto the wrong spans, not noisy corrections. ar60's per-span CorrectionFactorSnapshot fixes the scope, so actuation is now detection informed by corrections only where they actually apply. FIX THE SCOPE, THEN TRUST THE NUMBER.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES for whoever takes it:
- preloadAdmissibleWindows (SkipOrchestrator.swift ~:2219) currently filters $0.confidence >= preloadConfidenceThreshold; change to the actuation read. Keep the '|| $0.userAssertion != nil' bypass — it is the same principle already encoded (qs0d) and must not regress.
- Dan considered and did NOT take 'bound the boost' — no second threshold. But ar60 measured that reinforcing corrections crossing 0.7 is a real effect, so add a rail that a reinforcement cannot lift a span over the floor without an overlapping correction.
- Needs a test that would FAIL on the raw-detection read (delete-the-call-site discipline): a span whose detection is under 0.7 but whose overlapping user correction lifts actuation over it must preload, and the converse.
- Interacts with q6y3: an INVERTED correction direction is far more damaging once the floor trusts corrections. q6y3 is Dan-ruled (the button must mean reinforcement) but not yet fixed — note the dependency, do not block on it.

title: [bug] fusion emission has no confidence floor: a sub-threshold detection still ships as a user-visible confirmed row
description:
Split out of playhead-ar60, which fixed the OTHER two thirds of the emission chain (the detection/actuation column split, and detectOnly no longer persisting `confirmed` for a span the user vetoed) but deliberately did NOT take a general emission floor, because that is a RECALL decision and recall is the dominant term in this program.

THE GAP. `rawPolicyAction` in `AdDetectionService.runBackfill` is hardcoded to `SkipPolicyMatrix.action(for: .unknown, ownership: .unknown)` = `.detectOnly`, so every fusion span that is not promoted to autoSkipEligible takes the detectOnly arm of `AdDetectionService.fusionDecisionState`. After ar60 that arm is `.suppressed` when the gate is `blockedByUserCorrection` and `.confirmed` otherwise — with NO reference to how strong the detection actually was. There is no floor anywhere on the fusion emission path.

MEASURED, 2026-08-02 device pull (n = 40 fusion rows in `ad_windows`; the numbers below are the recovered `decision_events.proposalConfidence`, i.e. the DETECTION number, not the actuation number the column used to hold):

    proposalConfidence   rows
    < 0.40                13
    0.40 - 0.55            8
    0.55 - 0.80           11
    >= 0.80                8

So THIRTEEN of forty persisted fusion rows — 32.5% — carry a detection confidence below the hot path's own 0.40 candidate threshold, and every one of them that is not user-vetoed persists `decisionState = confirmed`. On the evening pull the same count is 13 of 48.

WHY IT IS NOT OBVIOUS WHAT TO DO. Two floors already exist downstream and disagree about the population:
  * `SkipOrchestrator.preloadConfidenceThreshold` = 0.7 (cross-launch cue continuity)
  * `AnalysisJobRunner.cueConfidenceThreshold` = 0.7 and the cross-user `cueConfidenceThreshold` = 0.7
  * the hot path's own candidateThreshold = 0.40
A fusion floor at 0.40 would drop 13/40 rows; at 0.70 it would drop 32/40. Against that: Dan's standing position is that the banner is a SKIP AFFORDANCE (feedback_banner_is_a_skip_affordance_2026-07-31) and that reach is the bottleneck (project_coverage_program_closed_2026-07-30: ZERO of 34 episodes at 95% scan). Suppressing a third of the emitted population is a reach decision, not a hygiene one.

THE QUESTION TO ANSWER FIRST, with data rather than a threshold argument: of the sub-0.40 fusion rows in the corpus, what fraction were CORRECT? The pull has Dan's `correction_events` as ground truth for the episodes he listened to. On DE0784D8 specifically all five fusion rows were false positives — but N=5 on one episode decides nothing.

NOT IN SCOPE HERE: the actuation number. After ar60 `ad_windows.skipConfidence` carries it separately, so a floor can be stated over DETECTION (is this an ad?) or ACTUATION (may we act?) and mean two different things — which is exactly the distinction ar60 existed to restore. Say which one before picking a number.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
DAN'S DECISION 2026-08-10: NO FLOOR — INSTRUMENT FIRST. The bead is re-scoped from 'pick a threshold' to 'build the measurement that makes a threshold decidable'.

WHY, from the orchestrator's re-derivation against db-marked (not quoted from the bead):
- 40 fusion rows; 13 below 0.40 detection (32.5%), 17 in 0.40-0.70, 10 at >=0.70.
- Only 13 of 40 fusion rows sit on an asset carrying ANY correction_events at all.
- Of the 13 sub-0.40 rows, only 4 sit on a judged asset. THREE of those four are on D9B513CD, whose corrections are ALL falseNegative (Dan marked MISSES there and vetoed nothing), so they were never contradicted. The fourth is DE0784D8 4800.5 (det 0.3789), the j4wi episode where all five fusion rows were false positives.
- So the bead's own question — 'what fraction of sub-0.40 rows were CORRECT?' — is UNANSWERABLE today: N=4, split roughly 3 not-contradicted vs 1 wrong, and 9 of 13 have no verdict of any kind. That is the finding.

WHAT LOWERS THE STAKES (both verified):
- These rows BANNER ONLY. rawPolicyAction is hardcoded to detectOnly, so a sub-0.40 fusion row is never autoSkipEligible; the cost of a wrong one is a banner Dan ignores, not lost show.
- They are ALREADY out of cross-launch continuity: per Dan's atr3 decision the 0.7 preload floor now reads ACTUATION, and these sit far below it on either quantity.

Against that: reach is the dominant term (ZERO of 34 episodes at 95% scan; 61% of ad slots have ZERO overlap), and the banner is a SKIP AFFORDANCE. Suppressing a third of the emitted population on N=4 would trade measurable recall for unmeasured tidiness.

NEW SCOPE — build the measurement, do not set a number:
1. Persist, per emitted fusion row, enough to later ask 'was this correct?' without re-deriving from decision_events: the detection number, the actuation number, and whether the row was subsequently overlapped by a falsePositive or falseNegative correction. ar60 already split the two confidences; this is the verdict join made durable and queryable.
2. Report it as a distribution over BANDS (the bead's four bands are the right shape), so the answer arrives as 'of rows in band X, N were vetoed / M were confirmed / K unjudged' rather than as an anecdote.
3. Explicitly count the UNJUDGED population — it is 9 of 13 today, and any future threshold argument that ignores it is the standing defect class (a ratio whose denominator nobody validated).
4. Do NOT add a floor, a threshold constant, or a suppression path in this bead. When the data exists, the threshold decision comes back to Dan, and it must state DETECTION or ACTUATION explicitly (ar60 exists to keep those distinct).

Ordering: unblocked, but lower priority than q6y3 (P0, promoted) and the rest of Queue 5. Its value is compounding — the sooner it records, the sooner the next episodes Dan judges become evidence.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
NEW GROUND TRUTH 2026-08-10 (db-corrected2): Dan judged a third episode, 48E903D7. This is exactly the evidence this bead's re-scope exists to accumulate.

  0.0-60.1     dayZeroRediffByteExact  conf 1.00  applied   -> NOT corrected = CORRECT (auto-skipped)
  596.3-676.6  semantic-sweep-v1       conf 0.70  reverted  -> VETOED = false positive (80.3s of show)
  2052.9-2112.9 userCorrection         conf 1.00  applied   -> DAN MARKED IT; the pipeline MISSED the post-roll
  2044.5-2048.8 (4.3s)                 no ad_windows row, no scan window overlaps 2040-2050 -> vetoed something not represented as a window; UNEXPLAINED, ask Dan

Corpus totals now: 30 correction_events across 6 assets (was 27 across 5).

WHAT IT ADDS TO THIS BEAD'S QUESTION: still nothing about the sub-0.40 fusion population — the only wrong row here is a sweep mark at 0.70, i.e. ABOVE every floor under discussion. A 0.40 detection floor would not have prevented it, and neither would a 0.70 one (it sits exactly AT 0.70). That is a second reason the emission-floor framing is the wrong lever: the measured false positives on judged episodes keep coming from a detector whose confidence is a CONSTANT (see the new playhead-92im, 22/22 rows at exactly 0.70), not from weak fusion detections.

ALSO NOTE for the instrumentation this bead now owns: the miss here (post-roll, 60s) is invisible to any floor — the pipeline emitted nothing at all there. Any 'was this correct?' report must count MISSES (falseNegative corrections with no overlapping window) alongside vetoes, or it will measure only precision and call it quality.

title: The coarse-scan / final-pass show-identity resolver is installed only from the WindowGroup .task — a sceneless background launch has no recovery source
description:
Found by the adversarial review of playhead-vtjx. NOT fixed there: the remedy is an app-bootstrap change (moving an install out of a SwiftUI WindowGroup .task), which is an architectural call rather than a bead-scoped one.

PlayheadApp.swift:215 (single resolver) and :239 (batch resolver) are the ONLY writers of PlayheadRuntime.episodePodcastIdResolverBox / episodePodcastIdBatchResolverBox, and both sit inside a WindowGroup content .task (PlayheadApp.swift:123), which fires only when the scene appears.

But PlayheadRuntime.init calls backgroundProcessingService.registerBackgroundTasks() at PlayheadRuntime.swift:2999 — in init, not start() — so the BGTask handler is live on a launch with no scene, and BackgroundProcessingService.swift:1551 says so in its own words: 'on a sceneless background launch the loop does not exist until this handler creates it'. That handler (:1557) is the sole caller of AnalysisCoordinator.runPendingCoarseScans.

CONSEQUENCE in that process: the box is nil, so playhead-vtjx's episode-store recovery cannot run and an unattributed episode is refused scan_claim:podcast_id_missing exactly as before. The same applies to the SHIPPED final-pass launch sweep, which polls the same box via awaitEpisodePodcastIdResolver and proceeds with nil on timeout — so FinalPassJob.podcastId is null on those launches too. This predates vtjx.

WHY IT IS A DELAY AND NOT A HOLE (and therefore P2): vtjx writes the recovered identity back into analysis_jobs.podcastId, so the recovery is needed at most ONCE PER EPISODE. The first grant that does have a scene repairs the lane permanently, and every later launch — sceneless or not — reads it from AnalysisStore.fetchRecordedPodcastId with no resolver involved. AnalysisCoordinator logs 'coarse_scan_show_identity_unknown … resolverInstalled=false', which is what distinguishes 'nobody knows this show' from 'nobody could ask' on a device pull.

NOT DECIDABLE FROM THE 2026-08-08 PULL: background_task_runs.scenePhase is a snapshot of UIApplication.applicationState (BackgroundTaskRunLedger.swift:173), which reads 'background' for both a backgrounded scene and a sceneless launch. All five podcast_id_missing refusals (11:00:32-11:31:06) fall inside scenePhase=background grants, so we cannot tell which they were. Worth adding a launch-mode field to that ledger.

PROPOSED FIX (Dan's call): hoist both setEpisodePodcastId*Resolver installs to a scene-independent launch hook — PlayheadApp.init() right after modelContainer is assigned, or PlayheadAppDelegate.application(_:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:), which already runs on every launch. Keep the .task install as an idempotent second write. The closures capture only modelContainer, which exists at both points. Note the @State-access-in-init caveat if PlayheadApp.init() is chosen.

title: Final-pass re-transcription is unreachable for late-arriving ad windows: EOF watermark resume guard + 0.5 floor over a skipConfidence-storing column exclude every post-batch candidate and user mark
description:
FOUND during playhead-j4wi R1 review, walking the 2026-08-02 device pull for asset DE0784D8-BE2F-4BEB-8BA1-3D9EF51AD659.

WITNESS (device pull): final_pass_jobs holds ONE enqueue batch, createdAt 2026-07-31 23:58:59 UTC, 7 windows, all complete; finalPassCoverageEndTime = 5522.6775510123671 (EOF, from the post-roll job). Four backfill runs follow (decision_events 00:42 / 15:24-15:26 / 06:11 / 06:43 UTC 08-01..08-02) creating the 5 fusion windows and, later, Dan's two userMarked pod windows (2838.18-2897.94, 2898.66-2953.68, confidence 1.0). ZERO new final_pass_jobs rows ever appear, and zero pass='final' chunks intersect 2820-2962.

MECHANISM (FinalPassRetranscriptionRunner.swift, eligibleWindows filter ~:303): a window is eligible only if (a) confidence >= 0.5 (defaultConfidenceFloor, :140) AND (b) endTime > watermark (resume guard). Once the initial batch's post-roll job drives the watermark to EOF, (b) is false for EVERY window whose endTime is inside the episode - permanently. The watermark models monotonic forward progress, but candidates arrive out of order (fusion backfill and user marks both post-date the launch batch here by 1-16 h). Additionally (a) reads ad_windows.confidence, which for fusion windows stores DecisionResult.skipConfidence (0.001-0.004 on this asset) - the playhead-ar60 family - so fusion candidates are doubly excluded even before the watermark.

CONSEQUENCE: 'final re-transcription is candidate-local' is only true for candidates that exist at the first drain. A candidate or user mark arriving after the watermark passes it can never get final-pass audio, so any consumer of pass='final' quality inside those spans (metadata extraction, mixed-pass display) silently runs on fast-pass text forever.

NOT re-filing ar60 (the column semantics) - this bead is the WATERMARK ordering gap; the floor interaction is cited as a compounding factor. Related: playhead-h7pr (pass mis-tagging) touches the same table's meaning but a different writer.

title: CorpusAnnotationLoader's default repoRoot reads the CALLER's #filePath through a walk-up written for its OWN path — callers not exactly 4 directories deep resolve outside the repo
description: Found by playhead-j4wi's regression suite. CorpusAnnotationLoader.init (PlayheadTests/Fixtures/Corpus/L2F/CorpusAnnotationLoader.swift:185-207) takes 'filePath: String = #filePath' and walks up FIVE fixed components, documented against the loader's own location ('PlayheadTests/Fixtures/Corpus/L2F/... ^ this file'). But a #filePath DEFAULT ARGUMENT expands at the CALL SITE, so the walk-up count is applied to whichever file constructs the loader. Every pre-existing caller happens to live exactly 4 directories deep (FusionLift ABs, NarlEval, the L2F tests), so it never fired; the first 3-deep caller (PlayheadTests/Services/AdDetection/DE0784D8MidRollPodRegressionTests.swift) resolved repoRoot to /Users/dabrams/playhead/.worktrees — one level ABOVE the worktree — and threw directoryNotFound. Witness: j4wi verification run 2026-08-07 23:44, 'Annotations directory not found at /Users/dabrams/playhead/.worktrees/TestFixtures/Corpus/Annotations'. A 5-deep caller would be worse: it would silently resolve to PlayheadTests/ (or, from a nested worktree layout, another checkout's TestFixtures) and read the WRONG corpus without any error. Same defect class as mfeq: a value documented as 'this file's path' actually carries the caller's. Fix direction: capture the loader's own #filePath in a static/file-scope constant instead of a defaulted parameter, or walk UP until a directory containing TestFixtures/Corpus/Annotations is found. j4wi's call site works around it by passing repoRoot explicitly.

title: AdDetectionService.episodeDuration is one actor-global scalar shared by every concurrent runBackfill entry — a second driver's write is read by the first driver's in-flight scan
description: PRE-EXISTING surface, wider after playhead-13kf. runBackfill (AdDetectionService.swift:4133, also 3483/3744) writes self.episodeDuration (line 2040, 'position-based scoring') on entry; readers (e.g. 9474-9479 acoustic-break range, position scoring sites) read it across actor awaits. Direct Stage-4 callers already coexist outside the scheduler's single-flight loop: AnalysisCoordinator finalize (2573), FinalPassRetranscriptionRunner (653), AnalysisJobRunner (972); playhead-13kf's runPendingCoarseScans adds a fourth (AnalysisCoordinator.coarseScanOneAsset), and it can pass 0 (episodeDurationSec absent pre-gtt9.1.1). Interleaving: driver A (asset X, dur 3600) suspends mid-run; driver B (asset Y, dur 0) enters and stamps 0; A resumes and position-scores/windows against 0. wxsv's markBackfillJobRunning CAS protects the ROW stamp, not this scalar; rkfp bounds FM time, not this. hygc.1.8's per-asset in-flight tracker shows the repo already handles this class for runHotPathResult. Remedy shape: thread episodeDuration as a parameter through the phase (the 2951 comment already does this deliberately for one path) instead of actor state.

title: A reclaimed grant's cancellation is swallowed inside runBackfill: runShadowFMPhase's catch-all eats CancellationError, so Stage 4 finishes its non-FM stages on a dead grant
description: AdDetectionService.runShadowFMPhase wraps runner.runPendingBackfill in a do/catch that treats EVERY error as 'Shadow FM phase failed (suppressed by invariant)' — including CancellationError. Under playhead-13kf the FM phase runs at the front of every granted background window and the OS expiry cancels the work task; the cancellation thrown out of the runner's per-job Task.checkCancellation is swallowed, so runBackfill proceeds through region proposal, feature extraction and fusion for the current asset on a grant that no longer exists. The 13kf coarse-scan loop exits at its next between-asset check (isTaskCancelled / catch is CancellationError), so the leak is bounded to one asset's post-FM stages, but those stages are exactly the work the expirationSettleGrace (3 s) budget assumes is NOT running. Fix shape: rethrow CancellationError from the shadow-phase catch (and audit the sibling catch in materializeTrainingExamples). Found during playhead-13kf establishment; out of that bead's ceiling.

title: Reach: transcript_chunks carries no write timestamp, so the drain's smallest durable artifact is unpriceable — the 13kf drain floor (0) cannot be re-derived upward without one
description: playhead-13kf resolved the lmrx F6 floor by deriving the backfill drain floor to ZERO, because the ledger cannot price a transcription pass's first durable artifact: transcript_chunks has no createdAt, and 96 of 115 measured transcription attempts (work_journal stage=analysisJobRunner.run.transcriptionTimeout, 2026-08-06 pull db-new-t2h) persisted zero chunks at any length (playhead-i2am). If a future bead wants a nonzero drain floor, the enabling measurement is a per-chunk (or per-batch) write timestamp: numerator = wall clock from dispatch to FIRST persisted chunk, denominator = dispatched transcription passes that persisted at least one chunk. Adding the column is V-schema work; do not derive the floor from anything less direct.

comments.text: REPRIORITIZED -> P2 in the 2026-08-11 triage.

title: backfill + backfill.charged BGTasks fire simultaneously every wake — 71 identical-instant pairs in the 2026-08-06 pull; establish whether both run a concurrent drain
description: From background_task_runs in the 2026-08-06 pull (db-new-t2h): every backfill wake records TWO rows with identical startedAt (to ~50 microseconds), identical finishedAt, distinct taskInstanceIDs — 71 pairs (numerator: startedAt values with >1 backfill row; denominator: distinct backfill wake instants). playhead-i6oi registers com.playhead.app.analysis.backfill and .backfill.charged with the SAME handler (BackgroundProcessingService.registerTaskIdentifiers, ~772-785), and iOS evidently launches both together when both constraint sets are satisfiable (overnight on charger). title: passB refinement rows do not carry the V45 wait-vs-infer split (suspendingLatencyMs / daemonPeersAtStart NULL)
description: playhead-rkfp threaded the same-span suspending-clock twin and the daemon census reading through the passA window paths only, because all 30 of the 30 over-30s rows in the 2026-08-06 pull are passA (numerator: rows with latencyMs>30000; denominator: rows with latencyMs>0, n=141). passB rows write NULL for both columns — honest 'not measured', never 0 — via the defaulted params on SemanticScanResult/makeRefinementScanResult. Threading mirrors passA: FMRefinementWindowOutput + the refinement failure sites in FoundationModelClassifier (windowStart at ~3684) get an FMClockPair + census read, and BackfillJobRunner's makeRefinementScanResult/makeRefinementFailureScanResult pass them through. Also NOT threaded inside passA, same honest-NULL contract: shrink-split retry outputs (runCoarseRetry / runCoarseSmartShrinkLoop measure their own sub-spans, so a whole-attempt twin would let suspending exceed continuous), subdividedCoarseOutput, and recoverCoarseWindowPermissively failures.

title: countResumableBackfillJobs cannot see a row re-opened below the newest enqueue batch
description:
Found by adversarial review of playhead-wxsv, 2026-08-07. Filed rather than fixed: the fix belongs to playhead-9ocm / the onn6 query, which wxsv was scoped out of.

## The shape

`AnalysisStore.countResumableBackfillJobs(assetId:)` scopes to a 0.5 s window below an UNFILTERED `MAX(createdAt)`. wxsv's `reopenBackfillJob` deliberately does NOT move `createdAt` — that is spec item 3, and it is what stops a re-opened row from evicting its own siblings from the window. The cost of that correctness is at the other end: a row re-opened in an OLDER batch is itself below the window, so the count cannot see it.

## The reachable sequence

1. Asset gets a `fullCoverage` plan: one `fullEpisodeScan` row, `createdAt = T0`.
2. `CoveragePlanner` flips to `targetedWithAudit` (the store's own doc names this flip as a live orphan producer). Three rows at `createdAt = T1`.
3. The plan comes back to `fullCoverage`/`periodicFullRescan` AND the transcript version has moved. `redrivableRow` re-opens the T0 row, keeping `createdAt = T0`.
4. `MAX(createdAt)` is T1. The re-opened row is outside the 0.5 s window, so `countResumableBackfillJobs` does not count it. If the T1 rows are all `complete`, the count is 0 and `AnalysisWorkScheduler.shouldMintAdScanRedrive` shuts.

## Severity: real but narrow

The invocation that re-opened the row also ENQUEUES it, so the work is not lost — it is drained by that same pass. What is lost is the later onn6 re-drive if that pass defers. Pre-wxsv this case minted a NEW row at `createdAt = now`, always inside the newest batch, always counted — so this is a narrow regression in reach, traded for not evicting siblings (which was the spec item).

`reopenDoesNotEvictTheBatch` (AdScanRedriveTests) covers the single-batch direction, which was already the safe one. The multi-batch direction is uncovered.

## Why not fixed in wxsv

The honest fix is to make the count ask the question the batch window is a PROXY for — "would a future `runPendingBackfill` enqueue this row?" — which means knowing which ids the current plan derives. That is a redesign of `countResumableBackfillJobs`, i.e. playhead-9ocm territory, and wxsv was explicitly scoped out of it. Moving `createdAt` on re-open is NOT an acceptable shortcut: it is what rail WX02 exists to catch.

Cheapest plausible fix: a `reopenedAt` column, and count `createdAt >= MAX - window OR reopenedAt >= MAX - window`. Note that is a second timestamp with its own meaning, so it needs the same "what would this read if the thing never happened?" scrutiny — NULL until a re-open, never defaulted to `createdAt`.

title: the coverage-lane drain LIVELOCKS if a liveness heartbeat can transition a row (found by mutant WX13)
description:
Found by playhead-wxsv's own mutation rail, 2026-08-07. NOT a shipped defect — the shipped code is correct. This is about a hazard the code is one edit away from, and about a rail that cannot currently be scored.

## What was measured

Rail WX13 mutates `AnalysisStore.touchBackfillJobLiveness` from

    UPDATE backfill_jobs SET updatedAt = ... WHERE jobId = ? AND status = 'running'

to a full start transition

    UPDATE backfill_jobs SET status = 'running', updatedAt = ... WHERE jobId = ? AND status <> 'complete'

Expected: `heartbeatCannotStartARow` goes red. Observed: the focused suites SPIN. Sim-side `Playhead.app/Playhead` at 699% CPU, 100 minutes of CPU time, log completely static. Every other WX batch finishes in ~2.5 minutes.

Isolation (batches split, re-run):
  WX12 alone -> KILLED, 2m03s
  WX13 alone -> still spinning at 420 s, killed by `timeout`

## Why it matters

A mutant that HANGS instead of failing is unscoreable — neither KILLED nor SURVIVED — so WX13 is currently carried as a rail with no verdict. More importantly, the hang says the hazard is worse than the rail claims: a heartbeat that can transition a row does not merely mislabel state, it lets some drain in the focused set re-admit work it has already retired, without bound. That is a livelock reachable from a one-token edit to a method four call sites use.

`heartbeatCannotStartARow` (BackfillJobStoreTests) is the behavioural witness and it passes. What is NOT established is that it is what fails FIRST under the mutant — the spin gets there before any assertion does.

## What to do

1. Find the spinning suite. Run WX13 with a narrowed `FOCUSED_SUITES` (bisect the ~150 suites) — the spin should localize to whichever drain re-admits. The candidates are the ones that loop over admission: `BackfillJobRunnerTests` (`noProgressRunnerCyclesStayBounded` runs 30 cycles), `BackfillCoarseCheckpointTests`, `DrainEligibleStartGateTests`.
2. Decide whether that drain deserves a bound of its own. A production loop that cannot terminate when a row keeps re-entering `running` is a real robustness gap even though nothing writes that state today.
3. Then either score WX13 against a bounded suite, or scope it to a store-only focused set.

## Related

playhead-ehz2 (the battery's baseline is unattainable) is a different problem — that one is starvation in the baseline, this one is a mutant that does not terminate.
