Not a downgrade of the finding — the queue-6 evidence establishes COMPLETION as the binding constraint (zero backfill_jobs have ever reached complete across 33 assets; FM evidence on 2 of 33). P1 is reserved for that path until it moves.

title: a transcript version change that REPLACES text rather than extending it should not inherit the cursor
description:
Fallout named by playhead-wxsv, deliberately NOT fixed there.

wxsv made a growing transcript CONTINUE its ad scan: `backfill_jobs.jobId` is
`f(assetId, phase, offset)`, the transcript version is a column
(`attemptTranscriptVersion`), and a terminal row whose stamp is stale is
re-opened by `AnalysisStore.reopenBackfillJob` KEEPING its `progressCursor`.
`BackfillJobRunner.narrowedForResume` then drops every segment ending at or
below the cursor.

That is right for GROWTH — more text over the same audio — which is the case
measured on the 2026-08-07 pull (one stale row per transcript version, exactly;
`CDD611C4` with four abandoned full-episode scans). It is WRONG for a
REPLACEMENT: same span, different text. The obvious producer is
`FinalPassRetranscriptionRunner` — final-pass chunks REPLACE the fast coverage
they overlap, so the text over [0, x] genuinely improves without x moving. A
re-opened row inherits a cursor at x, `narrowedForResume` empties the plan
list, and the job completes on a `phaseProducedNoAnchors` sentinel having read
nothing. Pre-wxsv this case got a full rescan, by accident (a new version =
a new jobId = a nil cursor) — the same accident that orphaned the old row.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN wxsv:

1. It is not reachable at HEAD. `AnalysisCoordinator.finalizeBackfill` calls
   `runBackfill` exactly once per session; no caller re-invokes the runner under
   a new transcriptVersion WITHIN a session. The R4-Fix6 comment at
   `BackfillJobRunner.swift` says the same thing ("defensive for a Phase 4
   re-trigger path that does not yet exist in production"). Every version change
   the field data shows is BETWEEN sessions, i.e. growth.
2. The cheap discriminator is type-unsound. "Did the transcript grow?" wants
   `newPlanListEnd > cursor`, but the cursor is an `EpisodeSeconds` and the plan
   list end is a `PlanListSeconds` — playhead-x0lb typed those apart precisely
   so they cannot be compared, and reaching for
   `EpisodeSeconds.unsoundPlanListPromotion` to do it would be the defect class
   the type exists to catch.

WHAT A FIX PROBABLY LOOKS LIKE: record, alongside the cursor, WHICH POPULATION
it was made over — e.g. the transcript's own covered span at the time — so
"extension" and "replacement" are distinguishable without comparing two
quantities that merely share a unit. Or: have the replacement WRITER (the final
pass) invalidate the cursor explicitly, since it is the only code that knows a
replacement happened; that avoids inventing a discriminator at all and is
probably the smaller change.

REACH IMPACT IF WRONG: one episode's fast-pass-only span never gets rescanned
against its better final-pass text. Bounded, and only once the Phase 4 re-trigger
path exists.

title: an adoption claim reads as .alreadySatisfied to SemanticScanClaim.record, so a closed FM gate leaves no durable claim
description:
playhead-7x1s / playhead-y8a3 R4 adversarial review, finding F1. FILED, not fixed —
the repair is cross-mechanism and belongs with the playhead-upm1 / playhead-9ocm /
playhead-t9nv unification, not inside 7x1s.

## The value that names one thing and is read as another

`BackfillJobRunner.adoptionClaim` (BackfillJobRunner.swift:5200) writes a row at
`id(asset, transcriptVersion, .fullEpisodeScan, 0)` with `status = .complete`. Its
documented meaning is narrow and correct: *no new row is owed at this id*.

`SemanticScanClaim.jobId(analysisAssetId:transcriptVersion:)`
(SemanticScanClaim.swift:373-380) derives THE SAME id — deliberately, so a claim
minted outside the runner is the row the runner later re-drives
(`makeJobIdForTesting` doc, BackfillJobRunner.swift:4861-4864).

`SemanticScanClaim.record` (SemanticScanClaim.swift:497-503):

    guard isOwed(adScanFraction: fraction) else { return .notOwed }
    if let existing = try await store.fetchBackfillJob(byId: jobId) {
        switch existing.status {
        case .complete:
            return .alreadySatisfied

`.alreadySatisfied`'s own doc reads: *\"A `complete` row already exists for this
asset+transcriptVersion — the scan this claim would request has already run.\"*
For an adoption claim **no scan has run at all**. Ask the standing diagnostic —
what would this value read if the scan had never happened? — and the answer is
the same. Note the internal contradiction one line up: `isOwed` has just measured
the asset BELOW the sufficiency floor, and the next statement concludes the scan
is satisfied. For a genuinely completed pass that pair is legitimate (it ran and
still fell short); for a claim it is not.

Introduced by this branch: before it, only a pass that really ran could put a
`complete` row at that id.

## Consequence, stated exactly rather than loosely

Nothing branches on `Outcome` in production (`@discardableResult`, tests only), so
the mislabel costs nothing by itself. What it costs is the WRITE that does not
happen: `record` returns without minting the durable `scan_claim:` row that
playhead-fil5 exists to leave.

In the common case no reach is lost — the claim's carrier IS a resumable
coverage-lane row, so `countResumableBackfillJobs` still reads >= 1 and onn6's
re-drive gate stays open. (The claim itself is `complete`, so it is not counted,
and it borrows the carrier's `createdAt`, so it does not evict the carrier from
the 0.5 s batch window.)

The hole is the conjunction:

  * the claim's carrier has reached `retryCount >= AdmissionController.maxRetries`
    (excluded by `countResumableBackfillJobs` AND by
    `fetchAssetIdsWithResumableBackfillJobs`), and
  * an FM gate closes for that asset at the SAME transcript version
    (`fmModeOff`, `foundationModelsUnavailable` — which
    `FoundationModelsUsabilityProbe` caches false for 15 min — or
    `podcastIdMissing`).

Then: count = 0, so onn6's `shouldMintAdScanRedrive` gate is shut;
`fetchAssetIdsMissingCoverageLaneJobs` skips the asset because it DOES own rows;
and `record` writes nothing. Pre-branch the same situation left id(V) empty, so
`record` minted a `deferred` / `retryCount 0` row that reopened the gate.

The escape that remains is the runner's own revival path
(BackfillJobRunner.swift:840-848): the next ordinary `runPendingBackfill` at that
version sees the expired claim and replaces it with work. That is why this is P2
and not P1 — but it is precisely the path a closed FM gate suppresses.

## Fix directions (pick one, do not do both)

1. `SemanticScanClaim.record` asks `existing.isAdoptionClaim` before concluding
   `.alreadySatisfied`, and treats a claim as \"a row exists, someone else carries
   it\" — a new `Outcome` case rather than a refresh, because refreshing would
   overwrite `deferReason` and destroy the carrier pointer the revival path reads.
2. Or unify the predicate: make `countResumableBackfillJobs` count what
   `fetchUnfinishedBackfillJob` would return (the same unification playhead-upm1
   and playhead-9ocm already own), so an expired claim can never take the count
   to zero and `record`'s answer stops mattering.
close_reason: duplicate of playhead-r8fl (filed by R3); analysis merged into r8fl as a note

title: [bug] the y8a3 claim insert is a throw site that can abort a whole runPendingBackfill invocation
description:
playhead-y8a3 R3 adversarial pass, finding F4.

BackfillJobRunner.runPendingBackfill's adopt path now calls store.insertBackfillJob for the adoption claim BEFORE enqueueing the adopted row. insertBackfillJob throws on duplicateJobId (a TOCTOU window exists: the by-id read and the claim write are separated by the fetchUnfinishedBackfillJob await, and SemanticScanClaim.record does its own fetch-then-insert at the same id from four runShadowFMPhase gates) and on any store error (SQLITE_BUSY, ENOSPC).

The throw is uncaught inside runPendingBackfill and swallowed at AdDetectionService.swift:9517 as .ranFailed. Net effect: a transient write failure converts 'resume the unfinished row' into 'this session does zero FM work and every remaining plan phase is skipped'.

Exposure is back to the PRE-BEAD level (pre-bead this path minted, which is also an insert), so it is not a regression against main — but it is a regression against the intermediate adopt-only path, which performed no write at all.

FIX: move the claim insert AFTER await admissionController.enqueue(unfinished), or make it best-effort (try? + logger.warning). Losing a claim costs one duplicate pass; losing the invocation costs the whole session's coverage — the asymmetry is the argument.

title: Reach: an ADOPTED backfill row can fall outside countResumableBackfillJobs' newest-batch window, shutting the onn6 re-drive gate
description:
## The dual of playhead-t9nv, created by playhead-7x1s

`playhead-t9nv` is "the count includes a row no pass can re-derive". This is the
opposite direction: **the count EXCLUDES a row a pass now CAN re-derive.**

playhead-7x1s added `AnalysisStore.fetchUnfinishedBackfillJob(analysisAssetId:phase:coveragePolicy:)`
and a fallback in `BackfillJobRunner.runPendingBackfill` (~:768) that ADOPTS an
existing unfinished row instead of minting a new one. Adoption means **no row is
inserted**, so `backfill_jobs.MAX(createdAt)` for the asset does not advance.

`countResumableBackfillJobs(assetId:)` (AnalysisStore.swift:16307) scopes to
`createdAt >= MAX(createdAt) - backfillEnqueueBatchWindowSec` (0.5 s). If the
asset holds ANY row newer than the adopted one by more than 0.5 s, the adopted
row is outside the window and is not counted. When it is the asset's only
resumable row, the count reads **0**, and 0 shuts BOTH onn6 gates:

  * `AnalysisJobReconciler.adScanRedriveCandidate` (:1651)
  * `AnalysisWorkScheduler.adScanRedriveJob` (:6392)

both via `shouldMintAdScanRedrive`, which opens
`guard resumableCoverageJobCount > 0 else { return false }`. And
`AnalysisWorkScheduler`'s own doc (:6360-6369) states that
`runPendingBackfill` **cannot be invoked standalone** — the re-drive mint is the
mechanism that causes a pass for an orphaned coverage row. So the gate shutting
is the loss of the follow-up passes, not merely of a counter.

**Pre-7x1s the same invocation minted a fresh row at `now`, which advanced
MAX(createdAt) and left the count at 1.** The coexistence of an unfinished row
with a strictly newer row is what this diff creates; the window itself is
pre-existing (playhead-onn6).

## Reachability — narrow, and honestly stated

In the steady post-fix full-coverage lane this is UNREACHABLE by construction:
adoption prevents a newer row from being minted while an unfinished one exists,
so the oldest unfinished row is also the newest row. Three ways in:

1. **Legacy rows, i.e. today's device.** The 2026-08-06 pull holds 30 rows /
   15 assets, 14 of them duplicates of a still-unfinished row, minted before
   this fix. An asset in state `{A@T0 unfinished, B@T1 complete}` (T1 > T0) reads
   count = 0 forever after, where pre-fix the next ordinary pass would have
   minted C@T2 and reopened the gate. Transitional, but the transition is
   exactly the population the bead measured. NOT verified against the pull —
   the pull is not on this box.
2. **The targeted lane** (`plan.phases` = 3 phases): one phase adopts an old row
   while the other two mint fresh ones, so MAX advances past the adopted row.
   Planner-reachable (`observedEpisodeCount >= coldStartEpisodeThreshold &&
   stableRecall`) but zero `targetedWithAudit` rows exist on any pull to date.
3. **The specialist phase** (`BackfillJobRunner.swift:810`), which mints beside
   an adopted full-episode row. `specialistScanEnabled` ships `false`
   (AdDetectionService.swift:1175), so inert today. See playhead-7enr.

A `SemanticScanClaim` row RESCUES the case rather than causing it: claims are
`status .deferred`, `retryCount 0` (SemanticScanClaim.claimRow), so a claim
minted after an adoption keeps the count at >= 1.

## Why it was not fixed inside playhead-7x1s

The asset does not stop being scanned — every ordinary transcript-driven
`runBackfill` still adopts and RUNS the row; what is lost is the onn6 follow-up
re-drive. The state is self-healing (once the adopted row completes, fails or
exhausts, the next pass mints fresh and MAX advances). And the fix belongs to
the window, not to the selector: `countResumableBackfillJobs` would have to ask
"is there a row the runner would ADOPT", which is `fetchUnfinishedBackfillJob`'s
own predicate — i.e. the same unification playhead-t9nv and playhead-upm1 are
about. Doing it here would have meant three queries disagreeing instead of two.

R2 review (playhead-7x1s R1 round) identified this shape and rejected it as
"needs a NEWER row to coexist ... that is the targeted lane, which no device
pull reaches, and it is a pre-existing onn6 property rather than anything this
diff created". The disposition was right; two clauses of the reasoning are not.
Legacy rows reach it in the FULL-COVERAGE lane, and the coexistence is created
by this diff.

## Suggested fix

Unify the predicate: have `countResumableBackfillJobs` (and
`fetchAssetIdsWithResumableBackfillJobs`) count exactly what
`fetchUnfinishedBackfillJob` would return, so "the count says there is work"
and "a pass would pick that work up" cannot disagree. That closes this,
playhead-t9nv and playhead-upm1's `failed`-counted-as-resumable half together.
notes:
## R4 REVIEW — independently re-found, and the P2 disposition is challenged (not overturned)

My adversarial pass re-derived this defect from scratch, without being told it
existed, and rated it the single thing on the branch worth fixing. Same
mechanism, same worked example (`{A unfinished @T0, B complete @T1}` reads
count 0). Two things it adds that are worth carrying:

1. **The MAX subquery is unfiltered by status** (AnalysisStore.swift:16381), so
   the window is set by the asset's newest row of ANY status. Combined with
   `fetchUnfinishedBackfillJob`'s `ORDER BY createdAt ASC` — which selects the
   OLDEST unfinished row — the claim's borrowed `createdAt` preserves the count
   only in the case where the carrier is ALREADY the newest row. That is the
   single-row case, i.e. the 7 of 15 field assets the bead is least worried
   about. On the 8 that hold >= 2 rows the borrowing buys nothing.

   Stated as this repo's own defect class: the claim doc
   (BackfillJobRunner.swift:5188-5199) reads `createdAt` as "which enqueue batch
   does this work belong to", and the query's predicate is "is this row in THE
   ASSET'S NEWEST batch". The two are the same sentence only while the runner
   always mints — which is the property this bead removed.

2. **The disposition rests on a clause worth re-testing.** The filing says the
   asset "does not stop being scanned (every ordinary transcript-driven pass
   still adopts and runs it)". The counter-argument is that with count 0 the
   onn6 re-drive is never minted, and `AnalysisWorkScheduler`'s own doc
   (:6360-6369), quoted in this bead's original note, says that mint is the only
   thing that causes a `runPendingBackfill` for such a row. If both are true the
   escape is narrower than P2 assumes. I did not settle it — resolving it means
   enumerating every caller of `runPendingBackfill` and which of them survive an
   episode whose analysis lane has gone terminal. That enumeration is the work
   this bead should start with.

Not started here: this bead is filed and explicitly off-limits to the review
round. Recording the re-finding so the next owner knows two independent passes
reached it by different routes, and knows which clause to attack first.

comments.text:
ABSORBS playhead-03mt (closed 2026-08-11). 03mt says so itself — 'the fix belongs to playhead-9ocm / the onn6 query'. Same query (countResumableBackfillJobs), same 0.5 s batch window, same consequence (count reads 0, shouldMintAdScanRedrive shuts). title: countResumableBackfillJobs counts a failed row as resumable, so a zombie keeps the onn6 re-drive gate open forever
description:
## The same zombie, one gate over

R2 review of playhead-7x1s found that a `backfill_jobs` row at
`status = 'failed', retryCount < AdmissionController.maxRetries` is startable by
nobody:

* `markBackfillJobRunning` accepts only `('queued','deferred','running')` (C3-2)
  and throws `invalidStateTransition`;
* `BackfillJobRunner`'s C3-1 catch arm logs "already in terminal state",
  releases the admission ticket and `continue`s WITHOUT touching `status` or
  `retryCount`;
* `markBackfillJobFailed` is idempotent-silent on an already-failed row and
  deliberately DISCARDS the caller's newer count, so the budget never advances;
* `resetStrandedBackfillJobs` reclaims only `running`.

7x1s's own selector now excludes `failed` for exactly this reason. Two callers
still count such a row as work:

    countResumableBackfillJobs(assetId:)          status <> complete AND <> running
    fetchAssetIdsWithResumableBackfillJobs(limit:) status <> complete AND <> running

## What that costs

`AnalysisJobReconciler.adScanRedriveCandidate` gates on
`countResumableBackfillJobs > 0`, so a zombie keeps the gate OPEN. Every sweep
mints a fresh `adScanRedrive` analysis job, the scheduler leases it, the runner
drains it, `markBackfillJobRunning` throws, the arm continues, and nothing is
scanned. The chain is capped at `maxAdScanRedrives = 2` per work key, but the
count never falls to zero on its own the way the doc at
`AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:7004-7008` assumes ("a pass that drains its rows to
`complete`, or fails them past `maxRetries`, drives that count to zero and the
chain stops on its own"). A row failed at `retryCount = 1` does neither.

It is churn rather than lost coverage — the asset now gets its fresh pass from
7x1s's exclusion — so this is P2, not P1.

## The other half: the by-id branch re-drives a failed row too

`runPendingBackfill`'s M-5 branch skips only `complete` and retry-exhausted, so
under an UNCHANGED transcriptVersion it hits the failed row and takes the same
no-op path every session. Pre-existing and same-version-only (a rotation escapes
it), which is why 7x1s did not widen into it. `markBackfillJobRunning`'s own
HIGH-R6-1 comment describes precisely this shape — it was fixed for `running`
by adding `running` to the IN clause, and the note even spells out the
consequence: "the runner's 'already terminal' catch arm would `continue` without
bumping `retryCount` — a zombie that loops forever."

## Suggested shape

Decide once, in one place, what "resumable" means, and make all four readers
(the two counts above, the by-id skip, and `fetchUnfinishedBackfillJob`) apply
it. The honest definition is "a status `markBackfillJobRunning` will accept",
i.e. `queued`/`deferred`/`running`, plus `retryCount < maxRetries`. Do NOT fix
it by letting `markBackfillJobRunning` accept `failed` — that is the silent
terminal resurrection C3-2 exists to prevent.

title: a targeted-lane job whose resume narrows to EMPTY is marked complete with a cursor from the list it was handed — zero work, near-end-of-list assertion, no retry spent, no telemetry
description:
## The path

`coverageTerminalDecision(for:)` opens with

    guard job.phase == .fullEpisodeScan else { return .complete }

(`BackfillJobRunner.swift:1856`). So for the targeted lane's three phases
(`scanHarvesterProposals`, `scanLikelyAdSlots`, `scanRandomAuditWindows`) the
measured terminal playhead-41mu installed does not apply, by design — those
phases' contract is a window, not the episode.

Now combine that with a resume that narrows to nothing.
`narrowedForResume` (`BackfillJobRunner.swift:3078-3090`) drops every segment
with `endTime <= cursor` and has NO floor: an over-claiming cursor (53FC53E3
carries 2,525.82 s) empties the list outright. `runJob` then returns at its
`guard !inputs.segments.isEmpty` short-circuit (`:3169`) having written only a
`.noAds` no-work sentinel and made zero FM calls.

Back in the drain loop the job takes `.complete`, and
`markBackfillJobComplete` (`:1163-1195`) writes

    lastProcessedUpperBoundSec: EpisodeSeconds.unsoundPlanListPromotion(
        jobInputs.segments.last.map { PlanListSeconds($0.endTime) },
        site: .segmentListCompletion)

`jobInputs` is the PHASE-narrowed list — it is what `runJob` was HANDED, before
`narrowedForResume` ran inside it. So a run that scanned nothing publishes a
near-end-of-list completion cursor and marks the row complete, spending zero
retry budget.

## Why it is the standing defect class

The cursor's meaning is an ASSERTION — "[0, x] of the EPISODE is covered" — and
here it is written from the end of the list the run was handed, on a run that
read none of it. What would this value read if the scan had never happened? The
same. That is the diagnostic.

## Blast radius today

Small, and stated honestly so nobody over-prices it:

* Not permanent. The completed row is excluded by `status <> 'complete'` in
  `fetchUnfinishedBackfillJob` and the current-version id was never inserted, so
  the next invocation mints a fresh cursor-less row. Cost is one wasted session.
* No targeted-lane row exists on any device pull to date — every one of the 30
  rows on the 2026-08-06 pull is `fullEpisodeScan`/`fullCoverage`, and
  `targetedWithAudit` needs `stableRecall`, which nothing has promoted.
* Pre-existing: a SAME-version resume reaches it too. playhead-7x1s only widened
  when it can happen (a cursor is now cashed across transcript versions).

## Also unobservable

`narrowedForResume` emits no counter and no log, and
`narrowingEmptyByPhase` / `narrowingAllPhasesEmptyCount` / `wasEmpty` all belong
to `narrowedInputs` (the earlier PHASE narrowing, `:5104-5145`), not to the
resume. So an empty resume is invisible in telemetry — if this is ever suspected
on device there is currently nothing to look at.

## Suggested shape

Either (a) `coverageTerminalDecision` refuses `.complete` for a run whose
resume-narrowed plan was empty, or (b) `markBackfillJobComplete`'s cursor is
built from what the run actually SCANNED rather than from the list it was
handed. (b) is the one that also helps `fullEpisodeScan`. Related: playhead-pfye
(the cursor is a contiguous prefix) and playhead-x0lb (the promotion sites).

title: two concurrent backfill passes with different transcriptVersions now adopt the SAME job row — cursor lost-update and retry under-spend on the value 7x1s protects
description:
## The two rows that are newly the SAME row

`fetchUnfinishedBackfillJob` is keyed on `(analysisAssetId, phase,
coveragePolicy-class)` with NO `transcriptVersion` term and
`ORDER BY createdAt ASC LIMIT 1`. So two `runPendingBackfill` invocations that
disagree about the transcript version now deterministically converge on ONE row.
Before playhead-7x1s they derived different ids, both missed the by-id lookup,
and each minted its OWN row — two concurrent passes, but on DISJOINT rows.

(The same-transcriptVersion concurrent case already shares a row today through
the M-5 by-id branch, which re-drives `running` too. This bead is about the new
precondition, not a new mechanism.)

## Concurrency is real, not hypothetical

* `backfillJobRunnerFactory` builds a NEW `BackfillJobRunner` and a NEW
  `AdmissionController` per call (`PlayheadRuntime.swift:968-972`,
  `AdDetectionService.swift:9411`), so actor isolation buys nothing across
  invocations.
* `AdDetectionService` is one shared actor and is REENTRANT — `runShadowFMPhase`
  suspends at ~12 `await`s before reaching `runner.runPendingBackfill`
  (`AdDetectionService.swift:9503`).
* Three uncoordinated drivers reach it: `AnalysisJobRunner.run`, 
  `AnalysisCoordinator.finalizeBackfill`, and `ShadowRetryObserver`'s drain.
* Leases are per-jobId, not per-episode (`AnalysisStore.swift:14459-14482`), and
  `fetchNextEligibleJob` has no clause excluding an episode that already has a
  running job. `nowCap` is 2 and `playback` bypasses the cap entirely.
* The codebase already enforces a no-concurrent-per-asset invariant on the HOT
  path (`hotPathRunInFlightAssetIds` + `assertionFailure`,
  `AdDetectionService.swift:3733-3742`). There is no equivalent on the backfill
  path.
* `markBackfillJobRunning` is deliberately idempotent on an already-`running`
  row (`AnalysisStore.swift:16058-16095`) so it cannot serve as a CAS.

## What actually breaks

1. **Cursor lost update, on the exact value this bead exists to protect.**
   `checkpointBackfillJobProgress` is an unguarded `UPDATE ... SET
   progressCursor = ?` (`AnalysisStore.swift:15968-15986`), and every caller
   computes the new value by merging against the IN-MEMORY snapshot captured at
   enqueue (`monotonic(from: job.progressCursor)`), never a re-read. Pass B can
   write a LOWER cursor over pass A's advance. Harm direction is toward
   RE-SCANNING, not toward skipping audio — i.e. it degrades toward the bug
   7x1s fixed rather than toward lost reach.
2. **Retry budget under-spend.** `recordUnderCoverageTerminal` computes
   `attempts = job.retryCount + 1` from the snapshot, so two passes both reading
   N both write N+1: the budget advances by one for two attempts. This weakens
   the escape hatch the 7x1s fallback's own doc leans on.
3. Terminal-state collisions are already handled — the status guards throw
   `invalidStateTransition` and the runner catches and continues. The second
   pass's scan rows are still persisted, so coverage is not lost.

## NOT established

Whether the two-different-transcript-versions concurrent interleaving actually
occurs on device. The drivers and the reentrancy are proven; no telemetry, test
or device-pull evidence pins the interleaving as observed. There is also no test
asserting concurrent `runPendingBackfill` behaviour for one asset.

## Why R1 review did not fix it

The remedy is a durable per-asset claim or a CAS on the row, which is an
architectural addition, not a scope-of-bead change. Excluding `running` from the
new selector is NOT the remedy — that is mutation SX08, and it re-opens the one
case that costs two concurrent full-episode FM passes.

title: coveragePolicyPeers has no compile-time obligation: a 4th CoveragePolicy case silently joins the full-episode class, which is the SUPPRESS-a-pass direction
description:
## What is silent

    private static func coveragePolicyPeers(of policy: CoveragePolicy) -> [CoveragePolicy] {
        let isTargeted = policy == .targetedWithAudit
        return CoveragePolicy.allCases.filter { ($0 == .targetedWithAudit) == isTargeted }
    }

The discriminator is "is it `.targetedWithAudit`". A fourth `CoveragePolicy`
case is not, so it joins `{fullCoverage, periodicFullRescan}` — the class this
query treats as ONE unit of work — with no compile error, no test failure and
no diff anywhere near this file.

## Which direction the failure takes, and why it is the bad one

That is the SX09 direction, and the battery's own note says why it is worse
than SX06's: "under-reaching mints a duplicate pass (waste), over-reaching
SUPPRESSES a pass that is genuinely owed (lost coverage)". Concretely, a job
minted under the new policy would be adopted by a `.fullCoverage` lookup (and
vice versa), so one of the two passes never runs and nothing downstream reports
it — `adScanFraction` would simply read low, indistinguishable from a slow scan.

## The doc claim this corrects

The shipped comment read "Driven off `allCases` rather than a literal pair so a
fourth policy is a compile-time member of exactly one class instead of a silent
omission." That sentence is literally true and reads as a safety guarantee it
does not provide: membership is exactly one class, but it is SILENT and it
defaults to the over-reach side. R1 review reworded the comment to say what
actually happens; this bead is the hardening the comment now points at.

## The fix

Replace the predicate with an exhaustive `switch`, so a new case fails to
compile until someone states which class it is in:

    private static func isFullEpisodeClass(_ policy: CoveragePolicy) -> Bool {
        switch policy {
        case .fullCoverage, .periodicFullRescan: return true
        case .targetedWithAudit: return false
        }
    }

This is the same shape as the repo's other compile-enforced obligations
(playhead-x0lb's `RegionFillDoor`): make the omission a build error rather than
enumerate the spellings a reviewer thought of.

## Cost, so whoever picks it up budgets it

Rails SX06 and SX09 (`scripts/mutation-battery.sh`, batches 577 and 578) both
anchor on the two lines above and must be re-cut and re-proven KILLED. That is
two battery invocations, which is the only reason R1 review filed this instead
of doing it — the change itself is five lines and zero behaviour change today.

title: the mutation battery's baseline gate is a coin flip — playhead-lmrx's grant suites blow their 60s limit under the focused run
description:
## Observed 2026-08-07 while running the SX series for playhead-7x1s

`scripts/mutation-battery.sh` refused to start **three times in a row**, each
time reporting `the focused suites are RED before any mutation` and naming a
DIFFERENT subset of `playhead-lmrx`'s background-grant suites:

    run 1 (11:01)  5 tests
    run 2 (11:04)  8 tests
    run 3 (11:08)  5 tests
    run 4 (11:11)  baseline green

Every failure is `Time limit was exceeded: 60.000 seconds`, recorded at ~81.5 s.
The same 58 tests pass in **4-7 s** when their 11 suites are run alone:

    scripts/fast-gate.sh -only-testing:PlayheadTests/BackfillSchedulerBoundingTests \
      -only-testing:PlayheadTests/BackgroundGrantBudgetArithmeticTests \
      ... (11 suites)   ->  58 tests, 11 suites, PASSED after 7.556 s

Files: `BackgroundGrantBudgetTests.swift`, `BackgroundProcessingServiceLedgerTests.swift`,
`BackfillSchedulerBoundingTests.swift`.

## Why it is a problem and not just noise

The refusal itself is CORRECT — a red baseline makes every verdict in the run
noise, and that guard is the reason the battery's verdicts are trustworthy. The
problem is that satisfying it is now a coin flip: those suites are in
`FOCUSED_SUITES` because LX01-LX41 need them, and under the ~200-suite focused
run they starve past a 60 s `.timeLimit`. Four invocations were needed to get one
verdict, and the natural response to that is to reach for a way around the gate,
which is strictly worse than the flake.

## Options (NOT decided)

* `PerfGate` them, the mechanism CLAUDE.md already prescribes for load-sensitive
  measurement tests, and add them to `MEASUREMENT_TESTS` in
  `scripts/perf-tests.sh`. **This is a coverage decision** — CLAUDE.md already
  lists PerfGate-ing behavioural flake families as deferred for Dan's call —
  because these test real behaviours (expiry durability, counter measurement),
  not latency budgets.
* Raise the `.timeLimit` on the affected tests. Cheapest, but a time limit that
  is raised until it stops firing is not a bound.
* Scope the battery's baseline check to the expectations actually SELECTED by
  `--only` / `--batch`. Tempting and dangerous: it would have let this run start,
  but it also weakens the guard for exactly the case it exists to catch. If it is
  done, the un-selected reds must still be REPORTED loudly, not dropped.

## Acceptance

* Ten consecutive `scripts/mutation-battery.sh --batch <n>` invocations reach a
  verdict without a baseline refusal.
* Whatever moves out of the default run is named, with what it stopped covering.

title: two more sites carry the duplicate-job defect playhead-7x1s fixed in the FM loop: the specialist-phase append and SemanticScanClaim.mint
description:
## Found while fixing playhead-7x1s

playhead-7x1s fixed the FM plan loop in `BackfillJobRunner.runPendingBackfill`:
when the deterministic jobId lookup misses because `transcriptVersion` rotated,
it now falls back to the oldest UNFINISHED row for the same
`(analysisAssetId, phase, coveragePolicy)` and re-drives that, instead of
minting a duplicate full-episode pass.

The specialist-phase append ~60 lines below (`if specialistScanEnabled,
specialistRuntime != nil`) has the identical structure and the identical defect:

    let specialistJobId = Self.makeJobIdForTesting(
        analysisAssetId: inputs.analysisAssetId,
        transcriptVersion: inputs.transcriptVersion,   // <- rotates
        phase: .specialistHostReadScan,
        offset: plan.phases.count
    )
    if let existing = try await store.fetchBackfillJob(byId: specialistJobId) { ... }
    else { insert }

It was left alone deliberately, to keep 7x1s's diff and its measured claim
exact: the phase is two-key gated (`specialistScanEnabled` AND a non-nil
`SpecialistAdClassifier.Runtime`) and with the shipped defaults it is never
enqueued, so there are **zero `specialistHostReadScan` rows on the 2026-08-06
pull** and nothing to measure.

## Fix

One call to `store.fetchUnfinishedBackfillJob(analysisAssetId:phase:coveragePolicy:)`
between the by-id miss and the insert, mirroring the FM loop. The store query and
its six rails (SX03-SX08) already exist.

## Acceptance

* A second `runPendingBackfill` under a new `transcriptVersion` with the
  specialist gate OPEN re-drives the existing specialist row rather than
  inserting a second one — the mirror of
  `newTranscriptVersionResumesRatherThanDuplicating`, in
  `SpecialistHostReadScanRunnerTests`.
* Before enabling the flag in production, not after.
notes:
## A THIRD site, found in the same sweep — `SemanticScanClaim.mint`

`Playhead/Services/AdDetection/SemanticScanClaim.swift:499`. Same shape,
different file:

    let jobId = jobId(analysisAssetId: analysisAssetId,
                      transcriptVersion: transcriptVersion)   // <- rotates
    ...
    if let existing = try await store.fetchBackfillJob(byId: jobId) { ... }
    try await store.insertBackfillJob(claimRow(...))

A rotated `transcriptVersion` misses the claim row an earlier version minted and
inserts a second one beside it. Because a claim row IS a `backfill_jobs` row the
runner later re-drives, a duplicate claim is a duplicate full-episode job — the
same cost playhead-7x1s measured.

**Why it was not fixed in 7x1s:** on the 2026-08-06 pull the claim path produced
NO duplicates. Three rows carry `deferReason = scan_claim:no_coverage_lane_row`
(assets 48E903D7, 4FF3A238, FCDDB309) and each of those assets holds exactly one
row, so there was nothing to measure and the fix would have widened 7x1s's claim
past its evidence. That is a reason to fix it here, not a reason it is harmless.

**Note the branch difference before copying the FM loop's fallback.** This site's
status switch is NOT the runner's: `running` and `failed` both return
`.leftInPlace` deliberately (see the comment at :503 — demoting a `failed` row
would erase why it lost, and a `running` row is owned by a live pass). So the
fallback here must find an unfinished row and then run it through THIS switch,
not through the runner's. `fetchUnfinishedBackfillJob` includes `running`, which
is the right input to a switch that then declines to touch it.

So the follow-up now covers TWO sites: the specialist-phase append in
`BackfillJobRunner` and `SemanticScanClaim.mint`.

title: the semantic-scan reuse key names the WHOLE transcript, and its lookup has no production caller
description:
## Found while fixing playhead-7x1s, on the 2026-08-06 pull

`AnalysisStore.semanticScanReuseKeyHash` is

    "<assetId>|<first>|<last>|<scanPass>|<transcriptVersion>|<cohort>|<scope>"

and `transcriptVersion` is `TranscriptAtomizer.versionHash`, a SHA-256 over the
normalized text of **every chunk in the whole transcript**. The FM work a WINDOW
represents depends only on the atoms inside that window. So a change anywhere in
the transcript rotates the reuse key of every window, including windows whose
atoms are byte-identical.

**The witness is in the pull.** On `F4CE7F47`, three transcript versions scanned
the same spans with the SAME atom ordinals:

    ordinals   0..82    0.0 -> 96.8    tv 0a0e5c52, 7174b714
    ordinals 154..244 157.7 -> 230.4   tv 0a0e5c52, 7174b714, 0322c0a6
    ordinals 245..341 231.2 -> 320.8   tv 0a0e5c52, 7174b714, 0322c0a6

Every one is a distinct `reuseKeyHash` — 53 distinct keys over 53 rows, zero
collisions. The final pass on that asset starts at 180.0 s, so nothing below it
had changed; the whole-transcript hash moved and took the unchanged windows with
it.

## And the lookup has no production caller

`AnalysisStore.fetchReusableSemanticScanResult` — the one function that can
answer "was this window already scanned?" — is called from
`SemanticScanPersistenceTests` and nowhere else. `grep -rn
fetchReusableSemanticScanResult Playhead` returns only its own definition.

So both halves are broken, and fixing either alone buys nothing:
* keyed correctly with no caller -> no FM call is skipped;
* called with the current key -> nothing to hit, because within one generation
  passA redundancy is already exactly **1.00x** on all four scanned assets.

## Sizing

Decomposing the pull's 2.03x (SUM of window spans 9642.2 s / UNION 4759.3 s):

    legitimate coarse->refine (within one generation)   1.27x
    duplicate (same audio, N separate passes)           1.59x

playhead-7x1s removed the duplicate GENERATIONS. This bead is about the residual
inside a single job that is re-driven across transcript versions: `planPassA` is
deterministic, so a re-drive re-plans the same windows and re-asks the FM the
same question over text that did not change.

## The shape of the fix (NOT decided — options only)

`CoarsePassWindowPlan` already carries `prompt`, which IS the question. A
window-local content fingerprint (over the window's segments, computed in ONE
place so insert and lookup cannot drift — see the note on
`TranscriptAtomizer.transcriptVersionHash` about two independently-written
hashes) would replace `transcriptVersion` in the key. Keep the atom ordinals in
the key: dropping them would collapse two different time ranges with identical
text into one row and LOSE coverage.

The caller is the harder half: the FM call happens inside
`FoundationModelClassifier.coarsePassAUnbounded`'s plan loop, which has no store.
The existing injection pattern there (`onProgress`, `onWindowsBanked`, both
added by playhead-26od) is the precedent.

## Watch

A reuse key that names a population WIDER than the one it dedups silently skips
real work — worse than the redundancy. State what the key names and what would
be true if the window's text HAD changed.

comments.text: REPRIORITIZED P1 -> P2 in the 2026-08-11 triage. Not a downgrade of the finding — the queue-6 evidence establishes COMPLETION as the binding constraint (zero backfill_jobs have ever reached complete across 33 assets; FM evidence on 2 of 33). P1 is reserved for that path until it moves.

title: the threaded BGTask identifier is never read back from the ledger (playhead-lmrx R8)
description:
playhead-lmrx R8 adversarial finding.

handleBackfillTask(_:identifier:budget:) threads `identifier` to emitStart (BackgroundProcessingService.swift:1298), recordRunStart(taskIdentifier:) (:1345) and emitExpire (:1772). Nothing asserts the handler USES it.

* The only assertion on that column is BackgroundProcessingServiceLedgerTests.swift:74, which drives handleBackfillTask(task) with the DEFAULT identifier — so it reads the same value whether the parameter is threaded or hardcoded.
* chargedSiblingUsesItsOwnBudget passes only budget:, never identifier:.
* R8's LX40/LX41 canary pins that the REGISTRATION hands the identifier over; nothing pins that the handler does anything with it.

Single-line regression missed: taskIdentifier: identifier -> taskIdentifier: BackgroundTaskID.backfillProcessing.

Why it matters more than a normal wiring gap: it IS the escape route for the .assumed charger budget. BackgroundGrantBudget.swift:368-381 argues at length that 'the pull has zero rows for this class' was an artifact of the instrumentation, and the entire remedy is that the NEXT pull can separate the classes by taskIdentifier.

Fix: extend chargedSiblingUsesItsOwnBudget (BackgroundGrantBudgetTests.swift:953) to inject an AnalysisStoreBackgroundTaskRunLedger, call handleBackfillTask(task, identifier: .backfillProcessingCharged, budget: .backfillProcessingCharged), assert latest.taskIdentifier == BackgroundTaskID.backfillProcessingCharged. Then add the rail.

title: the threaded BGTask identifier is never read back from the ledger, so reverting it to the hardcoded id is invisible
description:
playhead-lmrx R8 adversarial finding.

`handleBackfillTask(_:identifier:budget:)` threads `identifier` to `emitStart` (BackgroundProcessingService.swift:1298), `recordRunStart(taskIdentifier:)` (:1345) and `emitExpire` (:1772). Nothing asserts the handler USES it.

* The only assertion on that column is BackgroundProcessingServiceLedgerTests.swift:74, `#expect(latest?.taskIdentifier == BackgroundTaskID.backfillProcessing)` — and it drives `handleBackfillTask(task)` with the DEFAULT identifier, so it reads the same value whether the parameter is threaded or hardcoded.
* `chargedSiblingUsesItsOwnBudget` passes only `budget:`, never `identifier:`.
* R8's LX41/LX40 canary pins that the REGISTRATION hands the identifier over; nothing pins that the handler does anything with it.

Single-line regression it misses: `taskIdentifier: identifier` -> `taskIdentifier: BackgroundTaskID.backfillProcessing`.

This matters more than a normal wiring gap because it IS the escape route for the `.assumed` charger budget: BackgroundGrantBudget.swift:368-381 spends twenty lines arguing that 'the pull has zero rows for this class' was an artifact of the instrumentation, and the whole remedy is that the NEXT pull can separate the classes by `taskIdentifier`.

Fix: extend `chargedSiblingUsesItsOwnBudget` (BackgroundGrantBudgetTests.swift:953) to inject an `AnalysisStoreBackgroundTaskRunLedger`, call `handleBackfillTask(task, identifier: BackgroundTaskID.backfillProcessingCharged, budget: .backfillProcessingCharged)`, and assert `latest.taskIdentifier == BackgroundTaskID.backfillProcessingCharged`. Then add the rail.

title: the threaded BGTask identifier has no test at any of its five write sites
description:
## What is unpinned

playhead-lmrx's second review round threaded the real BGTask identifier through
`handleBackfillTask` because the handler serves TWO identifiers and hardcoded
the plain one on every ledger and telemetry write — which made "the pull
contains zero rows for the charged class" true by construction rather than an
observation about the class. The in-file comment argues that at length
(`BackgroundProcessingService.swift:839-868`).

Every WRITE site of the threaded value is unpinned:

| site | call |
|---|---|
| `:1298` | `emitStart(identifier: identifier, …)` |
| `:1345` | `recordRunStart(taskIdentifier: identifier, …)` |
| `:1145`, `:1162`, `:1210`, `:1242`, `:1264` | the early-return `emitExpire`/telemetry paths |
| `:1772` | `emitExpire(identifier: identifier, …)` on the expiry path |

Delete-the-call-site test: change any of them back to
`BackgroundTaskID.backfillProcessing` and nothing goes red. The charger class is
recorded as a plain-class window again, and the NEXT device pull is unable to
settle what iOS grants that class — which is the whole reason
`BackgroundGrantBudget.backfillProcessingCharged` is still `.assumed`.

## What IS pinned, and why it is not this

Round 7 added rail LX40 and
`chargedRegistrationThreadsItsIdentifierAndBudget`, which pin the REGISTRATION —
that the charger-class `BGTaskScheduler.register` closure hands
`identifier: BackgroundTaskID.backfillProcessingCharged` to the shared handler.
That covers where the value comes FROM. Nothing covers where it goes.

`chargedSiblingUsesItsOwnBudget` drives the handler with the charged budget but
asserts only on the work deadline the coordinator was handed.

## Repro / fix sketch

Cheap and behavioural, no new production seam needed: drive
`handleBackfillTask(task, identifier: BackgroundTaskID.backfillProcessingCharged,
budget: .backfillProcessingCharged)` against a recording
`BackgroundTaskRunLedger` stub that captures `recordRunStart`'s
`taskIdentifier`, and assert it is the charged id. A telemetry recorder covers
`emitStart`/`emitExpire` the same way. Then one rail per site (or one rail on
`recordRunStart`, which is the site the ledger queries actually group by).

Found in review round 7 of playhead-lmrx and filed rather than fixed: the round
had already spent its budget closing the teardown-guard gap (D1) and the
registration wiring, and a partial fix here would have shipped a third
instrument nobody had time to attack.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: ABSORBS playhead-rj3b (closed 2026-08-11). Same defect, filed one day apart from lmrx R7/R8: the threaded BGTask identifier is unpinned. rj3b named one site and one test; this bead enumerates ALL EIGHT write sites and proposes the same recording-ledger-stub test, so it is the superset. Carrying rj3b's argument, which is the sharper motivation: it IS the escape route for the .assumed charger budget.

title: the three awaitJobsSettled CALL SITES are pinned only probabilistically
description:
## What is unpinned

`AnalysisWorkScheduler.awaitJobsSettled(_:within:pollInterval:)` has three
production call sites, all added by playhead-lmrx:

| site | file:line |
|---|---|
| backfill work-deadline return | `BackgroundProcessingService.swift:1650` |
| backfill expiration handler | `BackgroundProcessingService.swift:1866` |
| recovery work-deadline return | `BackgroundProcessingService.swift:2407` |

The METHOD is railed twice — LX17 (`return true` immediately) and LX20 (waits on
"is anything running" rather than on the identities). Neither can see a handler
that stops CALLING it.

Delete any one call site and `setTaskCompleted` fires without waiting for the
cancelled job's requeue to commit, which is the durability the cancel exists to
buy.

## Why round 7 did not close it

The nearest thing to a pin is `expiredRowLandsBeforeTheSettleWait`'s final
assertion — `after.state == "queued"`, read from the store after
`task.awaitCompletion()`. With the settle deleted, the handler calls
`markComplete` while the cancelled job is still unwinding on the scheduler's own
task; whether the test's store read observes `queued` or `running` is a race
between the unwind's SQLite writes and the test's next actor hop. It usually
reddens. It is not guaranteed to.

Round 7 built a deterministic seam for the sibling defect (the teardown
`guard !Task.isCancelled`) by PARKING the expiration handler inside its own
`finishRun` — which is UPSTREAM of `markComplete` — so the work task became the
only party that could complete the task. That construction does not transfer
here: `awaitJobsSettled` sits DOWNSTREAM of the ledger write on every one of the
three sites, so parking the ledger holds the handler on the wrong side of the
statement under test.

Four routes were considered and rejected:

* **Read `completedSuccess` right after the ledger write.** The mutant still
  needs a few actor hops to reach `markComplete`, so a `nil` read proves
  nothing — the race runs the wrong way and the rail would SURVIVE
  intermittently.
* **A `WorkJournal` recorder stub as a synchronous witness** (the `preempted`
  row is emitted strictly before the registry removal the settle waits on). The
  mutant's completion still races the unwind; the margin is large but not a
  guarantee.
* **A bounded spin for the negative.** That is a duration test wearing an
  assertion, and this file has already gone red twice under the battery's own
  suite load for exactly that.
* **Gating `handleExpiredProcessingTask`.** This would work, and it is the only
  construction that does — but it means a production seam whose sole purpose is
  to be parked from a test, downstream of the settle. That is a design decision,
  not a review action.

## What closing it needs

An injectable "teardown step" seam downstream of `awaitJobsSettled` and upstream
of `markComplete`, on both handlers, so a test can park there the way
`GatedRunLedger` parks at the ledger write. Then three rails (one per call site)
become deterministic, and the existing `after.state == "queued"` assertion can be
re-anchored to the park instead of to a store read after completion.

Filed rather than papered over: round 6 identified this as D5 and round 7
confirmed the shape rather than fixing it.

title: a killed mutation-battery leaves its xcodebuild child running, so the next run collides with a build nobody owns
description:
## Observed

2026-08-06, while demonstrating `playhead-pu7e`'s crash recovery. `kill -9` on `scripts/mutation-battery.sh` (pid 36127) left its `xcodebuild test -scheme Playhead …` child (pid 41050) alive and running to completion — several minutes of full CPU and simulator on a box whose rule is ONE BUILD AT A TIME. It was noticed only because `pu7e`'s new `mb_warn_if_xcodebuild_running` printed it at the start of the very next invocation.

The same thing happens on `TERM` and on `Ctrl-C`: the battery's `INT`/`TERM` trap restores sources and exits, but nothing signals the child. The header's own recovery note for the batch-320 wedge already says "TERM the script so its trap restores sources (it did) — **then kill xcodebuild by PID**", which is this bug written down as a manual step.

## Why it matters more now, not less

`pu7e`'s lock is worktree-scoped and released promptly on exit. So the next battery starts immediately and *correctly* — straight into a shared simulator and `.derivedData` that an orphan from the previous run is still using. That is the `database is locked` / wedged-runner family, and `pu7e` made it *diagnosable* rather than impossible.

## What would close it

Run `run_focused`'s `scripts/fast-gate.sh` in its own process group and signal the group from the trap, or record the child pid and `kill` it in `on_exit`. Either needs care: the gate has its own one-shot wedged-simulator retry, so killing mid-retry has to leave the sim in a state the next run can recover, and the existing `restore_and_verify` FATAL path must still run.

Worth measuring first: whether `xcodebuild` reliably dies on TERM or needs the group.

title: mutation-battery verdicts are collected by hand from per-invocation logs, and a stale log is indistinguishable from a fresh KILLED
description:
## What happens

The battery is driven one `--only <NAME>` at a time and each invocation is redirected to its own file (`dr-DR01.log`, …). Nothing then relates those files to a run. `playhead-e75l` R7 nearly credited a whole batch that never executed: every `dr-*.log` from the previous round read `KILLED`, and the collector could not distinguish *"this batch did not run"* from *"this batch passed"*. It was caught only because that round happened to collect verdicts by mtime against the run's start.

Same shape as `playhead-pu7e`'s two defects: a value that names one thing read as though it named another.

## What pu7e already did, and why it is not enough

`scripts/mutation-battery.sh` now stamps every run with its start time, pid and argv at the HEAD and the FOOT of the output, so a stale file is self-identifying **from its own contents**. That closes the "I cannot tell when this was produced" half.

It does not close the collection half. An operator (or an agent) still has to remember to look at the stamp, and a `grep -c KILLED` over a directory of logs — which is what actually gets run — reads a stale file exactly as before.

## What would close it

A collector, not a convention. Roughly: `scripts/mutation-battery-collect.py <dir> --since <run-id>` that reads the stamp out of each log, refuses any file whose stamp predates the run being collected, and prints one table plus an explicit list of the names that produced NO log at all. The last part is the important one — the population that "did not run" has to be *named*, not inferred from an absence.

Worth considering at the same time: have the battery write its results to a machine-readable file (the `$WORK/results` pipe-delimited file already exists) under a stable per-run path, so collection reads structure instead of parsing prose.

## Why P2 and not P1

`pu7e` made the failure detectable by reading one line. This makes it undetectable-by-omission, which is a real improvement but a smaller one — and the battery is usually driven a batch at a time, where the ambiguity does not arise.

title: priority inversion: dl9k's rescue for a 13%-covered episode queues behind ad-scan redrives for better-covered ones
description:
## Observed live on the 2026-08-06 device build

playhead-dl9k's cap-out rescue fired correctly ~18 min after install -- two rows minted at
01:14:17 UTC, at a fresh ordinal, on the base workKey, `attemptCount = 0`:

    2C5C3699  queued  ...7874f9186efbf3d8:1:preAnalysis:capRetry:1
    44F076BB  queued  ...d304679e762e4f78:1:preAnalysis:capRetry:1

**44 minutes later, at the 01:58 pull, neither had run.** Their fast watermarks were byte-identical
across all five snapshots: 2C5C3699 at 900.0 / 6925.5, 44F076BB at 1620.0 / 1977.0. Meanwhile the
scheduler processed a wave of `adScanRedrive` jobs (CDD611C4, 48E903D7, FCDDB309, 4FF3A238,
52CD8F5B all re-queued at 01:54:25) and ran preAnalysis for D29CF74B, 16F3CB88, F2F2FC4C.

## Why this matters more than it looks

The scheduler runs **one job at a time** (`currentRunningTask`), so queue ORDER is the entire
allocation policy. And the ordering is inverted against need:

* `2C5C3699` has a **900.0 s fast watermark on a 6925.5 s episode** and is the worst-covered asset
  in the pull. Its rescue waited.
* The `adScanRedrive` jobs that went ahead of it were for assets that already have far more
  coverage -- and three of them had ALREADY deferred at 00:56:26 with
  `scan_claim:no_coverage_lane_row`, i.e. they declined immediately on the previous sweep and were
  re-queued to decline again.

So the single most starved episode waits behind work that is both better-off and, in three cases,
predictably about to no-op.

## What to establish before changing anything

1. **Is there an ordering policy at all, or is it insertion order?** Name it. If ranking exists
   (`BacklogScarcityRanking` is in `AnalysisJobReconciler`'s signature), measure what it actually
   ranks on and whether cap-out retries participate.
2. **Should a rescue outrank a redrive?** Argue it rather than assume. A rescue targets an episode
   with NO path back; a redrive targets one already progressing. But a rescue is also speculative
   -- playhead-6r4z showed 2 of 3 rescued assets would have re-read covered audio first.
   **Do not fix this before 6r4z lands**, or the measurement will be of the wrong system.
3. **The `no_coverage_lane_row` re-queue loop is a separate question** -- three jobs deferring on
   one sweep and being re-queued on the next, to defer again, is either a retry policy working as
   designed or a spin. Establish which; file separately if it is a spin.

## Verify against the field

Snapshots at `scratchpad/db-aug5`, `db-t2min`, `db-t5min`, `db-t15min`, `db-t35min` (2026-08-06,
install ~00:55 UTC), plus `db-aug3-work/analysis.sqlite`. **Re-derive every figure, naming
numerator and denominator.** `fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime` is a WATERMARK, not coverage --
see playhead-346z; conflating them is this repo's standing defect class and it was committed
against these very snapshots while they were being read.

LABELS: reach, scheduler

title: a pass that produces zero new coverage re-queues with no circuit-breaker (transcription:zeroCoverage observed looping on device)
description:
## Observed live on the 2026-08-06 device build, not inferred

Five device pulls between 00:56 and 01:58 UTC, ~1h after installing main `a08b70d0`.
Asset `F2F2FC4C` ("Neil deGrasse Tyson On Aliens, Simulation...", 6636.6 s):

    analysisState   queued
    fastWM          4680.0
    finalWM         6636.6      <- the WHOLE episode
    lastErrorCode   transcription:zeroCoverage
    attemptCount    0

Fast watermark measured across the pulls: 2580.0 -> 4620.0 -> 4680.0 -> 4680.0 -> 4680.0.
It advanced at 11.3x realtime for eight minutes, then FROZE for 40+ minutes while the device
was busy, ending each pass with `transcription:zeroCoverage` and re-queueing.

## Why it produced nothing -- this part is playhead-6r4z, and is NOT this bead

Chunks for that asset: fast reaches 4619.8 s, final reaches **6636.6 s**, union **100.0 %**.
The episode is FULLY transcribed. `mptr`'s ordering index reads `pass='fast'` alone, so the
final-covered audio sorts UNREAD and floats to the front; the pass re-reads it, produces no new
FAST coverage, and reports zeroCoverage. playhead-6r4z fixes the ordering.

**Do not close this bead when 6r4z lands.** 6r4z removes the current CAUSE of the loop; it does
not add a brake. Any future condition that makes a pass produce zero coverage -- a wedged
recognizer, an unreadable shard, a policy that filters everything -- reproduces the same silent
spin, and the pull shows the spin is invisible: state `queued`, attemptCount `0`, no terminal.

## The defect

`transcription:zeroCoverage` is a job that did work and moved nothing. Nothing counts it. The row
re-queues with `attemptCount = 0`, so neither `AdmissionController.maxRetries = 3` nor y8f3's
cap-out terminal nor dl9k's `isNoProgressTerminal` (which requires `state='complete'` with
`coverageInsufficient:noProgress`) can ever see it. It is a THIRD road to a dead end, and unlike
the other two it does not even terminate -- it burns the single-job scheduler indefinitely.

Compare the sibling that IS handled: a coarse pass that moves none of the four coverage measures
writes `complete` / `coverageInsufficient:noProgress` and stops. The transcription stage has no
equivalent.

## The fix (argue it, do not assume it)

A bounded consecutive-zero-coverage counter on the same row, terminating to a state dl9k's
rescue can already see (`complete` + a named no-progress code) rather than inventing a fourth
terminal class. Reuse the `kvs8`/`e75l` shape: a NAMED cause, a preserved attempt budget, and a
drain-level stop after N consecutive refusals. **The cost of being wrong is asymmetric** -- too
eager and an episode stops early with audio left unread, which is the exact failure REACH exists
to prevent -- so the threshold needs measuring against the pull, not picking.

## Verify against the field, do not trust this bead

Pull at `scratchpad/db-aug3-work/analysis.sqlite` (2026-08-03) and the five 2026-08-06 snapshots
under `scratchpad/db-aug5`, `db-t2min`, `db-t5min`, `db-t15min`, `db-t35min`. **Re-derive every
number and name numerator AND denominator.** Note the trap this bead's own author fell into:
`fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime` is a WATERMARK, not coverage -- reading 4680.0/6636.6 as "70.5 %
transcribed" is false, the union is 100 %. That is playhead-346z's territory and the standing
defect class, committed while writing this up.

LABELS: reach, transcription

comments.text:

title: mptr's shard-ordering index reads pass='fast' alone, so final-pass-covered audio sorts UNREAD and floats to the front
description:
## The gap

`FastTranscriptCoverageIndex` (playhead-mptr, #335) orders unread audio first so the flat 300 s transcription stage cap is not spent re-reading a covered prefix. Its input is `AnalysisStore.fetchFastTranscriptCoveredRanges`, which selects `WHERE pass = 'fast'` alone.

A region the FINAL pass covers therefore has no artifact the index can see — either because the two passes ran over disjoint spans, or because `TranscriptChunkCanonicalizer.canonicalize` drops the fast chunks a final chunk fully contains. `isShardAlreadyTranscribed` requires BOTH the watermark past the shard end AND a `pass='fast'` chunk overlapping it, so those shards fail condition 2, sort as UNCOVERED, and — the partition being stable over playhead-proximity order — float to the FRONT, ahead of the audio a pass was minted to read.

This is the same fast-only under-report playhead-9y9e fixed for the ad-scan bound (`fetchTranscriptCoveredRanges`, the canonical union of both passes, already exists) and did not fix for this index.

## Measured — 2026-08-03 device pull, 30 s shards

Shards BELOW the asset watermark that nonetheless sort UNREAD, against the genuinely-new audio behind them:

| asset | phantom-unread below watermark | new audio | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| 44F076BB | 0 of 54 (0 s) | 357 s | mptr works |
| 2C5C3699 | 20 of 30 (600 s) | 6,025 s | weakened |
| 48E903D7 | 41 of 67 (1,230 s) | 103 s | INVERTED 12:1 |
| AD5F3A0A | 79 of 142 (2,370 s) | 0 s | n/a |
| D9B513CD | 39 of 115 (1,170 s) | 480 s | 2.4:1 |
| 0C2FC22E | 31 of 70 (930 s) | 0 s | n/a |

Six of twelve assets carry phantom-unread audio; on 48E903D7 the re-read prefix exceeds the new audio by 12x, so a 300 s pass can plausibly never reach the 103 s that matter.

## Why it is filed rather than fixed in playhead-dl9k

dl9k is the VEHICLE (it mints a pass for rows that previously got none) and its cost of being wrong is bounded by maxCapOutRetries. Changing this index changes what the transcription stage decodes on every run — a behaviour decision, and mptr's own header argues explicitly for ordering-not-skipping and for the artifact test that H3/0sro required. Widening the input to the canonical union preserves both properties (it still checks artifacts; it still only re-orders) but it must be argued and measured on its own.

## Probe that found it

R1 review of playhead-dl9k, probe 4 ("can the minted retry loop?"). dl9k's premise — mptr makes a retry productive — was checked against the pull rather than accepted, and holds on 1 of the 3 assets dl9k rescues.

comments.text:

R1 REVIEW — one round, aimed at under-decoding. 3 findings, all fixed in e6b44c18. Tree clean.

VERDICT ON UNDER-DECODING: NO. No audio can be skipped or deprioritised that should have been read. Probed by planting, not by reading:

FINDINGS

1. HIGH (harness). `$MPTRIDX` was never in `MUTABLE_FILES`, since playhead-mptr. NINE of the thirteen K2 mutations target it (K201-K205, K208-K210, K212; batches 200-203, 205). `restore_sources` only checks out that list and `restore_and_verify` only hashes it, so a batch touching the file did both halves of the failure that helper exists to prevent. That abort is luck (shared focused suite), not design — a non-overlapping batch would have been scored against an already-buggy codebase, and one naming a reddened test would have been a false KILL. Worse, an author who runs a batch then commits, commits a one-token `>=`/`<=` flip in the half-open-interval file. Negative control: removing `$MPTRIDX` again names all nine and exits 2. RE-PLANT: all 6 batches re-run, baseline green each time, tree CLEAN after each.

2. MEDIUM. A false measured claim in shipped source — and it is this bead's own defect class. Those numbers are `episodeDurationSec - watermark`: the SPAN above the watermark, read as though it named the covered audio inside it. Measured union of chunks in that span: D9B513CD 50.3 s of 479.9 (10.5 %), 83592353 58.0 s of 95.9 (60.5 %). Ten times smaller on the bigger of the two, which changes whether the follow-up earns its slot. The tell is the standing one — D9B513CD's final-pass `MAX(endTime)` is 3,929.8 s against a 3,929.9 s episode: 100 % by reach, 10.5 % by area. It was standing in for the question with content, since `overlaps` is satisfied by ANY overlap: how much of a moved shard a real row actually backs.
