title: Two atomize call sites still use the pre-hc7e 'filter final' timeline collapse
description:
FOUND while mapping atomize call sites for playhead-r5um. Not fixed there:
r5um is an ORDERING fix, and this is a COVERAGE bug whose fix changes which
audio the evidence catalog describes — a detection-behaviour decision.

playhead-hc7e removed this exact selection from `AdDetectionService.runBackfill`
and replaced it with `TranscriptChunkCanonicalizer`:

    let filtered = chunks.filter { $0.pass == "final" }
    return filtered.isEmpty ? chunks : filtered

It collapses the whole timeline to the candidate-local `final` rows the moment
ONE final row exists, because `FinalPassRetranscriptionRunner` only creates
`final` rows around already-detected candidate windows. Two call sites still
do it verbatim:

  * `AnalysisCoordinator.pushEvidenceCatalog` (~line 2218) — the catalog the
    SkipOrchestrator attaches to every banner. On a mixed-pass asset the banner
    evidence describes only the audio a previous pass already flagged.
  * `AdDetectionService.runPhase5ProjectorPhase` (~line 8713).

Separately, THREE more production `atomize` call sites pass raw persisted
chunks with no canonicalization at all — `runShadowFMPhase`
(AdDetectionService ~8889, which PERSISTS scan rows stamped with the resulting
`transcriptVersion`), `RegionShadowPhase.run` (~163) and
`DebugEpisodeExportService` (~228). Those are not wrong in the same way, but
it means the app mints `transcriptVersion` values from two different transcript
SELECTIONS for the same asset, which is why `semantic_scan_results` carries 31
distinct versions across 19 assets on the 2026-07-30 pull. Worth deciding
whether canonicalization belongs inside `atomize` too, or whether the shadow
lane should call it.

Related stale documentation: `FusionLiftHarnessSupport.swift:65-80` still
describes `runBackfill` as doing the `filter { pass == "final" }` collapse. It
has not since hc7e, so the harness's sticky-provider transcript version and
production's can already differ on a mixed-pass asset.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: KILLED 2026-08-11 in the full-backlog triage. SUPERSEDED by playhead-iu0t (#349, b2024119). Both named sites now canonicalize. The two remaining raw-chunk atomize sites are recorded on iu0t as a deliberate exclusion.

title: chunkIndex is not a per-asset identity — the counter resets to 0 mid-episode
description:
ROOT CAUSE named while fixing playhead-r5um. NOT fixed there: r5um made the
atom sequence immune to it (the ordering comparator is now a total order,
falling through to `id`), so this is no longer load-bearing for detection.
Filing rather than compensating further downstream.

`TranscriptEngineService.chunkCounter` is an in-memory `var` seeded to 0 and
reset in four places — asset switch in `startTranscription`, first
`appendShards` after `activeAssetId == nil`, `stop()`, and
`stopTranscription(analysisAssetId:)`. Persisted rows from the prior session
survive all four. So a re-transcribed episode re-mints indices that already
exist on that asset.

MEASURED, 2026-07-30 device pull (scratchpad/db2/analysis.sqlite):

  assets with duplicate chunkIndex values          21 of 30
  worst: asset 594732D7  1776 rows, 1455 distinct  (3 rows at chunkIndex 0)
         asset 8FECFDDE  6390 rows, 4002 distinct  (3 rows at chunkIndex 0)
  assets with >1 row at chunkIndex 0               10, up to FIVE rows at 0

Asset 8FECFDDE's three `chunkIndex 0` rows are `(0.42, 1.08, fast)` twice —
byte duplicates, same segmentFingerprint, distinct ids, the playhead-6av0
duplicated-child-row family, all `model_version = 'pre-instrumentation'` so
plausibly pre-dating that fix — and `(3540.0, 3540.42, fast)`, written after
a counter reset near the end of a 59-minute episode.

Deduplication cannot prevent this: it keys on `segmentFingerprint` =
hash(text, startTime, endTime), so a re-transcription that produces DIFFERENT
text for the same audio inserts a new row. That is the normal case, not the
exotic one — device asset C25FF8CF has "T. Rowe Price" and "Borgata online"
ad reads both covering [0, 30] because DAI rotated the slot between fetches.

FORWARD-LOOKING FIX (no row repair — the product owner has declined historical
repair three times): seed the counter from `MAX(chunkIndex) + 1` for the asset,
exactly as `FinalPassRetranscriptionRunner.nextFinalChunkIndex` already does.
It is one store read per session start.

STILL EXPOSED TODAY, i.e. why this is worth doing even after r5um:
  * `MusicOffsetLexicalGate.onsetWindowText` and `EpisodeSummarySampler.sample`
    use `chunkIndex` as the equal-startTime tiebreak. Colliding values make
    that tiebreak meaningless (it does not make it non-deterministic — both
    sort startTime first — but it stops ordering what it claims to order).
  * `chunkIndex` is what a human reads in a debug export or a bug report to
    locate a row. Three rows numbered 0 make that impossible.

NOT a correctness risk for atom ordering, prompts, scan-window geometry or
`transcriptVersion` any more — playhead-r5um's comparator resolves the tie on
`id` and is pinned by
`TranscriptAtomTimeOrderTests.idTiebreakResolvesOtherwiseIdenticalKeys`.

title: TestFlight and App Store submission are blocked: only a BETA Xcode 27 is installed, and Apple refuses beta-SDK builds for distribution
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-30 by the first end-to-end TestFlight attempt. The archive SUCCEEDED; the upload was refused by App Store Connect.

    error: exportArchive Unsupported SDK or Xcode version. Your app was built with an SDK or
    version of Xcode that isn't supported. Although you can use beta versions of SDKs and Xcode
    to build and upload apps to App Store Connect, you need to use the latest Release Candidates
    (RC) for SDKs and Xcode to submit the app.
    (ID: TGFSREI47NKXT7U6YDR2USWGSE)
    ** EXPORT FAILED **

WHAT IS AND IS NOT BROKEN. Auth was FINE — the upload reached App Store Connect and came back with a server-side rejection carrying a request ID, which it could not have done unauthenticated. Signing was FINE — both `Apple Development` and `Apple Distribution: Daniel Abrams (36Z6VYTT9X)` identities are present and the archive signed clean. Entitlements were FINE — the stale-profile failure mode that playhead-#273 fixed did not recur. The ONLY problem is the toolchain.

THE CONSTRAINT:
  * The only Xcode on this machine is `Xcode-beta.app` at 27.0. There is no release or RC Xcode installed.
  * `project.yml` pins `deploymentTarget: iOS "27.0"` and `xcodeVersion: "27.0"`.
  * 12 files import FoundationModels / Speech, and there are 7 `@available(iOS 27` annotations across ChapterLabelingService, FoundationModelClassifier and SemanticScanStatus. So the iOS 27 dependency is real and load-bearing, not incidental.

THEREFORE, and this is the part that matters beyond TestFlight: **NEITHER TestFlight NOR App Store submission is possible from this toolchain today.** It is not a script defect and not something a code change fixes. Two external gates have to open first:
  1. Apple ships an Xcode 27 RC or release. Beta SDKs are accepted for UPLOAD but explicitly refused for SUBMISSION.
  2. For an App Store release specifically, iOS 27 itself has to be publicly available — an app cannot ship with a deployment target of an unreleased OS.

IMPACT ON THE RELEASE PLAN. The recorded target is ~2026-08-25 to 09-01. That date is now contingent on Apple's calendar, not ours. Nothing in the backlog moves it. This should be treated as a schedule input rather than an engineering task, and playhead-jw63 (Phase 1 release readiness) cannot actually complete while it holds.

WHAT STILL WORKS, so this does not read as worse than it is: DIRECT DEVICE INSTALL is unaffected. `xcodebuild -destination generic/platform=iOS` + `devicectl device install app` does not go through App Store Connect and has worked repeatedly today. Dogfooding is not blocked. Only distribution is.

OPTIONS, none of which are purely ours to take:
  (a) WAIT for the Xcode 27 RC. Cheapest, and the only option that preserves the iOS 27 feature set. Requires knowing Apple's date, which we do not.
  (b) LOWER the deployment target and gate the iOS 27 APIs behind availability checks, so the app builds and ships against a supported SDK. This is a real engineering project — 12 files import the 26/27-era frameworks, and FoundationModels IS the ad classifier, so a lower floor means a materially different product on older devices. It also reopens playhead-2fd's settled policy (download-only + unavailable messaging rather than a hardware bar). NOT a decision to take casually and NOT one to take without Dan.
  (c) SHIP LATER, deliberately, and use the extra time on reach and detection quality — which the 2026-07-30 measurements say is where the product actually needs it (zero of 34 episodes at 95% ad-scan coverage).

RECOMMENDATION: treat as (a) plus (c) — assume the date slips to Apple's RC, and keep spending the interval on coverage rather than on release mechanics. Do NOT start (b) without an explicit decision; it is a product-scope change disguised as a build fix.

ACTION NEEDED FROM DAN: check developer.apple.com/news/releases for the Xcode 27 RC date and decide whether the release target moves. Everything else here is informational.

Related: playhead-jw63 (release readiness — blocked by this), playhead-2fd (the settled hardware-floor policy that option (b) would reopen), playhead-qdyj (feedback address sign-off, still a real pre-release gate), and the #273 TestFlight signing fix (which this run incidentally VERIFIED end-to-end for the first time — it got all the way to Apple).
=== DAN'S DECISION 2026-07-30 ===

"thats fine i expect the rc will be available by august  we will release when ios 27 is released... but only if detection is good enough"

So the toolchain blocker is ACCEPTED and de-escalated: no action, no deployment-target change, no reopening of playhead-2fd. Option (b) from above is explicitly OFF the table. Wait for the RC; release when iOS 27 ships publicly.

THE CONSEQUENCE THAT MATTERS: the release gate is no longer a build problem, it is DETECTION QUALITY. That moves the critical path entirely onto reach and accuracy, and it means the calendar is now the LESS binding constraint of the two.

WHERE DETECTION ACTUALLY STANDS AGAINST THAT GATE, measured 2026-07-30, not estimated:
  * ad-scan coverage: ZERO of 34 episodes over 15 min reach 95%; 29 are under 25%
  * of 44 rediff-confirmed true ad slots: 27 (61%) have ZERO overlap with any pipeline window
  * of all true ad audio: 15% covered, 51% lost to slots missed entirely, 34% to narrow windows
  * of 17 slots that WERE detected: 14 are covered by a single window, mean largest uncovered run inside the slot 71 s

By any reading, detection is not close to "good enough" today. The gate is real and distant, and it is the thing to work on — not the release mechanics.

WHAT IS MISSING, AND IS NOW THE HIGHEST-VALUE UNBLOCKED WORK: there is no agreed DEFINITION of "good enough". Without one, the decision gets made by feel on the day, against whichever number is nearest to hand — which is exactly how this project has been burned repeatedly (the 18% width figure that was a selection artifact; the checkmark that keyed on a DSP watermark; "148 free ad-seconds" that counted show as ad). A release gate defined at release time is not a gate.

PROPOSED BAR, for Dan to accept or move — deliberately in listener terms, not internal metrics:
  1. PRIMARY: fraction of ad-seconds the listener does not hear, per episode, on a held-out corpus. Currently ~15%. This is the number that means "don't hear ads".
  2. GUARD, and it is not symmetric: show-seconds wrongly skipped must be ~ZERO for anything auto-skipped. Eating content is far worse than missing an ad — Dan's own framing, and the reason inner edges matter more than outer ones.
  3. REACH: fraction of episodes where analysis completed far enough for (1) to be meaningful at all. A great score on 15% of the library is not a product.
  4. REPEATABLE: measured by the corpus lane, same command, run-to-run deterministic, so the number moves for real reasons. The corpus lane was already designated the pre-release gate and cert path.

DO NOT credit an improvement measured on the same episodes that motivated the change. Held-out only — the FM prompt program (playhead-xsdz.63) already proved a curated eval was overfit, and the 4xqf N=12 conclusion inverted at N=44.

Related: playhead-jw63 (release readiness), playhead-hvk0 (the biggest reach lever), playhead-xsdz.65 (pod completeness), playhead-xdh7 (corpus growth, which the measurement depends on).
=== CORRECTION 2026-07-30 — THE TESTFLIGHT HALF OF THIS BEAD WAS WRONG. TestFlight is NOT blocked. ===

Empirically settled by three upload attempts. TestFlight works; the cause was far smaller than filed.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG: this machine had **Xcode 27 beta 2 (27A5209h, 22 Jun 2026)**. App Store Connect's own release notes, 2026-07-21: "You can now submit apps built with **Xcode 27 beta 4** using the SDK for iOS 27.0 beta 4 ... for internal and external testing." Beta 4 is **27A5228h (20 Jul 2026)**. A beta SDK IS accepted — but only the CURRENT beta. Being two betas behind was the entire cause.

RULED OUT, each verified rather than assumed:
  * AUTH — fine. The upload reached App Store Connect and returned a server-side rejection carrying a request ID, which is impossible unauthenticated. Xcode is correctly signed in; my earlier "no account found" check looked in pre-Xcode-16 locations.
  * SIGNING — fine. Both `Apple Development` and `Apple Distribution: Daniel Abrams (36Z6VYTT9X)` identities present; the archive signed clean every time.
  * ENTITLEMENTS — fine. The stale-profile failure that #273 fixed did not recur. **This run incidentally verified #273 end-to-end for the first time.**
  * `testFlightInternalTestingOnly` — does NOT exempt a stale beta. I set it and got the identical error. Corrected in the script comment (commit 8d496ff8) so nobody repeats the experiment.

FIX: install Xcode 27 beta 4 or later. `xcodes` CLI is now installed at ~/.local/bin/xcodes (Homebrew could not build it on macOS 27 — no bottle, source build fails — so the prebuilt arm64 binary from the project's GitHub release was used). One command, needs Dan's Apple ID: `xcodes install "27.0 Beta 4"`. Dan also has beta 4 on his office machine.

NOTE the recurrence risk: "current beta only" means EVERY new Xcode beta re-breaks TestFlight until the RC. Expect to chase it roughly every 2-4 weeks.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE, and is why this bead stays open at P2: **App Store SUBMISSION is still blocked** and will be until (1) Apple ships an Xcode 27 RC/release, and (2) iOS 27 itself ships publicly — an app cannot ship with a deployment target of an unreleased OS. Dan's decision stands: release when iOS 27 releases, and only if detection is good enough. That gate is detection quality, not the toolchain.

MY PROCESS FAILURE, recorded because it cost three runs and a wrong bead:
  1. I read Apple's generic error text as the complete explanation and filed "blocked until RC". The message names neither the required version nor the one used.
  2. I then reversed myself on an AI-GENERATED SEARCH SUMMARY rather than a primary source, and acted on it.
  3. Only the third pass — reading Apple's actual release notes, then comparing our build number to beta 4's — found it.
I had primary evidence (a server-side rejection with a request ID) and twice preferred secondary sources to it. The one-step diagnostic was "which beta, exactly?" — a version comparison — and I did not ask it until last. Same shape as the recurring "ask what the quantity measures" failure: I had a value (27A5209h) and never checked what it meant.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: KILLED 2026-08-11 in the full-backlog triage. NOT A WORK ITEM, by its own correction: 'THE TESTFLIGHT HALF OF THIS BEAD WAS WRONG. TestFlight is NOT blocked.' Dan's recorded decision de-escalates the rest ('we will release when ios 27 is released'), option (b) explicitly off the table, and the bead concludes it is 'a schedule input rather than an engineering task'. It closes when Apple ships an RC. Its 'good enough to release' bar is preserved on playhead-jw63.

title: A second empty catch on the launch path: downloadManager.bootstrap() failures are swallowed with an unverified comment
description:
FOUND 2026-07-30 by playhead-se2h's implementer while fixing the sibling defect. Named in its report as "one sibling swallow remains on the launch path that I did not touch" — filing it so it is not carried only in a merged PR description.

THE DEFECT. `downloadManager.bootstrap()` is called on the launch path inside a catch with an EMPTY BODY, alongside a comment asserting behaviour that has not been verified. This is the same shape playhead-se2h just fixed one call earlier in the same function:

  * se2h's version: `try await speechService.loadFastModel()` wrapped in `catch { }` with a comment claiming "the transcript engine will surface failures when first used". That claim was FALSE — the failures landed in a per-shard catch that logs and continues, so a single transient failure permanently disabled transcription for the life of the install, with no retry and no diagnostic.
  * This one has the same structure and an equally unverified claim. It has NOT been traced, so do not assume the consequence is equally severe — establish it.

WHAT TO ESTABLISH FIRST, do not assume:
  * What does `bootstrap()` actually do, and what is lost if it throws? Downloads not resuming? Suspended transfers never scanned? Nothing at all? The answer decides whether this is a real defect or a genuinely-safe no-op that merely needs an honest comment and a log line.
  * Is the failure RECOVERABLE later by some other path, or is it once-per-launch like se2h's was? se2h's severity came entirely from being invoked exactly once with nothing else ever retrying.
  * Is it observable today? If a bundle cannot distinguish "bootstrap succeeded" from "bootstrap threw and we carried on", that is the same undiagnosability se2h fixed, independent of how bad the functional consequence is.

FIX SHAPE, in the order that respects what the investigation finds:
  1. At minimum, LOG IT AND MAKE IT OBSERVABLE. That half is cheap, carries no behavioural risk, and is worth doing even if the functional consequence turns out to be nil. `SpeechModelLoadJournal` (se2h) and `AnalysisStoreHealthJournal` (playhead-wvdz) are the established pattern for a durable, locally-exported subsystem-health signal — reuse rather than invent a third.
  2. Correct or delete the comment. A comment asserting unverified behaviour is worse than no comment; se2h's whole premise was a comment that lied, and the review of se2h then caught a NEW overclaiming comment introduced by the fix itself.
  3. Only add a retry if the investigation shows the failure is both consequential and non-recoverable. If a retry is added it MUST be bounded with a no-progress guard — five beads in a row (gqx4, onn6, wvdz, se2h, and se2h's own review) hit the rule that an unbounded retry is a worse bug than the one being fixed.

WHY IT IS WORTH A BEAD RATHER THAN A DRIVE-BY. The launch path is where "best-effort" comments accumulate, and this is now the second confirmed instance in a single function. It is worth ALSO sweeping the rest of the launch sequence for empty and `try?`-swallowed catches while here, and reporting the count — the defect class matters more than either instance. Related: playhead-se2h (merged, #300), playhead-wvdz (merged, #299), and the recurring "a value that names an absence" pattern.

title: The ◐ partly-analysed state shows a sighted user no number at all — and the fix is probably not 'add a caption'
description:
FOUND 2026-07-30 by Dan asking a plain question — 'where do I look' — about the pz32 states. The answer exposed a gap I passed in review.

THE GAP. `episodePreparationCaption` returns nil for `.partiallyAnalyzed` (EpisodePreparationReadiness.swift:314), so the library row renders a 13pt grey half-circle and NOTHING ELSE. The scan percentage and the 'Amount scanned unknown' string exist only as `.accessibilityValue` (:353-360), reachable via VoiceOver. A sighted user gets the honesty of 'not complete' with none of the actionable part.

The code's own comment concedes the requirement: 'partly without a number is not actionable information'. It then puts the number where only a screen reader can reach it. I reviewed this and it looked right because the accessibility strings were unusually thorough — thoroughness in one channel masked absence in the other.

A SHARPER SYMPTOM — DISCONTINUITY. While working, the caption DOES show a number: 'Downloaded · analyzing 47%' (:321). So the user watches a percentage climb, the scan stops short, and the number VANISHES at exactly the moment it became a permanent fact rather than a transient one. The information is least available precisely when it stopped changing.

WHY 'JUST ADD A CAPTION' IS PROBABLY THE WRONG FIX, and this is the part worth thinking about before implementing. Measured on the 2026-07-29 device pull with pz32's definition: ZERO of 34 episodes over 15 minutes reach 95% ad-scan coverage; 29 are under 25%. So a visible percentage would put a LOW NUMBER ON NEARLY EVERY ROW, permanently. That is not reassurance, it is a persistent advertisement of our own incompleteness, and it collides with [[feedback_peace_of_mind_not_metrics]] — not because a coverage figure is a vanity metric (it is functional progress, and that memory explicitly endorses 'transparent reasoning, graceful degradation, quiet correctness'), but because SURFACING IT ON EVERY ROW AT REST turns a quiet state into a nag. 'Respect your attention' cuts against a number the user cannot act on.

THE OPTIONS, with the tradeoff each makes:
  A. Visible percentage on the row. Maximally honest, maximally anxious. Every row reads like a defect report until reach improves.
  B. Qualitative visible caption ('Partly checked'). Honest about incompleteness, no number to compare or worry at. Loses actionability entirely — arguably no better than the glyph alone.
  C. Status quo (glyph only), but make the number REACHABLE ON DEMAND — tap or detail view. The row stays quiet; the fact is available to anyone who wants it. Aligned with attention-respect.
  D. Sequence it behind playhead-onn6 and make ◐ ACTIONABLE. Today a tap re-drives nothing (pz32 traced this: INSERT OR IGNORE on a workKey the completed job owns), which is exactly why pz32 deliberately did NOT make ◐ tappable — an affordance that no-ops is a lie. Once onn6 gives under-scanned episodes a real re-drive, tapping ◐ can mean 'finish scanning this one', which is user-initiated rather than nagging, and it makes the number worth showing because it is finally attached to an action.

RECOMMENDATION: D, with C as the interim. The gap is real but the honest fix is blocked on there being something to DO about it. Adding a number the listener cannot act on optimises for our transparency rather than their experience.

DO NOT implement A without Dan's explicit sign-off — it is the one option that changes the felt character of the library screen on every episode.

DEPENDS ON: playhead-onn6 (re-drive) for the D form. Related: playhead-pz32 (which built the states and correctly refused to fake an affordance), [[feedback_peace_of_mind_not_metrics]], and the 'Respect your attention' framing in the founder reorder.
=== BETTER FIX, from Dan 2026-07-30: "how do i tell downloaded vs analyzed or get a sense of how much analysis remains?" ===

His question exposes that the gap is WIDER than the missing number, and it also supplies a fix that is better than the caption options above. Withdraw option A entirely.

WHAT THE CONTROL ACTUALLY DOES. `workingBar` renders TWO 26x3pt capsule zones side by side — left = `downloadFraction`, right = `analysisFraction`, copper fill on a 20% track (EpisodePreparationControl.swift:89-93, :109-119). But `workingBar` is only reached for `.waitingForWifi` / `.downloading` / `.analyzing`. The three RESTING states (`.idle`, `.partiallyAnalyzed`, `.ready`) go through `glyph(...)` instead, so AT REST BOTH ZONES DISAPPEAR.

Consequences, all of which are Dan's question restated:
  * You cannot tell how much analysis remains — no bar, no number.
  * You cannot tell downloaded-vs-analysed, because the DOWNLOAD zone vanishes too.
  * A downloaded episode with nothing scanned yet is indistinguishable from one scanned to 90%.
  * The discontinuity is now clearly a UI-structure bug rather than a copy bug: the user watches a two-zone bar fill, and at the moment work stops the bar is REPLACED by a glyph. The information does not fade, it is structurally removed.

THE FIX: KEEP THE TWO-ZONE BAR IN `.partiallyAnalyzed` (and consider `.idle`), with the analyze zone partially filled to the measured fraction.

Why this beats every caption option above:
  * It answers "how much remains" SPATIALLY, with no number — so it does not collide with [[feedback_peace_of_mind_not_metrics]] and does not put a low percentage on every row. A 3pt quiet bar is not a nag; a text percentage is.
  * It restores the download/analyse distinction for free, because the zones already encode it.
  * It removes the discontinuity by construction: the bar the listener was watching STOPS rather than disappearing.
  * It reads correctly for the shape we cannot currently express at all — downloaded, nothing scanned = left zone full, right zone empty.
  * It needs no new vocabulary, no new surface, and no copy. It deletes a special case rather than adding one.

OPEN DETAILS worth deciding while implementing:
  * `.ready` should probably KEEP the sage ✓ rather than showing two full bars — done is a different kind of statement from in-progress, and the ✓/bar contrast is a clearer distinction than full-bars/partial-bars.
  * An UNMEASURED fraction must draw an EMPTY analyze zone, never a guessed one — `analysisFractionIsMeasured` already exists for exactly this and defaults to false so a careless caller under-claims. Do not let "unknown" render as "0% and therefore nearly nothing" if that is visually indistinguishable from a measured zero; if it must be, prefer the empty zone and let VoiceOver carry "Amount scanned unknown".
  * Whether the glyph disappears entirely or sits alongside the bars is a taste call for Dan; the ◐ carries "at rest, incomplete" which the bar alone does not.
  * Still sequence the ACTIONABLE version (tap ◐ to finish scanning) behind playhead-onn6, per option D above. The bar makes the state legible; onn6 makes it fixable. They are complementary, and the bar is worth shipping first because it is inert and reversible.

title: A Catalyst-hosted test target so migrations can be verified against a real device database
description:
Recommended by playhead-6av0 review round 2 after two rounds hit the same wall.

THE PROBLEM: a 52 MB real device database was pulled from Dan's phone and is the ONLY ground truth for several migrations and measurements — but it cannot be put in front of a simulator test host. Three routes were tried and all failed the same silent way, ZERO TESTS RUN:
 - xcodebuild's TEST_RUNNER_* env forwarding does not reach a simulator host on this toolchain.
 - A simulator host cannot read the host machine's /private/tmp or /Users.
 - The app's Documents container is replaced on reinstall before the test runs.
FIVE BUILDS were lost to this in one round. The harness was deleted rather than shipped silently doing nothing, which was the right call.

Coverage was closed differently — by mutation plus direct sqlite3 experiments against the real file — and that is adequate for playhead-6av0. But it means the migration's SQL was proven against real data while the COMPILED BINARY was proven only against fixtures. Two proofs, not one, and they have never disagreed; still, a migration that deletes thousands of rows on a user's device deserves the real file in front of the real code.

THE UNTRIED ROUTE: a macOS / Mac Catalyst hosted test target, which CAN read the host filesystem. Dan has explicitly suggested Catalyst as the fallback for anything needing a device, and there is precedent — the l2f capture lane already runs via Mac Catalyst.

READ project_catalyst_capture_lane_quirks FIRST. Known traps recorded there: env only via a PATCHED xctestrun; -testPlan needed for a single xctestrun; isAliasFile is true for symlinks; resolvingSymlinksInPath strips /private; mach_vm_allocate 0x4 spam is benign.

SCOPE THIS DELIBERATELY. It is a new test target plus a capture lane, not a review-round change — which is exactly why round 2 declined to start it with two builds left. Treat it as its own bead with its own budget.

VALUE IF IT LANDS: every future migration can be verified against a real device database before it ships, instead of against fixtures that encode what we already believe. Given this project has now shipped one migration that would have silently deleted a user's entire database and one that duplicated 7,339 rows, that is not a luxury.

Related: playhead-6av0 (where the wall was hit twice), playhead-0hi9 (the migration that caused the duplication), playhead-wvdz (a failed migration deletes the store).
acceptance_criteria: A test target that can read a real device database from the host filesystem and run the SHIPPED migration code against a copy of it. Proven by pointing it at the existing 52 MB pull and reproducing playhead-6av0's measured before/after counts (transcript_chunks 64,749 -> 57,410, decoded_spans 78 -> 74, ad_windows unchanged) through the compiled binary rather than through transcribed SQL. Documented so the next migration uses it by default. If Catalyst also proves unworkable, record WHY with the same specificity as the three simulator routes, so nobody spends another five builds.

title: fetchTranscriptChunk probes without pass while the new unique index includes it — a final row can be skipped for its fast twin
description:
Found during playhead-6av0 review round 2. NOT a V40 regression — the asymmetry pre-dates it — but V40's new unique index makes it REACHABLE, so it should be closed while the context is fresh.

THE MISMATCH:
  fetchTranscriptChunk keys on (analysisAssetId, segmentFingerprint) with LIMIT 1.
  idx_chunks_asset_pass_fingerprint (added by V40) keys on (analysisAssetId, pass, segmentFingerprint).

So the index now PERMITS a fast/final twin pair that the writer's pre-insert dedupe can only ever see ONE of. The writer probes without `pass`, finds the first row, and concludes the segment is already present — even when the row it found is the other pass. Before V40 nothing enforced uniqueness at all, so the asymmetry was inert; now the index actively allows the pair the probe cannot distinguish.

WHY pass MUST STAY IN THE INDEX (do not "fix" this by dropping it): computeFinalPassFingerprint deliberately prefixes fp-final- (FinalPassRetranscriptionRunner.swift:919-936) so a final row never dedupes against its fast twin. That is intentional — the two passes are different content and both are wanted. playhead-6av0 measured 1,309 rows on Dan's device that are fast/final twins correctly protected by `pass` being in the key; dropping it would destroy them.

SO THE FIX IS ON THE PROBE, NOT THE INDEX. Establish first whether the probe SHOULD be pass-aware:
 - If yes, fetchTranscriptChunk gains a `pass` parameter and callers pass theirs. Check every caller — TranscriptEngineService.swift:1487 is the hot one.
 - If the probe is deliberately pass-agnostic for some reason, that reason needs to be written down and the index's permissiveness needs a different guard.
Do not assume; the fp-final- prefix says the two passes are meant to coexist, which argues the probe is simply missing a dimension.

BLAST RADIUS IF LEFT: a final-pass row can be skipped because its fast twin was found, losing the higher-quality transcription for that segment. That is silent content loss of exactly the kind playhead-kcz.1 was fixing when it removed a display-level collapse.

Related: playhead-6av0 (added the index), playhead-kcz.1 (the canonicalizer that reconciles fast/final at read time).
acceptance_criteria: Established whether the pre-insert probe should be pass-aware, with the reasoning recorded rather than assumed. If yes, every caller passes its pass and a regression proves a final row is no longer skipped because a fast twin exists. The index KEEPS pass in its key — 1,309 real rows on the owner's device depend on that. If the probe is deliberately pass-agnostic, that rationale is documented and the permissiveness gets a different guard.

title: Five interruption-reporting arms in runTranscriptionLoop are unpinned: deleting their report changes no test
description:
Left open deliberately by playhead-ngev's review round 1, with the blast radius measured rather than guessed.

playhead-ngev made every silent return in runTranscriptionLoop report a named failure instead of returning in silence. Two `.preempted` arms and three shard-0-backfill arms report correctly BY INSPECTION, but no test fails if you delete their reportInterruption call. They are the residue of a thirteen-arm sweep where the other eight are pinned by mutation.

WHY IT WAS NOT WORTH BUILDS AT THE TIME: the failure mode is a return to PRE-BEAD SILENCE, not a new defect — the arm goes back to returning quietly, which is exactly what it did before ngev. And the runner already intercepts preemption via the sticky PreemptionSignal (LanePreemptionCoordinator.swift:86-88, "never flipped back to false") BEFORE it journals, so the preempted arms in particular are belt-and-braces over a path that is already handled one level up. The review had spent its budget on the accounting regression, which was HIGH severity and reachable by ordinary scrubbing.

WHY IT IS STILL WORTH DOING: an unpinned arm in a sweep whose entire purpose is "no return is silent" is the seam where the sweep quietly becomes incomplete again. The next person to touch those arms has nothing telling them the reporting call is load-bearing. This is the same shape as the defects ngev itself fixed — a diagnosis computed and then lost on the way out — and it would regress invisibly, because the symptom is an absence.

WHAT TO DO: delete each arm's reportInterruption call in turn and confirm a test reddens. Where none does, add one. Five arms, and they should be individually attributable rather than batched, since a mutation that kills everything proves nothing — ngev's own review hit that twice (M17 masking M19, and M14 masking M6) and had to re-run in isolation to attribute correctly.

DO NOT settle for a single test that covers all five. The point is that each arm independently reports; one test passing while four arms are dead is precisely the failure being guarded against.

Related: playhead-ngev (parent, merged), and note its round-1 finding 4 — a control test that was vacuously green because both halves of an A/B died at stage 2 before reaching the code under test. Add a premise assertion to any new fixture here for the same reason.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the five arms (two .preempted, three shard-0-backfill) is individually mutation-proven: deleting its reportInterruption call reddens a test attributable to that arm alone, not to a batch. Where no test exists, one is added with a premise assertion so the fixture cannot pass while dying earlier in the pipeline. A single test covering all five is explicitly NOT sufficient.

title: Shard cache fail-open can still serve a partial decode's shards after the audio is evicted (0hi9 residue)
description:
FOUND IN playhead-8ysk REVIEW ROUND 2, by measurement. 8ysk's source-identity stamp does NOT close 0hi9's propagation path on one branch, and the 8ysk source now says so explicitly at AnalysisAudioService.isShardCacheValid.

THE CHAIN:
1. A partial decode is still CACHED. saveShards runs whenever isTruncated is false, and 8ysk's own measurement establishes that a headerless CBR MP3 prefix (a shape podcast CDNs serve) declares its own prefix length, so it decodes 120.01s of a declared 120.01s and reads as complete TO ITSELF. isTruncated is false and the prefix is cached.
2. The 8ysk stamp kills that entry the moment the source file GROWS (download completes). That is the dominant path and it is fixed.
3. It CANNOT kill it if the file is DELETED first. DownloadManager.evictIfNeeded() (LRU, over-budget cache) and clearCache() both delete complete audio and leave the AnalysisShards cache standing — only SettingsViewModel's transcript-DB clear wipes AnalysisShards, and that is a different user action from clearing the audio cache.
4. A decode after that measures nothing, so isShardCacheValid FAILS OPEN (deliberately — see below) and serves the prefix shards.
5. persistSpooledEpisodeDuration reads that outcome and records the PREFIX duration as the episode duration. That is 0hi9's original symptom: placeholder rows at 528-561s, i.e. 8 MiB at ~123 kbps.

WHY FAIL-OPEN IS STILL RIGHT: with no source there is nothing to re-decode from, and 0hi9's own cachedDecodeReportsNotTruncated depends on a warm-cache re-spool being answered. Mutating the branch to fail CLOSED kills that test (measured, 8ysk r2 MUT-M4). So the fix is not to flip the branch.

THE FIX SHAPE: the manifest must record decode COMPLETENESS, not just source identity — e.g. stamp whether the decode reached the container's declared duration, and refuse to fail open for an entry that did not. That is a 0hi9-flavoured change (duration truth), not an 8ysk one (cache keying), which is why 8ysk r2 documented it rather than implementing it.

Bounded: needs LRU eviction or a manual audio-cache clear of an episode whose PARTIAL decode was cached, with no completed decode in between.

title: Gate load storms have three different measured culprits — including 5x ReportCrashService at 380% CPU
description:
The "documented load-flake families" carried in every bead brief on this project may be substantially an artifact of MACHINE CONDITION rather than an inherent property of those suites. Three separate observations, and they do NOT agree on a single culprit — which is itself the finding.

OBSERVATION 1 (playhead-8ysk review round 1, 2026-07-29): `appstored` inside the iOS 27 simruntime spinning at 123% CPU, system load average 123. Killing it dropped load to 13.9 and cut gate failures from 10 suites to 2. The 2 survivors passed in isolation at 2.1s and 0.057s against 128.0s and 134.9s under load.

OBSERVATION 2 (playhead-8ysk review round 2): load average 154.27 at gate launch, attributed to a WindowServer / loginwindow / WallpaperAerials storm. Re-running the failing families at load 9.33 gave EXIT=0, 28 tests in 4 suites passed.

OBSERVATION 3 (2026-07-29, during round 3's gate): load average 106-143 with `appstored` at **0.0% CPU** — so it was NOT the cause this time. The actual consumers were FIVE concurrent copies of
  /System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/OSAnalyticsPrivate.framework/XPCServices/ReportCrashService.xpc/.../ReportCrashService
at 83.0 / 80.4 / 75.4 / 74.3 / 65.4 percent CPU — roughly 380% between them — plus `diskimagesiod` at 39.2%.

I killed appstored during observation 3 on the strength of observation 1, before checking its CPU. That was acting on a stale premise; it was idle and killing it changed nothing. Recording the mistake because it is the same error this project keeps finding in code review — asserting a cause from a prior context instead of measuring the current one.

WHAT OBSERVATION 3 SUGGESTS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT: ReportCrashService running five-up means CRASH REPORTS ARE BEING GENERATED AND PROCESSED during the gate. That is a stronger lead than a single idle daemon, because it implies something is actually crashing — repeatedly — while tests run. It does NOT establish what is crashing. Candidates to check rather than assume: simulator processes dying under memory pressure, the test host crashing between suites, XCTest's own child processes, or a backlog of stale .ips reports from earlier sessions being chewed through.

WHAT TO ESTABLISH:
 - What is generating the crash reports? Look in ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports and the simulator's equivalent for timestamps correlating with gate runs. If the app or test host is crashing repeatedly, that is a far more serious finding than a slow gate.
 - Does the load storm PRECEDE the gate or is it CAUSED by it? Observations 1 and 2 named different culprits; observation 3 a third. If the common factor is "the gate makes the machine crash things", the flake families may be downstream of a real defect.
 - Whether scripts/fast-gate.sh should measure and report load in its preflight (playhead-y27o added toolchain preflight and a terminal PASS/FAIL line). Reporting the load at launch alongside the verdict would let every future triage start from data instead of a prior.

DO NOT relax the triage rule on any of this. The duration tell (>=97s starved, ~2s real) has been correct every time it was applied, and verifying a suspicious failure against the base commit caught a REAL regression wearing a perfect starvation signature (playhead-8ysk's appendShardsAfterCompletion: 164s under load, deterministic 60s hang in isolation, base commit green in 1.6s).

VALUE IF RESOLVED: quieter gates, fewer builds burned on isolation re-runs, and possibly the discovery that something in this project is crashing repeatedly on this machine without anyone noticing.
acceptance_criteria: Established across several gate runs whether killing the runaway daemon reproducibly shrinks the failing set, rather than on one observation. If confirmed, scripts/fast-gate.sh preflight detects it and either kills it or warns loudly with the measured load. The triage rule (>=97s starved / ~2s real, verify against base when the suite is in the diff's blast radius) is NOT relaxed regardless of outcome. Report whether this changes the deferred decision about PerfGate-ing behavioural suites out of the default gate.

title: AnalysisJobRunner has a second shard-sum duration write that can still persist a truncated duration
description:
Flagged by the playhead-0hi9 implementer as deliberate scope containment rather than silent growth. 0hi9 fixed the truncated-duration write in AnalysisCoordinator.runFromSpooling; this is its sibling.

AnalysisJobRunner around :434 performs a SECOND shard-sum duration write. It was left alone because it goes through the AnalysisAudioProviding protocol, so surfacing truncation there means changing the protocol and every conforming stub — a materially wider blast radius than 0hi9's change, which deliberately kept decode(...) projecting .shards so the protocol and its stubs were untouched.

WHY IT IS LOWER RISK THAN THE ONE 0hi9 FIXED, but not zero: its input is completeness-gated by wrj8, so in the common path it should not see a partial file. That gate is the only thing standing between it and the same defect, and nothing asserts the coupling. If the wrj8 gate is ever relaxed, moved, or bypassed on a new path, this write silently reacquires the 0hi9 bug — persisting an ~8 MiB prefix duration (528-561s on the owner's device) that then poisons every coverage ratio computed against it.

THE FIX SHAPE, when taken: extend AnalysisAudioProviding to surface the truncation verdict the way 0hi9 extended the concrete service (AnalysisDecodeOutcome carrying shards + verdict, with decode(...) projecting .shards for compatibility). Update conforming stubs. Then gate this write the same way persistSpooledEpisodeDuration is gated — taking the whole outcome rather than a caller-supplied flag, so the verdict cannot drift from the decode that produced it.

Do NOT simply add a caller-supplied boolean here; 0hi9 specifically avoided that shape because a flag passed by the caller can disagree with the decode it claims to describe.

Related: playhead-0hi9 (the sibling fix and the pattern to follow), playhead-csbq (the >100% coverage ratios this defect class produces).
acceptance_criteria: The truncation verdict is available through AnalysisAudioProviding rather than inferred, and AnalysisJobRunner's duration write is gated on it using the same whole-outcome shape as persistSpooledEpisodeDuration. Conforming stubs updated. A regression proves a truncated decode cannot set a duration on this path, mirroring 0hi9's coverage. If instead the decision is that the wrj8 completeness gate is sufficient, then assert that coupling with a test so relaxing the gate reddens something — do not leave it as an undocumented assumption.

title: IncrementalShardAppend drain-loop coverage is fixture-incidental: repairing the fixture would silently delete it
description:
Flagged during playhead-8m2w review round 4 as ledger entry B6, classified PROVEN (fragile). This is a trap laid for a future maintainer, and it is exactly the vacuous-test failure mode this repo keeps hitting — just deferred rather than present.

THE SITUATION. The drain loop's per-shard 'catch ... continue' at TranscriptEngineService.swift:601 IS covered: mutation M24 (changing it to 'return') is killed by IncrementalShardAppendTests / appendShardsAfterCompletion, which goes from passing to a 60s hang.

THE PROBLEM. That kill is INCIDENTAL. The fixture omits insertAsset, so persistence throws — and it is that unintended throw which exercises the catch. The test does not deliberately fail a shard; it accidentally fails every one.

CONSEQUENCE: a future maintainer who notices the missing insertAsset and 'repairs' the fixture will silently delete the only coverage of the drain loop's blast-radius guard. Nothing will go red. The test will keep passing and keep looking like it covers something it no longer does. That is the vacuous-test pattern, pre-armed.

Round 4 deliberately did NOT fix it, and was right not to: repairing the fixture is the risk, so a mid-round change could have removed the coverage while everything stayed green.

FIX SHAPE: make the coverage intentional rather than incidental. Add a test that deliberately fails one shard in the DRAIN loop (the sibling of abandonedShardDoesNotAbortTheLoop, which covers the FIRST loop at TranscriptEngine.swift's per-shard catch) and asserts the remaining shards still process. Prove it non-vacuous by re-running mutation M24 against the new test specifically. THEN the existing fixture can be repaired safely — but verify M24 is still killed AFTER the repair, or the repair has re-opened the hole.

Related: playhead-8m2w (origin), playhead-auz3 / playhead-ugy4 / playhead-xc6b (the vacuous-test family on this repo).
acceptance_criteria: A test deliberately fails a shard in the DRAIN loop and asserts the rest still process. Mutation M24 (drain-loop catch...continue -> return) is killed by that new test specifically, verified by running it in isolation rather than relying on the suite. If the appendShardsAfterCompletion fixture's missing insertAsset is repaired, M24 is re-run afterward to prove coverage survived the repair.

title: The 300s stage budget is a bare literal duplicated across files — no shared constant couples the watchdog to the runner
description:
Flagged during playhead-8m2w review round 4 as ledger entry A13, classified UNPROVEN-ACCEPTED. Not a defect today; a coupling hazard.

The 120s holder watchdog in TranscriptEngine is calibrated against two premises. The lower bound is >= 4x a shard's 30s duration, and that IS pinned — shippingDeadlineIsCalibrated asserts it against AnalysisAudioService.defaultShardDuration. The upper bound is 'less than the 300s stage budget', and that is NOT pinned, because AnalysisJobRunner.swift:648 writes the 300s as a bare literal (Task.sleep(for: .seconds(300))) with no shared constant.

So the two numbers are coupled by comment only. If someone lowers the runner's stage budget below 120s, the watchdog silently becomes useless — it would never fire before the stage above it gave up — and no test would notice.

Round 4 declined to fix it because the fix requires editing AnalysisJobRunner, which is outside 8m2w's scope, and the reviewer correctly refused to widen the blast radius mid-round.

FIX SHAPE: extract the 300s into a shared named constant that both the runner and the watchdog calibration test reference, then extend shippingDeadlineIsCalibrated to assert the upper bound too. Keep the assertion in terms of the constant, not a re-typed 300 — the whole point is that the two move together.

Related: playhead-8m2w (origin), and the watchdog design at TranscriptEngine.swift:426.
acceptance_criteria: The 300s stage budget exists as one named constant referenced by both AnalysisJobRunner and the watchdog calibration test. shippingDeadlineIsCalibrated asserts the upper bound (holder deadline < stage budget) against that constant, and the assertion fails if either value moves independently. No re-typed literal in the test.

title: Device-lane test: an abandoned recognizer holder meeting the next real request (SFSpeechErrorDomain Code=16)
description:
Identified during playhead-8m2w review rounds 3 and 4 as the one part of the watchdog contract that CANNOT be covered on simulator. Filed so the gap is tracked rather than forgotten, since no simulator test can honestly close it.

THE CONTRACT AT ISSUE. TranscriptEngine.swift:368 documents a deliberate short overlap window: when the 120s holder watchdog fires, the hung Speech call is ABANDONED and the request permit is freed, rather than every later transcription in the process parking behind it. The comment argues the overlap is short BECAUSE the abandoned call is cancelled. Releasing the permit while a real recognizer session still holds hardware is exactly what produces SFSpeechErrorDomain Code=16 — the overlap error the gate exists to prevent — so this is a deliberate, bounded risk, not an oversight.

WHAT IS ALREADY COVERED ON SIMULATOR (do not redo):
 - The permit IS released while the wedged call is still parked — wedgedHolderDoesNotWedgeALaterAcquire.
 - The abandoned call IS cancelled — abandonedCallIsCancelled (added round 3; dropping work.cancel() makes it hang its full 60s time limit).
 - The watchdog fires at the deadline SCALE, not merely at some deadline — a lower-bound clock assertion added round 3 after the mutation timeout: deadline/4 survived the entire suite.
 - A failed shard does not abort the job — abandonedShardDoesNotAbortTheLoop, added round 3 after catch...continue -> return survived.

WHAT REMAINS UNCOVERED AND WHY IT CANNOT BE FAKED. Producing Code=16 requires a real SpeechAnalyzer session still holding audio hardware while a second prepareToAnalyze runs. No stub or mock can emit that error, so any simulator test claiming to cover it would pass without exercising anything — a vacuous test, which on this repo is worse than no test. Round 3 explicitly declined to write one.

WHAT THE DEVICE TEST SHOULD ASSERT: force a genuinely hung prepareToAnalyze on hardware, let the 120s watchdog fire and abandon it, then start the NEXT shard's recognizer request and assert that it either succeeds or fails with Code=16 — and specifically that it does NOT wedge. The distinction that matters is failure-vs-hang, not success-vs-failure: the whole point of abandonment is that the process keeps moving.

PRACTICAL NOTE: a 120s watchdog makes this a slow test. Consider exposing the deadline for injection so the device lane can use a short one — but if you do, keep the shipped default asserted separately (shippingDeadlineIsCalibrated already pins 120s, and the round-3 lower-bound test pins the scale), so a test-only injection point cannot silently become the production value.

Related: playhead-8m2w (the bead this came from), playhead-xc6b (the parked-continuation hazard class).
acceptance_criteria: A device-lane test exercises a real hung recognizer request, the watchdog's abandonment, and the next request's outcome on actual hardware. It asserts the next request does not WEDGE — failing with Code=16 is an acceptable outcome, hanging is not. If the deadline is made injectable for test speed, the shipped 120s default remains independently asserted. If it turns out this cannot be forced reliably even on device, record that finding and close rather than leaving a test that passes without exercising the path.

title: Sign off (or swap) the feedback recipient address before release
description:
NEEDS-DAN, one decision, small. playhead-jw63.5 (merged 1d0b1e91) ships an in-app feedback channel whose mail goes to d.abrams@icloud.com — Dan's real personal inbox.

WHY IT WAS CHOSEN: no support domain exists anywhere in the repo, and shipping an address that bounces would turn 'a listener can tell us anything in 10 seconds' into a silent dead end — the worst possible failure for a channel whose entire purpose is hearing from people. So the implementer used the one address known to work, put it in exactly ONE constant, and pinned it with a test so swapping it is a deliberate edit rather than a search-and-replace.

WHAT TO DECIDE before the App Store release (~4 weeks out from 2026-07-27):
(a) Accept it — simplest, and at v1 volume a personal inbox is genuinely fine. Cost: the address is then public in a shipped binary and on the App Store listing's support surface, and it is the same address as the git committer identity, so it is already semi-public.
(b) Register a support alias (support@ / hello@ on a domain you control) and point the constant at it. Costs a domain and 10 minutes; buys separability later and looks more like a product than a side project to a stranger reading the listing.
(c) Use an Apple-provided route only (App Store Connect support URL / email field) and drop the in-app mail recipient — but this weakens the bead's promise, since the point was zero-friction from inside the moment.

RECOMMENDATION: (b) if a domain already exists or is cheap to add, otherwise (a). This is not worth blocking the release over; it IS worth deciding deliberately rather than discovering post-launch that your personal address is in a shipped app.

Note the same question applies to the two fallback notices, which name the address in selectable text when Mail cannot open — they read from the same constant, so one edit covers all three surfaces.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded and the constant reflects it. If the address changes, the pinning test is updated and the two fallback notices are re-checked (they read the same constant, so they should follow automatically — verify rather than assume). If the address stays, the reasoning is written down so a future reader does not treat it as an oversight.
notes:
2026-07-28 DAN DECISION, in two parts.

INTENT: the personal address should NOT be the long-term answer — Dan's preference is to rely on the App Store Connect support route rather than shipping d.abrams@icloud.com in the binary.

DECISION FOR NOW: KEEP jw63.5 AS BUILT and revisit at submission. title: Sweep follow-ups: weak-observable suggest test + 8 latent incoherent revertWindow fixtures
description:
Found 2026-07-28 by the playhead-auz3 sweep. STATIC analysis only — the build budget was consumed by the full battery run, so these are CANDIDATES, not mutation-proven survivors. Treat accordingly.

Its own comment states the contract as 'must not synthesize a window', and its only probe is confirmedWindows(). A synthesized promotion lands .applied, which that accessor filters out — so the assertion cannot fail for the reason the test names. Identical defect to gateFlipClearsSuggestEntry's step 4, repaired in auz3. REPAIR: add #expect(await orchestrator.activeWindowIDs().isEmpty) and assert the call returns false. HONEST CAVEAT from the sweeper: it could not name a source mutation that reddens this even after repair (the phantom-id guard is suggestWindows.removeValue returning nil), so this is a weak-observable finding rather than a demonstrated coverage hole. Repair it, but do not expect a dramatic mutation kill.

INERT TODAY because persistRevertedAdWindow makes no feedbackAssetMatches call, which is exactly why playhead-auz3's bead ruled this family out. But revertWindow is the ONE correction seam whose siblings all have that ownership check, and the battery's KNOWN GAP note says it is waiting on a production caller. title: Banner volume may spike: unanchored fusion spans now surface as suggest-tier cards (playhead-2350 consequence)
description:
NEEDS-DAN, product judgment. Consequence of playhead-2350 (merged 08c68bc4), flagged by its implementer and confirmed by me before merging.

WHAT CHANGED: 2350 demotes any fusion span with an unanchored edge from eligibilityGate=eligible to markOnly. markOnly routes into the suggest tier (SkipOrchestrator:2042, :2113), which emits a Yes/No banner card at ingest. Previously such a span could sit at 'eligible' but unpromoted — and therefore SILENT.

THE RISK: essentially no dogfood span currently carries a rediff slot or a stinger snap, so in practice nearly every fusion detection is unanchored. That makes this close to ONE CARD PER DETECTION. If that holds on a real device it is a flood, and it cuts directly against the product line 'Respect your attention' — an app that interrupts you constantly to ask whether it was right has replaced one annoyance with another.

WHY I MERGED IT ANYWAY rather than shipping it dormant: it is your stated certainty-tiered policy (auto-skip the deterministic, MARK/banner the uncertain, banner as the safety valve), and the two failure modes are not symmetric — a surplus banner costs one tap, while a wrong auto-skip eats show audio, which is what actually destroys trust. Blocking unsafe auto-skip was the P0; banner volume is tunable.

WHAT TO DECIDE: install a build, listen to a real episode, and count the cards. Then choose among: (a) accept the volume; (b) surface only the top-N most-confident markOnly spans per episode; (c) require a minimum presence confidence before a markOnly span earns a card; (d) make markOnly silent-but-marked on the timeline, reserving cards for a narrower tier — noting this drops the banner safety valve 2350 deliberately preserved.

Kill switch if it is intolerable before a decision: AdDetectionConfig.unanchoredExtentBlocksAutoSkip = false reverts to the old behaviour — but that reinstates auto-skip on invented edges, so it is a last resort, not a tuning knob.

Related: playhead-2350 (the gate), playhead-qs0d (widens auto-skip and leans on this gate), playhead-1mq1.1 (banner copy — the words on these cards).
acceptance_criteria: Dan installs a build, listens to at least one full real episode, and records the observed card count per episode. A decision is recorded among accept / top-N / confidence-floor / silent-marking, and implemented. If volume is accepted, the reasoning is written down so a future reader does not treat it as an oversight.
notes:
2026-07-28 FIRST DEVICE OBSERVATION (Dan, dogfood build add2f623): THE CARDS DID NOT FEEL INTRUSIVE. Volume is not the problem we feared.

Dan also observed that banners appeared to come up mainly AFTER he manually corrected or tapped 'hearing an ad' — i.e. the suggest tier did not obviously fire on its own at detection time. If that holds, the premise of this bead is inverted: playhead-2350's markOnly demotion is NOT producing a card-per-detection flood, and the open question becomes the opposite one — whether detections are reaching the suggest tier at all.

CONSEQUENCE FOR playhead-bllt: Dan chose 'close it now, consistency wins' having accepted MORE banner cards as a cost. That cost now looks much smaller than priced. The decision stands; the tradeoff was over-stated in its favour, not against.

NOT YET CONFIRMED BY DATA: the diagnostics bundle from this session was not retrievable (saved to a path that does not exist on this machine), so banner_count and the suggest/auto_skipped split are still unmeasured. Priority dropped P1 -> P2 on the felt-experience evidence, but keep it open until a tally is actually read — 'felt fine on one episode' is weaker than a number, and one listen is one show.

title: View layer reads live podcastId AFTER an await, misattributing corrections on a mid-flight episode change
description:
Found 2026-07-27 by the eighth reviewer during the playhead-i08e loop. PRE-EXISTING, in the VIEW layer — one level above SkipOrchestrator, so it is NOT fixed by i08e (which hardened the orchestrator's own seams against exactly this class of race).

NowPlayingView.swift:569-575 and TranscriptPeekView.swift:744-773 read runtime.currentPodcastId AFTER awaiting store.recordVeto / submitNotAdChunks. If the listener switches episodes while that await is in flight, the correction's receipt, trust penalty, and per-show threshold-control sample are all attributed to the NEW episode's show rather than the one the user actually corrected.

This is the same defect class i08e just eliminated inside SkipOrchestrator: capture the attribution identity BEFORE the suspension, not after. The orchestrator now binds podcastId/assetId/spans as locals ahead of every await; the view layer still resolves them late.

CONSEQUENCE: a correction can teach the wrong show. With per-show threshold control flag-OFF today the controller half is latent, but the RECEIPT and TRUST penalty are live, so a mis-timed episode switch writes a real durable correction against the wrong podcast.

FIX SHAPE (mirrors the orchestrator fix): capture podcastId (and any other attribution identity) into a local before the first await, and pass that captured value to the post-await calls instead of re-reading runtime.currentPodcastId. Verify no other view-layer correction entry point does the same late read.

Related: playhead-i08e (orchestrator-side fix + the behavioural lifecycle-race test pattern that can be reused here — see SkipOrchestratorRevertLifecycleRaceTests and revertPersistenceBarrierForTesting).
acceptance_criteria: The correction's attribution identity is captured before the first suspension point in both NowPlayingView and TranscriptPeekView, and a mid-flight episode change can no longer misattribute the receipt, trust penalty, or controller sample. A behavioural regression test parks the gesture at the await, switches episodes to a DIFFERENT show, and asserts the durable receipt names the original show — following the SkipOrchestratorRevertLifecycleRaceTests pattern. Audit the remaining view-layer correction entry points for the same late-read.
close_reason: Merged to main as 204d617f. RESOLVED AS ALREADY-FIXED + RAILS ADDED, not as a repair. The audit found the late runtime.currentPodcastId read was removed by b072e72f — the playhead-o4qr merge, 2026-07-26 — ONE DAY BEFORE I filed this bead from a pre-merge worktree. My filing was based on stale evidence; the implementer verified rather than inheriting the claim. Every view-layer correction entry point was audited with its capture position recorded (NowPlayingView onNotAnAd/confirm/revert/accept/decline, onAlwaysSkipSponsorAsync, onRevertAdWindows/onMarkAd, the transcript Button, NowPlayingViewModel.handleListenRewindAwaitingAction and .reportHearingAd, TranscriptPeekView submitMarkedChunks/submitUntranscribedTailMark/submitNotAdChunks, AdRegionPopover, AdBannerView) — NONE has the late read. Since nothing pinned the fixed behaviour, this adds the rails: 5 XCTest source canaries over the entry points, plus a behavioural race (transcriptVetoSurvivesEpisodeReplacement) that drives the transcript veto's production entry form, parks it at revertPersistenceBarrierForTesting, replaces the episode with a DIFFERENT show, and asserts the receipt names the original show, the controller sample lands on it and nowhere else, and the trust penalty is on it — plus staleTranscriptVetoIsRefused pinning the other half. Honest scope, corrected in review: the source canary is the only rail on the view LAYER; the behavioural test drives SkipOrchestrator directly and proves the seam behind the capture honours it.

title: Listen-revert gesture never feeds the per-show threshold controller (recordListenRevert has no production caller)
description:
Found 2026-07-26/27 during the playhead-i08e review loop (independently noted by two reviewers, R1 and R3). PRE-EXISTING — not introduced by i08e.

SkipOrchestrator.recordListenRevert() carries a doc comment calling the listen-revert the canonical FALSE-POSITIVE signal, and it does call recordThresholdControlSignal(.falsePositive, ...). But it has NO production caller. The live banner Listen path routes through retireLiveSkipForListen() + recordListenRewind(), neither of which reaches recordThresholdControlSignal. Similarly, NowPlayingView's closure named 'revertWindow' actually routes to denyAutoSkippedBanner, not to SkipOrchestrator.revertWindow.

CONSEQUENCE: when a listener hits Listen on a banner — arguably the single most common 'you were wrong' gesture — the per-show threshold controller learns nothing from it. The calibration signal the code documents as canonical is not wired.

WHY NOT FIXED IN i08e: wiring it CHANGES CALIBRATION BEHAVIOR (it would start moving per-show thresholds on a gesture that currently doesn't), which is a product decision about what counts as a false-positive signal, not a review fix. Note per-show threshold control is currently flag-OFF in production (perShowThresholdControlEnabled = false), so this is latent rather than live — but it means the flag would ship under-wired if flipped on.

NEEDS-DAN: is a listen-revert a false-positive calibration signal? It is weaker evidence than an explicit 'not an ad' tap — the listener may simply be curious. Options: (a) wire it at full weight, (b) wire it at reduced weight, (c) leave it unwired and delete the misleading doc comment + the dead method.

RELATED dead/misleading surface found alongside: SkipOrchestrator.revertWindow also has no production caller. And TranscriptPeekView writes two .manualVeto receipts per gesture (:751 directly, then again via revertByTimeRange) — pre-existing, dedupes to one row via appendCorrectionEvent's identity key, so not a live bug, but it is confusing.
acceptance_criteria: Dan decides whether listen-revert is a calibration signal and at what weight. Implement the decision: either wire the gesture to the controller (at the chosen weight, with a test proving the sample lands) or remove the dead recordListenRevert/revertWindow methods and the doc comments that claim a wiring that does not exist. Either way the code and its comments must agree. Audit the remaining SkipOrchestrator public surface for other methods with no production caller.

title: fast-gate.sh: preflight the toolchain and print a terminal PASS/FAIL line so piped invocations can't read as green
description:
Found 2026-07-26 while gating playhead-txq3/i6oi. Two ways a fast-gate run can LOOK green when it did nothing:

1) TOOLCHAIN: this box's global xcode-select is /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools (no xcodebuild/simctl — see the 2026-07-16 gotcha). Running scripts/fast-gate.sh WITHOUT DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode-beta.app/Contents/Developer dies in ~1s with 'xcode-select: error: tool xcodebuild requires Xcode', zero tests run. The script propagates that correctly (RC=1), but the output is two lines that scroll past and look like a config notice, not a gate failure.

2) PIPE MASKING: the natural agent/human invocation 'scripts/fast-gate.sh | tail -40' returns TAIL's exit code (0), silently discarding the gate verdict. This actually happened this session and produced a false green until caught. set -o pipefail inside the script does not help — the masking pipe is OUTSIDE it.

Neither is a logic bug in the script; both are ergonomics that make a no-op run indistinguishable from a pass on casual reading. For a wrapper whose entire purpose is being the trustworthy gate, that is worth closing.

PROPOSED:
- Preflight: verify 'xcodebuild -version' succeeds before doing anything; if not, print an actionable one-liner naming DEVELOPER_DIR and the Xcode path found on this box, and exit non-zero.
- Terminal summary: always print a final unmistakable line, e.g. 'fast-gate: PASS (N tests)' or 'fast-gate: FAIL rc=N — M failing tests' as the LAST line, so even a piped/truncated invocation shows the verdict in the tail.
- Optional: if the run produced 0 executed tests, treat it as FAIL regardless of rc — 'no tests ran' must never read as success.
acceptance_criteria: Running fast-gate.sh with the global CommandLineTools toolchain and no DEVELOPER_DIR prints an actionable toolchain error naming DEVELOPER_DIR and exits non-zero. Every run ends with a single unambiguous PASS/FAIL summary line as its last stdout line, including the failing-test count. A run that executes zero tests exits non-zero. Verify by invoking through a masking pipe and confirming the verdict is still visible in the tail.
notes:
2026-07-27 PROMOTED P2->P1 and SCOPE EXPANDED. A second, worse fast-gate.sh defect found independently TWICE today (by me and by the ia2s implementer): the wedged-simulator auto-recovery is gated on [ -n "$SIM_ID" ], and SIM_ID is ONLY ever derived from an 'id=' inside PLAYHEAD_DEST. The default DEST is 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17' — no id= — so SIM_ID is always empty and THE RECOVERY PATH HAS NEVER FIRED IN NORMAL USE. The wrapper documents self-healing behaviour it does not actually have.

This cost real time today: three consecutive gate runs died to 'Mach error -308 (ipc/mig) server died' / 'test runner exited with code 0 before establishing connection' with ZERO tests executed, and the built-in recovery stayed silent every time. Manual 'simctl shutdown && simctl erase && simctl boot' fixed it instantly, and a re-run then passed 13/13. Passing PLAYHEAD_SIM_ID explicitly is the only way to reach the recovery code today.

FIX: when PLAYHEAD_DEST has no id=, resolve the UDID by NAME via 'xcrun simctl list devices --json' (match the device name + booted/available state) and populate SIM_ID from that. Then the documented Snag-3 recovery works as written. Note the erase also fails if the device is still Booted ('Unable to erase contents and settings in current state: Booted') — shut down and CONFIRM shutdown before erasing, don't just fire the commands in sequence.

Also fold in the original y27o scope (toolchain preflight + terminal PASS/FAIL line + fail-on-zero-tests). 'Zero tests executed' is exactly what happened here three times, and a run that executes no tests must never exit 0.
