title: A listener can tell us anything in 10 seconds: in-app feedback channel
description: Customer outcome: friction-free 'this felt wrong' → our inbox. Settings + banner-context entry point; prefilled mail compose (or share sheet) with app version + optional diagnostics bundle (legal checklist applies — never audio/transcripts). No server required.
notes:
2026-07-27 DAN: implement this bead with the iterative-implementation-with-review-loops skill (implementer subagent, then FRESH reviewer subagents that FIX what they find, until TWO CONSECUTIVE zero-finding rounds; cap 20 per this repo's convention, not the skill's default 5).

APPLY THE COST PROTOCOL learned on playhead-i08e (see memory feedback_review_loop_economics_2026-07-27) — without it rounds balloon to ~85 min each:
- Give every round a HARD BUILD BUDGET (12-16 xcodebuild invocations) and require it to report usage.
- FULL GATE EXACTLY ONCE, at the end of a round, on the final committed state. Validate everything else against focused suites. Running the full gate mid-round adds no information and costs ~5.5 min a time.
- COMMIT AFTER EVERY DISCRETE STEP. Rounds get interrupted; uncommitted work is lost work.
- Don't re-derive known checks by hand — scripts/mutation-battery.sh (on main) runs the established battery in one command.
- MUTATE, DON'T READ: a finding you cannot demonstrate with a surviving mutation probably isn't one; a mutation that survives the gate definitely is. On i08e, three separate rounds found mutations surviving the whole ~8.5k-test gate, and one round's confident 'zero findings' was later proved wrong.
Measured costs on this box: warm no-op focused run 68s; focused run after touching a production file 85s; full gate ~5.5 min; whole battery 10 builds/~17 min.

Every round must set DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode-beta.app/Contents/Developer, never pipe a gate through a mask (a pipeline returns the LAST exit code, so a failed gate reads as 0), and never run two xcodebuild processes concurrently (16 GB box; the loser is OOM-killed with no test failure).
close_reason: Merged to main as 1d0b1e91. Settings -> Feedback -> 'Tell us anything', plus banner long-press -> 'Something felt wrong'; prefilled mail compose with app/OS/device version (+ moment offset and salted reference for the banner entry), opt-in scrubbed diagnostics bundle, share-sheet fallback. COMPOSES the existing diagnostics export service/presenter/coordinator rather than adding a second mail path — the hatch ALIASES whichever diagnostics hatch the configuration compiled instead of duplicating the environment graph a third time. Banner coexistence with jw63.1's one-tap Yes/No is by ADDING NOTHING (context menu = zero pixels, zero taps on the primary path); the card already carries six controls and a seventh would compete with the one signal we most want. Independence enforced mechanically: the affordance depends only on whether a handler is wired, never on tier or feedback-claim flags. Bundle attachment OPT-IN default OFF — the bundle passes the legal checklist but consent is a separate product call, and silently attaching device-state JSON to a one-sentence note undercuts the About screen's 'Your podcasts never leave your device' promise this channel exists to reinforce. Every failure downgrades rather than aborts; the share fallback deliberately KEEPS Copy/Messages/AirDrop because the failure mode is a listener with no route at all. canSendMail is an injected closure so BOTH branches are real simulator assertions, not skipped tests. 47 new tests incl. a mechanical external-copy-rule sweep and a sentinel sweep over the entire envelope. Budget 3/12. ONE ITEM NEEDS DAN BEFORE RELEASE: the recipient is d.abrams@icloud.com (his real inbox) — no support domain exists in the repo and shipping a bouncing address would be a silent dead end, so it was used deliberately and pinned by a test in exactly one constant. Sign off or swap it.

title: Day-0 aligner monotonic-reject is the recall CEILING (Fresh Air) — recover multi-break non-monotonic chains; + K=2-varied-persona config
description:
## Finding (minutes-apart measurement 2026-07-23)
The bottleneck for day-0 recall is NOT bandwidth — it's the byte aligner's **wholesale monotonic-clean reject**. 5 of 12 varied-B alignments were rejected, ALL on `monotonic_clean=False` (multi-break non-monotonic chaining), NONE on chainedFractionB<0.5. FRESH AIR is the cautionary case: persona divergence demonstrably exists (frac_b 0.917, ~8% differs = real rotated ads) but the strict monotonic gate harvested **0 slots** -> Fresh Air day-0 detects nothing. More K does NOT fix this (both varied personas failed the same gate); it needs an aligner fix.

## Fix A — aligner (recovers Fresh Air-class shows)
`RediffByteAligner`/`gateAndDiffBytes`: when the chained runs are non-monotonic (a later ad break's run sorts before an earlier one due to differing ad LENGTHS shifting byte offsets), the aligner drops the WHOLE fetch. Instead: tolerate/segment around non-monotonic breaks (align each contiguous monotonic segment, or a bounded dropped-run count) so a 0.92-aligned fetch with real divergent ads isn't discarded wholesale. CAUTION: `gateAndDiffBytes` is SHARED with the lagged path — measure lagged-path impact (false-widening, boundary) before/after; gate behind a flag if risky.

## Fix B — day-0 persona config (production K decision)
`RediffActivation.dayZeroKWayFetchCount` + the persona selection: production K = **2 VARIED personas DISTINCT from the download's own UA**. The download persona collides (byte-identical) on pinned shows, so re-fetching with it is a wasted ~54MB. Pick K=2 from {Mac, Overcast, empty} that differ from the download persona. ~108MB/play. (This is also the lagged productionKWayFetchCount question — currently 1; day-0 wants >=2 varied.)

## Evidence
Minutes-apart run: Conan single(same-persona)=0 / union=4 slots(211s); Fresh Air both varied personas monotonic-rejected=0; SYSK +1 slot. Data + driver in scratchpad/rediff-minutes/. Feeds the xsdz.36 day-0 activation go/no-go.

title: day-0 >=2-persona quorum is net-negative — add quorum-unreachable->single-fetch fallback + reconsider wholesale monotonic reject
description:
## Finding (spot-check measurement 2026-07-23, N=6 gold DAI episodes / 18 breaks)
Day-0 byte-exact detection is PRECISE and effective, but the `RediffSlotOwnership.kWayRobustPlayedSlots` **>=2-persona quorum** (day-0 design choice, stricter than the lagged k-way union) was **net-negative**: k-way lift = union - single = **-2** (recovered 0, cost 2).

### Numbers (spot-check; NOT a corpus verdict)
- Excluding 4 structurally-blind host-read/baked breaks (DOAC baked + THEMOVE host-read Hims/Lagoon — rediff-blind by design, FM's lane): **14 byte-rotating DAI breaks**.
- **single-fetch (1 persona): 14/14 = 100%** of DAI breaks. **>=2-persona union: 12/14 = 85.7%** (loses 2).
- Boundary: sub-second median (start p50 0.49s, end p50 0.20s) — byte-exact where it fires.
- Precision: union 19 slots, 6 overlap-no-gold but ALL 6 are REAL ads gold under-labels (Progressive/AppleTV+/WeatherTech/etc) -> ~0 genuine FP.

### Root cause of the -2
On THEMOVE (libsyn), mac+overcast personas were rejected by the byte gate's **wholesale monotonic reject** (chainedFraction 0.94 — HIGH, not a re-encode; a single non-monotonic run drops the WHOLE fetch's alignment). So only 1/3 personas aligned -> the >=2 quorum was **unreachable** -> minted NOTHING, while single iPhone cleanly caught THEMOVE's dynamic pre-roll [0,74.3] + post-roll [2779,2853]. Where all 3 personas aligned (conan/morbid/smartless/SYSK), single-fetch already caught everything -> the quorum's collision-recovery benefit never triggered.

## Fixes
1. **Quorum-unreachable -> single-fetch fallback (targeted, safe):** when <2 personas align for a region, fall back to the single-fetch (highest-aligned-persona) slots instead of minting nothing. Only kicks in when the quorum can't form -> recovers recall, doesn't touch precision-when-quorum-forms. Recovers both THEMOVE breaks.
2. **Loosen the wholesale monotonic reject (delicate — shared gate):** `gateAndDiffBytes` rejects the whole B on ANY dropped/non-monotonic run; tolerate a bounded dropped-run count so a 0.94-aligned fetch isn't discarded wholesale. NOTE this gate is shared with the LAGGED path — measure impact there before changing.

## Caveats / next
Spot-check N=6; A-side ~2mo older than B (maximizes rotation — favorable). The k-way collision-recovery benefit IS real per the xsdz.36.2 spike ("B vs C missed mid-2; B+C+D recovered") — rare, may show on a larger corpus, so DON'T drop the quorum entirely; add the fallback + a corpus run. Directly informs the xsdz.36 day-0 activation go/no-go: day-0 byte-exact is a strong deterministic DAI detector (unlike the FM-nondeterminism-blocked lagged auto-skip) once the quorum fallback lands.
notes: MINUTES-APART MEASUREMENT (2026-07-23, decisive) — CORRECTS the fix. At realistic close timing (A + persona-varied B fetched back-to-back, 4 live DAI shows): same-persona single-fetch COLLIDES ~50% — Conan + Fresh Air (both simplecast/client-pinned) returned byte-IDENTICAL to A (frac_b=1.000), K=1 same-persona harvested ZERO slots (cache-buster does NOT defeat same-persona collision). A VARIED persona breaks it: Conan Overcast recovered the ENTIRE 210.7s ad load (pre+2mid+post) single-fetch missed; SYSK +15s. Total k-way recovery 5 slots/225.8s. THEMOVE/SYSK (libsyn/omny) re-stitch per-request so single suffices there; the collisions are exactly on the PINNED networks. So a >=2-AGREEMENT quorum is WRONG (Conan: only Overcast diverged -> quorum drops the 211s). FIX (redirected): day-0 uses UNION (quorum=1) = the lagged unionedPlayedSlots, NOT kWayRobustPlayedSlots. Precision guard = the per-persona byte gate (spot-check ~0 FP). CONFIG (measurement-forced): production K = 2 VARIED personas DISTINCT from the download's own UA (never re-fetch with the download persona — that's the collision); ~108MB/play. K=3 buys marginal insurance, would NOT rescue Fresh Air (aligner ceiling, see below).

title: 3xtw/cthe: reconcile the two 'ready' checkmark indicators before wiring Episode.coverageSummary
description: EpisodeListView renders BOTH the new EpisodePreparationControl - which shows a checkmark.circle/mutedSage in its .ready state (EpisodePreparationControl.swift:54-55) - AND the existing playhead-cthe readiness checkmark (libraryRowShouldShowReadinessCheckmark -> checkmark.circle/mutedSage, EpisodeListView.swift:478-481). Today there is NO double-render because cthe keys on Episode.coverageSummary via derivePlaybackReadiness, and coverageSummary is DORMANT (no pipeline writer) so derivePlaybackReadiness returns .none and the cthe checkmark is always hidden. The new control instead derives .ready live from AnalysisStore coverage (EpisodePreparationStatusModel.analysisFraction). title: 3xtw: 'Download & Analyze' does not promote an ALREADY-queued background analysis job to the .now lane
description: markEpisodeUserIntent / enqueueUserIntentAnalysis route the NEXT enqueue for an episode to priority 20 (.now lane). But AnalysisStore.insertJob is INSERT OR IGNORE keyed on workKey (Playhead/Persistence/AnalysisStore/AnalysisStore.swift:8378). If an analysis job with the same workKey is ALREADY queued (the auto-pipeline enqueued it earlier), the user-intent enqueue is a silent no-op: the existing row keeps its background priority (0), and the one-shot flag is consumed (AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:793-794) without promoting it. This is documented as intended (AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:653-656) and the control still shows live 'analyzing' status - BUT this is exactly the 'starving background job' case the feature exists to accelerate (the foreground on-demand reliability fix). For an already-enqueued episode the tap gives status, not the promised .now preemption.
design: Suggested fix: in the user-intent enqueue path, when insertJob returns false (no insert = row already exists), UPDATE the existing job's priority to 20 guarded to state='queued' (never a leased/running job), then wakeSchedulerLoop() so it re-ranks into the .now lane and preemptLowerLanes fires. Must coordinate with playhead-glo9 (opportunistic backlog drain / admission matrix) and respect the epoch/generation stamping. Judgement: NOT a fix-forward - it is a real feature-reliability gap but the behavior is intentional+documented, no crash/regression, and promoting an in-progress job is a design decision (lease/epoch correctness) better made deliberately.
notes:
## QUEUE 2 — EXTENDED to eight (Dan 2026-08-02)

    3nfa(done) -> le02(done) -> bllt -> ug9m -> pggn -> kkzu -> kanf -> 5n8k

**Slots 7 and 8 added on Dan's instruction. Rationale:**

**kanf (7) — TIMELINESS, the magic lever.** "Download & Analyze" routes the NEXT enqueue to
priority 20 (.now lane), but `insertJob` is INSERT OR IGNORE on workKey. If the auto-pipeline
already queued that episode, the user-intent enqueue is a SILENT NO-OP: the row keeps background
priority 0 and the one-shot flag is consumed without promoting. So the tap gives status, not the
promised preemption — and it fails in exactly the case the feature exists for, an
already-queued starving background job. Dan's standing bar is that the work must be finished
BEFORE he presses play; this is a user asking for that explicitly and being ignored.
It sits beside kkzu deliberately: both are the download->analysis path that feeds the
"analyzed before play" population.
NOTE the bead's own judgement: promoting an IN-PROGRESS job is a lease/epoch design decision.
Scope to state='queued' only, never a leased/running row. Coordinate with playhead-glo9.

**5n8k (8) — the triage tax, and the integrity of every verdict.** The coarse-pass diagnostic
observer is a `nonisolated(unsafe) static var`; under Swift Testing's in-process parallelism another
test's coarse pass lands in this test's capture box. It appeared in essentially EVERY gate triage
on 2026-08-02. What makes it worth a slot rather than a shrug: the failure is FAST (0.14-0.27s),
which is the shape the triage rule reserves for REAL defects — the >=97s load-flake heuristic does
not apply. So it costs a full triage round every time and looks like a regression in whatever is
under test. Fix direction: per-test scoping (task-local or a confirmation-scoped install that
fails loudly on double-install), not a global that silently interleaves.

Both are device-free and on-box verifiable. Constraint unchanged: Dan is away and cannot install
a build or produce a device pull.

title: 3xtw: broadcastBackgroundProgress completion-reset reopens the monotonicity window it guards
description: DownloadManager.broadcastBackgroundProgress (Playhead/Services/Downloads/DownloadManager.swift:422) drops out-of-order background-transfer ticks via a high-water mark (lastBackgroundProgressBytes) so the delivered fraction is monotonic 'within a transfer'. On the completion tick (bytesWritten >= totalBytes) it resets the slot to nil (lines 433-434). Each didWriteData callback spawns an unstructured Task that hops to the actor (onBackgroundDownloadProgress ~line 1959), so Task execution order is NOT guaranteed. If the final (100%) tick's Task wins the race against an earlier tick's Task, the earlier tick then reads highWater = (nil ?? 0) = 0, passes the '>= highWater' guard, and broadcasts a regressed (<100%) fraction AFTER 100% was already delivered - the exact regression the guard exists to prevent. Window is bounded to between the 100% tick and the isCached flip (didFinishDownloadingTo).
design: Impact: sub-second progress-bar dip near completion in the new prepare control / Activity screen; largely masked because EpisodePreparationReadiness pins downloadFraction=1 once isDownloaded flips. Cosmetic + self-healing, no crash/data issue - hence P2 bead not fix-forward. Suggested fix: on completion keep the high-water at totalBytes (stragglers then drop) and rely on the existing fresh-start reset in backgroundDownload (~line 1382: lastBackgroundProgressBytes[episodeId]=nil) to clear it for a re-download; OR clear the slot in the didFinishDownloadingTo handler instead of on the byte threshold. SECONDARY (same area, optional): progressSnapshot() (line 1836) reads only foregroundAssistProgress and explicitly excludes the background lane, and broadcastBackgroundProgress deliberately bypasses noteTransferProgress. So on a COLD list refresh an in-flight BACKGROUND (auto pre-cache) download shows no download fraction in the prepare control until the first live tick arrives via observeDownloadProgress. Minor new-surface nicety (bg transfers were log-only pre-3xtw). Consider treating bgInFlightEpisodes as an in-flight signal in EpisodePreparationStatusModel.refresh.
notes: INVESTIGATION 2026-07-24: the fix is ALREADY PRESENT in main (DownloadManager.swift broadcastBackgroundProgress ~line 505): the completion slot is no longer reset to nil — it is set to `min(bytesWritten, totalBytes)`, pinning the high-water at totalBytes so a post-100% straggler fails the `>= highWater` guard and is dropped. An explicit comment there describes the y3q5 race + fix; the fresh-start reset in backgroundDownload clears the slot for a re-download. No dedicated regression test was found for it. RECOMMEND: close as fixed (cosmetic P2), or add a focused monotonicity test if a regression guard is wanted. The SECONDARY item (cold-refresh bg-lane fraction via bgInFlightEpisodes in EpisodePreparationStatusModel.refresh) remains unaddressed.

title: Chromaprint rediff path: silence false-sync guard (2s clean-run floor OR silence-content reject)
description: Split out from xsdz.73 (which was CLOSED — the byte-exact RediffByteAligner is structurally immune to silence false-sync). The REAL problem the rediff test found lives in the CHROMAPRINT fuzzy-match path: l2f-dai-rediff.py uses MIN_RUN_FPS=8 (~1s) and demonstrably leaks spurious short false-sync runs on byte-identical/repetitive silence — on freshair it produced a 1.0s run @ offset -108 and a 3.0s run @ offset 3265 (nonsensical offsets = classic silence coincidence) that fragmented one 132s break into 25.4s + 107.3s pieces. Its sibling rediff_multi.py already hard-codes MIN_RUN=32768 (~2s, 'skip byte-identical silence'). FIX: port a >=2s clean-run floor (or silence-content/low-entropy rejection) into the production chroma fallback (Playhead/Services/AdDetection/RediffDiffer.swift) — but FIRST confirm whether any production/eval flow actually consumes the chromaprint output vs the byte aligner (byte-align is PRIMARY + immune; chroma is the fallback, so impact is narrow -> P2). Evidence: scratchpad per-pair JSON from the xsdz.73 verify.

title: Cross-device rediff: the user's own 2nd device as a B-side provider (defeats IP/device-pinned rotation)
description:
Dan 2026-07-21. A rediff B-side variant that uses the user's OWN second device (Mac + iPhone) as the divergent fetch. Different device = different UA + often different IP (cellular vs wifi) => the ad server draws a DIFFERENT DAI fill => rediff has something to diff, WITHOUT waiting >=24h and WITHOUT a bot-UA trick. Directly defeats the IP/device-pinned-rotation case (the one vector same-device context-variation can't beat on a single network).

LEGAL (my read, NOT counsel - confirm against the 2026-07-17 fingerprint-facts opinion that cleared the CROSS-USER atlas; cross-device same-user is a strict, safer SUBSET): safe IF (1) sync via the USER'S OWN private iCloud/CloudKit private DB, NEVER our servers - keeps the on-device/no-our-cloud posture ([[project_legal_ondevice]]); (2) sync FINGERPRINTS (chroma) + ad-slot maps, NOT audio/transcripts; (3) the rediff diff + ad determination still run ON-DEVICE. Then it's the user's own data, in the user's own cloud, classified on the user's own device.

EFFICACY: strongest when the two devices are on DIFFERENT networks (different IP); the hole is both on the same home wifi + purely-IP-pinned server (then same fill). Complements - does not replace - xsdz.45 (context-variation) and xsdz.64 (bot-UA). Note: THEMOVE is per-request (rediff test 2026-07-21: 6/6 same-client fetches distinct), so cross-device is a BONUS (free B-side) there, and the real payoff is on any pinned show. Part of the [[feedback_detection_portfolio_belt_suspenders]] rediff-activation cluster (xsdz.36).

title: Rediff-complement: cross-episode ad-creative fingerprint bank (day-0, non-rotating, re-encode-robust DAI)
description: Fable rediff-alternatives brainstorm 2026-07-21. Rediff exploits 'same episode differs across TIME' and is blind to non-rotating/baked-in shows (~12-15pct DAI), defeated by re-encode CDNs, and lagged (>=24h so drop-day listeners get width retroactively). This epic builds the COMPLEMENT: exploit 'same AD appears across DIFFERENT episodes/shows' (programmatic DAI is massively repeated) via a cross-episode ad-creative FINGERPRINT BANK that catches a DAI ad DAY-0, on a non-rotating show, with NO re-fetch. Two fused members: (1) ad-copy TEXT fingerprint (transcript MinHash, immune to any audio re-encode, strong detection, atom-granular width); (2) acoustic/chroma creative fingerprint (survives re-encode, transfers known creative extent = rediff-grade sample-exact WIDTH day-0). Flywheel: more listening = bigger bank = more day-0 hits. Ship a STATIC STARTER bank of top-N national creatives as an app resource (like the stinger bank) to kill empty-library cold-start. Layered composition (auto-skip gated on DETERMINISTIC members only): bank first (day-0 repeated) -> rediff confirms/sharpens on re-analysis -> specialist backstops the novel/smooth tail -> stinger structural boundaries. Complementary cold-starts: rediff-blind=never-rotating show, bank-blind=never-before-seen creative; their INTERSECTION falls to the specialist; bank self-heals after first contact. On-device mandate: bank from user listening + static app-shipped starter, NO cloud. Consolidates dormant spikes xsdz.17/.47/.33/.51 (cross-checks xsdz.46/.53). Builds on ChromaFingerprinter, ad_copy_fingerprints, repeated_ad_cache. Avoid dead-ends: acoustic splice (recall 21pct, xsdz.15 OFF), MusicUnderstanding (AUC 0.495).

title: AnalysisJobRunner subscribe-after-start race: events has no replay, can miss .completed under load then 300s timeout then spurious transcription failure
description:
Found by de-flake2 investigation (2026-07-20, could NOT reproduce so filed not fixed). AnalysisJobRunner.run subscribes to transcriptEngine.events (~L613) AFTER startTranscription + finishAppending. TranscriptEngineService.events has NO replay (L458/L991). So if the engine active task reaches emitEvent .completed BEFORE the runner subscribes -- plausible only under full-suite cooperative-pool saturation -- the runner misses .completed, waits out the Stage-3 300s timeout, and returns a spurious .failed transcription:zeroCoverage. Would surface as a heavy AnalysisJobRunner-test 300s hang/failure under load.

FIX (small but shipped-code async-ordering change, so its own reviewed change per the no-unilateral-change policy): move the `let transcriptStream = await transcriptEngine.events` subscription ABOVE startTranscription so the subscription is established before emission can begin (subscribe-before-start). Verify no other consumer relies on the current ordering.

Note: the 3 literal Stage-1 persistence tests are deterministic (episodeDurationSec persisted before the Stage-3 timeout) and passed 20/20 under load -- this production race is the real latent issue in that heavy path, not a test flake.

title: ud4n hardening: reconcileBackfillWindows read/write-ordering race can clobber a concurrently-applied row's decisionState
description:
Found by ud4n R1 review (2026-07-20). reconcileBackfillWindows reads the protected-set snapshot via fetchAdWindows OUTSIDE the reconcileBackfillAdWindows write transaction (two separate AnalysisStore actor hops). If a candidate->.applied transition (SkipOrchestrator.updateAdWindowDecision) lands BETWEEN the fetch and the reconcile write, the just-applied row is not in protectedIDs, so the content-addressed INSERT-OR-REPLACE (writes all 23 cols) clobbers decisionState back to .confirmed and loses wasSkipped in the DB.

IMPACT: narrow. Requires a backfill rerun concurrent with active auto-skip of the SAME span. In-memory orchestrator .applied still holds -> no live skip is undone in-session. But a subsequent relaunch preload reads the clobbered .confirmed row and could re-surface the span as a candidate. Pre-existing-category (no worse than pre-ud4n, which created duplicate rows on rerun).

FIX (needs Dan approval — ARCHITECTURAL change to the approved Design B reconcile contract): (a) fold the reconcilable-predicate filter INTO the store transaction so read+filter+write are atomic; OR (b) add a store-level guard in reconcileBackfillAdWindows: INSERT-OR-REPLACE must never overwrite a row whose EXISTING decisionState is terminal (.applied/.reverted). Option (b) is the tighter, more localized fix (a WHERE guard / pre-check inside the txn) and keeps persistence/detection decoupled. Recommend (b).
notes: ud4n R2 also flagged a RELATED, currently-UNREACHABLE variant: for a .reverted fusion row (which preloadEligibleDecisionStates does NOT preload), the collision-dropped window's AdDecisionResult is still forwarded in Step 17 and could transiently re-add that id in-memory as .confirmed. DB .reverted row stays protected by the collision guard + finalizeBackfill re-fetch reasserts DB truth. NOT reachable in current product (auto-skip default-OFF, so fusion rows never reach .applied/.reverted). Same fix (store-level terminal-guard) covers it. Awareness only.

title: iOS-27 error taxonomy gap in ChapterLabelingService + EpisodeSummaryExtractor (parallel to l3r2/cle1)
description:
Found by cle1 R1 review (2026-07-20). Two other FM-using services carry their own error taxonomies that still handle ONLY the legacy LanguageModelSession.GenerationError and were never migrated to the iOS-27 error types (LanguageModelError / LanguageModelSession.Error / GeneratedContent.ParsingError / SystemLanguageModel.Error) — the same gap l3r2 + cle1 closed for SemanticScanStatus:
- Playhead/Services/AdDetection/ChapterLabelingService.swift:404-429 (classify(_:))
- Playhead/Services/EpisodeSummaries/EpisodeSummaryExtractor.swift:585 (permissive-retry predicate)
On iOS 27 these misroute the new error shapes into their fallback buckets (e.g. refusal/context-overflow no longer recognized), degrading their retry/permissive behavior. Separate features from the ad path; fix mirrors cle1 (new-first/legacy-fallback casts, availability-guarded, watchOS omitted for SystemLanguageModel.Error). Phone-free.

title: Bridge remaining iOS-27 FoundationModels error types at SemanticScanStatus.from(error:)
description: playhead-l3r2 bridged the new iOS-27 LanguageModelError type (6 legacy GenerationError cases) so refusal (permissive-fallback) and contextSizeExceeded (smart-shrink) route correctly. But iOS 27 split the legacy LanguageModelSession.GenerationError into FOUR types, and three legacy cases migrated to types still UNHANDLED at SemanticScanStatus.from(error:) — so on iOS 27 (project min deployment target = 27, i.e. every user) they fall through to .failedTransient: (1) GenerationError.decodingFailure -> GeneratedContent.ParsingError (iOS 27.0-only); should map to .decodingFailure (gates simplifySchemaAndRetryOnce + the refinement graceful-abandon at FoundationModelClassifier.swift:2543). (2) GenerationError.concurrentRequests -> LanguageModelSession.Error.concurrentRequests; should map to .rateLimited (backoffAndRetry). LanguageModelSession.Error also has .transcriptMutationWhileResponding (a usage error) — decide status (likely .failedTransient). (3) GenerationError.assetsUnavailable -> SystemLanguageModel.Error.assetsUnavailable (thrown on iOS 27, in addition to pre-flight Availability.unavailable(.modelNotReady)); should map to .assetsUnavailable (deferUntilAssetsReady). ALSO: FoundationModelClassifier.swift refinement-refusal explanation fetchers at lines 4273-4274, 4490-4491, 4546-4547 cast only to legacy LanguageModelSession.GenerationError.refusal; on iOS 27 refusals throw LanguageModelError.refusal (different Refusal struct, whose .explanation is a Response<String>), so the diagnostic explanation text is silently lost on iOS 27. Add a from(languageModelError:) branch for these fetchers. Remedy: add availability-gated casts in from(error:) mapping to existing SemanticScanStatus values, with tests mirroring the l3r2 test; update the explanation fetchers to also handle LanguageModelError.refusal.

title: Spectral/matched-filter stinger capability: template-NCC detector for brief high-freq transition stingers (doac page-turn) that the envelope bank cannot hold
notes:
VALIDATED (2026-07-17, offline prototype). A raw-waveform matched filter (0.6s template, chunked FFT NCC) detects the doac page-turn stinger across BOTH episodes at 0.77-1.00 NCC, threshold ~0.45-0.5, content baseline <=0.13 = clean bimodal precision. Finds ALL labeled mid-roll boundaries + internal ad-to-ad splices + GOLD-MISSED breaks (07-09 ~1651-1668, 07-13 ~1614-1632) => higher coverage than transcript gold + doubles as a gold-audit signal. A template from one episode generalizes to the other (banked template works on unseen episodes). Gives EXACT (~sub-second) ad boundaries -> feeds the crisp/skip lane like rediff + clips FM over-anchors (FIX-A pattern). SPEC at scratchpad/promptiter/spectral-stinger-spec.md: new templateStingers section in StingerBank.json (PCM base64 ~26KB/show), SpectralStingerDetector (vDSP/Accelerate cross-correlation on device, gate to candidate regions or run in the background rediff pass, NOT hot path), emit .stingerMatch boundary evidence. AUTO-MINES (cluster tight transients cross-episode) = scales, no hand-labels (Dan 8 marks were validation). title: Episode ad-atlas: cross-user FACTS federation — content-coordinate slot map makes width detection arithmetic (legal opinion 2026-07-17)
notes:
UNLOCKED by Dan's legal clarification 2026-07-17: sharing FACTS about a show (ad timestamps, intro/outro structure) across users is legally fine; content/audio/transcripts must never leave the device; processing stays on-device. THE KEY TECHNICAL INSIGHT: absolute timestamps do NOT federate for DAI (different users get different fills/widths at the same slots — user A has 62s at slot 2, user B has 93s). What IS universal across all users' copies is THE CONTENT (rediff's own foundation). So federate in CONTENT COORDINATES: (episode GUID, total content duration, slot insertion points in content-time, inter-slot content durations, fill-width distributions, pod grammar, show structure incl. intro/outro/stinger facts). THE PAYOFF — WIDTH BECOMES ARITHMETIC: a device knowing inter-slot content durations + its own presence cores (solved, 97.8% precision) computes its own fills: local gap between content landmarks MINUS known content duration = its ad width. One good observation by ANY teacher anywhere (rediff, premium diff xsdz.52, HLS manifest xsdz.50, byte dedup xsdz.51) makes width detection near-trivial for EVERY user of that episode — teachers become global, students become arithmetic. ALSO FEDERATES: per-show structure for cold-start (a new user inherits the show's stinger/grammar/slot map day-0 — the 7hm5 self-learning bank crowd-accelerates); slot count/grammar priors; (legal sub-check first) creative fingerprints for the xsdz.47 dictionary. ENGINEERING COSTS (the real work): (a) TRUST/ANTI-POISONING — quorum of k independent devices before a fact activates, plausibility bounds from show grammar, signed observations; a poisoned atlas must never eat content (veto valve stays the last line); (b) PRIVACY — contributed facts reveal listening; aggregate/anonymize/opt-in; (c) INFRA — preserves zero-marginal-cost monetization: CloudKit public database (free tier, Apple-native, no server) is the natural vehicle. notes:

Suffix-array/dedup across the user's already-downloaded episodes: byte runs shared across episodes = inserted objects (creatives/stingers/intros) with EXACT edges — content is unique per episode, insertions repeat. notes:

MECHANISM: an acoustic object recurring across DIFFERENT shows in the user's library is an ad creative near-certainly (content never repeats cross-show; frequency-capped campaigns repeat constantly). Width = the creative's exact extent; POD width = creatives TILING the break end-to-end. title: SPIKE: codec-forensic splice scars — MP3 bit-reservoir breaks + mid-file Xing/LAME/ID3 tags as sample-exact DAI edges
notes:
WIDTH BRAINSTORM 2026-07-17 (Dan-approved filing). MECHANISM: DAI stitchers CONCATENATE compressed segments (proven — rediff only works because content outside slots is byte-identical across fetches). Concatenation forces structural scars in MP3: (a) bit-reservoir chain break at every splice (ad frames cannot reference content frames' reservoir; main_data_begin resets), (b) encoder-flush padding signatures, (c) stitched segments often retain their own mid-file Xing/LAME/Info headers and ID3/PRIV frames = 'a new file starts here'. Yields potentially SAMPLE-EXACT edges for microseconds of CPU, DAY-0, no second fetch, invisible to every acoustic method. EVIDENCE: xsdz.8 explicitly SKIPPED codec-level edit-scars with rationale 'concatenate without re-encoding -> artifacts below noise floor' — that reasoning is correct for ACOUSTIC artifacts and inverted for STRUCTURAL ones: concatenation-without-re-encode is exactly what CREATES byte-level scars. Nobody has looked. KILL TEST (afternoon, pure Python, no app changes): parse the 68 corpus mp3s' frame headers + reservoir pointers + mid-file tag scan; compare discontinuity locations against gold v6 edges (836b8188). Success = discontinuities cluster at gold edges with usable precision/recall on the DAI subset. BONUS same parser: bits/frame VBR allocation time series as a free 26ms-resolution segmentation signal.
SPIKE VERDICT: PARTIAL (2026-07-17). 4/5 scar classes empirically DEAD across all 35 gold episodes (~35h): zero mid-file Xing/Info/LAME/VBRI, zero embedded ID3, zero resyncs, zero param changes. Live class: main_data_begin reset — START-edge recall 90.3% +-2s (median hit 0.38s) on the 21 clean-encoder files (mdb0 base rate <=0.5%), but END recall 30.6%, event precision 16.1%, FA 5.9/content-hr; 14/35 files lack the signal entirely (themove mdb0=100%, unexplained 22-29%). VERDICT SHAPE: not a width oracle; a legitimate DAY-0 attention/snap-to-START signal per the lexical-as-attention principle, gated on per-file encoder base-rate. Composite recommendation: 44 slots + 51 dedup + 43 start-snapping, one parser.
CLOSING as superseded: Splice-calibration NO-GO verdict (2026-07-06) killed acoustic/codec splice detection — recall 21%, feasibility ceiling 6%, xsdz.15 stays OFF. Codec-forensic splice scars (bit-reservoir/Xing/LAME) are the same dead lever. Rediff (double-fetch byte diff) is the production DAI width oracle instead.

title: SPIKE: pipeline-seeded cross-episode stinger recurrence (the xsdz.42 GO path)
description: xsdz.42 proved a show's stinger recurs cross-episode at NCC 0.75-0.98 from just 2 episodes WITHOUT gold labels (Claim A), but naive top-motif mining banks the INTRO not the ad stinger because intros/splice-silence recur harder (Claim B false). Inherits the 'where are the ads' prior → sidesteps intro-dominance; stays gold-free, on-device (FFT envelope-NCC), saturates at 2 episodes. comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: SPIKE VERDICT: PARTIAL — zero-manual-audit self-learner is NO-GO as tested; consensus follow-up is the credible GO path (report xsdz42b-seeded-mining-spike-2026-07-16.md, prototype scripts/l2f-xsdz42b-seeded-stinger-mine.py). Seeding DID fix intro-dominance (false-intro top-1 1/9→0/9, e.g. nikki intro@61s → seeded@1569s inside a real break) and lifted stinger rank (top-k recovery NCC>=0.70: 2/6→4/6; smartless-post rank10→2, morbid-post missed→4). BUT it trades intro-dominance for a NEW failure: the hardest-recurring cue near a pipeline candidate is often an OUTRO / mid-ad cue / splice-silence / the pipeline's OWN false-positive candidate. On-ad-boundary top-1: 3/9→2/9 (no net gain); TOP-1 recovery only 1/6 (morbid-pre) — and top-1 is what a no-audit learner must trust. Seed sensitivity: no universal margin (conan needs tight region0, morbid/themove need >=30-60s, nikki fails at all) — right margin is a per-show function of pipeline boundary error, unknowable without gold. ROOT RISK: seeding inherits the pipeline's boundary-undersizing (playhead-4xqf, 10-40s mispositioning) + its FPs; envelope-NCC recurrence can't distinguish 'recurs near a TRUE boundary' from 'recurs near a FALSE candidate'. So: Claim A (stinger recurs, recoverable from 2 episodes) stays SOLID; naive AND seeded top-motif are both NO-GO for zero-audit; next idea below.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: xsdz.42c CONSENSUS spike VERDICT: PARTIAL — zero-audit auto-bank stays NO-GO, but consensus is the best gold-free candidate generator yet + reframes the path (report xsdz42c-consensus-mining-spike-2026-07-16.md). NUMBERS (top-1 on-ad-boundary: naive 3/9 → seeded 2/9 → CONSENSUS 4/9, doubles seeded): pipeline-FP top-1 landings seeded 1/9 → consensus 0/9 (voting eliminated every RANDOM per-episode FP — worked as designed); BUT outro top-1 landings 3/9 UNCHANGED (the wall: conan/unexplained/themove). KEY FINDING — why it fails: the pipeline SYSTEMATICALLY FP-flags the musical outro/theme near a candidate in EVERY episode, so the outro gets a consistent cross-episode partner at a stable relative offset and recurs as hard as the true stinger. Consensus suppresses RANDOM FPs + intros but is structurally blind to SYSTEMATIC recurring FPs. No (K,tol,offset,gate) is universal (outro-position gate fixes conan/unexplained but zeroes themove's post-roll ad). IMPORTANT SILVER LINING: the true stinger is at rank <=3 for EVERY recoverable side (conan post NCC 1.000 rank 3, morbid pre rank 0) — so a NEAR-zero-audit 'confirm 1 of 3 candidates' UX is viable NOW. Only 1 of 4 on-boundary wins is a genuine interior mid-roll (morbid); 3 are pre-roll freebies (ad at t=0).

title: Calibrate ad-break boundaries across continuous music beds
description: The completed retained-audio ear audit (Audits/earaudit-boundary-review-2026-07-12-6b11a85754db5d1ea2fb0243b3b53fd2c61375e7ba54ad42c444102690b98e99.json) found a recurring error cohort: shows carry the same music bed out of editorial content, through the ad break, and back into content. Detection often finds the transition zone but places one or both edges inconsistently within the music. Analyze the rebound decisions as full-break labels, identify the music-bed subset, and improve boundary calibration without treating an internal ad-to-ad transition as a break edge.
acceptance_criteria: Create a reproducible music-bed boundary cohort from fingerprint-bound human reviews; report start/end absolute error before and after; reduce both-edge error on that cohort without reducing ad-break precision or splitting multi-ad breaks; preserve full contiguous-break semantics.
notes:
DAN OBSERVATION (2026-07-15): Morbid has a consistent structural pattern — show -> musical outro -> ~90s commercial pod (1-2s variance per Dan's ear) -> musical intro -> show. Corroboration from tonight's data: human-reviewed full break on listener-tales = 88.0s; tier-a slot clusters (5s merge gap) mass at 91.7/101.1/112.8/117.1s across the 4 morbid episodes (though tier-a edges carry ~36% boundary error, so the +-2s tightness rests on Dan's ears until the 2026-07-15 oracle ear-audit rows land). Morbid is also the worst boundary case in the corpus: 26/34 tier-a slots at zero baseline coverage, largest per-show slot population. IMPLICATION for this bead: the musical outro/intro brackets ARE the continuous-music-bed cohort; a bracket-transition detector + per-show fixed-width pod prior (~90s for morbid) could snap boundaries where acoustic/lexical evidence is ambiguous. Related: ShowAdSlotModel (playhead-4my.13.4) is the per-show prior home if this generalizes beyond morbid.
REFINEMENT (Dan, 2026-07-15, mid ear-audit): the musical outro and intro are the SAME audio every break (fingerprintable per-show stinger => near-exact boundary anchors; connects to xsdz.17 repeated-audio prior, aimed at boundaries not creative). Pod durations are MULTIPLES OF 30s UP TO 90s (just audited a 60s break; snap-to-grid prior {30,60,90}). Corroboration: human breaks 58.4s~60 and 88.0s~90. Combined recipe for morbid-class shows: stinger fingerprint anchors one edge, quantized pod width picks the other from 3 candidates.
SYSK PATTERN (Dan, 2026-07-15 oracle audit): Stuff You Should Know's transition music OVERLAPS the ad boundaries — music starts during the last ~1s of the final ad and ends during the first ~1s after the break edge. Consequence: music-onset/offset snapping alone is systematically ~1s off on this show; per-show edge-offset constants are needed on top of any bracket detector. Contrast with morbid where the stinger brackets the pod cleanly. Pattern tally strengthens the per-show structural-prior thesis: morbid (clean stinger + 30s grid), SYSK (straddling music + ~1s offsets), OTM (attribution templates), SmartLess (framing phrases; xsdz.37).
NETWORK-LEVEL CUES (Dan, 2026-07-15 oracle audit): TED Business's musical in/out cues are recognizably the SAME audio as other iHeart Radio network podcasts. Stinger fingerprints therefore generalize at the NETWORK level, not just per-show — one iHeart cue bank covers many shows including never-played ones (cold-start win for any bracket detector). Production already has NetworkPriors/NetworkIdentity/OwnershipGraph scaffolding to hang this on. Cross-check candidate: SYSK is also iHeart — its straddling transition music (see earlier note) may be the same network cue audio, in which case the ~1s edge offsets may be NETWORK constants rather than per-show.
STINGER PROTOTYPE MEASURED (2026-07-15, commit 564756fb; report /Users/dabrams/playhead-baselines/stinger-prototype-report-20260715.json). Offline leave-one-out refinement of baseline production window edges vs the 44 gold breaks, scored by l2f-score-oracle-gold. Engine: PCM envelope NCC at 50Hz (chromaprint v1 was phase-fragile cross-file); edge-hugging 7s templates; learned per-show offsets (spread-gated 2s); 30s grid; per-show confidence gates; 75s move cap; presence-overlap revert. RESULTS: corpus end p50 18.0s->9.3s; snapped cohort n=16: start median 40.4s->25.5s, END median 4.8s->0.4s (sub-tolerance); 3 breaks fully within +-0.3s; veto hits and matched counts unchanged (no precision loss, no splitting). Models learned exactly per Dan's ear: morbid pre+post+grid, nikki pre+grid (grid=DISCOVERY: nikki pods are 30s-quantized too), smartless post, TED pre. Nikki start snaps landed 0.1-0.2s from gold. REMAINING GAPS: (a) starts weaker than ends — morbid pre-template matches neighbor breaks' identical stingers (proximity tiebreak experiments made nikki worse; needs smarter disambiguation, e.g. joint two-edge + grid consistency scoring); (b) shows with <3 gold breaks learn nothing — NETWORK-level banks (iHeart cue observation) are the fix; (c) smartless-class starts are spoken framing phrases (lexical, xsdz.37) not music. title: Counterfactual family-aware evidence fusion and quorum evaluation
description:
## Problem

DecisionMapper sums calibrated ledger rows and FM quorum counts distinct source kinds, even though SourceEvidenceFamily explicitly records that lexical/classifier/metadata, acoustic variants, and reference matches are correlated within families. Several same-modality rows can therefore self-corroborate or saturate confidence.

## Scope

On frozen production candidate/ledger traces, replay the existing raw-source sum against at least: max-within-family, capped/noisy-OR-within-family, and cross-family quorum variants. Do not rerun FM for downstream counterfactuals. Use cleaned corpus labels, show-disjoint splits, and hard-negative strata. Report firing geometry as well as score metrics. Only implement a production aggregation change if the replay clears a predeclared false-content budget without material recall loss.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic replay compares current and family-aware variants on identical ledgers; results report span precision/recall, ad-seconds recall, false content seconds per listening hour, calibration, and per-family firing rates with confidence intervals and show-disjoint breakouts; a written go/no-go selects one rule or keeps current behavior; any selected implementation includes family-level quorum and cap tests.
notes: Deferred 2026-07-24 (founder reorder): retention-phase work — revisit at ~$5k MRR / after listeners love the core. Not deleted, just not now. Categories: Mac, TTS, chapters, federation, ad-atlas, specialist/fancy-AI, detection improvements users won't notice.

title: Wire user-correction read-side + overturn the two pinned invariants (veto flywheel, Dan-approved full scope)
description:
DAN-APPROVED 2026-07-07 (full-scope option): turn on the user-correction flywheel AND make the two policy changes that overturn PINNED invariants. This is an architecture change touching deliberate design decisions — DESIGN-DOC FIRST, then implement via the iterative loop; document every overturned invariant with rationale (do NOT weaken tests to pass — update them to the new INTENDED behavior with a comment explaining the deliberate change).

WHY: users tap 'not an ad' to veto regions; the WRITE path exists (PersistentUserCorrectionStore, recordVeto from popover/peek views, wired at PlayheadRuntime.swift:776) but the READ path is the NoCorrectionMaskProvider STUB — user vetoes NEVER reach detection. This is the highest-precision signal available, dropped. It matters most once xsdz.29 activation WIDENS spans ~5x: a false skip then eats ~5x more content (the product's stated worst outcome), and the user's veto is the safety valve. Must land BEFORE enabling auto-skip of widened slots.

SCOPE (three parts):
1. READ-SIDE WIRING (the safe subset): implement a real CorrectionMaskProvider so user .exactSpan vetoes become .userVetoed atoms feeding the slot pass's EXISTING vetoedRanges / .vetoNewlyEnclosed gate (xsdz.20). No invariant touched by this part alone.
2. OVERTURN xsdz.20 PINNED-ORPHAN INVARIANT: today a correction against an absorbed span ORPHANS (a pinned test). Change so an .exactSpan veto against a would-be-absorbed span PREVENTS the absorption (route it into vetoedRanges so .vetoNewlyEnclosed blocks it — this is exactly the forward-path already noted in xsdz.20's code comments). Update the pinned orphan test to the new behavior + rationale.
3. OVERTURN the '0.3x weak-labels-never-act-alone' DESIGN (implicit-signal -> markOnly demotion): Dan-approved to let signals act that previously could not alone. CAUTION — this was deliberate: PRESERVE the intent for genuinely NOISY implicit signals; the defensible change is that an EXPLICIT user veto (high-precision, not a weak implicit label) may act alone. Read the current 0.3x design + weak-label fusion before touching; the design doc must justify precisely which signals gain act-alone authority and why, and must NOT let a noisy implicit playback signal auto-skip on its own unless the evidence supports it. If, on reading the design, part 3 looks genuinely unsafe, STOP and re-present to Dan rather than shipping a regression.

TESTS: read-side veto flows to .vetoNewlyEnclosed (blocks a slot); absorbed-span veto now prevents absorption (updated invariant); the act-alone authority change covered + the preserved never-alone-for-noisy-implicit cases still hold; no false-skip regression on the existing corpus. CONSTRAINT: production-target code -> full FastTests gate required.

SEQUENCING: parallel P2; MUST precede auto-skip of widened slots (a gate LATER than the xsdz.29 flag flip); not on the immediate fingerprinter critical path.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc pins each overturned invariant + rationale before implementation; read-side CorrectionMaskProvider wired (user vetoes reach .vetoNewlyEnclosed); absorbed-span veto prevents absorption (invariant test updated, not weakened); act-alone authority change scoped to justified signals with noisy-implicit never-alone preserved (or part 3 re-presented to Dan if unsafe); full FastTests gate green modulo known pre-existing; landed before any auto-skip of widened slots is enabled.
notes: XSDZ.34 R1 OWED FOLLOW-UP (2026-07-17, defense-in-depth): when the future Layer-B promotion WRITE path is wired (the bead that gives BroadCorrectionEvaluator.shouldActAloneSuppress a production caller), derive CorrectionLedgerEntry.direction from the correction's CorrectionSource at the construction site rather than relying on the .suppress default. Latent today (no production constructor; shouldActAloneSuppress has no prod caller — both test-only, exactly like shouldPromote). Worst case if mis-defaulted = over-suppression (missed skip), never a content-eating false skip, so NOT a guardrail-3 breach — but derive-at-source is the correct fix at wiring time.

title: Cross-episode creative-repetition measurement (shared gate for xsdz.17 + rediff-confirmed creative flag)
description: STRATEGY PANEL 2026-07-07: one-day offline measurement that bounds TWO ideas at once. Measure cross-episode creative repetition: fraction of the 198-slot tier-a corpus where a confirmed ad slot shares >=15s of creative audio with another corpus episode's slot (fpcalc / xsdz.23 tooling / the xsdz.26 fingerprinter). Two consumers: (1) xsdz.17 positive self-fingerprinting (its whole premise is repetition => ad prior); (2) a rediff-CONFIRMED-creative flag — at rediff time, before audio deletion, fingerprint the CONTENT of each confirmed ad slot into the xsdz.27 store; a first-play match gives presence AND width INSTANTLY (no 24h wait, no rotation) as an authoritative-extent slot. PANEL DECISION: do NOT build a standalone creative-bank bead and do NOT grant rediff EXISTENCE/mint authority now — fold the creative match into xsdz.17's store as a PROVENANCE FLAG (rediff-confirmed), observe-only. KILL GATE: if <20% of tier-a slots share >=15s creative audio with another corpus episode, drop the creative-flag idea (repetition too rare to matter); xsdz.17 proceeds on its own unsupervised terms regardless. This is the ONLY candidate signal that covers the FIRST-LISTEN window rediff is structurally blind to (0/10 back-to-back).
acceptance_criteria: Cross-episode >=15s-creative-repetition rate over the 198-slot corpus reported with honest N; xsdz.17 and the creative-flag idea both gated on it; if >=20%, a rediff-confirmed provenance flag folded into xsdz.17's store design (not a separate bank); if <20%, creative-flag dropped in writing.

title: Offline FM-free treatment-projection harness — run the xsdz.15 activation eval on the simulator
description:

title: SpliceSlot shadow instrumentation + rediff eval + activation decision
description:
Bead C — shadow instrumentation, eval, and activation decision for slot ownership. SELF-CONTAINED. Blocked by playhead-xsdz.20 (chain: playhead-xsdz.19 + playhead-xsdz.22 -> .20 -> this).

SHADOW GATING (pinned): own flag spliceSlotShadowEnabled (AdDetectionConfig, default OFF; ON in dogfood capture builds). Both-OFF: pipeline byte-identical (test-proven). BOTH-ON: shadow emits NOTHING (test that). Shadow cost: dogfood builds only.

INTERVAL SEMANTICS (mirrored verbatim from bead B, used in all mirroring and assertions): overlap = POSITIVE-DURATION intersection; intervals touching at an endpoint are DISJOINT; enclosed = subset-or-equal.

SHADOW BEHAVIOR (ownership OFF, shadow ON): obtain per-span would-be dispositions by INVOKING BEAD B'S SHARED PURE DISPOSITION FUNCTION (the TWO-PHASE shape pinned in playhead-xsdz.20: pre-awaited bank VERDICT TABLE, then the pure synchronous passes 2-4 with the empty-set check folded in before pass 3 — do NOT reimplement the pass policy; shadow == flag-ON by construction, incl. the FIXPOINT overlap pass with ABSORPTION COMPUTED ONLY AT THE FIXPOINT (a demoted would-be absorber's enclosed spans revert to their prior-pass reasons and emit those — never absorbed), all-or-nothing absorbee bank checks over OTHER non-kept spans only, and greedy collision; the mirror fixtures below remain as regression pins, not as the mechanism). Emit ONE breadcrumb per span (subsystem com.playhead; precedent: fm.coarse.run_budget). FROZEN FORMAT (v3):
  spliceslot.shadow assetId=<id> mintedStart=<s> mintedEnd=<s> slotStart=<s> slotEnd=<s> widthDeltaSec=<s> startEdgeScore=<f> endEdgeScore=<f> coreCoverage=<f> qualified=<bool> reason=<qualifying|degenerateCore|noCandidatePairs|durationOutOfRange|edgeBelowFloor|slotConfidenceBelowFloor|coreCoverageBelowMinimum|vetoNewlyEnclosed|negativeBankVeto|slotCollision|partialOverlapFallback|emptyAtomSet|absorbed>
mintedStart/mintedEnd = the span's post-decode (post-Use-A-snap) interval, per bead B's core-interval pin. REASON PRECEDENCE (pinned): reason = FINAL disposition in the pass order — a LATER pass overrides an earlier one. A collision loser (or gate-failure span) whose minted interval is then enclosed by a KEPT slot emits absorbed; a loser NOT enclosed emits slotCollision and keeps its minted interval. Exactly ONE breadcrumb per span. SLOT-FIELD SOURCES (pinned): qualifying -> winning slot; resolver gate-failures (edgeBelowFloor/slotConfidenceBelowFloor/coreCoverageBelowMinimum/vetoNewlyEnclosed) -> diagnostics.bestGeometryValidPair; negativeBankVeto/slotCollision/partialOverlapFallback/emptyAtomSet -> the span's own resolved-then-discarded slot; absorbed -> the ABSORBING span's slot; no-pair reasons (degenerateCore/noCandidatePairs/durationOutOfRange) -> sentinels slotStart=-1 slotEnd=-1 startEdgeScore=0 endEdgeScore=0 coreCoverage=0. widthDeltaSec PIN: (slotEnd − slotStart) − (mintedEnd − mintedStart) whenever slot fields are real (incl. absorbed rows — reads as consolidation delta vs the absorbing slot); 0 on sentinel rows. Format frozen via pure static formatter + unit test asserting BOTH widthDeltaSec branches (pattern: coarseRunBudgetBreadcrumb + format test, CapabilitySnapshotTests.swift:380-395). Also record structured entries via the FragilityDiagnosticObserver pattern.

DECISION DELTAS (per span, slot arm vs minted arm): ledger mass, distinctKinds, skipConfidence. Slot arm: no refiner adjustment; .audioForensics suppressed (when audioForensicsEnabled) — record ledger mass BOTH with and without suppression. Minted arm: today's exact path. CALIBRATION CAVEAT (document in readout): edgeBelowFloor/slotConfidenceBelowFloor buckets can mask qualifying non-champion pairs (bead A gates the champion only) — champion-level signals, not proof no qualifying pair existed.

DOGFOOD: ~2 weeks on Dan's library; capture via Mac Catalyst run path (chapter-eval precedent) + dogfood diagnostics export. REQUIRED CONFIG: audioForensicsEnabled=true (default false, :483) + spliceSlotShadowEnabled, else the suppression comparison is vacuous while acceptance looks green; assert/log both; log crossEpisodeMemoryEnabled (veto + absorbee mirrors live iff ON).

EVAL: pipeline dumps per docs/bd-4xqf-measurement-recipe.md, ADAPTED (ignore its spanFinalizerEnabled toggles — p56a; both arms run current pipeline). PROJECTION: PREFERRED — a PLAYHEAD_PIPELINE_DUMP mode emitting would-be dispositions in the SAME run. FALLBACK — join script (e.g. scripts/l2f-spliceslot-project.py); per xsdz.14 FM variance shifts spans between runs: tolerance-based interval join + reported unmatched-record count as validity guard. SUBSTITUTION RULE (pinned): ONLY reason=qualifying substitutes the slot interval; reason=absorbed minted intervals are REMOVED; all other reasons keep minted — mirrors flag-ON truth; assert treatment-arm pairwise disjointness (positive-duration semantics) in the projection tooling. Then scripts/l2f-bd4xqf-compare.py --baseline <pre-slot dump> --treatment <projected dump> --rediff <tier-a rediff>. HEADLINE: mean pipeline coverage of true DAI width vs ~18% baseline — overall AND reason=qualifying-only. GUARDS: FP content-seconds enclosed per episode; per-pair regression; precision-gate pass-rate deltas; xsdz.7 fragility distribution shift; QUALIFICATION RATE — report BOTH raw (qualified-true/total) AND consolidation-adjusted (denominator excludes absorbed + slotCollision; a perfectly-consolidated 3-ad pod scores 33% raw — correct behavior, not failure), with FULL reason breakdown.

TESTS (shadow-specific): strong-inner-splice pod (slot1=[L,B], slot2=[B,R], bitwise-identical B) -> TWO qualified=true breadcrumbs; OVERSHOOT pod (span1 minted crosses B ~5s) -> still TWO qualified=true (fixpoint excludes kept slots' minted intervals — no phantom demotion); weak-inner-splice pod -> exactly ONE qualified=true, enclosed losers emit absorbed, non-enclosed losers emit slotCollision; absorbee-bank-check mirror ALL-OR-NOTHING (slot enclosing one clean + one matched span -> slot emits negativeBankVeto, BOTH enclosed spans keep minted with their prior-pass reasons, zero absorbed rows); ABSORBER-DEMOTED mirror (K2 enclosing clean P demoted in round 2 -> P emits its prior-pass reason, NOT absorbed, its minted interval stays in the treatment arm); both-flag matrix; formatter branches.

ACTIVATION: go/no-go per xsdz.14 noise-aware A/B discipline (multi-run CIs where FM variance matters). Flag flip requires Dan's explicit approval — present readout first (no-unilateral-swaps applies to activation). Revisit bead B's .audioForensics-suppression default against the with/without data.

NOTE: guard-metric resolvability depends on playhead-xdh7; shadow can start regardless. Related: playhead-4xqf (this eval measures its headline metric).

title: Phase C: SPIKE — Core AI on-device fine-tuning of ad classifier
description: New iOS 27 Core AI framework: load/specialize/fine-tune models on-device. Prototype fine-tuning a custom ad classifier using FoundationModelsFeedbackStore as training data; measure vs today's prompt-based classifier. SPIKE ONLY — report findings and get approval before wiring into the pipeline (no-unilateral-swaps: this is a new architecture).
notes: SPIKE DONE (docs/phase-c-coreai-spike.md). Key finding: premise doesn't hold — CoreAI.framework has NO public API (empty swiftinterface, private/system framework); the real on-device customization surfaces (FoundationModels SystemLanguageModel.Adapter [load-only, offline-trained, shipped via BackgroundAssets] and CreateML MLTextClassifier [on-device trainable]) were BOTH already present in iOS 26.5 — iOS 27 adds NO new fine-tuning API (its on-device gain is the bigger model + 32k = Phase B). Recommendation: if pursuing on-device learning, CreateML MLTextClassifier trained from FoundationModelsFeedbackStore is the mandate-aligned path, but (a) it's a standalone decision unrelated to the iOS 27 upgrade and (b) it's GATED on a device probe confirming CreateML training actually runs on iOS at runtime (historically macOS-only despite iOS-annotated APIs). Awaiting user decision: device probe / offline-adapter path / drop Phase C.
close_reason: Spiked and dropped per user decision 2026-07-04. Core AI has no public API; real on-device customization surfaces (FM Adapter, CreateML MLTextClassifier) both predate iOS 27, so this is a standalone product decision independent of the iOS 27 upgrade — not epic scope. title: wire SpanFinalizer into AdDetectionService backfill (then measure bd-4xqf impact)
description:
## Context

PR #209 verified `SpanFinalizer.swift` (440 lines) is compiled into the
Playhead target but has ZERO production callers. The file header describes
it as a "deterministic span finalizer — safety layer after fusion" applying
5 constraints in fixed order: non-overlap resolution, minimum content gap
enforcement (<3s merge), duration sanity (5-180s), chapter penalties, and
action cap. Only callers are in `PlayheadTests/.../SpanFinalizerTests.swift`.

PR #211's updated code-path map (`docs/bd-4xqf-codepath-map.md`) identifies
SpanFinalizer's natural insertion point as `AdDetectionService.swift:~2828`,
between `BackfillEvidenceFusion` output and `buildFusionAdWindow` invocation.

The bd-4xqf finding (12/12 pairs, 18% mean coverage of true DAI ad slots)
suggests boundary-collapse is happening between Stage 3a (live refinement at
3120-3155) and persistence. SpanFinalizer's constraint #2 (`minimum content
gap <3s → merge`) is EXACTLY the kind of safety layer that could re-merge
candidates the upstream merge-gap=3.0s threshold dropped, mitigating
CAND_NARROW. If correctly wired, this could measurably increase pipeline
ad-window coverage of rediff slots.

## Scope

**Wire SpanFinalizer into the production decision path. Then measure.**

The user's explicit preference is wire-in over removal: "I think we should
wire in then measure if we can." (2026-06-01.)

In scope:
1. Identify the canonical insertion point (designed to be around line 2828
   per PR #211, but verify against current `runBackfill` structure — this
   document is a snapshot and lines drift).
2. Wire `SpanFinalizer.finalize(...)` after fusion produces DecisionResults
   and BEFORE `buildFusionAdWindow` constructs persisted AdWindows.
3. Maintain behavior-neutral fallback: if SpanFinalizer changes nothing,
   the AdWindow row should be byte-identical to today's. Initially gate via
   a config flag (e.g., `spanFinalizerEnabled: Bool` defaulting to false)
   so production behavior is opt-in until measurement confirms safety.
4. Hermetic tests covering all 5 constraints + integration test verifying
   no diff against baseline when flag is OFF.
5. Measurement: run the existing pipeline-dump test (`PlayheadFastTests` +
   PLAYHEAD_PIPELINE_DUMP=1 on Mac Catalyst) with the flag ON vs OFF and
   compare `boundaryRefinementStartAdjustment` / `boundaryRefinementEndAdjustment`
   / `adWindows` boundaries via `scripts/l2f-bd4xqf-analyze.py`. Surface
   a per-pair before/after table.

Out of scope (NOT this bead):
- Wiring `applyBoundaryRefinement` private helper at `AdDetectionService:5219`
  (PR #211 confirmed it's a duplicate of the live path at 3120-3155;
  wiring would be redundant). Remove or document in a separate bead.
- Wholesale removal of SpanFinalizer.swift — explicitly opposite of this
  bead's intent.

## Acceptance criteria

1. SpanFinalizer is invoked exactly once per `runBackfill` after fusion,
   before persistence, behind a config flag (default OFF for safety).
2. PlayheadFastTests passes (cmd+U; ~3 min simulator).
3. With flag OFF: AnalysisStore rows are byte-identical to the pre-PR baseline
   for a known asset (regression test).
4. With flag ON: at least one constraint demonstrably fires on the corpus
   (e.g., a known short cluster gets merged into a wider one), and no
   constraint causes a test failure.
5. The pipeline-dump JSON (PR #210 + PR #211) gains an optional
   `spanFinalizerConstraintsFired: [String]` per AdWindow when the flag
   is ON (and is omitted when OFF), so the bd-4xqf analyzer can attribute
   coverage changes to constraint #N.
6. The dead-code note in `docs/bd-4xqf-codepath-map.md` is updated to
   reflect SpanFinalizer's new status (wired, gated, default-off → being
   measured).
7. Codebase cleaner than found (within touched files) — lint, types,
   dead code in touched files cleared.
8. Any flaky tests surfaced during this work are fixed deterministically
   (no sleeps/retries to mask).

## Constraints

- No framework swaps (CLAUDE.md decision authority).
- On-device only (CLAUDE.md project_legal_ondevice memory).
- Test plan: PlayheadFastTests for per-iteration verification;
  PlayheadIntegrationTests reserved for final gate (not required per
  bead, unless reviewer requests it).
- Use existing patterns: SpanFinalizer's signature already takes
  `[FusedSpan]` and returns `[FinalizedSpan]`; preserve that contract.
- Behavior under flag OFF must be byte-identical (zero-diff regression).

## Implementation skill

This bead is to be implemented via the
`iterative-implementation-with-review-loops` skill with cap=20 per the
Playhead memory `feedback_iterative_review_cap.md`. Two-consecutive-clean
stop applies. Fix ALL severities, including Low. Leave touched files
cleaner than found.

## Cross-references

- PR #207 — original bd-4xqf code-path map
- PR #209 — SpanFinalizer reachability investigation (UNREACHABLE)
- PR #210 — pipeline-dump captures wasSkipped + boundary-refinement delta
- PR #211 — code-path map points at live refiner (3120-3155); SpanFinalizer
  insertion point estimated at ~2828
- PR #212 — F_PAST guard + corpus scrub (unrelated but same session)

title: width is lost at ANCHORING, not fusion: 84.5 of 87.6 lost points are gone before fusion runs (AtomEvidenceProjector anchors one atom per lexical hit; FM anchors nothing)
description:
## Finding

On 12/12 rediff-confirmed DAI ad slots across 5 new corpus episodes (Casefile, TED Business, SmartLess, Morbid, TechCrunch, Why-Is-This-Happening, Nikki Glaser), the production pipeline produces AdWindows whose clipped overlap with the rediff slot is **systematically narrower** than the slot itself.

- Pairs analyzed: 12
- Pipeline NARROWER than rediff (clipped overlap < 60% of slot width): **12/12 (100%)**
- Mean coverage ratio: **0.18** (pipeline covers ~18% of true ad-slot duration)

Examples:
- Casefile Homechef slot 1913-1995s (82s) → pipeline 36s clip (44%)
- SmartLess slot 2758-2941s (183s) → pipeline 13s clip (7%)
- TED Business slot 922-1071s (149s) → pipeline 36s clip (24%)
- Morbid slot 0-120s (120s) → pipeline 22s clip (18%)

## Interpretation

Pipeline IS detecting most DAI mid-rolls but collapsing onto a tiny sub-span (likely the first sponsor disclosure or loudest single segment). The 80%+ of remaining true-ad audio inside the same DAI block is missed.

Likely root causes:
1. DecodedSpanCandidateBuilder emits short spans rather than continuous blocks for DAI mid-rolls.
2. Evidence quorum / fragility scoring rejects longer-block candidate in favor of tighter one.
3. AdWindow merging stops short on silent beats inside DAI inserts.

## Why this matters

Skipping 18% of a 150s ad leaves the user listening to ~120s of ad. Product promise is "don't hear ads" — current behavior partially fails on DAI mid-rolls even when detection fires.

## Why corpus-gated

N=12 across 5 episodes; 32 more episodes downloaded into autonomous-loop pipeline (will be processed tonight 03:30 local). Re-confirm after ~30 episode corpus matures.

## Data source
- pipeline windows: playhead-dogfood-diagnostics-pipeline-dump-new9.json
- rediff slots:    playhead-dogfood-diagnostics-tier-a-rediff.json

## Proposed next steps (post corpus maturity)
1. Extend FragilityDiagnosticObserver to dump per-candidate decoded-span boundaries.
2. Test which stage drops the long span (candidate gen vs evidence quorum vs merge).
3. Possible fixes (in order of risk):
   a. Loosen AdWindow merging gap-tolerance for DAI-likely regions.
   b. Candidate-coalescer merges adjacent shorts inside continuous ad envelope.
   c. Re-weight evidence-quorum to favor longer continuous segments at low fragility.

=== DEMOTED P0 -> P1 on 2026-07-29 — superseded in framing, not in substance ===
The 18%-of-true-ad-duration measurement is real and still matters. What changed is that it is the WRONG SHAPE to act on.

Dan observed on 2026-07-29, by ear, on a live episode: the pre-roll failed to reach t=0 and over-ran into the show; the post-roll began inside the show and failed to reach the episode end. Both windows SHIFTED INWARD — too narrow where widening is free, too wide where it eats content.

A single width ratio averages across four edges whose costs are not equal, so it cannot distinguish "we are uniformly 82% too narrow" from "we are shifted inward" — and those need opposite corrections at different edges. playhead-aqo9 names that geometry and is promoted to P0 in this bead's place.

WHAT THIS BEAD SHOULD BECOME once aqo9's per-edge measurement exists: the residual magnitude error AFTER the positional policy is applied. If snapping outer edges to the episode boundary and tightening inner edges closes most of the 18% gap, this bead may largely dissolve; if a large gap remains on mid-roll windows — where neither edge is free and the positional policy offers nothing — that residue is the real detection-accuracy problem and this bead should be promoted back with the new measurement attached.

Do NOT start width-accuracy work before aqo9 reports per-edge numbers. Tuning against an averaged figure risks correcting the wrong edge.
=== RE-MEASURED 2026-07-30 ~03:30 ET AT N=44 — THE BEAD'S PREMISE IS FALSE, AND ITS THREE PROPOSED FIXES TARGET A STAGE THAT NEVER RUNS ON THE DOMINANT LOSS ===

Ran the bead's own "proposed next steps" 1 and 2 (identify which stage drops the span) against the two data files it cites, which are both still present. No new capture needed. N went from 12 pairs to 44 slots across 9 episodes with both sides.

THE HEADLINE: 27 of 44 slots (61%) have ZERO overlap with any pipeline AdWindow. They are not narrow — they are ABSENT.

  total true ad audio        3868 s
  lost to TOTAL MISSES       1983 s   51% of all ad audio
  lost to NARROW windows     1320 s   34%
  actually covered            566 s   15%

BY POSITION:
  pre :  14 slots | 7 missed entirely | 7 detected, their coverage 0.13
  mid :  18 slots | 10 missed entirely | 8 detected, their coverage 0.37
  post:  12 slots | 10 missed entirely | 2 detected, their coverage 0.48
  Median coverage is 0.00 for BOTH mid and post — most slots are missed outright, not clipped.
  Of the 17 slots detected at all, only 4 reach >=60% coverage.

WHY THE ORIGINAL N=12 SAID THE OPPOSITE. This bead states "Pipeline IS detecting most DAI mid-rolls but collapsing onto a tiny sub-span." That conclusion is a SELECTION ARTIFACT: the original measurement analysed PAIRS, i.e. it conditioned on an overlap existing, so a slot the pipeline missed entirely could not appear in the sample. Conditioning on detection and then concluding "detection works, width is the problem" is circular. At N=44 without that conditioning, misses are the majority and the larger term.

AND THE MISSES ARE NOT THE CLASSIFIER REJECTING ANYTHING. For each missed slot I checked whether a candidate decoded span existed inside it:

  a candidate existed in the slot but no AdWindow survived:  0
  NO candidate span at all in the slot:                     17
  (no candidate data in the dump):                          10

ZERO of the misses are "candidate generated, then rejected". Nothing was ever proposed in that region. So all three fixes this bead proposes —
  (a) loosen AdWindow merging gap-tolerance,
  (b) candidate-coalescer merges adjacent shorts,
  (c) re-weight evidence quorum toward longer segments
— operate DOWNSTREAM of where 51% of the loss happens. They can only improve the 34% narrow-window term, and they cannot touch material for which no candidate exists. Implementing them first would be tuning a stage that never runs on the dominant failure.

WHAT THIS MAKES 4xqf. The narrow-window term (34%, aggregate 0.30 among detected slots) is real and IS this bead's legitimate territory. But it is the SMALLER half, and it is downstream of candidate generation, so it should be sequenced AFTER the missing-candidate problem — otherwise any width tuning is measured against a corpus where most slots have no candidate to widen.

WHERE THE MISSING-CANDIDATE PROBLEM ALREADY LIVES: this is the reach/coverage program, not a detection-quality problem — playhead-gqx4 (completeFull declared at 3% scan), playhead-i7qe (assets never drain), playhead-8ysk (jobs acquired vs finalized). "No candidate in the region" is the expected consequence of never scanning the region, which is what those beads describe. playhead-pz32 (merged 2026-07-30) now makes that reach visible in the UI instead of hiding it behind a checkmark.

CAVEAT ON THE CORPUS, stated rather than buried: this is the CATALYST corpus dump from 2026-07-16, not Dan's device. On his device DB the pre-roll picture is different (13 of 21 first windows already start at 0.0), so the pre-roll aggregate of 0.06 here should not be read as his lived experience. The mid-roll and post-roll misses are the part to trust as a direction; the absolute pre-roll number is corpus-specific. Also 10 of 27 misses could not be classified for candidate presence because the dump lacks candidate data for those episodes — the 17/0 split is a floor on "no candidate", not the full picture.

RECOMMENDATION: do NOT start this bead's width work yet. Fix candidate generation / scan reach first (gqx4 / i7qe), then re-measure, then take the residual width error — which is exactly the sequencing this bead's own 2026-07-29 note asked for, just with "positional policy" replaced by "candidate coverage" as the thing that must come first.
notes:
---

emits `episode.candidateDecodedSpanList` with per-candidate boundaries +

the env-gated Mac Catalyst dump (PLAYHEAD_PIPELINE_DUMP=1) and the

HOST-READ WIDTH MEASURED (2026-07-17, host-read gold = 27 hand-labeled reads/12 eps/6 shows; scored vs pipeline treatment-dump windows). On RUN episodes (themove x3 + doac-07-09; excludes doac-07-13/huberman which were not staged=0 detected): DETECTION recall 15/19 = 79%. WIDTH: IoU median 19% / mean 32%; start-edge error median 39s / mean 35s; end-edge error median 2.7s / mean 6.1s. MECHANISM: the pipeline catches the END of host-reads accurately (~3s) but starts ~35-50s LATE = it detects only the CTA/URL tail, missing the setup+pitch lead-in. Width correlates with read length: SHORT reads good IoU (Next Bets 78%, Ventum 69%), LONG reads tail-only (Helix 60s->16% IoU, Pipedrive 79s->12%, Lagoon 108s->12%, LMNT missed). This is host-read boundary-COLLAPSE (start-side), distinct from the DAI boundary-undersizing this bead tracks. FIX = the sliding/overlapping-window host-read pass (sb41): windows aligned earlier catch the pitch, extending the detected span to the read start; my sliding experiment showed alignments covering the pitch -> AD where the tail-only production window slices. FALSE-POSITIVE check clean: true-negative episodes (smartless-sting/nate, nikki x2, mel-robbins) had 0 spurious host-read windows (smartless-nick 3 windows = real DAI pre-roll, not host-read).

PRECISION (lower bound, gold completeness imperfect) = 38/44 = 86.4%. So the pipeline is PRECISE but massively UNDERSIZES (~8x) - coverage/width is the problem, NOT detection. Consistent with l2f8 (~10% width coverage) + this bead (boundary-undersizing). riiz/featureVersion did NOT move coverage (expected - they fixed music-bed discrimination, a different signal).
