=== 2026-08-11 ESTABLISH ROUND (playhead-4xqf, establish-only; no production behaviour changed) ===

STEP 1 — the 0.18 does not hold, and the bead cites the SMALLEST of three rediff oracles it could have used.
`playhead-dogfood-diagnostics-tier-a-rediff.json` (44 slots / 16 eps) is the file this bead names. Next to
it on disk, unused, are `-byte.json` (135 slots / 40 eps, byte-exact) and `-composite.json` (147 / 43). Both
are the same 2026-07-17 capture. Re-measured against the byte-exact oracle, N=135 slots / 10,286 slot-seconds,
using the rediff-OFF dump (the config this bead's 0.18 was measured under):
    numerator   = seconds of a rediff slot covered by ANY pipeline AdWindow = 1,383
    denominator = seconds of rediff byte-exact slot                          = 10,286
    AGGREGATE coverage 0.134 · mean per-slot 0.133 · 78/135 slots have ZERO overlap
    detected-only (the conditioning the original N=12 used): 57 pairs, aggregate 0.247, mean 0.315
So the bead's headline number — a mean of 0.18 over 12 pairs CONDITIONED ON DETECTION — reads 0.315 over 57
pairs today. The unconditional number is 0.134. The 2026-07-30 note's 44-slot figures reproduce exactly
(569/3868 = 0.147, 27/44 zero-overlap, 51/34/15 split) — that analysis is sound and I confirm it.

The corpus did NOT mature past 2026-07-17. No newer rediff capture and no newer pipeline dump exists.

DEVICE, CURRENT BUILD (db-vtjxverdict, pulled 2026-08-10, schema 47): 15 windows carry
`boundaryState=dayZeroRediffByteExact` — the oracle, now persisted as windows. 905 slot-seconds.
Seconds of those slots covered by DETECTOR-derived windows (`acousticRefined`) = 108 => 0.119, 10/15 slots
zero. So the detector's own width is ~12% of oracle width on the shipped build. Rediff-ON raises the MEASURED
Catalyst number to 0.430 aggregate / 0.789 detected-only, but that is the rediff differ grading windows it
minted itself — do not read it as detector improvement.

STEP 2 — THE WIDTH IS LOST AT CANDIDATE GENERATION. Measured, not argued.
`decoded_spans` is the candidate generator's own output: `AdDetectionService.runBackfill` persists it at
AdDetectionService.swift:4479, BEFORE the refinement loop opens at :5004. So the device DB already contains
the upstream observable. Splitting the loss on the 14 oracle slots whose asset has decoder rows:
    slot-seconds 875 → covered by decoded_spans 135 (15.5%) → covered by AdWindows 108 (12.4%)
    downstream retention 79.8%; EXCLUDING the one slot touched by a user correction: 94 → 108 = 114.6%.
Downstream of candidate generation the pipeline NET WIDENS. 84.5 of the 87.6 lost points are gone before
fusion ever runs.

HYPOTHESIS 2 (quorum rejects the longer candidate) is ruled out STRUCTURALLY, not just statistically:
`buildFusionAdWindow` (AdDetectionService.swift:8840) copies `span.startTime`/`endTime` verbatim; every
quorum path (`BackfillEvidenceFusion.swift:1312/:1375/:1452`) returns a `SkipEligibilityGate` and touches no
geometry; the fragility gate multiplies `skipConfidence` only. There is no code path by which quorum picks a
tighter candidate — a demoted span keeps its width and becomes a mark.

HYPOTHESIS 3 (AdWindow merging stops short) is ruled out TWICE. There is no post-window merge in the shipped
config — `SpanFinalizer` is OFF (`spanFinalizerEnabled:false`) — so the only merge is the decoder's own Step 2
at `mergeGapSeconds = 3.0`. And a sweep bridging existing windows at gap ≤ G, clipped to the slot, N=135:
    G=3s  → 0.131      G=30s → 0.141      G=90s  → 0.186
    G=15s → 0.133      G=60s → 0.154      G=180s → 0.202   (overshoot 215s → 628s)
An infinitely permissive merge buys 7 points and triples overshoot. The seconds are not there to join.

HYPOTHESIS 1 is where the loss is, but the bead names a type that DOES NOT EXIST: there is no
`DecodedSpanCandidateBuilder` anywhere in the tree. The real generator is
`MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder.decode` (MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder.swift:66), and it is not the culprit
either — it faithfully reproduces the ANCHORING EXTENT it is handed. Width is decided one layer up, in
`AtomEvidenceProjector.project` (AtomEvidenceProjector.swift:58): a span is a maximal run of atoms with
`isAnchored == true` (:307-314), and anchoring is region-range membership (`firstAtomOrdinal...lastAtomOrdinal`).
So the pipeline can only propose as much width as some channel ANCHORED.

WHAT ACTUALLY ANCHORS, on Dan's device (66 decoded spans, provenance counted):
    evidenceCatalog 45 · sustainedMusicOffset 49 · classifierSeed 8 · empty(user-confirmed) 7
    fmConsensus 0 · fmAcousticCorroborated 0   ← FM anchors NOTHING
Median span width by proposer: user-drawn 59.8s · music-bed 14.9s · lexical 11.6s. The widest spans in the
store are the ones a human drew. And Path 2 anchors `entry.atomOrdinal` — ONE ATOM per lexical hit
(AtomEvidenceProjector.swift:243-247), which is why 50 of 53 `acousticRefined` windows start at EXACTLY
`evidenceStartTime` and the median width is 15.4s.

ONE SLOT, END TO END (device, asset D9B513CD, Conan, oracle slot 3194.5–3371.2 = 176.7s):
    HOP 1 transcript  — 382 chunks, fast+final, the slot is fully transcribed. Not a reach failure.
    HOP 2 anchoring   — 2 decoded spans: 3238.6–3261.3 (22.7s) and 3321.4–3330.0 (8.6s), BOTH provenance
                        `sustainedMusicOffset` only. 145 of the 176.7 slot-seconds contain no anchored atom.
                        Candidate coverage 31.4s = 18%.
    HOP 3 windows     — 3235.6–3264.3 (28.7s) and 3318.4–3331.9 (13.5s), both `acousticRefined`, both
                        markOnly. Refinement ADDED 11s. Plus the rediff window at full slot width.
    HOP 4 listener    — 42.3s of a 176.7s ad break. The two marks sit on the music stings at each end of the
                        pod; the ad copy between them was transcribed, was never anchored, and was never
                        proposed.

STEP 3 — options, each against the per-edge and certainty-tier rulings.
  (a) DEAD: the bead's own three fixes. Measured above. Do not spend a round there.
  (b) MAKE THE COARSE FM VERDICT A WIDTH PROPOSER. The machinery exists (Path 1 anchors an fmConsensus
      region's whole ordinal range) and fires zero times on device. playhead-2350 recorded FM correctly
      saying containsAd over 17–1183s / 3010–3575s while fusion attached presence to narrow seeds. RISK is
      the inner edge: FM coarse windows are ~1,000s wide, and the 180s SPLIT would chop them at an arbitrary
      internal gap. Per Dan's per-edge ruling this is only admissible on the MARK tier. FALSIFIED BY: track
      overshoot-seconds (predicted ad outside any slot) against covered-seconds; reject if overshoot grows
      faster.
  (c) POD-ENVELOPE EXTENSION FROM A CONFIRMED SEED — `AdPodContinuation` already ships ON
      (maxLinkGapSeconds 30, maxExtensionSecondsPerSide 180) and is already mark-only, which is the safe
      tier by construction. On device it emitted 7 windows averaging 18.6s. Lowest-risk lever; it is
      natively per-edge, so an outer edge can run to the episode boundary for free while the inner edge
      needs a return-to-show stopping rule. FALSIFIED BY: it extends from a seed, so measure false-seed
      extension separately.
  (d) NOT A WIDTH SOURCE, ruled out here so nobody spends a round on it: `semanticSweepMark` proposes 2,876
      window-seconds averaging 137s — by far the widest thing in the store — and on the 8 rediff-bearing
      assets, 0.0 of its 299 seconds land inside a byte-exact DAI slot. It is finding something, but not this.

INSTRUMENTATION DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED (test-only, commit b85d7a25 on bead/playhead-4xqf):
`candidateDecodedSpanList`, added 2026-06-01 for this bead's own "proposed next step 1", CANNOT answer the
question. `FragilityDiagnosticObserver` fires at AdDetectionService.swift:5543 and records `refinedSpan` —
downstream of every refiner. Measured: across all 53 episodes of the new9 dump the list is
interval-for-interval IDENTICAL to `adWindows`, 132 rows of 132. So the 2026-07-30 finding "no candidate
existed in the slot" is really "no WINDOW existed" — circular in the same way the original N=12 was, and the
17/0 candidate-presence split should be read as a window-presence split. Added `decoderOutputSpanList` to the
dump (the persisted `decoded_spans`, with atom ordinals and anchor-provenance kinds) so the next Catalyst
capture can do the upstream/downstream split at N=135 that I could only do at N=14 on device.

STILL UNKNOWN: why FM never anchors on device (region qualification vs FM never running vs consensus
strength floor) — that is the single highest-value next question and it is not answered here. Also unknown:
whether the 78/135 zero-overlap slots are reach (gqx4/i7qe) or anchoring; the device trace above shows at
least one fully-transcribed slot failing on anchoring alone, so "no candidate" is NOT synonymous with "never
scanned".

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
CAPTURE TRAP for whoever runs the next Catalyst dump — found by the R1 reviewer, and it would bias the result in the FLATTERING direction.

decoderOutputSpanList is pure decoder output ONLY while no RediffBSideProvider is injected.

'rediffSlotOwnershipEnabled' defaults TRUE. The rediff-slot ownership pass (upsertDecodedSpans at :7947, invoked at :4987) is therefore ENABLED — it no-ops today solely for want of a B-side provider. If the next capture runs with one injected, that pass rewrites decoded_spans BEFORE the field is read, and the 'upstream' term silently becomes rediff-WIDENED geometry.

WHY THAT IS THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION: the whole point of the field is the stage split — how much width the DECODER proposed, versus how much survived refinement. If the upstream term is secretly rediff-supplied, the decoder appears to have proposed width the ORACLE actually gave it, and the split reads as 'candidate generation is fine, the loss is downstream'. That is the exact opposite of what this round established (84.5 of 87.6 lost points are gone BEFORE fusion), and it would send the next round to fix a stage that is innocent.

The docstring names the condition. Nothing enforces it at capture time.

BEFORE THE NEXT CAPTURE, do one of:
  (a) assert no RediffBSideProvider is injected on the dump path, or
  (b) record the resolved config (rediffSlotOwnershipEnabled, spliceSlotOwnershipEnabled, whether a B-side
      provider was present) INTO the dump itself, so a reader can tell which population they hold.

(b) is better — it makes the dump self-describing rather than relying on the capturer having read a comment. It is also the same discipline that would have caught the defect this round fixed: candidateDecodedSpanList was named for one thing and recorded another, and nothing in the artifact said so.

RELATED CONFIG FACT, verified this round: spliceSlotOwnershipEnabled defaults FALSE and a precondition at :1059 makes the two ownership passes mutually exclusive — so naming only rediff in the docstring is correct, not an omission.

ALSO UNRECONCILED, recorded so it is not rediscovered: computing covered seconds from adWindows independently gives 1,345 s (0.131) against the reported 1,383 s (0.134) — a 38 s / 2.7% numerator gap. The denominator matched to 0.1 s, so this is a population detail (likely the user-corrected slot), not arithmetic. It moves no conclusion.

comments.text:
RE-TITLED 2026-08-11. The old title — 'pipeline DAI boundary-undersizing: candidate windows cover only 18% of true ad-slot duration' — is measured dead in three ways, and leaving it up was actively misleading whoever picked this bead up next:

1. THE NUMBER. 0.18 was a mean over 12 pairs CONDITIONED ON DETECTION, against the SMALLEST of three rediff oracles sitting on disk. Against the byte-exact oracle (135 slots / 10,286 slot-seconds) it is 0.134 unconditional, 0.315 detected-only. Neither is 0.18.

2. 'BOUNDARY-UNDERSIZING' NAMES THE WRONG STAGE. Downstream of candidate generation the pipeline NET WIDENS — 94s of decoded_spans coverage becomes 108s of AdWindow coverage (114.6%) once the one user-corrected slot is excluded. Fusion is not narrowing anything.

3. THE FINDING / INTERPRETATION / PROPOSED-NEXT-STEPS SECTIONS ARE ALL REFUTED and are kept only as history. 'DecodedSpanCandidateBuilder' does not exist in the tree. Hypothesis 2 (quorum picks the tighter candidate) is ruled out structurally — buildFusionAdWindow copies span geometry verbatim and every quorum path returns a SkipEligibilityGate. Hypothesis 3 (merging stops short) is ruled out twice — SpanFinalizer is OFF, and an infinitely permissive merge sweep buys 7 points while tripling overshoot.

WHAT IT IS INSTEAD, and what the new title says: width is decided in AtomEvidenceProjector.project — a span is a maximal run of atoms with isAnchored==true, so the pipeline can only propose as much width as some channel ANCHORED. On Dan's device, across 66 decoded spans: evidenceCatalog 45, sustainedMusicOffset 49, classifierSeed 8, user-confirmed 7, fmConsensus 0, fmAcousticCorroborated 0. Path 2 anchors ONE ATOM per lexical hit, which is why 50 of 53 acousticRefined windows start at exactly evidenceStartTime with a 15.4s median width. The widest spans in the store are the ones a human drew (59.8s median).

The blocking sub-question — why FM anchors nothing — is playhead-881t's answer, recorded there before it was closed: the consensus floor is structurally unreachable via all three legs (uniqueWindows>1 fails because windows partition with zero overlap; hasAnchors is suppressed on 9 of 11; minimumIoU>=0.4 measures 0.213/0.258). Do NOT lower the floor — computeGate would make 70-329-atom regions auto-skip eligible.

title: Grow + diversify the eval corpus so ad-detection signals are resolvable (activation blocker)
description:
Extends playhead-l2f (Labeled Test Corpus). The 2026-05-29 activation campaign (7 A/Bs of the xsdz precision signals) proved the current 12-episode / 24-ad-span dogfood corpus CANNOT resolve ANY signal — the FM intra-run noise floor (~±2 FP span, ~±0.14 coverage precision) is larger than any measured effect, AND 4 of 7 signals don't even fire on it. l2f's original "min 15 episodes / category coverage" spec predates these findings; this bead adds the SPECIFIC dimensions the campaign showed are missing:

1. SCALE for statistical power: target ≥30-50 episodes / ≥60+ annotated ad spans, so a real ±1-2 FP effect can clear the noise floor (current 12/24 is far too small; pair with the multi-run-aggregation bead).
2. CROSS-SHOW SPONSOR RECURRENCE: the same sponsor entities (BetterHelp/Shopify/Squarespace/etc.) appearing across ≥3+ DISTINCT shows and spanning >14 days — required for xsdz.13 cross-show syndication to fire at all (0 gated entities on current corpus; its spread≥0.40 / ≥3-shows / ≥14-day gate never triggered).
3. MULTIPLE EPISODES PER SHOW (≥3-5 episodes each for several shows) — required for the FEEDBACK signals to be measurable via time-split: xsdz.9 negative-bank needs cross-episode FP recurrence within a show; xsdz.11 per-show threshold needs a within-show corrections→eval split. Current corpus has ~1 episode/show.
4. DAI-rich episodes (dynamic insertion, different production/room) to give xsdz.8 audio-forensics (the cleanest re-test candidate — fired on 16 spans) something to discriminate; plus ample non-ad content for FP measurement.

Keep l2f's host-read / DAI / blended / edge-case category coverage. On-device/offline curation (no runtime services), human-verified boundary annotations in the existing CorpusAnnotation JSON format.

BLOCKS: re-measuring the 7 off-by-default xsdz signals (the activation re-tests) AND xsdz.4 (CoreML ranker, already corpus-gated for non-overfit training). See l2f for the base composition/format.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
DECIDED APPROACH (2026-05-29): feed-diff first, LOCAL-ONLY (no cloud, no model-labeling — keeps eval-data creation consistent with the on-device philosophy). Three tiers, automatic-first:

TIER 1 — Ad-free vs ad-supported alignment-diff (automatic, exact, physical ground truth): for shows that publish BOTH a free (with ads) and a premium ad-free feed, align the two audio streams (cross-correlation / reuse the existing AcousticFingerprint / AdCopyFingerprintMatcher infra); the segments present in free but ABSENT in premium are the ads, with exact boundaries → CorpusAnnotation JSON, no human, no model. GATING DEPENDENCY: requires access to the ad-free/premium feed for each chosen show (Patreon/Supercast/Apple subscription) — episode selection should prioritize shows where we can obtain both feeds.

TIER 2 — Same-episode-different-fill diff (automatic, for DAI without a premium feed): download the same episode twice; DAI re-fills ads per request, so the DIFFERING segments are the dynamic ad slots. Aligns the identical content, flags the inserted slots. Misses static/baked-in ads.

TIER 3 — Host-read / blended ads (baked into single audio, invisible to diff): use the EXISTING local pipeline (l2f-local-transcribe whisper → l2f-draft-annotation heuristic draft → human review queue → l2f-promote-reviewed-corpus). Broaden episode selection via more RSS feeds; speed the review queue.

SIZING (size × runs tradeoff with xsdz.14 multi-run): Phase 1 = ~30-40 eps / ~80-100 spans + N=5 runs/arm (composed for cross-show sponsor recurrence + ≥3-5 eps/show), enough to re-test audio-forensics + make xsdz.13/.9/.11 fire + rule out small effects; THEN use xsdz.14's measured per-run variance to size Phase 2 (~75-100 eps / ~200+ spans) empirically for confident go/no-go + non-overfit xsdz.4 training. NOT a guess-and-build — measure variance after Phase 1, then size.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
EMPIRICAL CORRECTION (2026-05-29) — same-session Tier-2 diff is DEAD. Tested: downloading a full DAI episode twice from the same machine seconds apart returns BYTE-IDENTICAL audio (confirmed on Last Week in AI / art19, full 13MB file; + first-2.5MB identical on SmartLess/podtrac, You Can't Make This Up/megaphone, The Rest Is History/pdst.fm, Morbid/podtrac). DAI serves a deterministic fill per requester/session, and content is static. So "download twice, diff" does NOT surface ad fills.

REVISED automatic-boundary methods (no cloud, no model):
- TIER A (scalable, no paywall, AUTOMATIC, but lagged): TIME-SEPARATED DAI diff. Snapshot a batch of DAI episodes NOW; re-download the SAME episodes in ~1-4 weeks (ad campaigns rotate, content stays static — proven static same-session); diff → the changed segments ARE the DAI ad slots with exact boundaries. Fits an ongoing corpus pipeline (every snapshotted DAI episode becomes labeled later). Build the differ as snapshot-now / rediff-later. Could also use geo/IP-separated downloads to avoid the lag.
- TIER B (instant, exact, but paywalled): ad-supported (free RSS) vs ad-free PREMIUM diff — needs the premium audio as a DOWNLOADABLE subscriber feed (Supercast/Patreon RSS), not app-locked.
- TIER C (always available): existing local whisper-draft → human-review → promote pipeline; broaden episode selection.

FEED CLASSIFIER built (scripts candidate: /tmp/probe_feeds.py) — iTunes search/lookup → RSS → classify by enclosure host (DAI proxy) + ad-free CTA + transcripts. Across 8 genres / 77 feeds: 51 DAI-hosted, 24 with ad-free CTAs. Good diverse candidate pool (news/comedy/true-crime/history/tech/interview/business). Diary of a CEO (existing corpus show) confirmed DAI (pdst.fm).

PRACTICAL NEXT STEP: (1) snapshot a diverse DAI batch now to start the time-clock for Tier-A; (2) use Tier-C to annotate a first expansion immediately; (3) pursue Tier-B only for shows with a downloadable premium ad-free feed.

title: Rhetorical act-sequence grammar (blind-spot: persuasion-program parsing)
description:
BLIND-SPOT CONVERGENCE from the dueling-wizards duel — surfaced only AFTER adversarial expansion, reached INDEPENDENTLY by both models: cc-BS1 ('Universal Ad Grammar': HOOK→PROBLEM→SOLUTION→EVIDENCE→OFFER→CTA) ≈ cod-BS3 (weighted finite-state ad grammar, Viterbi best-path over the cue stream). High novelty.

MECHANISM: operate on the PRAGMATIC FUNCTION of the speech — what it is trying to DO (persuade/sell), not what words appear. Classify each sentence into ad-rhetoric roles via keyword/phrase rules, then score the ORDERED co-occurrence. No single role is ad-specific (content can ask questions, mention brands, cite stats, give URLs), but 3+ roles IN CANONICAL SEQUENCE is almost exclusively an ad — robust even when specific lexical cues (sponsor/promo/URL) don't fire. Optionally a WFSA + Viterbi grammar-fit score.

ON-DEVICE: ~150 lines — deterministic role classifier + sequence scorer (order-violation penalty). Negligible compute, per-candidate.

RISKS: keyword role classifiers are imperfect; 'native'/conversational ad reads deliberately blur the structure (no explicit hook); role taxonomy may need show-type tuning (interview vs narrative).

SUCCESS: precision lift against the dominant FP modes — editorial mentions (SOLUTION-only), self-promos (CTA-only), product reviews (EVIDENCE+SOLUTION, no OFFER/CTA) — which have 1-2 roles vs a real ad's 3-6.

title: Lightweight temporal regularization (isolation penalty + min-dwell; NOT a full HMM)
description:
CONSENSUS #4 from the dueling-wizards duel — a RESOLVED disagreement. cc#13 cluster-contagion (cod 515) vs cod#1 sequence-decoder/HMM (cc 520). Both models EXPLICITLY REJECTED a full HMM/CRF as over-engineered for a 12-episode / 41-example corpus and converged on a lightweight deterministic form.

MECHANISM: ads are contiguous + clustered; isolated single-segment high scores are suspect. Apply deterministic post-fusion constraints: (a) an ISOLATION PENALTY for detections with no high-confidence neighbor within ±120s; (b) a MINIMUM-DWELL constraint on ad islands. If any neighbor-boost is used, gate it on high-confidence neighbors only (>0.80) — a one-sided/gated signal, NOT a symmetric naive boost.

ON-DEVICE: ~30 lines in the post-fusion decision pass; one decay constant + dwell threshold. Operates on the pipeline's own output.

RISKS (the reason it must be one-sided/gated): naive contagion amplifies correlated mistakes — two nearby editorial FPs boost each other, and FPs adjacent to true breaks get cemented. Hence isolation-penalty + high-confidence gating, not symmetric reinforcement. Some shows have single standalone mid-rolls (no cluster context) — the dwell/isolation logic must not erase those.

SUCCESS: reduction of isolated FPs without clipping short true ads; bootstrap CIs over episodes (not windows) via the harness.

title: Negative fingerprint bank + cross-episode alignment (FP-suppression memory)
description:
CONSENSUS #3 from the dueling-wizards duel. cod#2 negative bank (cc 580 — cc called it 'the one idea I should steal') + cc#6 Smith-Waterman alignment (cod 815). Both #3 post-reveal.

MECHANISM: store compact fingerprints (audio sketch + transcript/lexical n-gram signature) of confirmed FALSE POSITIVES (user reversions / high-confidence known-FP patterns) → suppress future near-matching candidates. Pair with Smith-Waterman LOCAL alignment for repeated POSITIVE ad copy — it tolerates token insertions/deletions/substitutions, exactly the mutations on-device ASR produces across runs of the same ad script (n-gram/exact matching misses these). Extends the existing SponsorKnowledgeStore / AdCopyFingerprintMatcher (positive side partially exists; the NEGATIVE bank is the novel precision lever).

ON-DEVICE: SQLite banks, LRU + time-decay for ad-inventory drift; near-neighbor similarity as a capped evidence channel; ~60-100 lines.

RISKS: memory pollution at 0.54 precision (auto-confirmed positives wrong ~46%) → gate WRITES on user-correction or very-high-confidence only; cold start (only helps recurring copy, not novel sponsors); MinHash loses sequence order (use Smith-Waterman as the matcher; MinHash only as a cheap LSH prefilter).

SUCCESS: FP-suppression + recall on recurring sponsors under a TIME-SPLIT eval (early episodes build memory, later episodes score).

title: Composite audio-forensics boundary channel (splice + environment + spectral discontinuity, merged)
description:
CONSENSUS #2 from the dueling-wizards duel. cc#1 splice (cod 845) + cc#8 spectral-residual (cod 685) + cc#12 recording-environment (cod 585) ≈ cod#3 boundary-forensics (cc 670) + cod#7 room-acoustic (cc 560). Both #2 post-reveal; both AGREED to MERGE cc's three forensic ideas into ONE capped channel (not three separate caps inflating the ledger).

MECHANISM: detect physical insertion artifacts at candidate boundaries that ad TEXT can't fake — LKFS/loudness jump, spectral-centroid shift, noise-floor change, reverb/spectral-tilt (recording-environment) discontinuity. One `audioForensics` EvidenceSourceType with sub-signals; sigma-normalized boundary deltas; fire only when corroborated by lexical/acoustic.

ON-DEVICE: Accelerate/vDSP over already-decoded audio, backfill-only (~1-2s/episode). Reuses the acoustic feature pass.

RISKS: DAI/produced ads ONLY (~33-50% of corpus) — host-read ads have no splice; content transitions (guest/segment changes) can false-trigger (require corroboration); spectral-subtraction has a profile-contamination chicken-egg (build the show baseline from HIGH-CONFIDENCE content only). SKIP codec-level edit-scars (cod#8, cc 320): most podcasts are mono pre-encoded AAC, splice servers concatenate without re-encoding → artifacts below noise floor.

SUCCESS: span-precision lift on the DAI subset via the harness; absence of artifacts as mild negative evidence for the DAI hypothesis.

title: Live A/B harness: cumulative lexical-scorer lift (xsdz.1+.2+.3) through real runBackfill+FM
description: Validation harness for the shipped lexical-scorer program. Needs: (1) thread NarrowingConfig so lexicalClusterSnapEnabled is settable through runBackfill (currently .default-hardcoded at the TargetedWindowNarrower.narrow() call sites in BackfillJobRunner — behavior-neutral at default). (2) A Phase-C-style env-gated Catalyst A/B (mirror ChapterFusionLiftABTests): run real runBackfill on the dogfood corpus, baseline (lexicalAutoAdQualifiedThreshold high=off + lexicalClusterSnapEnabled=false) vs treatment (defaults=all on), both fmBackfillMode .full, scored vs CorpusAnnotation golden via SpanMetrics. Measures the CUMULATIVE end-to-end live lift; xsdz.1 is already FM-free-measured so the new info is xsdz.2+.3's effect through the FM pipeline (flagged risk: analogous chapter-steering showed zero). Orchestrator runs the ~1hr Catalyst A/B.
acceptance_criteria: NarrowingConfig threadable (default-neutral); env-gated Catalyst A/B harness runs real runBackfill baseline-vs-treatment on the corpus + scores vs golden; compiles iOS sim + Catalyst; skips clean in default suite. Live lift number produced by the orchestrator Catalyst run.

title: Fix hardcoded chapterIndex/totalChapters/previousDisposition (1/1/nil) in chapter-labeling test adapters
description: Idea N3 (cc 690 / cod 620 — both: real measurement artifact, fix it, but won't rescue recall alone). ChapterLabelingService.buildPrompt already emits 'Context: chapter {N} of {M}. Previous: {P}', but the test adapters in ChapterFusionLiftABTests / ChapterPlanPipelineSnapshotCaptureTests (LiveLabelerAdapter) hardcode chapterIndex=1, totalChapters=1, previousDisposition=nil for EVERY call — so all prior diagnostics + A/Bs ran with three priors disabled (episode position, sequential ad-run momentum, episode structure). Thread the real index/count and accumulate previousDisposition across the labeling loop (~5 lines). Zero token cost. NOT expected to fix the 21%% conversational-read failure, but it removes a measurement-credibility artifact — do it before trusting future chapter-labeling A/B conclusions.
acceptance_criteria: Test adapters thread real chapterIndex/totalChapters and accumulate previousDisposition across the labeling loop; a re-run diagnostic confirms the priors are now populated; no regression.
close_reason: Merged. Real chapter context threaded into labeling test adapters; pure sequencer + actor unit-tested (no-deadlock + prior-not-current); test-only; R1-R3 two-consecutive-clean.

title: Two-stage labeling: lexical scanner nominates ad-likely regions, FM confirms (never a veto)
description: Idea #8 (cc 810 / cod 760). Invert today's 'FM labels every region': the LexicalScanner (high recall) nominates the ~15-25%% ad-likely regions; the FM only confirms/rejects those — a simpler task than 7-way cold classification, and ~75%% fewer FM calls. CRITICAL (cod's caveat): if the FM says content on a region with strong lexical hits, it must NOT get veto power over the lexical signal — treat FM as supporting evidence, lexical coverage as the recall floor. Composes with the C1 auto-ad rules (decisive lexical combos skip the FM entirely).
acceptance_criteria: Only lexically-nominated regions hit the FM; FM is confirming evidence, not a veto over strong lexical hits; FM call count down ~75%; recall >= lexical-coverage floor; measured on the SpanMetrics harness.
close_reason: Merged. Lexically-nominated FM audit-window selection (the remaining half; FM-no-veto was done in xsdz.1). Sim coverage proxy: nominated 0.870 vs random 0.333 ad-span coverage at equal budget. END-TO-END FM EFFICACY UNVERIFIED — Catalyst follow-up (analogous chapter-steering showed zero lift). R1-R2 two-consecutive-clean; no regression.

title: Tighter ad-candidate regions: snap boundaries to acoustic breaks + lexical-cue clusters
description: Idea #2 (cc 730 / cod 830 — strong consensus). Current chapter-boundary regions are large and dilute ad copy with surrounding content (diagnostic: identical 'brought to you by Mint Mobile' text labels correctly in a pure-ad region, wrong in a mixed editorial+ad region). Snap candidate-region boundaries to acoustic breaks (already extracted) + LexicalScanner hit-timestamp clusters so detection sees cleaner, ad-dense windows. Foundational input-quality improvement that sharpens every downstream signal (lexical density, the local scorer, CoreML features) and skip-boundary placement. Risk: boundary jitter / over-segmentation — guard against it.
acceptance_criteria: Candidate regions snap to acoustic/lexical cluster boundaries; ad-copy dilution reduced (measured: pure-ad-region detection rate up on the golden set); no over-segmentation regression on the existing pipeline.
close_reason: Merged. Lexical-cluster inward-only region tightening; corpus A/B: coverage recall +30%, precision +26%, no FP increase, no regression. R1-R3 two-consecutive-clean.

title: Chapter FM still misreads ~79% of ad regions as content after prompt guidance (few-shot / region tightening / alt labeling)
description:
Follow-up to playhead-au2v.1.25 (PR #170). The prompt+schema ad-classification guidance doubled correct ad detection (ad-overlap→adBreak 5/45→10/47 on the dogfood corpus, live Catalyst diagnostic) but the FM still labels ~79% of ad-overlapping regions as content. The chapter signal will not clear the eval bar (disposition accuracy ≥0.7) at 21% ad detection.

Next levers to evaluate (use ChapterLabelingDiagnosticTests on Catalyst to measure each, baseline 10/47):
- Few-shot examples in the prompt (1-2 short host-read + programmatic ad exemplars) — biggest expected lift, watch token budget.
- Region tightening: candidate regions are [detectedStart, nextDetectedStart) and can be large, diluting ad copy with surrounding content. A tighter ad-region proposal (or labeling sub-windows) may sharpen the signal. NOTE: region/boundary changes are detector-side and need care.
- Previous-disposition context: the labeler receives previousDisposition; verify it's threaded usefully in the capture/diagnostic path (the diagnostic passed nil).
- Alternative: a dedicated ad-vs-content binary pass before the 7-way taxonomy.

Validation: ChapterLabelingDiagnosticTests on Catalyst (keychain-unlocked); target adBreak rate well above 10/47, then re-run the threshold harness. Decision-authority note: a labeling-strategy change (binary pass, region redesign) is an architectural choice — present options before implementing.
acceptance_criteria: ad-overlap→adBreak rate materially above the 10/47 post-au2v.1.25 baseline on the dogfood corpus (live Catalyst diagnostic), without increasing operational/guardrail failures; path to clearing the disposition-accuracy floor documented.
notes:
2026-05-26: First attempt (two generic few-shot exemplars, one hostReadAd + one programmaticAd) did NOT help. Deterministic 5x A/B on Mac Catalyst: baseline (main, au2v.1.24+.25) = 10/47 adBreak on all 5 runs; few-shot = 9/47 on all 5 runs. So the exemplars marginally HURT (10->9) for added prompt-token cost. Branch discarded, NOT merged (per the merge-only-if-it-wins criterion). The lever isn't necessarily dead — different/more exemplars or a different framing might help — but THIS attempt failed. Recommend: (a) land the eval-harness work (au2v.1.27) first, then (b) iterate exemplars with that harness, or pivot to the deferred levers (region tightening / binary ad-vs-content pass — architectural, needs an approach decision). Bead stays OPEN.

description:

title: au2v.1.24: expose raw-audio → ChapterFeatureSnapshot helper to unblock pipeline-snapshot capture
description:
Follow-up surfaced during playhead-pzfg (au2v.1.23) implementation 2026-05-20.

The pipeline-snapshot capture path implemented in au2v.1.23 (PlayheadTests/Services/ReplaySimulator/NarlEval/ChapterPlanPipelineSnapshotCaptureTests.swift) cannot produce real ChapterPlan snapshots from raw audio today because there is no callable raw-audio → ChapterFeatureSnapshot helper. The only path that builds a populated snapshot (music windows + speaker windows + lexical hits + pause windows) is inside AdDetectionService.runBackfill, which requires a fully-populated AnalysisAsset row and the upstream service graph.

Scope:
- Expose a public (or @testable-internal) ChapterFeatureSnapshotBuilder API that takes an audio URL + minimal context (transcript, FM availability flag) and produces a ChapterFeatureSnapshot suitable for ChapterBoundaryDetector.
- OR: split the runBackfill feature-extraction subgraph so it can be invoked standalone against an audio URL.
- DO NOT change pipeline behavior — the new helper should be a refactor of existing wiring, not a parallel code path.

Acceptance:
- ChapterPlanPipelineSnapshotCaptureTests.captureSnapshot(...) drops in the helper and successfully captures snapshots for all 12 dogfood episodes when run on a device with the audio staged and Apple Intelligence enabled.
- au2v.1.23 harness flips from "skip if snapshot missing" to "assert thresholds" once the 12 snapshots are committed.

Blocks: real threshold floors in ChapterPlanQualityRealCorpusHarnessTests.

title: au2v.1.23: capture ChapterPlan snapshots for dogfood corpus + flip quality eval to thresholds
description:
Continuation of playhead-au2v.1.22 (PR #166 merged 2026-05-20).

The merged scaffold ChapterPlanQualityRealCorpusHarnessTests pins the loader→evaluator path against 12 dogfood goldens but uses an empty ChapterPlan (recall denominator = total chapters, precision = 0/0, dispositionMatched = 0). To produce real quality signal we need pipeline-output ChapterPlan snapshots per episode and threshold assertions.

Approach (C2 - chosen 2026-05-20 over shadow-mode export C3 to unblock immediately):
1. Add an env-gated Swift Testing test (PLAYHEAD_CHAPTER_SNAPSHOT_CAPTURE=1, mirroring PLAYHEAD_FM_SMOKE pattern in PlayheadFMSmokeTests.swift) that runs ChapterGenerationPhase against each of the 12 dogfood corpus episodes and writes ChapterPlan JSON snapshots to PlayheadTests/Fixtures/ChapterPlanGoldenSet/pipeline-snapshot/<episode_id>.json
2. Run the capture once locally; commit the 12 JSON snapshots
3. Extend the dogfood harness test in ChapterPlanQualityRealCorpusTests.swift to load the snapshots (when present) and swap the empty plan for the real snapshot in evaluator.evaluate(pairs:)
4. Assert thresholds per-episode and aggregate: recall ≥ 0.6, precision ≥ 0.5, disposition accuracy ≥ 0.7

Acceptance:
- Capture test is gated; PlayheadFastTests is unchanged
- Pipeline-snapshot fixture committed for all 12 episodes
- Harness loads + uses snapshots
- Threshold assertions pass on current main's pipeline (or test reports honest failures with a clear path to follow-up tuning)
- Privacy: snapshots contain no raw advertiser/product/confidence text from annotations; topic labels follow the same anonymized allowlist as the goldens

Followup (au2v.1.24): consider shadow-mode export from dogfood app as a higher-fidelity capture source.
notes:
2026-05-25: Capture step (4-step approach, step 2) executed via Mac Catalyst (tooling landed PR #169 / playhead-au2v.1.23). Result: chapter signal MISSES the eval bar on real dogfood data. Transcript-starved: recall 0.48 / precision 0.11 / disposition 0.44. Snapshots NOT committed (would fail harness + bake misleading baseline). title: Player surface polish: one-line status below scrubber + 'Always skip this sponsor' on Skipped banner
description:
**Scope:** Two small SwiftUI items from UI design `docs/plans/2026-04-16-podcast-bg-ui-design.md` §C (Player surface) that aren't wired today. Both finish the player to design spec. Single bead because they live in adjacent files and a single PR is the right unit of work.

## Item 1 — One-line player status below scrubber (§C-2)

**Design contract:** "One-line player status below the scrubber, mirroring the episode-detail status line. Hidden when fully analyzed. Tap → Activity scoped to this episode."

**Source of truth:** Same `EpisodeSurfaceStatus` reducer used by the episode-detail status line (delivered by `5bb3` and rendered by `zp5y`). No new reducer code — purely a new render target.

**Work:**
- Add a slim row below the scrubber in the player view that subscribes to `EpisodeSurfaceStatus` for the currently-playing episode.
- Render the same string variants the detail view does: "Skip-ready · first 18 min," "Downloaded · queued for analysis," "Paused — phone is hot · will resume automatically," etc.
- Hide the row entirely when `playbackReadiness == complete` (fully analyzed) — UI design explicitly calls this out: a fully-analyzed episode shows nothing.
- Tap → push Activity screen scoped to this episode (re-use Library nav-bar Activity entry point with a `focusedEpisodeId` parameter, or open a sheet — match the existing detail status-line behavior).
- No spinner anywhere on the player during background analysis (§C honesty constraint — "reads as 'the app is struggling'").

## Item 2 — "Always skip this sponsor" affordance on Skipped banner (§C-3)

**Design contract:** "'Skipped' banner gains an 'Always skip this sponsor' affordance alongside Undo. Routes through existing UserCorrectionStore / FoundationModelsFeedbackStore (Phase 7 infra)."

**State today:** `ConfidenceBand.swift:97` defines `case alwaysSkipThirdPartyPaid` on the action enum, but no SwiftUI button is wired. UserCorrectionStore + FoundationModelsFeedbackStore (Phase 7) are shipped.

**Work:**
- Add an "Always skip this sponsor" button on the existing "Skipped Xs ad · Undo" banner, alongside Undo.
- Tap → call into UserCorrectionStore / FoundationModelsFeedbackStore with the `alwaysSkipThirdPartyPaid` action and the SpanDecision identifier from the just-skipped span.
- Confirmation: brief inline state change ("Will always skip this sponsor") that auto-dismisses. No modal.
- Honesty constraints (§C): no confidence percentages, no per-segment numbers.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Player view shows the status row when an episode is downloaded but not fully analyzed
- [ ] Row hides on `playbackReadiness == complete`
- [ ] Tap on row opens Activity scoped to that episode
- [ ] Skipped banner shows "Always skip this sponsor" + "Undo" simultaneously
- [ ] Tap → correction persisted via UserCorrectionStore / FoundationModelsFeedbackStore
- [ ] No spinner on the player during background analysis
- [ ] Snapshot tests for both surfaces across Dynamic Type sizes
- [ ] VoiceOver labels for both controls

## Cross-references
- Reducer: `playhead-5bb3` (EpisodeSurfaceStatus)
- Detail-view companion: `playhead-zp5y` (episode detail status line)
- Correction stores: Phase 7 user-correction-loop (already shipped per plan §1)
- Existing player UX: `playhead-ef2.6.3` (gray-band markOnly + Skipped banner)

title: Phase 12 shared lexicon verification suite
description: Build the focused Phase 12 verification suite covering schema validation, signature verification, download/cache rollback, shared/local lexicon merge semantics, quarantine-to-active confirmation flow, local correction overrides, contribution privacy guards, central dedupe/publish behavior, and user-control/failure-policy diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: Tests prove invalid signatures and incompatible schema fail closed. Shared entries are quarantined and cannot auto-skip until locally confirmed. Local corrections and blocked entities override shared entries. Contribution tests prove transcripts, audio, snippets, timestamps, episode IDs, subscriptions/listening history, and user identifiers never serialize. End-to-end fixture downloads a signed lexicon, merges it, detects candidates, and preserves local override semantics. All affected PlayheadTests pass.
notes: This is the acceptance gate for closing Phase 12. Prefer deterministic fixtures and local fake transport/signing keys; no real network dependency in tests.
close_reason: Implemented Phase 12 shared sponsor lexicon subbeads with signed artifact validation, cache rollback, quarantined merge semantics, privacy-preserving export, deterministic publish/dedupe, controls/diagnostics, and verification suite.

title: Shared lexicon user controls, telemetry, and failure policy
description: Add the product/operational controls around shared lexicon use: consumption default-on toggle, contribution opt-in toggle, local reset/disable behavior, operational telemetry for artifact version/cache/validation outcomes, and explicit failure policy. Telemetry must be aggregate and must not include sponsor text from private local discoveries unless already present in the public shared artifact.
acceptance_criteria: User can disable shared consumption without deleting local sponsor knowledge. User must opt in before any contribution payload is produced or sent. Telemetry records artifact version, validation status, cache age, merge counts, and contribution eligibility counts without private transcript/audio/listening data. Failure states are visible in diagnostics and never block local-only detection.
notes: This bead keeps Phase 12 operable and debuggable without weakening the privacy model.
close_reason: Implemented Phase 12 shared sponsor lexicon subbeads with signed artifact validation, cache rollback, quarantined merge semantics, privacy-preserving export, deterministic publish/dedupe, controls/diagnostics, and verification suite.

title: Central dedupe and signed publish pipeline
description: Create the lightweight central-side path for receiving privacy-safe contribution payloads, deduplicating sponsor entities and aliases, applying blocklists/conflict rules, producing a deterministic versioned shared lexicon JSON artifact, signing it, and publishing it to the configured distribution location. Server logic should remain minimal: merge, validate, sign, publish.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline rejects invalid or privacy-unsafe contribution payloads. Deduplication is deterministic across equivalent aliases/vanity URLs/pattern descriptors. Published artifact validates against the shared schema and includes signature/version metadata. Publish is atomic and retains prior artifacts for rollback. No raw contribution metadata that can identify a user is included in the published lexicon.
notes: Keep this backend intentionally boring. The device must still quarantine shared entries locally; central inclusion is not enough for auto-skip eligibility.
close_reason: Implemented Phase 12 shared sponsor lexicon subbeads with signed artifact validation, cache rollback, quarantined merge semantics, privacy-preserving export, deterministic publish/dedupe, controls/diagnostics, and verification suite.

title: Privacy-preserving contribution exporter
description: Build the opt-in device-side exporter for shared sponsor contributions. It may export only active lifecycle sponsor entities that have sufficient local confirmation and low rollback/correction conflict risk. Payloads must contain public sponsor facts only: canonical entity, aliases or normalized pattern descriptors, type/category, confidence/lifecycle summary, and schema version. It must never export transcripts, audio, evidence snippets, episode IDs, timestamps, subscriptions, listening history, or per-user identifiers.
acceptance_criteria: Exporter is disabled unless contribution opt-in is enabled. Ineligible/quarantined/blocked/conflicted entities are excluded. Serialization has a privacy guard that fails closed if any transcript-like snippet, timestamp, episode identifier, asset identifier, or user identifier field is present. Unit tests cover positive export and every forbidden data class.
notes: This bead is export construction only. Transport/central ingestion is handled by the central publish bead.
close_reason: Implemented Phase 12 shared sponsor lexicon subbeads with signed artifact validation, cache rollback, quarantined merge semantics, privacy-preserving export, deterministic publish/dedupe, controls/diagnostics, and verification suite.

title: Merge shared entries into CompiledSponsorLexicon with quarantine
description: Integrate verified shared lexicon entries with the existing CompiledSponsorLexicon/SponsorKnowledgeStore flow. Shared entries should improve candidate detection, but enter the local lifecycle as quarantined/shared-origin entries and must earn at least one local confirmation before becoming active for hot-path skip eligibility. Local user corrections and blocked/decayed local entities always override shared entries.
acceptance_criteria: Shared sponsor aliases, vanity URLs, CTA descriptors, and disclosure phrases participate in candidate detection after verified load. Shared-origin entries are marked as shared/quarantined locally and cannot become active without local confirmation. Local blocked/corrected entities suppress matching shared entries. Existing local-only lexicon behavior is unchanged when shared consumption is disabled or no artifact is available.
notes:
This is the main device behavior bead. Preserve the quarantine lifecycle from Phase 8 and keep scan-time evidence separate from decision-time policy.
Depends conceptually on the Phase 8 SponsorKnowledgeStore/CompiledSponsorLexicon architecture, but bd disallows task-to-epic dependency edges; keep that as implementation context rather than a graph edge.
close_reason: Implemented Phase 12 shared sponsor lexicon subbeads with signed artifact validation, cache rollback, quarantined merge semantics, privacy-preserving export, deterministic publish/dedupe, controls/diagnostics, and verification suite.

title: Shared lexicon download, cache, and rollback client
description: Build the device-side client that loads the shared sponsor lexicon artifact from bundled fixtures or a remote CDN location, verifies the signed manifest, stores the last-known-good artifact atomically, and fails closed on corruption or signature/version errors. Consumption is default-on, but must be disableable without affecting local-only sponsor knowledge.
acceptance_criteria: Client verifies signatures before cache promotion. Failed download, invalid signature, incompatible schema, or corrupt cache leaves the previous valid lexicon in use. Offline startup works from last-known-good cache. Consumption can be disabled locally. No network/download failure can block local ad detection.
notes: This bead is consumption plumbing only. It should not merge entries into hot-path logic; that happens in the CompiledSponsorLexicon merge bead.
close_reason: Implemented Phase 12 shared sponsor lexicon subbeads with signed artifact validation, cache rollback, quarantined merge semantics, privacy-preserving export, deterministic publish/dedupe, controls/diagnostics, and verification suite.

title: Shared lexicon artifact schema + signature validation
description: Define the versioned shared sponsor lexicon artifact consumed by devices and produced by the central publisher. The artifact must contain only public sponsor facts: canonical sponsor names, aliases, vanity URLs, CTA pattern descriptors, disclosure phrases, entity category/type, provenance/version metadata, and no transcript/audio/user context. Include a signed manifest format, key rotation/version fields, schema migration rules, deterministic canonicalization, and validation errors that fail closed.
acceptance_criteria: Schema is documented in code and tests. Decoder rejects unknown incompatible versions, invalid signatures, malformed entries, transcript-like snippets, timestamps, episode IDs, or user identifiers. Canonicalization is deterministic. Signature verification is mandatory before entries can be merged.
notes: Foundation bead for Phase 12. Keep payload privacy-safe by construction: no raw evidence snippets, no quotes, no per-user or per-episode data.
close_reason: Implemented Phase 12 shared sponsor lexicon subbeads with signed artifact validation, cache rollback, quarantined merge semantics, privacy-preserving export, deterministic publish/dedupe, controls/diagnostics, and verification suite.

title: Make false_ready_rate dogfood audit playback-window aware
description: The playhead-e2a3 dogfood audit showed that scripts/false_ready_rate.swift overcounts false-ready cases when used as a gate by itself: it treats every ready_entered as denominator, including cold_start and analysis_completed transitions with no same-session playback/skip evidence, and cannot classify skip-before-ready ordering. Add an audit mode that groups by session_id + episode_id_hash, reports unique playback proxies, and classifies ready transitions as same-session skip-after-ready, skip-before-ready-only, no-playback-evidence, or confirmed false-ready. Keep the existing reference rollup available for compatibility.

Fixtures cover cold_start without playback, analysis_completed without playback, skip before ready, skip after ready within 60s, and skip after ready later in the same session. The output makes raw ready_entered denominator caveats explicit.

It reports playback proxy counts, session/episode ready classifications, trigger splits, and DOGFOOD_GATE_AUDIT; added audit fixture covering cold_start no playback, analysis_completed no playback, skip-before-ready, skip-after-ready within 60s, and skip-after-ready later in-session. Verified legacy fixture, audit fixture, dogfood bundle, --help, and git diff --check.

title: Stabilize 8 pre-existing flaky tests surfaced by au2v.1 phase-close (scheduler / BG-task / runtime / perf)
description:
8 distinct timing-dependent / pre-existing flaky tests surfaced during the playhead-au2v.1 phase-close gate (2026-05-08). These are NOT regressions from au2v.1 — they pre-date the subepic and are unrelated to chapter-signal work. They were deferred from phase-close so the schema-version drift fixes (PR #162) could land cleanly.

The flake set was captured by running both PlayheadFastTests and PlayheadIntegrationTests against `main @ c6b81179` on iPhone 17 Pro simulator. Run-to-run reproducibility is intermittent — a prior orchestrator's deferred set only partially overlapped this run's 8, confirming these are timing/scheduler races rather than deterministic failures.

## Flakes (file:line · symptom)

1. `PlayheadTests/Services/AdDetection/AnalysisWorkSchedulerOutcomeBookkeepingTests.swift:150`
   `cancelCurrentJob mid-decode increments attemptCount` — race between cancel signal and decoder bookkeeping.

2. `PlayheadTests/Services/AdDetection/AnalysisWorkSchedulerOutcomeBookkeepingTests.swift:394`
   `repeated mid-decode cancellation reaches maxAttemptsReached and supersedes the job` — multi-cancel timing.

3. `PlayheadTests/Services/AdDetection/AnalysisWorkSchedulerOutcomeBookkeepingTests.swift:477-479`
   `a poisoned-decode asset does not block queued work behind it indefinitely` — head-of-line / queue progress race.

4. `PlayheadTests/Services/AdDetection/AnalysisWorkSchedulerOutcomeBookkeepingTests.swift:235-239`
   `repeated decode failure (.failed outcome) reaches maxAttemptsReached and supersedes the job` — attempt-counter ordering.

5. `PlayheadTests/Services/Background/BackgroundProcessingServiceTests.swift:337`
   `Expiration handler requests pause with cause=.taskExpired and fails task` — BG-task expiration timing.

6. `PlayheadTests/Runtime/RuntimeShutdownLifecycleTests.swift:80,94,369`
   `shutdown() after startup drives a clean exit and is idempotent` — shutdown race / lifecycle ordering.

7. `PlayheadTests/Services/AdDetection/SchedulerReconcilerRegressionTests.swift:764`
   `scheduler resolves a real analysis asset for jobs that start with nil analysisAssetId` — reconciler resolution timing.

8. `PlayheadTests/Services/AdDetection/MinimalContiguousSpanDecoderTests.swift:544`
   `Performance: decode 15,000 atoms with ~50 anchors + ~100 acoustic hints in < 200ms` — perf budget flake (observed 568ms vs 500ms threshold).

## Acceptance criteria

- Each of the 8 tests passes deterministically across 10 consecutive runs on iPhone 17 Pro simulator (PlayheadFastTests + PlayheadIntegrationTests as appropriate).
- Fixes are at the architectural seam (scheduler/BG-task/runtime), not via sleeps/retries/longer timeouts unless the test was genuinely measuring wall-clock budget.
- The performance test (#8) gets a budget review: either tighten the implementation, widen the threshold with justification, or move it to a perf-only test plan that's not on the phase-close gate.
- No regressions in unrelated subsystems.

## Constraints

- Do NOT mask flakes with sleeps, retries, or by widening timeouts beyond what is justified by measured baseline + headroom.
- Tests that genuinely race on shared state should be fixed by adding deterministic synchronization at the test seam (e.g., explicit await on a published state, not arbitrary delays).
- Per project memory, do not refactor unrelated subsystems while in here. Touched files only.
- The 8 flakes likely cluster into 3-4 root causes (scheduler-attempt bookkeeping; BG-task expiration; runtime shutdown idempotency; perf-budget). Investigate by cluster, not by individual test.

## Background

- Schema-version drift fixes (PR #162) widened `AnalysisStore.currentSchemaVersion` access modifier so tests reference the constant. That work landed clean; these 8 are the leftover.
- Phase-close for playhead-au2v.1 was declared "passed except known-flaky list" with this bead as the follow-up scope.
- See conversation 8af24b25-b397-45cc-970b-ac7eb221ae76 for full triage history (post-fix run logs at /tmp/fasttests-postfix.log etc.).

## Why this is its own bead, not absorbed elsewhere

These flakes were pre-existing pollution unrelated to au2v.1. Bundling them into phase-close would have either (a) blocked a clean merge over unrelated noise, or (b) padded the au2v.1 PR set with debt-paydown work that obscures the chapter-signal feature shape. Carving a discrete follow-up keeps both stories honest.
notes: 2026-05-08 verification: targeted flake cluster from the bead passed on iPhone 17 Pro simulator. Initial selected xcodebuild test run executed 48 Swift Testing tests across AnalysisWorkSchedulerOutcomeBookkeepingTests, ContinuedProcessingHandlerTests, RuntimeShutdownLifecycleTests, SchedulerRegressionTests, and MinimalContiguousSpanDecoderTests. Then 10 consecutive xcodebuild test-without-building repetitions passed using the same selected suites. No source changes were required; current main already contains the scheduler/BG-task/runtime/decoder hardening. Sandbox repeat attempts failed only because CoreSimulatorService/log access was unavailable in sandbox, then passed outside sandbox.
close_reason: Closed after verification: all named flaky-test clusters passed once under xcodebuild test and then passed 10 consecutive selected test-without-building repetitions on iPhone 17 Pro simulator; no current code change needed.

title: Case study fixture set: 5-10 known-miss episodes with before/after assertions
description: Curate 5-10 case-study fixtures from the dogfood diagnostics corpus covering: missed mid-episode conversational ads, removable false positives, pre/post-roll edge cases, monologue/short edge cases, and intentionally-no-signal sanity cases. Each case has anonymized fixture data, an expected-behavior English description, and a Swift Testing assertion that runs ChapterSignalGate and verifies the documented before/after. Provides the qualitative evidence half of Q2-C.
design:
Files affected:
- PlayheadTests/Fixtures/ChapterSignalCaseStudies/ (new directory)
- Curated dogfood diagnostic JSON snippets — anonymized
- A README/index file documenting each case study

Purpose: produce concrete before/after evidence for the design's case-study bar (Q2-C from brainstorm). Eval lift in aggregate (E2) tells us if the system improved overall; case studies tell us whether it caught a SPECIFIC known miss we care about.

Selection criteria for case studies (target 5-10 episodes):
1. Currently-missed mid-episode ads on conversational shows (the Conan-style coverage-gap problem). At least 3 cases.
2. False positives the chapter signal could plausibly remove (content-disposition chapters with high quality should suppress ads). At least 2 cases.
3. Pre/post-roll edge cases (boundary singleton territory). At least 1 case.
4. Edge cases: pure-monologue episodes, very short episodes, episodes with both creator and inferred chapter possibility. At least 1 case.
5. A case where chapter signal CORRECTLY does nothing (signal absent or no candidates) to verify no false-promotion. At least 1 case.

Sources for selection:
- Existing dogfood diagnostic JSONs in repo root and Playhead/
- Manual corrections by Dan during dogfood (most actionable signal — Dan rewound to skip something the system missed, or correctd a false-positive auto-skip)
- Diagnostics with explicit pipeline_coverage_limited classification

Per-case-study fixture format:
- episode_anonymous_id (hashed)
- show_archetype (conversational, narrative, comedy, news)
- baseline_diagnostic_excerpt (relevant fields from real diagnostic, anonymized)
- expected_behavior_with_chapter_signal (English description)
- success_criteria (measurable assertion: 'detection rate at this timestamp transitions from 0 to ≥0.5')
- hand_labeled_chapters (where applicable, for E4 cross-reference)

Privacy:
- Strip episode titles, advertiser names, transcript snippets before checking in
- Fixtures live in test bundle, not shipped with app
- README in fixture directory documents anonymization process

Replay-driven assertions:
- Each case study has a corresponding test that runs ChapterSignalGate on the case's frozen trace
- Asserts: expected before-behavior with mode=.off, expected after-behavior with mode=.enabled
- Tests fail loudly if behavior regresses on a previously-passing case study
- Tests are written in Swift Testing format (not XCTest) per project default

What this bead does NOT do:
- Hand-label every chapter in every case (that's E4 if needed for plan-quality eval)
- Compute aggregate metrics (E2)
- Build the gate infrastructure (E1)

Maintenance:
- As the system evolves, new case studies get added; old ones may become obsolete (e.g., if the underlying issue is fixed by other means)
- Document deprecation in the fixture README

Why this matters:
- Aggregate metrics can hide important regressions in narrow cases

title: Aggregate metrics: precision/recall/F1/FM-cost on dogfood corpus
description: Compute aggregate metrics across the dogfood corpus for each ChapterSignalMode (off/shadow/enabled) using the gate from E1. Produces the lift report that decides whether to flip the mode in production. Bar: measurable lift on ≥1 of {recall, precision} without regression on the other; FM cost ≤2× current refinement-pass cost.
design:

Bar to keep:
- Measurable lift on at least one of {recall, precision} on dogfood corpus
- No regression on the other
- FM cost increase ≤2× current refinement-pass cost

Metrics computed per mode:
- Aggregate precision: (true positives) / (true positives + false positives)
- Aggregate recall: (true positives) / (true positives + false negatives)
- Aggregate F1
- Per-show breakdown (recall on Conan, Diary of a CEO, etc.)
- FM call count delta (mode=.enabled / mode=.off)
- Phase wall-clock latency p50, p90, p99
- Plan generation success rate, abort rate by category (operational, pathological, no-candidates, creator-skipped)

Comparison structure:
struct ChapterSignalLiftReport:
  - baseline: PerModeMetrics (from off mode)
  - shadow: PerModeMetrics
  - enabled: PerModeMetrics
  - liftPrecision: Double  (enabled.precision - baseline.precision)
  - liftRecall: Double  (enabled.recall - baseline.recall)
  - liftF1: Double
  - fmCostMultiplier: Double
  - perShowLift: [ShowName: PerModeMetrics]
  - barMet: Bool  (true if criteria above hold)

Reporting:
- Print structured table to stdout when run as a tool
- Persist a JSON report to a known location (e.g., .narl-eval-output/chapter-signal-lift-<date>.json) for offline analysis
- Diff-friendly format so successive runs are comparable

- Ground-truth labels: extract from existing dogfood corpus where user manually corrected, OR from hand-labeled fixtures (E4)

Limitations to document:
- Dogfood corpus is biased toward Dan's listening habits — not a fully representative test set
- Sample size limits statistical power on per-show breakdowns
- Manual corrections in dogfood are sparse (most listens don't trigger correction); ground truth is approximate

- JSON serialization round-trip
- Deterministic output for fixed input

Outcome: a CLI-style tool or test suite that produces the lift report. The report is what tells us whether to flip ChapterSignalMode from .off → .shadow → .enabled in production.

title: FM prompt builders inject compact chapter context
description: Second of two new chapter-signal consumers. Extends FoundationModelClassifier.buildPrompt + buildRefinementPrompt and FoundationModelExtractor.buildPrompt to inject ~30-50 tokens of compact chapter context before the existing Evidence catalog block: 'Chapter context: 4/7 hostReadAd. Prev: content. Topic: <topic>.' Provides macro-structure context to per-window FM calls that today see only 2-3 segments at a time. Source-agnostic: works for both creator and inferred chapters. Token-budget guard drops context when window content fills nearly all available budget.
design:
Files affected:
- Playhead/Services/AdDetection/FoundationModelClassifier.swift (extend buildPrompt + buildRefinementPrompt with chapter context injection)
- Playhead/Services/AdDetection/FoundationModelExtractor.swift (extend buildPrompt similarly)

Today's prompt builders:
- buildPrompt (coarse, FoundationModelClassifier.swift:2795): assembles L<n> > 'segment text' lines + optional 'Evidence catalog:' entries.
- buildRefinementPrompt (FoundationModelClassifier.swift:2829): half token budget via coarseBudgetDivisor=8.
- buildPrompt (FoundationModelExtractor.swift:110): metadata extraction prompt.

Schema overhead: ~3700 tokens fixed; per-window content budget ~300-400 tokens; refinement prompt half that.

Chapter-context injection:
- Before the existing 'Evidence catalog:' section (or wherever appropriate per current structure), insert a compact chapter context blob.
- Format target: ≤30-50 tokens of chapter context.
- Shape:
  Line: 'Chapter context: 4/7 hostReadAd. Prev: content. Topic: <topicDescriptor>.'
- Fields:
  - chapter index / total (from ChapterPlan.chapters position of this window)
  - this chapter's labelDisposition (from L1's raw taxonomy preserved in plan)
  - previous chapter's labelDisposition
  - this chapter's topicDescriptor (truncated to ~10 tokens if longer)
- Compactness: prefer abbreviations (e.g., 'hostReadAd' is fine; topicDescriptor truncated; no full English sentences).

Token-budget guard:
- Compute estimated chapter context tokens (use existing token-counting helper if one exists in the codebase, otherwise ~3 chars/token approximation).
- If chapter context would exceed 50 tokens (long topicDescriptor), truncate the topicDescriptor.
- If even the abbreviated context can't fit (very rare; only if window content fills nearly all of budget), drop chapter context entirely for this window. Diagnostic emitted: chapter_prompt_dropped_budget.

Source-agnostic:
- Same handling for creator chapters and inferred chapters. Creator chapters use ChapterDisposition (adBreak/content/ambiguous) directly; inferred chapters use the L1 raw taxonomy preserved in ChapterPlan.
- For creator chapters, map ChapterDisposition → string ('adBreak' for ad-break, 'content' for content, 'ambiguous' for ambiguous). For inferred chapters, use the richer raw taxonomy directly.

Mode gate:
- Read ChapterSignalMode from injected config (same approach as F2).
- mode=.off or .shadow → don't read plan, don't inject context. Behavior identical to today's prompt.
- mode=.enabled → inject context if plan exists for current episode + planConfidence ≥ 0.3.

Cache lookup:
- For each per-window FM call, look up chapter for the window's time range:
  - If window straddles two chapters, use the chapter that contains the larger overlap.
  - If no chapter covers the window, omit chapter context (window is in unscanned region).
- Cache lookup is O(log N) on chapter count; cheap.

What this bead does NOT do:
- Tests (M2)
- Per-window FM call routing changes (just prompt content changes)

Diagnostic events:
- chapter_prompt_injected: per-call when chapter context was added (with chapter index/disposition for offline tuning)
- chapter_prompt_dropped_budget: per-call when budget guard kicked in
- chapter_prompt_no_chapter_for_window: per-call when window had no covering chapter (sanity check; shouldn't happen often)
acceptance_criteria:
- buildPrompt (coarse) extended with chapter context injection
- buildRefinementPrompt extended (half-budget aware)
- FoundationModelExtractor.buildPrompt extended consistently
- Compact format: chapter index/total + this disposition + prev disposition + truncated topic descriptor
- Token-budget guard truncates or drops context as needed
- Mode gate respected: off/shadow → no injection; enabled → injection when plan exists + planConfidence ≥ 0.3
- Source-agnostic: creator chapter sources mapped, inferred chapter raw taxonomy used directly
- Diagnostic events emitted at injection / drop / no-chapter decision points
- All existing FM prompt tests still pass; new tests in M2 cover chapter-context paths

title: CoveragePlanner consumes chapter evidence for audit-window selection
description: First of two new chapter-signal consumers. Extends CoveragePlanner to read ChapterEvidence (from any source — creator or inferred) and replace ~50% of random audit windows with chapter-informed selections: ad-disposition chapters always audited, high-quality content chapters excluded, ambiguous chapters at normal random probability. This is the 'attention-direction' half of the design's Q3-C decision and is expected to deliver the biggest lift on conversational/Conan-style shows where coverage gaps drive misses.
design:
Files affected:
- Playhead/Services/AdDetection/CoveragePlanner.swift (extend with chapter-aware audit-window selection)
- Playhead/Services/AdDetection/CoveragePlannerContext.swift (add chapterEvidence parameter to context)

Today's CoveragePlanner.plan(for: context):
- For mature shows in 'targeted+audit' mode, picks ~12% random audit windows.
- These random windows are the source of the 'pipeline coverage gap' on conversational shows (memory: project_ad_detection_weak_on_conan.md).

Chapter-aware change:
- Add `chapterEvidence: [ChapterEvidence]?` to CoveragePlannerContext.
- When mode == .enabled (gate from F2) and chapterEvidence is non-nil and has any ad-disposition or high-quality content-disposition chapters, planner enters chapter-informed selection.
- Replace fraction (configurable, start at 0.5) of random audit windows with chapter-informed selections:
  1. Prioritize ad-disposition chapters (ChapterDisposition.adBreak) above audit threshold (qualityScore > 0.4): ALWAYS include in audit set.
  2. Deprioritize content-disposition chapters with high qualityScore (>0.7): exclude from audit set unless their boundary borders an unscanned region.
  3. Ambiguous chapters: include with normal random probability.
- Remaining audit slots after chapter-informed selection: filled with random selections from un-classified regions (don't double-cover chapter regions with random audit).

Source-agnostic:
- Reads ChapterEvidence regardless of ChapterSource — creator chapters and inferred chapters look the same to the planner.
- Creator chapters have higher qualityScore (typically 0.9+); inferred chapters have lower (label confidence). Planner naturally weights via qualityScore comparison; no need for source-specific logic.

Configurable parameters:
- replacementFraction: Double = 0.5 (what fraction of random audit slots to replace with chapter-informed)
- adChapterMinQualityForAuditInclusion: Double = 0.4
- contentChapterMinQualityForExclusion: Double = 0.7
- These live in CoveragePlannerConfig (or equivalent existing config struct). Tunable via shadow-mode A/B.

Edge cases:
- Episode has 0 chapters → planner falls back to today's random selection (no change in behavior)
- Episode has chapters but mode=.shadow → planner doesn't read; baseline behavior
- Episode has only ambiguous chapters → planner falls back to today's random selection
- Plan exists but planConfidence < 0.3 (low overall trust) → planner ignores plan, falls back to random

What this bead does NOT do:
- Tests (C2)
- Wiring of chapterEvidence into CoveragePlannerContext caller (this bead extends the call site too — verify all callers updated)

Diagnostic events:
- coverage_plan_chapter_informed: when planner used chapter info to select audit windows (record fraction replaced, count of ad-chapter windows, count of content-chapter exclusions)
- coverage_plan_chapter_skipped: when planner had access to chapter evidence but decided not to use (low planConfidence, no usable chapters, mode disabled)

Why this matters:
- This is the 'attention-direction' half of the design's Q3-C decision.
- Replaces speculative random sampling with informed targeting.
- The biggest expected lift on conversational/Conan-style shows where coverage gaps are the bottleneck.
acceptance_criteria:
- CoveragePlannerContext accepts optional chapterEvidence parameter; all callers updated
- mode=.enabled + non-nil chapter evidence + sufficient planConfidence → chapter-informed selection
- replacementFraction (default 0.5) of random audit slots replaced
- Ad-disposition chapters (qualityScore > 0.4) always in audit set
- Content-disposition chapters (qualityScore > 0.7) excluded from audit
- Ambiguous chapters: normal random probability
- Plan with planConfidence < 0.3 → planner falls back to random
- Source-agnostic: creator and inferred chapters use same code path
- Diagnostic events emitted on chapter-informed and chapter-skipped paths
- All existing CoveragePlanner tests still pass; new tests in C2 cover chapter-aware paths

title: Wire ChapterGenerationPhase into AdDetectionService backfill + integration tests
description: Wire the phase into AdDetectionService.runBackfill() between final-pass transcript completion and BackfillEvidenceFusion. Gate on ChapterSignalMode (off → no phase, shadow → phase but consumers ignore, enabled → full path). Cache-hit short-circuit: skip phase when valid plan exists for content hash. Integration tests cover end-to-end happy path, mode gates, cache hits, creator-chapter precedence, cancellation, transcript revision race, and all failure modes.

- PlayheadTests/Services/AdDetection/ChapterGenerationPhaseIntegrationTests.swift (new — full-phase integration tests)

Wiring location:
- AdDetectionService.runBackfill() (or whatever the equivalent entry point is — verify exact location during impl).
- After final-pass transcript completion, BEFORE BackfillEvidenceFusion runs.
- Sequence: final-pass transcript → ChapterGenerationPhase (gated by mode) → BackfillEvidenceFusion (already reads chapter evidence via ChapterMetadataEvidenceBuilder).
- Phase invocation must respect existing backfill ordering and cancellation token.

Gate behavior:
- mode == .off: phase never invoked. Same wall-clock and outcome as today.
- mode == .shadow: phase invoked, plan written to cache, BUT consumers (CoveragePlanner, FM prompts in M1) ignore the plan. Diagnostics still emitted (so eval can compute lift).
- mode == .enabled: phase invoked AND consumers read.

Phase invocation policy:
- Run only after final-pass transcript is complete (don't fire on fast-pass).
- Don't run if phase has already produced a valid plan for this content hash (cache hit).
- Don't run if creator-chapter check (P2) tripped at last attempt (cache hit on creator-chapter parsed evidence).

Integration tests:

End-to-end happy path (with mocks for FM):
- Set up mock TranscriptEngineService with fixed final-pass output
- Set up mock features (boundary detector inputs)
- Set up MockFoundationModel with deterministic responses
- Run AdDetectionService.runBackfill() with mode=.enabled
- Assert: ChapterPlan written to cache, ChapterPlanReady event fired, BackfillEvidenceFusion sees inferred ChapterEvidence
- Assert: candidate ad windows updated with chapter evidence (verify fusion ledger output)

Mode gate:
- Run with mode=.off: ChapterGenerationPhase never invoked, no FM calls, no plan, baseline behavior
- Run with mode=.shadow: phase invoked, plan written, but mock CoveragePlanner and prompt builder do NOT read plan
- Run with mode=.enabled: phase invoked, plan written, consumers read

Cache hit:
- Pre-populate ChapterPlanCache with a valid plan for content hash H
- Run runBackfill() — phase should detect cache hit and skip FM
- Assert: zero FM calls, plan from cache used downstream

Creator-chapter precedence (P2 integration):
- Pre-populate ChapterEvidence cache with creator chapters (ChapterSource.id3)
- Run runBackfill() with mode=.enabled
- Assert: phase emits skipped_creator_chapters diagnostic, no FM calls, no inferred ChapterPlan written

Cancellation:
- Start runBackfill(), cancel mid-phase
- Assert: phase emits preempted diagnostic, no plan written, downstream stages still complete with baseline behavior

Transcript revision race:
- Start phase, mid-run change the transcript content hash (simulate revision)
- Assert: phase detects mismatch on exit, discards plan, emits race diagnostic

Failure modes:
- DeviceAdmissionPolicy denial: phase emits admission diagnostic, no FM cost
- Boundary detector returns 0 candidates: phase emits no_candidates diagnostic
- 50% operational unclear rate: phase emits operational_rate_exceeded, no plan written
- Pathological boundary rate from detector: phase emits pathological_rate, no plan written

- Phase wall-clock with real FM (8 chapters, ~500ms per call, concurrency 2): expected ~2.5 seconds, document but don't gate test on it (real FM is environment-dependent)

title: ChapterGenerationPhase parallelized labeling + ChapterPlanReady event
description: Parallelize per-candidate FM labeling within the phase, capped at the existing FM concurrency limit (~2 on-device). Reconstruct results in start-time order. Emit ChapterPlanReady event after successful plan write for future async coordination (current consumers read cache directly). Per-call failures don't abort the batch; plan-level threshold from L2 decides whether to keep the plan.
design:
Files affected:
- Playhead/Services/AdDetection/ChapterGenerationPhase.swift (extend phase with parallelized labeling)
- Playhead/Services/AdDetection/ChapterPlanReadyEvent.swift (new event type for fusion/consumer notification)

Parallelism design:
- For each ChapterCandidate from D1+D2, dispatch one ChapterLabelingService.label() call.
- Use Swift TaskGroup with concurrency capped at the existing FM concurrency limiter (typically 2 for on-device FM; verify exact value from FoundationModelClassifier).
- Per-candidate labeling is independent; safe to parallelize.
- Total wall-clock time for 12 chapters @ ~500ms per FM call with concurrency 2: ~3 seconds. Acceptable for a backfill phase.
- If any single label fails operationally (after retry), keep going — don't abort the whole batch. The plan-level threshold (L2) decides whether to drop the plan after all results are in.

Order preservation:
- TaskGroup results may arrive out of order; phase orchestrator reconstructs in start-time order before passing to L2 plan assembly.

Cancellation:
- TaskGroup respects parent cancellation token. If phase is cancelled, all in-flight FM calls cancel and partial results are discarded.

ChapterPlanReady event:
- After successful plan write, phase emits a typed event so other components can react.
- Currently the only built-in consumer is BackfillEvidenceFusion (which already reads ChapterEvidence on its own — no event subscription needed; the event is informational for now).
- Reserve the event for future async coordination (e.g., a coverage-plan refresh worker that wants to re-plan after chapter signal arrives).
- Event payload: { episodeContentHash, planConfidence, chapterCount, generatedAt }

Phase outcome (after this bead):
- mode == .off → no work done
- mode != .off → run boundary detection + parallelized labeling + plan assembly + cache write
- on success → emit completed diagnostic + ChapterPlanReady event
- on failure (any of the documented gates) → emit specific diagnostic, no plan written, no event

What this bead does NOT do:
- Wiring into AdDetectionService backfill pipeline (P4)
- Integration tests across the full phase (P4)
- Consumer subscriptions to ChapterPlanReady (deferred; consumers read cache directly for now)

Test coverage in P4:
- 4 candidates with mock FM → 4 labels back, plan written with 4 chapters
- 12 candidates with concurrency cap 2 → all 12 labeled, total wall time consistent with 6 sequential rounds
- Mid-run cancellation → all in-flight tasks cancel, partial results discarded
- 1 operational failure mid-batch → other 11 still complete, plan written if op rate <30%
- Order preservation: out-of-order task completion still produces sorted ChapterPlan.chapters
- ChapterPlanReady event fires once per successful plan, never on failure paths
acceptance_criteria:
- TaskGroup-based parallelization at the FM concurrency cap
- 12-chapter plan completes in ~6 sequential FM-call cycles (concurrency 2)
