- No event on any failure/abort path
- Tests in P4 cover all parallelization scenarios

title: Skip ChapterGenerationPhase when creator chapters present (creator-chapter precedence)
description: When an episode has any ChapterEvidence with ChapterSource ∈ {id3, pc20, rssInline} (i.e., creator-provided Podcasting 2.0 / ID3 / RSS chapters), ChapterGenerationPhase exits early without invoking the FM. Creator chapters are near-ground-truth; inferred chapters are statistical inference. Avoid paying FM cost when ground truth is already available. This implements Dan's 2026-05-06 directive on creator-chapter precedence.
design:
Files affected:
- Playhead/Services/AdDetection/ChapterGenerationPhase.swift (extend with creator-chapter check)

Behavior:
- Before invoking ChapterBoundaryDetector and ChapterLabelingService, query the existing chapter-evidence cache for the episode's content hash.
- If any ChapterEvidence with ChapterSource ∈ {id3, pc20, rssInline} exists (i.e., creator chapters were parsed via ChapterEvidenceParser), exit early.
- Emit chapter_phase_skipped_creator_chapters diagnostic with creator chapter count.
- Do NOT generate inferred chapters; do NOT incur FM cost; do NOT write any ChapterPlan.

Why:
- Creator-provided chapters (Podcasting 2.0, ID3 CHAP frames, RSS inline) are near-ground-truth.
- Inferred chapters are statistical inference with lower trust weight.
- Per Dan (2026-05-06): when creator chapters exist, prefer them — paying FM cost on inferred chapters is wasted compute when ground truth is already available.
- This is the answer to the design's reconciliation note about creator-chapter precedence.

Where to find creator chapters:
- ChapterEvidenceParser (Playhead/Services/AdDetection/ChapterEvidenceParser.swift) emits ChapterEvidence at episode-analysis time.
- Output is cached somewhere keyed by episode content hash (verify location during implementation; likely the same cache layer as other ad-detection artifacts).
- If creator chapters are stored alongside other parsed-feed metadata rather than in an ad-detection cache, this bead may need to bridge the two — document this if so.

Edge cases:
- Creator chapters present but quality is low (qualityScore < some threshold): still skip FM. Even low-quality creator chapters beat statistical inference. (This is a policy decision worth documenting; revisit if shadow eval shows we should override low-quality creator chapters.)
- Creator chapters partial coverage (e.g., only first half of episode has chapters): still skip FM for now. Mixed creator+inferred chapters is a follow-up bead if it proves necessary.
- Episode has 0 creator chapters but the parser ran: proceed to FM generation (no creator-chapter override).
- Episode has creator chapters but all are content-disposition (no ad-break chapters): still skip FM. The user-facing outcome is what matters; if creator says nothing here is an ad, trust it.

Consumer impact:
- Downstream consumers (CoveragePlanner, FM prompt) read ChapterEvidence regardless of source — they just see chapters. Whether the source is creator or inferred is informational (in ChapterSource enum), not behavioral, except where weighting differs.
- Creator chapters get full quality weight; inferred chapters get the existing metadata-cap discount via fusion.

Diagnostic payload for chapter_phase_skipped_creator_chapters:
- creator_chapter_count: int
- creator_chapter_sources: [ChapterSource] (which sources provided chapters)
- creator_quality_score_min/max/avg

Test coverage in P4:
- Episode with id3 chapters → skip FM, diagnostic emitted, no ChapterPlan written
- Episode with pc20 chapters → skip FM
- Episode with rssInline chapters → skip FM
- Episode with mixed creator + no inferred path → skip FM
- Episode with 0 creator chapters → proceed to FM generation
- Episode with creator chapters of all .content disposition → skip FM (trust creator)
acceptance_criteria:
- Episode with any creator-source ChapterEvidence skips FM phase entirely
- chapter_phase_skipped_creator_chapters diagnostic emitted with creator chapter count + source breakdown
- No ChapterPlan written when skipped
- No FM call cost incurred when skipped
- Episodes without creator chapters proceed to FM generation as normal
- Tests in P4 cover all ChapterSource combinations including mixed and edge cases

title: ChapterGenerationPhase shell: admission, transcript-snapshot race protection, cancellation
description: The skeleton ChapterGenerationPhase that ties together boundary detection (D1+D2) and labeling (L1+L2). Handles admission control via DeviceAdmissionPolicy (no FM cost when system can't run FM), transcript-snapshot-hash race protection (don't write plans against stale transcripts), and cancellation token honoring (preempted phases discard partial work). Skip-on-creator-chapters (P2) and per-chapter parallelism (P3) extend this shell.
design:
Files affected:
- Playhead/Services/AdDetection/ChapterGenerationPhase.swift (new — the phase shell + admission gating + race protection)

Phase shell responsibilities:
- Entry: caller passes (episodeContentHash, transcriptSnapshotHash, config). Phase computes and runs only if mode != .off (gate from F2).
- DeviceAdmissionPolicy check at entry: if denied (thermal, FM unavailable, region/hardware unsupported), emit chapter_phase_skipped_admission diagnostic and exit cleanly. Use exact admission API from existing FM phases (FoundationModelExtractor's admission check).
- Transcript snapshot capture: read final-pass transcript from cache; record its hash on entry.
- Run boundary detection (D1+D2) → candidates.
- If candidates empty, emit chapter_phase_no_candidates and exit.
- (Skip-on-creator-chapters check is in P2 — that bead extends this shell.)
- Run labeling (parallelized in P3 — that bead extends this shell).
- Re-check transcript hash on exit: if final-pass transcript content hash CHANGED while we were running, discard partial results (don't write a stale plan).
- If hash matches, write ChapterPlan to cache via ChapterPlanCache (from F1) and emit chapter_phase_completed diagnostic.

Race protection:
- Reason: final-pass transcripts can be revised (e.g., if more audio arrives, or a re-pass produces different chunks).
- Capture transcript content hash on entry (cheap; cached in TranscriptEngineService).
- On exit (just before cache write): re-fetch current transcript hash. If different, discard plan, log diagnostic. New transcript-completion event will trigger fresh phase run.

Cancellation:
- Phase honors backfill cancellation tokens (existing pattern from FoundationModelExtractor).
- On preempt: emit chapter_phase_preempted diagnostic with phase-stage info, discard partial work.

Concurrency:
- Phase is async; uses Swift concurrency (Task / actor).
- Phase itself is not actor-isolated, but ChapterPlanCache is (from F1).
- Per-chapter labeling parallelism is in P3.

What this bead does NOT do:
- Skip-on-creator-chapters logic (P2)
- Per-chapter parallelization (P3)
- Wiring into AdDetectionService backfill (P4)
- Integration tests across the whole phase (P4)

Logging discipline:
- Every exit path emits exactly one phase-completion diagnostic (success or specific failure).
- Don't emit redundant logs for the same outcome.

Test coverage in P4:
- Phase entry with mode=.off → no diagnostic, no work
- DeviceAdmissionPolicy denial → admission_skipped diagnostic, no FM cost
- No candidates → no_candidates diagnostic, no plan written
- Transcript revised mid-run → discard, no plan written, race diagnostic
- Cancellation mid-run → preempted diagnostic, no plan written
- Successful run → completed diagnostic, plan written, returnedPlan reflects what was cached
acceptance_criteria:
- Phase entry honors ChapterSignalMode gate (no work when mode == .off)
- DeviceAdmissionPolicy denial emits diagnostic and exits without FM cost
- Transcript content hash captured on entry, re-checked before cache write
- Hash mismatch → discard plan, log diagnostic
- Cancellation token honored; preempted runs emit diagnostic + discard partial state
- Successful path runs detector → labeler → cache write → completed diagnostic
- Tests in P4 cover entry/admission/race/cancellation/success paths

title: Plan-level failure handling: operational rate threshold + plan confidence math
description: Plan-level policy on top of per-call labeling (L1). When >30% of chapters fail operationally (FM was sick during this run), abort the whole plan rather than persist garbage. Compute duration-weighted plan confidence. Distinguish semantic unclears (kept; informational) from operational unclears (dropped or aborted).
design:
Files affected:
- Playhead/Services/AdDetection/ChapterGenerationPhase.swift (or wherever the assembly logic lives — this code may be in P3)
- Playhead/Services/AdDetection/ChapterPlan.swift (extend with operational rate calculation + plan-confidence math)

This bead is the gluing logic between L1 (per-chapter labeling) and the persisted ChapterPlan. It owns the policy decisions about what to keep and what to drop.

Operational unclear rate threshold:
- After all chapters labeled: count operational unclears (LabelFailureMode.operational) vs total chapters.
- If operational rate >30%, treat as system-distrust signal.
  - Action: do NOT write ChapterPlan to cache.
  - Emit chapter_phase_operational_unclear_rate_exceeded diagnostic with the rate observed.
  - Phase exits cleanly; baseline pipeline takes over.
  - Phase will retry on next backfill window when FM is healthier.
- Why 30%: starting placeholder. Tune via shadow-mode diagnostics.

Semantic unclears are kept:
- LabelFailureMode.semantic outcomes go into ChapterPlan.chapters with disposition = .ambiguous and qualityScore from the FM's reported confidence (typically low).
- Downstream consumers (CoveragePlanner, FM prompt) weight by qualityScore, so semantic unclears naturally contribute less.

Plan-level confidence math (lives in ChapterPlan struct):
- planConfidence = sum(chapter.qualityScore × chapter.duration) / total_duration
- Duration-weighted: a short low-confidence chapter has less impact than a long low-confidence chapter.
- planConfidence is informational (diagnostic + tuning) and may be used as a global down-weight on consumer reads.

Schema coercion (extends L1's per-call coercion):
- L1 already coerces invalid output at call time. L2 adds plan-level coercion: if too many chapters end up .unclear (semantic + operational > 50% of total), warn diagnostic but still write plan (the pipeline already weights by per-chapter confidence so this is OK).

Order of operations after labeling:
1. Collect all LabelingResults from L1 (parallelized by P3).
2. Compute operational rate; if >30%, abort phase.
3. Otherwise, assemble ChapterPlan with all chapters (operational unclears flagged for diagnostics but discarded? Or kept with qualityScore = 0 so consumers ignore? Decide and document).
   - Recommendation: discard operational unclears (we don't know what was there, so don't fabricate). Adjust subsequent chapter index/total accordingly.
4. Compute planConfidence (duration-weighted).
5. Emit chapter_phase_completed diagnostic.
6. Return ChapterPlan to phase orchestrator (P3) for cache write.

What this bead does NOT do:
- Phase orchestration / parallelism (P3)
- Cache write (P3)
- Wiring to AdDetectionService (P4)

Test coverage in L3 includes:
- Plan with 0% operational unclear → written normally
- Plan with 35% operational unclear → aborted, no plan written, diagnostic emitted
- Plan with 25% operational + 30% semantic unclear → written (operational below threshold)
- planConfidence math: empty → 0; uniform 0.8 → 0.8; mix of (0.9, 5min) and (0.1, 1min) → ~0.78
- Operational unclears removed from final plan; chapter index adjusted
acceptance_criteria:
- Plan with >30% operational unclear → abort, no plan written, diagnostic emitted
- Plan with high semantic unclear rate but low operational → still written (semantic unclears are valid information)
- Operational unclears removed from final plan (don't fabricate); chapter indices adjusted
- planConfidence is duration-weighted: sum(c.qualityScore × c.duration) / total
- Tests in L3 cover threshold edge cases and confidence math

title: ChapterLabelingService: Generable schema + single-call FM orchestration
description: FM-backed chapter labeler. One SystemLanguageModel call per candidate region, with @Generable structured-output schema. Emits a typed ChapterLabel that maps to existing ChapterDisposition (adBreak/content/ambiguous) plus a richer raw taxonomy preserved in ChapterPlan for downstream use. Retry-once on operational failure, distinguishes operational vs semantic unclear outcomes (informs L2's plan-level threshold).
design:
Files affected:
- Playhead/Services/AdDetection/ChapterLabelingService.swift (new)
- Playhead/Services/AdDetection/ChapterLabelSchema.swift (new) — @Generable schema for FM structured output

@Generable schema for FM output:
struct ChapterLabel: Generable, Sendable, Codable
  let disposition: ChapterDispositionRaw  // enum bridged to existing ChapterDisposition
  let confidence: Double                  // 0..1 self-reported confidence
  let topicDescriptor: String?            // optional ~1-sentence topic label, can be nil

ChapterDispositionRaw enum (mirrors existing ChapterDisposition + adds taxonomy):
  - intro
  - content
  - hostReadAd       (maps to ChapterDisposition.adBreak with disposition-detail flag)
  - programmaticAd   (maps to ChapterDisposition.adBreak with disposition-detail flag)
  - outro
  - recap
  - unclear          (maps to ChapterDisposition.ambiguous)

Why split rather than reuse ChapterDisposition directly:
- ChapterDisposition (adBreak/content/ambiguous) is the fusion-side type — semantically minimal.
- ChapterDispositionRaw is what FM emits — taxonomy richer for prompt-engineering and per-window context.
- After the FM call, ChapterLabelingService maps Raw → ChapterDisposition for the persisted ChapterEvidence (stored in ChapterPlan.chapters), preserving the rich taxonomy in a separate field if needed.
- This keeps existing code (ChapterMetadataEvidenceBuilder, fusion) unchanged.

Prompt builder (single FM call per chapter candidate):
Inputs:
- transcriptSegmentText: text within candidate boundary range
- prevChapterDisposition: ChapterDisposition? (for context — none for first chapter)
- positionInEpisode: (chapterIndex, totalChapters) — e.g., 4 of 7
- episodeMetadata: episode title, show name, duration (lightweight context)

Prompt shape (target ≤80 content tokens after schema overhead):
Line 1: "Classify this podcast chapter region. Output disposition, confidence, brief topic descriptor."
Line 2: "Context: chapter X of Y. Previous: <prevDisposition or 'none'>."
Line 3: "Region transcript: <text>"
Schema constraint via @Generable.

Single-call orchestration:
- One FM call per candidate (parallelized by phase orchestrator P3, not by labeler).
- Retry-once on operational failure (timeout, rate limit, transient FM unavailability).
- Out-of-taxonomy or invalid output → coerce to .unclear with operational flag.
- Exponential backoff between retry attempts (50ms-200ms).
- Hard timeout per call: 8 seconds (matches existing FM call budget).

Outputs:
struct LabelingResult (Sendable, Equatable):
  let chapter: ChapterEvidence  // with ChapterSource.inferred, qualityScore = label.confidence
  let labelDisposition: ChapterDispositionRaw  // raw taxonomy preserved separately
  let topicDescriptor: String?
  let failureMode: LabelFailureMode? // nil on success; .operational or .semantic on fallback to .unclear
  let attempts: Int  // 1 or 2 (retry-once)

LabelFailureMode (Sendable, Equatable):
  - operational: FM call failed (timeout, rate limit, schema validation). Means: FM was sick during this run.
  - semantic: FM returned successfully but said it doesn't know. Means: this chapter genuinely ambiguous.

Why distinguish: L2 uses operational rate >30% across plan to drop the whole plan (system distrust signal). Semantic unclears are kept as legitimate information.

Reuse existing patterns:
- DeviceAdmissionPolicy check at service level (probably caller's job, but verify in service entry).
- @Generable schema validation matches existing FM extractors (FoundationModelExtractor, PermissiveAdClassifier patterns).
- Shared FM concurrency limiter (from FoundationModelClassifier) — labeler doesn't manage its own concurrency, just makes calls.

What this bead does NOT do:
- Plan-level operational threshold (L2)
- Tests (L3)
- Phase orchestration / parallelism (P3)
acceptance_criteria:
- ChapterLabel @Generable schema compiles + validates
- Per-call orchestration calls FM with target ≤80 content tokens of context
- Retry-once on timeout/rate-limit/schema-validation
- Out-of-taxonomy output coerced to .unclear with .operational failure flag
- Successful semantic-unclear output preserved with .semantic failure flag
- Output ChapterEvidence has ChapterSource.inferred and qualityScore = label.confidence
- Hard 8s per-call timeout
- All existing FM tests still pass; new unit tests in L3 cover labeler behavior

title: Boundary density gates: pathological rate abort + cap-and-merge
description: Two safety nets for the heuristic boundary detector. (1) Pathological rate gate: if the detector emits more than 1 boundary per 90 seconds on average, it's glitching — abort, no plan written. (2) Cap-and-merge: target ~1 chapter per 5 minutes, floor of 8 chapters for episodes >40min, drop low-confidence boundaries and merge their flanking chapters. Both gates emit diagnostics so we can tune the thresholds empirically against real episodes.
design:
Files affected:
- Playhead/Services/AdDetection/ChapterBoundaryDetector.swift (extend with density management)

Two protections:

1. Pathological rate gate
- Compute average rate over episode: candidateCount / episodeDuration.
- If average rate is faster than 1 per 90 seconds (i.e., candidateCount > episodeDuration / 90), the detector is glitching (likely flickering music probability or thrashing speaker clustering).
- Action: emit chapter_phase_pathological_rate diagnostic, return empty list (phase exits cleanly without writing a plan; baseline pipeline takes over).
- Why 1/90s: chapters shorter than 90s are not really chapters — they are segmentation. The threshold tunes empirically via diagnostics from real episodes.

2. Cap-and-merge density management
- Target density: 1 chapter per 5 minutes.
- Floor: at least 8 chapters attempted, but only if episode is long enough (skip floor for episodes <40 min).
- Cap: keep top-N by boundaryConfidence where N = min(detected, max(8, ceil(episodeMinutes / 5))).
- Merge: dropped boundaries' flanking chapters merge based on which neighbor is closer in feature space (reuse triggeringSignals to compute similarity).
- For a 60-min episode: target ~12 chapters, floor 8 — typical retention 8-12 chapters.
- For a 30-min episode: skip floor → target 6 chapters, no minimum.
- For a 3-hour episode: target ~36 chapters; cap-and-merge keeps the strongest.

Order of operations:
1. Run detect() to get candidates.
2. Apply pathological rate gate first (cheap; abort early if glitching).
3. Apply cap-and-merge (sort by boundaryConfidence desc, keep top-N, merge dropped ones).
4. Re-sort by startTime ascending.
5. Return refined candidate list to phase orchestrator.

Edge cases:
- Episode <5 min: skip both gates. Take whatever the detector produces (may be just t=0).
- Detector returns 0: phase emits chapter_phase_no_candidates. Not an error.
- All candidates have boundaryConfidence < 0.3 (low-confidence detection): still proceed; FM labeler will assess each anyway. Diagnostics record this case for tuning.

Diagnostics events emitted:
- chapter_phase_pathological_rate (with detected count, episode duration, rate)
- chapter_phase_cap_applied (with before/after counts and dropped boundaries' confidences)
- chapter_phase_no_candidates (when detector returns empty list)

Testing in D3 covers:
- Pathological rate input → empty output + diagnostic emitted
- Dense input → cap applied, top-N retained
- Sparse input → all kept
- Floor of 8: when detected count >8 but density would imply <8, floor enforced
- Episode <5 min: no cap, no floor
acceptance_criteria:
- Pathological rate gate: input with >1 candidate/90s avg returns empty list + chapter_phase_pathological_rate diagnostic
- Cap-and-merge: when detected count exceeds target, top-N by boundaryConfidence retained; dropped boundaries' chapters merge to nearest neighbor in feature space
- Floor of 8: enforced only for episodes >=40min
- Episodes <5min skip both gates
- Cap operation emits chapter_phase_cap_applied diagnostic
- Unit tests in D3 cover all edge cases

title: ChapterBoundaryDetector core algorithm (heuristic, no FM)
description: Heuristic boundary candidate generator for inferred chapters. Reads existing acoustic + lexical + speaker-clustering features (already computed by upstream services) and emits ordered boundary candidates with per-boundary confidence. Pure CPU work — no FM, no new acoustic computation. The boundary skeleton is what the FM labeler (L1) decorates with chapter types and disposition.
design:
Files affected:
- Playhead/Services/AdDetection/ChapterBoundaryDetector.swift (new)
- May read from existing feature snapshots in TranscriptEngineService / ClassifierService / FeatureExtractionService

Inputs (all already computed by existing services — no new acoustic computation required):
- Music probability windows (~2s windows from FeatureExtractionService)
- RMS / spectral flux windows
- Speaker cluster IDs (from speaker clustering pipeline; per-chunk or per-window)
- Lexical hits with category densities (from LexicalScanner output)
- Pause-length features (from VAD/pause anchors that drive transcript chunking)

Heuristic boundary signals:
1. Music onset / offset: significant change in music probability (>0.5 delta) is a strong chapter boundary signal (intros, outros, ad jingles).
2. Speaker shift: speaker cluster ID transition that lasts >5s (filters out crosstalk).
3. Lexical category density jump: sudden shift in dominant lexical category (e.g., normal-content → ad-cue density spike).
4. Long pause: silence/non-speech window >2s often marks structural transitions.
5. Combined: weighted sum of (1)-(4) with empirical weights; weights start at 0.4/0.3/0.2/0.1 and tune via shadow eval.

Output:
struct ChapterCandidate (Sendable, Equatable):
  startTime: TimeInterval (boundary timestamp; chapter starts here)
  boundaryConfidence: Float (0..1, weighted sum normalized)
  triggeringSignals: [BoundarySignal] (which signals fired; for diagnostics)

func detect(features: ChapterFeatureSnapshot) -> [ChapterCandidate]
- Returns boundaries in order
- Includes a synthetic episode-start boundary at t=0 (always; first chapter starts at episode start)
- Does NOT include episode-end boundary (chapters use start times; the last chapter implicitly ends at episode duration)

What this bead does NOT do:
- Density gates (D2 — pathological rate abort, cap-and-merge)
- FM labeling (L1)
- Phase wiring (P1)
- Synthetic feature input mocking for tests (D3)

Performance target:
- Detector should run in <50ms per episode on a 60-min show. It is pure heuristic computation over already-cached features. No FM, no allocation hot loops.

Notes on edge cases:
- Pure-monologue episode (no speaker shifts, no music): may produce only the t=0 boundary plus a few weak lexical/pause boundaries. Fine — D2 will apply the floor of 8 chapters minimum density target if possible.
- Talk-heavy show with many topic shifts: many candidates. D2 caps to ~1/5min density.
- Episode shorter than 5 minutes: detector still runs; D2 sets floor differently (don't force 8 chapters into a 4-min episode — produce as many as detected, no cap).

Tuning:
- Weights for signal-combination start at 0.4/0.3/0.2/0.1 (music/speaker/lexical/pause). Document why.
- Tune empirically via shadow-mode eval (E4) on hand-labeled fixtures.
acceptance_criteria:
- ChapterBoundaryDetector emits ordered ChapterCandidate list from existing feature snapshots
- Synthetic episode-start (t=0) boundary always included
- Music/speaker/lexical/pause signals all contribute via weighted sum
- Per-episode runtime <50ms on a 60-min show
- No new feature extraction added (reuses everything already cached)
- Unit tests in D3 cover synthetic-feature scenarios

- chapter_phase_started: episode hash, transcript content hash snapshot, mode
- chapter_phase_skipped_creator_chapters: episode has ChapterSource ∈ {id3, pc20, rssInline}, no FM cost incurred
- chapter_phase_skipped_admission: DeviceAdmissionPolicy denied (thermal, FM unavailable, region/hardware unsupported)
- chapter_phase_no_candidates: ChapterBoundaryDetector returned 0 candidates (short episode, monologue, pure music)
- chapter_phase_pathological_rate: candidate rate >1 per 90 seconds avg → detector glitch detected, abort
- chapter_phase_cap_applied: detected count exceeded target density, cap-and-merge applied (record before/after counts)
- chapter_phase_label_failed: per-call FM failure (op-vs-semantic flag in payload), retry attempted, final outcome
- chapter_phase_operational_unclear_rate_exceeded: >30% operational unclear → plan dropped
- chapter_phase_completed: success, plan written, chapter count, plan confidence, FM call count, latency
- chapter_phase_preempted: backfill cancellation token fired mid-phase
- chapter_phase_decode_failure: cache decode failed on read (rare; emit so we can detect cache corruption in field)

Each event:
- episode_id_hash (matches existing scheduler_events keying)
- timestamp (epoch)
- event_type (one of above)
- payload (per-event JSON blob)

Why this matters:
- Eval (E2-E4) needs structured signals to compute lift, FM cost, and case studies.
- Field debugging: when chapter signal misbehaves we need to know which gate fired without re-running.
- Tuning: the 30% operational unclear threshold and the 1/90s pathological rate are placeholders. Diagnostics tell us what real episodes produce so we can tune empirically.

Privacy: all keys hashed; no episode titles, no transcripts, no advertiser names in diagnostics. Same redaction policy as existing scheduler_events.

Schema versioning: add chapter_phase_events as a new top-level array in diagnostics JSON, sibling to scheduler_events. Bumping its schema is independent.

Testing:
- Each event type emits with expected payload shape
- Hashed episode ID matches scheduler_events keying convention
- Privacy: no PII in payloads (assert against fixture episode with known title/advertiser)
- Diagnostics JSON parses with existing diagnostics tooling (don't break the bundle pipeline)
acceptance_criteria:
- Each documented event type emits with the documented payload shape
- Events keyed by hashed episode ID (no PII)
- Privacy review: zero leakage of episode titles, transcripts, advertiser names, user-identifiable data
- chapter_phase_events appears as a new top-level array in dogfood diagnostics JSON
- Existing diagnostics tooling parses the new schema without errors
- Unit tests for each event type with golden payload fixtures

title: Add ChapterSignalMode gate to AdDetectionConfig (mirror FMBackfillMode)
description: Add a tri-state gate that controls chapter-signal generation and consumption. Mirrors the existing FMBackfillMode pattern (Playhead/Services/AdDetection/FMBackfillMode.swift) so engineers and operators have a familiar shape. Gate is what allows the eval harness (E1-E4) to run shadow comparisons safely.
design:
Files affected:
- Playhead/Services/AdDetection/ChapterSignalMode.swift (new)
- Playhead/Services/AdDetection/AdDetectionConfig.swift — add chapterSignalMode field
- Whatever file holds the live config wiring (typically AppEnvironment or PlayheadRuntime)

ChapterSignalMode states:
- off: ChapterGenerationPhase never runs. Consumers (CoveragePlanner, FM prompts) ignore any cached plans. Equivalent to today's behavior. THIS IS THE DEFAULT.
- shadow: ChapterGenerationPhase runs and writes ChapterPlan to cache, but consumers do NOT read the plan. Used for plan-quality eval and FM-cost telemetry without affecting detection behavior. Phase-quality metrics still feed diagnostics.
- enabled: Phase runs AND consumers read. Full activation.

Optional richer states (only if needed during shadow tuning):
- coverageOnly: phase runs, only CoveragePlanner reads (FM prompt context disabled)
- promptOnly: phase runs, only FM prompt builders read (CoveragePlanner unchanged)
- These help isolate consumer-by-consumer impact during shadow tuning. Defer to a follow-up bead if not needed initially.

Pattern reference: FMBackfillMode has off/shadow/rescoreOnly/proposalOnly/full. Use exactly the same enum + Codable shape so config plumbing is interchangeable.

Wiring:
- Add a chapterSignalMode field to AdDetectionConfig defaulting to .off.
- The config is already injected through AdDetectionService init (find current call sites with grep before adding the param).
- Phase entry guard: skip generation when mode is .off.
- CoveragePlanner read guard: only consult chapter plan when mode is .enabled.
- FM prompt read guard: same as CoveragePlanner.
- Shadow telemetry: when mode is .shadow, ChapterPlanReady event still fires (for eval), but consumer reads do not happen.

Testing:
- Default config has chapterSignalMode = .off (production safe by default)
- Decoding old config JSON without the field → defaults to .off
- All three modes decode/encode round-trip
- A 'mode-disabled fallback' integration test asserting CoveragePlanner and FM prompt behavior is byte-for-byte identical to today when mode == .off and == .shadow
acceptance_criteria:
- ChapterSignalMode enum exists with off, shadow, enabled (and any documented richer states); Codable, Equatable, Sendable
- Wired into AdDetectionConfig with default .off
- Phase entry guard, CoveragePlanner consumer guard, FM prompt consumer guard all reference the mode
- Backwards-compat: old serialized configs deserialize with mode = .off
- Tests verify each mode produces expected behavior

title: Extend ChapterSource enum with .inferred + define ChapterPlan cache artifact
description: Foundational data-model work for the chapter signal sub-epic. Add a new ChapterSource.inferred variant so FM-generated chapters can ride the existing ChapterEvidence + ChapterMetadataEvidenceBuilder + BackfillEvidenceFusion path with no fusion changes. Define the ChapterPlan cache artifact (the orchestration envelope) and its content-hash-keyed cache. This is the foundation every other bead in the sub-epic depends on.
design:
Files affected:
- Playhead/Services/AdDetection/ChapterEvidence.swift — extend ChapterSource enum.
- Playhead/Services/AdDetection/ChapterPlan.swift (new) — ChapterPlan struct.
- Playhead/Services/AdDetection/ChapterPlanCache.swift (new) — content-hash-keyed cache, modelled on existing FM artifact caches under AnalysisAsset.

ChapterSource extension:
- Add case 'inferred' alongside existing id3/pc20/rssInline.
- Update ChapterEvidence.qualityScore comment to note that .inferred uses ChapterLabelingService confidence (not parser-based scoring).
- Update any existing exhaustive switches over ChapterSource (grep before adding to make sure compile-time exhaustiveness still holds).

ChapterPlan struct:
- episodeContentHash: String (the AnalysisAsset content hash key)
- chapters: [ChapterEvidence] (the inferred chapters; all have ChapterSource.inferred at construction time)
- planConfidence: Double (duration-weighted: sum(chapter.qualityScore × duration) / total_duration)
- generatedAt: Date
- schemaVersion: Int (start at 1; increment on serialization-breaking changes, triggers cache invalidation)
- generationDiagnostics: ChapterPlanDiagnostics (small struct: candidate count detected, candidates kept after cap, operational unclear count, semantic unclear count)
- Codable + Sendable + Equatable
- Default JSONEncoder/JSONDecoder for cache persistence (match existing FM artifact pattern)

ChapterPlanCache:
- Storage location: same content-hash-keyed cache directory as existing FM artifacts (AnalysisAsset-adjacent).
- API: get(contentHash) -> ChapterPlan?, put(contentHash, plan), invalidate(contentHash)
- Schema version mismatch on read → return nil (treat as missing), regeneration triggered by phase.
- Decode failure → return nil + log diagnostic, don't crash.
- Concurrency: actor-isolated, mirroring existing artifact caches.

Note that ChapterPlan.chapters is [ChapterEvidence], not a new Chapter type. ChapterEvidence already has start/end/title/source/disposition/qualityScore — those are the fields we'd want on a Chapter anyway. Reusing the existing type means: zero changes to ChapterMetadataEvidenceBuilder, zero changes to BackfillEvidenceFusion, and creator/inferred chapters look identical to consumers (except via the source enum).

What this bead does NOT do:
- Boundary detection (D1)
- FM labeling (L1)
- Phase orchestration (P1)
- Consumer integration (C1, M1)
- Wiring into AdDetectionService (P4)

Testing scope:
- ChapterPlan Codable round-trip (serialize → deserialize → equality)
- Schema version mismatch returns nil from cache
- Duration-weighted planConfidence math: empty chapters → 0; all-confident → ~1.0; mixed → expected weighted value
- ChapterPlanCache concurrent read/write does not corrupt
- Decode failure on corrupted file is handled gracefully (returns nil, no crash)
acceptance_criteria:
- ChapterSource.inferred variant compiles + all existing exhaustive switches updated
- ChapterPlan struct compiles, Codable, Sendable, Equatable
- ChapterPlanCache supports get/put/invalidate, content-hash keyed, actor-isolated
- Schema version mismatch → cache miss
- Decode failure → cache miss (no crash)
- planConfidence = sum(chapter.qualityScore × duration) / total_duration (duration-weighted)
- All existing chapter-evidence tests still pass
- New unit tests for ChapterPlan and ChapterPlanCache pass on PlayheadFastTests

title: Chapter signal: inferred generation + new consumers (2026-05-06)
description: Refines and extends the chapter-evidence work begun in playhead-rxuv and playhead-w7oi. Reconciles the 2026-05-06 brainstorm design (docs/plans/2026-05-06-chapter-signal-for-ad-detection-design.md) with the existing ChapterEvidence/ChapterParser/ChapterMetadataEvidenceBuilder code. Replaces the original 'single per-episode FM call' approach in playhead-w7oi with a chunked, heuristic-skeleton + per-chapter FM labeling approach that fits the actual on-device FM token budget (~300-400 content tokens per call after ~3700-token schema overhead). Adds two net-new chapter-signal consumers beyond fusion: CoveragePlanner attention-direction and per-window FM prompt context augmentation. All work runs in backfill (charging+idle), is gated by a ChapterSignalMode mirroring FMBackfillMode, and falls back to today's pipeline behavior on any failure path.
design:
Why this exists: the dueling-wizards epic identified chapter evidence as a high-value signal (rxuv/w7oi). Implementation work since then revealed that (a) FM token budget rules out single-call episode chaptering and (b) chapter evidence has more downstream uses than fusion alone. This sub-epic captures the refined plan.

Architecture summary:
- Existing types reused: ChapterEvidence (add ChapterSource.inferred variant), ChapterDisposition (already covers adBreak/content/ambiguous), ChapterMetadataEvidenceBuilder (no changes), BackfillEvidenceFusion (no changes — chapter evidence already rides metadataEntries with cap 0.15).
- New: ChapterPlan cache artifact (content-hash-keyed envelope holding [ChapterEvidence] with .inferred source + phase metadata), ChapterPlanCache, ChapterBoundaryDetector (heuristic, no FM), ChapterLabelingService (FM-backed, one call per chapter), ChapterGenerationPhase (orchestrator).
- Gate: ChapterSignalMode (off/shadow/enabled) added to AdDetectionConfig, mirroring FMBackfillMode pattern.
- New consumers: CoveragePlanner reads chapter evidence (from any ChapterSource) to inform audit-window selection; FM prompt builders inject ~30-50 tokens of chapter context.
- Creator-chapter precedence (Dan 2026-05-06): when episode already has ChapterEvidence with ChapterSource ∈ {id3, pc20, rssInline}, the generation phase exits early without invoking FM.

Failure-mode discipline: every new path is purely additive. Missing chapter plan, FM unavailable, low-confidence labels, schema validation failures — all fall back to today's pipeline behavior. Gate-driven shadow mode allows generating + measuring chapters without affecting decisions.

Eval bar (Q2-C from brainstorm): measurable lift on at least one of {recall, precision} on dogfood corpus without regression on the other AND at least one specific known-miss case-study fix; FM cost increase ≤2× current refinement-pass cost.
acceptance_criteria:
Epic complete when:
- All foundation/detection/labeling/phase/consumer beads closed
- ChapterSignalMode flipped from off → shadow → enabled in production
- narl-eval shadow-mode reports show measurable lift on dogfood corpus
- 5-10 known-miss case studies documented with before/after diagnostic captures
- FM cost stays within 2× current refinement-pass budget
- playhead-w7oi superseded or refined to point at this work
- Updated design doc reflects shipped architecture
notes:
REFUSAL-CRACK TRANSFER (2026-07-19, E5 measurement): the chapter-labeling ~40% guardrail-abort problem may be largely solvable — the E-program found EXTRACTION task shape (extract framing + extraction schema output, e.g. AdMetadataSchema) collapses FM output-classifier refusals ~3x on the SAME sensitive editorial content (124→40 primary failures on the 24-ep corpus) where classification framing, taxonomy framing, schema-suppress, permissive guardrails, and greedy-off all did NOTHING (8-lever sweep, [[project_coverage_program_2026-07-18]] §7/§9). If chapter labeling reframes its region call as extraction (list topics/entities) + deterministic mapping instead of classify-this-region, the abort rate should drop sharply. Caveat: extraction fields are NOT verbatim-faithful (paraphrased artifacts) — use for attention/labels, verify deterministically.
Deferred 2026-07-24 (founder reorder): retention-phase work — revisit at ~$5k MRR / after listeners love the core. Not deleted, just not now. Categories: Mac, TTS, chapters, federation, ad-atlas, specialist/fancy-AI, detection improvements users won't notice.

title: C26 H-1 follow-up: evaluate listen-rewind weak signal feeding demotion counter
description:
Open question after C26 H-1 doc fix (option B): the current divergence between recordListenRewind (0.05, bypasses TrustScoringService state machine) and TrustScoringService.recordFalseSkipSignal (0.10, runs state machine) is documented as deliberate (listen-rewind is a weaker signal than explicit 'Not an ad' tap). But the state-machine BYPASS may be a real defect: multiple listen-rewinds in a row should plausibly contribute toward demotion via recentFalseSkipSignals. Today recordListenRewind increments recentFalseSkipSignals but does NOT run evaluateDemotion, so the counter accumulates without ever triggering a mode transition.

Question: should N consecutive listen-rewinds at weight 0.05 be enough to demote? Or does the existing FalseSkipSignal path (0.10 each) provide sufficient demotion pressure on its own and listen-rewind should remain pure-signal?

Resolution proposed (option C from the original analysis): add a separate listen-specific trust API on TrustScoringService (e.g. recordWeakFalseSkipSignal) that decrements by 0.05 but still runs the state machine. Preserves the deliberate magnitude difference while unifying the writer path.

Gating: do not implement until NarlEvalHarness eval shows that listen-rewind-driven demotion either (a) catches real false-positive shows the current path misses, or (b) demotes shows the user actually trusts. Without eval evidence, no behavior change is justified.
notes: Deferred 2026-07-24 (founder reorder): retention-phase work — revisit at ~$5k MRR / after listeners love the core. Not deleted, just not now. Categories: Mac, TTS, chapters, federation, ad-atlas, specialist/fancy-AI, detection improvements users won't notice.

title: FrozenTrace lifecycle threading: terminalReason + coverage fields into corpus-builder
description:
## Problem

NARL real-data findings (2026-04-24) called out that gtt9.8 telemetry (`asset-lifecycle-log.jsonl` with `terminalReason` + transcript/feature coverage end times) is written by `AnalysisStore` and the live runtime, but the **NARL corpus builder doesn't thread those fields into FrozenTrace JSON**. Inspection of new fixtures showed:

```
71F0C2AE: durationSec=None, analysisState=None, terminalReason=None,
          fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime=None, featureCoverageEndTime=None
34C7E7CF: same — all None
```

Without these fields in fixtures, the harness can't classify pipeline-coverage failures against lifecycle ground truth — it has to fall back to evidence-ledger inference, which doesn't distinguish 'never analyzed' from 'analyzed up to 90s then stopped.'

## Proposed fix

Extend the corpus builder + FrozenTrace schema to thread these per-episode fields:

- `durationSec: Double?`
- `analysisState: String?` (e.g., 'transcribing' / 'classifying' / 'backfill' / 'completed')
- `terminalReason: String?` (full coverage / interrupted / paused / etc.)
- `fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime: Double?` (seconds into asset)
- `featureCoverageEndTime: Double?` (seconds into asset)

Source these from the live `AnalysisStore` snapshot at capture time (or replay them from `asset-lifecycle-log.jsonl` if the live store doesn't carry historical state). Codable back-compat — all fields optional.

## Acceptance

- New fixture captured under this build has non-None values for all five fields.
- Harness can compute a 'pipeline coverage classification' axis (e.g., 'fully-covered' vs 'stalled-at-Xs' vs 'never-started').
- Existing harness still loads pre-fix fixtures (decode handles missing fields).

## Reference

- Doc: `docs/narl/2026-04-24-real-data-findings.md` Finding 3
- Lifecycle telemetry source: `asset-lifecycle-log.jsonl` schema v1
- Schema touchpoint: PlayheadTests/Fixtures/NarlEval/<date>/FrozenTrace-*.json
- Harness consumer: `PlayheadTests/Services/ReplaySimulator/NarlEval/NarlEvalHarnessTests.swift`
close_reason: Threaded lifecycle fields through corpus export/builder fallback with focused tests and two clean iterative review rounds.

title: L2F replay adapter: position-derived AdSegmentType mapping (replace hard-coded .midRoll)
description:
The L2F replay adapter (`CorpusAnnotation+ReplayAdapter.swift`) currently maps every `CorpusAnnotation.AdWindow` to `GroundTruthAdSegment.AdSegmentType.midRoll` because the existing simulator enum has only `.preRoll`/`.midRoll`/`.postRoll` and no neutral case.

This loses fidelity for two evaluation paths:
1. Pre-roll detection — corpus episodes with ads at start_seconds == 0 (or near-zero) should map to `.preRoll`, not `.midRoll`. Conflating them masks pre-roll-specific false-positive/false-negative analysis.
2. Post-roll detection — corpus episodes with ads at the end (end_seconds near duration_seconds) should map to `.postRoll`. Same conflation issue.

## Implementation
1. Decide between (a) extending `AdSegmentType` with a neutral `.unspecified` case OR (b) deriving position from `start_seconds` / `end_seconds` relative to `duration_seconds`. (b) is preferred — the corpus annotation already has the necessary timestamps and adding cases to the enum risks breaking exhaustive switches in the simulator.
2. In `CorpusAnnotation+ReplayAdapter.swift`, replace the hard-coded `.midRoll` with position-derived mapping:
   - `start_seconds < pre_roll_threshold` (e.g., 30s OR < 1% of duration) → `.preRoll`
   - `end_seconds > duration_seconds - post_roll_threshold` (e.g., 30s OR > 99% of duration) → `.postRoll`
   - Otherwise → `.midRoll`
3. Add a `// TODO` removal note matching the one in the PR.
4. Tests: assert pre/mid/post-roll classification at boundary values (≤ threshold, == threshold, > threshold) for both start and end positions.

## Risk
Low — purely a mapping change scoped to L2F adapter. No simulator-side changes if option (b) is chosen.

## Success criteria
- All 4 corpus annotation categories (clear host-read, dynamic insertion, blended, edge cases) get correctly typed segments based on timestamp position.
- Simulator-side ad-type analytics (per-segment-type FP/FN rates) stop being polluted by misclassified pre/post-roll ads as mid-roll.
- Existing 31 L2F tests still pass.

## Source bead
Surfaced by skeptical-iterative-code-review for playhead-l2f (PR #110, merged at eb5d907b). The TODO is in CorpusAnnotation+ReplayAdapter.swift.

title: Final-pass per-shard cooperative thermal check (B-1)
description:
Add per-shard thermal/charge/LPM check inside FinalPassRetranscriptionRunner.retranscribeWindow's intersectingShards loop so a warming device defers cleanly mid-window instead of leaving the row stranded in 'running' when the app is suspended mid-transcribe.

Why: Today retranscribeWindow only honors Task.checkCancellation() between shards — it does NOT re-check currentDeferReason() per shard. A window starts on a nominal device, thermal climbs, the app is backgrounded mid-transcribe, and the row is left in 'running' with retryCount=0 until the 10-min stranded-row reaper unsticks it on next cold launch. Combined with the launch-only retry trigger, that produces user-visible 'doesn't finish processing'.

How to apply: At the top of the for-shard loop in retranscribeWindow (FinalPassRetranscriptionRunner.swift:502-547):
  1. Re-check await currentDeferReason(); if non-nil:
  2. Persist any newChunks accumulated so far (so partial work isn't lost on subsequent runs that re-enter the same window).
  3. Mark current job 'deferred' via markFinalPassJobDeferred.
  4. Throw a typed sentinel (FinalPassDeferredMidWindow) that the outer runFinalPassBackfill catches and treats as 'gate trip — defer remaining siblings + return'.

Tests: arm capabilitySnapshotProvider to flip .nominal -> .fair after shard N; assert the row ends in 'deferred', that partial chunks landed, and that siblings are also deferred.

Risk: medium — touches the ASR hot loop. Verify partial-chunk dedupe via segmentFingerprint still works on resume (existing hasTranscriptChunk guard at line 538-541).

title: Final-pass thermal-recovery observer (B-2)
description:
Add ProcessInfo.thermalStateDidChangeNotification observer in PlayheadRuntime that, on state == .nominal AND charging AND !LPM, kicks off runFinalPassBackfillForAllAssetsAtLaunch (debounced: 1 outstanding, rate-limited to ~120s).

Why: Without this, the only retry trigger for thermalThrottled-deferred final_pass_jobs is a fresh cold-launch on a cool, charging, non-LPM device. Real device evidence (xcappdata 2026-05-02): one Acast asset has 17 final_pass_jobs deferred (all retryCount=0, all deferReason='thermalThrottled') and one stuck running with the same deferReason audit-trail. They never drain. User-visible symptom: 'doesn't appear to be finishing processing'.

How to apply: New observer alongside existing thermal observers in PlayheadRuntime.start. Reuses runFinalPassBackfillForAllAssetsAtLaunch as the single admission source of truth. Debounced by an outstanding-Task guard; rate-limited by a last-fired timestamp. Cancellable via existing shutdown() Task tracking (mirrors H-Z1).

Tests: simulate thermal .fair -> .nominal while charging+!LPM; assert sweep fires and admits previously-deferred jobs. Plus debounce test (two rapid notifications -> one sweep).

Risk: low — purely additive trigger source.

title: Fusion path: buildFusionAdWindow does not stamp eligibilityGate, gate stripped on app-restart preload
description:
Bug 8 forensic review (commit 457fa922) found that `buildFusionAdWindow` in `AdDetectionService.swift:2503` does NOT stamp `eligibilityGate` on the persisted fusion window.

The fusion path consumes the gate via `AdDecisionResult` at decision-time (so live runs are correct), but on app-restart preload (`SkipOrchestrator.beginEpisode`) the persisted row has NULL `eligibilityGate` — silently stripped.

**Direction:** under-restriction risk — a window that was correctly demoted to `markOnly` at decision-time could be re-armed for auto-skip after app restart.

**Fix scope:** stamp `eligibilityGate` (and `precisionGateRationale` if non-null) on the row `buildFusionAdWindow` persists. Add a regression test that drives a fusion window through persist → restart → preload and asserts the gate survives.

**Found by:** Bug 8 forensic SQL review on captured xcappdata 2026-04-30.

title: Precision gate: catalogMatchSimilarity dead-pass at AdDetectionService.swift:4256
description:
Bug 8 forensic review (commit 457fa922) found that the precision gate call site at `AdDetectionService.swift:4256` does NOT pass `catalogMatchSimilarity` to the gate. The `SafetySignal.catalogMatch` field wired up in playhead-gtt9.13 is silently dead at this call site.

Empty AdCatalogStore on the captured device made it moot for now, but once the catalog has entries this gate becomes load-bearing for borderline windows.

**Fix scope:** plumb `catalogStoreMatchSimilarity` (already on `AdWindow`) into the `precisionGateLabel` call. One-line wiring + a focused test that proves catalog-match raises a markOnly window to autoSkip when score is borderline.

**Found by:** Bug 8 forensic SQL review on captured xcappdata 2026-04-30.

title: UI handler reconcile: paused/cancelled copy + ActivityViewModel routing post-own9
description:

2. ActivityViewModel.makeSnapshot — user-cancelled jobs now flow into pausedRows. Previously dropped via terminalOutcome returning nil for unfinished cancelled jobs. Decide whether pausedRows is the right home, or if cancelled-by-user should be filtered out of the activity surface entirely.

Same applies to .userPreempted (now also routes to (paused, cancelled, none)).

title: Shareable transcript quotes with deep links
description:
## Background

Shareable transcript quotes: long-press (or text-selection toggle) on transcript lines in TranscriptPeekView, select a passage, get an editorial-formatted share artifact via UIActivityViewController with a deep link back into the app.

This is the only idea in either dueling-idea-wizards top-5 list that creates **user acquisition** (every other idea improves the experience for existing users). For a pre-launch app, that's existential — when someone shares a beautifully formatted quote with "Shared from Playhead" attribution, every reader is an organic acquisition channel.

## Cross-Model Validation

- CC self-score: 600 — "Tiny implementation, outsized word-of-mouth; fits design identity"
- COD cross-score: 710 — "Low engineering risk, fast to ship, high delight for vocal user segment; good organic distribution channel if share artifact is tasteful"
- Verdict: HIGH consensus; not in backlog (no overlapping bead found)

## Goals

- One-gesture sharing of a verbatim transcript passage with episode/timestamp attribution
- Editorial typographic format (matches TranscriptPeekView aesthetic, not growth-hacky)
- Deep-link round-trip: tapping a shared link opens Playhead at that timestamp
- Share-from-app converts to user acquisition for the pre-launch growth phase

## Implementation Approach

1. `TranscriptPeekView` — add long-press gesture on transcript lines (or a subtle text-selection mode toggle). User selects a range; selection highlighted with Copper tint (matches existing word-highlight color).
2. Context menu: **Copy Quote** / **Share Quote**.
3. Output format (editorial, no emoji except optional headphones):
   ```
   "Selected quote text here, possibly multi-line."

   — Show Title, "Episode Title"
   12:47

   🎧 Shared from Playhead
   ```
4. **Copy Quote** → `UIPasteboard`. **Share Quote** → `UIActivityViewController` with text + optional `playhead://episode/{id}?t={seconds}` deep link.
5. URL scheme registration (if not already registered) + handler in `PlayheadAppDelegate` that resolves episode ID, opens NowPlayingView, seeks to timestamp.
6. New `QuoteFormatter` struct (~50 lines) that composes the share text from episode metadata + selected text + `TimeFormatter`.
7. Total scope: ~200 lines SwiftUI + small formatter. No new services, no new data stores, no new analysis.

## Risks and Concerns

- **Legal/attribution posture around quoting podcasts.** Mitigations: same as transcripts already shown in TranscriptPeekView (display is settled); explicit show + episode + timestamp attribution; "Shared from Playhead" line includes the source app for plausible-fair-use framing. Same posture as Snipd and Apple Podcasts share clip.
- **"Growth-hacky branding chrome" risk** (COD's specific concern). Mitigation: editorial serif format, no emoji proliferation, understated "Shared from Playhead" not "✨ Made with Playhead AI ✨". Match the restraint of Quiet Instrument identity.
- **Deep-link reliability** — URL scheme handler must work from cold launch (not just resume). Test against background-suspended state.
- **iOS share-sheet variability** — different recipient apps render rich text differently (Twitter strips formatting, Notes preserves it). Format as plain text with line breaks for maximum portability.

## Success Criteria

- Long-press on a transcript chunk produces a selection in <100ms
- Share artifact renders identically across iMessage, Notes, Mail, Twitter, Slack (plain text)
- Deep-link tap opens app and seeks within ±2 seconds of source timestamp 100% of the time on a suite of 10 fixture URLs
- Beta-user qualitative feedback: "I'd actually share this" (not "this looks like ad copy")
- No design-identity violations on the share artifact

## Provenance

- Source: 2026-04-29 dueling-idea-wizards run, CC #4
- Cross-model verdict: HIGH on both sides; novel against backlog
- Full context: DUELING_WIZARDS_REPORT.md, WIZARD_IDEAS_CC.md (idea #4), WIZARD_SCORES_COD_ON_CC.md (score 710)

title: Structure-aware silence compression
description:
## Background

Structure-aware silence compression: selectively compress non-content audio (music beds between segments, dead air during transitions, long intro/outro jingles) while preserving speech cadence, dramatic pauses, and conversation rhythm.

This is the highest-scoring blind-spot idea from the 2026-04-29 dueling-idea-wizards run (orchestrator score 820/1000). It's a Smart Speed killer: Overcast Smart Speed compresses all silence uniformly and gets disabled on narrative shows; this knows what kind of silence it's compressing because Playhead already computes the structural data per FeatureWindow.

## Cross-Model Validation

- Origin: CC blind-spot idea #1 (post-adversarial round)
- Orchestrator score: 820 (highest of all blind-spot ideas)
- Not cross-scored adversarially (blind-spots phase is one-pass)
- Distinct from playhead-pfn (Per-Show Playback Speed Memory), which is about *remembering* a chosen speed

## Goals

- Compress non-speech audio (music beds, dead air between segments, long jingles) without touching speech cadence
- Recover 8-15 minutes per day for a 2-hour-daily listener — invisibly
- No "minutes saved" counter (peace of mind, not metrics)
- No user-facing toggle in primary UI (it just works)
- Per-show override available ("keep full music on this show")

## Implementation Approach

1. New `SilenceCompressor` helper (~300 lines on `PlaybackService`).
2. Reads `FeatureWindow` data for the upcoming 60 seconds:
   - `musicProbability > 0.7` AND `musicBedLevel != .none` → music-bed candidate
   - `pauseProbability` high AND adjacent to `speakerChange` → dead-air candidate
   - `pauseProbability` high BETWEEN two windows with same `speakerClusterId` → dramatic pause, PRESERVE
3. Uses `musicBedOnsetScore` / `musicBedOffsetScore` to mark precise compression boundaries.
4. Adjusts AVPlayer `rate` in real time: 2.0–3.0x in compressible regions, return to user's base speed on exit.
5. Transitions use the existing 0.15s volume-duck mechanism so speed change is inaudible on music beds.
6. Higher compression ratios use `.timePitchAlgorithm = .varispeed` on music-only segments (pitch shift is acceptable on jingles); `.spectral` on speech-adjacent segments.
7. Already-classified `AdWindow` regions can be compressed more aggressively (or skipped, which already happens). The compression targets non-ad, non-speech gaps.
8. Subtle visual signal only: the playhead moves slightly faster through compressed regions on the timeline scrubber. No banner, no toast, no counter.

## Risks and Concerns

- **Rate changes on music might sound bad.** Mitigation: higher compression only on sustained music beds (`musicBedLevel .medium`/`.loud`, `musicProbability > 0.8`), not brief transitions. Speech-adjacent music stays at base rate.
- **Users who enjoy podcast music intros.** Per-show override: "Keep full music on this show." Default: compression-on (target audience values time over ambiance).
- **AVPlayer audio artifacts** — `.spectral` algorithm clean to 2.0x; `.varispeed` introduces pitch shift but acceptable on jingles. **Test on AirPods, built-in speaker, and car audio before promoting beyond TestFlight.**
- **IP concerns** — Smart Speed is Overcast marketing, not a patent. Structural compression using classified audio features is a different mechanism. No known IP conflict.
- **Edge case: audiobooks/narrative podcasts** — pauseProbability between same-speaker windows must be preserved (dramatic pauses). Algorithm handles this; verify with regression tests on narrative fixtures.

## Success Criteria

- 8+ minutes recovered per 2 hours of listening on a typical interview podcast (measure via `bytesPerCpuSecond`-style instrumentation)
- 0 perceptible artifacts on AirPods Pro and CarPlay (manual A/B listen test on 5 episode fixtures across genres)
- 0 dramatic-pause compressions on narrative-podcast fixtures (regression test against marked-up reference episodes)
- Settings has only one control: "Keep full music on this show" toggle on each podcast's detail view (not a global setting)

## Provenance

- Source: 2026-04-29 dueling-idea-wizards blind-spot phase, CC blind-spot #1
- Full context: DUELING_WIZARDS_REPORT.md, WIZARD_BLINDSPOTS_CC.md (idea #1)
