title: Cushion only the trailing ad in a pod
description:
# Goal

Skip ends should land slightly *earlier* than the detected ad-end —
but only when the next thing is program audio, not another ad. This
caps the cost at "≤ N seconds per pod" instead of "≤ N seconds per ad."

User decision (2026-04-27): "for the last ad we should cushion a few
seconds for safety."

# Behavior

When SkipOrchestrator emits a skip target for an ad span:

1. Look at the *next* confirmed span (whatever comes after this ad-end
   in the ordered span list).
2. If the next span is also an **ad** → no cushion. Skip target =
   detected ad-end exactly.
3. If the next span is **program** OR there is no next span (this is
   the trailing ad of the last pod) → apply cushion. Skip target =
   detected ad-end **minus** \`adTrailingCushionSec\`.

The cushion direction is **earlier** (subtract). This cedes a small
sliver of ad audio rather than clipping program audio — exactly the
trade-off the user requested.

# Constants

Add to wherever skip-related constants live (e.g.
\`SkipOrchestrator\` static config or \`PlaybackConfig\`):

\`\`\`swift
/// Cushion (seconds) subtracted from the detected ad-end when the
/// next span is program (or end-of-episode). Trades a small sliver
/// of ad-tail audio for protection against program-start clipping.
static let adTrailingCushionSec: TimeInterval = 1.0
\`\`\`

Initial value: 1.0 s. Make it a single named constant, not magic
literals at use sites.

# Edge cases

- Cushion is clamped at \`max(adStart, adEnd - cushion)\`. A 5 s ad
  can't have its end pushed before its start.
- Manual user-initiated skip ("hearing an ad") path: out of scope.
  Cushion only applies to the **automatic confirmed-span skip**
  pipeline.
- If \`adTrailingCushionSec\` is 0, behavior is identical to today
  (no cushion). Verify in tests.

# Where to wire

Most likely seam: where SkipOrchestrator constructs its CMTimeRanges
from confirmed ad spans. \`pushMergedCues\` (
\`Playhead/Services/SkipOrchestrator/SkipOrchestrator.swift:~1229\`)
is the prime candidate, but the implementer should confirm the
cleanest spot — the policy needs visibility to "next span is ad vs
program," which may live one frame up the stack from the cue conversion.

# Tests

\`PlayheadTests/Services/SkipOrchestrator/\` — mirror existing test
file conventions there.

Cases:
- Single ad followed by program → cushion applied; skip end = adEnd - 1.0.
- Pod of two ads (ad, ad, program) → first ad-end has no cushion;
  second ad-end has cushion.
- Pod of three ads with program after → middle ad-ends have no cushion;
  last has cushion.
- Ad at end of episode (no next span) → cushion applied (treated as
  trailing).
- 5s ad with 10s cushion → cushion clamped, skip end = adStart (no
  negative duration).
- \`adTrailingCushionSec = 0\` → no behavior change vs pre-fix.

# Acceptance

- All test cases pass.
- \`xcodebuild test -scheme Playhead -testPlan PlayheadFastTests
  -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17 Pro'\` green.
- No regressions in existing SkipOrchestrator tests.

# Out of scope

- Boundary-snap clamping (depends on instrumentation results from
  vn7n.1; separate follow-up if needed).
- Per-show / per-feed cushion tuning.
- User-configurable cushion in Settings.

title: Instrument ad-skip boundary-snap stages and skip-cue trigger
description:
# Goal

Add diagnostic logging at three points in the ad-skip pipeline so we
can confirm where the user-perceived "few seconds clipped from program"
overshoot originates.

# Why

Read-only triage on parent bead \`playhead-vn7n\` showed:

- No tail-pad constants in SkipOrchestrator (ruled out).
- All seek calls use zero tolerances (ruled out).
- Two forward-snap stages can compound up to 11 s:
  \`MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder.applyBoundarySnap\` (\`snapRadiusSeconds = 8.0\`)
  + \`BoundaryRefiner\` (\`maxBoundaryAdjust = 3.0\`).

We want logs that pin which stage (if any) accounts for the observed
2–5 s overshoot, before we change snap clamps.

# Log points

## 1. \`MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder.applyBoundarySnap\`
File: \`Playhead/Services/AdDetection/MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder.swift\`
(~line 90).

Log per span end snap:
- \`atomEnd\` (pre-snap)
- \`snappedEnd\` (post-snap)
- \`delta = snappedEnd - atomEnd\` (positive = forward overshoot)
- spanIndex / span identifier if available

## 2. \`BoundaryRefiner.resolveBoundary\`
File: \`Playhead/Services/AdDetection/BoundaryRefiner.swift\` (~line 142).

Log per END-boundary refinement (start-side optional):
- \`candidateTime\` (pre-refine)
- \`resolvedTime\` (post-refine)
- \`adjustment = resolvedTime - candidateTime\`
- \`boundaryType\` (start vs end)

## 3. SkipOrchestrator pre-seek state
File: \`Playhead/Services/SkipOrchestrator/SkipOrchestrator.swift\`
(near \`pushMergedCues\` ~line 1229 OR the actual seek emit site —
implementer pick the cleanest one).

Log per cue committed:
- \`cue.start\`, \`cue.end\`
- \`adWindow.endTime\` (the underlying detection value)
- distance to next cue if any (helps identify ad→ad vs ad→program transitions)

# Constraints

- Use the project's existing \`os.Logger\` pattern (look at any nearby
  service for the right category/subsystem).
- Log at \`.info\` level — these need to be visible in default field logs
  for diagnosing real-world reports, not just \`.debug\`.
- \`privacy: .public\` on numeric fields (timestamps, deltas) so they
  appear in logs without redaction.
- Logs must be cheap — no allocations in a hot loop. Prefer
  \`logger.info(\"... \\(value, privacy: .public)\")\` over string-building.
- No production behavior changes. Logs only.

# Tests

Single test per log site is enough — confirm the log fires with the
expected payload shape. Mirror existing logger-test patterns in the
codebase if any exist; otherwise the unit test that exercises the code
path is sufficient (logs are observable via OSLogStore in test, but
that's brittle — fine to settle for "the code path is exercised; the
log statement is in the diff").

# Acceptance

- All three log points land.
- \`xcodebuild test -scheme Playhead -testPlan PlayheadFastTests
  -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17 Pro'\` green.
- No production behavior change (existing tests still pass identically).
- A short README-style note in the bead's commit message explaining how
  to grep these logs in a sysdiagnose / Console.app session.

# Out of scope

- Snap-clamp policy changes (separate bead).
- Cushion / tail-pad behavior (separate bead, vn7n.2).

title: Ad-skip overshoots ad-end, clips first seconds of program
description:
# Symptom

User reports (2026-04-27): ad detection has improved, but skips
consistently overshoot — the player lands a few seconds INTO the
returned program, clipping the first 2-5 seconds of program audio.

# Investigation so far

Read-only triage ruled out two suspects:

- **No tail-pad / cushion.** \`SkipOrchestrator.pushMergedCues()\`
  (line ~1229) converts ad ranges to CMTimeRanges directly, no
  manipulation. \`SpanFinalizer\` does not extend ends after
  finalization. \`BoundaryExpander\` only runs on user-initiated
  \"hearing an ad\" expansion, not auto-skip.
- **Seek tolerances are correct.** All four seek calls in
  \`PlaybackTransport.swift\` (~196, 210, 299, 374) use
  \`toleranceBefore: .zero, toleranceAfter: .zero\`.

Plausible but doesn't explain seconds-scale overshoot:

- Timing race in \`PlaybackTransport.checkSkipCues\`: 250 ms observer
  tick + Task hop + 150 ms duck delay before seek. Seek target is
  the cue's fixed \`end\`, so latency-late firing should still land
  at \`end\`. Net effect: ~50–200 ms, not seconds.

Most likely culprit (not yet verified):

- **Ad-end is over-extended upstream of \`SpanFinalizer\`.** Worth
  checking \`adEndSec\` provenance from ad classification: window
  granularity (5-second feature-extraction frame boundaries?),
  rounding, music-bed consumption, etc.

# Proposed fix path

Two beads' worth, separated:

## .1 — Instrumentation (small)

Add temporary logging at three points to measure actual overshoot:

1. \`confirmedAdSpan.end\` when committed (post-classification).
2. \`cue.end\` in \`SkipOrchestrator.pushMergedCues\`.
3. \`currentTime\` 200 ms after the post-skip seek lands.

If point 1 is already 2-5 s past program-start, root cause is
upstream classification. If 1 ≈ program-start but 3 > 1, root cause
is in skip orchestration / playback path.

## .2 — User-facing policy: cushion only on the **last** ad in a pod

User decision: cushion the *trailing* ad-end in a pod (ad → program
transition), not mid-pod ad-ends (ad → ad transition). Implementation:
when emitting skip targets, if the next confirmed span is also \`ad\`,
\`tailPad = 0\`; if next is program (or end-of-episode), apply the
cushion. Caps cost at \"≤ N seconds per pod\" rather than \"≤ N seconds
per ad.\"

Cushion direction is **earlier** (skip ends sooner, cedes a sliver of
ad audio). Initial value: 1.0 s, configurable.

# Acceptance

- Instrumentation lands first; data confirms whether overshoot is
  upstream (ad-span end-time) or downstream (skip orchestration).
- Policy fix lands second; user-visible test on real episodes shows
  no clipping when the trailing ad is the last in a pod, and no
  added gap when ads chain.

# Out of scope

- Decoded-time vs container-time clock divergence (separate concern;
  for files with bad container metadata, see \`playhead-gyvb.2\`).
- AVPlayer keyframe quantization (sub-second; orthogonal).

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
# H2 deep grep findings (read-only, 2026-04-27)

## adEndSec provenance chain (output → input)

1. SkipOrchestrator reads `managed.snappedEnd` / `adWindow.endTime`
   (`SkipOrchestrator.swift:354, 381, 635, 891, 913, 1724`).
2. SpanFinalizer applies hard constraints only — no extensions
   (`SpanFinalizer.swift:106, 419`).
3. AdDetectionService composes `endTime: span.endTime + endAdj`
   where `endAdj` comes from BoundaryRefiner
   (`AdDetectionService.swift:1724`).
4. **BoundaryRefiner** calls `TimeBoundaryResolver.snap()` and
   clamps adjustment to `maxBoundaryAdjust = 3.0` s
   (`BoundaryRefiner.swift:118-134`). **±3 s of forward snap.**
5. Pre-refiner DecodedSpan end comes from
   `MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder.applyBoundarySnap` snapping to
   nearest acoustic break within `snapRadiusSeconds = 8.0` s default
   (`MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder.swift:90-97, 120`).
6. Atom-level end is transcript-ASR atom.endTime
   (`TranscriptSegmenter.swift:33-34`), passed through unchanged.

## Frame granularity

Feature window width = **2.0 s** (`FeatureExtraction.swift:50`).
BracketDetector uses 10 s search margin (5 × window) but only feeds
evidence score, NOT boundaries.

## Most likely root cause

**Two-stage forward snap can compound to 2–11 s.**
Stage 1 (`MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder.applyBoundarySnap`,
±8 s) picks an acoustic break past the atom end; Stage 2
(`BoundaryRefiner` ±3 s) snaps further to a feature-window-derived
break. If both walk forward, total overshoot = up to 11 s. Even one
stage at typical 3–5 s matches the user-reported "few seconds"
exactly.

Music bed detection exists (`MusicBedClassifier`,
`MusicBedLedgerEvaluator`, `BracketDetector`) but no code path
extends ad-end *into* trailing music bed by design — yet the snap
scoring may **prefer** a music-bed offset point as the "acoustic
break," yielding the same effect.

## Instrumentation to land first (.1)

1. `BoundaryRefiner.resolveBoundary` (
   `BoundaryRefiner.swift:142-151`): log
   `(candidateTime, boundaryType, resolvedTime, adjustment)` for
   end snaps.
2. `MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder.applyBoundarySnap` (
   `MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder.swift:90-97`): log
   `(atomEnd, snappedEnd, delta)`.
3. SkipOrchestrator pre-seek log (already exists in many places —
   audit and consolidate).

If logs show snap-stage deltas account for the user-perceived
overshoot, fix is to **reduce or zero the forward-end clamp** for
the ad→program transition. Backward (earlier) snaps stay allowed.

title: Settings toggle + PipelineProgressStripView + Activity render
description:
# Settings toggle + PipelineProgressStripView + Activity render

## Problem

With the data fully plumbed (beads 1–3), this bead adds the user-visible
pieces: a Settings toggle that controls a `@AppStorage` flag, a small
reusable strip view, and the `if showPipelineStrip { ... }` render in the
three Activity row views.

## Files

- `Playhead/Views/Components/PipelineProgressStripView.swift` — **new**
  reusable view.
- `Playhead/Views/Activity/ActivityView.swift` — embed the strip in
  `NowRowView`, `UpNextRowView`, `PausedRowView` behind the
  `@AppStorage("debug.showPipelineStrip")` flag.
- `Playhead/Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift` — add a Toggle row in a
  Debug section (or extend an existing one) bound to the same
  `@AppStorage` key.

## PipelineProgressStripView shape

```swift
struct PipelineProgressStripView: View {
    let downloadFraction: Double?
    let transcriptFraction: Double?
    let analysisFraction: Double?
    let sectionId: String   // "now" | "upNext" | "paused" — for accessibility
                            // identifier "ActivityView.<sectionId>.pipelineStrip"

    var body: some View {
        Text(line)
            .font(AppTypography.mono(size: 11, weight: .regular))
            .foregroundStyle(AppColors.textSecondary)
            .padding(.top, 2)
            .accessibilityIdentifier("ActivityView.\(sectionId).pipelineStrip")
    }

    private var line: String {
        "DL \(format(downloadFraction)) · TX \(format(transcriptFraction)) · AN \(format(analysisFraction))"
    }

    static func format(_ fraction: Double?) -> String {
        guard let fraction else { return "--%" }
        let clamped = min(1.0, max(0.0, fraction))
        return "\(Int((clamped * 100).rounded()))%"
    }
}
```

`format` is `static` so the formatter test can hit it directly without
constructing the view.

## Activity render

In each of `NowRowView`, `UpNextRowView`, `PausedRowView`:

```swift
@AppStorage("debug.showPipelineStrip") private var showPipelineStrip = false

var body: some View {
    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 2) {
        // existing content...
        if showPipelineStrip {
            PipelineProgressStripView(
                downloadFraction: row.downloadFraction,
                transcriptFraction: row.transcriptFraction,
                analysisFraction: row.analysisFraction,
                sectionId: "now"  // or "upNext" / "paused"
            )
        }
    }
}
```

`@AppStorage` reads are cheap and SwiftUI auto-invalidates on change, so
flipping the toggle in Settings shows the strip live without an Activity
refresh.

## Settings row

In `SettingsView.swift`, in the existing Debug section:

```swift
Toggle("Show pipeline progress on Activity", isOn: $showPipelineStrip)
    .accessibilityIdentifier("Settings.debug.showPipelineStrip")

@AppStorage("debug.showPipelineStrip") private var showPipelineStrip = false
```

Toggle row visible in Release builds (per design — works on any build,
flippable on TestFlight). Wrap in `#if DEBUG` later if it bothers us.

## Tests

`PlayheadTests/Views/Components/PipelineProgressStripViewTests.swift` — new
file pinning the formatter:

- `nil` → `"--%"`.
- `0.0` → `"0%"`.
- `0.876` → `"88%"` (rounding-up boundary).
- `1.0` → `"100%"`.
- `1.05` (overflow) → `"100%"`.
- `-0.1` (underflow) → `"0%"`.

No view-snapshot tests for row composition — Activity rows aren't
snapshot-tested today and we will not grow that surface for a debug-only
feature.

## Acceptance

- Toggle is visible in Settings, default off.
- With toggle off: Activity rows render exactly as today (existing tests
  pass; visual diff is zero).
- With toggle on: Now / Up Next / Paused rows render the mono one-liner
  beneath their existing copy. Recently Finished does NOT render it.
- Strip reads `--%` for any nil fraction; numerics for known values.
- Formatter tests pass.

## Out of scope

- Bars, animation, alternate rendering.
- Hiding the toggle row in Release (`#if DEBUG`) — defer.
- Strip on Recently Finished.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by bead 1 (row fields).
- Blocked by bead 3 (provider populates real values — without it the strip
  always shows `--%` and the dogfood signal is useless).

title: Populate DL/TX/AN fractions in LiveActivitySnapshotProvider
description:
# Populate DL/TX/AN fractions in LiveActivitySnapshotProvider

## Problem

With bead 1 (input/row plumbing) and bead 2 (download snapshot) landed, the
provider can finally compute the three fractions and forward them to the
view-model. This bead does that one job.

## Files

- `Playhead/Services/Activity/ActivitySnapshotProvider.swift`
  - `LiveActivitySnapshotProvider.loadInputs()` (line 101+): tap the
    download snapshot, compute fractions per asset, pass to
    `ActivityEpisodeInput.init(...)`.
  - Constructor: take a `@Sendable () async -> [String: Double]` provider
    closure for the download snapshot (parallel to the existing
    `runningEpisodeIdProvider`). Tests inject a stub returning whatever map
    they need.
- `Playhead/App/PlayheadRuntime.swift`
  - `LiveActivitySnapshotProvider(...)` construction site (line 1786): wire
    the new closure to `{ [downloadManager] in await
    downloadManager.progressSnapshot() }`.

## Computation

In `loadInputs()`, after the bulk asset fetch:

```swift
let downloadFractions = await downloadProgressProvider()

for episode in episodes {
    let episodeId = episode.canonicalEpisodeKey
    guard let asset = allAssets[episodeId] else { continue }

    let durationSec = asset.episodeDurationSec ?? 0
    func fraction(_ watermark: Double?) -> Double? {
        guard let watermark, durationSec > 0 else { return nil }
        return min(1.0, max(0.0, watermark / durationSec))
    }
    let transcriptFraction = fraction(asset.fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime)
    let analysisFraction = fraction(asset.confirmedAdCoverageEndTime)
    let downloadFraction = downloadFractions[episodeId]
        .map { min(1.0, max(0.0, $0)) }

    inputs.append(
        ActivityEpisodeInput(
            ...,
            downloadFraction: downloadFraction,
            transcriptFraction: transcriptFraction,
            analysisFraction: analysisFraction
        )
    )
}
```

Clamping in the provider (not the view) so the row struct's contract is
"already in `[0, 1]` if non-nil."

## Tests

`PlayheadTests/Services/Activity/ActivitySnapshotProviderTests.swift` — add:

- Asset with `fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime = 60, episodeDurationSec = 300`
  → input's `transcriptFraction == 0.2`.
- Asset with `confirmedAdCoverageEndTime = 600, episodeDurationSec = 300`
  (overflow) → input's `analysisFraction == 1.0` (clamped).
- Asset with `episodeDurationSec = 0` or `nil` → both `transcriptFraction`
  and `analysisFraction` are `nil`.
- Stub download provider returning `{ "ep-1": 0.42 }` → only `ep-1` carries
  `downloadFraction == 0.42`; other episodes are `nil`.
- Stub download provider returning `[:]` → all episodes have
  `downloadFraction == nil` (no download in flight).

## Acceptance

- `LiveActivitySnapshotProvider` constructs with a download-snapshot
  closure; production call site in `PlayheadRuntime` wires it.
- All five test cases above pass.
- Existing provider tests continue to pass (stubbed download closure
  defaults to empty map in tests that don't care).

## Out of scope

- Settings toggle / strip view (bead 4).
- Choosing a different download source (foreground vs background).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by bead 1 (input fields).
- Blocked by bead 2 (`progressSnapshot` exists to wire).

title: DownloadManager.progressSnapshot() — episode → fraction map
description:
# DownloadManager.progressSnapshot() — episode → fraction map

## Problem

The Activity provider needs a one-shot, per-refresh view of in-flight
download fractions to populate `ActivityEpisodeInput.downloadFraction`.
Today `DownloadManager` exposes per-event streams (`progressUpdates()`,
legacy `progressStream`) and a per-episode test helper
(`foregroundAssistProgressForTesting`), but no bulk snapshot keyed by
episode ID. This bead adds the snapshot.

## Files

- `Playhead/Services/Downloads/DownloadManager.swift`
  - `actor DownloadManager` (line 148).
  - The new method consumes the existing `foregroundAssistProgress: [String:
    ForegroundAssistProgress]` map (line 207).

## API shape

```swift
extension DownloadManager {
    /// Snapshot of the per-episode foreground download fraction for
    /// in-flight transfers. Episodes not currently downloading are absent
    /// from the map. Computed from the same `ForegroundAssistProgress`
    /// state that drives `progressUpdates()`. Per-call: O(N) over active
    /// downloads (typically tiny — single-digit episodes).
    func progressSnapshot() async -> [String: Double] {
        var result: [String: Double] = [:]
        for (episodeId, progress) in foregroundAssistProgress {
            guard progress.totalBytes > 0 else { continue }
            result[episodeId] =
                Double(progress.bytesWritten) / Double(progress.totalBytes)
        }
        return result
    }
}
```

`async` because `DownloadManager` is an `actor`. Caller awaits it once
per Activity refresh tick.

## Tests

`PlayheadTests/Services/Downloads/DownloadManagerTests.swift` (or a focused
new file under that directory) — pin:

- Empty map → empty snapshot.
- One in-flight episode with `bytesWritten: 50, totalBytes: 100` →
  snapshot returns `{episodeId: 0.5}`.
- `totalBytes: 0` is skipped (avoid divide-by-zero).
- Two in-flight episodes both appear with their own fractions.

`seedForegroundAssistProgressForTesting` (existing helper at line 656) is
the seam for setting up the actor's state in tests.

## Acceptance

- New method on `DownloadManager` returning the documented map.
- Four-case test coverage above.
- No change to `progressUpdates()` / `progressStream` callers.

## Out of scope

- Background-session progress (`bgInFlightEpisodes`) — the foreground-assist
  map is what the Activity strip cares about while the user is on screen.
  Background progress can be added later without changing the shape.
- Caching the snapshot — Activity already re-aggregates on every
  `ActivityRefreshNotification`; an internal cache adds invalidation hazards
  with no win.

## Dependencies

None.

title: Plumb DL/TX/AN fractions through ActivityEpisodeInput → row structs
description:
# Plumb DL/TX/AN fractions through ActivityEpisodeInput → row structs

## Problem

The Activity screen needs to render three optional pipeline percentages per
row (DL / TX / AN) on Now, Up Next, and Paused. Today the value-type chain
`ActivityEpisodeInput` → `ActivityNowRow` / `ActivityUpNextRow` /
`ActivityPausedRow` carries no slot for them. This bead adds the wires only
— no provider population, no UI render. Sibling beads handle those.

## Files

- `Playhead/Views/Activity/ActivityViewModel.swift`
  - `ActivityEpisodeInput` (lines ~47–86): add three optional `Double?`
    fields, append to the init signature with `nil` defaults so existing
    tests / previews compile unchanged.
  - `ActivityNowRow` (lines ~110–119): add the three fields.
  - `ActivityUpNextRow` (lines ~123–128): add the three fields.
  - `ActivityPausedRow` (lines ~135–142): add the three fields.
  - `ActivityRecentlyFinishedRow`: **no change** (terminal rows do not
    surface the strip per design).
  - `aggregate(...)` (lines ~351–461): forward the three fractions onto
    each constructed row in the Now / Up Next / Paused branches.

## Field contract

Three optional `Double?` fields on each in-flight row (and on the input):

- `downloadFraction: Double?` — `0.0...1.0`. `nil` when no in-flight or
  recorded download exists for this episode this refresh.
- `transcriptFraction: Double?` — clamped `0.0...1.0`. `nil` when either
  watermark or duration is unknown / `<= 0`.
- `analysisFraction: Double?` — clamped `0.0...1.0`. Same nil rules.

Bead 3 (provider population) computes and clamps; this bead only carries.

## Tests

`PlayheadTests/Views/Activity/ActivityViewModelTests.swift` — add cases:

- An input with all three fractions populated lands its fractions on the
  resulting `ActivityNowRow` (input is `isRunning: true`, queued).
- An input with all three fractions populated lands them on
  `ActivityUpNextRow` when `isRunning: false`.
- An input with all three fractions populated lands them on
  `ActivityPausedRow` when `disposition == .paused`.
- A terminal-disposition input (Recently Finished bucket) does NOT carry
  the fractions — `ActivityRecentlyFinishedRow` has no slot for them; this
  is asserted structurally (the row type doesn't expose the fields).

## Acceptance

- All three row types and the input compile with the new optional fields.
- `aggregate(...)` forwards the fractions intact onto the right row.
- Existing `ActivityViewModelTests` still pass with default `nil` fractions
  on every fixture.
- New tests pin that the three fractions ride the snapshot end-to-end.

## Out of scope

- `ActivitySnapshotProvider` changes (sibling bead 3).
- `DownloadManager.progressSnapshot()` (sibling bead 2).
- Settings toggle + `PipelineProgressStripView` (sibling bead 4).

## Dependencies

None. Pure scaffolding; lands first.

title: Debug pipeline strip on Activity (DL / TX / AN)
description:
# Debug pipeline strip on Activity (DL / TX / AN)

## Goal

Surface per-episode pipeline progress on the Activity screen for debugging:
download %, transcription %, analysis %. If an episode is not on Activity it
is considered done — Activity is the single home for in-flight work and
therefore the single home for the strip.

Renders as a monospaced one-liner under the existing copy on Now / Up Next /
Paused rows:

```
DL 100% · TX 87% · AN 64%
```

Recently Finished does not render the strip.

## Gating

Runtime, on any build, off by default. New `@AppStorage("debug.showPipelineStrip")`
boolean toggled from a row in `SettingsView`. Production data path stays
unchanged when the flag is off; the UI is purely additive.

## Data sources (already on hand)

- **DL**: `DownloadProgress.fractionCompleted` (byte-level, from
  `DownloadManager.foregroundAssistProgress`).
- **TX**: `AnalysisAsset.fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime / episodeDurationSec`,
  clamped to `0.0...1.0`.
- **AN**: `AnalysisAsset.confirmedAdCoverageEndTime / episodeDurationSec`,
  clamped.

All three live on existing types — no new persistence, no new schema.

## Architecture

Production-shaped path so a future polished UI can ride the same wires:

```
AnalysisStore + DownloadManager
        ↓
ActivitySnapshotProvider (taps both, computes fractions)
        ↓
ActivityEpisodeInput (3 optional Double fields)
        ↓
ActivityViewModel.refresh(from:) (passes through unchanged)
        ↓
ActivityNowRow / ActivityUpNextRow / ActivityPausedRow
        ↓ (only if @AppStorage flag is true)
PipelineProgressStripView
```

## Child beads

1. Plumb fractions through `ActivityEpisodeInput` and the three row structs.
2. Add `DownloadManager.progressSnapshot()` returning `[String: Double]`.
3. Populate fractions in `LiveActivitySnapshotProvider`.
4. Settings toggle + `PipelineProgressStripView` + render in Now/Up Next/Paused.

## Out of scope

- Bars, animation, sparklines, or any non-monospaced rendering.
- A Recently Finished strip.
- A second debug data path (everything rides the production provider).
- Streaming subscriptions (snapshot per refresh tick — same shape Activity uses
  for everything else).

## Design doc

`docs/plans/2026-04-27-activity-pipeline-debug-strip-design.md`
(committed at `badfc0e`).

title: gtt9.1.2: test coverage for skipEnabled=true path
description:
# gtt9.1.2: test coverage for skipEnabled=true path

## Problem

playhead-dzmu (gtt9.1) ships 8 tests for the acoustic transcript gate, but every test uses `skipEnabled: false`. The production-skip teeth (`AnalysisJobRunner.swift` `transcribed = !acousticGateConfig.isProductionSkipActive` → `if transcribed { keptShards.append(shard) }`) are completely uncovered. Cross-review surfaced this as P1 future-proofing risk: when a future bead flips `skipEnabled=true` in production, the first regression will land in production rather than in the test runner.

## Fix

Add at least one test that:

1. Constructs a runner with `skipEnabled=true, safetySampleFraction=0.0`.
2. Seeds clean-speech feature windows (low likelihood, below threshold).
3. Asserts the transcript engine spy receives **zero** shards (or that `transcribed=false` rows are emitted for every shard).

Add a parallel test with `safetySampleFraction=1.0` asserting the engine receives every shard.

Optionally: a property-style test that for any `safetySampleFraction ∈ {0.0, 0.5, 1.0}` and seeded RNG, the kept-shard count matches the expected statistical outcome.

## Acceptance

- New tests in `AcousticTranscriptGateTests.swift`.
- Cover both `skipEnabled=true` corners (sample=0 → none kept, sample=1 → all kept).
- Use the existing deterministic-RNG injection (`safetySampleRNG`) — no flake.
- PlayheadFastTests green.

## Out of scope

- Actual `skipEnabled=true` production wiring (separate bead, gated on eval data from gtt9.1.1).

## Dependencies

- gtt9.1 (playhead-dzmu) — shipped.

title: Lever B: correction-loop audit (catalog fingerprint tightness)
description:
## Problem

`playhead-gtt9.13` shipped catalog fingerprint matching: when the user marks an ad span (or corrects an auto-skip), the corrected content gets fingerprinted and stored in `AdCatalogStore`. Future episodes are supposed to cross-match against this catalog as one of the evidence channels.

We have not measured how *tight* this loop is. Open questions:

- Does the catalog match fire on the next episode of the same show, or does it require some ramp-up?
- Are fingerprints durable across episode types (cold open ad vs mid-roll ad vs outro ad)?
- Does the matcher's tolerance pick up "same sponsor read with different host intonation" or only near-identical audio?
- What's the false-positive rate on real-data corpora?

In the latest NARL eval, evidence-source counts show `catalog=5` out of 147 windows (3.4%). That's tiny. Either the catalog isn't being populated (corrections aren't reaching it), the matcher is too strict, or the corpus lacks repeat ads (less likely for sponsor-heavy podcasts).

## What this bead is

An investigation, not an implementation. Run a controlled audit:

1. Pick one show with multiple captured episodes that share known recurring sponsors (Conan + Squarespace would be ideal — verify with show notes).
2. On episode 1, simulate user correction by feeding the GT ad spans through the correction path.
3. Replay episode 2 through the harness; assert the catalog evidence channel fires on the same sponsor regions.
4. If it doesn't fire: trace through `AdCatalogStore` ingest, fingerprint generation, similarity matcher; identify the gap.
5. If it fires but at low confidence: investigate the threshold; potentially reweight.

## Why now

The catalog channel is the only evidence source whose value scales with user corrections — every other channel is purely classifier/feature/heuristic-driven. If the catalog loop is loose, every user correction is a wasted teaching signal. Tightening it converts the user's growing labeled corpus into a compounding precision win.

## Design questions

1. **What does "tight" mean quantitatively?** First episode after correction: catalog should fire ≥ X% on the corrected sponsor; refine X based on what we observe.
2. **Cross-episode fingerprint reuse**: does the existing fingerprint key pin to (showId, content) or just content? If pinned to show, a sponsor that runs across multiple shows gets no cross-show benefit (separate lever D, not in scope here).
3. **Deduplication**: if the same correction is replayed twice, do we get one fingerprint or two? Drift over time?

## Acceptance

- Investigation report committed (e.g. `docs/narl/correction-loop-audit-<date>.md`).
- Concrete metrics: catalog fire-rate on a controlled multi-episode corpus before/after correction.
- Either: confirmation the loop is tight enough (closes bead) OR a fix bead filed with the specific gap.

## Out of scope

- Cross-show fingerprinting (lever D, separate bead).
- Catalog UI / management.
- Implementing fixes — this bead is investigation only.

## References

- gtt9.13 (catalog fingerprint matching, shipped)
- vjxc (banner evidence catalog, shipped — different "catalog," verify they share infrastructure)
- 2026-04-25 NARL eval: `.eval-out/narl/20260425-160022-E1D7EB/report.md`
close_reason: Duplicate of closed playhead-gtt9.25; correction-loop audit completed and follow-up telemetry gap captured/closed in playhead-epfk.

title: Lever G: acoustic-likelihood trigger for transcript scheduler
description:
## Problem

Acoustic features (music-bed onset/offset, level changes, speaker-change proxies) are wired into `BackfillEvidenceFusion` as evidence-channel inputs (gtt9.12, gtt9.16). They contribute to the *fusion score* on a window once that window has been transcribed. They do NOT influence *which windows get transcribed*.

For long episodes that don't reach pipeline-coverage completion, this is wasteful: the transcript marches linearly through the audio in chunks of `desiredCoverageSec`, regardless of whether those chunks contain anything ad-relevant. By the time backfill is killed by BG-task budget, we may have transcribed 600 s of content with no ad in it and 0 s of the actual sponsor break.

## What this bead is

Promote acoustic features from "fusion input" to "transcript-scheduler trigger." The pipeline:

1. Acoustic feature pass runs cheaply across the entire episode early (it's already cheap — features extract at ~50× realtime).
2. The scheduler scores each unscored window for *acoustic ad-likelihood* (music-bed onset/offset, level discontinuity, speaker change clusters).
3. High-likelihood windows get prioritized for transcription over linear-progression windows.

Result: even a partial-coverage episode has its likely-ad windows transcribed first. Non-ad regions stay un-transcribed (no harm — they were never going to fire).

## Why now

Pipeline-FN dominates by ~5× in the NARL eval (2914 s vs 570 s classifier-FN). Foreground catch-up (`playhead-yqax`) reclaims pipeline-FN time when the user is actively playing. Acoustic-triggered transcription reclaims it when they're NOT — the BG-task budget that today gets spent linearly gets spent on the highest-likelihood windows.

## Design questions

1. **Acoustic-likelihood score**: combine which features and how? Music-bed level + speaker change + spectral discontinuity?
2. **Scheduler integration**: does this replace the current `desiredCoverageSec` linear-progression filter, augment it (e.g., "60% linear, 40% acoustic-triggered"), or fully redirect?
3. **Cold-start behavior**: on the first pass before any acoustic features exist, what does the scheduler do? Linear fallback?
4. **False-positive cost**: if acoustic-likelihood incorrectly flags a non-ad as high-likelihood, we transcribe that window and waste a BG-task wake. Bounded — measure how badly the heuristic mis-fires on the existing fixtures before shipping.
5. **Interaction with `playhead-yqax`**: foreground catch-up is playhead-driven (transcribe ahead of user). Acoustic-triggered is content-driven (transcribe likely-ad regions). They should compose, not conflict.

## Acceptance

- Acoustic-likelihood score function lives in `AcousticFeaturePipeline` (or similar), produces per-window score in [0, 1].
- `AnalysisWorkScheduler` consults the score when picking next window to transcribe; high-acoustic windows promoted ahead of linear progression.
- Regression fixture: synthetic episode with one obvious music-bed-bracketed ad region and a lot of clean speech; assert ad region transcribes before equivalent-position clean-speech region.
- Telemetry: scheduler decisions stamped with reason (`linearProgression` / `acousticPromoted`) for harness analysis.
- NARL re-run on a real fixture shows pipeline-FN time drop on a partial-coverage episode.

## Dependencies

This bead depends on the 5uvz reliability-tail completing — without reliable BG-task chaining, the scheduler reordering wouldn't even get a chance to fire. Block on the same family `playhead-yqax` blocks on.

## References

- gtt9.12 (acoustic feature expansion, shipped)
- gtt9.16 (acoustic wired into AdDetectionService hot path, shipped)
- 2026-04-25 NARL eval: `.eval-out/narl/20260425-160022-E1D7EB/report.md`
close_reason: Duplicate of closed playhead-gtt9.24; acoustic likelihood scorer, scheduler promotion, acousticPromoted telemetry, and regression tests are landed.

title: Lever F: Platt-scaling calibration layer for classifier raw output
description:
## Problem

The 2026-04-25 NARL eval shows classifier confidence concentrated in the 0.30–0.40 mode (78 of 147 windows, 53%). On the `completeFull` cohort (where transcription DID finish), AutoSkip Precision = 1.00 but AutoSkip Recall = 14%. That extreme precision-recall imbalance combined with the confidence distribution mode strongly suggests the classifier raw output is poorly calibrated: the boundary between "ad" and "not ad" is at a probability much lower than the threshold we'd naively set (0.55).

A Platt scaling pass (logistic regression) trained on user corrections — which we have a growing supply of — would map the raw classifier output to better-calibrated probabilities. The auto-skip threshold could then be set at a meaningful confidence level (e.g., 0.85 calibrated) without the current dependency on hand-tuned raw thresholds.

## What this bead is

A small per-show calibration layer that sits between the FoundationModels classifier and `AutoSkipPrecisionGate.classify`. Inputs: raw classifier probability + user-correction history. Output: calibrated probability.

Method options to evaluate:
- **Platt scaling** (logistic regression on raw → label). Simple, well-understood, low data requirement.
- **Isotonic regression**. More flexible but needs more data per show.
- **Per-show vs global**. Probably global to start; per-show only if we have ≥ N corrections per show.

## Why now

We have user corrections accumulating from the 2026-04-22 onward dogfood captures. The labeled corpus is small but growing. A calibration layer can bootstrap from a tiny corpus (Platt scaling works with dozens of examples).

The aggregate FN-time bucket is bounded — 570 s of classifier-FN across the corpus vs 2914 s of pipeline-FN — so this is a smaller lever than coverage. But it's *uncovered* (4my.14.1 covers learned fusion calibration, which is a Phase 10 future-state full retrain, not a near-term Platt-scaling pass).

## Design questions

1. **Where does calibration live?** Pre-fusion (calibrate the raw classifier probability before it enters fusion) or post-fusion (calibrate the fused score before threshold)?
2. **Training data shape**: do we use only spans the user explicitly added/removed, or also spans the user implicitly accepted (no correction = label correct)?
3. **Online vs offline**: refit on every correction, batch-refit on a schedule, or refit only on test fixtures?
4. **Distribution shift detection**: classifier output distribution may shift as we change FM prompts. Calibration must auto-detect drift and refit.
5. **Existing infrastructure**: gtt9.21 stamped detectorVersion + buildCommitSHA into FrozenTrace — calibration must respect detector-version boundaries (don't apply old calibration to a new model).

## Acceptance

- Calibration module with selected method (probably Platt) producing calibrated probability.
- Wired into the pipeline at chosen stage (pre-fusion or post-fusion).
- NARL eval re-run on the existing corpus shows calibrated probability that better separates GT-ad from GT-non-ad windows (e.g., AUC-PR improvement).
- Auto-skip threshold can be set at a meaningful calibrated value (e.g., 0.85) without changing observed behavior — i.e., calibration moves the numbers, recalibrating the threshold then becomes principled rather than ad-hoc.

## Out of scope

- 4my.14.1 (learned fusion calibration model — full Phase 10 retrain).
- Threshold recalibration itself (`gtt9.3` — the post-calibration threshold pick).
- Distribution-shift auto-detection (start fixed-fit; add drift detection later if needed).

## References

- 4my.14.1 (P3, learned fusion calibration — adjacent but distinct work)
- gtt9.3 (P2, threshold recalibration — depends on this bead's output to be principled)
- gtt9.21 (detectorVersion stamping, shipped)
- 2026-04-25 NARL eval: `.eval-out/narl/20260425-160022-E1D7EB/report.md`
close_reason: Superseded by closed playhead-gtt9.26; calibration layer and tests are landed, while production fitted coefficients remain intentionally deferred pending enough labeled data.

title: Debounce duplicate corpus-export storm
description:
## Problem

The 2026-04-25 device snapshot contained four byte-identical (md5 `432e1d7b362000175baa10802ba4e759`) `corpus-export.jsonl` files written within 1.8 seconds:

- corpus-export.2026-04-25T11-43-35.384Z.jsonl
- corpus-export.2026-04-25T11-43-36.017Z.jsonl
- corpus-export.2026-04-25T11-43-36.651Z.jsonl
- corpus-export.2026-04-25T11-43-37.218Z.jsonl

This happened ~2 minutes after asset 3B96D187 reached `completeFull` at 11:41:39. Either the reconcile path fired the export trigger 4× for the same state-change, or the export sink double-wrote on a single trigger that retried.

Cost is small (each file is ~8 KB) but it pollutes NARL eval input (duplicate windows skew counts) and burns disk + CPU + I/O. It's also a tell that some idempotency invariant is broken upstream — better to fix the cause than tolerate the symptom.

## What this bead is

1. Trace the cause: who is calling the export, why 4× in 1.8s. Likely candidates: AnalysisJobReconciler firing repeatedly on the same completeFull event, or a fan-out where multiple subscribers all trigger an export on the same notification.
2. Fix at the most upstream defensible layer:
   - **Preferred**: idempotency at the export sink (skip if last export of same content-hash within N seconds).
   - **Acceptable**: debounce at the trigger (coalesce identical state-change events within a window).
   - **Avoid**: surface-level "wait 2s then export" — masks the underlying re-trigger.
3. Regression test: simulate the trigger event firing 4× in rapid succession; assert only one corpus-export file is produced.

## Why now

Reconcile correctness matters more than ever now that gjz6 + 5uvz.x have hardened the BG path. Future NARL evals must trust their input corpus. A multi-write storm tonight is a single user; left in place, every dogfooder produces noise.

## Design questions

1. **Content-hash dedupe vs time-window dedupe**: content-hash is stronger (catches even non-identical-trigger duplicates) but requires hashing the export body. Time-window is cheaper and sufficient for the observed bug.
2. **Where in the reconcile flow does the multi-fire originate?** Investigate before deciding the fix layer.
3. **Existing test fixture**: is there one for export trigger paths? If not, this bead adds the first.

## Acceptance

- Cause identified and named in the PR description (which trigger fired 4×).
- Fix at the appropriate layer (sink-idempotency preferred).
- Regression test: trigger N×, assert 1 file.
- NARL eval re-run on the existing 4-file corpus shows identical result vs treating it as 1 file (sanity check that no real signal was being captured by the duplicates).

## Out of scope

- BG-task telemetry (separate bead).
- Reconcile-loop refactor.

## References

title: Wire AnalysisWorkScheduler.enqueue to BackgroundProcessingService.scheduleBackfillIfNeeded when backgrounded (Gap-4 prod follow-up to 5uvz.9)
description:
**From audit playhead-5uvz Gap-4 second-half (companion to 5uvz.9 regression test).**

Discovered while attempting to write the regression test for playhead-5uvz.9: the contract the test wanted to pin — "calling `AnalysisWorkScheduler.enqueue` while `schedulerScenePhase == .background` triggers `BackgroundProcessingService.scheduleBackfillIfNeeded()`" — **does not currently exist in production code**. The orchestrator instruction was "do not silently change prod code; STOP and file a follow-up", so the test bead was paused and this bead captures the missing wiring.

**Current state (verified 2026-04-25 in worktree bd-5uvz-9):**

- `AnalysisWorkScheduler.enqueue` calls `store.insertJob` and `wakeSchedulerLoop`. It does NOT call into BPS.
- The scheduler already tracks `schedulerScenePhase: .foreground | .background` (set by `PlayheadApp.onChange(of: scenePhase)` via `updateScenePhase`).
- The scheduler has no `BackfillScheduling` (or analogous) injection. The only `scheduleBackfillIfNeeded` callers from outside BPS are `BackgroundFeedRefreshService` (via `5uvz.4` Gap-5 fix) and `PlayheadApp` `.background` scenePhase observer (`fuo6` Gap-4 first-half fix).
- Inverse-class bug the audit warns about: app launches in background (or is already backgrounded) and a download completes via background `URLSession` → `DownloadManager.completeDownload` calls `scheduler.enqueue` → no fresh `BGProcessingTaskRequest` is submitted because no `.background` *transition* fires.

**Fix scope (production):**

1. Add a `BackfillScheduling`-style injection (or reuse the existing protocol from `BackgroundFeedRefreshService.swift`) into `AnalysisWorkScheduler`.
2. In `enqueue`, after `wakeSchedulerLoop()`, when `schedulerScenePhase == .background` call the injected `scheduleBackfillIfNeeded()`.
3. Wire it in `PlayheadRuntime` (passing the live `BackgroundProcessingService` via `ProductionBackfillScheduler`).

**Test:** the original 5uvz.9 regression test — assert that `enqueue` while `schedulerScenePhase == .background` triggers exactly one `scheduleBackfillIfNeeded()` call on a stub backfill scheduler; assert it does NOT trigger when foreground.

**Files:** `Playhead/Services/PreAnalysis/AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift`, `Playhead/App/PlayheadRuntime.swift`, `PlayheadTests/Services/PreAnalysis/AnalysisWorkSchedulerTests.swift` (or BackgroundProcessingServiceTests.swift).

See: `docs/audits/2026-04-25-episode-job-dag-audit.md` Gap-4.

title: Classifier calibration layer: Platt scaling on raw classifier output between FM and AutoSkipPrecisionGate
description:
## Problem

The 2026-04-25 NARL eval shows classifier confidence concentrated in the 0.30–0.40 mode (78 of 147 windows, 53%). On the `completeFull` cohort (where transcription DID finish), AutoSkip Precision = 1.00 but AutoSkip Recall = 14%. That extreme precision-recall imbalance combined with the confidence distribution mode strongly suggests the classifier raw output is poorly calibrated: the boundary between "ad" and "not ad" is at a probability much lower than the threshold we'd naively set (0.55).

A Platt scaling pass (logistic regression) trained on user corrections — which we have a growing supply of — would map the raw classifier output to better-calibrated probabilities. The auto-skip threshold could then be set at a meaningful confidence level (e.g., 0.85 calibrated) without the current dependency on hand-tuned raw thresholds.

## What this bead is

A small per-show calibration layer that sits between the FoundationModels classifier and `AutoSkipPrecisionGate.classify`. Inputs: raw classifier probability + user-correction history. Output: calibrated probability.

Method options to evaluate:
- **Platt scaling** (logistic regression on raw → label). Simple, well-understood, low data requirement.
- **Isotonic regression**. More flexible but needs more data per show.
- **Per-show vs global**. Probably global to start; per-show only if we have ≥ N corrections per show.

## Why now

We have user corrections accumulating from the 2026-04-22 onward dogfood captures. The labeled corpus is small but growing. A calibration layer can bootstrap from a tiny corpus (Platt scaling works with dozens of examples).

The aggregate FN-time bucket is bounded — 570 s of classifier-FN across the corpus vs 2914 s of pipeline-FN — so this is a smaller lever than coverage. But it's *uncovered* (4my.14.1 covers learned fusion calibration, which is a Phase 10 future-state full retrain, not a near-term Platt-scaling pass).

## Design questions

1. **Where does calibration live?** Pre-fusion (calibrate the raw classifier probability before it enters fusion) or post-fusion (calibrate the fused score before threshold)?
2. **Training data shape**: do we use only spans the user explicitly added/removed, or also spans the user implicitly accepted (no correction = label correct)?
3. **Online vs offline**: refit on every correction, batch-refit on a schedule, or refit only on test fixtures?
4. **Distribution shift detection**: classifier output distribution may shift as we change FM prompts. Calibration must auto-detect drift and refit.
5. **Existing infrastructure**: gtt9.21 stamped detectorVersion + buildCommitSHA into FrozenTrace — calibration must respect detector-version boundaries (don't apply old calibration to a new model).

## Acceptance

- Calibration module with selected method (probably Platt) producing calibrated probability.
- Wired into the pipeline at chosen stage (pre-fusion or post-fusion).
- NARL eval re-run on the existing corpus shows calibrated probability that better separates GT-ad from GT-non-ad windows (e.g., AUC-PR improvement).
- Auto-skip threshold can be set at a meaningful calibrated value (e.g., 0.85) without changing observed behavior — i.e., calibration moves the numbers, recalibrating the threshold then becomes principled rather than ad-hoc.

## Out of scope

- 4my.14.1 (learned fusion calibration model — full Phase 10 retrain).
- Threshold recalibration itself (`gtt9.3` — the post-calibration threshold pick).
- Distribution-shift auto-detection (start fixed-fit; add drift detection later if needed).

## References

- 4my.14.1 (P3, learned fusion calibration — adjacent but distinct work)
- gtt9.3 (P2, threshold recalibration — depends on this bead's output to be principled)
- gtt9.21 (detectorVersion stamping, shipped)
- 2026-04-25 NARL eval: `.eval-out/narl/20260425-160022-E1D7EB/report.md`

title: Correction-loop audit: measure how tightly user corrections feed back into AdCatalogStore matching
description:
## Problem

`playhead-gtt9.13` shipped catalog fingerprint matching: when the user marks an ad span (or corrects an auto-skip), the corrected content gets fingerprinted and stored in `AdCatalogStore`. Future episodes are supposed to cross-match against this catalog as one of the evidence channels.

We have not measured how *tight* this loop is. Open questions:

- Does the catalog match fire on the next episode of the same show, or does it require some ramp-up?
- Are fingerprints durable across episode types (cold open ad vs mid-roll ad vs outro ad)?
- Does the matcher's tolerance pick up "same sponsor read with different host intonation" or only near-identical audio?
- What's the false-positive rate on real-data corpora?

In the latest NARL eval, evidence-source counts show `catalog=5` out of 147 windows (3.4%). That's tiny. Either the catalog isn't being populated (corrections aren't reaching it), the matcher is too strict, or the corpus lacks repeat ads (less likely for sponsor-heavy podcasts).

## What this bead is

An investigation, not an implementation. Run a controlled audit:

1. Pick one show with multiple captured episodes that share known recurring sponsors (Conan + Squarespace would be ideal — verify with show notes).
2. On episode 1, simulate user correction by feeding the GT ad spans through the correction path.
3. Replay episode 2 through the harness; assert the catalog evidence channel fires on the same sponsor regions.
4. If it doesn't fire: trace through `AdCatalogStore` ingest, fingerprint generation, similarity matcher; identify the gap.
5. If it fires but at low confidence: investigate the threshold; potentially reweight.

## Why now

The catalog channel is the only evidence source whose value scales with user corrections — every other channel is purely classifier/feature/heuristic-driven. If the catalog loop is loose, every user correction is a wasted teaching signal. Tightening it converts the user's growing labeled corpus into a compounding precision win.

## Design questions

1. **What does "tight" mean quantitatively?** First episode after correction: catalog should fire ≥ X% on the corrected sponsor; refine X based on what we observe.
2. **Cross-episode fingerprint reuse**: does the existing fingerprint key pin to (showId, content) or just content? If pinned to show, a sponsor that runs across multiple shows gets no cross-show benefit (separate lever D, not in scope here).
3. **Deduplication**: if the same correction is replayed twice, do we get one fingerprint or two? Drift over time?

## Acceptance

- Investigation report committed (e.g. `docs/narl/correction-loop-audit-<date>.md`).
- Concrete metrics: catalog fire-rate on a controlled multi-episode corpus before/after correction.
- Either: confirmation the loop is tight enough (closes bead) OR a fix bead filed with the specific gap.

## Out of scope

- Cross-show fingerprinting (lever D, separate bead).
- Catalog UI / management.
- Implementing fixes — this bead is investigation only.

## References

- gtt9.13 (catalog fingerprint matching, shipped)
- vjxc (banner evidence catalog, shipped — different "catalog," verify they share infrastructure)
- 2026-04-25 NARL eval: `.eval-out/narl/20260425-160022-E1D7EB/report.md`
close_reason: Audit complete; gap captured in playhead-epfk — see docs/narl/correction-loop-audit-2026-04-25.md.

title: Acoustic-triggered transcription scheduling: promote acoustic features from fusion input to scheduler trigger
description:
## Problem

Acoustic features (music-bed onset/offset, level changes, speaker-change proxies) are wired into `BackfillEvidenceFusion` as evidence-channel inputs (gtt9.12, gtt9.16). They contribute to the *fusion score* on a window once that window has been transcribed. They do NOT influence *which windows get transcribed*.

For long episodes that don't reach pipeline-coverage completion, this is wasteful: the transcript marches linearly through the audio in chunks of `desiredCoverageSec`, regardless of whether those chunks contain anything ad-relevant. By the time backfill is killed by BG-task budget, we may have transcribed 600 s of content with no ad in it and 0 s of the actual sponsor break.

## What this bead is

Promote acoustic features from "fusion input" to "transcript-scheduler trigger." The pipeline:

1. Acoustic feature pass runs cheaply across the entire episode early (it's already cheap — features extract at ~50× realtime).
2. The scheduler scores each unscored window for *acoustic ad-likelihood* (music-bed onset/offset, level discontinuity, speaker change clusters).
3. High-likelihood windows get prioritized for transcription over linear-progression windows.

Result: even a partial-coverage episode has its likely-ad windows transcribed first. Non-ad regions stay un-transcribed (no harm — they were never going to fire).

## Why now

Pipeline-FN dominates by ~5× in the NARL eval (2914 s vs 570 s classifier-FN). Foreground catch-up (`playhead-yqax`) reclaims pipeline-FN time when the user is actively playing. Acoustic-triggered transcription reclaims it when they're NOT — the BG-task budget that today gets spent linearly gets spent on the highest-likelihood windows.

## Design questions

1. **Acoustic-likelihood score**: combine which features and how? Music-bed level + speaker change + spectral discontinuity?
2. **Scheduler integration**: does this replace the current `desiredCoverageSec` linear-progression filter, augment it (e.g., "60% linear, 40% acoustic-triggered"), or fully redirect?
3. **Cold-start behavior**: on the first pass before any acoustic features exist, what does the scheduler do? Linear fallback?
4. **False-positive cost**: if acoustic-likelihood incorrectly flags a non-ad as high-likelihood, we transcribe that window and waste a BG-task wake. Bounded — measure how badly the heuristic mis-fires on the existing fixtures before shipping.
5. **Interaction with `playhead-yqax`**: foreground catch-up is playhead-driven (transcribe ahead of user). Acoustic-triggered is content-driven (transcribe likely-ad regions). They should compose, not conflict.

## Acceptance

- Acoustic-likelihood score function lives in `AcousticFeaturePipeline` (or similar), produces per-window score in [0, 1].
- `AnalysisWorkScheduler` consults the score when picking next window to transcribe; high-acoustic windows promoted ahead of linear progression.
- Regression fixture: synthetic episode with one obvious music-bed-bracketed ad region and a lot of clean speech; assert ad region transcribes before equivalent-position clean-speech region.
- Telemetry: scheduler decisions stamped with reason (`linearProgression` / `acousticPromoted`) for harness analysis.
- NARL re-run on a real fixture shows pipeline-FN time drop on a partial-coverage episode.

## Dependencies

This bead depends on the 5uvz reliability-tail completing — without reliable BG-task chaining, the scheduler reordering wouldn't even get a chance to fire. Block on the same family `playhead-yqax` blocks on.

## References

- gtt9.12 (acoustic feature expansion, shipped)
- gtt9.16 (acoustic wired into AdDetectionService hot path, shipped)
- 2026-04-25 NARL eval: `.eval-out/narl/20260425-160022-E1D7EB/report.md`

title: Sync podcast subscriptions + entitlements via iCloud (CloudKit)
description:
Sync user state across devices so the iPhone + Mac apps share the same library and unlocks.

## What needs to sync

**1. Podcast subscriptions (feed list)** — the user's library of podcasts they've added. Currently SwiftData / on-device only. Without sync, the Mac app launches empty and the user has to re-add every show by hand.

**2. Episode-level state**: played / unplayed flags, playback position, queue order. Without sync, you finish an episode on iPhone, open Mac, and it shows the same episode unplayed at 0:00.

**3. One-time purchase entitlement** — already handled by StoreKit 2 + Apple ID (no work for us as long as we use the same App Store record). Confirm in close-out.

**4. User corrections / skip overrides** — the playhead-7d8 / Phase-7 user-correction store. If the user trains the model with corrections on iPhone, those should reach the Mac.

## What does NOT sync (deliberate)

- **Transcripts** — copyright, on-device only mandate, see project memory
- **Detection analysis output (ad windows, confidence, etc.)** — on-device only per the same mandate. The bbrv (cross-user share) bead handles that separately with fingerprint anchoring.
- **Foundation Models / classifier internals** — on-device, never leave

## Approach

**CloudKit private database** — the obvious fit. Private to the user, propagates across that user's iCloud devices, free up to generous quotas, and Apple-supported sync conflict resolution.

**Schema sketch**:
- `PodcastSubscription` (showId, addedDate, category, sortOrder)
- `EpisodePlaybackState` (episodeId, playbackPosition, durationMs, lastPlayedDate, completed)
- `QueueEntry` (episodeId, position, addedDate)
- `UserCorrection` (episodeId, windowId, isAd, confidence, correctedAt)

**Conflict resolution**: last-write-wins for playback position (user's most recent device is authoritative). User-corrections are append-only; no conflicts. Subscription add/remove is set-union with a tombstone for removes.

## Pre-reqs / dependencies
- Mac port (playhead-izvj) — sync only matters once there's a second device to sync with. But the sync work can land first since iPhone↔iPhone (e.g. user upgrades phone) is also a real case.

## Out of scope (file as follow-ups if needed)
- Public sharing / family sharing
- Show-import via OPML round-tripping through iCloud Drive
- Real-time multi-device Now Playing (different from playback position sync — that's complicated and not v1)

title: Mac port spike: Catalyst
description:
Time-boxed spike: enable Mac Catalyst on the existing Playhead target, fix the iOS-only islands, see what runs.

## Goal
Validate that the analysis/detection service layer + SwiftUI views run unmodified under Catalyst on an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 26+.

## Steps
- Enable Mac (Designed for iPad / Catalyst) in target's Supported Destinations
- Build, gate iOS-only imports with `#if os(iOS)` — known offenders: UIKit imports in PlayheadRuntime + DownloadManager, AVAudioSession in audio playback path, BGTaskScheduler in BackgroundProcessingService (fuo6 wiring)
- Get to first launch on Mac, then first successful episode analysis on Mac
- Verify Foundation Models actually loads + classifies on Catalyst (this is the highest-risk question — FM availability on Catalyst has historically lagged iOS)
- Verify SpeechAnalyzer transcribes correctly on Catalyst

## Out of scope
- UI polish / Mac-native look
- App Store submission
- Mac-specific features (multiple windows, sidebar, etc.)
- Native AppKit rewrite (that's the .2 sibling)

## Decision output
Pick: Catalyst is good enough → ship Catalyst. OR Catalyst is too compromised → escalate to native (.2). Document which and why in close-out.

## Time box
2-3 days. Stop and report back if you blow past — likely means Catalyst hits a wall worth surfacing.

title: Mac port
description:
Ship a Mac version of Playhead. Foundation Models, SpeechAnalyzer, AVFoundation, SwiftData, and MPNowPlayingInfoCenter all work on macOS 26+ Apple Silicon — the detection/analysis service layer is reusable as-is.

## What's iOS-only and needs replacement / gating

- `UIKit` imports (PlayheadRuntime, DownloadManager) — replace with SwiftUI or AppKit, gate with `#if os(iOS)`
- `AVAudioSession` — iOS-only; Mac uses AVAudioEngine directly
- `BGTaskScheduler` (the fuo6 wiring) — iOS-only; Mac apps don't background the same way, no equivalent needed (just keep working when minimized)

## Strategic angle

- Mac dogfood = parallel episodes visible at once → faster signal collection
- Pairs with playhead-bbrv (cross-user analysis sharing): user A's iPhone + user A's Mac is the cleanest first peer-pair to validate the share path
- Mac users skew older/higher-income — better fit for one-time purchase monetization
- Apple Silicon-only is fine; Intel Macs are out by 2026

## Two forks (children: .1 Catalyst spike, .2 native scoping)

Decide between Catalyst (days, iOS-y feel, ships fast) and native (weeks, better aesthetics, separate target). The decision should follow the spike + scoping work, not before.
notes: Deferred 2026-07-24 (founder reorder): retention-phase work — revisit at ~$5k MRR / after listeners love the core. Not deleted, just not now. Categories: Mac, TTS, chapters, federation, ad-atlas, specialist/fancy-AI, detection improvements users won't notice.

title: Regression test: enqueue while backgrounded must submit BG task (Gap-4 follow-up)
description:
**From audit playhead-5uvz Gap-4 (HIGH — main fix already shipped in playhead-fuo6 / commit aba849a).**

playhead-fuo6 fixed the proximate cause of the 12-hour overnight blackout (no `appDidEnterBackground()` hook → no BGProcessingTask submitted → iOS never woke the app). Per the commit message, fuo6 added the test asserting `scheduleBackfillIfNeeded` is invoked on `.background` scenePhase transition.

**Symmetric gap not yet covered:** any `enqueue` call where the app is already backgrounded should also submit a BG task. Otherwise: user enqueues an episode while app is already backgrounded → no BG task ever gets requested → same blackout class.

**Fix scope:** Add a defensive regression test that asserts:
- Calling `AnalysisWorkScheduler.enqueue` (or whatever the public download-completion hook is) while `scenePhase == .background` triggers `BackgroundProcessingService.scheduleBackfillIfNeeded()`.

If the test fails, add the call-site to whichever enqueue path is missing it.

**Files:** `PlayheadTests/Services/BackgroundProcessing/` (new test file), `Playhead/Services/AnalysisCoordinator/BackgroundProcessingService.swift`.

See: `docs/audits/2026-04-25-episode-job-dag-audit.md`

title: TranscriptEngineService.stopTranscription for AnalysisJobRunner timeout (Gap-6)
description:
**From audit playhead-5uvz Gap-6 (MEDIUM).**

`AnalysisJobRunner.swift:249` carries a known TODO:

```swift
// TODO: Stop the transcript engine to prevent orphaned work if the timeout fired.
// TranscriptEngineService does not yet expose a stopTranscription() method.
```

If the 5-minute transcription timeout fires before the engine emits .completed, the runner returns `.failed("transcription:zeroCoverage")` but `TranscriptEngineService` keeps running in the background. The orphan's subsequent persistence writes target an analysisAssetId whose owning scheduler has already moved on. The job row's transcriptCoverageEndTime advances out-of-band after the row was marked failed — confusing coverage-guard recovery and the partial-coverage gate.

**Fix scope:**
1. Add `stopTranscription(analysisAssetId:)` to `TranscriptEngineService`. It should cancel the underlying SpeechAnalyzer task and drop any in-flight chunks for that asset.
2. Call it from `AnalysisJobRunner.run` zero-coverage timeout branch.
3. Test: pin the contract with a stalled-engine simulation that asserts no writes against a stopped asset.

**Files:** `Playhead/Services/AnalysisJobRunner/AnalysisJobRunner.swift` (line 249), `Playhead/Services/Transcript/TranscriptEngineService.swift`.

See: `docs/audits/2026-04-25-episode-job-dag-audit.md`

title: BackgroundFeedRefreshService should rearm backfill BG task after refresh (Gap-5)
description:
**From audit playhead-5uvz Gap-5 (MEDIUM).**

`BackgroundFeedRefreshService` (playhead-fv2q) and `BackgroundProcessingService` register independent `BGTaskScheduler` identifiers. Feed refresh runs `refreshEpisodes` and triggers auto-download. `handleBackfillTask` drains the analysis queue. **Nothing reconciles their lifecycles.**

If feed refresh adds 4 downloads and finishes, but iOS doesn't grant backfill BG time for 6 hours, those 4 downloads sit unanalyzed. The flow only works because `discoverUnEnqueuedDownloads` runs at app launch and the scheduler loop is constantly polling — neither helps when the device is locked overnight.

This is the same class of gap as playhead-fuo6 (which fixed the .background scenePhase → BG task submission link).

**Fix scope:** When `BackgroundFeedRefreshService` finishes a refresh that produced new downloads, it should explicitly call `BackgroundProcessingService.scheduleBackfillIfNeeded()` so a BG task is requested even if none was outstanding.

Test: assert refresh-with-new-downloads triggers `scheduleBackfillIfNeeded` (counterpart to fuo6's regression test).

**Files:** `Playhead/Services/Feed/BackgroundFeedRefreshService.swift`, `Playhead/Services/AnalysisCoordinator/BackgroundProcessingService.swift`.

See: `docs/audits/2026-04-25-episode-job-dag-audit.md`

title: Wrap AnalysisWorkScheduler.processJob outcome arms in single transaction (Gap-3)
description:
**From audit playhead-5uvz Gap-3 (MEDIUM).**

The outcome switch at `AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:1664-1869` is a sequence of separate `await store.X(...)` calls under `writeIfStillOwned`:

`updateJobProgress` → switch → state-specific updates (tierAdvance.insertNext, tierAdvance.markComplete, coverageInsufficient.requeue, failed.requeue, etc.) → final `releaseLease.tail`.

Each is a separate transaction. **Crash between `updateJobProgress` and `tierAdvance.markComplete` leaves the job at state=`running` with progress recorded but no terminal mark.** Orphan recovery does eventually requeue it via lease expiry (~30s scheduler-side), but the row is stuck `running` until the next reconciler pass.

The `runSchedulingPass` helper exists in `AnalysisStore` but is exercised only by `simulateCrashInSchedulingPassForTesting` and by acquireEpisodeLease/releaseEpisodeLease. The outcome arms could batch their writes under a single `runSchedulingPass` block.

**Reference pattern:** `BackfillJobRunner.markBackfillJobComplete` and `markBackfillJobFailed` are guarded against silent terminal resurrection by the C3-2 `IN ('queued','deferred','running')` guard plus the idempotent-on-self-state probe. The scheduler's `analysis_jobs` outcome arms have no equivalent guard.

**Fix scope:**
1. Wrap each outcome arm in `runSchedulingPass` so progress + state + lease release are one transaction.
2. Add a `SchedulerProcessJobInterruptionTests` that crashes between outcome arms — analogous to `InterruptionHarnessTests` for Pipeline A.
3. Optionally add C3-2-style status guards to the analysis_jobs terminal transitions.

**Files:** `Playhead/Services/PreAnalysis/AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift` (lines 1664-1869), `Playhead/Persistence/AnalysisStore/AnalysisStore.swift` (`runSchedulingPass`).

See: `docs/audits/2026-04-25-episode-job-dag-audit.md`

title: Phase A spike: full-file-hash analysis sharing on a non-DAI show
description:
Spike to validate the cross-user analysis sharing thesis (parent: playhead-bbrv) with the simplest possible mechanism.

## Scope
- Compute SHA-256 of full episode audio at ingest, persist alongside AnalysisStore record
- Tuple key: (showID, episodeID, fileSHA)
- Build a minimal share path: device A's analysis (ad spans + isAd + confidence + ad-type) is fetchable by device B keyed on tuple
- On device B, if tuple match found, apply imported analysis and SKIP the FM pass entirely
- Measure: FM minutes saved on episode, latency from queue->ready, battery delta if observable
- Test bed: Conan O'Brien Needs a Friend (simplecast feed, non-DAI per memory)

## Out of scope (Phase A)
- DAI shows (deferred to Phase B)
- Anti-poisoning consensus (single trusted peer = Dan's other device for spike)
- k-anonymity / privacy hardening
- Production sync infrastructure (CloudKit, custom server, etc.) — pick whatever is fastest for spike

## Acceptance
- Two of Dan's devices, same Conan episode, second device imports analysis from first and renders banners without running FM
- Wall-clock and battery measurements documented in bead close-out
- Decision: ship to Phase B / iterate / kill, with rationale
