title: Cross-user analysis sharing (fingerprint-anchored)
description:
Share derived ad-window analysis between users to amortize FM inference cost across the user base. Transcripts stay strictly on-device (copyright). Analysis (ad spans, isAd, confidence, ad-type) is fact-like metadata about the recording — defensible to share.

## Phases

**Phase A — full-file hash, non-DAI shows:**
- Compute SHA-256 of episode audio file at ingest
- Tuple key: (showID, episodeID, fileSHA)
- If a peer has analysis for the same tuple, fetch + apply locally instead of running FM
- Anti-poisoning: require consensus from N>=2 peers OR fingerprint-evidence (catalog match) before trusting shared analysis
- Privacy: k-anonymize the share (no per-user attribution leak)
- Validation: pick one non-DAI show (Conan O'Brien Needs a Friend), share analysis between two of Dan's own devices, measure FM-skip win

**Phase B (deferred) — chunked acoustic fingerprints, DAI shows:**
- Full-file SHA fails for Megaphone/Art19/Wondery DAI feeds (each listener gets different stitched bytes)
- Chunked acoustic fingerprints over host-read sections survive ad swaps
- Reuses existing catalog fingerprint infra (gtt9.13)
- Out of scope for Phase A

## Why now

FM inference is the dominant on-device cost. Transcription is 0.1-0.3x realtime; FM analysis is the ceiling on backfill throughput and battery. Sharing analysis amortizes that cost across the user base for free.

## Why this isn't a cloud-mandate violation

Memory: 'all transcription/classification must be on-device, no cloud'. This proposal does NOT move analysis to the cloud — analysis still runs on-device. It only redistributes the *output* peer-to-peer or via a server. Structurally different from cloud inference.
notes: Deferred 2026-07-24 (founder reorder): retention-phase work — revisit at ~$5k MRR / after listeners love the core. Not deleted, just not now. Categories: Mac, TTS, chapters, federation, ad-atlas, specialist/fancy-AI, detection improvements users won't notice.

title: Filter rollups by pipeline-coverage classification
description:
## Problem

Headline rollup metrics (Sec-F1, Win F1, AutoSkip Prec/Recall) average across captures regardless of whether the pipeline actually completed transcript coverage. From the 2026-04-25 report:

- ALL allEnabled Sec-F1 = 0.451 (mixed)
- completeFull cohort: AutoSkip Prec **1.00**, Recall 0.14
- completeTranscriptPartial cohort: 0/0/0 across the board

Pre-9.1.1 captures whose transcript stalled at 90s drag the headline down even though the detector itself can't be blamed for what it didn't see.

## Fix

Filter rollups to exclude `pipeline-coverage-limited` captures the same way `wholeAssetVeto` already excludes 9 corrected assets.

- Per-episode table: keep all rows (visibility)
- Rollups (ALL/Conan/DoaC): exclude `pipeline-coverage-limited`
- Add row to "Excluded episodes" section with reason `pipelineCoverageLimited:<assetId>`
- Headline metrics then reflect detector quality on captures the pipeline actually finished

## Acceptance

- New rollup table shows lower episode counts where exclusions apply
- Per-episode table unchanged
- Excluded list lists the pipeline-coverage-limited episodes with reason
- Test: synthetic harness run with one `pipeline-coverage-limited` fixture proves it's excluded from rollups but present in per-episode

## Reference

`PlayheadTests/Services/ReplaySimulator/NarlEval/NarlEvalReport.swift` (rollup aggregator)

title: NARL corpus builder must not silently default shadow weight=0 when isAd missing
description:
## Problem

`NarlEvalCorpusBuilderTests.assembleTrace` (PlayheadTests/Services/ReplaySimulator/NarlEval/NarlEvalCorpusBuilderTests.swift:541-548) folds every shadow row into evidenceCatalog with `weight = (s.shadowIsAd ?? false) ? 1.0 : 0.0`. When the exporter omits `isAd` (today's state — see gtt9.4.4), `shadowIsAd=nil` and every shadow row lands as weight=0 — **indistinguishable from genuine disagreement**.

This masks any disagreement-vs-missing-field bug and creates silent false-negative signal for any downstream consumer that keys on shadow weight.

## Fix options

- If shadow row lacks `isAd` / `shadowConfidence`: SKIP folding (don't emit a spurious 0-weight row) rather than defaulting to 0.
- Or: fold into a separate field (e.g. `shadow-unknown` source) so 0-weight rows are recognizable as 'no signal captured' not 'shadow disagreed'.

## Why this matters even after gtt9.4.4

Defense in depth: even if the exporter fix ships, old captures on disk won't carry the new field. A schema-tolerant builder should degrade gracefully instead of silently zeroing.

## Acceptance

- Corpus builder either skips or disambiguates weight=0 shadow rows that lack a meaningful isAd/confidence field.
- Test: a JSONL line without `isAd`/`shadowConfidence` should NOT produce a weight=0 FrozenEvidenceEntry indistinguishable from a real disagreement.

## Reference

- Spike verdict: docs/narl/2026-04-24-shadow-weight-zero-spike.md (gtt9.4.2)

title: ShadowDecisionsExporter must export shadow isAd boolean into JSONL
description:
## Problem

`ShadowDecisionsExporter.serialize` (Playhead/Services/AdDetection/ShadowDecisionsExporter.swift:101-119) writes only the opaque `fmResponseBase64` blob. No `isAd` / `shadowIsAd` top-level field is emitted.

`NarlEvalCorpusBuilderTests.parseShadowLog` (PlayheadTests/Services/ReplaySimulator/NarlEval/NarlEvalCorpusBuilderTests.swift:327-353) reads for `obj["isAd"]` / `obj["shadowIsAd"]`. Since neither is written, `shadowIsAd = nil` → corpus builder maps to `weight = 0.0` for EVERY shadow row (assembleTrace line 544: `weight: (s.shadowIsAd ?? false) ? 1.0 : 0.0`).

Empirical proof: in FrozenTrace 71F0C2AE, 111 / 111 shadow entries have weight=0 — including the entry at [5670, 5700] covering the high-confidence LIVE-agreed ad span [5670.6, 5690.52]. If the shadow model truly disagreed, we'd expect at least that entry to be non-zero.

## Fix

Either (a) decode `ShadowFMPayload.refinementResponse` in the exporter and emit a top-level `isAd` boolean, OR (b) emit the shadow classifier's confidence/score into a top-level `shadowConfidence` field so the corpus builder can populate a meaningful weight.

Prefer (b): the corpus-builder fold (line 542-548) hardcodes weight=1.0/0.0 — pair this change with gtt9.X.X (below) so the builder reads a real confidence.

## Acceptance

- Export path writes `isAd` (or `shadowConfidence`) per row.
- Re-derive a fresh 71F0C2AE FrozenTrace and confirm shadow entries show non-uniform weights where live classifier agreed.

## Reference

- Spike verdict: docs/narl/2026-04-24-shadow-weight-zero-spike.md (gtt9.4.2)

title: Hot-path high-confidence candidates need boundary expansion before emitting decision log
description:
## Problem
Commit 6e37335 promotes hot-path classifier ≥0.80 → autoSkipEligible in the decision log. Good. But the bounded window is still the raw 2-second classifier slot (e.g. [7006, 7008]).

User FN corrections on long closing-block ads mark the full ad region (e.g. [7007.34, 7037.34], 30 s). After NarlGroundTruth mergeOverlaps, the GT span becomes [7006, 7037.34].

Window-level IoU of pred [7006, 7008] vs GT [7006, 7037.34] = 2/31.34 = 0.064, well below the 0.3 threshold. The detector is correct; the prediction is too narrow.

## Evidence
Conan 71F0C2AE @ [7006, 7008] — classifier 0.8154 — would be a clean TP with any reasonable boundary expansion. Today it's a FN regardless of threshold tuning.

## Fix shape (to explore)
Options:
1. Carry SpanFinalizer boundary-expanded endpoints into the hot-path decision log rather than raw classifier slot bounds.
2. Post-hoc ±15s tolerance window in the harness IoU computation when the prediction is a head-of-ad hot-path candidate (classifier-only evidence, no FM).
3. Emit the raw slot AND the expanded span and let fusion choose.

Preferred: option 1, because it fixes the real user-facing contract (the AdWindow shown in the player UI) rather than the harness alone.

## Acceptance
- Hot-path candidates ≥0.80 emit decision logs with expanded spans that match SpanFinalizer's production output.
- Re-run NARL harness on 2026-04-24: Conan 71F0C2AE reaches Sec-F1 ≥ 0.55.
- FP precision does not regress by > 2 points on DoaC.

## Parent
Diagnosis: docs/narl/2026-04-24-finding1-conan-classifier-diagnosis.md (investigation/gtt9.18).
Depends on gtt9.19 landing first — the corpus builder fix must precede this so its effect is measurable.

title: narl-coverage-threshold-config-struct
description:
## Goal
Promote the 0.95 coverage threshold in `NarlEvalReport.swift` into a named config struct so future harness tunables have a canonical home.

## Context
gtt9.15 landed pipeline-coverage bucketing with the classifier hardcoding `0.95` as the threshold distinguishing "scoring-limited" (≥ 95% coverage) from "pipeline-coverage-limited" (< 95% coverage). Flagged as follow-up #3 in the GREEN report: "consider promoting it into a config struct alongside other harness tunables once a second similar threshold appears." The user asked for this immediately.

## Scope
- Create a `NarlPipelineCoverageThresholds` (or similarly named) struct in `PlayheadTests/Services/ReplaySimulator/NarlEval/NarlEvalReport.swift`
  - Field: `scoringLimitedCoverageFloor: Double` (default 0.95)
- Replace the inline `0.95` literal in `classify(_:)` with the struct field
- Pass-through: accept threshold struct as a parameter on `classify(_:thresholds:)` with a default value, OR expose as a static constant. Prefer the parameter pattern for testability.
- Update `NarlPipelineCoverageBucketTests.swift` to exercise non-default thresholds (e.g. 0.90) to prove the plumbing works
- Back-compat: Codable shape of `NarlPipelineCoverageBucketRollup` unchanged

## Success
- PlayheadFastTests pass
- No behavior change on existing fixtures (default threshold preserved)
- At least one test uses a custom threshold value

## Dependency
Blocked by gtt9.15 merging to main (same file).

## Source
Flagged as follow-up #3 from gtt9.15 GREEN report, 2026-04-24.
close_reason: Promoted the 0.95 coverage floor from a bare static constant into a NarlPipelineCoverageThresholds config struct (Sendable, Equatable, .default factory). classify(_:thresholds:) and countsPerBucket(traces:thresholds:) now accept a threshold parameter with a default value; all existing call-sites remain source-compatible. New test classifyHonorsCustomThresholds proves the plumbing by picking a 0.92 ratio that sits strictly between a custom 0.90 floor and the default 0.95 floor. PlayheadFastTests: 4462 passed, 0 failed on iPhone 17 Pro sim. Merged via 12084f3.

title: Repro 71F0C2AE on a post-fix capture: confirm 6e37335 + a4ea4ca actually moved Sec-F1
description:
## Problem

Two real fixes shipped on 2026-04-23/24 that target the 71F0C2AE catastrophe:

- **6e37335** (`emitHotPathDecisionLogs`): promote `action="hotPathCandidate"` → `"autoSkipEligible"` when adProbability ≥ 0.80.
- **a4ea4ca** (`makeClassifierProposals`): seed classifier-only high-conf windows so they reach BackfillEvidenceFusion.

The fixture used in this spike (`PlayheadTests/Fixtures/NarlEval/2026-04-24/FrozenTrace-71F0C2AE-7260-4D1E-B41A-BCFD5103A641.json`) was captured at 2026-04-24 01:34 UTC — **before both commits** (02:29 UTC and 03:28 UTC respectively). So we don't yet know whether they delivered.

## Asks

1. Capture a fresh dogfood session of the same episode (Conan 117-min, episodeId `flightcast:01KM20WJPKVFHRVJZWTNA6Q1XT`) on a current build.
2. Drop the new FrozenTrace into `PlayheadTests/Fixtures/NarlEval/<date>/` and re-run `NarlEvalHarnessTests` to compare:
   - `isAdUnderDefault` distribution at the 7006-window (should flip true under fix).
   - Predicted span extent vs GT [7007.34, 7037.34] (still expected ~2 s — feeds into 9.4.1 priority).
   - Sec-F1 / AutoSkip Precision / AutoSkip Recall delta vs prior fixture.
3. Update `docs/narl/2026-04-24-real-data-findings.md` with the post-fix numbers.

## Acceptance

- A new fixture under `2026-04-2*` exists with `capturedAt` after 2026-04-24 03:28 UTC for episode 71F0C2AE.

title: Spike: shadow:allEnabledShadow weight=0 across GT region
description:
## Problem

In FrozenTrace 71F0C2AE (Conan, 117 min), the GT ad span [7007.34, 7037.34] has 14 `shadow:allEnabledShadow` evidence entries scattered across [6900, 7050] — and **all of them carry weight=0**. Yet two strong-signal `policyAction=detectOnly` events at [0, 29.82] and [5670.6, 5690.52] reached `fusedSkipConfidence=1.0` via FM corroboration in the LIVE path.

Three competing hypotheses (need disambiguation):
1. Shadow classifier truly disagreed with the live classifier — actual signal of model weakness.
2. Shadow path is not exporting confidence into the `weight` field — corpus-builder bug.
3. `ShadowDecisionsExporter` is writing weight=0 for non-positive shadow decisions by design — but corpus-builder folds them in regardless, so they look like silent disagreements.

## Asks

1. Inspect `ShadowDecisionsExporter` (`Playhead/Services/AdDetection/ShadowDecisionsExporter.swift`) and the corpus-builder shadow-fold (`PlayheadTests/Services/ReplaySimulator/NarlEval/NarlEvalCorpusBuilderTests.swift:540-550`) to determine which hypothesis holds.
2. If hypothesis 2 or 3: file a fix bead to thread shadow confidence through.
3. If hypothesis 1: cross-check shadow confidence on episodes where live AND shadow agreed (the [0, 29.82] window) — is shadow always 0?

## Reference

- Spike notes in playhead-gtt9.4 (2026-04-24 follow-up section, "Gaps that couldn't be verified" #3).

title: Thread lifecycle fields into FrozenTrace for coverage-aware harness classification
description:
The NARL harness's FrozenTrace JSON schema is missing the gtt9.8 lifecycle telemetry fields, so the harness cannot distinguish 'ad missed because transcript never covered the window' from 'ad missed despite full coverage' — the exact question the 2026-04-24 findings raised for episode 71F0C2AE (full coverage 1.000/1.000) vs 34C7E7CF (stopped at tx=840, ft=726).

gtt9.8 writes these fields to `asset-lifecycle-log.jsonl` and the live `AnalysisStore`:
- terminalReason
- analysisState
- durationSec
- fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime (→ transcriptCoverageEndSec in FrozenTrace)
- featureCoverageEndTime (→ featureCoverageEndSec in FrozenTrace)

The NARL corpus builder does not read those fields and does not write them to the FrozenTrace JSON. Inspection of the two new 21:34 fixtures from 2026-04-24 shows all these fields as None in the FrozenTrace JSON. Classification of 'why did this episode miss' currently must be inferred from the evidence ledger rather than read from truth.

Fix: extend FrozenTrace JSON schema (Codable back-compat), update NARL corpus builder to read lifecycle state from AnalysisStore / asset-lifecycle-log.jsonl and populate them, update NARL harness to use them when classifying why an episode missed.
acceptance_criteria:
1. FrozenTrace JSON emitted by NARL captures includes the 5 lifecycle fields when the source AnalysisStore has them.
2. Existing FrozenTrace JSON files (without the fields) continue to decode cleanly (Codable back-compat).
3. Harness report at minimum buckets episodes into 'pipeline-coverage-limited' vs 'scoring-limited' using the terminalReason / coverage-end fields.
4. Re-run of 2026-04-24 fixtures shows 71F0C2AE classified as 'scoring-limited' (full coverage) and 34C7E7CF classified as 'pipeline-coverage-limited' (stopped at tx=840).
notes: Reference: docs/narl/2026-04-24-real-data-findings.md Finding 3. Unblocks cleaner follow-up investigations like the 71F0C2AE full-coverage spike currently running under gtt9.4.
close_reason: Landed in 2024f1d. Harness now buckets episodes into scoring-limited / pipeline-coverage-limited / unknown via NarlPipelineCoverageBucket (terminalReason substring match first, then fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime/durationSec ratio ≥ 0.95). 71F0C2AE = scoring-limited, 34C7E7CF = pipeline-coverage-limited validated on real 2026-04-24 fixtures. All 3916 PlayheadFastTests green. No review fixes required — scope verified that gtt9.8 had already shipped the 5 FrozenTrace lifecycle fields; this branch only adds the 3-bucket classifier, rollup, report section, and 16 new tests.

title: Catalog as precision signal — fingerprint user corrections, cross-match future episodes
description:
## Why

Per the 2026-04-23 expert review (§8): the local catalog should be one of the strongest precision signals. Today `catalog` fires on 5 of 147 windows (3%). Ads on podcasts often repeat across episodes (same sponsor, same creative, same campaign). **Every user correction is a labeled example we can fingerprint and reuse on-device.**

## Scope

When a user marks (or auto-skip confirms) an ad span, store locally:

1. Compact audio fingerprint or embedding of the span (on-device compute, durable).
2. Transcript snippets when available.
3. Sponsor / brand tokens when available.
4. Show, episode position (pre/mid/post-roll), duration.
5. Optional: confidence of the original detection.

Then on future episodes: search the catalog for approximate matches and let the match feed fusion.

Promotion integration:

```
if catalogSimilarity is high:
  allow lower classifier threshold (catalog match IS the safety signal, gtt9.11)
if catalogSimilarity is absent:
  require stronger acoustic / lexical / metadata evidence
```

## Acceptance

1. Every user correction + auto-skip triggers a catalog insert on-device.
2. New episodes emit `catalog` evidence on windows that match stored fingerprints above a similarity floor.
3. Catalog firing rate on the 2026-04-23 corpus re-analyzed after a warm catalog ≥ 15% of windows (from 3%).
4. Fingerprints + embeddings stay local (no cloud, per legal mandate).

## Related

- Depends on: gtt9.10 (segment aggregator produces the spans worth fingerprinting).
- Pairs with: gtt9.12 (repetition fingerprint / acoustic embedding is shared infrastructure).
- Pairs with: gtt9.11 (catalog match is a core safety signal for auto-skip).

title: Acoustic feature expansion — transcript-independent ad evidence
description:
## Why

Per the 2026-04-23 expert review (§7): `MusicBedLevel` fired on only 3 of 147 windows. Podcast ads have distinctive production signatures that should be detectable without a transcript. Acoustic is currently the quietest evidence source (2% firing rate) despite being the one most likely to help when transcript is incomplete (which, per gtt9.6/gtt9.9, is the dominant real-world failure mode).

## Scope

Add or validate these local, on-device acoustic features:

| Feature | Why it helps |
|---|---|
| Music bed probability | Many ads use background music or jingles |
| Loudness / LUFS shift | Inserted ads are mastered differently from host audio |
| Dynamic range / compression | Ads often tighter compression |
| Speaker embedding shift | Host/guest conversation → ad voiceover |
| Spectral profile shift | Studio conversation vs. produced ad bed |
| Silence / bumper boundary | Transition gaps at ad breaks |
| Repetition fingerprint | Same creative reused across episodes (pairs with gtt9.13 catalog) |
| Tempo / rhythm / music onset | Ad beds and intros |

Each feature becomes a source in the existing evidence fusion pipeline with a calibrated weight.

## Acceptance

1. Each new feature has a "source funnel" (gtt9.4) — computed / produced-signal / passed-gate / included-in-fusion counts per episode.
2. Combined acoustic-evidence firing rate ≥ 20% of windows on the 2026-04-23 corpus (up from 2%).
3. On assets with zero transcript coverage, acoustic evidence produces at least one candidate per plausible pre/mid/post-roll region.
4. All features are on-device compute (per legal no-cloud mandate).

## Related

- Depends on: gtt9.9 (feature-only scoring path) — this bead populates it.
- Pairs with: gtt9.4 (source funnel) — funnel telemetry validates each feature is actually doing work.
- Pairs with: gtt9.13 (catalog) — repetition fingerprint is shared infrastructure.

title: Split detection recall from auto-skip precision (two-layer operating model)
description:
## Why

Per the 2026-04-23 expert review (§5): the detector currently has one knob (fused confidence vs promotion threshold) that tries to serve two very different goals. **A missed ad is annoying; skipping real content breaks trust.** These should be separate operating layers with different thresholds.

## Scope

Introduce three distinct operating layers:

| Layer | Goal | Threshold source | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| Detection | High recall | `candidateThreshold` | surface for telemetry, future learning |
| UI candidate | Balanced | `segmentScore ≥ uiThreshold` | show "possible ad" marker in timeline / skip chip |
| Auto-skip | High precision | `segmentScore ≥ autoSkipThreshold` AND `≥1 safety signal` | automatic skip |

Auto-skip safety-signal gate:

```
autoSkipEligible =
  calibratedSegmentScore ≥ autoSkipThreshold
  AND duration is plausible (min + max)
  AND at least one of:
    - catalog match
    - strong lexical ad phrase
    - metadata slot prior (pre/mid/post-roll position)
    - sustained acoustic ad signature
    - repeated sponsor pattern
    - user-confirmed local pattern
```

Without ≥1 safety signal, a high score stays at "UI candidate" — visible to the user but not auto-skipped.

## Acceptance

1. `autoSkipEligible` requires the safety-signal conjunction above.
2. `candidateVisible` (new) represents the "UI candidate" layer for timeline markers.
3. Re-eval on 2026-04-23 capture shows `autoSkipPrecision` improves vs. `autoSkipRecall` trading off (expected: fewer promotions, each higher quality).
4. No auto-skip on a window with classifier-only evidence (default behavior today for hotPathCandidate).

## Related

- Depends on: gtt9.10 (segment aggregator — this bead operates on segment scores).
- Pairs with: gtt9.11 (catalog) and gtt9.12 (acoustic) — they produce the safety signals this layer consumes.
- Pairs with: gtt9.2 — rejection reasons from the promotion gate should include the specific missing safety signal.

title: Show-label heuristic fails on URL-form podcastIds; hides per-show signal
description:
## Problem

Eight of 11 non-vetoed real episodes in the 2026-04-23 corpus roll up as `"unknown"` in the harness report because their `podcastId` is the full feed URL:

```
https://feeds.simplecast.com/dHoohVNH::311e3daa-60b3-4428-b780-c9a7b8512be8
```

The show-label heuristic at `PlayheadTests/Services/ReplaySimulator/NarlEval/NarlEvalHarnessTests.swift:390-405` matches substring patterns like `"flightcast"`, `"conan"`, `"diaryofaceo"`. The URL-form podcastIds contain those tokens nested in URLs, but the current matching logic doesn't descend into URLs reliably.

## Consequence

1. Per-show rollups in the eval report lose most of the real-data signal.
2. The memory entry `project_ad_detection_weak_on_conan.md` — which attributes detection weakness to Conan's "conversational/comedy content" — is based on unreliable show attribution. Finding 1 suggests the real cause is pipeline completion, not content style.

## Asks

1. Harden the show-label heuristic to handle URL-form `podcastId`:
   - Parse as URL; match on host + path segments
   - Known feed hosts: `feeds.simplecast.com` (Conan), `feeds.flightcast.com` or similar (DoaC)
   - Include a fallback to title-substring-matching on the asset's display title
2. Add a test case for each known podcastId form in the 2026-04-23 corpus
3. Re-run the 2026-04-23 eval; confirm per-show rollups show real Conan/DoaC breakdowns

## Acceptance

- Zero `"unknown"` entries in the rollup for podcasts the corpus has known test-data for
- Per-show F1 and coverage numbers visible in the regenerated report
- Passes through if we add new shows: the logic degrades gracefully rather than misattributing

## Reference

Full writeup: `/Users/dabrams/playhead/docs/narl/2026-04-23-real-data-findings.md` — Finding 5
notes:
**Expert-evaluation report (detailed data):** `/Users/dabrams/playhead/docs/narl/2026-04-23-expert-report.md`
2026-04-23 expert review (§12) broadens scope: robust podcastId parsing (URL-form, feed hostname/path, episode-ID patterns) with fallback to title metadata. Not just fixing the heuristic — a principled show-key derivation. Re-run per-show rollups after landing to validate gtt9.1.1 eliminates the Conan/DoaC delta. Promoted to P2 because gtt9.6 (metric split) and comparative quality claims depend on reliable show attribution.

title: Investigate evidence-source firing rates; classifier-dominance on real data
description:
## Problem

Across 147 real scored windows, the classifier decides every window (100%), while other evidence sources fire <10% of the time.

| Source | Count | % of windows |
|---|---|---|
| classifier | 147 | 100% |
| metadata | 10 | 7% |
| fm | 8 | 5% |
| lexical | 5 | 3% |
| catalog | 5 | 3% |
| acoustic | 3 | 2% |

The NARL metadata-activation gates (`lexical` priors, `metadata` priors, `fm` scheduling) touch <10% of decisions. If this is by design, NARL activation is a second-order lever (can't move detection quality much even when tuned right). If it's a symptom (sources not firing when they should), it's a separate quality issue with its own root cause.

## Acoustic specifically

`MusicBedLevel` tracked but fires 3 of 147 times. Ads have distinctive production characteristics (music beds, voiceover compression, stingers) — acoustic signal should plausibly be much more active than 2%.

## Investigation asks

1. Is low non-classifier firing **by design** (gates too conservative, rare sources) or **accidental** (source pipelines not reaching fusion, early-exit before scoring, dropouts)?
2. If accidental — which source pipeline is silent, and why? Trace at least one source from detection → fusion to find where the drop happens.
3. If by design — is the gating correct, or should thresholds be relaxed to match real-world signal density?
4. MusicBedLevel specifically: is it being computed? Gated? Thresholded too strictly?

## Why this matters

Even perfect priorShift (gtt9.3) or perfect metadata activation can't move the needle if the evidence sources those systems gate are already silent. This bead is a "check the premise before retuning the knobs" investigation.

## Acceptance

- Evidence-firing percentages for each source explained (by design vs accidental)
- If accidental: at least one fix that raises a source's firing rate to an expected level
- Re-run on the corpus; document source-firing deltas

## Reference

Full writeup: `/Users/dabrams/playhead/docs/narl/2026-04-23-real-data-findings.md` — Finding 4
notes:
## 2026-04-28 closure note

All four investigation asks ANSWERED (see prior 2026-04-24 spike notes). Highest-leverage remediations shipped via playhead-sqhj:
- `MusicBedLedgerEvaluator` + `buildMusicBedLedgerEntries` wired into `AdDetectionService.swift` (the 2026-04-24 "disconnected pipeline" claim is now stale).
- `MetadataActivationConfig.counterfactualGateOpen` flipped to `true` (the 2026-04-24 "shipped disabled" claim is now stale at the master-gate level; per-gate flags remain false pending separate decisions).

Numeric re-measurement of per-source firing percentages requires a fresh post-sqhj device capture (fixtures can't reproduce live evidence-source firing). That work continues under the epic, not under this spike. Remaining open child playhead-gtt9.4.3 reparented to playhead-gtt9 since it verifies gtt9.4.1's shipped fix on a fresh capture rather than gating this spike.

Proposed follow-ups (not filed — listed for visibility):
- Verification: post-sqhj dogfood capture; recompute per-source firing percentages vs 2026-04-23 baseline.
- Spike: audit MetadataActivationConfig per-gate flags now that master gate is open.
- Feat: FM disposition telemetry to validate Positive-Only Rule blast radius.

title: Retune priorShift band against real classifier confidence distribution
description:
## Problem

PriorShift activation targets windows whose classifier confidence falls in the half-open band `(classifierShiftedMidpoint, classifierBaselineMidpoint]`. Configured today as `(0.22, 0.25]`.

**On 147 real scored windows, the band contains zero.** PriorShift cannot flip any decisions because no windows land where it operates.

## Confidence distribution (real data, 147 windows)

```
[0.10, 0.20): 11   ███████████
[0.20, 0.22):  0
[0.22, 0.25):  0   ← priorShift band, empty
[0.25, 0.30): 12   ████████████
[0.30, 0.40): 78   █████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████
[0.40, 0.50): 11   ███████████
[0.50, 0.70): 23   ███████████████████████
[0.70, 1.00):  8   ████████
```

Mode is `[0.30, 0.40)` — 53% of windows. The synthetic fixtures put windows in the priorShift band artificially; real classifier output doesn't cluster there.

The two "adds" priorShift contributes in the eval both come from synthetic fixtures (verified during the 2026-04-23 dig).

## Ask

Retune priorShift midpoints against real confidence distribution. Candidate band: `classifierShiftedMidpoint=0.28, classifierBaselineMidpoint=0.32` — puts the band where real windows actually live. Need to validate experimentally, not just pick numbers.

## Acceptance

- PriorShift band overlaps the real confidence mode
- Non-zero windows land in the band on the current corpus
- Counterfactual eval confirms priorShift contributes measurable adds on real data (not just synthetic)
- Retune does not regress F1 at stricter thresholds (@0.5, @0.7)

## Reference

Full writeup: `/Users/dabrams/playhead/docs/narl/2026-04-23-real-data-findings.md` — Finding 3

Eval output: `.eval-out/narl/20260423-175930-22C2B0/` (regenerate with cmd in findings MD)
notes:
**Expert-evaluation report (detailed data):** `/Users/dabrams/playhead/docs/narl/2026-04-23-expert-report.md`
Audit 2026-04-29: code/tests show the priorShift band retuned to (0.33, 0.37] and latest eval shows non-zero priorShiftAdds (31 in .eval-out/narl/20260429-033503-6BC845/report.md). Keeping open because the same eval has allEnabled below default at stricter window F1 thresholds: tau=0.5 0.116 vs 0.121, tau=0.7 0.083 vs 0.086. Remaining decision: adjust retune/activation or explicitly revise the strict-threshold acceptance criterion.
2026-05-08 verification: current source already carries the second priorShift retune to (0.345, 0.37] with gtt9.3 regression guards in MetadataActivationConfig/MetadataPriorShift tests. Re-ran NarlEvalHarnessTests with xcodebuild on iPhone 17 Pro simulator, derivedDataPath /tmp/gtt9-3-narl-dd: TEST SUCCEEDED. Fresh report .eval-out/narl/20260508-190733-12AD38/report.json shows priorShiftOnly has 12 real-data priorShift adds, 0 lexical adds, and matches default F1 at strict thresholds exactly: ALL tau=0.5 0.1206896551724138 vs default 0.1206896551724138; tau=0.7 0.08620689655172414 vs default 0.08620689655172414. allEnabled still dips slightly at strict thresholds, but lexicalOnly reproduces that dip while priorShiftOnly is metric-neutral; the remaining regression belongs to lexical injection, not this priorShift bead. A direct xcodebuild filter for MetadataActivationTests selected 0 tests, so not counted as verification.
close_reason: Closed after current-code verification: priorShift band is retuned to (0.345, 0.37], fresh NARL harness report shows 12 real-data priorShiftOnly adds with no strict-threshold F1 regression versus default; allEnabled strict-threshold dip is attributable to lexicalOnly, not priorShift.

title: Per-episode gate-flip recommendation engine (narl Phase 1 bead 3)
description:
Per-episode `counterfactualGateOpen` recommendation engine, consuming the harness's report. Phase 1 Bead 3 of 3. Full design in `docs/plans/2026-04-21-narl-eval-harness-design.md`.

## Problem

The narl bead's acceptance criteria calls for "gating strategy specified (per-episode trust threshold vs. global)". The harness (Bead 1) produces metrics. A human can read them and decide whether to flip `counterfactualGateOpen` — but that doesn't scale as the corpus grows and as we want to evaluate specific activation flags per-episode.

This bead automates the *recommendation* step: given a harness JSON report, emit a per-episode decision on whether to recommend flipping the gate.

## Policy rule (initial, tunable)

```
recommend flip for episode E if:
  allEnabled.recall(E)    >= default.recall(E)
  AND allEnabled.precision(E) >= default.precision(E) - ε   (ε default 0.02)
  AND episode is fully shadow-covered (so fmScheduling evidence is real)
```

Three output states per episode:
- `recommendFlip` — policy rule satisfied, evidence trustworthy.
- `holdOff` — policy rule fails on at least one condition.
- `insufficientData` — episode is partial-coverage or was excluded (whole-asset veto).

## Open design question (to decide during THIS bead's own brainstorming — not locked in by the design doc)

Does this bead stop at *recommending*, or does it also *execute*?
- **Recommend-only** (current lean): Writes `recommendations.json` alongside the harness report. Dan applies recommendations by hand (e.g., per-episode override stored in a config file, or a future "approved episodes" feature).
- **Recommend+execute**: Persists per-episode overrides into a store that the runtime consumes, effectively flipping `counterfactualGateOpen=true` for approved episodes automatically.

Recommendation path is simpler and lower-risk; execution path is more useful but more invasive. To be re-brainstormed with `superpowers:brainstorming` when this bead is started.

## Components (recommend-only scope; grows if execute is chosen)

1. **Policy evaluator**
   - Pure helper: `(ReportSummary, Policy) -> PerEpisodeRecommendation[]`.
   - Configurable ε; configurable shadow-coverage threshold for "fully covered".
   - Unit-tested against synthetic report fixtures.

2. **Recommendation report**
   - Written to `.eval-out/narl/<timestamp>/recommendations.{json,md}` — same sibling dir as the harness report.
   - JSON: schema-versioned per-episode decisions + policy parameters used.
   - Markdown: table of (episode, show, decision, reasoning).

3. **Integration with harness run**
   - Either: (a) harness calls the recommender as a final step; or (b) separate Swift Testing suite that reads the latest harness report and runs the recommender. (b) keeps scopes clean.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given a harness JSON report, produces `recommendations.json` with per-episode decisions (recommendFlip / holdOff / insufficientData).
- Policy rule parameterized: ε configurable, shadow-coverage threshold configurable.
- Unit tests cover: all three output states, threshold boundary behavior, partial-coverage episodes.
- Report cross-links: recommendations reference the specific metric values that drove each decision.
- Gracefully handles missing `fmSchedulingEnabled` data (emits `insufficientData` rather than failing).

## Non-goals (this bead, recommend-only scope)

- Executing the flip (mutating production config or persisting per-episode overrides).
- Global gate-flip based on aggregate metrics (deferred).
- Trust-threshold-based auto-flipping (deferred — that's the `metadataTrust` alternative mentioned in the parent narl bead).

## Dependencies

- Depends on: `playhead-narl-harness` (report format must be stable).
- Blocks: nothing direct; unblocks informed human gate-flip decisions.
- Complementary with: `playhead-narl-shadow-capture` (fmScheduling recommendations only meaningful once shadow data accrues).

## Labels

narl, narl-phase1, activation, policy

title: FM dual-run shadow capture production path (narl Phase 1 bead 2)
description:
Production dual-run capture of `.allEnabled` FM responses so the harness can evaluate `fmSchedulingEnabled` honestly. Phase 1 Bead 2 of 3. Full design in `docs/plans/2026-04-21-narl-eval-harness-design.md`.

## Problem

The replay harness (`playhead-narl-harness`) can evaluate `lexicalInjectionEnabled` and `classifierPriorShiftEnabled` from a `FrozenTrace` deterministically. But `fmSchedulingEnabled` changes *which windows FM ever runs on* — under `.default`, FM runs only on seeded windows; under `.allEnabled`, it also runs on a wider set. The frozen trace can't know what FM would have said about the un-seeded windows, because those calls never happened.

This bead populates that gap in production so the harness's `.allEnabled` replay has real FM evidence for un-seeded windows.

## T4 two-lane capture strategy

**Lane A — JIT during strict playback.**
- Fires only when `AVAudioSession` is actively playing (strict — not just foreground, not paused).
- For a lookahead region `[playhead, playhead + N seconds]` (N tunable; start with 60s, parameterize), identify windows `.default` didn't schedule FM on but `.allEnabled` would.
- Fire bounded-budget shadow FM calls on those windows. Budget shape (windows-per-second, max-concurrent) TBD during implementation; start conservative.
- Cost scales with listening time, not episode size.

**Lane B — background thorough pass.**
- Runs when `ProcessInfo.processInfo.thermalState == .nominal` AND the device is charging (`UIDevice.batteryState`).
- Walks episodes flagged "shadow coverage incomplete", fills in remaining un-seeded windows.
- Writes through the same path as Lane A.
- Integrates with the existing scheduler lane infrastructure if practical; otherwise a new background worker.

Both lanes obey the kill switch and tag their writes with `capturedBy ∈ {"laneA","laneB"}` for diagnostics.

## E1 — sqlite storage (source of truth)

New table in `analysis.sqlite`:

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS shadow_fm_responses (
  assetId       TEXT    NOT NULL,
  windowStart   REAL    NOT NULL,
  windowEnd     REAL    NOT NULL,
  configVariant TEXT    NOT NULL,  -- "allEnabledShadow" for Phase 1
  fmResponse    BLOB    NOT NULL,  -- same serialized format as prod FM response
  capturedAt    REAL    NOT NULL,
  capturedBy    TEXT    NOT NULL,  -- "laneA" | "laneB"
  PRIMARY KEY (assetId, windowStart, windowEnd, configVariant)
);
```

(Exact shape — separate table vs column on existing FM response table — decided during implementation.)

## E3 — export via `shadow-decisions.jsonl`

- New sibling file in the exported `.xcappdata` bundle's Documents dir alongside `decision-log.jsonl`.
- One JSON line per shadow FM response with stable schema (schemaVersion, assetId, windowStart, windowEnd, configVariant, fmResponse, capturedAt, capturedBy).
- `ExportedAnalysisStore` export manifest writes this file.
- Corpus builder in `playhead-narl-harness` reads this file when present.

## Kill switch

`ShadowCaptureConfig.dualFMCaptureEnabled: Bool` (default `true` for Dan's build). When `false`, both lanes no-op at their entry points. Flag location: alongside `MetadataActivationConfig`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Lane A fires shadow FM during strict playback with a bounded budget (verifiable via unit test: simulate playback progression, assert bounded number of shadow FM calls in a time window).
- Lane B fills in shadow coverage when thermal `.nominal` + device charging (verifiable via unit test with mocked environment signals).
- `shadow_fm_responses` rows written durably to sqlite; schema migration lands without breaking existing tests.
- Export round-trip test: export a bundle → unpack → corpus builder produces a FrozenTrace whose `.allEnabled` FM evidence is populated from shadow responses. This is the binding AC — without it the harness can't consume the data.
- Kill switch verified: with `dualFMCaptureEnabled=false`, no shadow FM calls, no new rows written, no export rows.
- No thermal regression measurable on backfill (Lane A's playback-scoped budget + Lane B's thermal gate).
- `PlayheadFastTests` plan stays green.

## Non-goals (this bead)

- Using shadow data in any production gate decision (only the harness reads it).
- Schema evolution for config variants beyond `allEnabledShadow`.
- Automated tuning of Lane A's lookahead size or per-second budget.
- UI surfacing of shadow capture state.

## Dependencies

- Depends on: none (self-contained production capture path).
- Blocks: full `fmSchedulingEnabled` metrics in `playhead-narl-harness` reports (harness still ships without this for the other two flags).
- Parallel with: `playhead-narl-harness`.

## Risks / gotchas

- Battery / thermal regression risk if Lane A's budget is too generous. Start conservative; measure before loosening.
- Charging detection via `UIDevice.batteryState` requires `isBatteryMonitoringEnabled = true`. Cost: a small amount of UIKit observer state.
- Schema migration path for existing installs — ensure the new table creates idempotently.
- FM response format versioning — shadow responses captured under one FM model shouldn't be consumed as gospel if the model changes. Consider a `fmModelVersion` column, or rely on downstream consumers to invalidate.

## Labels

narl, narl-phase1, activation, production

title: Counterfactual eval replay harness (narl Phase 1 bead 1)
description:
Replay-based counterfactual eval harness for the `playhead-narl` gate. Phase 1 Bead 1 of 3. Full design in `docs/plans/2026-04-21-narl-eval-harness-design.md`.

## What this bead delivers

A Swift Testing suite that takes `FrozenTrace` fixture JSONs, replays the deterministic stages of the ad detector (fusion + gate + policy) under `MetadataActivationConfig.default` and `.allEnabled`, and emits a precision/recall/F1/IoU report per (show, config, threshold).

Ships the first report against the 2026-04-21 corpus export (4 test episodes: 2× Diary of a CEO, 2× Conan O'Brien Needs a Friend). Covers `lexicalInjectionEnabled` and `classifierPriorShiftEnabled` fully; `fmSchedulingEnabled` evaluated only for episodes marked "fully shadow-covered" (requires `playhead-narl-shadow-capture` to have accrued data).

## Components to build

1. **Corpus builder** (`PlayheadTests/Services/ReplaySimulator/NarlEvalCorpusBuilderTests.swift`)
   - Env-gated Swift Testing `@Test`: `.enabled(if: ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["PLAYHEAD_BUILD_NARL_FIXTURES"] == "1")`.
   - Input: path to exported `.xcappdata` bundle (env var or well-known dev path).
   - Reads `analysis.sqlite` (feature windows, atoms, evidence catalog, FM responses) + `decision-log.jsonl` + `corpus-export.jsonl` + `shadow-decisions.jsonl` (if present).
   - Output: one `FrozenTrace-<episodeId>.json` per episode written to `PlayheadTests/Fixtures/NarlEval/<YYYY-MM-DD>/`.
   - Dan runs this once per corpus refresh and commits the resulting JSONs.

2. **Ground-truth construction** (`Playhead/Services/AdDetection/Eval/NarlGroundTruth.swift` or inside replay simulator)
   - Pure helper. Input: FrozenTrace + corrections. Output: positive ad-window set.
   - Rules: start with `decision` spans; remove anything overlapped by `falsePositive exactTimeSpan` corrections; add every `falseNegative exactTimeSpan` correction; resolve ordinal-range `exactSpan` corrections via atoms; exclude episodes carrying `exactSpan:<assetId>:0:INT64_MAX` vetoes.
   - Unit-tested in isolation: `NarlGroundTruthTests.swift`.

3. **Eval runner** (`NarlEvalHarnessTests.swift`)
   - Swift Testing suite, runs in `PlayheadFastTests`.
   - Iterates fixture JSONs, for each config replays fusion/gate/policy, emits predicted ad windows, compares against ground truth.
   - Asserts only: (a) both configs ran without throwing, (b) `.eval-out/narl/<timestamp>/report.json` and `report.md` exist.
   - Metric regressions must NOT fail the build. They surface in the report for human judgment.

4. **Metrics (M3)**
   - Window-level IoU at τ ∈ {0.3, 0.5, 0.7}: precision, recall, F1, mean IoU of matched pairs.
   - Second-level: project windows onto second timeline, report precision/recall/F1 over ad-seconds.
   - Roll up per (show ∈ {DoaC, Conan, ALL}, config ∈ {.default, .allEnabled}).

5. **Output (O1)**
   - `.eval-out/narl/<timestamp>/report.json` — versioned schema.
   - `.eval-out/narl/<timestamp>/report.md` — tables per (show × config × metric family).
   - `.eval-out/narl/trend.jsonl` — append one row per (run timestamp, show, config, metric, value). Local-only, gitignored.
   - Add `.eval-out/` to `.gitignore`.

## Acceptance criteria

- `xcodebuild test -scheme Playhead -testPlan PlayheadFastTests` produces `.eval-out/narl/<timestamp>/report.{json,md}` without build failure.
- First report covers ≥2 Diary of a CEO and ≥2 Conan episodes from the 2026-04-21 export, with per-show and per-config precision/recall/F1 populated for `lexicalInjectionEnabled` and `classifierPriorShiftEnabled`.
- Corpus builder successfully converts the 2026-04-21 `.xcappdata` bundle into FrozenTrace fixtures.
- Ground-truth construction unit tests pass (falseNegative add, falsePositive remove, veto exclude, ordinal resolution).
- Whole-asset veto (`exactSpan:<id>:0:INT64_MAX`) causes the episode to be dropped from metrics and flagged in the report's excluded list.
- Trend log appended by each run.
- No regression in `PlayheadFastTests` (3587 tests green baseline).

## Non-goals (this bead)

- Production code changes to capture shadow FM data (→ `playhead-narl-shadow-capture`).
- Recommending gate-flip decisions (→ `playhead-narl-approval`).
- Committed run-over-run eval history.
- Tuning of specific `.allEnabled` config parameters.

## Dependencies

- Depends on: none (uses the existing 2026-04-21 corpus-export for fixtures; no-FM-scheduling data is fine because fmSchedulingEnabled evaluation is punted to shadow-capture).
- Blocks: `playhead-narl-approval` (needs the harness's JSON report format).
- Parallel with: `playhead-narl-shadow-capture` (shadow data flows into harness reports once available, but harness ships without it).

## Labels

narl, narl-phase1, eval, activation

title: Persist show title + episode title in AnalysisStore for self-describing exports
description:
Today the AnalysisStore identifies entities only by feed URL (podcast_profiles.podcastId) and feed-item GUID URL (analysis_assets.episodeId). Human-readable titles like 'Diary of a CEO' and 'Conan O'Brien Needs a Friend' live on the SwiftData side, so an exported analysis.sqlite is opaque on its own — you have to cross-reference a separate source to know which show/episode any row belongs to.

This matters because we may want to share exports (support handoff, eval datasets, a future user-facing export/share feature). An exported snapshot should be legible without also needing the SwiftData store.

Concretely: when we pulled com.playhead.app 2026-04-21 19:00.11.706.xcappdata to reason about the end-of-input race fix, we had no way to tell from the sqlite alone that the flightcast feed was DoaC and simplecast was Conan.
acceptance_criteria:
- podcast_profiles has a 'title' column (show name)
- analysis_assets has an 'episodeTitle' column
- Writes populate both on first observation (pulled from the feed entry / SwiftData)
- Existing rows backfilled on next access or via a one-shot migration
- An exported analysis.sqlite is legible standalone: SELECT on any asset yields a human-readable show + episode

title: Audit episode job DAG + checkpoint ledger for gaps (wizard idea #3)
description:
Post-reveal synthesis from Dueling Idea Wizards (2026-04-16) said: ~85% of the durable episode job DAG already exists (PipelineStage, BreakerManager, WorkJournal, ShardCoordinator). Audit what's there — don't rebuild.

Scope:
(a) Enumerate every pipeline stage transition and confirm each writes a durable ledger row BEFORE doing the work (not after).
(b) Confirm shard-level checkpoints survive process death — kill the app mid-shard and verify resume picks up at the persisted cursor, not the shard start.
(c) Confirm recovery is idempotent — replaying a partially-completed stage must not double-charge FM budget or corrupt WorkJournal state.
(d) File any gaps found as follow-up beads; add ledger rows only where concrete gaps exist.

## Context
Cross-score detail: Codex scored 520 (CC argued existing infra). Synthesis verdict in DUELING_WIZARDS_REPORT.md §Tier 1 #3: 'Don't rebuild what's built.'
acceptance_criteria: Audit report produced listing every pipeline stage, its ledger write behavior, and pass/fail for the idempotent-replay test. Zero gaps discovered OR follow-up beads filed for each gap. No new infrastructure built unless a gap requires it.

title: narE: Debug-menu corpus export (CorrectionEvent + DecodedSpan → JSONL in Documents)
description:
## Background

Supersedes narA (playhead-l3hg, closed). Discovery: Playhead already has the correction UX wired — PersistentUserCorrectionStore captures structured \`CorrectionEvent\` rows in \`analysis.sqlite\` from both the \"Not an ad\" transcript-modal button (→ \`recordVeto\`, exactSpan scope, \`.falsePositive\`) and the \"I'm listening to an ad\" button (→ \`recordFalseNegative\`, synthetic ±15s span, \`.falseNegative\`).

narA-as-debug-annotator was redundant. What's actually missing: a **one-tap way to export this corpus data off device in corpus-useful format**, without having to run Xcode's Download Container and pick apart \`.xcappdata\`.

## Scope

### Debug-menu action: \"Export corpus log\"
- New debug-only action (same dev gate as narL).
- Reads from \`analysis.sqlite\`:
  - All \`CorrectionEvent\` rows (with decay weights applied)
  - All \`DecodedSpan\` rows joined by \`analysisAssetId\`
  - Episode/asset metadata needed to interpret spans
- Writes JSONL to \`Documents/corpus-export.<timestamp>.jsonl\` — goes straight into the file-sharing-visible directory (Info.plist flags already land this turn).

### Record schema
One line per corpus-relevant event, tagged by type:
- \`type: \"correction\"\` — full CorrectionEvent payload (scope, source, correctionType, causalSource, targetRefs, createdAt)
- \`type: \"decision\"\` — DecodedSpan payload (assetId, ordinal range, start/end times, anchorProvenance)
- \`type: \"asset\"\` — episode metadata needed to interpret IDs
- \`schemaVersion: 1\` up front so replay tools handle drift.

### Join-key consistency
Records use the same \`analysisAssetId\` and atom-ordinal keys as narL's \`decision-log.jsonl\` so both feeds combine into a single corpus pipeline downstream (narE = what happened + what was corrected; narL = richer per-window decision inputs for counterfactual replay).

### Optional: join with narL's log
If narL has been running and \`decision-log.jsonl\` exists, emit a pointer/manifest that references it, so \"Export corpus log\" produces a coherent bundle you can drag out in one Finder operation.

## Acceptance

- Debug action is reachable during playback or from a diagnostics menu.
- Tapping writes \`Documents/corpus-export.<timestamp>.jsonl\` (verified by Finder or Files app).
- JSONL parses cleanly; one record per CorrectionEvent and one per DecodedSpan for the exported asset(s).
- Dev-gate test: action is unavailable in release builds (same assertion as narL).
- Manual smoke test: after running against Dan's existing 4–5 episodes, the exported JSONL contains his falsePositive/falseNegative correction events with scope + timestamps intact.

## Explicitly out of scope

- User-facing export UX (this is debug-only).
- Any modification to the correction UX itself — UserCorrectionStore is the source of truth, we just read it.
- Server upload / cloud sync (on-device mandate; not needed for personal corpus use).

## Depends on / relates to

- Supersedes \`playhead-l3hg\` (narA).
- Pairs with \`playhead-8em9\` (narL): narL captures decision-pipeline inputs for replay; narE captures the ground-truth labels from existing correction UX. Together they feed \`playhead-8xap\` (nar0, parking-lot harness).
- Exposed via the \`UIFileSharingEnabled\`/\`LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace\` Info.plist flags added 2026-04-21.

title: narA: In-app correction annotator (debug menu)
description:
## Background

Pairs with `playhead-narL`. While narL logs every decision, narA captures ground-truth labels in the moment Dan notices a wrong skip or a missed ad. Turns normal listening into corpus growth as a side effect.

This is the smallest possible version — not a full correction UX, just a labeling hook.

## Scope

### Minimal debug menu
- Two actions accessible from debug overlay or dev-only menu during playback:
  - **\"That was an ad\"** — stamps current playback window as `groundTruth: ad`.
  - **\"That wasn't an ad\"** — stamps current playback window as `groundTruth: notAd`.
- Each action writes one line to `FileManager.default.urls(for: .documentDirectory)[0].appendingPathComponent(\"corrections.jsonl\")`:
  - episodeID, timestamp, currentPlayheadSeconds, windowBounds (±N seconds around playhead — configurable default 15s), label (ad/notAd), optional freetext note field.
- Log record must include enough context to join back to `decision-log.jsonl` records by (episodeID, time range) for offline corpus construction.

### Join key consistency
- `corrections.jsonl` and `decision-log.jsonl` MUST use identical episodeID format so offline replay can pair labels to decisions without fuzzy matching.

## Acceptance

- Two debug actions exist and are reachable during playback.
- Tapping either writes a record to `corrections.jsonl`.
- Records can be joined to `decision-log.jsonl` entries by (episodeID, time range) — verify with a test that builds a synthetic log+correction pair and parses them.
- Debug actions are compiled out of release builds (wrapped in the same dev gate as narL).

## Explicitly out of scope

- End-user banner correction UX (that's `playhead-r83k`-family work — different surface, different constraints).
- Correction anchor precision (blind-spot idea #4 from COD duel — separate bead if pursued).
- Retroactive annotation across entire episode (only stamps the window around current playhead).

## Why now

Corpus growth at zero marginal effort. Every wrong skip becomes a labeled datapoint.

## Depends on / blocks

- Depends on: `playhead-narL` (uses same log directory, episodeID format, dev gate).
- Contributes to eventual `playhead-nar0` corpus requirements.
close_reason: Rescoped/superseded by narE (see new bead) — original narA duplicates the existing correction UX: PersistentUserCorrectionStore + 'Not an ad' / 'I'm listening to an ad' buttons already capture structured CorrectionEvent rows in analysis.sqlite. Force-closing because the blocker relationship (depends on 8em9 narL) no longer applies — this work path is abandoned, not deferred.

title: Activate metadata lexical injection + classifier prior shift + FM scheduling (counterfactual gate)
description:
Dead-evidence sweep finding from 2026-04-21 (follow-up to dueling-wizards synthesis). A three-part metadata activation system is fully built, tested, but gated off in production.

Components (all in Playhead/Services/AdDetection):
- MetadataLexiconInjector — built, no external caller in production
- MetadataPriorShift — built, no external caller in production
- FM scheduling for seeded regions — integrated but config-gated

All three consumption points are gated by MetadataActivationConfig. The production default sets:
- lexicalInjectionEnabled: false
- classifierPriorShiftEnabled: false
- fmSchedulingEnabled: false
- counterfactualGateOpen: false  (master gate — disables all three even if individual flags were true)

The allEnabled variant exists for testing and 'counterfactual-approved episodes'. The inline comment says: 'Production default: all consumption points disabled pending counterfactual evaluation.'

So the gate isn't arbitrary — the system is waiting for counterfactual evaluation methodology to demonstrate the activation helps rather than hurts.
design:
Two phases:

Phase 1 — counterfactual evaluation methodology:
- Define what a counterfactual-approved episode looks like (criteria, trust thresholds).
- Build or confirm the evaluation harness: run with both .default and .allEnabled on the same episode corpus, compare outcome quality.
- Per-episode approval can then flip counterfactualGateOpen case-by-case, or a trust-gate on metadataTrust can flip it globally above a threshold.

Phase 2 — graduated activation:
- Start with one consumption point (probably lexicalInjection since it's least invasive — just expands the lexicon context).
- Measure. Then graduate classifierPriorShift and fmScheduling.

Risk: without counterfactual evidence, flipping these on could degrade precision. The gate exists for a reason. Do not flip blindly.
acceptance_criteria:
- Counterfactual evaluation methodology documented and runnable
- Corpus comparison report (default vs. allEnabled) on representative episodes
- At least one consumption point activated with measured precision/recall delta
- Gating strategy specified (per-episode trust threshold vs. global)
- No regression on false-positive rate after activation
close_reason: Activated lexical-only metadata injection with production scanner wiring, ownership-context safeguards, frozen NARL counterfactual baseline, corpus-builder contamination guard, decision documentation, focused tests, build verification, and two clean review rounds after cap override.

title: Thread PriorHierarchyResolver into AdDetectionService with real network/trait/show-local inputs
description:
Follow-up to playhead-p2iv (duration-as-prior, implemented 2026-04-21). The subagent that implemented p2iv surfaced that PriorHierarchyResolver has NO production call site — it is only invoked from PriorHierarchyTests.swift. Even deader than the duration prior's dead output.

Current state after p2iv: DurationPrior is applied in DecisionMapper using DurationPrior.standard, which derives from GlobalPriorDefaults.standard.typicalAdDuration (30...90s). The prior modulates, but with global defaults only — not show-aware.

Gap: to make the prior (and any future consumers of ResolvedPriors) actually show-aware, the full resolver needs to run in production with:
- network priors (aggregated across shows)
- trait profile (does the podcast profile feed TraitProfile?)
- show-local priors (observed per-show episode priors)
design:
Steps:
1. Identify producers for each input tier (network, trait, show-local). Audit whether ShowLocalPriors etc. have real population paths or are only built in tests.
2. Call PriorHierarchyResolver.resolve(...) at episode-analysis entry in AdDetectionService or upstream orchestrator, producing a ResolvedPriors per episode.
3. Replace DurationPrior.standard at the AdDetectionService backfill call site with DurationPrior(resolvedPriors: resolved) — the type already supports this initializer (added in playhead-p2iv).
4. Add lightweight regression tests covering show-local override (e.g. a show with atypical ad lengths gets a differently-shaped prior).

Risk: if any input tier has no real producer, this bead expands. Keep it scoped — if network-level aggregation is also missing, file that separately and ship show-local + global first.
acceptance_criteria:
- PriorHierarchyResolver.resolve() is called from production code (not just tests)
- ResolvedPriors is available to the backfill fusion path
- DurationPrior uses the resolved typicalAdDuration, not the global default
- Show-local priors measurably override global defaults when enough episodes are observed
- No regression on shows without accumulated priors (graceful fallback to global)

title: LLM-inferred chapters from transcript + acoustic features (on-device FM)
description: Follow-on to playhead-rxuv (activate chapter evidence). For the majority of podcasts that do NOT ship Podcasting 2.0 chapters, generate a chapter structure with an on-device FoundationModels pass using transcript chunks + acoustic feature timeline as input. Feeds the same ChapterEvidence type as the creator-chapter path, with a distinct provenance tag and a lower trust weight in fusion.
design:
Motivation: bead playhead-rxuv only benefits episodes with creator-provided chapters (minority). On-device FM (live since Phase 3) can segment any episode from existing inputs — transcript + 2s feature windows (RMS, spectral flux, music probability, pause probability, speaker cluster) — producing chapters labeled with types like {sponsor, interview, qa, main, transition, ...}.

Architecture:
- Sibling service to ChapterParser; same output type (ChapterEvidence) with provenance='inferredChapter'.
- One episode-level FM call with structured-output schema: ordered chapters with startTime, endTime, label, confidence.
- The FM prompt accepts transcript chunks + an acoustic event timeline (music starts/stops, speaker changes, high-energy regions).
- Allowed to return 'no clear chapter structure' for low-structure episodes — absence is neutral, not negative.

Confidence tiering (mandatory):
- creatorChapter (from playhead-rxuv): near-ground-truth weight.
- inferredChapter (this bead): lower weight in fusion. Statistical inference, not creator truth.
- Downstream consumer (decision mapper, scorer adjustments) same for both.

Circular-reinforcement guard: inferred chapters are derived from the same features the ad detector uses. To avoid double-counting, either (a) weight inferred-chapter evidence sharply below creator-chapter evidence, (b) ensure the chapter inference consumes transcript-level inputs while ad detection consumes window-level inputs, or (c) explicitly discount the chapter vote when the ad detector's other signals already fired. Pick the simplest that measurably avoids reinforcement.

Cost: one FM pass per episode at analysis time. Measure latency and thermal impact.
acceptance_criteria:
- On-device FM segments episodes lacking creator chapters
- Output feeds ChapterEvidence with provenance='inferredChapter' and lower trust weight
- Graceful 'no structure' return accepted by downstream
- Circular-reinforcement guard validated via shadow comparison
- No measurable regression vs. creator-chapter-only baseline
- Latency and thermal cost within budget
notes:
Refined and elaborated by sub-epic playhead-au2v.1 (Chapter signal: inferred generation + new consumers, 2026-05-06). The original 'single per-episode FM call' approach is superseded by chunked-heuristic-skeleton + per-chapter FM labeling because on-device FM token budget (~300-400 content tokens after ~3700-token schema overhead) rules out single-shot episode chaptering. The sub-epic also adds two consumers beyond fusion: CoveragePlanner attention-direction and per-window FM prompt context. Recommend closing this bead when sub-epic playhead-au2v.1 closes.
Deferred 2026-07-24 (founder reorder): retention-phase work — revisit at ~$5k MRR / after listeners love the core. Not deleted, just not now. Categories: Mac, TTS, chapters, federation, ad-atlas, specialist/fancy-AI, detection improvements users won't notice.

title: B2-followup: real cascade-attributed proximal-readiness SLI from production timing
description:
Replace the synthetic latency-model SLI test (PlayheadTests/Services/PreAnalysis/CandidateWindowCascadeProximalReadinessSLITest.swift, swws option (b) reframing) with a real cascade-attributed measurement.

What we have now (from swws option (b)):
- A self-contained simulation that generates per-episode latencies from a log-normal model and asserts the empirical P50/P90 satisfy TimeToProximalSkipReadyThresholds.
- The cascade is exercised in the loop only as a sanity check that .proximal windows are still emitted; cascade contribution to latency is NOT measured.

What this follow-up needs:
1. An injected clock plumbed into AnalysisWorkScheduler / CandidateWindowCascade / AnalysisJobRunner so timing can be driven synthetically without wall-clock dependency.
2. End-to-end driving of the real explicit-download → first-proximal-window-ready event sequence:
   download complete → enqueue → cascade seed → scheduler dispatch → first proximal slice ready.
3. Aggregation of N synthetic episodes through that sequence with the injected clock, computing the real cascade-attributed P50/P90.
4. Replace (or supplement) the current swws SLI test with this real measurement.

Acceptance:
- A test that, when the cascade or scheduler regresses such that the first-proximal-window-ready event is delayed past the SLI envelope, fails.
- The cascade's contribution to the measured latency is causal — flipping a cascade or scheduler knob changes the observed P90.

title: Follow-up to o45p: wire real AnalysisEligibilityEvaluator into EpisodeSurfaceStatusObserver
description:
Code review of playhead-o45p raised: `EpisodeSurfaceStatusObserver.eligibility` hardcodes `hardwareSupported = true` and `regionSupported = true` with a Phase 2 TODO. For Wave 4 dogfood with eligible US iPhones this is correct, but the hardcoded defaults silently mis-attribute ready transitions on ineligible hardware — a non-US or old-hardware dogfooder would see `ready_entered` fired when the real eligibility gate should have suppressed it.

Dan is the primary dogfooder (eligible device) so this stays hidden in Wave 4 runs, but the observer should eventually pull from the real `AnalysisEligibilityEvaluator` / `CapabilitiesService` instead of hardcoded defaults.

Scope:
- Replace the `hardwareSupported = true` / `regionSupported = true` defaults in `eligibility(from:)` with reads from the real evaluator.
- Add a test asserting ineligible hardware suppresses `ready_entered`.

Non-blocking for Wave 4 (acceptance criterion numerically works for eligible devices, which is the entire dogfood cohort).

title: Follow-up to o45p: bound lastReadyByEpisode growth in SurfaceStatusReadyTransitionEmitter
description:
Code review of playhead-o45p raised: `SurfaceStatusReadyTransitionEmitter.lastReadyByEpisode` grows unbounded over process lifetime. Each unique episode hash leaves a `Bool` entry that never clears. For a dogfood session spanning days and hundreds of episodes, this is a small leak (bytes per hash) but has no eviction or TTL.

Mitigations:
- Clear the entry when the emitter sees a non-ready reduction with explicit `.stopped`/terminal trigger.
- Or cap with a small LRU (per-process replay memory doesn't need to be perfect across long sessions — idempotence only matters for near-term repeats).

Non-blocking for Wave 4 — the memory footprint is bytes-per-hash, won't cause issues in 10-day dogfood.

title: Follow-up to o45p: lock SurfaceStatusReadyTransitionEmitter single-owner contract at type system
description:
Code review of playhead-o45p (M1 hash-fix round) raised: SurfaceStatusReadyTransitionEmitter is marked `@unchecked Sendable` with a doc-comment asserting 'single-actor ownership', but `EpisodeSurfaceStatusObserver.init` accepts `emitter: SurfaceStatusReadyTransitionEmitter = ...` as a defaulted parameter. A caller could (in theory, not today) retain the same emitter and hand it to two observers, violating the contract.

In practice only PlayheadRuntime constructs the observer and uses the default, so this is latent not live. But the type system doesn't enforce what the doc-comment claims.

Scope: either
- Drop the external emitter parameter; construct inside the actor. Expose a test-only init that takes a closed-over sink instead.
- Or: change `@unchecked Sendable` to explicit actor-held, with the actor guarding all state.

Non-blocking for Wave 4 dogfood.

title: Legal checklist (a)-(d) audit + I4: wire InstallIDProvider into production diagnostics flow
description:
Post-ghon followup, split into two scopes:

Scope 1 — I4: InstallIDProvider production wiring
- ghon defined InstallIDProvider but no production call site threads a UUID into DiagnosticsExportCoordinator's environment.
- Phase 2 l274 (UI placement) will own this; file here for tracking.
- Integration test: 'provision InstallIDProvider-derived UUID → coordinator → bundle contains salted hash'.

Scope 2 — Legal checklist audit (a)-(d)
- (a) Default bundle shape verified at type level (no episodeId), but end-to-end contract should be explicitly audited by user / legal.
- (b) OptInBundle isolation: transcript_excerpts + feature_summary only present in opt-in bundle.
- (c) Hashing: per-install salt, confirmed SHA-256 lowercase hex, unicode UTF-8 handled.
- (d) Opt-in reset policy: .sent/.saved clears flag; .cancelled/.failed preserves.

Deliverables:
- One test that loads the sample default bundle JSON and asserts key presence ⊆ {app_version, build_type, device_class, analysis_eligibility, summaries} (never episodeId).
- One test that loads the sample opt-in bundle JSON and asserts transcript_excerpts has a hashed episode_id (64 lowercase hex).
- Markdown checklist doc in docs/plans/ referencing the test file + line numbers.

Priority 2 (should fix, not blocking). Lands before Phase 2 l274 UI exposure.

title: Refactor DebugEpisodeExporter + TranscriptPeekViewModel to consume EpisodeSurfaceStatus only
description:
## Context

Followup to playhead-ol05 (SurfaceStatus invariants + contract tests).

That bead extended the `SurfaceStatusUILintTests.testNoSchedulerOrPersistenceTypesInUIViews` scope from just `/Playhead/App/` to also cover `/Playhead/Views/`. The lint caught 4 legitimate pre-existing violations:

- `Playhead/Views/Settings/DebugEpisodeExporter.swift:39` — `store: AnalysisStore` parameter
- `Playhead/Views/Settings/DebugEpisodeExporter.swift:237` — same type reference
- `Playhead/Views/NowPlaying/TranscriptPeekViewModel.swift:41` — forbidden module-boundary token
- `Playhead/Views/NowPlaying/TranscriptPeekViewModel.swift:55` — forbidden module-boundary token

Both files are UI-layer (`/Views/` subdirectories) but reach across the module boundary to persistence / analysis types instead of consuming `EpisodeSurfaceStatus`. That defeats the invariant this lint is meant to enforce.

To unblock ol05 merge without a scope-creep refactor, these two filenames were added to `SurfaceStatusUILintTests.uiPathExemptFilenames` with a comment pointing to this bead.

## Scope

Refactor both files to consume `EpisodeSurfaceStatus` only (the documented UI-layer contract from playhead-5bb3). Concretely:

1. `DebugEpisodeExporter` should not take `AnalysisStore`. Move the asset/chunk/window fetching to a thin service that hands UI a fully resolved `DebugEpisodeExport` value, or restructure the export call site to be invoked from a non-UI context.
2. `TranscriptPeekViewModel` should accept whatever typed data it needs via a boundary type, not a module-internal reference.

## Done criteria

- Both files no longer appear in `uiPathExemptFilenames`
- `SurfaceStatusUILintTests.testNoSchedulerOrPersistenceTypesInUIViews` still passes
- `PlayheadFastTests` green
- Debug-episode export still works end-to-end (manual smoke test, as before)
- Transcript peek still renders (manual smoke test)

## Why

The ol05 lint is now silent because we allow-listed two legacy files. That's fine as a temporary measure — the lint *will* still catch any *new* violation — but the allow-list is spec rot: it documents an exception that should be retired. Until both files land on the UI-layer contract, the invariant "UI consumes EpisodeSurfaceStatus only" has two holes.

title: Migrate invariantViolated(String) to real InvariantCode values
description:
Tech debt from playhead-ol05: the string-only entry-point SurfaceStatusInvariantLogger.invariantViolated(_ description: String) synthesizes a SurfaceStateTransitionEntry whose invariantViolation.code is HARD-CODED to .unavailableWithRetryHint regardless of the actual condition described in the message.

This causes downstream miscategorization: playhead-e2a3's dogfood audit groups entries by code, so the three reducer call-sites (EpisodeSurfaceStatusReducer.swift:181, :232, :307) that call invariantViolated with messages like "user-paused rule matched an unknown cause" will surface as .unavailableWithRetryHint in the audit — which has nothing to do with user-paused logic.

THE FIX:
1. Add an InvariantCode case per actual invariant condition reachable via the string entry-point (or fold those sites into the code-typed entry-points).
2. Change the three reducer call-sites to pass the real code.
3. Either deprecate SurfaceStatusInvariantLogger.invariantViolated(String) or rename it to .recordUnknown(String) with an explicit .unknown code so the miscategorization is no longer implicit.
4. Grep for any other string-path callers; migrate all of them.

Non-blocking for ol05 since the description field preserves the human-readable text verbatim; blocks only if e2a3 needs code-based grouping to be accurate, which per plan §6 Phase 1.5 pass-criterion 1 it does.

CROSS-REFS:
- Source of debt: playhead-ol05 commit 82004e5 (SurfaceStatusInvariantLogger.swift:148-165).
- Consumer: playhead-e2a3 (10-day dogfood gate).

title: Reconcile reducer ↔ CauseAttributionPolicy divergence
description:
The EpisodeSurfaceStatus reducer's cause→(disposition, reason, hint) routing disagrees with CauseAttributionPolicy.attribute(...) for four InternalMissCause variants. The policy (dfem, v11 taxonomy) is the canonical source; the reducer should delegate to it rather than duplicating (and diverging) the logic.

CURRENT DIVERGENCES (discovered during playhead-5bb3 landing, pinned with MARK block + tests; surveyed by playhead-ol05 spec review):

- .noRuntimeGrant:
  - policy → (queued, waitingForTime, wait)  [CauseAttributionPolicy.swift:386-391]
  - reducer → (failed, couldntAnalyze, retry)  [EpisodeSurfaceStatusReducer.swift:324-331]

- .unsupportedEpisodeLanguage:
  - policy → (unavailable, analysisUnavailable, none)  [CauseAttributionPolicy.swift:467-472]
  - reducer → (failed, couldntAnalyze, retry)

- .noNetwork:
  - policy → (paused, waitingForNetwork, none)  [CauseAttributionPolicy.swift:421-426]
  - reducer → (paused, waitingForNetwork, wait)  [reducer emits wait hint; policy emits none]

- .userCancelled:
  - policy → (paused, cancelled, none)  [CauseAttributionPolicy.swift:455-461]
  - reducer → (cancelled, cancelled, retry)

WHY NOT RECONCILED IN ol05:
Reconciling cascades into snapshot goldens, contract-pair fixture, multiple reducer targeted tests, and possibly dfem's table if the reducer is declared authoritative instead. Too large for ol05's invariant-layer scope.

WHAT THIS BEAD DOES:
1. Decide canonicity: the policy is authoritative (single source), reducer should delegate. Document this in the reducer header.
2. Replace the reducer's inline ladder logic for these four causes with delegation to CauseAttributionPolicy.
3. Drop the 4 divergence-pinning assertions from the reducer tests' MARK block; replace with contract tests asserting reducer-output matches policy-output.
4. Regenerate golden fixture; diff should only touch the 4 affected cause rows.
5. Run PlayheadFastTests to confirm no regression.

CROSS-REFS:
- Discovered: playhead-5bb3 merge commit + playhead-ol05 spec review.
- Authority: playhead-v11 (taxonomy) + playhead-dfem (policy table).
- Consumer: playhead-5bb3 (reducer).

title: LanePreemptionCoordinator round-trip: 5s budget flakes under parallel load
description:
Observed flake in PlayheadIntegrationTests (run during playhead-fpsl/ss38 fix work, 2026-04-18):

```
Test "Round trip: preemptLowerLanes flips signal → FeatureExtraction acks at post-shard boundary" recorded an issue at LanePreemptionCoordinatorTests.swift:653:9: Expectation failed: (elapsed → 5.152437959 seconds) < (LanePreemptionCoordinator.preemptionLatencyBudget → 5.0 seconds)
```

Plus cascading expectation failures at lines 663, 676 once the budget assertion fails.

Same root cause family as ss38: production budget used directly as test threshold. Cooperative-pool jitter under heavy load can push wallclock past production budget by hundreds of ms.

Fix recipe: assert median sample meets production budget; loosen the per-sample ceiling to a hang-detection threshold. See LanePreemptionCoordinatorTests promotionLatencyUnder100ms() for the template applied in ss38 fix.

Frequency: 1 in ~6 integration runs observed. P2.

title: Phase2Verification: 1800-window latency budget flakes under parallel load
description:
Observed flake in PlayheadIntegrationTests (run during playhead-fpsl/ss38 fix work, 2026-04-18):

```
Test "Processes 1800 windows (60-min episode) under 100ms" recorded an issue at Phase2VerificationTests.swift:146:9: Expectation failed: (elapsedMs → 159.799375) < 100.0
```

Same root cause as ss38: hard latency-budget assertion (max < 100ms) is fragile under cooperative-pool starvation from 3000+ parallel tests. Microbenchmark-style test running inside a heavy parallel test process.

Fix recipe (per ss38): replace single-sample max assertion with median-based check + generous hang ceiling. Pattern landed in commit fixing playhead-ss38 — see LanePreemptionCoordinatorTests promotionLatencyUnder100ms() for template.

Frequency: 1 in ~6 integration runs observed. P2 — same priority as ss38.

title: DownloadManager – Resume: NWListener localhost race under parallel load
description:
## Symptom
`DownloadManagerResumeContractTests/ignoredRangeResponseDoesNotCorruptPartialFile()` (Swift Testing) fails intermittently when run as part of full-suite parallel execution (3064 tests):

```
Caught error: Error Domain=NSURLErrorDomain Code=-1009 "(null)"
```

NSURLErrorNotConnectedToInternet on a localhost (127.0.0.1) URLSession request to an in-process NWListener-based test HTTP server.

## Reproduction
- Failed in PlayheadIntegrationTests run #1: 2026-04-18 11:01 (full suite)
- Failed in PlayheadIntegrationTests run #2: 2026-04-18 11:08 (full suite)
- PASSED in isolation: 0.017s, 1 of 1 (`-only-testing:'PlayheadTests/DownloadManagerResumeContractTests'`)
- PASSED in PlayheadFastTests run: 2026-04-18 11:11 (same 3064 tests, different flake hit instead — playhead-ss38)

## Root cause hypothesis
`IgnoringRangeHTTPServer` uses NWListener bound to ephemeral port 0. Under heavy parallel test load, the URLSession client may attempt to connect before the listener is fully reachable, or the OS networking stack may surface -1009 transiently. Test code at PlayheadTests/Services/Downloads/DownloadManagerTests.swift:289-327.

## Fix options
1. Add retry-on-1009 to URLSession path inside test (or production AssetProvider for resilience)
2. Mark suite as `.serialized` to avoid concurrent NWListener pressure
3. Replace NWListener with URLProtocol stub — no real socket needed

## Priority
P2: pre-existing test, not regression. Both PlayheadFastTests and PlayheadIntegrationTests have one flake each per parallel run (~99.97% pass rate each). Filed for follow-up; not blocking Phase 1 close (epic playhead-6f8p).
close_reason: Replaced NWListener with URLProtocol stub keyed by per-test UUID. Eliminates real loopback, no more -1009 under load. Verified 3x integration + 3x fast = 6/6 green. Commit 11ed665, merged in af26644.

title: Plumb live StorageBudget snapshot into AdmissionGate
description:
Follow-up from playhead-bnrs. The bnrs scheduler-integration fix (commit bfbfffe) landed with a hard-coded `plentiful` StorageSnapshot at `AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:629-636` (`canAdmit = true` for all 3 classes, `remainingBytes = Int64.max`). Consequence: admission-gate storage axis NEVER rejects in production. StorageBudget.admit still enforces at write-time, but the pre-admission gate is effectively disabled.

## Scope

- Inject `StorageBudget` into `AnalysisWorkScheduler` (actor).
- In `evaluateAdmissionGate(for:)`, synthesize a real `StorageSnapshot` by calling `storageBudget.canAdmit(class:bytes:)` and `storageBudget.remainingBytes(class:)` for each artifact class the job touches.
- Preserve testability: keep the `evaluateAdmissionGate` method injection-friendly (accept a `StorageSnapshot` parameter or a `StorageBudgetSnapshotting` protocol for tests).

## Acceptance

- On a device with low media storage, admission rejects a media-writing job pre-work with `.mediaCap` (not after write attempt).
- Existing AdmissionGateTests still pass.
- Integration test: simulate `StorageBudget.canAdmit(.media, 1 GB)` returning `false`; assert scheduler rejects pre-work.

## Depends on
