- playhead-bnrs (closed)
- playhead-h7r (closed) for StorageBudget surface

title: Live TransportStatusProvider: NWPathMonitor + user cellular prefs
description:
Follow-up from playhead-bnrs. The bnrs scheduler-integration fix (commit bfbfffe) landed with a stub TransportStatusProvider (`WifiTransportStatusProvider` at AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift:53) that hard-returns `.wifi` + `allowsCellular=true`. Consequence: the admission gate cellular/unreachable paths NEVER fire in production.

## Scope

- Implement `NWPathMonitor`-backed `LiveTransportStatusProvider`.
- Read user `allowsCellular` preference from settings store (if exists; create the preference if not).
- Wire the live provider into `AnalysisWorkScheduler.init` as the default (replacing `WifiTransportStatusProvider`).
- Preserve tests: existing test stubs (`StubTransportStatusProvider` in `AnalysisWorkSchedulerLaneAdmissionTests.swift:246`) should continue to inject cellular/unreachable in tests.

## Acceptance

- On a simulator with no network, scheduler admission rejects with `.noNetwork`.
- On a cellular-only device with `allowsCellular=false`, scheduler admission rejects maintenance-session jobs with `.wifiRequired`.
- Existing `testAdmissionGateRejectsMaintenanceOnCellular` still passes.
- Integration test verifying the live provider correctly reports state (on simulator network flip).

## Depends on

- playhead-bnrs (closed)

title: ForceQuit resumeConsumesBlob test leaks live URLSession
description: Code-quality follow-up from playhead-hyht review. ForceQuitResumeTests.swift:287-306 hands garbage Data([0xAB, 0xCD]) to a real background URLSession on the interactive lane and asserts .resumed without invalidating the session. The garbage task stays alive, leaking into sibling tests that construct DownloadManager (com.playhead.transfer.interactive identifier is process-global). ## Two fix options 1. Add invalidateBackgroundSessionsForTesting() and call after the assertion (smaller change). 2. Split resumeSuspendedTransfer so the URLSession handoff is behind an injectable boundary; the unit test exercises a fake (cleaner long term). ## Pick (1) for minimal scope.

title: Remove or DEBUG-wrap *ForTesting seams in ForceQuitResumeScan
description: Code-quality follow-up from playhead-hyht review. Five *ForTesting methods in ForceQuitResumeScan.swift (persistResumeDataForTesting, loadResumeDataForTesting, deleteResumeDataForTesting, persistedResumeDataEpisodeIdsForTesting, resumeSuspendedTransferForTesting) are exposed as 'internal' in release builds despite being thin pass-throughs to already-internal methods. Tests use @testable import Playhead, so they should call the production methods directly. ## Scope - Delete the five *ForTesting methods. - Update PlayheadTests/Services/Downloads/ForceQuitResumeTests.swift call sites to use production methods. - Verify build + tests still pass.

title: Infra: wire testPlans into Xcode scheme via project.yml
description:
Pre-existing infra gap surfaced during playhead-24cm work.

## Problem
`project.yml` does not emit `testPlans:` under the Playhead scheme. The .xcshareddata/xcschemes/Playhead.xcscheme file (checked in) does reference test plans via XML, but running xcodegen regenerates the scheme without testPlan wiring, breaking `xcodebuild -testPlan PlayheadFastTests`.

CLAUDE.md documents the two-plan workflow as canonical (`-testPlan PlayheadFastTests` for per-bead work, `-testPlan PlayheadIntegrationTests` for phase-close). Today that command succeeds after `bd worktree add` but fails after `xcodegen generate` in the worktree.

The 24cm agent worked around this with `-skip-testing` lists matching the fast plan's skips. That's not durable — every bead will rediscover the issue.

## Root cause
xcodegen's `project.yml` does not support `testPlans:` at the scheme level natively. The current setup relies on a hand-edited .xcscheme XML file that xcodegen does not regenerate. When a bead runs `xcodegen generate`, the scheme XML is preserved but any new file references bypass the test plan wiring.

## Options
A. Pin `project.yml` scheme definition to include explicit testPlan refs (requires xcodegen >= version with that feature; check capability).
B. Check in the .xcscheme XML and add a pre-commit guard that rejects xcodegen-generated schemes (keep hand-edited).
C. Migrate to tuist or manual pbxproj (larger scope; out of scope here).

Recommend A if supported, else B.

## Acceptance
- `xcodebuild test -scheme Playhead -testPlan PlayheadFastTests ...` succeeds on a fresh clone after xcodegen generate.
- CLAUDE.md test commands work verbatim.
- Regression: `xcodegen generate` does not wipe test-plan wiring.
close_reason: Resolved by commit 9751911 — added testPlans block to project.yml + ran xcodegen generate. Both PlayheadFastTests and PlayheadIntegrationTests now wired into Playhead.xcscheme via XcodeGen source-of-truth.

title: uzdq follow-up: WorkJournal silent corruption masking
description:
Gating follow-up for playhead-uzdq. Must land BEFORE playhead-1nl6 starts consuming WorkJournal data, otherwise silent data corruption poisons InternalMiss telemetry.

## Findings from uzdq code review (#3 + #4)

### #3. readWorkJournalEntry silently substitutes a random UUID
File: Playhead/Persistence/AnalysisStore/AnalysisStore.swift (~line 4779)

```
let generationUUID = UUID(uuidString: generationRaw) ?? UUID()
```

Store invariant: every row's generation_id was written as UUID.uuidString. A non-UUID is corruption — silently substituting a fresh random UUID hides the bug AND breaks the {episode_id, generation_id} identity used by orphan recovery.

Fix: throw AnalysisStoreError.queryFailed(\"Non-UUID generation_id: \\(generationRaw)\").

### #4. readWorkJournalEntry downgrades unknown cause raw values to .pipelineError
File: Playhead/Persistence/AnalysisStore/AnalysisStore.swift (~line 4774)

```
cause = InternalMissCause(rawValue: rawCause) ?? .pipelineError
```

Silently misattributes an unknown cause to a specific known cause. Poisons any InternalMiss telemetry that playhead-1nl6 builds on top. Future InternalMissCause enum additions will silently rewrite historical rows.

Fix options (pick one):
A. Throw on unknown raw values (treat as corruption).
B. Add `.unknown(String)` case to InternalMissCause for forward-compat with schema evolution.

Recommend B — matches the canonical \"breaking-change plan\" pattern and preserves legacy telemetry.

## Acceptance
- Unit: seed a work_journal row with `generation_id = 'not-a-uuid'`; readWorkJournalEntry throws.
- Unit: seed a work_journal row with `cause = 'futureCauseXYZ'`; readWorkJournalEntry either throws (option A) or returns `.unknown(\"futureCauseXYZ\")` (option B).
- Integration: round-trip every enumerated InternalMissCause case through write → read without data loss.

## Gating
Blocks playhead-1nl6 (Slice-completion instrumentation + InternalMissCause emission) from starting work on journal consumption.

title: 24cm follow-up: delegate cache dir + weak fingerprint hardening
description:
Gating follow-up for playhead-24cm. Must land BEFORE flipping `useDualBackgroundSessions = true` in any cohort.

## Findings from 24cm code review (I3 + I4)

### I3. EpisodeDownloadDelegate.didFinishDownloadingTo hardcodes defaultCacheDirectory()
File: Playhead/Services/Downloads/DownloadManager.swift (~line 1230)

```
let cacheDir = DownloadManager.defaultCacheDirectory()
    .appendingPathComponent("complete", isDirectory: true)
```

A DownloadManager instantiated with a custom cacheDirectory (as tests do via makeTempDir()) writes progressive downloads there, but any file arriving through the background-session delegate goes to the real user Caches dir. Footgun for tests and for future multi-profile support.

Fix: move file placement logic out of the delegate and into an actor method (handleBackgroundDownloadComplete). Delegate synchronously stages the file into a process-global temp dir (file is only valid on the delegate queue), then hands the staged URL to the actor, which uses completeFileURL(for:) that respects cacheDirectory.

### I4. Delegate emits empty "weak" fingerprint
File: Playhead/Services/Downloads/DownloadManager.swift (~line 1086)

```
if let strongHash = try? FileHasher.sha256(fileURL: fileURL) {
    fingerprintCache[episodeId] = AudioFingerprint(weak: "", strong: strongHash)
}
```

Invariant break: makeWeak never produces "". Downstream weak-fingerprint comparisons treat these as a distinct (empty) bucket. Also: `try?` silently swallows hash failures, leaving the file in complete/ unindexed.

Fix:
- Synthesize a weak fingerprint from originalRequest.url + HTTPURLResponse metadata harvested before file move.
- Log hash failures via logger.error rather than producing a partial fingerprint.

## Acceptance
- File placement honors DownloadManager.cacheDirectory in both the delegate path and the actor path. Test: inject custom cacheDirectory and verify background-delegate completions land there.
- No fingerprints with `weak: ""` can be inserted; assertion test covers this.
- Hash failures emit an error log AND either synthesize a weak-only fingerprint from request/response metadata OR skip the cache insertion entirely (decision: pick one).

## Gating
Blocks any change that sets `PreAnalysisConfig.useDualBackgroundSessions = true` as a default OR per-cohort flag flip.

title: Scoped music-bed generalization (recurring jingle detection per show)
description:
Detect recurring jingle patterns across episodes within a subscription; promote music-bed signal weight only on shows where pattern detection succeeded N times. Plan §6 Phase 3 deliverable 4.

1. Scope bound: intro/outro jingles + recurring music-bed cues within a subscription; duration ≤ 10 seconds per cue.
2. Pattern algorithm: chromaprint hash correlation within a show; pattern confirmed when ≥ 3 episodes of the same show have matching hashes (Hamming ≤ 8) at episode-start or episode-end.
3. Signal promotion rule: only for shows where a pattern has been confirmed, raise the music-bed feature weight in fusion from 0.10 baseline to 0.25 for spans overlapping a detected jingle.
4. Guardrails: confirmations stored in ShowMusicBedProfile table; profile versioned; evicted if 30 consecutive episodes show no match.
5. Acceptance: precision ≥ baseline on non-jingle-show corpus (no cross-show leakage); recall ≥ +8% on jingle-show corpus.
6. Rollback: feature flag scoped_music_bed_generalization; per-show disable via Diagnostics.

title: [epic] Phase 3: Optimization
description: Reduce cost without regressing quality. Plan §6 Phase 3.

title: B3: local RepeatedAdCache (repeated-ad tile memoization)
description:
Cache short audio fingerprints for high-confidence ad spans. On match in new episodes, reuse prior transcript/classification/boundary data. Local-only — no shared cloud intelligence. Plan §6 Phase 3 deliverable 1.

1. Fingerprinting: 128-bit chromaprint-style audio hash over the detected ad span; stored per-show in a local RepeatedAdCache table keyed by (showId, adFingerprint) with (boundaryStart, boundaryEnd, confidence, lastSeenAt).
2. Match policy: Hamming distance ≤ 6 bits AND same show AND confidence ≥ 0.85 at original detection; cache hit skips ASR+classifier for that span.
3. Eviction: LRU with per-show cap of 200 entries, global cap 2000; entries older than 90 days purged.
4. Success SLI: repeated_ad_cache_hit_rate ≥ 30% on B3-target shows (recurring-sponsor podcasts) by end of 30-day field window; disable cache automatically if hit rate < 5% after 14 days.
5. Acceptance: contributes ≥ 10% of the Phase 3 30% compute-reduction goal.
6. Rollback: feature flag b3_repeated_ad_cache_enabled + Diagnostics switch; disabling clears the cache.

title: B1 adaptive learning loop (replace config table)
description:
Replace the Phase 1 per-device-class config table with an on-device adaptive estimator that adjusts slice sizes per actual grant-window history. Plan §6 Phase 3 deliverable 5.

1. Scope: this bead is the Phase 3 adaptive loop that extends the Phase 1 static table (playhead-dh9b). Phase 1 ships the static seed; Phase 3 replaces it with on-device learning.
2. Algorithm: Welford's-style online estimator of grantWindowSeconds per device class, with EWMA smoothing (α=0.2 per observation, min 30 samples before departing from seed values); slice size recomputed as sliceSize = nominalSlice × (estimatedGrantWindow / seedGrantWindow), clamped to [0.5×, 2.0×] of seed.
3. Safety rails (mirror B5 playhead-hqhh): activation floor of 30 samples; max one-notch change per 24h; never zero out.
4. Persistence: estimator state in a new LearnedDeviceProfile table with version stamps; readable by Diagnostics (playhead-ghon).
5. Acceptance: P90 slice completion ≥ seed baseline across locked-core fixtures (playhead-ym57) after 14-day learning window.
6. Rollback: feature flag; fallback to seed table (playhead-dh9b) if estimator diverges.

title: Per-show capability profiles (deferred from Phase 2)
description:
Observed (not user-set) internal classification: chapter-rich, host-read-only, music-bed-reliable, etc. Used by scheduler to modulate budget ONLY after baseline SLIs are stable. Exposed only in Settings → Diagnostics. Always-on minimum per-episode budget — profile can never zero out work. Deferred from Phase 2 to avoid cold-start bias. Plan §6 Phase 3 deliverable 7.

1. Deferral rationale (inline): originally scoped for Phase 2 but moved to Phase 3 because observed profiles would suffer cold-start bias before Phase 1 baseline SLIs (playhead-d99) stabilize and before Phase 2 coverage derivation (playhead-cthe) produces reliable per-show signals. Without these, early profiles would systematically mislabel shows as "not worth analyzing."
2. Activation floor: profile observed only after show has ≥ 5 analysis-completed episodes AND Phase 2 SLIs are within defended bounds per playhead-d99 for that cohort.
3. Profile types (observed, not user-set):
   - chapter-rich (≥ 80% of episodes have publisher chapters matched to detected ads)
   - host-read-only (ads detected as host-voiced in ≥ 70% of episodes)
   - music-bed-reliable (playhead-2hpn jingle pattern confirmed)
   - sponsor-declared (RSS/show-notes pre-seed produces positives in ≥ 50% of episodes)
   - dynamic-insertion-heavy (ad boundaries shift episode-to-episode)
4. Profile use: modulates per-show analysis budget within safety rails (always-on minimum budget preserved — never zero out); different profiles bias different detectors in the fusion ensemble.
5. Acceptance: profile-guided analysis reduces average-compute per show by ≥ 15% on profile-matched shows vs baseline, with zero regression in false_ready_rate cohort thresholds.
6. Rollback: feature flag; profiles pinned to unknown disables the bead's modulation.

title: B5 bounded local controller (observe_only boot + hierarchical backoff + activation floor + version handoff)
description:
Boot in observe_only mode using Phase 1 config table as shipped defaults. EWMA/Beta estimators with hierarchical backoff: base cohort = device class × work type × execution condition; show profile only above minimum observation floor. Activation floor: no actuator changes until N slices, M episodes per cohort. Version handoff: OS/model/policy-version change decays or resets learned state; fall back to boot policy. Beta priors seeded from internal fixture-lab results. Safety rails: min per-episode budget, max one-notch-per-actuator-per-24h, never zero out an episode. Fully local; any uploaded telemetry aggregate-only + optional. Plan §6 Phase 3 deliverable 6.

1. Output API: controller writes decisions to a new BoundedControllerDecisions persistence table with version stamps: {timestamp, actuatorId, previousValue, newValue, justification}. Scheduler reads latest decision via BoundedControllerReader.currentActuatorValue(actuatorId) — pull model, not push.
2. Persistence & diagnostics: all actuator decisions surfaced in Diagnostics (playhead-l274); version-stamped per Phase 0 playhead-7mq schema.
3. Staging strategy for testing: controller ships observe_only=true by default; dogfood feature flag b5_active_actuators=true permits live actuation on internal devices only. Staged rollout after 14-day observe window passes review.
4. Actuators (initial set): slice-size, lane concurrency limits, quality-profile threshold, media-cap, analysis-cap. Each has declared min/max and one-notch-per-24h constraint.
5. Rollback: manual reset affordance in Diagnostics ("Reset to boot policy"); resets all actuators to seed values and disables active mode. Automatic reset if any SLI (playhead-d99) regresses beyond defended threshold for 24h.
6. Acceptance: observe-only decisions on dogfood fleet match human intuition for ≥ 95% of proposed changes (reviewer signoff) before active mode is enabled.
close_reason: User decision 2026-04-21: skip B5 SLO + closed-loop controller. Static heuristics deemed good enough for MVP; premature to build an adaptive controller before we know which scheduling knobs actually matter in dogfood. Parked; can be reopened post-launch if telemetry surfaces a real miss-cause distribution that heuristics can't address.

title: Lightweight inventory sanity check
description:
Catches obviously-bad skips: spans <2s, spans in first/last 3s of episode, spans overlapping declared content chapters. Post-hoc safety — not a readiness driver. Plan §6 Phase 3 deliverable 3.

## Acceptance

- Post-hoc filter rejects **≥ 98%** of synthetically invalid spans, measured against a test corpus of known-bad spans covering:
  - spans <2s in duration,
  - spans in the first/last 3s of the episode (edge 3s),
  - spans overlapping declared content chapters.
- **No regression in `false_ready_rate`** per playhead-d99 (measured against playhead-ym57 locked-core fixtures).

## Rollback

Feature flag `lightweight_inventory_checks_enabled` + Diagnostics (playhead-l274) toggle.

When disabled, the filter passes all spans through unchanged (no-op), restoring pre-Phase-3 behavior.

title: B4: fast local revalidation from persisted features
description:
On model/policy version bump, run 'revalidate from features' path that skips ASR and re-runs only classifier + fusion + boundary stages from persisted TranscriptChunk + FeatureWindow rows. Build on shipped Phase 4 shadow-retry. Plan §6 Phase 3 deliverable 2.

## Acceptance

On model/policy/feature-schema version bump:

- **≥ 85%** of episodes revalidate-from-features in **≤ 50%** of original full-pipeline runtime.
- `false_ready_rate` **does not regress** (per playhead-d99 thresholds).
- Measured against the **playhead-ym57 8-locked-core fixtures** + the **Phase 4 `Phase3ShadowReplayHarnessTests` replay**.

## Rollback

Feature flag `b4_revalidation_from_features_enabled` + Diagnostics toggle.

When disabled, the revalidation path falls back to **full re-analysis** (pre-Phase-3 behavior); no persisted features are consulted on version bump.

## Test corpus

- playhead-ym57 8-locked-core fixtures (golden-artifact comparisons).
- Phase 4 `Phase3ShadowReplayHarnessTests` replay (shadow-retry corpus).

title: Gray-band markOnly UX
description:
⚠️ REQUIRES PRODUCT APPROVAL before implementation.

For spans in 0.60-0.80 confidence range:
- Show lightweight 'likely sponsor segment' marker (not auto-skip)
- One-tap actions: skip this segment, always skip third-party paid, don't skip house promos

Thresholds: candidate 0.40, markOnly 0.60, confirm 0.70, auto-skip 0.80.

This is a significant product decision affecting user experience.
Threshold values and UI treatment need explicit sign-off.

title: Broader learned correction scopes (Layer B)
description:
Rule promotion from repeated corrections:
- phraseOnShow: 3 corrections, 2 distinct episodes, 2 distinct dates
- sponsorOnShow: 2 corrections, 2 distinct episodes
- domainOwnershipOnShow: 2 corrections, 2 distinct episodes
- jingleOnShow: 3 corrections, 2 distinct episodes

Diversity requirement: corrections must span multiple episodes AND dates.
Combine explicit corrections and implicit feedback (weak labels at 0.3× weight).

Decay: phraseOnShow 120d, sponsorOnShow 180d, domainOwnership 360d, jingleOnShow 90d.
Permanent exactSpan vetoes never decay (preserved from Layer A).

title: Skip-policy override integration
description:
First-class distinction in core decisioning:
- classificationOverride: 'this is/isn't an ad' (affects Stage 2 classification)
- skipPolicyOverride: 'don't skip this type' (affects Stage 4 policy only)

'That was a house promo' ≠ 'never skip house promos.'

Skip-policy overrides live in SkipPolicyMatrix, affect eligibility gating
without changing confidence score.

Enables future configurable behavior: skip third-party only, show house promos as markers.

title: Phase E: Broader Learned Corrections + Skip Policy
description:
Requires sufficient correction volume and implicit feedback from Phases B-D.

Contents:
- Broader learned correction scopes (phraseOnShow, sponsorOnShow, domainOwnership, jingleOnShow)
- Rule promotion with support + diversity requirements
- Skip-policy override (classification vs policy distinction)
- Gray-band markOnly UX (requires product approval)
- Decay and expiration semantics

title: Composite fingerprint upgrade
description:
Extend AdCopyFingerprintMatcher to composite signatures:
1. Transcript minhash / character n-gram similarity (ASR-robust)
2. Lightweight acoustic signature (music bed contour, prosodic rhythm, spectral sketch)
3. Sponsor-marker alignment (URL, promo code, disclosure positions)

Text similarity gated by TranscriptReliability.

Same-show matching: composite score >= threshold + anchor alignment + ownership validation.
Cross-show matching (future, not this bead): same-network or high-composite + commercial markers.

Acoustic fingerprinting is substantial engineering — validate same-show first.
close_reason: Composite fingerprints landed — transcript+acoustic+marker signatures, 28 tests

title: EVI budget scheduler + BudgetCoordinator
description:
Replace fixed FM tier allocation with expected-value-of-information scoring:
  EVI = P(decision flip) × utility gain / compute cost

BudgetCoordinator manages FM, DSP, and thermal/battery budgets.
Near-playhead windows always serviced first.
Shared feature caches across CoveragePlanner, FineBoundaryRefiner, FingerprintMatcher.

Priority reasons: nearConfirmationThreshold, coldStartShow, metadataSeededUnanchored,
boundaryUncertain, pharmaFallback, recentCorrection, lowTranscriptReliability.

Ship tier-based allocation + energy gating first. Upgrade to full EVI once
counterfactual evaluator provides P(decision flip) estimates.
close_reason: EVI scorer + BudgetCoordinator landed — 3-pool budget mgmt, 36 tests

title: Network identity + network priors
description:
Derive network identity from RSS metadata:
- <itunes:author>, <managingEditor>, feed URL domain patterns, publisher field
- NetworkIdentity with networkId, derivedFrom, confidence

Aggregate network priors across same-network shows:
- commonSponsors, typicalSlotPositions, typicalAdDuration
- musicBracketPrevalence, metadataTrustAverage
- Confidence-weighted aggregation with outlier trimming (not raw averages)

Feed into classifier priorScore when show-level priors < 3 episodes.
Weight: 0.5× show-level trust, decaying as show data accumulates.
close_reason: Network identity + priors landed — extraction, aggregation, decay, 39 tests

title: Prior hierarchy integration
description:
Implement hierarchy: global defaults → network priors → trait-derived → show-local.

Each level overrides above when sufficient data. Show-local wins at >= 5 episodes.

Guardrail: hierarchical priors mostly affect ranking/prioritization and classifier
priorScore, not direct auto-skip authority or evidence fusion weights.
close_reason: 4-level prior hierarchy landed — global/network/trait/show-local cascade, 30 tests

title: ShowTraitProfile: continuous show characterization
description:
Replace hard archetypes with continuous trait vector:
- musicDensity, speakerTurnRate, singleSpeakerDominance
- structureRegularity, sponsorRecurrence, insertionVolatility, transcriptReliability

Computed after 2-3 episodes, updated incrementally. Stored on PodcastProfile.
Optional debug archetype label for logging/QA.

Priors, trust defaults, and scheduler consume trait vector directly:
- musicDensity + structureRegularity → musicBracketTrust default
- singleSpeakerDominance + low musicDensity → FM gets more budget
- structureRegularity → metadata trust expectations
- insertionVolatility → fingerprint transfer confidence

title: Phase D: Priors + Scheduling + Fingerprints
description:
Consumes data accumulated in Phases A-C. Ranking/scheduling changes,
not direct skip changes.

Contents:
- ShowTraitProfile (continuous, not hard archetypes)
- Network identity extraction + network priors
- Prior hierarchy (global → network → traits → show-local)
- EVI budget scheduler with BudgetCoordinator (energy-aware)
- Composite fingerprint upgrade (text + acoustic + sponsor markers)

title: Implicit feedback signals (weak labels)
description:
Collect behavioral signals as weak labels:
- immediateUnskip (within 3s) → likely FP
- seekBackIntoSkipped → boundary error or FP
- rapidRewindAfterSkip (within 5s) → boundary error
- repeatedManualSkipForward → likely FN
- showAutoSkipDisabled → broad distrust (flag for diagnostic)

Weak labels:
- Never create permanent vetoes alone
- Contribute to support/diversity counts at 0.3× explicit correction weight
- Influence source trust updates
- Priority reason for FM audit

Begin collecting immediately. Use in Layer B rule promotion (Phase E).

title: Refactor transcript framework boundaries into explicit adapters
description: The transcript pipeline currently crosses AVFoundation and Speech framework boundaries inside AppleSpeechRecognizer. That makes format negotiation, temp-file bridging, SpeechAnalyzer session setup, and Apple result mapping harder to reason about and regression-test. Plan and execute a refactor that treats each framework boundary like a protocol: narrow contract, normalized inputs/outputs, typed domain errors, and contract tests around the real framework edges.
notes: Phase 1 landed: extracted AppleSpeechAssetBootstrapper, AppleSpeechAudioBridge, AppleSpeechAnalyzerRunner, and AppleSpeechResultMapper from AppleSpeechRecognizer. TranscriptEngineService and SpeechService APIs remain unchanged. Contract coverage now targets the extracted audio bridge and result mapper directly. Verified with xcodebuild build-for-testing for generic iOS.

title: A7: Metrics Split + Live Skip-Usefulness Metrics
description:
## Background
Binary hit/miss tracking cannot distinguish 'found the ad but only covered the last 15%' from 'missed it entirely,' nor measure whether the system knows early enough to skip. Design doc section A7 specifies span-quality and live-usefulness metrics to fill this gap.

## What to build

### Offline span quality metrics
- Seed recall: % of ground-truth ads where at least one anchor fired
- Span IoU: intersection-over-union between detected and ground-truth spans
- Median start error (seconds)
- Median end error (seconds)
- Signed start bias: median(detectedStart - gtStart); positive = systematically late
- Signed end bias: median(detectedEnd - gtEnd); negative = systematically early exits
- Coverage recall: % of ground-truth ad seconds covered by detected span
- Coverage precision: % of detected ad seconds inside ground-truth

### Live skip-usefulness metrics
- Lead time at first confirmation: seconds between first skip-eligible confirmation and GT ad start

### Slicing dimensions
All metrics sliced by: ad format (host-read, produced, dynamic), podcast, live path vs backfill path.

## Acceptance criteria
- All 9 metrics above computable from test harness output
- Slicing by ad format, podcast, and path implemented
- Integration with existing PlayheadIntegrationTests corpus verification
- Baseline values captured for current Phase A implementation
- Metric computation does not regress fast test runtime (offline only)

title: A6: Preserve repetition density in EvidenceCatalogBuilder
description:
## Background
EvidenceCatalogBuilder currently deduplicates by (normalizedText, category) and keeps only the first occurrence. Later duplicates are discarded entirely — count is lost. But repetition density is strongly ad-like (a brand mentioned 4 times across 60 seconds is very different from mentioned once). This signal is currently thrown away.

## What to build

### 1. Add `count` field to EvidenceEntry
EvidenceEntry (EvidenceCatalogBuilder.swift:26) already has `startTime` and `endTime` fields. Add:
- `count: Int` — how many times this (normalizedText, category) pair appeared

### 2. Widen startTime/endTime semantics during dedup
The `deduplicate(_:)` method (EvidenceCatalogBuilder.swift:497) currently keeps only the first RawMatch per key. Modify it to:
- Accumulate `count` across all matches sharing the same dedup key
- Set `startTime` to `min(all matching startTimes)`
- Set `endTime` to `max(all matching endTimes)`

This preserves the existing field names and avoids adding redundant firstTime/lastTime.

### 3. Surface repetition in FM prompt
Two render methods exist:
- `EvidenceCatalog.renderForPrompt()` (EvidenceCatalogBuilder.swift:57) — debug/test path
- `PromptEvidenceEntry.renderForPrompt(redactor:)` (FoundationModelClassifier.swift:423) — **production FM prompt path**, called at line 2272

Both should include repetition info when `count > 1`. The production path format becomes:
`[E3] "BetterHelp" (brandSpan, line 4, ×4, 12s–67s)`

The debug path format becomes:
`[E3] "BetterHelp" (brandSpan, atom 2, ×4, 12s–67s)`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] EvidenceEntry has `count: Int` field (default 1)
- [ ] `deduplicate(_:)` accumulates count and widens startTime/endTime across all matches
- [ ] `PromptEvidenceEntry.renderForPrompt(redactor:)` in FoundationModelClassifier.swift includes repetition info when count > 1
- [ ] `EvidenceCatalog.renderForPrompt()` includes repetition info when count > 1
- [ ] Unit tests for dedup with repeated evidence verifying count, startTime, endTime
- [ ] Test that existing single-occurrence evidence has count=1 and unchanged startTime/endTime
- [ ] Existing tests in CueHarvesterTests and Cycle2FixesTests still pass

title: A7: Span quality metrics + live lead-time metrics
description:
## Background
Current metrics are binary hit/miss. This can't distinguish 'we found the ad but only covered the last 15%' from 'we missed it entirely.' The expert also flagged that offline IoU can improve without improving the live skip experience if lead time isn't measured.

## What to build

### Offline span quality metrics
- Seed recall: % of ground-truth ads where at least one anchor fired
- Span IoU: per-segment intersection-over-union between detected and ground-truth spans (the existing harness computes sample-level precision/recall at 0.1s resolution but NOT per-segment IoU)
- Median start error: seconds between detected start and GT start (note: existing BoundaryQualityMetrics uses abs() — preserve absolute error AND add signed variant)
- Median end error: seconds between detected end and GT end (same abs() note)
- Signed start bias: median(detectedStart - gtStart); positive = systematically late starts. Requires new signed fields in BoundaryQualityMetrics since current implementation takes abs() at SimulatedPlaybackDriver.swift:269
- Signed end bias: median(detectedEnd - gtEnd); negative = systematically early exits. Same abs() issue.
- Coverage recall: % of GT ad seconds covered by detected span (per-segment, not just aggregate sample-level)
- Coverage precision: % of detected ad seconds that lie inside GT (per-segment)

### Live skip usefulness metrics
- Lead time at first confirmation: seconds between first skip-eligible confirmation and GT ad start. Note: existing LatencyMetrics.timeToFirstUsableSkip measures first skip time, NOT first confirmation relative to GT ad start — this is a different metric.

### Slicing
All metrics sliced by:
- Ad format (host-read, produced / pre-roll, dynamic if applicable). IMPORTANT: GroundTruthAdSegment.AdSegmentType currently does NOT carry DeliveryStyle — CorpusLoader.mapAdType() maps only AdType (pre/mid/post) and drops DeliveryStyle. Must add deliveryStyle to GroundTruthAdSegment and pipe it through from TestAdSegment.
- Podcast (already supported — corpus annotations carry podcastId)
- Live path vs backfill path. IMPORTANT: SimulationCondition has audioMode (streamed/cached) but no live-vs-backfill concept. TranscriptChunk.pass carries "fast" in production but the replay simulator doesn't model this. Must add analysisPath to SimulationCondition or ReplayConfiguration.

## Existing infrastructure (verified 2026-04-12)

### Evaluation harness: PlayheadTests/Services/ReplaySimulator/
- SimulatedPlaybackDriver.swift — drives simulated playback, computes DetectionQuality, BoundaryQuality, Latency, UserOverride metrics
- ReplayMetrics.swift — metric types (DetectionQualityMetrics, BoundaryQualityMetrics, LatencyMetrics, UserOverrideMetrics), EpisodeReplayReport, CorpusReplayReport with aggregate()
- ReplaySimulatorTests.swift — tests for the harness itself

### Ground-truth corpus: PlayheadTests/Fixtures/Corpus/
- CorpusAnnotationTypes.swift — TestEpisodeAnnotation, TestAdSegment with startTime/endTime/AdType/DeliveryStyle/Difficulty, CorpusManifest
- EmbeddedCorpusAnnotations.swift — 15 episodes, 30+ labeled ad segments with precise timestamps. Covers: dynamicInsertion, hostRead, blendedHostRead, producedSegment. Includes no-ad episode for FP testing.
- CorpusLoader.swift — loads, validates, converts to ReplayConfiguration

### What already works

title: B10: Fingerprint full-span recovery via anchor-aware local alignment
description:
## Background
AdCopyFingerprintStore stores only MinHash signature + normalized text. No span boundaries. Matches identify ~30-atom CTA fragments, not full ads. Expert recommendation: store span offsets AND anchor landmarks, then use anchor-aware alignment for robust transfer.

## What to build

### New fields on FingerprintEntry
- spanStartOffset: Double — seconds from match start to full ad start
- spanEndOffset: Double — seconds from match end to full ad end
- spanDurationSeconds: Double — total ad duration when created
- canonicalSponsorEntity: NormalizedSponsor? — for entity-aware matching
- anchorLandmarks: [AnchorLandmark] — typed anchor positions within the ad

### AnchorLandmark struct
- type: AnchorType (disclosure, url, promoCode, etc.)
- offsetSeconds: Double (from match start)
- normalizedText: String? (e.g., 'betterhelp dot com')

### Anchor-aware transfer logic
- Strong match (Jaccard ≥ 0.8): transfer full boundaries ONLY after anchor-landmark alignment + TimeBoundaryResolver validation
- Normal match (0.6–0.8): seed a hypothesis using matched fragment + landmark priors for SpanHypothesisEngine verification

### User-marked ad fingerprint seeding
When user marks an ad and BoundaryExpander produces span with confidence ≥ 0.7, seed fingerprint at candidate state. Normal trust lifecycle applies (candidate → quarantined → active).

## Acceptance criteria
- FingerprintEntry has span offsets, sponsor entity, anchor landmarks
- Strong matches transfer with landmark validation
- Normal matches seed hypotheses
- User-marked ads can create fingerprint candidates
- Landmark alignment handles host ad-lib variation
- Unit tests for offset transfer
- Tests for anchor-landmark alignment
- Tests for user-marked fingerprint seeding lifecycle

title: Widen Use A boundary snap radius from ±3 to ±15 atoms
description:
MinimalContiguousSpanDecoder Use A boundary snap currently reaches ±3 atoms (~6s). Ads are missing 20-30s of lead-in because anchors land on CTAs/promo codes at the end. Widen to ±15 atoms (~30s) so span start boundaries can snap backward to acoustic breaks (music stingers, tone shifts, pauses) that commonly mark ad transitions.

The snap logic already prefers the earliest break on the left edge, so widening the radius lets it find the natural ad entry point. Combined with FM in full mode anchoring atoms in the lead-in, this should capture full ad spans.

title: Graduate FM from shadow to full mode

Minimum change set:
1. AdDetectionService.swift line 72: AdDetectionConfig.default — change .shadow to .full
2. AdDetectionService.swift line 50: AdDetectionConfig.init default parameter — change .shadow to .full (consistency)
3. BackfillJobRunner.swift line 199: init default parameter — change .shadow to .full (consistency)

title: Add lifecycle tests for PlayheadRuntime shadow retry observer teardown
description: The shadow retry observer lifecycle fix adds shutdown() and a deinit fallback, but there is still no dedicated test proving shutdown prevents observer startup/re-arming or that the best-effort deinit path stops the observer cleanly. Add focused tests around runtime teardown and startup/teardown races.
acceptance_criteria: There are tests covering explicit shutdown, teardown-vs-startup race behavior, and the observer does not remain armed after runtime teardown.
close_reason: Merged to main. Three lifecycle tests for PlayheadRuntime shadow retry observer teardown now live at PlayheadTests/Services/AdDetection/RuntimeShutdownLifecycleTests.swift: (1) shutdown() idempotency after full startup, (2) startup-vs-teardown race where shutdown() before observer.start() leaves the observer unarmed via the isShutdown guard, (3) cycle avoidance under deinit-only teardown. Scenario 3 was REWRITTEN from the bead's original 'deinit releases the observer' framing after investigation: the observer loop holds strong self across runObserverLoop until an explicit .shutdown wake arrives, and a non-async deinit cannot deliver that — the observer legitimately leaks its loop when shutdown() is skipped (documented best-effort contract, not a bug). Additionally, the PlayheadRuntime migrate chain holds the only strong reference to the runtime and awaits its way through startShadowRetryObserverIfNeeded before completing, which means by the time deinit CAN fire, the observer loop has already started — so the documented 'deinit cancels the startup task' safety net is dead code in practice. The one meaningful invariant scenario 3 now pins is cycle avoidance: nothing owned by the observer (capability publisher closures, drainer protocols, the loop task) may transitively retain the runtime. Test file includes a 'DO NOT RELAX THIS ASSERTION' guardrail comment so a future failure is not dismissed as 'test is wrong' — with a suspect list for debugging real regressions. Verified: 953 tests pass in 73.9s on main (32b8a8f).

title: Rename AnalysisCoordinator.start() → startCapabilityObserver() and call once at launch
description:
Follow-up from commit 740f727 review.

AnalysisCoordinator.start() (line 194) is misnamed: it is purely a capability-observer setup that cancels any existing observer task and spawns a new one. It does not "start the coordinator" in any semantic sense. Today it is called from:

  1. BackgroundProcessingService.playbackDidStart() (line 329) — every time audio starts
  2. BackgroundProcessingService.handleCapabilityUpdate() (line 550) — when resuming from an all-paused state

PlayheadRuntime calls backgroundProcessingService.start() (line 568), which is a different method on BackgroundProcessingService — NOT coordinator.start(). There are only 2 call sites for coordinator.start().

The AnalysisCoordinating protocol (BackgroundProcessingService.swift line 54-61) also declares func start() and must be renamed in tandem.

Calls 1 and 2 re-spawn the capability observer task each time, cancelling the previous one. This is wasteful but not broken because the observer body is idempotent.

Desired end state:
  - Rename AnalysisCoordinator.start() → startCapabilityObserver() to make intent clear
  - Update the AnalysisCoordinating protocol declaration accordingly
  - Call it exactly once (either from BackgroundProcessingService.start() at launch, or from playbackDidStart on first playback)
  - Remove the redundant call from handleCapabilityUpdate() resume path
  - Audit the resume-from-pause path: if AnalysisCoordinator.stop() cancels the observer too (it does — stop() at line 211 cancels capabilityObserverTask at line 214), then handleCapabilityUpdate DOES need to re-start the observer after resuming. Think through whether stop() should leave the observer alive.

Risk: medium — "rename + move" touches multiple call sites and the protocol, and requires reasoning about the stop()/start() observer lifecycle coupling. Not blocking Phase 3.

Files:
  - Playhead/Services/AnalysisCoordinator/AnalysisCoordinator.swift (start at line 194, stop at line 211)
  - Playhead/Services/AnalysisCoordinator/BackgroundProcessingService.swift (protocol at line 54, call sites at lines 329 and 550)
  - Playhead/App/PlayheadRuntime.swift (calls backgroundProcessingService.start() at line 568 — not coordinator.start())
  - PlayheadTests/Services/PreAnalysis/BackgroundProcessingServiceTests.swift

title: Expected false positive: first-party domain mentions (documented, no Phase 3 fix)
description:
Document a known false-positive class that Phase 3 will surface but
MUST NOT attempt to fix. This bead exists so that future developers
(or future Claude) don't waste time trying to prompt-engineer a fix
that belongs in a later phase.

## The case

On the Conan "Fanhausen Revisited" test episode, at 3:17-3:26, the
host says:

  "Conan O'Brien needs a fan. Want to talk to Conan? Visit
   teamcoco.com slash call Conan."

This is show structure — it's the call-in instructions for a
call-in-based podcast. It is NOT a sponsor ad. teamcoco.com is
Conan O'Brien's own first-party domain.

The 2026-04-06 FM PoC classified this segment as commercial at
confidence 1.00. FM's reasoning: "The segment includes a URL
followed by a call to action, which is a strong indicator of
commercial intent." The prompt already included guidance that "show
call-in instructions are editorial" — FM ignored that in favor of
the URL + CTA pattern.

## Why this is expected

The fundamental problem is that teamcoco.com is semantically
indistinguishable from a sponsor URL unless you already know it's
the host's own domain. There is no linguistic signal in the 10-
second window that disambiguates it.

This also reproduces on LexicalScanner and EvidenceCatalogBuilder —
all three detection layers flag it.

## Why Phase 3 must not try to fix it

- Prompt engineering won't fix it reliably. The same URL + CTA
  pattern is exactly what real sponsor ads use.
- Adding teamcoco.com to a hardcoded blocklist is a one-off hack
  that won't generalize.
- The real solution is Phase 8: SponsorKnowledgeStore with
  first-party domain tracking and a quarantine lifecycle
  (candidate → quarantined → active → decayed → blocked).
  Phase 8 builds a per-show knowledge graph of first-party vs
  sponsor entities and treats first-party mentions differently.
- Even simpler first-party heuristics (domain matches podcast
  title/author) belong in Phase 8's scope, not Phase 3.

## What Phase 3 SHOULD do about it

- Record first-party-looking hits in shadow mode without filtering
  them out — we need the data to train/evaluate Phase 8's logic.
- Do NOT add a blocklist or exception carve-out in
  FoundationModelClassifier or its prompts.
- Do NOT add a "first-party" category to the CoarseScanResult
  schema — keep the three-value commercial/editorial/mixed enum.
- The SemanticScanResult table should capture the full evidence
  reference so Phase 8 can later analyze which first-party mentions
  got flagged.

## Regression test

PlayheadTests/IntegrationTests/FoundationModelClassifierTests.swift
has a segment labeled "teamcoco.com call-in (3:17-3:26) - false-
positive test" that explicitly checks this case. Expected: it
SHOULD still be classified commercial in shadow mode until Phase 8
lands. Do not "fix" the test by changing the expected label.

## Phase 8 cross-reference

When Phase 8 SponsorKnowledgeStore + CompiledSponsorLexicon land,
the teamcoco test should flip to correctly classify as editorial.
That's the signal that first-party tracking is working. Until then,
this is a known, expected, documented miss.

## Related beads

- playhead-4my.8 (Phase 8 — SponsorKnowledgeStore): where the real
  fix lives
- playhead-4my.3.2 (coarse scanner): where the scanner code is
- playhead-4my.3.7 (Phase 3 tests): regression test reference
notes: Verified this bead is already satisfied in-repo: docs/benchmarks/fanhausen-revisited.md documents the teamcoco false positive, Conan fixture metadata calls out the Phase 8 fix path, and FoundationModelClassifierTests explicitly preserves the known-false-positive expectation until Phase 8.

title: [epic] Phase 12: Shared Sponsor Lexicon (Central)
description:
Opt-in shared sponsor lexicon — an ad-block filter list for podcast ads. Users contribute confirmed sponsor entities; a central service deduplicates and publishes a versioned lexicon that all users download.

## What gets shared (not copyrighted)
- Canonical sponsor names + aliases
- Vanity URLs (e.g. squarespace.com/podcastname)
- CTA patterns (e.g. "use code X for Y% off")
- Disclosure phrases (e.g. "brought to you by", "sponsored by")

## What NEVER leaves the device
- Transcripts, audio, raw evidence snippets, training examples
- Per-user listening history or podcast subscriptions
- Any quoted transcript text

## How it works
1. Device contributes: only active lifecycle entities (2+ episode confirmations, low rollback, no correction conflicts) from SponsorKnowledgeStore
2. Contribution payload: canonical entity + type + category. No transcript snippets, no episode IDs, no timestamps.
3. Central service: lightweight dedup + versioning. Publishes a signed JSON lexicon on CDN. No server logic beyond merge + publish.
4. Device consumes: CompiledSponsorLexicon (Phase 8) merges local + shared lexicon. Shared entries enter as quarantined locally — still require one local confirmation before reaching active on the hot path. User corrections override shared entries.
5. Opt-in: contribution is opt-in. Consumption is default-on (like an ad-block list).

## Privacy guarantees
- No differential privacy needed — entities are public facts ("Squarespace advertises on podcasts")
- No user attribution in contributions (anonymous upload)
- Signed lexicon prevents tampering
- Local corrections always override shared entries

## Value
- New users get day-one detection quality without FM discovering anything
- Long-tail shows benefit from entities discovered on popular shows
- Zero marginal cost (JSON on CDN)

Verification: Shared lexicon downloaded and merged into CompiledSponsorLexicon. Shared entries require local confirmation before hot-path. User corrections override shared entries. Contribution only sends active entities without transcript context.

title: Full Transcript View
description:
# Full Transcript View

## Goal
Expand the existing transcript peek into a full-screen scrollable transcript with synced playback, ad highlighting, and in-episode search.

## Rationale
Transcript Peek (playhead-kcz) provides a small bottom sheet preview. The full view makes transcripts a first-class feature: readers can follow along, visually see where ads were, tap to seek, and search within the episode. This was planned for v0.2 but its value is high enough to prioritize alongside MVP — it's the most natural extension of existing work.

## Implementation

### Full Transcript View
- New file: `Playhead/Views/Transcript/FullTranscriptView.swift`
- Full-screen view (push navigation from Now Playing or transcript peek "Expand" button)
- Scrollable transcript in editorial serif (Newsreader). TranscriptChunks are segment-level (typically a sentence or phrase each); group consecutive non-ad chunks into display paragraphs by inserting breaks at pauses > 2s (gap between chunk N endTime and chunk N+1 startTime) or ad boundaries (chunk falls within an AdWindow time range).

#### Scroll State Machine
```swift
enum TranscriptScrollState {
    case autoScrolling            // transcript follows playback
    case userScrolling            // user dragging — auto-scroll paused
    case userScrolled             // user released — "Jump to now" visible
}
```
- `autoScrolling`: ScrollViewReader scrolls to current paragraph on each PlaybackService time update (throttled to 1 update/sec to avoid jank)
- `userScrolling`: entered when `DragGesture` detected on scroll view (or `UIScrollViewDelegate.scrollViewWillBeginDragging` via UIViewRepresentable if SwiftUI gesture detection is insufficient). Auto-scroll stops.
- `userScrolled`: entered when drag ends. "Jump to now" floating button appears (bottom-center, Copper tint, `.capsule` shape, 8pt padding). Tap transitions back to `.autoScrolling`.
- Auto-scroll re-engages automatically if user manually scrolls to within 100pt of the current paragraph (proximity-based re-engagement).

#### Rendering
- Render using `LazyVStack(spacing: 12)` inside `ScrollViewReader` for memory efficiency — episodes can have 1000+ chunks
- Current paragraph: Copper left border (4pt width, `.leading` edge) via `.overlay(alignment: .leading)`
- Ad regions: transcript text within AdWindow time ranges shown in Steel color (`.secondary`) with inline "Ad" pill badge (Copper background, white text, `.caption2`, corner radius 4pt)
- Tap any paragraph: calls `PlaybackService.seek(to: chunk.startTime)` for that paragraph's first TranscriptChunk

#### Paragraph Grouping
```swift
struct TranscriptParagraph: Identifiable {
    let id: String                      // first chunk's segmentFingerprint
    let chunks: [TranscriptChunk]       // consecutive chunks in this paragraph
    let startTime: TimeInterval         // first chunk startTime
    let endTime: TimeInterval           // last chunk endTime
    let isAd: Bool                      // true if any chunk overlaps an AdWindow
    let text: String                    // concatenated chunk texts with space joins
}
```
- Group by iterating chunks sorted by startTime. Break into new paragraph when:
  - Gap between consecutive chunks > 2.0s
  - Current chunk's time range overlaps an AdWindow but previous chunk's does not (or vice versa)

### In-Episode Search
- Search bar at top of full transcript view (`.searchable` modifier or custom search bar)
- Highlights all matches in Copper within the transcript text (using `AttributedString` with `.backgroundColor` attribute set to Copper at 30% opacity)
- Up/down arrows (chevron SF Symbols) to jump between matches (ScrollViewReader scrolls to match)
- Shows match count: "3 of 7" in IBM Plex Mono, `.caption`
- Search is local string matching against `TranscriptParagraph.text` (not FTS5 — this is in-episode, not cross-episode)
- Case-insensitive matching via `text.range(of: query, options: .caseInsensitive)`

### Speaker Segments (stretch — deferred if complex)
- WhisperKit does not provide speaker diarization. Heuristic approach: detect speaker changes via pauses > 3s combined with significant acoustic shift in consecutive chunks (if energy/pitch metadata is available from FeatureExtractionService).
- Label as "Speaker 1", "Speaker 2" with divider lines between detected speaker turns
- This is speculative and should be validated with real podcast audio before committing to the approach

### Tests
- Unit: scroll state transitions (autoScrolling -> userScrolling -> userScrolled -> autoScrolling via "Jump to now")
- Unit: proximity re-engagement (user scrolls near current paragraph -> auto re-engages)
- Unit: paragraph grouping logic (consecutive non-ad chunks grouped, ad boundaries cause breaks, 2s gap causes break)
- Unit: tap-to-seek sends correct TranscriptChunk.startTime to PlaybackService
- Unit: ad region styling applied to chunks whose timerange falls within an AdWindow
- Unit: in-episode search highlights all matches and navigates with up/down
- Snapshot: full transcript at multiple Dynamic Type sizes
- Snapshot: ad-region styling (Steel text + "Ad" pill), current-paragraph highlighting (Copper border), search results
- E2E: play episode, open full transcript, verify scroll follows, tap paragraph to seek, verify position changes

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Full transcript scrolls smoothly with large episodes (1000+ chunks) using LazyVStack
- [ ] Auto-scroll follows playback (throttled to 1 update/sec)
- [ ] Manual scroll pauses auto-scroll with "Jump to now" re-sync button
- [ ] Proximity re-engagement when user scrolls near current paragraph
- [ ] Tap-to-seek accurate to TranscriptChunk.startTime
- [ ] Ad regions visually distinguished (Steel muted text + "Ad" pill badge)
- [ ] In-episode search highlights matches with Copper background and up/down navigation
- [ ] Paragraph grouping correctly handles ad boundaries and 2s pauses
- [ ] Editorial serif typography (Newsreader) at all Dynamic Type sizes
- [ ] VoiceOver: each paragraph readable, ad regions announced, tap-to-seek accessible

title: See why Playhead acted: skip-confidence visualization on the timeline
description:
# Skip Confidence Visualization on Timeline

## Goal
Show detection confidence on the Now Playing timeline so users can see when the system is sure vs. uncertain about ad boundaries.

## Rationale
Currently ad segments on the timeline are uniform recessed blocks. Adding a confidence gradient (opacity/saturation) educates users about the system's certainty, builds trust (transparent about limitations), and helps with the trust-scoring learning period. Minimal effort — AdWindow already stores confidence scores.

## Implementation

### Timeline Enhancement
- Modify skip marker rendering in the Now Playing timeline (playhead-m3d)
- Ad segments currently shown as uniform recessed blocks on the timeline rail

#### Opacity Mapping
```swift
/// Maps AdWindow.confidence to visual opacity for timeline segments.
func adSegmentOpacity(confidence: Double) -> Double {
    switch confidence {
    case 0.9...:     return 1.0    // full opacity (solid — no visual regression from current)
    case 0.7..<0.9:  return 0.7    // slightly transparent
    case 0.5..<0.7:  return 0.5    // noticeably lighter, indicating uncertainty
    default:         return 0.4    // minimum visible opacity for sub-0.5 (shouldn't appear normally)
    }
}
```
- Color stays the same (recessed Ink tone) — only opacity changes via `.opacity(adSegmentOpacity(confidence:))`

#### Visibility Filter
- Only visualize AdWindows that:
  1. Have `confidence >= SkipPolicyConfig.default.enterThreshold` (currently 0.65)
  2. Have reached at least `SkipDecisionState.candidate` (i.e., appear in SkipOrchestrator's managed windows)
- Sub-threshold windows are not displayed. This prevents showing uncertain/noise detections.
- Note: the `default` threshold reference at the minimum. In practice, SkipOrchestrator filters candidates below `enterThreshold`, so only windows that pass the threshold will have a decision state to check.

#### Long-Press Popover
- Long-press gesture (`.onLongPressGesture(minimumDuration: 0.5)`) on an ad segment block
- Show a custom popover view (not a native tooltip — iOS has no tooltip API):
  ```swift
  struct ConfidencePopover: View {
      let confidence: Double
      
      var body: some View {
          HStack(spacing: 4) {
              Text("Ad detected")
                  .font(.custom("InstrumentSans", size: 13))  // .caption equivalent
              Text("(\(Int(confidence * 100))%)")
                  .font(.custom("IBMPlexMono", size: 13))
          }
          .padding(.horizontal, 12)
          .padding(.vertical, 8)
          .background(Color("Bone").opacity(0.95))
          .cornerRadius(8)
          .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.15), radius: 4, y: 2)
      }
  }
  ```
- Positioned above the tapped segment using `.overlay` with `.offset` or `GeometryReader` to calculate placement
- Dismiss on tap outside (use `.onTapGesture` on a full-screen transparent overlay behind the popover)
- Entrance animation: `.transition(.scale.combined(with: .opacity))` with `.easeOut(duration: 0.15)`

### Files Modified
- Primary: the file containing skip marker rendering from playhead-m3d (likely `Playhead/Views/NowPlaying/TimelineView.swift` or similar)
- New: `Playhead/Views/NowPlaying/ConfidencePopover.swift` for the popover component

### Tests
- Unit: opacity mapping function covers all ranges (0.5, 0.65, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 1.0 inputs -> expected outputs)
- Unit: sub-threshold AdWindows (confidence < enterThreshold) excluded from visualization
- Unit: only AdWindows with SkipDecisionState >= .candidate are visualized
- Snapshot: timeline with ad segments at confidence 0.5, 0.7, 0.9, 1.0 — visually distinct opacity levels
- Snapshot: long-press popover with various confidence values (50%, 87%, 100%), Dynamic Type sizes
- Snapshot: popover positioning above segment (not clipped by screen edge)
- E2E: play episode with known ad segments at varying confidence, verify timeline segments render with distinct opacities, long-press shows correct percentage

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Ad segments visually differentiate by confidence level via opacity (4 tiers: 1.0, 0.7, 0.5, 0.4)
- [ ] High-confidence segments (>= 0.9) look solid (no visual regression from current uniform blocks)
- [ ] Sub-threshold AdWindows not displayed on timeline
- [ ] Long-press shows confidence percentage in custom popover (dismiss on tap outside)
- [ ] Popover entrance animated (0.15s scale + opacity)
- [ ] No performance impact on timeline rendering (confidence already in memory from AdWindow struct)
- [ ] VoiceOver announces confidence level for ad segments (e.g., "Ad segment, 87% confidence")
- [ ] Dynamic Type scales popover text correctly
- [ ] Popover positioned above segment, not clipped by screen edges
