title: New Episode Notifications
description:
# New Episode Notifications

## Goal
Notify users when subscribed podcasts publish new episodes.

## Rationale
Expected feature for any podcast app. Without it, users must open the app to check for new episodes. Background app refresh + UNNotification is the standard iOS pattern. Keeps users engaged and returning to the app.

## Implementation

### NewEpisodeMonitorService
- New file: `Playhead/Services/Notifications/NewEpisodeMonitorService.swift`
- `actor NewEpisodeMonitorService`
- Dependencies: RSS/Atom Feed Parser (playhead-db9), `ModelContext` (SwiftData), `UNUserNotificationCenter`

#### Background Refresh
- Register `BGAppRefreshTask` in PlayheadApp init:
  ```swift
  BGTaskScheduler.shared.register(
      forTaskWithIdentifier: "com.playhead.new-episode-check",
      using: nil
  ) { task in ... }
  ```
- Also register this identifier in Info.plist under `BGTaskSchedulerPermittedIdentifiers`
- Task handler: call `checkForNewEpisodes()`, then reschedule:
  ```swift
  func scheduleNextRefresh() {
      let request = BGAppRefreshTaskRequest(identifier: "com.playhead.new-episode-check")
      request.earliestBeginDate = Date(timeIntervalSinceNow: 4 * 3600)  // 4 hours
      try? BGTaskScheduler.shared.submit(request)
  }
  ```
- Also checks on app foreground: observe `scenePhase == .active` in PlayheadApp and call `checkForNewEpisodes()` for immediate freshness

#### Feed Checking Logic
```swift
func checkForNewEpisodes() async {
    let subscribed = // fetch all Podcast from SwiftData where subscribedAt != nil
    for podcast in subscribed {
        guard podcast.notificationsEnabled else { continue }  // per-show toggle
        let feedEpisodes = try? await feedParser.parse(podcast.feedURL)
        let newEpisodes = feedEpisodes?.filter { feedItem in
            // New if no Episode exists with matching feedItemGUID for this podcast
            !existingEpisodeGUIDs.contains(feedItem.guid)
        }
        for ep in newEpisodes ?? [] {
            // Create Episode in SwiftData
            let episode = Episode(feedItemGUID: ep.guid, feedURL: podcast.feedURL, ...)
            modelContext.insert(episode)
            pendingNotifications.append((podcast: podcast, episode: episode))
        }
    }
    // Fire notifications (rate-limited)
    await fireNotifications(pendingNotifications)
}
```

#### Notification Delivery
- Notification category identifier: `"NEW_EPISODE"`
- Custom action: `UNNotificationAction(identifier: "PLAY_NOW", title: "Play", options: .foreground)`
- Register category at app launch:
  ```swift
  let playAction = UNNotificationAction(identifier: "PLAY_NOW", title: "Play", options: .foreground)
  let category = UNNotificationCategory(identifier: "NEW_EPISODE", actions: [playAction], ...)
  UNUserNotificationCenter.current().setNotificationCategories([category])
  ```
- Notification content per episode:
  ```swift
  let content = UNMutableNotificationContent()
  content.title = podcast.title
  content.body = episode.title
  content.subtitle = episode.duration.map { formatDuration($0) } ?? ""
  content.categoryIdentifier = "NEW_EPISODE"
  content.userInfo = ["episodeKey": episode.canonicalEpisodeKey]
  ```
- Rate limiting: fire at most 10 individual notifications per refresh. If more:
  ```swift
  // Batch remaining into summary
  content.title = "New Episodes"
  content.body = "\(remaining.count) more new episodes available"
  ```
- Default tap: handled in `UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate.didReceive` — extract `episodeKey` from `userInfo`, navigate to episode in Library
- "Play" action: extract `episodeKey`, call `PlaybackService.loadAndPlay(episodeKey:)`

### Notification Setup
- Request authorization during onboarding (after subscription import step, so value prop is clear):
  ```swift
  UNUserNotificationCenter.current().requestAuthorization(options: [.alert, .sound, .badge])
  ```
- Settings -> Notifications section:
  - Global toggle: `notificationsEnabled: Bool` on UserPreferences (default: `true`). Add to init and schema migration.
  - Per-show toggle: `notificationsEnabled: Bool` on Podcast model (default: `true` — opt-out pattern). Add to init and schema migration.
  - Both require lightweight SwiftData schema migration.
- Per-show: accessible via long-press podcast in Library -> "Show Settings" sheet -> "Notifications" section (shared pattern with playhead-pfn, playhead-x5l, playhead-5w4). Shows `Toggle("Notify on new episodes")`.

### Edge Cases
- No duplicate notifications: Episode existence in SwiftData (keyed by `canonicalEpisodeKey`) serves as the dedup check. Once an Episode is created, it won't trigger again.
- Feed fetch failures: `catch` errors silently, log via `Logger`, retry on next refresh cycle. Don't surface errors to user.
- App not authorized for notifications: check `UNUserNotificationCenter.current().notificationSettings()` before attempting delivery. If denied, skip silently (user revoked in Settings.app).
- System Focus modes: respected automatically by `UNUserNotificationCenter`

### Tests
- Unit: feed comparison correctly identifies new episodes (new GUID not in SwiftData Episode store)
- Unit: no notification for already-seen episodes (Episode already exists)
- Unit: per-show notification toggle respected (notificationsEnabled == false -> skip)
- Unit: global notification toggle respected
- Unit: rate limiting fires max 10 individual + 1 summary notification
- Unit: "PLAY_NOW" action handler calls PlaybackService with correct episodeKey
- Unit: BGAppRefreshTask reschedules after completion
- Snapshot: notification settings section in Settings view, per-show toggle in Show Settings sheet, Dynamic Type sizes
- E2E: simulate feed update with new episode, verify notification fires and Episode created in SwiftData

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Notifications fire for new episodes from subscribed shows
- [ ] Per-show and global notification toggles work
- [ ] Tapping notification navigates to the episode
- [ ] "Play" action starts playback directly
- [ ] Permission requested at appropriate onboarding moment (after subscription import)
- [ ] Battery-efficient (system-managed BGAppRefreshTask, 4h minimum interval)
- [ ] No duplicate notifications for same episode (Episode existence is dedup)
- [ ] Rate limited to 10 individual notifications per refresh + 1 summary
- [ ] BGTaskScheduler identifier registered in Info.plist
- [ ] Lightweight SwiftData schema migration for new fields on both UserPreferences and Podcast

title: Queue / Up Next Management
description:
# Queue / Up Next Management

## Goal
Let users build and manage a playback queue so they can line up episodes in their preferred order.

## Rationale
Queue management is a standard podcast player feature. Daily listeners queue episodes for commutes, workouts, etc. Without it, users must manually navigate to the next episode each time. This is a parity feature — its absence is notable.

## Implementation

### QueueEntry Model
- New file: `Playhead/Models/QueueEntry.swift`
- New SwiftData `@Model`:
  ```swift
  @Model
  final class QueueEntry {
      var episodeKey: String       // references Episode.canonicalEpisodeKey
      var position: Int            // 0-based ordering index
      var addedAt: Date

      init(episodeKey: String, position: Int, addedAt: Date = .now) { ... }
  }
  ```
- Register `QueueEntry.self` in `SwiftDataStore.schema` array and create `PlayheadSchemaV2` with frozen V1 snapshots per the migration warning in SwiftDataStore.swift. Requires lightweight SwiftData schema migration.

### QueueService
- New file: `Playhead/Services/Queue/QueueService.swift`
- `actor QueueService`
- Dependencies: `ModelContext` (SwiftData), `PlaybackService`

#### Public API
```swift
func addNext(_ episodeKey: String) async throws    // insert at position 0, increment all existing positions
func addLast(_ episodeKey: String) async throws    // append at max(position) + 1
func remove(_ episodeKey: String) async throws     // delete entry, compact positions
func reorder(from: IndexSet, to: Int) async throws // standard List move, update positions
func clear() async throws                          // delete all entries (no confirmation at service level — UI handles that)
func peek() async -> QueueEntry?                   // next up (position 0), nil if empty
func popNext() async throws -> QueueEntry?         // remove and return position 0, compact remaining
func allEntries() async throws -> [QueueEntry]     // sorted by position ascending
var count: Int { get async }
```

#### Auto-Advance
- PlaybackService posts `Notification.Name("PlaybackDidFinishEpisode")` when AVPlayerItem reaches end (observed via `AVPlayerItem.didPlayToEndTimeNotification`)
- QueueService observes this notification via `NotificationCenter.default.notifications(named:)` async sequence
- On episode finish: wait 3s (countdown phase), then call `popNext()` and `PlaybackService.loadAndPlay(episodeKey:)` if entry exists
- Countdown is cancellable: if user taps "Cancel" during countdown, QueueService cancels the pending `Task`
- Queue persists across app termination. On cold launch, queue remains intact but does NOT auto-play (user must explicitly start playback).

### QueueView
- New file: `Playhead/Views/Queue/QueueView.swift`
- Accessible from Now Playing screen: "Up Next" button in transport area
- Sheet presentation (`.presentationDetents([.medium, .large])`) showing ordered list:
  - Episode title (Instrument Sans, `.headline`) + podcast name (Instrument Sans, Soft Steel, `.subheadline`) + duration (IBM Plex Mono, `.caption`, formatted as `mm:ss` or `h:mm`)
  - Drag handles for reorder via `List { ... }.environment(\.editMode, .constant(.active))` with `onMove` handler
  - Swipe-to-remove via `.onDelete` modifier
  - "Clear Queue" button at bottom (`.destructive` role, with `.confirmationDialog` before executing)
- Episode List View (EpisodeListView.swift): add swipe actions to each EpisodeRow — "Play Next" (calls `addNext`) and "Play Last" (calls `addLast`), both with Copper tint
- Mini Player: shows next-up episode name in secondary line (Bone text, Instrument Sans, `.caption`)
- Empty state: "Queue is empty. Swipe an episode to add it." in Soft Steel on Ink background

### Countdown Overlay
- New file: `Playhead/Views/Queue/CountdownOverlay.swift`
- Overlay on Now Playing when auto-advance countdown is active
- Shows "Up next: [Episode Name]" (Newsreader for episode title, Copper accent) with circular countdown ring (3s, Copper stroke) and "Cancel" button (Bone text, `.bordered` style)
- Countdown ring: `Circle().trim(from:to:)` animated with `.animation(.linear(duration: 3))`

### Tests
- Unit: queue CRUD operations (add next shifts positions correctly, add last appends, remove compacts, reorder updates)
- Unit: addNext with empty queue sets position 0; addNext with 3 items shifts all +1
- Unit: auto-advance pops correct next episode on PlaybackDidFinishEpisode notification
- Unit: auto-advance cancellation stops playback start
- Unit: persistence survives simulated app restart (insert entries, create new ModelContext, verify order)
- Unit: duplicate prevention (adding same episodeKey twice is idempotent or moves to new position — decide: move to new position)
- Snapshot: queue sheet with 0, 1, 5 episodes; drag state; countdown overlay; Dynamic Type sizes
- E2E: queue 3 episodes, play through first, verify second starts automatically after 3s countdown

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Episodes can be added to queue from episode list (Play Next / Play Last swipe actions)
- [ ] Queue is viewable and reorderable from Now Playing sheet
- [ ] Auto-advances to next episode with 3s countdown (cancellable)
- [ ] Queue persists across app launches (including force-quit); no auto-play on cold launch
- [ ] Swipe-to-remove works; Clear Queue requires confirmation
- [ ] Empty queue state is clear and helpful
- [ ] VoiceOver: all queue actions accessible, reorder via accessibility rotor
- [ ] Dynamic Type scales queue sheet correctly
- [ ] QueueEntry registered in SwiftData schema with lightweight migration

title: OPML Import/Export
description:
# OPML Import/Export

## Goal
Remove the biggest barrier to switching from other podcast apps by supporting OPML subscription import and export.

## Rationale
Power users (early adopters, exact target market) have 20-50+ subscriptions in Overcast, Pocket Casts, Apple Podcasts. They won't manually re-add them. OPML is the universal podcast subscription format — every player exports it. Supporting import in onboarding reduces time-to-value from minutes to seconds. Export ensures users don't feel locked in (reduces adoption anxiety).

## Implementation

### OPMLService
- New file: `Playhead/Services/OPML/OPMLService.swift`
- `actor OPMLService`
- Dependencies: `PodcastDiscoveryService` (for feed validation/metadata), `ModelContext` (for SwiftData Podcast creation)

#### Types
```swift
struct OPMLFeed: Sendable {
    let title: String?
    let xmlUrl: URL        // feed URL
}

struct ImportResult: Sendable {
    let imported: Int           // successfully created
    let skippedDuplicate: Int   // already in library
    let failed: [(url: URL, reason: String)]  // unreachable or invalid
}

enum OPMLError: Error, LocalizedError {
    case invalidFormat          // not valid OPML XML
    case emptyFile              // valid XML but no <outline> elements with xmlUrl
    case fileReadFailed(Error)  // couldn't read file data
}
```

#### Public API
```swift
func parseOPML(from data: Data) throws -> [OPMLFeed]
func importFeeds(_ feeds: [OPMLFeed], progress: @Sendable (Int, Int) -> Void) async -> ImportResult
func exportOPML(podcasts: [Podcast]) -> Data  // UTF-8 encoded OPML XML
```

#### Parsing
- Use Foundation `XMLParser` (delegate-based) — no external dependencies
- Parse `<outline>` elements: extract `xmlUrl` attribute as feed URL, `title` or `text` attribute as title
- Handle nested outline groups (OPML allows `<outline>` nesting for categories): flatten recursively, only extract leaf nodes with `xmlUrl`

#### Import Concurrency
- Validate feeds concurrently with `TaskGroup`, limited to 5 concurrent feed fetches (via a semaphore pattern: `actor ConcurrencyLimiter { var active = 0; let max = 5 }`)
- For each feed: call `PodcastDiscoveryService.resolve(feedURL:)` to fetch metadata and validate. If valid, create Podcast entry in SwiftData. If already exists (feedURL unique constraint), increment skippedDuplicate count.
- Report progress via callback: `progress(completedCount, totalCount)`

### Import Flow
- Onboarding: "Coming from another app? Import your subscriptions" card with file picker
- Library: overflow menu -> "Import Subscriptions" -> SwiftUI `.fileImporter(isPresented:, allowedContentTypes: [.init(filenameExtension: "opml")!, .xml])` modifier
- Import progress: determinate `ProgressView(value: completed, total: total)` with "Importing 12 of 34 podcasts..." label (Copper fill on Ink track, count in IBM Plex Mono)
- Result summary sheet: "Imported 32 podcasts. 2 could not be found." with dismissible list of failures (each showing URL and reason)
- Error state: if file is not valid OPML, show alert: "This file doesn't appear to be an OPML subscription list" (from `OPMLError.invalidFormat`)
- Note: OPML only carries feed subscriptions, not episode state (play positions, downloads). Import summary should set this expectation with subtitle text.

### Export Flow
- Settings -> "Export Subscriptions" -> generates `.opml` file via `exportOPML(podcasts:)` -> `ShareLink(item: opmlFileURL)` (write to temp directory first)
- Or: Library overflow menu -> "Export as OPML"
- OPML output format:
  ```xml
  <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
  <opml version="2.0">
    <head><title>Playhead Subscriptions</title></head>
    <body>
      <outline text="Show Title" xmlUrl="https://feed.url/rss" type="rss"/>
    </body>
  </opml>
  ```

### Tests
- Unit: OPML parsing (standard format, nested groups flattened, missing xmlUrl skipped, malformed XML throws .invalidFormat, empty file throws .emptyFile)
- Unit: export generates valid OPML that re-imports identically (round-trip test)
- Unit: duplicate feed detection during import (feeds already in library skipped, count correct)
- Unit: concurrent import respects 5-feed concurrency limit
- Unit: progress callback reports incrementing counts
- Snapshot: import progress view, result summary (all success, partial, all failed, error), Dynamic Type sizes
- E2E: import sample OPML with 10 feeds, verify all appear in Library with correct titles
- Fixture: sample OPML files from Overcast, Pocket Casts, Apple Podcasts exports (checked into test fixtures)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Imports standard OPML files from major podcast apps
- [ ] Handles malformed/partial OPML gracefully (imports what it can, reports what it can't)
- [ ] Import available in onboarding and Library menu
- [ ] Export produces valid OPML 2.0 that other apps can import
- [ ] Progress shown during import with final summary
- [ ] Duplicate feeds detected and skipped (not duplicated in library)
- [ ] Concurrent feed validation limited to 5 simultaneous requests
- [ ] Uses SwiftUI .fileImporter() and ShareLink (no UIKit bridging)
- [ ] VoiceOver accessible throughout import/export flow
- [ ] Dynamic Type scales import/export views correctly

title: Transcript Search UI
description:
# Transcript Search UI

## Goal
Let users search across all transcribed episodes, turning passive listening into a searchable knowledge base. "What was that book someone recommended?"

## Rationale
FTS5 backend is already built and indexed in AnalysisStore. TranscriptChunk has word-level timestamps. The only missing piece is the search UI. This is a genuine differentiator — no mainstream podcast player offers full-text search across episodes. The more episodes users listen to, the more valuable search becomes (lock-in effect). Sub-50ms query performance thanks to FTS5.

## Implementation

### TranscriptSearchService
- New file: `Playhead/Services/Search/TranscriptSearchService.swift`
- `actor TranscriptSearchService`
- Dependencies: `AnalysisStore` (for FTS5 queries), `ModelContext` (for Episode/Podcast joins)

#### Types
```swift
struct SearchResult: Sendable, Identifiable {
    let id: String                    // TranscriptChunk rowid or composite key
    let analysisAssetId: String       // for join to Episode.lastPlayedAnalysisAssetId
    let episodeTitle: String          // denormalized for display
    let podcastTitle: String          // denormalized for display
    let snippet: String               // from FTS5 highlight() with <mark> tags
    let timestamp: TimeInterval       // TranscriptChunk.startTime
    let rank: Double                  // FTS5 rank (lower = more relevant)
    let publishedAt: Date?            // Episode.publishedAt for recency tiebreaking
}

struct SearchResultPage: Sendable {
    let results: [SearchResult]
    let totalEstimate: Int            // from FTS5 count for "X results" display
    let hasMore: Bool
}
```

#### Public API
```swift
func search(query: String, offset: Int = 0, limit: Int = 20) async throws -> SearchResultPage
func sanitize(_ query: String) -> String  // strips FTS5 special chars: ^*":(){}[]
```

#### Query Construction
- Simple terms: `word1 word2` -> FTS5 `word1 AND word2` (implicit AND)
- Quoted phrases: `"exact match"` -> FTS5 `"exact match"` (passed through)
- Sanitization: strip `^*:(){}[]` from non-quoted input to prevent FTS5 syntax errors
- FTS5 highlight() call: `highlight(transcript_chunks_fts, 0, '<mark>', '</mark>')` for snippet extraction
- Results ordered by FTS5 `rank`, with recency tiebreak: `ORDER BY rank, timestamp DESC`
- Pagination: `LIMIT ? OFFSET ?`

### SearchView
- New file: `Playhead/Views/Search/SearchView.swift`
- Accessible from Library tab (search bar at top) and as a dedicated "Search" tab in navigation (TabView)
- Search bar with "Search transcripts..." placeholder (Instrument Sans)
- As-you-type results with 300ms debounce (via `Task` with `Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(300))`, cancelling previous task on new input)

#### View States
```swift
enum SearchViewState {
    case idle                      // empty query, show recent searches
    case searching                 // debounce active or query in-flight
    case results(SearchResultPage) // results returned
    case empty(String)             // query returned zero results (carries query text)
    case error(Error)              // query failed
}
```

#### Result Display
- Results grouped by episode, showing:
  - Episode title (Instrument Sans, `.headline`) + podcast name (Instrument Sans, Soft Steel, `.subheadline`) + date (RelativeDateTimeFormatter)
  - Matching transcript snippet with `<mark>` tags rendered as Copper highlight on Bone background (parse `<mark>` tags into AttributedString). Snippet text in Newsreader (editorial serif).
  - Timestamp of the match (IBM Plex Mono, `.caption`, formatted as `mm:ss` or `h:mm:ss`)
- Tap result: navigates to Now Playing, calls `PlaybackService.seek(to: result.timestamp)` then `PlaybackService.play()`. Navigation via `NavigationPath` push or deep link through app coordinator.
- Empty query state: "Search everything you've listened to" with illustration (Soft Steel text on Ink background)
- Zero results state: "No matches for \"\(query)\"" (distinct from empty query state)
- Recent searches: persisted in `UserDefaults(key: "recentSearches")` as `[String]`. Shown when search bar is focused and query is empty. Capped at 20 entries (drop oldest), newest first. Tap to re-execute search.
- Partial transcription: results only include fully transcribed chunks. If an episode is mid-transcription, available chunks are searchable; a subtle indicator ("Transcription in progress") shown below episode header for those episodes.
- Infinite scroll: when user scrolls near bottom (last 5 items visible via `onAppear`), load next page via `search(query:offset:limit:)`

### Tests
- Unit: FTS5 query construction (simple term, quoted phrase, multiple terms, special character sanitization preserves quoted phrases)
- Unit: result ranking (FTS5 rank ordering, recency tiebreak)
- Unit: snippet `<mark>` tag parsing into AttributedString
- Unit: pagination returns correct windows with offset (page 1 = offset 0, page 2 = offset 20)
- Unit: debounce cancels previous in-flight query
- Unit: recent searches persistence (add, cap at 20, dedup)
- Snapshot: search results at multiple Dynamic Type sizes, empty query state, zero results state, recent searches list
- E2E: transcribe episode with known content, search for specific phrase, verify result appears with correct timestamp, tap to seek

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Search returns results in < 100ms for typical queries
- [ ] Results show highlighted matching text (Copper on Bone) with surrounding context
- [ ] Tap-to-seek navigates to correct timestamp and starts playback
- [ ] Quoted phrase search returns exact matches only
- [ ] Results paginate smoothly (infinite scroll, no jank)
- [ ] Empty query state and zero-results state are distinct and helpful
- [ ] User input sanitized against FTS5 syntax injection
- [ ] 300ms debounce prevents excessive queries during typing
- [ ] VoiceOver reads results with episode context and timestamp
- [ ] Recent searches persist across app launches (UserDefaults, capped at 20)

title: Sleep Timer with Transcript-Aware Pause
description:
# Sleep Timer with Transcript-Aware Pause Points

## Goal
Provide a standard sleep timer that leverages Playhead's unique transcript data to pause at natural sentence boundaries instead of cutting mid-word.

## Rationale
Sleep timer is table-stakes for podcast players — its absence is a notable gap. The twist: using transcript word timestamps to find the nearest sentence boundary makes the cutoff graceful instead of jarring. If the timer fires during a detected ad, skip to end of ad first. This subtly demonstrates AI value in a personal, delightful way. No competitor does this.

## Implementation

### SleepTimerService
- New file: `Playhead/Services/SleepTimer/SleepTimerService.swift`
- `actor SleepTimerService`
- Dependencies: `AnalysisStore` (for TranscriptChunks and AdWindows), `PlaybackService`

#### State Machine
```swift
enum SleepTimerState: Sendable {
    case idle                          // no timer set
    case running(fireAt: Date)         // countdown active
    case firing                        // timer fired, searching for boundary
    case fadingOut                     // 2s volume ramp in progress
    case paused                        // playback paused, timer complete
}
```

#### Public API
```swift
enum SleepDuration: Sendable, CaseIterable {
    case minutes15, minutes30, minutes45, hour1, endOfEpisode, custom(TimeInterval)
    
    var seconds: TimeInterval? {
        // .endOfEpisode returns nil — handled specially
    }
    
    static var allCases: [SleepDuration] // excludes .custom
}

func start(_ duration: SleepDuration) async
func cancel() async
var state: SleepTimerState { get }  // observable via AsyncStream or @Published on a @MainActor wrapper
func remainingTime() -> TimeInterval? // nil if idle
```

#### Timer Mechanics
- Uses `Task.sleep(for:)` for the countdown (cancellable via stored `Task` reference)
- "End of Episode": subscribes to PlaybackService's current item duration minus current position; fires when remaining time crosses 0
- When timer fires (`state -> .firing`):
  1. Query AnalysisStore for AdWindows containing current playback position (via episode's `lastPlayedAnalysisAssetId`)
  2. If inside an AdWindow: seek to `adWindow.endTime + 0.5s`, then proceed to step 3
  3. Query AnalysisStore for TranscriptChunks in window `[currentTime - 10s, currentTime + 10s]`
  4. Find nearest sentence boundary: look for chunk text endings matching regex `[.?!]$` or gaps between consecutive chunks > 500ms
  5. If boundary found within window: wait until playback reaches that timestamp (observe via PlaybackService time updates)
  6. If no boundary found (no TranscriptChunks available): fall back to immediate pause with 1s fade
- Fade out (`state -> .fadingOut`): ramp `AVPlayer.volume` from current value to 0.0 over 2s using a `Timer.publish(every: 0.05)` (40 steps over 2s, linear interpolation). Not AVAudioMix — that's for asset-level mixing and doesn't support live ramps on streaming playback.
- After fade completes: call `PlaybackService.pause()`, reset volume to previous value, set `state -> .paused`

### UI
- New file: `Playhead/Views/NowPlaying/SleepTimerButton.swift`
- Sleep timer button in Now Playing transport controls (SF Symbol `moon.fill`, Soft Steel when `.idle`, Copper when `.running`)
- Tap: presents duration picker sheet (`.presentationDetents([.medium])`, compact). Durations in Instrument Sans, countdown in IBM Plex Mono.
- When `.running`: countdown badge on the moon icon showing remaining time formatted as `mm:ss` (or `h:mm:ss` if > 1h)
- Cancel option in picker sheet when timer is running
- Settings: `defaultSleepDuration: String?` added to UserPreferences (stored as SleepDuration case name, not TimeInterval, so `.endOfEpisode` round-trips). Decoded via `SleepDuration(rawName:)`. Requires lightweight SwiftData schema migration (add field to PlayheadSchemaV2).

### Tests
- Unit: timer fires at correct time (mock `Task.sleep` or use short duration)
- Unit: sentence boundary search finds nearest period/question-mark ending in TranscriptChunks within 10s window
- Unit: ad-region detection triggers seek-to-ad-end-then-pause sequence
- Unit: fade-out duration is 2s, volume reaches 0.0, volume restored after pause
- Unit: graceful degradation when no TranscriptChunks available (immediate 1s fade)
- Unit: "End of Episode" fires when episode reaches end
- Unit: cancel mid-countdown returns to .idle state
- Snapshot: sleep timer button states (idle, running with countdown badge), picker sheet, Dynamic Type sizes
- E2E: set 1-minute timer during playback, verify pause occurs at sentence boundary (not mid-word)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Timer presets work correctly (15m, 30m, 45m, 1h, End of Episode)
- [ ] Pause occurs at nearest sentence boundary (within +/- 10s of timer expiry)
- [ ] Audio fades out over 2s via AVPlayer.volume ramp (40 steps at 50ms intervals)
- [ ] If timer fires during ad, seeks to ad end first
- [ ] Falls back to standard pause with 1s fade if TranscriptChunks unavailable
- [ ] Moon icon shows active state with countdown badge (mm:ss format)
- [ ] Volume restored to pre-fade value after pause
- [ ] VoiceOver announces timer state and remaining time
- [ ] Dynamic Type scales the picker sheet correctly
- [ ] Lightweight SwiftData schema migration for defaultSleepDuration field

title: Time Saved Dashboard + Widget
description:
# Time Saved Dashboard + Widget

## Goal
Make Playhead's ad-skipping value tangible and shareable. Users should see exactly how much time they've saved, creating a retention loop and viral sharing moments.

## Rationale
The core value proposition of Playhead — skipping ads — is invisible. Users can't quantify what they're getting. A "Time Saved" dashboard turns this invisible value into a concrete number ("Playhead saved you 4h 23m this month") that users screenshot and share. This is the single highest-ROI feature for retention and word-of-mouth growth.

## Implementation

### Data Foundation
- SkipOrchestrator currently manages skip decisions in-memory per episode. To power stats, we need persisted skip outcomes.
- New SQLite table `skip_events` in AnalysisStore:
  ```sql
  CREATE TABLE skip_events (
      id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,          -- UUID string
      analysisAssetId TEXT NOT NULL, -- links to analysis_assets
      adWindowId TEXT NOT NULL,      -- links to ad_windows
      skippedDurationSec REAL NOT NULL,
      skipBehavior TEXT NOT NULL,    -- "auto" | "fastForward" | "mute" (matches SkipBehavior raw name)
      timestamp REAL NOT NULL        -- Unix epoch seconds
  );
  CREATE INDEX idx_skip_events_timestamp ON skip_events(timestamp);
  CREATE INDEX idx_skip_events_asset ON skip_events(analysisAssetId);
  ```
- Written by SkipOrchestrator when a skip fires or ad region is exited (i.e., when SkipDecisionState transitions to `.skipped`).

### SkipStatsService
- New file: `Playhead/Services/Stats/SkipStatsService.swift`
- `actor SkipStatsService`
- Dependencies: `AnalysisStore`, `ModelContext` (for SwiftData Episode/Podcast joins)
- Public API:
  ```swift
  struct SkipStats: Sendable {
      let totalTimeSaved: TimeInterval       // seconds
      let totalAdsSkipped: Int
      let averageAdLoadPerShow: TimeInterval  // seconds per episode, across subscribed shows
      let longestSingleAd: TimeInterval       // seconds
  }

  struct ShowSkipStats: Sendable, Identifiable {
      let id: String                         // Podcast feedURL absoluteString
      let podcastTitle: String
      let artworkURL: URL?
      let totalTimeSaved: TimeInterval
      let adsSkipped: Int
  }

  struct DailyTimeSaved: Sendable {
      let date: Date                         // calendar day (midnight)
      let timeSaved: TimeInterval
  }

  enum TimePeriod: CaseIterable, Sendable {
      case thisWeek, thisMonth, allTime
  }

  func stats(for period: TimePeriod) async throws -> SkipStats
  func perShowBreakdown(for period: TimePeriod) async throws -> [ShowSkipStats]
  func dailyTrend(days: Int = 30) async throws -> [DailyTimeSaved]
  func invalidateCache()
  ```
- Caches aggregates in-memory; invalidated when SkipOrchestrator posts a `Notification.Name("SkipEventRecorded")` notification. SkipStatsService observes this via `NotificationCenter.default.notifications(named:)` async sequence.
- Joins against Episode/Podcast SwiftData models for per-show attribution via `analysisAssetId` -> `Episode.lastPlayedAnalysisAssetId` -> `Episode.podcast`

### Stats View
- New file: `Playhead/Views/Stats/StatsView.swift`
- Headline number: "4h 23m saved" in large editorial serif (Newsreader, `.largeTitle` equivalent)
- Time period selector: segmented picker with `TimePeriod.allCases`
- Per-show breakdown: `List` of `ShowSkipStats` ranked by `totalTimeSaved` descending, with Copper accent bars (proportional width via `GeometryReader`)
- Trend sparkline: `Canvas` view plotting `DailyTimeSaved` over last 30 days, Copper stroke on Ink background
- Design: follows Quiet Instrument aesthetic — Ink background, Bone text, Copper accents for the headline number
- Empty state: "Start listening to see your stats" with subdued illustration in Steel
- View states: `.loading` (ProgressView), `.loaded(SkipStats)`, `.empty` (no skip events), `.error(Error)`

### iOS Widget (WidgetKit)
- New widget extension target: `PlayheadWidget`
- Small widget: headline "time saved" number + Playhead Copper line motif
- Medium widget: time saved + currently playing episode title
- App Group container identifier: `group.com.playhead.shared`
- SkipStatsService writes a lightweight JSON snapshot to the App Group on each skip event:
  ```swift
  struct WidgetSnapshot: Codable {
      let totalTimeSavedSeconds: TimeInterval
      let totalAdsSkipped: Int
      let currentEpisodeTitle: String?
      let updatedAt: Date
  }
  // Written to: containerURL.appending(path: "widget-snapshot.json")
  ```
- WidgetKit timeline provider (`SkipStatsTimelineProvider`) reads from this JSON file
- Timeline: single entry refreshed via `WidgetCenter.shared.reloadTimelines("SkipStatsWidget")` called from SkipStatsService after writing snapshot
- Note: WidgetKit timeline refresh is system-managed; "within 15 minutes" is a best-effort target, not guaranteed

### Tests
- Unit tests for SkipStatsService aggregation logic (empty state returns zeroes, single skip, many skips across episodes, time period filtering with date boundaries)
- Unit tests for skip_events persistence in AnalysisStore (insert, query by date range, query by analysisAssetId)
- Unit tests for cache invalidation (post notification -> cache cleared -> next query hits DB)
- Snapshot tests for StatsView at multiple Dynamic Type sizes, including empty state and loaded state
- Widget timeline provider tests with mock JSON snapshot (verify parsing, verify stale snapshot handled)
- E2E: play episode with known ad segments, verify skip_events row written, stats increment correctly

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] skip_events table correctly populated by SkipOrchestrator on each skip (SkipDecisionState -> .skipped)
- [ ] Stats view shows accurate time saved with < 1s query time
- [ ] Per-show breakdown correctly attributes skips to podcasts via analysisAssetId join
- [ ] Widget updates after new skip events (best-effort, system-managed cadence)
- [ ] All text scales correctly with Dynamic Type
- [ ] VoiceOver reads all stats with appropriate labels
- [ ] Empty state handled gracefully ("Start listening to see your stats")
- [ ] App Group container (`group.com.playhead.shared`) configured for widget data sharing
- [ ] View states (loading, loaded, empty, error) all handled
close_reason: Superseded by 'peace of mind, not metrics' design principle: surfacing quantified counters like 'time saved' to users conflicts with selling the felt experience of seamless listening.

Replace them with production metadata or remove the dormant external-model flow entirely so future settings/onboarding changes cannot re-expose dead downloads.

title: Final Integration Gate (All E2E Pass)
description:
The "golden path" E2E test: proves the complete user journey works end-to-end. This is the single most important test — if this passes, the app delivers its core value.

## Test: First-Launch to First Skip
1. App launches fresh (no models, no data)
2. CapabilitiesService runs self-test, logs snapshot
3. Fast-path ASR model downloads (use bundled test model for speed)
4. User searches for a test podcast (pre-seeded iTunes response)
5. User subscribes, episode list appears
6. User taps play on episode from labeled corpus (known ad at ~3:00)
7. Audio starts playing via AVPlayer
8. AnalysisCoordinator creates AnalysisAsset with fingerprint
9. AnalysisAudioService decodes audio to 16kHz mono shards
10. TranscriptEngineService produces fast-pass chunks ahead of playhead
11. Lexical scanner detects ad candidate near 3:00
12. SkipOrchestrator confirms, snaps boundaries to silence
13. PlaybackService fires skip: duck → seek → release
14. Banner appears with correct copy (or generic if metadata not ready)
15. Banner auto-dismisses after 8 seconds

**Assertions at each step:**
- Step 6: Episode.playbackPosition starts at 0
- Step 8: AnalysisAsset created in SQLite with correct fingerprint
- Step 10: TranscriptChunks appear in SQLite with pass=.fast
- Step 11: AdWindow created with decisionState=.candidate
- Step 12: AdWindow promoted to .confirmed, then .applied
- Step 13: Playback position jumps past ad end time (±2s tolerance)
- Step 14: Banner visible, shows either advertiser or "Skipped sponsor segment"
- Step 15: Banner dismissed, no UI artifacts

**Timing assertions:**
- Time from play to first TranscriptChunk: < 5s on iPhone 15 Pro
- Time from first chunk covering ad to skip firing: < 3s
- Total time-to-first-usable-skip: < 30s from play start

## Test: Listen Reversion
1. Continue from golden path
2. When next ad is skipped, tap "Listen"
3. Verify: playback rewinds to snapped start of ad window
4. Verify: AdWindow.decisionState → .reverted
5. Verify: auto-skip disabled for this exact span
6. Verify: PodcastProfile.recentFalseSkipSignals incremented
7. Play through the ad normally
8. Verify: next ad (if any) still gets detected and skipped

## Test: Resume After Kill
1. Play episode, let analysis reach ~5 minutes
2. Force-kill app
3. Relaunch
4. Verify: AnalysisSession persisted with correct state
5. Play same episode
6. Verify: analysis resumes from checkpoint, doesn't redo work
7. Verify: previously detected ads still have skip cues

## Test: Preview Budget Enforcement (Free Tier)
1. Ensure no premium entitlement
2. Play episode, let analysis consume 12 minutes of budget
3. Verify: analysis continues if inside an ad break (grace window)
4. Verify: analysis stops at 20 minutes cap
5. Verify: playback continues normally after budget exhausted
6. Verify: PreviewBudget record in SQLite shows correct consumed seconds
7. Start a DIFFERENT episode → verify fresh 12-minute budget

## Test: Premium Unlock
1. Trigger StoreKit test purchase
2. Verify: EntitlementManager.isPremium flips to true
3. Play episode → verify no budget enforcement
4. Kill and relaunch → verify premium persists via Transaction.currentEntitlements

Acceptance criteria:
- All 5 test flows pass on device
- Each step has specific numeric/boolean assertions (not "works correctly")
- Timing assertions enforce performance targets
- Full structured log output for debugging failures
- Tests use labeled corpus episodes with known ad positions
notes: reprioritized 2026-07-21 (post-b6jq, release-plan): re-charter Final Integration Gate around corpus certification
