title: Onboarding Flow
description:
First-launch experience. Handle model downloads while communicating value. The aha moment should happen ASAP.

Flow:
1. Welcome screen: dark background, animated copper playhead line (brand motif), "Playhead" wordmark
2. Value prop (1 screen): "Your podcasts, without the ads. All on-device, all private." Brief, not a tutorial.
3. Model download: progress bar showing fast-path ASR model download (~200MB). Message: "Setting up your listener..." User CAN proceed before download completes if they want to browse.
4. Search and subscribe: directed to Browse tab, prompted to find a podcast
5. Play episode: experience first skip → this is the aha moment

Preview budget (12 min + grace) designed so first-listen encounters at least one ad break and experiences a skip.

Model download details:
- Fast-path model downloads first (required for any analysis)
- Final-path model downloads in background (not blocking onboarding)
- If download fails: retry button, or proceed without analysis (graceful degradation)
- Download progress via AssetProvider (playhead-coi)

Acceptance criteria:
- Model download shows clear progress (percentage + MB remaining)
- User can start listening before final-path model finishes downloading
- User can browse/search during fast-path model download
- Flow feels premium and not utilitarian (no raw progress bars, Quiet Instrument aesthetic)
- Completes in under 60 seconds on WiFi (excluding model download time)
- VoiceOver: all screens accessible, progress announced
- Flow only shows once (persisted flag)
- Skip to main app possible at any point (for returning users after reinstall)

title: Foundation Models Metadata Extraction (Layer 3)
description:
Optional enrichment using Apple Foundation Models framework. Extracts structured metadata for banner copy from non-suppressed ad windows (confirmed + candidate; suppressed windows are excluded). NEVER the primary classifier — only used for banner enrichment.

Gated by CapabilitiesService. If Foundation Models unavailable, only banner enrichment degrades; detection and skip still work normally.

Implementation:
- Use Apple FoundationModels framework SystemLanguageModel
- Schema-bound guided generation via @Generable macro (iOS 26+)
- Input: transcript text from the detected ad window (evidenceText range)
- Output schema struct AdMetadataSchema: { advertiser: String?, product: String?, evidenceText: String, confidence: Double }
  NOTE: there is NO adDescription field; the schema has evidenceText (verbatim transcript support), not adDescription
- Evidence-bound: only extract when transcript text clearly backs it
- If extraction confidence < 0.60 (AdBannerView.metadataConfidenceThreshold), banner falls back to generic copy
  NOTE: the 0.7 confidence threshold described previously is incorrect; the gate is 0.60 in AdBannerView.bannerCopy(for:)
  FoundationModelExtractor itself does not apply a confidence cutoff — it returns all results; the banner view gates on 0.60
- Prompt versioned via MetadataPromptVersion.current ("metadata-v1"); stored in AdWindow.metadataPromptVersion
- Re-run lazily when prompt version changes (MetadataExtractorFactory.needsReExtraction checks promptVersion only; no system model version tracking)
- Never sole reason a skip fires — only enriches metadata AFTER detection

Backfill only — runs on non-suppressed AdWindows (confirmed + candidate) after skip has already fired. Never on the hot path.
  NOTE: AdDetectionService step 15 comment confirms: "Extract metadata for windows visible to the user (confirmed + candidate, not suppressed)."
  The prior description's "confirmed AdWindows" was inaccurate — candidate windows also receive metadata extraction.

Error handling:
- Model not available → skip enrichment, return nil (guard returns before any model call)
- Model returns low-confidence → banner degrades gracefully (confidence check is in AdBannerView.bannerCopy(for:), not extractor)
- Model errors (refusal, decodingFailure, etc.) → FoundationModelExtractor throws the error; AdDetectionService.swift (line 1576) catches and logs a warning — net effect is no metadata update, extraction skipped gracefully
  NOTE: The extractor throws rather than returning nil on errors; "return nil" in prior description was inaccurate. The caller handles the throw.
- NOTE: There is no 5-second hard timeout in FoundationModelExtractor; the timeout claim was incorrect
- NOTE: There is no "max 5 ad windows per minute" rate limit implemented in FoundationModelExtractor; the rate limit claim was incorrect

Acceptance criteria:
- Extracts advertiser/product from clear transcript evidence (e.g., "brought to you by Squarespace" → advertiser: "Squarespace")
- Falls back gracefully (nil) when Foundation Models unavailable
- Falls back gracefully (nil) when evidence is ambiguous
- Schema-bound output only — no free-form generated text (AdMetadataSchema constrains output)
- Prompt version tracked in every AdWindow it enriches (metadataPromptVersion field)
- Never blocks hot-path detection or skip orchestration
- Works correctly when CapabilitiesService reports locale not supported

Implementation notes (code-verified):
- AdMetadataSchema fields: advertiser (String?), product (String?), evidenceText (String, verbatim transcript support), confidence (Double)
- AdMetadataSchema and AdMetadata have no adDescription field; AdWindow (persistence struct) retains a legacy adDescription column always set to nil
- metadataSource stored as "foundationModels" (String) when FM extractor runs; "fallback" when FallbackExtractor runs; "none" for no extraction
- FallbackExtractor (used when FM unavailable) produces source: "fallback", confidence ~0.1–0.3
- CapabilitiesService.currentSnapshot.canUseFoundationModels gates MetadataExtractorFactory.makeExtractor
- On model errors: FoundationModelExtractor.extract() throws; AdDetectionService catch block at line 1576 logs warning and continues — no crash, no metadata written
- Metadata extraction runs on ALL non-suppressed windows (confirmed + candidate), not just confirmed

title: Settings View
description:
Settings screen providing user control over all configurable behaviors. All settings persist via UserPreferences in SwiftData.

Sections:
1. **Ad Skip Behavior**: auto / manual / off (segmented control). Explains each mode.
2. **Playback Defaults**: default speed (picker: 0.5x–3.0x), skip intervals (±15s or ±30s)
3. **Models**: WhisperKit model selection with per-model size display, download/delete buttons, download progress. Shows currently active model.
4. **Storage**: breakdown showing model files, cached audio, transcript DB, total. Per-category clear buttons. Shows remaining device storage.
5. **Background Processing**: WiFi only toggle, charging only toggle, low-power fallback explanation
6. **Purchase**: "Restore Purchases" button (only shows when not premium). Premium status indicator.
7. **About**: version, build number, "Your podcasts never leave your device" privacy statement

Design: Quiet Instrument aesthetic. Uses design tokens. Grouped list style. No custom chrome — let the content breathe.

Acceptance criteria:
- All settings persist across app launches via SwiftData
- Skip behavior change takes effect immediately (no restart)
- Model download shows progress bar with percentage and size remaining
- Model delete frees disk space and ModelInventory updates
- Storage sizes accurate within 1MB
- Restore Purchases calls StoreKit and updates entitlement state
- VoiceOver: all controls accessible with descriptive labels
- Renders correctly with Dynamic Type up to AX3

title: AdmissionController 'enqueue of 1000 jobs completes quickly' fails the SERIAL perf pass by 617 microseconds
description:
Found running scripts/perf-tests.sh for playhead-o89d on 2026-08-13, once its destination was fixed (the pass could not start before that, so nobody had seen this).

    Expectation failed: elapsed < 0.1
    1000 enqueues should be < 100ms (was 0.10061705112457275s)

Parallelism off, 13 tests in 12 suites, nothing else on the box. A 0.6 % margin is not a budget: the assertion's own comment says it exists to catch an O(n log n) per-insert regression, and at 0.6 % it cannot distinguish one from ordinary variance. Either the constant needs re-deriving from a measured distribution (median of N, with the spread stated) or the test needs a shape check rather than a wall-clock one — e.g. compare 1,000 against 10,000 enqueues and assert the ratio, which is what 'not O(n log n) per insert' actually claims and is indifferent to the box.

NOT widened in o89d: that bead is explicitly forbidden from loosening assertions.

title: a caller that JOINS an in-flight background-session crossing gets its refusal unlogged and unrecorded
description:
FOUND by playhead-gpdb R1 review, 2026-08-13. Narrow, but it is a hole in exactly the record gpdb exists to create.

`DownloadManager.backgroundSession(for:requestedBy:)` joins concurrent callers onto one crossing:

    if let inFlight = _sessionCreationsInFlight[resolvedRole] {
        return await inFlight.value
    }

The joiner returns the Task's value directly. On a REFUSAL that value is `nil`, and the joiner takes neither of the two reporting paths — no `logger.error`, and no `invariantRecorder?(.backgroundSessionCreationRefused, ...)`. Only the ORIGINATOR reports, and it reports its OWN `site=`.

CONSEQUENCE for a device pull, which is the surface gpdb built. The refusal record's `site=` field is load-bearing precisely because the four sites have unrelated consequences (a refused `background_download` is one retryable episode; a refused `background_relaunch_wake` is a launch that will now deliver no completion callbacks at all). When two sites race, the stream shows one of them and silently drops the other — so a pull can read `site=transfer_retirement` for a window in which a `background_relaunch_wake` was ALSO refused, and conclude the wake was never attempted.

WINDOW. A joiner exists only between the crossing completing and the originator resuming to clear `_sessionCreationsInFlight` — microseconds, and only for genuinely concurrent callers on the same resolved role. Note this does NOT cover the `retireBackgroundTransfers` loop: with `useDualBackgroundSessions` false all three roles resolve to `.legacy`, but the loop is sequential, so on a refusal each iteration starts its own crossing and each reports.

REMEDY when someone takes it: move the log + record out of the originator-only path so any caller that observes `nil` reports its own site — or have the joiner report on its own after `await inFlight.value` returns nil. Cheap either way; it is filed rather than fixed because it is a diagnostic-fidelity defect inside a race, not a behavioural one.

RELATED, same loop, also not fixed: on a refusal `retireBackgroundTransfers` pays the 10 s bound THREE TIMES for what resolves to one identifier (three sequential crossings for `.interactive`/`.maintenance`/`.legacy`, all resolving to `.legacy` when the 24cm flag is off), and writes three refusal records for one daemon stall. Before gpdb the same loop paid one unbounded construction, so this is strictly better than what it replaced — but a reader of the invariant stream counting refusals will over-count by 3x on the deletion path, and a user deleting a cached episode waits 30 s rather than 10.

title: the mode gate in evaluateWindow lost its coverage to wq34's diversion — two of the three remaining doors are still unprobed
description:
FOUND 2026-08-13 by the R1 review round on playhead-wq34, by mutating the production behaviour each of the 37 repaired tests was written to protect.

WHAT WAS LOST. Before wq34, at least three tests reddened when `SkipOrchestrator.evaluateWindow`'s `.manual` arm was changed to return `.applied` instead of `.confirmed` — `manualModeNoAutoSkip`, `userMarkDoesNotAutoSkipInManualMode`, and `eligibleNonAutoModesStayNonAuto`. Each delivered a row through `receiveAdWindows`/`receiveAdDecisionResults` on a non-`.auto` show and asserted no `.applied` decision, so the mode switch was the thing under test.

After wq34 those rows are DIVERTED to the suggest tier and never reach the mode switch at all. The repairs are honest about it — they now assert the diversion — but nothing replaced the mode-gate claim.

MEASURED, not inferred. R1 mutant M9 (`case .manual:` in `evaluateWindow` returns `.applied`) run against the FULL `PlayheadFastTests` plan: `RED (76 known / 4 NEW)`, and all four NEW are in the scheduler/grant/checkpoint families that the same box produces on a clean tree. Zero failures on this surface. M10 (the `.shadow` arm) survives the 133-test wq34 scope identically.

WHY IT MATTERS: THE ARM IS STILL LIVE. Three production paths put a row in `windows` without passing an admission door, so the mode switch is the only thing between them and a skip:
  * `injectUserMarkedAd` — the in-session "Hearing an ad" / transcript mark — writes STRAIGHT into `windows` and calls `evaluateAndPush` (playhead-d2it).
  * A row admitted while its class was `.auto` and demoted mid-episode by the skip control (playhead-4xw4).
  * `acceptSuggestedSkip`'s promoted row when `confirmationWouldSkip` refuses the extent: it stays `.confirmed` in `windows` and is re-evaluated (playhead-k683).

CLOSED IN THIS ROUND, PARTLY. R1 added `managedRowOnANonAutoShowIsNeverSkipped` to `EligibilityLadderMonotonicityTests`, which reaches the arm through `injectUserMarkedAd` for both `.shadow` and `.manual` and kills M9/M10. This bead is the REMAINDER: the other two doors (4xw4's mid-episode demotion, k683's refused-extent promotion) are still unprobed, and both are states a listener can actually be in.

title: the suggest tier has NO scrubber presence: broadcastAppliedSegments reads only the managed map, so a card is a span's entire visible life
description:
FOUND 2026-08-13 implementing playhead-wq34, by asking what a diverted row LOSES rather than only what it gains.

`SkipOrchestrator.broadcastAppliedSegments` filters `windows` (the managed map) to `.applied || .confirmed`, and that stream is the ONLY source of `NowPlayingViewModel.adSegmentRanges` — the ad bands on the scrubber. `suggestWindows` is never read by it.

So a mark-only span has never had any scrubber presence at all, and after wq34 a row diverted from the managed tier loses the band it used to get as a silent `.confirmed`. The trade is monotone overall — an actionable card strictly dominates a passive band, which is why wq34 took it — but it means a suggest span's ENTIRE visible life is one card that fires once, on playhead entry, and is gone.

WHY THAT IS WORTH FIXING SEPARATELY. `receiveAdWindows`' own comment says a `markOnly` window "is visible in the UI as a possible-ad marker". Measured on this tree, it is not: nothing reads suggest windows for display. The comment describes an intention nobody implemented, and it is the kind of stale claim that makes the next reader believe a surface exists.

It also interacts with playhead-d3g0's once-per-revision rule: a listener who dismisses the card, or who was not looking, has no second way to find the span. A band would be the durable half of the affordance.

SCOPE NOTE: this is a UX addition (more visible marks), not a correctness fix, so it is Dan's call in the same way wq34's "more cards" was. Do not fold it into a bug fix.

title: the wq34 monotonicity fallback routes at ADMISSION, so a mid-episode skip-control demotion still silences already-admitted managed windows
description:
FOUND 2026-08-13 while implementing playhead-wq34, and named there rather than fixed because it is a different decision point.

wq34 routes a row to the suggest tier at ADMISSION — `receiveAdWindows` / `receiveAdDecisionResults` — because that is the one place per door where tier membership is decided, and because the tiers must stay disjoint (playhead-rfu-sad).

`activeDetectorSkipModes` has exactly two writers. `beginEpisode` clears `windows` on its way through, so a mode resolved there cannot disagree with an admitted row. `SkipOrchestrator.setActiveSkipMode` — the Settings / Now Playing pill — does NOT clear `windows`; it re-runs `evaluateAndPush()` over rows that were admitted under the OLD modes.

So: a window admitted to the managed tier while its class was `.auto`, and not yet `.applied`, goes SILENT if the listener turns the control down mid-episode. `evaluateWindow` returns a `.confirmed` nobody sees, exactly as it did before wq34. Its `.markOnly` twin would still card, because the suggest path never consults the mode.

This is pre-existing and unchanged by wq34, but it is now the ONLY place left where the eligibility ordinal inverts, which is why it is worth a bead of its own rather than a comment.

WHAT MAKES IT MORE THAN COSMETIC: the pill is how a listener says "stop skipping, just tell me". Under this defect that instruction silently costs them the marks as well as the skips, for every span already in flight.

NOT DONE HERE BECAUSE it is a re-route of live rows rather than an admission decision, and moving a window from `windows` to `suggestWindows` mid-episode has to answer questions admission does not: what happens to a row that has already bannered, to `banneredWindowIds`, to an armed-but-unfired suggestion for the same id. The rfu-sad invariant is exactly what a careless sweep would break.

COVERAGE TODAY: `EligibilityLadderMonotonicityTests.inSessionAppliedWindowIsNotDivertedToSuggest` drives `setActiveSkipMode(.manual)` mid-episode, but only to prove an APPLIED receipt survives it. The un-applied case is unprobed.
notes: 2026-08-13, during wq34 implementation: the UPWARD direction of this same gap turned out to be a REGRESSION wq34 would have shipped rather than a pre-existing one, so it was fixed in that bead rather than deferred here. Before wq34 a row delivered on a shadow show sat silently in the managed tier and `setActiveSkipMode(.auto)` promoted it on the spot; after the diversion it is a suggest card, and `evaluateAndPush` iterates `windows`, which no longer holds it — so 'turn auto-skip on' would have stopped working for everything already delivered. `SkipOrchestrator.readmitModeDivertedSuggestions` closes that by RE-DELIVERING the mode-eligible suggest rows through `receiveAdWindows` (one admission path, so the catalog fail-closed check and the terminal fences re-run for free). THIS BEAD IS THEREFORE DOWNWARD-ONLY: a row admitted to the managed tier under .auto, still un-applied when the listener turns the control DOWN, still goes silent. It was not fixed by the same mechanism because re-delivering a managed row resurrects one the runtime has since .suppressed — the producer row carries the original decisionState, not the runtime one.

title: the enumeration canary's .tasks narrowing is escapable through a typealias — verified, rc=0
a lost live-task enumeration lets the force-quit scan prompt for an episode that is still downloading, and the resume path then deletes its partial
description:
FOUND in playhead-rouw R1 review, 2026-08-13.

`ForceQuitResumeScan.liveBackgroundDownloadEpisodeIds` exists to SUPPRESS a force-quit resume prompt for an episode whose transfer the OS still owns. playhead-rouw routed its `await session.allTasks` through the bound and made an unanswered session contribute nothing (`?? []`, ForceQuitResumeScan.swift:404). The comment says the cost is 'at most one dismissable phantom prompt, reconciled by the next scan', and cites the pre-existing case of a session the scan deliberately does not instantiate.

THE PREMISE IS RIGHT — this is the same failure mode, and the change is strictly better than the unbounded await it replaced, which could stall a cold launch forever. What R1 checked is the SIZE of 'at most one dismissable prompt', and it is larger than the phrase suggests.

An episode wrongly absent from `liveEpisodeIds` is not skipped at `scanForSuspendedTransfers`:287. It lands in `resumableTransferIds` with a `recordPreempted` row. If the user then accepts, `resumeSuspendedTransfer` (ForceQuitResumeScan.swift:441) has NO guard against a live transfer for the same episode — it checks for a complete pinned artifact, for a blob, for blob emptiness, and for validator freshness, and none of those knows about an in-flight task. On the validator-mismatch branch it calls `removeAllAudioArtifacts(for:)` and `deletePin(for:)` and starts a FRESH `backgroundDownload`. So the outcomes are a second concurrent OS transfer for one episode, and on the fresh path the deletion of the partial the live transfer is still building toward.

`backgroundDownload`'s in-flight reservation (`bgInFlightEpisodes`) does not stop this: a transfer reattached from a previous process is not in it, which is the same gap as playhead-sq80.

WHY THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED. The exposure predates playhead-rouw — an uninstantiated session already produced it — and rouw only widens the population from 'sessions we chose not to bring up' to 'sessions whose daemon was slow for 10 s'. Closing it means adding a live-transfer guard to `resumeSuspendedTransfer`, which is a behaviour change to the resume path and outside rouw's ceiling.

RELATED, and worth reading together: playhead-ia9y asks whether 10 s is the right bound for this call site at all, given its documented 2 s SLA. If the scan's bound came down, this window would shrink with it — but not close, because the uninstantiated-session case has no timeout to shorten.

title: the enumeration bound is one SERIAL queue for three sessions, so one silent session costs all three
description:
FOUND in playhead-rouw R1 review, 2026-08-13, checking whether the enumerationIO separation is sufficient or merely moved the contention.

playhead-rouw gave background-task ENUMERATION its own `BackgroundSessionIO` instance so a stalled enumeration cannot starve `downloadTask(with:)`. That separation is measured and correct: sharing the instance produced 17 blown bounds and 217 lost test verdicts in one full-plan run, own queue produced 4 and 3.

WHAT IT DID NOT DO is make the enumerations independent of EACH OTHER. `BackgroundSessionIO`'s work queue is serial by design (the file's own comment: an unbounded concurrent queue would answer a wedged daemon with a thread explosion), and `retireBackgroundTransfers` (DownloadManager.swift:2751) adds one child task per distinct background session to a `withTaskGroup`, all submitting to the SAME `enumerationIO`. With a silent first session:

  * body A runs, its inner `DispatchSemaphore` latch waits the full 10 s;
  * B and C never reach the front, so their OUTER deadlines fire at 10 s and they return nil having never asked their daemon anything;
  * when A finally returns, B and C hit `mayRunBody() == false` and log 'starved: reached the daemon queue after its caller had already given up'.

The CALLER-side bound is intact — nobody waits more than `io.timeout`, which is what the code comment claims and it is true. The cost is coverage: one silent session loses the identities of all three, so `retireBackgroundTransfers` falls back to the admitted-identity map for sessions that were perfectly healthy.

WHY THIS IS P3 AND NOT P2. `useDualBackgroundSessions` defaults to false (PreAnalysisConfig.swift:25), and `retireBackgroundTransfers` dedups by session identifier, so production instantiates ONE session today and the amplification is latent. It is user-togglable in Settings (flag 24cm), so it is not unreachable. Every `allTasks` timeout observed in the three post-fix full-plan runs names `com.playhead.episode-downloads` — the legacy identifier — which is consistent with the flag being off in the test suite too.

THE SHAPE OF A FIX, and it is a design question rather than a patch: the right concurrency here is bounded by the number of sessions (three), not one and not unbounded. Either give each session its own `onItsOwnQueue` sibling — the mechanism playhead-rouw already added — or make the enumeration queue `.concurrent` with a width cap. The first reuses existing machinery and keeps 'a wedge strands exactly one thread' true per session; it costs two DispatchQueues per session per DownloadManager instance, which matters in a test suite that builds thousands of managers. That tradeoff is why R1 filed it rather than choosing.

Do not fix this by widening the queue without also re-reading BackgroundSessionIO.swift's header: the serial choice is load-bearing against a thread explosion, and the cap is the part that must survive.

title: the trust episode claim is spent BEFORE a mutate that can silently fail — the exact failure both writers' docs say the ordering prevents
description:
FOUND 2026-08-12 (playhead-mn5e R5). Both new writers state this invariant as absolute, and neither holds it.

THE STATED INVARIANT, twice, in the branch's own prose:
  * AnalysisStore.swift:14061 — "The claim is taken only when the observation is actually recorded."
  * AdDetectionService.swift:12938 — "A claim standing for an observation nobody made would cost the show that episode's credit permanently."

WHAT THE CODE DOES. `claimEpisodeTrustObservation` is its own statement and commits the row. Then:
  * `AdDetectionService.recordConfirmedWindowObservation` claims (:13010) and then calls `TrustScoringService.recordSuccessfulObservation` (:13048). That method's `store.mutateProfile` sits in `do { … } catch { logger.warning(…); return }` (TrustScoringService.swift:579) and the method returns Void — the caller cannot learn it failed, and does not check.
  * `TrustScoringService.recordCorrectObservation` claims (:1029) and then calls `store.updateProfileIfExistsCapturing` in a `do { … } catch { … return }` (:1046). Same shape, one actor down.

So a transient SQLite failure between the claim and the mutate spends the claim on an observation nobody recorded, and the row is a permanent claim: `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` means no later backfill or tap can ever count that episode for that show.

SEVERITY, honestly. Conservative direction (a show is under-credited by one episode, never over-credited), and store errors on this path are rare. It is filed because the invariant is asserted as absolute in two places and is relied on by the reasoning that chose "claim before mutate" over "mutate then claim" — the ORDER was chosen specifically to avoid this failure, and the order alone does not achieve it.

DIRECTION. Either (a) have `recordSuccessfulObservation` / the correct-observation mutate return whether the write landed, and DELETE the claim row when it did not, or (b) run the claim and the profile mutate inside one `AnalysisStore` transaction so they commit or roll back together — which is also what makes "the claim and the test are ONE statement" true end to end rather than only inside the claim itself.

title: the Library row's Transcript link appears at download time and opens an empty reader
description:
playhead-fzrw R5 finding F-C (verified, filed not fixed — LOW, and arguably a product judgement rather than a defect).

Playhead/Views/Library/EpisodeListView.swift:639 gates the expanded row''s Transcript NavigationLink on resolvedAnalysisAssetId != nil, which loadSummary sets at :696 whenever store.fetchAssetByEpisodeId(key) returns a row (:686). Same defect class as fzrw''s F1/F3: 'an asset row exists' read as 'there is a transcript to open'.

The comment at :633-638 states the intended contract in words: 'Available once the row has resolved an analysis asset id (so the FullTranscriptViewModel has something to fetch). When resolution is still pending the link is omitted rather than rendered disabled — the row collapses cleanly to just Play until analysis catches up.'

playhead-fzrw registers the row at download time, so for a downloaded-but-unanalysed episode the link now appears up to the measured 13,678 s before any transcript exists. Pre-bead the row arrived when the lane STARTED, which is still before transcript content but only by seconds.

USER-VISIBLE OUTCOME IS MILD: FullTranscriptView renders a graceful empty state, 'No transcript yet' (Playhead/Views/Transcript/FullTranscriptView.swift:158-195). Reasonable people could call the new behaviour neutral or even better than a silently-absent link — which is why this is filed rather than fixed.

CANDIDATE REMEDY if it is judged a regression: in loadSummary, set resolvedAnalysisAssetId only when the asset has transcript reach (asset.fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime != nil), so the link means what its own comment says.

title: the duplicate-asset fold silently declines to adopt a completion terminal when the SURVIVOR's analysisState is not a SessionState
description:
FILED BY playhead-fzrw R2 review (outside that bead's ceiling).

`AnalysisStore.foldDuplicateAssetsIntoSurvivor` adopts a victim's completion
terminal onto the survivor only if BOTH states parse
(AnalysisStore.swift:19416-19420):

    guard let victimState = SessionState(rawValue: victim.analysisState),
          victimState.isTerminalCompletion,
          let survivorState = SessionState(rawValue: try currentAnalysisState(id: survivor.id)),
          !survivorState.isTerminalCompletion
    else { return outcome }

A survivor whose `analysisState` does not parse fails the guard, so the merged row
KEEPS its own non-terminal state and the victim's `terminalReason` (which carries
the coverage numbers) is dropped. The nil-parse case was written for "the row is
gone" — `currentAnalysisState` returns `""` on a missing row and the doc at :19430
says so explicitly — but it now also covers a LIVE row in a state the enum does
not name.

REACHABLE SINCE playhead-fzrw R2, which registers download-time rows as
`AnalysisAsset.registeredNotQueuedState` (`"new"`, the column's own schema
DEFAULT, deliberately not a `SessionState` because no session exists). Such a row
can be the survivor of a fold.

SEVERITY IS LOW AND THE DIRECTION IS SAFE: the outcome is an UNDER-claim — a
merged row reads as not-complete rather than falsely complete — and the sweep is
one-shot (`did_duplicate_asset_reconcile_v1`), already spent on shipped devices,
so it can only bite a device that has not yet run it. It is filed because the
guard's INTENT ("do not downgrade a survivor that already owns a terminal") is
satisfied by a survivor in `"new"`: it owns no terminal, so adoption is exactly
what should happen.

SUGGESTED SHAPE (not a decision): distinguish "no row" from "a row whose state is
not a terminal completion". `currentAnalysisState` could return `String?` so the
missing-row case stays a refusal, and a present-but-unparseable state is treated
as not-a-terminal-completion, which is what it is.

title: PlayheadRuntime's force-quit-scan comment understates when the scan was skipped, which is what hid hyht being dead
description:
CARRIED FROM playhead-hkh6, closed 2026-08-11 as decided-by-default.

hkh6 flagged that cnql R1's fix silently activates playhead-hyht's force-quit resume scan, which had been dead in production since it shipped. cnql merged as #367 (ff338693), so option (a) — let it activate — already happened, and option (b) can no longer prevent the first-launch burst it was written to prevent.

WHAT SURVIVES: the comment at PlayheadRuntime.swift:3044 still reads that the skip was logged 'on exactly those launches' (headless ones). It was EVERY launch — DownloadManager.shared was nil at didFinishLaunching universally, because registerShared had one call site inside a SwiftUI .task, which runs after didFinishLaunching returns.

That understatement is precisely what hid a dead scan for as long as it did: a reader checking whether hyht ran would conclude it ran on ordinary launches. Fix the comment to say every launch.

Comment-only. Fold into the next PlayheadRuntime bead.

title: Two source comments still assert the pre-ar60 coupling between mark confidence and the preload floor, and are now false
description:
CARRIED FROM playhead-4f3h, closed 2026-08-11 as premise-severed.

4f3h's thesis was that SpecialistMarkComposer and AdPodContinuation both pin mark confidence at exactly 0.70 'so the mark survives cross-launch preload'. After playhead-ar60 (#363) split detection from actuation and playhead-atr3 moved the floor, SkipOrchestrator.preloadAdmissibleWindows filters on actuationConfidence >= preloadConfidenceThreshold (SkipOrchestrator.swift:2258-2264). The DETECTION confidence these composers mint no longer governs preload at all.

WHAT SURVIVES, and it is the whole of this bead: two comments still state the old coupling as fact.
  - SpecialistMarkComposer.swift:63-66
  - AdPodContinuation.swift:208-213

A comment that asserts a false invariant is worse than no comment: the next reader tunes 0.70 believing it controls preload, and it does not. Both should say what the constant now does — and does not — do.

Comment-only. Do it inside the next bead that touches either file rather than as its own cycle.

title: final_pass_jobs has no retryCount cap, and playhead-jzj0 widened which rows can retry
description:
FILED from playhead-jzj0 as a named residual risk of that fix, not as a defect it introduced.

AnalysisStore.swift (~:17268) documents the design explicitly: final-pass retries are bounded by the admission gates (charge, nominal thermal, low-power, disk), not by a retryCount cap; each launch re-admits queued/deferred/failed rows and each failure bumps retryCount.

Before jzj0 that policy had an accidental second bound. The runner's eligibility filter required endTime > analysis_assets.finalPassCoverageEndTime, so once any span drove the frontier past a failing job, that job stopped being re-admitted — permanently. It looked like a retry cap but it was the ordering defect jzj0 fixed, and it 'capped' correct retries and incorrect ones alike. On the 2026-08-02 V47 pull (db-evening2) exactly this had happened: asset F7BB38BB holds a failed job for span 0.000-72.180 that a completed 87.9-150.0 neighbour had made unreachable.

jzj0 removed that clause, which is correct — but it means a job that fails DETERMINISTICALLY (corrupt audio, a shard the recogniser always throws on) will now be retried on every launch that clears the admission gates, forever, incrementing retryCount without bound. Under the documented policy that is intended behaviour; it is simply exercised more often now.

Worth deciding, with numbers: what fraction of final_pass_jobs failures are transient (thermal, I/O, cancellation) versus deterministic? If a deterministic tail exists, a cap — or a backoff keyed on retryCount, which is already persisted — costs little. Do NOT add one on intuition: the admission gates already make the retry cheap, and a cap that fires on a transient failure reintroduces exactly the permanent-exclusion class jzj0 just closed.

title: Final-pass confidence floor (0.5) excludes mid-detection fusion candidates now that ar60 restored the DETECTION number
description:
FOUND during playhead-jzj0, establishing whether the bead's clause (a) survived playhead-ar60.

Pre-ar60 the fusion path wrote DecisionResult.skipConfidence into ad_windows.confidence, so FinalPassRetranscriptionRunner's 0.5 floor (defaultConfidenceFloor) compared an ACTUATION number against a DETECTION threshold and excluded fusion windows at 0.001-0.004. V47 fixed the semantics: confidence is now proposalConfidence.

The floor is therefore no longer pathological, but it IS now a live and differently-shaped filter. Simulating the V47 repair on the 2026-08-02 pull (db-corrected2, schema 46, asset DE0784D8) by joining decision_events the way migrateAdWindowSkipConfidenceSplitV47IfNeeded does, the five fusion rows' restored detection numbers are:

  fusion-fdb0b42c16139351  0.626  (clears)
  fusion-d4e332f1a5d9221c  0.553  (clears)
  fusion-7892299324c9e90f  0.488  (EXCLUDED)
  fusion-f8d4c169288e9a37  0.456  (EXCLUDED)
  fusion-05f4ddfceef0e09d  0.379  (EXCLUDED)

3 of 5 fall below 0.5, two of them by under 0.05. On the post-V47 device pull (db-evening2, schema 47) the picture is different again: 11 of 11 windows clear the floor, minimum 0.789 — so the floor excluded nothing there.

QUESTION, not an assertion of defect: 0.5 was chosen pre-ar60 against a column that meant something else. Nobody has re-derived it against the restored detection distribution. Numerator/denominator to establish: of the fusion windows that a listener would call a real ad, what fraction carry proposalConfidence below 0.5, and does re-transcribing them change any downstream verdict? The floor's stated purpose (runner header) is to avoid burning battery on candidates the classifier has not flagged, which is a legitimate policy — this bead only asks whether 0.5 is still the right number for the quantity it now reads.

Deliberately NOT changed in playhead-jzj0: that bead's scope was the watermark ordering gap, and the floor is a separate quantity with a separate justification.

title: An episode-keyed record can still be released or deleted by a caller that owns only one transfer
description:
Generalisation of playhead-7l6n, found in the playhead-nsjn R4 audit. 7l6n fixed ONE collection (bgInFlightEpisodes) by making its release conditional. Two related exposures remain. Both are narrow; neither is a regression from main. Filed so the class is recorded, not because nsjn should have fixed it.

(1) THE RESERVATION CAN BE STOLEN. backgroundDownload reserves bgInFlightEpisodes before its first suspension precisely so a second caller cannot start a duplicate transfer (see the comment at DownloadManager.swift:2478). But finishBackgroundTransfer's release is conditional on activeBackgroundTransfers, and during that suspension the reserving call has registered NOTHING. So any terminal callback for the same episode that completes in that window — handleBackgroundDownloadComplete or handleBackgroundDownloadFailed — finds no claimant and removes the episode, clearing a reservation it does not own. A third caller then passes the in-flight guard. Consequence is a duplicate transfer, de-duplicated downstream by the servingURLIfComplete guard at :3891, so it costs bandwidth rather than correctness. NOT worse than main: pre-bead, resumeSuspendedTransfer already ran an await (a network HEAD in currentServerValidator) with no reservation at all.

(2) deleteDownloadAttribution IS EPISODE-KEYED AND UNCONDITIONAL on both new timeout branches (:2506 and :2540) — the same shape 7l6n fixed one collection over. The reattached-completion claimant is immune because handleBackgroundDownloadComplete reads its attribution once up front at :3822 by design. Harm needs (1) above AND process death before the surviving transfer completes, and then it reappears as the playhead-kkzu defect: a NULL analysis_jobs.podcastId.

The general fix is to make an episode-keyed record claim-counted rather than presence-tested, which is architecture, not a patch.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
ABSORBS playhead-6kc0 and playhead-byfd (both closed 2026-08-11). All three are DownloadManager under a stalled daemon, all from playhead-nsjn R1-R4 within 72 hours.
  - 6kc0: verified the same two lines this bead names — deleteDownloadAttribution(episodeId:) at DownloadManager.swift:2506 and :2540. It carries the cheap fix (capture whether a sidecar already existed before persistDownloadAttribution); this bead carries the class plus a second distinct exposure, so this one survives.
  - byfd: the auto-download loop pays the nsurlsessiond bound PER EPISODE inside a ~30 s BGTask window — 2 x 10 s per episode, sequentially. Same file, same stalled-daemon condition.
Five P3s fell out of nsjn's reviews into two files; this is the DownloadManager half.

title: BackgroundSessionIO: run discardingLateResult on its own queue, not the work queue
description:
playhead-nsjn R2 hardening (filed, NOT a defect - see the reachability argument).

BackgroundSessionIO.perform (BackgroundSessionIO.swift:229-233):
    let value = body()
    if !waiter.deliver(value) { discard?(value) }

discard runs SYNCHRONOUSLY on the shared serial work queue and is unbounded. For a URLSession task discard is { $0.cancel() }, so a cancel that blocks strands the one queue thread that BackgroundSessionIO.shared owns process-wide, and every later background-session call then reports nil after its own 10s bound - downloads dead for the life of the process.

WHY THIS IS NOT A REACHABLE DEFECT. The discard only runs when the body RETURNED after the deadline (mayRunBody() blocks a body that had not started). So the daemon answered downloadTask(with:) - it is alive. For the following cancel to strand the queue the daemon must wedge again, and a synchronous XPC connection wedge is not per-message-kind: the same wedge that would block cancel also blocks creation. There is no state in which the discard-cancel takes the process from 'downloads work' to 'downloads dead' - it can only occur inside a wedge that has already done so. That failure is the one the file header explicitly declines to claim it fixes ('a wedged daemon still strands the one queue thread that is inside the XPC call, and work submitted behind it waits its own full deadline before reporting nil'), and the incremental cost over that accepted residual is zero.

WHY IT IS STILL WORTH DOING. It is the only work on that queue that NOBODY is waiting for, sharing the queue with work that callers ARE waiting for. Moving disposal to its own serial queue (the same reasoning the file already applies to deadlineQueue: 'the work queue is precisely the thing that may be blocked') means a wedged disposal costs disposals only, not new downloads. ~4 lines: add a third serial queue and change the call to 'disposalQueue.async { discard(value) }'. T is already Sendable so the capture is legal; the rail 'A result produced after the bound is handed to the discard hook' polls rather than assuming synchronous ordering, so it still passes.

title: abandonUnstartedTransfer over-releases the episode's in-flight slot when a second identity holds it
description:
playhead-nsjn R2 finding (LOW, filed not fixed).

DownloadManager.abandonUnstartedTransfer (DownloadManager.swift:2567) ends with an UNCONDITIONAL
    bgInFlightEpisodes.remove(episodeId)
where finishBackgroundTransfer (:2761) uses the conditional form
    if !activeBackgroundTransfers.values.contains(episodeId) { bgInFlightEpisodes.remove(episodeId) }

R1 assumed a second identity naming the same episode is impossible because of the in-flight guard in backgroundDownload. That is FALSE. The guard only governs backgroundDownload. handleBackgroundDownloadComplete (DownloadManager.swift:3817-3818) writes activeBackgroundTransfers[identity] = episodeId and inserts the episode in-flight with NO guard, for a task reattached from a prior process.

Reachable chain (all from source):
 1. backgroundDownload(E) reserves the slot, creates T1, registerBackgroundTransfer -> I1.
 2. It then suspends at 'await sessionIO.perform(resume:)'.
 3. The delegate hook (DownloadManager.swift:672-685) delivers a completion for a reattached prior-process task T2 (I2 != I1) through an unstructured Task, which hops onto the actor DURING that suspension. backgroundCallbackIsRetired is false on a cold launch, so :3817 registers I2 -> E.
 4. resume() times out -> abandonUnstartedTransfer(T1) removes I1 and then unconditionally drops E from bgInFlightEpisodes while I2 still names it.

Cost: bgInFlightEpisodes is not only the duplicate-transfer guard - it is also an EVICTION protection set (evictIfNeeded, :3505 and :3535). So the window admits (a) a redundant concurrent backgroundDownload(E) until the completion's pin lands and servingURLIfComplete(for: E) becomes non-nil, and (b) loss of eviction protection for the episode whose artifact is mid-placement.

Severity LOW: needs a cold launch after a force-quit (reattached completion) AND a >10s nsurlsessiond stall on resume(), and the exposure ends when the completion pins.

FIX: use finishBackgroundTransfer's conditional form. NOTE this also requires amending the rail 'Abandoning an unstarted transfer releases the episode's in-flight slot' (BackgroundSessionIOTests.swift:279), which registers a RANDOM identity and abandons a DIFFERENT one, so it currently asserts the over-release as correct. The sibling rail at :320 registers the MATCHING identity and would still pass.

Not fixed in R2: a production+test change costs two more clean review rounds on a P1 that unblocks every merge gate, for a narrow window whose harm is waste rather than corruption. Dan's call.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: REPRIORITIZED P2 -> P3 in the 2026-08-11 triage: real but off the critical path while completion is the binding constraint.

title: No rail proves production passes discardingLateResult at the two task-creation sites
description: BackgroundSessionIOTests.aLateResultIsDiscardedRatherThanDropped proves the EXECUTOR calls the hook it is given (verified in nsjn R1: it fails an implementation that abandons the loser). Nothing proves that backgroundDownload and resumeSuspendedTransfer actually SUPPLY 'discardingLateResult: { $0.cancel() }'. Deleting that argument from either call site compiles - the parameter is defaulted nil - and fails no test, while the consequence is the residue class the bead exists to stop producing: a task the daemon creates after the deadline, live, and tracked by nobody in this process. Not closed in R1 because reaching it needs a body that really is slow rather than refused, which no seam currently models. Fix shape: make the parameter non-defaulted at these call sites, or add a seam that delays rather than refuses.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: ABSORBS playhead-rl34 (closed 2026-08-11). Both are BackgroundSessionIO, both fell out of the playhead-nsjn review rounds within 72 hours: g5bh is 'no rail proves production passes discardingLateResult at the two task-creation sites', rl34 is 'run discardingLateResult on its own queue, not the work queue'. Same file, same seam, one diff. Note rl34's settled finding so it is not re-derived: the discard cancel is NOT independently reachable, because mayRunBody() means discard runs only when the body returned — i.e. the daemon answered — so its incremental cost over the accepted residual is zero. It is worth doing as hardening, not as a defect.

title: The auto-download loop pays the nsurlsessiond bound per episode inside a ~30s BGTask window
description: BackgroundFeedRefreshService enqueues auto-downloads in a strictly sequential loop ('for episode in toDownload { await downloader.enqueueBackgroundDownload(...) }'). Since playhead-nsjn each iteration can cost up to 2 x BackgroundSessionIO.defaultTimeout (creation + resume = 20s) when nsurlsessiond does not answer. That loop runs inside a background refresh task whose iOS budget is around 30s before the expiration handler fires, so ONE stalled episode consumes most of the window and two blow it. Strictly better than the pre-nsjn behaviour (an unbounded block that also burned a cooperative thread), so this is a tuning question, not a regression. Options: break the loop on the first daemon-unavailable (needs backgroundDownload to report started/not-started - see playhead-dpvo), or lower the bound for the background-refresh lane specifically. The 10s value itself is chosen, not measured.

title: A daemon-unavailable backgroundDownload can delete an attribution sidecar it does not own
description: Both daemon-unavailable paths in backgroundDownload call deleteDownloadAttribution(episodeId:) unconditionally. The sidecar is keyed by episode, not by transfer, and playhead-kkzu keeps it alive across process boundaries precisely because a suspended transfer's completion may land in a LATER process. bgInFlightEpisodes is process-local, so after a relaunch the OS can still own a live transfer for an episode this process believes is idle; if a caller then invokes backgroundDownload for it and the daemon stalls, the delete removes the LIVE transfer's sidecar and its eventual completion enqueues analysis with a NULL podcastId - the exact defect kkzu closed. Triple conjunct (relaunch + a caller the scan dedup was supposed to suppress + a stalled daemon), which is why it was filed rather than fixed in nsjn R1. Cheap fix shape: capture 'did a sidecar already exist' before persistDownloadAttribution and only delete when this call wrote it.

title: resumeSuspendedTransfer reports .redownloadedFresh for a fresh download that never started
description: The stale-validator branch of resumeSuspendedTransfer deletes the resume blob, the artifacts and the pin, then calls 'await backgroundDownload(...)' and returns .redownloadedFresh unconditionally. Since playhead-nsjn, backgroundDownload is fallible: it can return having started nothing because nsurlsessiond did not answer. So the outcome names a fresh download that did not happen, after the only copy of the fetched bytes has already been destroyed. The branch's own rail (staleResumeStillReportsFreshRedownload, BackgroundSessionIOTests.swift) asserts .redownloadedFresh under a stalled daemon and documents the reading 'the stale blob was discarded, which did happen' - defensible for that half of the contract but it leaves the caller unable to distinguish 'refetching' from 'gone, nothing running'. Low production impact TODAY only because resumeSuspendedTransfer has no production caller (tests only); it becomes user-visible the moment a Resume CTA is wired to it. Fix shape: give backgroundDownload a started/not-started result and propagate, or add a .redownloadFailed outcome.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: REPRIORITIZED P2 -> P3 in the 2026-08-11 triage: real but off the critical path while completion is the binding constraint.

title: .org and .io are the only TLDs with no bare-domain URL pattern, and one measured ad is invisible because of it
description:
Found while measuring playhead-absa; OUTSIDE its named term list
(.ai/.co/.fm/.tv), filed not fixed.

After absa, `EvidenceCatalogBuilder`'s URL patterns carry a bare-domain
form for .com/.ai/.co/.fm/.tv, but .org and .io remain PATH-ONLY
(`\b\w+\.org\/\w+`, `\b\w+\.io\/\w+`). A sponsor read that says the
domain without a path is therefore seen for five TLDs and missed for two.

MEASURED (2026-08-10, 94,692 transcript_chunks over 31 assets, fast +
final, 2026-08-02 device pull):

  `\b\w+\.org\b`   1 match, 1 in-ad, 0 on content.
                   16F3CB88 @ 5745.1 "Plan your summer visit at osb.org."
                   — the Old Sturbridge Village read, whose whole CTA is
                   that bare domain, currently invisible.
  `\b\w+\.io\b`    0 matches. No measured benefit and no measured cost.

Same structural argument as .ai: a literal dot with no space in front of
the TLD is not something ASR produces at a sentence boundary, which is
why the measured false-positive count for the whole bare-domain family
is zero.

Small, but do NOT land it without re-running the corpus eval — "org" is
a real English word in a way "ai" is not ("the org chart"), and the
protection here is only the no-space dot.

Acceptance: patterns added, `brandStem` separator list updated in step
(it already has ".org"/".io"), and the per-term census re-run so the
false-positive count is recorded rather than assumed.

title: the window-less veto gate admits a correction on a span the transcript no longer draws (SkipOrchestrator:4854)
description:
FILED FROM playhead-d666 R5 review (outside that bead's scope: orchestrator, and no behaviour changed on the branch — only the premise the code reasons from).

`SkipOrchestrator.revertByTimeRange`'s window-less branch (SkipOrchestrator.swift:4854-4861) admits a durable `manualVeto` `CorrectionEvent` only when some persisted `decoded_spans` row overlaps the range. Its stated justification:

    "A persisted `decoded_spans` row overlapping the range is exactly what
     distinguishes them — it IS what the transcript drew."

After playhead-d666 that sentence is false. The transcript no longer paints a span whose only anchor is `.sustainedMusicOffset`, so the gate now admits vetoes over audio the app never flagged to the listener. The consequence is not cosmetic: the correction is durable, it feeds `AnalysisStore.userVetoedTimeRanges` (:19511), and that suppresses every decoded span OVERLAPPING the vetoed range — claiming ones included.

Reachable via `TranscriptPeekView.submitNotAdChunks` (the header "Not ad" selection mode), which can select any rows, and via the residual unpainted-row popover (a ratified design call, Dan's).

This is the mildest of the four R5 filings: nothing regressed, the gate is merely reasoning from a premise the display seam no longer honours. Fix is to ask `carriesOnlyMusicPresenceHint` here too, or to restate the gate's purpose in terms of what is PERSISTED rather than what is DRAWN — the two are no longer the same population, and that is the thing worth writing down.

Also noted in the same sweep, not filed separately:
- `CorpusExporter.swift:714` emits every decoded span as a `"type": "decision"` record and counts it in `spanCount`, with no music-only marker. Analytics/corpus-eval only; `anchorProvenance` is exported verbatim so a downstream consumer can still tell.
- `TranscriptPeekViewModel.decodedSpansOverlapping(startTime:endTime:)` has ZERO production callers (tests only) and no claim filter. Dead code, and the next `.first` waiting to happen.
- `TimelineRailView` takes `[ClosedRange<Double>]` from the orchestrator, never a `DecodedSpan` — clean today, but its deferred "vend the DecodedSpan for the tapped segment" work is exactly where this class lands next.

title: The hot-path reconcile's skipConfidence forward (AdDetectionService:10470) is unpinnable today — buildAdWindow never sets it, so it forwards nil
description:
Filed by playhead-hcpa's copy-site survey (item 4 of the brief). NOT a live
defect — recorded so a future hot-path change cannot turn it into one silently.

THE SITE: `AdDetectionService.reconcileHotPathWindows`, the `preservedWindow`
copy, `skipConfidence: adWindow.skipConfidence`. `adWindow` there is the FRESH
row from this run, and the only producer of those rows is `buildAdWindow`
(AdDetectionService.swift:~12355), which does not pass `skipConfidence` at all.
So the forward is `nil -> nil` on every execution today, and deleting it is
behaviourally identical.

WHY IT WAS NOT PINNED. A rail would have to fabricate a two-number hot-path row
that production never produces — i.e. prove the mechanism works, not that anyone
uses it, which is the exact antipattern this repo keeps paying for. hcpa pinned
the two sites that ARE reachable with a two-number row and fail OPEN
(SkipOrchestrator:5754, PreRollStartClamp:276) and left this one measured.

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT LIVE: any change that gives the hot path an actuation number
distinct from `confidence` (hot-path calibration, or routing a fusion/corrected
row through `reconcileHotPathWindows`). At that moment the omission becomes a
fail-open of exactly hcpa's shape: `actuationConfidence` falls back to the
higher DETECTION score, and a span the user suppressed clears the 0.65 enter
threshold. Whoever makes that change owes the rail.

CHECK BEFORE CLOSING: `rg -n "skipConfidence" ` over `buildAdWindow` and every
other producer feeding `reconcileHotPathWindows`. If they all still pass nil,
this stays filed rather than fixed.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
Two refinements from playhead-hcpa's adversarial self-check — the original
framing understated the site, though the conclusion (do not pin now) stands.

1. "The forward is nil->nil" is only half true. The SOURCE row (`adWindow`) is
   indeed always a fresh `buildAdWindow` output with skipConfidence nil —
   verified: `adWindows` at AdDetectionService:4025 is built exclusively from
   the append at :3966 in the same function; `aggregatorWindows` and
   `correctionReplayWindows` are assembled separately and never reach
   `reconcileHotPathWindows`. But `existing` — the row being reconciled AGAINST
   — CAN carry a non-nil, correction-discounted skipConfidence:
   `currentHotPathCandidateWindows` filters on
   `detectorVersion == config.detectorVersion && decisionState == .candidate`
   (:10544-10548), and fusion rows are written with that same detector version
   and can be `.candidate`. So the site does not preserve a two-number row; it
   OVERWRITES a persisted actuation number with this run's nil.

   That is not a defect: it is ar60's explicit intent at :10465-10469 ("both
   confidences come from THIS run — taking them from different runs is how a
   row would come to report a detection score the actuation number never
   saw"), and same-geometry conservative `eligibilityGate` retention plus
   HotPathExtentGate's unanchored demotion keep the result off the auto-skip
   path. Recording it so the next reader does not mistake the site for inert.

2. Related, and the more likely place a future edit goes wrong invisibly:
   `CrossUserAnalysisSnapshot.Window.init`
   (AnalysisStore+CrossUserSharing.swift:202) declares
   `skipConfidence: Double? = nil`. Both production constructions forward it
   (:254 `init(adWindow:)`, :304 `exported(from:)`) and the one production
   actually calls (:814) is covered non-vacuously by
   `AnalysisStoreCrossUserSharingTests.skipConfidenceSurvivesExportAndImport`.
   But a defaulted parameter is the one shape that can be DROPPED silently —
   an omission is invisible to any grep for `skipConfidence:`. Worth a glance
   whenever this bead is picked up.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: KILLED 2026-08-11 in the full-backlog triage. VACUOUS AS WORK. Its own acceptance is 'this stays filed rather than fixed', and Dan's comment concludes the site 'is not a defect: it is ar60's explicit intent'. Verified buildAdWindow (AdDetectionService.swift ~:12392) constructs AdWindow( with no skipConfidence argument. A reviewer recording a fact, filed as work — and the knowledge already lives in the code comment at :10465-10469.

title: [bug] correctionReplayCandidates reads the RAW correctionType column, not effectiveCorrectionType — the one direction reader that does

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
FOUND IN playhead-q6y3 REVIEW (R1) while independently verifying that bead's central claim. Filed, not fixed: it is outside q6y3's scope and has ZERO live instances today, but it corrects a claim q6y3's own ESTABLISH note makes.

THE CLAIM (q6y3 R0, and its code comment at NowPlayingView.swift:451-458): "Every live read-side consumer keys on `event.source?.kind` ... and reads `correctionType` only as the legacy FALLBACK when source is nil."

That is true of eight readers — correctionPassthroughFactor, both correctionBoostFactor overloads, correctionFactorSnapshot, activeFalse{Positive,Negative}Scopes, TrainingExampleMaterializer, LearningArtifactIngestor.applySponsorSideEffect — and FALSE of one:

  AdDetectionService.correctionReplayCandidates (AdDetectionService.swift:11789, :11799)
      for event in replayEvents where event.correctionType == .falsePositive { ... }
      for event in replayEvents where event.correctionType == .falseNegative { ... }

This is a live production path (the correction-replay synthesizer that re-emits user-reported misses as suggest-tier windows). It reads the RAW optional column, so it consults neither `source?.kind` NOR `effectiveCorrectionType` — the accessor that exists precisely to resolve this. A row with `correctionType == nil` is invisible to BOTH loops, so a legacy `.manualVeto` veto does not mask an overlapping FN range, and a legacy FN is never replayed.

WHY IT DOES NOT BITE TODAY, measured: device pull (scratchpad/db-corrected2/analysis.sqlite, read from a copy) has 30 correction_events rows and 0 of 30 with `correctionType IS NULL` — every production writer sets `correctionType` and `source` in the same initializer. The legacy nil-column population the fallback was written for does not exist on this device.

WHY IT IS STILL WORTH CLOSING: the whole q6y3/ar60 family of bugs is "two fields that mean the same thing, read inconsistently in different places". This is the last reader that has not been brought onto the one accessor, and it is the only one where the divergence is silent in BOTH directions rather than defaulting to the safe one.

FIX: `event.effectiveCorrectionType == .falsePositive` / `== .falseNegative`, or (preferable, matching the other eight) `event.source?.kind`. Note `effectiveCorrectionType` collapses the four boundary-shift types to FP via the ingestor's `kindFor` only in the ingestor — here the raw switch would newly admit `.startTooEarly` etc., so pick the predicate deliberately rather than by search-and-replace.

NOT A REGRESSION FROM q6y3: q6y3's button now writes `source` and `correctionType` in agreement, and this function additionally requires `case .exactTimeSpan`, which a `sponsorOnShow` scope never satisfies — so the always-skip-sponsor row never reaches either loop in any direction.

Related: playhead-q6y3, playhead-ar60.

title: AnalysisStore.backfillJobPodcastId accepts an empty podcastId, and a '' write is irreversible
description:
Unreachable today (the ONLY caller, AnalysisCoordinator.resolveShowIdentity, passes a value that already cleared RecurrenceMaterialIdentity.canonicalIdentifier, hence non-empty) — filed because the consequence of reaching it is permanent.

backfillJobPodcastId is 'UPDATE analysis_jobs SET podcastId = ? WHERE episodeId = ? AND podcastId IS NULL'. Passing '' fills every unattributed row of the episode with the empty string. There is no path back: the WHERE clause matches only NULL, so a later correct repair changes 0 rows. And fetchRecordedPodcastId filters on 'podcastId IS NOT NULL', so it would then return '' forever — which canonicalIdentifier rejects, so the coarse phase falls to the episode-store resolver on EVERY scan and, on any window without a resolver, refuses the episode permanently with no repair possible. That is strictly worse than the NULL it replaced.

The method's doc deliberately declines to restate the identity policy, citing playhead-fil5 R2 (a duplicated policy that agrees is one no mutant can kill). That argument is about the CANONICALITY rule and is right. It does not cover a precondition that refuses the one value that is provably destructive to the column's own recovery reader — a guard a test can kill by passing '' and asserting 0 rows changed.

Suggested shape: refuse '' at the store boundary (throw, or return 0 with a logged warning — NOT a silent 0, which would be indistinguishable from the idempotent steady state). Measured: 0 of 72 analysis_jobs rows carry '' on the 2026-08-08 pull, so nothing needs migrating.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
ABSORBS playhead-05mk and playhead-h0hy (both closed 2026-08-11). Three P3 cycles for three WRITES OF ONE RULE: an absent podcast id must not be stored as though it named a thing.
  - 05mk: the runner's mint writes "" raw, where SemanticScanClaim.claimRow maps "" -> nil. Two claim mechanisms disagreeing on the same empty value.
  - h0hy: the .refreshed branch never fills a NULL podcastId.
  - this bead: AnalysisStore.backfillJobPodcastId accepts "" and the write is irreversible.
Two files, one afternoon — versus 6 to 15 review rounds across three separate bead cycles. Fix them as one rule with one test that pins all three writers.

title: A refreshed semantic scan claim keeps backfill_jobs.podcastId NULL forever, so a device pull cannot group claims by show
description:
Found by the adversarial review of playhead-vtjx; outside that bead (it is fil5's row, and vtjx repairs analysis_jobs, not backfill_jobs).

SemanticScanClaim.record (Playhead/Services/AdDetection/SemanticScanClaim.swift:519-539) sets podcastId only on the INSERT path via claimRow. When a row already exists it takes the .refreshed branch, and AnalysisStore.markBackfillJobDeferred updates deferReason only. So a claim minted while the show was unknown keeps backfill_jobs.podcastId = NULL for the life of the asset even after the show becomes known.

All five claim rows on the 2026-08-08 pull carrying scan_claim:podcast_id_missing (DE0784D8, AD5F3A0A, 53FC53E3, 83592353, and 44F076BB) are in exactly this state, and they stay there after playhead-vtjx: vtjx repairs analysis_jobs.podcastId, which is what the SCAN reads (AssetInputs.podcastId comes from the runBackfill argument, AdDetectionService.swift:9491), so the scan itself is unaffected. What is affected is diagnostics: the standing device-pull query 'SELECT analysisAssetId, deferReason FROM backfill_jobs WHERE deferReason LIKE ''scan_claim:%''' cannot be grouped or joined by show for exactly the population whose refusal was ABOUT the show.

Not a regression and not urgent — recorded so it is not mistaken for one later. Adjacent to (but distinct from) the settled playhead-05mk, which is about the two claim mechanisms disagreeing on an EMPTY podcastId at insert time; this is about the refresh path never writing one at all.

LIKELY FIX: have the .refreshed branch also fill podcastId when the row holds NULL and the caller supplied a canonical identity — the same 'fill only NULLs, never re-point' rule AnalysisStore.backfillJobPodcastId uses.

title: mutation-battery: full FOCUSED_SUITES baseline is red with load-flake timeouts (48-120s) on a quiet box — SS-series verdicts were obtained via the documented narrowed-FOCUSED_SUITES isolated run
description: Observed 2026-08-08 during playhead-3oyz R1 review: 'scripts/mutation-battery.sh --batch 700' baseline (UNMUTATED tree, one xcodebuild on the box) failed ~20 tests, every one a 48-120s timeout in suites the branch never touched (listen-revert/banner calibration, scheduler queue/deadline, migration-ladder v42/v44) — the same load-sensitive families CLAUDE.md names for the full gate. The battery's FOCUSED_SUITES union has grown large enough that its baseline now behaves like a mini full-run and starves those families. The battery correctly refused (exit 2, 'Fix the tree first'). Workaround used (per the script's own line-6140 precedent): a temporary narrowed FOCUSED_SUITES for an isolated run — baseline green in ~80s, all six SS rails KILLED. Follow-up options: per-series FOCUSED_SUITES scoping (run only the selected rails' victim suites), or admit the gate-baseline tolerance into the battery baseline. Logs: scratchpad batt-3oyz-700.log (red full-list run) vs batt-3oyz-narrow-*.log (green).
close_reason: duplicate of playhead-ehz2 (settled): the FOCUSED_SUITES baseline starvation redness is already tracked there. This R1-review observation (2026-08-08, playhead-3oyz SS-series run: full-list baseline red with 48-120s timeouts on a quiet box; narrowed isolated run green, all 6 SS rails KILLED) is additional evidence for ehz2, not a new issue.

title: 13kf ordering chain does not pin loop-start-after-coarse; and coarse-phase candidacy skips the reconciler's finalize floor + pending-work guard (policy question for Dan)
description: Two non-counted R1 findings on playhead-13kf. (1) TEST GAP: the ordering pin (BackfillCoarseFirstOrderTests, queue snapshot at coarse entry) kills delete-call-site and coarse-after-drain, but nothing pins ensureSchedulerLoopStarted() AFTER runPendingCoarseScans — moving loop-start above the coarse call stays green whenever the run loop's first dispatch loses the race, yet the handler comment calls that order load-bearing ('does not set the run loop dispatching a grant-long pass in parallel with the scan'). A deterministic pin needs a loop-started observation point on AnalysisWorkScheduler; none exists, and adding one is new surface — hence filed, not fixed. (2) POLICY: runPendingCoarseScans drives fetchAssetIdsMissingCoverageLaneJobs(limit:8, offset:0) RAW, while the shipped fil5 consumer (AnalysisJobReconciler.mintSemanticScanClaimsThrowing) applies transcriptClearsFinalizeFloor + the active-episode guard one layer up. So the phase spends grant FM on below-floor assets (2 of 4 zero-row assets on the 2026-08-03 pull) and can drive an asset whose episode is mid-pass in the live process (qk44 shape), duplicating Stage-4 work that wxsv reopen later reconciles. Defensible (scan-what-exists banks real windows; every drive writes a row/claim so offset 0 self-advances), but it is a broader population than the name 'fil5's query' implies, and the reconciler's guards exist for stated reasons. Dan should decide: keep structural candidacy, or borrow the reconciler's two guards.

title: the attributed() seam is unobserved: dropping the V45 split fields from the scan-row attribution copy would NULL every production row while all FZ rails stay green
description:
Instrument gap found in playhead-rkfp R1 review — the production code is CORRECT today; this is missing coverage, not a defect.

SemanticScanResult.attributed(createdAt:scenePhase:runCorrelationId:) (SemanticScanResult.swift ~line 232) is the ONE seam every runner-persisted scan row passes through (BackfillJobRunner sites 2975/3421/3511/3551/3567 all insert 'await attributed(result, ...)'). It rebuilds the struct field-by-field, and playhead-rkfp correctly threads suspendingLatencyMs + daemonPeersAtStart through it.

But nothing observes that threading:
* CoarseLatencySplitTests asserts the split at the CLASSIFIER output boundary (FMCoarseWindowOutput / CoarseWindowFailure) — before attributed().
* SemanticScanPersistenceTests.latencySplitColumnsRoundTrip inserts a hand-built row DIRECTLY — bypassing attributed().
* FZ08/FZ09 mutate the classifier arms, FZ06/FZ07 mutate the store bind/read. No rail mutates SemanticScanResult.attributed.

So the mutation 'delete suspendingLatencyMs: suspendingLatencyMs, daemonPeersAtStart: daemonPeersAtStart from attributed()' compiles, passes every focused suite and every FZ rail, and NULLs the split on every real device row — regressing the next pull to exactly the one-number latencyMs the bead exists to end, invisibly.

Fix shape: one runner-level test that drives runPendingBackfill with a TestFMRuntime, fetches the PERSISTED row via the store, and #requires non-nil split fields (the FMDaemonMetadataStallTests harness already has everything needed); plus one FZ rail (FMSCAN file, target SemanticScanResult.swift) anchored to it. Same shape as the hx6n attribution-drop hazard this copy function was built around.

title: failure scan rows carry NULL inputTokenCount/outputTokenCount, so 'was the prompt oversized' is unanswerable for exactly the rows under investigation
description: Found during playhead-rkfp establishment: the 1,955.6 s permissive_decoding_failure row (F4CE7F47, 51.5 s window) carries NULL for both token-count columns — every failure factory in BackfillJobRunner passes inputTokenCount: nil / outputTokenCount: nil (e.g. makeFailureScanResult), while success rows populate them. The rkfp bead asked to correlate latency with inputTokenCount and the answer for failure rows is 'not recorded'. The plan's promptTokenCount is in hand at every coarse failure site (CoarsePassWindowPlan.promptTokenCount), so at least the input side is free to thread. Output tokens are genuinely unknown on most failures (no response) — NULL stays honest there.

title: a backfill row retired by claim-failure alone (NULL attemptTranscriptVersion, at budget) has no reopen escape
description:
Found in playhead-wxsv R1 review, 2026-08-07. NOT a shipped regression — reachability is contrived — filed so the residual is on record rather than only in a doc comment.

## The state

A backfill_jobs row can in principle reach 'failed' at retryCount >= maxRetries with attemptTranscriptVersion NULL. reopenBackfillJob demands positive evidence (attemptTranscriptVersion IS NOT NULL), so this row can never be re-opened at ANY version; countResumableBackfillJobs excludes it (retryCount filter); markBackfillJobRunning refuses it. The phase is permanently retired for the asset. BackfillJobRunner.redrivableRow logs it as fm_backfill_job_unreachable (error level) — observability exists, an escape does not.

## The only producer, and why it is contrived

The stamp is written in the SAME statement as the claim (markBackfillJobRunning), and the claim is the first store write of every attempt. The only pre-stamp terminal write is the drain's typed-error catch (BackfillJobRunner ~line 1230/1275): if markBackfillJobRunning ITSELF throws a store error that is not invalidStateTransition, the catch marks the never-claimed row failed with retryCount+1. step() maps failures to .insertFailed(sqlite errmsg), which isPermanent() classifies non-permanent (its two permanent prefixes are never emitted by sqlite), so the short-circuit-to-maxRetries path is unreachable from the claim. Reaching the terminal state therefore requires the claim to fail with a store error while the markBackfillJobFailed one statement later SUCCEEDS, on maxRetries (3) separate invocations. Every intermediate state (failed under budget, NULL stamp) is recoverable by ordinary re-drive.

## Options if it ever matters

(a) let reopenBackfillJob accept a NULL stamp on 'failed' rows specifically (a claim that never succeeded attributes no work, so re-opening it mis-credits nothing) — contradicts the deliberate positive-evidence design, so it is Dan's call; (b) have the typed-error catch skip the failed write when the thrown site is the claim itself (the row was never this attempt's to fail); (c) wontfix with this reachability analysis as the record.

Related: playhead-wxsv (the design), the reopen doc in AnalysisStore.swift now states this producer precisely (R1 doc fix).

comments.text: KILLED 2026-08-11 in the full-backlog triage. EMPTY POPULATION — reaching it requires the claim to fail with a store error while markBackfillJobFailed one statement later SUCCEEDS, on maxRetries (3) separate invocations. The bead's own option (c) is 'wontfix with this reachability analysis as the record', the record already lives in AnalysisStore's reopen doc, and fm_backfill_job_unreachable logs at error level if it ever happens.

title: SY02's test name claims a general property its one-row fixture cannot see (7x1s claim batch window)
description:
playhead-7x1s R4 review. INSTRUMENT defect, not production. Filed, not fixed.

`claimDoesNotEvictTheClaimedRowFromTheNewestBatch`
(BackfillJobRunnerTests.swift:1914-1960) is named *"the claim joins the claimed
row's enqueue batch and does not zero the resumable count"* and is rail SY02's
expected test (`T_Y8A3_BATCH`, mutation-battery.sh:2973).

Its fixture seeds exactly ONE backfill row. With one row the carrier IS
`MAX(createdAt)`, so `countResumableBackfillJobs` (AnalysisStore.swift:16373-16383)
returns 1 whatever `createdAt` the claim borrows — the window is
`createdAt >= MAX(createdAt) - 0.5` and the MAX subquery is **unfiltered by
status**, i.e. it is over every row of the asset.

So the borrowed `createdAt` preserves the count only when the carrier is already
the asset's newest row, and `fetchUnfinishedBackfillJob` is `ORDER BY createdAt
ASC` — it selects the OLDEST unfinished row, which is systematically the least
likely to be newest on exactly the multi-row assets the bead was measured on
(8 of 15 hold >= 2 rows). Seed `{A unfinished @T0, B complete @T1}` and the count
is 0 with or without the claim.

The general property is FALSE; the narrow one the fixture proves is true. Same
shape as the tautological `scans.count >= first` arm R1 removed from
`noProgressRunnerCyclesStayBounded` — an assertion that cannot fail for the
population it is handed.

The BEHAVIOUR is playhead-9ocm and is deliberately filed rather than fixed. What
is wrong here is only the name and the fixture: rename to what one row proves, or
add a second, newer row and assert the count 9ocm predicts, so the rail stops
reading as a guarantee of the general case.

Note SY02 anchors on the `createdAt: adopted.createdAt` line, so re-cutting the
fixture does not require re-cutting the rail — only re-running batch 581.

title: [test-gap] no test exercises the y8a3 adoption path under the targetedWithAudit plan
description:
playhead-y8a3 R3 adversarial pass, category 6 (mutations the new tests survive).

All three y8a3 tests seed a single stale row with coveragePolicy .fullCoverage, and makeInputs defaults (observedEpisodeCount: 0, stableRecall: false) force CoveragePlanner to the one-phase fullCoverage plan. The only targeted fixture in BackfillJobRunnerTests seeds a row at the runner's OWN id, so it takes the by-id branch and never reaches the fallback at all.

Consequence: this mutation survives the entire suite —
    if rowAtJobId == nil {            ->  if rowAtJobId == nil && plan.policy != .targetedWithAudit {
i.e. the targeted lane keeps producing exactly the duplicate the bead exists to remove, and nothing fails.

Two more survivors from the same gap:
    phase: phase                      ->  phase: .fullEpisodeScan   (in adoptionClaim)
    coveragePolicy: plan.policy       ->  adopted.coveragePolicy

Also unpinned: the claim's createdAt is asserted only via countResumableBackfillJobs == 1, which is satisfied by anything inside the 0.5s window OR older — so 'adopted.createdAt + 0.4' and 'adopted.createdAt - 86400' both survive. It pins 'not clock()', not 'the claimed row's batch'.

Wanted: an adoption test on a three-phase targetedWithAudit plan, and an exact assertion that claim.createdAt == the claimed row's createdAt.
