title: [bug] two claim mechanisms disagree on empty podcastId: BackfillJobRunner writes "", SemanticScanClaim maps it to nil
description:
playhead-y8a3 R3 adversarial pass, finding F5.

BackfillJobRunner.adoptionClaim writes podcastId: inputs.podcastId raw. SemanticScanClaim.claimRow (SemanticScanClaim.swift:421-424) deliberately maps "" -> nil, with the reason stated in its own doc: 'an empty id is the ABSENCE of a podcast... would hand the planner-state lookup a key that matches nothing and reads as a real miss'.

"" is reachable — that is exactly what SemanticScanClaim.Gate.podcastIdMissing exists for (the final-pass hook passes request.podcastId ?? "").

So two claim rows in one table treat the same value oppositely. Inherited from the runner's mint (which has always written it raw), so not a defect y8a3 introduced — but the mint has the same bug and both should map "" -> nil.

This is an instance of the standing defect class: a value that names an absence being stored as though it named a thing.

title: close the two rail gaps in fetchUnfinishedBackfillJob: the asset clause and the runner call site
description:
## Rail gaps left open by playhead-7x1s, named rather than papered over

R1 adversarial review of `AnalysisStore.fetchUnfinishedBackfillJob` found two
clauses that have a TEST but no mutation rail. Both are real gaps; neither was
closed in 7x1s because no plausible single-site mutation reproduces them without
also breaking the query's binding arithmetic (which would report as a build
failure, not a rail).

**1. The `analysisAssetId` clause.** `WHERE analysisAssetId = ?` / `bind(stmt, 1,
analysisAssetId)`. This is the most dangerous over-reach in the query — matching
ANOTHER asset's row suppresses this asset's full-episode pass entirely, which
costs coverage silently. `fetchUnfinishedBackfillJob_scopesByAsset` covers it;
nothing rails it. Dropping the clause shifts every subsequent bind index, so the
mutant does not compile; a self-consistent version needs a two-site edit.

**2. The CALL SITE arguments.** SX06/SX07/SX09 mutate the STORE's binds and its
equivalence-class helper. A mutation at `BackfillJobRunner.runPendingBackfill`'s
call — `phase: phase` -> `plan.phases[0]`, or `inputs.analysisAssetId` ->
something else — is invisible to every store test by construction. It is also
invisible to most runner tests, because they use single-phase plans.
`periodicFullRescanResumesTheFullCoverageJob` (added in R1) is the only runner
test that varies the planner at all, and it varies the POLICY, not the phase
count.

## What would close both

A runner test driving a `targetedWithAudit` plan — three phases
(`scanHarvesterProposals`, `scanLikelyAdSlots`, `scanRandomAuditWindows`) — across
a transcript-version rotation, asserting each phase resumes its OWN row and no
phase resumes another's. That single test makes a call-site `phase:` mutation
killable and gives the asset clause a second observer. `makeTargetedInputs`
already exists in `BackfillJobRunnerTests`.

## Also worth knowing (nits from the same review, not worth their own bead)

* `fetchUnfinishedBackfillJob_returnsOldestUnfinishedRow` pins ASC-vs-DESC (rail
  SX05) but would likely NOT catch removing `ORDER BY` altogether — SQLite would
  scan `idx_backfill_jobs_asset_phase` and return the same row anyway. No rail
  depends on that, so no verdict is affected.
* `aCompletedJobStillGetsAFreshPassForANewTranscript` asserts a job was admitted
  under a NEW id; it does not assert exactly one new row was created.
* Pre-existing asymmetry, now more visible: a retry-exhausted row with an
  UNCHANGED transcript is skipped and no work happens; the same row with a
  CHANGED transcript falls through and a fresh row is minted. Same asset, same
  exhausted work, two outcomes decided by a transcript hash.
notes:
## R2 REVIEW: a third gap, and it is on the R1 finding's OWN rail

`periodicFullRescanResumesTheFullCoverageJob` never ASSERTS that run 2's plan
is actually `.periodicFullRescan`. It asserts run 1's policy
(`firstRow.coveragePolicy == .fullCoverage`) and then only that
`second.admittedJobIds == [firstJobId]`. Whether the policy flipped at all is
left to the fixture.

Traced, and it currently flips for the right reason — but on a boundary:

    CoveragePlanner.defaultColdStartEpisodeThreshold = 5
    plan(for:) tests shouldUseFullCoverage FIRST, and that is
        observedEpisodeCount < coldStartEpisodeThreshold || ...
    the fixture passes observedEpisodeCount: 5  ->  5 < 5 is FALSE
    so control reaches shouldUsePeriodicFullRescan, and
        episodesSinceLastFullRescan 10 >= max(1, 10)  ->  .periodicFullRescan

So the test is non-vacuous TODAY, and SX06's kill of it is genuine. But raise
`defaultColdStartEpisodeThreshold` to 6 — a one-constant change nobody would
connect to this file — and `shouldUseFullCoverage` short-circuits, run 2 plans
`.fullCoverage` exactly like run 1, and the test becomes a re-run of the
same-policy case. It would still PASS with the exact-policy predicate SX06
restores, i.e. the rail for R1's central finding would go quiet without any
test going red.

**Fix, when qi5t is worked:** assert the flip directly, e.g.

    #expect(
        CoveragePlanner().plan(for: makeInputs(
            episodesSinceLastFullRescan: 10, observedEpisodeCount: 5
        ).plannerContext).policy == .periodicFullRescan,
        "the fixture must actually flip the policy or this test is a re-run of run 1"
    )

Not fixed in R2 because it is an instrument imperfection, not a production
defect, and the round's scope is the bead's contract.

title: the five guarded pendingCancelCause clears are covered incidentally, by no named rail or test (playhead-lmrx R8)
description:
playhead-lmrx R8. The five guarded clears of the GLOBAL pendingCancelCause — AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift :4499 (processJob entry), :4585 (defer), :4824 (cancel-race arm), :4869 (lostOwnership arm), :5127 (non-cancel path) — are named by no rail and by no test's stated claim. LX26 restores the DESTRUCTIVE READ at the cancel-catch arm (:4905); it does not touch the five guards, and R7's ledger row for them was the softest in the ledger by its own admission.

MEASURED, PARTIALLY. R8 planted all five as unconditional clears in one batch (probe LXP1-LXP5) against a GREEN baseline of the focused suites. The batch did not reach a verdict — after 45 minutes the reviewer terminated it and the battery reported ERROR for all five — but the run's own log is evidence: with the mutants applied, lmrx fixtures that the baseline requeues (slow-unwind, never-settles, mid-settle, early-return, late-dispatch, recovery-strand, recovery-expiry-door, recovery-mid-settle) each ran to their 120 s decode sleep and then logged 'abandoned after 5 attempts'. That is the attempt-spending arm the .taskExpired exemption exists to avoid, so the guards are NOT inert and the suites very likely DO kill these mutants — incidentally, via timeouts, rather than by a named assertion.

Two things to do:
1. Build LX-series rails for the five sites so the coverage is named rather than incidental.
2. Note the cost first: an incidental pin that expresses itself as a 2-minute-per-test timeout turned a ~1 minute focused run into a 45-minute one. A rail whose kill is a timeout is a rail nobody will run. Either give the mutants a fast-failing assertion to hit, or record why they cannot have one.

title: the per-job lease heartbeat is named by a test and observed by nothing (playhead-lmrx R8)
description:
playhead-lmrx R8 adversarial finding.

siblingLeaseHeartbeatSurvivesAnotherJobsExit (BackgroundGrantBudgetTests.swift:2154) claims 'the other must still hold a heartbeat and its lease must still be its own'. Its assertions read cancelledRunTaskJobIdsForTesting() and hasCurrentRunningTaskForTesting() — both of which read runTask — plus survivor.leaseOwner != nil, a DB column the heartbeat's cancellation does not change for leaseExpirySeconds. Nothing in the repo observes RunningJob.leaseRenewalTask.

Single-line regression: at AnalysisWorkScheduler.swift ~:4551 change finished?.leaseRenewalTask?.cancel() to cancelling every OTHER job's heartbeat, leaving the runner cancel on the next line intact. Every assertion stays green, and the production consequence is exactly the one the test's own comment describes: a live job with no lease renewal, reaped out from under itself. LX30 mutates both lines together and cannot isolate this half.

Fix: a leaseHeartbeatJobIdsForTesting() accessor (same shape as R8's runnerStartedJobIdsForTesting()) plus an assertion, then a rail.

title: no mutation rail pins 'an episode-scoped cancel raises no un-aimed flag'
description:
playhead-lmrx R4 deleted `shouldCancelCurrentJob = true` from `episodeDeleted` and `retireDownloadAnalysis`. The deletion is redundant by construction (currentEpisodeId != nil implies the job is in runningJobs, which cancelRunningJobs already reaches by identity), so no behavior is lost -- but the claim it REMOVES, that a sibling on an undeleted episode is not preempted, has no rail.

It is not pinnable from outside the actor. The flag's only clearer is processJob's own cancel-race arm (~4789) and its defer (~4531), both of which run during the unwind of the very job whose episode was just deleted -- and episodeDeleted then awaits six fetchJobsByState round-trips before any external observation can happen. So a test that reads the flag after episodeDeleted returns sees 'false' under the DEFECTIVE code too, and a rail on it would print SURVIVED.

Two ways forward, neither cheap enough for a review round:
* a DEBUG seam that parks a sibling immediately upstream of the cancel-race check, so the false preempt is observable as a DB state revert; or
* fold the flag into RunningJob entirely (it is now redundant with cancelRequested at its ONE reader) and rail the reader instead. That is the cleaner fix and overlaps playhead-hrs5's refactor.

Severity of the residual: none -- the flag no longer over-reaches. This bead is about the missing PROOF, not a live defect.

title: TranscriptCoverageIndex condition 1 is still the FAST watermark, so final-pass-covered audio ABOVE it sorts UNREAD and floats to the front
description:
## The gap

`TranscriptCoverageIndex.isShardAlreadyTranscribed` requires BOTH:

1. `fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime >= shardEnd` — the FAST watermark, and
2. a persisted chunk of either pass overlaps the shard (playhead-6r4z widened this half).

Condition 1 is still the FAST watermark, deliberately: playhead-6r4z changed
which ARTIFACT backs a claim and left alone what "some pass claims to have gone
this far" MEANS. The consequence is that final-pass coverage ABOVE the fast
watermark returns `false` before the artifact index is ever consulted, so it
sorts UNCOVERED and floats to the FRONT — the same shape 6r4z fixed below the
watermark, one guard earlier.

## Measured — 2026-08-05 device pull (`db-t35min`), 30 s shards

Per asset, the span above the fast watermark and the UNION of transcript chunks
inside it (not `MAX(endTime)`, which is a reach — see below):

| asset | dur | fast wm | span above wm | union of chunks in that span |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `53FC53E3` | 2528.4 | 2490.0 | 38.4 s | **34.0 s (88.3 %)** |
| `83592353` | 7325.9 | 7230.0 | 95.9 s | **58.0 s (60.5 %)** |
| `D9B513CD` | 3929.9 | 3450.0 | 479.9 s | **50.3 s (10.5 %)** |
| `F2F2FC4C` | 6636.6 | 4680.0 | 1956.6 s | **58.6 s (3.0 %)** |
| `AD5F3A0A` | 4280.9 | 4280.9 | 0 s | — |

Whole-corpus: 10,870 s sits above a fast watermark, of which **252 s (2.3 %)**
is already backed by a persisted chunk and still sorts first. At 30 s shards
that is 8 shards across 4 assets — real, and much smaller than it looks.

## Why the number in `playhead-6r4z` was wrong, and it is worth recording

6r4z's own header and bead comment quoted "480 s on D9B513CD and 96 s on
83592353 — ALL of the remaining unread audio on both". Those are
`episodeDurationSec - watermark`: the SPAN above the watermark, read as though
it named the covered audio inside it. D9B513CD's final-chunk `MAX(endTime)` is
3,929.8 s against a 3,929.9 s episode — 100 % by reach, 10.5 % by area. Same
defect class as the bead it appears in. Corrected in the header at R1 review.

## Why this is not simply "raise it to max(fast, final)"

The watermark is a REACH with a documented right to outlive its chunks
(playhead-0sro), and `reconcileFastTranscriptCoverage` is defined over
`pass = 'fast'` alone. `max(fast, final)` widens the claim half of a two-part
test whose whole design is that the two halves disagree — condition 1 says what
a pass CLAIMS, condition 2 says what is on disk. A cheaper and more honest
alternative exists and should be measured first: drop condition 1 entirely and
let the artifact test stand alone. It is strictly the artifact question, it
needs no new watermark semantics, and on this pull it moves the same 8 shards.
Either way it is an ordering, so being wrong costs latency, not coverage.

## Not in scope here

`playhead-z3jg` (the `transcription:zeroCoverage` circuit breaker) and
`playhead-346z` (watermark-vs-area semantics) are the neighbours; this is only
the ordering guard.

title: fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime does not mean the same thing on every row — two assets on the same pull disagree

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
Found while implementing playhead-dl9k, which depends on this column and works correctly for its own population — this is NOT a dl9k regression, it is a latent ambiguity dl9k's measurement exposed.

THE COLUMN IS READ AS 'how far the FAST transcript pass reached'. On the 2026-08-03 pull two assets disagree about that, split by `transcript_chunks.pass`:

  D9B513CD  fast chunks 4.0 -> 3449.9   final chunks 4.0 -> 3929.8   watermark 3450.0
            => watermark == the FAST pass reach. The final pass does NOT advance it.

  2C5C3699  fast chunks 0.0 ->  300.0   final chunks 300.1 -> 900.0  watermark  900.0
            => watermark == the UNION max, i.e. the FINAL pass DID advance it.

Both cannot be the rule. Whatever writes this column either treats the two passes
differently in different code paths, or one of these rows was written by a path that
does not distinguish them.

WHY IT MATTERS, in the direction that costs reach: the column is the numerator of
`outstandingTranscriptTarget`, which decides whether an episode has audio left to read.
If the column tracks only the fast pass, an episode transcribed to the end BY THE FINAL
PASS still reads as short and earns passes that will find nothing (D9B513CD reads 87.8%
while its chunks reach 99.997%). If it tracks the union, a fast-pass-only consumer gets a
number that overstates what IT can rely on.

NOT dl9k's to fix, and dl9k is not affected: for all three assets dl9k rescues the
watermark equals max(endTime) over ALL chunks (900.0/900.0, 1620.0/1619.3, 2010.0/2010.0),
so its 'is there unread audio' test is reading an honest number in every case it acts on.

RELATED BUT DISTINCT from playhead-ps9j. ps9j asks whether the watermark is the right
INPUT to `capOutRetryDecision` and what type to give the parameter. This bead is about the
COLUMN'S WRITER — the two disagree about what the value means before any consumer sees it,
so ps9j cannot be answered honestly until this one is. Suggest doing this first.

REPRO: sqlite3 on the 2026-08-03 pull —
  select substr(analysisAssetId,1,8), pass, min(startTime), max(endTime)
  from transcript_chunks group by analysisAssetId, pass;
  select substr(id,1,8), fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime from analysis_assets;

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
ABSORBS playhead-ps9j, playhead-pwsu and playhead-vkwr (all closed 2026-08-11). Verified in the 2026-08-11 triage: L3/L4/L5 are THREE CONSECUTIVE LINES of one audit block — CoverageQuantities.swift:1381, :1388, :1391. And this bead says outright that 'ps9j cannot be answered honestly until this one is. Suggest doing this first.'
  - ps9j: capOutRetryDecision's transcriptCoverageSec is fed a WATERMARK
  - pwsu: classifyBackfillTerminal's transcript ratio is a WATERMARK under an AREA name
  - vkwr: the dogfood wire field transcript_watermark_sec carries the transcript AREA
All three are the same defect class this bead is about — a watermark and an area are different quantities and the code interchanges them. ONE bead: settle what fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime means here, then type every consumer. Four cycles collapse to one.

title: A sibling swept by a daemon-refusal drain stop records no unrun-audit and no operational-metrics evidence; the same sibling swept by an admission defer records both
description:
## The asymmetry

`BackfillJobRunner` sweeps the remaining jobs of a batch in TWO places, for the same
reason — the batch cannot proceed and the siblings must not be stranded in `.queued`.

ADMISSION DEFER (thermal / battery / low-power), ~line 779-850. Per swept candidate:

    markBackfillJobDeferred(...)
    deferred.append(...)
    recordUnrunRandomAuditEvents(job: candidate, ...)   // if phase == .scanRandomAuditWindows
    recordOperationalMetricsEvent(job: candidate, ...)

DAEMON-REFUSAL STOP (playhead-kvs8's throttle, playhead-e75l's metadata stall),
~line 1493-1516. Per swept candidate:

    markBackfillJobDeferred(...)
    deferred.append(...)
    sweptSiblingCount += 1

That is all. No unrun-audit evidence, no operational-metrics row.

## What it costs

`recordUnrunRandomAuditEvents` mints one evidence event per narrowed audit window with
`fmDisposition: nil`, `wasFlagged: false` and a `<jobId>|unrun|<idx>` stable id. It is
the record that a window was OWED an audit and never got one — the honest denominator.
Nothing in Swift reads it (`rg "unrun"` over Playhead returns exactly the one write
site), so it is an audit artifact read by a device-pull query, the same shape as
`backfill_jobs.deferReason` and playhead-fil5's `scan_claim:` family. Which is precisely
why the omission is invisible: an operator counting owed-but-unrun audit windows sees
the thermally-deferred ones and not the daemon-refused ones, and nothing anywhere
disagrees.

Reachable: `CoveragePlanner.plan` returns up to three phases, the drain stops at two
consecutive refusals, so a third job in the audit phase is exactly what the sweep
touches.

## Scope

PRE-EXISTING and kvs8-era — the daemon-refusal sweep has had this shape since
playhead-kvs8 (#320); playhead-e75l changed only the `reason:` token it writes and added
`sweptSiblingCount`. Filed rather than widened into e75l's diff for that reason.

## Acceptance

Decide whether the two sweeps should agree (most likely yes — the situations are
identical) and if so extract the per-candidate defer body so there is one of it rather
than two that drift. A test that a `.scanRandomAuditWindows` sibling swept by a
daemon-refusal stop carries the same unrun-audit evidence as one swept by an admission
defer.

title: Two residual limits in the FMDaemonRefusal source canaries: the emission ORDER rule and one-level constant resolution
description:
Both were named as open by playhead-e75l R4 and left open by R5 deliberately. Each
is a bounded, STATED limit of a source canary rather than a defect, and each would
be closed by a capability rather than by another enumeration.

## 1. The ordering rule is undefeated but unprobed against a mutant that also moves
##    the emission sites

`testDaemonRefusalLogEventsAreNotHardCodedInTheRunner` requires `logEvent` to be
read exactly once, `drainStoppedEvent` exactly once, and the first to precede the
second — which is a CONSEQUENCE of control flow (the per-job event is emitted inside
the drain loop's catch arm, the drain-stop event after the loop breaks), not a
pinned accident. Mutation DR11 (the SWAP) is killed by it.

A mutant that swapped the two properties AND relocated the drain-stop `logger.error`
to inside the loop would satisfy the order again. R5's call was to FILE rather than
chase it: moving a log emission across a `break` is a control-flow change that the
runner tests observe behaviourally, and "a plausible author writes this" is not
credible. It is recorded because the reasoning, not the coverage, is what protects
it.

## 2. Constant resolution follows exactly one level of naming

`resolvingLeadingInterpolation` resolves `"\(Self.someConstant)-…"` through a
`let NAME = "literal"` in the same file. Two levels, a computed property, or a
constant in another file remain invisible. This is stated in the source at the site
and guarded from silent collapse by the two anchor tokens plus the `>= 5` family
floor.

## What would actually close them

Not more enumeration — that is the treadmill R4 measured (eight probes planted,
seven walked past). The repo has already found the shape that works: a
**compile-enforced naming obligation**, the way `RegionFillDoor` closed playhead-x0lb's
limit L-F. "One identifier, every spelling" beats "the spellings the last reviewer
thought of". Whether a durable cause token can be given the same treatment — a token
type that a `deferReason` write must be constructed through, so a bare interpolated
literal does not compile — is the question worth answering, and it is a design
change rather than a review finding.

## Explicitly CLOSED rather than filed (R5)

R4's third open item — `collapsedCode` joins lines with no separator, so it could in
principle synthesize a false positive across two unrelated lines — is closed, not
filed. Joining without a separator can only ADD substrings, never remove one, so its
failure direction is a LOUD false positive and never a silent miss. It is also
exactly what Swift does to a `\` continuation whose indentation matches its closing
delimiter, which is the shape being modelled.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: KILLED 2026-08-11 in the full-backlog triage. VACUOUS — the bead's own words: 'Each is a bounded, STATED limit of a source canary rather than a defect', and its own conclusion is that closing them needs a design capability (a token type), not this bead. It even records that R4's third item was 'explicitly CLOSED rather than filed'. A reasoning record that already lives at the site.

title: The mutation battery cannot record a mutation that spans TWO files, so CN-B1's rail is verified by hand and re-verified by nobody
description:
## The gap

A `MUTATIONS` record is `NAME|BATCH|FILE|EXPECTATIONS` and `rec_file` resolves ONE
anchor key to ONE path. Probe **CN-B1** (playhead-e75l R4) needs two edits in two
files:

1. rewrite playhead-41mu's durable token in `BackfillJobRunner.swift` as
   `"\(Self.underCoverageFamily)-\(phase.rawValue)"` — behaviour-identical on the
   device, but `isDurableTokenShaped` requires a LETTER first and a backslash is
   not one, so the derivation silently loses that family;
2. then plant a refusal token INTO the family the derivation just lost.

Step 1 alone is invisible (six families fall to five and the `>= 5` floor still
clears); step 2 alone is killed. Only the pair is the defect, and it is the pair
that R4-Fix4's one-level constant resolution was written to stop.

## Why this matters more than one probe

The general shape is **"the rail was not evaded by touching the rail — it was evaded
by refactoring the writer it reads"**. Any canary that DERIVES its rule from
production source has this exposure, and this repo now has several
(`testDaemonRefusalCausesDoNotJoinAForeignTokenFamily`,
`testEveryProductionInferenceBudgetIsEnumerated`,
`testDrainStopSiblingCountIsTheSweepNotTheDrainTotal`, and the x0lb `--check-inventory`
preflight). Every one of them can be defeated in two files and recorded in none.

## What it would take

Let `rec_file` accept a comma-separated anchor list, or let an `apply_mutation` arm
call `patch` against a file it names itself rather than the one the record passes.
The restore path already hashes every `MUTABLE_FILES` entry, so multi-file restore
is already correct — it is only the record format that is single-file.

## Not urgent, and say why

R4 verified CN-B1 by hand (survives the R3 canary, killed by the R4 one) and wrote
the result into the battery header rather than hiding it. The cost of the gap is
that nobody re-verifies it on later rounds, so a regression in
`resolvingLeadingInterpolation` would be silent.

title: The drain's consecutive-refusal RESET is unrailed — deleting it turns a consecutive counter into a lifetime one and nothing goes red
description:
## The probe

playhead-e75l R5 planted, against production verbatim:

```swift
guard let refusalThatStoppedUs = daemonRefusalThisJob else {
    consecutiveDaemonRefusals = 0   // <- deleted
    continue
}
```

SURVIVED. All eight suites in e75l's scope green (36 Swift Testing tests in 6
suites, 5 XCTest tests, 0 failures in both formats).

## Why it was NOT fixed in e75l

Three reasons, and the third is the binding one.

1. The line is **playhead-kvs8's**, unchanged in substance by e75l — only the
   identifier was renamed (`consecutiveThrottledJobs` -> `consecutiveDaemonRefusals`)
   when the counted population broadened from throttles to every `FMDaemonRefusal`.
2. The shipped cost of the divergence is **a delayed drain, not lost reach**. With
   lifetime counting the drain stops earlier; the siblings it sweeps are DEFERRED
   with `*-batchSibling` and `retryCount` preserved, so they are re-driven on the
   next invocation. Nothing is disqualified and no coverage is claimed.
3. **It is unobservable in any fixture the planner can build.** The difference needs
   a drain of at least FOUR jobs (refusal, success, refusal, and a fourth job left to
   sweep). `CoveragePlanner.plan` returns at most THREE phases — `targetedWithAudit`
   is `[.scanHarvesterProposals, .scanLikelyAdSlots, .scanRandomAuditWindows]`, and
   both full-coverage policies return one. With three jobs the mutant stops after
   job 3, which is the last, so the sweep is empty and the DB state is identical;
   only a log line differs.

## What railing it would take

A fourth job means the specialist phase (`specialistScanEnabled` AND a live
`specialistRuntime`, both constructor parameters no e75l fixture passes), which
drags an unrelated subsystem into a test whose subject is the drain's counter. That
is a fixture decision, not a review-round decision.

## The honest alternative

Make the drain's stop decision a pure function over a sequence of per-job outcomes
and test THAT, instead of driving four real jobs through a runner to observe a
counter. `FMDaemonRefusal.shouldStopDraining` already exists as the threshold half;
what has no pure surface is the RESET, because it lives inline in the drain loop.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: KILLED 2026-08-11 in the full-backlog triage. UNMEASURABLE — the bead proves its own no-witness case: the divergence needs a FOUR-job drain and CoveragePlanner.plan returns at most THREE phases. Its stated consequence is 'a delayed drain, not lost reach... nothing is disqualified and no coverage is claimed' — one log line differs. Railing it means dragging the specialist subsystem into a drain-counter test.

title: A drain-stop log line reports deferredSiblings= but prints every deferred job in the drain
description:
## The defect

`BackfillJobRunner`'s drain-stop line (playhead-kvs8, generalized by playhead-e75l) ends:

    <drainStoppedEvent> consecutive=N siblingCause=<token> deferredSiblings=\(deferred.count)

`deferred` is the run-wide accumulator. It is appended at FIVE sites in the drain loop — the admission-defer sweep, two cancellation/stop-short defers, the daemon-refusal defer of the job that WAS refused, and only lastly the batch-sibling sweep. So on a three-job drain where jobs 1 and 2 are refused and job 3 is swept, the line reports `deferredSiblings=3` when exactly ONE job was a sibling.

The standing defect class: a value that names one thing and counts another. What would this read if no sibling had been swept at all? The same non-zero number.

## Why it is filed rather than fixed

Pre-existing: `deferredSiblings=\(deferred.count)` is kvs8's spelling and predates playhead-e75l, which only changed the EVENT NAME and the `siblingCause=` field on that line. Fixing it means either renaming the field (`deferredTotal=`) or counting the sweep separately, and both are kvs8's line to change.

## Fix sketch

Count the sweep: `var sweptSiblings = 0` incremented in the `for candidate in enqueuedJobs` loop, reported as `deferredSiblings=\(sweptSiblings)`, with `deferredTotal=\(deferred.count)` alongside if the total is wanted. No behavior change; the line is diagnostic only.

Found by playhead-e75l R2 review.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text: KILLED 2026-08-11 in the full-backlog triage. SUPERSEDED — the bead's own fix sketch is already in the source, landed with e75l R5. BackfillJobRunner.swift:1505 'var sweptSiblingCount = 0', :1516 increments inside the sweep loop, :1535 reports deferredSiblings=sweptSiblingCount, and :1488 comments 'R5-Fix1: and deferredSiblings= counts THE SWEEP, not deferred.'

title: kvs8's rateLimited-prologue documents a position the throw does not always have
description:
## The defect

`FMDaemonThrottle.DeferCause.passPrologue` ("rateLimited-prologue") documents
itself as:

> the coarse pass PROLOGUE was throttled — a `tokenCount` / schema-size round
> trip threw **before a single window was planned**. NOTHING was scanned, so
> there is no cursor to advance and no scan row to write.

The second sentence is false on at least one live path. `BackfillJobRunner.runJob`
awaits `classifier.planAdaptiveZoom(...)` with a bare `try await` AFTER
`coarsePassA` has returned (verified at BackfillJobRunner.swift ~3482), and
`planAdaptiveZoom` makes its own `runtime.tokenCount(...)` round trips
(FoundationModelClassifier.swift ~3047, ~3065). A throttle there escapes
`runJob` and lands in the same catch arm, so it is recorded as
`rateLimited-prologue` — with `coarsePassA` having already screened and, since
playhead-26od, CHECKPOINTED windows. `planExpansionWindow` (~3442, reached via
`planExpansionWithTrim`) is the same shape.

The consequence is not a wrong disposition — deferring is still correct, and
`markBackfillJobDeferred` preserves whatever cursor exists — it is an operator
reading a device pull who concludes from the token that the episode is
untouched when it may be substantially scanned.

## Scope

PRE-EXISTING (playhead-kvs8, #320). playhead-e75l inherited the property name
`passPrologueCause` on `FMDaemonRefusal` but named its own token for the BOUND
that elapsed (`inferenceTimeout-metadata`) rather than for a position, so the
NEW token does not make the claim. e75l R1 corrected the doc comments on
`FMDaemonRefusal.passPrologueCause` and the runner's "examined nothing" comment
(commit 6e404f3b) and deliberately did NOT touch kvs8's token or its doc.

## The decision this needs

The token spelling `rateLimited-prologue` must NOT change — device pulls and
support bundles already grep for it (that is why kvs8 froze it). So the options
are: fix the DOC only (cheap, honest, leaves a token whose name overstates); or
add a second throttle cause for the post-coarse paths and accept that pulls now
need two greps. The second is only worth it if an operator actually acts
differently on the two, which is what should be decided before anyone writes
code.

title: boxing is unguarded at 22 sites — a wrong number in a right-named box is INVISIBLE downstream
description:
playhead-x0lb limit **L-I**, the second of the four doors a quantity is unprotected at, and the one R4 found had never been counted anywhere.

## The measurement, re-derived at x0lb R5

`SomeQuantity(rawDouble)` in production code outside `CoverageQuantities.swift`, comment lines excluded:

* **23** at `78892f0d` (R4's own definition, reproduced)
* **22** at x0lb HEAD — 13 `AnalysisStore`, 6 `BackfillJobRunner`, 2 `AnalysisCoordinator`, 1 `EpisodePreparationReadiness`

Both counts REPRODUCED independently at x0lb R5 review, including the 13/6/2/1 per-file split.

The tighter reading — "a quantity built from an UNLABELLED expression" — is **18**, and the derivation this bead was filed with does not produce it: it named two labelled constructors (`AnalyzedSeconds(clipping:to:)`, `AdScanSeconds(examined:within:bridging:)`) and `22 - 2` is 20. There are **four**; `ReachRatio(examined:ofDeclaredDuration:)` and `DensityRatio(transcribed:ofDeclaredDuration:)` are R1's and were already labelled. The reading is also under-specified at its edge: the two LITERAL boxes (`BridgeToleranceSec(5.0)`, `ReachRatio(0.98)`) are unlabelled expressions too, and x0lb's own file header says a literal has no provenance to lose — exclude them as well and it is **16**. Quote **22** unless you say which narrowing you mean; all three readings are in L-I.

## Why it matters more than the `.rawValue` surface

At a demotion the type merely stops applying. At a BOX the type makes the mistake INVISIBLE, because everything downstream reads a correctly-typed value. Three probes, all COMPILED: PA6 boxed the FEATURE column as the final-pass `WatermarkSeconds`; PA11 boxed that same column as the reach DENOMINATOR (the one term every ratio in the path divides by); PA12 boxed the transcript AREA as the transcript WATERMARK — the exact inverse of L-A and unnamed anywhere.

x0lb R5 added a fourth, at a genuine boundary: probe **PF3** swapped the two SQL columns at `FastTranscriptRegion.append(start:end:)` and it COMPILED. Three such sites exist, one per region, and no type closes them — `sqlite3_column_double` returns a `Double` and nothing else.

## What to build

No type can close a box by construction — a `CoverageQuantity` is `RawRepresentable` over `Double` and its initialiser must accept any `Double`. What CAN close a given box is **evidence at the box**, and x0lb shipped four working examples: `AnalyzedSeconds.init(clipping:to:)`, `AdScanSeconds.init(examined:within:bridging:)`, `FastTranscriptRegion.init(spanningFromZeroTo:)` and `FastTranscriptRegion.unionedSeconds`. Each takes the OTHER operand as a type, so the box cannot be pointed at the wrong source.

Doing that for the remaining sites is the work. Start with the ones whose source is an `analysis_assets` COLUMN — those are where PA6/PA11/PA12 landed, and where `CoverageProvenance` already sits recording which column was used (a LABEL, so limit L-D applies to it verbatim: nothing type-checks that it records the right one).

## How to know it worked

A rail per closed box in `scripts/mutation-battery-untypeable.py`, mutant = the pre-fix expression verbatim, verdict UNTYPEABLE. Plant BEFORE fixing; a probe that was never seen to compile is a formality, not evidence.

title: the dogfood wire field transcript_watermark_sec carries the transcript AREA
description:
## Found by the types, not by reading

`ActivitySnapshotProvider` builds `DogfoodDiagnosticsPipelineSnapshot` with

    transcriptCoveredSec:  transcriptCoveredSec
    transcriptWatermarkSec: transcriptCoveredSec     // <- the same value

so the wire field `transcript_watermark_sec` carries the transcript AREA
(`AnalysisCoverageSummary.fastTranscriptCoveredSec`), not a watermark. The real
reach ships separately and correctly as `fast_transcript_watermark_sec`
(`fastTranscriptCoverageEndSec`), so the snapshot has one honest field and one
that contradicts its own name.

It surfaced as a compile error the moment `fastTranscriptCoveredSec` became a
`CoveredSeconds` — nobody had noticed it by reading.

## Why playhead-x0lb did not change it

It is a WIRE field. Two dogfood snapshots on disk already carry the current
meaning, and deciding whether to correct the value, drop the field, or rename it
is a diagnostics-schema call, not a typing one. x0lb added a `.rawValue` and a
comment naming this bead; behaviour is byte-identical.

## Measured

On the 2026-08-03 pull, AD5F3A0A's fast AREA is 1,645.9 s and its fast WATERMARK is
4,280.9 s — so on that asset the field under-reports the watermark it names by
2.6x, while duplicating the field beside it exactly.

## Options

  1. Feed it `fastTranscriptCoverageEndSec` (it then duplicates
     `fast_transcript_watermark_sec` instead — arguably fine, the two provenances
     differ).
  2. Drop it and leave `transcript_covered_sec` + `fast_transcript_watermark_sec`.
  3. Keep the value, rename the key.

Recorded as L5 in `Playhead/Persistence/AnalysisStore/CoverageQuantities.swift`'s
audit block.

title: capOutRetryDecision's transcriptCoverageSec is fed a WATERMARK
description:
## The mismatch

`AnalysisWorkScheduler.capOutRetryDecision(transcriptCoverageSec:)` is a `Double`.
`AnalysisJobReconciler`:1004 hands it `asset?.fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime ?? 0` —
the WATERMARK COLUMN — under a parameter named for coverage seconds. Other call
sites pass literal 0 or `outcome.transcriptCoverageSec`, which is a different
producer again.

## Why it is worth a bead rather than a comment

The value feeds `outstandingTranscriptTarget`, which decides how deep the next
decode goes. A watermark over-reports a gappy transcript (2.6x on AD5F3A0A, the
2026-08-03 pull), so the ladder can conclude there is nothing left to transcribe on
an episode whose AREA is far short — and the ad scan that follows then has nothing
to read. That is the shape playhead-9y9e and playhead-fil5 both paid for.

Whether the watermark is the RIGHT input here has not been established; this bead
is to establish it and then say so in the type.

## The fix

Type the parameter (`WatermarkSeconds` or `CoveredSeconds` from
`Playhead/Persistence/AnalysisStore/CoverageQuantities.swift`) once the intended
quantity is decided, and make every caller agree.

Recorded as L4 in that file's audit block.

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
Evidence from playhead-dl9k, which depends on this parameter being a watermark and deliberately did NOT type it — that decision is this bead's.

RE-DERIVED ON THE 2026-08-03 PULL. For the three assets dl9k rescues, `fastTranscriptCoverageEndTime` is HONEST — it equals the transcript's true reach, so `outstandingTranscriptTarget` is reading the right quantity there:

  asset      watermark   max(endTime) over ALL chunks   episodeDurationSec
  2C5C3699      900.0            900.0                      6925.5
  44F076BB     1620.0           1619.3                      1977.0
  48E903D7     2010.0           2010.0                      2113.1

WHERE IT IS NOT HONEST, and this is the case to design against: D9B513CD reads a
3450.0 watermark while its chunks reach 3929.8 of a 3929.9 s episode. Split by
pass, its FAST chunks end at 3449.9 and its FINAL chunks at 3929.8 — i.e. the
column tracks the fast pass and the final pass does not advance it. But
2C5C3699 contradicts that reading: its fast chunks end at 300.0, its final
chunks at 900.0, and the watermark is 900.0. So the column is NOT simply
'the fast pass reach' on every row, and whatever it is, the two assets disagree
about it. That is worth settling before the type is chosen.

A THIRD MEASURE, so the choice is made with all of them in view: de-overlapped
UNION coverage over the duration, which is the AREA the L4 note contrasts the
watermark with. It is far below the watermark on every asset — and crucially it
is below 95% on ALL TWELVE, including nine whose watermark reads 100%:

  83592353  wm 98.7%  union 90.2%      53FC53E3  wm 98.5%  union 87.0%
  2C5C3699  wm 13.0%  union 11.7%      48E903D7  wm 95.1%  union 85.5%
  DE0784D8  wm 100%   union 93.8%      0C2FC22E  wm 100%   union 87.2%
  AD5F3A0A  wm 100%   union 88.0%      44F076BB  wm 81.9%  union 70.2%
  D9B513CD  wm 87.8%  union 79.2%      4FF3A238  wm 100%   union 89.2%
                                       FCDDB309  wm 100%   union 87.3%
                                       58882C47  wm 100%   union 85.3%

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD'S DECISION: substituting CoveredSeconds (the area) for
the watermark here is NOT a free correctness win. The gaps are non-speech, so an
area-based test would report outstanding work on every fully-transcribed asset
and mint the retry budget for all twelve. dl9k rejected exactly that gate for
this reason. If the answer is CoveredSeconds, it needs a floor calibrated to the
85-94% that a FINISHED episode actually measures, not to 0.95/0.98.

title: classifyBackfillTerminal's transcript ratio is a WATERMARK under an AREA name
description:
## The mismatch

`AnalysisCoordinator.classifyBackfillTerminal` computes

    let coverageEnd = chunks.map(\\.endTime).max() ?? 0     // a WATERMARK
    let transcriptRatio = coverageEnd / episodeDuration

and passes the same value to `contradictedCoverageDenominator(transcriptCoveredSec:)`
— a parameter named for an AREA. `AnalysisCoverageSummary` has both quantities and
keeps them apart; this path has one value under both names.

## The honest verdict, stated because it is NOT simply a defect

The VALUE is defensible. `finalizeBackfillMinCoverageRatio` (0.95) is documented as
the TRANSCRIPT floor 'calibrated to tolerate the few seconds a decoder chops off the
end of an episode' — a REACH question, which a watermark answers and an area does
not. So this is a naming defect, and the risk is that the next reader takes the
name at face value and swaps in the area, which on a gappy transcript is a large
silent tightening.

## Measured

On the 2026-08-03 pull, AD5F3A0A's fast watermark is 4,280.9 s and its fast AREA is
1,645.9 s — a 2.6x difference. A ratio against a 4,280.9 s duration reads 1.000 one
way and 0.385 the other.

## The fix

Rename the parameter to say reach, or type it `WatermarkSeconds` from
`Playhead/Persistence/AnalysisStore/CoverageQuantities.swift` and let the compiler
carry the statement. Then state the floor's calibration at the constant.

Recorded as L3 in that file's audit block.

title: perf-tests.sh does not run the disk preflight, so the one lane where a wedge looks like a slow run is unprotected
description:
Found by playhead-26od R5. STRUCTURAL, and stated separately from the anecdote that prompted it because the anecdote does not carry the weight R5 first gave it.

THE STRUCTURAL FACT: `scripts/fast-gate.sh` runs `scripts/disk_preflight.py` before lint, before the xcodegen bootstrap and before xcodebuild, and exits 28 when the volume is short (playhead-3nfa). `scripts/perf-tests.sh` runs no preflight at all. So the perf lane has no refusal, and it is the lane where a genuine wedge is HARDEST to see: a run with parallelism off and wall-clock measurement tests is supposed to sit quiet, so "no output for ten minutes" is the normal appearance of a healthy run rather than an alarm.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY OBSERVED, stated at the limit of the evidence: two attempts on 2026-08-04 to run the perf plan from the primary checkout at 14 GiB free, each ending at EXIT 143 (SIGTERM) — the first killed by a ten-minute tool timeout, the second while a watcher was being stopped. At the moment each died: `.derivedData-perf` never created, log frozen after the command-line invocation header, xcodebuild at 0.0 % CPU.

THAT IS CONSISTENT WITH A STALL AND IS NOT PROOF OF ONE. playhead-3nfa's wedge signature is a process that hangs INDEFINITELY; both of these were killed before indefiniteness could be established. Do not open this bead expecting a reproducer — there isn't one, and the first job is to get one (run the perf plan on a deliberately short volume and see what it does).

THE FIX IS SMALL: call the same preflight from `perf-tests.sh` with the same exit 28, honouring PLAYHEAD_DISK_MIN_GIB and PLAYHEAD_SKIP_DISK_PREFLIGHT. Threshold: 13.5 GiB was measured against a FULL plan. The perf plan is a much smaller run and its drawdown was NOT measured (3nfa recorded the same caveat for selective -only-testing runs), so either reuse 13.5 deliberately or measure the perf plan's own drawdown with scripts/gate-disk-sample.sh and record it the way CLAUDE.md's table records the gate's. Do not guess a smaller number.

WHILE IN THERE: scripts/disk-cleanup.sh reclaims `.worktrees/<slug>/.derivedData` but not `.derivedData-perf`, which this lane creates as a sibling. Orphan cleanup should cover both, and the canonical bead-close sequence in CLAUDE.md removes only the former too.

title: Persistence identity: duplicate segmentIndex collides semantic_scan_results row keys, so one INSERT can destroy a sibling window's row
description:
Recorded by playhead-26od R4, filed by R5. PRE-EXISTING and not introduced by that bead.

`BackfillJobRunner.makeScanResult` derives the row key from `atomWindowKey(firstAtomOrdinal:lastAtomOrdinal:)`, and those ordinals come from `inputs.segments.first(where: { $0.segmentIndex == windowOutput.lineRefs.first })`. `first(where:)` on a transcript with duplicate `segmentIndex` values resolves to the WRONG segment, so two different coarse windows can produce the same deterministic id and the same `reuseKeyHash`. `INSERT OR REPLACE` then makes the second window's row destroy the first's.

Duplicate `segmentIndex` is a tolerated input, not a hypothetical: `FoundationModelClassifier` builds its segment lookup with `uniquingKeysWith` precisely so it cannot trap, and `coarse pass tolerates duplicate segmentIndex without crashing` pins that tolerance.

WHY 26od DID NOT FIX IT: the end-of-pass digest has the identical exposure through the same helper, so this is a persistence-identity question rather than a checkpoint question, and changing the row key changes reuse and idempotency semantics for every existing row.

WHAT 26od DID CONTAIN: the cursor. `coarseCoverageWalk` now requires a UNIQUE superset when attributing an outcome to a plan, so two plans sharing a line ref credit NOBODY and no resume cursor is ever issued over the collision. The rows can still collide; the cursor can no longer claim the lost one.

ONE HONEST GAP LEFT, worth stating in the fix: `CoarseCheckpointBox.durableWindowCount` is documented as "how many banked windows are actually IN the store", and what it actually measures is how many inserts did not throw. A colliding insert does not throw — it replaces — so under this defect the two quantities differ. R5 could construct no reachable case (the uniqueness guard refuses to credit either plan in every duplicate arrangement tried), which is why this is filed rather than fixed.

title: Observability: a coarse pass killed mid-flight leaves its successes and none of its failures, so qbib's denominator reads clean
description:
Recorded by playhead-26od R5. The mid-flight checkpoint (`BackfillJobRunner.checkpointCoarseWindows`) writes SUCCESS rows only, deliberately: `insertSemanticScanResult` sets `attemptCount = max(existing + 1, incoming)` for a non-success row, so writing a failure row both mid-flight and again at the end-of-pass digest would report a single failed window as two attempts and corrupt exactly the failure accounting playhead-qbib and playhead-8d5r exist to make trustworthy.

The cost, which the code's own comment understated as "nothing is lost by that": nothing is lost FOR THE CURSOR (the covered prefix stops at the first plan that is not a clean success, so every failed window is at or after the cursor and a resume re-attempts it). Something IS lost for the MEASUREMENT. A pass killed mid-flight now leaves its successes durable and zero of its refusals, guardrail violations, inference timeouts or rate limits — on exactly the thermally-degraded devices this whole reach program targets. Read back later, those episodes look like they scanned cleanly.

Concretely wrong afterwards: qbib's honest scanned-duration denominator (which distinguishes "scanned and found clean" from "refused"), 8d5r's `SUM(latencyMs)` over failure rows, and any triage that counts `status != success` rows per asset.

THE FIX NEEDS A STORE CHANGE, which is why it was not made here: an idempotent insert for non-success rows — either an explicit "do not bump the attempt counter" flag, or keying the bump on something that distinguishes a re-offer of the same attempt from a genuine retry. Once that exists the checkpoint can bank failures alongside successes and the digest's second write becomes a no-op for both.

INTERIM: a reader triaging a killed pass should treat missing failure rows as unknown rather than absent, and cross-check the `backfill_jobs` cursor against `max(windowEndTime)` of the persisted rows — a gap between them is where the failures went.

title: scripts/perf-tests.sh default destination is a simulator this box does not have

title: Day-0 rediff: a BLOCKED exit that cannot be persisted leaves no durable trace (.assetRowMissing)
description:
Successor to playhead-p70f (review round 3), filed rather than fixed in-bead because the fix is a schema step and p70f deliberately did not expand the schema past what its own accountability needed.

THE GAP. `RediffDayZeroExit.assetRowMissing` is the one exit in the day-0 taxonomy with NO durable trace anywhere:

  * `rediff_day_zero_attempts` is keyed `analysisAssetId ... REFERENCES analysis_assets(id)` and the store runs `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON`. `.assetRowMissing` means there IS no asset row, so the insert fails the FK check by construction. `AnalysisStoreRediffRefetchRecorder.recordDayZeroAttempt` swallows the throw and logs it (RediffRefetchProduction.swift, the `catch` around `upsertRediffDayZeroAttempt`).
  * It is a zero-byte exit (`spentBandwidth == false`), so `accumulateDayZeroBandwidth` is called with `unmarkedRunSpentBytes: false` and moves NO counter either.

So the entire evidence that day-0 declined this episode is one `os_log` line — recoverable only from a sysdiagnose, which is exactly the retrieval cost playhead-p70f existed to remove.

THE RESIDUE, which is worse than nothing at all. The recorder still calls `accumulateRediffBandwidth` with all-zero deltas, and the ledger's ON CONFLICT arm sets `lastUpdatedAt = excluded.lastUpdatedAt` unconditionally. So the ledger's timestamp advances while every counter stays 0 — a faint echo of the exact shape that made the original 299.6 MB unreadable ("the ledger was written; nothing to show for it"). Pinned as of round 3 by `RediffDayZeroAttemptStoreTests.assetRowMissingCannotBePersisted`, which now asserts every counter stays 0 AND that `lastUpdatedAt` moves, so the residue is documented in an executable place.

WHY IT WAS ACCEPTED FOR THE p70f SHIP (round 3 judgement, reversible):
  * zero bytes. The exit cannot contribute to the bandwidth bleed p70f is about, so it does not weaken that bead's acceptance criterion.
  * near-unreachable in production. `DayZeroRediffTrigger` is called with an `analysisAssetId` the runtime just resolved from `analysis_assets`; reaching `.assetRowMissing` needs the row to vanish between that resolution and day-0 reaching the store (episode deletion / library purge racing a play start).
  * the tautology is already documented on the enum case and pinned by a test, so nobody re-derives it as a bug.

THE FIX WHEN IT IS WORTH A SCHEMA STEP. Add a global blocked-exit counter to `rediff_bandwidth_ledger` — NOT per-asset, since the per-asset table is precisely what cannot hold this row. Two candidate shapes:
  (a) one `blockedExitCount INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, incremented for any day-0 exit whose attempt-row write throws. Cheapest; answers "did this happen at all?" and nothing more.
  (b) a small `rediff_day_zero_blocked` table keyed by exit rawValue with a count + lastAt. Answers "which exit, how often, when last" without a per-asset key, and would also catch a genuine store failure hiding behind the same `catch` (today `.assetRowMissing` and a real `upsertRediffDayZeroAttempt` failure are indistinguishable in the ledger — both silent).

(b) is the better answer because the `catch` is shared: a broken `rediff_day_zero_attempts` write for ANY exit currently disappears the same way, which is a bigger blind spot than `.assetRowMissing` itself.

Whichever lands, also decide whether an all-zero `accumulateRediffBandwidth` should touch `lastUpdatedAt` at all — the honest options are "don't write the ledger for a zero-delta free exit" or "write it and have a counter to show for it", not today's third thing.

ACCEPTANCE
A day-0 attempt whose durable per-asset write is refused increments something readable from a diagnostics bundle, and `.assetRowMissing` is distinguishable in that surface from a genuine store failure. `rediff_bandwidth_ledger.lastUpdatedAt` never advances against an all-zero delta with no counter to explain it. `RediffDayZeroAttemptStoreTests.assetRowMissingCannotBePersisted` is updated to assert the new counter rather than the residue.

title: SPIKE: silent-push wake signal (content-available) for background analysis — gated on measuring #1+#2 first
description:
Dan 2026-07-22: likes the idea but wants it GATED. From Fable's background-analysis reliability analysis. Server feed-watcher sends content-available pushes (new episode / nightly nudge); app wakes ~30s, kicks downloads + re-arms BG requests. All inference stays ON-DEVICE -> mandate-compatible as a WAKE SIGNAL only.

SPIKE PROTOCOL (do in order): (1) FIRST ship + measure #1 charger-class backfill (playhead-i6oi) and #2 playback-session backlog-drain (playhead-glo9). (2) MEASURE whether they closed the background-coverage gap using shpy submit/grant telemetry + hygc.1.4 run-ledger over several nights of dogfood. (3) ONLY if a material gap remains, evaluate silent-push.

title: drainEligible busy-spin under persistent DB write-lock: add inter-pass yield / no-progress guard
description: Found by gy2s R2. drainEligible(deadline:) can busy-spin in one narrow pathology: the eligibility SELECT succeeds but acquireLeaseWithJournal's UPDATE throws (persistent write-lock), so runSingleDispatchPass returns true while the row stays queued -> tight loop until the caller deadline (5/25min) or Task.isCancelled. Bounded + only under a broken DB + strictly better than the pre-fix perpetual 30s loop, so NOT blocking. Cheap fix: add an 'await Task.yield()' between passes AND/OR a no-progress guard (break if N consecutive passes dispatch 0 jobs). A fully-throwing DB does NOT spin (selectNextDispatchableJob uses try? -> nil -> break). Low priority.
notes: PR #283 (branch bead/playhead-bbut): added 'await Task.yield()' between passes in drainEligible — the cheap fix from the bead. NOT gate-verified (box memory-saturated ~130MB free + swarm active; a cold-build gate would OOM-contend per ekpn/#282). One-line cooperative yield in an existing async loop — compiles trivially. Needs a gate run before merge.

title: FM usage-accounting + divisor retune (Lever 2): wire Response.usage/session.usage ground-truth, retune the ÷8 budget factor after measuring iPhone contextSize
description:

1. `Response.usage`/`session.usage` report real input.total/cached + output.total/reasoning on iOS 27 — replaces estimation with ground truth.
2. `fallbackTokenEstimate` OVER-counts prompts 2.21x vs Apple's native `tokenCount` => the ÷8 window-budget safety factor is now very conservative; a retune could relieve window-count pressure (more transcript per window).
BUT: contextSize is platform-dependent — Mac Catalyst on-device model reports 8192, iPhone reportedly still 4096 (see project_ios27_context_4096_device memory). So MEASURE real iPhone contextSize + native tokenCount FIRST (phone-gated), then retune the divisor on ground-truth usage, not speculation. Do NOT retune blind. Depends-on the LanguageModelError taxonomy fix landing first (same error surface).
notes:

title: Two-lane FM: separate DAI vs host-read prompts + sliding-window multi-pass; pass-agreement = host-read skip-vs-mark confidence
notes:
BLOCK 2 RESULT (2026-07-17): separate DAI/host-read prompts do NOT beat the omnibus iter5 on the weak on-device FM. Recall (all-AD fixtures): DAI-class omnibus 0.80 vs DAI-specialist 0.57 (WORSE - the focused prompt drops the ownership/first-party negatives the omnibus uses to disambiguate); host-read omnibus 0.88 vs host-specialist 0.88 (TIE). CAVEAT that keeps the idea alive: the omnibus is 46 lines and cannot go on the standard-guardrail MAIN path (refusal risk, see xsdz.63 note); a SHORT specialist could - but at 0.57 DAI it is not worth it yet. LOAD-BEARING DISCOVERY: the format scaffolding (esp. "do NOT output literal L<n>, substitute real numbers") is essential - dropping it collapsed specialists to 0.00 (model emits template literals -> parser drops -> UNCERTAIN). CONCLUSION: the two-CLASS value is in CERTAINTY ROUTING (rediff=DAI-skip vs skipConfidence=host-read gate, wraj), NOT separate prompts. The remaining sb41 value = the MULTI-PASS / sliding-window recall lever (Block 5).
BLOCK 5 RESULT (2026-07-17) - sliding-window multi-pass VALIDATED. The themove LMNT host-read "miss" was purely a WINDOWING artifact: the production break-middle window [973-995] (sliced mid-pitch) -> NO_AD, but 5 of 6 OTHER alignments of the SAME read -> AD (shift-left [955-985], aligned [935-965], wide [930-975]/[930-995], shift-right [985-1015]). So (1) a sliding/overlapping-window UNION recovers host-reads that a single break-aligned window slices; (2) pass-AGREEMENT (5/6) is exactly the host-read confidence signal wraj [[feedback_certainty_tiered_skip]] needs for skip-vs-mark. Dan two ideas converge: multiple passes fix host-read RECALL and produce the CERTAINTY dial in one mechanism. RECOMMEND: implement overlapping-window host-read pass (e.g. 30-40s windows @ ~15s stride over played timeline) with union + agreement-rate; feed agreement into AutoSkipPrecisionGate as the non-rediff confidence floor. Supersedes the ensembling framing of xsdz.61 (sliding windows are a better confidence source than k-identical-greedy repeats).
GENERALIZED (2026-07-17): sliding-window recovery confirmed on a SECOND show+sponsor. doac Pipedrive host-read: 4/5 window alignments -> AD; the only miss is the pre-product SETUP slice [2819-2849] ("One of the things you have heard me talk about...", before "pipedrive.com/CEO"). Identical pattern to themove LMNT (5/6, only the setup-slice missed). ROBUST FINDING across 2 shows / 2 sponsors: host-read misses are windowing artifacts localized to the pre-product-naming setup; any window that contains the actual pitch (brand+URL/code) -> AD; sliding/overlapping-window UNION recovers the read; pass-AGREEMENT (4/5, 5/6) = the host-read confidence signal that feeds wraj T~0.9. IMPL RECOMMENDATION stands: overlapping host-read pass (~30-40s @ ~15s stride over the played timeline), union the AD spans, use agreement-rate as the AutoSkipPrecisionGate non-rediff confidence.
SYSTEMATIC sliding-window result (2026-07-17, 13 themove host-reads x 5 window alignments each, iter5 greedy): single production-GRID window recall 10/13=0.77 (consistent with the ~0.64-0.79 held-out single-window numbers) -> SLIDING-UNION recall 12/13=0.92, a +0.15 detection lift. Only 1/13 (a Ventum read) is a genuine FM CAPABILITY miss (0/5 alignments); the other misses are pure windowing that overlapping windows recover. AGREEMENT distribution [0,1,2,3,4,4,5,5,5,5,5,5,5]: 7 reads caught by ALL 5 alignments (high confidence), 2 by 1-2 (marginal). => (1) the sliding/overlapping-window pass closes most of the host-read detection gap; (2) the AGREEMENT RATE across overlapping windows is a stronger host-read confidence signal than single-window skipConfidence, and is the natural non-rediff confidence input for wraj AutoSkip floor. IMPL: overlapping-window host-read pass (~30-40s @ ~15s stride over played timeline), union AD spans, agreement-rate = confidence.
SLIDING-WINDOW REGION AGGREGATOR prototyped (2026-07-17, branch worktree-agent-a562aeff47c6ac0c7 / bcc42c23, NOT merged). SCOUT CONFIRMED THE ROOT CAUSE: the coarse windowing (FoundationModelClassifier.planPassA ~:1643) is a NON-OVERLAPPING, token-budget-packed grid (grows a window to ~4096 tokens then jumps lowerBound=upperBound+1; no stride/overlap). An ad straddling a seam is SPLIT, each half looks sub-threshold = the measured late-start/boundary-collapse. New pure FM-free component SlidingWindowRegionAggregator.aggregate(windows,config) -> [PromotionalRegion{startTime,endTime,agreement,adWindowCount,overlappingWindowCount}]: maps overlapping-window verdicts to UNIONED regions + per-region AGREEMENT (fraction firing) = banner/per-user-learning candidate, NOT a skip boundary (correct per gradient reframe). 10/10 tests pass. Wiring plan in docs/sliding-window-region-pass.md: map coarsePassA FMCoarseWindowOutput.disposition -> VerdictWindow, feed aggregator, regions become banner candidates (sibling to RegionProposalBuilder ProposedRegion, agreement->confidence band). OPEN (deferred): overlapping-window GENERATION is N× coarse FM calls/episode -> needs a gating heuristic + device thermal/latency budget before wiring; gapBridgeSeconds default 5s needs corpus tuning.

title: FM over-anchors musical/comedic show intros as ad-consensus (conan monologue) — demote-FM precision
notes:
FILED from the xsdz.58 diagnosis (2026-07-17). FM (FoundationModel) consensus over-anchors musical/comedic show intros as ad material. CASE: conan-2026-07-13-mick-jagger — FM anchored atoms across the White Stripes theme song (83-100s) + Conan's intro monologue (101-204s) → decoded span [89.6-204.24] with NO byte-slot backing → blockedByEvidenceQuorum. FRAGILE: held back ONLY because it has 1 evidence kind (FM); the theme-song music is a latent 2nd corroborator — if MusicBedLedgerEvaluator emitted a .musicBed entry over it, FM+musicBed=2 distinct kinds → eligible → 144s of host content auto-skippable. LATENT CLASS for late-night/variety formats (FM firing on cold-open+theme+monologue). This is the epic's DEMOTE-FM long game ([[feedback_lexical_as_attention]]: FM is a bad final judge, good attention signal) — NOT a width/rediff fix (xsdz.58 FIX A handles the byte-backed [0-88] overrun; this is the no-byte-slot FM over-anchor). OPTIONS (from diagnosis): tighten FM anchoring on intro music/monologue (AtomEvidenceProjector.swift:82-140), or the quorum FIX B (byte-refutation hardening, MEDIUM recall risk, BackfillEvidenceFusion.swift:1043-1069). Blocks auto-skip robustness but NOT the current eligible-only gate (this window is blocked, not eligible). Also surfaced: FM NON-DETERMINISM (~40% guardrail refusal) makes A/B measurements non-reproducible run-to-run — a measurement-integrity concern worth a baseline-variance quantification.
PROMOTED TO HARD AUTO-SKIP BLOCKER (FM-variance series, 2026-07-17). 3 identical-code/identical-data treatment runs: eligible-only false-widening gate = 27.8s PASS / 27.8s PASS / 113s FAIL. The auto-skip go/no-go GATE FLIPS PASS↔FAIL on FM non-determinism alone. Run-3 culprit: unexplained-2026-07-10 — FM over-anchored a NEW eligible window [2359-2464] (~105s) that CLEARED the evidence quorum as ELIGIBLE (would auto-skip ~105s of content); absent in runs 1,2 (eligible_fw 14s→119s). Two systemic findings: (1) FM produces eligible content-eating over-anchors ~1/3 of runs; (2) the evidence quorum does NOT reliably contain them — blocked conan but passed unexplained-run3 as eligible; its containment is as non-deterministic as FM. CONSEQUENCE: auto-skip CANNOT be gated on this measurement until FM is deterministic OR demoted from setting eligible widths. Byte-boundary accuracy is UNAFFECTED (deterministic byte differ); mark-only is SAFE (no auto-skip → FM instability = wrong banner at worst). This is the sharpened statement of the demote-FM epic goal. Variance data: scratchpad/variance-run-{1,2,3}.json + variance-gate outputs.
SCOPING COMPLETE (2026-07-17, read-only). MECHANISM CONFIRMED: FM is the SOLE nondeterministic input (all deterministic channels byte-identical across 3 runs: catalog 16, lexical 12 hits, acoustic 47 breaks, byte differ; only FM anchoring swung 8→49 atoms in run 3). The quorum is a DETERMINISTIC AMPLIFIER. unexplained run-3 window [2359-2464] (105s) ate ~50s of Ted Binion murder narrative + drew ad evidence from the outro self-promo tail; became eligible because FM (nondeterministic) + a STANDING deterministic non-FM kind (catalog-CTA 'subscribe and rate the show' and/or lexical self-promo, identical all runs) = 2 kinds. THE FLAW (isolated, one predicate): quorumGateForFMConsensus() BackfillEvidenceFusion.swift:1043-1069 counts .fm as a full distinct kind (it's a COUNT not weighted sum → FM(1)+1 standing(1)=2→eligible). ★ KEY: the SISTER gate quorumGateForFMAcoustic() :1077-1106 ALREADY EXCLUDES .fm (requires ≥1 non-FM external) — so the codebase already enforces 'FM can't corroborate itself' on one path; fmConsensus is the inconsistent one. RECOMMENDED FIX = OPTION 1: require ≥2 NON-FM distinct kinds on fmConsensus (drop .fm from the count) — one predicate, makes fmConsensus consistent with fmAcoustic, FM keeps anchoring/localizing/skipConf but can't carry a window to AUTO-SKIP alone-plus-one. Breaks 1 test (Phase6ComprehensiveTests:806 'FM-only conversational ad' = .fm+.classifier = the conscious recall trade). ⚠️ GATED ON VERIFICATION: dumps don't carry per-window ledger sources, so UNCONFIRMED whether [2359-2464] has exactly 1 vs ≥2 non-FM kinds — if ≥2, Option 1 doesn't fix it (it's a WIDTH problem → boundary/rediff track). NEED a source-annotated re-dump (add anchorProvenance + scoringLedger sources to the dump schema). Option 2 (fmConsensus caps at markOnly) = guaranteed fix but kills auto-skip for ALL FM-detected conversational ads (the Phase-3 value prop) — viable only as a measurement-mode stopgap. TEST: (1) unit pin FM+1-non-FM→blocked; (2) FM-anchoring-INVARIANCE regression (hold deterministic evidence, toggle FM anchor, assert eligible set identical). ADOPT WORST-OF-N (≥3) as the go/no-go methodology regardless. COMPOSES WITH: xsdz.62 (rediff-as-a-kind restores DAI auto-skip under Option 1 — rotation is a non-FM kind); xsdz.60/61 (FM reliability); host-read ads → banner-not-autoskip under Option 1 until FM reliable ([[feedback-fm-hostread-irreplaceable]]).
OVERNIGHT: implement Option 1 on a branch IF the xsdz.36.1.1 instrumentation confirms the culprit window has exactly 1 non-FM kind. Do NOT merge — Option 1 changes production eligibility (auto-skip requires 2 non-FM kinds); present for Dan's merge decision.
DE-RISKED by measurement greedy #1 (2026-07-17). FIX A removed the conan [0-88] intro over-anchor (windows now at real breaks 1201/2677/3850). Across 10 eps: 0 eligible windows held on <2 non-FM kinds -> FM is NEVER load-bearing for an auto-skip, so the "quorum counts FM as a full kind" concern does not manifest post-FIX-A. Option-1 (require >=2 non-FM) would be a no-op here. Recommend DEMOTE/park unless a future run surfaces an FM-only eligible window.
CLOSING: RESOLVED by measurement - FIX-A removed the conan intro over-anchor + 0 eligible windows held on <2 non-FM kinds (FM never load-bearing for a skip)

title: Transcript-space rediff fallback: text-diff A/B when fingerprint alignment fails (re-encode CDNs, repeated content)
notes:
WIDTH BRAINSTORM 2026-07-17. MECHANISM: when fingerprint alignment fails — (a) per-stitch re-encoding CDNs (Megaphone: alignedFractionB<0.5 wholesale reject in RediffSlotOwnership), (b) acoustically-repeated content (Morbid non-monotonic, 5/8 pilot failures) — diff the TRANSCRIPTS of A and B fetches instead. Text survives re-encoding perfectly; spoken content repeats far less than music beds. We already own on-device ASR (whole pipeline transcribes A-side). COST: transcribing the B-side (~minutes/episode on-device, offline lane only). Alignment = text-space LCS/anchor diff (words with timestamps) -> divergent regions = rotated ad slots; boundary precision limited to word timestamps (~0.5-1s — worse than fingerprints ~0.12s but usable vs the 90s budget, and infinitely better than NO width on the failed-alignment shows). ROLE: FALLBACK lane behind fingerprint rediff, not a replacement. RELATION: xsdz.44 (byte-level alignment) attacks the same holes from the byte side and is cheaper — spike 44 FIRST; 49 is the backstop if bytes fail on re-encoding CDNs (bytes CANNOT fix Megaphone since re-encode changes all bytes; text is the only signal that survives re-encode + repeats less than audio). KILL TEST: transcribe one Megaphone-re-encoded A/B pair + one Morbid A/B pair (after a --retain-audio Morbid re-fetch), text-diff, compare recovered slots vs fpcalc truth where fpcalc works / vs gold where it does not.
CONCRETE TARGET LIST NOW EXISTS (2026-07-17): 8 corpus episodes fail BOTH byte and fpcalc alignment (casefile-340, ted-business-05-25, nikki-glaser-514, charlie-kirk-05-30, rest-is-politics-05-28, daily-show-05-29, pod-save-america-05-31, last-week-in-ai-05-29). title: Rediff-supervised acoustic bank growth: mine stingers + pod grids without gold labels
description: The stinger bank and pod grids currently learn ONLY from gold audits (xsdz.39 cadence) — which caps growth at Dan's listening time. Rediff slot edges provide label-free weak supervision at library scale (87% rotation at ~3d): mine edge-adjacent envelope templates and width-grid statistics per show from rediff-corroborated edges, using the SAME gates as the gold-driven learner (offset-spread, distinct-episode support, confidence floors) plus a trust discount for the weaker supervision (rediff edges carry ~36% boundary error per the 2026-07-07 ruler — expect templates to need more support and wider spread tolerance, then tighten against any gold that exists). Corpus-side first (tier-a + daysgap artifacts exist today); on-device later behind xsdz.28 plumbing. Auto-grown entries enter the bank SHADOW-TIERED (scored, never bounds-affecting) until they pass the gold-scored gate — mirrors the curated-vs-self-learned distinction Dan set for the v1 bank decision.
acceptance_criteria: Corpus-side miner produces candidate show entries from rediff edges alone; on shows with gold, mined templates agree with gold-learned ones (offset within tolerance) or are rejected; shadow-tier entries demonstrably cannot affect bounds until promoted; promotion requires the standard dump + gold scorer + both-gates pass.

comments.text: SPIKE VERDICT: PARTIAL — NO-GO for naive top-motif mining, GO for a pipeline-seeded variant (report: playhead-baselines/xsdz42-unsupervised-mining-spike-2026-07-16.md; prototype scripts/l2f-xsdz42-unsupervised-stinger-mine.py). The hypothesis split cleanly into two claims: (A) 'a show's stinger recurs across episodes and is acoustically recoverable WITHOUT labels' = VALIDATED — 5/6 banked stinger-sides recur cross-episode at median envelope-NCC 0.75-0.98 (conan-post 0.98, morbid-pre 0.92, smartless-post 0.87, morbid-post 0.75, nikki-pre 0.75; only nikki-post fails 0.56, its weakest bank entry), and the signal SATURATES AT JUST 2 EPISODES. (B) 'top-recurring-motif mining will PICK the ad stinger' = FALSE — the stinger's recurrence rank is 3/10/20/21/30/270; intros/outros/theme music recur HARDER, so naive mining banks the intro, not the ad stinger. Mechanism: envelope-NCC partly measures shared silence/pause structure, common to splices AND intros (themove 'no-stinger' control's top motif was 30% silence = a splice-silence gap, not music). RECOMMENDED PATH = pipeline-seeded recurrence learning: restrict cross-episode mining to windows NEAR the app's existing coarse ad CANDIDATE regions, then learn the stinger from the sub-region that recurs — inherits the 'where are the ads' prior, sidesteps intro-dominance, stays gold-free/on-device/2-episodes. This is the direct path to a per-user self-learning stinger bank with NO manual audit. CAVEAT: OTM/TED have only 1 corpus episode so couldn't be tested; recovery evidence rests on morbid/nikki/conan/smartless.

title: Lexical anchor miner: self-supervised per-show phrase discovery from rediff edges
description: Executable successor to the auto-growth design note on xsdz.37 (2026-07-17). Build the miner: recurring normalized 2-8-token n-grams near weak-label break edges (rediff slot edges as label-free supervision; gold labels; later xsdz.34 corrections — NEVER lexical-channel-placed edges), support >= K distinct episodes, offset-spread gate, edge-affinity ratio vs in-show base rate, exact-only short phrases, verb-exact attribution templates. Output: per-show lexical bank (StingerBank-shaped: phrase/side/offset+-spread/support/confidence), committed generator with content-addressed provenance, candidate-frontier report for Dan's accept/reject GUI review. Cadence: ride l2f-daily-loop once stable. Validation targets the prototype already identified: nikki 'when we get back', OTM station-ident resume, techcrunch preroll opener must all be DISCOVERED (not hand-added) by the miner from corpus data.
acceptance_criteria: Miner discovers the three known-waiting anchors from corpus data without hand-seeding; frontier report + accept/reject flow demonstrated; bank regeneration gated through gold scoring before any commit; no anchor learned from lexical-channel-placed edges (circularity guard tested).
notes:
ON-DEVICE GENERALIZATION (Dan asked 2026-07-17: must work for users' shows, not just the corpus): yes by design — rediff edges are generated on-device (xsdz.16/xsdz.28), on-device ASR provides transcripts, so the miner's inputs exist per-user per-show under the on-device mandate. Corpus phase proves miner precision; ON-DEVICE promotion replaces the gold gate with CORROBORATION tiers (agreement with rediff widths + presence cores across >=N episodes, no xsdz.34 corrections against, standard guards) — shadow-tier until then. Cold start: curated shipped bank for popular shows; per-user mining covers the long tail; bbrv fingerprint-anchored sharing is the eventual cross-user seed path. Battery: incremental per-episode mining on the existing BG-processing infra.
MINER LANDED (2026-07-15, commit 07858798): scripts/l2f-lexical-anchor-miner.py + scripts/tests/test_l2f_lexical_miner.py (21 tests; full scripts suite 343 OK). Zero hand-seeded phrases; VALIDATION_TARGETS is post-hoc reporting only.

description: Dan's 2026-07-15 audit observation: TED Business's musical in/out cues are the SAME audio as other iHeart network podcasts (SYSK also iHeart; its ~1s straddle offsets may be NETWORK constants). A network-level cue bank generalizes stinger anchoring to shows the user has NEVER played — the cold-start gap per-show banks cannot cover — and pools learning support across sibling shows (would have rescued TED/OTM-class support problems). Production scaffolding exists: NetworkPriors/NetworkIdentity/OwnershipGraph. Keep offline-prototype-first discipline.
acceptance_criteria: Offline evidence that >=2 iHeart shows share cue audio (cross-show NCC); bank schema supports network entries with show-level precedence; measured against gold on at least one show absent from the per-show bank; no regression on per-show-bank shows.
notes:
EVIDENCE PHASE (2026-07-16): hypothesis REFUTED at the envelope-NCC level on the current corpus. Method: scripts/l2f-network-cue-evidence.py (new, reuses EnvelopeCache/ncc_align from l2f-boundary-stinger-prototype.py by import) — every gold v2 break-edge template NCC-aligned against every other edge clip for the 3 iHeart shows in gold (ted-business, stuff-you-should-know, plus the-nikki-glaser-podcast, auto-identified via iHeart's Omny org GUID e73c998e-... in its feed URL; TED membership is manual/Dan's assertion, Acast feed encodes no network), with morbid+smartless as non-iHeart noise-floor controls. Cross-side (pre<->post) blocks at/below same-side. COROLLARY (SYSK ~1s straddle as network constant): moot/refuted — offsets vs best shared exemplar disagree by seconds (sysk:pre +3.69s, ted:pre +4.52s, nikki:pre +0.12s); straddle stays per-show. title: Stinger bank growth: re-qualify OTM and TED, define the audit-to-bank cadence
description: Two shows with real stingers fell out of the shipped bank for honest data reasons: on-the-media has only 2 unique gold breaks post-dedupe (below the >=3 learning support gate; its v2 model rode on a duplicated break and scored 0.1/0.2s in production before removal) and TED Business failed the 2.0s offset-spread gate on the full corpus (4.4s).
