acceptance_criteria: OTM back in the bank with >=3 unique gold breaks and passing gates; TED explicitly re-qualified or rejected with measured spread; the regenerate-on-new-gold cadence documented in the bank provenance workflow; every regeneration re-measured against gold before commit.
notes:
STANDING AUDIT-TO-BANK CADENCE (defined 2026-07-16, applies to every future gold audit): (1) NEW GOLD — every completed ear audit is frozen content-addressed (ledger+review, filename carries the file sha256) into TestFixtures/Corpus/Audits/. (2) PROMOTE — scripts/l2f-promote-oracle-earaudit.py with the frozen 2026-07-15 base pair as default and each newer audit as --extra-ledger/--extra-review, emitting a new content-addressed earaudit-oracle-gold artifact under TestFixtures/Corpus/Evaluations/. (3) REGENERATE BANK — scripts/l2f-boundary-stinger-prototype.py --evaluation <new gold> --emit-bank Playhead/Resources/StingerBank.json; the bank is NEVER hand-edited, only regenerated from gold. (4) PINS — update the hermetic bank pins in PlayheadTests/Services/AdDetection/StingerBankTests.swift to the regenerated asset. (5) RE-MEASURE — fresh pipeline dump + scripts/l2f-score-oracle-gold.py --evaluation <new gold> --dump <dump>, and re-check both bank gates (>=3 unique gold breaks learning support; offset spread <= 2.0s OFFSET_SPREAD_MAX) for every show, not just the newly audited ones. (6) COMMIT — only after re-measure is green/understood; bank + pins + gold artifact land in the same commit so the bank never drifts from its provenance. Morning queue for OTM/TED re-qualification prepped 2026-07-16: ledger /Users/dabrams/playhead-baselines/otm-ted-requalify-ledger-20260717.jsonl (8 spans: 3 OTM, 5 TED, validated against l2f-earaudit-gui load_audit_entries incl. audio fingerprints), runbook /Users/dabrams/playhead-baselines/otm-ted-requalify-README.md.
DOAC PAGE-TURN STINGER (Dan, 2026-07-17): Diary of a CEO ads are DAI dressed up to SOUND like live host-reads, but they are bounded by a CONSISTENT audio stinger (a page-turning sound) at BOTH start and end. => doac ads are deterministically boundable via stinger detection, NOT true host-reads. The host-read WIDTH measurement (playhead-4xqf note) showed doac detected END accurately (~2s) but START ~54s late = the pipeline is likely catching the END page-turn but MISSING the START page-turn. ACTION: mine the doac page-turn stinger into the bank (start+end signature) -> deterministic start+end boundary for doac ad spans -> moves doac from the banner/host-read lane to the deterministic SKIP lane. Check whether doac is in the current 6-show bank; if not, add it. This SHRINKS the true-host-read residual (themove/Lance-live is the real no-signal class).
DOAC STINGER SPIKE (2026-07-17): tried to auto-verify the page-turn from the gold ad boundaries via 3 methods on doac-07-09 (envelope-NCC = the bank method, spectral-NCC, onset-aligned tight-window spectral) - ALL INCONCLUSIVE. content->ad NCCs 0.1-0.5, ad->content 0.1-0.5, cross-group baselines comparable => no clean consistent signature. ONE strong hit: onset-aligned out1(2958s)-out2(4035s) = 0.91 (two ad-END transitions match) - hints the END page-turn is real + consistent (also fits the pipeline detecting doac ad ENDS accurately ~2s while missing STARTS by ~54s). ROOT CAUSE of inconclusiveness: gold boundaries are +/-seconds imprecise; a short page-turn transient windows in/out unreliably; onset-peak picks the loudest transient (may be a word/music hit, not the page-turn). CONSEQUENCE: mining doac is NOT a quick automated win - needs PRECISE boundaries first (the seeded-miner would hit the same wall). PATH: (a) human-in-the-loop - snippets extracted at scratchpad/stinger/doac0709-{in1..3,out0..3}.wav for Dan to listen + pinpoint exact page-turn times, then re-verify tight + mine; or (b) proper onset-clustering across BOTH doac episodes (07-09 + 07-13) to self-localize the recurring transient without gold. doac still NOT in the 6-show bank (Conan/Morbid/OTM/Smartless/Ted/Nikki).
DOAC PAGE-TURN STINGER CONFIRMED + AUTO-LOCALIZED (2026-07-17, subagent, validated against Dan hand-marks). It self-mines by acoustic clustering across both episodes - BIMODAL: 6 boundaries at raw-waveform NCC 0.945-1.000 (essentially IDENTICAL PCM) vs everything else + 14 content probes <=0.133. Zero overlap. Spans DIFFERENT sponsors (Pipedrive/Ketone/Stan/HeyGen/Extra) = an inserted TRANSITION element (audio logo), not ad-creative. SIGNATURE: ~0.4-0.5s cluster of ~4 broadband transient bursts, loudest tick ~35ms, spectral centroid ~3630Hz, 78% energy >2kHz - broadband/transient, not tonal. Template + occurrences at scratchpad/stinger/ (STINGER_template.wav, findings.json, stinger_3occ.png). CRITICAL ENGINEERING FINDING: it does NOT fit the existing envelope-based StingerBank (50Hz log1p-RMS): present-mean env-NCC 0.890 vs content-max 0.814 = heavy overlap; a 35ms high-freq tick is unresolved by 20ms RMS frames + its >2kHz character is discarded. BANKING IT NEEDS A SPECTRAL / RAW-WAVEFORM MATCHED-FILTER stinger capability (new) - the envelope bank only holds loud sustained musical stings (Conan/Morbid). COVERAGE ~50% (6 of ~12 interior splices, n=2 eps) = HIGH-PRECISION PARTIAL marker, pairs with FM for uncovered splices. Label reconciliation: auto-localizer (0.95 threshold, high-precision) confirms ~5 of Dan 8 hand-marks; the 3 Dan-marked-not-auto (HeyGen-e@2958, Extra-s@3976, Stan-e@2514) are weaker/variant or approximate. NetSuite/Helix outros = musical-sting post-roll (Dan: different marker) - correctly absent. Earlier ±2s NCC (0.1-0.5) + my hand-mark NCC (0.52) were UNDER-RESOLVED: wide window diluted a 35ms tick + mixed present/absent marks; tight 35-200ms raw-waveform template @0.5ms lag resolves to 0.95.

title: SUPERSEDED by playhead-xc6b: do NOT migrate these suites to PerfGate
description: Every review round of the l2f.6 wire-in (2026-07-15/16) independently confirmed the same pre-existing flake population under parallel FastTests on the loaded 16GB machine: BackfillTaskHandlerTests, BackgroundProcessingServiceLedgerTests, SettingsRecheckFlowTests, TranscriptEngineStopTranscriptionTests, ShadowRetryTests, RouteChangeTests, ScanForSuspendedTransfersTests, PlayheadAppDelegateScanWiringTests, LanePreemptionCoordinatorTests, SkipCueSmoothingTests, BackgroundTaskRunLedgerTests, PlaybackReliabilityInterruptionTests (60-104s wall-clock/latency budget signatures; all deterministic in isolation; reproduced at parent commits). Per CLAUDE.md/playhead-zx0l these belong behind PerfGate + scripts/perf-tests.sh (or need deterministic completion signals instead of bounded waits). Migrate case-by-case; do NOT mask with sleeps/retries.
acceptance_criteria: The identified suites either run green under a saturated parallel FastTests run or are PerfGate-gated into the serial perf pass; MEASUREMENT_TESTS list in scripts/perf-tests.sh updated; no assertion weakened.
close_reason:
WONT-FIX-AS-FRAMED. Superseded by playhead-xc6b, whose category analysis (two independent readers, 50 tests across PlaybackServiceActorTests + RuntimeShutdownLifecycleTests) found ZERO measurement tests, ZERO timing-is-the-contract tests, and FIFTY behavioural-with-an-incidental-timeout tests. Neither file contains a latency assertion, Task.sleep, pollUntil-on-a-budget, ContinuousClock, or Date()-elapsed computation. PerfGate exists for tests whose ASSERTION is meaningless under load; these assertions are perfectly valid under load — only the DEADLINE was too short. Migrating them would have deleted real behavioural coverage from the default gate to fix a problem PerfGate does not solve.

The corrected fix shipped on branch bead/playhead-xc6b instead: finite 3-minute hang backstops on all 50 tests (38 had NONE, so a regression hung the gate host rather than failing a test), three fail-open yield budgets replaced with positive-control-plus-barrier waits, real assertions for two assertion-free tests, teardown hygiene for 22 tests leaking process-global MPRemoteCommandCenter targets, and a test-local retain cycle fixed.

Anyone re-reading the original flake list should start from playhead-xc6b and CATEGORISE before migrating anything. The remaining suites named here (BackfillTaskHandlerTests, RouteChangeTests, SkipCueSmoothingTests, etc.) have NOT been categorised — file a fresh bead per family if they still flake, and do not assume PerfGate is the answer for them either.

title: Per-show lexical ad-read templates: station-attribution prefixes (OTM 'WNYC is brought to you by')
description: Dan ear-audit observation (2026-07-15, On The Media/WNYC): three consecutive ad reads each opened with the exact template 'WNYC is brought to you by...'. Signal: per-show/station lexical templates at read onset — exact recurring prefix + consecutive repetition — are categorically stronger than the lone generic 'brought to you by' that LexicalAutoAdEvidenceBuilder deliberately refuses to fire on (its guardrail exists for the GENERIC phrase; a per-show exact template with within-pod repetition defeats the FP rationale that gated xsdz.1 OFF in xsdz.6). These station-read underwriting spots are typically BAKED-IN — precisely the class the rediff width oracle cannot see (xsdz.31: only premium-feed diffing covers baked-ins) — so this is a complementary presence+onset anchor, not competition for rediff. Candidate shape: per-show template bank (learned from transcript n-gram repetition at high-confidence ad onsets, or curated), template hit => read-onset anchor; consecutive template hits => pod structure. Sibling insight: morbid stinger fingerprint + 30s-quantized pods (see l2f.6 notes 2026-07-15) — both are per-show structural priors, natural ShowAdSlotModel (4my.13.4) tenants.
acceptance_criteria: A measured eval on the labeled corpus: template-anchored read onsets vs silver labels for at least OTM; precision/boundary-onset error reported; explicit interaction analysis with the xsdz.6 lexical gate decision before any production wiring.
notes:
SECOND INSTANCE (Dan, same OTM audit session): next spot opened 'On The Media is sponsored by...'. Template family generalizes to '<station|show name> is {brought to you by|sponsored by|supported by}...' — parameterized on entities the app already has (feed title; station via a small public-radio mapping). First-pass template bank can therefore be COMPILED from metadata rather than learned: for each show, generate the crossproduct of {show title, station} x {sponsorship verb phrases}, exact-match at transcript onset. Self-referential show-name disclosure is a high-precision anchor the generic lexicon structurally cannot express.
THIRD PATTERN (Dan, SmartLess, same audit session): ad breaks open with host-spoken 'we'll be right back' and content resumes with 'and now back to the show'. This is a distinct anchor family from read-onset templates: BREAK-EDGE FRAMING PHRASES — they mark the boundary edges themselves, so they feed l2f.6 boundary refinement directly (pre-break outro phrase => break start just after; resume phrase => break end just before). Scope of this bead now: per-show lexical anchor bank with two families: (a) read-onset templates (OTM station/show attribution), (b) break-edge framing phrases (SmartLess). Both compile from small phrase sets + show metadata; both measured against silver labels before wiring. Running tally of per-show structural priors tonight: morbid stinger+30s grid (l2f.6), OTM templates, SmartLess framing — three shows, three exploitable signatures.
OFFLINE PROTOTYPE MEASURED (2026-07-15 overnight): scripts/l2f-lexical-anchor-prototype.py vs gold v2 (c45c86fc, 41 breaks, 22.4h). Family (a) read-onset templates: GO where compiled — 3/3 onset anchors on OTM+Radiolab, onset error +0.7..+1.3s, 6 in-break re-attributions, 0.09 FF/h (only real FP: fuzzy 'is produced by'~'is sponsored by' @0.85; ratio>=0.88 kills it, loses 0 hits → exact-verb match for production). Family (b) framing phrases: GO for core pair only — SmartLess 4/4 mid-rolls open 'we('ll| will) be right back' (-3.1..-1.0s) AND 4/4 resume '(and now|and) back to the show' (-2.0..+2.2s); 2-word/fuzzy resume phrases ('we're back','welcome back','welcome back to the show') are 0/12 traps — drop them. Corpus-wide 7/41 breaks edge-anchored = 7/8 addressable mid-rolls in the target shows (prerolls at t=0 structurally out of reach). Bonus: 4 uncorroborated pre-fires pair with resume-fires at 66-96s widths → suspected REAL unlabeled breaks (ear-check candidates); Nikki Glaser uses per-show variant 'when we GET back' (3 gold starts, ratio 0.815 sub-threshold) → strongest data yet for learned per-show bank; OTM resumes with station ident 'This is On The Media'. Report: playhead-baselines/xsdz37-lexical-prototype-20260716.md (+.json); tests scripts/tests/test_l2f_lexical_anchor.py (30 green). Nothing committed — morning review.
AUTO-GROWTH DESIGN (Dan asked 2026-07-17; discussed and banked): learn per-show lexical anchors WITHOUT manual curation. Signal source: rediff slot edges as label-free weak supervision (87% of library at ~3d gap) + gold labels + future xsdz.34 corrections; NEVER learn from lexical-channel-placed edges (circularity rule per xsdz.31). Mining: recurring normalized 2-8-token n-grams near weak-label edges, support >= K DISTINCT episodes (dedupe lesson), offset-consistency spread gate (stinger-bank discipline). Discrimination gates from the 2026-07-16 prototype data: edge-affinity ratio (phrase rate near edges vs base rate in-show — kills the welcome-back trap), exact-only short phrases (fuzzy short went 0/12), verb-exact attribution templates (produced-by/sponsored-by confusion at 0.85). Bank: StingerBank-shaped per-show lexical entries (phrase, side, offset+-spread, support, confidence), committed generator, content-addressed provenance, hermetic pins, flag-gated consumer; every regen measured via dump + gold scorer + both FP gates. Cadence: ride l2f-daily-loop; human-in-the-loop reduced to accept/reject of NEW candidate phrases in the GUI (frontier review, not break audits). Known auto-discoverable validations waiting: nikki 'when we get back' (fired at 3 gold starts sub-threshold), OTM station-ident resume, techcrunch preroll opener.

title: FM economics on iOS 27: includeSchemaInPrompt=false + session.usage + refusal-rate re-measure
description:
Exploit iOS 27's FM economics改 (NOT capacity — on-device stays 4096, confirmed twice on device): three levers, measure-first then implement approved wins.

LEVER 1 — includeSchemaInPrompt=false (new ContextOptions on every respond/streamResponse overload, iOS 27): the @Generable schema's serialized form in-prompt is the DOCUMENTED cause of the 8-10x token undercount that forced coarseBudgetDivisor=8 (bd-34e Fix B v4 comment block; schema-overhead probe test schemaTokenCountReflectsGenerableSchemaOverhead). If guided generation stays constrained with the schema OUT of the prompt, effective budgets at 4096 rise substantially — potentially collapsing coarse window counts WITHOUT any bigger model. MEASURE on device: window count + budget + quality with schema in vs out, before touching divisor math.

LEVER 2 — session.usage / Response.usage (iOS 27: Input.totalTokenCount/cachedTokenCount, Output.totalTokenCount/reasoningTokenCount): replaces estimator guesswork with ground-truth accounting. Also adopt the new typed LanguageModelError.contextSizeExceeded carrying contextSize+tokenCount — replaces the fragile error-STRING parsing in FoundationModelClassifier.extractActualTokenCount (two pinned regex formats). Also probe reasoningLevel (.light for classification?) for latency/quality trade.

LEVER 3 — REFUSAL RE-MEASURE: Apple reduced guardrail false positives in 26.4 and again in 27 (WWDC26 session 241) and rebuilt the model (gen-3). Our ~40% plan-abort figure on sensitive shows (2026-05-25, Morbid corpus) is STALE. Re-run the refusal eval on iOS 27 hardware over the sensitive-show set (PermissiveAdClassifier/SensitiveWindowRouter paths already exist) and update the number BEFORE any further refusal-workaround engineering.

Also quick-probe: UseCase.contentTagging (exists since 26.5, ZERO codebase adoption) for the coarse ad/not-ad screen vs .general.

ORDER: measure (device runs) -> report -> implement approved changes with tests (divisor/budget changes gated on the measured schema-out numbers — do NOT retune speculatively; we have been burned). NOTE: requires real device (FM graceful-unavailable on sim); keychain unlock before device builds (security unlock-keychain); DEVELOPER_DIR=Xcode-beta.
acceptance_criteria: Device-measured: schema-in vs schema-out budget/window-count/quality table; usage-API accounting adopted in measurement tooling; typed overflow error adoption assessed; refusal rate re-measured on the sensitive corpus vs the stale 40%; contentTagging quick-probe result; recommendations with numbers; any production change implemented only after the measurements and with tests.
notes:
SEQUENCING (strategy panel 2026-07-07, 5-lens convergence to keep 4my.19 BEFORE 4my.18): run the guardrail-REFUSAL RE-MEASURE as the FIRST deliverable — the ~40% Morbid/true-crime abort figure is 2026-05-25 vintage, pre-26.4/27 guardrail reductions + pre-gen-3 model, and it underwrites BOTH the 4my.18 own-a-model premise AND xsdz.17's 'refusal-proof' valuation. Attempt Mac-side FIRST (fm CLI / Catalyst batch on the 96GB M2 Max) to dodge the iPhone 95s-to-serious thermal ceiling + device-slip risk; confirm on-device only for the final figure. Panel caveat F: this stays BEHIND the rediff critical path in felt impact — FM window/budget relief does NOT fix width (width is rediff's, zero model).
HARDWARE READY (2026-07-20): iOS 27 refusal re-measure unblocked — Dan iPhone on iOS 27, and FoundationModels/gen-3 runs on the minidev Mac mini (macOS 27) via the Catalyst lane. Runnable now. Stale figure to replace: ~40% plan-abort (2026-05-25 Morbid). Last-night E-program already established refusals are content-driven + prompt-unfixable (permissive/taxonomy/schema-suppress all failed) — this measures the iOS-27 general coarse RATE + whether includeSchemaInPrompt=false fixes the budget.
MEASURED 2026-07-20 on minidev Mac mini (macOS 27.0 build 26A5378n, Xcode 27 beta), FoundationModels via Mac Catalyst. Throwaway harness FM4my19RemeasureTests (worktree bead/playhead-4my19-remeasure @0bbfea88, NOT merged). Ran the production coarse @Generable ad/not-ad call (schema-in, one-shot instructions, greedy, raw text no redaction) over 1499 real 30s windows: 1133 sensitive (morbid/casefile/unexplained/american-scandal/radiolab) + 366 benign control (conan/business-wars). All 4 levers' iOS-27 symbols verified PRESENT in the shipping macOS 27.0 dylib (dyld_info -exports) AND live-run.

=== LEVER 3 (HEADLINE) — REFUSAL RE-MEASURE ===
Per-window coarse safety-refusal rate ("May contain sensitive content"/"unsafe content"):
  SENSITIVE overall: 326/1133 = 28.8%   (vs stale ~40% plan-abort, 2026-05-25 Morbid)
  morbid            156/546 = 28.6%
  american-scandal   59/74  = 79.7%  (outlier — dense graphic crime)
  unexplained        60/243 = 24.7%
  casefile           41/190 = 21.6%
  radiolab           10/80  = 12.5%
  BENIGN control     56/366 = 15.3% (conan 12.5%, business-wars 25.3%)
  by label (sensitive): ad 32.3%, not_ad 28.3% (crime NARRATION, not ads, refuses ~as often)
Refusals are content-driven safety rejections, NOT prompt-fixable (confirms E-program). iOS-27 gen-3 model refuses LESS than the stale ~40% but the floor is still ~29% on true-crime and ~80% on the worst show — a refusal-free owned specialist still buys materially on sensitive shows. Apple did NOT close the gap. NOTE metric mismatch: stale 40% = episode plan-abort; this = per-window rate (cleaner). Coarse latency p50 888ms / p90 1223ms (Mac ANE).

*** iOS-27 ERROR-TAXONOMY BUG (found by re-measure) ***
Concrete thrown type on iOS/macOS 27 is the NEW `LanguageModelError` (382/382), NOT legacy `LanguageModelSession.GenerationError`. Our production `SemanticScanStatus.from(error:)` only casts to the legacy type -> EVERY refusal + context-overflow maps to `.failedTransient` on iOS 27. Consequences: (1) permissive-fallback/SensitiveWindowRouter path keyed on `.refusal` will NOT fire; (2) smart-shrink retry keyed on `.exceededContextWindow` will NOT fire (overflow also throws LanguageModelError.contextSizeExceeded); refusals/overflows get wrongly retried transiently. This is a real P1-class regression latent in shipped iOS-27 handling. Fix = add `error as? LanguageModelError` mapping in SemanticScanStatus.from(error:). RECOMMEND bead.

=== LEVER 1 — includeSchemaInPrompt=false ===
Mac on-device model reports contextSize=8192 (NOT 4096; still availability=available, on-device not PCC). CAVEAT: iPhone iOS 27 reportedly still 4096 — window is platform-dependent; the dormant ÷8->÷4 large-context branch is ACTIVE at 8192 on Mac.
Ground-truth schema-injection cost (Response.usage.input.totalTokenCount, same prompt in vs out): schemaIN=417, schemaOUT=247 -> schema costs 170 input tokens (native coarse-schema tokenCount=179; fallback estimate 128 UNDER-counts). Coarse budget @8192 ÷8: schemaIN=973 vs schemaOUT=996 (+23 tokens); @4096 ÷8 the delta is +22. => schema-out barely moves the budget; the DIVISOR dominates, not the schema. Dispositions identical in vs out (containsAd/containsAd). VERDICT: Lever 1 (schema-out) alone is NOT worth a bead — negligible budget effect. The real economics lever is the divisor, which needs ground-truth accounting (Lever 2), not schema-out.
Bonus: our fallbackTokenEstimate OVER-counts prompt tokens 2.21x vs Apple native tokenCount (avg over 20 windows) -> the ÷8 safety factor is now very conservative on iOS 27.

=== LEVER 2 — session.usage / Response.usage / typed error ===
ALL available and functional on macOS 27: Response.usage / session.usage report input.totalTokenCount, input.cachedTokenCount, output.totalTokenCount, output.reasoningTokenCount (reasoning=0 for classification). Typed overflow: `LanguageModelError.contextSizeExceeded(contextSize:8192, tokenCount:40054)` carries both fields directly. Our regex extractActualTokenCount still parsed 40054 (string unchanged) BUT status-mapping is broken (Lever 3 bug). RECOMMEND bead: adopt LanguageModelError mapping + typed contextSizeExceeded (kills the fragile 2-format regex) + wire usage accounting to replace the 2.21x-over estimator so the divisor can be safely retuned. Highest-value lever because it both FIXES the taxonomy bug and unlocks real window-count relief.

=== LEVER 4 — UseCase.contentTagging (probe) ===
Available (availability=available). But WORSE for the coarse screen: it's a tagger (returns "podcast, sponsorship, promotion, discount" not ad/not_ad), ParsingError on plain content, and STILL refuses pharma (cvs read -> LanguageModelError "May contain sensitive content"). .general handled all 4 probes cleanly (not_ad/ad/ad/not_ad). VERDICT: do NOT adopt contentTagging; not refusal-free, wrong output shape. No bead.

=== RECOMMENDATIONS ===
1. Lever 2 error-taxonomy fix (LanguageModelError mapping in SemanticScanStatus) — YES, P1 bead (latent iOS-27 regression; blocks permissive-fallback + smart-shrink).
2. Lever 2 usage-accounting adoption + divisor retune — YES bead, but MEASURE contextSize on the actual iPhone (4096 vs Mac 8192) first; retune gated on ground-truth usage, not speculative.
3. Lever 1 schema-out — NO standalone bead (negligible; ~20 tokens).
4. Lever 4 contentTagging — NO.
SPECIALIST DECISION (4my.18): iOS-27 refusal dropped 40%->~29% on true-crime but did NOT close — refusal-free owned specialist still materially valuable on sensitive shows (up to 80% on worst). Refusal advantage is real, just smaller than the stale figure implied. Consistent with 4my.18 Phase-2 GO-WITH-CAVEATS (specialist shrinks not replaces FM).
Note: minidev logged CriticalMemoryPressure during FM runs (16GB tight). Full artifacts in session scratchpad/4my19 (refusal_sweep_rows.json, sweep.log, probes.log).

title: SpanFinalizer split (>180s) produces both halves sharing parent DecodedSpan.id
description:
## Context

PR #214 wired SpanFinalizer into AdDetectionService.runBackfill. R2's review identified that when SpanFinalizer's constraint #3 (`splitAboveMaxDuration` at 180s) fires, both halves of the split inherit the parent's `DecodedSpan.id` (because the id is derived from `(assetId, firstAtomOrdinal, lastAtomOrdinal)` and the splits reuse the parent's atom range).

The wire-in's `traceById` map appends both halves' traces under the same key, so the resulting trace becomes `[.splitAboveMaxDuration, .splitAboveMaxDuration, .policyOverrideApplied, .policyOverrideApplied]` etc. Both half-spans then receive the same combined trace via the emission-loop lookup, doubling up the trace.

Additionally, both half-spans share `spanFingerprint`/`spanFeatureWindows`/`spanTopCatalogSimilarity`, which would cause two `AdCatalogStore` inserts with the same fingerprint but different bounds. `AdCatalogStore.insert` UPSERTs on `(show_id, fingerprint_blob)` so the second is at best a no-op upsert; at worst silently fails or skews `originalConfidence`.

## Scope

When SpanFinalizer's split (>180s) fires:
- Either: assign distinct `spanId`s to the halves (requires extending the id derivation to include split-index) so trace and catalog lookup behave correctly per-half
- Or: change the wire-in to use a `(spanId, index)` compound key for trace lookup, AND deduplicate catalog inserts on split
- Or: document this as known behavior (current) and ensure bd-4xqf analyzer doesn't double-count trace entries when computing per-window attribution

## Acceptance

title: SpanFinalizer merge (constraint #2) drops curr's ledger/fingerprint/catalog context
description:
## Context

PR #214 wired SpanFinalizer into AdDetectionService.runBackfill behind a default-OFF flag (`spanFinalizerEnabled`). R2's review (Finding #2, Medium) identified a data-loss issue in the wire-in's interaction with SpanFinalizer's merge constraint:

When SpanFinalizer's constraint #2 (`minimum content gap < 3s → merge`) collapses two pending decisions, the surviving WorkingSpan carries `prev.spanId`. The wire-in's `pendingByOriginalId[span.span.id]` lookup resolves to `prev`'s pending record only — `curr`'s pending record (its `ledger`, `effectiveLedger`, `spanFingerprint`, `spanFeatureWindows`, `spanTopCatalogSimilarity`) is silently dropped from emission.

Downstream `AdCatalogStore.insert` and `RepeatedAdCache` ingress use only `prev`'s fingerprint context. Not a production bug today (flag OFF by default), but a real ON-arm semantic that the bd-4xqf measurement run needs to account for.

## Scope

When SpanFinalizer's merge fires:
- Decide: should `curr`'s ledger be MERGED with `prev`'s into a single combined ledger? Or should `curr`'s data be PRESERVED via a sibling entry? Or is dropping `curr` the correct semantics?
- If merge: define how to combine `effectiveLedger` (union? intersection? max-confidence-per-source?)
- If preserve: emit both decisions but with the merged span bounds
- Update the wire-in's `pendingByOriginalId` lookup to handle the chosen semantics

## Acceptance

- Behavior under SpanFinalizer merge is explicitly tested (currently pinned by p56a `spanFinalizerMergeKeepsFirstCandidateIdAndDropsSecond` test, but that test only asserts the current data-loss, not corrected behavior)
- `spanFinalizerConstraintsFired` trace correctly attributes the merged span
- Documentation in `docs/bd-4xqf-codepath-map.md` reflects the chosen semantics

## Cross-references

- PR #214 (p56a wire-in)
- bd: playhead-p56a (parent)
- bd: playhead-4xqf (FUSION_DROP investigation)
- R2 commit: 331dc380

title: Cross-show syndication signal (blind-spot: ad-marketplace structure across the user's library)
description:
BLIND-SPOT CONVERGENCE from the dueling-wizards duel — reached INDEPENDENTLY by both models post-adversarial: cc-BS3 (sponsor-entity spread across the user's subscribed shows) ≈ cod-BS1 (cross-show near-duplicate audio/text fingerprint graph). Highest-novelty idea in the duel.

MECHANISM: use the user's MULTI-SHOW subscription portfolio as a signal source. Ad campaigns are sold across show networks — a sponsor (BetterHelp, Shopify, etc.) or a near-duplicate segment recurring across many UNRELATED subscribed shows is overwhelming evidence of a paid network campaign; an editorial brand mention is show-specific. The signal is invisible at the single-show level. The existing SponsorKnowledgeStore is keyed per-podcast — nothing aggregates entities/fingerprints ACROSS shows.

ON-DEVICE: ~100 lines — SQLite cross-show observation table (sponsor_normalized, podcast_id, counts, confidence) + spread-ratio query (distinctShows / totalShows) + capped evidence builder. Reuse existing sponsor normalization for ASR variation.

RISKS: users with 1-2 shows get no signal; brands with genuine multi-show EDITORIAL bursts (Apple at a product launch, a major news story) → require spread-ratio > 0.3 AND temporal persistence (multi-month, not a one-week burst); cold start measured in weeks of normal listening.

SUCCESS: precision lift for portfolio listeners (boost true network-campaign ads, suppress show-specific editorial FPs); spread-ratio as a capped channel, off-by-default until measured.
notes:
---
2026-06-01 CLOSURE RATIONALE (was previously closed with no documented reason; this note pins the evidence):

Closed based on the negative result from the xsdz.13 feasibility prototype landed
2026-06-01 in PR #205 (`scripts/l2f-syndication-prototype.py` +
`analysis/syndication-prototype-2026-06-01.md`).

Findings on the live 41-episode corpus:
  - 23,043 of 26,005 windows (89%) tripped a "cross-show tight match" — overwhelming
    false-positive rate.
  - Root cause: cross-episode random-pair Hamming distance on chromaprint+SimHash
    averages 19.2 bits — well below the 32-bit expectation for random 64-bit hashes.
    The fingerprint is picking up a generic "this is podcast speech" signature, not
    per-segment content.
  - Discriminating control test: best cross-show Hamming for known audit_priority=1
    ad spans (mean 4.9, n=8) is statistically indistinguishable from random windows
    (mean 3.5) — even slightly in the wrong direction.

Conclusion: chromaprint+SimHash is not a viable substrate for cross-show ad
syndication on a podcast-speech corpus. The conceptual signal (sponsor reuse
across networks) may still exist but a viable implementation would require:
  (a) a less voice-biased acoustic fingerprint (MFCC+DTW, openl3), OR
  (b) a much larger corpus where real syndicated ads recur enough to clear the
      speech-bias floor, OR
  (c) contiguous raw-chromaprint matching like l2f-dai-rediff.py uses on per-
      episode pairs (extended to N-way cross-show pairwise comparison — expensive).

Re-opening this bead requires NEW evidence beyond what PR #205 already disproved.
The duel-wizard "blindspot convergence" between cc-BS3 and cod-BS1 is preserved
in the analysis report for archeology; the conceptual idea isn't wrong, just the
chromaprint+SimHash implementation path is.

title: Per-show threshold control from user feedback (PID/PI-like, defer learned models)
description:
CONSENSUS #5 from the dueling-wizards duel. cc#15 PID controller (cod 735) ≈ cod#5/#15 (online learner + user micro-signals). RESOLVED disagreement: both converged on a SIMPLE bounded scalar controller first, deferring richer learned models as too data-hungry (<50 corrections/show).

MECHANISM: a PID-like (start with PI — drop the noisy derivative term) bounded controller that adapts the PER-SHOW autoSkip threshold from user actions. Listen-through an auto-skipped section = FP error (raise threshold); manual scrub through undetected content = miss error (lower threshold); accepted skip = no error. Per-show adaptation handles the heterogeneity a single global threshold can't.

ON-DEVICE: small PID/PI state (offset, integral, last_error) per show in the existing UserCorrectionStore; runs on user-action events only (zero compute cost); threshold bounded [0.55, 0.95]; small gains (Kp~0.02, Ki~0.005).

RISKS: sparse/noisy feedback → minimum-sample gate before adjusting; cold start (default threshold until corrections accumulate); passive users provide no signal; user may scrub for non-ad reasons.

SUCCESS: per-show convergence to the user's tolerance operating point; FP reduction in offline replay before activation. DEPENDS ON the user-correction event infrastructure.

title: Evidence-window CoreML ad ranker over deterministic features (golden-trained, NOT FM-distilled)
description: Idea C3 (cod 810; cf cc #16 distill=540). title: Plan-quality eval: hand-labeled golden set for boundary/disposition accuracy
description: Hand-labeled golden chapter set + automated quality eval that measures boundary recall/precision and disposition accuracy independent of downstream detection lift. Decouples 'is the chapter signal sound?' from 'does it help ad detection?' so detector and labeler can be tuned in isolation. Lower priority than E1-E3 because aggregate eval and case studies cover the headline 'does this work' question; this bead is for tuning insight.
design:
Files affected:
- PlayheadTests/Fixtures/ChapterPlanGoldenSet/ (new directory with hand-labeled chapter fixtures)
- PlayheadTests/Services/ReplaySimulator/NarlEval/ChapterPlanQualityEval.swift (new — quality scoring against goldens)

Purpose: separately measure how well ChapterGenerationPhase produces correct chapters, independent of whether downstream detection improves. This decouples 'is the boundary detector good?' and 'is the labeler good?' from 'does the chapter signal help ad detection overall?'

Why decouple: aggregate detection lift (E2) can be noisy or negative due to many factors (consumer wiring bugs, weight tuning, fusion interactions). Plan quality eval tells us whether the chapter signal itself is sound, even when downstream consumption is broken. Lets us tune detector + labeler independently.

Hand-labeled golden set (target 5-10 episodes):
- Per episode: human-curated [GoldenChapter] annotations
- GoldenChapter: { startTime, expectedDisposition: ChapterDisposition, expectedTopicLabel: String? }
- Coverage: include conversational, narrative, comedy archetypes
- Mostly overlap with case study set (E3) but may include extras

Quality metrics:

Boundary recall:
- For each ground-truth chapter boundary, did the detector find a candidate within ±15s?
- recall = found / total_ground_truth

Boundary precision:
- For each detector candidate, was there a ground-truth boundary within ±15s?
- precision = matched / total_candidates

Disposition accuracy:
- For each (matched detector boundary, ground-truth boundary) pair, did the FM labeler assign the correct ChapterDisposition?
- accuracy = correct_dispositions / total_matched

Topic label sanity (optional, lightweight):
- For each labeled chapter with a topicDescriptor, does it overlap >50% with the ground-truth label's keywords?
- (Loose check; topic labels are nice-to-have, not load-bearing.)

Output report:
struct ChapterPlanQualityReport:
  - boundaryRecall: Double
  - boundaryPrecision: Double
  - dispositionAccuracy: Double
  - perEpisode: [EpisodeId: PerEpisodeQuality]
  - perDispositionConfusion: [Disposition: [Disposition: Int]]  (confusion matrix)
  - thresholdsUsed: { boundaryToleranceSeconds, topicOverlapMinimum }

Use the report to tune:
- Boundary detector signal weights (bump music if recall drops on creator-chapter-validated boundaries)
- FM labeler prompt wording (if disposition accuracy is consistently wrong on certain types)
- Density gate thresholds (if many low-confidence boundaries are dropped that turn out to be real)

What this bead does NOT do:
- Build the gate infrastructure (E1)
- Aggregate detection lift (E2)
- Case studies (E3, though may share fixtures)
- Tune the system based on findings — that's a follow-up bead

Run cadence:
- Run on each PR that touches detector, labeler, or phase
- Compare metrics across runs; regressions in any metric require justification

Test coverage:
- Synthetic golden set replays against a stubbed phase produces expected metrics
- Confusion matrix correctness on known mappings
- Threshold parameters configurable

Hand-labeling effort:
- Estimated 30-60 minutes per episode at first; ~6 episodes total (3-6 hours of labeling)
- Best done by Dan since these are his dogfood episodes; he knows the ground truth from listening
acceptance_criteria:
- ChapterPlanQualityEval evaluator implemented at PlayheadTests/Services/ReplaySimulator/NarlEval/ChapterPlanQualityEval.swift
- ChapterPlanQualityReport struct with: boundaryRecall, boundaryPrecision, dispositionAccuracy, perEpisode, perDispositionConfusion, thresholdsUsed
- Configurable boundary tolerance (default ±15s) and topic-overlap minimum (default 0.5) parameters
- Synthetic golden-set fixtures (≥3 hand-coded synthetic episodes covering happy-path / partial-recall / disposition-confusion) checked into PlayheadTests/Fixtures/ChapterPlanGoldenSet/synthetic/
- Synthetic-fixture tests pass deterministically and exercise: full-recall path, partial-boundary-miss path, disposition-confusion-matrix correctness, threshold-parameter sensitivity
- Quality report runnable on demand against frozen-trace inputs (test entry point)
- Privacy: no PII or advertiser names in synthetic labels (anonymized synthetic only)
- Real dogfood-episode golden labels are NOT in scope here — that work moves to a follow-up bead requiring human (Dan) hand-labeling
notes:
2026-05-08 — SCOPE SPLIT (Dan + orchestrator):
Original bead bundled (a) ChapterPlanQualityEval infrastructure + (b) 5–10 hand-labeled real dogfood episode goldens.
Split per Dan: (a) stays in this bead and is dispatched autonomously via iterative-implementation-with-review-loops; (b) moves to follow-up bead playhead-au2v.1.22 because it requires human listening + hand-curation of ground-truth chapter boundaries/dispositions/topics. Acceptance criteria above narrowed accordingly.

title: reconcileStrandedFinalPassJobs clears deferReason on running->queued flip (B-3)
description:
Optional cosmetic: extend resetStrandedFinalPassJobs UPDATE to also set deferReason=NULL when flipping running -> queued. The audit-trail string ('thermalThrottled' etc.) is misleading after the row is being retried fresh.

Why: A stranded 'running' row with deferReason='thermalThrottled' (preserved from an earlier deferred->running transition per the audit-trail design at AnalysisStore.swift:6852-6856) reads confusingly to operators inspecting the DB — looks like the row is stuck on a thermal block when actually it's been re-queued. After the reaper flip, the audit trail has served its purpose.

How to apply: AnalysisStore.swift:7240-7253 resetStrandedFinalPassJobs SQL: add 'deferReason = NULL,' to the UPDATE SET clause.

Risk: low — cosmetic; no behavior change because no caller reads deferReason for routing.

title: harden duration-backfill OFFSET cursor against concurrent INSERT/DELETE
description: rfu-csp M2/M3 deferral. AnalysisCoordinator's duration-backfill sweep paginates by SQL OFFSET. Concurrent INSERT or DELETE on the asset table during the sweep can cause the cursor to skip or duplicate rows. Cycle-3 documented the brittleness in code but did not fix it. Proper fix: switch to keyset pagination (WHERE id > :lastSeenId ORDER BY id LIMIT :pageSize) or take a snapshot read at sweep start. Low priority because backfill is run on a schedule when contention is low, but worth pinning before we start running multiple backfill sweeps concurrently.

title: replace BackgroundProcessingService injectionWait 15s with deterministic seam
description: rfu-csp L3 deferral. The injectionWait timeout was reduced from 20s to 15s in cycle-1, but the underlying design (poll-and-wait for the BG-task scheduler to honor a submission) remains timing-fragile. A test-only seam that completes synchronously when the stub scheduler accepts the submission would eliminate the wall-clock dependency entirely. Risk: under heavy device load, 15s may still flake — we just made the failure window smaller, not closed it.

title: Mac port spike: native macOS app scoping
description:
Scope a native macOS app target (separate from iOS) sharing the analysis/detection service layer.

## Goal

## Pre-req

## What to scope

title: Analysis-version bump should produce fresh jobs in same reconciler pass (Gap-10)
description:
**From audit playhead-5uvz Gap-10 (LOW).**

`AnalysisJobReconciler.supersedeStaleVersions` (step 4) marks every non-terminal job with a stale analysisVersion as `superseded`. But it does NOT enqueue replacement jobs at the new analysis version. The new job for the same episode only gets created on the next `discoverUnEnqueuedDownloads` pass (step 7), which only fires for episodes whose downloads exist but have no active job rows.

**Open question for this bead:** Reading `AnalysisStore.fetchActiveJobEpisodeIds`: does it filter `superseded` out of the active set? If yes, the same-pass re-enqueue works (step 7 sees no active job, creates a fresh queued one). If no, the same-episode re-enqueue happens on the NEXT launch's reconciler pass.

Either way, **analysis-version bumps shipped via in-process update (e.g. test harness, hot config) won't see new jobs until the next launch.**

**Fix scope:**
1. Verify `fetchActiveJobEpisodeIds` filtering — read `AnalysisStore.swift`.
2. If `superseded` IS treated as terminal: same-pass re-enqueue already works on cold launch but may not work in-process. Add an explicit re-enqueue from `supersedeStaleVersions` for clarity.
3. If `superseded` is NOT treated as terminal: filter it explicitly in `fetchActiveJobEpisodeIds` AND have `supersedeStaleVersions` enqueue a replacement.
4. Add regression test that bumps `PreAnalysisConfig.analysisVersion` mid-test and asserts `reconcile()` produces new `queued` rows for every superseded one.

**Files:** `Playhead/Services/PreAnalysis/AnalysisJobReconciler.swift` (`supersedeStaleVersions`, `discoverUnEnqueuedDownloads`), `Playhead/Persistence/AnalysisStore/AnalysisStore.swift` (`fetchActiveJobEpisodeIds`).

See: `docs/audits/2026-04-25-episode-job-dag-audit.md`

title: Emit work_journal row on transcription timeout with structured metadata (Gap-9)
description:
**From audit playhead-5uvz Gap-9 (LOW).**

The 5-minute `Task.sleep(for: .seconds(300))` race in `AnalysisJobRunner.run` fires silently when transcription stalls. The runner returns `.failed("transcription:zeroCoverage")` (becomes `lastErrorCode` on the analysis_jobs row), but the journal sees nothing (Gap-1).

If a class of episodes (long, refusal-prone, music-heavy) systematically times out, there's no aggregate signal — operators have to grep `lastErrorCode = 'transcription:zeroCoverage'` across all rows. A journaled `failed/transcriptionTimeout` event with episodeDuration and chunksPersisted in metadata would immediately surface the pattern.

**Depends on:** playhead-5uvz.1 (Gap-1) — without journal rows being written in production, this is a no-op.

**Fix scope:** After Gap-1 lands, emit a structured `work_journal` row from the timeout branch with eventType=failed and metadata containing episodeDuration, transcriptCoverageEndTime, chunksPersisted, and the chunk persistence rate at timeout.

**Files:** `Playhead/Services/AnalysisJobRunner/AnalysisJobRunner.swift` (transcription timeout branch).

See: `docs/audits/2026-04-25-episode-job-dag-audit.md`

title: AnalysisJobRunner should persist episodeDurationSec after stage 1 (Gap-7)
description:
**From audit playhead-5uvz Gap-7 (LOW).**

The coverage guard at `AnalysisCoordinator.runFromBackfill:1336` needs `analysis_assets.episodeDurationSec` to compute the coverage ratio.

- **Pipeline A (coordinator)** writes it after decoding shards in `runFromSpooling`.
- **Pipeline B (scheduler/runner)** decodes shards but does NOT call `store.updateEpisodeDuration`.

If a job is exclusively driven through Pipeline B (user enqueues 4 episodes overnight and never presses play — the fuo6 scenario), `episodeDurationSec` stays NULL. The coverage guard's fail-safe shortcut to `.restart` triggers (gtt9.1.1 introduced this fail-safe specifically to prevent silent over-reports). The gap here is that it bites every Pipeline-B-only episode.

**Fix scope:** Have `AnalysisJobRunner.run` write `store.updateEpisodeDuration` after stage 1 if the asset's value is NULL. Cheap one-liner.

**Files:** `Playhead/Services/AnalysisJobRunner/AnalysisJobRunner.swift` (stage 1), `Playhead/Persistence/AnalysisStore/AnalysisStore.swift` (`updateEpisodeDuration`).

See: `docs/audits/2026-04-25-episode-job-dag-audit.md`

title: Phase B: chunked acoustic fingerprint matching for DAI shows
description:
Extend cross-user analysis sharing (parent: playhead-bbrv) to dynamic-ad-insertion feeds (Megaphone, Art19, Wondery, NPR).

Full-file SHA fails on these because every listener receives a different stitched MP3. The host-read content is still bit-identical between listeners; only the ad slots differ.

## Approach
- Reuse existing catalog fingerprint infrastructure (playhead-gtt9.13)
- Chunk audio into N-second windows
- Compute acoustic fingerprint per chunk
- Match host-read chunks across listeners; treat unmatched chunks as DAI ad slots (themselves a useful signal)
- Project shared analysis onto local timeline using chunk alignment

## Blocked on
- playhead-bbrv.1 (Phase A spike) — validate the thesis on the easy case before tackling DAI complexity

## Open questions
- Chunk size / fingerprint algorithm choice (lifted from gtt9.13 vs. tuned)
- How to handle slight encoder differences (CDN re-transcodes) — fingerprint must be robust
- Privacy: chunk fingerprints are smaller leak surface than full-file SHA but still listening-behavior-adjacent

title: Stamp device detector-version / git-SHA into FrozenTrace capture provenance
description:
## Problem
FrozenTrace.capturedAt reflects when the harness ingested the corpus export, not when the device session actually ran. When debugging a regression, there is no way to tell whether a fixture was produced by a device binary built before or after a given commit.

## Evidence
2026-04-24 investigation (gtt9.18) found the Conan fixture at capturedAt=2026-04-24T03:33:48Z — 1 h after commit 6e37335 fixed the hot-path log-action bug — but the fixture still contains policyAction='hotPathCandidate' for a 0.815 score (pre-fix behavior). It took a commit-log archaeology round to decide whether this was a fix regression or a capture provenance issue.

## Fix
Add two fields to FrozenTrace schema:
- detectorVersion: mirror AdDetectionConfig.detectorVersion at session time
- buildCommitSHA: short SHA of the app binary that produced the DecisionLog

Both thread through corpus-export → FrozenTrace → harness reports.

## Acceptance
- New capture bundles carry both fields.
- Harness reports group rollups by detectorVersion so a mixed-binary fleet shows its own variance.
- Unit test confirms FrozenTrace round-trip decoding preserves both fields.

## Parent
Diagnosis: docs/narl/2026-04-24-finding1-conan-classifier-diagnosis.md (investigation/gtt9.18).
Not blocking gtt9.19/gtt9.20 — can ship independently.

title: nar0: Counterfactual-eval harness (dual-config diff + metrics + report emitter)
description:
## Background

Parking-lot bead. Blocked on labeled corpus existing — estimated \"a while\" from 2026-04-21. Don't start this until `playhead-l3hg` (narA corrections) has generated enough real labels to make metrics meaningful (rough threshold: 20+ labeled episodes spanning the ad-type × ad-position taxonomy).

Purpose: the measurement apparatus that eventually unblocks `playhead-narl` (metadata activation for all users).

## Scope

Extend `PlayheadTests/IntegrationTests/CorpusVerificationTests.swift`:

### Dual-config mode
- Run each corpus episode through both `MetadataActivationConfig.default` and `.allEnabled` (and later, per-component variants for staged activation).
- Offline replay path: ingest `decision-log.jsonl` from narL and reconstruct `.default`-equivalent decisions without re-running the pipeline — faster iteration than full re-execution.

### Metric computation
Against `GroundTruthAdSegment` annotations (from narA corrections + any hand-crafted fixtures):
- **Precision**: TP skips / (TP + FP skips)
- **Recall**: TP skips / ground-truth ads
- **Boundary IoU**: overlap of decided window vs. true ad window
- Per-metric 95% CIs so \"no regression\" claims are statistical, not vibes.

### Report emitter
- Markdown + CSV outputs per run.
- Per-episode deltas (not just aggregates) — catches cases where aggregate looks fine but individual episodes regress hard.
- Easy to eyeball which episode × ad-type cells are driving the numbers.

### Per-component variants
- Not just `.default` vs `.allEnabled` — also `lexicalInjectionEnabled` alone, `classifierPriorShiftEnabled` alone, etc.
- Enables staged activation decisions (narl-1/narl-2/narl-3) instead of all-or-nothing.

## Decision rule (applied downstream, not here)

Activation gate flips only when:
1. Precision not lower than baseline within 95% CI.
2. At least one metric measurably improved.
3. No individual episode regresses from auto-skip to wrong-skip.

nar0 produces the numbers; the flip decision is still a human judgment call.

## Explicit blockers before starting

- `playhead-l3hg` (narA) must be landed AND producing corrections.
- ≥20 labeled episodes covering taxonomy cells (midRoll/pre/post × dynamic/host-read/blended/produced).
- Corpus expansion can happen via Dan's dogfooding (narA) OR hand-crafted golden fixtures OR both.

## Why parking-lot P3

- Corpus doesn't exist yet; methodology without data is theater.
- narL unblocks personal activation benefit without needing this.
- When corpus arrives, promote to P1 and scope this bead concretely.

title: Evaluate / activate B9 structured boundary extraction (alternative FM path)
description:
Dead-evidence sweep finding from 2026-04-21. FoundationModelClassifier.swift:1822 exposes an entire alternative FM boundary extraction path gated by the comment: 'B9: Structured boundary extraction (not yet wired into pipeline — coarsePassA/refinePassB retained as active path)'.

The function extractBoundaries takes plans and candidateSpans and returns FMBoundaryExtractionOutput with per-discourse-unit role labels carrying commercial intent and ownership metadata. This is structurally different from the coarsePassA/refinePassB path that is currently live — it's a more structured schema per segment.

Because the two paths coexist but only one is wired, this is an architectural decision point rather than a straightforward activation. If B9 is strictly better on quality/cost, sunset the old path. If the old path is strictly better or if the difference is marginal, delete B9 rather than let it rot.
design:
Investigation pass, not an implementation bead:

1. Measure — run both paths on a representative corpus; compare boundary quality, latency, token cost, refusal rate.
2. Decide — B9 replaces, B9 supplements (e.g. for sensitive / ownership-critical windows), or B9 is deleted.
3. If activate: wire B9 into AdDetectionService, deprecate the old path, update tests.
4. If delete: remove the B9 dead code + schema to reduce maintenance surface.

This is priority 3 because it's not obviously value-accretive in either direction and the current path works. But leaving a parallel FM schema around indefinitely is tech debt.
acceptance_criteria:
- Empirical comparison of B9 vs. coarsePassA/refinePassB on quality + cost metrics
- Explicit decision: activate, supplement, or delete
- If activate: old path sunset on a schedule
- If delete: B9 code + schema + related types removed cleanly
- No dormant alternative path remaining

title: BackgroundProcessingService: taskExpired pause-cause flake under parallel load
description:
Observed flake in PlayheadIntegrationTests (run during playhead-fpsl/ss38 fix work, 2026-04-18):

```
Test "Expiration handler requests pause with cause=.taskExpired and fails task" recorded an issue at BackgroundProcessingServiceTests.swift:309:9: Expectation failed: (failedJournalCalls.first?.cause → nil) == .taskExpired
```

Test expected the BG-task expiration handler to fire and journal a failed-task entry with cause=.taskExpired, but the journal was empty at assertion time. Likely an async ordering race: the assertion ran before the expiration handler's effect propagated to the journal.

Suggested investigation: add an explicit await on a journal-flush signal, or poll the journal with a short timeout instead of single-shot read.

Frequency: 1 in ~6 integration runs observed. P3 (lower than ss38 because not a latency-budget pattern; appears to be a one-off async ordering race in this specific test).
notes: INVESTIGATION 2026-07-24: ALREADY FIXED. BackgroundProcessingServiceTests.expirationHandlerTriggersPauseAtNextCheckpoint no longer does the racy single-shot journal read the bead describes — it now awaits an event-driven signal (task.awaitExpirationHandlerInstalled(), commented 'Event-driven (playhead-vsot): no deadline to starve under load'), deterministically triggers expiry via expireContinuedProcessingTaskForTesting, and the stub coordinator gates the workflow on pauseAtNextCheckpointCalls so it 'exits deterministically without wall-clock races.' Fixed under the playhead-vsot de-flake work. RECOMMEND close as fixed.

title: LanePreemption promotion-latency microbenchmark flakes under PlayheadFastTests parallel load
description:
The 1000-tap `promotionLatencyUnder100ms` test (in `LanePreemptionCoordinatorTests`, "Hard User Preemption" suite) measures `preemptLowerLanes(.now)` against a 100ms ceiling. Production budget is correct but the test is sensitive to cooperative-pool contention from the 446-suite parallel PlayheadFastTests run — observed ~1 in 4 flakes with `maxElapsed ≈ 700ms–980ms` on iPhone 17 Pro simulator under heavy load (post-OOM 2026-04-17 incident, and again on a calmer machine 2026-04-18).

Fix options:
1. Extract into a dedicated `@Suite("LanePreemptionPromotionLatency")` with `.serialized` and route only that suite into PlayheadIntegrationTests (keeps the test alive but removes from per-bead default).
2. Mark the existing `@Test` with `.serialized` and increase budget headroom.
3. Convert from microbenchmark to coarser correctness check (e.g. assert <= 500ms rather than 100ms — but this defeats the purpose).

Option (1) is preferred — preserves architectural intent, removes per-bead noise.

Discovered while fixing playhead-01t8 round-trip flake (separate issue, fixed in commit 26bca6f).

title: Polish: MockBackgroundTaskScheduler lock pattern + MockStorageBudget forcedDecision reset
description:
Code-quality review of playhead-iwiy flagged two non-blocking defensive-programming items:

**I1**: `MockBackgroundTaskScheduler.submit(_:)` at `PlayheadTests/TestSupport/InterruptionMocks.swift:52-60` uses manual `lock.lock()` + pair of unlocks (one for the throw path, one at end) rather than `defer { lock.unlock() }`. Sibling methods in the same type use defer. A future early-return/throw addition would deadlock. Change to `lock.lock(); defer { lock.unlock() }` at method start.

**I2**: `MockStorageBudget.forcedDecision` at `InterruptionMocks.swift:143-146` persists across cycles within a test method. Current tests don't mix cycle types within one method so it's safe, but a future mixed-type umbrella test could observe a stale forced decision. Either clear `forcedDecision` at the end of `runStoragePressurePathway` or clear per-cycle in `cycle(...)` after the release.

Neither is a bug in the shipped harness; both are latent footguns against hypothetical refactors. Addresses code-review findings I1 + I2 from playhead-iwiy review.

title: Test hygiene: move remaining test callsites to makeTempDir + tearDown
description:
Low-priority cleanup surfaced during test teardown audit. Fixes narrow leaks that don't cause user-visible disk pressure but make flaky-test debugging harder.

## Findings from teardown audit

Seven callsites bypass the existing makeTempDir / TestTempDirTracker helpers and leak small artifacts per run:

### 1-2. makeTestRequest helpers (leak on every @Test invocation)
- PlayheadTests/Services/AnalysisJobRunner/AnalysisJobRunnerTests.swift:11
- PlayheadTests/Services/RunnerMaterializerRegressionTests.swift:35

Each mints \`<NSTemporaryDirectory>/<Prefix>-<UUID>/episode.m4a\` (empty file + dir). Called by dozens of @Test cases per run. No defer, no tracker. ~0 B per file but inode leak under repeated runs without sim reset.

**Fix**: wrap both in defer { try? FileManager.removeItem } or take a caller-provided tracker URL.

### 3-4. SkipOrchestrator XCTest suites (AnalysisStore + WAL/SHM per test)
- PlayheadTests/Services/SkipOrchestrator/SkipCueMaterializerTests.swift:13
- PlayheadTests/Services/SkipOrchestrator/SkipOrchestratorPreloadTests.swift:14

XCTest \`setUp()\` creates \`<prefix>-<UUID>\` and opens AnalysisStore inside it. No \`override func tearDown\`. Each test leaves ~20-60 KB of sqlite + WAL + SHM.

**Fix**: add \`override func tearDown\` that closes the store and removes the dir; capture \`dir\` as a private property.

### 5. CoreServiceTests storage size test writes to real app paths
- PlayheadTests/Services/CoreServiceTests.swift:1958 (SettingsStorageContractTests.computeStorageSizesUsesCurrentServicePaths)

Writes 3 marker files into ApplicationSupport/.../AnalysisShards, ModelInventory.defaultModelsRoot(), DownloadManager.defaultCacheDirectory(). Has defer for markers but not the dirs themselves.

**Fix**: snapshot pre-existence, remove dirs only if the test created them.

### 6-7. Ad-hoc FileManager.temporaryDirectory usage
- PlayheadTests/Services/FoundationModelsFeedbackStoreTests.swift:17
- AssetProvider suite within CoreServiceTests.swift

**Fix**: migrate to makeTempDir(prefix:) helper.

## Acceptance
- Zero test files use \`FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory.appendingPathComponent(...UUID...)\` directly; all go through makeTempDir.
- All XCTestCase subclasses that hold an AnalysisStore have an \`override func tearDown\`.
- Audit script can be re-run post-fix and report zero callsites.

## Gating
None. Low priority. Note: audit confirmed this is NOT the culprit for the disk issues we hit in parallel agent runs — that was xcodebuild derivedData (~2 GB per worktree), not test artifacts.

title: Flake: RuntimeShutdownLifecycleTests.shutdownStopsObserverAndIsIdempotent times out under parallel load
description:
Pre-existing flake flagged during playhead-r835, playhead-uzdq, and playhead-24cm work. Not introduced by any of those beads.

## Symptom
Under full PlayheadFastTests runs with parallel simulators active, the test times out with:
\"observer loop did not start within 5.0s\"
(29 s elapsed).

In isolation (single-test run) it passes in ~0.013 s.

## Root cause hypothesis
Deadline-driven test with a 5 s timeout for observer loop startup. Under CPU contention from parallel test execution, the observer task doesn't get scheduled within 5 s. The test is polling for a signal that depends on GCD scheduling under load.

## Related
CLAUDE.md / TestHelpers.swift references playhead-qtc as the broader flaky-test tracking bead.

## Options
A. Raise the 5 s timeout to 30 s. Cheap fix; preserves intent.
B. Convert to an awaitable primitive (Task + Continuation) that doesn't rely on a polling deadline.
C. Mark `.serialized` so the test doesn't contend for CPU.

Recommend A as a tactical fix, B as the strategic fix.

## Acceptance
- Test passes in 50 consecutive full-fast-plan runs under parallel pressure.
- No sleep() or polling deadline pattern left in the test.

## File
PlayheadTests/Services/AdDetection/RuntimeShutdownLifecycleTests.swift
notes: INVESTIGATION 2026-07-24: appears ALREADY FIXED. RuntimeShutdownLifecycleTests.shutdownStopsObserverAndIsIdempotent no longer uses the 5s polling deadline the bead describes — it now awaits a synchronous arm seam (`_startShadowRetryObserverForTesting()` + `observer.testIsLoopRunning()`, PlayheadRuntime.swift:2651), i.e. the bead's option B (deterministic awaitable, no polling deadline). No 'did not start within 5.0s' / Task.sleep / poll remains in the file. Landed in #243 'test: deterministic fixes for the contention-flake families (vsot/zqhz/m9xk)'. title: ym57 follow-up: rotation script + manifest hardening
description:
Non-gating follow-ups for playhead-ym57 fixture substrate. Can land any time.

## Findings from ym57 code review

### 1. rotate-fixtures.swift silently swallows malformed pool JSON
File: scripts/rotate-fixtures.swift (~line 136)

Uses `try?` on pool JSON decode. Distinguishes neither \"missing pool\" (legitimate, exit 0) from \"decode failure\" (hard error, should exit non-zero).

Fix: catch decode errors explicitly, exit non-zero with diagnostic.

### 2. FIXTURES_LICENSING.md anchor check is loose
File: PlayheadTests/Fixtures/FixtureManifestIntegrityTests.swift

Current check is a substring match. A typo in a licensingRef can pass if another fixture's anchor happens to contain the typo string.

Fix: parse Markdown anchors (lines matching `^#+\\s+fixture-NN` or explicit `{#anchor}` syntax) and require an exact match.

### 3. SyntheticFixtureGenerator.swift references a non-existent regen script
File: PlayheadTests/Fixtures/Corpus/Tools/SyntheticFixtureGenerator.swift:17

Comment claims `scripts/regenerate-synthetic-fixtures.swift` exists. It does not.

Fix: either create the regen script (would regenerate all 8 synthetic placeholders on demand) or remove the false reference from the comment.

### 4. Pool entry validation missing
File: scripts/rotate-fixtures.swift

No validation that pool entry `id` contains only safe chars, `file` is free of path traversal (`..`), `sha256` is 64-char hex.

Fix: validate each pool entry before using; reject malformed pools early.

### 5. corpusDirectoryURL relies on #filePath
File: PlayheadTests/Fixtures/Corpus/CorpusLoader.swift

Uses `#filePath` to locate Media/ — silently wrong if the file is ever moved under Xcode's file reorganization.

Fix: anchor on a stable marker file (e.g., the manifest itself) rather than #filePath. Or document the constraint explicitly and add a test asserting manifest is reachable.

## Acceptance
- rotate-fixtures.swift exits non-zero on malformed pool JSON.
- Licensing anchor check uses exact-match parsing.
- Regen script exists OR comment reference removed.
- Pool entry validation covers id/file/sha256 shape.
- corpusDirectoryURL has a regression test asserting manifest reachability.

## Gating
None. Ship when convenient.

title: B11: Selective typed redaction fallback
description:
## Background
Current redaction replaces all pharma/service/product names with generic placeholders like [DRUG], erasing distinctions the FM needs. But the FM is on-device — the legal requirement is 'no data leaves the phone,' not 'the local model can't see sponsor names.' Expert recommendation: minimal redaction by default, typed placeholders only for refusal-triggering categories.

## What to build

### Two-tier redaction policy
1. Default path: minimal / no redaction for ordinary sponsor names in on-device FM calls
2. Fallback path: typed placeholder redaction for categories that trigger FM refusals or when using permissive fallback

### Typed placeholders (fallback tier only)
- [DRUG] → [DRUG_A], [DRUG_B] (per unique original string)
- [SERVICE] → [SERVICE_A], [SERVICE_B]
- [PRODUCT], [CONDITION], [TEST] similarly

### Assignment rule
First unique original string in a category gets _A, second gets _B, etc. Deterministic (alphabetical by first-occurrence). Same string always maps to same ID within a pass.

### Preserve sponsor identity
Maintain internal sponsorEntityHandle outside redacted text so pipeline can reason about identity even when redaction is active.

### Changes to PromptRedactor
- Mapping ephemeral — rebuilt per pass
- Trigger/cooccurrent gating unchanged
- Two-tier policy configurable

## Open question
Is there a non-negotiable policy requiring all FM input be redacted? If so, typed placeholders + sponsorEntityHandle are the only path. **Resolution path:** Dan to confirm legal stance. If no answer by implementation time, proceed with two-tier as default + compile-time flag for always-redact mode.

## Acceptance criteria
- Default path uses minimal redaction
- Fallback path produces typed placeholders
- Same entity gets consistent ID within a pass
- sponsorEntityHandle preserved for pipeline identity reasoning
- Unit tests for typed placeholder assignment
- Tests for two-tier policy switching
- Tests for sponsorEntityHandle preservation

title: FM refinement: Kelly Ripa #1 refusal — test includeSchemaInPrompt:false, fall back to refusal-retry-permissive
description:
## Source

Follow-up to the FM Safety Classifier + Permissive Guardrails architecture (commits 1b70822, 6ae352f, abc82f1, 086e002) that recovers Conan recall from 2/4 → 4/4 on real device. One residual refusal remains: the Kelly Ripa #1 cross-promo window refinement call refuses even with permissive guardrails wired and router showing zero trigger matches in the prompt.

Full reasoning chain and expert response captured in `docs/fm-safety-classifier-kelly-ripa-mystery.md`.

## Current state (non-blocking)

Conan recall is already 4/4 via outward expansion: sourceWindow=5 (SiriusXM credits) expands downward by 2 segments and sweeps lineRefs 4-5 (Kelly Ripa #1) into a clean refinement prompt. The mechanism is fragile because it depends on Apple safety classifier non-determinism and the outward-expansion path firing. This bead hardens the path so we don't rely on the side effect.

## Expert diagnosis (2026-04-08)

> The router is checking less text than Apple's guardrails are checking. `router.routeText(plan.prompt)` only inspects the visible rendered prompt, but Apple's guardrails inspect the full augmented input on the guided-generation path: session instructions, framework-injected schema text (Foundation Models auto-includes `Generable` type details unless `includeSchemaInPrompt: false`), guide descriptions, tool descriptions. So `routeText(plan.prompt) == .normal` does NOT prove the actual guarded input lacks pharma-shaped triggers. It only proves *our visible part* lacks them.
>
> The second mystery is not really "Why does Kelly Ripa trigger a hidden celebrity classifier?" It is "Why are you still treating plan.prompt as the full guarded input on guided generation?" Once you account for the framework-added schema/instruction surface, the behavior stops being mysterious and starts looking like a false positive on the augmented prompt.

There is no documented Apple "celebrity cross-promo" category. Apple staff in developer forum threads on parallel benign false positives (Tailwind, JFK/KJFK, frunk, Lock Pride) explicitly say guardrails are classifier systems and prompt/rule attempts often cannot suppress them.

## Test plan (~half a day)

Fork the existing refinement path into a third code path that goes through guided generation with `includeSchemaInPrompt: false` + a one-shot example in instructions instead of an auto-injected schema. Run on the Kelly Ripa #1 window.

```swift
let session = LanguageModelSession(
    instructions: Instructions {
        "You are a transcript span extractor. Return only ad-span line ranges."
        """
        Example output:
        {"spans":[{"firstLineRef":4,"lastLineRef":5}]}
        """
    }
)
let response = try await session.respond(
    to: prompt,
    generating: RefinementWindowSchema.self,
    includeSchemaInPrompt: false,
    options: GenerationOptions(sampling: .greedy)
)
```

On refusal, log `refusal.explanation` — model-generated `Response<String>`, strictly better diagnostic than `contextDebugDescription`. Capture on every refusal going forward.

## Out of scope

- **Extending SensitiveWindowRouter with new lexicon categories.** Per the expert, this is a known dead end — guardrails are classifier systems, not lexicon-tunable. Don't chase undocumented classifier boundaries.
- The `refusal.explanation` instrumentation is a pure diagnostic addition; it does NOT change routing dispatch logic.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Real-device A/B run: submit the Kelly Ripa #1 refinement window through (a) the existing default `@Generable` path, (b) the existing permissive string path, and (c) the new `includeSchemaInPrompt: false` + one-shot example variant. Capture `refusal.explanation` strings for any path that refuses.

2. Decision branch based on (c):
   - **If (c) succeeds**: keep guided generation for refinement, strip the auto-injected schema preamble, rely on the one-shot example. Production refinement gets `includeSchemaInPrompt: false` everywhere.
   - **If (c) refuses too**: implement **refusal-retry-permissive** — any default-path refinement refusal automatically retries through the permissive string path, regardless of router verdict. Router becomes an *optimization hint* (skip the doomed `@Generable` call when we can predict it), not a *correctness gate*.

3. In either branch, instrument the production refinement refusal path to log `refusal.explanation` so future mysteries are easier to diagnose. Strict additive change.

4. File Feedback Assistant on the case with the exact Kelly prompt, OS build, device model, the failing default-path call, the succeeding permissive-path call, and the result of the (c) A/B test. Use `logFeedbackAttachment(sentiment:issues:desiredOutput:)` per the expert's pointer. Include the Feedback ID on this bead's notes when filed.

5. Conan recall stays at 4/4 throughout.

6. No regression on existing permissive coarse + permissive refinement test suites.

title: Decide fate of scheduleContinuedProcessing: migrate to BGContinuedProcessingTask or delete
description:
Follow-up from commit 740f727 review.

scheduleContinuedProcessing() in BackgroundProcessingService submits a BGProcessingTaskRequest under the identifier "com.playhead.app.analysis.continued". iOS has a separate BGContinuedProcessingTask type (iOS 26+) with different lifecycle semantics, intended for user-initiated long-running foreground-continuation work (file uploads, long downloads) that keeps a visible indicator.

Current state after the follow-up fix pass:
  - handleContinuedProcessingTask is now a deliberate no-op marked success=true
    (see commit addressing Finding 3). There is NO code path that actually
    submits scheduleContinuedProcessing from user-initiated work today.
  - The identifier and handler are kept registered so a future wiring can
    slot in without touching the registration dance.

Decisions needed before implementing:
  1. Is there any user-visible continuation work Playhead actually needs?
     The obvious candidate is the initial FM asset download via AssetProvider,
     but that is already handled synchronously at first-launch onboarding.
  2. Does BGContinuedProcessingTask actually fit Playhead's model? It requires
     foreground-initiated submission and a user-visible indicator. Idle backfill
     is the wrong fit.
  3. If we decide not to use BGContinuedProcessingTask, rename the identifier
     and delete scheduleContinuedProcessing entirely to reduce confusion.

Recommended: investigate for ~30 minutes, then either delete the dead
identifier path or migrate to the real BGContinuedProcessingTask API if
a user-facing continuation work stream emerges.

title: [epic] Phase 13: Federated CoreML Learning
description:
Federated learning for the CoreML hot-path classifier. Each device trains locally on its Phase 10 training corpus, then uploads differentially-private gradient updates. A central aggregation service merges updates and publishes improved model weights.

## Why Phase 13 (not earlier)
- Requires Phase 10 training data pipeline to be mature and producing quality examples
- Requires Phase 11 rollout infrastructure for safe model deployment
- Requires Phase 12 shared lexicon to prove the central distribution pattern works
- CoreML on-device training is the most complex piece — only worth it once we know the model architecture matters

## Architecture
1. On-device training: Apple CoreML on-device training APIs. Train on local Phase 10 training examples (all four buckets). Short fine-tuning passes, not full training.
2. Gradient privacy: Differential privacy on gradient updates (clip + noise). No raw text, no training examples, no transcripts uploaded. Only noised model deltas.
3. Central aggregation: Federated averaging (FedAvg or similar). Merge gradient updates from N devices, produce updated global model weights. Publish as a signed CoreML model package on CDN.
4. Device consumption: Download updated model, validate against local replay harness (Phase 11), promote if benchmarks pass. Rollback to previous model if regression detected.
5. Contribution gating: Only devices with sufficient training corpus size (e.g., 50+ examples across 3+ buckets) contribute. Prevents low-quality updates from poisoning the global model.

## Privacy guarantees
- Differential privacy with formal epsilon budget per contribution round
- No raw text or training examples leave device
- Gradient clipping prevents memorization of individual examples
- Contribution rounds are anonymous (no user ID in updates)
- Local replay harness validates received models before deployment

## Open questions (resolve before implementation)
- CoreML on-device training API maturity — check latest WWDC sessions
- Epsilon budget per round vs cumulative privacy loss
- Minimum device participation threshold for meaningful aggregation
- Model architecture (sequence classifier? transformer? — depends on Phase 10 findings)
- Whether Apple federated learning infrastructure (used for keyboard predictions) is accessible to third-party apps

Verification: On-device training produces model updates. Gradient updates are differentially private. Central aggregation improves global model. Devices validate received models against local benchmarks. Regression triggers rollback.

The plan and UI design §F also mention a per-show popover: "Auto-download new episodes: Off / Last 1 / Last 3 / All. Default Off." Per-show overrides allow a user with "Last 3" globally to disable for a noisy show, or vice versa.

**Work:**

- Global auto-download default + cellular toggle + Download Next N default — covered by `l274`.
