title: Bookmark Moments
description:
# Bookmark Moments

## Goal
Let users save interesting moments during playback for later reference, anchored to transcript text.

## Rationale
Podcast listeners frequently think "I want to remember this part" but have no way to act on it. Bookmarks + transcript context make moments findable later. Builds on existing transcript infrastructure. Creates another reason to keep using Playhead over competitors.

## Implementation

### Bookmark Model
- New file: `Playhead/Models/Bookmark.swift`
- New SwiftData `@Model`:
  ```swift
  @Model
  final class Bookmark {
      var episodeKey: String          // references Episode.canonicalEpisodeKey
      var timestamp: TimeInterval     // seconds into episode (not CMTime — SwiftData cannot persist CMTime)
      var transcriptSnippet: String?  // auto-captured ~30 words, nil if transcript unavailable
      var userNote: String?           // optional user annotation
      var createdAt: Date
      
      init(
          episodeKey: String,
          timestamp: TimeInterval,
          transcriptSnippet: String? = nil,
          userNote: String? = nil,
          createdAt: Date = .now
      ) { ... }
  }
  ```
- Register `Bookmark.self` in `SwiftDataStore.schema` array (in `Playhead/Persistence/SwiftDataStore/SwiftDataStore.swift`) alongside Podcast, Episode, UserPreferences. Add to PlayheadSchemaV2 frozen snapshot. Requires lightweight SwiftData schema migration.

### Transcript Snippet Extraction
```swift
/// Extracts ~30 words of transcript context around a timestamp.
func extractSnippet(
    at timestamp: TimeInterval,
    analysisAssetId: UUID
) async -> String? {
    // 1. Query AnalysisStore for TranscriptChunks where startTime is nearest to timestamp
    // 2. Find the chunk containing or nearest to the timestamp
    // 3. Collect that chunk + adjacent chunks (before and after) until total word count >= 30
    // 4. Concatenate chunk texts with spaces
    // 5. Return nil if no TranscriptChunks exist for this analysisAssetId
}
```
- This function lives on a `BookmarkService` actor (see below) or as a method on AnalysisStore.

### BookmarkService
- New file: `Playhead/Services/Bookmarks/BookmarkService.swift`
- `actor BookmarkService`
- Dependencies: `ModelContext` (SwiftData), `AnalysisStore`

#### Public API
```swift
func create(
    episodeKey: String,
    timestamp: TimeInterval,
    analysisAssetId: UUID?,
    note: String? = nil
) async throws -> Bookmark

func delete(_ bookmark: Bookmark) async throws
func bookmarks(for episodeKey: String) async throws -> [Bookmark]  // sorted by timestamp
func allBookmarks() async throws -> [Bookmark]                      // sorted by createdAt DESC
func updateNote(_ bookmark: Bookmark, note: String?) async throws
func backfillSnippets(for episodeKey: String, analysisAssetId: UUID) async throws
```

#### Backfill Mechanism
- When a transcript becomes available for an episode that has bookmarks with nil `transcriptSnippet`:
  - Listen for `Notification.Name("TranscriptionCompleted")` posted by TranscriptEngineService (includes `analysisAssetId` in userInfo)
  - On notification: query Bookmark entries where `episodeKey` matches and `transcriptSnippet == nil`
  - For each: call `extractSnippet(at: bookmark.timestamp, analysisAssetId:)` and update the bookmark
- This is fire-and-forget — if extraction fails, leave snippet as nil (no error surfaced to user)

### Bookmark Creation
- Now Playing: bookmark button (SF Symbol `flag.fill`) in transport controls, positioned near existing controls
  - Tap: creates bookmark at `PlaybackService.currentTime` with haptic (`UIImpactFeedbackGenerator(style: .light)`, reuse pattern from playhead-81x)
  - Brief visual confirmation: flag icon momentarily pulses Copper (scale 1.0 -> 1.2 -> 1.0 over 0.3s)
  - Long-press: creates bookmark + opens inline note editor. Note editor: `TextField("Add a note...", text:)` appearing below the transport controls with keyboard, Instrument Sans. "Done" button dismisses.
- Transcript Peek / Full Transcript View: long-press any transcript line -> `.contextMenu` -> "Bookmark this moment" (creates bookmark at that chunk's `startTime`)

### BookmarksView
- New file: `Playhead/Views/Bookmarks/BookmarksView.swift`
- Accessible from Library tab -> "Bookmarks" navigation link (with SF Symbol `flag.fill`)
- Grouped by episode (using `Dictionary(grouping:by:)` on `episodeKey`), sections sorted by most recent bookmark's `createdAt`
- Section header: episode title (Instrument Sans, `.headline`) + podcast name (Soft Steel, `.subheadline`)
- Each bookmark row:
  - Transcript snippet in Newsreader, `.body` (or "No transcript yet" in Soft Steel, `.body.italic()` if nil)
  - Timestamp formatted as `mm:ss` or `h:mm:ss` in IBM Plex Mono, `.caption`
  - User note (if present) in Instrument Sans, `.caption`, Soft Steel
  - Relative date via `RelativeDateTimeFormatter` (`.abbreviated`), IBM Plex Mono, `.caption2`
- Tap: calls `PlaybackService.loadAndPlay(episodeKey:)` then `PlaybackService.seek(to: bookmark.timestamp)`
- Swipe actions:
  - Delete (SF Symbol `trash`, `.destructive`): calls `BookmarkService.delete(bookmark)`
  - Share (SF Symbol `square.and.arrow.up`): copies `"\(snippet ?? "") [\(formattedTimestamp)]"` as text via `ShareLink`
- Empty state: "No bookmarks yet. Tap the flag icon while listening to save a moment." in Soft Steel on Ink background, with SF Symbol `flag` in Steel at 48pt

### View States
```swift
enum BookmarksViewState {
    case loading
    case loaded([(episode: Episode, bookmarks: [Bookmark])])
    case empty
}
```

### Tests
- Unit: bookmark creation captures correct timestamp and transcript snippet from AnalysisStore
- Unit: bookmark with and without user note
- Unit: bookmark creation with nil transcript (analysisAssetId nil or no chunks available)
- Unit: bookmark deletion removes from SwiftData
- Unit: transcript snippet extraction finds nearest TranscriptChunks and captures ~30 words
- Unit: backfill mechanism updates nil snippets when TranscriptionCompleted fires
- Unit: backfill no-ops when all snippets already populated
- Unit: allBookmarks returns sorted by createdAt DESC
- Snapshot: bookmarks list (with snippets, without snippets, with notes), empty state, Dynamic Type sizes
- E2E: play episode, create bookmark, navigate to bookmarks view, tap to seek back to correct timestamp

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Single tap creates bookmark at current position with haptic and visual pulse
- [ ] Transcript snippet auto-captured when available (~30 words around timestamp)
- [ ] Bookmark created without snippet when transcript unavailable (backfilled later via notification)
- [ ] Long-press allows adding a note via inline text field
- [ ] Context menu on transcript lines creates bookmark at that chunk's timestamp
- [ ] Bookmarks view shows all bookmarks grouped by episode, sorted by recency
- [ ] Tap-to-seek works accurately (TimeInterval -> PlaybackService seek)
- [ ] Share action copies snippet + timestamp as text
- [ ] Bookmark.self registered in SwiftData schema with lightweight migration
- [ ] VoiceOver: bookmark button labeled, list navigable, snippet and timestamp announced
- [ ] Dynamic Type scales bookmark cards correctly

title: Playback History / Recently Played
description:
# Playback History / Recently Played

## Goal
Provide quick access to recently listened episodes with resume positions.

## Rationale
"What was I listening to yesterday?" is a common need. Currently users must navigate to specific podcasts to find recent episodes. A simple chronological list sorted by last-played time is a basic quality-of-life feature. One view, one query.

## Implementation

### Model Change
- Add `lastPlayedAt: Date?` to Episode SwiftData model (in `Playhead/Models/Podcast.swift`). nil for never-played episodes.
- Requires lightweight SwiftData schema migration (add field to PlayheadSchemaV2 frozen snapshot).
- PlaybackService sets `episode.lastPlayedAt = .now` in the play/resume handler whenever playback starts or resumes for an episode. This is a SwiftData write on `@MainActor` (since Episode is a SwiftData model, writes must happen on the context's actor).

### History Query
- SwiftData `@Query` or `FetchDescriptor<Episode>`:
  ```swift
  var historyDescriptor: FetchDescriptor<Episode> {
      var fd = FetchDescriptor<Episode>(
          predicate: #Predicate<Episode> { $0.lastPlayedAt != nil },
          sortBy: [SortDescriptor(\.lastPlayedAt, order: .reverse)]
      )
      fd.fetchLimit = 50
      return fd
  }
  ```
- Progress calculation: `episode.playbackPosition / (episode.duration ?? 1.0)` clamped to 0...1. If `episode.isPlayed == true`, show "Finished" regardless of position.

### HistoryView
- New file: `Playhead/Views/Library/HistoryView.swift`
- Accessible from Library tab: "Recently Played" section at top of LibraryView, or as a navigation link "See All" that pushes to full HistoryView
- Each row:
  - Podcast artwork (40x40pt, from `episode.podcast?.artworkURL`, `AsyncImage` with placeholder)
  - Title: episode title (Instrument Sans, `.headline`)
  - Subtitle: podcast name (Instrument Sans, Soft Steel, `.subheadline`)
  - Date: relative time via `RelativeDateTimeFormatter` configured with `.dateTimeStyle = .named` and `.unitsStyle = .abbreviated` — produces "2h ago", "Yesterday", "3d ago" (IBM Plex Mono, `.caption`)
  - Progress bar: `ProgressView(value: progress)` with Copper `.tint` on Ink track, 4pt height. Hidden if `isPlayed == true` (show "Finished" text badge instead in Copper, `.caption2`)
- Tap: navigates to Now Playing, calls `PlaybackService.loadAndPlay(episode:)` which resumes at saved `playbackPosition`
- Swipe actions:
  - "Remove from History" (SF Symbol `xmark.circle`, destructive): sets `episode.lastPlayedAt = nil`. Does NOT affect `playbackPosition` or `isPlayed`.
  - "Play Next" (SF Symbol `text.insert`, Copper): calls `QueueService.addNext(episode.canonicalEpisodeKey)` — only available if playhead-05i is built. Guard with `#if` or runtime check.
- Empty state: "Nothing played yet. Browse your library to get started." in Soft Steel on Ink background, with SF Symbol `play.circle` in Steel at 48pt.

### View States
```swift
enum HistoryViewState {
    case loading
    case loaded([Episode])    // non-empty results
    case empty                // no episodes with lastPlayedAt
}
```
- `.loading` is brief (SwiftData query is synchronous on main thread via @Query, so this may not be needed — but include for consistency if using async fetch)

### Tests
- Unit: history query returns correct order (most recent first) and respects fetchLimit of 50
- Unit: `lastPlayedAt` updated on playback start/resume (mock PlaybackService scenario)
- Unit: progress display (50% for position=30/duration=60, "Finished" for isPlayed==true, 0% for position=0)
- Unit: "Remove from History" clears lastPlayedAt without affecting playbackPosition or isPlayed
- Unit: query excludes episodes where lastPlayedAt == nil
- Snapshot: history list with mixed states (in-progress at various %, finished, various relative dates), empty state, Dynamic Type sizes
- E2E: play an episode, navigate to history view, verify it appears first with correct progress

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `lastPlayedAt: Date?` field added to Episode model with lightweight SwiftData schema migration
- [ ] Recently played episodes appear in reverse chronological order
- [ ] Progress indicator shows completion state (Copper bar for in-progress, "Finished" badge for completed)
- [ ] Tap resumes playback at saved position
- [ ] "Remove from History" clears lastPlayedAt without affecting play state
- [ ] List limited to 50 entries with no performance issues
- [ ] Relative date formatting via RelativeDateTimeFormatter (abbreviated style)
- [ ] VoiceOver reads episode title, podcast name, relative date, and progress percentage
- [ ] Dynamic Type scales correctly
- [ ] Empty state handled with icon and helpful text

title: Variable Skip Behavior (Skip/FF/Mute)
description:
# Variable Skip Behavior (Skip / Fast-Forward / Mute)

## Goal
Give users control over how detected ads are handled: auto-skip (default), fast-forward at 2x, or mute — per-show or globally.

## Rationale
Some users want to support podcast creators by hearing ads, just faster. Others prefer muting. This respects user agency and creator relationships. Leverages existing AdWindow boundaries — just changes what happens when an ad region is entered.

## Implementation

### Extending the Existing SkipBehavior Enum
- Modify `Playhead/Models/UserPreferences.swift`
- The codebase already has `enum SkipBehavior: Int, Codable, Sendable, CaseIterable` with cases `.auto` (0), `.manual` (1), `.off` (2).
- Add two new cases with explicit raw values to preserve backward compatibility:
  ```swift
  enum SkipBehavior: Int, Codable, Sendable, CaseIterable {
      case auto = 0          // seek past ad (existing)
      case manual = 1        // show skip button (existing)
      case off = 2           // pass through (existing)
      case fastForward = 3   // 2x rate during ad (new)
      case mute = 4          // silence during ad (new)
  }
  ```
- Existing persisted values (0, 1, 2) decode correctly. New values (3, 4) only appear after user explicitly selects them.

### Podcast Model Change
- Add optional `skipBehavior: SkipBehavior?` to Podcast SwiftData model (in `Playhead/Models/Podcast.swift`). nil = use global `UserPreferences.skipBehavior`.
- Requires lightweight SwiftData schema migration (add field to PlayheadSchemaV2 frozen snapshot).

### SkipBehavior Resolution
```swift
/// Returns the effective skip behavior for an episode.
func effectiveSkipBehavior(for episode: Episode) -> SkipBehavior {
    episode.podcast?.skipBehavior ?? userPreferences.skipBehavior
}
```

### SkipOrchestrator Changes
- Modify `Playhead/Services/SkipOrchestrator/SkipOrchestrator.swift`
- In the skip execution path (when `SkipDecisionState` transitions to `.skipped`), switch on effective SkipBehavior:

```swift
switch effectiveSkipBehavior(for: episode) {
case .auto:
    // Existing behavior: seek to adWindow.endTime
    await playbackService.seek(to: adWindow.endTime)

case .fastForward:
    // Store pre-ad rate, set 2x
    let preAdRate = await playbackService.currentRate  // may be 1.5x from per-show speed
    await playbackService.setRate(2.0)
    // Schedule rate restore at ad end
    scheduleAdEndAction(adWindow: adWindow) {
        await playbackService.setRate(preAdRate)  // restore original, NOT hardcoded 1.0x
    }

case .mute:
    // Mute during ad
    await playbackService.setMuted(true)  // AVPlayer.isMuted (not AVAudioMix)
    // Show "Ad muted" indicator via SkipOrchestrator published state
    // Schedule unmute at ad end
    scheduleAdEndAction(adWindow: adWindow) {
        await playbackService.setMuted(false)
    }

case .manual:
    // Existing behavior: show skip button in Now Playing
    break

case .off:
    // Do nothing — pass through ads, no banners
    break
}
```

#### Ad End Monitoring
- `scheduleAdEndAction` uses PlaybackService's periodic time observer (already exists at 0.25s interval) to check when `currentTime >= adWindow.endTime`. When reached, execute the restore closure and remove the observer.
- Edge case: if user seeks out of the ad region manually, also fire the restore action (detect via seek notification from PlaybackService).
- Edge case: if episode ends during an ad, restore mute/rate on `AVPlayerItem.didPlayToEndTimeNotification`.

### Settings UI
- Modify `Playhead/Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift`
- Existing Settings -> Playback -> "When ads are detected" picker. Extend with new options.
- Display names:
  ```swift
  extension SkipBehavior {
      var displayName: String {
          switch self {
          case .auto: "Auto-Skip"
          case .fastForward: "Fast Forward (2x)"
          case .mute: "Mute"
          case .manual: "Show Skip Button"
          case .off: "Off"
          }
      }
  }
  ```
- Per-show: long-press podcast in Library -> "Show Settings" sheet (shared with playhead-pfn, playhead-snp, playhead-5w4) -> "Ad Handling" section with same Picker. Include "Use Default ([current global])" option at top (sets `podcast.skipBehavior = nil`).

### Timeline Markers
- All modes except `.off` still show ad region indicators on the timeline (playhead-m3d skip markers)
- `.off` mode: no ad region indicators, no banners (complete pass-through)

### Tests
- Unit: each behavior mode triggers correct action (seek for .auto, rate change for .fastForward, mute for .mute, button for .manual, nothing for .off)
- Unit: AVPlayer.rate correctly restored to pre-ad value at ad end boundary (test with pre-ad rate of 1.5x — not hardcoded 1.0x)
- Unit: AVPlayer.isMuted restored to false at ad end boundary
- Unit: restore fires if user seeks out of ad region manually
- Unit: restore fires if episode ends during ad
- Unit: per-show override takes precedence over global default (podcast.skipBehavior != nil)
- Unit: nil per-show falls back to global
- Unit: timeline markers still display in all modes except .off
- Unit: backward-compatible deserialization: raw values 0, 1, 2 decode to existing cases
- Snapshot: settings picker with all five options (with display names), per-show ad handling in Show Settings sheet with "Use Default" option
- E2E: set fast-forward mode, play episode with known ad, verify rate changes at ad boundary and restores after

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All five modes work correctly (auto-skip, fast-forward at 2x, mute, manual button, off)
- [ ] Rate restored to correct pre-ad value at ad end (respects per-show speed, not hardcoded 1.0x)
- [ ] Mute restored at ad end boundary
- [ ] Restore fires on manual seek out of ad or episode end
- [ ] Per-show setting in shared Show Settings sheet overrides global default
- [ ] "Use Default" option in per-show settings sets skipBehavior = nil
- [ ] Timeline markers display in all active modes, hidden in .off mode
- [ ] Existing SkipBehavior raw values (0, 1, 2) preserved — backward compatible
- [ ] Settings UI shows clear display names for each option
- [ ] VoiceOver announces current mode in settings
- [ ] Lightweight SwiftData schema migration for new Podcast field

title: Smart Resume (Post-Ad Boundary)
description:
# Smart Resume (Post-Ad Boundary)

## Goal
When resuming playback after a long pause, skip past any ad region the user was in, landing on the next content boundary.

## Rationale
Common frustration: user pauses podcast, returns hours later, and resumes in the middle of a Squarespace ad. With existing AdWindow data, PlaybackService can detect this and seek forward to the ad's end boundary. Prevents a frustrating "why am I hearing an ad?" moment.

## Implementation

### Episode Model Change
- Add `pausedAt: Date?` to Episode SwiftData model (in `Playhead/Models/Podcast.swift`). Set to `Date.now` when playback pauses, set to `nil` when playback starts/resumes. Requires lightweight SwiftData schema migration.
- This must be persisted (not in-memory) because smart resume needs to survive app termination — the user may kill the app while paused and return hours later.

### PlaybackService Enhancement
- Modify `Playhead/Services/PlaybackTransport/PlaybackTransport.swift`
- In the resume/play handler, after restoring saved `Episode.playbackPosition`:

#### Smart Resume Logic
```swift
func shouldSmartResume(episode: Episode) -> Bool {
    guard let pausedAt = episode.pausedAt else { return false }
    let pauseDuration = Date.now.timeIntervalSince(pausedAt)
    return pauseDuration > 30  // only after > 30s pause
}

func smartResume(episode: Episode) async {
    // 1. Resolve effective SkipBehavior
    let behavior = episode.podcast?.skipBehavior ?? userPreferences.skipBehavior
    guard behavior != .off else { return }  // user opted out
    
    // 2. Check SkipMode from TrustScoringService
    let skipMode = await trustScoringService.skipMode(for: episode)
    guard skipMode != .shadow else { return }  // low trust, no smart resume
    
    // 3. Query for AdWindow at current position
    guard let adWindow = try? await analysisStore.adWindow(
        containing: episode.playbackPosition,
        analysisAssetId: episode.lastPlayedAnalysisAssetId
    ) else { return }  // not in an ad region
    
    // 4. Verify confidence meets threshold
    guard adWindow.confidence >= skipPolicyConfig.enterThreshold else { return }
    
    // 5. Apply behavior
    let seekTarget = min(adWindow.endTime + 0.5, episodeDuration)  // clamp to episode end
    
    switch behavior {
    case .auto, .fastForward, .mute:
        seek(to: seekTarget)
        episode.playbackPosition = seekTarget
        showToast("Skipped past ad break", duration: 2.0)
    case .manual:
        showPrompt("Skip past ad?", onConfirm: {
            seek(to: seekTarget)
            episode.playbackPosition = seekTarget
        })
    case .off:
        break  // already guarded above
    }
}
```

#### SkipBehavior Resolution
- Per-show override: `episode.podcast?.skipBehavior` (added by playhead-x5l; if field doesn't exist yet, falls through to global)
- Global default: `userPreferences.skipBehavior`
- SkipBehavior modes:
  - `.auto`: smart resume active (seek past ad, show toast)
  - `.fastForward`: seek past ad (don't fast-forward on resume — user expects instant skip)
  - `.mute`: seek past ad (same rationale — don't mute and play through on resume)
  - `.manual`: show "Skip past ad?" prompt instead of auto-seeking
  - `.off`: no smart resume (user opted out of ad handling)

### Toast and Prompt Views
- Toast: "Skipped past ad break" — reuse the toast pattern from playhead-pfn (SpeedPromptToast style). Instrument Sans, `.subheadline`, Bone on Ink background with 90% opacity. Auto-dismisses in 2s. No user interaction needed.
- Prompt (manual mode): "Skip past ad?" with "Skip" (Copper) and "Stay here" (Soft Steel) buttons. Same toast container but persistent until user acts. Auto-dismisses in 10s (defaults to "Stay here").

### Edge Cases
- If no analysis data exists for the episode yet (`lastPlayedAnalysisAssetId == nil`): skip smart resume entirely (no-op)
- If the ad window's `endTime` is past the episode duration (corrupt data): clamp seekTarget to `episode.duration ?? .infinity` (if duration is nil, don't seek — safeguard)
- If `pausedAt` is nil (e.g., app was force-killed before writing pausedAt): skip smart resume (no-op, conservative)
- Multiple consecutive AdWindows: only seeks past the one containing the current position. If user lands in another ad, normal SkipOrchestrator handling takes over during live playback.

### Tests
- Unit: resume inside ad region -> seeks to endTime + 0.5s
- Unit: resume outside ad region -> no seek (plays from saved position)
- Unit: resume after < 30s pause -> no smart resume (plays from saved position)
- Unit: pausedAt correctly written on pause, cleared on play
- Unit: respects SkipBehavior (.off = no smart resume, .manual = prompt, .auto/.fastForward/.mute = auto-seek)
- Unit: respects SkipMode (.shadow = no smart resume regardless of SkipBehavior)
- Unit: confidence below enterThreshold = no smart resume
- Unit: seekTarget clamped to episode duration (no seek past end)
- Unit: pausedAt == nil -> no smart resume (conservative)
- Snapshot: "Skipped past ad break" toast, "Skip past ad?" prompt for manual mode, Dynamic Type sizes
- E2E: pause during known ad segment, wait > 30s, resume — verify playback starts at content

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `pausedAt: Date?` added to Episode model with lightweight SwiftData schema migration
- [ ] Resume inside ad region seeks to adWindow.endTime + 0.5s
- [ ] Only activates after > 30s pause (computed from persisted pausedAt)
- [ ] Brief toast confirms the skip (auto-dismisses in 2s)
- [ ] Respects per-show SkipBehavior (resolved from per-show override or global default)
- [ ] No smart resume when SkipBehavior is .off or SkipMode is .shadow
- [ ] Prompt shown in .manual mode (auto-dismisses in 10s, defaults to no-skip)
- [ ] Episode.playbackPosition updated to new post-skip location
- [ ] Gracefully handles missing analysis data, nil pausedAt, corrupt endTime
- [ ] VoiceOver announces "Skipped past ad break" toast
- [ ] Dynamic Type scales toast and prompt correctly

title: Haptic Feedback on Skip Events
description:
# Haptic Feedback on Skip Events

## Goal
Provide subtle tactile confirmation when ads are auto-skipped, so users feel the app working for them.

## Rationale
Auto-skip is silent and invisible — users might not notice it happened. A light haptic pulse at the moment of skip creates sensory confirmation: "I just saved you time." UIImpactFeedbackGenerator.light is barely perceptible but registers subconsciously. Tiny implementation effort, meaningful UX signal. Optional in Settings for users who don't want it.

## Implementation

### SkipOrchestrator Integration
- Modify `Playhead/Services/SkipOrchestrator/SkipOrchestrator.swift`
- SkipOrchestrator is an actor, but `UIImpactFeedbackGenerator` must be called on the main thread.

#### Prepare Phase
- When an AdWindow's `SkipDecisionState` transitions to `.confirmed` (the state before `.skipped` — this is the "approaching" moment), dispatch to MainActor to call `.prepare()`:
  ```swift
  if userPreferences.hapticsOnSkip {
      Task { @MainActor in
          hapticGenerator.prepare()
      }
  }
  ```
- Store a `@MainActor`-isolated `UIImpactFeedbackGenerator(style: .light)` instance — reuse rather than creating new instances per skip (Apple docs recommend reuse for better latency)

#### Fire Phase
- When `SkipDecisionState` transitions to `.skipped`, fire the haptic:
  ```swift
  if userPreferences.hapticsOnSkip {
      Task { @MainActor in
          hapticGenerator.impactOccurred()
      }
  }
  ```
- Fire for these SkipBehavior modes: `.auto` (seek past ad), `.fastForward` (rate change), `.mute` (silence)
- Do NOT fire for: `.manual` (user-initiated, they already have tactile feedback from button tap), `.off` (no ad handling)
- Note: `.fastForward` and `.mute` are added by playhead-x5l. If that bead is not yet built, fire only for `.auto`. Guard with a check on SkipBehavior cases available at compile time.
- Respects system haptic settings automatically (UIFeedbackGenerator returns no-op when system haptics are disabled)

### UserPreferences Change
- Add `hapticsOnSkip: Bool` to UserPreferences model (in `Playhead/Models/UserPreferences.swift`), default: `true`
- Add to init: `hapticsOnSkip: Bool = true`
- Requires lightweight SwiftData schema migration (add field to PlayheadSchemaV2 frozen snapshot)

### Settings UI
- Modify `Playhead/Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift`
- Settings -> Playback section -> "Haptic on Ad Skip" `Toggle` bound to `userPreferences.hapticsOnSkip`
- Subtitle text below toggle: "Feel a subtle tap when ads are skipped" (Instrument Sans, `.caption`, Soft Steel)

### Tests
- Unit: haptic fires on `.skipped` transition when `hapticsOnSkip == true` (verify MainActor dispatch via mock/protocol — extract `HapticProvider` protocol for testability)
- Unit: haptic does NOT fire when `hapticsOnSkip == false`
- Unit: haptic does NOT fire for `.manual` or `.off` SkipBehavior
- Unit: `.prepare()` called on `.confirmed` transition (before `.skipped`)
- Unit: haptic fires for `.fastForward` and `.mute` modes (when playhead-x5l cases are available)
- No snapshot tests needed (haptic is non-visual)
- Note: `UIImpactFeedbackGenerator` cannot be meaningfully asserted in unit tests. Use a `HapticProvider` protocol to verify the call pattern:
  ```swift
  protocol HapticProvider: Sendable {
      @MainActor func prepare()
      @MainActor func fire()
  }
  ```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Light haptic fires on `.skipped` transition for active ad-handling modes (auto, fastForward, mute)
- [ ] `.prepare()` called on `.confirmed` transition for zero-latency feedback
- [ ] No haptic on `.manual` or `.off` SkipBehavior
- [ ] Toggle in Settings -> Playback to disable (default: on)
- [ ] Respects system-level haptic settings
- [ ] Reusable UIImpactFeedbackGenerator instance (not created per-skip)
- [ ] `HapticProvider` protocol for testability
- [ ] MainActor dispatch for all UIKit haptic calls
- [ ] Lightweight SwiftData schema migration for hapticsOnSkip field

title: Per-Show Playback Speed Memory
description:
# Per-Show Playback Speed Memory

## Goal
Remember each podcast's preferred playback speed so users don't manually adjust every time they switch shows.

## Rationale
Power listeners (the target audience for an ad-skipping app) listen to different shows at different speeds — conversational interviews at 1.0x, news briefings at 2.0x. Having to manually adjust is friction. High value-to-effort ratio. The app feels like it "learns" the user.

## Implementation

### Model Change
- Add optional `preferredSpeed: Double?` to Podcast SwiftData model (in `Playhead/Models/Podcast.swift`)
- nil = use global default from `UserPreferences.playbackSpeed`
- Valid range: 0.5-3.0 (matching AVPlayer supported range). Clamped on write.
- Requires lightweight SwiftData schema migration (new field in PlayheadSchemaV2, add to frozen Podcast snapshot)

### Speed Resolution
```swift
/// Returns the effective playback speed for an episode.
/// Priority: per-show override > global default
func effectiveSpeed(for episode: Episode) -> Double {
    episode.podcast?.preferredSpeed ?? userPreferences.playbackSpeed
}
```
This pattern is used in PlaybackService and should be extracted as a shared utility if multiple services need it.

### PlaybackService Integration
- Modify `PlaybackService` (in `Playhead/Services/PlaybackTransport/PlaybackTransport.swift`)
- On episode load: resolve effective speed via `episode.podcast?.preferredSpeed ?? UserPreferences.playbackSpeed`, apply to `AVPlayer.rate`
- When user manually changes speed during playback via the speed picker in Now Playing:
  - If new speed differs from `episode.podcast?.preferredSpeed` (or preferredSpeed is nil and speed differs from global default):
    - Show inline toast: "Remember [speed]x for [Show Name]?" with "Yes" / "Just this time" buttons
    - Toast auto-dismisses after 4s if no interaction (treated as "Just this time")
    - "Yes" writes `newSpeed` to `episode.podcast?.preferredSpeed` via SwiftData
  - If new speed matches existing preferredSpeed: no prompt (avoid redundant prompts)

### Toast View
- New file: `Playhead/Views/NowPlaying/SpeedPromptToast.swift`
- Positioned above transport controls, horizontally centered
- Background: Ink with 90% opacity, corner radius 12pt
- Text: "Remember 1.5x for [Show Name]?" in Instrument Sans, `.subheadline`, Bone color
- Buttons: "Yes" (Copper tint) | "Just this time" (Soft Steel tint), `.caption` size
- Entrance animation: `.transition(.move(edge: .bottom).combined(with: .opacity))` with `.easeOut(duration: 0.25)`
- Dismissal: fade out over 0.2s after 4s timeout or button tap

### Settings UI
- Per-show settings accessible via long-press on podcast in Library -> contextual menu -> "Show Settings" sheet
- The "Show Settings" sheet is a shared per-show settings pattern used by multiple beads (playhead-x5l for ad handling, playhead-snp for notifications, playhead-5w4 for auto-download). All per-show overrides should appear in this single sheet, organized in sections.
- New file (shared): `Playhead/Views/Library/ShowSettingsSheet.swift`
- Speed section: `Picker("Playback Speed", selection:)` with options from 0.5x to 3.0x in 0.25x increments
- Current display: shows current saved speed or "Default ([current global]x)" when preferredSpeed is nil
- Reset option: "Use default speed" button that sets preferredSpeed = nil

### Tests
- Unit: PlaybackService applies per-show speed on episode load (mock Episode with podcast.preferredSpeed = 1.5)
- Unit: fallback to UserPreferences.playbackSpeed when preferredSpeed is nil
- Unit: speed persistence round-trips through SwiftData (write, read back, verify)
- Unit: prompt not shown when speed matches existing preferredSpeed
- Unit: prompt not shown when speed matches global default and preferredSpeed is nil
- Unit: "Yes" saves speed; "Just this time" does not modify preferredSpeed
- Unit: 4s timeout dismisses toast without saving
- Snapshot: speed prompt toast (active with buttons, dismissed), per-show speed picker in Show Settings sheet, Dynamic Type sizes
- E2E: set speed for show A, switch to show B (different speed), switch back to A — verify speed restores

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Per-show speed applied automatically on episode load
- [ ] Falls back to UserPreferences.playbackSpeed when no per-show preference set
- [ ] Speed change prompt is non-intrusive (dismisses automatically after 4s)
- [ ] Toast entrance/exit animated (0.25s in, 0.2s out)
- [ ] Per-show speed editable in shared Show Settings sheet (long-press podcast)
- [ ] Speed persists across app launches
- [ ] Speed clamped to 0.5-3.0 range
- [ ] Lightweight SwiftData schema migration handled for existing installs
- [ ] VoiceOver announces speed prompt and picker
- [ ] Dynamic Type scales prompt and settings correctly

title: E2E: Performance & Resource Budgets
description:
Prove the app meets performance targets and stays within resource budgets. These are hard numeric gates.

## Test: Time-to-First-Usable-Skip
For each device tier in corpus:
1. Cold start (fresh episode, no prior analysis)
2. Measure: time from play tap to first correct skip firing
3. Assert: < 30s on iPhone 15 Pro, < 45s on iPhone 16

## Test: Analysis Throughput vs Playback Speed
1. Play at 1.0x → verify: analysis stays ahead by ≥ 30s audio
2. Play at 2.0x → verify: analysis stays ahead by ≥ 15s wall-clock
3. Play at 3.0x → verify: analysis stays ahead OR graceful degradation (no crash, skip when ready)

## Test: Memory Budget
1. Play a 90-minute episode at 2x
2. Sample memory usage every 60 seconds
3. Assert: memory usage < 200MB throughout (no leaks)
4. Assert: memory usage at minute 45 within 10% of minute 5 (stable)

## Test: Battery Impact
1. Play 30 minutes of a podcast with analysis running
2. Measure battery drain via MetricKit or simulated battery API
3. Assert: battery impact < 10% per hour of audio processed
4. Compare: analysis running vs analysis disabled (baseline)

## Test: Storage Growth
1. Analyze 10 one-hour episodes
2. Measure: total SQLite DB size
3. Assert: < 5MB per hour of audio (transcript chunks + ad windows + features)
4. Verify: model files accounted for separately in storage display

## Test: Decode/ASR/Detect Pipeline Latency (os_signpost)
1. Run replay simulator on labeled episode
2. Collect os_signpost intervals for each pipeline stage
3. Assert: decode latency < 100ms per analysis shard
4. Assert: fast-pass ASR < 500ms per chunk on iPhone 15 Pro
5. Assert: lexical scan < 10ms per chunk
6. Assert: classifier < 100ms per candidate
7. Assert: skip decision < 5ms per AdWindow

## Test: Concurrent Playback + Analysis Thread Safety
1. Play episode while analysis runs
2. Run for 10 minutes
3. Assert: zero main thread hangs > 100ms (verified via Thread Sanitizer or hang detection)
4. Assert: zero data races (verified via Thread Sanitizer)
5. Assert: audio never glitches (no underruns reported by AVAudioSession)

Acceptance criteria:
- All numeric assertions pass on target hardware
- Pipeline latency within budget at each stage
- Zero memory leaks, zero thread hangs, zero data races
- Battery impact within stated budget
- Results reproducible across 3 consecutive runs (< 10% variance)

title: E2E: Dynamic Ad Insertion
description:
Prove the asset fingerprinting system correctly handles dynamic ad insertion — the same episode URL serving different audio. This is critical for real-world correctness.

## Test: Same Episode, Different Ad Fill
1. Load episode A from corpus (variant 1: Squarespace ad at 3:00)
2. Run full analysis → verify AdWindows match labeled positions
3. Load same episode A (variant 2: Athletic Greens ad at 3:00, different audio bytes)
4. Verify: different assetFingerprint generated
5. Verify: new AnalysisAsset created (not reusing variant 1 results)
6. Run analysis on variant 2 → verify AdWindows match variant 2 labels
7. Verify: Episode.lastPlayedAnalysisAssetId updated to variant 2

## Test: Same Audio, Same Fingerprint
1. Load episode A variant 1 twice
2. Verify: same assetFingerprint both times
3. Verify: second load reuses existing AnalysisAsset (no re-analysis)
4. Verify: cached AdWindows served immediately

## Test: Progressive Fingerprinting
1. Start streaming episode (not fully cached)
2. Verify: weakFingerprint generated from HTTP metadata (ETag, Content-Length)
3. As audio caches progressively, verify: weak fingerprint used for initial analysis
4. Once fully cached: verify: strong fingerprint (content hash) computed
5. If strong fingerprint matches weak → analysis results preserved
6. If strong fingerprint differs → new AnalysisAsset, re-analysis triggered

## Test: Preview Budget Across Variants
1. Play episode A variant 1 (free tier), consume 8 minutes of budget
2. Play episode A variant 2 (different ad fill)
3. Verify: same canonicalEpisodeKey → shared preview budget
4. Verify: only 4 minutes of budget remaining (12 - 8 = 4)
5. This prevents users from getting extra free analysis by triggering different ad variants

## Test: Multiple Analysis Assets Per Episode
1. Play episode A over 3 sessions with dynamic ads (3 different fills)
2. Verify: 3 AnalysisAsset records in SQLite for same episodeId
3. Verify: Episode.lastPlayedAnalysisAssetId points to most recent
4. Verify: old AnalysisAssets still queryable for evaluation

Acceptance criteria:
- Different audio bytes always produce different fingerprints
- Same audio bytes always produce same fingerprint
- No stale ad windows served for changed audio
- Preview budget correctly shared across variants
- Multiple analysis assets coexist cleanly per episode

title: E2E: Banner Accuracy
description:
Prove that banners show correct, evidence-backed copy and behave correctly. Maps to Success Criterion #9.

## Test: High-Confidence Banner Copy
1. Skip ad where lexical scanner found "brought to you by Squarespace, build your website"
2. Foundation Models extracts: advertiser="Squarespace", product="Build your website"
3. Verify: banner shows "Skipped · Squarespace · \"Build your website\"" (product wrapped in straight ASCII double-quotes, not typographic quotes; code uses Text("\"\\(detail)\"") at AdBannerView.swift line 241)
4. Verify: AdWindow.metadataSource = "foundationModels" (raw string; metadataSource is a String, not an enum)
5. Verify: AdWindow.evidenceText contains the matched transcript fragment

## Test: Low-Confidence Fallback
1. Skip ad where lexical scanner found "check out the link in the description"
2. No clear advertiser/product extractable
3. Verify: banner shows "Skipped sponsor segment" (generic)
4. Verify: NO brand name guessed or hallucinated

## Test: No Foundation Models Available
1. Mock CapabilitiesService to report Foundation Models unavailable
2. Skip ad with strong lexical evidence
3. Verify: banner shows lexical-derived copy if confident, generic otherwise
4. Verify: AdWindow.metadataSource = "fallback" (FallbackExtractor uses source: "fallback"; there is no "regex" or "lexicon" source value)
5. Verify: skip still fires correctly (detection not degraded)

## Test: Banner Queue Coalescing
1. Three ads detected within 10 seconds (back-to-back sponsor segment)
2. Verify: single banner shown (coalesced), not three stacked
3. Banner copy reflects the most recent or most confident skip

## Test: Banner Auto-Dismiss
1. Skip fires, banner appears
2. Wait 8 seconds
3. Verify: banner dismissed automatically
4. Verify: no UI artifacts left behind

## Test: Listen Rewind Behavior
1. Skip fires, banner appears
2. Tap "Listen"
3. Verify: playback rewinds to snapped start of ad window (stored as adStartTime in AdSkipBannerItem, populated from snappedStart)
4. Verify: audio plays through the ad
5. Verify: same ad is NOT auto-skipped again this playthrough
6. Verify: AdWindow.decisionState = "reverted" (raw string; SkipDecisionState.reverted in-memory)
7. Verify: PodcastProfile trust updated (skipTrustScore decremented via TrustScoringService.recordFalseSkipSignal)

## Test: Banner During Speed Change
1. Playing at 2x speed
2. Ad detected and skipped
3. Verify: banner appears with correct timing (not 2x fast dismiss)
4. Auto-dismiss still at 8 wall-clock seconds

## Test: No Banner on Manual Mode
1. Show is in .manual skip mode (SkipMode enum; stored as rawValue string in PodcastProfile.mode)
2. Ad detected; SkipOrchestrator transitions window to .confirmed (not .applied)
3. Verify: "Skip Ad" button appears AND banner IS shown simultaneously (SkipOrchestrator.evaluateAndPush emits bannerItem for .confirmed windows — same logic as shadow mode; manual mode does NOT suppress banners)
   NOTE: The "Skip Ad" button UI is not yet implemented in NowPlayingView. SkipOrchestrator.applyManualSkip() and confirmedWindows() are the complete API; the button that calls them is a pending Phase 8 deliverable. Steps 4–6 below describe the intended end-to-end flow once the button is wired.
4. Verify: NO auto-skip (playback continues through the ad until user taps "Skip Ad")
5. User taps "Skip Ad"
6. Verify: skip cue fires (applyManualSkip promotes window to .applied); NO second banner (banneredWindowIds prevents re-emission)

## Test: Shadow Mode — Banner Shown, No Skip Fired
1. Show is in .shadow skip mode (SkipMode enum; stored as rawValue string in PodcastProfile.mode)
2. Ad detected; SkipOrchestrator transitions window to .confirmed (not .applied)
3. Verify: banner IS shown (SkipOrchestrator.evaluateAndPush emits bannerItem for .confirmed windows — shadow mode does NOT suppress banners)
4. Verify: NO skip cue fired (playback continues through the ad)
5. Verify: NO "Skip Ad" button (manual-mode UI is not shown)
6. Verify: AdWindow still logged in SQLite for evaluation
NOTE: Prior description said "NO banner" in shadow mode — this was incorrect. Code at SkipOrchestrator.swift lines 667-672 emits bannerItem for any .confirmed window, including those held in shadow mode. Shadow suppresses the skip action, not the banner.

Acceptance criteria:
- Zero hallucinated brand names across all test scenarios
- Generic copy shown whenever evidence is weak
- Listen rewind precise to within 1s of snapped boundary
- Coalescing prevents visible banner pile-up
- All trust modes produce correct banner/button/nothing behavior

Implementation notes (code-verified):
- metadataSource is a raw String on AdWindow; known values: "foundationModels", "fallback", "none"
- decisionState is a raw String on AdWindow; SkipDecisionState enum (candidate/confirmed/applied/suppressed/reverted) in-memory
- PodcastProfile trust is tracked via skipTrustScore (Double), observationCount (Int), recentFalseSkipSignals (Int) — not a named "trust signals" property
- Skip mode is SkipMode enum (.shadow/.manual/.auto) stored as rawValue String in PodcastProfile.mode
- Banner confidence gate is 0.60 (AdBannerView.metadataConfidenceThreshold)
- Coalesce gap is 10.0 seconds (AdBannerQueue.coalesceGap)
- Product detail wrapped in straight ASCII double-quotes in banner copy (not typographic); AdBannerView.swift line 241: Text("\"\\(detail)\"")
- In both shadow and manual modes, banner fires when window first reaches .confirmed (SkipOrchestrator lines 667-672); banneredWindowIds Set prevents re-emission on subsequent state transitions
- Skip Ad button UI (calls applyManualSkip / reads confirmedWindows) is not yet built in NowPlayingView; SkipOrchestrator API is complete

title: E2E: Skip Quality & Trust Lifecycle
description:
Prove that skips are accurate, boundaries are clean, and the trust system works. Maps to Success Criteria #4 (wrong-content skip rate), #5 (boundary error), #7 (fail-open), and #14 (trust demotion).

## Test: Boundary Accuracy on Labeled Corpus
For each episode in the labeled corpus:
1. Run full analysis pipeline
2. Compare detected AdWindow boundaries to labeled ground truth
3. Assert: median boundary error < 2 seconds
4. Assert: no detected window overlaps actual content by > 3 seconds
5. Assert: false-positive skip seconds < 5% of total episode duration
6. Log: per-episode boundary error distribution

## Test: Hysteresis Prevents Flicker
1. Feed SkipOrchestrator a sequence of AdWindows with oscillating confidence (0.7, 0.8, 0.7, 0.8)
2. Verify: single continuous skip cue, not rapid on/off
3. Feed sequence that drops below exit threshold (0.7, 0.3, 0.3)
4. Verify: skip cue ends cleanly

## Test: Gap Merging
1. Create two AdWindows 3s apart → verify merged into single skip cue
2. Create two AdWindows 5s apart → verify NOT merged (separate cues)
3. Create three AdWindows: 2s gap, 3s gap → verify all three merged

## Test: Silence Snapping
1. Create AdWindow with boundary at t=180.0s
2. Provide FeatureWindows showing silence at t=179.2s and t=181.5s
3. Verify: skip boundary snaps to 179.2s (nearest silence before ad)
4. Verify: resume point snaps to silence after ad end

## Test: Fail-Open Behavior
1. Feed ambiguous candidates (confidence 0.4-0.6) to SkipOrchestrator
2. Verify: NO skip fires (fail open)
3. Verify: no "possible ad?" UI appears
4. Verify: AdWindow.decisionState = .suppressed

## Test: Late Detection (No Rewind)
1. Playhead is at t=200s
2. Ad detected for range t=150s-t=180s (already past)
3. Verify: NO rewind occurs
4. Verify: AdWindow logged but decisionState = .suppressed (too late)

## Test: Seek Suppression
1. User seeks from t=100s to t=300s
2. There's a known ad at t=305s
3. Verify: auto-skip suppressed for configurable duration after seek
4. After suppression window passes, verify: skip fires normally

## Test: Trust Lifecycle — Shadow to Auto
1. Subscribe to new show (not in corpus, no PodcastProfile)
2. Verify: mode = .shadow
3. Play 3 episodes, all with correctly detected ads
4. Verify: after threshold observations, mode promotes to .manual
5. User sees "Skip Ad" buttons (not auto-skip)
6. User taps "Skip Ad" for 5 ads with no Listen reversions
7. Verify: mode promotes to .auto
8. Next ad auto-skips

## Test: Trust Demotion — Auto to Manual
1. Show is in .auto mode
2. User taps "Listen" on 3 consecutive skips
3. Verify: recentFalseSkipSignals incremented each time
4. Verify: mode demotes to .manual after threshold
5. Next ad shows button instead of auto-skipping

## Test: Trust Override
1. Show is in .shadow mode
2. User manually sets show to .auto in settings
3. Verify: mode = .auto regardless of trust score
4. Next ad auto-skips

Acceptance criteria:
- Boundary accuracy meets numeric thresholds on labeled corpus
- Trust lifecycle completes full promotion and demotion cycles
- Zero wrong-content skips on labeled corpus (false-positive skip of actual content)
- All assertions have specific numeric values
- Full per-episode metrics report generated

title: Replay Simulator
description:
Test harness that replays labeled episodes under configurable conditions and produces quantitative metrics. This is the foundation for all skip quality E2E tests.

## Core Capability
Given a labeled episode (audio + JSON annotations with ad boundaries), the simulator:
1. Configures playback conditions (speed, streamed vs cached, etc.)
2. Runs the full analysis pipeline (decode → features → transcription → ad_detection → cue_materialization)
3. Records every skip decision, boundary, and timing
4. Compares results against ground truth labels
5. Produces a structured metrics report

## Simulated Conditions (configurable per run)
- Audio source: streamed (progressive cache) vs fully cached
- Playback speed: 0.5x, 1.0x, 1.5x, 2.0x, 2.5x, 3.0x
- User actions: scrub to specific time, speed change mid-episode, pause/resume
- Late detections: inject a detection that arrives after playhead has passed the ad
- Dynamic ad variants: swap audio mid-test to simulate DAI
- System state: thermal throttling (.serious, .critical), Low Power Mode
- Foundation Models: available vs unavailable

## Metrics Report (structured Swift types, serialized to JSON)

Metrics are organized into four nested structs — NOT a flat JSON object with snake_case fields:

### DetectionQualityMetrics
- falsePositiveSkipSeconds: total seconds incorrectly skipped
- falseNegativeAdSeconds: total seconds of ads not skipped
- precision, recall, f1Score
- missedSegmentCount: ground-truth segments with zero detection overlap
- spuriousSegmentCount: detections with no ground-truth overlap

### BoundaryQualityMetrics
- cutSpeechAtEntryMs: [Double] — entry error per skip (not a single scalar)
- cutSpeechAtResumeMs: [Double] — resume error per skip
- p50EntryErrorMs, p95EntryErrorMs
- p50ResumeErrorMs, p95ResumeErrorMs
- NOTE: no single boundary_error_ms field; no skip_transition_duration_ms field

### LatencyMetrics
- timeToFirstUsableSkip: Double? — seconds (not milliseconds) from play start to first skip
- p50BannerLatencyMs, p95BannerLatencyMs
- meanPipelineLatencyMs, p95PipelineLatencyMs

### UserOverrideMetrics
- listenTapCount: simulated Listen taps (bead said manual_override_count — wrong name)
- rewindAfterSkipCount: rewind-after-skip events
- overrideRate: overrides / total skips applied

Aggregate (CorpusReplayReport):
- p50 and p95 of each per-episode metric (NO p99 — not implemented)
- total episodes tested, total false positives, missed/spurious segment counts

## Instrumentation
- os_signpost: single "DetectionPipeline" interval in SimulatedPlaybackDriver covering the detection batch per chunk. Individual per-stage spans (decode / ASR / lexical scan / classify / skip decision / banner render) are NOT present in the replay simulator.
- Production pipeline stage signposts (PreAnalysisInstrumentation.swift): decode, features, transcription, ad_detection, cue_materialization. Note: the pipeline stage for ASR is called "transcription", not "ASR"; the detection stage is "ad_detection" not "classify"; there is no "skip decision" or "banner render" stage.
- Versioned diagnostic output: EpisodeReplayReport carries simulatorVersion string ("replay-sim-v1"). NOT tied to analysisVersion + policyVersion pair.
- MetricKit: NOT IMPLEMENTED. No MXMetricManager or MXMetricPayload code exists anywhere in the codebase; mentioned only in planning documents.

## Regression Mode
NOT YET IMPLEMENTED. No baseline comparison storage or threshold-based regression detection exists. The 10% threshold acceptance criterion is aspirational.

Acceptance criteria:
- Can replay any labeled episode and produce complete metrics report
- Simulated conditions produce measurably different behavior (faster speed = different timing)
- Regression mode catches intentional degradation (not yet implemented)
- Report parseable by CI for automated threshold checking
- Completes replay of a 60-minute episode in < 5 minutes (faster than real-time)

title: readmitModeDivertedSuggestions re-delivers on a DOWNWARD pill tap, where it provably cannot promote anything
description:
FOUND 2026-08-13 by the R1 review round on playhead-wq34. Marginal, filed so it is not re-derived.

`setActiveSkipMode` writes `mode` into EVERY entry of `activeDetectorSkipModes.byDetector`, so after it returns `admissionSkipMode` yields `mode` for every row. When `mode != .auto`, `managedTierWouldBeSilent` is therefore true for every suggest-tier candidate (the `.applied` rows among them are re-diverted by the catalog-authority check that put them there), and `readmitModeDivertedSuggestions` cannot move a single row into the managed tier. It is a provable no-op.

It is not free, though, and the cost is the one the method's own doc names as its ONE KNOWN NARROWNESS: re-delivery calls `nextProducerMutationGeneration()`, so a genuine producer revision for one of those ids that is suspended at the catalog-authority hop when the pill is tapped finds itself stale and is dropped. The doc justifies paying that for the upward case, where the listener gets their skips back. On a downward or lateral tap they get nothing for it — the listener loses one revision of one window in exchange for a re-admission that could not have changed anything.

FIX SHAPE: guard the call on `mode == .auto` (or, equivalently and more honestly, on \'the new modes can admit something the old ones could not\'). Cheap, and provably behaviour-preserving by the argument above — but it needs a rail, and the rail wants an observable for "the row was not re-delivered", which R1 established is the ingest census (`adWindowIngestOutcomeCount(.armedSuggest)`), not the tier maps: a re-delivered suggest row is routed straight back, so tier membership cannot see it. That is the same measurement `pillRestoresAutoSkipForAlreadyDeliveredRows`\' control now uses.

title: Remove dead code: applyBoundaryRefinement helper at AdDetectionService.swift:5429
description:
## Context

PR #211's bd-4xqf code-path map identified that the private helper `applyBoundaryRefinement` at `AdDetectionService.swift:5429` (was line 5219 before p56a's +213 lines) is unreachable in production. The live boundary refinement runs inline at lines 3186-3260 inside `runBackfill`'s per-span loop, using `BracketAwareBoundaryRefiner.computeAdjustments(...)` with `BoundaryRefiner.computeAdjustments(...)` fallback.

The dead helper duplicates the legacy `BoundaryRefiner.computeAdjustments` call path. It has no in-file callers per grep. It compiles into the Playhead target but is never invoked.

## Scope

Remove `applyBoundaryRefinement` from `AdDetectionService.swift`. Verify no indirect callers (DI, factory, runtime lookup, generic dispatch). If verification reveals an indirect caller, document the wiring instead and update `docs/bd-4xqf-codepath-map.md`.

## Acceptance

- `grep -rn "applyBoundaryRefinement" Playhead/` returns zero hits OR documented wiring
- PlayheadFastTests passes
- Build clean (no orphaned-reference warnings)
- `docs/bd-4xqf-codepath-map.md` SpanFinalizer status section's "applyBoundaryRefinement VERIFIED UNREACHABLE" note is removed (no longer needed once the dead code is gone)

## Constraints

- NO changes to the live refinement path at lines 3186-3260
- NO changes to BoundaryRefiner or BracketAwareBoundaryRefiner (they're used by the live path)

## Cross-references

- PR #207 (codepath map original)
- PR #209 (SpanFinalizer reachability verification — used same grep methodology)
- PR #211 (codepath map fix that flagged applyBoundaryRefinement as dead)
- PR #214 (p56a wire-in that this is companion cleanup to)
